lines_before.dialogue: The hidden chamber hums with a different quality than the Spire's calming blanket—this frequency is sharp, clinical, and carries the sterile scent of preserved knowledge. Crystalline data banks line the walls, glowing with trapped light.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air shimmers with containment harmonics.

lines_before.dialogue: It feels like we're about to graduate from ignorance to something far heavier. I don't understand anything about why they'd keep this hidden.
lines_before.stage_directions: Runs a hand over a dusty resonator console.

lines_before.dialogue: What kind do you like? What style of truth do you prefer—the peaceful lie or the dangerous one? My entire order... we listened for natural harmony while they conducted this... this butchery of frequencies.
lines_before.stage_directions: Voice trembles between reverence and rage.

lines_before.dialogue: Look at this! 'Controlled Lattice Collapse'—they were playing with fire! This isn't research, it's arson with sound!
lines_before.stage_directions: Points angrily at etched crystal plates.

lines_before.dialogue: Prototype resonator. Still active. They left the weapon here like it was just another experiment. The arrogance.
lines_before.stage_directions: Taps the dormant device cautiously.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay alert. This place feels... watched. That log entry said the test went wrong, but someone authorized it first.
lines_before.stage_directions: Hand on weapon, scanning the shadows.

lines_before.dialogue: As the final log entry's implications settle—a radical faction, an unauthorized test, the Echo of Dawn as collateral damage—the chamber's harmonics shift. A security resonance triggers, sealing the entrance with a wall of shimmering sound.
lines_before.stage_directions: The doorway dissolves into vibrating crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: A harmonic containment field activates, wrapping the chamber in layers of dissonant frequencies. The air grows heavy, pressing against eardrums and lungs.
lines_after.stage_directions: Geometric patterns of light cage the room.

lines_after.dialogue: The truth was never going to let us leave quietly. They built this place to keep secrets in... and now it's keeping us in.
lines_after.stage_directions: Staff pulses with anxious light.

lines_after.dialogue: I can't make it back! The exit frequency is jammed! This isn't scary at all! Just a fancy cage!
lines_after.stage_directions: Pounds uselessly on the resonant barrier, bravado cracking.

lines_after.dialogue: The prototype—it's our way out or our tomb. But which?
lines_after.stage_directions: Already examining the resonator's connections.

line.dialogue: The containment field feeds on harmony—break it violently with the prototype, and we risk triggering another lattice disturbance. Or... I might be able to unravel it note by note. But slowly. And if I'm wrong...
line.stage_directions: Eyes fixed on the shimmering barrier, hands trembling slightly.

choices.description: Arthit steps forward with tattooed routes, ready to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
The lattice has other plans. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.description: Malee uses crystal prosthetic to record the spectral signature near the resonance anchor

line.dialogue: Malee finds the key. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The resonance turns hostile. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.description: Have the monk focus lattice study on the resonance anchor to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the monk pulls it off. Crystal bowls shatter in harmonic sympathy.
the monk misreads the situation. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: Back on the main observation deck, the Anchor's hum wraps around you like a shroud. The Lattice below glitters with false serenity, while the damning evidence in your hands feels impossibly heavy. Three figures stand before you: the Monk, the captured Pirate, and a new arrival—a Tonal Order envoy in immaculate crystalline robes.
lines_before.stage_directions: The envoy stands unnervingly still, hands folded. The Pirate is bound but alert. The Monk shifts nervously.

lines_before.dialogue: The truth doesn't stay hidden forever. But what happens when you uncover it? Do you stay still, or do you move?
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit holds up the log and resonator, the artifacts catching the strange light.

lines_before.dialogue: We have to show everyone. The Orders have been lying about the Silencing, about the risks. I don't agree with him.
lines_before.stage_directions: He gestures sharply at the envoy, his voice trembling with resolve.

lines_before.dialogue: They sabotaged their own research ship! They let people die to protect their charts! How can we just sit tight with this?
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida paces, her anger cutting through the calming hum.

lines_before.dialogue: Check the envoy's posture. Calm as a statue. He's not here to argue—he's here to deal. The kind of deal that makes problems disappear.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee's eyes scan the envoy, her hand resting on her weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay right there. Everyone. We don't know what they'll do. That hum... it's too calm. It's pressing down on my thoughts.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly in front of the party, tense and protective.

lines_before.dialogue: The envoy finally speaks, his voice a smooth, modulated tone that seems to sync with the Anchor's frequency.
lines_before.stage_directions: A subtle vibration in the air makes the moment feel surreal, detached.

lines_after.dialogue: The envoy's offer hangs in the acoustically-deadened air. The Pirate looks at the ground, then at you, his fate now tied to your choice.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Pirate's bindings seem to tighten as the envoy smiles placidly.

lines_after.dialogue: A discovery that fractures your world. You can't stay the same after this. You either stay complicit, or you become a target.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff pulses with a faint, conflicted light.

lines_after.dialogue: Listen. We don't stay in touch after this, no matter what you pick. You expose this, every Order enforcer from here to the sky-rim will be hunting for the 'bandit who talked.' My crew scatters. I disappear. That's the deal if you're honest.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Pirate's voice is low, pragmatic, stripped of its usual bravado.

lines_after.dialogue: Then we make sure the truth disappears with you—into every port, every floating city! We can't just let this stay buried!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida steps forward, ready to act.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit's final choice: Accept the Order's deal (gain resources, ensure Pirate's freedom, but bury the truth), or publicly expose the evidence (triggering political upheaval, making enemies, and freeing the truth but risking lattice-wide panic).
line.stage_directions: The Monk meets Pichit's gaze, fearful but steadfast. The envoy watches, his calm a weapon.

choices.description: Pichit steps forward with Listener training, ready to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
A costly mistake by Pichit. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

choices.description: Have Arthit focus tattooed routes on the calm tones to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
Arthit fails. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.description: Convince the pirate to use disruptor weapon and decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: the pirate makes it work. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the pirate misreads the situation. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Khrueang Market hangs suspended between two floating islands, a chaotic tapestry of rope bridges, swaying platforms, and makeshift stalls. The air hums with the low resonance of crystal-powered lanterns and the murmur of desperate commerce. Below, the Lattice glimmers like a frozen sea of shattered glass.
lines_before.stage_directions: The camera pans across crowded walkways. People barter with guarded expressions, their eyes flicking toward the sky where the angular silhouettes of Tonal Order patrol ships occasionally drift past.

lines_before.dialogue: Anywhere you like, we should start. Asking discreetly is the best way. The truth is out here, somewhere... but it's worth waiting for.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit adjusts the grip on his staff, its crystalline tip pulsing faintly with his own resonant frequency. He scans the crowd, his expression a mix of determination and uncertainty.

lines_before.dialogue: Discreet? Look at this place! How do you be discreet in a shouting match? Let's just ask that merchant about unstable frequencies.
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points aggressively toward a spice vendor, nearly knocking over a basket of glowing moss.

lines_before.dialogue: And get reported before we take three steps. The Orders control all official charts. Asking about 'uncharted lattice zones' here is like asking where to find treason. I'm checking our funds. This might get expensive.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee keeps her hand near her toolbelt, her eyes calculating the worth of every stall and the likelihood of each face being an informant.

lines_before.dialogue: Keep your voices down. We're being watched. Not by the Orders... someone rougher.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit subtly shifts his stance, putting himself between the party and a shadowed alcove where several figures in patched flight leathers linger.

lines_before.dialogue: The party's cautious inquiries begin—a dropped question to a map-seller, a hypothetical posed to a resonator technician. The responses are nervous, clipped denials. Then, a voice cuts through the market din.
lines_before.stage_directions: A burly sky pirate, his face scarred from lattice-storm exposure, pushes off from the shadows Arthit noted.

lines_before.dialogue: 'Unstable frequencies'? You sound like you're about to graduate... from breathing. The Orders would arrest you for such naive questions. Makes my job easier—less competition for the real paths.
lines_before.stage_directions: He laughs, a rough, grating sound. His crewmates echo it, their hands resting on the harmonic blades at their hips. The intimidation is casual, practiced.

lines_before.dialogue: Before tension can snap, a contact—a nervous moss-trader Malee once repaired a resonator for—tugs at her sleeve. He whispers urgently.
lines_before.stage_directions: The trader's eyes dart between the pirates and the party.

lines_before.dialogue: Not here. A surface scavenger—deep diver, name of Kael. He was asking about 'safe paths through the scream-zones' last week. Paranoid. He's at the old tea stall on the lower rim. I'm leaving soon, didn't see me.
lines_before.stage_directions: The villager melts back into the crowd, leaving the party with a direction and a warning.

lines_before.dialogue: The lower rim is a world apart from the market's core—quieter, colder, where the lattice's hum is a tangible vibration in the platform grates. The tea stall is little more than a tarp and a steaming kettle. A figure in worn, crystal-dusted gear is hastily packing a satchel.
lines_before.stage_directions: Kael the scavenger moves with jerky, efficient motions. He glances over his shoulder every few seconds.

lines_before.dialogue: I'm about to go. No business today. The tea's cold.
lines_before.stage_directions: He doesn't make eye contact, his fingers tightening around a leather-wrapped cylinder peeking from his bag—a map case.

lines_before.dialogue: We're not here for tea. We heard you know the surface... the places the charts don't show.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit steps forward, keeping his staff low and non-threatening.

lines_before.dialogue: You heard wrong. I chart stable paths. Licensed. I'm about to graduate to a proper resonator ship pilot. Anything else is Order suppression.
lines_before.stage_directions: A lie, poorly delivered. His eyes betray fear, but also a flicker of pride. He's guarding something monumental.

lines_before.dialogue: Your resonator's tuned for dissonance-shielding. Not a standard license configuration. That's for volatile frequency zones. The 'scream-zones'.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee nods at the modified crystal apparatus on his pack. Her tone is matter-of-fact, not accusatory.

lines_before.dialogue: ...Fine. I mapped them. The unstable veins, the volatile harmonics. Places where the Lattice sings itself to pieces and reforms. The Tonal Orders bury this knowledge. They say it's chaos. But it's a pattern. A beautiful, dangerous pattern. This...
lines_before.stage_directions: He finally looks at them, a desperate fervor in his eyes. He touches the map case. "This is the Open Frequency Map. It's priceless. And if they find it on me, it's a death sentence."

lines_after.dialogue: The weight of the revelation hangs in the air. This isn't just information; it's a key to the world's locked places, and a target for every power in the sky.
lines_after.stage_directions: The scavenger watches them, poised to run. The distant hum of the market feels like a closing net.

lines_after.dialogue: He's going to graduate soon from scavenger to the most hunted person in the floating cities. We can't let that map fall to the pirates... or the Orders.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff glows brighter, reflecting his resolve. The decision is his.

lines_after.dialogue: Well, well. Lower rim's popular today.
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate captain's voice echoes from the walkway above. He and two others look down, their smiles predatory. The confrontation has been moved up the timeline.

lines_after.dialogue: Or we could just take the map from him and go! Faster!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida's hand goes to her weapon, eyes on the pirates above, then on the scavenger's satchel. She's already moving into a defensive stance.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide how to gain the scavenger's trust: offer a substantial trade (risking their funds), offer protection (a promise they may not keep), or imply a threat (aligning with pirate methods).
line.stage_directions: Kael clutches his map, eyes wide, trapped between the party and the looming pirates. The moment stretches, thin and sharp as crystal.

choices.description: Split up and blend in—Pichit and Chanida work the market stalls while Malee and Arthit scan the crowd for watchers.

line.dialogue: Good. We move like we belong here, and we meet back at the teak bridge before the sun moves one hand's width.
Split up? In this place? We'll lose each other before the next bell—and that's exactly what they're hoping for.

choices.description: Approach the old herbalist woman Arthit noticed earlier—her stall is tucked away where eyes can't easily follow.

line.dialogue: She's the kind who hears everything and sells to everyone. If anyone knows where the whispers started, it's her.
Too obvious. She just made a signal under her tray—we're not the only ones who spotted her. Back away, now.

choices.description: Buy four bowls of noodles from the nearest cart and sit together, talking casually while letting the conversation around them do the work.

line.dialogue: Ears are loose when mouths are full. We listen, we don't ask, and we let the rumors come to us like flies to sugar.
The noodle vendor just looked at the Orders officer and nodded. We're sitting down to eat in a

lines_before.dialogue: The scavenger's eyes dart between the party members, then toward a shadowed alcove between two humming crystal merchant stalls. The air there is cooler, thick with the ozone scent of old resonators.
lines_before.stage_directions: The market's ambient noise lowers to a murmur in the alcove.

lines_before.dialogue: My stomach is starting to growl! But that's no problem. Finding this is more important than a meal. I believe we can do this—find a path the Orders haven't charted.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit touches the warm crystal of his staff, its gentle pulse a comfort.

lines_before.dialogue: Alright. In here. Quick. This... it's not a chart. It's a log. My family's life, written in safe whispers through storms that'd shatter your ship. 'Quiet paths' through the screaming lattice.
lines_before.stage_directions: The scavenger unclasps a worn leather case, revealing parchment covered in delicate, intuitive markings, not rigid coordinates.

lines_before.dialogue: A family log? That's incredible! You're not going anywhere with this, are you? You should be sharing it!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida leans in, her eyes wide with excitement, ignoring the scavenger's flinch.

lines_before.dialogue: Incredible and illegal. The Tonal Orders would flay you for having this. It requires a Singer's intuition to read? Or a lifetime of listening? That's no simple map.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee scans the alcove entrance, her hand resting on the hilt of her tool-knife.

lines_before.dialogue: Keep your voice down. This is a life's work. We're not here to take it. We're here to... understand it.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly between the map and the market, his posture defensive.

lines_before.dialogue: A heavy boot scuffs the grating outside the alcove. The shadow that falls across the entrance is broad, blocking the fractured light.
lines_before.stage_directions: The sky pirate from the docks fills the doorway, a smirk on his scarred face.

lines_after.dialogue: The alcove becomes a pressure cooker of silent tension. The scavenger slams the case shut, clutching it to their chest like a child.
lines_after.stage_directions: Three factions frozen in a triangle of want and fear.

lines_after.dialogue: There’s something in my eye... a moment of clarity. This isn't just a transaction. It's a choice between preservation and plunder.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff glows faintly as he assesses the standoff.

lines_after.dialogue: Salvage rights, surface-rats. Finders keepers. And I found you finding it. That log'll lead to wrecks full of pre-Silencing tech. Worth more than your scruples.
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate takes a step forward, his hand on a weapon at his belt.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't let him have it! It'll be lost, or worse, used to break more of the world! Come on!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida's fists are clenched, ready to spring.

line.dialogue: Please. It's all I have. Don't let him take it. Don't let anyone take it the wrong way.
line.stage_directions: The scavenger's voice is a desperate whisper, eyes pleading with Pichit.

choices.description: Pocket the family log quietly while Malee argues with the scavenger about reporting it.

line.dialogue: Done — tucked inside my shirt. Now *everyone* stop yelling and let's eat before my stomach gives us away.
The pages crinkled — Malee heard it. She's staring at my jacket like she can see through the fabric.

choices.description: Ask the scavenger what price would keep their silence permanently.

line.dialogue: Three months of rations and a name I never have to hear again. You've got yourself a deal, Chanida.
Silence? You think I dragged you down here to negotiate? I brought you because *someone* has to know before they find it on my corpse.

choices.description: Read a random entry aloud to understand what the Tonal Orders are hiding.

line.dialogue: This entry — it's dated the week the Belltower fell. They *knew*. Every family in this district knew and did nothing.
Stop reading! Those words carry resonance — say the wrong phrase and every Tuned ear within a block will feel it. You're ringing a bell you cannot un-ring.

lines_before.dialogue: The scuffle spills onto a narrow market balcony, the carved railing the only barrier between you and the endless crystalline sea below. The pirate's crew blocks the archway back to the bazaar, their hands resting on weapon hilts. From this height, the Lattice looks like frozen music.
lines_before.stage_directions: The balcony creaks. Far below, the crystal surface hums with latent energy.

lines_before.dialogue: Knowledge shouldn't be left open like a door for anyone to walk through. Some doors lead to places that can't be closed again. We have to conserve what's precious, not exploit it.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit glances at the scavenger's clenched hands, then at the humming map case.

lines_before.dialogue: He's right. This map... it's a living record. It was made to conserve life, to find safe paths after the Silencing. Not to line pockets or raid trade routes. Look at it.
lines_before.stage_directions: The scavenger opens the case a crack. Inside, a crystal key pulses with a soft, unstable light. A faint, discordant hum leaks out.

lines_before.dialogue: It's... broadcasting? Don't leave it on! That's like shouting in a silent forest full of predators!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida's hand goes to her own weapon, eyes darting between the pirate and the glowing case.

lines_before.dialogue: Predators and authorities. The Tonal Orders sell their sanctioned frequencies at the guild halls for a fortune. They'd pay even more to destroy a rogue map. This is a liability with a pulse.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee checks the balcony's structural integrity, her expression grim.

lines_before.dialogue: We're cornered. There's no u-turn from this. We protect the scavenger, or we protect ourselves. But that thing... it's a beacon.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly in front of Pichit, shield-arm tense.

lines_before.dialogue: The pirate leader steps forward, his grin gone, replaced by cold calculation. The scavenger's resolve has changed the game.
lines_before.stage_directions: The market sounds from beyond the archway seem to fade, muffled by the tension.

lines_after.dialogue: A heavy silence falls, broken only by the map's erratic hum and the distant groan of the floating city.
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate's crew shifts, awaiting their leader's signal.

lines_after.dialogue: A choice to conserve, or a choice to consume. The Lattice remembers every note. What will it remember of us here?
lines_after.stage_directions: The crystal in Pichit's staff glows in sympathetic resonance with the map's key.

lines_after.dialogue: Enough philosophy. Last offer. Hand over the map, or I start shouting for the Order's market guards. I'll tell them you're frequency thieves, broadcasting illegal harmonics. They'll impound your ship, cage you in a silent cell. Your choice.
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate raises his voice, projecting toward the bazaar. It's not a bluff.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't just stand here! We either fight, flee, or... do something he won't expect.
lines_after.stage_directions: She edges toward the balcony railing, eyeing the lattice sea below as a potential, desperate route.

line.dialogue: It's your call, wanderer. I'd rather shatter it on these crystals than let him use it to plunder. But maybe... maybe you see another path?
line.stage_directions: The scavenger holds the map case over the railing, the pulsing light reflecting in their determined eyes.

choices.description: Smash the resonator crystal with the butt of your scavenged pry-bar before it finishes pinging.

line.dialogue: Good — crystal dust. Let them try to triangulate *dust*," Pichit says, brushing shards off his gloves.
You cracked the housing but the crystal's still singing — now it's screaming on *every* frequency," Chanida says, backing away from the rising hum.

choices.description: Let Malee splice her tuner into the map's output and invert the signal, turning the broadcast into noise.

line.dialogue: There — pure static on their end. They'll hear the Lattice breathing but nothing *specific*," Malee says, adjusting the phase until the amber glow flattens to grey.
You inverted the wrong harmonic — now it's repeating our position on a *deeper* band, the one the Orders monitor exclusively," Malee says, yanking the leads apart too late.

choices.description: Ask the scavenger to read the map's living record quickly, then fold it shut and commit the route to memory only.

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The gamble fails. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_before.dialogue: In the cramped cellar beneath a spice merchant's stall, the air tastes of dust and damp crystal. The only light comes from a single glow-moss lantern, casting long shadows that seem to listen.
lines_before.stage_directions: The space is tight, shelves of trade goods looming like silent witnesses.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay still. Everyone. We don’t know who might be listening above. We don’t stay in touch with luck like this for long.
lines_before.stage_directions: He leans against the wall, staff held loosely but ready, his breath fogging in the cool air.

lines_before.dialogue: You saved the data. The *map*... it’s gone, burned to keep it from him. But the truth… I can feel it here, in the lattice beneath us. It’s weeping.
lines_before.stage_directions: They sit slumped, cradling their head, voice raw with a grief that isn't personal.

lines_before.dialogue: Weeping? It’s a crystal sheet, not a person! What was on that thing that the pirate wanted so badly?
lines_before.stage_directions: She gestures wildly, nearly knocking over a jar of dried fungus.

lines_before.dialogue: Profit. Control. The usual reasons. But our friend here is shaking like a resonance ship in a storm. There’s more.
lines_before.stage_directions: She checks the cellar door, then eyes the scavenger with clinical suspicion.

lines_before.dialogue: Easy. They’re hurt. And I don’t want people knowing we’re down here any more than you do. Pirate’s friends might be looking.
lines_before.stage_directions: He stands guard at the foot of the stairs, hand on his weapon, listening intently.

lines_before.dialogue: The scavenger lets out a long, shuddering breath. In the silence that follows, a faint, discordant hum vibrates up through the stone floor—a lattice frequency no chart would ever sanction.
lines_before.stage_directions: The glow-moss flickers in sympathy with the sound.

lines_after.dialogue: The hum fades, leaving a deeper quiet. The scavenger’s revelation hangs in the air, heavier than the market above.
lines_after.stage_directions: Dust motes drift in the lantern light like falling stars.

lines_after.dialogue: A record of pain... to help it heal. All this time, the Tonal Orders navigate by forcing it. The Listeners just… listen. But you were trying to *answer* it.
lines_after.stage_directions: He looks at his staff, its crystal tip pulsing with a soft, sympathetic light.

lines_after.dialogue: You hear that? The market’s settling. My window’s closing. You got a shard of a ghost story. I got buyers for real charts. We don’t stay in touch.
lines_after.stage_directions: His voice is a rough whisper from a grille high in the wall—he was listening. A coin clinks on the floor. "For the trouble." Then, the scuff of boots fading away.

lines_after.dialogue: He’s gone. Coward. So, what now? We can’t just sit tight down here with a… a wound in the world.
lines_after.stage_directions: She picks up the cold crystal shard, its internal fractures catching the light.

line.dialogue: The data on that shard… it’s a single, unstable frequency. A scar. You can try to trace it to its source—dangerous, immediate. You can hide, study it slowly, quietly. Or… you can take it to the Listeners. They might understand, or they might see it as heresy. The lattice’s pain is now yours to carry. Don’t leave it on. Don’t leave this truth open.
line.stage_directions: They press the warm crystal shard into Pichit’s hand, their eyes holding a desperate hope.

choices.description: Grab the scavenger by the collar and demand to know what was on that burned map.

line.dialogue: Talk. Now. Whatever was worth burning is worth killing for, and I need to know which side of that fire we're standing on.
Get your hands off me, stranger. I've survived worse than your threats by staying quiet—and I'll stay quiet longer than you'll stay patient.

choices.description: Signal Pichit to keep watch while you quietly examine the crystal sheet's remaining fragments.

line.dialogue: Eyes on the corridors, Pichit. If anyone comes, we buy time—not with bullets, but with silence. Now let me see what Chanida's so eager to dismiss.
Too late—the fragments just crumbled at my touch. Whatever data lingered in those cracks, it's dust now, same as the map. We're working blind.

choices.description: Turn to Malee and ask directly: who hired them to destroy the map, and what happens now that they failed?

line.dialogue: You're calm for someone whose employer just watched their leverage go up in smoke. So tell me—who's coming to collect, and what do they
The attempt backfires on the scavenger. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_before.dialogue: The crystalline expanse stretches to the horizon, a frozen ocean of geometric fractures catching the pale sky-light. Anomalous harmonics hum just below hearing.
lines_before.stage_directions: Vast, silent, alien landscape. Crystal formations like frozen waves.

lines_before.dialogue: It’s peaceful here. Almost too peaceful. You can almost forget the Silencing happened... but the Lattice remembers. Every fracture tells a story.
lines_before.stage_directions: Tracing a gloved hand along a crystal seam, listening intently.

lines_before.dialogue: Don't! Don't come closer! I'm just... I'm nearly done. Just let me finish this and I'll go.
lines_before.stage_directions: A man in patched scavenger gear crouches by a massive crystal monolith, hurriedly etching onto a portable shard. He's terrified.

lines_before.dialogue: Who is this guy? What's he doing? Those patterns... they're not natural!
lines_before.stage_directions: Points excitedly at the geometric designs glowing faintly on the monolith.

lines_before.dialogue: He's copying it. A map. Look at the angles—those are frequency coordinates. Uncharted ones. This could get us all killed if the Orders find out.
lines_before.stage_directions: Eyes scanning the patterns, hand resting on weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: We're not alone. Multiple contacts approaching from the crystal canyons. Armed. Not Order patrols.
lines_before.stage_directions: Steps protectively in front of the group, shield humming to life.

lines_before.dialogue: Figures emerge from the light-fractured landscape, their silhouettes sharp against the crystal. The scavenger panics.
lines_before.stage_directions: Five sky pirates drop from hovering gliders, weapons drawn.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal shard lands in Pichit's hands, warm and vibrating with captured light. Both groups freeze, weapons trained.
lines_after.stage_directions: Close-up on the etched shard in Pichit's grip.

lines_after.dialogue: I’m the luckiest person alive... to be holding what everyone wants to kill each other over.
lines_after.stage_directions: The shard's resonance makes Pichit's staff pulse in sympathetic vibration.

lines_after.dialogue: They're not getting it! That map could free everyone! Look at the scavenger—he's a nice guy, just trying to help his family!

lines_before.dialogue: The crystal platform glows with a faint inner light, its etched patterns shimmering like frozen soundwaves. Around them, the Lattice hums with latent energy—a chorus of frequencies waiting to be matched.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air vibrates with subsonic resonance.

lines_before.dialogue: First you have to understand... true harmony isn't about a single perfect note. It's about voices finding their place together, even when they don't naturally align.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit traces the etched patterns with his staff.

lines_before.dialogue: My contact was a disgraced Listener. He whispered about 'natural charts' in the Lattice itself. Said the Tonal Orders' monopoly can't compare to what's already written here. I know the starting tone—a low hum, like distant thunder.
lines_before.stage_directions: The villager's hands tremble slightly as he speaks.

lines_before.dialogue: In only five minutes we could have this thing singing! Why are we still talking? Let's match those frequencies already!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida bounces on the balls of her feet, energy barely contained.

lines_before.dialogue: I've never understood why people rush toward glowing ancient crystals. The second option is usually 'run away screaming.' But here we are.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee scans the platform for structural weaknesses.

lines_before.dialogue: Keep your weapons ready. This 'harmony' the crystals want—it feels like a trap waiting to spring.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself between the party and the pirates.

lines_before.dialogue: As the villager begins the low hum, the platform shudders. Crystalline shards rise from the surface like frozen notes given form.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air grows thick with resonating energy.

lines_after.dialogue: The completed tones hang in the air—a perfect chord that etches itself into the crystal. But from the humming depths of the Lattice, something answers the call.
lines_after.stage_directions: A dissonant shriek echoes from below.

lines_after.dialogue: The map shows a 'Silent Node'—a place of perfect stillness. But to reach it, we first have to survive the noise we've awakened.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff pulses with sympathetic resonance.

lines_after.dialogue: That's no ordinary vibration! It's a harmonic predator—drawn to strong frequencies like ours. My crew's resonators are no match for that thing if it surfaces!
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate leader backs away from the platform's edge.

lines_after.dialogue: The map's almost complete! We can't stop now—who cares what's coming? Let's finish this!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida readies her weapon, eyes fixed on the glowing patterns.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: The activation sequence reveals the path but also attracts a dangerous harmonic predator from the Lattice. Pichit must decide who coordinates the defense and who continues the delicate singing to finalize the map's imprint.
line.stage_directions: Tense moment.

Pichit* — "Your rhythm is fractured, discordant. Pull back before the feedback loop burns through you.

choices.description: Demand the disgraced Listener's name from the villager before going further.

Villager* — "I gave you my trust and you give me interrogation. The name dies with my patience.

choices.description: Follow Malee's caution and power down the artifact before it fully activates.

line.dialogue: Malee* — "Finally, someone who listens. Glowing things glow brightest right before they consume whoever's standing nearby.
Malee* — "Five minutes. She said five minutes. Now the hum is inside my teeth and won't stop.

lines_before.dialogue: The final resonance fades, leaving the map glowing within the crystalline surface. But the air feels heavier than before—charged with more than just harmonic energy.
lines_before.stage_directions: The lattice pulses with faint light, revealing intricate pathways.

lines_before.dialogue: I think that's right. The map is complete. But... what do you think about what happens now? It's something to think about.
lines_before.stage_directions: He rests his staff against the glowing lattice, watching the light climb the wood.

lines_before.dialogue: You have to give it to us. To the people. Not to them.
lines_before.stage_directions: He steps forward, hands trembling but voice steady.

lines_before.dialogue: What? Why? We all worked together!
lines_before.stage_directions: She gestures between the villagers and pirates, disbelief on her face.

lines_before.dialogue: Don't be naive. Look at their faces.
lines_before.stage_directions: She nods toward the pirates, hand resting on her weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit, something's wrong. They're spreading out.
lines_before.stage_directions: He positions himself slightly in front of the group, tense.

lines_before.dialogue: The lead pirate captain grins, a sharp, merciless expression. His crew moves to flank the party, weapons subtly drawn.
lines_before.stage_directions: Metal whispers against leather in the sudden quiet.

lines_after.dialogue: The predator's roar shakes the very lattice, a discordant wave that forces hands to ears. For a moment, survival is the only allegiance.
lines_after.stage_directions: Crystalline shards rain down as everyone ducks for cover.

lines_after.dialogue: I thought it was okay to trust. I think it's alright to hope. But this... this is different.
lines_after.stage_directions: His staff pulses with a defensive light as he looks between the factions.

lines_after.dialogue: Time's up, hero! That beast won't wait! Choose!
lines_after.stage_directions: He snarls, backing toward his ship while keeping an eye on the roiling lattice.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't stay here! The vibrations are getting worse!
lines_after.stage_directions: She points to where the lattice is beginning to fracture, already moving toward their own vessel.

line.dialogue: My family has a safe-house! We can hide you! Please—don't let them sell our future to the highest floating city bidder. This is for everyone!
line.stage_directions: He holds out a simple, worn key, his expression desperate and defiant.

lines_before.dialogue: The aftermath of the harmonic predator's attack hangs in the air. Its dissolving crystal form drifts away like ash, leaving the two factions panting and staring at each other across the Lattice. Their weapons are still raised—not at the beast, but at each other.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Lattice hums with residual aggression, the crystal surface scarred from the fight.

lines_before.dialogue: Listen. That sound—the predator's final frequency. It wasn't just noise. It was a warning. 'Could you speak more slowly?' That's what the Lattice is asking of us now. To stop shouting over each other.
lines_before.stage_directions: He plants his staff into the crystal. It pulses with a calming, steady light.

lines_before.dialogue: They attacked us! They'd have taken everything!
lines_before.stage_directions: A farmer gestures wildly with a makeshift crystal-tipped spear.

lines_before.dialogue: And you'd have hidden the map forever! Wanna try some cooperation? It just saved your lives!
lines_before.stage_directions: She steps between them, hands on her hips.

lines_before.dialogue: She's not wrong. The math is simple. We fought together. We survived. Doing it again increases survival probability.
lines_before.stage_directions: She wipes predator residue off her scanner with detached precision.

lines_before.dialogue: The threat is gone, but the tension remains. This is a fragile moment.
lines_before.stage_directions: His eyes scan the pirates, hand resting on his weapon's hilt.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit takes a deep breath, the sound echoing in the sudden quiet. He turns to face both groups, his voice carrying not with force, but with clarity.
lines_before.stage_directions: All eyes turn to him. The Lattice seems to listen.

lines_after.dialogue: Silence follows his proposal. Then, a low murmur builds—not of conflict, but of calculation. The pirate leader scratches his chin. The head resident clutches her shawl, thinking.
lines_after.stage_directions: The two factions eye each other, then the map, then Pichit.

lines_after.dialogue: This isn't about who owns the song. It's about making sure everyone can hear it. The map gets copied. The Residents' network shares it. But you need distributors who know the hidden frequencies. You need each other.
lines_after.stage_directions: He gestures to both groups. His staff's light bridges the gap between them.

lines_after.dialogue: So we're your delivery crew? For a cut, not a monopoly. Less profit, but also less Tonal Order heat on our necks... and a steady job. Huh. Sustainable piracy. I can speak that language.
lines_after.stage_directions: He barks a laugh, rough but considering.

lines_after.dialogue: Then it's settled! Come on, we've got a pact to swear on the Lattice itself! Let's get this harmony started!
lines_after.stage_directions: She grins, already pulling out resonance chalk to mark the ceremonial circle.

line.dialogue: The pact is sworn, the first copies begun. But now the real work starts. This network is fragile. Someone needs to guide it. What is your role, Pichit?
line.stage_directions: The villager looks at him, hope and fear mixed. The pirates watch, waiting to see who they'll really answer to.

choices.description: Forge the pact by cutting your palm and pressing it to the resonant stone, offering blood to seal it.

line.dialogue: The frequency accepts you—it hums in your bones now. We hear the same world.
The stone stays cold. Your blood carries doubt, and doubt has no resonance.

choices.description: Grab the villager by his collar and demand he show where he buried the map right now.

line.dialogue: Finally! Someone with sense. Dig it up, old man—before I dig it up myself.
You threaten me after I bled for you? The map stays where it is. I'll die first.

choices.description: Kneel beside the predator's corpse and trace its frequency pattern into the dirt with your knife.

line.dialogue: You see it too. The pattern matches the map's missing coordinates. We don't need the villager.
The lines won't hold. Whatever this creature was, its frequency is already fading beyond recovery.

lines_before.dialogue: Phrao Monastery hangs suspended between heaven and the silent Lattice below, its gardens a tapestry of crystalline flora that hum with restrained energy. The air itself vibrates with disciplined quiet.
lines_before.stage_directions: The monastery's spires catch the fading light, casting long shadows across geometric gardens.

lines_before.dialogue: I now know... this place is built on more than stone. Every whisper here feels measured, controlled. They're guarding something.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit's fingers trace the carved railing, feeling its subtle vibration.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah, newcomers! Permit me to offer some context—I travel these routes often. The Listeners' knowledge is their most valuable commodity. Stability is profitable, you see.
lines_before.stage_directions: The merchant adjusts his sleeves, his smile not quite reaching his eyes.

lines_before.dialogue: They're hiding something! Did you see how that monk jumped when you asked about the lattice's 'sickness'?
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida gestures animatedly toward the scriptorium.

lines_before.dialogue: I think it's alright to be cautious. Knowledge has weight here. Every scroll we touch has been approved by someone.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee runs a finger along a shelf, checking for dust patterns.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay close. The way the Abbot watched us... this conditional access feels like a leash.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's hand rests near his weapon, eyes scanning the garden paths.

lines_before.dialogue: In the scriptorium, Pichit finds a scroll unlike the others—its edges burned, its text marred by deliberate inkblots where certain harmonics should be notated.
lines_before.stage_directions: The parchment feels cold despite the warm air.

lines_after.dialogue: The oily liquid from the weeping crystals evaporates into acrid mist. The Listener Monk's hands tremble as he resets the resonator.
lines_after.stage_directions: The garden's hum has shifted to a wary, dissonant thrum.

lines_after.dialogue: Now I know why they fear certain frequencies. That wasn't just a reaction—it was a wound.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff pulses with sympathetic energy, its crystal glowing faintly.

lines_after.dialogue: You must understand—some harmonies are forbidden for a reason. The Dissonant Choir... it's not just a legend. Please, continuing your research through sanctioned channels is the best way.
lines_after.stage_directions: The monk's eyes dart toward a shadowed archway where another Listener watches.

lines_after.dialogue: I'm heading out now to check the perimeter. If they're hiding this much, what else is buried here?
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already moving toward the garden's edge, her movements quick and purposeful.

line.dialogue: Interesting, isn't it? The monastery sells acoustic crystals but forbids certain frequencies. Knowledge has a price—sometimes it's access, sometimes it's silence. So, Pichit: one way or round trip? Will you play by their rules, or chart your own course?
line.stage_directions: The merchant leans against a crystal pillar, his expression unreadable.

lines_before.dialogue: The evening acoustic meditation begins, a low hum of focused voices that vibrates through the monastery's crystalline walls. As the Listeners chant, the party slips away into the shadowed corridors beneath the harmonic gardens.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air grows colder, humming with a deep, contained resonance. Glowing crystal veins pulse in the walls.

lines_before.dialogue: Every step feels like a trespass. We still don't know yet what we're truly looking for, only that something is being hidden here.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit runs a hand along the humming wall, his staff glowing faintly in response.

lines_before.dialogue: This place is alive. Can you feel it? Not just the chanting upstairs—something deeper. It's... restless.
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida presses her ear to a crystal formation, eyes wide.

lines_before.dialogue: Restless or trapped? These archives are sealed for a reason. Let's find what they're so afraid of and get out.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee checks the corridor behind them, hand on her weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay close. The resonance is masking our sounds, but we're not the only ones who know these passages.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself at the rear, watching every shadow.

lines_before.dialogue: They reach a chamber lined with crystalline shelves holding scrolls that shimmer with captured frequencies. The air tastes of ozone and old secrets.
lines_before.stage_directions: Fragmented light patterns dance across ancient records. The hum grows more pronounced.

lines_before.dialogue: These aren't navigation charts. They're... observations. Listen, this one mentions a 'Ground Tone'—not a destructive frequency, but a revelatory one.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit unrolls a brittle scroll, its symbols glowing as he reads.

lines_before.dialogue: The fragmented records reveal the truth: the Ground Tone strips away the harmonic layers the Tonal Orders use for navigation, revealing a raw, chaotic 'undersong'—the true sound of the post-Silencing world.
lines_before.stage_directions: As Pichit reads aloud, the crystals in the room resonate differently, producing a discordant, unsettling harmony.

lines_before.dialogue: You heard that, didn't you? The shift in the resonance when you said 'undersong.' It's like the lattice... answered.
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida steps back, looking at the vibrating shelves with a mix of awe and fear.

lines_before.dialogue: So the forbidden harmonic doesn't break the world—it shows you the world they've been hiding. No wonder they locked this away.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee scans another scroll, her expression hardening.

lines_before.dialogue: A soft footfall echoes in the corridor. Before they can react, the Trade Negotiator steps into the chamber's light, his merchant's smile replaced by something sharper.
lines_before.stage_directions: He stands in the doorway, not blocking it, but filling the space with a new kind of presence.

lines_before.dialogue: I know. I already know that you're looking for the Dissonant Choir.
lines_before.stage_directions: He walks calmly into the room, his eyes scanning the open scrolls without surprise.

lines_before.dialogue: How well do you know them? You're supposed to be a merchant, not a scholar of heresies.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit moves between the Negotiator and the others, posture defensive.

lines_before.dialogue: It was a good experience for me, learning their truth. I trade in more than goods—I trade in revelations. The Groundless Movement has the only commodity that matters: what really happened during the Silencing.
lines_before.stage_directions: His voice drops, fervent and earnest. The merchant persona has completely fallen away.

lines_before.dialogue: Before anyone can respond, another figure appears at the door—the Listener Monk who first welcomed them. His face is pale, his hands trembling slightly.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Monk looks at the open archives, then at the Negotiator, then at the party. His shoulders slump in resignation.

lines_before.dialogue: You heard that, right? The undersong. When the Ground Tone resonates through the lattice... it speaks of a world not shattered, but... changed. Purposely silenced.
lines_before.stage_directions: He whispers, eyes darting toward the corridor as if expecting others.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Orders didn't just survive the Silencing—they engineered it. They remade the world's song to hide something. The Groundless Movement seeks to uncover what.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Negotiator spreads his hands, a trader presenting his most valuable offer.

lines_before.dialogue: My oath demands I suppress this. My scholarship demands I pursue it. I can't say yet if helping you is wisdom or sin.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Monk wrings his hands, caught between fear and a desperate need for truth.

lines_after.dialogue: The archive hums with the tension of three conflicting truths: the monastery's enforced peace, the Negotiator's fervent heresy, and the raw undersong vibrating in the crystals.
lines_after.stage_directions: The light pulses erratically, shadows stretching and contracting.

lines_after.dialogue: Every foundation we've known about the Silencing is cracking. But the cost of truth... I can't say yet if it's worth the breaking.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff pulses in time with his heartbeat, casting uncertain light on the faces around him.

lines_after.dialogue: The orthodox leadership will arrive for dawn meditation. You have until then to decide what to do with what you've learned.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Monk backs toward the door, his voice trembling with urgency.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't unhear what we've heard. That undersong... it's still there, waiting. We have to know more.
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida moves toward the Negotiator, already leaning toward his offer.

line.dialogue: So, Pichit. Will you trust a heretic and a frightened monk to learn what the world has been hiding? Or will you report us and preserve the fragile silence?
line.stage_directions: The Negotiator meets Pichit's eyes, all pretense gone. The Monk watches, terrified but waiting.

choices.description: Press your palm against the pulsing wall to read its memory through touch.

line.dialogue: The stone remembers faces — hundreds, all kneeling. We're walking through a graveyard of devotion.
It pulled from me. Something drank my warmth through the contact. Don't touch it again — it's still hungry.

choices.description: Follow the low chanting vibration eastward toward the sealed bronze doors.

line.dialogue: The resonance thins here — they built this corridor to funnel sound, not contain it. We're being guided.
Wrong way. The vibration doubled back and now it's behind us. Whatever's chanting knows we moved.

choices.description: Unroll the stolen archive parchment to cross-reference the wall glyphs before proceeding.

line.dialogue: These aren't records — they're warrants. Every name listed was buried alive in the foundation. This garden was grown on prisoners.
The ink bled through the parchment when I opened it near the wall. It's reacting. The archive wasn't stolen — it was *summoned out.*

lines_before.dialogue: The air in the hidden cavern is thick with the scent of damp stone and ozone. Luminescent crystal veins pulse with a faint, nervous light, casting long shadows that dance with every tremor from the monastery above.
lines_before.stage_directions: A low hum vibrates through the stone floor.

lines_before.dialogue: The prices for knowledge are never listed. You only see the cost after you've already paid.
lines_before.stage_directions: He runs a hand over the ship's resonator, feeling its unfamiliar resonance.

lines_before.dialogue: The price for this crystal alignment was steep, but fair. The knowledge we'll gain? Reasonably priced.
lines_before.stage_directions: He polishes a tuning crystal with a satisfied smirk.

lines_before.dialogue: Stop talking about prices and help me with this coupling! The frequency matrix is unstable!
lines_before.stage_directions: Her fingers fly over the crystal interface, her brow furrowed in concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: The harmonic feedback is spiking. This isn't a lecture hall—if our 'professor' here is wrong, we're not getting a bad grade. We're getting vaporized.
lines_before.stage_directions: She monitors a bank of flickering diagnostics.

lines_before.dialogue: We should have left home in a hurry the moment this was suggested. Now we're in too deep.
lines_before.stage_directions: He stands guard at the cavern entrance, hand on his weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: With a final, shuddering whine, the ship's resonator locks onto the frequency. The Ground Tone blooms into existence—a deep, foundational hum that doesn't part the Lattice, but unravels it.
lines_before.stage_directions: The cavern walls become ghostly, transparent. The world beyond is a shimmering, sorrowful song.

lines_after.dialogue: The dirge is unmistakable. A structured, intelligent lament of a lost world, overlaid with a brutal, artificial damping frequency—the Silencing, laid bare as an act of violence, not an accident. Then, the harmonic bleed hits.
lines_after.stage_directions: A sharp, crystalline CRACK echoes from above, followed by a cascading shatter of breaking glass.

lines_after.dialogue: Truth has a resonance... and a recoil.
lines_after.stage_directions: He stares at his hands, the staff in his grip glowing with the aftershock of the tone.

lines_after.dialogue: The gardens... the singing crystals... we've shattered them. My home. What have we done?
lines_after.stage_directions: He sinks to his knees, face ashen with horror.

lines_after.dialogue: We proved it! We have to go, now! Show everyone what we heard!
lines_after.stage_directions: She grabs Pichit's arm, pulling him toward the exit tunnel.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide: take the evidence and flee, protecting the heretical Monk and Negotiator, or stay and face the monastery's justice to mitigate the damage they've caused.
line.stage_directions: Alarms begin to wail from the monastery above. Dust rains from the ceiling.

choices.description: Override the coupling manually, forcing the harmonic frequency down before it ruptures.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Brute force worked. The coupling is holding, but don't ever touch my equipment like that again.
Chanida — "You've cracked the housing. Now we're bleeding resonance into the Garden itself.

choices.description: Demand the merchant explain what price was actually paid for this crystal alignment.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "He traded memories. Seven years of his daughter's life, gone. The crystal remembers what he cannot.
Merchant — "Ask again and I'll dissolve the alignment entirely. Some knowledge curdles when spoken aloud.

choices.description: Follow the harmonic spike's source deeper into the Garden to find what's resonating with them.

line.dialogue: Malee — "There — beneath the roots. Something alive is singing back at our frequency. It's learning our pattern.
Malee — "The feedback loop is closing. Whatever's down there, it now knows exactly where we stand.

lines_before.dialogue: The Harmonic Garden lies in ruin. Shards of crystal litter the ground like frozen tears, their perfect geometries shattered into chaotic fragments. The air still hums with the dissonant echoes of revelation, and a ring of orthodox Listeners stands between you and every exit.
lines_before.stage_directions: The garden is a scene of beautiful destruction. The crystalline structures, once singing in perfect harmony, are now jagged and silent. Novices huddle in the cloisters, their faces pale with fear.

lines_before.dialogue: The one who opened the door is standing right in front of us. We brought this storm to his doorstep.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit's gaze is fixed on the trembling heretical monk, his staff cold in his hand. The weight of discovery feels like chains.

lines_before.dialogue: Don't listen to them! This is just another transaction! They're offering you silence for peace—a terrible bargain! He's still single, isn't he? Unwed to reality! Unbound by the truth! We can still sell this truth to the world!
lines_before.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator gestures wildly, his eyes calculating even now, seeing rebellion as a commodity to be marketed.

lines_before.dialogue: After everything we've seen? The Lattice's pain, the buried song? We can't just walk away!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida's fists are clenched, her body coiled like a spring, ready to fight against the closing circle of monks.

lines_before.dialogue: Look around. The broken crystal, the scared children. That's all, isn't it? The sum of your revelation. Is everything under control? Clearly not.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee scans the perimeter, counting the monks, assessing the shattered garden with a cynical, weary eye.

lines_before.dialogue: They have us surrounded. Any move we make... he pays for it first.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly in front of Pichit, his hand resting on his weapon, his entire body tense as a drawn bowstring.

lines_before.dialogue: The Abbot steps forward, his robes sweeping through the crystal dust. His face is not angry, but profoundly tired, etched with the grim resolve of a surgeon preparing to amputate.
lines_before.stage_directions: The circle of Listeners parts for the Abbot. The heretical monk flinches as the Abbot's shadow falls over him.

lines_after.dialogue: The garden holds its breath. The only sound is the faint, pained whisper of the broken crystals.
lines_after.stage_directions: A heavy, waiting silence. The faces of the orthodox Listeners are masks of stern expectation.

lines_after.dialogue: Truth shouldn't require a martyr. But sometimes peace demands a prisoner.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit looks from the defiant Negotiator to the broken Monk, then to his own companions. The staff in his hand feels like it holds the weight of the choice itself.

lines_after.dialogue: Please. Do not... do not let it be for nothing.
lines_after.stage_directions: The heretical monk speaks in a shattered whisper, his eyes begging not for mercy, but for meaning.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit. Whatever you choose. We're with you.
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida's impulsive fire has banked into a low, steady burn of solidarity. She stands ready, waiting for his lead.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit's final choice: Accept the Abbot's deal—leave in silence, condemning the Monk to re-education and abandoning the immediate fight—or publicly defy the Abbey, sparking an immediate schism within the Listeners to protect the Monk and his truth.
line.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator's eyes lock with Pichit's, a final, desperate sales pitch hanging in the air.

Malee misreads the situation. The escape tunnel collapses.

choices.description: Have Chanida focus hidden frequencies on the ancient texts to uncover the suppression

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Things don't go as planned. The villagers' courage breaks.

choices.description: Have the merchant risk using information network to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: Exactly as the merchant hoped. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
Things don't go as planned. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire rises from the crystalline ocean of the Lattice like a needle piercing heaven. Your resonance skiff docks at the mid-level platform, its crystal resonators humming down to silence as you secure the mooring lines. Immediately, the Spire's primary harmonic tone envelops you—a deep, constant vibration that seems to press against your very emotions, flattening them into something calm yet unnervingly clear.
lines_before.stage_directions: The platform is austere, crystalline structures humming with resonant energy. Far below, the Lattice shimmers like frozen music.

lines_before.dialogue: Strange... my worry feels distant, like someone else's problem. I went to bed late last night preparing for this, but now the fatigue is just data. Don’t work too hard, they said. But here, how can you feel the weight of work at all?
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit touches the haft of his staff, feeling its subtle pulse against the Spire's overwhelming tone.

lines_before.dialogue: Welcome to the Anchor Spire. I am Brother Eiran. You must be the investigators. The tone here is pure—a foundational harmonic that stabilizes navigation for leagues. My duty is to record its constancy.
lines_before.stage_directions: Brother Eiran is clad in simple Listener robes. His eyes keep flickering toward the Lattice below, his fingers nervously adjusting a recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: Pure? Can I... listen closer? There's something else. Faint, like a ghost humming just under the main tone. A counter-melody that shouldn't be here!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida presses her ear against a crystalline wall, her expression shifting from curiosity to unease.

lines_before.dialogue: Great. Haunted harmonics. Just what we needed. And stealth is impossible—every step sings on this crystal. I have no one to help me watch our backs if everything echoes.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee tests her footing, wincing as even a careful step produces a clear resonant chime.

lines_before.dialogue: City folk. Always listening for pretty songs. You hear ghosts; I hear salvage opportunities. But something's wrong here. The Lattice below... it answers differently near the Spire.
lines_before.stage_directions: Kael leans against a rail, his patched surface-suit dusty. He watches the party with guarded, calculating eyes.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit, we should check the maintenance corridors. Official charts might not tell the whole story. And that scavenger... he knows something.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit keeps his hand near his weapon, posture tense as he scans the platform.

lines_before.dialogue: Brother Eiran becomes visibly agitated at Chanida's mention of the ghost-echo. He walked back and forth along the observation rail, his recording crystal clutched too tightly.
lines_before.stage_directions: The monk's nervous pacing creates a rhythmic, anxious tapping that blends unnervingly with the Spire's tone.

lines_after.dialogue: In a dusty maintenance corridor, behind a loose crystal panel, Pichit and Arthit find it: a manually logged resonance chart, old and frayed. It shows a ship's signature—the 'Echo's Lament'—that vanished near these coordinates seven years ago. The final entry is a frantic scrawl about a 'harmonic rupture.'
lines_after.stage_directions: The parchment is brittle, the ink faded but the desperation in its last marks still palpable.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost ship. A ghost-echo. And a monk who paces like a trapped animal. This 'purity' the Orders preach... it's built on silence.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff pulses with a warmer light, reacting to his rising determination despite the Spire's emotion-dampening field.

lines_after.dialogue: You shouldn't be in restricted areas! The Spire's tone is pure. Stray echoes are... atmospheric interference. Nothing more. Please, focus on your original mission.
lines_after.stage_directions: Brother Eiran has followed them, his face pale. He wrings his hands, his earlier reverence now edged with fear.

lines_after.dialogue: Atmospheric interference that sounds like a crying ship? No way. Pichit, we have to follow this! That ghost-echo is a message!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already moving toward the corridor leading deeper into the Spire, her curiosity overriding caution.

line.dialogue: So. You found the chart. That ship... it didn't just vanish. It was silenced. The monk knows it. The Orders know it. Now you know it. What's your play, city folk?
line.stage_directions: Kael steps from the shadows of the corridor, his gaze sharp. He's been listening the whole time.

choices.description: Ask Chanida to listen for the ghost ship's echo, drawing on unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
Chanida hits a wall. The echo fades to silence.

choices.description: Pichit steps forward with monk wisdom, ready to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.description: The scavenger takes the lead, employing crystal fragments to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the scavenger pulls it off. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
Defeat. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The spiral staircase descends into a throat of ancient stone. The air grows thick with harmonic pressure, vibrating through the soles of boots and into marrow. Faint crystal conduits pulse with residual light, casting long, trembling shadows.
lines_before.stage_directions: The stairs wind down into oppressive darkness, lit only by sporadic, sickly glows from the walls.

lines_before.dialogue: This vibration... it's not just sound. It's memory. I'll have a look at the resonance pattern down here. It might be a good experience, understanding this place.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit presses a hand against the wall, feeling the thrum. His staff glows in response.

lines_before.dialogue: Do you hear that? Under the hum... voices? They're all broken up!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida stops, head tilted, her hand on her weapon hilt.

lines_before.dialogue: Distorted resonance echoes. Probably just lattice feedback. Though the pattern is... unusually coherent for random noise.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee scans the area with a small crystal resonator, frowning at the readings.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay close. This feels like a tomb. The air is wrong.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit moves to the front, shield held ready, his eyes scanning the gloom.

lines_before.dialogue: The ghostly counter-melody swells, resolving into fractured words that seem to bleed from the stone itself.
lines_before.stage_directions: The faint voices become clearer, layered with static and despair: '...lattice fracturing... can't hold the tone...'

lines_before.dialogue: You hear it too, then. Good. Saves me explaining. I'm not just here to trade scrap.
lines_before.stage_directions: Kael steps from a shadowed alcove, his usual guarded expression replaced by raw intensity. He holds a tarnished ship's badge.

lines_before.dialogue: My grandfather's ship. The 'Echo's Mercy.' The Tonal Orders said it was lost to a rogue frequency storm. That report 'was a lie.' A complete fabrication to cover their tracks.
lines_before.stage_directions: He thrusts the badge forward, his hand trembling not with fear, but with decades-old anger.

lines_before.dialogue: A cover-up? For what?
lines_before.stage_directions: She steps toward Kael, her suspicion momentarily overshadowed by curiosity.

lines_before.dialogue: Stop! Please, you must stop!
lines_before.stage_directions: Brother Eiran stumbles down the stairs, his robes disheveled, face pale with panic.

lines_before.dialogue: Don't listen to it! Some harmonies are not meant to be heard. It's not scary at all! It's... it's just sad. A sad memory trapped in the stone. I hear it every night. It whispers. I can't make it back to silence once it starts!
lines_before.stage_directions: He wrings his hands, his eyes darting between the party and the vibrating walls.

lines_before.dialogue: A psychic resonance imprint? That would explain the coherent distress signals. But the energy required...
lines_before.stage_directions: Her analytical tone falters as she recalculates the implications.

lines_before.dialogue: Before anyone can respond, the harmonic tone in the spire peaks. The crystals blaze with painful light, and the world dissolves into a shared scream of resonance.
lines_before.stage_directions: A blinding surge of light and sound washes over them, erasing the present.

lines_after.dialogue: The vision recedes as suddenly as it came, leaving behind the smell of ozone and a profound, ringing silence in the soul.
lines_after.stage_directions: The party is back in the dim stairwell, breathless. The faint glow of the crystals seems accusatory.

lines_after.dialogue: A test... a flawed Spire calibration. They were caught in the feedback. It wasn't an accident. It was negligence. That... was a good experience. Terrible, but true.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's voice is low. The crystal in his staff pulses with a slow, mournful rhythm, mirroring his realization.

lines_after.dialogue: You see? Now you see. The Listeners... some of the elders know. They've always known. They say to let sleeping echoes lie. But it's not sleeping. It's screaming.
lines_after.stage_directions: Eiran slumps against the wall, the fight gone from him, replaced by exhausted honesty.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't just leave this buried. That ship, those people... they deserve more than to be a 'sad memory' in a wall.
lines_after.stage_directions: She's already turning, looking back up the stairs as if planning to confront the whole Spire.

line.dialogue: So. You felt it. You *know*. The Tonal Orders murdered a ship to test their theories and wrote a lie as its epitaph. My family's waited a generation for someone with the guts to listen. What do you do with the truth?
line.stage_directions: Kael's eyes are locked on Pichit, demanding an answer. Brother Eiran watches, terrified.

choices.description: Press your palm flat against the resonating wall and let the vibration crawl into your bones.

line.dialogue: I see them—thousands of hands, reaching through stone. They want us to remember what they couldn't forget.
My fingers went numb. Whatever lives in this wall, it doesn't want witnesses—it wants silence.

choices.description: Hum back at the frequency you hear, matching its pitch until something answers.

line.dialogue: It answered. The voices sharpened into words—names, I think. Names of people who died singing this exact note.
I matched the wrong harmonic. The voices screamed and now everything sounds like drowning.

choices.description: Draw your blade and strike the floor where the vibration pools deepest.

line.dialogue: The stone cracked and something poured out—not blood, not water. Light shaped like bones. We found what they buried.
The blade shattered against the floor and the hum turned angry. Whatever's below us just woke up hungry.

lines_before.dialogue: The final chamber opens before you—a cathedral of crystal where the Anchor Spire meets the Lattice. The air shimmers with visible harmonic distortion, and the tone here is deafening, a physical pressure against your skin.
lines_before.stage_directions: The chamber is vast, with the crystalline wreckage of a resonance ship fused into the lattice walls like a fossil.

lines_before.dialogue: It's not that I'm afraid... it's that this feels like a tomb we weren't meant to open. To conserve energy for what's ahead, we need to be smart.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit grips his staff, its light dimming in the oppressive field.

lines_before.dialogue: There! See that blackened crystal formation at the tip? That's the ship's core resonator—crystallized data. My dream job would've been to recover something like this... before I knew what it cost.
lines_before.stage_directions: Kael points with a trembling hand, face etched with grim determination.

lines_before.dialogue: We're so close! We just have to cross that... shimmering death field. What's the worst that could happen?
lines_before.stage_directions: She takes an eager step forward before Arthit pulls her back.

lines_before.dialogue: Worst case? Our personal resonators overload and cook us from the inside. My scanner's not working. It's out of order in this field. We're flying blind.
lines_before.stage_directions: She slaps her wrist-mounted device in frustration.

lines_before.dialogue: Brother Eiran, you know this place. How do we survive that?
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself between the party and the shimmering energy currents.

lines_before.dialogue: You must turn off your personal resonators! To conserve energy for the shielding! The field will drain them instantly! This is desecration... but... you must know.
lines_before.stage_directions: Eiran's hands shake as he gestures. His eyes are wide with conflict.

lines_before.dialogue: Following Eiran's frantic advice, you power down non-essential equipment. The world grows quieter, colder. You begin picking your way across the chamber, navigating the treacherous energy currents manually.
lines_before.stage_directions: The party moves like divers in heavy current, avoiding pulsing nodes of harmonic energy.

lines_before.dialogue: He's right! He's spot on! Look at the resonance pattern—it's too perfect, too structured. This isn't natural lattice formation. It's artificial... a containment field.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's eyes widen as he reads the energy flows.

lines_before.dialogue: A containment field? To preserve the evidence... and hide it. The Tonal Orders built this prison for the truth.
lines_before.stage_directions: She traces a crystalline conduit with her finger.

lines_before.dialogue: You reach the crystallized wreckage. At its heart, a dark crystal pulses with captured light. The core resonator of the 'Echo's Mercy.' As Pichit reaches for it, the air stills.
lines_before.stage_directions: The harmonic pressure drops suddenly, creating an eerie silence.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal comes free with a sound like breaking glass. Then it plays its final recording: a clear, haunting echo. A Singer's voice, realizing their sacrifice was deliberate, sings a single note of perfect, heartbreaking betrayal before the silence of the Silencing consumes it.
lines_after.stage_directions: The echo hangs in the air, then fades. The chamber feels colder.

lines_after.dialogue: All this stability... built on that note. That choice. We carry their silence now.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit holds the dark crystal. His staff pulses with sympathetic resonance.

lines_after.dialogue: The Spire's calming tone... it's generated partly by suppressing this echo. They preserved the wreckage here not out of respect, but because moving it would release the truth. What will you do with this knowledge?
lines_after.stage_directions: Eiran looks aged, his faith shattered but his purpose clarified.

lines_after.dialogue: We have to tell people! We can't let this stay buried! The truth has to mean something!
lines_after.stage_directions: She's already moving toward the exit, energy renewed by outrage.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: With the proof in hand, Pichit must decide: expose the truth now using the resonator (which would cause a scandal and possibly destabilize the Spire), or keep it secret to maintain stability, honoring the dead only in silence.
line.stage_directions: Kael watches Pichit, waiting. The crystal feels heavy with consequence.

choices.description: Channel your resonator at minimum output and slide across the shimmering membrane sideways, 15 words

line.dialogue: See? Controlled resonance. The membrane parts like wet silk when you don't force it.
The membrane wrapped around my ankle—I can feel it *pulling* something out of me!

choices.description: Rig two resonators in series and blast a clean hole straight through the shimmer, 15 words

line.dialogue: Hole's clean and stable—move now, you've got maybe forty seconds before it seals!
The feedback loop—our own signal amplified back tenfold—my ears are bleeding, everyone down!

choices.description: Wait for the shimmer to pulse dim and sprint across barefoot during the trough, 15 words

line.dialogue: The trough held—bare feet on that surface felt like walking across a sleeping beast's back.
I misread the cycle—the pulse came back mid-crossing and my resonator is screaming, I'm cooking.

lines_before.dialogue: The main deck of the Anchor Spire feels different—the oppressive silence replaced by a low, mournful hum. The air shimmers with residual resonance as you emerge from the depths, carrying the weight of what you've learned. Kael clutches the resonator containing the final echo, his knuckles white. Brother Eiran trails behind, looking both terrified and strangely resolute.
lines_before.stage_directions: The platform is bathed in the Spire's pale light. Three figures in Tonal Order robes stand waiting, their expressions stern.

lines_before.dialogue: The truth makes you look younger. It strips away the years of comfortable lies.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit's grip tightens on his staff, which vibrates faintly in sympathy with the Spire's new tone.

lines_before.dialogue: That's Overseer Malek. Nasty piece of work. He's the one who chased my family off the western lattice fields.
lines_before.stage_directions: Kael steps slightly forward, positioning himself between the party and the robed figures.

lines_before.dialogue: These formal robes are so uncomfortable! Can't they investigate in something practical?
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida shifts her weight, hand resting near her weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: They're here for the energy spike. Standard procedure when a memorial site goes 'active.' They'll want to contain the narrative.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee's eyes scan the Overseer's guards, counting weapons.

lines_before.dialogue: Stand together. We have the truth. That has to count for something.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit moves to flank Pichit, protective and tense.

lines_before.dialogue: Overseer Malek strides forward, his robes embroidered with navigation sigils. His eyes fix on the resonator in Kael's hands.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Overseer's guards fan out, blocking the path to the resonance lift.
