Sunlight fractures through prisms into rainbows that dance across etched frequency diagrams. Archivists move like ghosts between shelves of singing stone tablets, their footsteps producing only the faintest harmonic chime.
lines_before.stage_directions: Vast chamber with crystalline shelves radiating soft light. Scholars whisper at reading stands.

lines_before.dialogue: In a place like this, speaking isn't just about words. It's about which frequencies you choose to voice. The wrong tone could shatter more than crystal.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit runs a hand over a glowing index plinth, watching the resonant glyphs shift.

lines_before.dialogue: Listen, you little chime-rat. I ain't asking. That Unbound Cadence record—you will speak its location. Or I'll find a way to make your bones sing.
lines_before.stage_directions: A scarred sky pirate leans into a nervous junior archivist, voice a gravelly whisper in a shadowed alcove.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit, look! That pirate's threatening the archivist! Should we—
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points subtly, her movement restrained but urgent.

lines_before.dialogue: Quiet. And don't point. Look at the other one approaching from the star-chart aisle. The one with the silk robes and the smile that doesn't reach his eyes.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee pretends to study a tablet, watching the merchant's reflection in polished crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: Backs to the shelf. We're exposed here. That negotiator has guards posted at both exits. No one wants to go causing a scene in a Tonal sanctum, but we might not have a choice.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's hand rests near his tool-harness, scanning for threats.

lines_before.dialogue: The junior archivist, pale, shakes his head. 'The Cadence is sealed. Protocol.' The pirate's sneer falters as the silk-robed merchant glides into the alcove, his voice a smooth counter-harmony.
lines_before.stage_directions: The merchant places a calming hand on the archivist's shoulder, his gesture at odds with his calculating eyes.

lines_after.dialogue: The archivist flees. The pirate and merchant turn as one, their gazes locking onto Pichit. In the hallowed quiet, a silent understanding passes—three parties, one prize. The Open Frequency Map is here, and it is real.
lines_after.stage_directions: A tense triangle forms in the alcove. Distant chanting from a ceremony echoes faintly.

lines_after.dialogue: They can't speak openly here. The ceremony of this place binds even them. But their intentions are louder than any chant.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's own resonance staff pulses once with a low, anxious thrum.

lines_after.dialogue: Friends. Let us not be hasty. Clearly, we all wish to... speak to the right people. My resources, your... determination. A temporary accord? Think of the frequency we could achieve together.
lines_after.stage_directions: The merchant steps forward, smile polished, hands open in a gesture of false partnership.

lines_after.dialogue: He's more dangerous than the pirate! But... he's not wrong. We'll never get past the restricted stacks alone.
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida leans in, her whisper fierce with excitement.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide whether to entertain the Negotiator's offer of a temporary, untrustworthy alliance or to refuse and go it alone, risking being outmaneuvered.
line.stage_directions: The pirate glowers, hand on knife-hilt. The merchant's smile remains, waiting.

choices.description: Signal Chanida to create a distraction while I slip behind the bandit's blind side.

line.dialogue: Chanida knocks over a scroll rack — the bandit flinches, and I'm already behind him with a blade at his kidney.
Chanida hesitates too long. The bandit hears my boot scrape on stone and wheels around grinning.

choices.description: Step between the bandit and archivist, hands raised, offering to translate the Unbo text myself.

line.dialogue: I speak the old trade dialect fluently — his eyes widen, and suddenly I'm more useful alive than threatening.
I mangle the pronunciation so badly the archivist winces. The bandit shoves me aside — 'Useless.'

choices.description: Follow Malee's lead and observe silently, memorizing the second bandit's approach route for later.

line.dialogue: Malee was right to wait. I map every shadow, every exit — when the moment breaks, we'll know exactly where to run.
I watch the second bandit circle wide — too wide. He spots Chanida's nervous fidgeting and changes course toward us.

lines_before.dialogue: The Grand Atrium of the Tonal Archives is a cavernous space where crystalline walls drink sound and amplify only what they choose. The air hums with a sub-audible frequency, a vibration felt in the teeth and bones rather than heard. Robed archivists move in silent procession, their footsteps swallowed by the resonant floor.
lines_before.stage_directions: Shadows pool between glowing crystal pillars. The air is thick with the scent of ozone and old parchment.

lines_before.dialogue: In this place, to speak is to shape reality. Every word must be measured. Could you speak more slowly, Master Archivist? I need to understand the weight of each note.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit watches the Master Archivist's lips, his own staff pulsing in time with the ambient hum.

lines_before.dialogue: All this fuss for a song and dance! Just point me at the vault. My crew’s got a resonance ship that can part anything.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Sky Pirate leans against a pillar, arms crossed, his posture radiating impatience.

lines_before.dialogue: She's more beautiful than anyone! Look at the way the crystal responds to her voice!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points excitedly at the lead archivist, whose chanting causes subtle rainbow patterns to bloom in the nearest wall.

lines_before.dialogue: Beautiful and fragile. One wrong note and this whole acoustic house of cards comes down. No one wants to go through that. Focus on the breath control, not the light show.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee tests her own vocal cords with a soft hum, watching a small crystal node for feedback.

lines_before.dialogue: This pressure... it's like the silence before a storm. I can't speak this language of perfect tones. My voice is meant for warning shouts, not precision.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's shoulders are tight, his hand resting on his weapon hilt as if expecting an attack from the quiet itself.

lines_before.dialogue: The Master Archivist, a severe woman with hair the color of tarnished silver, gestures for silence. The instruction begins.
lines_before.stage_directions: The ambient hum drops to a whisper. All other sound is vacuumed from the room.

lines_after.dialogue: The Sky Pirate is dragged out by two stone-faced archivists, his coarse curses muffled by the acoustics. A tense, purified silence returns. The ceremony begins in earnest. Dozens of voices rise in a complex, interlocking harmony. The great crystal doors at the far end of the atrium begin to pulse with an inner light, their intricate locking mechanisms rotating in response to the sound.
lines_after.stage_directions: The massive vault doors, etched with frequency patterns, shimmer and begin a slow, silent swing inward. A rush of ancient, potent resonance washes out.

lines_after.dialogue: The map isn't a thing. It's a living sound. They keep it locked away because it can't be controlled. To free it is to change everything.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff vibrates violently in his grip, resonating with the unstable frequencies leaking from the open vault.

lines_after.dialogue: The final lock is inside. A harmonic seal keyed to the map's own resonance. A puzzle for those who understand value. Shall we proceed as planned? The prize awaits those who move with purpose.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator's chant ceases. He turns to Pichit, his friendly smile not reaching his eyes, and gestures toward the yawning darkness of the Deep Vault.

lines_after.dialogue: We're so close! Can you hear it? It's like a heartbeat!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already three steps ahead, peering into the vault, her body thrumming with excitement.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: The vault is open. Pichit must decide whether to stick with the agreed plan (with the Negotiator or solo) or to rush ahead/fall behind strategically, knowing the final obstacle is just inside.
line.stage_directions: Tense moment. The Negotiator watches Pichit, waiting. Chanida is poised on the threshold. From outside, the faint, angry shouts of the ejected Sky Pirate echo.

choices.description: Chanida attempts to chart resonance pathways, relying on frequency mapping

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The gamble fails. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.description: Convince Arthit to use captain experience and map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
A costly mistake by Arthit. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.description: The pirate presses forward with disruptor weapon to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
the pirate is thwarted. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_before.dialogue: The Deep Vault opens into a single, vast chamber. The air is thick with a resonant silence that vibrates in your bones. At the chamber's center, on a crystalline plinth, hovers a faint, ever-shifting cloud of light and sound—a living aurora of harmonies.
lines_before.stage_directions: The walls pulse with slow, deep light. The Map glows like a captured star.

lines_before.dialogue: It’s not a thing you take. It’s a thing you... witness. I'm afraid there'll be a problem if we treat it like loot.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit's staff glows in sympathy with the Map's light.

lines_before.dialogue: Magnificent. A proprietary harmonic sequence of incalculable value. We must approach with respect, of course.
lines_before.stage_directions: The merchant's eyes gleam with avarice as he smooths his robes.

lines_before.dialogue: Who is this lady? The guardian? She looks... ancient.
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points to a motionless figure seated cross-legged before the plinth.

lines_before.dialogue: A Listener. A real one. How good is this guy at staying quiet? Let's see if she's just decoration.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee scans the chamber for traps, her hand on her knife.

lines_before.dialogue: Steady. This place feels sacred. That resonance... it's alive.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself between the party and the Map, shield ready.

lines_before.dialogue: The ancient Listener monk opens her eyes. She does not speak, but raises a hand. Her gaze holds centuries of silent vigil.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Merchant immediately steps forward, bowing with false humility.

lines_before.dialogue: Venerable one. We come seeking the Open Frequency. For the betterment of trade, for the unity of the cities. Name your price.
lines_before.stage_directions: He spreads his hands in a gesture of openness.

lines_before.dialogue: The Listener regards him, then turns to the shimmering Map. She gestures to it, then cups a hand to her ear. Slowly, deliberately, she makes a motion like shattering glass.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Map's light dims momentarily, as if flinching.

lines_before.dialogue: She’s saying it's fragile. A recording would break it. A static snapshot would be a dead thing.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit interprets, his voice hushed with realization.

lines_before.dialogue: A crash echoes from a side passage. The Sky Pirate stumbles in, followed by his crew, weapons drawn.
lines_before.stage_directions: Dust falls from the ceiling. The Pirate grins, eyeing the prize.

lines_before.dialogue: Well, ain't this cozy? Step aside, gramma. That pretty light's coming with us. When's he coming? Your backup? Don't see any.
lines_before.stage_directions: He gestures with his cutlass toward the silent monk.

lines_before.dialogue: Barbarian! You'll destroy its value! Venerable lady, an exclusive licensing agreement with me is your only protection!
lines_before.stage_directions: The merchant's friendly mask slips, revealing panic and greed.

lines_before.dialogue: The Listener is a statue of calm. She taps a sequence on a crystal slab at her feet: a simple drawing of an ear, then a broken chart.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Pirate snorts. The Merchant fumes. Both see only a prize to be owned.

lines_before.dialogue: Enough mime show. Grab the glowy bit! He winked at me. Think that'll stop me?
lines_before.stage_directions: The Pirate signals his crew, who fan out, resonance-capture devices humming to life.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit. They're going to kill it.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's knuckles are white on his sword hilt.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber thrums with hostile intent. The living Map flickers, sensitive to the discord.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Pirate's devices whine. The Merchant unholsters a sleek resonator.

lines_after.dialogue: This isn't about finding a map. It's about hearing a song.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's resolve hardens. He looks from the Listener's serene face to the rivals' hungry ones.

lines_after.dialogue: Choose a side, wanderer! Help me secure it, and you'll have a percentage of all future tolls!
lines_after.stage_directions: The merchant's offer is desperate, his smile gone.

lines_after.dialogue: They're moving! What do we do?
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida nocks an arrow, aiming at a Pirate's capture device.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: The Pirate and Negotiator are poised to try and capture the resonance. Pichit must decide: side with one rival to stop the other and seize the Map, or protect the Listener and the Map's living state, making an enemy of both.
line.stage_directions: Tense moment. The Pirate lunges toward the plinth. The Merchant aims his device.

choices.description: Have Malee risk using engineering to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Malee pulls it off. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.description: Pichit channels staff meditation toward the ancient texts, hoping to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.description: The pirate steps forward with secret frequencies, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
the pirate loses control. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The vault’s crystal walls pulse with the afterglow of conflict—not of blades, but of sound. The air vibrates with spent harmonies, dissonance now settling into an uneasy quiet.
lines_before.stage_directions: Faint, shimmering echoes linger in the crystalline lattice.

lines_before.dialogue: We live near each other, in this world of frequencies… yet so far apart in what we choose to hear.
lines_before.stage_directions: He touches the humming plinth, feeling its resonance through his staff.

lines_before.dialogue: You think you’ve won? You just made the whole vault a beacon! The Orders’ patrols will be here before sundown.
lines_before.stage_directions: He leans against a cracked resonator, nursing a bruised ear from the sonic clash.

lines_before.dialogue: And you’d have stolen it! You’d have silenced it forever! There’s no one else who could have defended it.
lines_before.stage_directions: She gestures fiercely at the bandit, her hands still trembling from channeling disruptive harmonics.

lines_before.dialogue: Defended a living resonance. Now we’re responsible for it. Where will you live when the Tonal Orders mark you as a threat?
lines_before.stage_directions: She scans the vault entrance, calculating the time until archivists arrive.

lines_before.dialogue: We stand together. From that day in the ruins, we’ve known the cost of silence. We won’t let it happen again.
lines_before.stage_directions: He positions himself between the party and the bandit, shield-arm raised.

lines_before.dialogue: The Listener approaches, her steps silent but her presence a calming frequency. She taps a crystal column, and the vault responds with a gentle, clarifying hum.
lines_before.stage_directions: The ambient light softens, focusing around her.

lines_after.dialogue: The antechamber is a liminal space—half vault, half world. The air smells of ozone and distant rain.
lines_after.stage_directions: Resonance ships hum faintly beyond the crystal gates.

lines_after.dialogue: I’m happy to hear the truth… but it weighs heavier than any secret.
lines_after.stage_directions: His staff pulses with a low, thoughtful rhythm.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, the young guardians. You’ve made a noble choice. But remember—the world trades in fragments, not philosophies. My ships still need safe paths.
lines_after.stage_directions: He smiles, but his eyes flick to the bandit, already scheming a new alliance.

lines_after.dialogue: Then learn to listen! The Map isn’t a commodity. It’s a… a practice.
lines_after.stage_directions: Already moving toward the exit, eager to carry the understanding outward.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide how to respond to the Negotiator's final words—with hostility, feigned alliance, or silent dismissal—defining their ongoing relationship. More profoundly, they must decide what to do with the understanding they've gained.
line.stage_directions: Tense moment. The merchant’s smile is a calculated offer.

choices.description: Channel the vault's resonance through your shared frequencies to seal it permanently.

line.dialogue: Pichit grips your shoulder, trembling — "I can feel every voice in the vault agreeing. They're choosing us.
Pichit screams as the frequency tears backward through him — "Too many voices! I can't hold them all!

choices.description: Turn the vault's resonance outward, broadcasting its living frequency across every nearby settlement.

line.dialogue: Malee steadies herself against the humming wall — "They'll hear us now. Every village, every silenced corner. This was always meant to be free.
Malee claps her hands over her ears, eyes wide — "It's screaming, not singing! We just weaponized a living thing!

choices.description: Offer the bandit a place within the resonance — let them carry a shard of the vault's frequency as penance.

line.dialogue: Chanida watches the bandit's hands stop shaking — "You don't silence what you've become part of. That's the point. That's always been the point.
Chanida grabs your arm as the bandit shatters the shard against the floor — "Some people would rather destroy beauty than admit they were wrong.

lines_before.dialogue: The Monastery of Phrao hummed with a thousand subtle frequencies. Crystalline spires rose from the floating island's edge, each resonating with the world's endless song beneath. In the grand hall, the air itself seemed to vibrate with unspoken secrets.
lines_before.stage_directions: Long shot of the monastery's crystalline architecture, light refracting through prismatic windows.

lines_before.dialogue: This place... the way the crystals respond to every footstep, every whisper. We came here looking for answers about the anomalous frequency we recorded, but I don't know where to begin.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit runs a hand along a wall that emits a soft, answering chime. His staff's crystal flickers with sympathetic resonance.

lines_before.dialogue: Echoes of The Silencing. That is all your 'anomaly' can be. Some frequencies are better left buried, young traveler. The Lattice remembers what we have tried to forget.
lines_before.stage_directions: The senior Listener sits perfectly still, his hands folded. His voice carries the weight of centuries, but his eyes avoid Pichit's.

lines_before.dialogue: Buried? We nearly got buried by that resonance spike! There's something active down there, not just some old ghost!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida gestures emphatically, causing a nearby crystal wineglass to ring faintly.

lines_before.dialogue: Notice how he didn't deny its existence. Just advised against looking. Classic authority move. We still don't know yet what they're actually afraid of.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee watches the monk retreat, her fingers tapping a silent rhythm on her thigh.

lines_before.dialogue: The tension here is thicker than storm clouds. Everyone's watching. How well do you know her? The one who gave us that initial frequency reading? Can we trust her data if the Listeners themselves deny it?
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly ahead of Pichit, his posture defensive as they enter the grand refectory.

lines_before.dialogue: The refectory was a cavern of polished stone and crystal, where the clatter of plates created a chaotic symphony. And at its center, a more discordant note.
lines_before.stage_directions: Focus shifts to a heated, hushed argument between the finely dressed Merchant and a scarred Sky Pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: ...your kind disrupts the harmonies of trade. Guest-right or not, your presence here is a dissonance.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Merchant smiles, but it doesn't reach his eyes. His fingers trace the rim of his crystal goblet.

lines_before.dialogue: Trade? You mean your stranglehold! Your 'harmonies' are just chains tuned to a rich man's key!
lines_before.stage_directions: The Pirate slams a fist on the table, making the crystalware shiver. He storms out, his leather coat snapping like a sail.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah, the seekers of lost songs! Please, join me. Ignore that unpleasantness. A man who hears only the crash of waves cannot appreciate a symphony. I couldn't help but overhear your... predicament with the elder Listeners.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Merchant turns his smile on the party, gesturing to empty seats. It's a friendly, calculated motion.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Orders restrict certain harmonic charts for stability's sake. But for friends... for those who might do a friend a future favor... such restrictions can become suggestions. I believe I have the specific charts you're looking for.
lines_before.stage_directions: He leans forward conspiratorially, his voice dropping to a melodic whisper.

lines_before.dialogue: Future favors. That's a vague price. And we don't know when such a favor might be called, or what it would entail.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit meets the Merchant's gaze, his own staff's crystal pulsing slowly at his side.

lines_before.dialogue: Later, in the acoustic gardens where shaped hedges focused the wind's song into eerie chorales, a shadow detached itself from the humming crystals.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Sky Pirate steps into Pichit's path as he walks alone, the garden's harmonies masking their conversation.

lines_before.dialogue: That snake's charts are tuned wrong on purpose. A dead zone frequency, disguised. Get you lost in the silent deep where no one asks questions. I don't know if you're fools, but I know what you're hunting.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Pirate speaks in a rough, urgent rasp, his eyes constantly scanning the garden paths.

lines_before.dialogue: The real key is a forbidden resonance. The Listeners recorded it during The Silencing and sealed it away. They're not just secretive—they're terrified of it. The Merchant wants you gone. I want that truth. Our interests align.
lines_before.stage_directions: He jabs a finger toward the monastery's central spire. His hand bears old lattice-burn scars.

lines_after.dialogue: The Pirate melted back into the sonic landscape, leaving Pichit alone with the garden's manufactured song and two conflicting paths.
lines_after.stage_directions: The wind shifts, causing the harmonic hedges to emit a low, warning drone.

lines_after.dialogue: Official charts that could be a trap, or a forbidden truth from an outlaw. Both want something from us. I can't say yet if either is telling the whole story.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit looks at his staff. The crystal within glows, not with its usual steady light, but with a faint, irregular flicker—a sympathetic response to the garden's hidden frequencies.

lines_after.dialogue: Make your choice, wanderer. Trust the hand that feeds the cage, or the one that knows how to pick the lock.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Pirate's voice is a distant whisper, carried oddly by the acoustic garden, seeming to come from everywhere at once.

lines_after.dialogue: Well? The smiler with the maps, or the growler with the secret? Either way, we're not leaving empty-handed!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida bounces on the balls of her feet, already turning as if to chase down both leads at once.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide whose lead to follow first: accept the Negotiator's bargain for the official (but possibly sabotaged) charts, or secretly pursue the Pirate's claim of a 'forbidden resonance.'
line.stage_directions: Tense moment.

choices.description: Press your palm against the largest crystal and hum a single sustained note, 15 words

line.dialogue: The harmonics just... answered. Every crystal in this chamber aligned to my pitch — this isn't residual energy, it's *waiting* for something.
Ah— the feedback nearly took my fingers. Whatever lives in these crystals doesn't want amateur musicians.

choices.description: Ask the monk directly what The Silencing did to the people who lived here, 14 words

line.dialogue: You want the truth? The Silencing didn't kill them. It *unmade* their voices from memory itself. Even their ghosts cannot scream.
Some questions carve themselves into the asker. I will not speak it here, where the walls still listen.

choices.description: Scan the resonance spike with Malee's frequency analyzer before the echo fades, 14 words

line.dialogue: The waveform is artificial — structured like language. Chanida, this 'spike' wasn't an accident. Someone *sent* a message through the crystals.
Too late. The signal collapsed into noise the moment I calibrated. Whatever it said, it wasn't meant for us to hear twice.

lines_before.dialogue: The monastery's silence feels heavier now, pregnant with secrets. Dust motes dance in shafts of colored light from crystalline windows.
lines_before.stage_directions: Close on dust motes, then wide shot of the party following their chosen guide.

lines_before.dialogue: Every choice carries a chance… a chance to learn, or a chance to be lost. We’ve committed to this path. We can’t miss out on the chance to understand what’s happening.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit grips his staff, its faint hum matching his pulse.

lines_before.dialogue: Just through here. My contact has a secure calibration chamber. But listen… there's a high chance the Tonal Orders will detect this access. Are you prepared for that?
lines_before.stage_directions: He pauses, his smile tight, calculating their resolve.

lines_before.dialogue: Detect us? What does that mean? Are they going to send guards? Is it necessary to use one of their crystals at all? Can't we just look at paper charts?
lines_before.stage_directions: She steps forward, hands on her hips, looking between the merchant and the heavy door.

lines_before.dialogue: Paper charts are outdated the moment they're printed. The Lattice shifts. He's talking about a live feed. High reward, high risk. Standard procedure.
lines_before.stage_directions: She runs a finger along the door's seam, checking for residue or recent use.

lines_before.dialogue: This feels like a trap. We're walking right into a monitored room. Pichit, we should reconsider.
lines_before.stage_directions: He positions himself slightly in front of Chanida, eyes scanning the shadows.

lines_before.dialogue: The merchant ignores the protests, working a complex sequence on a crystalline lock. The door slides open with a deep, resonant groan, revealing not a chart room, but a forgotten laboratory.
lines_before.stage_directions: The interior is a mess of toppled equipment, shattered glass, and one massive, dormant central crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: On a cracked data-slate, schematics flicker. Not for navigation. For a limb. A prosthetic leg of intricate crystal latticework, designed not just to receive resonance, but to project it. Violently.
lines_after.stage_directions: Close-up on the schematic: 'Resonant Amplification Limb - Prototype 7. Caution: Broadcast Function Unstable.'

lines_after.dialogue: This wasn't for healing… This was a weapon. The anomalous frequency we've been tracking… it's a weapon signature. This is what the Listeners were trying to warn us about.
lines_after.stage_directions: He looks from the schematics to the merchant, whose expression has shifted from helpful to greedily fascinated.

lines_after.dialogue: Fascinating. My sponsors… they would pay a fortune for such a device. 'For study,' of course. A discovery like this… you could name your price. We're not finished yet here.
lines_after.stage_directions: He reaches for the slate, his movements suddenly eager.

lines_after.dialogue: Wait, look! In the corner!
lines_after.stage_directions: She points to a debris-covered workbench where the physical prototype lies, cracked and dark. 'It’s irreparable.'

line.dialogue: The dilemma is before you. This knowledge is pure volatility. Do we destroy it here and now, bury it again and hope no one else finds it, or secure it? Knowing that forces beyond these walls will hunt for it.
line.stage_directions: He watches Pichit intently, his friendly mask gone, replaced by naked ambition.

choices.description: Squeeze through the rusted cargo door before the automated patrol sweeps the alley, 14 words

line.dialogue: My heart's still pounding but we're through — and I counted their rotation gap for next time.
The sweep caught my backpack strap and tore it clean off — everything I packed is scattered back there.

choices.description: Ask the merchant to explain what 'detect us' means before following him inside, 13 words

line.dialogue: He laid it out plain — motion signatures, thermal residue, the works. Now I know what we're evading.
He clammed up the second I pressed him. Whatever he's not telling us, we're walking blind into it.

choices.description: Pull out the paper charts and cross-reference the merchant's route against known dead zones, 16 words

line.dialogue: Outdated or not, these charts just saved us — his 'secure' corridor overlaps a decommissioned sensor grid that still pings.
I traced the route but the ink bled through at the junction — now I can't tell which fork he actually marked.

lines_before.dialogue: The monastery's archives feel different now—not a place of quiet study, but a crime scene they've stumbled into. The air hums with tension, not just resonance.
lines_before.stage_directions: Crystalline walls seem to watch them. Distant chimes feel like warnings.

lines_before.dialogue: You still don't understand? This isn't about breaking rules. It's about a truth someone closed the door on loudly, hoping we wouldn't hear.
lines_before.stage_directions: Taps his staff against the floor, sending a soft pulse through the crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: A misunderstanding, surely. My associate here—the Bell-Master—has a class to teach in the morning on tonal stability. We can't have you disrupting the monastery's delicate work.
lines_before.stage_directions: Smiles placatingly, hands spread in a calming gesture.

lines_before.dialogue: Your 'associate'? He just threatened to have us thrown into a resonance-dampening cell! That's not teaching—that's covering something up!
lines_before.stage_directions: Steps forward, fists clenched, voice echoing in the chamber.

lines_before.dialogue: Check the harmonics on his prosthetic. It's not just a leg—it's amplifying something. Her mom told me about the old research already. This matches the descriptions.
lines_before.stage_directions: Eyes narrowed, studying the Bell-Master's crystalline limb with clinical intensity.

lines_before.dialogue: Everyone stay calm. We're surrounded by Listeners who think we're vandals. One wrong frequency could collapse this entire wing.
lines_before.stage_directions: Positions himself between the party and the approaching monastery guards.

lines_before.dialogue: Then the sky pirate's diversion hits—a shattering resonance burst from outside that echoes through the corridors like breaking glass.
lines_before.stage_directions: The crystal walls flicker. A corridor nearby goes acoustically dead—utterly silent.

lines_after.dialogue: In the dead zone's unnatural quiet, the truth becomes clear. The prosthetic isn't just medical tech—it's a weapon prototype.
lines_after.stage_directions: The silent corridor looks like a ghost of The Silencing.

lines_after.dialogue: That 'forbidden frequency'... it's a fracture tone. Amplify it with something like his leg, and you could shatter lattice structures permanently. Create new Silencing zones on purpose.
lines_after.stage_directions: His staff pulses with understanding, not power.

lines_after.dialogue: See? The whole system's rotten! I'm gonna rush off right now to grab the research logs before they burn them. You coming, or you waiting for permission from the people who want you silenced?
lines_after.stage_directions: Already at the window, one foot on the ledge.

lines_after.dialogue: They're not just hiding history—they're weaponizing it! We can't let them control this narrative!
lines_after.stage_directions: Tuning her own resonance blade, ready to follow.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: With the authorities compromised, Pichit must decide how to expose the truth. Do they work with the untrustworthy Pirate to steal the evidence and go public, or do they play the Negotiator's game, pretending compliance to get close to the Bell-Master and find irrefutable proof?
line.stage_directions: Tense moment.

choices.description: Grab the merchant by his collar and slam him against the canal wall, demanding the Bell-Worker's true name.

line.dialogue: His name? You think I know his *name*? I know his invoice number—that's how this works!" the merchant squeaks, his composure cracking like cheap ceramic.
Touch me again and you'll learn why the Bell-Workers chose *me* as their intermediary," the merchant whispers, his breath carrying a faint metallic hum that makes your teeth ache.

choices.description: Signal malee to scan the prosthetic's harmonic signature while you keep them talking about the shipment schedule.

line.dialogue: There—it's broadcasting on three frequencies simultaneously. This isn't a prosthetic, it's a *relay*," malee says, her eyes widening as the data streams across her scope.
It's cycling too fast—I can't get a clean read without him noticing," malee mutters, and the Bell-Worker's synthetic eye clicks toward her with deliberate, predatory slowness.

choices.description: Step between chanida and the Bell-Worker, palms raised, offering to negotiate a "revision" to whatever deal was struck.

line.dialogue: Now *this* is how professionals conduct business. Your colleagues could learn from you," the Bell-Worker purrs, his prosthetic fingers
The attempt backfires on the merchant. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: The hidden vault is a chamber of frozen music. Crystalline pillars rise like petrified soundwaves, each facet holding a captured harmonic echo from before The Silencing. In the center, mounted on a resonator pedestal, the prototype gleams—a latticework of singing metal and humming crystal, pulsing with unstable light.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air shimmers with visible sound. Dust motes dance to a silent rhythm.

lines_before.dialogue: Some truths... we don't stay in touch with them for a reason. They're too heavy.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit grips his staff, its crystal tip vibrating in sympathy with the chamber's hum.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah. The final bid. Stay right there. Don't move. This doesn't have to end with more broken things. Walk away. Let me 'lose' this in a favorable trade. I'll clear your names, provide passage anywhere. A profitable silence for all.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Negotiator stands between them and the device, hands open, smile gone—replaced by cold calculation.

lines_before.dialogue: After everything? You think we'll just sit tight while you sell a weapon?
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida's hand drifts to her blade, eyes flicking to the other entrance.

lines_before.dialogue: The readings are bad. It's interfaced with the monastery's main harmonic stabilizer. Don't leave it on. Don't leave it open to the lattice. It's trying to resonate with something deep below.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee watches a crystalline display, its glyphs flashing amber.

lines_before.dialogue: Everyone, stay still. Don't work too hard. Don't overwork yourselves. We need clear heads now, not heated blades.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly in front of the others, shield arm tense.

lines_before.dialogue: The second entrance groans open. The Sky Pirate enters, not with stealth, but with the clamor of conviction. His eyes lock on the device, then the Negotiator.
lines_before.stage_directions: Dust falls from the archway. The Pirate's crew flank him, weapons humming with crude resonance.

lines_after.dialogue: The standoff holds. The device's hum climbs in pitch, a thin, keening sound that makes the crystal pillars weep fine dust. The Pirate's fanaticism, the Merchant's cold greed—both are anchors dragging the moment toward violence.
lines_after.stage_directions: The light in the chamber throbs. Cracks spiderweb across one pillar.

lines_after.dialogue: I don't want people knowing what this can do. Not like this. Not as a thing to be owned or broken, but as a truth that needs... a different keeper.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit looks from his weary companions to the pulsing device. His staff's light steadies, matching his resolve.

lines_after.dialogue: Smash it! Let the song be free! Or I'll bring this whole mountain down on top of it! You think he'll control it? He'll sell it to the highest bidder, and then we all burn!
lines_after.stage_directions: The Pirate raises a jagged resonator crystal, its frequency set to shatter.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit. It's now or never. That thing isn't getting quieter.
lines_after.stage_directions: She steps beside him, blade half-drawn, ready to follow his lead.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit's final choice: Give the device to the Negotiator (enriching him and trusting his 'control'), give it to the Pirate (embracing anarchic destruction of the tech), destroy it themselves (taking responsibility but erasing the knowledge), or secretly disable and hide it (becoming its reluctant guardians). This choice defines the subplot's resolution and future repercussions.
line.stage_directions: The Merchant's eyes are hard currency. The Pirate's are fire. The device wails.

choices.description: Overload the monastery's interface by feeding Malee's readings back into it, 15 words

line.dialogue: The feedback loop worked—it's consuming itself, but we have maybe three minutes before total collapse.
That wasn't a buffer flush—I just routed the instability directly into our position.

choices.description: Let the merchant complete the final bid and watch what walks through, 15 words

line.dialogue: Now you understand why I told you not to move—some transactions require a witness, not a hero.
You flinched. The chord registered your hesitation, and now it's pricing us all at clearance.

choices.description: Grab Chanida and run for the eastern cloister before the chord stabilizes, 15 words

line.dialogue: I won't pretend that wasn't cowardly—but cowardice keeps you breathing, and I'd rather
the pirate overreaches. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns like a stone throat, swallowing the last violet light of dusk. Inside, the air doesn't just hum—it vibrates against the skin, a low, grinding frequency that feels less like sound and more like a physical pressure.
lines_before.stage_directions: The cavern walls are jagged crystal, glowing with a sickly internal light that pulses in time with the drone.

lines_before.dialogue: Listen. This isn't a natural resonance. It's structured, like a broken machine trying to remember its purpose. In only five minutes, the pitch has shifted twice. Something here is on a timer.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit runs a hand along his staff, feeling the crystal tip vibrate in sympathy.

lines_before.dialogue: You! Outsiders! You break the silence! You must join the chant or leave now. The safety of our island depends on it. Could you repeat that? You will join us, or you will go.
lines_before.stage_directions: An older woman steps forward from a circle of villagers. Her hands are raised, palms outward in a warding gesture. Her eyes are wide with genuine fear.

lines_before.dialogue: Join the chant? We're here to investigate, not to sing nursery rhymes to scared rocks! Look at that crystal formation—it's glowing in a harmonic pattern. This isn't spirits, it's mechanics!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points impatiently at the pulsing crystal cluster at the cavern's center, around which the villagers are arranged.

lines_before.dialogue: Pragmatic, cynical. She's right about the pattern. It's a dampening field. These people aren't just superstitious—they're performing active frequency suppression. Crude, but intentional. The second option is they know exactly what this thing is and are trying to keep it quiet.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee has a small resonator crystal in her hand, its faint glow syncing with the cavern's pulse. She's studying it, not the people.

lines_before.dialogue: Cautious, protective. Stand down, Chanida. Their fear is a weapon. How long are you going for with this confrontation? We gain nothing by making enemies. But look—up on the eastern ledge. Movement.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's hand rests on his weapon, his eyes scanning the higher shadows. He keeps his voice low, tense.

lines_before.dialogue: A scrape of boot on crystal. A silhouette detaches from the gloom of a high ledge—a figure clad in patched leather and scavenged metal. For a heartbeat, you lock eyes. Then they turn and flee, vanishing into a black fissure in the wall.
lines_before.stage_directions: The fleeing figure is a blur of motion. The lead villager gasps, and the chanting falters, causing the central crystal to flare brighter, its hum spiking painfully.

lines_after.dialogue: The cavern's frequency wavers, becoming jagged and sharp. The villagers' chant rises in desperate unison, trying to wrestle the sound back into its rhythmic box.
lines_after.stage_directions: The air itself seems to crackle. Glowing motes of crystal dust shake loose from the ceiling.

lines_after.dialogue: Reflection. Growth. That scout wasn't just watching them. He was watching the crystal, timing the cycle. They know the frequencies here. This isn't just a haunted hole—it's a site someone wants to control.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff pulses with a soft, steady light, a counterpoint to the erratic glow around him.

lines_after.dialogue: NPC raises stakes. From the dark tunnel, a rough, echoing laugh floats back. 'Run along, surface-dwellers! Tell your Tonal Masters the Hollow sings for new masters now!'
lines_after.stage_directions: The voice is mocking, already growing distant. It carries the distinct accent of the sky lanes.

lines_after.dialogue: Eager to press on. Pirates! I knew it! They're after whatever's making that noise. We can't let them get it first! The trail is getting cold!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already at the mouth of the fissure, peering into the darkness, one hand on her blade.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide: Do they respectfully participate in the villagers' ceremony to gain trust, or refuse and immediately pursue the sky pirate scout into the dangerous depths?
line.stage_directions: The lead villager blocks the way to the fissure, her expression a mix of fear and defiance. The other villagers' chanting grows louder, more insistent.

choices.description: Arthit attempts to uncover the suppression, relying on captain experience

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
Arthit is thwarted. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.description: Malee channels leg resonance toward the ancient ruins, hoping to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee loses control. The escape tunnel collapses.

choices.description: The pirate volunteers to uncover the suppression, leveraging secret frequencies

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
the pirate overreaches. A spy alerts the authorities.

lines_before.dialogue: The tunnels tighten, walls of translucent crystal humming with trapped vibrations. Each footstep sends shivering harmonics through the stone underfoot.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air shimmers with latent sound.

lines_before.dialogue: There’s something in my eye. Crystal dust, maybe. This place… it’s like walking inside a giant, sleeping instrument.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit rubs his eye, his other hand steadying himself against the vibrating wall.

lines_before.dialogue: The air tastes wrong. My grandmother told stories of places that remembered the Silencing. They hummed before they… broke.
lines_before.stage_directions: The villager looks around nervously, clutching a simple tool.

lines_before.dialogue: Look! Scorch marks, and fresh boot prints. Someone else is down here. I believe we can catch them!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points excitedly at the ground, already moving ahead.

lines_before.dialogue: Pirates. Smells like cheap engine oil and desperation. Their scout’s camp is up ahead, abandoned in a hurry.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee kneels, examining discarded ration wrappers and a hastily doused fire.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay behind me. These frequencies are destabilizing the structure. A wrong note could bring the ceiling down.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit spreads his arms, ushering the others back as a low groan echoes through the tunnel.

lines_before.dialogue: The tunnel opens into a vast, cathedral-like chamber. At its heart, fused with the island's bedrock, throbs a monstrous machine of brass and crystal.
lines_before.stage_directions: A pre-Silencing 'World-Singer' resonator, half-melted, pulses with dangerous light.

lines_after.dialogue: The violent resonance surge passes, leaving behind a cloud of dust and the ominous groan of settling stone. The way you came in is now a wall of rubble.
lines_after.stage_directions: Beams of light cut through the dust, illuminating the trapped parties.

lines_after.dialogue: That’s no problem. We brought it. The knowledge, I mean. We can figure this out.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's grip tightens on his staff, which glows in sympathetic resonance with the humming machine.

lines_after.dialogue: Well now. Looks like we're all sharing a tomb unless someone's got a clever idea. My crew knows this old tech. We've got charts. You've got… what, bravery?
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate captain steps forward, a jagged crystal resonator humming on his belt.

lines_after.dialogue: I'm starting to get hungry! But first, let's not get crushed. Pichit, what's the call?
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida cracks her knuckles, eyes darting between the pirates and the unstable machine.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: With the exit blocked and the device pulsing erratically, Pichit must decide: Do they temporarily ally with the pirates to understand/disable the device, or try to fight/outwit them immediately?
line.stage_directions: The villager looks desperately from Pichit to the pirates, the World-Singer's hum rising in pitch.

choices.description: Follow the boot prints deeper, keeping low and quiet along the crystalline walls.

line.dialogue: The prints split here — two went left toward the hollow, one climbed up. We take the high ground first.
I stepped on a crystal shard. The crack echoed through the whole chamber. So much for the element of surprise.

choices.description: Examine the scorch marks closely to identify what weapon or engine made them.

line.dialogue: Plasma cutters, old model. These marks are maybe six hours old. Whoever did this wanted to breach something fast and dirty.
I touched the wall where it burned and my fingers came away black. The residue stings — my hand is going numb.

choices.description: Call out toward the darkness, announcing yourselves as traders rather than threats.

line.dialogue: A voice answered from somewhere ahead — rough, cautious, but willing to talk. Maybe they're as lost as we are.
Chan

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber thrums with a rising, unstable energy. The ancient resonator's crystalline surfaces pulse with sickly amber light, casting jagged shadows across the faces of your uneasy alliance.
lines_before.stage_directions: The central console flickers, etched with pre-Silencing glyphs. Pirate and villager stand on opposite sides of the room, eyeing each other.

lines_before.dialogue: The log entries... they're fragmented. Like someone left in the middle of a sentence. Why didn’t you finish the job? The whole catastrophe might have been avoided.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit traces the glyphs on the console, his brow furrowed in concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: See? Sabotaged, not broken. Means it can be fixed. Or better—repurposed. I've seen diagrams in Listeners' scrap. We dampen the core frequency, bleed off the energy. My ship's got a crystal catcher. We sequester the power signature... could buy a whole fleet.
lines_before.stage_directions: The pirate captain grins, a gold tooth catching the pulsing light.

lines_before.dialogue: No! That's the greed that cracked the world! You'll siphon it off and leave us with the backlash! You have to finish the shutdown, the *right* way! Destroy it!
lines_before.stage_directions: A farmer, Elara, steps forward, her hands shaking but her voice firm. She clutches a simple tool like a weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: Whoa, whoa, whoa! He just said 'sequester the power.' That sounds like a 'we probably can't finish shutting it down without that' kind of problem!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points frantically between the console and the smug pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: She's not wrong. The console diagnostics are clear. The abort sequence damaged the primary regulator. It needs a new control crystal to channel the energy safely into dormancy. Without it... we're looking at an uncontrolled cascade.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee taps the flickering readout, her expression grimly pragmatic.

lines_before.dialogue: And where do we find a crystal of that purity and power on a floating island? Why didn’t you call for the Tonal Orders first? This is beyond us.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly in front of Pichit, hand on his weapon, eyeing the pirates.

lines_before.dialogue: The pirate captain barks a laugh, the sound ugly in the resonant chamber.
lines_before.stage_directions: He pats a heavy case at his belt. The hum in the room spikes, making the very air feel thick.

lines_before.dialogue: You need a crystal? I've got one. Perfect harmonic match. It's the core from my ship's main resonator.
lines_before.stage_directions: He doesn't open the case. His meaning is clear. It's his bartering chip.

lines_before.dialogue: Your ship's heart! Then your plan is suicide for your crew! Or a lie! You'd never give that up.
lines_before.stage_directions: Elara's eyes widen in horror and disbelief.

lines_before.dialogue: Give it? Who said give? I said I *have* it. You want it to do your 'noble' shutdown? That's a trade. You let me catch the device's energy signature first. My new core. Then you can use my old one to put the lullaby to bed. Everybody wins.
lines_before.stage_directions: He spreads his hands, the picture of reasonable piracy.

lines_before.dialogue: The energy signature he'd capture would be a weapon. A city-killer. He's not finishing the job, he's just taking a bigger slice before the rest goes bad.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee's voice is low, meant only for the party.

lines_before.dialogue: You see? It's the same choice! Power over people! Last time, they didn’t finish the shutdown because they wanted to keep the power flowing. And the Lattice answered with The Silencing! I didn’t finish my harvest today because I came here to stop this!
lines_before.stage_directions: Tears of frustration mix with the grime on Elara's face. Her plea is raw, grounded in the simple fear of losing her home.

lines_after.dialogue: The resonator groans. A hairline fracture races up a support column. Time is a crystal, and it's about to shatter.
lines_after.stage_directions: Amber light flares violently, then dims to a menacing, rhythmic throb.

lines_after.dialogue: A sacrifice or a gamble. To finish what was started, or to try something new and hope we don't eat the whole catastrophic meal.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's grip tightens on his staff, which vibrates in sympathy with the dying machine.

lines_after.dialogue: Clock's singing, friend. My offer stands. Let me hook up my gear, or try to smash it and see if the island can take the hit. What's it gonna be?
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate's hand rests on the case. His crew members tense, hands drifting toward weapons.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit! We can't just stand here! The whole room's gonna finish us if we don't finish *something*!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida bounces on the balls of her feet, ready to spring in whatever direction Pichit chooses.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: The crystal is the only way to safely sequester the device's energy. Pichit must decide: Do they force the pirates to surrender their ship's core crystal for the greater good (likely causing a fight), or attempt a far more dangerous total overload/destruction of the device that could damage the island?
line.stage_directions: Tense moment.

choices.description: Direct Arthit to challenge skycity propaganda using forbidden paths

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.description: Pichit presses forward with tonal knowledge to expose surface colonization truth

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Pichit. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The lattice has other plans. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.description: The pirate channels secret frequencies toward the darkness, hoping to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
the pirate loses control. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber hums with unstable energy. The ancient resonator pulses erratically, casting jagged shadows across crystalline walls. Every surface vibrates with the strain of containment.
lines_before.stage_directions: The device glows with dangerous intensity.

lines_before.dialogue: I have work to do. Stabilizing this... it requires precise acoustic labor.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit wipes sweat from his brow, studying the resonator's frequency patterns.

lines_before.dialogue: Can you promise me? Promise this won't bring the sky down on our heads?
lines_before.stage_directions: The villager wrings their hands, eyes darting between the device and the pirates.

lines_before.dialogue: Don't work too hard. But actually, do work hard! That thing's looking angrier by the second!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida keeps her weapon trained on the pirate captain.

lines_before.dialogue: It's not working. The dampening circuit keeps rejecting the pirate's crystal. The harmonics are fighting us.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee adjusts her tools with clinical precision, frustration evident.

lines_before.dialogue: Don't change the subject! Captain, your men stay back or we overload the whole chamber.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself between the pirates and the work area.

lines_before.dialogue: The air crackles with competing intentions. Every adjustment to the resonator sends painful vibrations through bone and crystal alike.
lines_before.stage_directions: The lattice walls shimmer with discordant colors.

lines_after.dialogue: With a final, deafening chime, the resonator falls silent. The oppressive hum ceases, leaving only the natural, mournful echoes of The Hollow.
lines_after.stage_directions: The device sits inert, its core either stabilized or shattered.

lines_after.dialogue: The work is done. But what we've learned... the true cost of such power. It's not usable for anyone.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit leans on his staff, exhausted but resolved.

lines_after.dialogue: You fools! That was a fortune you just buried! The Tonal Orders would've paid anything!
lines_after.stage_directions: The pirate captain gestures angrily but makes no move toward the dormant device.

lines_after.dialogue: Good. Now let's get out of this echo chamber before my ears start bleeding.
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida sheathes her weapon, already moving toward the exit.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: With the device neutralized, Pichit faces the final choice: Do they reveal the full truth of what happened here to the Tonal Orders (giving them control), leave it hidden for the Listeners to study, or entrust its secret to the Groundless-sympathetic villagers?
line.stage_directions: The villager looks from the silent resonator to Pichit, awaiting judgment.

choices.description: Direct Malee to support the rebels using crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The villagers rise with their agricultural tools.
Malee loses control. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing tonal knowledge to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Things don't go as planned. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.description: Ask the villager to rally the villagers, drawing on local knowledge

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the villager pulls it off. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
The risk doesn't pay off. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The Khrueang Market isn't a place, it's a frequency. A thousand overlapping tones—hawkers' cries, the low thrum of illicit resonance engines, the crystalline clatter of shifting inventory—all press against the party like a physical wall. Above, the Lattice's fractured surface glimmers, casting prismatic shards of light through the perpetual steam of a hundred food stalls.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air shimmers with heat and vibration. Makeshift awnings flutter in the resonant breeze.

lines_before.dialogue: It’s like trying to study the Lattice by myself... overwhelming. We need to find a starting point in all this noise.
lines_before.stage_directions: He grips his staff, its crystal tip vibrating faintly in sympathy with the market's chaotic hum.

lines_before.dialogue: Start with food! I’ve never tried Lattice-crab before, but it smells amazing. Information flows where the spices do.
lines_before.stage_directions: She points eagerly at a stall where something sizzles on a humming crystal griddle.

lines_before.dialogue: And how do you propose we question anyone? There’s nowhere to park a thought here, let alone a ship. We stick out.
lines_before.stage_directions: She scans the crowd, her hand resting on the hilt of her blade, checking for tails.

lines_before.dialogue: Keep your voices low. The Tonal Orders have ears in places like this. We look for the argument, not the announcement.
lines_before.stage_directions: He positions himself slightly ahead of the group, tense, his posture protective.

lines_before.dialogue: As if summoned by Arthit's warning, a sharp, pained whisper cuts through the ambient drone from a nearby noodle stall.
lines_before.stage_directions: The party's attention snaps to a cloaked figure with a crude, glowing crystal prosthetic replacing his lower leg, arguing with a scarred man in sky-leathers.

lines_before.dialogue: The lock’s faulty! It hums a half-tone off and now the whole leg resonates with every wrong step on the surface. I can feel it in my bones!
lines_before.stage_directions: He leans heavily on the stall, face etched with pain and paranoia, his prosthetic emitting a discordant, faint buzz.

lines_before.dialogue: You calibrated it wrong, rock-scrabbler. Or your own frequency’s unstable. Not my problem. You paid for the tool, you live with its song.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Sky Pirate leans back, aggressive but dismissive, picking at his teeth with a shard of crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: This ‘tool’ is going to shatter and take my hip with it!
lines_before.stage_directions: With a snarl, the scavenger shoves away from the table and limps hurriedly into the crowd, the irregular pulse of his leg leaving a faint, sickly glow in his wake.

lines_before.dialogue: The pirate watches him go, then turns his glare to the party, who have clearly been observing. His eyes narrow, calculating. Pichit takes a steadying breath and steps forward.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit approaches the now-vacant seat opposite the bandit.

lines_before.dialogue: Mind if I join you? I think... I need to see a menu.
lines_before.stage_directions: He gestures vaguely at the stall, keeping his tone neutral, his staff held non-threateningly.

lines_before.dialogue: Ordersman? You got that look. The ‘I-regulate-your-breath’ look.
lines_before.stage_directions: He doesn't invite Pichit to sit, his hand drifting to a weapon at his belt.

lines_before.dialogue: I studied resonance by myself. Their charts mean less to me than the natural hum of the Lattice.
lines_before.stage_directions: A slight, truthful admission. Pichit lets a fragment of his own connection to the Lattice’s base frequency resonate through his staff—a subtle, pure tone amidst the market's cacophony.

lines_before.dialogue: Hmph. Not a drone, then. Just lost. This market’s got menus for things you won’t find scribbled on slate. Specialized tools. For navigating... rough surfaces.
lines_before.stage_directions: His hostility ebbs into opportunistic interest. He leans in, voice dropping. He gestures with his chin toward a labyrinth of darker, narrower alleys where the market's orderly hum breaks into chaotic, individual rhythms.

lines_before.dialogue: But you gotta know who to ask. And what to ask for. My friend there... he asked for a leg. Didn't ask if the carpenter knew his harmonics.
lines_before.stage_directions: A cruel smile. He’s testing them, offering a hook without a line.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the air, thick as the stall's steam. The scavenger's pained, discordant frequency is fading into the crowd. The bandit's sly offer sits on the table between them, a silent challenge.
lines_after.stage_directions: Two paths diverge in the shimmering market haze.

lines_after.dialogue: A faulty tool is a danger to its user and everyone nearby. We need to understand the cost.
lines_after.stage_directions: He looks from the retreating scavenger to the smirking bandit, his staff's pulse quickening with his resolve.

lines_after.dialogue: Tick-tock, wanderer. The market waits for no one. You want a name, or you want a lesson?
lines_after.stage_directions: He drums his fingers on the table, the sound a deliberate, taunting rhythm.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't lose him! The one with the leg, he's the proof!
lines_after.stage_directions: She's already half-turned, poised to slip into the current of bodies after the scavenger.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide: follow the Scavenger to learn about the prosthetic's dangers firsthand, or stay and press the Sky Pirate for the broker's name.
line.stage_directions: The bandit's expectant gaze. The last flicker of the scavenger's malformed crystal leg vanishes around a corner.

choices.description: Signal Arthit to lead you through the back alleys toward the night market stalls. [15 words

line.dialogue: Arthit nods and guides the group through narrow passages where the humming walls muffle conversation.
Arthit freezes mid-step as a Tonal acolyte rounds the corner, forcing you all to pretend you're browsing fermented fish.

choices.description: Pull Pichit aside and ask what specific Lattice phenomenon he's observed near the eastern docks. [15 words

line.dialogue: Pichit's eyes light up as he whispers about resonance patterns disrupting the tide schedules — something the Orders would kill to suppress.
Pichit stammers, loses his train of thought, and Arthit shoots you both a withering glare for drawing attention with furtive whispering.

choices.description: Suggest Chanida order the Lattice-crab so you can observe whether the kitchen staff react strangely. [15 words

line.dialogue: Chanida grins and approaches the hunched vendor, whose trembling hands and darting eyes confirm he knows exactly what the crab means.
Chanida announces "Lattice-crab for everyone!" far too loudly, and Malee grabs her arm as conversations at nearby tables go suddenly, unnervingly silent.

lines_before.dialogue: The market's cacophony twists into a labyrinth of sound. Crystal chimes now ring with hidden menace; the chaotic frequencies feel less like celebration, more like a desperate cover.
lines_before.stage_directions: Overhead, resonance ships drift like silent predators. The lattice below pulses with erratic, sickly light.

lines_before.dialogue: We've been picking our way through this noise, but what kind of truth do we prefer? The safe one, or the dangerous one that might actually help?
lines_before.stage_directions: He pauses, staff glowing faintly as he senses a discordant harmonic beneath the stall's curtain.

lines_before.dialogue: You followed? Good. See what he's doing! See it! My cousin chose one of these. Now he's dead on the lattice, shattered by his own leg!
lines_before.stage_directions: He gestures wildly at the curtained stall, face etched with raw fury and grief.

lines_before.dialogue: Why are you doing this to me? We're trying to help! But this... this is a butcher's shop!
lines_before.stage_directions: She steps forward, hand on her blade, eyes scanning for hidden threats.

lines_before.dialogue: Calibration's a mess. Scavenged lattice shards, unstable frequency matrix. The Orders outlawed this for a reason. It's not just control; it's basic safety.

lines_before.dialogue: It’s really a great place to live, isn't it? So ordered. So... curated. I wanna ask you something about how you maintain such perfect harmony. How do you write the schedules for these acoustic studies?
