The harmonic structure is complex but... beautiful. It defies the rigid patterns of the Orders. It feels organic.
Organic? It sounds like the whispers before The Silencing. My grandma told stories. You're catching something you can't put down.
A living resonance within the Lattice. This changes everything. It suggests the Silencing wasn't an end, but a... transformation.
You speak of truth, but without the weight of duty! To follow this song is to abandon the safe harbors!

lines_after.dialogue: The green pulse on the terminal suddenly synchronizes with a deep, sub-audible thrum from the Archives' very foundations.
The structural resonance is aligning with the open frequency. We are no longer just observing. We are participating.
It's a door! And it's opening!

line.dialogue: The Archives themselves begin to vibrate in harmony with the rogue frequency. The path is revealing itself, but so is the attention of the Tonal Orders.

choices.text: Record the frequency coordinates and retreat before Order enforcers arrive. (Easy)
choices.leads_to: act_3
choices.description: Tune the receiver to match the harmonic structure before the signal destabilizes.

line.dialogue: I've locked the phase alignment—the frequency is resolving into something structured, deliberate, *alive*.
The harmonics collapsed—whatever is transmitting, it shifted away from us the moment I got close.

choices.text: Attempt to 'answer' the call with a resonator, risking a full harmonic lock. (Medium)
choices.leads_to: act_3
choices.description: Override monk's objections and pull the raw feed data directly to your screen.

line.dialogue: There—look. Coordinates embedded in the waveform. This isn't noise, it's a *destination*.
Nothing but garbage data. Either something scrambled it on purpose, or we were never meant to read it.

choices.text: Convince the conflicted Monk to help you shield the signal, hiding your discovery from the Orders. (Hard)
choices.leads_to: act_3
choices.description: Cut the connection entirely and demand monk explain what they know.

line.dialogue: The feed is dead. Now talk—why did you react before we even touched the signal?
I tried to sever it but the connection is holding on its own. Whatever this is, *it's* choosing to stay.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before a towering, sealed crystal cabinet. The air hums with a low, dissonant frequency.
This is it! The restricted section. The Open Frequency Map has to be in here. I can feel the energy!
Or it's a very expensive, very loud paperweight. I really wonder what the Tonal Orders will do if they catch us.
The locking mechanism is acoustic. We need the correct harmonic sequence. One wrong note could trigger an alarm... or worse.
The silence here is different. It's not empty... it's waiting. Listen.
You shouldn't be here. The map... it shows frequencies the Orders have declared unstable. Forbidden. I'm really hurting, knowing what they've hidden.
My cousin's ship vanished using an 'approved' route. If there's a safer path, we deserve to know! Why couldn't you tell us?
That's really easy to guess! They're keeping us dependent. Now, how do we open this thing?

lines_after.dialogue: The cabinet emits a soft chime. The crystal door slides open, revealing not a scroll, but a large, dormant resonator crystal.
Great. The map is a rock. For the adventurous, I suppose.
No. The map *is* the frequency. This crystal holds the song. To read it, someone must sing *to* it.

line.dialogue: The dormant crystal awaits activation. Who will attempt to resonate with the Open Frequency Map?

choices.text: [EASY] Let Chanida try. Her raw enthusiasm might spark a connection.
choices.description: Hum the lullaby from the Foundation charter, matching the resonance pattern etched above the doorframe.

line.dialogue: * "The harmonics are shifting — the lock is recognizing the tonal signature, keep going, don't you dare stop now.
* "Wrong key — the mechanism just sealed tighter. Whatever you're humming, it's the opposite of an invitation.

choices.text: [MEDIUM] Pichit should do it. His philosophical connection to sound is deepest.
choices.description: Place your palm flat against the door and listen for the frequency it's already emitting, then mirror it back with your voice.

line.dialogue: * "I can feel the vibration through the floor — you've matched it, the door is breathing with you now.
* "It threw the frequency back at us doubled. My teeth are aching and that door just got angrier.

choices.text: [HARD] The Listener Monk knows the old ways. He should interface with it.
choices.description: Have Pichit speak the silence's name — the word he swears he can hear it whispering from between the shelves.

line.dialogue: * "It answered. It said my name back, but — the door is open. I don't think it's letting us leave.
* "It heard me. God, it heard me, and now the silence is screaming — everyone, step back, STEP BACK.

lines_before.dialogue: As the chosen one approaches, the crystal brightens. The air thickens with potential sound. Distant, hurried footsteps echo in the stacks.
Archivists are coming. We have moments. Whatever happens, it happens now.
The Head Archivist told me about this crystal already. He fears it. It doesn't just show safe paths... it shows the Lattice's *true* state.
Last night, I had a bad dream. Of the Silencing happening again. Is this going to stop it, or start it?
That's really easy to guess! It'll probably do both. Brace yourselves.
The song isn't a route. It's a... diagnosis. The Lattice is sick. The 'safe' paths are just avoiding the wounds.
So we've been sailing on a corpse? We need this truth! Sing!

lines_after.dialogue: A pure, clear tone rings out. The crystal projects a complex, shimmering harmonic lattice into the air—a map of fractures, healing points, and dead zones. The Head Archivist and guards arrive, frozen by the sight.
The truth is now visible to all. The monopoly on knowledge is shattered. But the unstable reality it reveals is terrifying.
The map is open. The song is free. Now we must decide what to do with a world more fragile, and more alive, than we ever guessed.

line.dialogue: The Open Frequency Map is revealed. The Tonal Orders stand ready to suppress it. What is the party's immediate course of action?

choices.text: [EASY] Protect the crystal. Defend the truth here in the Archives, rallying the Listeners and villagers.
choices.consequence: A standoff begins, turning the Archives into a fortress of knowledge. The truth spreads slowly but securely.
choices.description: Press the crystal against the monastery's central pillar to amplify its resonance before the Archivists breach the gate.

line.dialogue: The pillar hums like a struck bell — I feel the unwritten song vibrating through my teeth," the monk whispers, eyes wide.
The crystal cracks in my trembling hand. The pillar stays dead. I've killed the song before it was ever born," the monk says.

choices.text: [MEDIUM] Broadcast the frequency. Use the Archives' resonators to send the map's song to every ship and city, now.
choices.consequence: Chaos and liberation erupt simultaneously across the sky. Navigation is revolutionized overnight, but the shockwaves are unpredictable.
choices.description: Give the crystal to the villager and ask her to sing what she heard in her nightmare dream into its facets.

line.dialogue: I didn't expect my own voice to come back strengthened, layered with harmonies I've never sung before — but it did," the villager says, tears running.
My voice breaks on the third note. The dream was too big inside me and the crystal spits it back shattered," the villager chokes.

choices.text: [HARD] Decode the healing points. Ignite the political fight and focus on using the map to mend the Lattice's fractures.
choices.consequence: A dangerous, generations-long project begins. You make enemies of both the Orders and those who fear any change.
choices.description: Have Malee improvise a counter-melody on her bamboo flute while Arthit shields the crystal with his body at the threshold.

line.dialogue: My ribs ache where the first Archivist's staff struck me but the flute holds — the melody wraps around the crystal like armor," Arthit grunts, still standing.
The flute's reed splits on the high passage. The melody collapses and the Archivist's silence pours through the gap like cold water," Malee says, staring at her instrument.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship 'Tradewind's Fortune' hums like a living thing, its crystalline hull vibrating with the deep, complex tone that parts the Lattice below. The deck is a polished expanse of wood and brass, but the air thrums with unseen energy. Crew move with practiced efficiency, their movements timed to the ship's resonant frequency.
lines_before.stage_directions: The skyway stretches to infinity. The Lattice below shimmers like a frozen, fractured sea.

lines_before.dialogue: I had a bad dream last night. A silent one, which is worse. Here, the noise is constant, but it feels... off-key. Like the lattice has a class on dissonance it's decided to teach us.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit grips his staff, its own faint resonance attuning to the ship's hum.

lines_before.dialogue: Welcome, welcome! So glad you could join us for this leg of the journey. The schedule is tight, profits wait for no one, but your expertise is... valued. I'm sure it's nothing.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator, Lirin, smiles broadly but his eyes dart to a brass chronometer on his wrist every few seconds. His fingers tap a nervous rhythm on his ledger.

lines_before.dialogue: Valued, but you want us to rush off right now, don't you? What's the hurry? The sky isn't going anywhere.
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida plants her hands on her hips, looking past Lirin to scan the crew.

lines_before.dialogue: Profit hurry. That's really easy to guess. But hurry makes mistakes. Let's see what we're actually dealing with before we 'rush off.'
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee's eyes are already cataloging the ship's fittings, looking for flaws, her hand resting on a toolkit.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay sharp. The Monk over there isn't praying. He's listening. And he doesn't look happy about what he hears.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly ahead of the group, his shield arm tense.

lines_before.dialogue: Before Lirin can offer another platitude, the ship's steady hum falters. A new sound bleeds through the deck plates—a low, visceral thrum that vibrates in the teeth and bones.
lines_before.stage_directions: The polished brass fixtures shiver. A young crewman, Kael, clutching a manifest, staggers as if struck.

lines_after.dialogue: Kael lies still on the deck, his breathing shallow. The eerie glow from his leg has faded, leaving the crystalline prosthetic looking dull and inert. The normal ship's hum returns, but it now feels like a lie covering a wound.
lines_after.stage_directions: The crew watches, a mixture of fear and confusion on their faces. The Monk remains kneeling, head bowed.

lines_after.dialogue: That was no fatigue. That was a resonance seeking a matching frequency. His leg wasn't broken; it was answering a call. A call from something in the lattice that shouldn't be there.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's own staff pulses once, softly, in sympathy. He looks from the anxious Merchant to the troubled Monk.

lines_after.dialogue: The Song is wounded here. This path we sail... it cuts through a scar. That device in his leg is a tuning fork, and it has found the discord. We proceed into this silence at our peril.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Monk, Brother Elian, stands. His usual reverent calm is replaced by a grave urgency. He looks directly at Pichit.

lines_after.dialogue: Well, we're not just going to ignore that! A scar in the sky? A leg that lights up like a warning beacon? That's our job! Let's go!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already moving toward the ship's interior, gesturing for the others to follow.

line.dialogue: Please, I have a class of merchants in Port Helios expecting this cargo on schedule! It's a minor resonance spike, a known hazard. The boy will recover. We must make way. Delay costs more than you know.
line.stage_directions: Lirin steps between the party and the interior hatch, his friendly mask slipping to reveal desperate calculation.

choices.description: Have Pichit risk using tonal knowledge to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.description: Chanida attempts to harness harmonic feedback, relying on frequency mapping

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.description: Convince the monk to use meditation and test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the monk pulls it off. Crystal bowls shatter in harmonic sympathy.
A costly mistake by the monk. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

lines_before.dialogue: In the ship's secured storage locker, the air hums with contained energy. The crystalline prosthetic leg rests on a velvet-lined crate, its inner facets glowing with a slow, rhythmic pulse that matches the deep thrum of the engines below deck.
lines_before.stage_directions: The light casts sharp, dancing shadows on the metal walls.

lines_before.dialogue: You have to finish your investigation before the Negotiator grows suspicious. This isn't just a malfunction—it's a key.
lines_before.stage_directions: He runs a finger along the prosthetic's cold surface, feeling the vibration sync with the ship's heart.

lines_before.dialogue: He's the only son in the family. His mother entrusted him to this ship for his future. To think his very body is being used as a tool...
lines_before.stage_directions: He paces back and forth, his robes whispering against the deck plates, agitation in every step.

lines_before.dialogue: Used? You mean this thing is doing more than just walking?
lines_before.stage_directions: She leans in, her eyes wide with horrified fascination.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance signature is too precise. It's not a byproduct—it's an amplifier. Cross-reference it with the charts.
lines_before.stage_directions: She spreads the navigational charts on a nearby crate, her fingers tracing lines of frequency notation.

lines_before.dialogue: The Negotiator provided these too easily. Watch the door.
lines_before.stage_directions: He stands guard, hand resting on the hilt of his blade, eyes fixed on the corridor.

lines_before.dialogue: The discrepancy is stark. The ship's plotted course is a standard skyway, but the prosthetic's resonance signature maps to a different, jagged frequency path—one that cuts through unstable lattice sectors.
lines_before.stage_directions: The charts seem to shimmer under the conflicting data.

lines_before.dialogue: I see you've been enjoying my hospitality. An experimental route, sanctioned by a forward-thinking faction within the Tonal Orders. Cheaper, faster. This movie is great! A really good movie for our profit margins.
lines_before.stage_directions: He leans in the doorway, arms crossed, a smile that doesn't reach his eyes.

lines_before.dialogue: You must see it—the damage this 'experiment' is causing. The lattice below us is being forced into a harmonic it can't sustain.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit steps between the Negotiator and the prosthetic, his staff glowing faintly.

lines_before.dialogue: As if triggered by the confrontation, the prosthetic leg flares. A jagged, painful harmonic shrieks from its core, a sound that feels like grinding glass on bone.
lines_before.stage_directions: The crystal projects a violent, strobing light.

lines_before.dialogue: Outside, through the viewport, the luminous lattice layer below the ship shudders visibly, crystalline facets cracking and reforming in distress.
lines_before.stage_directions: The ship lurches slightly, a deep groan echoing through the hull.

lines_after.dialogue: The harmonic fades, leaving a ringing silence. The prosthetic goes dark, but the lattice below continues its pained, sluggish pulse.
lines_after.stage_directions: The light from the viewport shows a wounded, shimmering world.

lines_after.dialogue: The leg isn't malfunctioning. It's resonating with the ship's forced frequency, turning a man into a living, suffering key for an illegal path.
lines_after.stage_directions: His own staff pulses in sympathetic, troubled rhythm.

lines_after.dialogue: This is sacrilege. The natural song is being torn. We must silence this false resonance before it fractures the lattice further and dooms us all.
lines_after.stage_directions: He clutches his prayer beads, his voice trembling with dogmatic certainty.

lines_after.dialogue: So do we stop the ship or stop the leg? Either way, we can't just stand here!
lines_after.stage_directions: She's already moving toward the door, ready for action.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide: confront the Negotiator now and demand he change course (risking violent refusal), or pretend to acquiesce while secretly working with the Monk to sabotage the resonator (risking the ship's safety).
line.stage_directions: The Negotiator's friendly smile has vanished, replaced by cold calculation.

choices.description: Hack the construct's core to trace the resonance signal back to its source, 15 words

line.dialogue: I've got it — the signature is broadcasting through the temple drainage system to somewhere beneath the negotiating hall.
The core just fried itself. Whatever's inside knew I was looking and burned the evidence before I could map it.

choices.description: Press the monk about who gave his son the construct and what promises were made, 15 words

line.dialogue: He says a woman in a grey veil approached them at the night market — promised the boy would 'speak with ancestors.
He shut down completely. Says I'm dishonoring his mother's memory by asking. He's protecting someone — or he's terrified of them.

choices.description: Set a false resonance trap using Chanida's equipment to lure whoever is receiving the signal, 15 words

line.dialogue: They took the bait. Something in the east wing just powered up — we have maybe six minutes before they realize it's a decoy.
Nothing. Either they spotted the fake signature immediately, or whoever's on the other end isn't monitoring anymore. We may have already lost our window.

lines_before.dialogue: The world below begins to scream. The lattice, once a placid sheet of crystal, now crackles with jagged fractures of sound—a spiderweb of dissonance spreading beneath the hull. The ship shudders, its standard resonators humming a desperate, straining counterpoint.
lines_before.stage_directions: Outside the viewports, the crystalline surface flickers with sickly purple light. The deck vibrates underfoot.

lines_before.dialogue: I want to make sure we understand what we're hearing. This isn't just turbulence. It's a wound.
lines_before.stage_directions: He braces against a bulkhead, staff held tight. His eyes track the spreading fractures below.

lines_before.dialogue: Full power! Divert everything to the forward array! I don't want people knowing about this route! This is my passage!
lines_before.stage_directions: The Negotiator's face is slick with sweat, his elegant composure shattered. He clutches a control panel, knuckles white.

lines_before.dialogue: Are you insane?! You're tearing the sky apart!
lines_before.stage_directions: She points an accusing finger at the merchant, her other hand gripping her sword hilt.

lines_before.dialogue: The energy readings are corrosive. That's not navigation—it's consumption. He's not parting the lattice; he's eating it.
lines_before.stage_directions: She checks a portable resonator-scanner, its display flashing warning sigils.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit, the assistant—
lines_before.stage_directions: His voice is tense. He's already moving toward the cot where the young man thrashes.

lines_before.dialogue: A cry of raw pain cuts through the mechanical whine. The assistant's prosthetic leg glows with a vicious, hungry light—the same purple as the fractures below. He claws at the crystal limb, trying to rip it free.
lines_before.stage_directions: The prosthetic pulses, emitting a low, corrosive hum. The air around it warps with heat.

lines_after.dialogue: The monk's revelation hangs in the air, heavier than the ship's shuddering. The prosthetic isn't just suffering—it's become a conduit for the lattice's stolen resonance, a lightning rod for parasitic energy.
lines_after.stage_directions: The monk holds the now-detached, still-glowing prosthetic carefully. It casts sharp shadows across his serene, resolved face.

lines_after.dialogue: So we can use the wound to heal the wound. But someone has to carry the knife.
lines_after.stage_directions: He looks from the monk to the terrified assistant, then to the selfish merchant. His own staff hums in sympathy with the lattice's distress.

lines_after.dialogue: The theory is sound. We channel this accumulated dissonance through the ship's main array, tuning it to a neutralizing frequency. It will be volatile. It will require someone to walk the energy to its destination.
lines_after.stage_directions: He looks at the assistant, his voice softening. "You can rest for as long as you want."

lines_after.dialogue: Then let's move! Who's carrying it? The lattice won't wait for us to debate!
lines_after.stage_directions: She's already at the door to the resonator chamber, hand on the latch.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide: who carries the unstable prosthetic to the resonator array? Do they go themselves, send a willing party member (like the Monk who understands the theory), or order the Negotiator to do it as penance (though he lacks the skill)?
line.stage_directions: The merchant watches them, calculating his survival, not their salvation.

choices.description: Override the merchant's console and force a full diagnostic scan before any more power flows, 15 words

line.dialogue: I've locked the array — now talk me through exactly what you were trying to channel.
The console's fried — my override burned out the only failsafe we had left.

choices.description: Rush to the viewport and record the energy patterns with your handheld spectrometer for analysis, 15 words

line.dialogue: These signatures match old war-era weaponized rift technology — this was never meant for navigation.
The readings overloaded my spectrometer — whatever's out there, it doesn't want to be measured.

choices.description: Physically tackle the merchant away from the controls before they can push power any higher, 15 words

line.dialogue: He's down — somebody cuff him before he gets back up and finishes cracking open that sky.
He threw me off like I was nothing — his eyes, they're not his anymore, something's driving him.

lines_before.dialogue: The storm of rogue resonance batters the ship. Outside, the Lattice itself churns—a sea of angry, violet crystal fracturing and reforming in jagged, dissonant patterns.
lines_before.stage_directions: The deck pitches violently. The main resonator array glows with a sickly, unstable light.

lines_before.dialogue: I don't know when the feedback loop will peak. But we can't wait to find out.
lines_before.stage_directions: He braces against the gale, the prosthetic leg in his hands pulsing with malevolent energy.

lines_before.dialogue: It's just cargo! A calculated risk! You don't understand the margins...
lines_before.stage_directions: Cowering near a secured hatch, his face a mask of defeat and calculation.

lines_before.dialogue: Your 'cargo' is trying to tear the sky apart! Move, Pichit!
lines_before.stage_directions: She points frantically toward the shuddering resonator array, hair whipping in the wind.

lines_before.dialogue: The structural harmonics are degrading. We still don't know yet if this will cause a full cascade failure.
lines_before.stage_directions: Checking a crystal readout panel, her expression grim.

lines_before.dialogue: Watch your step! One wrong move and the entire array could overload.
lines_before.stage_directions: Tense, holding a safety line, ready to pull Pichit back.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit staggers forward, each step a battle against the ship's lurching and the leg's violent resonance.
lines_before.stage_directions: He reaches the array. The Listener Monk shouts instructions, barely audible over the howl.

lines_after.dialogue: A pure, clean tone erupts from the array—a single, perfect note that cuts through the chaos. The violent churning of the Lattice outside slows, then stills, the violet scars beginning to fade into a gentle, healing azure.
lines_after.stage_directions: The prosthetic leg in Pichit's hands goes dark and inert, a dead, silent crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: I'm glad to know that... it can still be healed.
lines_after.stage_directions: He looks from the dead prosthetic to the calming Lattice, his own resonant staff pulsing softly in sympathy.

lines_after.dialogue: The wound is deep, but the song returns. The evidence, however, remains. The illegal resonator, its logs... and him.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Monk looks peacefully but sorrowfully from the healed sky to the cowering Merchant, then to Pichit, awaiting leadership.

lines_after.dialogue: So, what's the plan? We have the proof. We have the witness. Do we turn this whole mess in?
lines_after.stage_directions: Already moving to secure the now-quiet illegal resonator, her expression eager for action.

line.dialogue: Wait! Please! You have the schematics from the leg, you have the logs. My silence, my compliance... they're yours. Expose me, expose my backers in the Order, and you'll start a war in the sky no one is ready for.
line.stage_directions: Tense moment. He kneels, not in supplication, but as a businessman making a final, desperate offer.

choices.description: Override the containment field manually, channeling raw resonance through your own body to stabilize the loop.

line.dialogue: You're insane — but the waveform is flattening. Don't you dare let go until I say.
The loop just doubled — your body can't absorb that much harmonic energy!

choices.description: Seize the merchant by the collar and force him to dump the resonant cargo overboard immediately.

line.dialogue: The merchant: "Fine! FINE! Jettisoning it — but you're paying for every crate, you hear me?!
The merchant: "I won't do it! That cargo is worth more than this entire station — I'll die before I let you touch it!

choices.description: Trust Malee's structural readings and reroute all station power to the harmonic dampeners before the cascade peaks.

line.dialogue: Dampeners holding at ninety percent — the sky is stabilizing. We bought ourselves maybe twenty minutes.
Power reroute failed — the dampeners can't sync with the degradation pattern. The collapse is accelerating.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Reading Room hums with the low thrum of the Lattice below, its crystal walls amplifying the ambient frequency into a gentle, persistent vibration. Dust motes dance in beams of filtered sunlight that cut through high, narrow windows.
lines_before.stage_directions: Rows of polished crystal reading stands. An Archivist stands watch by the door, expression unreadable.

lines_before.dialogue: Interesting. The silence in here isn't quiet at all—it's just a different kind of noise. The kind they want us to think is normal.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit runs a hand over a crystal table, feeling its vibration. His eyes scan the room.

lines_before.dialogue: Excuse me. Just... shelving. Don't mind me.
lines_before.stage_directions: A Skycity Resident in simple work clothes pushes a cart of scrolls. He avoids eye contact, hands trembling slightly as he places a scroll on a nearby stand.

lines_before.dialogue: There it is! Pichit, look at this! The *Starward Gull's* log from three cycles ago—it lists a transit frequency that doesn't match the master chart for that sector!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida leans over a spread of documents, her finger jabbing at a line of script. Her voice rises before she catches herself.

lines_before.dialogue: Keep your voice down. That's interesting, but 'interesting' gets you noticed here. Check the supplemental indices.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee glances toward the Archivist, then begins quietly flipping through a heavy ledger of cross-references.

lines_before.dialogue: The Trade Negotiator at the far station is watching us. Not directly, but his reading has slowed. He's listening.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly to block the Negotiator's line of sight to Chanida's findings. His posture is tense.

lines_before.dialogue: The ambient hum seems to deepen for a moment. The Skycity Resident freezes, then hurriedly moves his cart away from the group, nearly knocking over a scroll tube.
lines_before.stage_directions: The light shifts as a cloud passes outside. The Archivist's head turns slightly.

lines_after.dialogue: After minutes of hushed, frantic searching, Malee's hand settles on a solitary, unmarked scroll case tucked behind a ledger on a low shelf. The parchment inside is brittle, its script an older form.
lines_after.stage_directions: The scroll is unfurled with care. The ink describes waveforms and resonant patterns.

lines_after.dialogue: 'The Hum of the Deep Lattice'... not a shifting path, but a stable, pervasive resonance. A foundation tone. This changes everything.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff, leaning against the table, gives off a faint, sympathetic pulse of light. His voice is a whisper of awe.

lines_after.dialogue: Come right in, the Archives are for all citizens, aren't they? Finding something... interesting?
lines_after.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator has approached, his smile polished and empty. He stands just a little too close.

lines_after.dialogue: We need to copy this. Now. Before it gets 'misfiled' again.
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida's hand hovers protectively over the ancient scroll, her eyes darting between Pichit and the approaching Negotiator.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide: report this 'find' to the Archivists (and likely have it suppressed) or secretly copy the scroll and continue investigating on their own.
line.stage_directions: The Skycity Resident watches from a distance, his face pale with fear. The Archivist begins to walk over.

choices.description: Touch the spine of the *Starward Gull's* logbook before Chanida pulls it free.

line.dialogue: The leather's warm—like something inside is still breathing. Chanida, wait. Read it slowly.
Ow—static bit me. Whatever's in this book doesn't want impatient hands.

choices.description: Signal Malee to follow the villager discreetly while he reshelves.

line.dialogue: I'll keep Chanida occupied. You track where he's putting those volumes—he's hiding something.
He glanced over. My gesture was too obvious. Now he's frozen mid-shelf, watching us.

choices.description: Whisper to the villager: "What are you hiding? We're not with the Registry."

line.dialogue: His shoulders drop an inch. 'The Registry burns everything unlogged. But this—this is older than them.
He backs into the shelf, knocking three volumes to the floor. 'Please. I can't lose my position here.

lines_before.dialogue: The disused calibration chamber feels like a forgotten lung—dust motes dancing in slanting crystal-light, dormant tuning forks standing like skeletal trees. The air smells of ozone and old parchment.
lines_before.stage_directions: The party gathers around a stone slab, the copied scroll unfurled. The chamber's walls are lined with resonant copper plates, now tarnished green.

lines_before.dialogue: Keep in mind... every forbidden note was once just a sound. I can't remember ever seeing a frequency chart this stable, yet undocumented.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit traces the scroll's lines with his staff-tip, which glows faintly in response.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah. I thought I might find curious minds here. You don't remember me from the trade hall? No matter. I bring a story—my grandfather's. He was a sailor during the Silencing.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator leans against the doorframe, his smile not quite reaching his eyes. He polishes a small lodestone coin.

lines_before.dialogue: We're busy. And I remember you—always hovering where knowledge flows.
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida steps slightly between the merchant and the scroll, hand resting on her tool-belt.

lines_before.dialogue: Let him talk. Information has a price, but sometimes the warning is free. I can't remember the last time a merchant offered a story without wanting something.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee keeps scanning the chamber's exits, her posture tense.

lines_before.dialogue: Remember, we are outside sanctioned research. We should be careful.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's hand drifts toward the hilt of his weapon, his eyes fixed on the Negotiator.

lines_before.dialogue: The Negotiator's smile tightens. He steps inside, and the chamber seems to grow colder.
lines_before.stage_directions: Dust settles. A faint, sub-audible hum resonates from the copper plates for a moment, then dies.

lines_after.dialogue: After the Negotiator leaves, the chamber feels heavier. The scroll seems to pulse with latent energy. Before the party can speak, a shadow detaches from behind a tuning fork.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Skycity Resident emerges, her hands trembling, eyes wide with fear and hope.

lines_after.dialogue: I remember her. From the lower market. She was watching when we first asked about the Archives.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff dims. He meets her gaze, his expression open but guarded.

lines_after.dialogue: You might change your mind about that scroll. Some doors are locked for a reason. Remember that.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Negotiator's voice echoes from the corridor outside, followed by the click of his boots fading away.

lines_after.dialogue: Let's go. We need to test this. If the Groundless are right, this isn't just a chart—it's a key.
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already rolling the scroll, her movements quick with pent-up energy.

line.dialogue: Please... you must listen. My grandmother whispered of 'The Hum' before the Orders took her. She said it was the Lattice's true voice, a right for all people. They call us Groundless, but we remember what was stolen. The Negotiator serves those who buried it. Whose memory do you trust?
line.stage_directions: Tears streak the dust on her cheeks. She clutches a faded ribbon—a Groundless symbol.

choices.description: Have Chanida focus unauthorized tones on the ancient texts to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. The villagers' courage breaks.

choices.description: Ask Arthit to challenge skycity propaganda, drawing on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
Arthit loses control. The villagers' courage breaks.

choices.description: Have the villager risk using irrigation to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
the villager loses control. The villagers' courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance monitoring station is a hushed, circular chamber deep within the Archives. Crystalline receptors, like inverted chandeliers, tap into the lattice below, their tips glowing with faint, shifting light. The air smells of ozone and old stone.
lines_before.stage_directions: The room is dark except for the pulsing crystals and the glow of monitoring scopes.

lines_before.dialogue: All that history, all that silence… and now we're standing right at the edge. We should give it a try.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit touches one of the cold crystal receptors, feeling its latent vibration.

lines_before.dialogue: My grandfather told stories about a sound beneath the world… a path for the free. I never thought…
lines_before.stage_directions: The Skycity Resident stands by the doorway, eyes wide with reverent hope.

lines_before.dialogue: Look at those scopes! They're waiting for us! Come on, do you wanna try it? Right here, right now?
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points excitedly at the humming equipment, bouncing on her heels.

lines_before.dialogue: The sequence is on the scroll. The input panel is there. It's a simple test. Why wouldn't we try it?
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee checks the scroll's transcription against the station's interface, her expression pragmatic.

lines_before.dialogue: If this is real… if we make it real here… the Orders will know. This isn't just reading. This is rebellion.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit stands guard near the door, tense, his hand resting on his weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: The debate hangs in the charged air. Beyond the chamber's archway, a shadow moves in the hall.
lines_before.stage_directions: A faint silhouette pauses in the corridor, listening.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit steps to the panel. He inputs the sequence. For a moment, nothing. Then, the room's crystals emit a deep, sub-audible vibration—a physical hum that settles in the bones. The monitoring scopes flare to life, painting a clear, unwavering resonance line across their chaotic graphs. Where there should be noise, there is perfect, stable harmony.
lines_after.stage_directions: The crystals glow with a deep, steady amber light. The hum is felt, not heard.

lines_after.dialogue: It's real. A path. No charts, no Singers… just this.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit stares at the scope, his staff pulsing softly in sync with the new resonance.

lines_after.dialogue: A frequency that doesn't decay… that doesn't require a licensed guide. The value of such a thing… is beyond calculation.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator has stepped fully into the doorway, his friendly smile gone, replaced by pure, intense assessment.

lines_after.dialogue: We have to tell everyone! This changes everything!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already moving toward the data console, eager to copy the proof.

line.dialogue: The proof is in your hands. But proof is power. And power attracts wolves. What do you do?
line.stage_directions: The Skycity Resident looks from the glorious scope to Pichit, his wonder now tinged with fear.

choices.description: Press the sequence symbols exactly as they appear on the scroll, left to right, 15 words

line.dialogue: The symbols are aligning — listen, listen, the Hum is rising from below us!
Wrong glyph order — the panel just sealed itself shut and the scopes went dark.

choices.description: Tap each symbol in reverse order, trusting the echo rather than the scroll's ink, 15 words

line.dialogue: The reversed sequence unlocked something deeper — the scopes are picking up a subsonic resonance!
Nothing happened. The panel rejected it — my grandfather's stories never mentioned a failsafe.

choices.description: Place your palm flat on the panel and hum the tone Pichit remembered from childhood, 15 words

line.dialogue: I knew it — the panel responds to the Hum itself, not just the symbols!
The panel stayed cold. Whatever frequency I carried… it's gone quiet after all these years.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance chamber grows quiet, the last harmonic echoes of your experiment fading into the crystalline walls. The proof—etched into resonance crystals and scrawled on parchment—feels heavier than stone. Outside the narrow windows, the floating city drifts, unaware that its foundations might soon tremble.
lines_before.stage_directions: The chamber is dim, lit only by softly pulsing crystal nodes. Dust motes float in shafts of pale light.

lines_before.dialogue: Knowledge that can change everything... probably won't change anything unless someone acts. That's probably right. It just sits here, vibrating in the air between us.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit stares at the resonance data, his fingers resting on the crystal recording slab.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah. I see you've confirmed it. That's probably right—a natural leyline. The Orders probably have known for centuries. They keep such things quiet. Profitable, you see.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator steps from the shadows, a smooth, practiced smile on his face. He holds a small recording crystal that glints faintly.

lines_before.dialogue: You were recording us? That's—how long have you been watching?
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida's hand goes to her weapon, posture defensive.

lines_before.dialogue: Of course he was. Probably had someone tailing us since we started asking the wrong questions. The Archivists probably won't be coming if we're quiet, is that your line?
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee checks the chamber entrance, her expression cynical but alert.

lines_before.dialogue: This is dangerous. That recording... if the Orders find it...
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly between the Negotiator and the data, protective.

lines_before.dialogue: Before the Negotiator can reply, the door whispers open again. A skycity resident—a woman with calloused hands and a determined set to her jaw—enters, her eyes fixed on the crystals holding your discovery.
lines_before.stage_directions: The woman wears simple work clothes. She looks between the party and the merchant, anxiety clear in her posture.

lines_after.dialogue: The two paths lie before you, stark and divergent. The merchant's offer hangs in the air, a transaction that would spread the frequency through shadow markets. The resident's plea vibrates with the raw hope of rebellion. The data itself seems to hum with potential energy.
lines_after.stage_directions: The resonance crystals on the table emit a faint, steady glow. The air feels charged, thick with decision.

lines_after.dialogue: A key that probably won't be too expensive for him to make... but the cost for everyone else? He must have... he must have a dozen plans already. Layers within layers.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit looks from the smooth-faced merchant to the earnest resident, then down at his own hands.

lines_after.dialogue: Time is a commodity, friends. My offer stands. Give me the data. My Singer contacts can have black-market resonators humming within the month. The Groundless get their freedom, I get my percentage, and the sky probably won't even notice the shift.
lines_after.stage_directions: He extends a hand, palm up, businesslike. His eyes are calculating.

lines_after.dialogue: Or we take it to the Movement directly! Cut out the middleman. If this is for the people, it should belong to the people!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida gestures toward the resident, already moving as if to gather the crystals.

line.dialogue: Please. He must have... he must have a plan to profit from our hope. Don't let him turn a key to freedom into just another locked door we can't afford. The knowledge should be free. But... I know what I'm asking. The Orders won't budge an inch if they catch us.
line.stage_directions: The skycity resident looks directly at Pichit, her expression a mixture of desperation and resolve.

choices.description: Slam your fist on the merchant's table and demand he hand over every recording immediately.

line.dialogue: You want them? Fine. But understand—once you see what's on these, there's no going back to who you were." — *the merchant
Temper won't get you answers. It'll just make me forget where I put them." — *the merchant

choices.description: Pull Chanida aside and ask her quietly what she remembers being recorded—anything she said that could be used against you.

line.dialogue: There was... a moment at the river crossing. I said something about your real name. I didn't think anyone was listening. I'm sorry." — *Chanida
I don't—I can't remember everything. It all blends together. What does it matter now? He already has it all." — *Chanida

choices.description: Turn to Malee and ask her directly—she expected this. Who told her to watch for it?

line.dialogue: Nobody had to tell me. I've survived long enough to know that anyone offering you knowledge for free is already selling you out. I just didn't think it'd be him." — *Male
the merchant overreaches. A rival merchant sabotages the plan.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hummed with the suppressed energy of forbidden knowledge. Sound-dampening crystals embedded in the vaulted ceilings absorbed every stray whisper, leaving only the dry rustle of parchment and the soft clink of reading lenses.
lines_before.stage_directions: Rows of crystalline shelves stretch into gloom, each pulsing with a faint, regulated hum.

lines_before.dialogue: They grant us access, then lock the real answers away. The archivist in the next alcove always closes his door loudly when we walk by. You still don't understand? This whole place is designed to make us give up.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit traces a finger over the catalog's etched crystal surface, his brow furrowed.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah, researchers! Stymied by bureaucracy, I see. A common tale. I, however, have a class of contacts who can... expedite things. For a future consideration, of course. No need to struggle when a friend can help.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Trade Negotiator appears in their cell doorway, his smile polished and his robes impeccable.

lines_before.dialogue: Expedite? You mean you can get us into the restricted stacks? The ones with the 'unstable harmonics' records?
lines_before.stage_directions: She leans forward, her eyes alight with impulsive hope.

lines_before.dialogue: Hold on. His mom—or his contacts, whatever—told him about our search already. He's not here by coincidence. He's here to broker our ignorance.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee doesn't look up from her notes, her voice a low, cynical murmur.

lines_before.dialogue: He's too smooth. And he arrived too quickly after we were denied. This feels like a transaction, not aid.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's hand rests near his side, tense and ready, though there is no visible weapon.

lines_before.dialogue: Across the aisle, a robed Listener Monk pauses in his transcription. His eyes, visible in the shadow of his hood, flick from the merchant's smiling face to Pichit's. Almost imperceptibly, he shakes his head once. A warning.
lines_before.stage_directions: The monk's quill stops moving. The air grows heavier.

lines_after.dialogue: The monk's subtle gesture hangs in the air, a silent counterpoint to the merchant's oily promise. The catalog before Pichit glows, the words 'Class 3 Acoustic Anomalies - ACCESS RESTRICTED' burning in cold crystal light.
lines_after.stage_directions: The light from the catalog casts long, sharp shadows across their faces.

lines_after.dialogue: A Class 3 restriction. That's not just bureaucracy; that's a seal. Someone declared this knowledge dangerous. But is the danger in knowing... or in not knowing?
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's own resonant staff, leaning against the desk, gives a single, faint pulse in response to his thoughts.

lines_after.dialogue: Forgive the interruption. I have a class to observe in the lower chantry. I'm going to hurry off right now.
lines_after.stage_directions: The monk stands, gathering his scrolls. As he passes their cell, his sleeve brushes the doorway. A small, folded slip of fibrous paper falls silently to the floor just inside.

lines_after.dialogue: Wait, did he just—? The silent ones are never silent without reason. We have a lead, Pichit. A real one.
lines_after.stage_directions: She points urgently at the fallen paper, already half out of her seat.

line.dialogue: So, my friend? A simple agreement, and the path to your 'Class 3' data opens. Or you can chase phantoms and monkish whispers. The safe way, or the hard way. Your choice.
line.stage_directions: He spreads his hands, the picture of reasonable assistance, but his eyes are calculating.

choices.description: Press the merchant on exactly who told him we were coming and what we're looking for.

line.dialogue: He names a name I recognize from the archive's internal staff—someone who owes us nothing and has every reason to sell us out.
He dodges with a grin and a shrug, and now he knows we're desperate enough to ask, which is worth more to him than any fee.

choices.description: Pay his expedite fee silently and follow him to the restricted section without asking questions.

line.dialogue: The lock clicks, the door swings, and rows of uncatalogued folios stretch before us—whatever he wants, the access is real.
He pockets our money and walks us to a door that opens onto a janitorial closet—'restricted' in the most literal sense.

choices.description: Refuse the merchant outright and instead bribe the night-shift archivist directly with a bottle of rice whiskey.

line.dialogue: The old archivist unwraps the bottle like a gift from a grandson and waves us toward the east wing without a single form signed.
She reports the bribe attempt to the head librarian within

lines_before.dialogue: The private auditory is a bubble of tense silence in the humming Archives. Polished crystal walls reflect the party's faces back at them, fractured and multiplied.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air shimmers with residual harmonic warmth.

lines_before.dialogue: The truth here feels like a living thing. It makes you wonder where you’re going to live—in the comfortable lies of the city, or out there in the raw, unknown truth.
lines_before.stage_directions: He runs a hand over the cool, singing surface of the wall.

lines_before.dialogue: A pleasure doing business. This is all I could… procure. A single fragment from a Class 3 resonance chart. Shows a chaotic zone. Unstable. Dangerous for trade. So, how long are you going for? When you inevitably investigate this… I’d like to arrange an exclusive transport contract. Premium rates, of course.
lines_before.stage_directions: He slides a crystal slate across the table with a practiced, oily smile.

lines_before.dialogue: You’re already planning our expedition? We haven’t even looked at it yet!
lines_before.stage_directions: She leans forward, eyes narrowing at the merchant.

lines_before.dialogue: Typical. Information as a commodity, people as cargo. Let’s just see what our coin bought.
lines_before.stage_directions: She picks up the slate, her fingers tracing the etched frequency lines.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay alert. This feels like a transaction with more than one price.
lines_before.stage_directions: His hand rests near his weapon, eyes scanning the room's exits.

lines_before.dialogue: As Malee activates the slate, a complex tonal sequence unfolds in the air—not the random noise of a hazard, but a precise, repeating cascade of harmonic intervals.
lines_before.stage_directions: The light in the room pulses in time with the pattern.

lines_after.dialogue: The pattern completes, then begins again from the start. Identical. Deliberate.
lines_after.stage_directions: The merchant's smile tightens. The monk, if present, pales.

lines_after.dialogue: It’s not chaos. It’s a message. The pressure of this knowledge… it would make anyone’s blood pressure go up and down.
lines_after.stage_directions: He studies the faces around him, weighing trust.

lines_after.dialogue: That pattern… fragments of the Old Song. Recorded before the Silencing. My order’s deepest secret—we believe the Lattice is *sentient*. The Silencing wasn’t an event. It was a scream. Are you going or not? Are you going to pursue this, knowing the Orders will call it heresy?
lines_after.stage_directions: He whispers, his reverence now edged with raw terror.

lines_after.dialogue: You’re not going to just stand here, are you? This changes everything!
lines_after.stage_directions: She’s already halfway to the door, vibrating with urgency.

line.dialogue: Interesting static, nothing more. Wild interpretations sink ships and ruin profits. So, what’s your read?
line.stage_directions: He folds his arms, his gaze sharp and calculating.

choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing lattice storms to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit hits a wall. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.description: Pichit channels staff meditation toward the ancient texts, hoping to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
A costly mistake by Pichit. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.description: The monk takes the lead, employing recording crystals to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the monk. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The risk doesn't pay off. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The Archive's humming silence feels heavier now, charged with unspoken meaning. Dust motes drift through the crystalline light like forgotten notes.
lines_before.stage_directions: The party stands between the Negotiator's cart and the monk's alcove, tension coiling in the air.

lines_before.dialogue: First you have to understand—we're not asking for certainty. We're asking for what you *believe* you've heard.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit's staff rests against his shoulder, its faint resonance mirroring the tension.

lines_before.dialogue: I don't agree with him. Turning resonance into mysticism is bad for business. It creates uncertainty.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Negotiator's smile is tight, his fingers drumming a profit-calculation rhythm on his ledger.

lines_before.dialogue: You still don't understand? This isn't about business! It's about whatever shattered the world!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida steps forward, her hands gesturing emphatically.

lines_before.dialogue: Or it's a convenient story. Charts are power. Why wouldn't the Orders hide something that challenges their monopoly?
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee's eyes scan the Negotiator's face, looking for a tell.

lines_before.dialogue: Careful. Accusations like that get people silenced in more ways than one.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's hand rests near his toolbelt, his posture defensive.

lines_before.dialogue: The Negotiator's friendly mask slips entirely. His gaze turns cold, pragmatic.
lines_before.stage_directions: He closes his ledger with a definitive snap.

lines_before.dialogue: Don't get so stressed out over monkish fantasies. Push this heresy, and I'll have no choice but to report it. For stability's sake.
lines_before.stage_directions: A clear, quiet threat.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk, who has been shrinking into his robes, suddenly straightens. A dam breaks behind his eyes.
lines_before.stage_directions: Tears of frustration well up, but his voice is clear.

lines_before.dialogue: I don't understand anything! Not fully! But I understand enough to know we stopped listening!
lines_before.stage_directions: His voice cracks with raw emotion. He fumbles beneath his robes.

lines_before.dialogue: We charted its pain and called it a hazard! Here! Listen!
lines_before.stage_directions: From a hidden pocket, he produces a small, worn resonator—a personal meditation device, forbidden by the Orders.

lines_before.dialogue: He places it on a reading stone. With a trembling touch, he activates it. The air doesn't just vibrate—it *weeps*.
lines_before.stage_directions: A deep, shuddering harmonic fills the alcove. It's the 'Class 3 anomaly,' but raw, unfiltered.

lines_before.dialogue: This is no navigational tone. It is a harmonic of profound loss, a resonant memory of cataclysm. A warning, etched in sorrow.
lines_before.stage_directions: The crystal lattices in the walls hum in sympathetic, mournful resonance. The emotional intent is unmistakable.

lines_before.dialogue: Oh. I... I understand.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit's breath catches. The truth settles in his bones, a chilling clarity. The Lattice is alive with grief.

lines_after.dialogue: The resonance fades, leaving a silence that screams. The Negotiator looks pale, his commercial certainty shattered by the song's visceral truth.
lines_after.stage_directions: He backs away slowly, conflict warring on his face.

lines_after.dialogue: They didn't just lose the knowledge. They suppressed it. To maintain control. To avoid panic.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's grip tightens on his staff, which pulses with a soft, troubled light.

lines_after.dialogue: The proof is yours. The fragment of the Old Song. What will you do? The Archives' rules demand silence. The truth demands a voice.
lines_after.stage_directions: The monk gently pushes the small resonator toward Pichit, his expression one of desperate hope.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't just leave it here! We have to get it out! People need to know!
lines_after.stage_directions: She's already looking for exits, her body humming with urgency.

line.dialogue: The dilemma: Pichit must decide: Now that they know, what do they *do*? Do they smuggle the proof out to expose the truth, or do they comply with the Archives' rules and remain silent, fearing another 'Silencing' event?
line.stage_directions: The Negotiator watches from the shadows, his loyalty to the Orders warring with what he just heard.

choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing resonant staff to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit fails. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.description: Direct Chanida to decode the cryptic message using hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida is thwarted. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.description: Direct the monk to decode the cryptic message using recording crystals

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the monk. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
A costly mistake by the monk. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in the main hall of the Archives is thick with the scent of aged vellum and charged crystal. Rows of resonant pillars hum with stored frequencies, their light casting long, accusing shadows across the polished floor. Every whisper echoes.
lines_before.stage_directions: The acoustics of the hall are perfect, amplifying even the softest footfall.

lines_before.dialogue: What's this called? A library? A tomb? It feels like we're standing in the throat of the world, holding a truth it's been forbidden to speak.
lines_before.stage_directions: He grips his staff, its crystal tip flickering in time with his anxious pulse.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah. There you are. A man called you from the Cartographer's Guild. He called you a security risk. What's this called? This is called containment.
lines_before.stage_directions: He steps from between two pillars, smooth and assured. Archive guards in Tonal Order livery fan out behind him, blocking the exits.

lines_before.dialogue: Containment? We're not cargo! We found something! Something important!
lines_before.stage_directions: She steps forward, fists clenched, eyes blazing with defiance.

lines_before.dialogue: Important and inconvenient. He's not here for a debate, Chanida. He's here to close the account.
lines_before.stage_directions: Her hand rests on her tool belt, eyes scanning the guards for weaknesses.

lines_before.dialogue: Easy now. Keep it together. Don't throw away our position.
lines_before.stage_directions: He positions himself slightly in front of Pichit, a protective stance, muscles coiled.

lines_before.dialogue: The Monk steps from the shadow of a data spire. In his hands, the forbidden resonator glows with a soft, mournful light.
lines_before.stage_directions: The air seems to still, the ambient hum of the Archives dropping to a whisper.

lines_after.dialogue: The tone fades, leaving a ringing, profound silence in its wake. The guards hesitate, their certainty fractured. The Negotiator's smile is gone, replaced by cold, institutional fury.
lines_after.stage_directions: The truth hangs in the air, visible in the wide eyes of the guards, in the Monk's serene defiance.

lines_after.dialogue: Someone called that tone heresy. Someone called it a lie. But we all heard it. You should keep that truth. Don't throw it away.
lines_after.stage_directions: His staff's pulse steadies into a firm, resonant glow. The moment of discovery has passed. The moment of choice is now.

lines_after.dialogue: The song has been sung. My part is done. The choice, and the consequence, are yours.
lines_after.stage_directions: He holds the resonator out toward Pichit, then lets his hands fall to his sides, ready for the guards.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit! We can't just leave him! What do they call that?
lines_after.stage_directions: She's already shifting her weight, ready to sprint, to fight, to do something.

line.dialogue: Surrender the contraband. Disavow this... noise. Walk away with your permits intact. Or become another footnote in the Archives' section on 'corrected heresies.' What do they call this? Your final invoice.
line.stage_directions: He gestures sharply. The guards advance, staves crackling with containment frequencies.

choices.description: Chanida volunteers to confront hidden knowledge, leveraging unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.description: Arthit attempts to confront hidden knowledge, relying on ship navigation

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit loses control. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.description: Ask the merchant to decode the cryptic message, drawing on negotiation

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Things don't go as planned. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard is a symphony of industrial decay—a thousand-ton orchestra of groaning metal, shrieking wind through twisted hulls, and the constant percussive clang of scavengers at work. The air tastes of rust and ozone.
lines_before.stage_directions: Wide shot of the chaotic graveyard of resonance ships, with the crystalline Lattice shimmering far below.

lines_before.dialogue: It's like a menu of destruction. Can I even read this? I studied the Lattice's frequencies by myself, but this noise... it's all wrong.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit presses a hand to his ear, his expression strained as he scans the metallic chaos.

lines_before.dialogue: This is a waste of time. Every frequency here is dead. We're looking for a whisper in a thunderstorm.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee taps her resonance meter, which flickers erratically.

lines_before.dialogue: Hey! You there! We're looking for strange frequencies! Anything that doesn't belong!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida waves energetically at a grizzled scavenger working on a resonator array.

lines_before.dialogue: Strange frequencies? Everything here is strange. Or dead. Mostly dead. Try the Silent Barge if you want strange—ship over yonder that don't clang. Don't hum. Don't nothing. Bad luck.
lines_before.stage_directions: The scavenger spits, doesn't look up from his work, but jerks a thumb toward a distant, listing hull.

lines_before.dialogue: Bad luck how? What happened there?
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit's hand drifts toward his weapon, eyes scanning the gantries above.

lines_before.dialogue: It's like the air itself is holding its breath. Can I see the menu of this place? Not sound... but absence.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit's staff glows faintly as he attunes to the unnatural quiet.

lines_before.stage_directions: The interior is spotless, dust-free, and utterly vacant. It feels wrong.

lines_before.dialogue: Well, well. Tourists picking through the dead. Looking for a souvenir? Or just lost?

lines_after.dialogue: We're being watched. This silence isn't empty. It's waiting.

lines_after.dialogue: Told you. Bad luck follows that ship. Now it's following you.

lines_after.dialogue: So? We came here for answers. That log has to mean something! Let's check the resonator chamber!

lines_before.dialogue: The interior of the Silent Barge was a tomb of unnatural quiet. Dust motes hung suspended in the still air, undisturbed by any vibration. The crew quarters were preserved in eerie perfection—a half-eaten meal on a table, a jacket draped over a chair, a logbook open to an unfinished entry. It was as if life had simply ceased.
lines_before.stage_directions: The light from their handheld resonators casts long, sharp shadows across the frozen scene.

lines_before.dialogue: Why couldn’t they finish? Why can’t you hear a single echo in this place? It’s like the sound itself died here.
lines_before.stage_directions: He touches the dusty logbook, his fingers tracing the last written word.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay close. This silence isn’t natural. It’s a cage.
lines_before.stage_directions: He keeps his hand near his weapon, eyes scanning the dark corners.

lines_before.dialogue: I can’t keep up with what you’re saying, Arthit. It’s too quiet! My ears are straining for anything!
lines_before.stage_directions: She shakes her head, frustrated by the acoustic void.

lines_before.dialogue: No struggle. No panic. They just... stopped. That’s worse than a fight.
lines_before.stage_directions: She examines the meal, noting the utensils laid neatly aside.

lines_before.dialogue: Arthit’s resonator, tuned to detect structural flaws, pinged softly against a wall in the ship’s core chamber. The panel was seamless, but the resonance pattern was wrong. He pressed, and a section of crystal lattice slid aside with a dry, grating whisper—the only sound they’d heard since entering.
lines_before.stage_directions: Behind the panel, a crude array of blackened crystals pulsed with a deep, sub-audible hum.

lines_before.dialogue: This is it. The source. A forbidden frequency. This resonator is tuned to cancel all sound, to create a dead zone. Illegal. Unstable.
lines_before.stage_directions: He points at the array, his face grim.

lines_before.dialogue: Well, aren’t you the clever little rats? Trespassing on my salvage. I lost my phone, you know. Had to come find it personally.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Sky Pirate steps into the chamber doorway, blocking the only exit. He’s armed, and his smile is predatory.

lines_after.dialogue: The Sky Pirate’s presence filled the silent room with a new, human tension. His eyes locked on the humming crystal array.
lines_after.stage_directions: He shifts his weight, ready to move.

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for this little secret. Or they’d destroy it to keep it quiet. So, can you catch what I’m saying? You’re standing on my profit. Now, what did you find?
lines_after.stage_directions: He raises his resonator blade, its edge singing a faint, threatening note.

lines_after.dialogue: May I see your driver’s license? This isn’t your ship.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit steps forward, his staff held low but ready. His voice is calm, but his mind races.

lines_after.dialogue: We’re not thieves! We’re investigating!
lines_after.stage_directions: She gestures angrily at the Sky Pirate.

lines_after.dialogue: He doesn’t care. He sees a prize. And rivals.
lines_after.stage_directions: She positions herself near Arthit, watching the pirate’s hands.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate’s resonator blade hums higher, a clear threat. Pichit must decide: Do they fight the Sky Pirate now, try to bluff or negotiate, or attempt to flee the ship with their discovery?
line.stage_directions: The illegal crystal array continues its silent, dangerous pulse behind them.

lines_before.dialogue: The Scavenger's mobile platform creaks like a dying beast as it crawls across the lattice surface, its makeshift workshop a chaotic nest of salvaged parts and flickering monitors. The air smells of ozone and desperation.
lines_before.stage_directions: The platform is a converted cargo sled, jury-rigged with solar panels and antennae.

lines_before.dialogue: What do they call this? This feeling of being watched by the thing you're trying to understand? Anyone’s okay to answer.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit watches the Scavenger nervously plug their data crystal into a console.

lines_before.dialogue: They call it wisdom. Keep it. You should keep that feeling. It might keep you alive.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Scavenger's hands tremble as he adjusts the scanner's gain.

lines_before.dialogue: Well? Is it valuable or not? The price is the same for our time either way!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida leans over the console, impatient.

lines_before.dialogue: The staff at the Tonal Archive were very unfriendly. But this... this makes them look welcoming.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee points at the spiking waveform on the screen, her voice flat.

lines_before.dialogue: What are we looking at?
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit places a protective hand on his weapon, eyes scanning the scrapyard horizon.

lines_before.dialogue: The Scavenger freezes. The waveform on the screen isn't just silent—it's actively inverting the ambient resonance of the lattice around it.
lines_before.stage_directions: The console's light paints his face a sickly green.

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate's ship descends with a predatory hum, casting a long shadow over the mobile platform. The air grows colder.
lines_after.stage_directions: The shadow of the pirate skiff crawls across the lattice.

lines_after.dialogue: The price is the same for every choice. Ruin or profit, disaster or survival. They both have the same price.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's hand goes to the resonance staff at his belt; it thrums with a low, anxious pulse.

lines_after.dialogue: It's not a silent frequency. It's a cancellation wave. A void-maker. If that resonator pulses wrong—if it decays—it could eat the lattice under a whole city. Pull it right out of the sky.
lines_after.stage_directions: He backs away from the console as if it's poisoned.

lines_after.dialogue: So we're standing next to a world-breaker? We need to move!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida is already gathering her gear, eyes locked on the approaching skiff.

line.dialogue: Smart people see opportunity. I've got a buyer. The price for silence is the same as the price for noise. Split it with me, and we all walk away rich. Or... you can try to play hero with a bomb.
line.stage_directions: The Sky Pirate leans against his skiff's ramp, a calculated smirk on his face.

choices.description: Examine the Tonal Archive's rejected records for cancellation patterns, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — every flagged entry traces back to the same censor node. We found the wound.
Nothing but redacted slashes and static. Whoever scrubbed this was thorough, I'll give them that.

choices.description: Tail the Archive staff member who kept watching you from the mezzanine, 15 words

line.dialogue: She leads me to a back room full of unsanctioned recordings. She's been waiting for someone to ask.
I turn the corner and she's gone — like the hallway swallowed her. That feeling of being watched? It's doubled now.

line.dialogue: He hands me a shard still warm with deleted voices. The Archive staff were unfriendly because they knew what they were destroying.
He laughs and says the cancelled material was pulped before it hit

lines_before.dialogue: The Silent Barge no longer feels silent. The air around its resonator shimmers like heat haze over the Lattice, and the sub-audible hum has become a vibration that travels up through your boots, into your bones.
lines_before.stage_directions: The derelict ship groans. Crystalline dust falls from its hull.

lines_before.dialogue: I don't feel the same as before. Standing here now... I have an uneasy feeling. Like we're standing at the edge of a hole we can't see.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit grips his staff, its crystal tip flickering in time with the ship's pulse.

lines_before.dialogue: There she is, lads! The payday! My buyer's already inbound. You just stand aside and let the professionals handle the transaction.
lines_before.stage_directions: The Sky Pirate grins, hand resting on his weapon. His crew fans out.

lines_before.dialogue: Professionals? You're scavengers with better weapons! This whole place is making my skin crawl!
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida shifts her weight, eyes darting between the pirates and the shimmering ship.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance spike is accelerating. Whatever we're doing, we need to do it now. That crystal won't hold forever.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee checks a handheld frequency scanner, its readings erratic.

lines_before.dialogue: Stay close. I don't like how the air is... thickening. It's not just sound anymore.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself between the party and the ship's main resonator, shield raised slightly.

lines_before.dialogue: As you move to enact your plan, the ghostly echo manifests. Not a memory, but a haunting. Whispers overlap into a chorus of panic: 'The lattice is fracturing!' 'A hole in the world!' 'It's eating the sky!' The resonance peaks, and for a moment, you don't just hear the lost crew—you feel their terror.
lines_before.stage_directions: Flickering afterimages of running figures appear and vanish in the shimmering air.

lines_after.dialogue: The crisis resolves. Whether through explosion, sale, or silencing, the immediate threat ends. The unnatural vibration fades, leaving only the normal, mournful winds of the scrapyard. The Sky Pirate departs with a triumphant curse. The Surface Scavenger watches from a distance, her expression grimly satisfied.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Silent Barge is now just another derelict, or a smoldering ruin, or a hollow prize.

lines_after.dialogue: Some echoes, once heard, cannot be unheard. That final scream... it made me feel better about our choice, but worse about the world that forced us to make it.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit looks at his hands. The faint resonance in his staff has changed its pitch, subtly.

lines_after.dialogue: It's done. The secret's buried, or sold, or blown to shards. But remember—out here, a person who knows too much doesn't have many friends. You've made your bed in the silence. Now you have to lie in it.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Scavenger turns and begins climbing down a latticework of cables, back to her mobile platform.

lines_after.dialogue: Let's just go. This whole place gives me the creeps. Next time we take a job, can it involve something that doesn't whisper?
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida kicks a piece of slag, already walking toward your own vessel.

line.dialogue: No new decision. The act resolves the episode's central conflict. The final state is the consequence of Pichit's Act 3 choice.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow is a jagged wound in the cliffside, the air inside thick with a crystalline hum that seems to vibrate in your teeth. Stalactites of resonant quartz weep slow tears of condensed sound.
lines_before.stage_directions: The cave mouth glows with faint, internal light from the Lattice-infused rock.

lines_before.dialogue: Why weren't you careful? The reports said this place remembers sound. Every step could be recorded. We need to move with purpose, not just curiosity.
lines_before.stage_directions: Pichit tests the ground with his staff, watching the crystal formations vibrate.

lines_before.dialogue: Hands where I can see 'em! This ain't a public gallery. You Tonal Order lackeys sent to clean up another mess? What's your plan?
lines_before.stage_directions: The sky pirate steps from behind a quartz column, hand resting on the hilt of a resonator-blade. His clothes are patched leather and scavenged metal.

lines_before.dialogue: I'm so excited! Look at that! It's like the whole cave is singing! Aren't you overthinking this? He's just one guy.
lines_before.stage_directions: Chanida points past the pirate, her eyes wide at the shimmering cavern beyond.

lines_before.dialogue: One guy with a weapon, standing between us and a phantom frequency strong enough to warp the local lattice. Pragmatism isn't overthinking. It's survival.
lines_before.stage_directions: Malee's eyes scan the pirate's equipment, noting the crude frequency recorder on his belt.

lines_before.dialogue: Easy now. We're all explorers here. But you need to be careful. That echo... it feels wrong. Like a wound that hasn't healed.
lines_before.stage_directions: Arthit positions himself slightly ahead of the group, his shield-arm tense.

lines_before.dialogue: Beyond the pirate, the central cavern opens. The ruins of ancient machinery—a pre-Silencing observatory—lie scattered. And at its heart, suspended in the air, a ghost ship shimmers.
lines_before.stage_directions: The outline of a Resonance Ship, the 'Sun-Chaser,' flickers, repeating a silent, looping fragment of its final descent.

lines_after.dialogue: The tension in the cavern crystallizes. The pirate's blade hums. The merchant's smile is fixed. The ghost ship turns in its endless, silent loop.
lines_after.stage_directions: The Echo pulses, casting long, wavering shadows.

lines_after.dialogue: A memory in crystal. A soul in frequency. It can't be fixed... but it can be understood. Or exploited.
lines_after.stage_directions: Pichit's staff pulses in time with the Echo, a soft blue against the ghost-ship's gold.

lines_after.dialogue: Please, let's not be hasty. This is a historical find! A tragedy preserved. My employer would pay handsomely for its... study. Surely we can come to an arrangement?
lines_after.stage_directions: The merchant's eyes dart to his own, more sophisticated recording apparatus, half-hidden by his cloak.

lines_after.dialogue: What are we waiting for? It's right there! We have to know what it's saying!
lines_after.stage_directions: Chanida takes an eager step forward, only to be blocked by Arthit's outstretched arm.

line.dialogue: Enough chatter! You gonna stand with this liar, try to play us both for fools, or clear out and let the real scavengers work? Choose!
line.stage_directions: The pirate's resonator-blade flares to life with a sharp, discordant whine.
