The Tonal Orders will hear of this. The world will hear of this. The lattice will sing a new song, however painful its first notes.
My leg... it's quiet. For the first time since the accident, it's just a leg. The silence here... it's different now. It's peaceful.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums, a deep, resonant tone that vibrates in your bones. Below, the crystalline Lattice shimmers like a frozen sea.
Whoa. This hum... it's like it's scrubbing my brain clean. I feel weirdly calm.
Don't get used to it. That 'calm' is a byproduct of a harmonic field strong enough to shatter lesser crystals. It's also broadcasting our presence to anyone with ears.
The Trade Negotiator's signal led us here. We should proceed with caution. The Tonal Orders patrol these anchors.
Yet, within this enforced stillness, there is a space for clarity. What do you think about the purpose of such a place? It’s something to think about.
Ah, my friends! You made excellent time. The Spire's tone is good for business—keeps emotions, and prices, stable.
I have the navigation charts you requested. A rare find, detailing a path through a dissonant zone the Orders avoid.
Great! Let's see them!

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, a small matter of payment first. The information... carries a certain risk for me.
I knew right away this was a shakedown. Your 'friendly' smile is as transparent as the Lattice.
A simple trade! Your ship's resonator logs for my charts. Knowledge for knowledge.
Our logs could reveal our own hidden frequencies. This is a significant concession.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator waits, hand outstretched. How do you respond?

choices.text: Agree to the trade. The charts are our immediate priority.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the humming bulkhead and let the resonance map your neural patterns.

line.dialogue: Arthit* — "The signal just pulsed back. It's not interference — something in the Anchor is *answering* you.
Malee* — "Your hand's gone numb to the wrist. That's not calm, that's your nerves shutting down. Pull back. Now.

choices.text: Refuse, but try to bluff him into giving up the charts anyway.
choices.description: Override the corridor lighting to strobe at the hum's frequency, breaking the enforced stillness.

line.dialogue: Pichit* — "There — behind the bulkhead plating. The strobe caught a seam that the stillness was hiding. A door.
Chanida* — "The strobe and the hum collided and now I can hear *both* backwards. My teeth won't stop vibrating. Turn it off, turn it OFF.

choices.text: Refuse outright and demand he honor the original agreement.
choices.description: Whisper the Trade Negotiator's authentication cipher into the wall and wait for a reply.

line.dialogue: Arthit* — "The hum dropped half a tone. That's a handshake protocol. Whoever built this was expecting us — or someone like us.
Malee* — "You just fed a living system a decryption key. The hum is *deeper* now. It's learning. What did you give it

lines_before.dialogue: Before a deal is struck, a dissonant shriek cuts through the Spire's hum. A ragged resonance ship, bristling with jury-rigged crystal shards, banks hard and lands on a lower platform.
Well, well! A merchant and some Order lackeys having a cozy chat! Don't mind if I help myself.
Sky pirates! The Groundless filth! They've been harassing my routes!
Groundless? You mean the movement that wants to settle the Lattice surface?
We want what's been denied! Starting with those charts! You lot, hand 'em over. I made this ship by myself from scrap, and I'll crack your hull the same way.
Charming. A visionary with a rustbucket and a bad attitude.
They have the high ground on that platform. A direct assault is ill-advised.
Their resonance is jagged, untrained. But powerful. I'll get it. I will open a dialogue. They are, perhaps, as lost as we are.

lines_after.dialogue: Dialogue? The only frequency we understand is 'surrender'! But... you don't smell like Order toadies.
Maybe you're just another bunch the merchants are trying to fleece. Heh. I have bad eyesight for pretty words, but I see a mark a mile off.
Don't listen to this rabble! They seek to unravel society itself!
The pirate leader gestures. Two crewmates drop down, blocking the exit. The merchant cowers behind a crystal conduit.

line.dialogue: The pirate demands the charts. The merchant is useless. The exit is blocked. What's your move?

choices.text: Fight! Charge the pirates on the lower platform.
choices.description: Draw your blade and stand between the bandit and the merchant's charts, 12 words

line.dialogue: Touch these charts and you'll pull back a stump — back off, skyrat.
I meant to block him, not trip over my own scabbard — move!

choices.text: Reason. Appeal to the pirate's supposed idealism about the Groundless cause.
choices.description: Ask the bandit what the Groundless actually need the charts for, 13 words

line.dialogue: You want navigation charts — where exactly are you trying to go that's been denied?
I had a whole speech prepared but he's already lunging — so much for diplomacy.

choices.text: Subterfuge. Fake handing over the charts, then use the Spire's overwhelming hum to disorient them.
choices.description: Signal the merchant to hand over decoy papers while you keep the bandit talking, 14 words

line.dialogue: Merchant — you heard the man. Hand over whatever you've got. *Now.* Trust me.
I winked too obviously. The bandit saw, the merchant panicked, and now everyone's staring at me.

lines_before.dialogue: The party ascends the winding stairs of the Anchor Spire. The harmonic vibration emanating from the crystal anchor below grows stronger, a steady, profound tone that resonates in their bones and makes their hearts feel heavy yet clear.
This hum... it's like it's scrubbing my brain. I feel calm, but also... exposed. Is stealth even possible here?
It's not necessary to attempt stealth. The Spire's tone broadcasts our presence to anyone with a resonator. We proceed openly.
Great. So the pirate and the merchant up there know we're coming. Do you need to use a frontal assault? Is it necessary to use one?
Perhaps not. The tone clarifies intention. Let our purpose be as clear as the vibration.

They reach the Spire's summit—a broad platform where the massive resonance anchor plunges into the Lattice below. The Trade Negotiator and the Sky Pirate are in a heated standoff, their argument amplified by the ambient hum.
Your 'hidden frequency' is worthless! The Tonal Orders have charted everything around the Spire. It's not necessary to risk my cargo on your pirate whims.
Worthless? My ship wouldn't budge an inch in the standard channels last week! These charts are stale. The Lattice shifts!

lines_after.dialogue: The party's arrival interrupts the argument. The steady tone of the Spire makes deception impossible; every word carries its full emotional weight.
Ah, the Listeners. Or... are you Singers? In this place, a lie would crack like a bad crystal. So, speak truth. What do you want?
We seek knowledge of the Groundless. Their belief that the Silencing was not a catastrophe, but a necessary... un-anchoring.
Groundless? Fools who think we should all sink into the crystal! But... their ideas about natural frequencies... ain't wrong. The Orders' charts are a cage.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator and the Pirate both possess fragments of the truth. The Spire's tone forces honesty. Who will you press for the crucial information about the Groundless Movement's location?

choices.text: Appeal to the Pirate's rebellion. (Chanida: 'Your ship was stuck! You know the charts are wrong! Help us find the real truth!')
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing engineering to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Malee misreads the situation. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: Negotiate with the Merchant's logic. (Arthit: 'The Groundless pose a market risk. Sharing their location mitigates that risk for your trade routes.')
choices.description: Arthit channels captain experience toward the crystal depth, hoping to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The villagers rise with their agricultural tools.
Arthit is thwarted. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.text: Challenge both with the Spire's own truth. (Pichit: 'This anchor hums a single, unwavering note. Your conflict is a dissonance. Harmonize, and tell us.')
choices.description: The pirate uses secret frequencies to record the spectral signature near the calm tones

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
the pirate fails. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision made, the information secured. The party now stands at the very edge of the platform, beside the immense anchor crystal. The hum is overwhelming, stripping away all pretense. Below, the Lattice glimmers, its surface rippling with the Spire's foundational tone.
So. The Groundless camp is on a drifting shard, uncharted, singing its own frequency. That's all, isn't it? That's the big revelation?
It's huge! It means we can find them! It means the Tonal Orders don't control everything!
It also means we are standing right in front of a choice. Do we report this to the Orders? Or do we attempt to reach the shard ourselves, using... unapproved methods?
The Spire asks us to be anchored. But the Groundless believe in being free. Which truth resonates?
Suddenly, the Sky Pirate steps forward, resonator in hand. The Trade Negotiator watches, calculating.
I got the frequency. The shard's song. I can punch a hole in the Lattice from here, right now. A temporary path. But it's risky. The Spire's tone might fight it.
He's still single, isn't he? A lone operator. I have a resonance ship below. Safer, slower, charted. I could take you... for a significant fee.

lines_after.dialogue: Two paths to the Groundless shard stand before them. The Pirate's wild, immediate, dangerous frequency. The Merchant's controlled, costly, sanctioned route. The Anchor Spire's unwavering hum judges the moment.
So we either leap into the unknown with a pirate, or buy a ticket with a snake. Lovely options we've anchored ourselves into.
This is not merely a choice of travel. It is a choice of belief. Do we anchor to the old system, or resonate with the new?
The crystal anchor pulses. The tone deepens. The Lattice below seems to wait.

line.dialogue: The climax. The path to the Groundless—and to potentially颠覆 the world's understanding of the Silencing—is here. How will you depart the Anchor Spire?

choices.text: Take the Merchant's ship. (Arthit: 'Calculated risk. We remain within the system's sight, able to negotiate later.')
choices.description: Transmit the Spire's anchoring signal toward the drifting shard, binding it to charted coordinates.

line.dialogue: The signal locked — the shard is stabilizing, and the Groundless camp just became stationary. We've found them, but we've also made a choice they didn't ask for.
The signal scattered into noise — the shard drifts faster now, and I think we just announced exactly where we stand to people who don't want to be found.

choices.text: Use the Pirate's frequency. (Chanida: 'Break the charts! Let's resonate with the shard's true song now!')
choices.description: Disable your tracking beacon and let the shard drift uncharted into the deep frequency.

line.dialogue: Beacon's dark. We're Groundless now — no anchor, no map, just the drift. I never thought freedom would feel this much like falling.
The beacon won't die — it's hardcoded into the Spire's network. They already see us. They already know we hesitated.

choices.text: Sing your own path. (Pichit: 'We are standing in front of the source. Let us listen, then sing a new frequency together.')
choices.description: Split the crew — half transmit the anchor signal, half go silent and approach the camp on foot.

line.dialogue: Two signals, two paths — Arthit holds the anchor while Pichit and I walk into the unknown. If this goes wrong, at least someone
Defeat. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow is cool and still, thick with the scent of wet stone and ancient dust. The walls, striated with veins of dormant crystal, catch the light from your lanterns and fracture it into a thousand shimmering points.
Whoa... look at the size of this place! It goes on forever. (I) wanna ask you something… do you think anyone’s been down here since The Silencing?
Unlikely. The entrance was perfectly concealed by rockfall. We only found it because of that odd echo pattern Malee documented.
Don't get too excited. Big, empty caves usually mean something big and *hungry* cleared out the previous tenants. (It)’s really a great place to live! If you're a cave worm.
Listen. Not just to us. To the space between our words. The resonance here... it's layered. Like pages in a book.
As Pichit speaks, his voice ripples through the cavern, returning a moment later, subtly altered—a harmonic, mournful note woven into the echo.
See? I told you it was strange. The whole island hums sometimes. My neighbor swears his teacups rattle. ‘It’s the latest fashion,’ he says, in haunted houses.
Well, fashion or not, let's see what's making the noise!

lines_after.dialogue: The party presses deeper, the tunnel opening into a vast, cylindrical chamber. In the center, a jagged spire of black stone rises from the floor, covered in intricate, spiraling glyphs.
Now *that* is not natural. Someone 'wrote' here. A lot.
The glyphs... they're not Tonal Order notation. This is older. Pre-Silencing.
It's a record. A story pressed into the stone by sound. Can you feel it? A low thrum, just below hearing.

line.dialogue: The ancient spire dominates the chamber. How should the party investigate?

choices.line: Have Chanida climb the spire for a better look.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with staff meditation to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit fails. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Instruct Arthit to meticulously document the glyphs.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and expose surface colonization truth

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
Arthit is thwarted. The villagers' courage breaks.

choices.line: Ask the Skycity Resident if they've heard local legends about this place.
choices.description: Have the villager focus local knowledge on the cave echoes to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
the villager is thwarted. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_before.dialogue: As Arthit carefully sketches the glyphs, a deep, resonant *tone* emanates from the spire itself. The crystals in the walls flare with sympathetic light.
It's a resonance lock! My tracing activated it. I... I wasn't careful.
Why aren’t you careful? We're poking a pre-Silencing artifact with a stick! What’s your plan if it starts singing us apart?
Too late for caution. Listen. The tone... it's breaking apart. Splintering into different pitches. It's unstable.
From a side passage, a figure emerges, clad in patched Lattice-leather. A Surface Scavenger levels a crude resonator-caster at the group.
Step back from the Spire! You city-folk with your clumsy noise... you'll bring the whole ceiling down. It’s irrepairable. You've already cracked the song.
We didn't mean to! We're just exploring!
This ain't for exploring. This is a grave. And a warning. The Listeners knew. The Lattice down here... it's sick. The song is wrong.

lines_after.dialogue: A warning? What do you mean? The subharmonic... it sounds like pain.
The Silencing wasn't the end. It was a symptom. This place... it records the Lattice's distress call. A call that's been going on for centuries. And it's getting louder.
Fantastic. So we're not in an ancient ruin. We're inside a screaming wound in the world.
The unstable tone from the spire wavers, and a section of the far wall shimmers, revealing a hidden archway filled with a faint, pulsating light. The Scavenger hisses in alarm.

line.dialogue: The activated spire has revealed a hidden passage, but its resonance is fracturing dangerously. What do you do?

choices.line: Retreat immediately, following the Scavenger's advice.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the Spire's surface and match your breathing to the breaking tone.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The resonance is stabilizing — I can feel the old pattern, it wants to harmonize, just hold still!
Arthit — "No, no, you're forcing it — the tone is splintering in two directions and I can't read either one!

choices.line: Attempt to stabilize the resonance with a counter-tone before proceeding.
choices.description: Ignore the scavenger and dump your canteen over the tracing instrument to kill the signal.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Quick thinking — the water's shorted the tracer, the lock's gone dormant before it cascaded.
Malee — "You've corroded the contacts — now we have a live lock AND no working tracer, brilliant.

choices.line: Rush through the new archway before it collapses.
choices.description: Raise both hands toward the scavenger and ask what song the Spire sang before the Silencing.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "He's loosening — the old songs are sacred to his people, and you showed respect instead of greed.
Pichit — "He's spitting on the ground — says outsiders always want something, never want to listen first.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends deeper into The Hollow, following the strange echo patterns. The air grows colder, and the crystal formations pulse with a faint, rhythmic light.
These vibrations... they're not random. It's a pattern. A slow, deep pulse. Like a heartbeat.
A geological heartbeat? That's impossible. What's your plan, Pichit? This feels like we're walking into the source of the disturbance.
The Listeners spoke of foundational tones. If this is one... we need to understand its message. Why weren't you careful, Arthit? You're stepping on unstable crystal.
Look! Up ahead! It's... it's a chamber. And there's light coming from it. A different kind of light!
The tunnel opens into a vast, spherical cavern. At its center, suspended in mid-air, is a massive, flawless crystal core. It throbs with the same slow pulse, emitting a low, resonant hum.
By the Silencing... I've seen surface nodes, but nothing like this. It's the heart. The island's heart.
It's beautiful... but it sounds sick. The hum is ragged. It can't be fixed, can it?

lines_after.dialogue: This isn't just a crystal. It's a memory. A recording of the world before. It still works, after all this time.
A recording of what? The Silencing? If we trigger it... I'm really hurting just thinking about the potential fallout.
The core's surface shimmers. Faint images flicker within—skyscrapers, not of crystal, but of metal and glass. A world without the Lattice.
It works really well as a historical archive. Too well. This is proof the Tonal Orders have been hiding.

line.dialogue: The core's pulse is growing unstable. The images are becoming chaotic, painful. The subplot_echo vibrates urgently: this is the Lattice's warning. How do we interact with the heart?

choices.text: Attempt to calm the resonance with a counter-tone. (Use Chanida's Singer intuition to find a stabilizing frequency.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the tunnel wall and match your breathing to the vibration's rhythm.

line.dialogue: The pulse slows when I sync with it—like it's *acknowledging* me. The chamber wants us to follow its tempo.
Your heartbeat's fighting the rhythm, Malee. The wall just spat you back like a wrong password.

choices.text: Download the data stream. (Use Arthit's technical skills to record the core's memories before it destabilizes.)
choices.description: Signal everyone to extinguish their lights and crawl the final twenty meters in complete darkness.

line.dialogue: The Listeners were right—blind, I can feel the tone in my *teeth*. It's guiding us. Don't open your eyes.
I can't see anything and I just put my hand in something *wet* that isn't water. Turn the lights back on!

choices.text: Commune directly. (Pichit will attempt a deep Listener meditation to understand the core's pain.)
choices.description: Hum the foundational tone Pichit

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
Things don't go as planned. Survival skills aren't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber trembles. The core's light fractures, and the hum rises to a deafening shriek. From the crystal, a final, overwhelming memory is unleashed.
The vision is absolute. Not an image, but a sensation—a chord of such catastrophic dissonance it shattered continents. The birth-cry of the Lattice. The Silencing itself.
It wasn't a natural disaster... it was a song. A song gone wrong. A resonance cascade.
I can feel it in my bones! The same wrongness is building here! This core is trying to repeat the pattern!
The Tonal Orders. Their navigation charts... they're not just maps. They're suppressors. They keep the Lattice dormant. It's nice and peaceful up there because they're drugging the world.
And this island's heart is waking up. If it fully resonates... it could trigger another local Silencing. Bring this whole floating city down.
Someone is waiting for you. Up there. My family. Everyone's family. You brought this knowledge. Now what do you do with it?
Can you promise me? Promise you can stop it? Make it peaceful again?

lines_after.dialogue: The core begins to crack. Harmonic fractures spiderweb across its surface. The chamber groans. The choice is now.
We didn't just bring knowledge. We brought a responsibility. The Listeners' warning was real. The Lattice is in pain, and it's crying out.
The subplot_echo resolves not with an answer, but with a final, desperate question hanging in the screaming air.

line.dialogue: The core will detonate, taking the island with it. You must choose how to resolve the resonant cascade. Each path saves the island but changes everything.

choices.text: Suppress the Heart. (Use Tonal Order principles to forcibly dampen the core, saving the city but perpetuating the lie. The Lattice's warning is silenced.)
choices.description: Sing the counter-frequency into the cave mouth before the resonance peaks

line.dialogue: I matched the island's heartbeat and bent it — the ground is settling under my feet!
My voice cracked against that wall of sound — the vibration threw me flat on my back.

choices.text: Redirect the Energy. (Channel the destructive resonance safely into the Lattice below, a temporary fix. The warning is acknowledged, but the root cause remains.)
choices.description: Rewrite the Tonal Orders' navigation chart with charcoal to redirect the frequency

line.dialogue: I scratched over their harmonic routes — the signal is scattering into dead water now!
The charcoal smeared when my hands shook — I've drawn a path straight into the island's throat.

choices.text: Heal the Song. (Chanida and Pichit must sing the corrupted chord back into harmony, a dangerous act that could change the Lattice locally forever. The warning becomes a lesson.)
choices.description: Anchor yourself to the coral pillar and let the wrongness build through your body

line.dialogue: I swallowed the dissonance whole and held — my bones are singing a new key now!
It was too much — the wrongness split through my ribs and I tasted blood on the second note.

lines_before.dialogue: Your resonance ship, the *Sky-Singer*, drifts into the Silent Zone. The familiar hum of the crystal resonator dies to a whisper, then nothing. Outside, the Lattice lies still and dead, reflecting no light, answering no sound.
I don't like this. It's like the world just... stopped breathing.
The readings are all flat. No frequency response. We're navigating blind. We should turn back.
Turn back? The Tonal Orders pay triple for charts of dead zones. That's no problem for our wallets.
This silence... it's not an absence. It feels like a held breath. There's something in my eye. The air feels thick with unsung notes.
A shape resolves in the gloom—a derelict listener outpost, its observation deck crumbling. A single robed figure stands at the railing.
You should not be here. The song does not reach this place. It is... profane.

lines_after.dialogue: Profane? Or just inconvenient for your monopoly on 'holy' sounds?
We do not control. We listen. And here... there is nothing to hear. My stomach is starting to growl! The quiet consumes even thought.
Then why are *you* here, monk?
The monk hesitates, glancing at a strange, silent crystal growing from the outpost wall.

line.dialogue: The Listener Monk is clearly hiding something about this place. How do you press him?

choices.text: Appeal to his duty. (Easy: He respects protocol.)
choices.leads_to: He may share official warnings.
choices.description: Have Arthit focus forbidden paths on the unresponsive lattice to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The lattice has other plans. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Threaten to report his presence here. (Medium: He fears the Orders.)
choices.leads_to: He might bargain for secrecy.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing frequency mapping to expose surface colonization truth

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.text: Ask about the strange crystal. (Easy: It's visibly unnatural.)
choices.leads_to: He's conflicted about it.
choices.description: Have the monk focus prayers on the dead silence to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the monk. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the monk misreads the situation. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk, Brother Solas, leads you inside the cold outpost. The air is stale. On a table, among scattered scrolls, lies a pamphlet: 'The Groundless Manifesto.'
Groundless literature? Here? This is a restricted zone!
They... they came. Before the silence fully claimed this place. They said the Lattice was a cage. That true freedom was in the dead zones.
A cage of sound... It's something to think about. If the Lattice responds to command, who commands us?
He ran out of the script. Listeners aren't supposed to ponder, just obey. These robes are so uncomfortable! No wonder he's dabbling in rebellion.
A sudden, harsh scraping sound echoes from the lower decks—metal on crystal. It's the first foreign noise you've heard in hours.
That's not the silence! Someone else is here!

lines_after.dialogue: You descend to find a sky pirate, her jacket patched with scavenged resonator shards, prying at a sealed door with a crowbar.
Well, look what the quiet coughed up. A monk and his choir. This scrap-heap's claimed, kids. Beat it.
That vault... it contains forbidden research! The early experiments that may have *caused* the Silencing!
Exactly. Paydirt. Knowledge the Tonal Orders buried. Knowledge that makes you look younger, kid. Frees you from their pretty songs.

line.dialogue: The pirate wants the forbidden research. Brother Solas wants it destroyed. The truth is behind the door.

choices.text: Side with the Monk. Destroy the research. (Easy: Uphold the Orders' law.)
choices.leads_to: Prevent the spread of dangerous knowledge.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with Listener training to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit is thwarted. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Side with the Pirate. Secure the research. (Medium: Ally with a criminal.)
choices.leads_to: Gain potent, dangerous secrets.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with unauthorized tones to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. The villagers rise with their agricultural tools.
Chanida overreaches. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.text: Demand to see the research first, for yourselves. (Hard: Play both sides.)
choices.leads_to: Risk angering both parties for the truth.
choices.description: The pirate uses pirate ship to decode the distress signal near the crushing quiet

line.dialogue: the pirate succeeds. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
the pirate's resolve isn't enough. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The air grows colder, the silence denser. The party's footsteps are the only sound in a world that has forgotten how to echo.
I feel uncomfortable. More than just the quiet. It's like the Lattice itself is holding its breath.
My stomach is starting to growl! But even chewing feels too loud here.
The monk's readings are erratic. He's only interested in the anomaly ahead, not our safety.
That's no problem. To find a truth, sometimes you must walk where safety ends.
There... the source of the silence. A fracture in the Lattice. Not natural. It was made.
You're gonna be sorry for leaving me tied up back there. That's a Tonal Order suppression rig. They didn't just study this place. They killed it.

lines_after.dialogue: Before them, a massive, dead resonator crystal juts from the ground, wrapped in rusted metal and silent cabling. It hums with a negative energy, a vacuum of sound.
They built this? To make the Silent Zone?
My order's texts spoke of a 'Great Dissonance' we were to avoid. They never said we created it.
Of course. The Tonal Orders monopoly on navigation. What better way to control the skies than to make parts of it unnavigable?

line.dialogue: The suppression rig is still active, its core crystal faintly pulsing. The unnatural silence radiates from it.

choices.text: Sabotage the power conduits. Chanida spots vulnerable cabling.
choices.consequence: A quick, physical solution. Loud sparks break the silence, potentially alerting anything nearby.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the flooded speakers until you feel the dead signal's rhythm.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the static, someone's breathing through the wires. I can feel their chest rising.
Nothing. Just cold metal vomiting noise into my bones. Whatever lived in this frequency already drowned.

choices.text: Have the Monk attempt a counter-frequency prayer. Use the Lattice's latent memory against the machine.
choices.consequence: A spiritual gamble. It could soothe the area or cause a violent feedback loop.
choices.description: Kneel beside the monk and match your breathing to his erratic pattern until your heartbeats synchronize.

line.dialogue: His rhythm just shifted to match mine. He's not erratic — he's translating. The water is speaking through him.
His breathing stopped. For three full seconds his chest didn't move. Then it started again, wrong, like something else resumed for him.

choices.text: Let the Sky Pirate try to 're-tune' it. He claims to know forbidden frequencies.
choices.consequence: Extremely risky. He might unlock the zone, or turn the suppression field on you.
choices.description: Chew the last of the dried provisions slowly, letting the sound echo through the flooded chamber on purpose.

line.dialogue: The echoes came back wrong. Each chew returned a half-second late — like something downstream is eating the sound and spitting it back.
I bit down and tasted salt that wasn't

lines_before.dialogue: As the suppression rig destabilizes, the Silent Zone shudders. A wave of pent-up sound—centuries of stifled echoes—rushes back in a deafening, chaotic roar.
The lattice resonance! It's returning! Roll up your sleeves, everyone! The ship's crystal will be overloaded!
That's it, right? The big secret? The Tonal Orders are groundless tyrants who broke the world to rule the pieces.
The truth of The Silencing... it's something to think about. My faith was in a song they helped mute.
Told ya you'd need me! Now the real music starts! And every pirate and rebel from here to the Spires will hear it!
The Groundless movement... they were right. The cities aren't our salvation. They're our cages.
That's all, isn't it? We float above a truth we were taught to fear. A world waiting to sing again.
The returning soundscape is not gentle. It is a screaming testament to violence. And within the cacophony, a new, deeper vibration begins—the Lattice, wounded, awakening.

lines_after.dialogue: The Silent Zone is silent no more. It is a chorus of revelation and rage. The party stands at the epicenter, their actions having torn the veil from a foundational lie.
We have given the world back its voice. What it says next is up to all of us.
Don't get poetic. The Orders will send everything they have to quiet this down again. Permanently.
Then we must ensure this frequency cannot be drowned again. The knowledge must travel.

line.dialogue: The awakened Lattice frequency is a beacon of truth and a target. How do you wield this terrible, beautiful knowledge?

choices.text: Broadcast it openly. Let every resonator on every ship and city hear the truth at once. A declaration of war.
choices.consequence: Instant, chaotic revolution. The Groundless movement swells, but the Orders react with immediate, overwhelming force.
choices.description: Press your palms against the trembling lattice and let the resonance sing through your bones.

line.dialogue: * "I can feel every thread — the Orders aren't lost, they're sleeping inside us!
* "Too much — it's slipping through me like water through a cracked bell!

choices.text: Entrust it to the Listeners. Let the monastic order decipher and disseminate it slowly, seeding doubt within the system.
choices.consequence: A slower, subtler schism. The truth becomes a heresy, a whisper that grows. The Monk's order is forever changed.
choices.description: Demand the monk recite the forbidden verses of the Tonal Orders before the resonance fades.

line.dialogue: * "I feared these words for decades — but hearing them now, they were never weapons. They were apologies.
* "My throat closes. The Silencing carved itself deeper into me than I ever knew.

choices.text: Become the frequency. As a Singer, Pichit can carry the true song within, a living catalyst. A quieter, more personal revolution.
choices.consequence: The most dangerous path. The power and the burden become Pichit's alone. He becomes both messiah and hunted artifact.
choices.description: Let the bandit strike the lattice with his blade to crack open whatever's sealed inside.

line.dialogue: * "HA! Hear that ring? Sometimes you don't solve a lock — you break the whole door!
* "It threw me back — the lattice bit into my arm. Thing's got teeth, this music!

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whispering Gull' hangs motionless over the Silent Zone. Below, the Lattice is a frozen, dead mirror. No hum, no vibration answers the ship's crystal resonators.
Navigation charts are useless here. The Tonal Orders have no data on this... emptiness. I thought it was okay to skirt the edge, but this deep?
Of course the charts are blank. The guilds only map where there's profit. A dead zone is just a blank space on their ledgers.
The quiet is crawling on my skin! Can't we just fire the main resonator, full power? Something has to give.
Force is a shout into a void. It's something to think about... perhaps the Zone isn't rejecting sound, but absorbing it. What do you think, Arthit?
The resonator readings are flat. It's like our sound... dies. I think it's alright to be cautious. We don't know what drained this place.
A faint, irregular ping appears on the scanner—a distress signal, weak and fragmented, originating from a drifting island-settlement below.

lines_after.dialogue: A settlement? Here? they're incredibly stubborn.
People in trouble! We have to check it out. What are we waiting for?
A beacon in the silence. An answer, of a sort. We should investigate.

line.dialogue: The signal is weak. Approaching the silent settlement will require navigating the dead Lattice manually.

choices.text: Take the ship down slowly, using minimal power. (Easy - Stealthy)
choices.consequence: Risk a slow, quiet descent into the unknown.
choices.description: Strike the hull with a tuning hammer and listen for what rings back.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "There — a harmonic, faint but consistent. Something out there has mass, and it's moving.
Arthit — "Nothing. The hammer's tone dies the instant it leaves the metal. This void swallows even vibration.

choices.text: Use short, powerful resonator bursts to clear a path. (Medium - Direct)
choices.consequence: Risk drawing attention with sudden noise in the silence.
choices.description: Have Chanida bleed a drop of ink into the water outside and watch which way it drifts.

line.dialogue: Malee — "The ink pulls southeast. Currents exist here whether the guilds admit it or not — follow the flow.
Chanida — "The ink just... hangs. Spreads in a perfect sphere. I don't think direction even exists here.

choices.text: Send a probe first to scout the island. (Easy - Cautious)
choices.consequence: Delay help but gather more data.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sing the lowest note he knows and hold it until something responds.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "I feel it — a pressure against my chest, pushing back. The void isn't empty. It's listening.
Pichit — "My voice cracks and falters. I can't hold pitch here. It's like the air refuses to carry me.

lines_before.dialogue: The settlement, 'Last Echo,' is a cluster of crumbling structures on a grey island. The air is thick and muffled. A lone figure, a villager, waves frantically but makes no sound.
You... you heard the beacon? Thank the silent stars. We can't make the Lattice sing. Our resonator array failed. I had to jury-rig the beacon all by myself.
Let me guess. You bought the array from a passing merchant. I've seen it before. Cheap crystals, faulty frequency bindings.
Without resonance, your island will drift into the deeper void. You have bad eyesight if you can't see that.
We know! Our elder, he... he went to bargain with the Trade Negotiator anchored at the edge of the Zone. For parts. He hasn't returned.
A merchant ship? Here? I had a bad dream about leeches swimming in silence. This feels like that.
A negotiation in a place where words lose their power. I did the repairs on our ship's resonator myself. Perhaps I can assess your array.
As Pichit speaks, Chanida notices something glinting in the villager's hut—a finely crafted, pulsating crystal prosthetic leg, clearly Resonant technology.

lines_after.dialogue: Hey! What's that? A crystal leg? That's not standard skycity issue.
The elder's! From before the Silencing, he says. It... it still hums sometimes, even here. He calls it his 'anchor.'
An antique Resonant prosthetic. No merchant sells those. Only the Listeners might have kept such things. Or Singers.
It resonates... in the Silent Zone? That is a profound contradiction.

line.dialogue: The villager points towards the foggy edge of the island where the merchant barge is moored. The elder is overdue.

choices.text: Confront the Trade Negotiator directly. (Easy - Confrontation)
choices.consequence: Risk a blunt negotiation with a professional manipulator.
choices.description: Press the villager for details about the elder's bargain with the Tethered.

line.dialogue: The Tethered don't bargain — they collect. Tell me exactly what your elder offered them, or we're already too late.
You're trembling so badly you can barely speak. Breathe. Slowly. Start from when the elder left.

choices.text: First, examine the Resonant prosthetic for clues. (Medium - Investigation)
choices.consequence: Delay the rescue to uncover the elder's secret.
choices.description: Examine the array yourself, looking for merchant tampering or deliberate sabotage.

line.dialogue: Ha — see these solder marks? Your passing merchant sold you a gutted relay. This array hasn't held resonance in years.
The wiring's a mess. I'd need three days and parts we don't have to even diagnose this thing.

choices.text: Split up: Pichit/Arthit to the barge, Chanida/Malee to the resonator array. (Hard - Division)
choices.consequence: Cover more ground but risk being isolated in the silence.
choices.description: Demand the villager lead you to where the elder went to meet the Tethered.

line.dialogue: Stop crying
The risk doesn't pay off. Local knowledge proves outdated.

lines_before.dialogue: The airship groans as it settles into the unnatural stillness of the Silent Zone. Outside the viewports, the Lattice hangs motionless and dark, reflecting no light, producing no hum.
I've run every diagnostic. Our resonator crystals are functioning perfectly. The Lattice just... isn't answering.
So we're stuck? In this... dead quiet? It's making my teeth ache.
Relax. The Trade Negotiator's ship is anchored nearby. They wouldn't have come here if there wasn't a way out. Probably a secret only profit can unlock.
This silence isn't empty. It's a presence. I have something to tell you all. Back in the Skycity archives, I found fragmented logs about this place. They called it 'The Scar'.
A Scar? From The Silencing? I've never understood how a catastrophe could leave a patch of... nothing.
A sharp, rhythmic tapping echoes from the hull—not from the Lattice, but from something outside. It's the Trade Negotiator, suited up and knocking with a metal rod.
My friends! You seem... becalmed. A unfortunate fate. I've seen it before. Ships drift here forever, crews slowly maddened by the quiet.

lines_after.dialogue: The Negotiator's smile doesn't reach his eyes. He gestures to a faint, jagged crack in the dead Lattice, visible only from a specific angle.
Consider it a professional courtesy. The Tonal Orders would have your ship for scrap if they knew you'd wandered here. Best we all keep this between us, yes?
A 'courtesy' with a price. What's in there, behind that friendly smile of yours?

line.dialogue: The Negotiator offers a way through the crack—a unstable, narrow passage he calls 'The Seam'. He claims his own ship is too large, but he'll share the coordinates for a 'small favor'. He eyes Arthit's resonant prosthetic leg.

choices.line: Agree to his terms. Let him briefly interface a scanner with Arthit's prosthetic to 'study its resonance signature'. He promises it's harmless.
choices.description: Channel the resonator crystals through Pichit's sensing equipment to amplify the signal, 15 words

line.dialogue: I can feel it now—threaded through the silence like veins of frozen light.
Nothing but static and my own heartbeat—I've never felt so alone in a signal.

choices.line: Refuse, but offer to trade valuable cargo instead. It will deplete your supplies, but keeps the prosthetic's secrets safe.
choices.description: Hail the Trade Negotiator's ship and request emergency resonator calibration assistance, 15 words

line.dialogue: They're responding—hull frequencies matching, they're feeding us alignment data right now.
Dead air. Either they can't hear us... or whatever silenced us got them first.

choices.line: Call his bluff. Threaten to broadcast your location to the Tonal Orders on a emergency channel, trapping him here too.
choices.description: Shut down all non-essential systems and listen to the silence with bare ears, 15 words

line.dialogue: I hear it—beneath the quiet, something breathing, vast and patient and waiting.
It's worse with everything off—the silence presses in like water filling my skull.

lines_before.dialogue: The Seam is a claustrophobic tunnel of fractured crystal. Your ship's lights cast long, trembling shadows. The silence here is absolute, a physical weight.
My leg... it's buzzing. Not from the ship. It's reacting to something *in* the walls. Something old.
What's in there? Behind the crystal? I can see... shapes. Frozen forms.
Singers. Listeners. Dozens of them. Petrified in the lattice mid-song. This isn't a natural dead zone. This is a tomb.
The Silencing wasn't just an event. It was a purge. This is where they fought. Where they lost.

The tunnel opens into a vast cavern. At its center floats a massive, obsidian spike—a anti-resonance weapon, still active after centuries. Its null-field is the source of the silence. And it's beginning to pulse.
It's waking up! The pulse pattern... it's syncing with my prosthetic! It's trying to use it as a focus to discharge!
You're home so late for a catastrophe! We need to break the sync or we'll end up like them!

lines_after.dialogue: The weapon thrums, its pulse deepening. Arthit grits his teeth as his crystal leg glows with stolen, inverse resonance. The frozen forms around the chamber seem to tremble.
It's not just destroying sound. It's consuming memory. The history of what happened here. We can't let it finish.
The Negotiator knew. He sent us in here as a test. To see if the weapon was still active. We're not explorers. We're canaries.

line.dialogue: The weapon's activation is imminent. Arthit's prosthetic is the unintentional key. The null-field will expand, permanently silencing a vast swath of the Lattice.

choices.line: Shatter the Prosthetic. Have Arthit overload the crystal with the ship's power core. It will destroy his leg and damage the weapon, but he'll be grounded.
choices.description: Press your palm against the crystal and let Arthit's leg guide the resonance, 13 words

line.dialogue: The crystal's singing to me — I can feel the frequency, like a second heartbeat syncing with the one in my stump.
Pain — white, blinding — the crystal bit back and my leg remembers screaming that I never lived through.

choices.line: Sing Against the Silence. Have Pichit and Chanida attempt a counter-resonance, using the ship's speakers and their own voices to disrupt the sync. It risks deafening them or worse.
choices.description: Chip a fragment from the nearest petrified Singer's hand for structural analysis, 13 words

line.dialogue: The carbon dating is wrong — these people were alive *before* our calendar started. This purge is older than writing.
It crumbled to powder — I destroyed the evidence of a genocide with a careless hand. I'm no better than them.

choices.line: Accept the Sync, Redirect the Pulse. Have Arthit deliberately complete the connection, then use his own will to try to turn the weapon's energy inward, destroying it. He may not survive the feedback.
choices.description: Stand before the crystal and sing the melody Malee taught you on the third night, 15 words

line.dialogue: They're moving — the Singers — fingers twitching, lips parting — the melody
A costly mistake by the villager. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The party arrives at Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, vast terraces of golden wheat and silver irrigation channels suspended at the edge of the skycity. The wind creates a soft, rhythmic hiss.
A good place to rest. The Tonal Orders have few patrols here. The local frequencies are... stable.
Stable and boring. I can already feel my brain turning to farm-porridge. Let's find the merchant, get the map, and leave.
Look at that view! It makes you look younger, Malee. All that fresh air!
Flattery won't make the merchant any less of a swindler.
Listen. Beneath the wind... a low hum from the Lattice below. It's different here. Uncharted.
Which is why we need the frequency map. Uncharted means unpredictable resonance surges.
I’ve never tried Greek food before, but I bet it’s more exciting than waiting! Let's go!

lines_after.dialogue: A panicked SKYCITY RESIDENT bursts from a nearby grain silo, his face pale.
You! Travelers! You have to help! He ran out of the shed! The merchant! He took my family's resonance stabilizer!
Of course he did. The 'Trade Negotiator.' Let me guess—friendly smile, promised you a fortune?
He said it was for the 'Open Frequency Map' project! A gift for all skyfolk! Lies!

line.dialogue: The villager points towards the lower terraces. The merchant is fleeing with vital equipment.

choices.line: Pursue directly through the open fields. (Straightforward chase)
choices.description: Search the abandoned miller's cart near the tree line for anything the patrols missed.

line.dialogue: Someone left in a hurry — there's a half-sack of grain and a rusted signal horn beneath the canvas.
Nothing but mouse droppings and a wheel missing two spokes. The Orders swept this place cleaner than I thought.

choices.line: Use the irrigation channels to cut him off. (Requires navigation)
choices.description: Press Malee about the merchant — what exactly did he overcharge them for?

line.dialogue: Three vials of silverleaf tincture for the price of seven, and the third one smells like watered-down rice wine. I'll carve the coins back from his hide when we find him.
Forget it. I already said too much, and dwelling on it just makes me want to hit something — which we can't afford right now.

choices.line: Calm the villager and get more details first. (Gather information)
choices.description: Climb the ridge where Chanida spotted the view to scout for smoke or movement beyond the wheat.

line.dialogue: There — two columns east-northeast, thin ones, maybe cookfires. And a
The attempt backfires on the villager. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The chase leads to a secluded, overgrown terrace where the TRADE NEGOTIATOR is frantically calibrating the stolen stabilizer, a bulky crystal device.
Ah! Customers! Smiling happily! I can explain. This is for the greater good!
The greater good of your wallet!
Since that day I first heard the true hum of the Lattice, unshackled by the Orders' charts, I've believed. This device will help me record it!
A villager's farm stabilizer? It's not rated for deep-frequency scans. You'll burn it out and cause a local cascade.
You seek an open map... a true song of the world.
Yes! Imagine it! Free navigation for all! Who would believe that a simple merchant could crack the Orders' monopoly?
I wouldn't. Because you're not recording anything. You're stripping the crystal to sell on the black market.

lines_after.dialogue: You doubt my faith? From that day forward, my path was clear!
He activates the device. A painful, screeching frequency whines from it, causing the surrounding wheat to vibrate violently.
The lattice resonance is destabilizing! He's creating a feedback loop!
His belief is real... but his method is deaf.

line.dialogue: The screeching frequency is causing the terrace structure to shudder. The unstable device must be dealt with.

choices.line: Rush and physically smash the device. (Forceful, immediate)
choices.description: Have Malee focus leg resonance on the sky-rice to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.line: Try to talk the merchant down, appealing to his true goal. (Persuasion)
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to expose surface colonization truth, leveraging frequency mapping

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida misreads the situation. A spy alerts the authorities.

choices.line: Have Pichit attempt to Sing a counter-frequency to safely dissipate the energy. (Risky, requires focus)
choices.description: Ask the merchant to follow the phantom route, drawing on market connections

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the merchant. His trade connections deliver the right information.
Defeat. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The sun dips lower over Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, casting long shadows across the terraces. The rhythmic rustle of grain takes on a somber note.
Are you ready to go back home yet? I don't like the feel of this quiet. The villagers have all vanished.
Vanished, or hiding? This 'peaceful' farming skycity suddenly feels like a trap. It’s a lot more fun when you're not expecting a knife in the back.
They saw us talking to that merchant! He left in a hurry, and now everyone's gone! We spooked them.
Or we confirmed their fears. The Trade Negotiator's friendly smile hid a warning. The Tonal Orders' monopoly isn't just about charts... it's about fear.
(Whispering from behind a water silo) You shouldn't be here. Asking about frequencies... about maps... they'll hear you.
Who will hear? The Tonal Orders? We're just travelers.
Everyone hears, up here. Sound carries on the wind. You bring trouble. The Silencing began with whispers, too.

line.dialogue: The villager points a shaking finger toward a secluded, overgrown terrace where the merchant was last seen. A low, aberrant hum vibrates through the soil.

choices.line: Send Chanida ahead to scout. Her impulsiveness might draw out any threat quickly.
choices.description: Have Chanida focus crystal hearing on the agricultural hum to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The risk doesn't pay off. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.line: Approach as a group, but slowly. Let Arthit analyze the resonant frequency of the hum first.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to challenge skycity propaganda, leveraging monk wisdom

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
Pichit misreads the situation. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Split up. Malee and Pichit circle around the back of the terrace to cut off any escape.
choices.description: Ask the villager to record the spectral signature, drawing on village secrets

line.dialogue: Exactly as the villager hoped. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the villager misreads the situation. Local knowledge proves outdated.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. As you move toward the source of the hum, the pastoral sounds of the gardens—water, wind, crops—seem to distort, twisting into a single, focused dissonance.
The map... the Open Frequency Map the merchant hinted at... it's not a chart. It's a weapon, isn't it? Something that could break their control!
Or a key. A memory of the world before The Silencing, etched not on crystal, but in the very resonance of this place.

lines_before.dialogue: At the heart of the overgrown terrace lies the source: an ancient, fractured resonator, half-swallowed by roots and vines. It pulses with a pained, trapped frequency.
(Stepping from the shadows, his friendly smile gone) I knew you'd follow the resonance. Remember... keep in mind... some secrets are buried for a reason.
So the smooth talker shows his true pitch. Here to silence us before we find your little stash?
This resonator... it's pre-Silencing. I can't remember my password! I mean, I can't remember if the old texts described a lattice node this crude, this... alive.
Alive with a memory. A frequency map of the Lattice as it was, not as the Orders dictate. Who would believe you?! The Orders would shatter this skycity to keep it hidden.
And you? Do you believe in profit, or in the truth it sings? This garden remembers a song. A song of open skies, not controlled channels.
We have to free it! Let it sing! Let everyone hear!
You'll doom us all! The dissonance will call them down on us like a storm!

line.dialogue: The fractured crystal whines, its song straining to break free. The Merchant readies a damping device. The fate of the map—and Mae Rim—hangs on a single resonant choice.

choices.line: Shatter the resonator. Destroy the map to save the skycity from the Orders' wrath. The secret dies, but the people live.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to test the prosthetic reaction using Listener training

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The lattice has other plans. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.line: Attempt to harmonize with it. Pichit must channel the memory-song, trying to copy its frequency into a portable crystal without triggering a catastrophic release.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with forbidden paths to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
Arthit fails. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.line: Amplify it. Unleash the garden's full, remembered song across the Lattice. Let every Listener and Singer hear the truth, no matter the consequences.
choices.description: The merchant steps forward with market connections, ready to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: the merchant makes it work. His network produces an ally at the critical moment.
the merchant's resolve isn't enough. The echo fades to silence.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice resonates. The very air of the Hanging Gardens shivers, the fate of the Open Frequency Map sealed. The consequences will ripple across the floating cities.
We have remembered what they tried to silence. Whether it becomes a whisper or a shout... that is now our burden.
Well. So much for a quiet rest in the country. The bill for this is going to be astronomical.

lines_before.dialogue: The deck of the Resonance Ship 'Aeolian Drift' thrums with a low, steady C-sharp. Below, the Lattice ripples like a frozen sea, its crystalline facets catching the weak sun.
Maintaining course. The Tonal Charts for this sector are... fragmented. We're navigating by extrapolation.
Fragmented? You mean we're guessing! In only five minutes, this whole route could collapse!
Relax. Arthit's 'extrapolations' are safer than the Guild's marked toll-roads. I've never understood why people pay for those maps. It's just organized fear.
The fear is real, Malee. The Silencing proved the Lattice is not just a path, but a memory. One wrong frequency...
A sudden, discordant shiver runs through the ship's resonator, making the deck plates vibrate unpleasantly.
What was that? See? I told you! The Drift is no match for these open vectors. We should've paid the Guild fee!
Now, now, friend. A little turbulence adds character to a journey. And it certainly can't beat the savings.

lines_after.dialogue: It's not turbulence. It's... rhythmic. Like an echo.
Scanners are picking up a phantom resonance signature. It's weak, but it's cycling. It doesn't match any known ship pattern.
Great. A ghost. Just what we needed.
Or a memory. The Lattice records everything. What if we're hearing the echo of a ship that was lost here?

line.dialogue: The phantom signal pulses, a faint, mournful tone against the engine's hum. It seems to be coming from a dense cluster of crystal spires below.

choices.text: Adjust course to investigate the signal directly. (Chanida: 'Let's see what's singing!')
choices.description: Override the console and force a manual tonal sweep of the surrounding frequencies.

line.dialogue: There—echoing off the hull. Something massive is breathing between the channels.
Nothing but noise. Either the sweep was too crude, or whatever's out there knows we're listening.

choices.text: Hail the signal on all harmonic frequencies. (Arthit: 'A cautious, formal approach.')
choices.description: Pull Chanida aside and ask her to translate the corrupted lattice fragments using her old pre-Silencing archives.

line.dialogue: My grandmother's phonetic tables still work. These aren't errors—they're *names*, Arthit. Something is calling itself.
The archive is degraded past the third glyph layer. I'm sorry—I'm reading shadows, not signals.

choices.text: Ignore it and plot a course around the spires. (Merchant: 'The profitable path is the clear path.')
choices.description: Kill the drive engines entirely and let the ship drift, listening with bare hull for the whisper Pichit claims to hear.

line.dialogue: Quiet—*there*. Under the radiation hum. It's not static, it's syllables. The Lattice is speaking again.
I swear I heard it before we went dark. Now there's only the blood in my ears. The silence took it.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship holds position at the edge of the crystal forest. The phantom signal is clearer now—a looping three-note descent, like a sinking sigh.
Hailing yielded no intelligent response. The signal is automated, or... residual. I think that's the one. The 'Echo of Peristera,' a supply runner lost seven cycles ago.
The Peristera! Its manifest was rumored to contain a fortune in pre-Silencing harmonic alloys. My associates would be very interested in its recovery.
Of course he's only interested in the cargo. Not the crew, or why a ship with a Guild navigator just vanished.
But the alloy could be worth a skycity! We have to go down there. You're gonna be sorry for leaving this if we just fly away.
The Listeners teach that such echoes are wounds in the Lattice. To approach is to listen to a dying breath. We must be respectful.
Respectful? It's a tomb! I think that's right. We shouldn't be here. This is bad luck.
The signal shifts, the three notes suddenly resolving into a single, clear, beckoning tone aimed directly at the Aeolian Drift.

lines_after.dialogue: The signal is actively scanning us. It's not just an echo. There's intent.
Intent to do what? Lure us in? I think so. Classic ghost-ship story.
Or maybe it's a distress call that never stopped. Someone might still be down there!
Or its automated systems are simply interested in any nearby resonance. Either way, the cargo holds are likely intact.

line.dialogue: The beckoning tone holds, a siren song from the crystalline depths. The path between the spires is narrow and treacherous.

choices.text: Deploy a probe first. Scan for physical hazards and life signs. (Arthit: 'Data before danger.')
choices.description: Lock the boarding tube onto the Peristera's cargo bay airlock and lead the team across immediately.

line.dialogue: I'm first through that door — nobody touches that alloy until I've verified its grade.
The hull's buckling under our docking pressure — get back before it shears the tube clean off!

choices.text: Match the ship's resonator to the signal's frequency. 'Answer' the call. (Pichit: 'To listen is to understand.')
choices.description: Deploy a tethered survey drone through the fractured hull to scan for survivors and atmospheric hazards first.

line.dialogue: Drone's picking up a heartbeat in the lower decks — someone's still alive in there, we are NOT leaving without them.
The drone's signal just dissolved into static — whatever killed their comms just ate ours too.

choices.text: Take the ship in directly. Follow the tone to its source. (Chanida: 'No time for scans! Someone needs help!')
choices.description: Hack the Peristera's emergency beacon to pull its black box data remotely before committing anyone to boarding.

line.dialogue: The black box is broadcasting a repeating distress code — but the timestamp says it's been looping for eleven years.
The risk doesn't pay off. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship's deck is shrouded in a low, unnatural fog. The usual engine tones have faded, replaced by a faint, ghostly hum.
That's it! The hum! It's the same frequency we picked up from the Echo's distress beacon. It's luring us.
Interesting. The Lattice below is crystallizing into strange, jagged patterns. It's reacting to the ghost ship's residual resonance.
We shouldn't follow it. The Trade Negotiator's charts showed this area as 'tonally unstable.' This is a trap.
But the lost souls on that ship... their final song is trapped here. To understand the Silencing, we must listen to echoes like this.
Come in. Come right into my cabin, if you're still sane. I've... locked myself in. The hum is getting inside my head!
We're all gonna be sorry for following this course! The Listeners warned about 'hungry echoes' that drain a ship's resonance!
A spectral shape materializes ahead—the ghostly outline of the lost Resonance Ship 'Echo.' Its deck lights flicker like dying stars.

lines_after.dialogue: The ghost ship's form solidifies, its resonance creating a bridge of unstable crystal between the two vessels.
It's inviting us aboard. Or demanding it.
He hung up. The Negotiator cut his comms. We're alone with this... interesting problem.

line.dialogue: The crystalline bridge pulses, unstable. We can attempt to cross to the Echo, or try to sever the resonant link from here.

choices.text: Cross the bridge quickly. (Chanida leads, using her impulsive speed.)
choices.description: Channel the haunting frequency through the Lattice resonator to decode the lost ship's final transmission.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "I've locked onto their last coordinates — the signal is resolving into voices, dozens of them, still singing.
Chanida — "The feedback loop is collapsing — I can hear them screaming but I can't pinpoint the source!

choices.text: Analyze the bridge's frequency. (Malee and Arthit work to find a safe harmonic path.)
choices.description: Descend to the crystallizing Lattice chamber and physically touch the forming structures to read their stored memory.

line.dialogue: Malee — "The crystal lattice is recording everything — I can feel the crew's final moments vibrating through my fingertips like braille from the dead.
Malee — "The crystallization is accelerating unpredictably — it's crawling up my arm and I cannot break contact!

choices.text: Sing against the link. (Pichit uses his latent Singer ability to disrupt the ghost ship's pull.)
choices.description: Override the Trade Negotiator's chart warnings and plot a direct intercept course toward the phantom signal's origin point.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "I'm overriding the
the villager is thwarted. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: Whether by bridge, analysis, or song, you stand on the deck of the Echo. It is a frozen moment of the Silencing—crystals grown through hull and crew.
I don't understand anything! The lattice didn't just engulf them... it preserved them. Like a recording.
The ship's main resonator is cracked. The final tone it emitted was a catastrophic feedback loop. It's... still emitting it.
This is the source of the 'tonally unstable' zone. If this feedback spreads to our ship, we'll be crystallized too. We don't know when it might surge.
You still don't understand? This isn't just a ghost ship! It's a weapon! The Tonal Orders would kill to control a resonance like this!
The cracked resonator glows with pent-up energy. The crystallized forms of the crew seem to stir, their final despair echoing in the hum.
My ship! My cargo! You'll regret that you led us here when my investors hear of this loss!
Please... just make it stop. I don't want to become part of the song.

lines_after.dialogue: The feedback loop within the resonator builds to a critical pitch. The entire ghost ship vibrates, threatening to shatter and release its deadly frequency.
Now I understand. This echo wants to be heard, then released. To finish the song that was silenced.
Make a choice. Quickly. It's going to decide for us.

line.dialogue: The catastrophic resonance must be dealt with. We can attempt to contain it, redirect it, or... complete it.

choices.text: Contain it. (Seal the resonator with crystal-shielding techniques, preserving the Echo as a tomb.)
choices.description: Malee channels leg resonance toward the deck wind, hoping to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
The attempt backfires on Malee. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: Redirect it. (Channel the feedback into the Lattice below, dispersing it but risking a wider instability.)
choices.description: Arthit uses ship navigation to support the rebels near the deck wind

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The villagers rise with their agricultural tools.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The escape tunnel collapses.

choices.text: Complete it. (Pichit must Sing the feedback loop's final, resolving chord, absorbing its meaning and danger.)
choices.description: The villager steps forward with terraces, ready to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the villager. The community rallies, creating unexpected strength.
the villager is thwarted. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whispering Current' drifts to a halt at the edge of the Silent Zone. The familiar hum of its crystal resonator fades into a profound, unnatural quiet. The Lattice below is dark, glassy, and still.
Well, this is... different. The charts just stop. It's like the world ended here.
All readings are null. No resonance feedback, no ambient frequency. It's acoustically dead. Proceeding is... ill-advised.
Ill-advised pays the bills, Arthit. The Tonal Orders don't send salvage contracts to safe places. What's she like, this zone? A graveyard?
Not a graveyard. An absence. As if something was meticulously removed, not destroyed. We should tread lightly.
A small, battered surface skiff approaches, piloted by a figure in patched enviro-gear. They signal to dock.
You're the contract team? Didn't think you'd actually come. This place... it doesn't like visitors. Why are you doing this to me? Dragging outsiders into this silence?
We're here for the lost Listeners' expedition. Their last signal came from in there. You know the way?

lines_after.dialogue: I know the surface trails. The quiet paths. But you don't navigate the Silent Zone. You survive it. The Lattice doesn't answer here.
Charming. So, our guide is a fatalist. Anywhere you like to start the tour? Preferably somewhere that doesn't get us erased.
There's an old waystation. Half-sunk. The Listeners might have used it. It's... a place to start.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points towards a faint, crystalline structure on the dead Lattice plain. The path to it is not clear.

choices.line: Follow the Scavenger's suggested surface trail. (Cautious, but predictable.)
choices.description: Direct Pichit to test the prosthetic reaction using tonal knowledge

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
A costly mistake by Pichit. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Attempt a short, cautious resonator pulse to scan for safer paths. (Risks attracting unknown attention.)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to uncover the suppression, drawing on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
A costly mistake by Arthit. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.line: Send a drone ahead to map the immediate area. (Slow, but safe.)
choices.description: Direct the monk to record the spectral signature using prayers

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the monk. Crystal bowls shatter in harmonic sympathy.
The attempt backfires on the monk. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The waystation is a crumbling dome of fused crystal, its interior choked with strange, sound-absorbent moss. Faded murals depict figures falling from floating cities.
Life. In a place that kills resonance. This moss... it's consuming the last traces of vibration. A biological silence.
These murals... they're not about The Silencing. They're newer. A plea, or a warning. 'The Sky is a Cage.'
Chanida pries open a sealed locker. Inside are journals, not of Listeners, but of the Groundless Movement.
Listen to this: 'The Tonal Orders lie. The Lattice's true song isn't for navigation—it's a memory. A memory of the ground. They silenced it to keep us adrift.'
Conspiracy theorists. Lovely. So we're in a dead zone hunting monks, and we find pamphlets. Why are you doing this to me, universe?
The Groundless... they say the cities float because we forgot how to land. That the Silent Zones are... wounds. Places the world is trying to forget.
A low, sub-audible tremor passes through the structure. The moss pulses faintly. From the shadows, a figure in Listener robes steps forward, hands raised in a gesture of peace.
You should not have come. But since you are here... you have seen their truth. The Groundless. What's she like, our world, when her song is stolen?

lines_after.dialogue: You're the survivor from the expedition. You stayed here to study... this?

To listen. In the only place left where you can hear nothing. In that nothing... sometimes, something whispers. My brothers and sisters... they went deeper, to the heart of the silence. They did not return.
Their last signal was a distress call. What happened?
They found something. Something that listens back. It asked them questions. About the sky, and the ground. It asked... 'Anywhere. Anywhere you like to be free?' And then... silence.

line.dialogue: The Monk indicates a deep fissure in the Lattice floor leading downward. The path to the lost Listeners—and the source of the whispers—lies below.

choices.line: Prepare thoroughly. Secure ropes, lights, and sound-dampening gear before descending. (Methodical, slow.)
choices.description: Chanida channels frequency mapping toward the lost signals, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The risk doesn't pay off. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.line: Have the Monk guide you, using his limited knowledge of the upper fissures. (Faster, but trusts a traumatized stranger.)
choices.description: Convince Malee to use mechanical repair and support the rebels

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
Malee is thwarted. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.line: Attempt to use a focused, high-frequency pulse to map the fissure's depth instantly. (Quick, but will broadcast your presence loudly in the silent dark.)
choices.description: Have the monk focus lattice study on the danger to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. Crystal bowls shatter in harmonic sympathy.
Things don't go as planned. The monk's faith wavers, breaking concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: The deeper you push into the Silent Zone, the heavier the quiet becomes. It's not just an absence of sound—it feels like an absence of *self*. The Lattice beneath your feet is dull, clouded, like frozen milk.
My head feels... hollow. Like someone scooped out all the background noise of being alive.
Don't say that. It's just quiet. We're fine. Right, Arthit?
Our resonator readings are flatlining. No harmonic feedback at all. It's as if this place is... dead to the Song. I've never seen charts for anything like this.
It's not dead. It's listening. But not to us.
The ancient texts spoke of places where the Lattice fell asleep. Or was put to sleep. I always thought it was metaphor.
It ain't sleep. It's a scar. My granddad said the Silencing didn't just break things—it *buried* things. Things that shouldn't be dug up.
Well, we're digging. So what's down here? Ghosts?

line.dialogue: A structure emerges from the fog—not crystal, but ancient, pitted metal. A pre-Silencing ruin, impossibly preserved. A low, sub-audible hum emanates from it, making your teeth ache. The Scavenger freezes.

choices.text: Approach with reverence. This is a tomb.
choices.outcome_line: You move slowly, hands open. The hum doesn't change. The Monk whispers a prayer of passing. The metal door is ajar, frozen in time.
choices.description: Force recalibration by cracking the resonator crystal against the floor, one sharp strike

line.dialogue: Harmonic spike — 0.3, 0.7, climbing — it's answering us now, keep talking!
Nothing. The crystal just... absorbed it. Like it drank the frequency whole.

choices.text: Scan for resonance signatures. Knowledge before risk.
choices.outcome_line: Arthit's scanner whirs uselessly, then gives a single spike of corrupted data—a scream recorded in crystal, millennia old. The sound, when played back, is a word: 'Containment.'
choices.description: Whisper your own name three times into the resonator's dead microphone

line.dialogue: It turned toward you — God, it actually turned — what did you say your name was?
Don't. Don't do that again. When you spoke, I heard something say it back, but wrong. Like it was tasting the syllables.

choices.text: Touch the metal. Feel its history.
choices.outcome_line: The moment your glove makes contact, a silent shockwave of pure memory hits you—visions of running figures, a sky on fire, and a desperate, final command: SILENCE IT ALL.
choices.description: Grab Malee's hand and run for the chamber exit before the silence deepens

line.dialogue: the scavenger's expertise pays off. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
Things don't go as planned. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_after.dialogue: I'm a Christian, my ma was, but this place... this feels older than God. Older than sin.
May I see your driver's license? No... forgive me. An old phrase. My thoughts are unraveling. This silence untethers the mind.
Shall we go to the seaside? I'd kill for some noisy, stupid waves right now. Anything but this.
This is where they tried to kill the Song. Not break it. Murder it.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the ruin, you find not corpses, but crystallized echoes—figures of Lattice caught in mid-flight, faces locked in silent screams. At the chamber's heart lies a machine: a massive, fractured resonator, its purpose clearly not for travel, but for erasure.
This isn't navigation tech. This is a weapon. The Tonal Orders' founding myth... they didn't just preserve knowledge after the Silencing. They caused it. To control the remnants.
The truth... the Listeners were founded to guard this lie. To ensure the Silent Zones stayed silent. To let the world forget what was done here.
The Groundless Movement thinks the Lattice is a cage. They're right. But the cage was built by the jailers.
That machine's still got a charge. A ghost in the wire. You can feel it in your bones.
So what now? We walk away and let the Orders keep lying? Let them call people like Pichit 'Singers' and treat them like freaks, when they're just remembering what the world used to sound like?
The Song isn't gone. It's trapped. In here. In the Silent Zones. We've been navigating a corpse, thinking it was the world.
The machine begins to glow. A dormant cycle completing. The Silent Zone is preparing to expand, to swallow another swath of the Lattice. The final act of the ancient weapon.

line.dialogue: The core of the machine pulses with captive resonance. Destroying it could release a catastrophic wave of pent-up sound—unmaking the Zone, or unmaking you. Leaving it means the Silence spreads. The Monk looks at you, awaiting a leader's choice.

choices.text: Shatter the core. Release the Song, whatever the cost.
choices.outcome_line: You strike the core. For a moment, nothing. Then, a light. Then, a sound—the first true sound in millennia. It is beautiful, and terrible, and it washes over you like a tide, scouring the Silence away. The Lattice around you shimmers, alive. You are deafened, forever, but you can feel the world singing again.
choices.description: Reach into the resonating chamber and manually sever the harmonic lattice threads before it cycles up. (14 words)

line.dialogue: * "Threads cut — the chord collapses. Whatever this thing was built to unmake, it stays made.
