* "The vibration got into my bones — my hands won't stop shaking. It's still humming.

choices.text: Attempt to contain and control the release. A calculated risk.
choices.outcome_line: Using your ship's resonator in reverse, you try to channel the energy. It's a desperate symphony of effort. The sound erupts, but in a controlled, brilliant column that pierces the fog. The Silent Zone recedes, leaving a scar of singing crystal. The truth is out, and its frequency is now etched across the Lattice for all to see.
choices.description: Convince the monk to chant the suppression sutra while you drain the residual charge through the floor grating. (17 words)

line.dialogue: * "The sutra holds. I can feel the old doctrine sealing what the founders feared. It sleeps.
* "My voice cracked on the third refrain. The chord answered back — and now I understand why they wept.

choices.text: Speak to it. You are a Singer. Sing it back to sleep.
choices.outcome_line: You step forward, close your eyes, and do not shout. You hum. The note is small, personal, fragile. You offer it to the machine. The pulsing core hesitates. Then, it answers. A harmony. The weapon's final purpose unravels in a duet. The Silence dissolves not with a bang, but a lullaby. The Zone becomes quiet, not dead. Peaceful.
choices.description: Let the scavenger hotwire the ghost-signal into a feedback loop, turning the weapon's resonance against itself. (15 words)

line.dialogue: * "She's eating her own tail now — beautiful, really. The Lattice just became its own prison wall.
* "Should've known better than to wire a living thing into itself. It's awake now, and it's *angry.*

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The consequences will ripple across the Floating Cities. The Tonal Orders will hear of this. The Groundless Movement will find a martyr or a miracle. Your journey... it's the best way. The only way forward.
I'm on my way out. Back to the charts. They're all wrong now. We have to redraw everything.
One way or round trip? I guess... we're not going back, are we? Not to the way things were.
The world just got a lot bigger, and a lot more complicated. I hate it. Let's go.
The Song is free. Now we learn how to listen to it all over again.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship, the *Whisper's Promise*, drifts into the edge of the Silent Zone. The ambient hum of the Lattice fades to nothing, replaced by a pressure that feels like cotton in the ears.
Readings are flat. No resonance feedback at all. It's like the Lattice is... asleep. Or dead.
This is creepy. Can we turn around? I don't like this quiet. It's too big.
The Tonal Orders pay triple for salvage charts of dead zones. They want to know what kills the song. Money talks louder than fear.
A place of absolute silence... What does it mean for a world built on resonance? What happened here that the Lattice refuses to answer?
Ahead, a derelict skycity fragment hangs motionless, its crystals dark. A single, flickering lamp denotes a makeshift dock.
You shouldn't be here! The quiet... it gets into your head. Nothing works right. No songs, no navigation. We're stuck.
Your resonator crystals are inert. How are you surviving?

lines_after.dialogue: Surviving? Barely. We ration echo-moss. Some folks... they've started listening to a new preacher. Says the silence is freedom. Calls themselves the Groundless.
A preacher in a dead zone? That's weird. I'll try it. Let's go talk to them. Maybe they know a way out.
Or a way to profit. I'll open it for you. Let's see what this 'freedom' is selling.

line.dialogue: The villager points towards the dark heart of the derelict city. The Groundless hold their sermons in the old resonance spire.

choices.line: Follow the villager's directions directly to the spire. (Straightforward approach)
choices.description: Press deeper into the corridor, recording resonance patterns with your tuning fork.

line.dialogue: The fork is vibrating now—faint, but there's something alive in here after all.
Nothing. The fork is dead in my hand. Whatever lived here is truly gone.

choices.line: Scout the perimeter of the settlement first, looking for resources or signs of what happened. (Cautious investigation)
choices.description: Signal Chanida to fall back while you and Pichit scout the chamber ahead.

line.dialogue: Fine. But if I hear anything—*anything*—I'm pulling you both out by your collars.
No. I'm not staying alone in this hallway. The silence behind me feels worse than what's ahead.

choices.line: Attempt to reactivate a small local resonator to get your bearings, despite the silence. (Technical attempt)
choices.description: Scratch a salvage marker into the wall and begin mapping for the Tonal Orders.

line.dialogue: Triple pay, and we're the first ones to chart it. This could fund the expedition for months.
The marker won't hold—the wall absorbs the chalk. Like this place wants to stay forgotten.

lines_before.dialogue: The interior of the derelict spire is a tomb of dead crystal. The air is stale, and every footstep is shockingly loud in the total absence of background resonance.
This architecture... it's designed to amplify sound, to focus it. Now it only amplifies the silence.
I don't see any preachers. I was cheated. That villager sent us on a dead-end trip!
Not quite. Look. Flicker-moss graffiti. 'The Song was a Cage.' 'Become Groundless.' Their manifesto is literally on the walls.
Scans show recent organic traces. They were here. Recently. The patterns suggest... waiting. Or hiding.
A low, scraping sound echoes from a higher balcony—not a resonance, but physical friction on crystal.
You should not have come. The Silence... it is not natural. It is a wound.
Who are you? Give it to me! The truth! What is this place?

lines_after.dialogue: I am a Listener. Or I was. I came to study the Silence. The Groundless... they found me. Their leader... she *speaks*, and the Silence... listens.
A Singer? Here? Are you finished yet? With your studies, I mean. Or did their preaching get to you too?
Finished? No. I am... conflicted. They say the Tonal Orders' charts are a swindle, a control. Here, with no song to follow... they say you find your own path.
And what do you believe?

line.dialogue: The Listener monk looks tormented. He gestures to a sealed archive door, then to a narrow service shaft leading deeper down.

choices.line: Press the monk to open the archive. He seems to know how. (Social pressure)
choices.description: Pichit attempts to test the prosthetic reaction, relying on Listener training

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The lattice has other plans. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Investigate the service shaft. The Groundless may have gone that way. (Pursuit)
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to rally the villagers, leveraging frequency mapping

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Chanida hits a wall. The escape tunnel collapses.

choices.line: Attempt to use a party member's latent resonance ability to 'feel' for the source of the Silence, despite the risk. (Dangerous resonance probing)
choices.description: The villager channels village secrets toward the unresponsive lattice, hoping to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: the villager finds the key. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
The attempt backfires on the villager. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The unnatural quiet of the Silent Zone presses in. The ground beneath your boots is unnervingly still—no vibration, no hum. Only the ragged sound of your own breathing.
I don't understand anything! Why would anyone want to live out here? It's like the world is holding its breath.
The Groundless pamphleteers called it 'liberation from the Lattice's song.' Looks more like a tomb to me.
Our resonator readings are flatlining. If we go much deeper, we might not find our way back. The charts are useless here.
This silence... it isn't empty. It's a different kind of presence. A weight. The Listeners must have records of this place.
We do. Forbidden ones. The Order calls it 'The Stillness'—a wound in the world-song from The Silencing. We were told to observe, never to question why it exists.
Some of us came out here with the Groundless folks. Said we'd build something free of the Tonal Orders' charts and fees. But the quiet... it gets inside you.
You still don't get it? This isn't freedom, it's a cage made of nothing!

lines_after.dialogue: A low, grinding tremor passes through the ground—not sound, but pure, sickening vibration. From a fissure ahead, a pale, crystalline structure begins to push its way to the surface.
Well. That's new. And undoubtedly bad.
It's not resonating. It's... absorbing. Like it's feeding on the absence.

line.dialogue: The silent growth pulses with a faint, stolen light. It feels deeply wrong.

choices.text: Investigate the structure cautiously. (Perception)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the tunnel wall and listen for vibrations through bone conduction.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the nothing, a pulse. Something vast is breathing down here, and every exhale swallows more of our frequency.
Nothing. My hand goes numb to the wrist. Whatever lives in this silence, it doesn't want to be found by touch alone.

choices.text: Attempt to provoke a resonance, to see if you can 'wake' the zone. (Daring)
choices.description: Deploy the resonator probe on a tether and reel it back to compare what returns versus what was sent.

line.dialogue: The return signal is... wrong. Same waveform, but the amplitude is inverted. This place doesn't just absorb sound — it turns it inside out and sends it back as its opposite.
The probe comes back empty. Not damaged, not silent — empty, like the concept of vibration was surgically removed from it while it was down there.

choices.text: Order a retreat and scout for the source of this growth from a distance. (Strategy)
choices.description: Hum the mnemonic tone Pichit taught you in the archive vault and see if the silence pushes back.

line.dialogue: It pushed back. The silence flexed against my hum like muscle against a wound. This isn't absence — it's a membrane, and we just confirmed there's something on the other side breathing against it.
I opened my mouth and forgot the tone. Not lost it — forgot that sound

lines_before.dialogue: You stand before the source: a vast, inverted crystal spire buried in the earth, its peak deep below. It doesn't sing. It *devours* sound, and around its base, the Silent Zone spreads like rot.
By the First Song... this is no natural formation. This was *made*. The records... they hinted, but I didn't want to understand. The Silencing wasn't an accident.
The Groundless leader... he's an old friend of mine. He said he found a 'truth' out here that would break the Orders' control. He went down there. He never came back.
Are you sure? Is that right? That this thing is actively killing the Lattice? If it grows, the floating cities will fall. Everything will fall.
Give it to me! The truth, I mean. The ugly, convenient lie the Tonal Orders built their monopoly on. They knew. They had to know.
So we break it! We shatter this stupid, quiet heart!

The truth is a weapon and a burden. We stand at the edge of a secret that could unmake our world... but I don't know where to begin. Do we destroy it and risk the unknown? Or try to contain it, and let the lie continue?
The anti-resonance from the spire intensifies. A deep, soundless ringing fills your bones. The Silent Zone is *hungry*, and you are the loudest thing in it.

lines_after.dialogue: The aftermath hangs in the dead air. The spire is still, for now. But the knowledge of what it is—and what was done to create it—changes everything.
My order will hear of this. The truth cannot be silenced again, no matter the cost.
We'll spread the word. The Groundless wanted freedom from control. Now we know the real price of that control.
The Lattice is wounded. We've just found the scar. The question is, do we heal it, or learn to live with the ache?

line.dialogue: The silent spire awaits your judgment. The fate of the truth, and perhaps the Lattice itself, rests on your choice.

choices.text: Shatter the spire. End the Silent Zone, whatever the consequences. (Conviction)
choices.description: Press your palm against the formation's surface and feel for its pulse.

line.dialogue: Malee — "It's warm. Gods help us, it's *breathing* — whatever this thing is, it's alive.
Malee — "Nothing. Cold stone. Either it's dead or it doesn't want us to know it's awake.

choices.text: Seal the fissure. Contain the threat, and return with the truth to confront the Tonal Orders. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Grab the villager by the shoulders and demand he take you to his Groundless friend now.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "He's shaking. Good — fear means he understands what's at stake. Move. We're going.
Arthit — "He won't look at me. 'I can't,' he whispers. Friendship won't save him from what's coming.

choices.text: Descend into the spire. Seek the lost Groundless leader and the full, terrible truth. (Sacrifice)
choices.description: Ask the monk to sing the First Song — the one that calmed the old sickness.

line.dialogue: Monk — "I haven't sung it since my master died. But if it can quiet this heart... I will try.
Monk — "The First Song is not a tool for the reckless. I won't waste it on guesses.

lines_before.dialogue: Phrao Monastery floats above the Lattice like a prayer held in suspension. The air hums with disciplined quiet—a silence so profound it feels like pressure.
It's too quiet. I can hear my own heartbeat. Makes me jumpy.
That's the point, Chanida. The Listeners maintain this acoustic purity to hear the Lattice's subtlest vibrations. We should tread carefully.
Tread carefully? They're monks, not trap-layers. Though I suppose faith can be its own kind of trap.
There is a reverence here... a seeking. I'm a Buddhist. I recognize the posture of devotion. But what are they devoted to? The song, or the silence around it?
You're the outsiders asking about the old frequencies? Look, most Thais are Buddhist, we respect the Listeners. But they guard their charts like dragon's gold. Don't stir up trouble.
Welcome, travelers. You seek knowledge of the Open Frequencies? The path to such maps is... fraught. The Tonal Orders say they are myth. We say they are memory.

lines_after.dialogue: Memory? So they were real! Where's the map?
Patience. The map is not a parchment. It is a resonance pattern, recorded in our oldest singing crystals. To access it... requires a certain attunement.
Attunement? You mean a Singer. But Singers are vanishingly rare. The Orders hunt them.
And if one were among us? What then?

line.dialogue: The monk's eyes hold a silent question. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Declare your purpose openly. (We seek the map to navigate freely.)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to harness harmonic feedback, drawing on forbidden paths

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Probe the monk's loyalties. (What do the Listeners believe about the Silencing?)
choices.description: Ask Malee to support the rebels, drawing on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The attempt backfires on Malee. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.line: Offer a gesture of respect. (We wish to learn, not to take.)
choices.description: Convince the monk to use lattice study and commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: the monk succeeds. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
A costly mistake by the monk. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk leads you deep into the monastery's harmonic core. Walls of singing crystal line the corridor, faintly glowing with captured light. The air thrums with latent sound.
Our archive. Each crystal stores a moment of perfect resonance. The Open Frequency Map... it's here. But it's fractured. Scattered across several records after the Silencing.

Let me guess. Putting it back together is against guild law. This is starting to feel like a forbidden epic. You know, the kind where the hero's the only son in the family carrying some doomed legacy.
This 'movie' is great! All mystery and hidden truths! You have to see it through!
This isn't entertainment, Chanida. It's a crime in the eyes of the Tonal Orders. A crime we're about to commit.
Knowledge should not be a crime. The monk is risking much to show us this. Why?
Because the Lattice's true song is fading. The Orders' controlled frequencies are... a cage. We Listen. We hear the strain. The map might show a way out.
He gestures to a central plinth where three crystal shards rest, inert. A fourth slot is empty.

lines_after.dialogue: Four shards were made. We have three. The fourth was taken years ago, by a Singer who fled. She said it was too dangerous to keep together.
So we find the fourth shard! It's a treasure hunt!
Or a wild goose chase set to a dramatic soundtrack. Where's the missing piece?
Hidden. She would have left a resonance clue—a sequence only another sensitive could follow. It would be in a place of natural, uncharted harmony.

line.dialogue: The clue points toward the monastery's most sacred, restricted space: The Chamber of First Echo.

choices.line: Ask the monk to guide you there officially. (Request an audience for study.)
choices.description: Touch the largest crystal and let the stored memory flood your mind directly.

line.dialogue: The images come clear — I see monks assembling these fragments in secret, and one face I recognize from the guild board.
My vision whites out, and when it clears the crystal has gone dark forever. Whatever it held is now lost.

choices.line: Sneak in after hours. (Use the monastery's acoustic routines as cover.)
choices.description: Ask the monk to explain which guild law specifically prohibits reassembling the crystals.

line.dialogue: So it's the Preservation Guild's decree — not law, just policy meant to keep fragments scattered. That means loopholes exist.
He won't talk. His hands are shaking and he keeps glancing at the door. Someone's already gotten to him.

choices.line: Create a sonic diversion. (Disrupt the ambient frequencies to mask your entry.)
choices.description: Quietly pocket one small crystal while Chan

line.dialogue: the villager makes it work. The islander's wisdom cuts through complexity.
the villager overreaches. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands in the monastery's inner sanctum. A massive, exposed section of the Lattice hums beneath a glass floor, its crystalline structure pulsing with faint light.
Our records... they are incomplete. The Tonal Orders provided the foundational frequencies, but our own observations show deviations. I don't know if this was deliberate obfuscation.
So the maps are wrong? The whole navigation system is built on a shaky foundation?
A dangerous revelation. How well do you know her, the High Cantor who certified these charts? Can we trust any of this?
Of course we can't. Monopoly 101: control the information, control the sky. They don't want anyone finding new routes, new islands. New power bases.
The truth vibrates just beneath the surface, waiting to be heard. But to what purpose was it buried?
I heard whispers... some ships using the old maps just... vanished. No wreckage. The Orders said it was pilot error. You think...?
We don't know when the divergence began. The data is fragmented. But the 'Open Frequency' you seek... it might be a correction. A true resonance.

lines_after.dialogue: The exposed Lattice reacts to the conversation, its hum shifting to a more discordant, anxious pitch.
The very stones are listening. We've stirred something.
Good. Let's stir it more. We need that true frequency!

line.dialogue: The Head Listener approaches, his face grave. 'To verify the true frequency requires a dangerous ritual: a direct, unshielded communion with the Lattice's core song. It has broken minds before. But there may be another way... a forbidden text in the sealed archives, if you dare the silence there.'

choices.text: Risk the mental communion. (Pichit's philosophical nature may provide resilience.)
choices.description: Search the monk's archives for the original Tonal Order charts before they were redacted, 15 words

line.dialogue: The monk presses his palms together. "I hid the true charts beneath the meditation hall. Even the Harmony Council cannot reach them there.
The monk shakes his head. "The original charts were burned decades ago. Whatever you hoped to find, the silence has already swallowed it.

choices.text: Brave the sealed archives. (Navigate physical and psychic traps of absolute silence.)
choices.description: Press Arthit to reveal what he knows about the Heretic Navigator and her connection to the corrupted maps, 15 words

line.dialogue: Arthit's jaw tightens. "She came to me three seasons ago, begging protection. I turned her away. That failure haunts every step we take now.
Arthit's expression shuts like a iron gate. "I owe you nothing, stranger. Ask your questions of someone who trusts you enough to bleed for them.

choices.text: Attempt both simultaneously, splitting the party. (Maximum risk for fastest results.)
choices.description: Have Malee forge false navigation data and leak it through three separate channels to expose who controls the monopoly, 15 words

line.dialogue: Malee grins, cracking her knuckles. "Three different versions, three different hands. Whoever reacts first is the spider sitting at
the villager loses control. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The sanctum is charged with energy. One group stands at the communion crystal, the other returns dusty and pale from the archives. The complete Open Frequency Map glows between them.
The archives... they weren't just sealed. They were censored. We've talked about this before—the Orders rewriting history. Whole resonance pathways were redacted.
And the communion... it showed me the Silencing. It wasn't an accident. It was a chord. A deliberate, catastrophic note.
A weapon. Used before. And the map... it's not just a navigation chart. It's a schematic of the world's resonant stability. The Orders aren't just gatekeepers. They're caretakers of a bomb.
Oh, you're here? Good. We've arrived at the precipice. The Head Listener has alerted the local Tonal Enforcers. They're coming to confiscate everything.
You have to understand before they get here! My family, everyone in the floating cities... we've never understood what we're floating on. You have to do something!
The choice is now yours. Use the map to flee—save the knowledge. Or use it here, now, to attempt a stabilizing counter-frequency. But the monastery may not survive the feedback.
The deep song of the Lattice swells, a rising pressure in the air. The first resonance ships of the Enforcers break the horizon, their warning horns blaring distorted chords.

lines_after.dialogue: The air itself seems to hold its breath. The fate of the map, the monastery, and perhaps the stability of the region hangs on a single, resonant decision.
Every note that came before has led to this moment. We do not act for ourselves alone, but for all the unheard songs.
Then let us choose wisely. Our next action will echo forever.

line.dialogue: The Enforcer ships descend, their hulls vibrating with aggressive, silencing frequencies. The Open Frequency Map pulses in your hands, a key to either escape or confrontation.

choices.text: Escape with the map. Preserve the truth for another day, but leave the monastery to its fate.
choices.description: Smash the resonance crystal against the map's sealed cartography to force the hidden routes visible.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "There — the veins beneath the ink, they're not rivers, they're wound-lines. Every one leads to the same depth.
Pichit — "The crystal shatters but the map drinks the light. Whatever's buried there, it doesn't want to be read. Not like this.

choices.text: Broadcast the map publicly. Flood the local resonance channels with the true frequencies, creating chaos to cover your escape.
choices.description: Ask Arthit directly what he gains from guiding four people toward a weapon that ended a civilization.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "I gain nothing. I already lost everything to the Silencing sixty years ago. I'm here to make sure it stops waking up.
Arthit — "You think I'm leading you? I'm following. The same way a shepherd follows sheep off a cliff — because the wolf is behind us all.

choices.text: Attempt the Stabilizing Chord. Use the monastery's acoustic focus to play the counter-frequency, risking everything to heal a fragment of the Lattice.
choices.description: Take Chanida's hand and ask her to share the communion vision again — this time with everyone connected.

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the monk. Ancient knowledge surfaces, connecting past and present.
the monk hits a wall. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hum with a low, pervasive drone, the sound of countless crystal shards vibrating in perfect, maintained harmony. Light filters through crystalline lattices, casting fractured rainbows across the polished stone floors.
Such a weight of knowledge... yet it feels like a cage. Every safe path charted, every resonance cataloged. Where is the room for discovery?
Discovery gets you killed, Pichit. Or worse, fined by the Tonal Orders. These charts are expensive. I didn't finish reading the last one we borrowed because the late fees were brutal.
Forget the charts! Give it to me! The real stuff, the lost frequencies! I heard there's a map here, one the Orders haven't locked down.
A map to where? The surface is unstable. We should stick to known routes.
*A figure emerges from behind a towering crystal data-spire, dust on their worn leathers.* You lot look like you're hunting trouble. Or treasure. Same thing, really.
*Smooth voice cuts through the hum.* Ah, prospective clients! I couldn't help but overhear. Knowledge of... unorthodox routes can be acquired. For a price, of course.
We seek understanding, not just profit. What do you know of the Open Frequency Map?

lines_after.dialogue: The Map? A fascinating relic. They say it charts the Lattice's natural resonance points, places where a skilled Singer could... improvise. The Tonal Orders would pay dearly to suppress it.
Suppress it? They'd shatter it. I've seen the surface. The old paths are still there, singing. But it's still cheap to think you can just walk out there.
We have to find it!

line.dialogue: The Scavenger and the Merchant exchange a look. The path to the map is unclear.

choices.line: Pay the Merchant for his information. (Spend resources)
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with resonant staff, ready to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The risk doesn't pay off. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.line: Convince the Scavenger to share their surface knowledge. (Persuasion check)
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to challenge skycity propaganda, leveraging hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The villagers rise with their agricultural tools.
Defeat. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.line: Search the Archives yourselves, using Pichit's philosophical insights. (Research check)
choices.description: Have the scavenger focus crystal fragments on the lost knowledge to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Hard-won survival skills turn the tide.
The lattice has other plans. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups in a secluded acoustic alcove. The ambient drone is softer here, allowing whispered conversations. Rainbows from a large overhead crystal prism dance across a stone table.
The Merchant's price was exorbitant. The Scavenger's directions are... vague. And our own search turned up nothing but restricted sections.
Told you. The price is the same everywhere: your safety, your savings, or your sanity. Take your pick.
We're close, I can feel it! The map is here! You, too, Scavenger! You want to see the old world, don't you?
I've seen it. It's really worth seeing! The crystal forests, the silent ruins... and the things that live there now. The price for that sight isn't coin.
*Approaching with a knowing smile.* My offer still stands. A partial transcription of the Map's last known location. A calculated risk.
A calculated suppression of truth. The Tonal Orders don't own the song of the world.
A low chime echoes through the Archives, signaling a shift in the resonators. Shadows lengthen as the crystalline light sources dim slightly.

lines_after.dialogue: The Archives are cycling. Security protocols will activate soon. We need to decide. Now.
The Merchant's 'calculated risk' is probably a trap. Or a fake. But it's the fastest lead.
My way is slower. More dangerous. But it's the truth I've walked with my own feet.

line.dialogue: Time is running out. The path to the Open Frequency Map splits.

choices.line: Buy the Merchant's transcription. Fast, but you trust his profit motive. (Acquire possibly flawed data)
choices.description: Trade your last medicine vial to the Scavenger for directions to the crystal vault.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger snatches the vial, holds it to the light, and grins. "Follow me. Stay close — the vault breathes.
The Scavenger tosses the vial back. "Empty. You think I got these scars trading for water? Come back with something that matters.

choices.line: Follow the Scavenger's cryptic surface-adjacent clues through the lower Archives. (Stealth/Navigation check)
choices.description: Grab Chanida's shoulder and demand she show you exactly where on the Merchant's map she sees the marker.

line.dialogue: Chanida's finger trembles as she traces a faded glyph near the map's edge. "There — see it? Three corridors past the flooded section.
Chanida wrenches free. "I don't answer to hands on me. I told you it's close. Either you trust that or you don't.

choices.line: Pichit insists on finding the Map's resonance frequency directly, using his innate connection to the Lattice. A pure, unguided attempt. (High-risk Resonance check)
choices.description: Whisper to Malee that you'll distract the Merchant while she slips behind the counter to copy the map.

line.dialogue: Malee's eyes flicker, then she smirks. "About time you started thinking like a survivor. Give me ninety seconds.
Malee grabs your collar. "Whisper that loud again and the Merchant hears it before I do. We do this clean or not at all.

lines_before.dialogue: The lower stacks of the Tonal Archives are a tomb of forgotten frequencies. The air is still, the crystalline walls absorbing all sound save for the party's tense whispers.
Great. A library where you can't even think loudly. I'm about to graduate from 'annoyed' to 'actively smashing crystals'.
Focus! The Scavenger said the old map fragment would be in this sector. You're not going anywhere until we find it, Malee.
The structural resonance here is unstable. A single wrong note could bring this entire wing down on our heads. Are you going to risk that?
Every silence holds a shape. We must listen for the gap in the recorded patterns—the frequency they deliberately omitted.
Psst. Over here. I see you're still poking around. You're not going to just walk out with it, are you? The Negotiator's got eyes everywhere.
Ah! I thought I might find fellow knowledge-seekers in the deep stacks. You're not going anywhere productive without the proper context, I hope?

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation leaves a ringing silence. The recovered map fragment hums faintly in Pichit's hand, its forbidden frequency a tangible weight.
Well, we've officially 'graduated' from nuisance to enemy of the state. Congratulations, class.
Save the lecture. We've got the key. Now we just need to survive long enough to use it.

line.dialogue: The Merchant blocks the only exit, his smile gone. The Scavenger looks ready to bolt or fight. The map fragment pulses. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Bargain. Offer the Merchant exclusive trade rights to whatever we find using the map.
choices.outcome: His greed overrides his caution. He creates a distraction, letting you slip past, but you now owe him a future debt.
choices.description: Signal the group to spread along the shelves and search by touch alone, no speaking, 15 words max

line.dialogue: Here — behind the codices. The fragment's real, and the Scavenger wasn't lying.
That shelf groaned. The whole eastern wall is shifting — we need to freeze. NOW.

choices.line: Deceive. Claim the fragment is a decoy and the real map is elsewhere, forcing a choice.
choices.outcome: The Scavenger, sensing an opportunity, backs your play, causing confusion. You escape in the chaos but make a powerful enemy in the Merchant.
choices.description: Have Pichit hum a single sustained note to find the gap in the silence, mapping it by echo

line.dialogue: The absence bends to the left. Something behind that wall is hungering for sound.
That's not an echo. That's a reply. Whatever's in here just learned our shape.

choices.line: Confront. Challenge the Merchant's authority to hoard knowledge that could save the Floating Cities.
choices.outcome: You appeal to the Archive's original purpose. The resonant crystals themselves seem to amplify your words, shaking the chamber and forcing a retreat. The act draws immediate, unwanted attention from the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Place your palm flat on the floor and feel for the vibration pattern of hidden chambers below

line.dialogue: Two hollows. One beneath us, one deeper still. The map fragment wants to be found.
You're bleeding from the ears. Whatever resonates through this stone — it isn't meant for human frequency.

lines_before.dialogue: You have reached the heart of the Archives: The Prime Resonator Chamber. A massive, flawless crystal dominates the space, etched with every 'safe' frequency. The air vibrates with suppressed power.
The containment field is buckling. Inputting the open frequency here… it's obvious that it will trigger a systemic cascade. We could unlock the Lattice, or shatter this city.
No more charts! No more paying the Orders' price! This is it! Which path do we choose, Pichit? The one they wrote, or the one we hear?
The guards are sealing the doors. So, is anyone home in that philosophical head of yours, or are we just going to stand here and look pretty while they arrest us?
Fools! You'll destroy the market! The stability! Without controlled knowledge, everything falls apart!
Don't listen to him! My people have lived and died on the surface, trapped by these walls! It's very clear that... we need to break the silence!
The Lattice is not a cage. It is a song waiting to be sung in full. We have listened to the whispers. Now, we must answer.

lines_after.dialogue: A profound, clean tone radiates from the Prime Resonator, not shattering it, but causing it to glow with internal light. Across the Archives, restricted crystal records illuminate, their knowledge becoming accessible.
In the distance, a deep, harmonic groan echoes from the Lattice surface below—a response. The world itself has heard the new frequency.

line.dialogue: The Open Frequency is now active in the world's resonance. The Tonal Orders are in disarray. The power is in your hands. What is the first command of this new song?

choices.line: Stabilize. Use the frequency to calm the Lattice, ensuring the Floating Cities' immediate safety and negotiating from a position of peace.
choices.outcome: You prevent panic and become indispensable mediators. The old system is challenged, not broken, leading to a slow, controlled reform.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to use the leg as a lattice probe, leveraging monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
A costly mistake by Pichit. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.line: Broadcast. Send the frequency out to all Listeners and potential Singers, democratizing navigation and breaking the guild's monopoly forever.
choices.outcome: You spark a revolution in travel and communication. New routes are discovered daily, but the sudden shift causes economic turmoil and power struggles in the cities.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to challenge skycity propaganda, drawing on singer voice

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
Things don't go as planned. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: Descend. Focus the frequency downward, parting the Lattice to reveal a glimpse of the lost Surface, no matter the risk.
choices.outcome: You tear a temporary window in the crystalline veil. The sight of the ancient world is breathtaking and horrifying, forever changing humanity's understanding of The Silencing and its own place in the world. The consequences are unknown.
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with valuable goods to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: the merchant finds the key. The merchant's ledger reveals the real story.
the merchant hits a wall. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard is a symphony of industrial decay. The groans of half-dismantled resonance ships mix with the rhythmic clang of salvage crews. The air shimmers with heat and the low, discordant hum of fractured Lattice crystals.
This place... it's a tomb for songs that failed. I guess so.
Focus, philosopher. The contact said the pirate would be by the old Storm-Catcher's hull. He probably has the frequency maps we need.
Or he's leading us into a trap. That's probably right. It's the Scrapyard, after all.
We should scout the perimeter first. I've analyzed the acoustics; that pile of resonator coils will mask our approach.
No time! The Tonal Order patrol probably won't be coming this deep into the yard, but I don't want to test that.
Chanida's probably right. Hesitation here just adds to the noise.
As you approach the designated hull, a figure detaches from the shadows—a sky pirate, her face scarred, a jagged resonator shard hanging from her neck.

lines_after.dialogue: You the suckers lookin' for a backdoor frequency? Cost you. And no, I ain't got no Tonal Order writ. They probably think I'm dead. Good.
Charming. Let's see the merchandise before we start haggling over your probably-stolen charts.
I must advise caution. Unverified frequencies could destabilize our ship's crystal core.

line.dialogue: The pirate offers a cracked data-crystal. 'The song's in there. Payment first.'

choices.line: Pay the asking price. (Spend resources for a straightforward deal.)
choices.description: Hack the graveyard's audio sensors to triangulate the pirate's signal before moving in.

line.dialogue: I've locked onto a distorted carrier wave — he's broadcasting from the eastern catacomb shaft, exactly where the contact promised.
The signal's bouncing off every dead resonance chamber in here — I'm reading fifty phantom sources and none of them are real.

choices.line: Challenge her authenticity. (Intimidate or bluff for a better deal/verification.)
choices.description: Send Malee ahead through the crooked headstones to flush out any ambush positions.

line.dialogue: Three shooters nested behind the broken bass monuments — I counted their breathing before they ever counted mine. We go around.
I stepped on a pressure chime and the whole graveyard sang — whoever's waiting out there now knows exactly where all four of us are standing.

choices.line: Offer a trade of equivalent salvage from the yard. (Barter using the environment.)
choices.description: Play the forbidden frequency the contact gave you — let the graveyard's dead songs call the pirate out.

line.dialogue: Listen... the silence between the notes just answered. Someone deep in the tombs is humming our melody back to us.
I played the frequency wrong and woke something older than the pirate — every failed song in this place just started playing at once, and I can't hear anything else.

lines_before.dialogue: The transaction is interrupted by the resonant chime of a prayer bell. A Listener monk steps from behind a corroded engine block, his grey robes stark against the rust.
Please, stop. We've talked about this before, the danger of these stolen songs.
You! I told you no one wants to go back to your dusty spire. Scram!
Great. A moral crisis. We're on a schedule here.
Wait. His concern seems genuine. A Listener here, in this place?
I study the fractures. The Lattice's song here... it is pained. These pirate frequencies are like screaming in a sacred space. They cause harm.
Harm is a relative term. We require navigation, not a sermon.
It is more than that. I have heard a new strain in the world-song. A warning. Using this,
he gestures to the pirate's crystal, 'will draw attention. From the Lattice itself. We're talked before, you pirates, about the Silencing. You never listen.'

lines_after.dialogue: He's spookin' you! The Lattice don't care. It's just crystal. My charts work. No one's gotten dead from my tunes.
Famous last words. But the monk's more persistent than anyone I've seen down here. There's a story.
A warning... The Silencing happened before. Could it happen again?

line.dialogue: The pirate holds the crystal. The monk pleads with his eyes. The scrapyard's din feels suddenly ominous.

choices.line: Take the crystal from the pirate anyway. (Proceed with the original mission, ignoring the warning.)
choices.description: Step between the monk and bandit, demanding the monk explain what danger he means.

line.dialogue: The Shadowless Brethren don't send monks into the Pit for idle chatter—speak plainly, brother.
I barely got the words out before the bandit shoved me aside—some mediator I am.

choices.line: Demand the monk explain his 'warning' in detail. (Investigate the subplot, delaying the deal.)
choices.description: Grab the bandit's shoulder and tell him to shut up so the monk can finish.

line.dialogue: Surprisingly, the oaf listened—maybe he's smarter than he looks, or just scared of me.
He shrugged me off like a fly and drew his knife—so much for intimidation.

choices.line: Try to forge a temporary truce, getting the crystal *and* the monk's insight. (Diplomacy to satisfy both parties.)
choices.description: Quietly circle behind the monk while the others argue, checking if he's alone or has backup.

line.dialogue: No one behind him. Either he's truly alone or his friends are better than me—and I doubt that.
I stepped on a loose stone and half the tunnel heard me—stealth has never been my gift.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in the canyon of broken ships, under the metallic groan of cranes, the Listener Monk leads you to a derelict hull. Its resonator crystal glows with a faint, irregular pulse.
Here. The Lattice's song... it's not a song anymore. It's a warning. I had a bad dream that showed me this place.
A dream? That's really easy to guess! The whole place is a nightmare!
The crystal's resonance is unstable. If this frequency spreads... it could destabilize other ships.
What is it warning us about, Monk? The Silencing happening again?
The Tonal Orders' charts... they are not just maps. They are filters. They silence parts of the song. Parts that speak of a coming fracture.
Of course they are. Knowledge is power, and power is profit. It's my dream job for them—controlling everything.
A shadow falls across the salvage. The Sky Pirate and her crew drop from a rusted gantry, cutlasses gleaming.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate grins, her hand on her weapon. 'That crystal's worth a fortune unstable. Hand it over, or we'll take it from the wreckage that used to be you.'

choices.text: [EASY: Intimidate] Use the Lattice's unstable song as a threat.
choices.leads_to: intimidate
choices.description: Direct Arthit to use the leg as a lattice probe using ship navigation

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Arthit loses control. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: [MEDIUM: Barter] Offer a trade—information on a safer salvage site.
choices.leads_to: barter
choices.description: Malee channels mechanical repair toward the broken ships, hoping to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
Malee fails. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: [HARD: Confront] Fight to protect the crystal and the Monk's discovery.
choices.leads_to: confront
choices.description: The pirate takes the lead, employing pirate ship to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. A secret frequency from the underworld shifts the balance.
A costly mistake by the pirate. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_after.dialogue: The scrapyard holds its breath. The clanging machinery seems to fade against the tense standoff.
This isn't just about salvage. It's about listening to a truth everyone else is trying to drown out.
The dream... it showed me this choice. A path splitting like a fractured crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The confrontation resolves, leaving the derelict hull echoing with aftermath. The unstable crystal's pulse grows stronger, thrumming through the metal deck.
The frequency is building. If we don't stabilize or contain it, the resonance could shear this entire scrapyard from its moorings.
He's an old friend of mine, trouble. Always shows up uninvited!
Are you sure? Is that right? That we can even fix this? The Tonal Orders probably have a protocol for this, locked away in some vault.
Protocols to hide it. Not to heal it. The Lattice is crying out. We must answer—not with charts, but with understanding.
The Monk is right. We've been given a warning. To ignore it would be to fail everyone floating on these islands.
The crystal flares, casting jagged shadows. A deep, subsonic groan issues from the Lattice below, vibrating the very plates beneath your feet. The scrapyard itself feels like it might come apart.

line.dialogue: The crystal's resonance is reaching a critical peak. You have moments to decide how to address the Lattice's warning cry.

choices.text: [EASY: Contain] Use the ship's resonator to dampen the frequency, saving the scrapyard but silencing the message.
choices.leads_to: contain
choices.description: Malee channels leg resonance toward the engine parts, hoping to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: [MEDIUM: Harmonize] Have Chanida attempt to sing a counter-frequency, a risky attempt to stabilize the crystal without losing the data.
choices.leads_to: harmonize
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing tonal knowledge to uncover the suppression

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The villagers rise with their agricultural tools.
Pichit misreads the situation. The escape tunnel collapses.

choices.text: [HARD: Amplify] Let the crystal shatter, releasing the full, unfiltered warning to anyone listening across the Lattice.
choices.leads_to: amplify
choices.description: The pirate steps forward with smuggling routes, ready to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The echo fades to silence.

lines_after.dialogue: The air shimmers with spent energy. The outcome of your choice ripples out, silent but profound.
Sometimes, a friend tells you a hard truth. And sometimes, the world itself does.
The song... it is changed now. As are we.

lines_before.dialogue: The first light of dawn paints the Resonance Ship's deck in hues of rose and gold. Below, the crystalline Lattice shimmers with the low, waking hum of morning frequencies. The air is crisp with promise.
A new day. The Lattice's song feels... clearer this morning. Like it's in a good mood.
Good night? More like a good morning to finally get moving! I can't wait to see what's over the next ridge.
Optimism before breakfast. How refreshing. Let's hope the pay for this 'exploration' is actually good.
We should run a full diagnostic on the resonators first. Morning stability can be deceptive.
A low, mournful tone, distinct from the ship's engine, vibrates through the deck plating. It comes from the mist ahead.
Do you hear that? It's not one of ours.
Is that... another ship? It sounds lost.

lines_after.dialogue: A ghostly silhouette of a derelict Resonance Ship materializes from the dawn mist, its crystal drives pulsing with a faint, erratic light. Its hull is scored with old burns.
By the Founders... that's the 'Echo's Lament.' It was lost during The Silencing. Its resonance signature shouldn't be possible.
Well, there's our interesting morning. A phantom ship. Just what we needed.

line.dialogue: The lost ship hangs in the air, a silent invitation. Its anomalous frequency is a mystery.

choices.line: Approach cautiously on low power. (Caution)
choices.description: Calibrate the resonators yourself before anyone touches them, working by the lattice-light alone.

line.dialogue: Already done — I couldn't sleep anyway, so I tuned them to the dawn frequency. We're sharp as a blade.
I tried calibrating solo, but my hands were shaking too much. Arthit's right — we do this properly, together.

choices.line: Attempt to match its erratic frequency to get a clearer scan. (Technical)
choices.description: Skim across the rooftop stones to listen where the Lattice's song echoes strongest, mapping its pulse.

line.dialogue: Here — the resonance pools beneath the eastern eaves like rainwater. If we anchor here, we'll hear it clearer than ever.
I leapt too fast, scattered the echo before I could trace it. Whatever the Lattice is trying to say, it'll have to wait.

choices.line: Hail it on all channels. Someone might be alive in there. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Pull Chanida aside and ask honestly whether last night's vigil revealed anything she hasn't shared yet.

line.dialogue: You noticed too, then. The song shifted at third bell — something new woven into it. I didn't want to panic everyone before breakfast.
She shut me down hard. Said I should worry about my own sleepless nights before interrogating hers. Fair hit, honestly.

lines_before.dialogue: The party's ship holds position a hundred yards from the derelict. The ghostly vessel emits no response to hails, only that same low, looping tone. Its deck is empty.
Scans are inconclusive. The hull is reading, but life signs are... scrambled. Where did you lose your crew, old ship?
We have to board it. I insist! There could be survivors, or salvage, or... answers!
Or a hull breach waiting to happen. I'm trying to lose weight, not my atmosphere.
The tone... it's not just noise. It's a pattern. A memory of a course, locked in the crystal.
A smaller, agile vessel suddenly drops from a cloud bank above, its hull bristling with jury-rigged resonator spikes. It blocks the path to the derelict.
Well, well! Look what the dawn coughed up! That ghostie is ours, see? We know its hidden frequencies. Hand over your nav-charts and we might let you drift away.
Like hell we will!

lines_after.dialogue: Before the standoff can escalate, a simple, unadorned skiff glides between the two ships. A figure in grey Listener robes stands at its prow.
Please, cease this discord! That vessel... it sings a song of great sorrow. A truth from before The Silencing. I'm glad to know others have heard its call, but it is not a prize to be fought over.
A monk! Spare us the lecture. The truth don't fill the coffers.
What truth, Listener?

line.dialogue: The pirate ship powers its weapons. The Listener looks torn. The derelict's tone shifts, becoming more urgent.

choices.line: Focus fire on the pirate's resonator array to disable them. (Combat)
choices.description: Suit up and breach the hull manually through the cargo bay doors.

line.dialogue: Pressure's holding. Cargo bay's intact — we have a way in. Move fast, stay paired.
The seal blew the moment I touched it. Decompression alarm is screaming — pull me back, pull me back NOW!

choices.line: Quickly decipher the derelict's shifting tone—it might be a key or a weapon. (Intuition)
choices.description: Isolate the audio pattern Pichit detected and run it through the linguistic database.

line.dialogue: It's old — pre-Collapse era encoding. Someone embedded a distress loop in the hull's vibration signature. They wanted to be found.
The pattern dissolved into static the moment I tried to isolate it. Whatever it was, it just went silent. Like it knew we were listening.

choices.line: Appeal to the Listener's duty. Urge them to use their knowledge to calm both the ghost ship and the pirates. (Persuasion)
choices.description: Launch a tethered probe through the gap in the starboard scanner array before committing anyone.

line.dialogue: Probe is inside. I'm reading breathable atmosphere on deck two and... something moving. Thermal signature, faint but rhythmic.
Probe fed back seventeen seconds of corridor footage before something severed the tether. The last frame shows a shadow that doesn't match any crew silhouette.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship cuts through the Lattice's shimmering surface. Below, ghostly echoes of the lost ship's frequency pulse like a dying heartbeat.
The pirate's charts show the coordinates, but what do you think about that distortion pattern? It's like the Lattice is... wounded here.
He's only interested in salvage. The 'treasure' he mentioned. I think that's right. Not some noble quest for truth.
The harmonic readings are unstable. If we follow the echo too deeply, we might not find our way back. I think it is a trap, or a tomb.
The Lattice remembers everything. That lost ship... its final moments are etched here. What do you think about listening, truly listening, to what it's trying to say?
This is forbidden knowledge. The Tonal Orders would silence this frequency forever. I think that's the one... the true reason for the Silencing. It wasn't an accident.
Enough chatter! The wreck's just ahead, singing its sad little song. I think so. Time to see what shiny bits it left behind.
A spectral shape materializes from the crystalline mist—the ghostly hull of a ancient resonance ship, its resonator arrays still faintly glowing.

line.dialogue: The ghost ship's main resonator chamber is accessible, but pulsing with unstable energy. A direct path leads inside, but the surrounding lattice formations look fragile.

choices.text: Approach directly. The clearest path is often the simplest.
choices.description: Override the harmonic stabilizers and follow the echo's source coordinates directly.

line.dialogue: I've locked the resonance frequency — the Lattice is opening a corridor, but hold onto something.
The harmonics collapsed — we're broadcasting our position to everything within a thousand kellicks.

choices.text: Scale the lattice spires. Use the natural crystal structures for cover and a higher vantage point.
choices.description: Offer the pirate captain a share of the salvage in exchange for his transponder codes.

line.dialogue: He bit. Codes are valid — we can approach the wreck masked as his salvage tender.
He wanted exclusivity. Now he's hailing his consortium and we're locked out entirely.

choices.text: Match the ghost ship's frequency. Attempt to harmonize with its dying song to calm the energy.
choices.description: Touch the Lattice fragment and let it show you what happened to the lost ship.

line.dialogue: I see them — the crew, their final moments — the Lattice kept everything, every scream, every coordinate.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice made, the air grows heavy with anticipation. The ghost ship's song rises in pitch, becoming a lament that vibrates in the bones.
It's reacting to us! The whole lattice is... I think that's the one. It's a memory, playing on a loop.
A memory of betrayal. I think that's right. The logs we found... the ship was scuttled. Purposely.
The subplot thickens: The Echo of the Lost Ship reveals itself not as a victim of the Lattice, but of a conspiracy. Its final broadcast—a warning about the Tonal Orders—was forcibly silenced.

lines_before.dialogue: Within the ghost ship's core, a massive primary resonator crystal floats, cracked and bleeding light. It holds the recorded truth. Pirate and Monk face each other, motives laid bare.
That's it! The motherlode! That crystal's worth ten skycities. Don't just stand there—lift it carefully! We can still get it out before this whole memory collapses!
No! You would destroy the evidence! That crystal is a testament. The truth must resonate, not be sold for scraps!
Interesting. So the pirate wants the treasure, and the monk wants the sermon. And we're caught in the middle. He hung up on the idea of compromise the moment we arrived.
The structural frequency is degrading. If we remove the crystal, the memory destabilizes instantly. If we try to play the recording... the energy surge might shatter our own ship.
There she is! The answer! Look—the crystal isn't just recording. It's still transmitting. On a loop. Someone... or something... is still listening on the other end.
A voice, unheard for generations, waiting for a reply. Do we silence it forever for profit? Do we broadcast it and risk everything? Or do we answer it?
The ghost ship's hull begins to dissolve into motes of light. The pirate draws a sonic blade. The monk braces at the resonator console. The choice is now.

line.dialogue: The climax: The crystal holds the proof of the Tonal Orders' ancient crime and a faint, repeating hailing signal. The pirate moves to grab it. The monk moves to play the broadcast fully.

choices.text: Seize the crystal. Secure the 'treasure' and flee. Let the past bury its own secrets. (Aligns with Pirate)
choices.description: Anchor the crystal with restraint wire before anyone touches it. (15 words)

line.dialogue: Wire holding — the frequency stabilizes. Now negotiate before I negotiate for all of us.
The wire snapped on contact — harmonic backlash, everyone back from the resonance field NOW!

choices.text: Activate the broadcast. Unleash the truth across the Lattice for all to hear, come what may. (Aligns with Monk)
choices.description: Let the bandit pry it free while you shield the monk from debris. (14 words)

line.dialogue: The crystal's out and the ceiling holds — for now. Bandit, you owe me a drink and an explanation.
The ceiling is coming down between us and the exit — the bandit's greed just buried us all.

choices.text: Answer the signal. Harmonize with the crystal's core frequency and establish contact with whatever has been listening all this time.
choices.description: Harmonize your voice to the crystal's frequency and sing it loose intact. (14 words)

line.dialogue: The crystal released without fracture — the evidence sings, and so do I. Praise be.
Your pitch cracked the lattice — we've lost the evidence AND angered whatever slept inside that crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision echoes through the crystal. A final, brilliant pulse of light—then silence. The ghost ship is gone. Only the consequences remain.
The subplot resolves: The Echo of the Lost Ship is laid to rest. Its truth is either commodified, weaponized, or transformed into a new, uncertain dialogue.
Well. That was interesting. We've either made a powerful enemy, a powerful friend, or just pissed off everyone who likes the status quo. Business as usual.
The resonance ship turns away from the empty space. The Lattice below seems different now—no longer just a tool or a hazard, but a witness. And it remembers everything.

lines_before.dialogue: The *Resolute Echo* hums through a low-hanging mist, its resonance engine thrumming a steady A-minor chord. Below, the crystalline Lattice glimmers like a frozen, fractured sea.
I swear the mist is thicker than yesterday. Can barely see the bow. Makes my skin crawl.
Relax. It's just condensed atmospheric resonance. Probably. Unless it's a Lattice bloom. Then we're all delicately, beautifully dead.
Let's not jump to conclusions. The charts from the Tonal Orders don't indicate any volatile zones here. Our course is clear.
Charts are interpretations of past echoes. The Lattice is a living thing. Its song changes.
A sharp, discordant ping rings from the port side. A small, battered skiff emerges from the mist, its hull scarred from surface travel.
Ahoy the *Echo*! You're off the sanctioned frequencies. That's a costly mistake for sky-farers.

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal Orders charge you for safe passage. I charge you for *not* telling them you're here. Call it a lattice-tax.
What about tomorrow? If we pay you today, does that buy silence for the next sunrise too? Or is this a daily fee?
Please translate that for me. You speak of prices, but what is the real cost? Your silence, or our compliance?

line.dialogue: The scavenger's hand rests on a crude sonic discharger. 'My price is simple. Supplies. Food, spare crystal shards. Or I sing a little song to the nearest Order patrol.'

choices.text: Pay the toll. Hand over some of your ship's supplies. (Lose resources, avoid conflict.)
choices.description: Direct Pichit to tune the prosthetic using resonant staff

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit is thwarted. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Bluff. Claim you're on a secret mission for a sympathetic Tonal Master. (Risk persuasion.)
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing singer voice to support the rebels

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida misreads the situation. The villagers' courage breaks.

choices.text: Refuse. Prepare for a potential fight. (Risk damage to the ship.)
choices.description: Direct the scavenger to follow the phantom route using crystal fragments

line.dialogue: the scavenger makes it work. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the scavenger overreaches. A scavenging tool breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Having dealt with the scavenger, the *Echo* pushes deeper into the mist. The ambient hum of the Lattice shifts, becoming a complex, layered chorus.
Is it real? This sound... it's not on any chart I've ever seen. It's beautiful and it's making my fillings ache.
It's a natural harmonic convergence. Rare, but documented. However, it can mask other signals. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Let's get to it! If this is uncharted, there could be pure resonance nodes down there. Worth a fortune!
Or it could be a place the Listeners spoke of—a 'Memory Knot' in the Lattice. The past might be singing here.
A distorted, aggressive frequency cuts through the harmony. A larger, jagged-hulled ship decloaks from the mist abeam, its decks crowded with rough figures.
Well, well. Fancy findin' a little songbird like you in a silent patch. You're lost.
Sky pirates! Don't let them see you! Everyone, get low!

lines_after.dialogue: We heard your little chat with the surface-rat. Looked like you paid easy. Means you've got more. Hand over your core resonator, nice and slow.
Let's go inside. To the bridge. We can seal the hatches and maybe overload a harmonic to shake them off.
Their ship is bigger, but clumsier in these convergences. We might outmaneuver them if we dive toward the lattice surface.
They are predators of opportunity. But even predators listen to a new song. What if we offered them something better than plunder?

line.dialogue: The pirate ship's forward crystal lances begin to glow with a predatory hum. You have moments to act.

choices.text: Flee inside. Seal the ship and attempt a risky resonance overload to escape. (Technical challenge.)
choices.description: Malee channels scavenger instincts toward the deck wind, hoping to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Outmaneuver. Use the complex harmonics to navigate where their larger ship cannot follow. (Piloting challenge.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to challenge skycity propaganda, drawing on resonant staff

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Things don't go as planned. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Parley. Broadcast an offer—share the location of this 'Memory Knot' for safe passage. (Diplomacy/Risk revealing subplot_groundless interests.)
choices.description: The pirate takes the lead, employing secret frequencies to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the pirate loses control. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship shudders violently as it descends toward a massive crystalline spire jutting from the Lattice—a known scavenger outpost. The air hums with a low, discordant frequency.
Are we sure this is where the Groundless signal originated? This place gives me the creeps. I can feel the vibrations in my teeth.
The coordinates are precise. But we must be cautious. Scavengers are territorial, and this spire is uncharted by the Orders.
Terrific. So we're trespassing in a place no one sane maps. Remind me why we're following a signal from a group that wants to dismantle society?
Because they might understand the Lattice's true voice. The Orders hear only commerce. The Listeners hear only prayer. But the Groundless... they might hear what's underneath.
(Emerging from a hatch, covered in crystal dust) You're a long way from your gilded cities. What's a Singer doing down here in the grit?
We're looking for the source of a signal. A call for... change.

Change. That's a word that gets people killed. You think you can just waltz in? I've bad eyesight from years down here, but I see your ship clear enough. You didn't build that. You didn't forge its crystals. I did it all myself—this outpost, my tools. Outsiders just take.

lines_after.dialogue: The signal you're chasing... it's not a beacon. It's a trap. The Groundless aren't philosophers. They're pirates now. They've allied with sky-bandits to hijack ships. They're using that signal to lure Tonal Order vessels.
A rebellion turned to piracy. How shockingly predictable.
We have to stop them! If they hijack a major resonator, they could destabilize a whole city!
The Scavenger is right. This is a trap. But for whom? The signal led *us* here. Not an Order ship.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points to a derelict resonance barge tethered to the far side of the spire—the likely pirate base. 'They're watching. You go that way, you're seen.'

choices.text: Use the Scavenger's hidden tunnels. ('I know a path through the crystal veins. I'll get it open for you.')
choices.consequence: Stealthy approach; avoid initial patrols.
choices.description: Channel your resonance into the corroded gateway, forcing it open before the stabilization field collapses, 12 seconds

line.dialogue: The lattice is screaming—I can feel it thrumming through my teeth, but the door is *yielding*.
The feedback just bit me—my fingers are numb and the gate sealed itself tighter than before.

choices.text: Create a sonic diversion with the ship's resonator. ('Overload a harmonic frequency to draw them out.')
choices.consequence: Draws attention, splits their forces; risky for the ship.
choices.description: Follow Pichit's instinct and press your bare palm against the whispering wall to let the Lattice read your intentions

line.dialogue: It *knows* us. The wall went warm and I can hear fragments—thousands of voices pressed together like pages of a book.
Well, that was horrifying—Pichit's hand went gray and the wall actually *flinched* away from us.

choices.text: Approach openly under a parley flag. ('We are not the Order. We wish to talk.')
choices.consequence: Direct confrontation with leaders; high risk of immediate capture.
choices.description: Deploy the signal tracer in silence and triangulate the Groundless source before whatever lives here wakes up

line.dialogue: Three pings, clean triangle—the signal's coming from directly below us, maybe forty meters down into something hollow.
the scavenger fails. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The party reaches the command deck of the pirate barge. It's a chaotic nest of rewired resonators and stolen Order charts. At the center stands the Sky Pirate leader and a Groundless ideologue—a woman with fierce, tired eyes.
Well, well. The Singer and his choir. We thought the signal might catch a smaller fish, but you'll do. Your ship's resonator is just what we need for the big strike.
This isn't the way. Hijacking, piracy—you're becoming the monster you fight.

The Tonal Orders are the monsters! They hoard the knowledge of the sky, let cities starve while they tax resonance paths! My brother... he used to be a sickly child. The Orders denied him medical resonance because our city couldn't pay the toll. He died listening to the ships we couldn't afford pass overhead.
A tragic story. Doesn't justify murdering crews and stealing ships.
Justify? Hah! The world's a parking lot, and there weren't any parking spaces left for us! We're taking ours!
You're not parking anything—you're going to crash the whole system!
Their primary resonator is overloading. If they engage the drive sequence now, the feedback could shatter the Lattice for miles.

lines_after.dialogue: The barge shudders as its stolen heart crystal flares to life. A dangerous, shrieking frequency builds, threatening to crack the world below.
You see? The old song must break before a new one can be sung!
No. A song isn't forced. It's found. Listen... beneath the scream. The Lattice is weeping.

Pichit closes his eyes. He doesn't shout over the frequency. He weaves his voice into it, a counter-harmony of profound sorrow, remembering the Scavenger's self-reliance, the Leader's lost sibling, the Pirate's desperate greed. The shrieking resonance begins to falter, then harmonize, then still.
The crystal dims. The immediate danger passes. But the choice of what comes next hangs in the silent air, heavier than any engine's hum.

line.dialogue: The barge is neutralized, but the Groundless and Pirates are defeated, not reconciled. The Scavenger watches from a distance. The Lattice below seems to hold its breath.

choices.text: Turn them over to the Tonal Orders. (Uphold the law, ensure punishment.)
choices.consequence: Order is restored, but the cycle of resentment continues. The Groundless movement is martyred.
choices.description: Chanida uses unauthorized tones to use the leg as a lattice probe near the sails

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Chanida is thwarted. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Let them go, but scatter them and destroy their barge. (Mercy, but no threat.)
choices.consequence: Lives spared, but the ideology scatters like seeds on the wind. Unpredictable future.
choices.description: Arthit channels captain experience toward the deck wind, hoping to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
Defeat. The villagers' courage breaks.

choices.text: Offer them a place, and their story, to the Listeners. (Seek understanding, not judgment.)
choices.consequence: A risky, radical bridge between factions. Could reform or destabilize everything.
choices.description: The pirate presses forward with disruptor weapon to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
the pirate fails. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard is a symphony of industrial decay. The air shudders with the groan of metal being sheared and the percussive clang of hammers. Piles of broken resonance ships rise like jagged mountains against the bruised sky.
Every broken resonator here... it's a story ended. A journey cut short by the Lattice. Can I take a break for a moment? The dissonance in this place is heavy.
Philosophizing won't find our contact. Look for the one-legged scrapper. In a place that eats ships, a man with a crystal leg should stand out. If he hasn't been melted down for parts.
Over there! That gantry! I saw a glint! Let's go!
Chanida, wait! The structural integrity of that pile is... questionable. We should proceed with caution.
You lot look lost. The yard-master doesn't like gawkers. Best move along.
We seek knowledge, not trouble. A man with a unique prosthetic. We were told he works here.
Old Kiet? Yeah, he's around. Keeps to the deep stacks. But I have no one to help me with my own haul, so I can't guide you. Can I? You understand.

lines_after.dialogue: Charming. Everyone here has a price, even for directions. Let's just follow the sound of someone who isn't trying to sell us scrap.
I'm detecting a faint, stable resonance signature... west of here. It's out of sync with the yard's chaos. That could be our target.
See? A little noise is good! Lead on, Arthit!

line.dialogue: The party locates the source: a small shelter built into the hull of a derelict ore-hauler. A figure is inside, tinkering with a device that hums softly. How do you approach?

choices.line: Call out a friendly greeting from a distance. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Sprint across the debris field to reach the gantry before the structure shifts further.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "I told you I saw something! Hands up, whoever's hiding up there — we found you!
Arthit — "I said the integrity was compromised! Now we're all buried under half a ton of scrap metal!

choices.line: Send Chanida ahead to quickly peek inside. (Stealth)
choices.description: Climb carefully through the resonator shells, using them as cover to approach unseen.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Quiet, precise, no wasted movement — this is how professionals locate a contact without getting shot.
Pichit — "A resonator just collapsed under me... I think I've added my own story to this graveyard.

choices.line: Have Arthit analyze the harmonic signature of the prosthetic first. (Lore)
choices.description: Signal Chanida to hold position while you scan the gantry with your frequency detector first.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Readings confirm one lifeform, stable footing on the east platform — now we move, with information.
Malee — "The signal bounced everywhere and now whoever was up there is gone — hesitation costs contacts, people.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the makeshift workshop, Old Kiet is a wiry man with a leg of fused, cloudy crystal that pulses with a faint inner light. He eyes the party warily over his workbench.
Kiet's voice is gravelly, worn smooth by years of yard-dust. 'The Tonal Orders send their lackeys now? To collect an old man's leg?'
We are not with the Orders. We seek understanding. Your prosthetic... it resonates with the Lattice's natural frequency. It's very important that we learn its origin.
He’s an old friend of mine from the Listeners' archive. In a manner of speaking. His name came up in records about... experimental integrations. Before the Silencing.
The crystalline matrix is non-standard. It doesn't match any known resonator schematics. It's organic. Grown.
You have sharp ears. It was a gift. From a Singer. Nobody knows what truly happened during the Silencing... but the Singers did. They tried to warn us.
A Singer gave you a leg? What happened to them?
Lost. Like all the true Singers. The Orders hunted them after the catastrophe. Said their 'uncontrolled' songs caused it. I was just an engineer they trusted. This leg... it's my reminder.

lines_after.dialogue: A living memory of a lost art. And you've hidden here, in the noise, so its song wouldn't be found.
Sentimental. And dangerous. If the Orders knew this existed, this whole scrapyard would be glass.
They might already. A Trade Negotiator was sniffing around yesterday. Asked about 'unique salvage.' Smiled too much. Didn't like his resonance.

line.dialogue: Kiet's revelation changes everything. The Negotiator's interest means the secret is already in play. What is the party's immediate priority?

choices.line: Convince Kiet to come with us to a safer location immediately. (Persuasion)
choices.description: Chanida uses frequency mapping to harness harmonic feedback near the salvage

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Chanida loses control. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Have Kiet disable the prosthetic's resonance to hide it, while you scout for the Negotiator. (Crafting/Stealth)
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with ship navigation, ready to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Things don't go as planned. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.line: Use the prosthetic's unique resonance as bait to draw out and confront the Negotiator on your terms. (Confrontation)
choices.description: Have the villager focus local knowledge on the broken ships to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: the villager's expertise pays off. Terrace-hardened resilience sees them through.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: In the heart of the scrapyard, a derelict Resonance Ship's hull creaks under its own weight. The air smells of ozone and rust.
The lattice scars on this hull... they sing of a violent impact. It's not scary at all! It's a testament to survival.
Let's get inside! I bet the core resonator is still intact. This salvage could fund the prosthetic for months!
Or it could be a Tonal Order trap. They don't just abandon ships with viable crystals. It was a good experience last time we got ambushed?
The structural integrity is questionable. We should map the weak points first. A collapse here would be... final.
Ah, my friends! I see you've found the 'Whispering Wreck.' A fascinating piece. Its logs might contain... unlicensed navigation data.
Data the Orders would bury. To remember is to resist.
A low, resonant hum begins to emanate from the ship's cracked crystal array. The surrounding lattice fragments glow faintly.

lines_after.dialogue: The hum stabilizes, revealing a hidden compartment behind the resonator. A single, pulsing crystal core lies within.
A core. Untouched. This is a miracle.
We take it! This is exactly what the prosthetic needs! The resonance frequency could sync with a living limb!

line.dialogue: The core is loose, but extracting it risks triggering the ship's failing stabilizers. The merchant watches intently.

choices.text: Cut power lines first. Methodical and safe, but time-consuming.
