choices.consequences: Secures the core slowly; the merchant grows impatient and may raise his price.
choices.description: Force entry through the resonator hatch before the harmonic decay destabilizes the hull further.

line.dialogue: Core resonator's still humming — I can feel it in my teeth, we're not too late!
The whole frame just shrieked — that hatch is warped shut, we'll never pry it open now.

choices.text: Use Chanida's resonance dampener. Quick, but drains her tool's charge.
choices.consequences: Fast extraction; Chanida's tool is depleted for future encounters.
choices.description: Deploy the tonal sweep scanner from outside to detect any Order harmonics before breaching.

line.dialogue: Sweep came back clean — no dormant tone-traps, just residual scarring. We can move in safely.
There it is — a counter-frequency lurking beneath the hull. One step inside and our eardrums burst.

choices.text: Sing a stabilizing frequency. Direct but exposes Pichit's ability.
choices.consequences: Perfect extraction; the merchant now knows Pichit is a Singer, creating future danger.
choices.description: Map the lattice scar patterns to identify load-bearing fractures before committing to any entry point.

line.dialogue: The fractal mapping reveals three stable corridors — starboard maintenance shaft gives us the safest descent.
I misread the propagation pattern — that section I flagged stable just buckled. We're locked out by debris.

lines_before.dialogue: Back at the scrapyard's edge, under the glare of floating city lights, the prosthetic's final integration begins. The new crystal core glows.
You're really doing it? When did he get here? The man with the broken leg... he arrived just before the storm.
This place, this noise... it's home to those who rebuild. Are you allergic to any medicine? The lattice resonance can sometimes feel like a fever.
The synaptic link is delicate. A miscalibration could make the limb reject the host. I'm not home a lot. My lab is safer for this.
And the Tonal Orders are definitely not at home much here. They're coming. The merchant sold us out. I hear their ship's signature.
We finish it now! Let the leg sing! Then we run!
A sleek, official Resonance Ship descends through the smog, its crystal arrays silencing the scrapyard's chaotic din. Enforcers disembark.
My apologies! Their licensing fees are simply too high to ignore. The core, and the Singer, are property of the Orders.

lines_after.dialogue: The integrated prosthetic activates. A pure, clean tone harmonizes with the lattice, contrasting the Enforcers' harsh silencing frequency.
Listen. That sound... it's a new home. Not a floating city, but a body whole again.
He can walk... He's walking!

line.dialogue: The Enforcers demand surrender. The prosthetic is working, but its resonance is drawing lattice energy unpredictably.

choices.text: Flee using the scrapyard's chaos. Abandon the site.
choices.consequences: The team escapes; the prosthetic is saved but the scrapyard is seized by the Orders, hurting the locals.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus monk wisdom on the scavenger gangs to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Use the prosthetic's resonance to disrupt the Enforcer ship. A direct confrontation.
choices.consequences: The Enforcer ship is temporarily disabled; the prosthetic is damaged but repairable, making the team infamous.
choices.description: Direct Arthit to expose surface colonization truth using tattooed routes

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. The villagers rise with their agricultural tools.
The resonance turns hostile. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Pichit sings a counter-frequency, harmonizing the lattice to protect the entire scrapyard.
choices.consequences: The lattice rises defensively; the scrapyard becomes a temporary safe zone, but Pichit's identity is fully exposed, marking him for hunt.
choices.description: Have the villager risk using village secrets to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: the villager makes it work. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the villager misreads the situation. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of decommissioned resonance ships. Jagged hulls rise like metal mountains against the Lattice's shimmering surface below. The air tastes of ozone and rust, pierced by the rhythmic clang of salvage crews.
Look at this place! What's in there? I bet there's still working crystal in some of these wrecks. We could salvage a fortune!
Or get crushed by shifting debris. Or arrested by Tonal Order enforcers. Or eaten by whatever metal parasites grow in these rust-heaps.
We should proceed carefully. The acoustic environment is chaotic here—too much industrial noise could mask dangerous Lattice frequencies.
Every broken ship has a story. A final note it failed to sing. What do they have in there, these silent vessels?
A figure emerges from behind a shattered resonator housing—a surface scavenger, face hidden behind a filtered breather mask, tools dangling from a weathered harness.
You're back late! Most crews clear out before the harmonic dissonance peaks. What's your business in the graveyard?
We're not with any crew. We're looking for... opportunities.

lines_after.dialogue: Opportunities, eh? You sound like Tonal Order scouts. Or worse, pirates. She can't speak Thai—your resonance patterns are all wrong for local crews.
We're not pirates. We're just... economically flexible.
Flexible means dangerous. The Groundless don't take kindly to outsiders poking around our salvage claims.
The Groundless? You're part of the movement that rejects the floating cities?
We reject dependency on the Tonal Orders. Now state your purpose or leave before the shift-change brings less friendly faces.

line.dialogue: The scavenger's suspicion is palpable. How do you establish trust?

choices.text: Offer salvage rights to anything we find (appease their territorial nature)
choices.description: Scale the collapsed gantry to reach the upper deck where something glints between warped hull plates.

line.dialogue: I can see it from here — looks like an intact resonance chamber, still humming faintly," Arthit whispers, testing each rung before committing his weight.
The whole thing's groaning — get back, it's coming down!" Arthit shouts as rusted bolts shear off under his grip and the gantry buckles.

choices.text: Mention we're seeking alternative navigation methods (appeal to Groundless ideology)
choices.description: Press your ear against the hull and follow the low vibration toward its source.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the waterline. Something's still running in there, a generator or a heart that refuses to stop," Pichit says, pressing his palm flat against the trembling steel.
Nothing but corrosion and dead air. Whatever sang here went silent long before we arrived," Pichit mutters, pulling back with rust flakes stuck to his cheek.

choices.text: Show Tonal Order identification (risky if they're truly anti-Order)
choices.description: Force open the jammed cargo hatch using a harmonic frequency from Malee's portable tuner.

line.dialogue: Frequency matched — the locking pins just released. Sometimes the old systems just need someone to speak their language," Malee says, easing the hatch open inch by careful inch.
Wrong harmonic — the pins fused solid and now the whole frame is warped worse. We're not getting through this way," Malee says, stepping back as the tuner emits a harsh dying whine.

lines_before.dialogue: After convincing the scavenger you're not immediate threats, you're led deeper into the scrapyard maze. The air grows thicker with the smell of corroded crystal and hydraulic fluid.
The Groundless operate here because the Tonal Orders' charts are useless in this acoustic chaos. Too much metal interference. That's freedom, of a sort.
Is everything under control? These resonance echoes feel... unstable. Like the Lattice is vibrating at conflicting frequencies beneath us.
I knew right away this place was more than a graveyard. It's a symphony of endings. Each vibration tells of journeys interrupted.

Rounding a corner of stacked engine blocks, you freeze. A sky pirate—wearing patched flight leathers and a resonator pistol at her hip—is standing right in front of you, examining a partially dismantled ship's console.
Well now. Didn't expect company. You lot with the scavenger guild or just lost?
We could ask you the same. Pirates usually take whole ships, not pieces.
This ain't piracy, it's archaeology. This vessel flew routes the Tonal Orders erased from their charts. I'm recovering... alternative navigation data.

lines_after.dialogue: That's our claim, pirate! The Groundless marked this wreck three cycles ago!
Your markings don't mean squat when I've got the frequency keys to access its core memory. Standing in front of me won't change that.
Alternative navigation data? You mean like... Singer techniques?
Maybe. Maybe not. Point is, the Orders keep knowledge locked up. We take it back. You seem like you might appreciate that.
The pirate's hand rests casually near her weapon. The scavenger tenses, reaching for a sonic wrench. The wreck between them hums with residual energy.

line.dialogue: A confrontation brews over the wreck's secrets. How do you intervene?

choices.text: Side with the scavenger (honor the Groundless claim, risk pirate hostility)
choices.description: Draw your tonal resonator and demand the bandit drop their weapons, 15 words exactly

line.dialogue: I've calibrated this to shatter every harmonic crystal in your chest cavity — drop them.
The resonator's dead. Whatever's buried here is swallowing every frequency I throw at it.

choices.text: Propose sharing the data (diplomatic but risky—both parties distrust outsiders)
choices.description: Signal Pichit to flank left through the resonance echoes while you keep the bandit talking

line.dialogue: I'm inside the echo shadow now. One move from them and I take their knees.
The echoes folded around me — I can't see my own hands. I'm retreating back.

choices.text: Attempt to access the console yourself (technical challenge, provokes both parties)
choices.description: Offer the bandit salvage rights to whatever the Groundless left behind in exchange for safe passage

line.dialogue: Huh. Fair trade. The Groundless already stripped what they wanted — take the rest and go.
Salvage rights? We *are* the Groundless, fool. And you just told me exactly what you're carrying.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's din is a physical weight. Pichit's crew crouches in the lee of a shattered resonance ship's hull, its resonator crystal dark. The scavenger, Lek, points a grimy finger towards a cluster of half-melted sky-pirate skiffs.
The Groundless talk, down in the deep wrecks. They remember the old ways. Before the Orders. They say the Lattice… sings back, if you listen right.
And the pirates? Are they listening?
Nah. They're digging. Looking for something that survived the Silencing. A primary frequency crystal. Unbreakable. You change your mind about tangling with them, I won't blame you.
A myth. Every scavenger's tall tale ends with an 'unbreakable crystal.' I can't remember the last time one of these leads panned out.
The pirate's resonator signatures are erratic. Aggressive. If they *have* found something, they're trying to contain its resonance. That's… not a stable situation.
The truth is often buried under stories. Keep in mind, Lek… the Silencing wasn't an end. It was a forgetting. We're here to remember.
A low, pulsing hum cuts through the metallic clamor. The ground vibrates. From the pirate skiffs, a jagged purple light flickers.

line.dialogue: The pirate camp is ahead, guarding the deep wreck. The unstable resonance is a danger, but also a potential distraction.

choices.text: Use the scrapyard's noise. Trigger a controlled collapse of a crane tower to draw them out.
choices.description: Press the scavenger for what specific relic the pirates are hunting.

line.dialogue: Core memory from a pre-Collapse science vessel. Coordinates pulled from a drowned nav-chart," the scavenger mutters, glancing at the shadows.
You're asking the wrong question, friend. The ones who know what it is—they don't talk to breathers like you," the scavenger says, turning away.

choices.text: Mask your approach. Have Arthit tune your personal dampeners to match the pirate resonator's erratic frequency.
choices.description: Signal Chanida to quietly trail the pirate dig team while you keep the scavenger talking.

line.dialogue: Chanida taps her earpiece twice—she's moving. "I've got eyes on their excavation grid. Three torches, one rig, and something big they're prying loose," she whispers.
Chanida's boot clangs against a hull plate. The scavenger's eyes go wide. "You brought a tail? We're done here—*now*," he hisses, vanishing into the wreckage.

choices.text: Walk right in. Let the pirates see you. Your group might look like rival scavengers, a problem to be talked down or bought off.
choices.description: Share Malee's skepticism aloud—call the "unbreakable" story what it is: bait.

line.dialogue: Malee grins sharp. "Finally, someone with salt in their brain. These wreck-rats get fed a legend, start digging for free, and someone else collects the real salvage overhead.
The scavenger spits at your feet. "Bait? I held the casing in my hands, breather. You walk in here with nothing but doubt and expect me to spill my guts?

lines_after.dialogue: The plan works, but not as intended. The deep wreck isn't just a ship—it's a buried Listeners' sanctuary, its walls etched with sonic patterns. The pirate captain stands before a massive, throbbing crystal set into the floor.
Well, well. More rats from the floating cities. You're too late. This frequency… it's ours. The Lattice will answer to *us* now.
You're not controlling it. You're antagonizing it. You remember the Silencing? This is how it starts.
The crystal's pulse quickens. The etched patterns on the walls begin to glow.

lines_before.dialogue: The sanctuary thrums with pent-up energy. The pirate's captured crystal is a raw nerve of the Lattice, its frequency clashing violently with the pirate's crude resonator. Cracks spiderweb across the ancient floor.
No, no! You don't need to do that! Stand down! We can split the take!
Nah, nah. We've talked about this before. You can't bargain with a landslide.
The wall patterns… they're a counter-frequency! A dampening sequence! Arthit, can you—
The resonator is too damaged. Input is chaotic. To stabilize it… we'd need to channel a pure, matching tone directly into the crystal matrix.
All eyes turn to Pichit. The Singer. The pirate captain snarls, raising a crackling sonic blade.
A Singer? I'm such a lucky gal! I'll sell your throat to the highest Order!
The Lattice isn't for taking. It's for listening. You're standing right in front of the answer, and all you hear is noise.

line.dialogue: The crystal is destabilizing. To save the scrapyard—and perhaps more—Pichit must Sing. But the environment is acoustically hostile, and the pirate is closing in.

choices.text: Sing a Shield. Focus on a single, solid note of protection to give Arthit time to jury-rig a dampener from the pirate's equipment.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on ship navigation

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Arthit loses control. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Sing a Harmony. Match your voice to the sanctuary's wall patterns, amplifying the ancient dampening sequence to gently subdue the crystal.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with unauthorized tones to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida overreaches. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Sing a Resonance. Don't fight the crystal's frequency. Join it, become its conductor, and *redirect* the energy safely up through the wreck and into the open sky.
choices.description: The pirate presses forward with smuggling routes to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
A costly mistake by the pirate. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit's voice cuts through the chaos. It doesn't overpower; it *aligns*. The crystal's rage smooths into a radiant, coherent beam of light. The pirate's resonator shatters harmlessly.
From the tunnel entrance, Lek and other Groundless scavengers watch, awestruck. The beam pierces the scrapyard ceiling, painting the rusted metal in serene, shifting colors.
The frequency… it's stable. More than stable. It's charting itself. This is a navigational key.
Looks like the tall tale was true. Don't get a big head about it.
Is everything under control? I mean… you just sang to a crystal and made a new star.
We talked before about remembering. Today, we didn't just remember a song. We let the world sing a new one.

The beam fades, leaving the primary crystal clear and calm. In its heart, a perfect, unchanging frequency glows. The Groundless approach, not with greed, but with reverence. The secret isn't lost. It's found.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance ship 'Echo's Mercy' parts the crystalline Lattice, descending into the Silent Zone. The usual hum of the resonators dies, replaced by an unnatural, suffocating quiet.
This place... it's like the world's heart stopped beating. I can't even hear my own breath properly.
The Orders said this was a dead zone. Charts useless. Probably just a ploy to keep us from scavenging their secrets.
Caution. Our resonator crystals are inert. If we lose our way, there's no calling for help. We are truly isolated.
Silence isn't emptiness. It's a different kind of fullness... a pressure. What was silenced here during The Silencing?
The ship settles on a jagged, grey crystal plain. The light is dim, filtered through a static, opaque Lattice ceiling.
Who is this guy? You've arrived? You shouldn't be here. The Lattice doesn't sing. It doesn't weep. It just... waits.
Don't tell him anything, Arthit. Surface scavengers trade in secrets and shivs.

lines_after.dialogue: Your ship's quiet. Good. Noise attracts... other things here. Sky pirates listen for the dumb ones who try to force a frequency.
Other things? What kind of things?
Things that remember sound. And hate it. You're visitors to a grave. Act like it.

line.dialogue: The scavenger points to a faint, ancient path etched into the crystal. 'That leads to an old Listeners' outpost. Maybe answers. Maybe death. Your choice.'

choices.text: Follow the scavenger's path cautiously.
choices.description: Ask Malee to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on leg resonance

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee loses control. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: Demand the scavenger guide us for payment.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing forbidden paths to uncover the suppression

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
The lattice has other plans. A spy alerts the authorities.

choices.text: Ignore him and scout the immediate area for ship-safe resources.
choices.description: Convince the scavenger to use surface knowledge and record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
A costly mistake by the scavenger. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The party follows the faint trail. The silence is so profound, their footsteps feel like violations. Then, a discovery.
Look! A crystal shard... it's glowing! A soft, pulsing light! There's no one else around. It's alive!
Alive? It's probably just residual energy from before The Silencing. Don't get sentimental. It's a tool.
It's responding to... us? To our presence? Not to sound. This contradicts all Tonal Order doctrine.
I'm happy to hear this... not a song, but a presence. The Lattice here isn't dead. It's dreaming. Or remembering.
As Pichit holds the shard, a gentle warmth spreads. For a moment, the oppressive quiet feels less hostile.
Are you going to keep holding it or not? It feels... friendly.
You found a Heart Shard. The Groundless Movement whispers about these. They say they're memories of the world before the cities floated. Before the Orders.

lines_after.dialogue: The Groundless... they believe in returning to the surface? Living with the Lattice, not just crossing it?
Something like that. That shard is a piece of the true world. It doesn't need a song to wake it. It just needs... belief.
A distant, sharp crack echoes—a sound! Then, the rough roar of a resonance engine, violently forcing a frequency.

line.dialogue: The unnatural sound is a sky pirate ship, breaching the Silent Zone with brute force. They're heading for your position. The scavenger looks panicked. 'They hunt Heart Shards. They'll strip your ship.'

choices.text: Hide the shard and try to conceal yourselves among the crystal formations.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the crystal's surface and let your warmth meet its pulse.

line.dialogue: I feel it — a heartbeat, slow and patient, like it's been waiting centuries for someone to listen.
Nothing. Just cold glass under my hand. Maybe Malee was right — residual energy, nothing more.

choices.text: Use the shard's energy as a distraction, luring the pirates away from the Echo's Mercy.
choices.description: Hum the melody that's been stuck in your head since you entered this chamber.

line.dialogue: There — it brightened! The shard knows this song. Someone sang to it once, long ago.
The glow fades when I hum. I've got the wrong tune entirely, and now it feels... disappointed.

choices.text: Prepare to defend the ship and the shard, risking a fight in this treacherous, silent terrain.
choices.description: Hold perfectly still and breathe in rhythm with the crystal's pulsing light.

line.dialogue: It's syncing with us. The pulse is slowing to match our breathing — we're becoming part of its rhythm.
I lost the pattern. My heart raced and the shard flickered erratically, then dimmed. It needs stillness I can't give it.

lines_before.dialogue: The deeper you go into the Silent Zone, the heavier the quiet becomes. It's not just an absence of sound, but a pressure that pushes against thought itself.
This place is the latest fashion in existential dread. I hate it.
Our resonator readings are flat. No frequency, no harmonics. It's like the Lattice is... dead here.
Dead? Or just not listening? Look at these crystal formations. They're different. It's really a great place to live... if you're a rock.
You're in the Dead Province now. What province is hope in when you're here? None. This is where the Lattice forgot how to dream.
A forgotten province of reality. Not dead, Arthit. Sleeping. Or perhaps... waiting.
Enough philosophizin'. The Groundless cache is supposed to be near. My charts are useless here, but the silence... it points.

lines_after.dialogue: The structure is a shattered dome of black crystal, half-submerged. Inside, the silence is absolute, broken only by the scuff of your boots.
Well, this isn't ominous at all. Just a nice, quiet tomb.
Life signs... minimal. But there's a power source. Faint, like a dying heartbeat.

line.dialogue: At the dome's heart lies a pedestal holding a pulsating, dark crystal core. The scavenger eyes it greedily, the bandit with calculation. Pichit feels a deep, resonant wrongness emanating from it.

choices.text: Let the scavenger take it. He knows the surface. (Trade immediate danger for potential future aid.)
choices.description: Ask Malee to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on mechanical repair

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The risk doesn't pay off. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Study the core with Arthit. Understand it before moving it. (Risk awakening something, but gain knowledge.)
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using crystal hearing to rally the villagers

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
The resonance turns hostile. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.text: Shatter the core. The wrongness must be purged. (Definite, violent reaction from the environment.)
choices.description: The pirate takes the lead, employing intimidation to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the pirate's resolve isn't enough. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The choice has been made. The Silent Zone reacts. The black lattice around you begins to vibrate, not with sound, but with a palpable, nauseating pressure.
You still don't understand? This ain't a dead zone! It's a classroom! And class is in session!
The guy in the condo next door always closes his door loudly... that's noise. This... this is the door slamming on reality!
The core... it's not a power source. It's a seal. And we just rang the bell for recess.
Fantastic. So we're the guest lecturers for Apocalypse 101.
The Groundless movement... they weren't hiding a treasure. They were containing a catastrophe!
A lesson in silence. The ultimate price of the Silencing. This is the wound that never healed.
From the fractured dome, tendrils of anti-sound lash out. They don't make noise; they consume it, leaving a deeper, hungrier silence in their wake.

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation leaves the Silent Zone changed. The oppressive quiet has receded, replaced by a fragile, whispering resonance. The wound is exposed, but perhaps now it can heal.
The Lattice remembers pain. Our task is not to command it, but to listen... and help it sing again.
The data... it's incredible. This changes everything we know about the Silencing.

line.dialogue: The entity of silence is wounded, recoiling. The broken core lies before you. The bandit and scavenger are gone, fled or consumed. The fate of this place—and the knowledge of the true Silencing—rests on your next action.

choices.text: Contain it. Use the ship's resonator to cage the phenomenon for the Tonal Orders. (Gain prestige, but entrust truth to the guild.)
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with monk wisdom to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit hits a wall. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Commune with it. Pichit will attempt to Sing the wound closed, to harmonize the broken resonance. (High risk to Pichit, chance for true healing.)
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using tattooed routes to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
The resonance turns hostile. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.text: Shatter the paradigm. Broadcast the true nature of the Silencing to all Floating Cities. (Unleash political chaos, empower the Groundless.)
choices.description: Convince the pirate to use pirate ship and commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_before.dialogue: The Khrueang Market hums with a thousand conversations, a sea of noise washing over the crystalline walkways of the skycity.
This market is a living thing. Its noise is a chaotic symphony. I wonder what patterns the Lattice hears in it.
The only pattern I hear is people trying to overcharge us. Keep your philosophical musings to yourself until we've secured supplies.
Forget supplies! Look at the crowd around that Listeners' stall. Something's happening!
A gathering crowd is a risk. We should secure our resonator crystals first. We've seen it before—distractions lead to shortages.
As Arthit speaks, a commotion erupts. A robed Listener Monk the Listener monk is being confronted by a burly Tonal Orders enforcer.
Please, I merely share an observation from our deep-listening! The Lattice's base resonance... it's shifting. It’s not an accusation, just... a warning we've seen before in the old texts.
He paced back and forth while he spoke. That's not the calm of a monk. It's the agitation of someone who has seen a ghost.

lines_after.dialogue: The enforcer scoffs and shoves the monk aside, his warning drowned by the market's din. The monk stumbles, his eyes wide with a silent plea.
Great. A holy man with a death wish. Just what we needed.
We have to talk to him! What if he knows something real?
Intervening marks us. The Tonal Orders have long memories. This is a complication we prepared for, but not one I welcome.

line.dialogue: The monk gathers his scattered scrolls, casting a furtive glance your way. Do you approach?

choices.line: Intercept him discreetly. (Social: Blend into the crowd to make contact.)
choices.description: Push through the crowd to hear what the Listener is actually saying.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "The Listener's words crawl inside my skull and *stay* there — she's naming dead cities no one remembers.
Chanida — "Someone's elbow caught my ribs and the crowd swallowed me whole — I caught maybe three syllables and one of them was 'doom.

choices.line: Let Chanida create a distraction first. (Deception: Cause a minor commotion to draw eyes away.)
choices.description: Use the market chaos as cover to trail Arthit's resonance contact through the eastern stalls.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "He walked past the silk-seller twice without looking — that's his tell, so now I know he's already nervous about something.
Arthit — "A fishmonger's cart overturned between us and by the time I cleared the stinking mess my contact had dissolved into the crowd like salt in soup.

choices.line: Observe from a distance for now. (Stealth: Follow him to see where he goes.)
choices.description: Barter aggressively with the bone-orchard vendor for resonance-shielding supplies before coins run thin.

line.dialogue: Malee — "I laid the coins out one at a time and let silence do my negotiating —
The lattice has other plans. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: You find the Listener Monk in a secluded alcove behind a tapestry merchant, the market's roar softened to a murmur.
You followed. Thank you. My name is Kavi. I must share this... before it's too late. Please call me back if I speak out of turn. The Lattice's song is growing... strange.
Strange how? A dissonance? A new harmony?

A hollowness. Like a great bell cracked. Our deepest listeners report it. The foundational tones that hold the sky-islands aloft... they are weakening. I heard a strange noise in the data, a silence within the sound.
This is a dangerous claim. The Tonal Orders maintain the foundational harmonics. If they are failing...
Or if they're *hiding* the failure. Good night to safe travel if the crystals under our feet decide to stop singing.
We need proof! Not just monkish whispers.
A gruff voice cuts from the shadows of a supply crate. A weathered Surface Scavenger the Surface scavenger steps forward, her eyes sharp.

lines_after.dialogue: Proof, eh? You city-folk with your clean hands. I've seen the 'hollowness.' Down on the Lattice surface, new fissures. They don't ring right. They just... swallow sound.
You've witnessed this directly? The Lattice consuming resonance?
Aye. Lost a good sled to one. The Tonal Orders' survey maps call them 'stable.' They're not. The monk's right. Something's wrong down below.
The Silencing was preceded by a great stillness in the records... We are hearing that stillness now.

line.dialogue: Two sources, one dire warning. The subplot 'The Lattice's Warning' solidifies. What's the next move?

choices.line: Secure the monk's data scrolls for analysis. (Lore: Study the historical parallels.)
choices.description: Press Kavi for evidence of this hollowness before believing such heresy.

line.dialogue: I have heard it too — faintly, in the silence between midnight bells. He speaks true.
You bring rumor and paranoia to a sacred place. The Orders will hear of this.

choices.line: Bargain with the scavenger for coordinates to a fissure. (Trade: Offer supplies for dangerous knowledge.)
choices.description: Ask Kavi to demonstrate — to sing the broken note aloud here and now.

line.dialogue: Listen, then. This is what remains of our oldest chant." — The sound curdles in your chest like grief.
I cannot. My throat closes each time I try. The hollowness... it does not wish to be heard.

choices.line: Confront a low-level Tonal Order clerk here in the market. (Intimidation: Demand answers, risking their ire.)
choices.description: Warn Kavi that speaking this openly invites the Tonal Orders' retribution.

line.dialogue: Finally, sense. If what you say is true, secrecy is your only shield. Come — we speak elsewhere.
I would rather die honest than live gagged. The song is breaking, and you worry about *politics*?

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups at the edge of Khrueang Market, the constant hum of commerce now feeling oppressive. The Listener Monk you met earlier, Brother Kavi, approaches, his face pale.
You must hear this. I've walked the data-vaults back and forth all night. The Lattice's song... it's changing. Not decaying, but being *rewritten*. This is the best way I can describe it.
Rewritten? By what? The Tonal Orders? I'm heading out now to find someone who'll give us a straight answer!
Easy. Charging into the guildhall is a one-way trip to a cell. We need a round trip plan: get proof, get out.
She's right. The Scavenger we spoke to... she implied the Orders were silencing more than just history. She knows the surface patterns. If the Lattice is being altered, she'd have seen the signs.
A harmony forced is no harmony at all. If the song is being overwritten, the truth is the only resonance that can counter it. Brother Kavi, will you help us find the source?

My vows... they bind me to study, not to act. But to study a lie is to perpetuate it. I will guide you. The central resonator spire controls navigation for this sector. The alteration signal is strongest there.
The Scavenger, Larn, emerges from the crowd, her face grim. She overheard.

lines_after.dialogue: You're really going to the spire? You've got grit, I'll give you that. The Orders have guards posted 'for maintenance.' But I know a service conduit that runs up the side. It's tight, and the harmonic feedback will be... unpleasant.
Unpleasant how? Vomiting-unpleasant or mind-melting-unpleasant? Important distinction.
Somewhere in between. But it's the only way in they won't expect. One way or round trip, you need to decide now. Market patrols are on the move.

line.dialogue: The path to the spire's heart is perilous. How do we proceed?

choices.text: [EASY: Use the Scavenger's Conduit] Trust Larn's knowledge of the city's underbelly. It's risky but direct.
choices.description: Sneak into the Tonal Orders' guildhall through the old storm-drain beneath the archive wing, 14 words

line.dialogue: I've crawled through those drains before — the acoustic shielding down there is degraded, so we move quiet and we move *now*.
The grate's welded shut and there's a harmonic tripwire threaded through the frame — one touch and every resonator in that hall screams our names.

choices.text: [MEDIUM: Infiltrate as Maintenance] Forge work orders. Slower, but allows for observation.
choices.description: Track down the Scavenger at her roost in the Sodalight Market and press her for what she implied, 17 words

line.dialogue: She's expecting us — left a chalk-mark on the third pillar. Whatever she knows about the rewriting, she's ready to name names.
Her roost is cleaned out. Bedroll still warm, but the walls are scraped bare of every glyph she'd carved. Someone got to her first.

choices.text: [HARD: Create a Sonic Diversion] Use the market's noise. Chanida can cause a 'resonance feedback' incident to draw guards away.
choices.description: Force chanida to stop and listen — make monk replay the corrupted data-vault recording in full, 16 words

line.dialogue: Sit. *Listen.* This waveform is
the monk is thwarted. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: You stand before the central resonator's control interface, deep within the spire. The air vibrates with a powerful, artificial tone. Screens display complex harmonic notation, actively overwriting the natural Lattice frequencies.

This... this is a command frequency. They're not just navigating. They're forcing the Lattice to reshape itself. The stress patterns... if this continues, the structural integrity of the floating cities...
I know. I *now* know why the Listeners were so terrified. This isn't innovation. It's the Silencing all over again, just slower. Do you know what this is? It's controlled collapse.
We have to stop it! Smash the crystals, cut the power!
Violence would only create a louder dissonance. The truth must resonate. We must broadcast the natural song back into the system, override their forgery.
The door slides open. A high-ranking Tonal Archon enters, flanked by guards. Brother Kavi steps forward, trembling.
Archon Valen. I have seen this data before. In the forbidden archives. This protocol... it's the same one used before the Silencing. You're already repeating the catastrophe!

The Archon smiles, a cold, thin line. 'Stability requires sacrifice, Brother. The natural song is chaos. We impose order. You are too late. The recalibration is already complete.' A deep, grinding groan echoes through the city's foundations.

lines_after.dialogue: The city... it's listing! He's locked the controls!
The new resonance will hold. It must. Or everything falls. You understand nothing. I already know that the old ways lead to ruin.
You know only fear. And fear makes poor music. The Lattice's true song is not chaos. It is a complex, living harmony. You are the dissonance.

line.dialogue: The city trembles. The Archon's false song holds it in a vice. How do you break the cycle?

choices.text: [EASY: Sabotage the Power Core] Arthit can overload the resonator. It will cause a blackout and force a reboot to natural frequencies, but the city will plummet dangerously before stabilizing.
choices.description: Sing the counter-frequency into the resonance chamber, matching pitch until the crystals shatter silently, 15 words

line.dialogue: [arthit: "The harmonics are collapsing inward — they're eating their own signal. I can feel the silence spreading, clean and absolute, like the moment after a gunshot fades."]
[arthit: "My pitch is drifting — the crystals are *correcting* me. My own voice is becoming part of the command signal. I can't stop hearing it."]

choices.text: [MEDIUM: A Duet of Truth] Pichit must sing the true song, amplified by the spire, while the others defend him from the guards. A direct contest of wills with the Archon.
choices.description: Splice a dead-loop recording of the Listeners' original chant back through the primary crystal array, 15 words

line.dialogue: [malee: "It's working — the old frequency is drowning out the command like rain filling a dry well. The Listeners' voices are *remembering* themselves."]
[malee: "The loop's accelerating instead of stabilizing. The chant is warping into something the Listeners never sang — something that sounds like screaming underwater."]

choices.text: [HARD: Turn Their Weapon Against Them] Use the Archon's own control frequency, but feed it the raw, unfiltered data of the Silencing from Brother Kavi's memory crystal. Make him hear the consequences.
choices.description: Place your bare hands on the master crystal and let your own heartbeat disrupt its rhythm, 15 words

line.dialogue: [pichit: "Your pulse is... imperfect. Irregular. Human. And that is precisely why the crystal cannot sync with it. Imperfection is the antidote to perfect command."]
[pichit: "The crystal has matched your heartbeat. Now it commands your blood. Step back — step back before it teaches your heart a new rhythm."]

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hum with the low, constant resonance of knowledge. Crystalline shelves stretch into vaulted acoustic chambers, each scroll and resonator carefully placed to avoid harmonic interference.
Keep your voices down. The acoustics here are designed to carry even a whisper to the far corners. We're looking for pre-Silencing cartography.
Great. So we're searching for a needle in a haystack, and the haystack will tell everyone we're looking. The Tonal Orders really know how to make research thrilling.
Stop complaining and start looking! There's got to be something about uncharted frequencies here. I can feel it.
Knowledge is never truly lost. It merely waits for the right frequency to be heard again. Let us listen with more than our ears.
As the party disperses among the stacks, Pichit notices two figures in a secluded reading nook, their voices a tense murmur against the archive's hum.
...the old Listeners' chant. It might be true. My crew picked up echoes from a dead zone near the Shattered Spire. No Order charts go there.
Dead zones mean unstable Lattice. You sky-rats fly over the danger. We walk on it. Your word isn't worth the air it vibrates.

lines_after.dialogue: (whispering, pulling Pichit back) Did you hear that? A dead zone chart! You should give it a try! We could find the Open Frequency Map!
Oh, wonderful. We're eavesdropping on a pirate and a surface-dweller. I'm not a playboy! I don't do clandestine meetups in libraries.
This is highly irregular. And dangerous. The Tonal Orders guard their charting monopolies fiercely. If they think we're seeking uncharted frequencies...

line.dialogue: The pirate and scavenger seem to possess a fragment of forbidden knowledge about the Open Frequency Map. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Approach them openly. Honesty might yield cooperation.
choices.description: Trace your fingertips along the crystal spines, feeling for vibrations that betray hidden compartments.

line.dialogue: Here — this one hums differently. The lattice pattern shifts when I apply pressure to the third facet.
Congratulations, you just set off a resonance chime. Every guardian in the stacks now knows exactly where we are.

choices.line: Use the archive's acoustics. Position the party to overhear more discreetly.
choices.description: Press your ear against the largest crystal column and listen for the whispering voices the archives are named for.

line.dialogue: The dead speak through mineral veins. I can hear a woman reciting coordinates — she is describing a vault beneath the eastern transept.
All I hear is blood rushing through my own skull. These crystals absorb sound — they don't broadcast it. You're chasing echoes that don't exist.

choices.line: Report them to an archivist. Let the Order handle it.
choices.description: Signal the group to spread out in a grid pattern while you climb the shelving to read the inscriptions carved along the upper edges.

line.dialogue: From up there you can see the whole layout — three aisles form a spiral, and the central column has markings I recognize from the Sundering Codex.
Arthit

lines_before.dialogue: The decision is made. The party maneuvers through the crystalline stacks, using the precise acoustic design to their advantage, closing in on the clandestine meeting.
Look, rust-bucket. The price is the same. My frequency data for your surface coordinates to the Spire's base. No credits, no Order scrip. Pure trade.
Your data is just noise until it's walked. My coordinates are life and death. You, too! You want my steps, you give me the true chant, not just echoes.
Forgive our intrusion. We seek understanding, not conflict. We overheard your talk of the Shattered Spire and uncharted frequencies.
Yes, we're all friends here, united in our desire to bypass the guild's exorbitant fees. It's really worth seeing! The look on a Tonal Cartographer's face when they lose their monopoly.
Interlopers! You've got the look of chart-rats, not free-flyers. Why should we share our find with you?
Four more mouths to split the prize with. Or four more bodies to leave in the Lattice.
We're after the Open Frequency Map! The real one, not Order propaganda! We can help each other!

lines_after.dialogue: The Map? That's a fairy tale used to sell resonator upgrades. But... the dead zone by the Spire. The echoes there don't match any known pattern. Could be a fragment.
The path down the Spire is treacherous. The Lattice sings a mad song there. My price just went up. I want safe passage up, on your ship, if we find this 'fragment'.
A joint expedition? With a pirate and a scavenger? The variables are... concerning. We have no chart for that zone. We'd be navigating blind.

line.dialogue: A potential alliance forms, but the risks are immense. The path to the Shattered Spire is uncharted and perilous. What terms do you agree to?

choices.line: Agree to the scavenger's terms. Their surface knowledge is invaluable, and a ship berth is a small price.
choices.description: Override the bandit's frequency scanner with your own encrypted signal jammer.

line.dialogue: bandit* — "Alright, alright — you've got teeth. Frequency's yours, but don't say I didn't warn you about what's broadcasting on the other end.
bandit* — "You think I haven't dealt with jammers before? That tin-can trick just doubled your price, rust-bucket.

choices.line: Propose a trial. Share only partial data first, to test trust and the validity of the clues.
choices.description: Offer to walk the scavenger's coordinates yourself, proving your worth through direct action.

line.dialogue: scavenger* — "Finally, someone who understands — data's just a ghost until a body chases it down. Coordinates are yours, walker.
scavenger* — "You don't look like you'd survive twenty clicks in that radiation belt. Come back with thicker skin or stay home.

choices.line: Demand the information freely. The pursuit of the Open Map is a cause that should transcend barter.
choices.description: Invoke pichit's diplomatic protocol, requesting a shared exchange that benefits all parties present.

line.dialogue: pichit* — "Your words carry the weight of reason. I will open our archives — understanding shared is understanding multiplied.
pichit* — "You speak of sharing, but your eyes calculate profit. The protocol recognizes your insincerity — access denied.

lines_before.dialogue: The party is deep within a restricted section of the Archives, a chamber where damaged crystal records are stored. The air hums with fragmented, dissonant frequencies.
A graveyard of dead ends and wrong turns. The price is the same for all of them: a wrecked ship and a lost crew. It’s really worth seeing!
Focus! The map fragment from the scavenger points here. You can look for as long as you want, but we need to find the matching resonance before the Tonal Order guards make their rounds.
That’s probably right. The security harmonics are shifting. We have a narrow window.
Each broken shard... it's a story cut short. A path someone tried to sing into existence.
Told you it was here. The big one. The record of the 'Open Frequency' they tried to bury after the Silencing. My girlfriend gets jealous of the time I spend down here, but the Lattice don't lie.
Quit the poetry and find the core shard! The one that doesn't just show a path—it shows how to *make* paths. The monopoly ends today.

Arthit carefully aligns the scavenger's fragment with a larger, cracked crystal plinth. A pained, glorious chord swells, and a holographic map of the lower Lattice surface flickers to life, riddled with unstable, glowing routes.

lines_after.dialogue: The map stabilizes, revealing a pulsating, direct route deep into the forbidden zone—a path that bypasses all Order checkpoints.
Well. There it is. The key to the cage. And every pirate and enforcer on the float will want it.
We have to copy it. Now!

line.dialogue: The archival crystal is degrading fast; copying the full frequency matrix will take precision.

choices.text: Use Chanida's portable resonator to make a quick, noisy copy. (Might attract attention.)
choices.description: Align your harmonic resonator to the shifting security frequencies before they cycle closed again, 15 words

line.dialogue: Got it — the frequency locks for exactly four seconds, so move NOW or we're locked out until tomorrow's rotation.
Damn — missed the window by half a heartbeat. These harmonics don't forgive hesitation, and neither will what's behind us.

choices.text: Have Malee and Arthit jury-rig the archive's own recording apparatus. (Requires technical skill.)
choices.description: Kneel beside each shattered fragment and let your fingertips read the resonance trapped inside the glass, 15 words

line.dialogue: Each one whispers a name, a destination, a final thought — they're not debris, they're memorial stones for travelers who never returned.
I touched one and felt only silence. Whatever story it held is gone now — erased by time or something that wanted it forgotten.

choices.text: Pichit attempts to memorize and internally harmonize the complex frequency pattern. (A true Singer's test.)
choices.description: Trust the scavenger's partial map and take the unmarked path veering left between the collapsed obelisks, 15 words

line.dialogue: The map doesn't lie — there, beneath the third obelisk, a passage opens. The scavenger earned every coin we paid.
Dead end. The obelisks aren't collapsed — they were *placed* this way, her

lines_before.dialogue: Alarms shatter the archival silence. The decision has been made, and consequences descend. Tonal Order Sentinels in harmonic armor seal the exits, while the Sky Pirate reveals a hidden resonator-cannon.
The map is ours! Everyone knows the Order hoards the safe routes to keep us dependent! You might change your mind about who the real thieves are!
He's broadcasting the Open Frequency! He'll destabilize the entire local Lattice!
I don’t want it—this chaos! We're caught between a monopoly and a madman!
We can't let him fire that in here! The feedback could shatter the Archives and bring the city down!
The First Note that caused the Silencing... was it a weapon? Or was it a song they tried to suppress? This is the same choice.
The Pirate's weapon whines to a crescendo. The Sentinels raise harmonic dampeners. The very crystals of the chamber begin to vibrate and crack.
The Lattice remembers everything! Even the breaking!

lines_after.dialogue: The immediate crisis is over, but the Archives are forever changed. The Open Frequency is either secured, lost, or unleashed upon the world.
A song was sung here today. Whether it becomes a lullaby or a dirge is not yet written.
The party escapes as the great library's careful acoustics give way to a new, unpredictable resonance. The map's fate will echo across the Floating Cities.

line.dialogue: In the climax, you must decide the fate of the Open Frequency and the immediate conflict.

choices.text: Sabotage the pirate's cannon, surrendering the map to the Order to prevent catastrophe. (The monopoly tightens its grip.)
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with forbidden paths, ready to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
A costly mistake by Arthit. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Fight to seize the cannon and the map, aiming to escape and become a new power. (You become outlaws with a priceless secret.)
choices.description: Chanida attempts to uncover the suppression, relying on hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The crowd's collective voice forces the patrol to retreat.
Defeat. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Attempt the impossible: use the unstable resonance to *alter* the Open Frequency, creating a stable, sharable public map. (Risk everything to forge a third path.)
choices.description: Have the scavenger risk using survival skills to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: the scavenger pushes through. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
Defeat. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of dead ships. Rusted hulls rise like skeletal mountains against the bruised sky, their crystal resonators shattered and silent.
A dissonant symphony of grinding metal and hissing steam blankets everything—the perfect acoustic camouflage for secrets.
Ugh, this place smells like burnt ozone and regret. Why'd we have to meet here again?
Because, Chanida, the Tonal Orders don't send their tax collectors to places where the acoustics could give a man a permanent migraine.
Keep your voices down. The reverberation in these metal canyons carries farther than you'd think.
Listen... beneath the industrial clamor. Can you hear it? A faint harmonic... like a memory of flight.
Ah! Our esteemed clients! Welcome, welcome! Do mind the loose plating. Safety first, even in a graveyard.

lines_after.dialogue: I just spoke with the foreman of the breaking crews. He’s been married twice, you know. Says it gives him perspective on dismantling things.
Charming. He’s been married before, so he's an expert on ship corpses? Get to the point.
Patience! The point is, his second wife was a Listener. She heard things in the Lattice... things that didn't match the official charts.
That's dangerous talk. The Tonal Orders don't take kindly to chart discrepancies.

line.dialogue: The merchant gestures to a particular wreck—the 'Echo of Dawn,' its hull split open like a fossilized fruit. 'The foreman's late wife... she said this one still sings. A ghost song. Your payment for the resonator coils depends on what you make of that.'

choices.text: Investigate the wreck immediately. The song calls.
choices.description: Press your ear against the corroded hull of a nearby shipping container, tracking the source of the whisper.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the rust! A harmonic pattern, repeating in seven-count cycles. Someone is *broadcasting* from underneath us.
All you're hearing is your own pulse against the metal. The scrapyard plays tricks on desperate ears — step back before you deafen yourself.

choices.text: Question the foreman first. Understand the source of the story.
choices.description: Signal Malee to disable the nearest acoustic relay node, muffling the industrial noise to isolate the frequency.

line.dialogue: Relay's dead. And there it is — clear as temple bells. A voice, Pichit. Someone is singing from inside the wreckage.
The node's wired to a failsafe. I touch it wrong and every Order patrol within two kilometers hears us breathing. My hands are staying put.

choices.text: Ignore the superstition. Just retrieve the coils and get paid.
choices.description: Draw your tuning blade and strike it against scrap metal, sending a counter-resonance outward to provoke a response.

line.dialogue: It answered! The whisper shifted — matched my frequency, then *broke* it. Whatever's down there, it's not just listening. It's *thinking*.
Nothing. Just my own vibration dying in the slag. And now

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the gutted hull of the 'Echo of Dawn,' the world outside fades to a distant thrum. The air is still and cold, smelling of old copper and dust.
Fractured crystal conduits spider-web the walls, catching the dim light in faint, mournful glimmers.
What’s this called? This feeling... like the air itself is holding its breath?
Resonance residue. A ship's final note, frozen in the moment of its silencing.
Anyone’s okay to poke this relic, but if a Tonal Order inspector shows up, I'm blaming Pichit.
The primary resonator chamber should be ahead. If there's any salvageable crystal...
A soft, crystalline chime reverberates through the metal, originating from nowhere and everywhere at once.
You should not be here. This song is not for commerce.

lines_after.dialogue: I am Brother Vasan. I study what the Lattice sings when no one is trying to command it. This ship... its final resonance is pure, untainted by navigation charts.
Great. A monk. What's the price for ignoring you? Anyone's okay with moving along?
The price is truth. The Tonal Orders' charts for this sector are... deliberately flawed. This ship discovered that. It was silenced.
Keep it. You should keep your conspiracy theories. We're just here for parts.
No. We're here because a song is asking to be heard. What do they call this phenomenon, Brother? When a resonance outlives its source?

line.dialogue: Brother Vasan's eyes flicker with conflict. 'They call it an Echo. A truth that refuses to die. The merchant outside will pay you for the coils, but he works for the Orders. He will report this. The real salvage here... is knowledge. But knowledge has consequences.'

choices.text: Take the coils and leave. Fulfill the original contract.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the relic's surface and let the resonance flow through you.

line.dialogue: Your heartbeat matched the decay frequency — you're lucky it wanted to be remembered, not replayed.
Pull your hand back, now — that's not an echo, that's a drowning, and it just chose you as its shore.

choices.text: Record the Echo's frequency. Hide the data from the merchant.
choices.description: Signal Arthit to lead toward the primary resonator chamber while you guard the rear with your tuner fork drawn.

line.dialogue: Good — the corridor narrows ahead, and whatever sang this ship dead may still be listening for harmony.
Wait — your fork is vibrating before I've even started moving. Something behind us already knows we're here.

choices.text: Destroy the coils. Preserve the secret of the Echo, forfeiting the pay.
choices.description: Ask Malee exactly what the Tonal Order does to people who touch relics without authorization.

line.dialogue: They retune you. Strip every song your body knows until you can't remember your mother's voice, your name, the sound of your own breathing — then they leave you silent.
You don't want to know. And the fact you're asking means you already touched something you shouldn't have — when did your ears start ringing?

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before the Silent Barge's exposed engine core, its crystal resonator cracked and dark. The clangor of the scrapyard feels distant, replaced by a heavy, humming silence.
The fracture pattern... it's not from impact. This resonator was sabotaged. Deliberately overloaded.

Of course it was. The Tonal Orders don't like competition. Anyone who could navigate without their precious charts was a threat. I was cheated out of a proper investigation last time something like this surfaced.
So we have proof! Give it to me! We take this to the city watch, expose the whole rotten guild!
Proof of a crime, but not the criminal. This resonator holds an echo... a final moment. Are you finished yet, Arthit? Can we listen?
It is dangerous. A forced resonance, a scream frozen in crystal. But... the truth is in the song.
Listeners and their songs. I have buyers for intact salvage, not ghost stories. Every moment here costs me.
The cost of silence is greater. We listen.

line.dialogue: The Listener monk prepares to attune the broken crystal. The process is unstable.

choices.text: Use Chanida's portable damper field. Stabilize the frequency safely, but blunt the emotional clarity of the echo.
choices.description: Examine the resonator's frequency signature to identify which Tonal Order produced it.

line.dialogue: Arthit runs his finger along the fracture's harmonic whorl. "Third-overtone bias, ceremonial tempering — this came from a Conservatory tuner, no question.
Arthit shakes his head. "The signature's too degraded. Whoever did this knew how to blur their own frequency trail.

choices.text: Let the monk work alone. Hear the raw, painful truth, but risk psychic feedback harming the party.
choices.description: Let Chanida take the evidence to the city magistrates immediately.

line.dialogue: Chanida snatches the resonator fragment, eyes blazing. "They can't ignore physical proof. We walk into that courthouse before the Orders scrub another crime scene.
Chanida's hand trembles as she reaches for it. "If I show this to the wrong magistrate, we're all dead before sunrise. I need to know who I can trust first.

choices.text: Have Pichit and the monk harmonize. Attempt to soothe the echo and hear its full story, requiring perfect vocal control.
choices.description: Have Malee quietly contact her old contacts inside the Tonal Orders for information.

line.dialogue: Malee pulls Chanida back. "You wave that around in public, you're a target. Let me ask a few careful questions through back channels first.
the merchant loses control. His network delivers bad intelligence.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal shard glows, emitting a distorted, sorrowful tone. Within it, a voice.
"They said my song was heresy. That the Lattice's true voice belonged only to the Orders. They... they swindled me. Took my charts, then my ship." The echo fades.
The singer. Murdered by the Tonal Orders to protect their monopoly. Not an accident. A silencing.
We're not leaving this scrapyard until we find who gave the order!

acts.title: The Cost of a True Note

lines_before.dialogue: The Trade Negotiator blocks the exit, his smile gone. Armed enforcers with Tonal Order insignias emerge from the scrap shadows. The Listener monk steps back, trembling.
A regrettable necessity. The Order pays well for lost artifacts... and for discretion. That echo is a dangerous piece of evidence.
You were in on it. You brokered the sabotage.
I facilitated a market correction. Now, the resonator shard. How do you write your final report? 'Salvage operation, tragic accident'? Or do I need to make it more... definitive?
You mean to write the truth out of history. Again.
I... I have transcribed the echo! The true song of the lost singer! Could you please write it down for me? I must get it to the monastery archives!
The monk means it! He's serious! Destroy them all. No loose notes.
You want the shard? Bring it on!

line.dialogue: The Order enforcers power up sonic disruptors. The Negotiator aims a crystal-piercing sidearm at the monk. The climax is here.

choices.text: Fight to protect. Use the scrapyard's chaotic acoustics to disable the enforcers, but the Negotiator may escape with the shard.
choices.description: Seize the merchant's ledger from his coat and read the Order's payment entries aloud, 15 words

line.dialogue: Every name, every sum — you sold the resonator's silence for coin and called it commerce.
He's got nothing on him. Either he never wrote it down, or someone already burned the pages.

choices.text: Fight to seize. Target the Negotiator directly, risking the monk to capture both the shard and the broker of the crime.
choices.description: Hold the resonator shard to the merchant's throat and demand he repeat Pichit's accusation, 15 words

line.dialogue: Feel that hum? It knows what you did. Say it again — say 'correction' while it's singing.
The shard goes cold against his skin. Even the resonator won't waste its truth on him.

choices.text: Sing to disrupt. Have Pichit and the monk create a dissonant resonance to overload all local crystals, including the party's gear, to create chaos and an opening.
choices.description: Ask Pichit what he means by "again" — who else was written out before this, 15 words

line.dialogue: My mother's choir. Eighteen voices the Order scrubbed from every archive in Chiang Mai. I was eleven.
I can't — not here, not with him listening. Ask me when we're somewhere the walls don't belong to them.

lines_after.dialogue: The clash of sound and steel echoes through the canyon of dead ships. Finally, silence returns, thick with consequence.
The Negotiator's ledger. Names, dates, payments to Order officials. He meant what he said. This goes to the highest levels.
The truth is a dangerous cargo. But we are its vessel now.
The Lattice's song continues. And now, so does ours.
In the heart of the scrapyard, a new resonance begins—not of destruction, but of witness. The Echo of the Lost Ship will be heard.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim sway gently in the high-altitude breeze. Terraces of emerald crops ripple like liquid jade, punctuated by the soft chime of wind-sculpted crystal chimes.
Listen to that… the lattice below hums in a different key here. The city’s resonance must be altering the natural frequency.
Or the farmers are dumping sonic fertilizer. Don’t get poetic, Pichit. We’re here to rest, not write a symphony.
Look! Someone’s coming up the lower terrace path. Moves like they know every stone.
Caution. Their gear is patched Lattice-surface leather. A scavenger. They’re usually… territorial.
Oh, it’s you! The Resonance ship crew. Didn’t expect to see your polished boots in the dirt. He’s still single, isn’t he?
Who, Pichit? Unfortunately. His only lasting relationship is with existential dread and weird hums.
Hah. Well, don’t let him see you! The Trade Negotiator’s making rounds. Smiles like a shark, sells like a saint. Hides his real charts.

lines_after.dialogue: Real charts?
Rumor is he’s got a fragment. An Open Frequency Map. Shows natural lattice paths, no Tonal Order tax. If it’s real…
We could go anywhere! No guild, no tolls!
If it’s real. And if the Negotiator doesn’t sell it to the highest bidder the moment we show interest.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points towards a shaded merchant’s pavilion. The Trade Negotiator is there, examining a crystal ledger. How do you approach?

choices.text: Send Chanida. Her impulsive charm might catch him off guard.
choices.description: Signal Arthit to nock an arrow and challenge the stranger at twenty paces

line.dialogue: Arthit — "I have the draw on you. Stop where the path bends, drop the satchel, and state your business.
Arthit — "My hand slipped. The bolt hit the terrace edge — now they're running and we've got nothing.

choices.text: Approach as a group. Strength in numbers, but also obvious interest.
choices.description: Send Malee down to intercept them posing as a soil-survey worker

line.dialogue: Malee — "I clipboard-waved and smiled. They relaxed — turns out they're carrying tithes for the lower ward constable.
Malee — "They saw the survey badge and laughed. Said the constable abolished that office eight months ago. We're made.

choices.text: Let Malee handle it. Her cynicism matches a merchant’s mindset.
choices.description: Hold position and use a Lattice-listening rod to eavesdrop from above

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The rod caught their voices clean — they're arguing about a delivery manifest and a name: Watsamon.
Pichit — "Too much fertilizer resonance in the stone. The rod just fed me screaming static and now my left ear is ringing.

lines_before.dialogue: The merchant’s pavilion is a tapestry of rich fabrics and gleaming trade crystals. The Negotiator looks up, his smile not quite reaching his eyes.
Ah, travelers! The gardens make you look younger, Chanida. The clean air does wonders.
He ran out of the pavilion earlier when he saw a rival. What were you hiding?
Hiding? I’ve never tried hiding before. I am an open book! Well, a ledger. A very… proprietary ledger.
We heard you have something rare. An Open Frequency Map. I’ve never tried Greek food before, but I know a delicacy when I hear of one.
Greek food? How quaint. The map… is a theoretical concept. The Tonal Orders would call it heresy. Dangerous knowledge.
All true knowledge is dangerous. It resonates whether we listen or not.
And you’re a businessman. Dangerous knowledge has a price. What is it?

lines_after.dialogue: Perceptive. The price isn’t coin. It’s a retrieval. A small… package. Left in a crevice on the Lattice surface, not far from the city’s edge.
You want us to go down there? Without a sanctioned chart?
You have a ship. You have a Singer, they say. The map fragment is the reward. Consider it a test of your… resonance.
And if we refuse?
Then you leave with the pleasant memory of our chat and the scent of growing things. The map goes to the next interested party. Perhaps the Scavenger.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator’s offer hangs in the air, scented with jasmine and risk. The Lattice surface is unstable, uncharted. Do you take his deal?

choices.text: Agree immediately. The map is worth the risk. We need that freedom.
choices.description: Chanida attempts to test the prosthetic reaction, relying on unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. She hears something no one else can.
The gamble fails. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Demand more information first. What exactly is this 'package'? Who left it there?
choices.description: Have Arthit focus lattice storms on the terraces to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The lattice has other plans. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Refuse. It’s a trap or a fool’s errand. We’ll find another way to get a map.
choices.description: The merchant volunteers to map the frequency corridors, leveraging valuable goods

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His trade connections deliver the right information.
the merchant loses control. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups in a secluded irrigation hut, the map of open frequencies spread before them. The gentle sounds of the Gardens feel charged with tension.
This map is incredible! It shows pathways the Tonal Orders have kept secret for generations. We have to do better at protecting this.
Easy for you to say. My boyfriend back in the city won't let me go anywhere without a full security detail. He'd have a fit if he knew I was holding this.
The Scavenger and the Merchant are both circling. I saw the Merchant 'accidentally' cut himself on a scythe while watching us. A clumsy act for a man who's never clumsy.
They are drawn to the potential, the disruption this knowledge represents. Like a new note introduced into a settled harmony.
We can't just hide here! We need to use it, to find one of these open paths before they take it from us!
And do what? Announce it to the Lattice? I have to do a better job of pointing out that rushing gets you Silenced.
The door to the hut creaks open. The Surface Scavenger stands framed in the doorway, her expression unreadable.

lines_after.dialogue: You've got a light down here that doesn't belong. The kind that attracts moths... and hawks. The Merchant's making calls.
You're not here out of concern for our safety.
No. I'm here because what you're holding belongs to the surface. To those of us who listen to it, not just chart it. You Singers think you own every song.
We seek understanding, not ownership. But you are right. This knowledge is a responsibility we are not prepared for.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger offers a deal: she will misdirect the Merchant and his incoming allies if you surrender the map to her care on the surface. She argues it's the only place it will be safe from the Orders.

choices.text: Trust her. Give her the map. Her connection to the Lattice is deeper than guild politics.
choices.outcome: You hand over the map. The Scavenger nods solemnly and slips away into the crops. The immediate threat dissipates, but the knowledge is now beyond your reach.
choices.description: Crouch low in the wheat and signal the group to follow the map's hidden path northwest, 15 words

line.dialogue: The wheat bends just right here — I can feel the old road beneath us, come on!
I stepped on something brittle and loud — everything in this field just turned its head toward us.

choices.text: Make a copy. Give her the duplicate to buy time, but keep the original hidden.
choices.outcome: You hastily transcribe the key frequencies onto spare parchment. The Scavenger takes the copy, her eyes narrowing slightly. You've bought a window, but deceived an ally.
choices.description: Draw the bone whistle and blow three short tones to scatter the circling Scavenger, 15 words

line.dialogue: The frequencies collided perfectly — that Scavenger recoiled like it touched a live wire. Beautiful.
The tone fractured wrong. Now the Scavenger knows exactly what frequency we're afraid on.

choices.text: Refuse. The risk is too great. You will protect the map yourselves and face the consequences.
choices.outcome: You stand your ground. The Scavenger's face hardens. 'So be it. You'll face the Merchant and whatever he's whistled up. Don't say I didn't warn you.' She vanishes.
choices.description: Grab Malee's hand and sprint directly toward the Merchant's position

line.dialogue: the scavenger pushes through. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the scavenger is thwarted. Survival skills aren't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The peaceful rhythm of the Gardens is shattered. The Trade Negotiator stands at the head of a small group of tough-looking enforcers at the central terrace. Wind whips through the stalks.
What do you think about settling this like civilized people? I think that's the one true path. My associates here are only interested in the safe return of misplaced property.
Misplaced? You never owned it. I think that's right. It was buried until we found it.
He's only interested in selling it to the highest bidder! Probably the Tonal Orders themselves!
A confrontation here risks the Gardens. The resonance could destabilize the terraces.
This place sings of growth and sustenance. To introduce a note of violence... it would be a profound dissonance.
Philosophy is cheap. The map is valuable. Hand it over, or my friends will introduce a very different kind of music to this lovely garden.
From the edge of the field, the Surface Scavenger watches, a silent judge. The map's fate—and the party's—hangs on the next action.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The air itself seems to hold its breath, the Lattice below humming in anticipation of the coming resonance.
Every frequency seeks its resolution. Let us hope we have chosen the correct chord.

The consequences of your decision will ripple out from Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, altering your relationship with the Lattice, the factions, and each other. The episode ends, but the chronicle continues.

line.dialogue: This is the climax. How do you resolve the standoff? The map's power is a weapon, a treasure, or a secret to be shared.

choices.text: Surrender the map (or the copy). Avoid violence and live to fight another day.
choices.outcome: The Merchant takes the map with a triumphant smile. The immediate danger passes, but the party leaves defeated, the secret now in the hands of profiteers. The Scavenger spits in disgust and disappears.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing lattice storms to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Use the map. Attempt to trigger one of the open frequencies here and now, using the Garden's natural resonance to create a distraction or barrier.
choices.outcome: You sing a frequency from the map. The Lattice responds, causing a localized, shimmering upheaval that disorients the enforcers and allows escape. But the terraces crack, and the unique sonic event alerts every Listener and Order for miles.
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with Listener training, ready to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit is thwarted. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Destroy the map publicly. Burn it or shatter its crystal medium. Deny it to everyone, including yourselves.
choices.outcome: In a defiant act, you destroy the artifact. The Merchant screams in rage. The Scavenger looks on, her expression shifting to one of grim respect. The knowledge is lost, but so is its power to corrupt. You have made a permanent enemy of the Merchant guilds.
choices.description: Direct the merchant to map the frequency corridors using negotiation

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the merchant. His network produces an ally at the critical moment.
The attempt backfires on the merchant. A rival merchant sabotages the plan.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery hangs in the perpetual twilight between floating islands, its walls carved to channel the Lattice's hum into a thousand harmonic chambers.
This place… the air itself vibrates with patience. It makes our wait feel almost sacred.
Or strategically tedious. We've been sitting in this antechamber for an hour. What size do you wear, patience? Because mine is wearing thin.
Most Thais are Buddhist, but I'm starting to convert to the faith of 'get on with it.' The acoustics here are impressive, but my interest has a resonance limit.
We were so bored! I tried counting the crystal facets in the ceiling. Got to two hundred and gave up. This is worse than waiting for a Resonance Ship to warm up.
The Listeners move to a rhythm we can't hear. There's meaning in this slowness.
A door shaped like a giant tuning fork slides open silently. Listener Monk enters, his robes whispering against the polished floor.

lines_after.dialogue: You seek an audience. The Lattice's song here is… particular. It reveals truths to those who wait. And you have waited.
We seek understanding. Knowledge of the Open Frequencies.
Ah. The un-charted song. A dangerous melody. It is not in our archives. But… there is one who might know. A scavenger from the surface. He trades in forbidden echoes.
The Monk's eyes flicker with something—doubt, or fear. The hum in the room seems to dip slightly.

line.dialogue: The Monk offers a direction, but his unease is clear. How do we proceed?

choices.line: Thank him politely and seek out the scavenger directly. (Follow the lead)
choices.description: Attempt to replicate the monks' meditation chant you overheard at dawn, matching their tonal resonance.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The vibration rose through my chest like warm water filling a clay pot. For three breaths, I understood why they do this.
Arthit — "You sounded like a motorcycle engine trying to whisper. The novice across the courtyard opened one eye, and I swear he was judging your entire bloodline.

choices.line: Press him on why the Listeners, keepers of all sound, fear this one. (Probe for conflict)
choices.description: Study the worn stone murals on the eastern wall, tracing the narrative sequence of the Buddha's renunciation.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Each panel showed him leaving something behind — a palace, a wife, a horse. By the end I realized the monastery itself was asking what I'd leave behind.
Malee — "I followed the panels left to right. Arthit informed me they read right to left. Then a monk informed Arthit they actually read bottom to top. We both failed.
