choices.line: Ask for a tour of the acoustic chambers first, to better understand the context. (Gain knowledge)
choices.description: Approach the elderly abbot during the permitted questioning hour and ask what "silent truth" actually means.

line.dialogue: Malee — "He looked at me for so long without speaking that I forgot my question. Then
the monk's resolve isn't enough. His recording crystal shatters.

acts.title: Echoes in the Hall of Whispers

lines_before.dialogue: You find the Surface Scavenger in a cavernous hall where sound from the Lattice below is focused into audible strands. He's running a grimy hand along a singing crystal column.
Listeners sent you, huh? Figures. They love to listen, hate to get their robes dirty. I can't speak their tonal poetry. I speak salvage.
We hear you might have a map. Not the Tonal Orders' sanctioned nonsense. The real, open frequencies.
Might. Dangerous thing to have. More dangerous to want. The second option is you turn around, float back to your cozy city.
And the first option?
The first option… you prove you can handle a truth that doesn't come from a Monk's chant. You give a speech. Here. Now.
A speech? In only five minutes? About what?
About why you want it. Convince the echo. This hall remembers. If your reason resonates… maybe it'll tell me something.

lines_after.dialogue: The Scavenger gestures to the center of the hall, where the acoustics converge. The party gathers, the weight of the Lattice's ancient song pressing down.
The truth of the world is a frequency we've been denied. We seek not to control it, but to hear it.
Hmph. Not bad. The crystals shivered on 'denied.' The hall is listening. But is it convinced?

line.dialogue: The Scavenger's challenge hangs in the charged air. Who should speak the final, convincing words to the hall?

choices.line: Let Pichit finish. His philosophical core might harmonize with this place. (Philosophical Appeal)
choices.description: Lean close and lower your voice, asking what the scavenger fears more than the Tonal Order finding out, 15 words

line.dialogue: Your hands are shaking — you're already protecting something. Talk, and we protect you too.
Great. Another cryptic wretch who thinks danger makes them interesting.

choices.line: Let Chanida burst in with passionate, impulsive truth. (Emotional Outburst)
choices.description: Pull a Listener's token from your coat and slide it across the crate between you, 15 words

line.dialogue: The Listeners don't send fools. That seal means we're worth the risk — pay it.
...Not convincing enough? Fine. Keep it. Maybe it buys you a nicer grave.

choices.line: Let Malee deliver a cynical, sharp-edged rationale about freedom from monopoly. (Cynical Truth)
choices.description: Mention the first option plainly — a way out that doesn't involve the map at all, 15 words

line.dialogue: You said 'first option,' which means
the monk misreads the situation. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: In the silent archives of the Phrao Monastery, the air hums with a latent, crystalline energy. The party stands before a vast, carved mural depicting the Lattice's original, untainted song.
Our ancestors charted the Open Frequencies. Pure, stable tones that could part the Lattice anywhere. The Tonal Orders... they locked this map away. Said it was too dangerous.
Convenient for their monopoly. 'Too dangerous' usually means 'not profitable for us.'
If these frequencies are real, and we reveal them, we'd be dismantling the foundation of every Floating City's economy. The Orders would come for us.
So? Let them! People deserve to sail free! This might be true. It *might* be the key to everything!
The monk's conflict... it mirrors our own. To hold a truth that shakes the world. Are we ready for the harmony, or the discord, it will create?
I've seen the surface. The Lattice isn't just pretty music. It *reacts*. If your monk's map is right... you could wake something up there. Or calm something down.
The Listeners have guarded this fragment for generations. We were told it was a sacred duty to keep it silent. But... I'm right, aren't I? Keeping it hidden is another form of the Silencing.

lines_after.dialogue: The monk places a Resonator Shard on the mural. It glows, and a section of the carving begins to emit a low, clear hum—a single, perfect note from the Open Frequency Map.
It's real! The map is real!
From deep within the monastery's foundations, a sympathetic vibration begins. The walls tremble softly, as if answering a long-lost call.

line.dialogue: The monastery shudders. The activated shard has resonated with something ancient below. We must decide how to proceed.

choices.text: (Easy) Secure the shard and retreat to study it safely.
choices.outcome_summary: Cautious preservation. The immediate danger is avoided, but the Tonal Orders may trace the resonance spike.
choices.description: Hack the monastery's sealed archive using Malee's smuggled decryptor, 15 words

line.dialogue: Malee grins, fingers dancing over the decryptor—"Cracked it. The ancestors' frequency maps are ours now, unredacted.
Malee curses as the decryptor sparks and dies—"Tamper-proofed. They rigged the archive to burn its own data on contact.

choices.text: (Medium) Follow the vibration to its source in the lower catacombs.
choices.outcome_summary: Direct investigation. Risk the unstable depths for a chance to understand the Lattice's deeper nature.
choices.description: Meditate in the resonance chamber overnight to attune your body to the Open Frequencies, 15 words

line.dialogue: Arthit opens his eyes, trembling with sensation—"I can feel them. Seven frequencies, threading through everything. They're singing.
Arthit collapses, bleeding from his ears—"Too much. The resonance shattered something in me. I heard... I heard the ones who tried before.

choices.text: (Hard) Amplify the resonance, using the monastery's acoustic architecture to broadcast the Open Frequency.
choices.outcome_summary: A bold declaration. It will alert friend and foe across the region, forcing the conflict into the open.
choices.description: Broadcast a test signal on Chanida's hidden frequency to see who's already listening out there, 15 words

line.dialogue: Chanida laughs wildly as responses flood in—"Sixteen ships answered in the first minute! We were never alone in wanting this!
Chanida's face drains of color as a single signal echoes back—"That's a Navy callsign. We just pinged the wrong people, right into our location.

lines_before.dialogue: The party chose to follow the vibration. Deep in the echoing catacombs beneath Phrao Monastery, they find the source: a massive, primordial crystal formation, pulsing in time with the shard's song.
The Heartstone... legends say it's the first note of the world. The Tonal Orders weren't just hiding a map. They were caging the source.
Of course. They weren't selling navigation. They were selling silence. I was cheated. We all were.
The structural integrity... if we disrupt its frequency, the entire monastery-city could fall from the sky.
The Listeners' true purpose was to soothe it, to keep it dormant. But its song is the Open Frequency. To free it is to break the Orders' control forever.
Then let's break it! Give it to me! I'll sing the note myself!
This is the choice. To maintain a fragile, silent world built on lies. Or to unleash a true, wild song and face the chaos of a new resonance.
Above, the roar of Resonance Ship engines shakes the cavern. The Tonal Orders have arrived. Their vessels blot out the sky, aiming harmonic disruptors at the monastery.

lines_after.dialogue: A voice booms from the lead ship. 'Surrender the artifact. Your heresy ends now.' The disruptors whine, preparing to fire.
Are you finished yet? Building your world on stolen silence?
The Heartstone's pulse quickens, reacting to the threat. The air cracks with latent energy. The final decision is upon you.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Orders are here to enforce their silence. The Heartstone awaits your command.

choices.text: (Easy) Use the shard to dampen the Heartstone, saving the monastery and surrendering to the Orders.
choices.outcome_summary: Safety through submission. The map is lost, the status quo endures, but the party lives.
choices.description: Strike the Heartstone with your tuning blade at its resonance point

line.dialogue: ** "The fracture cascaded perfectly — its frequency is collapsing inward, not outward!
** "I hit the wrong harmonic — the whole chamber is vibrating apart around us!

choices.text: (Medium) Harmonize with the Heartstone, defending the monastery in a resonant shield that drives the Orders back.
choices.outcome_summary: A defiant stand. You protect the truth and the city, but become permanent targets of the Orders' wrath.
choices.description: Sing the Listeners' soothing cadence while pressing both palms to the stone

line.dialogue: ** "I feel it calming under my hands — the old melody still lives in me.
** "My voice cracked on the third verse — it's screaming louder now, I can't hold it!

choices.text: (Hard) Unleash the Heartstone's full Open Frequency, shattering the disruptors and broadcasting the map to every Resonator in range.
choices.outcome_summary: A world-changing climax. The monopoly is broken, navigation is freed, but the resulting global resonance shift is unpredictable and violent.
choices.description: Feed the corrupted navigation shard into the Heartstone's central fissure

line.dialogue: ** "The shard's broken frequency is poisoning its resonance — it's destabilizing exactly as I calculated!
** "It rejected the shard and now it's harmonizing with the corruption instead — we made it worse!

lines_before.dialogue: The terraced gardens of Mae Rim hang like emerald steps from the floating city's edge. The air is thick with the scent of damp soil and blooming night-flowers. A soft, resonant hum from the Lattice far below underpins the rustle of crops.
Listen. The wind through the barley... it's a different pitch tonight. Almost questioning.
Or it's just wind. You're always looking for a sermon in the breeze, Pichit.
No, he's right! My stomach is starting to growl! That means it's time for adventure, not philosophy.
We should be cautious. The Trade Negotiator by the water clock has been watching us. Calculating.
Ah, travelers! The harmony of the gardens welcomes you. Could you speak more slowly? My old ears sometimes miss the finer tones of a deal.
We're just listening.
A noble pursuit! But listening without a map... that's like sailing without a resonator. Dangerous. I might have something to ease your journey.

lines_after.dialogue: The Open Frequency Map. Not a chart, mind you—the Tonal Orders would have my head. More of a... listener's diary. Frequencies where the Lattice sings back, unregulated.
Sounds like a great way to get lost forever. Why are you offering this?
Let's just say some whispers are worth more than coin. And your group seems adept at hearing them.

line.dialogue: The merchant offers the cryptic map fragment in exchange for a future favor, his smile unreadable.

choices.text: Accept the map. Knowledge is worth a debt. (Easy: Gain the map, but owe the merchant.)
choices.description: Follow the wind's whisper toward the barley field's eastern edge, where the stalks bend lowest.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "There! You see how the grain kneels eastward? Something walks among those rows — something heavy, something patient. The wind names what our eyes have not yet found.
Pichit — "I swore the bending pointed us somewhere, but the gusts shifted and now every direction looks the same. The barley keeps its secrets today.

choices.text: Politely decline. We find our own path. (Medium: No map, but no obligation.)
choices.description: Approach the Trade Negotiator's camp by the watermill and quietly observe before announcing yourselves.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Good — three guards, one ledger, and a fourth man whose hands never touch the table. We negotiate from knowledge, not desperation. That is how you keep your gold and your throat.
Arthit — "I miscounted the shadows near the millwheel. There were six, not three, and now a crossbow bolt is buried in the post where my head was. We retreat and rethink.

choices.text: Press him for his real motive. (Easy: Risk offending him, but might learn more.)
choices.description: Stop and eat the salted fish from Chanida's pack before her stomach growls louder and gives away your position.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Oh thank the harvest — my gut was about to announce us to every bandit in the valley. Pass me
The lattice has other plans. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: Whether accepted or refused, the merchant's proposition has tuned the air to a new frequency of tension. The party moves to a secluded overlook, the vast, crystalline expanse of the Lattice shimmering below.
Okay, so we have this weird map... or we don't. There's something in my eye! Ugh, this dust. But also, there's something *here*. I can feel it!
The map fragment indicates a resonant node here in the gardens. An uncharted one. That's no problem for the Orders... because they don't know it exists.
Or it's a myth. Or a trap. First you have to understand, anything 'free' from a merchant has a price you haven't seen yet.
The local villagers are avoiding this terrace. See how the irrigation channel diverts around it? That's deliberate.
You shouldn't be here! That ground... it listens back. Old stories say a Singer once wept here, and the stone never forgot the tune.
A Singer? Here? What kind of place do you prefer for tragic historical resonance, a cliffside or a garden? This is huge!
A low, throbbing hum rises from the very earth, causing the hanging vines to tremble in unison. A patch of soil glows with a soft, blue light.

lines_after.dialogue: The resonance is stable, but unknown. Interacting could attract attention... or reveal a path the Orders have hidden.
Or it could unravel the terrace and send us all into the Lattice. Just a thought.
This is a memory. A frequency brought to the surface. We can listen, or we can answer.

line.dialogue: The glowing node pulses, waiting. The strange hum vibrates in your bones.

choices.text: Touch the node. Listen to the memory fully. (Easy: Gain deep lore, but risk psychic feedback.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the carved stone and listen for the resonant hum, 15 words

line.dialogue: I feel it — the vibration climbs through my bones like a second pulse.
Nothing. Just cold stone and my own heartbeat mocking me.

choices.text: Use the map (if you have it) to safely calibrate and record the frequency. (Medium: Secure the data without risk.)
choices.description: Show the map fragment to the village elder and watch where his eyes refuse to go, 16 words

line.dialogue: His gaze flicks left, then down — he knows exactly what's buried under that terrace.
He spits at the fragment and walks away without a word. We learn nothing.

choices.text: Attempt to disrupt or silence the node. It's too dangerous to leave active. (Hard: Potential combat or environmental hazard.)
choices.description: Cross the terrace alone at dusk carrying only a clay pot of river water, 15 words

line.dialogue: The ground hums when the water touches it — the node is real, and it's hungry.
I made it halfway before the sound hit — like teeth grinding inside my skull. I ran.

lines_before.dialogue: The party reconvenes at a secluded irrigation pool in the Gardens, the water's soft trickle masking their conversation. The Trade Negotiator's map is spread on a stone bench.
First you have to understand... this isn't a navigation chart. It's a registry of 'open' Lattice frequencies. Places the Tonal Orders haven't locked down.
Uncharted resonance zones. That's incredibly volatile. The second option is we burn this and forget we ever saw it.
Volatile means powerful! Look at this marking—a frequency nexus right below the city's underbelly. In only five minutes of descent, we could see what's really down there!
A place the Orders don't control... a natural resonance. The Listeners would call it a sacred whisper. But accessing it...
A Skycity Resident approaches, her face drawn with worry, clutching a basket of wilted sky-root.

You're the ones asking about the deep hum? The one that's making our top-tier crops sour? It's gotten louder. The foreman says it's not a problem, but my stomach is starting to growl thinking of next season's harvest.
Correlation isn't causation, but... a new frequency disturbing growth lines up with the map. The Lattice is reacting.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the fragrant air. Below, the Lattice hums a subtle, discordant note.
We investigate this. Not for profit or power. To understand the song the world is trying to sing.
Then we do it quietly. And we be ready for anything.

line.dialogue: How do we investigate the open frequency nexus below the gardens?

choices.text: Use the map to calibrate the party's personal resonators for a subtle, passive scan.
choices.outcome: Gain data without alerting the Tonal Orders, but learn little of the frequency's nature.
choices.description: Press your palm against the marking and let the frequency flow through you unfiltered.

line.dialogue: Chanida* — "Yes! You feel it too—that's not static, that's the zone *breathing*, and it's calling us deeper!
Arthit* — "Pull your hand back, now—your fingertips are bleeding from the inside, that resonance is shredding you.

choices.text: Have Chanida use her Singer's intuition to 'hum' the open frequency, creating a temporary window.
choices.outcome: Get a clear sensory impression of the nexus, but risk a detectable resonance spike.
choices.description: Sketch the marking's geometry into your field journal and cross-reference it against known Order charts.

line.dialogue: Pichit* — "There—see the overlap? The Orders *mapped* this place but deliberately struck it from their records. They're afraid of it.
Malee* — "You've got it wrong—those aren't Order symbols, they predate the Orders by centuries, and you're reading them backwards.

choices.text: Overload a garden's irrigation crystal to channel the frequency upward, making it visible.
choices.outcome: See the nexus's full form, but will definitely damage crops and draw immediate attention.
choices.description: Hum the tone you heard when the zone first revealed itself and watch how the marking responds.

line.dialogue: Malee* — "It's harmonizing with you—the zone doesn't just tolerate your frequency, it's *mirroring* it. We've found our way in.
Chanida* — "Stop—that's not an echo, that's the zone pushing back, and now everything within ten meters is vibrating at a pitch that makes my teeth ache.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in the Hanging Gardens vibrates with a low, pervasive drone. The chosen method has made the open frequency nexus visible—a shimmering, twisting pillar of unstable light piercing up from the Lattice below the terraces.
It's... beautiful. And hungry. It's pulling on the resonance of the soil. Anywhere you look, the crops are wilting faster.

The Trade Negotiator wasn't selling a map. He was selling a liability. He knew this 'open' frequency was a leak, poisoning the gardens. What kind of profit do you prefer—silver or a city's food supply?
Orders' patrol ships are vectoring in. Our spike was a beacon. We have minutes.
The Negotiator emerges from behind a trellis, his friendly smile now a razor-thin line.

Ah! I see you've appreciated my merchandise. A rare natural formation, yes? Now, what style do you prefer? Letting the Tonal Orders arrest you for unauthorized resonance manipulation, or cutting me in on whatever you find at the nexus's heart?
Why are you doing this to me? To *us*? These people just need to eat.
Why? The oldest song. Profit. Now, choose. The nexus is destabilizing. It can be sealed, harvested, or left to burst. Anywhere you like, but choose quickly.

lines_after.dialogue: The drone becomes a shriek. Crystals in the terrace walls begin to fracture. The fate of Mae Rim's harvest—and the party's freedom—hangs on a single, resonant choice.
We don't play his game. We play the Lattice's.

line.dialogue: The unstable nexus must be dealt with before the Tonal Orders arrive. What is your final, resonant action?

choices.text: Seal the Nexus: Use controlled harmonics to collapse the frequency, saving the gardens but destroying the map's secret.
choices.outcome: The gardens are saved, the Negotiator flees. The Tonal Orders commend your 'responsible' action, tightening their control.
choices.description: Malee attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on mechanical repair

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Malee loses control. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: Harvest the Core: Plunge into the nexus to extract its primal resonance crystal—a power source beyond the Orders' understanding.
choices.outcome: Gain a powerful artifact and escape. The gardens suffer a blight, creating refugees you are now responsible for.
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing Listener training to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The risk doesn't pay off. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.text: Redirect the Flow: Chanida sings, not to close or take, but to guide the chaotic frequency into a harmonious pattern within the Lattice.
choices.outcome: A new, stable resonance enriches the soil for generations. The Negotiator and the Orders are confounded. You become a legend to the Listeners.
choices.description: Convince the merchant to use negotiation and map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: the merchant makes it work. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the merchant's resolve isn't enough. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship glides into the Silent Zone. The familiar hum of the crystal resonators fades to nothing, replaced by a vacuum of sound so profound it feels like pressure on the eardrums.
This is wrong. The Lattice just... stops. It's like looking at a dead ocean. I'm gonna ask him... Pichit, are you sure these coordinates are right?
The charts are clear, Chanida. This is the place. A perfect geometric silence. What did you say, Malee, about the old Listeners' texts?
They called it 'The Stillness That Devours.' I thought it was poetic nonsense. Standing here, I wanna ask you something, Pichit... is this a place, or an absence?
An absence with very real dangers. No resonance means no navigation. We're drifting on momentum alone. I want to ask you a few questions about our power reserves, Chanida.
A shape detaches from a jagged crystal spire below—a scavenger's skiff, cobbled together from salvage. It moves with eerie, silent grace towards the ship.
You're off-course. Or stupid. Which is it?

lines_after.dialogue: We seek understanding. This silence... it contradicts the nature of the Lattice.
Nature? Nothing natural about this graveyard. Your ship's quiet. Good. Noise attracts worse things than me.
Worse things? In a place where nothing makes a sound? How delightfully ominous.

line.dialogue: The scavenger eyes your vessel, her gaze lingering on the resonator housing. She hasn't raised a weapon... yet.

choices.line: Offer trade for local knowledge. (Use supplies.)
choices.description: Direct Malee to tune the prosthetic using crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The risk doesn't pay off. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Press for information about the 'worse things.' (Risk provoking her.)
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing ship navigation to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
A costly mistake by Arthit. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Mention the Resonant Prosthetic subplot. Ask if she's seen related crystal tech. (Might pique her professional interest.)
choices.description: Have the scavenger focus survival skills on the lost signals to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Guided by the scavenger's terse directions, you anchor at a derelict Listeners' observatory, half-swallowed by the inert Lattice. The air is cold and still.
The access door wouldn't budge an inch! The mechanisms are frozen solid. It's as if the silence itself has seeped into the metal.
Told you. This place doesn't give up its secrets. Or its dead. My father, rest him, wouldn't let me scavenge here. Said the quiet steals your thoughts.
Great. So we're in a zone that's also a nursery rhyme. Let's just pry it open. I dreamt my tools were stolen last night, so I double-checked the kit. We're good.
A pragmatic nightmare. How useful. The scavenger's right, though. This structural crystal... it's not just inert. It's *absorbing* the vibration from Arthit's prying bar. Look.
A resonator that doesn't resonate, but consumes... What principle is at work here?
A sharp, cacophonous *crack* shatters the quiet—not from your work, but from above. A grappling hook embeds in the observatory roof. Sky pirates.
Well, ain't this a quiet little party! Don't bother yellin' for help. Sound don't travel here... which makes this the perfect spot for a bit of unfriendly acquisition.

lines_after.dialogue: Pirates! Here? Their ship must be using dampeners... or they're as mad as they look.
Mad? We're pragmatic! Found a frequency that lets us skim this muck like ghosts. Now, your ship's resonator core... it won't move an inch from my cargo hold once we're done.
Over my dead body!
Likely outcome. They know tricks. Hidden harmonics. Fight smart or don't fight at all.

line.dialogue: The pirates are descending, weapons drawn. The silent environment nullifies sonic attacks, forcing close-quarters combat. The scavenger readies a crude cutter, waiting to see your move.

choices.line: Stand and fight at the doorway. Use the choke point. (Direct confrontation.)
choices.description: Pry open the access panel and hotwire the door's hydraulic override with exposed wiring

line.dialogue: Ha! Give me thirty seconds and a live wire — I'll wake this sleeping giant up myself.
The wiring's fused solid. I almost lost a fingertip for absolutely nothing.

choices.line: Fall back into the observatory. Lure them into the unknown interior. (Risky terrain.)
choices.description: Ask the scavenger to reveal whatever they clearly know about this door's weakness

line.dialogue: Fine. There's a maintenance bypass — but you owe me, and I collect with interest.
I told you it doesn't give up secrets. I wasn't offering to play tour guide.

choices.line: Try to use the environment. Have Malee attempt to destabilize the crystal they're anchored to with a precise frequency burst. (High skill, could backfire.)
choices.description: Have Chanida scan the door frame for hidden sensors or alternate entry points

line.dialogue: There — behind the corroded sealant. A secondary hatch, barely visible. Nursery rhyme's got a back door.
Nothing but dead circuits and rust. Even my scanner's giving up on this graveyard.

lines_before.dialogue: The sky pirate's ship, the *Iron Dirge*, sits crippled on a jagged crystal shelf. The unnatural silence of the Zone is now broken only by the groaning of stressed metal and the faint, erratic hum of a damaged resonator.
Price is the same for all of you! Hand over your charts, your spare crystal shards. Everything. Or you'll be joining the Silence permanent-like.
You, too! Look at your ship. It's a wreck. You're in no position to make demands. The price of your arrogance is a broken resonator.
I was bad! I should've seen their ambush coming from the cloud cover. But you won't get another shot.
They both have the same price: our cooperation or our lives. But look… their resonator's frequency is bleeding. It's creating a weak spot in the Lattice beneath them.
A bargain where both sides lose is no bargain. Your ship is dying here. We might all die here. But there might be another price… a way out for everyone.
You surface-dwellers and your noise. Always a price. My people learned that during the Silencing. Your pirate friend's resonator is making the dead zone… twitch. That's ill-mannered. Dangerous.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The damaged pirate resonator continues its dissonant whine, causing faint, spider-web cracks to spread in the crystalline surface below.
Fine! Have it your way. But when the big quiet comes for you, don't come crying to me!
The Zone doesn't forgive. You've stirred it. Now we all pay.

line.dialogue: Pichit, how do you resolve the standoff with the desperate pirates?

choices.text: Offer to combine resonator knowledge to find a safe frequency to escape. (Diplomacy/Knowledge)
choices.description: Draw my sidearm and fire a warning shot past the bandit's ear, demanding they back off.

line.dialogue: That shot wasn't for you—it was for your courage. Walk away while you still have both.
Great, now they're shooting at us AND we've got no charts. Perfect plan, genius.

choices.text: Propose scavenging the pirate ship for parts to jury-rig a single vessel, leaving the pirates behind. (Cunning/Resourcefulness)
choices.description: Offer to share a copy of our charts if the bandits help repair our damaged hull first.

line.dialogue: We trade ink for labor. You get your maps, we get our hull patched. Nobody dies today.
They took the charts AND stripped our hull plating. I trusted the wrong leverage.

choices.text: Suggest using the pirate's unstable resonator to deliberately fracture the Lattice below, creating a temporary 'sound-path' to dive through. (Daring/Resonance Theory)
choices.description: Signal Chanida to hack the bandit's comms while I keep them talking about the price.

line.dialogue: I've locked out their distress beacon. They're deaf and blind now—our move, captain.
They caught my signal trace. Now they want the charts AND our nav computer or we're dead.

lines_before.dialogue: The plan is in motion. The Silent Zone is no longer silent. A deep, grinding shudder runs through the world-crystal, a wrongness felt in the bones. From the fractures, a pale, soundless light bleeds upward.
The resonance cascade is propagating! I thought it was okay, a controlled break, but… it's feeding on itself. We're not making a path; we're waking something up.
It's something to think about: did the Silencing start in a place just like this? A spot where the song just… stopped?
My prosthetic… it's vibrating. Not from our ship. From *down there*. It's like it's… listening to the light.
What do you think about silence? Is it an absence… or a presence waiting to be filled? That light isn't an echo. It's an answer.
The old stories… they talk of a Hunger in the deep places. A thing that consumed the First Song. You've poked it with a stick.
Forget the loot! My ship's coming apart! The quiet's not just quiet anymore—it's pulling!
The fractured Lattice begins to *sing* a single, crushing, subsonic note. The crystal of Chanida's leg glows with sympathetic agony. The world is holding its breath, ready to exhale oblivion.

lines_after.dialogue: The climactic choice reverberates through the Zone. The unnatural light either fades, surges, or transforms. The fate of the party, the pirates, and perhaps a little more of the world, is sealed.
Every sound leaves a mark. Every silence is a choice. We have made ours.
My leg… it's quiet now. Or maybe I just can't hear anything else over the memory of that… note.

line.dialogue: Pichit, the awakened resonance is consuming all sound. How do you silence the Silence?

choices.text: Order a full retreat, overloading all resonators in a discordant shriek to blast a path out, sacrificing the chance to learn the Zone's secret. (Survival)
choices.description: Override the ship's dampeners to sync with the prosthetic's vibration frequency, 15 words

line.dialogue: The frequency locked — my prosthetic is translating something. These aren't random oscillations, they're *words*.
The dampeners shattered. My prosthetic is screaming now, and I can feel every echo crawling up into my skull.

choices.text: Use Chanida's resonant prosthetic as a tuning fork, having her 'Sing' a counter-frequency to cancel out the hunger, risking her connection to the Lattice. (Sacrifice/Unity)
choices.description: Seal the resonance cascade by venting the affected deck into open vacuum, 15 words

line.dialogue: Cascade contained. Whatever was propagating through that deck just got silenced by the void — ironically.
The venting failed. The cascade is *feeding* on the vacuum now. It's not sound, it's something worse.

choices.text: Do not fight it. Guide the party into the heart of the light, into the perfect quiet, to witness what—or who—caused the Silencing. (Truth/Discovery)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to meditate into the silence and describe what he finds there, 15 words

line.dialogue: It's not absence. The silence is *full* — crowded with voices that stopped existing. They want to be
the pirate's resolve isn't enough. The disruptor backfires, jamming itself.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whisper's Wake' drifts into the edge of the Silent Zone. The ambient hum of the crystal resonators dies first, then the distant Lattice-song fades to nothing. An unnatural, oppressive quiet descends.
Well. This is cheery. It's like the world just put on earplugs.
My ears are ringing from the lack of ringing. It's wrong.
Scans confirm it. No harmonic feedback. The Lattice here is... inert. Our charts from the Tonal Orders are blank.
A place that does not answer. What question was so terrible it broke the world's voice?
Ah, my friends! A slight detour, I promise. The trade route through the Zone's edge is... less regulated. More profitable. May I have some time? I need to recalibrate our silent-running protocols.
Profit? In this graveyard? What are we really looking for here?
Opportunity, dear Chanida. Where others hear silence, I hear... potential. Could you tell me how to get to the starboard observation blister? I wish to survey the dead lattice.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant is hiding his true cargo. This silence isn't a shortcut; it's a shroud.
Agreed. Our passive sensors are picking up a faint, repeating structure on the surface. Metallic. Not natural lattice.
Great. A wreck. In a silent zone. I'm sure it's full of friendly, chatty survivors.

line.dialogue: The anomaly is a derelict Resonance Ship, half-submerged in the dead crystal. The Silent Zone presses in.

choices.line: Approach cautiously, scanning for structural hazards.
choices.description: Malee attempts to test the prosthetic reaction, relying on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee hits a wall. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Attempt to use minimal resonator pulse to 'ping' the wreck, risking attention.
choices.description: Ask Arthit to decode the cryptic message, drawing on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Arthit overreaches. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.line: Send a drone first, keeping the 'Whisper's Wake' at a safe distance.
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using information network to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: the merchant succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Things don't go as planned. Hidden debts come due.

lines_before.dialogue: The derelict ship, the 'Echo of Dawn,' looms like a fossil. Inside, the silence is absolute. Dust hangs motionless. Flickering light comes from a single, fractured resonator core.
Life support failed decades ago. But the core... it's cycling. On. Off. Like a heartbeat.
What's this called? A tomb with a pulse?
A man called this place a 'dead zone.' He undersold it.
Listen. Not with your ears. Feel the air. There is a... pressure. A memory of sound.
You shouldn't be here.
A figure melts from the shadows near a shattered console—the Surface scavenger, clad in patched lattice-weave.
This wreck is claimed. Surface law. Someone called you here. The merchant. He's selling what he shouldn't.

lines_after.dialogue: Selling what? Scrap?
The core. The last echo of the 'Dawn.' It's not tech. It's a recording. Of the Silencing.
A recording of the end of the world. And our smooth-talking friend wants to put it on the open market. Charming.
An echo of the trauma that created this silence... to play it here could be catastrophic.

line.dialogue: The scavenger points to the flickering core. The 'echo' is unstable. The merchant is on his way, expecting his prize.

choices.line: Secure the core to contain the echo, then confront the merchant.
choices.description: Place your palm flat against the core's housing and let the vibration travel up your arm.

line.dialogue: Pichit* — "There. You feel it? That's not machinery. That's breathing. Something in there thinks it's alive.
Pichit* — "Your hands are shaking too much. You're listening to your own fear instead of what's underneath.

choices.line: Attempt to safely discharge the core's energy into the dead Lattice, destroying the echo.
choices.description: Ask arthit to reroute auxiliary power from the dead life support systems into the core's diagnostic terminal.

line.dialogue: Arthit* — "Routing now. The terminal's lighting up — dozens of processes still running. Someone left this running and never came back.
Arthit* — "Nothing. The power nodes are corroded past anything I can bridge. Whatever's in there, it doesn't want us reading its mail.

choices.line: Risk listening to the echo fragment to learn the truth of the Silencing, hoping it doesn't break your mind.
choices.description: Follow the low-frequency hum deeper into the corridor toward the sealed chamber marked "PRIMARY CONSCIOUSNESS."

line.dialogue: Malee* — "The hum's getting thicker — like walking through syrup. Whatever's in that room knows we're coming. I almost prefer the dead zones.
the scavenger's resolve isn't enough. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The party ventures deeper into the Silent Zone. The unnatural quiet presses in, making even their own breathing sound like a violation. The faint, ghostly outline of the lost Resonance Ship, the *Echo of the Lost*, now hangs in the dead air ahead, fused into a jagged spire of inert crystal.
Well, there it is. The ghost ship. Looks about as welcoming as a tomb. Which, I suppose, it is.
Do you feel that? It's not just quiet... it's hungry. This place *wants* sound.
Our resonator readings are flat. No resonance at all. If we go in there, we're cut off. No calling for help.
The Scavenger said the ship's final log might be intact. The answer to what happened here... it's waiting.
So, are you ready to go back home yet? Or are we seeing this through?
(He) left home in a hurry, chasing whispers. Now we're chasing silence. Poetic, really.
This place... it's a lot more fun than the Merchant's endless haggling, in a terrifying way. Let's move.

line.dialogue: The entrance to the fused wreck is a jagged tear in the hull. Inside, darkness swallows the little light from the zone. Faint, frozen screams are etched into the crystal walls.

choices.text: Light the chemical flares. Create a safe, well-lit perimeter before proceeding.
choices.outcome_tag: Cautious and bright. The light pushes back the oppressive dark, revealing safe passage but also making the party perfectly visible.
choices.description: Force the airlock manually, risking the vacuum backlash, 14 words

line.dialogue: Seal holds—minimal decompression. We're in, but watch your step.
Blowout! The seal shattered—grab something solid before the current takes you!

choices.text: Rely on Arthit's resonance scanner in passive mode. It won't emit sound, but can map the structure from residual energy.
choices.outcome_tag: A ghostly map of the ship's interior forms on the scanner. It guides you, but shows chilling anomalies moving in the static.
choices.description: Let Chanida extend her senses into the corridor before anyone crosses the threshold, 15 words

line.dialogue: It's not hostile—not yet. It's tasting us. Move slowly and don't speak its name.
Something just noticed me back. Everyone stop. *Do not move.*

choices.text: Move in total darkness and silence. Feel your way. The ship's memory might communicate more directly if you don't disrupt it.
choices.outcome_tag: The silence becomes a canvas. Faint pressure, cold spots, and the overwhelming sense of *presence* guide—or herd—you forward.
choices.description: Send Pichit's drone ahead to locate the final log while the team holds position, 14 words

line.dialogue: Drone's through. I can see the log archive—three decks down, door's open.
Signal just... folded. The drone's still broadcasting but it's facing us now.

lines_after.dialogue: {{outcome_tag}} Deeper within, the ship's command spire is a cathedral of frozen catastrophe. At its center, the captain's chair is occupied by a crystalline statue, its face a mask of final horror.
The lattice... it didn't just stop responding. It *inverted*. It absorbed every sound on the ship, then... kept pulling.
A feedback loop of silence. Charming. So this whole zone is a sound-sucking wound.
The log! The crystal core... it's still recording. It's not data. It's a *scream*.

lines_before.dialogue: The crystal core of the *Echo* hums with captive agony. Touching it risks being consumed by the same silence that took the crew. But within that captured scream lies the truth of The Silencing—and a way to heal the Zone.
The core holds the pattern. A perfect anti-resonance. We can use it... to cancel the Zone's effect. Or amplify it.
Most Thais are Buddhist. We understand karma. This thing is pure karmic debt. We meddle, we pay.
The energy release would be catastrophic. It won't cost so much if we contain it, but containment...
Containment means one of us has to channel it. Be the anchor. (The price) is rather expensive for Thais... or anyone.

A voice, smooth as oil, crackles from a salvaged comms unit. *Ah, the heroes find the treasure! The knowledge of the Silent Zone's origin... the Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for its suppression. I can make you rich.*
Another voice, gritty and real, cuts in from a different channel. *Don't listen to that vulture! That knowledge belongs to the Listeners! To everyone! Use it to break the Orders' monopoly!*
So. We can sell the secret for wealth. Give it to the rebels for a revolution. Or... we can try to fix the wound. And pay the price ourselves.

line.dialogue: The core's scream intensifies, vibrating the very air. A choice must be made, and the act will echo forever.

choices.text: Sell the data to the Merchant. Let the Tonal Orders bury the truth. Take the wealth and guarantee safe passage out.
choices.outcome_tag: Practical and cold. The Zone remains, a secret kept. The party gains immense wealth but carries the guilt of complicity. The world does not change.
choices.description: Malee channels leg resonance toward the crushing quiet, hoping to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Transmit the data openly to the Scavenger's network. Break the Orders' control. Spark a revolution across the Floating Cities.
choices.outcome_tag: Ideological and dangerous. The Silent Zone becomes a rallying cry. Chaos and hope erupt across the Lattice. The party becomes both heroes and fugitives.
choices.description: Chanida uses crystal hearing to decode the cryptic message near the lost signals

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Things don't go as planned. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Channel the anti-resonance. One of the party must become a temporary Singer of Silence, absorbing the Zone's hunger to neutralize it, risking their mind or life.
choices.outcome_tag: Sacrificial and profound. The Silent Zone 'sings' a final, healing tone before falling truly silent. The Lattice elsewhere thrums with renewed vitality. One party member is forever changed, a living scar of silence.
choices.description: Ask the merchant to trace the anomalous signal, drawing on negotiation

line.dialogue: the merchant's expertise pays off. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the merchant overreaches. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_after.dialogue: {{outcome_tag}} As the decision resolves, the Silent Zone reacts. The dead lattice shudders. For the first time in centuries, sound returns—a single, clear tone that is a death rattle.
We have changed this place. For better or worse, we have spoken into the silence. Now we must live with the echo.
Resonance readings are... stabilizing. Or dispersing. The math is new.
Well. That was probably the most expensive trip of my life. And I don't just mean the fuel.
Look. The sky... it's not just grey anymore. You can see a color. I think it's blue.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Echo's Promise' glides through the empty sky, its crystal resonators humming a low, steady tone that parts the shimmering Lattice below. The wind carries the scent of ozone and distant rain.
Look at it! The way the light fractures on the crystals... it's a lot more fun than staring at the same old city walls.
Fun? We're kilometers above a reactive energy field with a single hull between us and dissolution. Please keep your hands inside the railings.
He complains a lot! He's really a complainer. Arthit, you used to be a sickly child. Did getting sick a lot make you afraid of heights, or just fun in general?
The complaints, the awe... they're both valid frequencies. This silence between the sky-cities holds more truth than the crowded markets.
A smaller, patched-together skiff pulls alongside, matching your ship's resonance. A weathered figure waves from its deck.
Ho there! You the ones asking about the old Listeners' outposts? The ones that went quiet before The Silencing?
We are. Their archives might hold patterns the Tonal Orders have forgotten.

lines_after.dialogue: Forgotten, or buried. I know a place. Surface-side. But my skiff's resonator is cracked. Your ship's stronger tone could get us through the local lattice turbulence.
Ah, a surface guide! How fortuitous. My own business in the next city could benefit from... alternative routes. Less toll-heavy ones. Perhaps we can come to a mutual arrangement?
The merchant's smile doesn't reach his eyes. The scavenger spits over the railing, watching the spittle vanish into the glowing lattice below.

line.dialogue: The scavenger has a lead, but wants passage. The merchant sees profit. The ship's course needs setting.

choices.line: Agree to the Scavenger's terms. Divert course for the surface. (Gain a guide, commit to the detour.)
choices.description: Have Malee focus mechanical repair on the cloud corridors to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee fails. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: Hear the Merchant's proposal first. Information has value. (Possible profit, but waste time and risk the scavenger's trust.)
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using lattice storms to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
The gamble fails. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Consult the ship's charts. See if the old outpost is even on our authorized Tonal Order routes. (Play it safe, but possibly miss the opportunity.)
choices.description: Have the scavenger risk using platform climbing to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the scavenger. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Things don't go as planned. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship descends toward a jagged protrusion of the Lattice, a 'mountain' of solidified sound. The air grows thick with harmonic feedback, making the deck plates vibrate.
Steady now... the frequency here is raw. Uncharted. Your resonator's holding, though. It was a good experience, choosing your ship.
The stress readings are approaching the red line. 'Good experience' is a subjective assessment of potential catastrophic failure.

Failure is just unmet expectation! Look at the crystal formations here—untapped resonance grade! I'm in a good mood just thinking of the procurement possibilities. Tell me, surface-dweller, is the pay good for harvesting these?
The pay is staying alive. This isn't a quarry. It's a graveyard. The Listeners who built here didn't just 'go quiet.' They screamed into the Lattice until it swallowed them.
Then what are we looking for? If it's not salvage, what's the point?
A scream leaves a shape. A permanent resonance. If we can find it, map its frequency... we might find what they learned before they fell.
Great. So we're here to document a disaster. My favorite kind of field trip.

lines_after.dialogue: The ship settles into a precarious equilibrium above a sheer crystal face. Etched into it, barely visible, is the outline of a door—a Listener's spire entry. The scavenger points to a crumbling ledge.
There. The entrance. My skiff can't get closer. Someone needs to go across. On foot. While your ship holds the frequency steady and keeps the lattice from... reacting.
On foot? On *that*? The liability alone... Perhaps the data inside can be scanned remotely? For a percentage, of course.
A low, pained groan echoes from the crystal itself. The deck shudders. The door's outline pulses with a faint, sickly light.

line.dialogue: The path is dangerous and requires someone to leave the safety of the ship. The ship itself must be expertly managed to maintain the stabilizing frequency.

choices.line: Send the Scavenger. They know the surface. We'll manage the ship. (Rely on their expertise, but trust them alone with whatever's inside.)
choices.description: Override the frequency limiter and push the crystal deeper into resonance mapping.

line.dialogue: * "The harmonic fold is stabilizing — I can see the pattern forming, right there in the noise!
* "The limiter cracked — I'm reading feedback through my own damn teeth.

choices.line: Pichit will go, with Chanida for support. Arthit and Malee manage the ship's resonance. (Balanced risk, but splits the party's key skills.)
choices.description: Pull the merchant aside and demand to know what they actually paid the scavengers for.

line.dialogue: * "You sold them a quarry job. This is something else. What did you really bring us into?
* "They just laughed — said I'd find out soon enough, and that my cut was already spent.

choices.line: Attempt a risky maneuver: use the ship's main resonator to blast the door open from here. (Fast and keeps everyone aboard, but could collapse the site or destabilize the Lattice violently.)
choices.description: Shut down the array and order everyone to fall back behind the shielding barricade.

line.dialogue: * "Everyone behind the barrier NOW — the red line isn't a suggestion, it's a countdown.
* "Too slow — the array kicked back online on its own and now it's singing in a key I can't shut out.

lines_before.dialogue: The deck is unnervingly quiet. The ship's engine hums at a lower frequency, a deliberate dampening as you navigate a narrow, shimmering canyon of crystal spires.
This is the path from the Scavenger's coordinates. The lattice resonance here is... chaotic. One wrong note and we shear the hull open.
And our new 'friend' the Negotiator is pacing below decks like a caged bird. He knows we're close to the Open Frequency source. His profit margins are getting a cramp.
Forget him! Look! The spires ahead are glowing in sequence. It's a pattern! It’s the map!
Not a drawn chart... a living one. A song played by the Lattice itself. The Listeners would weep to hear it.
A low, grinding shiver runs through the ship. From the starboard rail, the Surface Scavenger points a gloved finger downwards, her voice tight.
Breach. Port side. Your fancy Negotiator's 'escort ship' just dropped its cloaking resonance. They're moving to intercept.
Now, now, let's not be hasty! I merely facilitated a meeting with my associates from the Tonal Orders. They're... concerned about unlicensed cartography.

line.dialogue: The rival ship is closing, its harmonic cannons powering up. The living map pulses ahead in the narrow canyon. Arthit shouts a warning.

choices.line: DIVE FOR THE MAP: Channel all power to forward resonators and plunge into the glowing spires, trusting the Lattice's song to guide you.
choices.consequence: You embrace the unknown frequency, but it's a wild, untamed path.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to test the prosthetic reaction, relying on captain experience

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Things don't go as planned. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.line: HOLD POSITION / NEGOTIATE: Use the Open Frequency as a bargaining chip. Try to talk the Tonal Orders down from firing.
choices.consequence: You play the merchant's game, but words are weak against prepared harmonics.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with monk wisdom to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
The resonance turns hostile. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.line: TURN AND FIGHT: Use the canyon walls for cover. Man the ship's defensive harmonics and face the escort head-on.
choices.consequence: You choose direct conflict in a perilously confined space.
choices.description: The merchant uses negotiation to decode the tonal pattern near the sails

line.dialogue: the merchant finds the key. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Defeat. A rival merchant sabotages the plan.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made in a heartbeat. The ship groans as it responds, crystal spires flashing past the railings.
Brace for resonant feedback! Everyone, hold onto something!
Oh, wonderful. I always wanted to get shot at in a glass maze. You, too, Merchant! Enjoy the show you arranged!
The map's lighting up faster! I think... I think it's responding to us!

acts.title: A Song Introduced to the World

lines_before.dialogue: Chaos on the deck. The escort ship's harmonic bolts scream past, shattering distant spires. The living map ahead is a storm of light and sound.
Please, you must understand! A friend in the Orders introduced us to this venture! I was just the middleman! Could you speak more slowly to them on the comms?
Save your breath. They're not listening. Their cannon's priming for a full burst. It'll crack this canyon open.

No. The map... it's not just a path. It's a key. Chanida, when you hummed that note yesterday... it reminded me of my childhood. I used to be a sickly child, listening to the wind in the pipes. It sounded like this.
Poetic, Pichit, but my calf has a cramp from bracing, and we have about thirty seconds!
He's right! The map's a song, and we're in the middle of it! We have to sing back! The right harmony could... could change the resonance field!
Theoretical! And if we're wrong, we amplify their blast into our faces!
A deep, punishing hum builds from the enemy ship. The lattice below begins to vibrate, a catastrophic sympathetic resonance.

line.dialogue: The escort's cannon glows white-hot. The living map's song reaches a frantic crescendo around you. Pichit feels a strange certainty humming in his bones.

choices.line: UNLEASH THE MAP'S SONG: Direct all resonator power into the lattice spires around you, amplifying the natural frequency to overload the enemy's systems.
choices.consequence: You weaponize the discovery, but the Lattice's reaction is unpredictable.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to test the prosthetic reaction, drawing on hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida misreads the situation. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: SHIELD AND TRANSMIT: Use the ship to shield the map's source while broadcasting the Open Frequency to every listener on public bands. Give the secret away to save it.
choices.consequence: You break the monopoly, but make enemies of every power.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing ship navigation to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
The gamble fails. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: SING THE SILENCE: Have Chanida sing the counter-frequency, the 'Silence' between notes. Attempt to dampen the attacking resonance entirely, a feat only theorized.
choices.consequence: You attempt the impossible, risking the singer and the ship's sanity.
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with trade ledger to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the merchant. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The resonance turns hostile. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice becomes action. A new sound joins the cacophony—a pure, clear tone from your ship that doesn't fight the chaos, but *weaves* it.
The lattice flashes. The enemy's harmonic blast distorts, unravels, and scatters into a thousand harmless echoes. The escort ship reels, its systems fried by the feedback.
And then, quiet. The living map's light stabilizes, pulsing gently like a heartbeat. It is no longer a secret path, but a broadcast beacon, its song now echoing across the resonant bands.
It's done. The Open Frequency... a friend introduced us to it, and now we've introduced it to the world.
Hmph. The Tonal Orders will be hunting you for this. But... the sky just got a little wider.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship 'Song's Lament' cuts through the high air. Below, the crystalline Lattice ripples and hums in response to the ship's calibrated engine tones. The deck is a stage of wind, light, and sound.
Finally! I thought we'd never leave that floating rock. Felt like we were stuck there for ages.
A necessary delay. Those Tonal Order charts had to be verified. One wrong frequency could send us into a dissonant cascade.
Verifying what? That they're still charging a fortune for maps to places they've probably never been? How noble.
Every departure is a small Silencing of its own. We leave a place, and its sounds become memory. Are we ever truly going home, or just chasing its echo?
Deep thoughts for a Tuesday, Pichit. I'm just glad to be moving. Though... did anyone else feel like we left home in a hurry? The port-master seemed anxious to see our stern.
A new figure emerges from the crew quarters—a woman in patched, Lattice-dusted leathers. Her eyes scan the horizon below with a hunter's focus. This is the Surface Scavenger.
You're back late from that port. Or early for the next. Hard to tell with you sky-dwellers. You feel that? The Lattice's song is... jittery. Like before a storm.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost resonance signature? That's not just unusual, it's nearly impossible unless...
Unless the ship that made it isn't lost. It's hiding. Or something is hiding it. Fantastic.
The 'Whisper of Dawn.' Vanished three cycles ago. No wreckage. No final song. Just silence. Then, last week, that echo. Are you ready to go back home yet? Or are you curious?

line.dialogue: The Scavenger has presented a mystery tied to the subplot of the lost ship. The faint echo is a lure into the unknown. How does the party respond?

choices.text: Dismiss it as Lattice static. Stay on the plotted course. (Avoid immediate risk, but ignore the mystery.)
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Log the coordinates for later. Promise to investigate if our route permits. (Commit cautiously, keeping options open.)
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing crystal hearing to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Chanida overreaches. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Ask the Scavenger to guide us. Plot a minor detour to investigate the echo now. (Pursue the mystery directly.)
choices.description: The scavenger uses surface knowledge to follow the dissonant trail near the sails

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Hard-won survival skills turn the tide.
the scavenger hits a wall. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship has altered course toward the coordinates. The Lattice below has changed from gentle azure waves to a jagged, violet plain. The engine's hum seems thinner here, fighting against a heavy, absorbing silence.
Resonance readings are... wrong. The Lattice isn't reflecting our tones properly. It's swallowing them. I feel uncomfortable with this atmospheric absorption.
It's just quiet. Spooky-quiet. I knew right away this place was different. The wind doesn't even whistle.
Of course it's different. We're in a graveyard. Every scavenger's tale says the same: some patches of the Lattice just... remember. And they don't like visitors.
To remember is to resonate with the past. But what if the memory is one of being unmade? The silence here doesn't feel empty. It feels full of something that has stopped speaking.
A second figure approaches—the Listener Monk, his simple robes stark against the high-tech deck. He holds a resonant recording crystal that glows with a faint, sickly pulse.
You feel it too. The absence. My Order has monitored this sector since the 'Whisper' vanished. The natural song here... I don't feel the same reverence as before. Only a wound.
Listener. Your kind charts the songs but never walks the strings. You hear the wound. I've seen it. Down there. Shapes in the crystal that don't match any ship I know.

lines_after.dialogue: My duty is to observe, not to intervene. But this... this is an unnatural silencing. It contradicts the First Vibration. The truth of this place is a scream trapped in silence.
So are we looking for a ship or a tomb? And what's making that echo if everything here is supposed to be silent?

The recording crystal in the Monk's hand flares suddenly. A distorted, fragmented sound escapes—a fractured chord, a desperate voice chopped into syllables, then the screech of tearing metal. It cuts off. The silence that follows is deeper, heavier.

line.dialogue: The haunting echo has been captured, however faintly. The Monk is conflicted, the Scavenger is wary, and the Lattice itself feels hostile. The source seems close. What is the next step?

choices.text: Send a probe. Scan from a safe distance without risking the ship. (Gather data cautiously, but remotely.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the nearest headstone and let the silence flood through your resonance sense.

line.dialogue: The stone is... singing backward. Drinking sound. This entire graveyard is a negative frequency sink.
Nothing. Dead signal. Either the Lattice can't reach here or something is swallowing it whole.

choices.text: Have the Monk and Scavenger try to purify/interpret the echo together. Use their combined expertise. (A diplomatic and investigative approach.)
choices.description: Split the party — send Chanida and Pichit to map the silence's edges while you and Malee hold center.

line.dialogue: The quiet has a *shape*, Arthit. It's not absence — it's architecture. Something built this stillness.
I can't — the silence moves when we move. It's herding us. We need to stay together.

choices.text: Drop resonance anchors. Lower the ship into the Lattice layer for a physical search. (A direct, high-risk confrontation with the unknown.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sing the Memorial Verse directly into the void and watch what answers back.

line.dialogue: They're listening. Every voice this earth has swallowed is listening. I can feel them leaning forward.
My throat closed. The words wouldn't come. Whatever lives in this silence — it doesn't want remembrance. It wants forgetting.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship hangs in a silent pocket of sky, its engines humming a low, steady tone. Below, the Lattice stretches like a frozen sea, its crystalline facets reflecting the pale light of distant floating cities.
We were so bored! Waiting for the right harmonic to pass so we could dive. But then we saw it—the ghost ship's silhouette, drifting just beneath the crystal surface.
A derelict? Probably picked clean by scavengers decades ago. What's so special about it?
It sings. Not with engine tones, but with the Lattice's own voice. A pure, unbroken note that has lasted since The Silencing. My order has studied its echo for generations.
And you never tried to board it? I have an uneasy feeling about this. A ship that shouldn't exist, singing a song that shouldn't be...
That's exactly why we have to go! The Tonal Orders would kill to have those charts. This could change everything!
A vessel that became part of the song it was meant to navigate. There's a profound lesson there. The boundary between tool and nature... dissolved.
Lesson or not, it's dangerous. The lattice around it is... unstable. Resonates wrong. But I'm a Buddhist. I believe in cycles. Maybe this ship's cycle isn't finished.

line.dialogue: The ghost ship's harmonic signature pulses through your own vessel's crystals. To approach, you must match its resonance—a delicate, potentially catastrophic procedure.

choices.line: Let the Listener Monk guide the approach. He knows the song best.
choices.description: Board the derelict through the hull breach near the engine housing, weapons drawn, 15 words

line.dialogue: * "I go first — if something's still alive in there, better it eats me than someone useful.
* "The breach collapsed under me — whatever's in there, it doesn't want guests through the back door.

choices.line: Use the scavenger's surface knowledge to find a physical anchor point on the Lattice.
choices.description: Match the monk's harmonic frequency to the Lattice song before approaching the derelict, 15 words

line.dialogue: * "I hummed its note back — and the hull groaned open like a throat accepting medicine.
* "I matched the tone wrong — the song curdled into something that bled from my nose for an hour.

choices.line: Have Chanida attempt to 'sing' the matching frequency, raw and untrained.
choices.description: Scan the derelict for life signs and

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The lattice has other plans. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_after.dialogue: The ship shudders as the frequencies align. A groaning shriek of crystal on crystal, then a sudden, profound silence. A portal of parted lattice opens, revealing the dark, ice-encrusted hull of the ancient vessel.
Well. We're committed now. Let's hope the 'profound lesson' isn't 'how to die frozen to a ghost ship.'
Life support readings are minimal. We have one hour before our own resonance link decays. Move quickly.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the lost ship, time stands still. Frozen crew, instruments locked mid-reading, all preserved in a sheath of resonant ice. At the heart of the bridge, a massive, fractured crystal core pulses with a weak, arrhythmic light.
The source of the song... and its cage. This core didn't just fail. It was overloaded. Purposely.
Sabotage? But why? Come in. Look closer. The captain's log—the final entry.
'We have learned the truth of The Silencing. It was not an accident. It was a... correction. The Lattice rejected our noise. The Orders know. They will silence us too.'
The Tonal Orders caused The Silencing? To maintain control? Interesting! No—that's monstrous!
He hung up. The log cuts off. They were hunted. For discovering that our masters are the ones who broke the world.

The core's instability is increasing. Our presence is agitating it. We have a choice: extract the data crystal and condemn this ship to final dissolution, or try to stabilize the song and leave this truth buried.
A truth that shakes the foundation of every floating city. To reveal it is to start a war. To conceal it is to live a lie.

line.dialogue: The core's pulse becomes erratic, casting jagged shadows. The ghost ship's song is dying, and with it, the only physical proof of the Order's ancient crime.

choices.line: Stabilize the core. Preserve the ship and its secret. Some truths are too dangerous.
choices.description: Smash the resonant cage with your staff, freeing the trapped frequency inside.

line.dialogue: The monk's eyes widen as pure tone floods the chamber — "It sings again! After centuries, it SINGS!
The monk cries out as the staff rebounds — "The cage amplifies resistance. We need its frequency first, brute force alone won't shatter it.

choices.line: Extract the data crystal carefully. Let the ship fade. The truth must be known, but discreetly.
choices.description: Examine the captain's log fragments scattered near the scavenger's console.

line.dialogue: The scavenger's hands tremble over the data — "Captain knew. Knew the Orders were bleeding the Resonance dry. She died protecting this evidence.
The scavenger hisses in frustration — "Corrupted sectors. Whoever purged this wanted the captain's final entry gone forever. I can only recover fragments.

choices.line: Overload the core completely. Let its final, catastrophic 'note' broadcast the truth to every Listener and Singer across the Lattice.
choices.description: Invoke the Tonal Orders' own doctrine against them, using their recorded admission as a weapon.

line.dialogue: Chanida's voice rings with cold satisfaction — "They documented everything. Their own archives condemn them — The Silencing was murder, and they called it 'stewardship.
Chanida slams the console — "Doctrinal encryption. The Orders locked their confessions behind riddles only a Master Tonalist could parse — and they're all dead now.

lines_after.dialogue: As your resonance ship pulls away, the fate of the ghost ship is sealed. Behind you, it either fades into eternal silence, vanishes in a shower of harmonic data, or erupts in a blinding pulse of light and sound that ripples across the crystalline plain.
The song... has changed. Or perhaps we are finally hearing it correctly. Our order has much to contemplate.
The surface won't be the same after this. Nothing will. You've dropped a stone in still water.
Was it the right choice? We'll never know. We just have to live with it.
Every choice resonates. Today, we have added our note to the world's long, broken song. Let us hope it leads toward harmony, not another Silencing.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Harmony's Echo' drifts into the Silent Zone. The crystalline lattice below ceases its shimmering response to the ship's hum. An unnatural stillness swallows the world.
The charts are dead. Nothing. Just... flat resonance. I'm afraid there'll be a problem. Why didn't you go with the Tonal Order's safe route?
Because the safe routes are known. The unknown holds the truth of The Silencing. This silence... it's a question, not an answer.
The question is whether we'll starve before our resonator crystals drain. This place sucks the song out of everything.
We should conserve power. Reduce all non-essential frequency output. The quiet is... deeply unsettling.
A flicker on the long-range scanner. Not a ship signature, but a ghostly echo of one, repeating a fragment of a lost distress frequency.
There. An echo. It's tied to the subplot_haunted_ship. The Echo of the Lost Ship. In a place with no sound, a sound persists.
Let's follow it! It's a clue! Maybe it leads to a way out, or... something that survived The Silencing!

lines_after.dialogue: Or it leads to whatever killed them. Brilliant plan.
The echo is unstable. Approaching could destabilize our own resonator field.
As the debate continues, a small, battered skiff emerges from behind a drifting crystal shard. A Listener Monk stands at its prow, his robes still humming faintly with residual song.
You are drawn by the echo. I have studied it. It is a memory of the lattice, a scar. Reverent but conflicted. My duty is to observe, but the truth... it whispers of a violence.

line.dialogue: The monk gestures toward the pulsing echo. 'The path is fraught. You seek the source?'

choices.text: Trust the Monk's Guidance. Follow his skiff cautiously toward the echo.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Chanida overreaches. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Scan the Echo Aggressively. Use the ship's resonator to probe the signal, risking feedback but gaining data.
choices.description: Arthit uses ship navigation to confront hidden knowledge near the unresponsive lattice

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
Things don't go as planned. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Hold Position and Observe. Stay back, studying the echo and the Silent Zone from a safe distance.
choices.description: The monk takes the lead, employing recording crystals to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the monk fails. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The chosen path leads deeper into the Silent Zone. The ghostly echo grows louder, a paradox in the quiet. It reveals the silhouette of a derelict Resonance Ship, frozen in the lattice like a fossil.
The 'Chorale's End'. It was caught here during The Silencing. Its final song... trapped. I listen, but I hear no peace. Torn between duty and truth.
Roll up your sleeves. We need to get inside. If there's a log, a survivor's record...
That's all, isn't it? The hope that someone left a note before they died. I'm just surprised the lattice hasn't crushed it yet.
The structural resonance is null. No vibrational support. Entering could collapse the hull. We need a stabilizing frequency.
The silence here is not natural. It is a forced quiet. Something... silenced this ship, this place.
A rough, amplified voice crackles over a pirate band frequency, cutting through the dead air. A Sky Pirate cutter, bristling with jury-rigged resonators, approaches.

Hah! Listeners and fools! Aggressive, opportunistic. That hulk's got a cargo hold full of stabilized crystal cores! Know hidden frequencies. We're cutting it open. Sky pirates. Stand aside or get scrapped!

lines_after.dialogue: The cores... they are the ship's heart. Removing them would erase the echo forever. The memory would be lost.
We can't let them! That echo is a clue to The Silencing!
History's dead! Profit's alive! Rough speech. You wanna fight over a ghost?
Their ship is armed with resonant disruptors. A direct conflict is dangerous.

line.dialogue: The pirate cutter moves to latch onto the derelict. The echo wavers. You must act.

choices.text: Negotiate with the Pirates. Offer a share of any find, or information on other wrecks, to avoid conflict.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use monk wisdom and calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Pichit hits a wall. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Sabotage the Pirate's Resonators. Use the Silent Zone's dampening effect to stealthily disable their cutter's systems.
choices.description: Chanida steps forward with singer voice, ready to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Board the Derelict First. Race to enter the 'Chorale's End' and secure the crystal cores before the pirates can.
choices.description: Direct the monk to map the frequency corridors using crystal bowls

line.dialogue: the monk's expertise pays off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
A costly mistake by the monk. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The party's ship drifts deeper into the Silent Zone. The oppressive quiet is now a physical weight, pressing in from all sides. The Lattice below is a dull, lifeless gray.
Navigation crystals are completely inert. We're flying blind. Every reading is just... nothing.
Of course they are. We're in a giant dead spot. I'm just surprised the sky pirates were desperate enough to come here.
Look! On the horizon! A shape... a ship! It's just... floating there. Not drifting. Holding perfectly still.
By the First Note... that vessel. Its design. It predates The Silencing. It should not be here. It *cannot* be here.
The lost ship from the tales. It's real. Its silence is older than this place.
There's your ghost ship, mates. My crew... we followed a weird frequency here. A whisper that led to this... nothing. Then the whispers started coming from *it*.
As you watch, a faint, impossible shimmer passes over the derelict's hull—a silent echo of a long-dead resonance drive.

lines_after.dialogue: We don't stay in touch with the Tonal Orders out here. No one knows where we are. If we board that thing and get trapped...
May I have some time? To listen? Not with instruments. With... intent. Even here, there may be a memory of a frequency.
Listen all you want. I'm calculating our food and power. When should I go into full conservation mode? Because our time is running out.

line.dialogue: The ghost ship hangs in the silent void. To approach it feels like stepping into a tomb.

choices.text: Send a probe first. Scan for residual energy signatures.
choices.outcome: A cautious, scientific approach. You'll gather data but may miss subtler clues.
choices.description: Sail closer and hail the derelict vessel, broadcasting peaceful tones across every frequency.

line.dialogue: I'm getting faint harmonic readings from its hull — something in there is still resonating, still *alive* in some way we don't understand.
Nothing. No response, no running lights, no signature. She's a ghost drifting in absolute silence, and every meter closer makes my skin crawl worse.

choices.text: Have the Listener Monk attempt a 'deep listen' from here. A spiritual reconnaissance.
choices.outcome: Risk a psychic or spiritual connection to the derelict. Unpredictable, but potentially insightful.
choices.description: Circle the ship at distance while Chanida sketches its design and the monk searches memory for records.

line.dialogue: These hull markings — they're not decorative. They're a warning script. Whatever happened to this crew, *they* wrote it themselves before the end.
