choices.description: Direct Chanida to confront hidden knowledge using singer voice

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Chanida hits a wall. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Chanida suggests making noise—shouting, banging metal—to 'wake the place up.' A dangerous provocation.
choices.description: Convince the monk to use prayers and decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. His recording captures a denied frequency.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: Within the structure, you find not ruins, but a machine—a colossal, broken resonator, its heart a cavity of perfect silence. It was designed to cancel all resonance. This is the source of the Zone.
By the First Vibration... this is a weapon. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was an attack that... overcorrected. Can I... can I even process this?
The big secret's a big gun that broke. Figures. The Tonal Orders would burn continents to keep this buried.

The machine's core is damaged. Its cancellation field is unstable. If it fluctuates... the feedback could shatter the Lattice for miles. We need to shut it down, but I have no one to help me understand this tech. It's pre-Order.
A cascade failure is imminent. The stress patterns are clear. We must leave. Now.
Leave? And let this thing keep sucking the song out of the world? No way! Bring it on!
This machine is a scar. To heal, we must close the wound. But the method... it could break everything.
The machine hums, a negative of sound. The floor shudders. Cracks race up the walls. The Silent Zone is about to scream.

lines_after.dialogue: As the machine dies, silence shatters. A wave of raw, chaotic resonance erupts, then settles into a fragile, new harmonic. The Lattice here glows with a soft, unfamiliar light.
The Song... it's different. But it's alive. The map of frequencies... it will need to be redrawn. Entirely.
Well. The Zone ain't silent no more. That's gonna cause some problems. And some opportunities.

line.dialogue: The machine's core lies exposed, a pulsating knot of dead frequencies. Destroying it risks a cataclysm. Stabilizing it might preserve a tool of terrible power. The true map of the Open Frequency is within reach—a truth that could break the Orders' control.

choices.line: Overload the core. Purge the silence with destructive resonance. The Zone will sing again, but the blast will be visible for leagues.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging Listener training

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Pichit overreaches. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.line: Carefully dismantle the machine, studying it. Recover the true frequency map. The secret is preserved, but carrying it is a deadly burden.
choices.description: Arthit channels tattooed routes toward the crushing quiet, hoping to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit loses control. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.line: Attempt to reverse the machine's polarity. Use it not to cancel, but to amplify the natural Song. A rebirth, but the outcome is unknown.
choices.description: The monk volunteers to decode the tonal pattern, leveraging recording crystals

line.dialogue: the monk succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the monk fails. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow hums with a low, persistent vibration. Ancient stone arches, carved with pre-Silencing glyphs, curve overhead like fossilized music.
Listen... the way the sound moves here. It's not random. It feels... called. Someone called this place into being with a specific intent.
Intent or not, I see carvings! Over there! What do they call this script? Can anyone read it?
They call it 'history we shouldn't be disturbing.' But since we're here, let's see what shiny trash they left behind.
Caution. The acoustics are unnatural. A wrong step, a loud noise... we don't know what frequencies might be dormant here.
A distant skittering of gravel echoes, multiplied by the chamber. From a side tunnel, a figure steps into the faint light.
Stop right there. You're not Tonal Order. What're you lot called, then? Scavengers like me, or something worse?

lines_after.dialogue: A man called Jerrik. Said he charted a whole network of open frequencies down here. A map to sail the Lattice without the Orders' charts. He's gone now. Left his notes.
An uncharted frequency map? That's not treasure, that's a target. No wonder the sky-rats are sniffing around.
A map of natural pathways... that's what the Listeners seek. Not control, but understanding. We must find it.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger eyes you warily, one hand on a crude sonic-blade.

choices.line: Promise we mean no harm, and offer to trade supplies for information.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the carved wall and hum a single sustained note.

line.dialogue: The vibration answers — these grooves are channels, not decoration. The whole wall is an instrument.
Wrong pitch. The wall rejected it — feel that? The stone went cold beneath my hand.

choices.line: Ask directly about the Open Frequency Map, appealing to shared resentment of the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Signal Arthit to hold position while you crawl forward to examine the carvings without footsteps.

line.dialogue: Good instinct. Belly-crawling kills the footfall echo. The carvings are deeper up close — ritual script, pre- Ayutthaya period.
Your knee struck the floor — hear that ripple? Every sound we make, the cave memorizes and replays.

choices.line: Suggest combining forces to explore deeper, splitting any non-frequency related finds.
choices.description: Ask Malee what she knows about this place before anyone touches anything further.

line.dialogue: Locals call it Tham Rong Hai — the Crying Cave. Merchants used it as a passage. None came back the same.
I told you what I know — history we shouldn't disturb. You're not listening, and the cave is.

lines_before.dialogue: Deeper in The Hollow, the walls glisten with embedded crystals that pulse softly in time with your footsteps. The air pressure changes, making ears pop.
The resonant signature is fluctuating. We need to adapt our dampeners, or we could trigger a crystallic feedback loop.
Don't change the subject! Look at this chamber! It's huge! The echoes... they're forming shapes!
It's a recording... a sonic memory of the place. The very stone remembers. But the memory is decaying, changing into something else.
Great. So the haunted cave is having bad dreams. Can we please focus on the map? The Scavenger said the next chamber.
A sharp, discordant chime rings out, not from your party. From a ledge above, a figure laughs.
Well, well! The harmonics led you right to us! Hand over the frequency data, and maybe we won't change your faces with a little dissonance!

lines_after.dialogue: Old Jerrik was a nice guy. For a surface worm. Talked too much. We know he hid the core resonator here. The thing that makes the map work.
You're just gonna smash it for the crystal!
Business is business. The Lattice changes, we adapt. Now, your move.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirates have the high ground, their crude resonators whining with charge.

choices.line: Try to negotiate, offering a copy of the map data in exchange for safe passage and the resonator.
choices.description: Touch the vibrating wall membrane directly to read the sonic memory with bare hands.

line.dialogue: I can feel it—the frequency is stabilizing under my palm. This place remembers everything that happened here.
No, no, no—the resonance is too strong, my whole arm is going numb. Pull me back!

choices.line: Use the chamber's unstable acoustics against them—shout a specific frequency to shatter their ledge.
choices.description: Have Arthit recalibrate the frequency scanner to match the chamber's shifting harmonics.

line.dialogue: Got it. The signature just locked onto a repeating pattern. Whatever this memory is, it's trying to show us something specific.
The fluctuations are too erratic—every time I match one frequency, three more branch off. I'm chasing echoes.

choices.line: Charge their position directly, hoping to overwhelm them before their resonators fire.
choices.description: Tell Malee to sing a sustained note into the chamber to test its acoustic response.

line.dialogue: Well, that actually worked. The walls are harmonizing with me. It's like the whole chamber is... breathing alongside my voice.
Yeah, that sounded like a dying cat in a drainage pipe. The walls just threw my voice right back at me.

lines_before.dialogue: The deeper you venture into The Hollow, the more the air itself seems to hum with latent energy. Strange, geometric patterns are carved into the walls, glowing with a soft, internal light.
Incredible. These carvings... they're pre-Silencing. This wasn't just a cave. It was a research facility.
Look! A central chamber up ahead. And... is that singing?
Not singing. Echoes. This place is playing back old sounds like a broken recorder.
In the chamber, a massive, fractured crystal column dominates the space. Around it, spectral echoes of researchers flicker, repeating fragments of their final moments.
Their last dream... preserved in the stone. To understand the Lattice, not control it.
He's right! Listen! One of the echoes... it's detailing a frequency matrix. A map!

lines_after.dialogue: The echoing voice completes its recitation. The 'Open Frequency Map' isn't a physical chart. It's a foundational resonance pattern, a master key to the Lattice's natural harmonics.
This is it. The subplot. This could break the Tonal Orders' monopoly. But recording it... it'll trigger every security echo in this place.
We have to try! It's my dream job to stick it to those guild pricks!

line.dialogue: The crystal column begins to pulse in time with the echoing data-stream. To capture the full Open Frequency Map, you must harmonize with it, but the system is unstable.

choices.text: Use Chanida's portable resonator to passively record the echoes. (Stealthy, but incomplete data.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the carved wall and listen for the dream's voice.

line.dialogue: * "The stone is warm — I can feel their heartbeat, their final vision flooding through me!
* "Nothing. The carvings stay dead under my hand. Whatever lived here, it won't open to me.

choices.text: Have Malee attempt to hack the ancient crystal console. (Risky, could attract attention.)
choices.description: Signal Chanida to crawl through the collapsed archway toward the singing.

line.dialogue: * "I can see them — shadows of the dreamers, still moving in a circle. We can reach them!
* "The passage is too narrow. The stones shift when I breathe. I have to pull back before it buries me.

choices.text: Pichit must attempt to 'Sing' the pattern back, completing the circuit. (Dangerous, requires perfect pitch.)
choices.description: Ask Malee to match her voice to the echoes and unravel their pattern.

line.dialogue: * "There — the harmonics lock together. The dream is a map, and now I can read where it leads.
* "I hit the wrong frequency. The echoes scatter into noise and the walls groan. I've broken the thread.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber shakes violently. Your attempt to interface with the ancient system has drawn unwanted attention. The air shatters with the roar of makeshift engines.
Well, well! Look what the echo dragged in! Heard you found somethin' shiny. We'll be taking that frequency map off your hands.
Two rusted resonance skiffs piloted by sky pirates crash through a weakened section of the cavern wall. The Scavenger ducks behind a stalagmite, eyeing both you and the pirates with equal distrust.
Pirates *and* a rat. I have a class to teach on terrible timing.
The crystal column is overloading! The entire harmonic balance of The Hollow is collapsing!
We can't let the pirates have it! But if this place comes down with us in it...
The map is more than data. It's a truth. We must ensure it survives, even if this place does not.
The surface told me about it already... this cave's core is a single, massive frequency anchor. Break it, and the whole island might drop.

lines_after.dialogue: Pirates advance, guns crackling with sonic charges. The great crystal shrieks, fractures spider-webbing across its surface. The fate of the map—and your lives—hangs on a single, desperate action.
No more waiting! Hand it over or get melted into the scenery!
There is no more time. We must act.

line.dialogue: The Hollow is dying. The Pirates are here. The Open Frequency Map is in your hands. How do you secure the future of this discovery?

choices.text: Fight a holding action against the pirates while Arthit rigs a data-crystal to eject safely. (Tactical, but leaves the ruins to the pirates.)
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using resonant staff to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit hits a wall. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Sabotage the pirates' skiffs, using the resulting resonance feedback to temporarily stabilize the core. (Dangerous, could backfire.)
choices.description: Malee attempts to decipher the monk's recording, relying on engineering

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Things don't go as planned. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Channel the map's frequency into the failing core, triggering a controlled collapse that will bury The Hollow—and the pirates—forever. (Sacrificial, ensures the secret dies with you, but protects it.)
choices.description: Convince the pirate to use intimidation and chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the pirate's resolve isn't enough. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship *The Wayward Note* glides silently through the cold air, its crystal resonators humming a low C-sharp. Below, the Lattice shifts like a frozen ocean of stained glass.
Look at it shift! It's a lot more fun up here than being stuck in that floating city library, isn't it?
Fun. Until the harmonics fail and we plummet into a continent of razor-sharp crystal. Such fun.
The Tonal Order charts show clear paths here. We should be safe if we maintain the prescribed frequency.
Safety is a pattern we impose on the chaos. The Lattice sings its own song, if we would only listen.
A figure emerges from the starboard companionway—Listener Monk Ilya, his simple robes flapping in the wind. His eyes are fixed on the shifting patterns below.
It hums differently today. A minor key, beneath the ship's tone. A lament.
Are you ready to go back home yet, Ilya? Or are you going to stare at the shiny rocks all trip?

lines_after.dialogue: Home? The monastery feels... distant. I left home in a hurry when I heard this voyage was seeking the old Listeners' outpost. The truth calls louder than duty sometimes.
How noble. Truth usually has a terrible salary. Is the pay good for Listeners these days?
Ilya ignores the jab, instead pointing to a jagged, dark spire rising from the Lattice surface far below.

line.dialogue: The spire is a known marker, but our charts are old. Ilya suggests we deviate slightly to 'listen' to the area. Arthit advises strict adherence to the charts.

choices.line: Trust Ilya's intuition. Deviate course to listen.
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing scavenger instincts to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Compromise. Slow our approach to observe from a distance.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use resonant staff and seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.line: Follow Arthit's caution. Stick precisely to the charted path.
choices.description: Convince the monk to use lattice study and decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. His recording captures a denied frequency.
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship holds position near the dark spire. The constant hum of the resonators is the only sound against the vast, silent sky. Something glints on the Lattice surface near the spire's base.
Scavenger camp! Look at those riggings! It's not scary at all! We should go down, they might have supplies... or information about the outpost!

Surface Scavengers are notoriously territorial. And the Lattice there is unstable. The charts mark this area as 'tonally discordant.' It was a good experience last time we ignored a chart warning? No, it was not.
He has a point. Getting crystal-sharded is a uniquely bad experience. But that glint... could be salvage. Could be the Resonant Prosthetic components we're tracking for that subplot.
Fear is a resonance of its own. It clouds perception. What does the Lattice tell us now, Ilya?
The song here is... broken. A record with a deep scratch. But within the break, I hear a faint pulse. Like a heartbeat.
A grappling hook clatters onto the deck, followed by a rope. A weathered woman in patched leathers hauls herself over the railing—Kael, a Surface Scavenger.
You Tonal types lost? Your pretty song's drawing fractals in the crystal. Unstable ones.

lines_after.dialogue: We're not lost! We're exploring! That's not scary at all!
Spoken like someone who's never seen the Lattice wake up angry. You're looking for the old Listeners' hole? It's nearby. Caved in. I've been picking through the rubble.
Find anything useful? Besides a dramatic entrance?

Maybe. But my partner's down there. Leg's pinned under a crystal fall. Your ship's frequency is making the whole zone vibrate. I can't remember my password for the damn pulley system to get him out! The mechanism's voice-locked.

line.dialogue: Kael needs help to rescue her pinned partner, potentially destabilizing the area further. She hints she found 'shiny leg parts' in the rubble—possibly the prosthetic components.

choices.line: Offer immediate help. Lower the ship and assist, prioritizing the rescue.
choices.description: Wave openly and call out a greeting to the nearest scavenger lookout, hands empty and visible.

line.dialogue: * "See? They're waving back — not everything down here wants to kill us, Arthit!
* "Congratulations, you just announced our position to every raider within earshot.

choices.line: Bargain. Secure the prosthetic components first as a guarantee, then help.
choices.description: Crawl through the rusted drainage pipes beneath the camp to slip past unnoticed.

line.dialogue: * "Tight squeeze, but I'd rather smell like rust than catch a crystal shard in my spine.
* "The pipe collapsed — even metal remembers what fear sounds like when you press too hard.

choices.line: Refuse. The risk is too great. Search for another path to the outpost, abandoning the scavenger and the components.
choices.description: Offer the scavengers a working battery cell from your supplies as a trade token.

line.dialogue: * "Power cells are currency up here. Smart — they'll talk before they throw now.
* "They took the cell AND threw a shard at us — guess manners cost extra on the surface!

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship cuts through the Lattice's surface, the crystalline layer parting like frozen water. The sky darkens with the approach of a harmonic storm.
Look! The Lattice is glowing brighter. It's reacting to the storm's frequency. Is the pay good for risking our necks in this?
The atmospheric pressure is destabilizing our resonator crystal. We need to find a stable harmonic to anchor to. Remember the protocols.
Protocols. Right. Because the Tonal Orders' charts are so reliable. I heard a strange noise from the engine housing. A dissonant scrape.
That's the Lattice remembering. It holds echoes of everything that's ever happened on it. The Silencing... it left a scar in the song.
Keep in mind... the prosthetic leg. Its crystal is pulsing in time with the storm. It's not just a tool. It's a memory.
You understand. The Lattice is a recording. Every fracture, every resonance... it remembers. Our duty was to listen, not to control.
So the leg is remembering something? What? A person? A place?

lines_after.dialogue: The prosthetic leg emits a sustained, clear tone. For a moment, the storm's chaotic frequencies seem to harmonize around it.
The resonance is stabilizing. The leg is acting as a tuning fork. It's recalling a perfect, foundational frequency.
Great. Our salvation is a haunted artifact. Nothing ominous about that at all.

line.dialogue: The Listener Monk approaches, his face etched with conflict. 'The leg's memory is a key. But to what? I can show you how to listen deeper, but it may awaken things the Orders have buried.'

choices.text: Trust the Monk's Guidance. Let him attune the prosthetic to reveal its memory. (Gain clarity, but attract attention.)
choices.description: Arthit attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on lattice storms

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Arthit misreads the situation. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Use the Ship's Resonator. Attempt to amplify the signal mechanically. (Maintain control, but risk damaging the memory.)
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with frequency mapping to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Chanida overreaches. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Have Pichit Attempt to 'Sing'. Try to harmonize with the leg's frequency directly. (High risk, potential for profound discovery.)
choices.description: Have the monk focus meditation on the sails to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The risk doesn't pay off. Tonal Order enforcers confiscate his equipment.

lines_before.dialogue: The storm rages, but a bubble of calm surrounds the ship, sustained by the prosthetic's resonant memory. A ghostly image shimmers above the Lattice.
By the First Song... it's a memory-echo. A moment from before The Silencing.
I've seen fragments in the crystal caves... but never anything this clear. You don't remember me? I'm the one who found that leg. It was singing in the wreckage.
The echo... it's a woman. She's... she's adjusting a massive resonator array. She looks determined. And scared.
The harmonic signature matches the theoretical 'Prime Frequency' the Orders claim is a myth. The foundation all sound is built upon.
She's not just adjusting it. She's sabotaging it. That's what caused The Silencing? An intentional overload? I'm really hurting trying to process this.
She was trying to stop something worse. The Lattice wasn't just a layer. It was a cage. And someone was trying to lock it permanently. I really can't remember who told me that...
The memory-echo solidifies. The woman—the leg's original owner—turns. She seems to look directly at Pichit, her mouth forming silent words. A deafening feedback shriek tears from the Lattice.

lines_after.dialogue: The feedback coalesces into a piercing, intelligent tone. A resonant silhouette, shaped from solidified sound, peels itself from the Lattice's surface below the ship.
A Warden. A harmonic immune system. The Lattice's memory has become self-aware and perceives us as a threat to the record.
It's made of the same crystal as the leg! Aim for the dissonant nodes!

line.dialogue: The Harmonic Warden rises, its form a jagged symphony of destructive sound. The prosthetic leg blazes with light, its memory now fully unlocked and acting as both a beacon and a weapon. The truth of The Silencing hangs in the air, fragile as a note.

choices.text: Shatter the Prosthetic. Use its resonant energy as a bomb to disrupt the Warden. (Destroy the evidence, save the ship, but lose the truth.)
choices.description: Direct Arthit to calibrate against the frequency using lattice storms

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Harmonize the Ship's Defenses. Use the leg as a focus to tune the ship's shields into a defensive chord. (Protect the crew and the memory, but risk being trapped.)
choices.description: Ask Malee to seek the dismissed truth, drawing on mechanical repair

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee overreaches. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.text: Complete the Memory. Have the Singer/Pichit channel the leg's final message into the Warden. (Reveal the full truth, with unpredictable consequences.)
choices.description: The scavenger uses harvesting tools to decode the tonal pattern near the sails

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Things don't go as planned. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

acts.title: A Hum in the Crystal Air

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market thrums with the discordant symphony of a thousand haggling voices. The very air, thick with the scent of spice and ozone, seems to vibrate against the crystalline Lattice far below.
Look at these stalls! The prices are reasonable, don't you think, Arthit? We could finally replace those frayed resonator coils.
Hush, Chanida. In this noise, a fair price is the one that doesn't get us robbed. We should secure passage first.
Passage? With what? The Tonal Orders' charts cost more than this whole floating bazaar. Their professors are really good at teaching one thing: how to drain your coffers.
The hum... it's different today. Beneath the market's greed, there's a tremor. Like the Lattice itself is whispering a warning it lost its voice to give.
You lot look like Resonant types. Heard the talk? Strange harmonics from the lower strata. My cousin, she lost her ship... and her nerve. Won't fly anymore.
See? Something's happening! We should ask around, find this cousin.
Or we should find a reputable chart-seller and mind our own business. The unknown is not a place for the unprepared.

lines_after.dialogue: A sudden, aggressive shove parts the crowd. A figure clad in scavenged plating and leather glares, their eyes scanning your group with predatory interest.
Well, well. Fresh meat sniffin' around the deep hums. You lookin' for a shortcut down? I know a frequency the Orders don't.
And I know a scam when I hear one. What's your price, besides our ship?

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate offers forbidden knowledge. How do you respond?

choices.text: Decline politely. Stick to official channels. (Avoid immediate danger, but gain no leads.)
choices.description: Buy the obsidian tuning fork from the deaf merchant before Arthit notices the price, 15 words

line.dialogue: You spent how much? ...Fine. It resonates true enough. Don't let Malee see the receipt.
That's not a tuning fork, it's a paperweight. The merchant felt you coming from three stalls away.

choices.text: Hear him out cautiously. What does he want in exchange? (Risk intrigue for potential information.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the crystal wall behind the spice vendor and listen inward, 15 words

line.dialogue: There. You feel it now too, don't you? The hum isn't beneath the market — it *is* the market.
Your hand's trembling. That's not resonance, that's the spice vendor's kiln radiating through the stone. Try again, but breathe first.

choices.text: Threaten to report him to the Tonal Orders. (Assert authority, likely making an enemy.)
choices.description: Pull Malee aside and ask what passage she's seeking and why the Tonal Orders matter, 15 words

line.dialogue: the villager pushes through. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The risk doesn't pay off. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: You opted to hear the pirate out. He leads you to a cramped stall shielded by noisy air-fans, where the market's din becomes a weapon against eavesdroppers.
Smart. The Orders' charts are garbage for the deep drift. I've got a sequence. Gets you past the Screaming Chasm. For a fee.
The Screaming Chasm is a deathtrap. Why aren't you careful with what you sell? This could get people killed.
Careful is for people who like walkin'. My info's good. The Listeners are spooked. They've been hummin' prayers non-stop. Aren't you tired of being in the dark?
The Listeners' fear is the true price here. Their prayers are a dissonance in the pattern. What have they heard?
We need that sequence! If the Lattice is giving warnings, we have to listen! Aren't you overthinking this, Arthit? Sometimes you just have to jump!
Jumping is how you find out the hard way she lost her ship. But... sitting here while the world hums a dirge isn't much better. What's your real fee, pirate?
A simple retrieval. There's a resonator core, a fancy one, in a derelict Listeners' spire on the market's edge. Guards are jumpy. You get it, I get you the sequence.

lines_after.dialogue: The deal hangs in the static-charged air. From the main thoroughfare, a distant, pure chime cuts through the noise—a Tonal Order patrol is near.
(Whispering from a nearby stall) Don't trust him! But... the Listeners *have* sealed their archive. Something has them terrified.
We're out of time. We need to decide. Now.

line.dialogue: The pirate's offer is a clear risk. The Order patrol is closing in. What is your move?

choices.text: Accept the deal. Steal the core for the sequence. (High risk, high reward; advance the subplot directly.)
choices.description: Flip the bandit a coin and demand he draw the Chasm route from memory, right now.

line.dialogue: Lines steady as a corpse's pulse—there, the dead water's edge. Follow it or rot.
Hand shakes. Ink bleeds. Even my own fingers won't obey when the Chasm's listening.

choices.text: Refuse, and try to infiltrate the sealed Listeners' archive yourselves. (Stealth challenge; seek the truth firsthand.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit what the Listeners actually pray *to*—and what answers back.

line.dialogue: They pray to silence, and the silence prays back. I've heard it breathe between words.
I—that's not for telling. Not here. The walls have teeth when you say its name.

choices.text: Turn the pirate in to the Order patrol, hoping for clemency and official information. (Dangerous gamble with authority.)
choices.description: Grab the bandit's collar and push him toward the Chasm's edge—prove his charts live.

line.dialogue: Fine! FINE! I'll walk first, damn you—but if I scream, don't follow that sound.
Get your hands off me! You think I'm stupid enough to go first? That's YOUR death.

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups at a spice stall, the air thick with cumin and tension. The market's ambient roar feels heavier now—less like commerce, more like a held breath.
I don't like this. We're drawing attention just standing here. That pirate's crew is watching from the alehouse roof.
Relax. They're just waiting to see if we're dumb enough to follow their 'lead.' Which, let's be honest, we probably are.
We have to do *something*. That Listener wasn't just scared—he was terrified. If the Lattice is screaming... we need to know why.
The truth is a frequency we haven't learned to hear. The pirate offered a key. Dangerous, but...

(nervously approaching) You're the ones asking about the Listeners? You should leave it be. My cousin works the lower docks. He says the resonance anchors... they're humming wrong. Like something's pulling from below.
See? Even the reasonable prices around here can't make this feel like a good idea.
A sharp, discordant chime cuts through the market noise. For a second, the crowd hushes. From a shadowed archway, the sky pirate makes a subtle 'come hither' gesture.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The party moves as one, slipping through the crowd toward the archway, the market's hum now feeling like a cage of sound.
I'll try it. But if this goes wrong, I'm blaming all of you. Especially you, Chanida.
I'll have a look first. If it's a trap, I'm faster than you anyway.
Sometimes the locked door is the one you must open yourself.

line.dialogue: The pirate waits in the shadows, holding a small, flawed resonator crystal that pulses with an unstable light.

choices.text: Offer a trade: information for safe passage off the skycity.
choices.description: Approach the humming monolith and press your palm flat against its warm surface.

line.dialogue: The frequency recognizes you—it's been waiting for someone who listens with their skin.
Your hand passed through like smoke. Whatever's in there, it doesn't want flesh. It wants something we don't have.

choices.text: Demand the truth upfront, ready for a fight.
choices.description: Signal Chanida to follow you and retrace the Listener's last path through the market crowds.

line.dialogue: There—residue on the paving stones where it knelt. It was communicating with something underground.
We circled back to nothing. The crowd swallowed its trail like they were trained to forget.

choices.text: Attempt to read the crystal's frequency directly, risking mental feedback.
choices.description: Stand perfectly still, close your eyes, and match your breathing to the hum's rhythm.

line.dialogue: You found the gap between tones. That's where the truth lives—the silence they've been hiding inside the noise.
Nothing happened. Just you standing there looking like a fool while every pair of eyes in this market locked onto us.

lines_before.dialogue: The archway leads to a dead-end storage yard, stacked with silent resonance crates. The pirate's crew forms a loose half-circle behind him. The market's noise is muffled here, replaced by the low, worrying thrum of the flawed crystal.

Smart choice, following. The Tonal Orders would have your tongues for what this stone sings. It's a fracture frequency. Picked it up from a Listeners' wreck. They weren't studying the Lattice... they were running from it.
You look run down. Stealing from monks must be exhausting work.
Laugh now. This crystal... it's a recording. A warning scream from the Lattice itself. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a response. And the signs are starting again.
What signs?

Resonance ships going silent. Lower anchors straining. The Listeners have been evacuating their remote monasteries for weeks. They know. And the Orders are silencing anyone who speaks of it to keep the prices reasonable on panic.
A civilization built on a foundation that remembers its destruction. We have been listening to the world's song, but not its memory.

The crystal in the pirate's hand flares violently. A painful, subsonic vibration shakes the crates. From the main market, a wave of panic-sounds rises—shouts, breaking glass, the collective fear of thousands.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision ripples outward. The market's chaos becomes a new kind of order—one of survival, revelation, or control.
It's reasonably priced, they said. Safety in ignorance. Look at that price now.
Well. The world's about to lose its virginity again. Hope it was worth it.
The first note of the next song has been struck. We must choose whether to sing along, or try to change the melody.

line.dialogue: The skycity shudders. The Lattice below flashes with angry light. The pirate holds out the crystal—the only key to understanding the warning.

choices.text: Seize the crystal and broadcast its warning to the entire market, causing chaos but spreading truth.
choices.description: Lean close to the crystal and hum a low resonant tone to test if it responds, 15 words

line.dialogue: The crystal vibrated — whatever frequency it holds, it's still alive, still waiting to be heard.
Nothing. Either it's dead, or it doesn't recognize my voice. Either way, that's not comforting.

choices.text: Smash the crystal to stop the destabilizing frequency, preserving order but destroying the evidence.
choices.description: Grab the bandit by his collar and demand he play the full recording right now, 15 words

line.dialogue: His hands were shaking too hard to resist — he played it, and we all heard the voice beneath the static.
He shoved me off and bolted into the trees. The crystal went with him. Should've been faster.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with the crystal's frequency, trying to 'answer' the Lattice's warning directly.
choices.description: Ask the bandit what the warning says before touching anything, keeping hands visible and calm, 15 words

line.dialogue: He swallowed hard and whispered — 'It says the monks aren't praying. They're keeping something asleep.
He clammed up, eyes darting to the treeline. 'You don't want to know. Believe me.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Aria's Dirge' drifts into the Silent Zone. The Lattice below is a flat, unresponsive pane of smoky crystal. No hum answers the ship's resonators. The air itself feels thick, swallowing sound.
All readings are null. It's not just quiet. It's... an absence. The Lattice is dead here.
Of course it is. We followed a pirate's 'secret chart' into a graveyard. Brilliant navigation, Pichit.
The Tonal Orders would never chart this. Exploring this... it's my dream job. To understand the Silencing itself.
Well, the ship's groaning is making me feel better. Said no one ever. Let's get down there. I see a wreck.
Below, the broken hull of a smaller resonance ship is half-submerged in the static Lattice. A faint, erratic glow pulses from within.
Life signs? Impossible. But that light... it's crystalline. Not ship-grade.
We have to do better! The Orders hide places like this for a reason. Let's find it.

lines_after.dialogue: The party descends. The silence is a physical pressure. Their footsteps on the Lattice make no echo. Inside the wreck, they find a skycity resident, the villager, trapped under a fallen resonator housing.
You... you're real? Thought I was hearing ghosts. My ship... lattice-fall caught us. Please.
As Arthit and Malee work to free them, Pichit spots the source of the glow: a crude prosthetic leg, fashioned from Lattice shards and wired with copper, fused to a skeleton in the cockpit.

line.dialogue: The rescued villager is weak but points a trembling finger deeper into the Silent Zone. 'The pirate... he went that way. After the big crystal. He has a map.' Pichit looks from the villager to the eerie prosthetic.

choices.text: Secure the villager on the Aria's Dirge. Safety first.
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with staff meditation, ready to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Defeat. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Study the crystal leg. It might hold a frequency to pierce the silence.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use frequency mapping and decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida misreads the situation. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Pursue the pirate immediately. Don't let the map get away.
choices.description: Have the villager focus irrigation on the crushing quiet to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: the villager finds the key. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The gamble fails. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The party chose to study the leg. Chanida, with careful hands, detached the resonant prosthetic. It thrums with a low, pained vibration in the utter quiet.
A Listener's work. Or a very desperate engineer. This isn't Tonal Order tech. It's... biological interface. You heard that, didn't you? A whisper in the crystal.
It's reacting to Chanida's pulse. I'm in a good mood. This is a breakthrough! This could be a key.
Thank you, Chanida. Your steady hands... May I have some time? I need to listen to what it's trying to say.
Pichit holds the leg. In the silence, a fragmented memory-song seeps into his mind: a melody of severance, of a Singer trying to anchor themselves as the world went quiet.
You... you can understand it? The pirate said that thing was a compass. To the Heart of the Silence.

lines_after.dialogue: A sharp crack echoes—impossible in the Silent Zone. A grappling hook embeds in the wreck's hull. The sky pirate, the sky pirate, swings down, landing with a thud that sounds muffled.
Hand over the peg-leg, dreamers. That's my ticket out of this ghost sea.
You left this person to die for a map!
Map? Hah! It's a frequency! The last thing that Singer ever sang. That leg's the only thing that can broadcast it. Now. Be grateful I'm asking nice.

line.dialogue: The pirate is armed and desperate. The prosthetic hums in Pichit's grip, its song a fragile thread in the dead air.

choices.text: Surrender the prosthetic. Avoid a fight in this unstable place.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with mechanical repair to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
A costly mistake by Malee. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: Try to negotiate. Use the villager's testimony as leverage.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use singer voice and seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida is thwarted. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Use the leg. Attempt to activate its stored frequency, unknown consequences.
choices.description: Convince the villager to use irrigation and decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
the villager loses control. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The airship drifts into a pocket of absolute stillness. The constant, low hum of the world's Lattice is gone, replaced by a vacuum of sound that makes your own breathing seem obscenely loud.
The resonator readings are flat. No resonance, no feedback. It's... unnatural. We're flying blind here.
My skin is crawling. It's too quiet. You can ask the crystals all you want, Arthit, they're not answering.
Of course. The one place in the sky where the rules don't apply. Perfect for hiding something, or someone.
This silence isn't empty. It's a pressure. A weight. Do you wanna try it, Chanida? Focusing past the quiet?
I'll try it. But if I start hearing whispers from the void, I'm blaming you.
A flicker of light catches your eye—a distress beacon, pulsing weakly from a derelict resonance ship lodged in a jagged crystal spire.
Well, look what the silence dragged in. Didn't think anyone was dumb enough to follow the charts *this* far.

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate's ship is a patchwork of scavenged parts, its own resonator silent. They are trapped here, same as you.
So the great sky pirates got lost in the quiet. How poetic. I suppose you know a way out?
Maybe. If you're willin' to listen to a different kind of frequency. The kind that doesn't play by the Tonal Orders' rules.

line.dialogue: The pirate offers a deal: a hidden, unstable frequency that might part the Silent Zone, in exchange for helping repair their ship's damaged resonator—a dangerous job requiring parts from the derelict vessel.

choices.text: Agree to the repair. Use the party's combined skills to carefully scavenge the derelict. (Chanida's agility, Arthit's technical know-how)
choices.description: Calibrate the resonator to detect absence instead of presence—tune to the void itself.

line.dialogue: There—barely a flicker, but something is *absorbing* the resonance rather than reflecting it.
Nothing. The equipment won't even acknowledge the void. It's like the silence refuses to be measured.

choices.text: Negotiate. Demand the frequency first as a show of good faith, risking the pirate's ire but gaining leverage. (Pichit's diplomacy, Malee's intimidation)
choices.description: Strip off your comms unit and walk ten paces forward in absolute silence.

line.dialogue: The pressure shifts. Whatever's listening, it noticed me when I stopped making noise.
My ears pop and my knees buckle. The silence hit me like a wall the moment I stepped forward.

choices.text: Refuse and attempt to force the information. The Silent Zone makes violence unpredictable and horrifyingly silent. (Direct confrontation)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to describe exactly what the pressure feels like—where it pushes, where it pulls.

line.dialogue: Behind the eyes. Like something is trying to read us from the
The gamble fails. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The hidden frequency works, but it's wrong. It doesn't sing—it *screams*. The Lattice around you groans and fractures, creating a temporary, shuddering tunnel through the silence.
The resonance is tearing the local structure apart! This isn't navigation, it's butchery! We have a class to teach these pirates about sustainable harmonics!
Too late for lectures! The whole zone is collapsing! I'm gonna rush off right now to the helm!
The pirate's told me about it already. They called it 'The Shriek.' They knew it was destructive. They just didn't care.
Look! The derelict ship—it's not empty. Life signs. Survivors from a skycity, hiding in the husk.
Please! Don't leave us! The silence... it gets into your head. Our resonator failed weeks ago.
The collapsing tunnel is narrowing. The pirate ship, now repaired, is already fleeing. You have seconds to decide.
Sentiment gets you killed, kid! The sky's for the strong! Their mom told me about it already when we took their supplies!

lines_after.dialogue: The Silent Zone seals itself behind you with a final, soundless shudder. The unnatural quiet is gone, replaced by the world's familiar hum. It has never sounded so sweet.
We have a new frequency now. Not one for charts. One for remembering what we choose to carry out of the silence.
Arthit's resonant prosthetic leg glows with a soft, steady light, having stabilized during the chaotic escape. It now hums in perfect, quiet harmony with the world.

line.dialogue: The escape tunnel is collapsing. You cannot save everyone. The choice defines what you resonate into the world.

choices.text: Save the villagers. Prioritize the helpless, sacrificing the chance to stop the pirates and letting their destructive 'Shriek' frequency spread. (Moral Victory)
choices.description: Reroute power to the scanning array, triangulate those life signs before the zone folds.

line.dialogue: Got them — three biosignatures clustered in the cargo hold, still breathing!" — Pichit
Static swallowed the feed. They're ghosts on my screen now, same as everywhere else." — Pichit

choices.text: Pursue the pirates. Try to disable their ship to contain the dangerous frequency, leaving the villagers to find their own way onto your already overloaded ship. (Strategic Victory)
choices.description: Force a hard dock with the derelict using the emergency grapple, breach the hull manually.

line.dialogue: Magnetic clamps bit. Hull's groaning but she's holding — move, before she twists free!" — Chanida
The grapple sheared clean off. She's drifting perpendicular and I can't track her anymore." — Chanida

choices.text: Attempt the impossible. Split the party and the ship's power to do both, risking total loss in the chaotic collapse. (The Gambit)
choices.description: Broadcast on the pirate frequency Malee knows, demand the survivors identify themselves before approach.

line.dialogue: They answered — ragged voices, civilian registry. These aren't combatants, they're trapped crew." — Malee
Dead air. Either they can't transmit, or they don't want to be found." — Malee

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whisper' drifts into the Silent Zone. The constant hum of its crystal resonator sputters, then fades into a vacuum of sound. The Lattice below is a frozen, grey expanse.
Readings are flat. No resonance feedback. It's like the ship is… deaf.
Can we turn it up? More power to the resonator? This quiet is crawling under my skin.
Don't bother. It's called the Silent Zone for a reason. The Lattice here doesn't sing back. It just… takes.
It's not an absence. It's a different kind of presence. A listening.
Ahead, the jagged silhouette of a derelict Resonance Ship is embedded in a floating island, its hull cracked open like a silent scream.
Is that… the 'Echo'? The lost survey ship from Order records?

lines_after.dialogue: Great. A ghost ship in a dead zone. This trip keeps getting better.
We need to know what happened here. Chanida, Malee, I want to ask you a few questions about the 'Echo's' last known cargo.
Caution, Pichit. The structural integrity of that wreck is questionable at best.

line.dialogue: How do we approach the derelict 'Echo'?

choices.text: Send a remote probe first. Scan for structural hazards and residual resonance.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the resonator's housing and feel for vibrations beneath the silence.

line.dialogue: There — under the floor. Something's breathing down there, slow and deep.
Nothing. My hand just goes numb. Whatever's down there, it doesn't want to be touched.

choices.text: Approach cautiously on foot. The direct sensory data could be vital.
choices.description: Kill the resonator entirely and drop a steel bolt onto the deck plating.

line.dialogue: Did you hear that? The bolt hit — but the sound never came back to us. It's being swallowed mid-air.
The bolt hits and... nothing. Not even impact vibration. I've never heard a sound die that fast.

choices.text: Hail it on all frequencies first. If anyone is alive in there…
choices.description: Ask Pichit to describe what he means by "a different kind of presence."

line.dialogue: Listen with your chest, not your ears. It's pressure. Like standing at the bottom of a very deep ocean made of stillness.
I can't explain it. Every time I try to find the words, they dissolve before they reach my mouth.

lines_before.dialogue: The interior of the 'Echo' is a tomb of frozen breath and twisted metal. No dust moves. Every footstep is swallowed whole by the silence.
Logs say they were mapping the Zone's edges. Then… nothing. It's over. Just static.
Not quite. Look at the resonator chamber. The main crystal is shattered from the inside. Something made it scream until it broke.
A forced resonance… or a resonance that was forced upon it.
A soft scuffling sound echoes—impossibly—from a collapsed corridor. It's the first distinct noise you've heard since entering the Zone.
Impossible. Audio sensors confirm… there was no sound. But we all heard it.
I'm not finished yet! There's a sealed door here. Bio-signs… faint, but present.

lines_after.dialogue: Let me guess. It's the sole survivor, who will have a perfectly reasonable explanation for all this.
The door hisses open. Inside, a Listener Monk the Listener monk kneels before a small, dead personal resonator, his hands trembling. He looks up, eyes wide with a horror that hasn't faded.
You shouldn't be here. It's not finished. The song… it never finished.

line.dialogue: The monk is terrified. How does Pichit engage him?

choices.text: Offer aid and comfort. Reassure him we are here to help.
choices.description: Touch the resonator crystal bare-handed and let your own pulse flood the lattice. 15 words

line.dialogue: The lattice answered me — it's not broken, it's *waiting*, like someone paused it mid-frequency.
Nothing. Dead silica. Whatever held the resonance is long gone — or hiding beyond my reach.

choices.text: Demand answers immediately. What happened to the 'Echo'?
choices.description: Pull the audio sensor logs from the last 90 seconds before contact was lost. 15 words

line.dialogue: There — below human hearing, a standing wave at 0.3 Hz. Something was singing in a voice we weren't built to hear.
The logs are corrupted — overwritten with pure silence, as if something scrubbed its own voice from the record.

choices.text: Remain silent and observant. Let his fear and the environment tell the story first.
choices.description: Hum the unfinished dirge into the chamber and see what harmonics the crystal gives back. 15 words

line.dialogue: It completed the phrase. Three notes we've never heard — and the chamber walls are *crying* condensation.
The crystal swallowed my voice whole. No reflection, no harmonic, just… hunger. I don't think this was a dirge. I think it was bait.

lines_before.dialogue: The party advances deeper into the Silent Zone. The unnatural quiet presses on them like a physical weight. The air is stale, the lattice beneath their feet dull and lifeless.
I have a cramp in my calf. This place is draining us. Literally.
Stop whining. Look! Ahead. Structures. Broken resonance ship hulls fused with the lattice.
The Echo of the Lost Ship... this must be its final resting place. The geometry is wrong. It's like the lattice... consumed it.
Consumed, or preserved? A tomb for a moment of catastrophe. We should proceed with reverence.
You understand. A friend... introduced us to this truth. The Tonal Orders lied. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a... correction.
Correction? What are you talking about? We just need to find salvage and get out!
From the twisted wreckage, a faint, impossible sound emerges—not through air, but as a vibration in the bones of the dead lattice.

lines_after.dialogue: Could you speak more slowly? This 'correction'... you mean the Lattice itself acted?
Yes. It rejected a certain frequency. A hubris. The ship we seek... its resonator was attempting that forbidden tone.
So it got smacked down. Okay. Where's its core? We need that data!
The bone-deep vibration grows stronger, forming a coherent, whispering pulse. It seems to emanate from a specific fracture in the central wreck.

line.dialogue: The whispering pulse is a guide, but also a lure. How do you approach the fracture?

choices.text: Send Chanida ahead quickly to scout the fracture visually.
choices.consequence: Chanida confirms the core is there, but triggers a minor lattice tremor that injures her.
choices.description: Squeeze through the collapsed hull plating where amber light seeps through the gap, 15 words

line.dialogue: I can feel airflow — this breach connects to something still pressurized." — Arthit
The plating shifted. My arm's pinned. Someone pull before it shears through the suit." — Malee

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze the pulse's pattern from a safe distance.
choices.consequence: Arthit deciphers a safe path, but the process takes time, allowing the haunting presence to strengthen.
choices.description: Touch the frozen resonance film clinging to the nearest wall with bare fingers, 15 words

line.dialogue: I see it — the ship's last thirty seconds, looping. Everyone was reaching for someone." — Pichit
It's not a recording. It pulled my hand inside the wall. I felt their panic." — Chanida

choices.text: Pichit attempts to 'listen' to the pulse with his innate sensitivity, mimicking a Singer's approach.
choices.consequence: Pichit makes a profound connection with the lost ship's final moment, gaining vital insight but risking psychological resonance backlash.
choices.description: Strike the tuning fork against the broken resonance to map the structure acoustically, 15 words

line.dialogue: Three decks below us, something answered back. Hollow space — or something breathing in it." — Chanida
The fork cracked. Whatever's down there swallowed the sound and sent back silence instead." — Arthit

lines_before.dialogue: The party reaches the fracture. Within the crystalline tomb, the Lost Ship's resonator core glows with a sickly, trapped light. The whispering pulse is now a clear, mournful song.
The data is intact... but fused with the lattice. Extracting it might be like... pulling a tooth from a living jaw.
I didn't catch what you said. A living jaw? This stuff is dead. Let's just crack it open.
No! Look at the shadows! They're... moving without sound!
Echoes of the lost crew manifest as silent, grasping shades, drawn by the party's presence and the disturbed core.
They are not hostile. They are trapped. Like the song. This entire zone is a prison for a memory the world wants to forget.
The truth. The Silencing was the Lattice purging a cancerous idea. This ship carried it. The Tonal Orders have built their empire on suppressing this knowledge.
Can you catch it? Are you with me? We have the core! We can expose them! But we need to get out NOW!

lines_after.dialogue: The shades converge, not attacking, but pleading. Their silent mouths form words in the lattice dust. The core's light flares, threatening to dissolve the fragile stability of the zone.
We have a choice. Take the data and run, leaving these echoes to their endless silence... or try to release the song, to let this memory finally resonate into the world.
The second option could destabilize the lattice locally... maybe catastrophically. Can we take that risk?
The monk and villager look at the party, awaiting their decision. The fate of the Echo, and perhaps a fragment of truth, hangs in the silent air.

line.dialogue: This is the climax. What is your final action regarding the Lost Ship's Echo?

choices.text: Secure the core data and evacuate immediately, sealing the fracture behind you.
choices.consequence: You possess the proof to challenge the Tonal Orders, but the Silent Zone remains a haunted tomb, and the truth is still buried.
choices.description: Direct Malee to calibrate against the frequency using mechanical repair

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee misreads the situation. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Attempt a controlled release, letting the song escape but trying to contain the lattice reaction.
choices.consequence: The song radiates out, alerting the Orders and freeing the shades. The Zone becomes unstable but not destroyed. You become targets.
choices.description: Arthit volunteers to question the Orders' silence, leveraging ship navigation

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit hits a wall. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.text: Pichit, with the party's support, fully resonates with the core, aiming to absorb and transform the song, not just release it.
choices.consequence: A profound, personal transformation for Pichit; the Echo is resolved peacefully, but the Lattice reacts unpredictably, changing the Zone forever and marking Pichit with its memory.
choices.description: Ask the monk to trace the anomalous signal, drawing on meditation

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the monk fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: In the hush of the Tonal Archives, the air itself feels curated. Each footstep on the polished crystal floor rings with a precise, sanctioned echo.
Can you feel that? It's like the whole place is holding its breath. Makes my skin prickle.
That's just the acoustics. The Tonal Orders designed it to make you feel insignificant. It's working.
We should be careful. The resonance fields in these data-crystals are unstable. A wrong vibration could scramble weeks of records.
Listen... beneath the sanctioned silence. There's a pattern. A faint, repeating call. It doesn't belong to any charted frequency.
Pichit's finger traces a line on a dusty resonator plate. A ghostly, fragmented harmonic shivers into the air—a distress signal, centuries old.
Ah, my friends! Researching new trade routes? I might have some... exclusive charts. For a friend's price.
We're listening to a call. A plea from the deep Lattice. The pain in the signal... it's gone now, faded to an echo. But the call remains.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost ship! We have to find it! Think of the artifacts, the history!
Or think of the perfectly good reason it's lost. Ships that vanish into the Lattice don't usually leave happy stories behind.
The signal origin is in a sector marked 'Resonance Dead Zone' on all public charts. That is not a coincidence.

line.dialogue: The ghostly signal hangs in the air. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Ask the Merchant about the Dead Zone. He trades in secrets.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the nearest wall and let the vibration travel up your arm.

line.dialogue: The frequency maps to a Tonal Order lock sequence — someone *wanted* this found.
Pull back — your heartbeat's syncing to the wall. It'll digest you if you hold contact.

choices.line: Cross-reference the signal frequency with the Listeners' old natural harmonic logs.
choices.description: Hum the pattern back, matching pitch and interval as precisely as you can.

line.dialogue: You matched it. The silence just... *parted*. There's a chamber beneath us.
Wrong harmonic. The walls just tightened — the architecture is *correcting* us.

choices.line: Report the finding to a Tonal Archivist. Follow protocol.
choices.description: Signal everyone to freeze and isolate the pattern by blocking out all other sound.

line.dialogue: There — seven beats, pause, three. That's a distress encoding. Someone's still alive in the deep archive.
Too slow. The pattern shifted while you were listening — it's *adaptive*, and now it knows we're here.

lines_before.dialogue: Deeper in the archives, among the forgotten resonance logs, the air grows colder. The curated silence feels more like a suppression field.
The Dead Zone? Oh, that's just bad for business. No stable tones, no trade. The Orders sealed those charts. I don't want people knowing I even looked at them.
Of course he doesn't. Means there's profit in the silence. Or danger he can't price.
I found it! A Listener's journal. It mentions a 'Singing Ship' that tried to map the Dead Zone generations ago. It never called back.
The journal's author... they heard the same call. They wrote, 'I don't want it—this knowledge. The ship isn't lost. It's waiting.'
As Pichit reads the words aloud, a shelf of crystal records nearby emits a low, sympathetic hum. The ghost signal strengthens momentarily.
You're the ones asking about the old songs? My gran used to hum a tune... said it was from the 'quiet ship.' We don't speak of it. Bad luck.
This goes beyond a shipwreck. An entire history has been silenced. We're not just finding a ship; we're finding the people they didn't want found.

lines_after.dialogue: The Lattice remembers what the Orders have tried to forget. This archive is a tomb for truths.
So we give it a voice! We find that ship and shout its story from the highest spire!
And get ourselves erased from the records for our trouble. You can sit and theorize for as long as you want, but acting on it? That's the hard part.

line.dialogue: The path is clear, but fraught. How do you uncover the full truth?

choices.line: Bribe the Merchant for the sealed Dead Zone charts. A simple transaction.
choices.description: Press the merchant for what he's really hiding about the Dead Zone's silence.

line.dialogue: His hands trembled when he said 'bad for business' — that's the tell of a man who's heard the Singing himself and paid to forget.
He shut down faster than a shuttered window — whatever's in that zone, he'd rather die than name it aloud.

choices.line: Piece together the route from the Listener's journal and the villager's folk tune. A scholarly approach.
choices.description: Read the passage in the Listener's journal aloud to see if Pichit recognizes the call.

line.dialogue: That cadence — I heard it beneath the rain three nights ago, pulling me toward the eastern corridors like a thread through my chest.
The words blur on the page, rearranging themselves when I try to focus — the journal resists being spoken, as if it's listening back.

choices.line: Attempt to resonate directly with the ghost signal here in the archives. Risky, but pure.
choices.description: Follow the journal's described route toward the Dead Zone before the merchant warns others.

line.dialogue: The author mapped every turning — cracked mirror in the third alcove, the staircase that doesn't echo — I can trace their path exactly.
The ink here isn't

lines_before.dialogue: The Archives' silence deepens, heavy with the weight of forbidden knowledge. The static from the Echo's ghost-path plays from a salvaged resonator, a discordant hum in the hallowed space.
I knew right away this was a mistake. That frequency... it's not just a lost route. It's a *wound* in the Lattice's song.
Great. So we're not just chasing a ghost ship, we're poking a cosmic scab. The Tonal Orders would have us silenced for even listening to this.
Which is exactly why we have to follow it! Look, the static forms a pattern against the main resonance charts. It's... standing right in front of us.
A path that refuses to be erased. The Lattice remembers what the Orders tried to forget.
Fascinating, truly! A wholly uncharted, albeit dangerously unstable, trade lane. The profit potential is... incalculable. If one could stabilize it.
You're all mad. My cousin was on a barge that heard a whisper like that. It never came back. Is everything under control here? It doesn't feel like it.
Chanida overlays the ghostly signal onto a massive crystal chart. A route flickers into existence, leading deep into a sector marked 'Shattered Resonance.'

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the air. The ghost-path is clear, but it vibrates with a palpable wrongness.
The adventurous choice is usually the stupid one. Just saying.
Yet, to turn away now is to let the silence win.

line.dialogue: We have the lost ship's final course. Do we trace its path?

choices.text: Decipher the route safely from here. (Study the pattern remotely, gaining knowledge but no immediate risk.)
choices.description: Have Chanida focus unauthorized tones on the ancient texts to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
The risk doesn't pay off. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.text: Prepare a cautious expedition. (Gather specialized dampeners, risking attention but increasing survival chance.)
choices.description: Direct Malee to confront hidden knowledge using crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: Follow the Echo now. (Pursue the ghost-signal directly into the Shattered Resonance, risking everything for the truth.)
choices.description: The villager attempts to follow the dissonant trail, relying on irrigation

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
A costly mistake by the villager. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The Archives' central atrium. The ghost-path data is loaded into the main resonator, painting the air with a jagged, painful light. The truth is a dissonant chord.
The Lost Ship... it didn't vanish. It was sacrificed. The Tonal Orders scuttled it to seal a fracture their charts couldn't contain.
All hands, silenced to protect the monopoly. This knowledge is a death sentence. Why couldn't you just let the past lie?
For the adventurous, right? Well, we found our adventure. It's a conspiracy. And the conspirators are at the door.
The great doors of the Archives groan open. Figures in the stark robes of the Tonal Orders march in, their faces stern. The Lead Archivist steps forward.
Ah, Archivist! A misunderstanding, I'm sure. These young researchers were merely... verifying historical anomalies. For a fee, such anomalies can remain historical.
Silence. You possess forbidden resonance. The penalty is erasure. May I see your driver's license? Your navigational permits are hereby revoked. Permanently.
You erased a whole ship! You don't get to erase us!

lines_after.dialogue: The Archivist gestures. The resonator holding the Echo's data begins to whine, overloading. The truth is moments from being burnt away.
They didn't want us to find it. But the Lattice... the Lattice *wanted* to be heard.
Don't let them! My cousin... he deserves a grave!

line.dialogue: The Orders will destroy the evidence. How do you preserve the Echo's truth?

choices.text: Surrender the data, but broadcast a fragment. (The truth becomes a public rumor, saving your lives but diluting the impact.)
choices.description: Malee channels leg resonance toward the hushed reverence, hoping to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee hits a wall. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Fight to protect the resonator. (A direct, dangerous confrontation that could get you branded as outlaws.)
choices.description: Have Chanida focus unauthorized tones on the hushed reverence to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Chanida fails. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Sing the path into the Lattice itself. (Pichit channels the raw, dangerous frequency, making it a permanent part of the world's song—at great personal cost.)
choices.description: The merchant takes the lead, employing valuable goods to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His trade connections deliver the right information.
The resonance turns hostile. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns before you, a jagged maw in the floating island's side. Inside, the air is cool and carries a faint, crystalline hum.
Anywhere. Let's just go anywhere you like. This place feels... alive.
Caution. The acoustics are unstable. Our resonance ship's charts don't cover this deep.
What kind of ruin do you like? Crumbling and haunted, or just boring and empty? I bet it's the first.
Every echo is a question. The Lattice here sings a different song.
Ancient, pre-Silencing structures loom in the gloom, carved from the island's heart. Strange glyphs pulse with a soft light in response to your footsteps.
Why are you doing this? Exploring these old bones? The Tonal Orders say it's forbidden. Bad frequencies down here.
We Listeners... we are told to study only the surface songs. But the truth hums deeper. Why are they treating this knowledge like a threat?

lines_after.dialogue: A central chamber opens up. In its center, a monolithic crystal obelisk rests, silent. Around it, the walls are covered in intricate frequency diagrams—a map unlike any modern chart.
That's... an Open Frequency Map. Subplot: frequency_map. It shows resonant pathways without Tonal Order encryption. This is pure, raw navigation data.
We can use this! We can go anywhere!
Or get obliterated anywhere. What style of catastrophe do you prefer?

line.dialogue: The obelisk is dormant. Your presence, however, has made the ancient map glow. A low, foundational tone begins to emanate from the stone floor.

choices.text: Send Chanida to tap the obelisk lightly with a resonator to test its response.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the singing wall and let the Lattice's vibration travel through your bones, listening for its source.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the harmonic decay, a secondary frequency. Someone carved intention into this stone, and it still remembers.
The resonance collapses the moment I touch it. Whatever lives in this wall, it does not want my hands near it.

choices.text: Ask the Listener Monk to chant a grounding frequency to stabilize the chamber.
choices.description: Hum a rising note against the corridor's acoustics, testing which chamber returns the echo slowest — that is where the air is thickest.

line.dialogue: The third archway swallowed my voice whole. No reflection at all. That is not silence — that is something listening before it answers.
Every note comes back wrong, transposed up half a step each time. The Lattice is not echoing — it is correcting me.

choices.text: Have Arthit quickly sketch a section of the map for later study before retreating.
choices.description: Ask Malee to describe both ruins in detail while you watch the stone's surface for flickering patterns that respond to her words.

line.dialogue: The haunted one — walls scored with grief-markers, ceiling collapsed inward like a prayer answered from below. And look: the stone just pulsed. It knows that place too.
I barely finish the first description and the corridor groans. The walls don't want comparisons. They want to be the only ruin that exists in our mouths.

lines_before.dialogue: The foundational tone swells, not loud, but pervasive. It fills The Hollow like a new dawn, washing the chamber in a pale, resonant light. The map on the walls brightens.
A fresh beginning. The stone is waking from a long silence.
I can't eat anything. The excitement... it's too much. We're seeing history wake up!
From morning until evening, we Listeners meditate on single notes. This... this is a symphony. It conflicts with everything the Orders teach.
We probably can't finish it all. Deciphering this whole map? It's too big. It'll take ages.
The risk increases with the light. If this frequency escapes The Hollow, the Tonal Orders' sensors might detect it.
You've been here from morning till night! Please, we should leave before it gets worse!
The obelisk's surface ripples like water. Images form within it—scenes of the pre-Silencing world, cities anchored to the ground, not floating.

lines_after.dialogue: The map is not just navigation. It's a memory. The Lattice recorded the world's last song.
Subplot: frequency_map. The pathways on the wall... they're aligning with the images in the obelisk. Each route corresponds to a lost place.
My duty is to observe and report. But this truth... it should be heard.
Then let's hear it all! Let's make the obelisk sing!

line.dialogue: The awakened obelisk is now emitting a clear, carrier frequency. The chamber resonates in harmony, but the energy is building, vibrating the very stone.

choices.text: Lower the resonator's output to dampen the feedback and quietly study a single mapped frequency.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging mechanical repair

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee hits a wall. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Attempt to synchronize the party's resonators with the obelisk to see if it reveals a specific, safe route.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using unauthorized tones to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida is thwarted. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Encourage the Listener Monk to fully vocalize the carrier frequency, to 'sing' with the obelisk and unlock a deeper layer of the map.
choices.description: Direct the villager to chart resonance pathways using village secrets

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The community rallies, creating unexpected strength.
Things don't go as planned. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The deeper chamber of The Hollow opens before you, a cathedral of crystal and shadow. Ancient machinery, dormant for centuries, hums with latent energy.
Look at these glyphs! They're... shifting. Like they're reacting to our footsteps. What's in there? Behind that sealed arch?
Probably more dead-end puzzles and dust. I can't speak the language of these ghosts, and I doubt they care to explain themselves.
The resonance here is unstable. That machinery isn't just old—it's *alive*, on some frequency we can't perceive. We should proceed with extreme caution.
This place... it feels like a home that remembers its owners. A memory etched in stone and frequency. We are guests in a dream that hasn't ended.
You're home so late... for this truth. The Listeners have known of this chamber for generations. We were commanded to never open it. The fear was... overwhelming.
You're back late from the edge of the world! My ancestors said this cave was a tomb for the old world's arrogance. We shouldn't be digging up graves.
A low, harmonic drone builds from the central machine. Glyphs on the walls begin to glow, casting long, dancing shadows. The air itself vibrates.

line.dialogue: The central machine's control panel is active, its interface a puzzle of resonant crystals. It seems to require a specific frequency sequence to unlock its core—potentially revealing the Open Frequency Map.

choices.text: Let Chanida attempt a brute-force harmonic override. (Risky, but direct.)
choices.description: Touch the shifting glyphs directly and let the memory flow through you.

line.dialogue: I understand now — these glyphs aren't language, they're *echoes* of everyone who lived here before us.
The glyphs bit back — something inside them rejected me like a failed blood match.

choices.text: Guide the Listener Monk to interpret the glyphs as a tonal code. (Requires trust.)
choices.description: Force the dormant machinery to restart by reconnecting the crystal conduits.

line.dialogue: There — the resonance is stabilizing. Whatever this machine was built for, it remembers its purpose now.
Wrong sequence. The conduits blew out and now the walls are screaming in frequencies I can barely hear.

choices.text: Have Pichit meditate, attempting to 'listen' for the sequence in the chamber's ambient song. (Unpredictable, profound.)
choices.description: Speak aloud to the walls, acknowledging the home and asking what it wants remembered.

line.dialogue: It heard me. The air just shifted warm — like walking into a room where someone just left a chair pulled out for you.
Silence. Worse than silence — the house held its breath, and I realized it doesn't want guests. It wants *witnesses*.

lines_after.dialogue: The chosen approach sends a pulse through the machine. The harmonic drone shifts, becoming a welcoming chord.
The lattice resonance in the chamber is now feedbacking into our own crystal resonators. We are part of the circuit now.
The map... it isn't a chart. It's a *state*. A permission to hear the world without filters.
A deep, resonant *thrum* echoes through The Hollow, and the far archway seals dissolve into light. The final chamber awaits.

lines_before.dialogue: The final chamber is not a room, but a vast, natural geode. The walls are pure, singing crystal. At its heart floats a luminescent orb—the source of the Open Frequency.
The First Song... It's real. We had forgotten all of it! Our order... we were taught to listen only to fragments, to safe echoes. This is the whole.
So, does the universe have a boyfriend? Or is it just screaming into the void? This 'song' looks like it could unravel every chart the Tonal Orders sell.
