I can barely hear you over the... the everything! It's beautiful and terrifying! It's like the sky itself is speaking!
My head... it's too much. We're not meant to hear this. The Silencing happened because we heard too much!
The orb is broadcasting the Open Frequency Map directly. It's integrating with our resonator cores. But the power is raw, unfiltered. It could overload our systems, or... rewrite them.
This is the choice. To listen fully, without the guild's gates, without fear. To accept the world's true voice, with all its chaos and grace.

The orb pulses, offering communion. The Tonal Orders' sanctioned frequencies feel thin and false next to this primal symphony. But the volume is rising—it could shatter the delicate balance of The Hollow, or your minds.

line.dialogue: The Open Frequency Map is being offered. To integrate it means freedom from the guild's monopoly and true navigation. But its power is immense and untamed. How do you receive the song?

choices.text: Capture a filtered fragment for study. (Safe, but leaves the guild's power intact.)
choices.description: Malee volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee misreads the situation. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize and integrate the frequency into your ship's core. (Empowering, but risky to your technology.)
choices.description: Chanida channels unauthorized tones toward the darkness, hoping to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Chanida hits a wall. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Open yourselves to the full, unfiltered resonance. (Transformative, but could permanently alter you and the Lattice around you.)
choices.description: The villager volunteers to chart resonance pathways, leveraging irrigation

line.dialogue: the villager makes it work. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the villager loses control. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber rings with the consequence of your choice. The crystal walls resonate in agreement or fracture in dissonance.
We have heard. And now, we are changed. The path ahead is no longer charted—it is sung.
The Listeners... we must return to our towers and tell them. The truth is not a secret to keep. It is a song to share.
I... I understand now. The fear was the silence. This... this is the world alive.
The Hollow settles, its eternal echo now carrying a new note—your note. The Resonance Chronicles have a new page, written not in ink, but in frequency.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Aria's Lament' drifts between the vast, crystalline waves of the Lattice. The ship's main resonator thrums a low, steady C-sharp, parting the shimmering surface below.
Steady as she goes. Keep the harmonic dampeners at 30%. Any fluctuation and we'll attract unwanted attention from below.
Unwanted attention. Right. Because sailing through a giant, sentient crystal sheet that eats cities is the pinnacle of subtlety.
We have to do something! Look at the readings—there's a pattern in the interference. It's not random static. It's... an echo.
An echo of what was, or a plea for what could be? The Lattice remembers everything. Every scream during the Silencing, every whispered hope.
A Skycity Resident, a passenger hitching a ride to the next floating settlement, approaches the party, wringing their hands.
Sorry to bother you navigators. But that sound... it's been in my head since we passed the Graveyard Drifts. Like a song stuck wrong.
I love it!! Not the bothering, the clue! He loves it!! The Lattice is trying to tell us something!

lines_after.dialogue: Great. The crystal apocalypse has a jingle. You can put your hand down now, Chanida. We all see you're excited.
This is a known anomaly. The Tonal Orders chart it as 'Phantom Frequency 143.' They advise rerouting. It's linked to... disappearances.
A frequency with a number. How clinical. To them, a lost ship is just a data point. To the Listeners, it would be a psalm of regret.

line.dialogue: The Phantom Frequency grows stronger, weaving into the ship's own resonance. A choice must be made.

choices.text: Follow the Tonal Charts. Reroute to avoid the anomaly. (Play it safe.)
choices.description: Override the dampeners to full — flood the hull with counter-frequency resonance, 14 words

line.dialogue: Resonance aligned — the whispers collapse into silence. Steady hands, everyone. We hold.
Too much — the hull's screaming. I've made it worse.

choices.text: Adjust the resonator to match the Phantom Frequency. See what answers. (Tune into the echo.)
choices.description: Open a channel and broadcast the signal back toward the source, 12 words

line.dialogue: It answered. Same pattern, reversed — whatever's out there, it's *listening*.
Nothing but static. And now something knows we're here. Brilliant.

choices.text: Ask the Skycity Resident for more details about the 'song.' (Gather local insight.)
choices.description: Deploy Chanida's probe directly into the distortion's densest reading, 11 words

line.dialogue: Probe intact — I'm seeing structure inside. Coordinates, repeated. This is *navigation*.
Lost telemetry in seven seconds. It swallowed the probe whole.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship holds its new course, the air thick with the mingled hum of engine and echo. The party is on edge, scanning the luminous expanse.
I've isolated the secondary signal. It's not one echo. It's a conversation. Two resonant signatures, locked in dissonance.
Wonderful. So we're eavesdropping on a crystal ghost argument. It comes with cucumber salad and rice, this madness? A side dish of insanity?
Pichit, drawn to the ship's stern, overhears hushed voices near the auxiliary resonator housing. He signals the others to listen.
...the 'Wind's Sorrow.' It's true. The Lost Ship. Its cargo hold was full of uncut primal resonators. Worth a skycity's ransom.
It might be true. That may be true. But the stories say its crew still sings its last frequency, dragging down any who listen...
Superstition! We have the counter-frequency. The Tonal Orders bury this knowledge, but we Skyfolk remember. We'll be rich!
(Whispering) Pirates! They're using our ship to get close! I'm not a playboy, but I know treasure hunting when I hear it!

lines_after.dialogue: Of course. It's served with cucumber salad and rice. A side of betrayal with our ghost-hunting. The resident's in on it.
They seek plunder from a grave. The echo isn't a lure—it's a warning. A boundary marker for the dead.
They've tampered with the resonator alignment. If they trigger their 'counter-frequency' now, it could shatter our harmonic stability. We'd be adrift.

line.dialogue: The pirates' plan is in motion. The Phantom Frequency swells, and the ship shudders. How do you intervene?

choices.text: Confront them directly. Overpower the pirates before they can activate their device. (Forceful.)
choices.description: Tap the crystal resonance chamber, broadcasting your identity before the ghost signal fades.

line.dialogue: Arthit says "It's responding — the Wind's Sorrow isn't dead, it's *waiting*, and now it knows we're here.
Arthit says "You flooded the chamber with raw static. Whatever was reaching out just went silent, and I can't get it back.

choices.text: Sabotage the auxiliary resonator housing. Cut off their access without a direct fight. (Technical.)
choices.description: Ask the villager to recite the old stories word-for-word while Malee cross-references the signal pattern.

line.dialogue: Malee says "The cadence matches — every verse maps to a pulse interval. This isn't a haunting, it's a *map*.
Malee says "The stories contradict themselves by the third verse. Either memory has rotted the truth, or someone deliberately seeded false versions across generations.

choices.text: Use the ship's comms to broadcast the Phantom Frequency at full power. Let the echo itself deal with them. (Dangerous.)
choices.description: Cut the antenna feed and order Bandit to track the signal's origin by foot through the ridge pass.

line.dialogue: Bandit says "Three clicks northeast, sheltered in the old lava tube. I can see hull plating catching moonlight — she's real, and she's *close*.
Bandit says "The signal bounced off the canyon walls so many times I've got six possible origins and no way to tell which is true. We're chasing our own echoes.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship shudders violently as a low, discordant hum vibrates through the deck. The Lattice below churns with unnatural, jagged patterns.
We have to do something! That signal is tearing the ship apart!
The pain is gone. The ache from the ghost frequency, I mean. It just... stopped. That's not comforting.
The harmonic dampeners are failing. If we don't recalibrate the resonator, the Lattice's feedback will crystallize the hull.
The lost ship isn't just calling. It's screaming. A final, desperate resonance trapped in time. We must answer.
A fractured, whispering voice crackles over the comms, cutting through the engine's whine. 'Please... call me back...'
That's the echo! It's coming from the starboard drift-crystal array!

lines_after.dialogue: The ghostly transmission stabilizes into a looping distress ping. The ship's instruments flicker, syncing with the ancient signal.
Well, we called. And something answered. Good night, common sense.
The silence after a scream is the loudest sound of all. We have found its source.

line.dialogue: The echo's source is a corrupted resonator frequency. To trace it, we must override the ship's safeties.

choices.line: Reroute power through the auxiliary crystals. (Chanida: 'Simple and direct!')
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with ship navigation to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Arthit hits a wall. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.line: Manually tune the main resonator to match the ghost frequency. (Arthit: 'Precise, but risky.')
choices.description: Malee volunteers to seek the dismissed truth, leveraging crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Malee. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Malee fails. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: Have Pichit Sing a counter-harmony to stabilize the field. (Malee: 'Show-off. Let's hope you're in tune.')
choices.description: Have the villager risk using irrigation to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: the villager makes it work. The islander's wisdom cuts through complexity.
The risk doesn't pay off. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the echo has led you to a graveyard of shattered crystal and frozen resonance. The spectral hull of the lost ship, *The Weeping Spire*, phases in and out of reality beside your own.
Now I know... why the Tonal Orders buried this. That ship isn't just wrecked. It's *infected* with the Silencing's final frequency.
There's a high chance the corrupted resonance will jump to our ship if we get any closer. Containment is impossible.
From the ghost ship's bridge, a single, solid figure emerges—a Sky Pirate, her resonator-blade crackling with stolen power.
Took you long enough! The Echo's mine! Its frequency can part the Lattice anywhere—no charts, no Orders! Hand over your resonator core.
You're the one who's been amplifying the signal! You're tearing the Lattice apart to loot a corpse!
Some silences are meant to be kept. Unearthing this one... this is the best way to ensure the Silencing doesn't repeat.
The pirate's ship, hidden by chaff frequencies, decloaks, its weapons humming. The ghost ship wails, its structure beginning to violently destabilize.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax of the confrontation leaves the ghost ship's echo finally, peacefully, dissolving into the Lattice's ambient song.
The anomalous frequencies are dissipating. The lattice patterns are returning to normal. We've... stabilized it.
Every echo fades. But the memory of its song, and the choice we made here, will resonate far longer.

line.dialogue: The pirate is defeated, but the unstable ghost ship is about to erupt. You can save the forbidden knowledge within, or purge it.

choices.line: Purge the Echo. Scatter the frequency forever. (Arthit: 'The safest path. Some knowledge is a burden.')
choices.description: Sprint toward Bandit and tackle him before he reaches the Echo's core, 15 words

line.dialogue: I caught his arm mid-reach — the crystal hummed against my chest and I felt every buried frequency scream through my bones at once.
He sidestepped me like I was standing still — whatever that signal did to him, his reflexes aren't human anymore.

choices.line: Harness the Echo briefly to disable the pirate fleet, then let it fade. (Chanida: 'Use their weapon against them!')
choices.description: Shatter the resonance amplifier with a thrown tuning blade to cut Bandit's connection, 15 words

line.dialogue: The blade hit true — the amplifier cracked and the corrupted frequency collapsed into silence, and for one breath the whole chamber went dead and still.
My throw went wide and cracked the wrong crystal — the feedback loop doubled and I heard something behind the walls answer it.

choices.line: Attempt to Salvage the Echo's core frequency for the Listeners. (Malee: 'Great. We're becoming librarians of doom.')

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Terrace-hardened resilience sees them through.
the villager misreads the situation. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The Lattice stretches to the horizon, a fractured sea of crystalline shards that hum with latent energy. Your observation platform creaks as it sways over the shimmering surface.
Look at those light patterns! Like the whole world is breathing. Why do the Orders keep everyone so terrified of this place?
Because one wrong step and the resonance liquefies your bones, Chanida. Beauty with teeth. The Tonal charts don't mark this sector as safe for nothing.
Scanners are picking up anomalous frequency pockets below the platform's starboard side. Could be salvage... or a harmonic trap. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Every hum from below is a memory of the Silencing. The Lattice remembers what we forgot. What if we're not supposed to be up in our floating cities, but down here, listening?

You the scavengers? Don't linger. The sky pirates have been snatching cargo from the lower platforms. Nasty business. My girlfriend gets jealous if I'm out here too long—worries I'll get snatched too.
Your girlfriend? What size does she wear? Maybe she needs some proper lattice-walking gear instead of worrying!
Easy for you to say. You've got a Singer with you. The rest of us need the Tonal charts just to not die. Does she have a boyfriend in the pirate gangs? Is that why you're not scared?

lines_after.dialogue: Charming. We're here to scavenge resonator crystals, not play matchmaker for paranoid villagers.
The villager's fear is a data point. Pirates imply they've mapped unauthorized frequencies. That's a significant breach of Order monopoly.
Or they're listening to the Lattice itself, like the old Listeners. Fear always masks a deeper truth.

line.dialogue: The villager points toward a glimmering crystal deposit below, but the path looks unstable. How do we proceed?

choices.text: Take the main, charted path down. Slow but safe.
choices.description: Channel your own harmonic frequency through the crystal floor to map the stable paths, 15 words

line.dialogue: I've got a solid read—the stable nodes are lighting up like a constellation under our feet.
Your frequency bounced wrong and now the whole chamber is ringing—everyone freeze before it amplifies further.

choices.text: Use Pichit's innate resonance to find a quicker, unmarked route.
choices.description: Drop a resonance marker into the nearest frequency pocket and record what echoes back, 15 words

line.dialogue: The echo came back layered—three distinct tones, which means we're standing above a Silencing archive, not a tomb.
It didn't echo back at all—the pocket swallowed it whole, and I've never seen the crystals go that dark.

choices.text: Send Chanida ahead to scout—she's the most agile.
choices.description: Touch the crystal wall directly and let the memory-hum surface through your bare skin, 15 words

line.dialogue: I can feel them—thousands of voices pressed flat
the villager hits a wall. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: You descend onto the Lattice proper. The ground isn't solid—it's a mosaic of interlocking plates that chime with each footfall. The air smells of ozone and old stone.
The crystal cluster is right there! But... the frequency feels off. Jittery. Like it's been tampered with.
Confirmed. Residual harmonic signatures don't match natural lattice patterns. This is artificial interference. Someone has been here recently.
Oh, it's you! I should have known. Sky pirates leave a stink like cheap resonator grease.
Well, well. Look what the lattice coughed up. The Singer and his little choir. Everyone knows you're poking around where you shouldn't!
You're using frequencies the Orders haven't charted. How?
The Groundless Movement ain't waiting for permission to live, Singer. We heard everything! The Lattice talks if you shut up and listen. Your floating cities are just cages with a nice view.
You stole those crystals, didn't you? That's not 'living free,' that's thievery!

lines_after.dialogue: Thievery? The Orders stole the world! We're just taking back the keys. Your villager friend up there? His whole block is whispering about going Groundless.
The subplot thickens. This isn't mere piracy—it's an ideological insurgency with access to forbidden acoustic knowledge.
Great. So we're caught between monopolist bureaucrats and anarchist crystal-humpers. My favorite.

line.dialogue: The pirate is guarding the crystal cluster, but seems more interested in preaching than fighting. The Groundless Movement's influence is spreading. What's our priority?

choices.text: Secure the crystals quickly and retreat—avoid entanglement.
choices.description: Slam my resonator tuning fork against the crystal cluster to shatter their harmonic lock.

line.dialogue: Chanida says, "The lattice screamed and let go — their anchor just collapsed, we move NOW!
Chanida says, "Wrong frequency — I just amplified their signal and now every pirate in the lattice knows exactly where we stand.

choices.text: Try to reason with the pirate, learn more about the Movement's goals.
choices.description: Feign surrender to the bandit while Malee circles behind through the refracted light corridor.

line.dialogue: Malee says, "He bought it hook and sinker — my blade's at his spine before he finished his second 'well, well.
Malee says, "The refraction shifted — I walked straight into his second mate and now we're both pinned with steel at our throats.

choices.text: Challenge their ideology. Argue that the floating cities preserve what's left of civilization.
choices.description: Trigger Arthit's harmonic decoy drone and sprint for the cluster while the pirates chase the

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform shudders. A jagged fracture snakes through the crystalline ground below, humming with a dissonant frequency. The distant glow of a grounded pirate skiff smolders where it crashed.
They're following us! The pirates must have a tracker on the resonator we took!
Calm. Panic is a higher-pitched frequency. The fracture is unstable, but it's also a shortcut. If we can cross...
If. Always 'if.' The Groundless rabble-rousers said this sector was 'awakening.' I didn't think they meant literally.
Listen. Beneath the fracture's groan... a counter-harmony. The Lattice isn't breaking. It's responding.
Don't leave it open! The crack, I mean! My cousin said a fissure like this once swallowed a whole salvage team. I don't want people knowing I was out here...
OY! You lot! You've got our property! Hand over the resonator core, and maybe we won't pitch you into the chasm!
Come and take it! See what singing the Lattice does to your rusty hull!

line.dialogue: The pirate leader raises a crackling sonic disruptor. The fracture pulses in time with your heart. Arthit sees a potential path across unstable crystal plates.

choices.text: Surrender the Core. Give them the resonator. It's just a tool. Avoiding a fight here... made me feel better about our chances later.
choices.outcome_line: You toss the glowing core to the pirates. They snatch it and retreat, cackling. The immediate threat is gone, but the path ahead is dark and silent.
choices.description: Chanida steps forward with singer voice, ready to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Chanida fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Distract and Dash. Have Chanida create a sonic diversion while you all sprint across the fracture plates.
choices.outcome_line: Chanida screams a piercing note. The Lattice flashes, stunning the pirates. You dash across the singing plates, each step a calculated risk as they chime beneath you.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to decipher the monk's recording using Listener training

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit hits a wall. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Sing the Fracture Closed. Pichit, you heard the counter-harmony. Try to resonate with it, to seal the crack and cut off the pirates.
choices.outcome_line: You focus, humming the unstable frequency back into stability. The crystal grinds, the fracture seals with a deafening CHIME, trapping the pirates on the far side. The effort leaves you breathless.
choices.description: The villager takes the lead, employing terraces to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the villager makes it work. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
The attempt backfires on the villager. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_after.dialogue: Across the now-sealed or now-crossed fissure, the pirate skiff's lights fade. The silence that follows is profound, broken only by the Lattice's deep, settling hum.
Well. That saved us. The Groundless will have felt that. 'Don't want people knowing,' he said. Too late.
They already know. The Lattice tells them. We're not hiding anymore. We're... broadcasting.

lines_before.dialogue: You stand at the Ephemeral Spire, a needle of pure crystal where the Lattice's song is clearest. Below, the Groundless gather—not a mob, but a silent congregation. Above, the Tonal Orders' flagship descends, its official channels screaming for your surrender.
The resonance is at a critical juncture. The Spire can amplify a signal to recalibrate the local Lattice... or shatter it. The Orders' ship is priming a suppression frequency.
Give it to me! Let me shout them down! I'll fill their bridges with so much noise they'll forget their own names!
Typical. We finally find the world's volume knob, and everyone wants to turn it to eleven. Are you finished yet, Pichit? Finished thinking?
The Orders' charts... they're a cage. The pirates' frequencies are a theft. The Groundless seek silence because the noise has cheated them. Swindled them of peace.
Please... you have to do something! They'll scorch the Spire to silence it!
Don't listen to 'em! The Orders, the Groundless—they all want to control the song! The real treasure is the noise itself! Bring it on!
A low, subsonic pulse emanates from the flagship. The Spire vibrates. Cracks begin to form at its base. The Groundless below cover their ears, some collapsing.

line.dialogue: The Spire is the key. It can receive, amplify, and project. But what you project will define this place forever. The Lattice holds its breath.

choices.text: Amplify the Orders' Suppression. Use the Spire to boost their 'silencing' frequency. It will pacify the region, restoring 'order.' You were cheated of a better choice, but survival isn't nothing.
choices.outcome_line: A wave of absolute silence rolls forth. The Lattice goes dull and grey. The Groundless weep in relief. The pirates flee. The Orders land, victorious. The song here is finished.
choices.description: Have Chanida focus hidden frequencies on the shifting light to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
The risk doesn't pay off. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.text: Broadcast the Pirate's 'Treasure' Frequencies. Unleash a cacophony of hidden, chaotic harmonics. It will break the Orders' control and create a permanent zone of anarchic resonance.
choices.outcome_line: The sky explodes in wild, prismatic noise. The flagship's systems overload. The Groundless are horrified. The Lattice becomes a shifting, unpredictable storm. Control is finished.
choices.description: Have Malee risk using scavenger instincts to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Malee. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee hits a wall. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: Sing a New Chart. Pour your understanding—of the Orders' precision, the Listeners' reverence, the pirates' freedom—into a new, living frequency. Not to control, but to guide.
choices.outcome_line: You sing. The Spire doesn't blast—it *resonates*. A complex, beautiful pattern of light and sound washes over the Lattice, healing the cracks. The flagship halts, sensors bewildered. The Groundless look up, hearing not noise, but music. The old war... is finished.
choices.description: Have the villager focus irrigation on the shifting light to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the villager finds the key. The islander's wisdom cuts through complexity.
The resonance turns hostile. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_after.dialogue: The consequences of your chord ripple across the crystalline plain. The Lattice's color and hum have changed, perhaps forever. The factions are stunned, recalibrating.
The resonance stability is... unprecedented. You've written a new equation on the world itself.
Huh. So that's what it sounds like when the salesman *doesn't* swindle you. Might almost be worth the headache.
They're all just... listening. Actually listening. What do we do now?
We listen, too. The song isn't over. It's just begun.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow tastes of cold stone and ancient dust. The party's boots crunch on crystalline debris as the tunnel from the surface widens into a cavernous, echoing dark.
Look at the walls! They're... humming. Like the Lattice, but different.
Or like we're walking into the world's biggest, most fragile glass harp. One wrong step and we become a permanent part of the acoustics.
We should map our path. These echo patterns are disorienting. A sound could come from anywhere.
Listen. It's not just humming. It's layered. A history, pressed into the crystal. We're not the first to seek answers here.
A sharp clatter of falling stone rings out from a side passage, the sound multiplying and warping as it bounces.
Stop right there! This is my claim. Surface folk like you shouldn't be poking around in the deep dark.
Your claim? The whole island is drifting! Finders keepers!

lines_after.dialogue: You have no idea what you're walking into. This place... it has a class. A structure. It's not some random cave. I have a class to teach about survival down here, and lesson one is: leave.
A structure? You mean the pre-Silencing ruins. You've found something.
Found trouble. And I'm gonna rush off right now if you're smart. Her mom—a Singer from the Floating Spires—told me about it already. The echoes here... they remember.

line.dialogue: The scavenger is hostile but fearful, clutching a strange, faceted crystal. How does the party proceed?

choices.text: Offer a trade: supplies for information.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use resonant staff and harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Press for details about the 'structure' and the Singer's warning.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to decode the cryptic message, leveraging engineering

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Malee fails. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: Stand your ground and demand passage, implying greater numbers.
choices.description: Have the scavenger risk using survival skills to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Exactly as the scavenger hoped. Surface knowledge reveals a safe path.
Defeat. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Past the scavenger's territory, the cavern opens into a vast chamber. Shattered crystal columns rise like petrified trees, cradling fragments of metallic walls—a ruin fused with the island's heart.
Incredible. The fusion is seamless. The Silencing didn't destroy this place; it... consumed it.
Over here! Symbols on this wall... they're glowing faintly where I stepped.
As Chanida's footfalls echo, the glyphs pulse with a soft blue light, racing along a circuit in the floor before sputtering out.
It's not working. The circuit's broken. Or we're using the wrong kind of sound.
Not broken. Sleeping. We need the right resonance to wake it. A specific tone...
A low, harmonious chant fills the chamber, causing the glyphs to flare steadily. A figure in grey robes steps from behind a column.
You approach the memory with trampling feet. Please. Be still. Listen.

lines_after.dialogue: My vigil is finished. I went to bed late last night, but sleep would not come. The song here... it has changed. Become a warning.
A warning? From the Lattice?
From before. A final message, etched in resonance when the world fell silent. My Order forbids its interpretation. They say it's out of order. But I must know. Give it to me! The truth!
You're a Listener. You hear the song. What is it telling you to do?

line.dialogue: The monk is desperate, torn between his vows and his need to understand the haunting echo. The party can attempt to activate the ancient panel.

choices.text: Let the monk try to coax the message forth with his chants.
choices.description: Channel your own breath into the wall symbols, matching their faint pulse rhythm by rhythm.

line.dialogue: [arthit: "The symbols are answering — the resonance is building, keep breathing with me!"]
[malee: "You pushed too hard. The glow's gone cold and now they won't respond to anything."]

choices.text: Have Chanida and Arthit attempt to repair the broken circuit with spare resonator parts.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to chant the old monastery waking-verses while you press both palms flat against the circuit.

line.dialogue: [pichit: "There — the circuit drinks the verse like water. It remembers us now."]
[chanida: "The verses clashed with the frequency. Something behind the wall just... retreated further in."]

choices.text: Pichit tries to 'Sing' to the panel, mimicking the patterns he feels in the stone.
choices.description: Trace the broken circuit path with your fingertip to find where the Silencing severed it, then bridge the gap with your own ki.

line.dialogue: [arthit: "You're the bridge. The current is flowing through you into the dead section — it's holding!"]
[malee: "Your ki recoiled. Whatever the Silencing left in that gap, it doesn't want living energy crossing it."]

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before a massive, ancient door in the deepest chamber of The Hollow. It is not stone, but a seamless, dark crystal. Faint, rhythmic patterns of light pulse within it, like a slow heartbeat.
It's... breathing. Do doors usually breathe? I don't like this.
The acoustics in this chamber are perfect. No echo at all. The sound is being absorbed. That's not natural.
Or it's being *used*. My resonator is picking up a subsonic hum. It's not a door; it's a lock. And we're the unwelcome guests.
A lock implies something worth protecting. Or imprisoning.
The Listeners' oldest texts... they spoke of a 'Heart Chamber.' A place where the Lattice's first song was recorded. I thought it was allegory.
Allegory or not, there's a seam here. See? The crystal grew around something. Something from before. Her mom told me about it already, old scavenger tales of a 'silent heart'.
So how do we open it? Smash it?
With what? Your profound lack of subtlety? Look at the patterning. It's responding to Malee's scanner. It's a resonance lock. That's really easy to guess! It needs a specific frequency.

line.dialogue: The pulsing crystal door awaits. The monk looks terrified, the scavenger greedy. The air grows heavy.

choices.line: Let the Listener Monk attempt a ritual chant. (Use tradition)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the door's surface and match your breathing to its rhythm.

line.dialogue: The wood warmed under my hand—and then the breathing slowed, syncing with mine, like it recognized me as something alive too.
I touched it and it *inhaled sharply*—the door sucked at my palm like a mouth and I ripped my hand back before it could swallow.

choices.line: Have Malee try to brute-force the resonance frequency with her tech. (Use ingenuity)
choices.description: Strike the tuning fork against the chamber wall and walk the perimeter, mapping where the resonance dies.

line.dialogue: The tone vanishes at exactly three points forming a triangle around the door—whatever's behind it is dampening sound in a deliberate pattern.
The fork shattered against the stone and the chamber absorbed the fragments without a single echo—this room eats sound, and I just fed it.

choices.line: Ask Chanida to shout, to see if raw, impulsive sound triggers something. (Use force)
choices.description: Unseal your resonator's containment field and let the subspace signal bleed raw into the chamber unfiltered.

line.dialogue: The signal blossomed into something visible—threads of light spiraling from the door's seams, and I heard *singing* from underneath, old and patient and waiting.
Raw signal flooded the chamber and my resonator screamed—one frequency bounced wrong and hit Pichit square in

lines_after.dialogue: A deep, resonant chime rings out, not through the air, but in the bones. The dark crystal becomes transparent, revealing a vast, geodesic chamber beyond. In its center, suspended in air, is a single, perfect, silent bell.
It never rang. The first bell, and it was never struck.
The Warning... it's not a message in the song. It's the absence of one. The Silencing started here.
Forget the philosophy! That bell is pre-Silencing crystal! One chip could buy a city!

As the scavenger takes a step forward, the ground trembles. From the shadows of the new chamber, shapes detach—sleek, obsidian constructs with blade-like limbs, their forms humming with stolen resonance. The guardians are awake.

lines_before.dialogue: The Heart Chamber is a cathedral of stillness. The silent bell hangs at its nexus. The obsidian guardians—Echo-Eaters—move with terrifying silence, absorbing sound to fuel their attacks. The party is surrounded.
They're damping our resonance! My shield projector is flickering!
They're the cause. The flaw in the Lattice. Self-repairing guardians that got corrupted, started consuming all sound. Who is this guy who designed this? A maniac!
Less history, more fighting! Their limbs are sharp!
The bell! It's the key! Someone called it the 'Conductor' in the old stories! A man called you, Pichit, didn't he? That Singer in the last port? He said you'd know what to do!
He said... 'the first note must be given, not taken.'
You cannot strike it. That would be violence. It must be... offered a sound. A true one.

An Echo-Eater lunges, its blade-arm shearing through stone. The Scavenger screams, clutching a bleeding arm. The Monk closes his eyes, beginning a frantic, desperate chant. The Lattice's Warning shrieks in your minds: *CONSUMPTION. SILENCE. END.*

line.dialogue: The guardians close in. The silent bell waits. The Monk's chant is being eaten by the creatures. The final choice is yours.

choices.line: Unite your voices. Sing a single, pure note together into the bell. (Unity)
choices.description: Strike the bell with Arthit's failing shield projector to amplify its resonance outward.

line.dialogue: The feedback loop caught — their damping field just shattered like glass!
Projector's dead. I poured everything into that strike and got nothing back.

choices.line: Sacrifice a resonator. Have Malee overload it, creating a burst of 'false sound' to feed the Echo-Eaters and distract them. (Sacrifice)
choices.description: Have Malee trace the Lattice flaw through the bell's surface to trigger self-repair.

line.dialogue: I found the fracture point — the Lattice is rewriting itself around the wound!
The flaw runs deeper than I can reach. It's pulling my fingers apart.

choices.line: Do nothing. Embrace the silence. Let the Monk's failed chant be the last sound, proving the bell's purpose is not to ring. (Faith)
choices.description: Chanida grabs the bell and charges directly into the closest enemy cluster.

line.dialogue: Ring loud, you ugly things — that's the sound of your teeth leaving your skulls!
Took the hit. Bell's still humming but my ribs aren't doing so great.

lines_after.dialogue: A sound emerges. Not from the bell, but from the Lattice itself—a deep, forgiving, fundamental tone that washes through the chamber. The Echo-Eaters dissolve into harmonic dust. The silent bell begins to glow, not with light, but with a profound, calming quiet.
It wasn't a warning to be heard. It was a lesson to be understood. The first sound is forgiveness.
The Warning... it's quieted. The Lattice's pain... eased. We were so wrong. We listened for a command, not a truth.
My arm... it's stopped hurting. The crystal... it healed it? What *is* this place?

The Heart Chamber is now warm, resonant, safe. The subplot of the Listener's Warning resolves not in a shouted alarm, but in a settled peace. The party has not found a weapon, but a cure. And the Floating Cities above will never know how close they came to a second Silencing, or how it was quietly averted.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch before you, a cascade of green terraces where the only sounds are the rustle of wind through grain and the gentle gurgle of irrigation channels.
Listen to that… the Lattice beneath us is almost silent here. It’s not a true silence, but a chorus of tiny, living vibrations.
It’s peaceful, sure, but we didn’t come here just to listen to crops grow. The scavenger said to meet by the old water shrine.
Probably a waste of time. Surface-dwellers are all the same—promise you salvage, sell you rust.
We should proceed with caution. This place is under the Tonal Orders' watch. We don’t want to draw attention.
A figure in ochre robes stands at the edge of a terrace, head bowed as if listening to the soil. It’s the Listener Monk.
You hear it too, don’t you? The way the roots hum… a different song from the Lattice’s usual resonance. We don’t stay in touch with the ground’s truth anymore.
What truth is that?

lines_after.dialogue: There was a ship… the *Echo of Dawn*. It fell from the sky-lanes generations ago. Its final resonance is still trapped in the Lattice here. A ghost in the crystal.
A lost ship? With salvage?
With a curse, some say. Its song is… wrong. I’ve tried to study it, but… I don’t know where to begin to untangle it from the garden’s own music.
A gruff voice calls from behind a stone water wheel. The Surface Scavenger steps out, eyeing the monk warily.
Don’t leave it open. The past, I mean. Some frequencies you shouldn’t wake. That monk’s been poking at a grave.

line.dialogue: The monk and scavenger offer conflicting paths regarding the lost ship's echo. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Trust the Monk’s spiritual approach. Ask to be shown the 'ghost song' directly. (Gain insight into the Lattice's nature.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the ground and feel for the Lattice's pulse through the root system.

line.dialogue: There—beneath the soil, a heartbeat. Faint, but the Lattice isn't dead here. It's *dreaming*.
Nothing. Either the roots are too deep or this section has gone completely numb. My fingers are just tingling from the cold.

choices.line: Side with the Scavenger’s caution. Demand practical details about the ship’s location and dangers first. (Gain tactical information.)
choices.description: Signal Arthit to take point with his blade drawn while you scan the tree line for movement or ward-marks.

line.dialogue: Ward-sigils on the third trunk—fresh cuts in the bark. Someone marked this path recently. We're not the first ones here today.
I see nothing but shadows and old growth. Either I'm blind or whatever's watching us doesn't want to be found. Either way, my sword arm is getting tired.

choices.line: Remain neutral. Suggest the party investigates the general area of the anomaly on their own. (Maintain independence.)
choices.description: Challenge Malee directly—ask what she actually knows about surface-dwellers that makes her so dismissive.

line.dialogue: Fine. Last surface team I worked with fed our position to a Hollow Choir patrol to save themselves. Eight people died. So forgive me if I don't trust the ground beneath their feet.
Don't. You don't get to open

lines_before.dialogue: Following the leads, you arrive at a secluded, overgrown terrace. The air feels denser here, and a faint, discordant hum vibrates up through your boots.
The resonance is localized… and unstable. This isn’t a natural Lattice formation.
Great. So we’re standing on a crystalline tomb. I feel so welcomed.
Told you. The *Echo’s* final crash-site is directly below this plot. The ground’s been… soft here ever since. Better if you don’t go prying further.
Why? What happens if we 'go prying'?
The song becomes a scream. It… it can attract things from the deeper Lattice. Or worse, rewrite the local resonance, making navigation impossible.
A memory, trapped in crystal… What could be so powerful it leaves a scar for generations?
A sudden, sharper pulse of sound emanates from the ground. A faint, ghostly shimmer, like a heat haze, forms the outline of a ship’s prow for a moment before fading.

lines_after.dialogue: A resonant phantasm! The energy is spiking!
We have to do something! If that fully manifests, it could shatter this whole terrace!
You can put your hand down now. The warning’s over. It’s happening.
Fantastic. So do we run, or try to sing it a lullaby?

line.dialogue: The Echo of the Lost Ship is destabilizing. The phantom is beginning to materialize. What is your immediate response?

choices.line: Evacuate the area. Get the monk and scavenger to safety and contain the anomaly from a distance. (Avoid direct risk.)
choices.description: Have Chanida focus crystal hearing on the terraces to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida misreads the situation. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Attempt to calm the resonance. Use your own ship's crystal or the monk's knowledge to counter the discordant frequency. (Risk a resonance feedback.)
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Things don't go as planned. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.line: Dive into the anomaly. Try to physically interface with the phantom ship's core resonance to understand—or claim—its source. (High risk, potential high reward.)
choices.description: The monk takes the lead, employing lattice study to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: the monk's expertise pays off. Ancient knowledge surfaces, connecting past and present.
the monk is thwarted. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk leads you to a secluded, overgrown terrace. A single, ancient crystal spire hums faintly, its base overgrown with luminous moss.
Here. The echo is strongest here. The Lattice remembers… and the professors are really good at teaching us to ignore it.
Ignore what? What did your precious Tonal Orders tell you to forget?
The ship, the *Echo's Lament*. It wasn't lost to a storm. Its captain, a Singer, discovered a flaw in the official charts. The prices are reasonable for silence, you see.
A flaw? In the navigation charts? That's… that's the foundation of everything.
Of course it is. And the monopoly charges very fair prices for keeping that foundation from crumbling. What was the flaw?
A dead zone. A place where the Lattice's song goes silent. The charts mark it as safe passage. The *Echo's Lament* sailed into it… and was unmade.
Unmade? Not destroyed? There's a difference in the resonance.

lines_after.dialogue: He's right. I've seen the wreckage from below. It's not broken. It's… frozen. Like a ghost in the crystal.
The spire's hum shifts, becoming a strained, discordant note. The air grows cold.
It's here, isn't it? The echo.

line.dialogue: The discordant note swells. A faint, shimmering image of a fractured ship's prow begins to materialize around the spire, weeping crystalline tears.

choices.line: Harmonize with the Echo: Pichit attempts to match the lost ship's final, desperate frequency to calm it.
choices.consequence: The image stabilizes, showing a clear memory of the flawed chart.
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing engineering to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee fails. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Reinforce the Memory: The party uses their own resonators to strengthen the ghostly image, forcing it to reveal its truth.
choices.consequence: The echo becomes painfully loud, revealing the coordinates but attracting unwanted attention.
choices.description: Arthit channels captain experience toward the peaceful breeze, hoping to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
A costly mistake by Arthit. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Question the Monk's Motive: Confront the Listener. Why show you this now? What does he truly want?
choices.consequence: The monk breaks, revealing he was sent to test your loyalty. The echo reacts violently to his confession.
choices.description: The scavenger steps forward with crystal fragments, ready to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: the scavenger succeeds. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the scavenger loses control. A scavenging tool breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The ghost-ship's wail pierces the pastoral silence. Crops wither momentarily in its wake. The Scavenger draws a makeshift resonator.
That's no problem for me. I've tangled with Lattice-ghosts before. But this one… it's hungry for acknowledgement.
My stomach is starting to growl! But for justice, not food. This secret's been festering long enough.
We have the coordinates of the dead zone. The Tonal Orders will know we have it. There's something in my eye… dust from a crumbling empire.
I… I was to report your reaction. But the truth… it resonates louder.
Forget your report! We have to do something! We can't let them bury this again!
The echo isn't just a memory. It's a warning, stuck in a loop. To silence it, we must break the loop. We must choose what to do with its truth.
The *Echo's Lament* fully manifests, a translucent cage of crystal and sorrow, its central resonator pulsing with corrupted light. The fate of the truth hangs on your next action.

lines_after.dialogue: The gardens are forever changed. The air holds a new, subtle vibration—a song of reckoning.
Well. The surface just got a lot more interesting. And dangerous.
So, we're whistleblowers now. I hope you all like the taste of rations and paranoia.

line.dialogue: The ghost-ship's core resonator flickers, containing the raw data of the fatal flaw. It is both a key and a weapon.

choices.line: Release the Echo: Guide the lost resonance to dissipate peacefully into the Lattice, erasing the evidence but granting the ship rest.
choices.consequence: Peace returns to the gardens. The secret is safe, but the Orders remain unchallenged. The monk leaves, disillusioned.
choices.description: Arthit channels tattooed routes toward the terraces, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The gamble fails. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Capture the Proof: Use your ship's resonator to carefully extract and record the coordinate data, creating undeniable evidence.
choices.consequence: You possess the truth, making you a target. The Scavenger offers a route to smuggle it to other cities.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with crystal prosthetic to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
The lattice has other plans. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.line: Amplify and Broadcast: Overcharge the echo, screaming its truth across the Lattice's resonant layer for all to hear.
choices.consequence: The revelation rocks the floating cities. Navigation is thrown into chaos, but the Orders' monopoly is shattered. You become fugitives.
choices.description: Have the monk risk using lattice study to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: the monk's expertise pays off. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The attempt backfires on the monk. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a low, steady tone that vibrates through the bones. High above the Lattice's crystalline surface, the air thrums with enforced calm.
Look at this place! It's like the whole spire is singing. Can you feel it in your teeth?
I feel it in my headache. This 'calming' resonance is just noise pollution with good PR. Most Thais are Buddhist, we appreciate quiet contemplation, not this... industrial hum.
The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for these coordinates. Maintaining this anchor can't be cheap. (It) probably won’t be too expensive for them, but for us? (The price) is rather expensive for Thais.
Yet, we pay. We always pay for knowledge. What does that say about the value we place on understanding?
A smooth-talking figure in rich silks approaches, a Trade Negotiator the Trade Negotiator with a ledger in hand.
Ah, newcomers! Welcome to the Anchor Spire. The harmonic stability here is excellent for business. No sudden emotional decisions, just clear-headed trade. Looking for anything specific?
We heard a story. An old resonance ship, lost years ago. The 'Echo's Lament.' They say its ghost-frequency sometimes whispers here.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, a tale for those who love adventure. Or tragedy. That ship... bad business. Its cargo was unstable, they say. Sank right through the Lattice. Why dig up old echoes?
Because old echoes sometimes carry valuable signals. If you know how to listen.
The merchant's smile doesn't reach his eyes. He hides something behind it.
Every lost thing seeks to be found. Even a memory.

line.dialogue: The merchant suggests the lost ship's frequency is dangerous junk, but offers a lead for a price. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Pay his fee. Knowledge has a cost, and we have coin.
choices.outcome: The merchant gives you a faded frequency chart.
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing resonant staff to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Pichit hits a wall. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.line: Appeal to his sense of history. The past shouldn't be forgotten.
choices.outcome: Intrigued, he shares a fragment of the story 'off the ledger.'
choices.description: Direct Arthit to seek the dismissed truth using captain experience

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
The resonance turns hostile. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.line: Bluff. Say we're with the Listeners, here on official study.
choices.outcome: Wary of the monastic order, he gives a basic direction to avoid trouble.
choices.description: The pirate presses forward with disruptor weapon to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the pirate's expertise pays off. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
the pirate hits a wall. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the lead deeper into the spire's lower galleries, the monolithic hum is punctuated by the clatter of loose crystal and rough voices.
This feels like a bad shortcut. The structural integrity here looks... adventurous.
(For) the adventurous, he says. Meaning 'for the stupid.'
A group of sky pirates the sky pirate block the way, their clothes patched, their eyes sharp.
Hold it! This is a toll road. You wanna pass, you pay the frequency tax.
A tax? This is a public anchor! Who do you think you are?
The local authority. Now, may I see your driver's license? Your ship's resonance permit? No? Then you're trespassing on our patch.
You speak of authority, yet you hide in the shadows of a greater power's structure. What does that make you?

lines_after.dialogue: It makes us practical! The Tonal Orders hoard all the good charts. We find our own ways. Like the whisper from that old wreck. You're after it too, ain'tcha?
Why couldn't you just... mine for crystal like normal pirates?
Why can't you do it? Boring! That ghost-ship's frequency is a key. Opens old vaults, they say. Now, you gonna contribute to our research fund, or get pitched over the railing?
The pirates fan out. The steady tone of the spire makes sneaking up impossible. Confrontation is inevitable.

line.dialogue: The pirates are armed and blocking the path to the lost ship's echo. How do you handle them?

choices.line: Fight. Their threat is clear, and the spire's resonance negates their stealth advantage.
choices.outcome: A direct but noisy clash that alerts others to your presence.
choices.description: Hack the bandit's comm frequency and broadcast their position to every authority in range, 14 words

line.dialogue: Their signal just lit up like a festival lantern — I'd start running if I were you.
You just told every pirate in range exactly where WE are, you absolute genius.

choices.line: Bargain. Offer them a share of whatever we find at the echo.
choices.outcome: They agree, but will be unreliable partners watching for a chance to betray you.
choices.description: Offer to repair their broken relay equipment in exchange for passage, no credits exchanged, 14 words

line.dialogue: Their relay was held together with spit and prayer — but now it works, and so does our deal.
You touched it and now it's worse than before. That'll cost you double, offworlder.

choices.line: Bluff with superior knowledge. Claim you know the echo's frequency is a trap that destroys resonators.
choices.outcome: If they believe you, they'll leave. If they call your bluff, the fight will be harder.
choices.description: Draw your sidearm and dare them to explain the "toll" to their boss, 14 words

line.dialogue: Easy, easy — maybe I miscounted the toll. A misunderstanding. Pass freely, friend.
Brilliant negotiation. Now we're paying in blood instead of credits — hope that exchange rate works for you.

lines_before.dialogue: The party ascends the Anchor Spire's final tier. The harmonic vibration is overwhelming here, a pure, unwavering tone that resonates in your bones. It strips away deceit, making every emotion raw and visible.
My head is ringing! This tone... it's like it's scrubbing my thoughts clean. I feel everything so sharply.
A wonderful place for a confrontation. No one can hide their true intentions here. What’s her personality like? The Trade Negotiator's, I mean. Underneath all those smiles.
Caution. The Sky Pirate and the Negotiator are waiting at the apex. The vibration may force honesty, but it also makes stealth impossible. We are exposed.
Welcome! The Anchor Spire welcomes all. Its truth-tone is a boon for honest trade. Anywhere you like, we can discuss terms.
Cut the fancy talk. The tone's got my nerves raw. Why are you doing this to me? Hiding the real charts behind your 'fair deals'?
The Lattice's pure frequency reveals the discord between you. The Negotiator's charts... they are incomplete. You've hidden the path to the Echo of the Lost Ship.
Hidden? A prudent business practice! That ship's resonance is unstable, dangerous. I sell safe routes. Why are you treating me like this? Accusing me of malice?

lines_after.dialogue: The Sky Pirate snarls, the pure tone amplifying his anger. He draws a jagged resonance blade.
Enough! The real charts are on that haunted ship. I'll take them from its wreck, and you won't profit from my suffering!
Typical. The truth-tone just makes the greed louder.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate moves to attack the Negotiator, but the path to the Lost Ship's echo is now clear. The party must intervene.

choices.text: Side with the Negotiator. Defend the merchant, uphold the 'lawful' trade. You'll gain his favor, but the pirate's knowledge of hidden frequencies will be lost.
choices.consequence: Gain Merchant's Trust, Lose Pirate's Secrets
choices.description: Press your palms against the resonance crystal and let the truth-tone scan you willingly.

line.dialogue: The ringing stops — it's showing me everything I refused to see, and somehow that's peaceful.
My teeth ache and my sins flash behind my eyes — I can't breathe, pull me back!

choices.text: Side with the Sky Pirate. Help him seize the truth from the Negotiator. You'll learn the hidden frequencies, but the Tonal Orders will mark you as outlaws.
choices.consequence: Learn Hidden Frequencies, Gain Tonal Order Hostility
choices.description: Signal Arthit to flank the merchant while Malee negotiates access to the inner chamber.

line.dialogue: He thinks he's controlling this conversation — good, that means he's not watching Arthit slip behind him.
The merchant's smile didn't waver — he already counted our moves before we made them.

choices.text: Attempt to mediate. Use the Spire's pure tone to force a temporary accord. Both parties remain hostile, but you might extract fragments of truth from each.
choices.consequence: Gain Partial Secrets, Both NPCs Remain Suspicious
choices.description: Draw your

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the merchant overreaches. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

acts.title: Dawn at the Edge of Silence

lines_before.dialogue: The confrontation resolves. As the first rays of dawn touch the Spire's peak, the harmonic tone shifts, softening into a hopeful, clearing frequency. The Echo of the Lost Ship materializes in the lattice below—a ghostly resonance image.
The dawn frequency... it reveals the memory of the ship. Not as a wreck, but as it was before The Silencing. Is it real? Or just a phantom of sound?
It's beautiful! A fresh beginning. The ship's final song is trapped there. We have to listen!
The echo is unstable. Interacting with it could anchor the memory here... or shatter it forever. Please translate that for me, Pichit. What does your Singer's instinct say?
What about tomorrow? If we pull this ghost-ship's song into the present, we might learn what really caused The Silencing. Or we might just break something priceless.
The Lost Ship's echo pulses with a sorrowful, unfinished chord. It holds the truth. The Sky Pirate and Trade Negotiator watch from the edges, silenced by the dawn's revelation.
The song is a key. It is a memory of a frequency that could harmonize the Lattice... or disrupt it entirely. The choice is ours.
Then let's finish its song! Let's give it a dawn!

lines_after.dialogue: The party's decision resonates through the Anchor Spire. The dawn light solidifies, and the fate of the echo is sealed.
The consequences will ripple across the floating cities. We have changed something fundamental.
Well. Now we live with it.

line.dialogue: The Echo of the Lost Ship awaits its final note. You must choose how to interact with this preserved memory of the past.

choices.text: Preserve the Echo. Let it remain a beautiful, untouched memorial. You honor the past but leave the mystery of The Silencing unsolved.
choices.consequence: Gain Listeners' Respect, Mystery Remains
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to use the leg as a lattice probe, leveraging unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. She hears something no one else can.
Defeat. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.text: Harmonize the Echo. Gently weave its unfinished chord into the Spire's dawn tone, creating a new, stable frequency for navigation. You learn part of the truth.
choices.consequence: Create New Navigation Tone, Learn Partial History
choices.description: Have Arthit focus tattooed routes on the deep vibration to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.text: Resolve the Echo. Sing its final, missing note, completing its song and releasing its full memory into the world. The full truth of The Silencing is revealed, with unpredictable repercussions.
choices.consequence: Learn The Silencing's Truth, Unlock World-Changing Resonance
choices.description: The pirate steps forward with pirate ship, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the pirate finds the key. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The gamble fails. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery hangs suspended over the Lattice, its halls shaped to channel and study the world's crystalline hum. The air itself vibrates with disciplined sound.
It's so... quiet. But not quiet. It's like the air is holding its breath, waiting for someone to whisper.
Precisely. Every surface is angled for acoustic perfection. A single mis-tuned note could destabilize the entire foundation. We must be cautious.
Great. So we're walking on an eggshell made of math. The Listeners sure know how to make a place welcoming.
This is a library of the world's song. A place of profound knowledge. We should listen, not just hear.
You're the outsiders asking about the old maps? Listen, just stop. The Tonal Orders have ears everywhere in these halls. I already know that trouble follows questions like yours.
Peace, brother. They are guests. Welcome to Phrao. I am Listener Kavi. You seek knowledge of the Lattice's Open Frequencies?

lines_after.dialogue: We heard rumors. Maps that aren't controlled by the Orders. Is it true?
The truth... is a complex resonance. Some truths can shatter a carefully tuned mind. I must ask you to stop this line of inquiry. For your safety.
He's still single, isn't he? That kind of devotion to 'safety' usually means a lonely life guarding secrets.

line.dialogue: Listener Kavi seems to know something but is afraid. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Respect his warning and ask for general teachings about the Lattice's song.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the nearest angled wall and listen through bone conduction.

line.dialogue: The geometry is transmitting harmonic residuals—this surface is still resonating with something recorded centuries ago.
Nothing. Just my own heartbeat bouncing back at me, and honestly, that's worse.

choices.text: Press gently, appealing to his duty as a seeker of truth.
choices.description: Hum a single sustained note and let the chamber's architecture shape it into its natural frequency.

line.dialogue: There—do you hear? The room *answered* you. It's been waiting for someone to speak first.
Yeah, that just sounded like a dying refrigerator in a cathedral. Let's maybe not do that again.

choices.text: Drop the subject for now and explore the monastery openly, looking for clues.
choices.description: Walk forward in absolute silence, counting steps until the acoustic shadow shifts.

line.dialogue: Twelve steps. The silence broke at twelve. Whatever this space is designed to protect, the threshold is physical, not metaphorical.
Your footfall clipped on the ninth step—the floor corrected you. It doesn't want us reaching the center uninvited.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the monastery's Harmonic Archives, the air grows still. The usual background hum of the Lattice is absent, replaced by an unsettling silence.
This archive is deadened. Acoustic null-points are engineered for storing unstable resonant records. Whatever is here, the Listeners didn't want it to sing.
Over here! This resonator console... it's cold. The crystal core won't vibrate at all. It's stuck, like a wagon wheel in deep mud.
It isn't broken. It's suppressed. A frequency has been deliberately locked away. A note the Lattice itself refuses to answer.
Let me guess. My father won't let me have a boyfriend, the Tonal Orders won't let people have a map. Control freaks come in all flavors.
You shouldn't be in this sector! This... this is the Forbidden Cadence. The resonance that precipitated The Silencing. The console won't move. It *can't* be made to work.

lines_after.dialogue: So there IS a map! A true one! And you've been hiding it!
Not hiding! Containing! Last night, I dreamt the archives were breached, that this knowledge was stolen. The dream felt like a pre-echo. The lattice itself is anxious.
If this frequency is so dangerous, why record it at all? Why not shatter the crystal and be done?

line.dialogue: The locked resonator holds the key to the Open Frequency Map, but the monk is terrified. What's the next move?

choices.text: Convince Kavi that containing the knowledge is making it a target; it must be understood to be safeguarded.
choices.description: Run your palm along the resonator's surface to feel where the suppression field breaks.

line.dialogue: Arthit* — "There — a hairline fracture in the null-point. If I press here, the frequency might bleed through.
Arthit* — "Nothing. Whatever's locking this down is seamless. My hand just slides across like dead glass.

choices.text: Attempt to bypass the lock using Chanida's impulsive resonance-tinkering, risking an unstable feedback pulse.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to hum the archive's root harmonic while you monitor the console's response.

line.dialogue: Chanida* — "I remember the calibration tone from Father's lessons. If I match it closely enough, the console should recognize me.
Chanida* — "I'm hitting the note but nothing's moving. It's like the console refuses to acknowledge the frequency even exists.

choices.text: Propose a dangerous ritual: having Pichit, as a potential Singer, attempt to 'hum' the forbidden frequency to unlock it.
choices.description: Demand Malee explain what she knows about her father's involvement in suppressing this frequency.

line.dialogue: Malee* — "Fine. He commissioned the suppression after the Resonance Collapse. He said the frequency was *infecting* people's thoughts. Satisfied?
Malee* — "I already told you — I don't know anything. He doesn't exactly brief me on his acoustic black projects, alright?

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the monastery's acoustic sanctum, the party stands before a massive, exposed section of the Lattice. The Open Frequency Map glows faintly on a crystalline slate.
Come and take a picture with us. We need to document this before the Tonal Orders erase it!
Wait. This map... it shows pathways the Orders claim are impossible. If it's wrong, a ship could be torn apart.
It is not wrong. Our measurements over decades confirm it. The Orders' official charts... they are the fiction. They suppress these frequencies to maintain control.
Of course they do. Monopoly 101. But broadcasting this? It's irrepairable. You think they'll just let you upend their entire economy?
The truth of the Lattice's song shouldn't be a commodity. This map... it's a record of the world as it truly resonates.
So we take it! We show everyone!
A distant, discordant hum vibrates through the stone. Crystal fixtures tremble.

lines_after.dialogue: The hum fades, leaving an unsettling silence. The monk looks pale.
They are here. The Orders' enforcers. They've come for the map.
Why weren't you careful? You knew they were watching.

line.dialogue: We need to decide what to do with the Open Frequency Map.

choices.text: Smash the slate. Destroy the evidence. Safety first.
choices.consequence: The physical map is lost, but the knowledge is safer inside your heads. The Orders have less to find, but the truth is harder to spread.
choices.description: Pull out your camera and frame all four of them around the map, capturing their faces and the forbidden pathways together, 15 words

line.dialogue: Perfect — this photo will burn through every firewall the Orders ever built.
The lens fogged from the cave humidity — we lost their faces but kept the map.

choices.text: Hide the slate within the monastery's acoustic maze.
choices.consequence: The map is concealed in a chamber of echoing harmonics, difficult to locate without a Listener's ear. It buys time, but the enforcers will tear the place apart looking for it.
choices.description: Grab the map from Arthit's hands and photograph it alone under your jacket hood, blocking any identifying background details, 15 words

line.dialogue: Smart. The pathways documented, our faces erased — they'll never trace this back to us.
Your shadow fell across the northern corridors — half the routes are unreadable now.

choices.text: Copy the key frequencies onto portable resonator crystals.
choices.consequence: You create multiple, fragile copies of the core data. The information can be dispersed, making it harder to suppress completely, but you now carry contraband that screams to any Order sensor.
choices.description: Hand the camera to Monk and position yourself between him and Malee, whispering for him to record video instead, 15 words

line.dialogue: I have captured the map, your voices, and the trembling in Malee's hands — proof alive.
My finger slipped and the recording stopped before anyone spoke a single word of evidence.

lines_before.dialogue: The monastery's great courtyard. Order enforcers in polished resonator-plate have cordoned off exits. A senior Tonal Master stands before you, her voice coldly modulated.
See? I told you they'd bring trouble! What size do you wear? A martyr's shroud?
You possess forbidden harmonics. The Lattice's stability is not a toy for amateurs. My Order gets jealous of such... interference. Hand over the illicit frequencies.
We seek only understanding. Not conflict.
She doesn't care. She has a monopoly to protect. Does the world have a girlfriend? No, it has the Tonal Orders, and they're the possessive type.
The Lattice belongs to everyone! Not just your guild!
A child's idealism. The Silencing happened because of unchecked resonance. We prevent that. Your 'open map' would lead to chaos. To another Silencing.
Or it would lead to freedom. You fear the song because you cannot control it all. Only a Singer could truly use this map... and you've hunted them near to extinction.
The Master's resonator gauntlets activate with a threatening whine. The very air tightens.

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation hangs on a knife's edge. The Listeners watch, torn. The villagers watch in fear. The Lattice itself seems to hold its breath.
The true song... it must be heard.
Last chance. Relinquish the data.

line.dialogue: This is the climax. How do you resolve the standoff?

choices.text: Surrender the data publicly, but recite the core frequencies aloud for all to hear.
choices.consequence: You give up the physical proof, but the secret is sung into the monastery's perfect acoustics, echoing endlessly. The knowledge becomes a rumor, a heresy, impossible to fully erase. The Orders' control is chipped, not broken.
choices.description: Channel the forbidden harmonics into the monk's Lattice amulet, overloading it

line.dialogue: You feel that? The harmonics don't belong to anyone — they flow where they're needed," I say as the amulet cracks in my palm.
The feedback — it's too much — I'm sorry, I've made everything worse," I gasp, dropping the smoking amulet.

choices.text: Challenge the Master's authority. Demand a Trial of Resonance, using the map's frequencies.
choices.consequence: You risk everything on a ceremonial duel of sound. If you win, the monastery gains the right to study the open frequencies openly. If you lose, you and the data are forfeit. It's a gamble that could legitimize the truth or destroy you.
choices.description: Kneel before the monk and offer to surrender the harmonics in exchange for dialogue

line.dialogue: I yield them freely. No monopoly, no war — just sit with us and listen to what we've learned," I say, extending open hands.
I offered everything and you still reached for the binding chains — I see now this was never about stability," I whisper as cold metal closes around my wrists.

choices.text: Activate the map's core frequency. Let the Lattice itself answer.
choices.consequence: You input the most unstable, beautiful harmonic from the map into the monastery's great resonator. The Lattice responds unpredictably—a localized, violent storm of crystal growth and sound that scatters everyone. It proves the map's power spectacularly, but causes massive collateral damage and marks you as dangerous radicals.
choices.description: Grab Malee's hand and run toward the village archive before the monk seals it

line.dialogue: The records inside will prove the harmonics were never forbidden — they were stolen! Move!" I shout, pulling Malee through the closing doors.
The seal activated — we're too late. Everything they erased from history is gone again," I breathe, pressing my palms against the locked stone door.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market thrums with ten thousand voices, a chaotic symphony of commerce and gossip that vibrates through the floating island's bones. The air smells of spice, ozone, and the faint, ever-present crystalline dust of the Lattice far below.
A place of such noise... it's a struggle to hear the underlying patterns. But even chaos has its rhythm, I suppose.
Rhythm? I hear a great place to spend some coin! And maybe find someone who knows something about that weird signal Arthit picked up.
Caution. The Tonal Orders have patrols here. Our... unauthorized listening could be seen as a challenge to their monopoly. We should be discreet.
Oh, they're too busy taxing the air merchants breathe to care about us. Look at them. Pragmatic, fearful little cogs. Just trying to get through the day without falling off the sky.
You lot look like you're listening for something. Bad idea. The Market's hum muddles the charts. Easy to get lost. The Orders don't like it when folk get lost.
We're not looking for charted paths. We're listening for... echoes. Things the hum might be hiding.
Yeah! Like a ghost ship! We heard a story about a lost resonance ship, the... what was it called?

lines_after.dialogue: The *Echo of the Seventh Dawn*? Don't speak its name! Its frequency is cursed. Sank into the Lattice cycles ago.
Let me guess. Everyone who goes looking for it vanishes, their resonators singing a mad song until the crystals shatter. I've heard a dozen variations. People love a tragic swindle.
Yet the initial detection was... precise. Anomalous. Not typical ghost story chatter. The data suggests a persistent, localized resonance fracture.
A fracture in the world's song... I know such things are possible. But I... don't know where to begin separating that truth from the market's noise.

line.dialogue: The villager scurries away, leaving you with a name and a warning. The Market's cacophony presses in. How to proceed?

choices.text: Follow Chanida's lead: Bribe a low-level Tonal Clerk for any 'declassified' reports on lost ships.
choices.description: Malee uses scavenger instincts to harness harmonic feedback near the crowded stalls

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee overreaches. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: Follow Malee's cynicism: Look for sky pirates in the darker stalls; they'd know real hidden frequencies, not fairy tales.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to decipher the monk's recording using Listener training

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The gamble fails. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Follow Arthit's caution: Use the party's own resonator to quietly scan for the anomalous frequency amidst the market hum.
choices.description: Convince the villager to use community ties and follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The resonance turns hostile. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: You find a sky pirate in a shadowy alcove behind a stall selling 'salvaged' resonator parts. Her eyes are sharp, scanning for profit and patrols in equal measure.
The *Seventh Dawn*? You got the coin for that kind of story? Or just death wishes?
We have coin! And we're not afraid of some old wreck!
Speak for yourself. I'm terrified of dying poor. So, pirate. What's the real story? Not the cursed nonsense for the rubes.
We seek data. Navigational anomalies. Any recorded frequencies from its last known position.
Its song was lost, but perhaps not silenced. We wish to listen.
Listeners, huh? Fine. I have something to tell you. But don't let anyone know you got it from me. The Tonal Orders would flay my hull for this.

The ship didn't just sink. It *phased*. Its resonator locked onto a forbidden frequency—a natural harmonic the Listeners natter about. The Lattice... swallowed it. But sometimes, when the market hum dips just right... you can hear its echo, crying from below.

lines_after.dialogue: A phased state? Theoretical, but... the energy signature would be immense, trapped in a resonant loop. It could be a goldmine of untainted crystal... or a cascade failure waiting to happen.
So it's the score of a lifetime. Fantastic. Could you tell me how to get to the nearest bar instead?
No! This is it! The pirate has the frequency! We can find it!
A ship, trapped in the world's song... To find it is to touch a mystery of the Silencing itself. But the pirate's price will be high, and her truth... partial.

line.dialogue: The sky pirate names her price for the forbidden frequency coordinates. The deal is on the table, but the risks are now clear.

choices.text: Pay the pirate's exorbitant fee in full. Secure the coordinates immediately, no questions asked.
