choices.description: Flash the coin purse openly, letting the weight speak louder than words.

line.dialogue: See that heft? Enough to buy your silence AND your cooperation, so start talking frequencies.
Great, now every cutthroat in port knows we're carrying. I hope you enjoy being robbed.

choices.text: Offer a smaller down payment, with the rest payable upon verification of the coordinates. A test of good faith.
choices.description: Mention a specific frequency number to prove you already know more than you should.

line.dialogue: 7700 megahertz, repeating pattern, yes? Now tell us what you've recorded alongside it.
Nobody knows that number unless they've been out there. You're either lying or you're trouble. Both cost extra.

choices.text: Refuse to pay. Try to deduce the approximate frequency from her clues and your own equipment, risking a faulty reading.
choices.description: Threaten to take the navigational data by force, hand resting on your weapon.

line.dialogue: My friend here asks nicely. I don't. The data — now — or we see how well you transmit with broken fingers.
Brilliant strategy.

lines_before.dialogue: The market's cacophony seems to sharpen, individual threads of sound pulling at the party's nerves.
I have something to tell you. I've been hearing it too—a faint, repeating harmonic beneath all this noise. It's coming from the old salvage docks.
The salvage docks? That's pirate territory. We shouldn't go poking around there without a plan.
Oh, great. So we're following a ghost song into a den of thieves. She's adorable! This plan, I mean. Utterly precious.
The Echo of the Lost Ship... its frequency is bleeding into the market's hum. It's a wound in the Lattice, and we're drawn to it.
You lot still askin' about that old wreck? Bad business. I was cheated out of good crystal by pirates who scavenged it. Don't let anyone know I told you!

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the air, a dissonant chord in the market's symphony.
Well? We're not getting any less haunted standing here.
Let's just hope the price of curiosity isn't our ship.

line.dialogue: We need to investigate the salvage docks to trace the Echo's source. How should we proceed?

choices.text: Bribe a Dockworker: Use funds to get a guide and safe passage. Fast, but costly and obvious.
choices.consequence: Gain immediate access, but attract unwanted attention from the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Jam the frequency with your own signal counter, buying silence before you move

line.dialogue: That bought us maybe twenty minutes," I mutter, watching the waveform flatten. "Move now, talk later—head down and stay close.
It's not just bleeding, it's *answering*," I snap, ripping my earpiece out as the feedback loops into something that almost sounds like my mother's voice calling me home.

choices.text: Blend with Traders: Use the market crowd as cover, slipping in slowly. Stealthy, but time-consuming.
choices.consequence: Gather more rumors and avoid initial notice, but risk the Echo's signal fading or changing.
choices.description: Demand Pichit replay the raw frequency capture so everyone hears what they're walking into

line.dialogue: Listen—right there, under the carrier wave," I say, pointing at the spectrogram. "That's not random noise. That's a distress beacon formatted in pre-Collapse naval code. Someone alive is trapped in that wreck.
I shouldn't have played it at full volume," I whisper, my hands still shaking. "Now it's in my teeth, in the bone. I can feel it humming even after I killed the playback.

choices.text: Confront a Pirate Directly: Challenge a sky pirate for information. Dangerous, but potentially decisive.
choices.consequence: Potential for a major clue or a violent confrontation that could close off other avenues.
choices.description: Strike a deal with the dock pirates through Malee's old contact, trading medical supplies for safe passage

line.dialogue: Klaew owes me from the Songkhla job," I
the villager is thwarted. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: At the derelict salvage docks, the market's noise funnels into a single, oppressive drone. The ghostly resonance is now a physical pressure.
Well, look what the static dragged in. You're the ones pokin' at the Screamin' Wreck. Bad idea. That frequency'll crack your mind open.
The resonance isn't screaming. It's trapped... a final, looping thought from the Silencing. It wants to be heard.
Pichit, the structural harmonics are all wrong here. This movie is great... for a disaster. One wrong note could cause a feedback cascade!
He's the only son in the family. The only 'ship' left singing this particular death song. We're going to soothe it.
I can feel it pulling! We have to do something now!
The spectral form of the Lost Ship shimmers into view above the docks, its crystal hull vibrating with a painful, silent tone. The pirate leader hefts a destabilizer resonator.
Enough! I'm shatterin' that echo for good. The Lattice here is mine to plunder!

lines_after.dialogue: Silence falls, deeper than the market's hum ever was. The fate of the Echo, and perhaps a fragment of the lost past, is sealed.
The song... is complete. Or silenced forever. The Lattice feels... different.
Readings are stabilizing. The immediate danger is passed.

line.dialogue: The pirate aims to destroy the Echo. The ghost ship's resonance is volatile. What is our final move?

choices.text: Overpower the Pirate: Focus on disabling the destabilizer. Direct, but ignores the Echo.
choices.consequence: Prevent immediate destruction, but the Echo remains a dangerous, unstable anomaly in the market.
choices.description: Channel the trapped resonance through Pichit's tuning fork to locate its source, 15 words

line.dialogue: The fork is vibrating in a pattern — it's a distress signal embedded in the static itself.
The resonance rejected the fork. Whatever's trapped in there, it doesn't want to be found yet.

choices.text: Harmonize with Chanida: Use her Singer ability to gently unwind the Echo's loop. Risky for her, but merciful.
choices.consequence: Chanida absorbs the traumatic resonance, gaining insight into the Silencing but carrying a psychic burden.
choices.description: Demand the bandit explain what "the static dragged in" means and who sent him, 15 words

line.dialogue: Alright, alright — we're not bandits. We're custodians. The Chorus sent us to intercept anyone who survived the fracture.
You're asking the wrong questions, stranger. Ask the right ones and maybe you walk out of here humming.

choices.text: Redirect the Resonance: Use the pirate's own device to shunt the Echo's energy safely into the Lattice. Technically perilous.
choices.consequence: The Echo is released, causing a permanent, benign change in the local Lattice frequency and altering travel charts.
choices.description: Ask Malee about the ship and whether it can still carry all of you out, 15 words

line.dialogue: The *Wandering Pitch
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

acts.title: A Whisper on the Crystal Plain

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands on a weathered observation platform, a rusting metal disc bolted to a stable crystal spire. Below and around them, the Lattice stretches to infinity—a jagged, shimmering plain of crystalline facets that hum and shift with a deep, resonant vibration.
I've checked the resonator frequencies. We're stable for now, but the harmonic patterns are... volatile. Which one would you like to scan first, Pichit?
The mother of all frequencies was heart-broken during the Silencing. We should listen for her remnant echoes. They might guide us.
Guiding sounds? Let's just go! The Tonal Orders probably have scouts nearby. We need to move!
Probably true. And probably also sky pirates. This platform is a known scavenger spot. Anyone with half a brain avoids it.
You shouldn't be here! The Groundless say the Lattice is waking up. It's not safe!

A sudden, sharp crystalline crack echoes from the east. A Resonance Ship, jury-rigged and patched with stolen plating, skims low over the Lattice, its dissonant resonator tones parting the crystals violently.
Hey there, ground-walkers! You look like you know a few hidden frequencies. Which do you prefer: handing over your charts, or getting swallowed by the Lattice?

lines_after.dialogue: We have no charts. We are Listeners.
Listeners? Even better! Your ears are worth more than Tonal Order scraps. May I kiss you goodbye before we take them?
You'll get a fist, not a kiss!
The pirate ship's resonator whines, adjusting its frequency. The Lattice nearby begins to shimmer with aggressive light.

line.dialogue: The sky pirates are priming their resonator for an attack. How do we respond?

choices.label: Easy: Offer a parley. Use our knowledge of natural frequencies to negotiate a temporary safe passage.
choices.consequence: The pirates might be intrigued by unknown harmonics, buying time.
choices.description: Calibrate the resonator to match the Crystal Plain's ambient harmonic before advancing, 15 words

line.dialogue: Frequencies aligned — the plain is singing with us now, not against us. We move clean.
The interference spike just shattered my calibration array. We're deaf out here now.

choices.label: Medium: Prepare for a fight. Chanida and Arthit ready weapons, while Malee scans for a destabilizing frequency to disrupt their ship.
choices.consequence: A direct confrontation risks damage but could disable their resonator.
choices.description: Scout the plateau ridge on foot, watching for sky pirate lookouts before committing the group, 15 words

line.dialogue: Two lookouts, eastern shelf — both facing the wrong way. We slip through the western gully.
Reflected light off my scope — they saw me. Three gliders already launching from the ridge.

choices.label: Easy: Flee. Use the platform's emergency descent chute to scramble onto the Lattice surface itself, hoping the pirates won't follow.
choices.consequence: Escaping into the raw Lattice is dangerous but might avoid immediate conflict.
choices.description: Channel a raw guiding tone directly into the crystal floor and dare the Plain to answer, 15 words

line.dialogue: The plain ANSWERED — listen, that harmonic is a road! It's showing us the way!
Nothing. Just my own voice screaming back at me from every direction. The plain doesn't care.

lines_before.dialogue: Having escaped the immediate threat, the party now treads carefully on the Lattice surface itself. Each step sends minute vibrations through the crystal, producing faint, echoing tones. The light from the facets is blinding, shifting in unpredictable patterns.
No one wants to go further into this. It's a beautiful death trap. She's more beautiful than anyone, this crystal plain, and she'll kill you for admiring her.
The resonance readings are becoming chaotic. We need to find a stable path. Go a bit further to that larger, dull-looking facet. It might be inert.
Inert? Perhaps. Or perhaps it is listening. The Groundless Movement believes the Lattice is conscious. We are walking on its thoughts.
If it's thinking, then it's thinking about swallowing us! Look—the cracks are widening!
A deep fissure splits the crystal ahead, revealing a glowing, intricate network of luminous veins beneath the surface. A low, melodic hum emanates from it.
You found it! The Heartvein! The Groundless whisper about this! It's the source of the old world's songs!
And it's also the source of my profit! Didn't think we'd follow, did you? That descent chute was a known route. Now, about those ears...

lines_after.dialogue: You're persistent! Like a bad resonance!
Persistence pays. Now, walk a bit further toward my ship. Or we'll see how the Heartvein reacts to... percussion.
The pirate brandishes a crude sonic hammer, a device designed to violently fracture crystal. The hum from the Heartvein grows anxious, the light pulsing rapidly.
That tool will cause a cascading fracture! The entire area could destabilize!

line.dialogue: The pirate is threatening to strike the Heartvein with a sonic hammer. The Groundless villager is pleading with us. We must act.

choices.label: Easy: Surrender. Offer ourselves as captives to prevent the hammer strike, trusting we can escape later.
choices.consequence: Prevents immediate catastrophic fracture but puts the party in the pirates' custody.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use tonal knowledge and harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit misreads the situation. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.label: Medium: Distract. Chanida and Malee create a loud, dissonant noise elsewhere to draw the pirate's attention away from the Heartvein.
choices.consequence: A risky gamble that might protect the vein but could attract other dangers or fail.
choices.description: Malee attempts to confront hidden knowledge, relying on engineering

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.label: Hard: Protect. Attack the pirate directly to seize the hammer, fighting on the unstable Lattice near the sensitive Heartvein.
choices.consequence: A direct fight here could trigger the fracture anyway, a high-risk attempt to save the site.
choices.description: The pirate attempts to chart resonance pathways, relying on disruptor weapon

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The resonance turns hostile. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The Lattice groans beneath the observation platform. The sky pirates' resonator has left the crystal surface fractured, with dangerous new frequencies bleeding through the cracks.
This platform won't hold forever. Those fractures are spreading. We need to get to that pirate ship, but the path is... unstable.
Unstable? It's a death trap. But I suppose anywhere's okay when you're desperate. Even a collapsing crystal sheet.
Look! The Groundless graffiti on those pillars! They've been here too. Maybe they have a safe route marked?
The fractures sing with new tones. Broken harmonies... but even broken things have patterns. Anyone's okay at reading them, if we listen together.
Hey, dreamers! Still alive? My ship's resonator is primed! Hand over that Singer's journal and maybe we don't leave you here to shatter!
Their resonator is the only thing holding their ship above the worst fractures. If we disrupt it...
Or we could just take it! A real ship, not some Tonal Order scow! Keep it. We should keep it.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice ripples across the Lattice. The crystal responds to the party's decisive frequency amplifying their gamble.
The entire surface is resonating with our action. We've changed the local harmonic balance.
Every choice leaves an echo in the crystal. Now we must follow the path we've sung into being.

line.dialogue: The pirate ship hovers, its resonator creating a fragile bubble of stability. How do we secure our way forward?

choices.text: Sabotage their resonator (HARD). Use Malee's knowledge to overload it, collapsing the fractures beneath them but risking a chain reaction.
choices.leads_to: The pirate ship drops violently as the resonator fails, but the sudden release of energy sends harmonic shockwaves racing toward you.
choices.description: Leap across the widening gap to photograph the Groundless graffiti before the pillar crumbles, 15 words

line.dialogue: The symbols shift when the light hits them—these aren't just tags, they're chord-sequences mapping the fractures themselves!
The pillar dust crumbled through my fingers and the image washed out—whatever language that was, it's gone now.

choices.text: Steal the ship (MEDIUM). Chanida's plan: rush the gangplank, overwhelm the distracted crew, and claim the vessel.
choices.leads_to: The pirates are caught off guard. The ship is yours, but their wounded captain screams a dissonant curse into the Lattice as you take off.
choices.description: Press your palm against the fractured platform and hum counter-frequencies to match Pichit's broken harmonies, 15 words

line.dialogue: Yes! You found the dissonance root—the fractures are slowing, the platform is listening to us, it wants to be repaired!
Your frequency clashed wrong and the platform shrieked—now the cracks are spreading faster, everyone get back!

choices.text: Negotiate passage (EASY). Use the Singer's journal as a bargaining chip, offering knowledge for safe transport off the crumbling surface.
choices.leads_to: The pirate captain, eyes gleaming with greed, accepts. You board, but the journal is now in ruthless hands.
choices.description: Anchor a rope to the nearest graffiti-pillar and rappel down into the fracture's glowing depths, 15 words

line.dialogue: The rope holds—there's a whole network of cables and walkways down here
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The Lattice is in upheaval. Your actions have triggered a local Resonance Cascade. The crystal plain heaves, massive shards rising and falling like a stormy sea.
Please! Our observation outpost is shearing off! You have a ship now—don't change the subject! Can you promise me you'll get my people out?
Promises? In this? My ship's crystal is cracking! The frequencies are all wrong! He's a nice person who dies first in a cascade!
The cascade is feeding on itself. If we don't find a stabilizing counter-frequency soon, this whole sector will crystallize into a deadly monochord.
The Groundless... they're here. On the largest rising shard. They're not running. They're... conducting the resonance.
They're trying to ride the cascade! To break the Lattice open! They'll bring the whole sky down!
No... they're listening to the change. The world is speaking in fractures. But we must choose what it says next. Survival or revelation?
At the epicenter, the leader of the Groundless turns. Their hands move through the screaming air, shaping the chaos. They offer not a threat, but a terrible choice.

lines_after.dialogue: The Lattice holds its breath. The cascade slows, settles into a new, permanent pattern—a monument to the choice made in the heart of the storm.
The world has changed. We have changed it. Every note we sing from this day forward will resonate in this new shape.
Well. We survived. Somehow that feels like the least important part of what just happened.

line.dialogue: The Groundless leader's voice cuts through the harmonic storm: 'Join the fracture! Let the old world of control shatter! Or impose your order, and save the skycities by silencing the truth.' The cascade reaches its climax.

choices.text: Amplify the Fracture (HARD). Add your resonance to the Groundless. Break the Tonal Orders' control forever, but risk unknown cataclysm.
choices.leads_to: The Lattice shatters in a glorious, terrifying chord. New frequencies flood the world. The sky cities will fall or adapt. Control is broken.
choices.description: Grapple to the shearing outpost and anchor it to the bandit's ship with cable

line.dialogue: Cable locked! The bandit's crystal buys us time — pull them in, NOW!
The cable snapped — I'm watching the outpost drift into the cascade with them still inside.

choices.text: Impose a New Order (MEDIUM). Use the Singer's gift to force the cascade into a stable, navigable pattern. Save the cities, but become the new monopoly.
choices.leads_to: The chaos bends to your will, crystallizing into safe passages. You have saved thousands, but you now hold the power you sought to challenge.
choices.description: Sprint across the rising shards toward the Groundless to confront them directly

line.dialogue: I see their silhouettes through the dust — whatever they're doing, I'm ending it myself.
The shard bucked under my feet and I'm sliding toward the edge — the Groundless haven't even noticed me.

choices.text: Find the Middle Frequency (EASY). Seek not control nor chaos, but a precarious balance. A temporary fix that leaves the deeper conflict unresolved.
choices.leads_to: The cascade subsides, leaving a fragile calm. The cities are safe for now, but the Lattice is scarred and unstable. The choice is merely postponed.
choices.description: Force the bandit's cracking crystal into the cascade to collapse the feedback loop

line.dialogue: The crystal screamed, then the cascade *inhaled* — it's stabilizing, I can feel the pulse settling!
Wrong frequency — the crystal shattered and now the cascade is chewing through everything faster.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns before you—a jagged maw in the floating island's underside. Inside, the air is cool and thick with the scent of wet stone and ancient dust.
Great. Another damp hole in the ground. My boots are still soggy from the last 'archaeological marvel'.
But listen! The echoes... they're different here. Like the cave itself is humming. There's a high chance we'll find something the Orders missed!
Proceed with caution. Uncharted resonance patterns could destabilize the local Lattice. Do you need to use your resonator here, Pichit? Is it necessary to use one?
Not yet. The natural song... it feels guided. Purposeful. Like a path laid down long before the Silencing.
Deep within the first cavern, a soft bioluminescent fungus clings to the walls, painting the chamber in ethereal blues and greens. Strange, geometric carvings catch the light.
Look at these carvings! (This cute and this inviting)... how could you pass it up? They're practically begging us to follow them deeper!
Or they're a warning. 'Abandon all hope, ye who enter here,' and all that. But the payday's probably back there, so let's go.

lines_after.dialogue: The tunnel opens into a vast, cylindrical chamber. A shaft of light from a crack high above illuminates a central dais. Upon it rests a perfectly smooth, obsidian disc.
Fascinating. No visible crystal lattice integration. The material is non-resonant. A deliberate silence in a place of song.
Not silence. A different kind of memory. One that doesn't need sound.

line.dialogue: The obsidian disc is featureless, yet it seems to be the chamber's focus. How do you investigate?

choices.text: Let Chanida tap it with a tool to test its resonance.
choices.description: Follow the resonance deeper, pressing your palm against the vibrating tunnel wall to track its pulse, 15 words

line.dialogue: Yes—the song grows clearer under your touch. It remembers hands that walked here long before us.
The vibration spiked. Your handprint is now seared into the stone, and the wall has stopped breathing.

choices.text: Have Arthit perform a detailed scan with his instruments first.
choices.description: Sing a single sustained note into the darkness and let the cave answer back with its truth, 15 words

line.dialogue: It answered! Three tones returned where one went in—the hollow is singing *with* you, not against you!
Nice going, opera ghost. Now every crack in the ceiling is groaning and I hear something *crawling* toward us.

choices.text: Place your hand directly on the disc, trusting your instinct.
choices.description: Draw your blade and strike the floor sharply to test whether the stone beneath is hollow or whole, 15 words

line.dialogue: Solid ring—good. At least we're not standing over a pit. One less nightmare to worry about down here.
The ring was wrong. Too deep, too long. You've announced us to whatever sleeps below the floor—and it is waking.

lines_before.dialogue: Your choice triggers a reaction. The obsidian disc remains inert, but the chamber's acoustics shift. The hum deepens, and from side passages, you're not alone.
Well, well. Look what the cave coughed up. You lot are a long way from your cozy city spires.
Sky pirates! I knew this place was too good to be unguarded.
Peace. They are... associates. Of a sort. We don't stay in touch, but our paths converge here.
A Listener consorting with bandits? Should've guessed. The 'truth' you're so torn about involves lining your pockets?
You misunderstand. The Groundless Movement seeks truths the Tonal Orders bury. Truths about what lies below the Lattice. But I... I don't know where to begin explaining the cost.
He's got cold feet. We don't. That disc isn't a toy. It's a key. And you just lit the lock. Now the real work starts.
A key to what? And what 'work'? You cannot simply activate ancient systems. The safety protocols—

lines_after.dialogue: Safety? The Orders' safety is keeping us all ignorant! This place hums with a frequency they've outlawed. A 'Groundward' frequency.

He speaks truly. The song here... it speaks of foundation. Of a world before we floated. The Movement believes we can return. But the process... it is perilous. Do not leave the resonator channel open if you value stability.
Return? You mean descend? Through the Lattice?
The pirate and the monk share a look. Around you, the cave's hum has taken on a rhythmic, almost pulsing quality. The light from above seems to dim.

line.dialogue: The Groundless reveal their goal: using The Hollow's unique frequency to attempt a controlled descent. The pirate is eager to proceed; the monk is hesitant. What is your stance?

choices.text: Side with the Monk. This is too reckless; we need to study this more.
choices.description: Draw your blade and challenge the bandit leader directly, demanding safe passage, 15 words

line.dialogue: [The bandit leader smirks, impressed by your nerve. "Alright, you've got spine. Walk through—but your coin stays with us."]
[The bandit's grin vanishes. "Wrong move, friend." Steel rings out along the cave wall as his crew levels crossbows at your chest.]

choices.text: Remain neutral. Demand more answers before committing to either side.
choices.description: Step behind the monk and whisper that you'll expose his bandit dealings to the Order, 15 words

line.dialogue: [The monk's jaw tightens. He turns to the bandits. "Let them pass. I'll handle this myself." His voice carries cold authority.]
[The monk laughs softly. "The Order already knows, child. Who do you taught me to listen in the first place?"]

choices.text: Side with the Pirate. The truth is worth the risk; let's see where this frequency leads.
choices.description: Grab Chanida's arm and retreat deeper into the cave before the bandits can encircle you, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Chanida moves like water through the dark, pulling you into a narrow fissure. The bandits' curses fade behind wet stone.
The risk doesn't pay off. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_before.dialogue: The party follows the faint, discordant hum deeper into the ruins. The air grows colder, and the walls shimmer with a faint, unnatural light.
The sound... it's not just an echo. It's pulling us. There’s a high chance we're walking right into its source.

Of course we are. Because subtlety is for people who enjoy living. I overheard that Listener back at the entrance muttering about a 'sealed frequency.' It's not necessary that we understand it to know it's bad.
The structural integrity here is... questionable. We should proceed with extreme caution. The ground won't move an inch if it's not there.
These carvings... they're not just maps. They're a warning. A record of the last time someone tried to command the song, not listen to it.
Ahead, a cavern opens up. In its center, a massive, fractured crystal column pulses with a sickly light. Two figures are locked in a tense standoff.
You're hoarding secrets, monk! That frequency you're guarding... it could punch a hole straight through the Lattice to the old world! My ship wouldn't budge an inch until I got it!
You misunderstand! It is not a key, it is a lock! A containment frequency from before The Silencing! I overheard the elders say that... that its release was what caused the catastrophe!

lines_after.dialogue: The bandit's eyes gleam with avarice. The monk's with desperation. The crystal's hum rises to a painful whine.
Great. A doomsday device and a greedy idiot. My favorite combination.
We have to intervene. This isn't just about treasure or knowledge anymore.

line.dialogue: The bandit raises a resonator, aimed at the crystal. The monk moves to block him. What do you do?

choices.line: Appeal to the Bandit's Greed. Offer a trade: information on other ruins for him to leave this one be.
choices.description: Pichit attempts to use the leg as a lattice probe, relying on monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
A costly mistake by Pichit. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Physically Interpose. Get between them, risking the unstable crystal's reaction to your presence.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with unauthorized tones to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
A costly mistake by Chanida. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.line: Use the Environment. Try to mimic the 'containment frequency' the monk mentioned using your own resonators, to calm the crystal.
choices.description: Ask the pirate to map the frequency corridors, drawing on pirate ship

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. A secret frequency from the underworld shifts the balance.
the pirate hits a wall. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

lines_before.dialogue: The cavern shudders. Cracks race up the ancient crystal. A deep, subsonic groan emanates from the earth itself.
It's destabilizing! The lock is breaking! I have something to tell you... the Groundless... they weren't wrong. The old world fell because we tried to own the song. We've seen it before!
Forget the philosophy! This whole island's gonna come apart!
He's correct! The resonance feedback is tearing the Hollow's foundation apart from the inside. We have minutes, at best.
We can't just run! That frequency is leaking out! It'll shred the Lattice for miles!
I've never understood why saving the world always involves standing directly under the falling part of it.
The monk is right. We have to seal it. Not control it. We have to prepare the counter-frequency before the final fracture.
The crystal pulses erratically. Shards break off and hover in the air. The very sound of the world seems to be unraveling around you.

lines_after.dialogue: The air crackles with spent energy. The great crystal is dark, its fracture lines sealed with a web of soft, harmonized light. The terrible groan has subsided into a deep, steady hum.
You... you harmonized with it. You didn't force it. You listened. The Listeners have forgotten this. I must bring this truth to my order.
Yeah, well, my ship's still stuck. But... I've seen enough. Some secrets are better left buried. I'm out.
The truth was here before us all along. Not in control, but in resonance.

line.dialogue: The immediate crisis is over, but the unstable Hollow is collapsing. The path out is splitting. What is your final priority?

choices.line: Secure the Monk's Knowledge. Ensure he and his revelations about the true cause of The Silencing escape safely to the surface.
choices.description: Malee uses crystal prosthetic to harness harmonic feedback near the unusual acoustics

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Salvage the Crystal Core. A stabilized shard could revolutionize resonator tech, but extracting it risks re-destabilizing everything.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to question the Orders' silence, leveraging singer voice

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Defeat. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.line: Record the Final Frequency. Use the last moments of stability to perfectly chart the sealing harmony, creating a permanent record for the Singers.
choices.description: The monk channels lattice study toward the unusual acoustics, hoping to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: the monk's expertise pays off. Crystal bowls shatter in harmonic sympathy.
The resonance turns hostile. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire is a needle of brass and crystal, driven deep from the floating island's base into the shimmering Lattice below. A profound, resonant hum fills the air, a physical pressure that smooths the edges of fear and anger.
This tone... it's meant to steady the island, but it steadies the soul too. Makes everything feel inevitable.
Or it's just a fancy paperweight for a world that's already shattered. Don't get poetic, Pichit.
Look at that view! The Lattice stretches forever. It's like... it's like that scene in 'Echoes of the Fallen Citadel'! You have to see it!
Chanida, focus. We're here to meet the Listener Monk. This isn't a movie.
But it *is* great! The hero discovers the truth about the Silencing in a place just like this! He's the only son in the family, carrying all that weight...
A figure in simple grey robes approaches, hands folded. His eyes are sharp, missing nothing.
Welcome to the Anchor. I am Brother Kavi. You hear the world's heartbeat here. But what do you wish to hear from me?

lines_after.dialogue: We seek knowledge, Brother. About the natural songs of the Lattice, the ones your Order studies. And... about those who say we shouldn't be up here at all.
The Groundless Movement. Their whispers reach even this spire. They believe the floating cities are a mistake, that true life is below. A dangerous fiction.
Or a dangerous truth. Your tone sounds steady, monk, but your voice wavers.
Before the monk can reply, a smooth, familiar voice cuts through the hum.
Brother Kavi! And my favorite clients! What a harmonic coincidence.

line.dialogue: The Trade Negotiator, Somsak, arrives with his usual polished smile. He glances between the monk and the party.

choices.line: Greet him warmly and ask about his business here.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with captain experience to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
The gamble fails. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.line: Ignore him and press the monk about the Groundless.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to decode the cryptic message using crystal hearing

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Chanida overreaches. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.line: Ask Somsak directly if he's heard the Groundless whispers.
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using trade ledger to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the merchant. Hidden leverage shifts the balance.
the merchant hits a wall. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The steady tone of the Spire makes the ensuing silence between the monk and the merchant feel deafening. Somsak's smile doesn't falter.
My business is harmony, dear friends. Ensuring the flow of goods... and information. That cloak, Chanida—Prachuap Khiri Khan silk? It's the latest fashion in the upper bazaars.
Really? What province is Hua Hin in again? I always get the southern districts mixed up.
Chanida. Not the time.
You deal in information, Somsak. What do you know of the Listeners' studies? The old songs, before the Tonal Orders charted them?
Dangerous merchandise, that. Uncharted resonance can shred a ship's crystal faster than you can say 'profit margin.' Brother Kavi understands.
We record. We do not distribute. The natural song is not a commodity.
But you've seen things. Ancient notations. How do you write the resonance for 'free fall'? Or 'shatter'?

lines_after.dialogue: Brother Kavi pales slightly. The merchant's eyes gleam with interest.
Such scripts... were lost. Purposely. After the Silencing. To suggest we rediscover them is to invite that calamity to be called forth once more.

Yet the Groundless call for it, don't they? A great un-anchoring. They whisper that the Spires like this one are what's keeping us from the true world below. Rebellious thoughts, but... marketable ones to certain buyers.
You're trading in sedition?
Somsak shrugs, his gaze drifting to a sealed scroll case at Brother Kavi's belt. The monk's hand moves to cover it instinctively.

line.dialogue: The monk is hiding something, and the merchant knows it. The Spire's hum vibrates through your bones.

choices.line: Confront Brother Kavi about the scroll case openly.
choices.description: Slide a pouch of coins across the table, asking about the forgotten script's origin, 15 words

line.dialogue: Ah, now we speak the same language. The script surfaced in a temple archive near Prachuap—three months ago, then vanished.
You flash coin before building trust? I am not some street vendor. Come back when you learn manners.

choices.line: Ask Somsak what he would pay for the monk's 'dangerous merchandise'.
choices.description: Lean forward and mention the merchant's name dropped in a intercepted letter, 15 words

line.dialogue: *eyes narrowing* "Someone has been careless. Yes, my name appeared—I handled a translation. The buyer was someone close to the palace.
I have never heard of this letter, and I resent the implication. My affairs are conducted with discretion, not gossip.

choices.line: Propose a bargain: you'll get the scroll for Somsak, in exchange for all his information on the Groundless.
choices.description: Watch Chanida closely, signal her to keep asking naive questions as distraction, 15 words

line.dialogue: Oh, Somsak, is it true what they say about the old script being cursed? My grandmother mentioned something once…" Somsak relaxes, charmed by her innocence, and begins talking freely
Defeat. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire's hum is a physical pressure as you ascend its final, open-air platform. The vast, crystalline Lattice stretches below like a frozen, singing sea.
Ah, you've arrived? I was beginning to think you'd gotten lost in the lower harmonics. I have the final shipment manifests here. All accounted for.
Who is this guy? Another Tonal Order stooge with a friendly face and empty ledgers?
Don't tell him. Don't tell her. Don't tell anyone. That's the vibe I'm getting. What are you really shipping?
Peace, please. Just supplies for the Listeners' research. Tools, rations, resonance dampeners... the latest fashion in acoustic safety gear.
Our sources say otherwise. The Groundless are using smuggled resonance disruptors. They're not just protesting; they're planning to sever an anchor.
This spire... its song is a lie. A forced, artificial note to suppress the Lattice's true voice. And the Order uses it to suppress dissent.
A lie to maintain control. The Silencing wasn't an accident, was it? It was a suppression of a truth someone didn't want heard.

lines_after.dialogue: You don't understand the commerce of silence! The stability I sell keeps cities floating!
Below, a dissonant shriek echoes up from the Lattice. A section of crystal darkens. The Anchor Spire's steady tone wavers for the first time in centuries.
Too late for ledgers. They've started.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator panics, clutching a data-crystal. The Monk moves to the edge, listening to the rising chaos below.

choices.label: [EASY: Seize the evidence] Confiscate the merchant's crystal. It holds the proof of the conspiracy.
choices.description: Press the merchant about who sent him and how he knew you were coming. 13 words

line.dialogue: He flinches when I mention the Tonal Order — so there's a thread worth pulling.
Smooth as oil, this one. Gives me nothing but that practiced merchant smile.

choices.label: [MEDIUM: Follow the sound] Join the Monk. The Lattice's true song might guide you to the disruptor's source.
choices.description: Signal Chanida to stay quiet while you inspect the supplies yourself first. 14 words

line.dialogue: Good. I count three crates that weren't on any manifest I approved. We take those.
Too late — he's already watching my hands. Next time don't wait for me to blink first.

choices.label: [HARD: Silence the Anchor] Use the spire's own harmonics. Overload the resonator to broadcast a warning, or to drown out the attack.
choices.description: Pay for the supplies without questions and leave before anyone else shows up. 13 words

line.dialogue: Wise. The Listeners appreciate discretion, and so do I. The road stays clear for you.
Merchant

lines_before.dialogue: The Spire shudders. The calming hum fractures into painful harmonics. Below, a floating slum-island grinds against its anchor chains, threatening to break free.
You fools! You'll destroy the market! The Groundless want to crash us all back to the surface!
No. They want to live. Truly live. Not in gilded cages floating on a silenced world. There's no one else who will speak for them.
Great. So we choose between a slow death by monopoly or a quick one by shattering crystal.
The disruptor is on that island. If we deactivate it, the Spire stabilizes, but the Groundless are crushed. If we don't... the cascade could unmoor this entire sector.
We live near each other. All of us, on these stupid, drifting rocks. Their fight is our fight.
The truth isn't in the Monk's scrolls or the Merchant's ledgers. It's in the choice we make right now. What song do we want the world to hear?
A final, deafening crack echoes as a major anchor chain snaps. The island begins to list, its people screaming into the harmonic storm.

lines_after.dialogue: In the new silence, a different sound emerges—not the Spire's forced tone, but the deep, complex, and unchained song of the Lattice itself.
I'm happy to hear this. It is the first true note in an age.
It's not an ending. It's a beginning. And we have to learn how to listen all over again.

line.dialogue: The crisis peaks. The unstable island, the shattered anchor, the fate of the movement—all hinge on your final resonance.

choices.label: [EASY: Reinforce the Spire] Use your ship's resonator to bolster the remaining anchors. Save the city, but the Groundless are arrested. Stability at a cost.
consequences: The Tonal Order's control tightens.
The subplot_groundless is suppressed.
The party gains Order favor but public distrust.
choices.description: Swim to the island alone and deactivate the disruptor before the market patrol catches you.

line.dialogue: The core is out. I can feel the current changing — the Groundless can breathe now.
The patrol spotted me halfway across. I'm pinned behind the breakwater with no cover.

choices.label: [MEDIUM: Redirect the Frequency] Tune the disruptor. Sever the island cleanly, setting it adrift as an independent, free-floating commune.
consequences: A new, rebellious city-state is born.
subplot_groundless evolves into a major faction.
The party becomes heroes to outlaws, enemies to the Order.
choices.description: Forge a temporary alliance with the merchant — his boats, your people, split the risk.

line.dialogue: He actually shook on it. Guess gilded cages make for strange bedfellows — we're moving out.
He sold our position to the patrol the second we turned our backs. Should've known better.

choices.label: [HARD: Shatter the Paradigm] Don't save the island or the spire. Amplify the fracture. Let the Lattice's raw song flood the sky, breaking the Tonal Order's acoustic monopoly forever.
consequences: The world enters a period of chaotic, dangerous resonance.
All navigation charts are obsolete.
The party are either revolutionaries or terrorists, hunted by all powers.
choices.description: Let the monk negotiate with the Groundless directly — appeal to their humanity before anyone acts.

line.dialogue: They laid down their arms. They only wanted to be seen — and now, finally, they are.
My words meant nothing. They've heard promises before — from people who looked like me.

lines_before.dialogue: The party rests in Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, where the only sounds are the rustle of crops and the gentle hum of the Lattice far below. The peace feels earned.

Listen to the rhythm of the water channels... It’s not scary at all! The Lattice’s resonance here is almost gentle. What style of sound do you prefer, this pastoral hum or the deep thrum of the open sky?
I prefer the style where we’re not starving. These terraces are beautiful, but I don’t understand anything about how they float. It’s all Tonal Order nonsense.
We should be cautious. This quiet is perfect for an ambush. The Order’s charts don’t fully map these edge-lands.
Ambush? From what, aggressive turnips? Look, a trade caravan is setting up by the central cistern! Let’s go see what they’ve got!
A sleek, well-maintained Resonance skiff has landed. A smooth-faced negotiator, the Trade Negotiator, is arranging crates with practiced efficiency.
Greetings, travelers! The prices are reasonable. Fresh supplies, purified water crystals... and perhaps other, more specialized goods for those with the right... frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: Specialized goods? You mean charts?

Charts? Oh, no, the Tonal Orders guard those jealously. I deal in... supplements. Resonator lubricants. Nothing illicit. But between us, the official maps for this sector are... incomplete. There are gaps.
Gaps you just happen to know about, I’m sure. For a price.

line.dialogue: The merchant hints at hidden knowledge of the local Lattice frequencies. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Politely inquire about his 'supplements.' (Gather information)
choices.description: Follow Pichit's lead — cup your ear to the canal stones and track the water's rhythm toward the source.

line.dialogue: Pichit whispers, "There — the flow reverses every thirty breaths. Someone is operating a sluice gate upstream.
Pichit sighs, "You're hearing your own heartbeat. Put your palm flat on the stone, not your ear — the vibration tells you everything.

choices.text: Press him directly about the map gaps. (Confront)
choices.description: Side with Malee — push toward the trade caravan at the terrace's edge before someone else claims the goods.

line.dialogue: Malee grins, "Now you're thinking. That canvas is covering dried fish — I can smell it from here. We negotiate first, philosophize later.
Malee mutters, "Too slow. That merchant just packed up and moved toward the eastern road. Hope your water rhythm was worth a skipped meal.

choices.text: Ignore him and search the gardens yourselves. (Investigate)
choices.description: Heed Arthit's warning — take position behind the terrace wall and observe the caravan before approaching.

line.dialogue: Arthit nods slowly, "Good. Three guards, one driver, and the canvas is too taut for grain — something heavy underneath. This isn't a routine run.
Arthit pulls you back roughly, "I said observe, not stare. The short guard just clocked you. Now we're the ambush they're waiting for.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the merchant's veiled clues or your own search, you discover a hidden irrigation control hut, its door slightly ajar. Inside, the air is still and thick.
Hold. Listen. Do you hear that? Just... breathing. The slow, deep resonance of old crystal machinery. The professors who built these systems were really good.
It’s reasonably priced! Look, an old resonator console! And... is that a data-sliver? It’s labeled 'Rim Sector - Anomalous Harmonics.'
Anomalous Harmonics. Sounds like a fancy way of saying 'unmapped and dangerous.' She lost her virginity to this kind of optimism, you know. Figuratively. Probably.
This could be a fragment of an Open Frequency Map. Knowledge the Orders suppress. But extracting it might trigger alarms or... worse.
As Pichit reaches for the sliver, the door slams shut. A figure emerges from the shadows behind a grain silo—the sky pirate, a sky pirate with a scarred resonator gauntlet.
Well, well. Diggin' in the garden, are ya? That little shiny's ours. Found it first. The Lattice 'round here sings a pretty song for those who listen... a song of easy pickin's.

lines_after.dialogue: Yours? You just stood there breathing heavily! We did the work!
Work's for suckers. The song's the thing. Now, hand it over, or we'll see how your bones resonate.
Two more pirates drop from the terraces above, cutting off your retreat. The merchant watches from a safe distance, his friendly smile gone, replaced by cold calculation.

line.dialogue: Cornered by pirates with the data-sliver in hand, you must act.

choices.text: Try to negotiate. Offer a trade or split the findings. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Touch the resonator console and hum a single sustained note into its surface.

line.dialogue: * "There — the breathing shifted. It's matching you. Whatever this thing is, it's listening, and it likes company.
* "Stop. You're stirring something that was sleeping. The breathing's getting heavier and I don't think it's friendly.

choices.text: Create a distraction using the old console's harmonics. (Technical)
choices.description: Pull pichit aside and demand to know where he learned about Open Frequency Maps.

line.dialogue: * "A dead woman's journal, three years ago, pages sealed with wax. She wrote 'the cost of knowledge is never paid by the one who seeks it.' I didn't understand until now.
* "I — I don't actually know. I just recognized the pattern. Please don't ask me to explain how, because I can't, and that terrifies me more than anything in this room.

choices.text: Fight. You're outnumbered, but the terrain is tight. (Combat)
choices.description: Ignore the breathing, grab the resonator console, and head for the exit immediately.

line.dialogue: * "Smart. We can study it somewhere the walls aren't inhaling. I know a place with wards thick enough to mute whatever's attached to this thing.
* "The breathing is coming *from* the

lines_before.dialogue: The sun begins to dip, casting long shadows across the terraced gardens. A tense quiet has settled, broken only by the rustle of crops and the distant hum of a hidden resonator.
I'm happy to hear the negotiator finally cracked. That map fragment is ours! This changes everything.
Don't get too excited. A map to 'open frequencies' sounds like a great way to get every pirate and Tonal Order enforcer in the sky to hunt us. There's no one else we can trust with this.
Malee's right. We need to verify this fragment's authenticity before we even think about using it. The merchant's 'fair price' might have been our heads.
The Lattice's song feels... anticipatory here. As if the gardens themselves are listening. Are we going to follow this thread, or not? The choice will resonate.
A sudden, discordant hum shatters the peace. From behind a waterfall-fed irrigation channel, the sky pirate and two rough-looking crewmates step out, their personal resonators glowing ominously.
Well, ain't this a ripe harvest. Heard you lot been askin' about open frequencies. Hand over the map scrap. We'll be takin' that seedling off your hands.

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation ends. The gardens are quiet again, but the air is charged with the consequences of the choice.
Great teacher, my foot. Now we've made a powerful enemy. Typical.
The path is set. The Lattice's melody has shifted. We must prepare for the final resonance.

line.dialogue: The pirate demands the frequency map fragment. How do you respond?

choices.line: Fight. Defend the map and drive them off.
choices.outcome: You win the skirmish, securing the map but alerting the Tonal Orders to violence in the gardens.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with scavenger instincts, ready to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The risk doesn't pay off. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: Bargain. Offer a copy of the map in exchange for safe passage and information.
choices.outcome: A tense trade is made. You gain a pirate's knowledge of a nearby unstable frequency, but they now have the map too.
choices.description: Chanida uses unauthorized tones to decode the cryptic message near the water channels

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida fails. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Deceive. Claim the map leads to a 'Silencing' echo—a death trap for any ship.
choices.outcome: The pirates hesitate, buying time. They leave, suspicious, and will return with reinforcements if they discover the lie.
choices.description: Have the pirate focus secret frequencies on the sky-rice to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the pirate. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the pirate misreads the situation. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Night has fallen on Mae Rim. The gardens are lit by bioluminescent fungi and the cold light of the Lattice below. In a secluded stone gazebo, the party examines the complete frequency map.
Remember... keep in mind that this doesn't chart safe paths. It charts *raw* paths. Frequencies that bypass the Tonal Orders' control entirely. It's the theory the Listeners were killed for.
So we can go anywhere! We can find out what really caused The Silencing!
I can't remember the last time something this 'free' didn't come with a world-ending catch. This map is a key to a door everyone agreed should stay locked.
The memory is in the resonance. I can't remember if it was a prayer or a scream that shattered the world... but this map sings of the moment before. We stand at the same precipice.

The Trade Negotiator emerges from the shadows of a vine-covered archway, no longer smiling. Behind him, three figures in the stark grey of the Tonal Orders step forward, hands on their tuned disruptors.

A regrettable conclusion. The Order pays far more for contraband knowledge than any pirate. I'm afraid your journey ends here. Hand over the map, and your resonance ship. Your memories will be... sanitized.
The gazebo's crystals begin to vibrate in sympathy with the disruptors. The very stones seem to weep with remembered sound.

lines_after.dialogue: The climactic resonance fades. The fate of the map, and the truth it holds, is decided. The Hanging Gardens will never be the same.
We have remembered what they tried to silence. The cost is high, but the song continues. We must carry it.
In the new silence, the natural sounds of the gardens return—a wind through the crops, a trickle of water—forever underscored by the echo of the choice made here.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Orders demand the map. This is the climax. What is your final resonance?

choices.line: Surrender the Map. Live to fight another day.
choices.outcome: You are 'cleansed' of the forbidden knowledge. The map is lost, but the party remains together, free yet neutered, under permanent Order surveillance.
choices.description: Touch the fractured resonance crystal and let the memory flood through you unfiltered.

line.dialogue: The silencing— it wasn't an accident. Someone *chose* this. I can see their hands on the frequency controls, cold and deliberate.
Too much at once— the resonance collapsed inward and all I got was static and a nosebleed. The memory doesn't give itself to impatience.

choices.line: Use the Map. Activate an open frequency here and now, risking a local 'Silencing' event.
choices.outcome: A devastating harmonic burst scours the gazebo, disabling the Order agents and damaging your ship. The map is consumed, but you escape with fragmented, dangerous truths etched into your minds.
choices.description: Follow the corrupted signal trail downward into the collapsed archive chamber alone.

line.dialogue: You found it— the original transmission log! It's degraded but the timestamp proves the Silencing happened *before* the official record says it did. Everything they told us was rearranged.
The floor gave out halfway down. You're lucky I heard you calling from three levels up— the archive chamber isn't just collapsed, it's *erasing itself* as we speak.

choices.line: Shatter the Map Crystal. Release its stored frequencies in a chaotic, untraceable burst.
choices.outcome: The data is lost to everyone, including you. The resulting harmonic chaos permanently deafens the Order agents to precise frequencies and marks you as infamous terrorists, but the monopoly on knowledge is irrevocably broken.
choices.description: Ask Malee to sing the frequency pattern she learned as a child and match it against the resonance echo.

line.dialogue: My mother taught me that melody... I never knew why. But the resonance just *answered* it— the walls are vibrating, Ar
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: A profound, almost oppressive quiet hangs over Phrao Monastery. The monastery-city is a vertical forest of listening horns and crystal spires, all angled toward the Lattice below. The air thrums with a barely perceptible hum.
I thought this was a city. Why’s everyone whispering? It’s like a library that forgot how to have fun.
Shh! You’ll disrupt their… listening thing. Look at all those horns! I wanna see what they hear.
We should proceed with caution. The acoustics here are meticulously designed. One loud noise could ruin years of their research.
It’s not necessary to shout to be heard. Sometimes, the most profound truths are found in the silences between notes.
You the new arrivals? The Head Listener is expecting you. But watch your step. The stones here… they remember every vibration.
Great. Even the floor is judgmental. I need a break from all this tension.

lines_after.dialogue: The Head Listener, an elderly woman with eyes like polished quartz, meets you in a circular chamber. A large, flawless crystal rests on a pedestal, pulsing with a soft light.
We seek understanding of the Lattice’s deeper song.

The Head Listener gestures to the crystal. "The Lattice sings of a coming dissonance. A fracture. We have heard it for weeks, growing louder. It’s not necessary that you believe us, but you must listen."

line.dialogue: The Head Listener offers to attune your minds to the warning frequency. It is a risky procedure, delving into the Lattice’s pain.

choices.label: Submit to the attunement. (Easy - Gain clarity, but take psychic strain.)
choices.description: Press your ear against the nearest stone pillar and hold your breath.

line.dialogue: I can hear it too — something humming beneath the surface, ancient and deliberate.
Great, now there's a ringing in my ears AND everyone's still staring at us.

choices.label: Request to study their records first. (Medium - Gain knowledge more slowly, but safely.)
choices.description: Signal the group to walk single-file, matching the whispered rhythm of the worshippers.

line.dialogue: Yes — yes, like that. They're parting for us. The sanctuary accepts our silence.
Your footfall cracked like thunder. The listeners have turned, and their eyes are not kind.

choices.label: Refuse. The risk is too great. (Easy - Avoid immediate danger, but remain in the dark.)
choices.description: Kneel before the central altar and mouth a question without voicing it.

line.dialogue: The air shifted. Your unspoken words were received — and something beneath us just answered.
You breathed too hard on the altar stone. The dust rose, and every whisper in this room stopped simultaneously.

lines_before.dialogue: Following your choice, you are led deeper into the monastery's acoustic heart. The air grows colder, and the hum becomes a chorus of faint, discordant whispers.
The structural harmonics in this chamber are… unstable. It’s very important that we do not introduce any foreign resonance.
Who’s this woman by the big crystal? The one who looks like she’s praying to it?
That’s Sister Kalaya. She’s been in a trance for three days, listening to the fracture-song. The Head Listener says she’s trying to find its source.
Three days? I’ll ask her if she wants a sandwich when she wakes up. Or a new hobby.
Her sacrifice is important. She is a conduit for a truth we are too deaf to hear.

lines_after.dialogue: Suddenly, Sister Kalaya gasps, her eyes flying open. The central crystal flares with a violent red light, and a shockwave of soundless force knocks you back.
Images flood your mind: A jagged wound in the Lattice. Sky-pirate vessels, marked with crude resonator arrays, drilling into the crystal. The fracture spreading like a web.
Sister Kalaya collapses, whispering one word before falling unconscious: "Pirates."
Pirates? Here? I’m gonna ask him—the Head Listener—what we do now! They’re causing this!

line.dialogue: The vision is clear. Sky pirates are actively damaging the Lattice near the monastery, causing the warning song. You must decide how to confront this threat.

choices.label: Alert the monastery guards and form a defensive plan. (Easy - Secure the monastery, but the pirates may flee.)
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to tune the prosthetic, leveraging Listener training

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Pichit. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit overreaches. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.label: Take a Resonance skiff and scout the fracture site directly. (Medium - Gather intelligence, but risk direct engagement.)
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing frequency mapping to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
The gamble fails. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.label: Attempt to use the monastery's acoustic array to disrupt the pirates' resonators from afar. (Hard - Technically complex, but could disable them without a fight.)
choices.description: The villager presses forward with community ties to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the villager's call. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the villager hits a wall. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_before.dialogue: The Listeners' forbidden archive... it's sealed behind a resonance lock. Breaking it will alert every Tonal Order ship in the sector.
Of course. The price is the same whether we're buying information or stealing it—attention from people who want us dead.
But the lattice hum... it's getting louder. I feel it in my teeth. We need to know what the Listeners found!
The old master said the lattice sings of change. But change for whom? For the floating cities, or for itself?
Please... the monks hid something in the central spire. They said the truth wasn't for ordinary folk. Too dangerous.
It's really worth seeing! What, you think they locked up shopping lists? This is the key to everything.
The spire's resonator is failing. If we trigger the archive, the whole acoustic environment could collapse. You, too, would be trapped in the silence.

lines_after.dialogue: The archive chamber opens with a crystalline chime that vibrates through the monastery's bones. Ancient scrolls float in stasis fields, glowing with forbidden frequencies.
The lattice isn't dying. It's waking up. And its dream is swallowing our world.
These charts... they show resonance patterns from before The Silencing. The lattice responded to something. A song that wasn't ours.

line.dialogue: The archive reveals three possible responses to the lattice's awakening. Which path do we follow?

choices.text: Use the old frequencies to calm the lattice temporarily—buy time for evacuation.
choices.description: Press your palm against the archive door and let the lattice hum resonate through your bones.

line.dialogue: The lattice recognizes you—it's pulling the door inward, the seal is unraveling thread by thread.
Your heartbeat fell out of rhythm. The lattice rejected you and the hum just doubled—I can taste copper in the air.

choices.text: Amplify the warning through every monastery spire—alert all Listeners, but reveal our location.
choices.description: Offer Pichit's old master coin to the door—burn it, speak the name, pay the old debt.

line.dialogue: Clever. The old debt settles, the door exhales—whatever's inside, it was waiting for someone to remember the price.
The coin blackened but the door didn't move. The old master's name has no weight here anymore—someone already spent it.

choices.text: Attempt communion—sing directly to the waking lattice and try to understand its intent.
choices.description: Ask Arthit what the Listeners actually sealed away—demand the truth before paying any price.

line.dialogue: You deserve to know. They sealed the first transcript—the original lattice song. Every truth we've been told is a shadow of what's inside.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The spire's shaking! I've seen it before—in my nightmares. The lattice is pulling the monastery down!
Pirates at the gates! Your little song woke up every crystal for miles. We're taking the archive before this place falls!
He paced back and forth by the resonator, trying to stabilize it. Stopped breathing when the first crystal shard fell from the ceiling.
The acoustic dampeners are failing. Before the lattice fully awakens, we need to decide—do we fight the pirates or save the knowledge?
The Listeners' final recording... they tried to sing back to the lattice during The Silencing. Their resonance patterns are still etched in the crystal.
It remembers our songs. Every navigation chart, every city's frequency signature. It's learning how to unmake us.
The lower levels are crumbling! We need to get to the resonance ships before—
The monastery groans as crystalline growths erupt through ancient stone. The air hums with a frequency that makes thought difficult, memory slippery.

lines_after.dialogue: As the decision takes effect, the lattice's song shifts—either retreating, amplifying, or turning toward the singers with terrible attention.
We've changed the melody. Whether for better or worse... that song will echo through every floating city before dawn.
Well. At least the pirates are as screwed as we are. Silver linings.

line.dialogue: The lattice's attention is upon Phrao Monastery. How do we face the awakening?

choices.text: Shatter the central resonator—create a discordant blast that drives the lattice's consciousness back temporarily.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus tonal knowledge on the crystal bowls to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Things don't go as planned. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Harmonize with the pirates' ships—use their combined resonance to lift the monastery to safety, forming an uneasy alliance.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to question the Orders' silence, drawing on singer voice

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
The gamble fails. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Sing the Listeners' lost song directly into the lattice—offer understanding instead of resistance, risking everything for communion.
choices.description: Have the villager focus community ties on the crystal bowls to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the villager pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. Local knowledge proves outdated.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hum with the low-frequency resonance of a thousand crystalline data-slates. The air smells of ozone and old parchment.
Keep your voices down. The acoustics here are designed to carry whispers to the monitors. We're here to research, not get arrested.
Arrested for what? Looking at old maps? This place is suffocating.
It's suffocating by design. Knowledge is power, and the Tonal Orders like to keep their power locked up tight. Look at them.
Malee gestures with her chin toward a pair of robed Archivists, their steps silent on the sound-dampening floors.
Every notation here... it's a song of survival. A record of paths through the chaos below. But it feels... incomplete.
Incomplete is dangerous. Incomplete means a ship gets lost in the Lattice. We need the full, official charts for the southern drift.
Then let's stop staring at the public terminals and go deeper. The restricted stacks. That's where the real songs are buried.

lines_after.dialogue: Bad idea. The restricted stacks have harmonic wards. Set one off, and the whole Order knows we're poking where we shouldn't.
Chanida's right. The answers we need about the old Listeners' paths won't be in the public records. They've been... sanitized.
Pichit, think. This is exactly what we agreed not to do. We find the official route, we take it. No deviations.

line.dialogue: The party stands at the threshold of the public reading room. A heavy resonator-locked door leads to the restricted stacks. The way is forbidden, but it calls.

choices.line: Follow the rules. Research only the official, sanctioned charts. (Safety, but limited knowledge)
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing tattooed routes to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Arthit is thwarted. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Attempt to bypass the harmonic lock quietly. (Risk detection for deeper insight)
choices.description: Pichit attempts to question the Orders' silence, relying on resonant staff

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Pichit. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Defeat. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.line: Look for an alternative entrance, perhaps through the maintenance ducts. (Stealthy, but time-consuming)
choices.description: The scavenger steps forward with harvesting tools, ready to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: the scavenger pushes through. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the scavenger hits a wall. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The restricted stacks are a cavern of gloom, lit only by the faint glow of inactive data-slates. The air is still and cold.
See? No wards. They were all deactivated. That's... interesting.
Interesting? It's a trap. Or someone got here first. Look at this.
Malee points to a data-slate lying open on a lectern. Its crystal surface is cracked, the information within scrambled into static.
Sabotage. This is a crime against the Archives. We need to leave. Now.
Wait. This slate... it wasn't cataloging ship routes. It was a personal journal. A Listener's journal. Look at the script.
Pichit gently touches the slate's frame. A fragmented, whispering voice emerges from the crystal.
'...the Orders silence the true songs. They call us Groundless, but we remember the earth. The Lattice sings of return...' The voice cuts out.

lines_after.dialogue: Groundless propaganda. Right here in the heart of the Order's power. Someone is planting seeds.
This isn't research anymore. This is sedition. If we're found near this...
He hung up. The journal entry just stopped. But where's the rest of it? There must be more!

line.dialogue: The damaged journal slate hints at a hidden cache of forbidden knowledge. The party can hear faint, furtive movements somewhere deeper in the stacks.

choices.line: Conceal the damaged slate and retreat. Report nothing. (Avoid immediate danger, lose the thread)
choices.description: Malee steps forward with scavenger instincts, ready to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The attempt backfires on Malee. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.line: Search the immediate area for more hidden journals. (Risk discovery, gain information)
choices.description: Arthit channels tattooed routes toward the recorded routes, hoping to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.line: Call out to the hidden presence. Announce you mean no harm to the Groundless. (Direct confrontation, high risk/reward)
choices.description: The scavenger takes the lead, employing crystal fragments to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Things don't go as planned. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives' main reading room is a cavernous space of polished crystal and brass, lit by the soft, resonant glow of knowledge-bearing prisms. The air hums with a low, controlled frequency.
The patterns in these restricted codices... they're not just navigation charts. They're a record of suppression. The Tonal Orders didn't just map safe routes; they mapped which ones to silence.
So the 'Silencing' wasn't just a catastrophe? It was... managed? We probably can't finish piecing this all together before someone finds us.
Oh, I think we can. The Groundless graffiti in the stacks points right to these shelves. Our 'allies' led us here on purpose. A cheap trick, but it's still effective.
Caution. This feels orchestrated. If the Groundless wanted us to see this, it's because they can't retrieve it themselves. We're the expendable ones making the grab.
You catch on quick, sky-farer.
The Surface Scavenger steps from behind a towering shelf of sonic scrolls, her boots silent on the acoustic-dampening floor. Her eyes are hard.

They keep the truth locked up here, same as they keep us locked down on the surface. You didn't finish your search. You found what we needed you to find. The proof that the Lattice can be calmed, not just parted.

lines_after.dialogue: You used us as a key!
Your Singer's resonance was the only key that wouldn't trigger the Archives' defenses. Now, hand over the core frequency schema. The one that proves the 'Silencing' is a lie.
And if we say no? You'll bring this whole crystal library down on our heads?

line.dialogue: The Scavenger's hand rests on a strange, humming device grafted to her belt. The air grows taut.

choices.line: Comply. Hand over the schema. (You secure a fragile alliance, but the truth leaves your hands.)
choices.description: Cross-reference the codex patterns with the Groundless graffiti locations on the stack maps.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The coordinates align perfectly — every Silencing epicenter matches a Groundless marker. They mapped it before it happened.
Pichit — "The ink's bleeding through from both sources — I can't separate signal from noise. We need cleaner data.

choices.line: Refuse. The knowledge is too dangerous. (You defy the Groundless, making an enemy but keeping the secret.)
choices.description: Remove the restricted seal and photograph the codex pages before anyone notices the breach.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Got all twelve pages — and look, these margin notes are in a curator's hand. They *knew* the Silencing was coming.
Chanida — "The seal triggered a ward — ink's vanishing off the pages as I grab them. We're losing evidence in real time.

choices.line: Propose a trade: the schema for their surface route maps. (A risky negotiation that could double-cross both the Orders and the Groundless.)
choices.description: Confront Arthit directly — demand to know what he's withholding about the Groundless connection.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "You're right, I've seen this before. Three years ago in the deep stacks. I was told to stop looking. I didn't.
Arthit — "I told you — caution. And cornering me in front of everyone isn't caution. Now I can't help you even if I wanted to.

lines_before.dialogue: Before the Scavenger can respond, the resonant lighting in the Archives shifts to a piercing, urgent amber. A dissonant alarm frequency shatters the silence.
They know! The Archivists know you're in the restricted zone! Just relax, don't make it worse—they're sealing the sector!
The Groundless device... it's a resonator bomb. Set to a dissonant frequency. She wasn't just here to retrieve data.
The truth needs a loud voice. Sometimes, a broken one. The Orders' monopoly is built on controlled sound. Let's see how they handle noise.
This archive isn't just their power. It's history. The last echoes of the world before. You'll destroy the very memory you want to liberate.
I'm just surprised it took this long for someone to try and smash the place. Sentimentality versus revolution. Always a messy finale.
We can't let her detonate it! The feedback could shatter the city's foundational crystals!
The Scavenger's device pulses with unstable light. The polished crystal walls begin to vibrate, emitting a painful, rising whine. The Archives themselves are becoming an instrument of destruction.

lines_after.dialogue: The Lattice responds to intent as much as frequency. This anger... this pain... it will resonate across the world.
Let it! Maybe then they'll finally listen!
The first crystalline shelf cracks with a sound like a dying chord. Knowledge centuries old begins to dissolve into harmonic dust.

line.dialogue: The core of the Archives—and the fate of its knowledge—hangs on the next few seconds. The Scavenger is lost to her cause, the device reaching critical resonance.

choices.line: Use Pichit's Singer ability to counter the dissonance with a stabilizing harmony. (Save the Archives, but the Groundless subplot is violently crushed.)
choices.description: Smash the resonator bomb against the archive's central indexing crystal to shatter the containment field.

line.dialogue: The crystal cracked — every restricted shelf just spilled open like a gutted fish, history pouring everywhere.
The crystal absorbed the frequency. Bomb's dead. And now the whole archive knows exactly where we're standing.

choices.line: Sabotage the Archives' own acoustic dampeners, containing the blast but sacrificing this wing entirely. (A contained loss, creating a permanent 'silence' in the record.)
choices.description: Signal Pichit to start dragging shelves down as barricades while you intercept the incoming Archivist patrol alone.

line.dialogue: Aisles are blocked, papers everywhere — they'll have to dig through a century of their own secrets to reach us.
The shelves won't budge — bolted to the floor. We're trapped in here with nothing but dust and their footsteps getting louder.

choices.line: Channel the bomb's resonance into the Lattice connection below, risking an unknown global feedback. (An irreversible act that will change the world's soundscape forever.)
choices.description: Grab the villager and force them to shout false coordinates through the archive's echo-chute to misdirect the patrol.

line.dialogue: Beautiful — they heard their own voice screaming about a breach in Sector Nine. Half the patrol just ran the wrong way.
The villager's voice broke. Cracked right in half. The patrol heard the fear in it and now they're coming straight toward that fear.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim sway gently in the high-altitude breeze, a symphony of rustling stalks and trickling irrigation channels.
Listen to that... the Lattice beneath us hums in counterpoint to the wind. It still works, even here, beneath the soil.
It's just farming noises, Pichit. Peaceful, but boring. I don't see what's so unknown about a bunch of wheat.
Spoken like someone who's never had to bargain for a loaf during a supply chain collapse. This 'peace' is subsidized by the Tonal Orders' charts.
