Quiet, both of you. We're here to rest, not draw attention. That figure by the terraces... they've been watching us.
You're not from the maintenance crews. Surface doesn't smell like you.
We mean no harm. We're just... listening.
Listening, huh? Dangerous hobby. I just spoke with a sky-watcher. Says a Singer passed through here, left something behind in the lower groves.

lines_after.dialogue: A Singer? Here? What did they leave?
Don't know. Didn't look. The Gardens have their own rules. He doesn't know me, and I don't know him. But the lower groves... the lattice resonance is strange there now.
A mysterious artifact and weird resonance. Of course. Because our 'rest' couldn't just be actual rest.
This could be a trap. Or a wild goose chase.

line.dialogue: The scavenger's information points to the lower groves. Do we investigate?

choices.text: Ignore it. Stay and rest. (Easy)
choices.consequence: We avoid potential danger but may miss a crucial opportunity.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the soil and feel the Lattice's rhythm, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — beneath the rootline. The hum carries patterns, old ones. Something remembers what grew here.
I felt nothing but mud and cold worms. Perhaps the Lattice sleeps where the land has been bled dry.

choices.text: Send Chanida and Malee to scout discreetly. (Medium)
choices.consequence: A balanced approach, but splits the party.
choices.description: Ask Malee what a fair price for lodging here would actually cost the group, 15 words

line.dialogue: Four copper and a favor. The favor's the trap. Always negotiate the favor before you hand over coin.
You haggle like a city child waving an empty purse. They'll smell your desperation and triple the ask.

choices.text: Press the scavenger for more details, risking suspicion. (Easy)
choices.consequence: Might get clearer information, but reveals our interest.
choices.description: Scout the treeline perimeter alone before settling in for the night, 15 words

line.dialogue: Clear to the eastern ridge. No tracks, no watchers. We sleep in shifts and leave before first threshing.
I found bootprints — fresh, heavy, military tread. Someone already knows we're here. We move now, not at dawn.

lines_before.dialogue: The lower groves are dimmer, the air thicker with the scent of damp earth and blooming night-flowers. A strange, low thrum vibrates through the crystal-laced tree roots.
Scout report: found it. It's... a leg. A crystal prosthetic, fused to a broken resonator. It's still glowing faintly.
Charming. A piece of someone. Probably the Singer the scavenger mentioned. Looks like it got shattered in a fall.
Don't touch it! The resonance pattern is unstable. If we could just... how do you write down a frequency like this? It's shifting.
It's not meant to be written. It's meant to be felt. Sung. This is a Resonant Prosthetic. Subplot crystal leg. The Singer must have used it to navigate without charts.
So this is the 'unknown' we're exploring? A dead man's leg? Could you please write down what you're sensing, Pichit? Before it fades?
A sharp whistle cuts through the grove. Rough figures drop from the upper vines, their clothes patched from a dozen different sky-ship hulls.
Well, well. Look what the lattice coughed up. That shiny limb there... that's ours. Found it first.

lines_after.dialogue: Yours? Did you file a claim? I must have missed the memo.
We don't write memos. We take. Hand it over, or we start taking pieces of you to match.
He means it! Look at their gear—jammed harmonic cutters. They're serious sky pirates.
This artifact... it's more than a tool. It's a memory of a way to navigate freely. We can't let them have it.

line.dialogue: The sky pirates block the only exit. The prosthetic hums dangerously in Chanida's hands.

choices.text: Try to negotiate, offering something else of value. (Easy)
choices.consequence: Risks losing the artifact but may avoid a fight.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the crystal and let the resonance flood through you unfiltered.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "There — you see? The frequency is grief. Old grief. She lost this leg running from something that wanted her silent.
Arthit — "I said don't — your nose is bleeding, pull back, pull back now before it rewires your auditory cortex!

choices.text: Use the prosthetic's unstable resonance as a distraction to fight your way out. (Medium)
choices.consequence: Dangerous and unpredictable, but proactive.
choices.description: Wrap the leg in signal-dampening cloth and run a harmonic analysis back at camp instead.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Clean read. The prosthetic was grown, not built. Biocrystal lattices keyed to one specific voice — we can trace her.
Chanida — "The cloth dissolved. It's eating through everything synthetic. Whatever power source is in there, it's still alive and it's angry.

choices.text: Attempt to 'write' the prosthetic's frequency onto our own resonator, hoping to use it. (Hard)
choices.consequence: High risk of catastrophic feedback, but potential for a powerful advantage.
choices.description: Sing a single sustained note matching the crystal's base frequency to calm its resonance pattern.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Stabilizing. You matched it within three cents. The lattice is breathing now — it remembers her gait, her rhythm. Follow where it points.
Pichit — "Wrong harmonic. The crystal just shrieked — every sensor in the valley is now awake and looking directly at us.

lines_before.dialogue: The peaceful afternoon in the Hanging Gardens is shattered by the distant, frantic tolling of a warning bell. The rhythmic sounds of wind and water are overtaken by a low, unsettling hum that vibrates through the very soil.
That's not the irrigation pump. The whole terrace is shaking!
A localized frequency tremor. It's destabilizing the island's connection to the Lattice below. We need to find the source before the structural integrity fails.
Perfect. Just when we thought we could fix one broken thing in peace.
You lot! It's them sky-rats! They're down at the old resonator spire, trying to pry out the main crystal. They'll crack the whole garden loose!
Why couldn't they just scavenge from the abandoned sectors? Why risk destroying a living place?
I didn't catch what you said about the spire's location. Point the way!
Follow the tremor. And hurry. I lost my phone in the last quake, or I'd call for the wardens. You're the only ones here.

lines_after.dialogue: The party races along shuddering walkways, leaping over newly formed cracks. The air grows thick with the discordant whine of a crystal being forced to resonate against its nature.
The feedback is catastrophic. If they succeed in removing it, the counter-frequency will snap. The gardens will drop.
Why can't you do it, Arthit? Jam their tools with a counter-harmonic?

line.dialogue: The spire is ahead. The Sky Pirates are using a crude sonic drill on the massive foundation crystal. How do you stop them?

choices.text: [CHARISMA] Appeal to their greed. Offer the schematics for the Resonant Prosthetic as a trade—a more valuable, portable crystal tech.
choices.description: Sprint down to the old reservoir and drive the sky-rats out before they nest further.

line.dialogue: I counted at least twelve——scattered them with a sonic pulse before they could burrow deeper into the reservoir walls.
Brilliant. You ran in, tripped on a support cable, and now half of them are circling above your head like vultures.

choices.text: [STEALTH] Use the tremor's noise. Sneak to the control console and manually recalibrate the spire to emit a pacifying, sleep-inducing frequency.
choices.description: Rig Arthit's frequency scanner to emit a counter-resonance and stabilize the terrace from here.

line.dialogue: The counter-wave held——tremor's dampened for now, and the structural integrity readings are climbing back to baseline.
You inverted the frequency. The terrace just dropped three centimeters. My pump readings are completely gone now.

choices.text: [BRAWL] Direct confrontation. Disable the drill by shattering its smaller resonator crystals, knowing the backlash could injure you.
choices.description: Question the scavenger about sky-rat behavior patterns before deciding anything.

line.dialogue: Good thinking——they nest at dusk, always near water. That gives us a two-hour window to reinforce the reservoir before they settle in.
The scavenger bolted. Turns out people who live in collapsed terraces don't stick around to chat when the ground starts shaking again.

lines_before.dialogue: The central terrace is a storm of noise and light. The pirate's drill screams against the spire crystal, which flashes with painful, jagged light. Soil spills from the edges of the floating island into the silent void below.
Back off! This crystal's worth ten of your rust-bucket ships! The garden's dead anyway—can't you hear it groaning?
It's not dead. It's in pain. You're making it scream.
How well do you know her? The Lattice, I mean? You think it's just rock to be broken? It remembers!
He's serious! That drill frequency is a known fracture pattern. One more minute and we all go for a very long fall.
Pretty speech. Don't know either if you're right. But I know profit. And this is it.
Pichit. The prosthetic's test crystal. It's tuned to a healing frequency from the old Listeners' texts. If we resonate it *with* the spire, not against it... we might stabilize the foundation.
We'd be risking the subplot_crystal_leg. Its only prototype crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: A choice hangs in the cacophonous air: save the immediate, living world of the gardens, or preserve the key to a single person's future mobility. The drill's whine reaches a piercing crescendo.
Well, philosopher? What's the grand equation? One leg versus ten thousand tons of soil and soul?
There's no time! I don't know when the crystal will fail!

line.dialogue: This is the climax. The fate of the Hanging Gardens—and the Resonant Prosthetic—rests on your next action.

choices.text: [SACRIFICE THE TOOL] Use the prosthetic's crystal. Channel its healing frequency into the spire, stabilizing the gardens. The prosthetic project is set back years, but the people and place are saved.
choices.description: Rush the bandit's drilling rig and yank the power coupling before the frequency shatters the crystal completely.

line.dialogue: Pichit grabs your arm, breathless — "You felt it too, right? That sigh of relief? It's still singing.
Malee shouts "WATCH THE SHARD SPRAY—" as the coupling tears free and ricochets a splinter of crystal into your shoulder.

choices.text: [DIVERT THE PIRATES] Lure the pirates away by faking a larger, more valuable crystal cache in the gardens' vaults. Saves both garden and prototype, but requires a flawless deception under extreme duress.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to sing the Lattice's root harmonic aloud, hoping the crystal recognizes an old friend's voice.

line.dialogue: Chanida hums a low wavering note and the crystal pulses warm amber — "See? Some of us remember what you sounded like before they started cutting.
Chanida's voice cracks on the third interval and the crystal screeches a dissonant chord that drops everyone to their knees, ears bleeding.

choices.text: [SYMPHONIC RESONANCE] Have Pichit attempt to 'Sing'—to harmonize with the wounded spire directly, using his own latent ability to calm the frequency. Risks his sanity and could fail utterly, losing everything.
choices.description: Level your weapon at the bandit and demand he hold the drill against his own skin to feel what the crystal feels.

line.dialogue: The bandit's hand trembles, drill bit hovering over his forearm — "That's... that's what I've been doing to it? Gods. Gods, I didn't—
The bandit laughs and revs the drill higher —

lines_before.dialogue: The Hollow's entrance is a jagged maw in the floating island's underside. Cold, mineral-scented air exhales from the darkness.
The structural integrity is... questionable. These formations look ancient. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Quiet! Listen to that hum! It's coming from deeper in. Let's go!
Of course. Drawn to the creepy, resonant hum in a dark hole. Classic.
This vibration... it feels like a memory. Not just stone, but a record.
You Listeners mean what you say about finding answers down here? You're serious?
We mean it. The Tonal Orders' charts... they omit this place. The past they teach is over. A finished story. Here, it may not be.
Your first steps into The Hollow send shivering echoes cascading through vast, unseen chambers. Crystalline structures catch your lamplight, fracturing it.

lines_after.dialogue: The tunnel opens into a cathedral-like cavern. Carved pillars, impossibly old and stylistically alien, support a ceiling glittering with embedded crystal.
Pre-Silencing. And not just a ruin. This was... engineered. The Lattice responds differently here. The echo pattern is all wrong.
Wrong, or just not what the Tonal Orders want us to hear?

line.dialogue: A strange, harmonic feedback begins to build from a central crystal formation. It feels... reactive.

choices.text: Have Chanida try to mimic the resonance with her voice. (Intuitive)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the vibrating wall and let the resonance flow through you, 15 words

line.dialogue: The memory—it's a warning. Something was sealed here. Something that listened for heartbeats.
My hand went numb instantly. Whatever lives in this stone, it doesn't want to be touched.

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze the crystal's frequency for a safe interaction. (Analytical)
choices.description: Follow the hum deeper while mapping load-bearing cracks with chalk as you advance, 15 words

line.dialogue: The fractures follow the hum's rhythm—structural stress radiating from a central chamber ahead. We can navigate around the worst of it.
The ceiling shifted. I'd estimate two minutes before this corridor becomes our tomb. Move. NOW.

choices.text: Have Pichit simply listen, trying to understand its intent. (Receptive)
choices.description: Hum back at the same frequency and see if the sound responds to your voice, 15 words

line.dialogue: It answered. The harmonics shifted when you matched its pitch. You're speaking its language now.
It screamed back at us. The hum became a roar—whatever's down there knows we're here and it's angry.

lines_before.dialogue: Your interaction with the crystal causes the cavern to hum with latent power. Faint, ghostly images—echoes of light—flicker against the walls: people moving, working.
Resonant imprints... like a fossilized song. I have studied the Lattice's harmonics by myself for decades. I thought I understood. But this... Can I even comprehend it?
The energy signature is stable, but the information density is staggering. It's not a navigation chart. It's a... record.
A record of what was here before the islands floated. Before the Silencing. They had no one to help them preserve this. They had to encode it in the stone itself.
The Groundless say our history is a lie. That we're clinging to driftwood and calling it a home. I never believed... but this place...
Believe what? That the all-knowing Tonal Orders might have missed a few chapters? Shocking.
It's more than that! Look! The light-echoes are forming a path, deeper in!

lines_after.dialogue: Following the ephemeral guide, you descend into a lower chamber. The air grows thick and silent, absorbing sound. In the center lies a massive, dormant crystal console, its surface etched with flowing, unfamiliar script.
This is a control node. Or a memory bank. The script... it's a foundational resonance language. I studied the basics by myself from forbidden texts. This is the source.
It's intact. Power is minimal, but... functional. A direct interface with whatever system this place was part of.

line.dialogue: The console awaits input. Activating it could reveal everything—or trigger a collapse.

choices.text: Urge the Listener Monk to attempt activation using his forbidden knowledge. (Trust Expertise)
choices.description: Have Malee focus scavenger instincts on the cave echoes to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee loses control. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Have the party attempt a coordinated harmonic trigger, using your combined skills. (Collaborative)
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing forbidden paths to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Arthit fails. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.text: Let Pichit, the Singer, approach it alone and unguided. (Instinctual Leap)
choices.description: The monk volunteers to trace the anomalous signal, leveraging lattice study

line.dialogue: the monk succeeds. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the monk hits a wall. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the Hollow, the air grows colder. The ruins here are more intact, strange crystalline formations pulsing with a faint, internal light that responds to your footsteps.
So much for 'ancient ruins.' This looks more like a machine that's just sleeping. I've never understood how the Silencing could leave something like this untouched.
Look! Carvings on this archway. They're... moving? Shifting with the echoes.
A resonance-locked archive. Incredible. But the harmonics required to unlock it... in only five minutes, the echo pattern in this chamber will reset. We'd be trapped.
The Listeners study the Lattice's song, but this... this is the song of what came before. The truth the Tonal Orders buried.
You shouldn't be here. This knowledge... it's unstable. I'm no match for the consequences if this gets out. The Orders, the Groundless... they'll tear each other apart.
He means it! The monk means what he says! My cousin joined the Groundless—they talk of digging too deep, of waking things that should sleep. The past is gone. Let it go.

lines_after.dialogue: The central crystal of the archive hums to life, projecting shimmering images of a world before the Lattice—a world of interconnected sound, not controlled, but shared.
The Silencing wasn't a natural disaster. It was a severing. A choice to silence the world rather than risk its song.
And the Tonal Orders are the guardians of that lie. No wonder they hunt Singers. You're a living reminder they failed to erase.

line.dialogue: The archive reveals the location of the 'Primordial Tone,' a sound frequency that could temporarily calm the Lattice's volatility. But accessing it requires a precise, dangerous resonance.

choices.text: Use the archive's own harmonics. Let the ancient machine guide the process. (Safer, but the knowledge may be lost.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the moving carvings and let the resonance flow through you.

line.dialogue: The harmonics are responding to your bioelectric signature — the archive recognizes you as an authorized user!
Your touch scrambled the patterns — they've gone dark, and I think that section of the archive just sealed itself permanently.

choices.text: Have Chanida and Arthit improvise a counter-melody. Use modern resonance tech to interface. (Risky, requires perfect coordination.)
choices.description: Hum the Lattice melody Pichit taught you, matching the shifting tones of the carvings.

line.dialogue: The song of the Lattice — you remember it! The archway is opening, and I can hear... thousands of voices preserved inside.
Wrong key, wrong note — the carvings just shrieked at you and the whole archway is vibrating like it's about to collapse.

choices.text: Pichit must Sing alone. Channel the raw, unshielded frequency directly. (Extremely dangerous, but could unlock deeper understanding.)
choices.description: Ignore the archway and search the walls for a manual override or secondary access point.

line.dialogue: Found it — hidden panel behind the moss. Looks like someone built a back door into this 'sacred archive' after all.
Nothing but dead stone and dead ends. Whatever this place was, it doesn't want to be opened by hands alone.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber of the Primordial Tone. It is not a room, but a vast, dark geodesic cavity. In its center hangs a single, flawed crystal, silent. The air pressure makes your ears pop.
I had a bad dream last night. That we'd find this place, and it would be... empty. That the truth was just another silence.
Readings are off the scale. My instruments are blind. I have bad vision here, in every sense. We're navigating by instinct alone.
The Groundless subplot messages... they're flooding the comms. They know we're here. They're saying this Tone could let us reach the ground. Really reach it.
You've done it. You've pieced together the fragments we Listeners feared to touch. I did it all myself, my research, my doubts... but I was too afraid to act.
Afraid of what? The Tonal Orders sending their resonance ships? Or afraid the Groundless are right, and the sky cities are a cage we built ourselves?
Please. Whatever you do... don't break it. We built everything by ourselves up here after the fall. What if there's nothing down there but the dream that broke the world?
The flawed crystal begins to vibrate. A low, foundational note that doesn't travel through the air, but through bone. The walls of the Hollow start to sing.

lines_after.dialogue: The Primordial Tone resonates. For a moment, the entire Lattice visible through cracks in the cavern ceiling seems to still, to soften. Then, the crystal shatters.
It wasn't a key. It was a... memory. A single, perfect note from a world that loved its people. The Silencing was the act of forgetting how to hear it.

The shards fall, not down, but outward, embedding in the walls. Each now glows with a captured fragment of the Tone. The knowledge is not lost, but scattered. The choice of what to do with it is now yours.

line.dialogue: The shattered Tone's fragments hold immense power. The Groundless are clamoring for them. The Tonal Orders' ships are on the horizon. The Listeners look to you.

choices.text: Gather the shards. Hide them. This truth is too dangerous for anyone to wield. (Preserve the secret, maintain the unstable peace.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the monolith's warm surface and let the dream-images bleed through.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The stone remembers me. I see the dreamer's face — it's been waiting for someone who already saw this place in sleep.
Pichit — "Nothing. Just cold. Whatever lives inside this thing, it doesn't recognize me — or it's chosen not to.

choices.text: Distribute the fragments. Give pieces to the Listeners, the Groundless, even the Orders. Force them to share the truth. (Risk chaos for a chance at reconciliation.)
choices.description: Override Arthit's instrument safeties and push the sensors into the distortion field's epicenter.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "There — behind the static — that's a heartbeat. Not electrical, not mechanical. Something alive is dreaming this entire place into existence.
Arthit — "The readings collapsed into noise. I fried three boards for white static. Whatever's here, it doesn't want to be measured.

choices.text: Use one shard to amplify Pichit's Song. Broadcast the Tone's memory to every resonance receiver in the sky. Let everyone hear. (The ultimate gamble. It will change everything.)
choices.description: Cross-reference the Groundless messages with the monk's fragments to reconstruct the dreamer's true name.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "The messages weren't flooding — they were assembling. The name was
the villager is thwarted. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform 'The Gaze' juts out from the floating city's underbelly, offering a breathtaking, terrifying view of the Lattice.
Below, the crystalline surface shimmers like a frozen sea, pulsing with faint, harmonic light. A low, resonant hum vibrates through the metal decking.
Wow. It's... it's nice and peaceful. In a 'could-kill-us-all' kind of way.
Peaceful? That hum is the sound of a billion potential fractures. One wrong frequency and this whole platform becomes glitter.
The Tonal Order charts mark this sector as stable. For now. We should proceed with the survey.
Listen... beneath the hum. There's a pattern. Like a memory the crystals are trying to recall.
Aren't you overthinking this? It's just resonance. Let's go inside the survey module and get the readings.
You the survey team? Don't linger. The pirates have been sniping scavengers near the old 'Echo' wreckage. Bad place.

lines_after.dialogue: 'The Echo.' That's the lost Resonance ship from the subplot logs. The one that just... vanished into the Lattice.
If pirates are interested, they might have found something the Tonal Orders missed. Or created a new hazard.
A vanished ship... an echo in the crystals. These aren't separate things. We should investigate.

line.dialogue: The path to the survey module is clear, but the villager's warning hangs in the air. What's our priority?

choices.line: Focus on the mission. Proceed directly to the survey module.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the largest crystal and let the hum resonate through your bones.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "I feel it too — the melody is a name, repeated over and over, waiting for someone to answer.
Arthit — "Pull your hand back! The resonance frequency just spiked — you nearly harmonized with a fracture point.

choices.line: Scout towards the 'Echo' wreckage first. Caution is key.
choices.description: Hum the counter-melody that Pichit's pattern suggests, matching pitch and rhythm exactly.

line.dialogue: Malee — "The crystals are dimming in sequence — you're speaking their language, and something deep below just heard you.
Chanida — "Wrong note. The whole chamber just rang like a struck bell and I think something behind the wall woke up.

choices.line: Question the villager further about the pirates and the wreck.
choices.description: Consult the Tonal Order charts Arthit carries and cross-reference the hum's frequency against known stable sectors.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "This frequency doesn't appear anywhere in the records. We're not in a stable
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: Choosing to scout, you navigate a series of crystalline spires. The light shifts, casting long, prismatic shadows.
Ahead, the shattered hull of a Resonance ship—the 'Echo'—lies half-submerged in the Lattice, glowing with a sickly, erratic light.
Whoa. What's this called? This glow... it's not on any chart.
Corrupted resonance. The ship's crystal drives are fractured, leaking. It's singing a dead song.
Movement! On the port side of the wreck. Pirates.
Well, look what the Lattice coughed up! A fresh crew for the picking. Anyone's okay. We're not picky.
You're trespassing on our salvage claim. The price for passage is your ship's frequency logs. Or your bones. Either works.
You're not just salvaging. You're listening to it, aren't you? To the Echo's final song.

lines_after.dialogue: Clever lad. The ship's screaming a hidden frequency. A path the Orders don't know. But that's our secret.
We're not giving you our logs! That's suicide!
He's right about one thing. That distorted song... it's a map to something. A dangerous one.
They're positioned to cut off our retreat. We need a plan, now.

line.dialogue: The pirates block the way forward to the wreck's core. How do we proceed?

choices.line: Fight. Engage the pirates directly to secure the area.
choices.description: Slam the emergency bulkhead shut and reroute power to the forward shields.

line.dialogue: Bulkhead sealed! That buys us maybe ninety seconds before they cut through.
The controls are dead — corrupted resonance fried the relay before I could touch it!

choices.line: Negotiate. Offer a partial data-share or a diversion to get past.
choices.description: Open a channel and offer the bandit a cut of whatever's inside the wreck.

line.dialogue: Pirates are businessmen. Offer enough and they'll hesitate long enough for us to reposition.
He laughed. He's not here for a deal — he already thinks everything here belongs to him.

choices.line: Resonate. Use the corrupted song from the wreck to disrupt their equipment and slip by.
choices.description: Reverse thrusters hard and loop beneath the wreck's hull to break line of sight.

line.dialogue: Skimming the hull — their targeting can't track us through the wreckage shadow!
The wreck's mass is pulling us in! I can't hold the vector against the resonance field!

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands on a precarious ledge overlooking a vast, silent basin in the Lattice. Below, the ghostly, crystalline hull of the lost ship is half-submerged, pulsing with a faint, sickly light.
There it is. The 'Echo.' Looks less like a ship and more like a giant, broken music box. I can already feel a headache coming on.
The resonance patterns here are... chaotic. Unstable. This isn't a safe descent. One wrong step, and the entire crystal field could shatter beneath us.
So we don't step wrong! That pirate said the ship's log is in the resonator chamber. The answers are down there. What are we waiting for?
We're waiting to listen. Can you hear it? Not just the ship's hum... but beneath it. A whispering. Like it's trying to tell us something.
A sharp, discordant chime rings out from the basin. The light within the ship flares, and for a moment, a shimmering, spectral figure is seen pacing the deck before vanishing.
Great. A haunted crystal ghost ship. Because this day wasn't weird enough. Why is it doing this to me? Why are you treating me like this, universe?
It's not 'treating' you any special way, Malee. It's a resonant echo, a memory trapped in the crystal. The real question is... what's *she* like? The consciousness powering this?

lines_after.dialogue: The path is treacherous, a series of resonant crystal plates that must be triggered in sequence to form a bridge. The ghostly figure watches their every move.
It's not hostile. It's... curious. Lonely. It's been repeating its final moments for decades.
Well, we're about to give it some new company. Ready to go meet our ghost?

line.dialogue: How do we approach the spectral echo on the deck?

choices.text: Attempt to mimic its resonant frequency. (Use Chanida's intuition to copy the ghost's 'song.')
choices.outcome: The echo calms, recognizing a familiar pattern. It gestures for you to follow below decks.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee overreaches. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Present a Tonal Order navigation chart. (Use Arthit's knowledge of formal frequencies.)
choices.outcome: The echo reacts with confusion, then agitation. The ghostly form flickers, forcing a quicker, more dangerous puzzle to pacify it.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with lattice storms to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Arthit is thwarted. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Have Pichit sing a counter-melody. (Challenge the echo's trapped memory directly.)
choices.outcome: A duel of resonances ensues. The entire ship shudders, but if successful, the echo clears, revealing the true path instantly.
choices.description: Ask the pirate to follow the dissonant trail, drawing on disruptor weapon

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
the pirate hits a wall. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the ship's crystal heart, the party finds the source: the ship's Singer, her form fused with the main resonator, her final desperate song holding the vessel in a single, eternal moment of destruction.
Stars above... she's still in there. Powering this whole... tomb. All guys like a tragic story, right? Well, here's the ultimate one.
The resonance feedback loop is catastrophic. If we disrupt it to free her, the released energy could vaporize this entire basin. And us with it.
*A voice woven from crystal chimes and static* ...break... the... song... please...
She's asking for help! We can't just leave her. Pichit, you're a Singer too. Do you wanna try it? Can you... sing her out?
It would be like trying to untangle two melodies that have become one. If I'm wrong, we don't just die. We become part of the echo.
The crystal walls begin to crack, light bleeding through the fractures. The basin outside groans as the Lattice itself strains under the unstable frequency.
We're out of time. We need a plan *now*. A precise frequency to sever the connection without triggering the cascade. Can I take a break for a moment to calculate? No. No, I cannot.

lines_after.dialogue: The air hums with potential energy. The fused Singer's eyes, like fractured gemstones, seem to plead with Pichit. The fate of the echo, the ship, and the party rests on a single, perfect note.
Everyone, find your note. Not to fight the song... but to complete it. To give it an ending it never had.
Fine. But if we all turn into pretty background noise, I'm haunting *you*, Pichit.

line.dialogue: How does Pichit resolve the trapped Singer's eternal song?

choices.text: Use the Lost Ship's Log. (Apply the precise frequency from the captain's final entry.)
choices.outcome: A clinical, correct solution. The loop severs cleanly. The Singer's echo dissipates with a sigh of thanks, and the ship settles into harmless, silent crystal. The data is saved, but the moment feels... sterile.
choices.description: Reach through the harmonic barrier bare-handed, matching her frequency with your own heartbeat.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "I can feel the song threading through my bones — her pulse and mine are almost synced, so I pull, *now*!
Pichit — "The resonance shredded through my palms — I wasn't steady enough, and she's screaming louder now.

choices.text: Improvise a New Melody. (Rely on instinct and the party's harmony to create a resolving chord.)
choices.outcome: A risky, beautiful harmony. The Singer's form glows, then gently dissolves. The ship's crystal blooms with new, stable patterns. The party is left emotionally drained, but with a profound sense of closure.
choices.description: Have Arthit invert the feedback loop's polarity while you sever the anchor crystal at its base.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "Arthit, flip it NOW — the crystal's cracking clean, and I can see *her* behind the fractures!
Pichit — "The polarity held for half a second — then it doubled back and threw us both against the far wall.

choices.text: Absorb the Echo. (Pichit attempts to take the fractured song into himself, to carry its memory.)
choices.outcome: A tremendous, personal sacrifice. The ship is freed instantly, but Pichit gains a permanent, whispering 'passenger' in his mind—a scar of resonance that grants unknown insight at a terrible cost.
choices.description: Sing back to her — a counter-melody Chanida taught you, the one that means *come home*.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "My voice is shaking and wrong but she *heard* me — the static parted and she reached
the pirate is thwarted. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Kinnari' descends through the final veil of mist, its crystal resonators humming a low, parting chord. Below, the Lattice Surface stretches to every horizon—a vast, fractured plain of crystalline structures that catch the dying sunlight in prismatic flares. A single, ancient observation platform, etched with weathered sigils, juts from the shimmering expanse.
Finally! Solid-ish ground. My legs are cramping. Is the pay good for this little sightseeing trip, Arthit?

The contract specifies hazard compensation based on recovered resonance-grade fragments. But we must take very good care not to trigger any unstable harmonic clusters. The platform's integrity scans are nominal... for now.
Nominal. What a comforting word. It usually means 'about to fail spectacularly.' Look at this place. The Silencing left its signature everywhere.
Yet, it breathes. Can you feel it? Not just light. A... pressure in the air. A held note from a world that hasn't finished singing.

You the scav team? Don't wander far. The Tonal Orders say this sector's stable, but my granddad said the Lattice remembers. It was a good experience for him, surviving down here once. Didn't make him any less nervous about it.
We'll be fine! I'm in a good mood. Fresh air, weird glowy rocks... what's not to like?
A low, melodic groan vibrates up through the platform's metal struts. Somewhere in the distance, a spire of crystal shatters silently, collapsing into a cloud of luminous dust.

lines_after.dialogue: Harmonic decay event at two hundred paces. Non-threatening, but a reminder. We should commence the fragment scan. Stay within visual range of the platform.
Oh, I'll take very good care of myself, don't you worry. Unlike some people who think this is a festival.
Listen. Beneath the groan... a counter-rhythm. Faint, like a heartbeat.

line.dialogue: The team needs to begin their scavenging sweep. Pichit decides the initial focus.

choices.line: Search near the platform's foundations. (Safe, low yield.)
choices.description: Malee uses engineering to harness harmonic feedback near the pre-Silencing ruins

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee is thwarted. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.line: Head towards the recent collapse site. (Risky, potential for high-grade fragments.)
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with captain experience, ready to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Things don't go as planned. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.line: Follow the faint rhythmic pulse Pichit heard. (Unknown, possibly nothing.)
choices.description: Direct the villager to decode the tonal pattern using terraces

line.dialogue: the villager pushes through. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the villager loses control. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: Time stretches on the Lattice Surface. The light shifts slowly. The party has been methodically scanning the area, the initial awe giving way to monotony. The only sounds are the hum of scanners, the occasional crystalline chime, and Chanida's impatient sighs.
Ugh. We were so bored! Shiny rock, slightly different shiny rock, crumbling shiny rock. What size do you even wear, Lattice? Because all this looks the same to me now.
Most Thais are Buddhist. They understand patience. You should try it. It's less whiny.
Scans are picking up a consistent low-frequency pulse from the north-east quadrant. It's not in the Tonal Orders' nav-charts for this sector. Anomalous.
That's the rhythm I heard. It's not decaying. It's... structured. A pattern.
A figure in ochre robes emerges from behind a crystal berm, moving with careful, deliberate steps. It is the Listener monk, a Listener, his face lined with worry.
You should not attune your devices to that song. Please.
Finally! Something that isn't a rock. Who are you?

lines_after.dialogue: A humble listener. I study the true songs of the Lattice, not the forced paths of the Orders. That pulse... it is a warning beacon. Left by my order long ago.
A warning? Of what? It's not catalogued.
Some truths are kept silent. For stability. For fear. I... I was sent to maintain the silence. But the song is changing. I am so bored of this duty.
A conflicted monk. How original. Let me guess, you want us to ignore the scary pulse and go home?

line.dialogue: The Listener Monk seems to hold a piece of the subplot—the Lattice's warning. How does Pichit engage with him?

choices.line: Respect his duty and agree to avoid the pulse. (Avoids conflict, gains no answers.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the rock and match your breathing to the pulse's rhythm.

line.dialogue: The vibration climbs through my wrist, up my arm, and settles in my chest like a second heartbeat — I understand now. It's not a signal. It's a summons.
My hand slips — the surface is slick with condensation, and the pulse stutters erratically the moment I touch it, as if I've interrupted something mid-sentence.

choices.line: Press him gently for details about the warning. (Diplomacy, may reveal partial truth.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to hum the rhythm he heard while Arthit records the frequency for pattern matching.

line.dialogue: When I hum it back, the rock responds — the pulse strengthens, harmonizes, and the scan spikes. Arthit grabs my arm: 'You're resonating with it. Keep going.
I can't hold the tune — my throat tightens and the pitch wavers. The pulse drifts further out of sync, and Arthit shakes his head: 'We're losing the pattern. It's degrading.

choices.line: Accuse him of hiding a truth that could endanger the skycities. (Confrontation, risks alienating him.)
choices.description: Sit in stillness beside the rock and meditate, letting the

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The community rallies, creating unexpected strength.
the villager is thwarted. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: Back on the Lattice surface, the platform groans. The crystalline floor nearby shifts, facets grinding with a discordant shriek.
The ground is moving! We can't just stand here.
Steady! The platform is anchored. But the resonance... it's changing. Listen.
Great. The world's biggest wind chime is having a tantrum. Don't change the subject from what the monk told us!
The Listener said the Lattice's song is shifting... becoming a warning. We might change our minds about what's 'safe' up here.
You hear it now, yes? The harmony is fraying. The old charts... they are becoming dangerous lies. My Order is torn.
Lies? What are you talking about? The Tonal Orders keep us fed! Don't leave these ideas out in the open, they're dangerous!
A deep, resonant pulse thrums up through your boots. A jagged crack, glowing with sickly light, races across the Lattice towards a distant crystal spire.

line.dialogue: The unstable spire shimmers. The Listener believes its core frequency could be recorded, a key to understanding the change. But it's deep in the fracture zone.

choices.line: Send a remote resonator probe. (Uses Chanida's tech, safe but limited data).
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the platform's core and let the resonance flow through you.

line.dialogue: You're reading it — the song isn't breaking, it's *branching*. Two melodies trying to coexist where there used to be one.
Pull your hand back! That frequency is meant for the Lattice, not for human bones — I can hear your teeth cracking from here.

choices.line: Navigate the shifting plates carefully. (Relies on Arthit's caution and Pichit's intuition).
choices.description: Shout for Pichit to finish the Listener's words before the vibration drowns them out.

line.dialogue: —because someone is *singing over it*! There, I said it. A second voice, threading through the Lattice like it belongs there. It doesn't.
I can't — the words won't come! It's like the air itself is swallowing syllables before they reach my mouth. Whatever is doing this doesn't want us to *name* it.

choices.line: Have Malee trigger a controlled harmonic burst to stabilize the path. (Risky, could attract worse instability).
choices.description: Grab the tether rope and rappel down toward the fracture line to see what's physically causing the shift.

line.dialogue: You're crazy — but you're *seeing* it, aren't you? The crack is glowing. That's not damage, that's a *doorway* being pried open from the other side.
Get

lines_after.dialogue: The operation is tense, the very air vibrating with potential shatter. You retrieve a sliver of the spire's core.
This frequency... it is a dirge. A song of structural failure. The Lattice isn't just changing; it is pleading to be heard.
A plea to change our course. The Silencing wasn't an end... it was a symptom. And it's happening again.

lines_before.dialogue: The recorded dirge pulses from your device. The surrounding Lattice reacts violently, facets shearing and rising like a storm of glass. The platform's integrity alarms blare.
What have you done?! What do your parents do to deserve this? We're all going to die!
We've got a lot of things to deal with right now! The resonator array is overloading!
The platform's anchor frequency is being drowned out. We have minutes before it shakes apart.
So the big discovery is we're all about to become very expensive glitter. Fantastic.
No! The Song... it is not attacking. It is *responding*. It matches the distress! We must answer, not fight!
He's right. The Lattice carries the memory of the Silencing. We're hearing its pain. We have to carry a new truth back. I'll take very good care of it.
The crystal maelstrom converges. To survive, you must not silence the dirge, but harmonize with it, using the very tools meant to suppress such sounds.

line.dialogue: The platform's main resonator can be reconfigured. Do you use the dirge's frequency to try and calm the storm?

choices.line: Broadcast a blanket damping wave. (Safe for the platform, but destroys the data and silences the truth).
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing unauthorized tones to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The lattice has other plans. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: Weave the dirge into a stabilizing counter-melody. (Uses the Listener's knowledge, saves the platform and the data).
choices.description: Pichit channels monk wisdom toward the harvesting, hoping to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
The lattice has other plans. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Amplify the dirge, let it peak and break. (A purge; could shatter the local Lattice permanently, ending the threat but at unknown cost).
choices.description: Have the villager risk using community ties to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_after.dialogue: The air itself seems to hold its breath as the final resonance echoes and fades. The crystalline storm settles into an uneasy, humming calm.
You listened. You answered. The Orders have forgotten how to do this. This... this is what we must carry forward.
Not just us. Everyone. The things we thought kept us safe are the very things blinding us. The warning has been given.
And now we must deliver it. No matter who doesn't want to hear it.

lines_before.dialogue: The deck of the resonance ship hums beneath your feet, a low C-sharp thrumming through the crystal-infused wood. The Lattice below is a shifting sea of fractured light, responding to the ship's engine tone.
Look at it all! It’s a lot more fun out here than staring at the same city spires every day, isn’t it?
Fun. Right. Until the harmonics destabilize and we plunge into a solid crystal sea. Such a delightful prospect.
The charts from the Tonal Order are holding steady. We should reach the trade nexus in six cycles. Stay vigilant.
The patterns... they’re not just random. There’s a rhythm to the Lattice’s response. Like it’s listening to more than just our engine.
Are you ready to go back home yet? I mean, really ready? Or are you still running?
I left home in a hurry for a reason. Some silences need to be broken.
A shadow detaches from a cloud bank—a smaller, sleeker resonance ship with jagged crystal shards welded to its hull. It pulses with a discordant, aggressive frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate ship closes, its resonator emitting a jarring screech that makes your ship's crystals vibrate painfully.
Heard you lot were sniffin' around for open frequencies! Hand over your charts, or we'll see how well your hull holds tone!
Sky pirates. They shouldn’t know we’re seeking that map. This is a targeted interception.
Of course. Because straightforward travel is far too simple a concept for our lives.

line.dialogue: The pirate ship is positioning to board. How do you respond?

choices.text: HAIL THEM. Try to talk them down or negotiate.
choices.description: Trace your finger along the nearest crystal spire and match the hum you feel vibrating through it.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "Yes! You feel it too — the spires are singing to each other, and we're standing in the middle of their conversation.
Malee — "Congratulations, you just set up a dissonant feedback wave. Everyone step back before the resonance collapses inward.

choices.text: SHIFT FREQUENCIES. Attempt an evasive maneuver by altering the ship's resonance.
choices.description: Pull out the Tonal Order charts and cross-reference the harmonic intervals against the drift patterns you're seeing.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The third and seventh nodes align perfectly — whoever mapped this wasn't guessing. We can navigate by these intervals safely.
Arthit — "These readings don't match the charts at all. Either the Order gave us outdated data, or the Crystal Drift is shifting faster than anyone predicted.

choices.text: PREPARE TO REPEL BOARDERS. Get ready for a physical fight on the deck.
choices.description: Cup your hands around your ears and isolate the faintest whisper threading beneath the dominant harmonic.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "You caught it — there's a second melody underneath! It sounds like... breathing. Like the whole drift is alive and trying to say something.
Pichit — "The overtone layers are too dense — you're picking up fragments of six different frequencies and weaving them into something that isn't really there.

lines_before.dialogue: Your choice has left the pirate ship momentarily off-balance. Instead of pressing the attack, it holds position, its aggressive frequency softening to a wary hum.
Alright, talkers. You want open frequencies? The map’s a myth. But the fella who sells the 'myth'... he’s docked at the next drift. Name’s Virot.
How wonderfully convenient. And I suppose he’s a trustworthy soul, just handing out forbidden charts?

Virot? Nah. He’s been married twice, and screwed over both spouses in the deals. But he knows things the Tonal Orders bury. Find him at the Gilded Echo tavern. I’ll see you there... if you survive him.
The pirate ship peels away, dissolving back into the cloud cover. The deck is quiet save for the wind and the ship's steady tone.
A trap. It has to be. We’re being herded.
Or we’re being given a real lead! The pirate knew about the map. That’s discovery! He’s been married before, so what? He still gave us a name!
Every relationship is a kind of resonance. Some harmonize. Some... create destructive interference. This Virot sounds like the latter.

lines_after.dialogue: You make for the designated drift—a chaotic cluster of tethered barges and floating platforms. The Gilded Echo is a garish vessel pulsating with overlapping, slightly off-key melodies.
Welcome, welcome! I am Virot. I hear you’re in the market for... unconventional cartography. A pleasure! The open frequency map is a rare piece. But for the right partners, anything is possible.
Your 'partners' usually end up divorced from their valuables, don’t they?
*chuckles* A cynical one! I like that. Let's just say my previous partnerships... reached their natural conclusions. Now, about your offer?

line.dialogue: Virot smiles, his eyes calculating. He will trade the map's location, but he wants something in return.

choices.text: PAY HIS PRICE. Offer a significant sum of crystal shards from the ship's stores.
choices.description: Pull the bandit aside and press him about who's really pulling Virot's strings.

line.dialogue: Look, you want the truth? Virot's a front. The frequencies route through a military relay in Khon Kaen — but that's all I know, I swear.
You're wasting my time with questions I can't answer. Either take the deal or walk — but don't expect a second offer.

choices.text: OFFER A TRADE. Propose exchanging a lesser-known but valuable harmonic sequence you've recorded.
choices.description: Signal Malee to play along while you quietly triangulate the frequency's origin point.

line.dialogue: Oh, how *delightful*, a map! I simply adore being led by the nose," Malee drawls, her fingers already working the receiver beneath her jacket — signal locked, coordinates cached.
Oh, how *delightful* — wait, the receiver's dead. Someone's jamming us. They knew we'd try this," Malee hisses, her smile vanishing.

choices.text: CALL HIS BLUFF. Accuse him of not having the real map location, and demand proof first.
choices.description: Grab Arthit and retreat to the alley to debate the offer out of earshot.

line.dialogue: Fine
The attempt backfires on the pirate. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: A dissonant hum shudders through the deck. The Lattice below churns, its crystalline patterns fracturing and reforming.
Well, isn't this just perfect. The charts are useless. The Tonal Orders sold us maps to a graveyard.
Forget the charts! Pichit, can you hear it? The open frequency Malee found... it's *singing* under all this noise!
It's... conflicted. A pure tone, but wrapped in static. Like a memory trying to surface.
Caution. We're straying far from known paths. The ship's resonator is straining.
A shadow falls across the deck. A ramshackle pirate skiff, bristling with jagged crystal shards, glides into view.
You're home so late! This ain't your sky-lane. Hand over that fancy resonator core, and maybe we won't drop you into the Lattice.
Over my dead body! You just want the map to the open frequency!

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate skiff reels, its own weapon turned against it. The open frequency map glows hot in Pichit's hands.
I'm sorry I'm late... to the party of watching pirates get a taste of their own medicine. That was... intense.
The frequency is now a beacon. And not just for us.

line.dialogue: The map is active, pulsing. The path ahead is clear but perilous.

choices.text: Follow the frequency directly. Speed is safety.
choices.consequence: Fastest route, but attracts attention.
choices.description: Tune the ship's resonance array to match the pure tone beneath the static, 15 words

line.dialogue: There—frequencies aligning—the static peeling back like skin from fruit, revealing something impossibly beautiful underneath.
Wrong harmonic—the static's multiplying, chewing through our array coatings—we're deafening ourselves chasing a ghost.

choices.text: Mask our resonance with the ship's engine tones.
choices.consequence: Stealthier, but slower and taxing on the ship.
choices.description: Drop emergency anchor and retreat to last verified coordinate before losing navigation lock, 15 words

line.dialogue: Sensors recalibrating—we held the line, and now the known paths find us again.
Anchor's not catching—void-current's pulling us deeper—the charts weren't useless, we were arrogant.

choices.text: Use the pirate skiff's wreckage as a decoy signal.
choices.consequence: Most deceptive, but risky if the ruse fails.
choices.description: Open the hull's acoustic dampeners fully and let Pichit listen with bare ears unfiltered, 15 words

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the pirate's call. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
the pirate loses control. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The deck shudders as the ship breaches a veil of shimmering mist. Before them lies the source: a colossal, floating monolith of raw Lattice, humming with the pure, open frequency.
Oh, it's you! The heart of the song... it's beautiful!
And completely unguarded. Don't let that fool you. The Tonal Orders would burn cities to keep this secret.
A Trade Negotiator's barge approaches. Fast. They've been tracking us.
My friends! What a fortunate crossing. I see you've found a... singular asset. He's still single, isn't he? The knowledge, I mean. Unclaimed. Let's discuss its acquisition.
This isn't a commodity. It's a truth. The Lattice isn't just a tool to be controlled.
All truths have a price. The Orders are already mobilizing. You are one ship. I offer protection, partnership.
He's lying! He just wants to sell the coordinates to the highest bidder!

lines_after.dialogue: The monolith's hum swells, reacting to the choice. The very air vibrates with potential.
The song... it's changing. It's listening.
Whatever you just did, you've rewired the neighborhood. The map's gone blank. The frequency is... free.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator's barge powers weapons. The monolith resonates with possibility. This choice will echo across the Lattice.

choices.text: Surrender the frequency data. Ensure the crew's safety.
choices.consequence: The secret is contained, but monopolized. The status quo hardens.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with unauthorized tones to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Chanida is thwarted. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Broadcast the open frequency to all ships. Break the monopoly.
choices.consequence: Chaos and liberation. Navigation is free, but the Lattice becomes unpredictable.
choices.description: Direct Malee to decipher the monk's recording using crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee overreaches. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Synchronize the ship with the monolith. Become the new source.
choices.consequence: You anchor the frequency, gaining immense influence but becoming a permanent target.
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with market connections to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the merchant pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on the merchant. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market churns like a living thing. The din of barter and gossip rises in a thick, shimmering haze—a thousand conversations blurring into a resonant wall. Crystal lanterns swing overhead, casting fractured light on stalls piled with Lattice-shards, salvaged tech, and imported sky-fruits.
Ugh, my head’s buzzing. How does anyone think straight here? It’s like the whole city is shouting in my ears.
They’re not shouting, they’re negotiating. Every word here has a price. Listen closer—that merchant over there is lying about his crystal purity. Badly.
We should keep moving. This level of ambient noise could mask an approaching resonance ship—or a pickpocket. Stay close.
There’s a pattern beneath the chaos. Each voice adds a note to the market’s chord. If we listen not to the words, but to the spaces between…
A well-dressed man in Tonal Order robes steps into your path, his smile polished but not reaching his eyes. Behind him, a skittish villager wrings her hands.
Ah, travelers! You have the look of those who appreciate… rare opportunities. My associate here has a problem. Perhaps you could lend your ears?

It’s my brother. He went down to the lower Lattice layers to scavenge. He found something—a map, he said. Not a Tonal chart. Something else. Now he’s gone silent. Could you… could you repeat that? Please? I just… I need someone to hear me.

lines_after.dialogue: She’s distraught, poor thing. I, of course, would be happy to facilitate any… retrieval. For a modest finder’s fee. The map she mentions? Likely junk. But family is priceless, no?
A ‘modest fee.’ Right. And the Lattice is made of candy. He wants the map. The brother is just the bait.
Who cares what he wants? Someone’s missing! We have to help!
A non-Tonal map? That violates Order monopoly. This reeks of a trap, or worse, heresy. We should report it.

line.dialogue: Pichit, the choice is yours. How do we respond to this request?

choices.line: Agree to help the villager directly, ignoring the merchant’s offer. (Compassion)
choices.description: Ask Malee to harness harmonic feedback, drawing on scavenger instincts

lines_before.dialogue: You agreed to investigate. The merchant’s smile tightens, but he provides a location: a derelict listening post on the market’s lower rim. The villager leads you through cramped alleys where the market’s roar dulls to a throbbing hum.
He said the map was ‘open.’ That it sang to him. I told him it was forbidden. Why weren’t you careful, you fool…

The post is a small, dome-like structure of cracked crystal. The door hangs ajar. Inside, the air is still and cold. Charts are strewn about, but one large vellum sheet is spread on the central table—covered in intricate, swirling lines that seem to shift in the low light.

Well, I’ll be damned. It’s not a navigation chart. It’s a frequency map. Raw, un-calibrated Lattice resonance signatures. No Order ciphers. This is… it’s irreparable. If the Orders find this, they’ll burn it and the man who made it.
Don’t touch it! The harmonics could be unstable. This is exactly why we have the Tonal Orders—to prevent amateurs from destabilizing the Lattice!
Too late for that. Look.

Chanida points to a corner. A young man lies unconscious, a faint, discordant hum emanating from his body. His fingers are stained with luminous ink. The map beside him seems to pulse in time with his shallow breath.
He didn’t just read the map. He tried to become part of its song. The resonance is feeding back through him.

lines_after.dialogue: Brother! Is he…? Come and take a picture with us. He always said that. Before he’d try something stupid. Please, you have to fix him!
We can’t ‘fix’ a feedback loop. We can break the connection, or try to harmonize with it. Both are incredibly dangerous.
The discordant hum grows louder. Crystalline dust shivers off the walls. Outside, you hear raised voices—the merchant, and others. They’ve followed you.
We’re out of time. The Orders or that profiteer will be here in moments. We need to decide. Now.

line.dialogue: The map is active, the brother is in crisis, and company is coming. What’s our move?

choices.line: Grab the brother and the map and run. Let the experts sort it out later. (Flight)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the map's glowing surface and listen for its song.

line.dialogue: Malee — "I can hear it. The resonance is layered — three distinct frequencies, each pointing somewhere different. Give me a moment to isolate them.
Malee — "Nothing. Either I'm tone-deaf to whatever frequency this thing broadcasts on, or it's already gone silent on us.

choices.line: Attempt to carefully fold the map, breaking its visual field and hopefully the resonance link. (Precision)
choices.description: Pull the villager close and demand he describe exactly what the map "sang" to him, word for word.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "He's describing a harmonic sequence — four ascending tones. That's a resonance key. If we reproduce those frequencies, we can safely read what this map is showing us without triggering another fracture.
Arthit — "He's babbling. Whatever the map did to him scrambled the memory — he can't distinguish the song from the noise in his own head anymore.

choices.line: Have Pichit try to ‘sing’ a counter-frequency, to calm the feedback loop through direct resonance. (Dangerous Empathy)
choices.description: Ignore the warnings and photograph the map's surface with your field camera before the light fades.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Got it. Every line, every pulsing node, captured clean.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

acts.title: The Price of a True Note

lines_before.dialogue: The crowd in Khrueang Market parts slightly, revealing the Trade Negotiator, the Trade Negotiator, standing by a stall of shimmering crystal shards. His smile is a practiced tool.
Ah, the illustrious seekers. I heard whispers you were asking about... open frequencies. A dangerous hobby.
We know you have the map. The one that doesn't just show safe paths, but the Lattice's own raw song. It's real, isn't it?
Real? Oh, it's very real. A cartographic heresy. The Tonal Orders would have my resonator for it. Which means my price is... substantial.
Let me guess. Everything we have, plus our firstborn. Spare us the theatrics. Name your real price.
Perceptive. Very well. Not coin. I need a... distraction. A small riot, near the Eastern Docks. While the enforcers are busy, I'll move certain goods. You cause the commotion, I give you the map.
That's not a transaction, that's arson. We could be exiled. The past is over, but we don't need to burn the present down for a chart.
He means what he says. This isn't a negotiation; it's a test. To see how far we'll bend our own resonance for knowledge.

lines_after.dialogue: Think on it. But not for long. The market's hum waits for no one.
He melts back into the throng, leaving you in the eye of the sonic storm.

line.dialogue: How do we respond to the merchant's demand?

choices.text: Easy: Refuse outright. The map isn't worth innocent chaos. (Pichit's philosophical integrity wins, but the trail goes cold.)
choices.description: Slide a pouch of coin across the table and mention the Tong's name casually.

line.dialogue: The Tong already knows you have it. Sell to us, and they never learn you sold twice.
Great. Now he's sweating AND calling for guards. Subtlety, Malee. Subtlety.

choices.text: Medium: Agree, but plan a non-violent 'distraction'—a resonant overload of market chimes. Risky, but clever. (Chanida's impulsiveness, guided by Arthit's caution.)
choices.description: Grab the merchant by his collar and press him against the map shelves.

line.dialogue: You're right, everything we have is the price. But I meant everything YOU have. Hand it over.
He fainted. He actually fainted. So much for the fearsome negotiator.

choices.text: Hard: Agree, then double-cross him. Steal the map during his own operation. Dangerous, potentially violent. (Malee's cynicism in action.)
choices.description: Lean back, smile, and ask what the map cost *him* — and who he's afraid of.

line.dialogue: That fear in your eyes isn't about coin. Someone wants this
The attempt backfires on the merchant. Hidden debts come due.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision hangs in the air, thick as the market's smell. Suddenly, a panicked the villager stumbles into your group, her eyes wide.
They're coming! Orders' enforcers! They know about the map! They're sealing the market!
A low, authoritative hum cuts through the chatter. Crimson-robed Tonal Order enforcers stride into the square, their resonators emitting a silencing pulse. The merchant is already gone.
We're trapped. The exits are blocked by that harmonic dampening field. Don't get so stressed out... he says, while sweating profusely.
I disagree with his entire approach to life. We don't stay in touch with common sense, do we? Now we're cornered rats.
No. We're a choir. Pichit, you can feel the Lattice under all this noise, right? The true frequency is here, in the chaos. We just have to... sing it back.
The map... it was never an object. It was the principle. Listen. Beneath the fear, the greed... the market's true hum. It's over for their monopoly if we amplify *that*.

lines_after.dialogue: As Pichit begins to vocalize a pure, clear tone that somehow harmonizes with the essence of the place, the enforcers' dampening field wavers. The very crystals of the market stalls begin to hum in sympathy.

The climactic resonance doesn't shatter the Lattice, but it shatters the Order's control, creating a fleeting path through the chaos. The episode ends with your escape, and a new, dangerous truth resonating in the air.

line.dialogue: How do we harness the market's latent resonance to break free?

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with its eternal, grounding tone. Dawn light fractures through the crystalline Lattice far below, painting the metal gantries in cold, sharp colors.
From morning until evening, this place tries to smooth the edges off the world. It makes everything feel... distant.
Ugh, I can’t eat anything. This constant vibration is turning my stomach. How do the Listeners stand it?
They acclimatize. The harmonic is meant to suppress emotional volatility. A necessary precaution at this altitude.
Necessary for them. For us, it's just annoying. We probably can’t finish it all before the meeting anyway. Let's just find this monk.
A figure in ochre robes approaches, their steps measured. The Listener Monk, the Listener monk, bows slightly, his face a mask of calm conflict.
You are early. The dawn chorus in the Lattice was particularly strained today. A sign of... unrest.
Unrest? Or truth straining to be heard?

lines_after.dialogue: The Groundless Movement... they whisper that the Tonal Orders' charts are lies. That the true frequencies would set us free.
Heretical and dangerous. Without the charts, resonance ships shatter.
And yet... I have heard gaps in the official songs. Silences where there should be tone. I requested this meeting because I fear what we are not being told.
So you want us to what? Go poking into silent parts of the world-song?

line.dialogue: The monk hesitates, the Spire's tone making his agitation seem like a distant rumor. 'I have a location. A frequency not on any chart. It is... unstable.'

choices.line: We'll need proper equipment. Let's secure it first.

Chanida — "No, no, that makes it worse. Now it's in my chest too. Everything is humming and I can't find where *I* stop.

choices.line: Tell us the frequency. We'll judge the risk.

Pichit — "The walls are seamless. Whatever drives this, it doesn't want to be found by guests. Or prisoners. Is there a difference here?

the monk fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk leads you to a secluded maintenance gantry, traditionally staffed by the spire's female engineers. The harmonic is thinner here, allowing whispers to carry.
Anywhere you like, he said. And he picks the one place where the Order's oversight is light. Convenient.
What’s she like? The head engineer here? If she's hiding Groundless sympathies, we need to know.
Before the monk can answer, the sharp report of a crystal lock breaking echoes. A figure drops from the latticework above—a Sky Pirate, the sky pirate, grinning wildly.
Well, look what the resonance dragged in! A Listener, consorting with outsiders. Why are you doing this to me? I had a clean sweep planned!
Pirate! The harmonic should have revealed your approach!
You Tonal Order lapdogs only know the songs they teach you. We know the hidden frequencies. The cracks in the world.
And you think that knowledge is just for theft?

lines_after.dialogue: Theft? I'm a liberator! These 'groundless' idiots have the right idea but no guts. The true songs *belong* to everyone.
You profane the Song!
I *listen* to it! Unlike you. And I heard your little secret meeting. That unstable frequency you found? It's a backdoor. A way down.
Down? Through the Lattice?
Anywhere. Anywhere you like. But it's gonna cost you.

line.dialogue: The pirate's eyes glint. The monk is pale, torn. The Spire's tone presses down, demanding resolution.

choices.line: Pay the pirate for the information. Let's see this 'backdoor.'

line.dialogue: That's the trick — drown his frequency before he reads ours," I growl, watching Bandit stagger against the railing, ears ringing.
You've overloaded the console — we're deaf AND blind now," I shout over the shrieking feedback loop consuming the walkway.

line.dialogue: Start talking or I introduce you to the fan housing six stories down," I snarl, my knuckles white against his greasy coat.
He's lighter than I expected — overcorrected —" I lurch forward as Bandit twists free and scrambles up the gantry cables like a rat.

line.dialogue: Two knocks. She knows," I murmur to Arthit as the blast doors groan shut behind us, locking Bandit in the gantry with us.
Three knocks came back — that's not Chanida, that's not the code

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire’s central chamber hums with overwhelming clarity. The Sky Pirate captain, Vex, stands defiant before the exposed control crystal, a shard of unstable resonance in hand.
It’s obvious that your monk friend here knows more than he’s singing. The Tonal Orders didn’t just lose this place. They buried it.
The Spire’s true purpose… it is a lock. And the key is a forbidden frequency. One that could… unmake stability.
Great. So we’ve got a pirate who wants to blow the lock, a monk who’s too scared to touch it, and a world that might fall apart. Anyone here have a better idea?
Why are you doing this to me? To us? You’re treating the whole sky like your personal loot chest!
The Groundless have the right idea! Why float on rules when you can sail on chaos? This shard can crack the lock. We can see what’s really under the Lattice.
The risk is catastrophic. The harmonic damping field here is the only thing containing the potential feedback. If we choose wrong…
Every choice resonates. Do we seek the monk’s guarded truth, the pirate’s destructive freedom, or try to preserve this fragile peace?

line.dialogue: The control crystal interface glows, awaiting input. Three potential frequencies hover in the air, represented by shimmering runes.

choices.line: Trust the Listener’s path. Use the monastic calibration to safely seal the lock.
choices.effect: Preserve stability, but accept hidden truths may remain buried.

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit overreaches. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.line: Attempt a synthesis. Use Pichit’s innate sense to forge a new, stable frequency.
choices.effect: A risky creation that could either harmonize or fracture the field.
