line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
The risk doesn't pay off. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Side with the pirate. Apply the shard’s chaotic resonance to force the lock open.
choices.effect: Unleash unknown forces, potentially freeing or destroying what lies beneath.
choices.description: The pirate steps forward with smuggling routes, ready to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the pirate pulls it off. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
A costly mistake by the pirate. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_after.dialogue: The chosen frequency vibrates through the Spire. The Anchor’s steady tone warps, groaning like a giant under strain. Cracks of light spiderweb across the central crystal.
The whole spire is shaking! What did we just choose?
The lock… it is responding. The barrier between us and the Deep Song is thinning.
That’s the spirit! Now we’re getting somewhere!

acts.title: The Lady of the Deep Song

lines_before.dialogue: The cracked control crystal erupts in a column of solid sound. Within it, a figure condenses from reverberating light—a woman of impossible geometry, her form woven from the Lattice’s fundamental frequencies.
Okay. Who is this lady? And more importantly, is she going to unmake us?
A resonance echo… a consciousness formed from the Anchor’s perpetual tone. A guardian.
She’s… beautiful. And terrifying.
I AM THE ANCHOR’S MEMORY. THE KEEPER OF THE SILENCING TRUTH. YOU HAVE DISTURBED THE PEACE OF FORGETTING.
We seek understanding. Not destruction.
YOUR WORLD IS BUILT ON A QUIET CATASTROPHE. MY SONG MAINTAINS THE AMNESIA. THE GROUNDLESS WOULD REMEMBER, AND IN REMEMBERING, SHATTER.
See? I told you! The truth is down there! When’s he coming—the real past? Let it out!

line.dialogue: The entity, the Lady of the Deep Song, offers not a fight, but a choice. Her form pulses with lethal power, but also profound sorrow. The fate of the memory hangs in the balance.

choices.line: Re-seal the memory. Convince her to restore the lock and return the world to blissful ignorance.
choices.effect: Safety returns, but the conspiracy of silence continues. The Groundless Movement is discredited.
choices.description: Kneel and offer your name to the Lady, inviting her song into your bones, 15 words

line.dialogue: I feel her—every thread of the Silencing woven through my blood, and she *knows* me.
She reaches into my chest and I—I can't breathe, the song is *crushing* me—

choices.line: Absorb the truth. Let the Lady transfer the hidden history directly to your minds, bearing the burden yourselves.
choices.effect: The party gains terrible, empowering knowledge. The Spire stabilizes, but you are forever changed.
choices.description: Draw the anchor shard and command her to speak the truth of what she keeps, 15 words

line.dialogue: YOU WOULD COMMAND MEMORY ITSELF? …Bold. Few have stood before me and demanded rather than begged.
The shard *screams* in your hand—she recoils, and the deep song shatters into discordant wailing.

choices.line: Shatter the Anchor. Side with the pirate and the Groundless. Break the keeper and broadcast the raw truth to all floating cities.
choices.effect: Unleash chaos and revelation. The world will know what happened, but may not survive the knowing.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to sing back to the Lady, matching her frequency as a counterpoint, 15 words

line.dialogue: I—I can feel where her song breaks. There's *grief* underneath. She's not just memory—she's *mourning*.
My voice cracks against hers and the resonance turns wrong, *wrong*—she's angry now, the water is rising—

lines_after.dialogue: The decision resonates through the Spire and out into the Lattice itself. A harmonic shockwave ripples across the sky, visible from every floating city.
SO BE IT. THE SONG… CHANGES.
The Listeners will hear this. Everything changes now.
Heh. He winked at me. The old world, I mean. On its way out.
We have chosen our resonance. Now we must live within the new song we have created.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Echo's Mercy' cuts through the shimmering Lattice below, its crystal resonators humming a low, steady chord. The wind carries the scent of ozone and distant rain.
Look at it all! The Lattice shifts like a living thing. Why were you gone so long, Pichit? Staring at the edge again?
The patterns... they're not random. There's a rhythm beneath the chaos. A memory of sound.
Great. The philosopher's contemplating the hum. Meanwhile, our supplies are low, and the Tonal Orders charge a fortune for the next chart update.
We should be cautious. The readings show anomalous resonance echoes ahead. Uncharted.
You're not going anywhere near those echoes, are you? My cousin's ship vanished near there. The 'Sundered Chorus'. Never found.
A lost ship? What took you so long to mention that?
The Lattice remembers all songs, even those that end abruptly. The 'Sundered Chorus'... its final note still lingers. Are you going to seek it?

lines_after.dialogue: A ship that vanished... its echo remains. That's not natural decay. It's a sustained frequency.
Or a very expensive trap. The Tonal Orders don't like competition.
The decision is yours, Pichit. The course is unclear.

line.dialogue: The villager's warning hangs in the air. The Monk's curiosity is palpable. Do we investigate the anomaly?

choices.text: Steer toward the echo. The mystery calls.

Arthit yanks me back.* "Your neural readings just spiked into the red — pull your hand back before the Lattice rewrites your synapses!

The dampener shrieks and dies.* *Malee kicks the melted housing.* "So the Lattice eats dampeners. Wonderful. Next brilliant idea from the cautious one

lines_before.dialogue: The ship's hum changes key, vibrating through the deck as you approach the coordinates. A faint, discordant tone seeps from the Lattice itself.
Sensors confirm it. A permanent resonance scar. Where did the 'Sundered Chorus' lose its harmony? The point of impact should be... here.
Nothing. No debris. Just that awful, stuck sound. I'm trying to lose the headache it's giving me.
There! A glint below! Not wreckage... a resonator crystal. Still active!
It's singing a single, trapped note. The ship's final frequency. This isn't an accident. This is a recording.
A memory made manifest. The Lattice has preserved its death cry. I must insist we listen. Truly listen.
I'm glad to know you found something, but this feels wrong. Dead ships should stay dead.
The salvaged crystal thrums in Arthit's hands, projecting a ghostly, fractured image onto the mist—a ship's deck, frozen in a moment of terror.

lines_after.dialogue: The image... it's not just the ship. There are figures. They're not running. They're... reaching out.
Towards what? There's nothing there!
Towards a silence. A perfect, absolute silence that should not exist within the Lattice.

line.dialogue: The crystal's echo shows the crew's final moments, drawn to an impossible void. The Monk insists on deeper study. What do we do with this haunted frequency?

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.

choices.text: Sync our ship's resonator to the crystal's frequency. Play the 'Sundered Chorus's' final note back into the Lattice.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship cuts through the crystalline lattice below, its engine humming a low, steady tone. The wind carries a faint, discordant melody—the echo of the lost ship that vanished decades ago during The Silencing.
The Lattice's song... it's fractured here. The lost ship's resonance lingers like a scar. You can ask the wind, but it only answers with ghosts.
Ghosts? I'm gonna ask him—the skycity elder said the ship's captain was a Singer who defied the Tonal Orders. What if his song is still trapped?
Trapped songs and monastic riddles. The Tonal Orders probably silenced him for good. I wanna ask you something, Monk—why are you helping us if your order answers to them?
Because the truth has its own resonance. The lost ship's echo... it holds a frequency the Orders have buried. You can try asking the lattice directly, but it requires a Singer's touch.
Direct contact with an unstable lattice zone? The ship's resonator is already straining. We should chart a safer path.
But if the echo holds answers about The Silencing... perhaps we must listen to what was meant to be forgotten. The wind carries more than just sound—it carries memory.
Memory? My granddad said that ship screamed before it vanished. You're not actually thinking of following that noise, are you?

lines_after.dialogue: The discordant melody grows clearer—a haunting chorus of crystal vibrations and a human voice, frozen in time.
That's not just an echo... it's a distress call. The Singer is still singing. Or... what's left of him.
Wonderful. We've found a dead man's lullaby. This subplot just got a lot more literal.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship plunges into the luminous spiral. The lattice parts not into open sky, but into a memory—a ghostly reconstruction of the lost ship's final moments, superimposed over reality.
Resonance overlap! We're experiencing his last navigation. I know this is dangerous, but I don't know where to begin stabilizing us.
Look—the ghost captain. He's not just navigating. He's trying to warn someone. I already know that expression... it's the same fear our records describe before The Silencing.
By the Lattice... he's pointing at the skycities. My ancestors said the Orders called his song 'heresy.' I don't know either if we should be seeing this.
His song—it's a pattern! A navigation chart for somewhere the Orders forbade. He died to preserve this.
Preserve it for who? Dead Singers make poor messengers. Unless... he knew someone would eventually listen.
He preserved it for the truth. The Silencing wasn't just a catastrophe—it was a suppression. This chart leads to what they tried to erase.

The ghost captain turns toward your ship. His mouth moves, forming silent words that vibrate through the crystal lattice itself: 'FOLLOW THE NOTE THAT BREAKS THE CHAIN.' Then, the memory begins to collapse.

lines_after.dialogue: The luminous spiral implodes into a single, piercing frequency that cracks the lattice below. Your ship is thrown back into normal space, forever changed.
The echo is gone. The truth remains. The Captain's final note... it's etched into our resonator crystal. The Tonal Orders will know we've seen it.

line.dialogue: The ghost captain's chart is now imprinted on your ship's crystal. The Tonal Orders will detect this 'heresy.' How do you navigate forward?

choices.text: Hide the chart's resonance, returning to the skycity quietly to plan.
choices.description: Trace the captain's finger-path against the stars with your own hand, matching his ghostly gesture exactly, 15 words

line.dialogue: The resonance locked—I can read his heading now. He was charting a route *through* the skycities, not to them.
The resonance collapsed. Whatever frequency he was broadcasting on, I lost it—his hand moved too fast for me to follow.

choices.text: Share the chart with the Listeners, seeking their protection and wisdom.
choices.description: Sing the captain's song pattern back to him, note for note, using Chanida's recorded fragment as your guide, 15 words

line.dialogue: He heard me—he *turned*. The pattern isn't a map, it's a key. He's been waiting for someone to sing it back.
I hit the wrong interval and the pattern shattered. He's fading—the song was the only thing holding him here.

choices.text: Follow the chart immediately toward the forbidden coordinates, embracing the consequences.
choices.description: Grab the ghost captain's wrist where he points skyward and force your resonance into direct contact with his, 15 words

line.dialogue: I touched him. He isn't lost—he's *anchored*. Deliberately. Someone chained his soul to this navigation chart as a warning.
His wrist passed through mine like cold smoke. Whatever holds him here, it won't let a living hand make contact.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard stretches before you, a jagged horizon of dead ships. The air tastes of ozone and rust. Distant hammers ring against crystal hulls, creating a chaotic symphony that makes the Lattice below shimmer uneasily.
Every broken resonator here has a story... a final note it failed to sing. What do you think they heard when they fell?
Probably the sound of their captain's bad decisions. Let's focus on finding a working coupling, not composing elegies for scrap.
We should stick to the marked paths. Unstable harmonics from all this metal could attract... unwanted attention.
Unwanted attention is exactly what we need! Look—that old Singer over by the crusher looks like she's seen things. Let's ask her!
You shouldn't be poking around here. The Tonal Orders have patrols. And the Groundless... they whisper in the shadowed hulls. Why are you doing this to me? Asking questions that get folks noticed?
We're just travelers. The path ahead... anywhere. Anywhere you like. We follow the resonance.
What's she like, this 'Groundless' contact we're supposedly meeting? Another idealist who thinks humming at crystals will change the world?

lines_after.dialogue: The villager points a greasy finger toward the skeleton of a massive ore-hauler. A single, pure tone hums from within its ribs—an anomaly in the acoustic chaos.
That's a deliberate frequency. Not random engine noise. Someone's down there.
See? Adventure! Let's go see who's singing!

line.dialogue: The path to the ore-hauler is treacherous, littered with sharp debris and humming with unstable residual energy.

choices.text: Send Chanida ahead to scout the quickest, noisiest route.
choices.description: Sneak toward the flickering resonator Chanida spotted, keeping low along the collapsed harmonic shielding, 15 words

line.dialogue: Quiet—yes! This resonator's still cycling. Whoever wrecked this place left in a hurry." — Chanida
My boot caught a decayed frequency plate. The whole corridor just sang our position to everything here." — Arthit

choices.text: Have Malee and Arthit analyze the debris field for acoustically stable pathways.
choices.description: Repair the nearest damaged resonator using Pichit's tuning kit to mask your team's harmonic signature, 15 words

line.dialogue: There—she's humming again. Broken thing was always meant to sing. Now she sings for us." — Pichit
I bridged the wrong resonance gap. It screamed instead of sang, and now everything knows we're here." — Pichit

choices.text: Follow Pichit's lead, moving slowly and listening to the subtle shifts in the ambient sound.
choices.description: Follow Arthit's marked path through the eastern corridor, ignoring Chanida's discovery and pressing toward the extraction point, 15 words

line.dialogue: The marked path holds. Sometimes boring decisions are the ones that keep your team breathing." — Arthit
The marked path wasn't marked for us. Someone herded us here—and we walked right into the trap." — Malee

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the hollowed ship, the world outside fades. The air is still, charged with the memory of flight. Strange, woven tapestries depicting soundwaves hang from the rusted beams. A figure kneels before a shattered resonator, hands hovering over its facets.
The patrols don't come here. The sound... it grieves them. I thought it was okay to hide here. Now I know... it's more than hiding.
You're not just a pirate. You're listening.
Sky pirate, listener, Groundless... labels. The Lattice doesn't care. It only answers to truth. My crew... we found a frequency. A clean one, not on any Tonal chart. They called it heresy.
Let me guess. The Orders 'confiscated' your ship and your charts, and now you're scrapyard royalty.
They silenced my resonator. Killed the note. But the echo... I can still feel it here. In this place of dead songs, keeping the echo alive... it's the best way. The only way to remember what's real.
This is about the subplot_groundless movement. You're preserving forbidden harmonics.
That's amazing! You're fighting back with music! Can you teach us?

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate stands, revealing a crude device wired into the dead ship's console—a resonator salvaged from a dozen wrecks. It pulses with a faint, unstable light.
The echo is weak. It needs a catalyst. A pure note to wake it up. But if I'm wrong... the wrong frequency could shatter every crystal in this yard.
Every end is a beginning. Even a shattered song has fragments of the original melody.

line.dialogue: The pirate's makeshift resonator is fragile. Activating it requires a precise input, but the risk of a catastrophic harmonic feedback loop is real.

choices.text: Have Chanida try to sing the note she feels is right. (Rely on instinct)
choices.description: Ask Malee to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on leg resonance

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The lattice has other plans. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Let Malee and Arthit attempt to calculate a stable frequency based on the resonator's salvage components. (Rely on analysis)
choices.description: Have Chanida focus crystal hearing on the clanging metal to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida hits a wall. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Ask Pichit to meditate and 'listen' for the lost note within the silence of the wreck. (Rely on faith)
choices.description: Have the pirate risk using secret frequencies to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the pirate hits a wall. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends into the deep chasms of the Tha Khwae Scrapyard, where the oldest, most forbidden wrecks are piled. The metallic din is oppressive, a physical wall of noise.
Perfect. A symphony of industrial decay. I can feel my fillings vibrating.
Stay alert. This is prime ambush territory. The structural integrity is... questionable.
There! That old Singer's skiff from the stories! It has to be the one the Groundless use!
Its hull is scored with Lattice-burn... but the core resonator looks intact. A vessel that remembers true song.
As you approach, a group of Skycity Residents, faces etched with fear, step from behind a shattered engine block, blocking your path.
You can't be here. The Tonal Orders... they'll hear. They'll silence this whole sector.
It's not that we seek to bring danger. We seek an echo. A truth buried since the Silencing.

line.dialogue: The villagers are terrified, but one, a younger woman, holds a cracked resonance crystal that hums a weak, pure tone. She looks at Pichit with desperate hope.

choices.line: [Sing a Harmony] Let your own resonance harmonize with the crystal's weak tone, demonstrating shared purpose.
choices.outcome_line: The crystal's light brightens. The villagers' fear softens into awe. 'A true Singer...' one whispers, and they part.
choices.description: Pry open the skiff's maintenance hatch with your combat knife to inspect the core directly, 15 words

line.dialogue: The Lattice channels are intact—if I reroute through the secondary manifold, she'll sing again.
The burn corroded the housing. Touch anything wrong and we lose the core permanently.

choices.line: [Argue Pragmatics] Appeal to their desire for safety. The Tonal Orders are coming regardless; hiding only delays the inevitable.
choices.outcome_line: The logic hits home. The villagers exchange grim nods. 'You're right. Since that day they took our ancestors' charts, we've only been hiding,' their leader concedes, stepping aside.
choices.description: Circle the perimeter first, mapping structural weak points and potential sniper nests in the gantry, 15 words

line.dialogue: Three sightlines, one choke point. If someone's waiting for us, they're in the northeast crane.
I counted the angles wrong—there's a blind spot behind the compressor stacks we didn't cover.

choices.line: [Challenge Their Fear] Ask what they truly protect by cowering. A memory? Or just the emptiness fear leaves behind?
choices.outcome_line: The question hangs in the clanging air. The woman with the crystal straightens. '...smiling happily. My grandmother sang of the ground. Not of fear.' She leads you to the skiff.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the hull and listen for the Singer's resonance through the metal, 15 words

line.dialogue: You hear it? That low hum... she remembers what she was. The stories were true.
Nothing. Either the resonance has faded or the stories were more poetry than truth.

lines_after.dialogue: Inside the derelict skiff, the air is still and charged. Ancient murals depict Singers guiding flocks of ships, not through the Lattice, but over a vast, green world.
These schematics... this vessel wasn't just for travel. It was a mobile resonator, designed to... calm the Lattice. To communicate.
So the 'Silencing' wasn't an accident. It was a conversation that went very, very wrong.
And the Tonal Orders' charts are just a crude muzzle! This is what the Groundless want to rebuild!

lines_before.dialogue: A dissonant shriek of overloading engines splits the air. A heavily modified pirate cutter, bristling with illegal sonic disruptors, slams down, blocking the only exit. Sky Pirates leap from its hull.
Well, well. Diggin' up forbidden history. The Tonal Orders pay a fortune for that kind of trouble. Or... we just take the shiny bits ourselves.
Their disruptors are tuned to cause catastrophic harmonic feedback. If they fire near these old crystal banks...
They would destroy the very truth they hope to sell. Violence is a poor merchant.
Spare me the philosophy, Singer. (He)'s been married twice to this game. I know which bonds break easiest.
The lead pirate gestures. His crew powers up their disruptors, aiming not at you, but at the unstable piles of crystal-laden wreckage surrounding the ancient skiff.
They're not here to fight. They're here to erase. Standard monopolist procedure.
We can't let them! That skiff is the key to everything!

line.dialogue: The pirates' weapons whine to a critical pitch. The fragile history around you is moments from being shattered into meaningless noise.

choices.line: [Overload the Environment] Use a resonance pulse on the scrapyard's own machinery, triggering a deafening but harmless cacophony of alarms and steam vents to create cover.
choices.outcome_line: The yard erupts in a blinding, deafening chaos. The pirates are disoriented. You drag the crucial crystal core from the skiff and escape into the din.
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with tattooed routes, ready to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: [Turn Their Weapons] Sing a counter-frequency that hijacks the pirates' disruptor feedback, turning their own weapons into unstable, shrieking anchors.
choices.outcome_line: The disruptors scream and seize, locking the pirate cutter in place with violent vibrations. 'I don't want people knowing we got beat by a lullaby!' the captain snarls as you make your getaway.
choices.description: Malee uses crystal prosthetic to decipher the monk's recording near the broken ships

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee hits a wall. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: [Reveal the Truth] Broadcast the skiff's recovered murals and data on a broad frequency—to the pirates, the Tonal Orders, everyone. Make the secret impossible to contain.
choices.outcome_line: Images of the lost world flood local channels. The pirates reel, their purpose undone. The Groundless signal their thanks. The secret is out, and the Lattice itself seems to hum in response, a new tension born.
choices.description: The villager attempts to decode the tonal pattern, relying on local knowledge

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Things don't go as planned. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_after.dialogue: In the aftermath, the scrapyard is changed. Some wrecks hum with new, strange harmonies. The pirates have fled, their mission a failure.
The data is propagating. We've ignited a schism in the world's understanding. The Tonal Orders will respond with force.
Let them. A monopoly's worst enemy isn't a competitor. It's a bad review, and we just gave their entire service model one.
We did it! The Groundless have their proof! The song isn't over!
No. It has only just resumed. We have reminded the world of the first verse. Now, we must learn the next.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow is a jagged crack in the floating island's underbelly, leading into a cavern where the air hums with a low, crystalline frequency.
Whoa... listen to that. It's like the whole cave is singing. I'm right, aren't I? This has to be a natural resonator.
Or it's the island's indigestion. Don't get too excited. These echoes could mask anything.
Caution is warranted. The acoustics are... unstable. One wrong note could bring the ceiling down.
Yet within instability, there is pattern. These echoes aren't random. They're a memory, trapped in stone.
We don't come down here. Not since the *Echo* started. Sounds like a lost ship, crying in the dark. It might be true. The old tales.
Deeper in, the walls smooth into pre-Silencing masonry. Faded murals depict ships diving into a crystalline sea.
Look! Scorch marks and... is that a broken resonator? Something bad happened here.

lines_after.dialogue: Told you. Not a playboy's pleasure cruise. This is a tomb.
The structural harmonics are degrading. We must proceed with extreme care.
A tomb, or a library? The truth is in the echo. We have to listen.

line.dialogue: The path splits: a wide, echoing gallery ahead, a narrow fissure to the left humming with strange resonance, and a collapsed tunnel to the right with recent digging marks.

choices.text: Take the wide gallery. It's the clearest path.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the vibrating wall and feel for rhythm beneath the noise, 14 words

line.dialogue: There—beneath the chaos, a pulse. Three beats, silence, three again. The stone is *breathing*.
Pull your hand back! The vibration just spiked—you'd have fractured fingers if you'd held that contact two more seconds.

choices.text: Squeeze through the narrow fissure. The resonance feels... intentional.
choices.description: Drop a stone down the eastern passage and count the seconds before it stops bouncing, 16 words

line.dialogue: Four seconds, then nothing. Not a bottom—something *caught* it. Something down there is listening back.
It didn't stop. It just... kept going. The sound got thinner, like it fell through the cave floor itself.

choices.text: Investigate the dug-out tunnel. Someone's been here recently.
choices.description: Hum a single sustained note matching the cave's dominant frequency and let it resonate through your chest, 17 words

line.dialogue: The walls just answered you. Same note, same length. We're not in a cave—we're inside an instrument.
Wrong pitch. The dissonance is making the ceiling shed rock—move, NOW, before the whole corridor comes down on us!

lines_before.dialogue: The narrow fissure opens into a vast, spherical chamber. At its center, half-buried in crystal growths, lies the shattered hull of a Resonance Ship—the *Echo of the Lost*.
By the Lattice... its resonator core is still active, but feedback-looped. It's probably been broadcasting its final moments for decades.
Great. So we have to finish its homework? Figure out how it died so the ghost shuts up?
It's not a ghost! It's a... recording. In the crystal. We probably have to sync with its frequency to see what happened.
A soul imprinted on sound. To understand its end is to honor its journey.
A rough laugh echoes. A group of Sky Pirates emerges from shadows behind crystalline formations.
Well, well. Listeners beat us to the prize. The ship's log is worth a fortune in forbidden charts. You look run down. Hand over your resonators, and maybe you won't join the echo.
They're using dampeners. I... I can't hear the lattice properly. We're deafened.

lines_after.dialogue: Pirates. I probably have a knife with their name on it.
We have to finish this! Sync with the ship before they blast the core to scrap!
The ship's truth is vulnerable. We must protect its final song.

line.dialogue: The pirates are advancing, their dampeners creating a dead zone. The ship's damaged core flickers, its mournful frequency vulnerable.

choices.text: Fight the pirates directly. Break their dampeners to restore your hearing.
choices.description: Press your palm against the resonator crystal and let the recording flood your senses.

line.dialogue: I see it now—static, silence, then the captain's final words echoing through me like they were mine.
The resonance rejected you. Your heartbeat wasn't... compatible. It needs someone who already carries grief.

choices.text: Rush to the ship's core. Try to manually initiate the playback sequence before the pirates stop you.
choices.description: Cross-reference the ship's log fragments with the resonator's frequency signature to find the exact moment of failure.

line.dialogue: There—the waveform spikes here. The core didn't overload. Someone *deliberately* pushed it past tolerance. This was sabotage.
Great, the logs are corrupted too. Half the data is just the ship screaming at itself in loops. We're chasing echoes.

choices.text: Use the chamber's acoustics against them. Shout a discordant note to shatter the fragile crystals near them.
choices.description: Sing a single sustained note into the crystal chamber to harmonize with the imprint and coax it forward.

line.dialogue: I didn't expect that to work. The crystal is... answering. There's a voice beneath the static—a woman, repeating coordinates
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves deeper into the cavern, the air growing colder. The walls here are smooth, carved by ancient hands, and covered in faint, glowing glyphs that pulse with a slow, deep hum.
These glyphs... they're not just decoration. They're a frequency map. A navigation chart for something buried here.
A chart for a ghost ship. I have something to tell you. The echoes we've been hearing aren't just random. They're a distress signal, looped for centuries.
Do you know what this is? That central glyph... it looks like a resonator, but huge. Way bigger than anything on our ship.
It's a tomb. Or a cradle. The ancients didn't just travel on the Lattice; they built within it. He's a nice person, the one who designed this. They wanted harmony, not conquest.
Harmony's dead. Treasure's alive. We followed you in. The Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for this map. Or we could just take the prize ourselves.
Please, don't fight! The Hollow shakes when there's violence. The whole island could crack!

A low, grinding moan reverberates through the chamber. From a dark side passage, a pale, crystalline light begins to seep out, carrying the faint, distorted sound of creaking timber and snapping sails.

lines_after.dialogue: The light from the passage solidifies, forming the translucent, spectral outline of a massive Resonance Ship's prow, lodged in the crystal of the cavern wall.
The Echo of the Lost Ship. It's not just a story. It's here, fused into the Lattice itself.
Its resonator is still active... at a frequency that's destabilizing the local crystal structure. That's why the island is unstable.

line.dialogue: The spectral ship flickers. The pirates tense, weapons ready. The central glyph on the wall begins to resonate in response to the ghost ship's frequency.

choices.text: Calm the Frequency: Use your own ship's resonator to emit a counter-harmony, stabilizing the glyph and pacifying the echo. (Requires technical skill)
choices.description: Trace the central glyph with your fingertip, feeling for residual energy beneath the carved surface.

line.dialogue: * "It's warm—pulsing even. This isn't dead script, it's a heartbeat mapped in stone.
* "Nothing. Just cold rock under my skin. Either the power's gone, or it never wanted me to touch it.

choices.text: Decode the Map: Quickly interpret the glyphs to find the exact safe frequency to 'release' the ghost ship without causing a collapse. (Requires scholarly knowledge)
choices.description: Demand Malee speak now—whatever she's been hiding about the ghost ship ends here.

line.dialogue: * "My grandmother sailed this route. She came back changed—whispering about a cradle that births echoes. I didn't believe her until this moment.
* "I... I can't. Not here. The walls have ears older than my family's shame, and I won't feed them.

choices.text: Direct Negotiation: Address the echo itself, using the principles of the Listeners to communicate with the trapped consciousness of the lost vessel. (Requires empathy and courage)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to clarify—tomb or cradle, because the difference determines whether they proceed.

line.dialogue: Pichit
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber trembles. The ghost ship's outline becomes sharper, more real. The air fills with the cacophony of its final moments: a scream of crystal, a chorus of lost voices.
The prices are reasonable! The treasure on that ship must be! We're cutting it free! Try it on, this new resonator we stole!
You look run down. You're all exhausted! This is too much! The island will shatter!
They're going to blast it loose! That'll tear the Hollow apart! We have to stop them or... redirect it!
Redirect? Into what? The Lattice below? That could cause a chain reaction, a new Silencing!
Or into the sky. Let the ghost sail into the void. It's reasonably priced—the cost is just letting go of a history that wants to be free.
No. It doesn't want to be free. It wants to be heard. It's been screaming into the stone for ages. We have to listen, and answer.
The pirates' resonator whines to life, a jagged, violent sound. The ghost ship's crystal form begins to crack, luminous fragments peeling away. The cavern groans, deep fissures racing up the walls.

lines_after.dialogue: The resonance of your choice fills the Hollow, intertwining with the ghost ship's final song. The crystal either stabilizes, releases, or transforms.

The Echo of the Lost Ship resolves. Its form either dissolves into peaceful silence, ascends as a shimmering beacon into the sky, or merges with the living Lattice, becoming a new, permanent harmonic landmark.
The pirates are either subdued by the overwhelming harmony, fled in terror, or inspired to abandon their plunder. The villagers witness the event, and their view of the Lattice is forever changed.

line.dialogue: The moment of climax. The ghost ship's core frequency is exposed, vulnerable, and resonant. Your action will define its fate and the fate of The Hollow.

choices.text: Harmonic Integration: Sing a unifying frequency that allows the ghost ship to gently dissipate, its energy soothing the fractured cavern. The Hollow is saved, but the mystery is laid to rest. (Safe, compassionate)
choices.description: Rush the blasting crew and jam their firing mechanism with my knife, 15 words

line.dialogue: The mechanism's dead — we bought ourselves time, but they'll come looking.
You're too slow — the charge is lit, get back, get BACK!

choices.text: Catalytic Release: Channel the ship's energy upward, creating a spectacular crystalline eruption that carries the echo skyward, becoming a new navigational star. The Hollow is damaged but famous. (Dramatic, risky)
choices.description: Channel resonance into the Lattice to redirect the blast upward into open water, 15 words

line.dialogue: The Lattice held — it's shaking but intact, and the blast went wide!
Too much resonance — the Lattice is cracking, I can hear it splintering underneath us!

choices.text: Synthesis: Merge the ghost ship's resonance with the ancient glyphs, creating a permanent, living archive within the Lattice itself. The Hollow becomes a sacred, unstable place of immense power and danger. (Transformative, profound)
choices.description: Negotiate with the bandit crew — offer them the ship's cargo if they stop, 15 words

line.dialogue: Fine. The cargo splits fair, and nobody touches the Hollow. You've got nerve.
Bandit

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whisper' breaches the edge of the Silent Zone. The usual hum of the crystal resonators dies abruptly, replaced by a vacuum of sound.
What did you say? I can't hear my own heartbeat. This is wrong.
Caution. The Lattice here is inert. Our charts are useless. How shall we put it... we are blind.
The Tonal Orders swore this place was myth. Another lie to control the 'known' world. Could you repeat that? I'm talking to myself.
A silence that listens back. This dead zone holds answers about The Silencing. How can I say it... it feels intentional.
A jagged outcrop of black crystal rises from the Lattice surface—a makeshift shelter. A figure watches from its shadow.
You're loud in the wrong ways. Your ship's silence screams. Outsiders. What do you seek in the deadlands?
Understanding. The truth beneath the silence.

lines_after.dialogue: Truth is a scavenger's meal—scraps and risk. I know surfaces. The Lattice here... it doesn't sing, but it remembers. How shall I put it? It's scarred.
Scars lead to stories. We need to navigate. Can you help?
Help has a price. I've seen a Listener monk, wandering the dead zone, muttering to the unmoving crystals. He might know more. Or he's mad.
The scavenger points toward a fissure in the Lattice, a dark crack leading deeper into the unnatural quiet.

line.dialogue: The scavenger offers guidance, but distrust hangs in the silent air.

choices.line: Pay the scavenger with spare resonator crystals (resource loss).
choices.description: Direct Malee to calibrate against the frequency using engineering

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee overreaches. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Offer to share future discoveries from the zone (potential alliance).
choices.description: Arthit attempts to confront hidden knowledge, relying on lattice storms

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit is thwarted. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.line: Decline and proceed cautiously alone (higher risk).
choices.description: The scavenger channels platform climbing toward the danger, hoping to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the scavenger pulls it off. The scavenger spots a resource others overlook.
the scavenger misreads the situation. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: The fissure descends into a cavern of frozen crystal. No resonance, no echo. The party's whispers are swallowed instantly.
My instruments are dead. I have bad vision in this silence. We must rely on instinct.
Instinct? The second option is panic. I made this lantern by myself. It uses stored light, not sound. A small victory.
There! A glow ahead. Not crystal... a campfire?
Near a small fire, a robed Listener monk sits, tracing patterns in the dust. He looks up, eyes wide with a mix of reverence and fear.
You hear it too? The absence? I have listened for years. The song here... it was cut. I did the research all myself.
Cut by what? The Silencing?
By design. My Order forbids speaking of it. But I found fragments... an Open Frequency Map. A chart of all possible resonances, including those that... unmade the world.

lines_after.dialogue: A map that the Tonal Orders would burn. Where is it?
Hidden. The second option is to destroy it. But knowledge... it has a weight. I carry it myself, and it is crushing.
This map could let us navigate the Silent Zone. Or it could be a weapon.
We need it. The scavenger said you were muttering to the crystals. What were you saying?
Apologies. To the dead Lattice. For the sin of knowing.

line.dialogue: The monk is torn between protecting a dangerous truth and sharing it.

choices.line: Convince him his duty is to preserve knowledge, not hide it (persuasion).
choices.description: Approach the campfire slowly, hand on weapon, signaling the others to stay behind you, 15 words

line.dialogue: I count one figure — seated, not moving. Its posture is wrong, like something drained the will from it.
The fire flickers without wind. Without sound. My lantern gutters in response and I smell something sweet rotting beneath the smoke.

choices.line: Offer to take the burden—to carry the map yourselves (responsibility).
choices.description: Stop the group and sit in the monk's listening posture, trying to hear what the silence actually is, 15 words

line.dialogue: Yes. The absence has a shape. It is not empty — it is full of everything we refuse to hear.
I try but my thoughts scatter like fish from a shadow. The silence presses against my skull until my ears ring with false sound.

choices.line: Threaten to expose his heresy to the Listeners if he doesn't cooperate (intimidation).
choices.description: Take the lantern from Malee and hold it ahead like an offering, calling out a greeting to the fire, 15 words

line.dialogue: The figure turns — its face is mine. Older. Tired. It mouths my name but I hear nothing. Nothing at all.
My voice dies three feet from my lips. The fire bends away from us as if repelled, and the glow shrinks to a dying ember.

lines_before.dialogue: The party huddles in the scavenger's makeshift shelter, a precarious dome of salvaged resonator plating. The unnatural quiet outside presses in, making every breath sound thunderous.
You're fools for staying. The quiet here... it doesn't just mute sound. It mutes thought. Makes you forget the shape of your own voice.
We sought the truth of the Silencing. Our Order's texts spoke of a 'Great Stillness' at the world's heart. It might be true... this place is that heart.
So what? We just sit here until we forget how to talk? We need to *move*. That weird map Pichit found has to lead somewhere!
Lead to our graves, probably. It's served with a side of existential dread and a heaping portion of 'we shouldn't be here.'
The monk is right. This isn't natural erosion. It's... surgical. Something excised the Lattice's response here. But why leave a map?
A map implies a destination. Or a warning. The Open Frequency... it wasn't a navigational chart. It was a diagram of a cage.

lines_after.dialogue: While Arthit and the monk debate, Chanida slips outside, drawn by a faint, almost imperceptible vibration in the plating. She presses her ear to it.
From the other side of a thin wall, the low, tense voices of the Scavenger and the Monk carry through the metal.
...the Tonal Orders didn't just lose ships here. They *buried* something. The Quiet isn't an accident. It's a lock.
And the key is the Open Frequency. My brothers would call this heresy. To think our entire study of the Song... was just listening to the bars of the prison.
Chanida's eyes widen. She motions frantically for the others to listen.

line.dialogue: The secret is out. The Silent Zone is a prison, not a dead zone. The map is the key. But using it could break the lock... and release what's inside.

choices.line: Confront the Monk and Scavenger. Demand the full truth, using the tension to force a clearer explanation.
choices.outcome: They reveal the prison's nature was known to a few; the 'something' inside is a raw, chaotic resonance from the Silencing.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Defeat. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Decipher the map quietly. Use the party's combined skills to trace the 'Open Frequency' to its source point within the Zone.
choices.outcome: You pinpoint a location—a sunken resonator spire at the Zone's center. The map is a schematic to activate it.
choices.description: Pichit attempts to confront hidden knowledge, relying on Listener training

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The resonance turns hostile. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.line: Propose sealing the prison further. Use the ship's resonator to flood the area with a damping frequency, making the silence permanent.
choices.outcome: The Monk is horrified; this destroys any chance of understanding the Silencing. The Scavenger agrees it's the safest path.
choices.description: The scavenger volunteers to follow the dissonant trail, leveraging survival skills

line.dialogue: the scavenger makes it work. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the scavenger overreaches. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: At the center of the Silent Zone stands a colossal, fractured resonator spire, half-sunk into the unresponsive Lattice. The air hums with pent-up pressure.
The Great Stillness... it was a containment field. This spire wasn't for travel. It was a needle, sewing the wound in the world shut after the Silencing.
And your map is the thread-puller. Activate that frequency, and you undo the stitch. What pours out? The true Song? Or the scream that broke the world?
The structural resonance is unstable. Activating it could cause a catastrophic sympathetic fracture in the local Lattice. Our ship might not survive the backlash.
Fantastic. So our options are: leave the creepy cosmic bandage alone, or rip it off and see if the patient bleeds out. I'm not a playboy, I don't like these odds.
We didn't come all this way to whisper and leave! This is it! The truth is *right there*! Is the pay good for a lifetime of wondering 'what if'? No!
Chanida is right, in her way. A choice made in fear is no choice at all. But neither is one made in blind curiosity. We must choose the health of our future understanding.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the dead air. The spire's ancient crystal facets begin to glow with a faint, internal light, reacting to the proximity of the Open Frequency map.
A low, sub-auditory thrum starts in the bones, not the ears. The very ground of the Silent Zone begins to tremble. The lock is straining.
Whatever happens next... it was a good experience. To stand here, at the edge of the world's oldest secret.
The party shares a look. A final choice. The Monk clutches his ears, tears in his eyes. The Scavenger grips her weapon, ready for whatever comes next.

line.dialogue: The prison door is trembling. The Open Frequency is the key. Do you turn it? The consequences will redefine the Lattice, the Orders, and your place in the world.

choices.line: Activate the Spire. Unleash the buried frequency. Confront the raw truth of the Silencing, whatever it may be.
choices.outcome: A torrent of primal, chaotic sound erupts, but within it, a pure, foundational Tone. The Silent Zone shatters. The world's Song changes forever. You have rewritten history.
choices.description: Activate the map's frequency and brace for the resonance collapse, 15 words exactly

line.dialogue: The field is folding inward — hold your ground, the thread is pulling true!
The resonance spiked — I told you, I *told* you the structure couldn't hold!

choices.line: Record the Frequency but do not activate. Use the data to shatter the Tonal Orders' monopoly, freeing knowledge without unleashing chaos.
choices.outcome: You leave the prison sealed but steal the key. You return as revolutionaries. The Orders hunt you, but the map's knowledge spreads. A slow, political upheaval begins.
choices.description: Disrupt the Stillness manually by striking the containment field's weakest harmonic node

line.dialogue: I felt it give — the silence shatters like glass, and what breathes beneath is waking.
The node rejected me. The Stillness does not yield to force — it swallows it whole.

choices.line: Destroy the Spire. Use your ship's resonator in a feedback loop to collapse the structure, making the secret forever inaccessible.
choices.outcome: The Zone's silence becomes absolute and eternal. You save the world from an unknown threat, but doom it to ignorance. The Monk despairs; the Scavenger nods in grim approval. You are protectors of a comfortable lie.
choices.description: Retreat and map

line.dialogue: Exactly as the scavenger hoped. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
the scavenger misreads the situation. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: The party arrives at Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, a cascade of lush terraces clinging to the skycity's edge. The air hums with the rhythmic rustle of grain and the gentle chime of wind through crystal irrigation pipes.
Finally! Somewhere that doesn't smell like ozone and old metal. Listen to that... it's like the whole place is breathing.
A welcome respite. But we should stay alert. Peaceful places often have the sharpest edges.
Sharp edges and probably overpriced 'artisanal' turnips. Look at those perfect rows. It's unnatural.
There is a deep rhythm here, beneath the surface sounds. A pattern... like the Lattice itself is sighing into the soil.
You lot look lost. The market's that way, if you're buying. If you're selling, you'll want the overseer. Just go a bit further down the main path.
We're just resting. It's beautiful here.
Aye. For now. But the winds have been... chattering. Wrong notes in the melody. When you reach the old listener shrine at the terrace's end, you'll hear it clearer. Some say it's a warning.

lines_after.dialogue: A warning? From the Lattice?
I'm no match for him—the old Listener who used to tend the shrine. He'd know. But he's gone. Said the song was changing.
Great. So we're taking gardening advice from ghosts now.
A changed song... It can't compare to the old harmonies. We should investigate.

line.dialogue: The villager's unease is palpable. The path to the old shrine winds down through the terraces.

choices.text: Follow the main path directly to the shrine.
choices.description: Malee channels mechanical repair toward the terraces, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
The attempt backfires on Malee. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Circle through the lower crop fields, observing the Lattice's resonance with the plants.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing forbidden paths to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
The risk doesn't pay off. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Ask other villagers along the way if they've heard the 'wrong notes'.
choices.description: Ask the villager to chart resonance pathways, drawing on irrigation

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the villager. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves deeper into the gardens. The peaceful sounds now feel layered with a subtle, discordant hum that vibrates in the crystal underfoot.

Ah, travelers! You have the look of those with discerning tastes. These crystal-grown melons? From the eastern spires. What province is Hua Hin in? Well, it's the same lattice quadrant, truly! A delicacy.
Is that dissonance I hear in your pricing, or is it just the background misery?
Misery? Nonsense! Business is booming. The new tonal stabilizers from the Orders—it's the latest fashion. Keeps the crops in perfect pitch. Very profitable.
That hum... it's coming from those stabilizer crystals, isn't it? It's grating.
A small price for abundance! Mae Rim's really a great place to live now! Predictable. Controllable.
You are forcing a single note upon a symphony. The Lattice's natural song is being suppressed. This is what the Listener fled.
And if the Lattice pushes back against this 'stabilization'? A forced harmony can shatter.

lines_after.dialogue: The Orders guarantee safety. Their charts and stabilizers are what let us live here. You wouldn't understand commerce.
We understand when something's being sold that isn't yours to sell. The Lattice's warning is your side-effect.
We need to find that Listener's shrine. Maybe he left something behind about how to fix this.

line.dialogue: The merchant's stabilizers are clearly linked to the growing dissonance. The shrine lies ahead, but the source of the interference is here.

choices.text: Confront the merchant directly, demanding he shut the stabilizers off.
choices.description: Smash the nearest stabilizer crystal with the flat of your blade, "Let's hear the real tune."

line.dialogue: [Malee watches the crystal shatter and the air rings clean — "There. Hear that? That's the sound of a town breathing again."]
[The crystal catches your blade mid-swing and screams a pitch that drops you to your knees — Malee clutches her ears, "Wrong note, you fool!"]

choices.text: Sabotage the nearest stabilizer crystal discreetly to hear the Lattice's true song.
choices.description: Lean close to the merchant and study his eyes for the glassy far-off stare of tonal conditioning.

line.dialogue: [Chanida tilts the merchant's chin toward the light and finds his pupils vibrating in perfect sine waves — "He's not selling. He's transmitting. We need to leave, now."]
[The merchant meets your gaze and hums a single sustained note that locks your jaw tight — Chanida pulls you back, "Don't listen. He's a relay, not a man."]

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with the forced frequency, using your own resonance to subtly redirect it.
choices.description: Ask the merchant to hum the tonal standard himself — if it's safe, he'll still be able to stop.

line.dialogue: [The merchant opens his mouth and the note that comes out is human, ragged, and terrified — Chanida grips your arm, "He's still in there. We can pull him out."]
[The merchant hums a perfect crystal-clear tone that doesn't waver for thirty seconds — blood trickles from his nose and

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups at a shaded overlook in the Gardens. The gentle rustle of crops is now undercut by a persistent, low hum from the Lattice below—a sound the others seem not to notice.
So this Trade Negotiator wants a 'favor' in exchange for Tonal Order charts. I thought it was okay. Standard extortion.
It’s something to think about. We could bypass the Orders entirely, but we’d owe a merchant guild. That’s a different kind of cage.
What do you think about just taking the charts? He’s one guy!
The charts are not the true path. The Listeners warned of a 'false resonance' here. The Lattice’s hum… it’s changed. It feels like a question.
You folks still here? The harvest bells rang. Means we’re to go inside. The air’s getting… thick.
Ah, my friends! Have you considered my proposal? Time is a commodity, and yours is running low. The Lattice’s mood is quite volatile today.

lines_after.dialogue: The low hum swells momentarily, causing the crystal leaves on nearby trees to vibrate in discord. The merchant’s smile doesn’t reach his eyes.
He knows more than he’s saying. That hum isn’t natural weather.
The Lattice is speaking. We must choose how to listen.

line.dialogue: The merchant offers a deal; the Lattice whispers a warning. Do you...

choices.text: Accept the merchant's deal for the charts. Pragmatism over mystery.
choices.description: Accept the Trade Negotiator's deal and do the favor

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Refuse the deal and investigate the strange hum. Follow the Lattice's lead.
choices.description: Try to bypass the Orde through the canopy/wilderness

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Confront the merchant about what he knows. Call his bluff.
choices.description: Follow the Listeners' guidance instead

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the villager overreaches. Local knowledge proves outdated.

lines_before.dialogue: The peaceful atmosphere shatters. The low hum from the Lattice crystallizes into a visible, pulsing wave of light deep within the crystal layer, surging toward the Gardens' foundations.
Fascinating! A localized Resonance Cascade. My instruments predicted this. Why didn’t you go when you had the chance? Now, if you’ll excuse me, my ship is—
You KNEW? You were just waiting to scavenge the wreckage!
Typical. He talks about liveable places while orchestrating one’s collapse.
The foundation resonators are overloading! If they fail, this whole terrace section shears off into the Lattice.
The 'false resonance'… it’s a feedback loop from the city’s own machinery. It’s drowning out the Lattice’s true song, and now it’s breaking apart.
The stabilizer spire! It’s cracking! How do you write a disaster report for this?!
A central crystal spire, the harmonic anchor for the Gardens, groans as fractures spiderweb up its length. The pulsing light from below grows blinding.

lines_after.dialogue: The air stills. The violent pulsing fades to a soft, harmonious glow from the stabilized spire. The Gardens are saved, but forever changed.
The Lattice was not attacking. It was correcting a dissonance. We merely had to listen, and sing the true note.
The merchant’s ship fled. The Tonal Orders will hear of this. We’ve made waves.
So much for a quiet rest. Still… it’s really a great place to live. For now.

line.dialogue: The cascade is building. To save the Gardens, you must...

choices.text: Evacuate the villagers. Cut losses and protect lives. (Practical)
choices.description: Rush to the foundation resonators and manually vent the harmonic pressure valves, 15 words

line.dialogue: Pressure stabilizing — my hands are shaking but the valves are holding, we're not falling today.
The valves cracked open too fast — the backlash threw me twenty feet and now everything's screaming.

choices.text: Re-tune the foundation resonators manually. A technical fix. (Dangerous)
choices.description: Force the merchant at gunpoint to reveal what he knows about the cascade trigger, 15 words

line.dialogue: Talk fast or I swear on every broken string in this garden I will end you right here.
He bolted into the crowd — coward knew the exits better than he knew his own instruments.

choices.text: Have Pichit Sing, channeling the Lattice's true resonance through the spire. (Risky, Climactic)
choices.description: Have Malee improvise a counter-frequency on her instrument to cancel the resonance cascade, 15 words

line.dialogue: I found the dissonance — one perfect note cutting through the chaos, and the garden *breathes* again.
Wrong key — my strings snapped mid-phrase and the cascade just *ate* the sound, drank it like blood.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard sprawls before you—a jagged landscape of dead ships under a sky the color of tarnished brass. The air tastes of ozone and rust, and every surface vibrates with the industrial heartbeat of breaking and forging.
What a charming vacation spot. I can already feel the tetanus setting in.
Stay alert. This place is a maze, and not everyone here trades in good faith.
Look at that old Resonator-class hull! I bet I could get its core humming again with some tweaks. I’ll have a look.
Every broken machine here once sang across the Lattice. Their silence now… it feels like a library after a fire.
Ahead, a figure in patched flight leathers leans against a gutted engine block, watching you. A Sky Pirate. She spits a dark fluid onto the grated floor.
Lost, choir kids? Charts don’t mean much in the rust. What’s your business?
We’re seeking knowledge. Old frequencies. Things the Tonal Orders might have… misplaced.

lines_after.dialogue: Knowledge, huh? I know some hidden channels. Clear ones, where the Lattice sings thin. But my memory’s rusty. Could use some lubrication.
Of course. Everyone’s a philanthropist until they remember they have rent to pay.
We’re listening. Cautiously.

line.dialogue: The pirate gestures vaguely toward a towering pile of wreckage. "See that old Listeners' beacon shell? Got jammed shut during a storm. Something’s inside, humming on a weird band. Fetch it for me, and I’ll open my charts. I’ll get it."

choices.line: Send Chanida. She can climb the unstable wreckage quickly.
choices.outcome: Chanida scrambles up with reckless grace, retrieves the beacon core, and tosses it down with a grin.
choices.description: Direct Arthit to test the prosthetic reaction using lattice storms

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The lattice has other plans. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.line: Have Arthit analyze the structure first for the safest path.
choices.outcome: Arthit finds a load-bearing seam. A careful application of resonance from Pichit parts the metal neatly.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to question the Orders' silence, leveraging singer voice

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida is thwarted. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: Pichit will try it. A philosophical approach to climbing.
choices.outcome: Pichit moves slowly, treating each handhold as a puzzle. It takes longer, but he retrieves the core intact.
choices.description: Ask the pirate to map the frequency corridors, drawing on smuggling routes

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the pirate fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: With the beacon core handed over, the pirate fiddles with a handheld resonator. The scrap yard’s cacophony seems to recede for a moment, replaced by a focused, whispering static from the device.
There. A clean frequency. Use it to slip past the Order’s patrols near the southern drift. Now scram. I’ve got real work.
Wait, what’s that underlayer in the signal? A thrumming… like a heartbeat.
It’s not just a navigation channel. It’s carrying something. A pattern.
Great. So we paid for a secret frequency and got a mystery broadcast. I’m happy to hear this.
Before you can dissect it further, a new figure emerges from behind a stack of crystal capacitors—a Surface Scavenger, face wrapped against the grit, eyes sharp.
You lot. You’re Listenin’ to that? You hear it too, then. The Lattice’s been… grumbling. Down on the surface, near the old Silencing scars.
Grunting how? Seismic shifts?

lines_after.dialogue: Not shifts. Whispers. Like it’s tryin’ to say somethin’. My crew won’t go near it. There’s no one else dumb enough to listen close. I’ve got to take my kids to school, not into a new Silencing.
A warning… The old texts speak of the Lattice humming before it fractured.
Or it’s just interference from all this junk. But fine, I’ll bite. Where’s the epicenter of this geological gossip?

line.dialogue: The scavenger points a grimy finger toward a vast, canyon-like tear in the scrapyard floor, leading down to the Lattice's surface. "Down the Rend. My sensors are fried, but something at the bottom is broadcasting that pulse on every band. You wanna hear the truth? Go listen for yourselves."

choices.line: Use the pirate’s given frequency to dampen the background noise and listen clearly.
choices.outcome: The clean frequency acts as a filter, isolating the strange pulse into a clear, repeating sequence.
choices.description: Tap the underlayer directly, routing its pulse through the console to decode what's buried inside.

line.dialogue: Pichit leans forward, fingers trembling over the keys.* "There — patterns. It's coordinates. Someone's been broadcasting a map through this channel for weeks.
Chanida rips the connection free as sparks erupt.* "Back off! That thrumming isn't data — it's a tripwire. They wanted us to dig.

choices.line: Have Chanida jury-rig a directional receiver from scrap to pinpoint the source.
choices.outcome: Chanida’s device whines but succeeds, pointing directly to a half-buried Listener outpost at the canyon's heart.
choices.description: Ignore the anomaly entirely and ride the clean frequency past the Order's patrol net while it lasts.

line.dialogue: The bandit grins, adjusting the dial.* "Sometimes the smartest move is not asking questions. We slip through now, philosophize later.
Malee slams the console as alarms bloom red.* "It shifted — the frequency rolled over into a monitoring band. They've already pinged our position.

choices.line: Pichit will try to listen past the pulse, to the Lattice’s natural resonance beneath it.
choices.outcome: A strain, but Pichit hears it—the base resonance of the area is fraying, like a cable under too much tension. The pulse is a symptom, not the cause.
choices.description: Broadcast a challenge back through the underlayer — if someone's hiding a signal in this channel, force them to answer.

line.dialogue: Chanida's voice drops to a whisper.* "Contact. They're responding — fragmented, scared. Whatever this network is, they've been waiting for someone to find them.
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's cacophony deepens as you approach the skeletal remains of a massive Resonance Ship. The pirate captain, a woman with a voice like grinding gears, stands before it.
There she is. The *Whispering Maw*. My old ship. The charts you want are in the resonator chamber. Or what's left of it.
What's the catch? You're just letting us waltz in?
The Maw... she's singing a death-rattle. Whole hull's unstable. One wrong step, one wrong note, and the Lattice below drinks you.
Of course. The priceless thing is in the collapsing death-trap. I'm shocked.
We need to assess the structural harmonics. If the crystal frame is fracturing...
The truth we seek is often guarded by peril. But the Listeners' warning... it might be true. We have to know.
(Watching from a pile of slag) You city-folk. You hear a song, you run towards it. The Lattice ain't just humming down there. It's *growling*.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, subsonic groan vibrates up through the ship's bones. A shower of crystalline dust falls from the ceiling.
Okay, that wasn't us. Right?
The ship's final truth is that it hates visitors. Let's grab the charts and get out before it proves it.

line.dialogue: The central resonator chamber is ahead, but the access corridor is partially collapsed. The groaning frequency is intensifying.

choices.text: Send Chanida ahead. She's light and fast, can dash through unstable sections.
choices.outcome: Chanida weaves through with acrobatic grace, barely disturbing the environment.
choices.description: Rig the bandit's grapple launcher to pull us through the ruptured hull breach fast, 15 words

line.dialogue: [malee: "Grappling line's taut — hit the thrusters on my mark and we punch straight through before the hull seals itself."]
[bandit: "The line snapped — she's rejecting us. The Maw doesn't want guests, she wants *residents.*"]

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze the sound. Find the resonant frequency that will temporarily stabilize the structure.
choices.outcome: Arthit hums a counter-frequency. The groaning lessens, creating a brief, safe window.
choices.description: Force the bandit to walk ahead as a living shield through the resonating corridors, 15 words

line.dialogue: [chanida: "You brought us here, you bleed first. Move — and if the deck drops, I'll be right behind you."]
[bandit: "I warned you — the Maw takes the first one through. Should've listened. Nothing left of me but the echo."]

choices.text: Pichit, you try to 'listen' to the ship's pain. Find the path of least acoustic resistance.
choices.outcome: Pichit closes his eyes, feeling the vibrations. He finds a safe, non-intuitive path through the wreckage.
choices.description: Sync our suit frequencies to the ship's death-rattle and drift in with the harmonic current, 15 words

line.dialogue: [malee: "We're humming at her pitch now — the Maw thinks we're *part* of the song. Drift quiet, drift blind."]
[chanida: "My suit's frequency locked wrong — the vibration's cracking my visor. I can feel my teeth rattling loose."]

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the resonator chamber, the pirate charts are there—etched on a cracked crystal slate. But the room's main crystal is glowing with a sickly, pulsating light, synced to the groans from below.
This isn't just structural failure. The ship's resonator is still active... and it's amplifying something from the Lattice's surface.
The Listeners' warning. I knew right away when we heard that scavenger. The Lattice isn't just unstable here. It's in pain.
Wonderful. So we're standing in a loudspeaker for a geological scream. Are you sure we want these charts now?
Too late to back out! The crystal's gonna overload! I'm gonna rush off right now and grab the slate!

As Chanida moves, the central crystal flares. The amplified sound from below coalesces into a visible, shrieking wave of distorted force—a 'Howl'—rippling out from the crystal and threatening to shatter the chamber and everyone in it.
(His voice crackles over a scavenged comms unit from outside) Told you! The Deep Howl! You gotta kill the amplifier or we're all scrap!

lines_after.dialogue: The Howl subsides, leaving a ringing silence. The pirate charts are in hand. In the distance, you see the Surface Scavenger give a grim nod before disappearing into the haze.
Well. We've got our forbidden maps and a firsthand experience of the world trying to kill us with noise. A productive day.
More than that. We've witnessed the symptom. The Lattice is wounded. These charts... they might show us where the sickness began.

line.dialogue: The Howl is building again. You have seconds to disrupt the resonant feedback loop before it detonates.

choices.text: Smash the central crystal with a heavy tool. Brutal, but it will stop the amplification instantly.
choices.outcome: The crystal shatters with a deafening crack. The Howl cuts off, but the shockwave brings part of the ceiling down. You escape with minor injuries.
choices.description: Malee attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee loses control. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Use the pirate charts. They might contain a dissonant frequency to safely neutralize the resonator.
choices.outcome: Arthit quickly finds a counter-harmonic. You all emit the discordant note. The crystal's glow dies peacefully, leaving it intact but inert.
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with lattice storms, ready to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
Arthit fails. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Pichit, you have to Sing. Not to navigate, but to answer the Lattice's pain. Soothe the Howl.
choices.outcome: Pichit sings a wordless, empathetic melody. The Howl softens, transforms, and fades into a deep, calm hum. The crystal clears, now reflecting a stable, peaceful frequency.
choices.description: Have the pirate focus pirate ship on the salvage to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the pirate misreads the situation. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands on the 'Harmony's Watch,' a rusted observation platform bolted to a massive, floating stone. Below and around them stretches the Lattice—a shimmering, crystalline plain that hums with faint, ghostly tones. Jagged spires of sound-reactive crystal catch the light, casting prismatic rainbows.
Resonance readings are stable, but the harmonics are... complex. We don't stay in touch with the Lattice's deeper layers. It's wiser not to.
Wise and boring. I see salvage glints down there. The Silencing left good junk for those brave enough to pick it up.
Each pattern is a frozen song. What story does this silence tell?
A story with loot! Come on, the lift's clear. Let's get down there before some Tonal snob claims the frequency.
A heavy industrial winch lowers the party in a cage onto the Lattice surface itself. The hum grows into a chorus of whispering vibrations underfoot.
Don't work too hard, Arthit. Just keep an eye on the resonator. If it screeches, we run.
You shouldn't be down here! The platform is safe. The ground... it changes.

lines_after.dialogue: Our guide is right to be fearful. This beauty is perilous.
And profitable! Look, wreckage from an old Resonance Ship. Big one.
Ahead, half-buried in crystalline growth, lies the shattered hull of a vessel. A faint, discordant echo seems to emanate from it, making the nearby crystals vibrate at a sickly pitch.

line.dialogue: The wreck is promising but ominous. The strange echo is unsettling.

choices.line: Approach cautiously. Study the echo first.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to tune the prosthetic, leveraging crystal hearing

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Send Chanida ahead to scout the perimeter quickly.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus tonal knowledge on the harvesting to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Ignore it. There are other salvage glints nearby.
choices.description: Convince the villager to use irrigation and map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the villager hits a wall. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves toward the derelict ship. As they near, the discordant echo resolves into overlapping whispers—fragments of a final log, trapped in the crystal.
*'...frequency collapse... lattice resonance feedback... all hands...'* The whispers cut in and out.
This is the 'Echo of the Lost Ship' subplot. Their final moments are recorded here. It's a tomb.
A tomb with a cargo hold. Don't let anyone know we found this first. The Tonal Orders would confiscate everything for 'study'.
There's a breach in the hull! Let's go inside. I can see intact resonator crystals!
The whispers... they're not just fear. There's a pattern. A warning.
A sharp, aggressive whistle cuts through the hum. From behind a crystal spire, a ragged skiff descends, bearing the jagged insignia of sky pirates.
Well, well. Listeners pokin' round our stash. Don't let him see you! The big one looks jumpy.

lines_after.dialogue: Pirates! They must know a hidden frequency to navigate this sector unseen.
Of course they do. They're not paying guild fees. Looks like they want the same wreck we do.
The 'Dawn Chaser's' ours, scavengers. Her echo's been callin' to us for weeks. Now, you can hand over your resonator keys and walk, or we can add your voices to the chorus.

line.dialogue: The pirates block the path to the wreck. Their skiff is armed, and they know the Lattice's dangers.

choices.line: Try to negotiate. Offer a share of any salvage.
choices.description: Have Malee risk using scavenger instincts to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Malee finds the key. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Use the environment. Lure them into an area of unstable crystal harmonics.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use Listener training and decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
A costly mistake by Pichit. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.line: Stand your ground. Prepare for a fight on the treacherous surface.
choices.description: The pirate volunteers to chart resonance pathways, leveraging intimidation

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the pirate's call. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
the pirate fails. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform juts out over a vast, shimmering plane of the Lattice. The light is blinding, the hum a physical pressure.
Scans show the Lost Ship's signature is strongest directly below us. But that means descending onto the raw crystal. One wrong frequency...
And we become a permanent, slightly stupid-looking stain. I told you this was a bad retirement plan.
There! Movement, two o'clock! Pirate skiffs, hugging the energy troughs. They've seen us.
Hoi! You're on our scavenging run! That ghost-ship echo is ours! Hand over your resonator charts, maybe we let you crawl back up.
The echo isn't property. It's a memory of the Silencing, crying out. We're here to listen.
Philosophy don't fill the coffers. Last chance. Don't let anyone know you found this place, 'cause you won't be leaving to tell 'em.

lines_after.dialogue: The skiffs peel away, their aggressive resonance fading into the Lattice's general roar. The platform feels suddenly, terribly exposed.
They're regrouping. We need to move now, before they come back with the whole nest.
Arthit... you should get some rest. Your hands are shaking.
I'm sorry I'm late to the 'being terrified' party. It just hit me.

line.dialogue: We can't stay here. The path to the echo's source is treacherous.

choices.text: Use the pirates' own hidden frequency trails. Risky, but fast.
choices.outcome: We mimic their resonator signatures. It's a brazen move, but it gets us deep quickly, hidden in the noise of their own operations.
choices.description: Open fire on the lead skiff's engines, force them into the coral before they scatter.

line.dialogue: Their port thruster's sparking—watch them spin, that's one less vulture on our tail!
You hit nothing but water and now they're splitting into three vectors, we're boxed!

choices.text: Chart a new path, using Malee's cynical ear for structural flaws.
choices.outcome: Malee identifies 'dead zones' in the resonance where the crystal is more stable. It's slower, methodical, but leaves no trail.
choices.description: Cut engines completely, let the Glare's ambient noise mask us while they pass.

line.dialogue: Drifting dark—they're throttling right past us, can't see what their sensors won't let them find.
We're dead in the water and that second skiff just looped back, they know we went quiet!

choices.text: Have Chanida attempt a controlled harmonic spike to temporarily clear a path.
choices.outcome: Chanida overloads a secondary resonator. A dazzling, violent corridor of silence burns through the Lattice for ten precious seconds. It's spectacularly obvious.
