choices.description: Hail the bandit, offer coordinates to a derelict we already stripped three cycles ago.

line.dialogue: He bought it—greedy fool's already breaking course, and we didn't have to scratch our hull for it.
He says he stripped that wreck six

lines_before.dialogue: You stand at the epicenter. The Lattice here is not flat, but warped into a gargantuan, frozen whirlpool—the tomb of the Lost Ship.
Well. There she is. Or where she was. The metal's all gone. Just... an impression. A scream in crystal.
The echo... it's not a sound. It's a feeling. It's... grief.
It's the last moment before the Silencing. Held here. Forever.
Please! You have to help!
A Skycity resident stumbles from behind a crystal spire, face etched with panic.
The pirates—they followed you! They're above the platform, cutting the tethers! We'll be stranded! I can barely hear my own thoughts over their jammers!
TOO LATE, SONG-BIRDS! We'll take the echo AND your ship! Let's see you sing your way out of this!

lines_after.dialogue: A deep, shattering CRACK echoes through the Lattice as the observation platform's main anchor shears away.
The resonance feedback... it's overloading the crystal field. This whole basin is going to fracture!
She forgot everything! The safety protocols, the retreat patterns—the echo is consuming itself!
No. It's remembering. And we need to hear what it has to say, before it's gone.

line.dialogue: The world is breaking. To save anyone, you must face the heart of the echo.

choices.text: Harmonize with the echo. Let it pass through you to dissipate safely.
choices.outcome: You open yourself. The ship's final moment—terror, love, despair—floods your mind. It is agony, but the crystal stills. The pirates flee the sudden silence.
choices.description: Press your bare hands against the scorched metal and let the echo flood through you.

line.dialogue: Malee — "I can feel her heartbeat in the corrosion. She was alive when they took the sound from this place.
Malee — "Nothing. Just cold metal and colder memory. Whatever was here, it's sealed behind something my hands can't reach.

choices.text: Redirect the energy. Use the ship's resonator to channel the fracture away from the skycity.
choices.outcome: You turn the dying scream into a controlled blast. It scours a canyon into the Lattice, saving the city but permanently scarring the world-map. A necessary wound.
choices.description: Grab the villager by the shoulders and demand to know what they saw the night of the Silencing.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "You saw them carry her toward the reservoir? Why didn't you scream — why didn't anyone scream?
Chanida — "They're shaking too hard to speak. Whatever happened here broke something in them that words can't cross anymore.

choices.text: Answer the echo. Not with listening, but with a new sound—a song of your own.
choices.outcome: You sing. A fragile, hopeful counter-melody against the dirge. The Lost Ship's echo shifts, changes, and resolves into a single, clear note of peace before fading. The Lattice where it rested is now calm, and forever changed.
choices.description: Hum the frequency Pichit described — the one that existed before silence — and listen for what answers.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "There! Beneath the hum. She's singing back from inside the void. The Silencing didn't finish — it *paused*.
Pichit — "My voice cracks and the echo swallows it whole. I got the frequency wrong, and now the silence is deeper than before.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship's hum dies the moment you cross the threshold into the Silent Zone. The Lattice below, usually a shimmering sea of reactive crystal, lies dark and inert.
Whoa. I can hear my own heartbeat. It's... too loud.
Sensors confirm it. Zero acoustic resonance. The ship's crystal is just dead weight here. We're drifting on momentum.
Fantastic. So we're sitting ducks in a place that breaks every rule of navigation. The Tonal Orders would have a collective stroke.
A place of perfect silence... It feels less like an absence and more like a presence. A held breath.
A smaller, older vessel drifts into view, its hull scarred. A figure in drab robes waves from its deck—a Listener Monk.
Peace upon your frequencies. You... you should not be here. This place is a wound.
We're looking for a missing trade envoy. He's still single, isn't he? Probably got lost chasing a profit.

lines_after.dialogue: The Negotiator? He passed this way. He spoke of... shortcuts. Of finding value in silence. A blasphemy.
Value? There's nothing here. That's all, isn't it? Just dead rock and a creepy quiet.
The monk's eyes dart nervously to the dark Lattice. His voice drops to a whisper you can barely hear.
You are mistaken. There is something here. I feel it... standing right in front of me. A pressure in the silence.

line.dialogue: The Monk is clearly terrified of something unseen. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Offer to escort him back to the edge of the Zone for safety.
choices.description: Climb into the vent shaft and follow the source of the anomalous low-frequency hum.

line.dialogue: There's something vibrating down here — faint, but rhythmic. Like breathing through metal.
The duct dead-ends at a bulkhead. Whatever I heard, it's gone now. Or it stopped for me.

choices.line: Press him for specifics: what exactly does he feel?
choices.description: Order Arthit to run a full spectral sweep and isolate any frequencies below human hearing.

line.dialogue: Got it. Subsonic pattern, sixteen-second intervals. Something down here is counting, and it knows we're listening.
The sweep's returning corrupted data — every reading contradicts itself. Whatever this place is, it doesn't want to be measured.

choices.line: Dismiss his fears and focus on finding the merchant's trail.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the hull and let the silence teach you what it wants.

line.dialogue: The metal is warm. It pulses under my skin, slow and patient. This silence isn't empty — it's waiting to be answered.
Nothing. Just cold steel and the thudding of my own blood. The silence swallows even the hope of contact.

lines_before.dialogue: You press the monk. He leads your drifting ship to a fractured lattice spire, a jagged tooth against the starfield. A sleek trade skiff is moored there.
Ah, visitors! And a Listener, too. Don't look so grim. It's nice and peaceful. No noise, no demands from the Orders.
Your beacon was off. You were reported missing. We were... concerned.
A necessary precaution. The Tonal Orders monopolize the charts for a reason. But here? Their maps are blank. New paths can be found.
Paths to what? There's nothing to trade here. Unless you're selling silence.
On the contrary. I'm brokering an understanding. There are those who believe the Floating Cities are a cage. The Groundless Movement. They seek... alternatives.
You're using this dead zone to meet them. A place beyond the Orders' ears.
So, what? They just live down in the dead Lattice? That's insane!

lines_after.dialogue: They believe the Silencing wasn't an end, but a transformation. One they can harness. But they need certain materials. Resonant cores. From old ships.
You would bleed the last song from the world's bones! Can you promise me this won't cause another catastrophe?
I promise opportunity. For you as well. Help me, and the profit is substantial. My Groundless contacts... someone is waiting for you. They have answers about the Zone's true nature.

line.dialogue: The Merchant offers a deal: help salvage a resonant core from a derelict nearby, in exchange for a meeting with the Groundless.

choices.line: Accept the deal. The promise of answers and profit is too great.
choices.description: Scan the empty horizon for hidden cargo lifts or buried access shafts, 13 words

line.dialogue: There — beneath the sand ridges. Cargo rails leading underground. You've been running a shadow market this whole time.
Nothing but dust and dead air. Either you're the worst merchant I've ever met, or the best liar.

choices.line: Refuse, but agree to meet the Groundless to hear their side, without committing to theft.
choices.description: Ask the merchant what the Tonal Orders are monopolizing and why it requires disappearing, 14 words

line.dialogue: So the Orders control the Resonance trade and you've been smuggling unregistered frequencies out from under them. Bold.
You're dodging the question with pretty words. People who hide behind metaphors usually have something uglier underneath.

choices.line: Refuse outright and threaten to report his activities to the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Draw your sidearm and demand the merchant explain why the beacon was really disabled, 14 words

line.dialogue: I've seen this pattern before. Someone tipped
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves deeper into the Silent Zone, the oppressive quiet now a physical weight. The crystal lattice here is not just silent—it's dead, a matte, lightless obsidian that seems to drink sound.
Our resonance engine readings are flatlining. We've talked about this before—when the lattice stops singing, the physics get... unpredictable.
Look! Something's carved into the crystal face ahead. It's... huge.
Not carved. *Grown.* The pattern is too precise. It's a message, or a memorial, written in crystal by the lattice itself... before The Silencing.
Great. A tombstone for a dead god. No one wants to go poking at that, but here we are.
By the First Vibration... this is it. The locus of the trauma. The scar. The Listeners have legends of this place. We call it the 'Anthem's Grave'.
Legends don't fill cargo holds. But intact pre-Silencing resonant formations? That's a different kind of song. The kind that buys cities.

lines_after.dialogue: As the monk chants a lament, the dead crystal around the 'grave' shivers. Not with sound, but with a deep, sub-audible tremor that runs through your bones.
It's... responding. Not to his voice. To his grief.
The tremor is destabilizing the island shelf! We need to move, now!

line.dialogue: The tremor reveals a fissure leading down into the lattice itself—a perfectly geometric shaft.

choices.text: Send a probe first. We need data before we commit.
choices.outcome_line: Arthit's probe shows stable, if eerie, geometry below. The safe, informed path.
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with tonal knowledge, ready to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Things don't go as planned. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: The monk says this is a pilgrimage. We follow his lead.
choices.outcome_line: The monk's reverence seems to calm the strange vibrations. A path of faith.
choices.description: Direct Malee to seek the dismissed truth using mechanical repair

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The attempt backfires on Malee. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: This is what we came for. Take the direct route down.
choices.outcome_line: You descend into the geometric dark, the silence so complete it hums in your teeth.
choices.description: The monk attempts to map the frequency corridors, relying on meditation

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the monk fails. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The shaft opens into a vast, spherical cavern at the world's heart. In its center hangs a perfect, complex crystal—the Source Shard. It is dark, but around it, the air shimmers with trapped, silent vibrations.
The World's First Note... frozen. This is not natural death. This was murder.
Do you have any idea what that is worth? We could buy the Tonal Orders! We could be kings! What style of kingdom do you prefer, Pichit?
He's right. That thing could power a fleet forever. Or it could be the bomb that finished the job. It's not scary at all! Just incredibly, stupidly dangerous.
Look at the walls! The shimmer... it's showing images. The Floating Cities... falling. The Silencing happening again!
It's a resonance echo—a memory of the catastrophe, playing on a loop. If we disturb the shard... we might not make it back. Ever.
This is the truth the Groundless want. The lattice isn't broken. It's wounded. And we've been sailing on its scar tissue for generations.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant reaches for a mining charge. The monk steps into his path. The silent vibrations in the air begin to coalesce, drawn to the conflict.
Out of my way, zealot! That crystal is leaving with me!
You will not repeat the sin! I cannot let you!

line.dialogue: The confrontation threatens to destabilize the frozen energies. The Shard pulses with a sickly light. You must act.

choices.text: Restrain the merchant. Preserve the shard, hide the truth.
choices.outcome_line: You secure the merchant, but the secret of this place remains with you—a heavy burden. The Groundless subplot simmers, unsatisfied.
choices.description: Touch the frozen Note directly, pressing your palm against its surface to feel what lies beneath the ice.

line.dialogue: monk - "I feel it—beneath the cold, there's a heartbeat, slow and ancient, waiting to be heard.
monk - "The cold burns through my hand like fire—I cannot reach what's sealed inside.

choices.text: Shatter the shard. Release the trapped resonance in a controlled burst.
choices.outcome_line: The shard explodes in a silent wave of light. The Silent Zone rings with a single, pure note for the first time in centuries. The Groundless find a symbol, but not a weapon.
choices.description: Study the shimmering images on the walls, tracing the patterns with your fingers to read what they show.

line.dialogue: chanida - "These images—they're a history, showing who froze the Note and why they feared its song.
chanida - "The shimmer shifts away from my touch like a startled fish—the images refuse to be read so easily.

choices.text: Try to Sing to it. Heal the wound, if you can.
choices.outcome_line: You pour your voice into the void. The dark crystal drinks it, then glows. A fragile, new song begins—a painful, hopeful sound. You have changed the world. The consequences are unknown.
choices.description: Attempt to shatter the ice encasing the Note using your weapon, striking precisely at

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: The *Resonance* cuts through banks of shimmering crystal mist. Below, the Lattice ripples like a frozen sea, responding to the low thrum of the ship's primary resonator.
Look! Off the starboard bow! Is that... debris?
Steady the scope. Could be Lattice formations. Or wreckage. We should maintain a safe distance.
Or it could be salvage. My resonator array could use some high-grade crystal. Just saying.
The patterns... they're too geometric for nature. Chanida, bring us closer. Carefully.
As the mist parts, the silhouette of a derelict resonance ship emerges, its hull fractured and crusted with wild Lattice growth.
That's it! There she is! The *Echo's Lament*. I've only seen her in the old skyport manifests.
Great. A ghost ship. Exactly what we needed to spice up this boring supply run.

lines_after.dialogue: Her registry shows she vanished during The Silencing. No distress call. Nothing. This is a tomb, Pichit.
And yet... listen. Can you hear it? A faint harmonic, bleeding from her broken resonator. It's... calling.
A sudden, sharp chime echoes from your ship's console. A hailing frequency, old and corrupted, blinks to life. Then, a burst of static, and a dead line.
He hung up. Or... something did.

line.dialogue: The derelict hangs silently in the mist. Your ship's instruments pick up a weak but stable energy signature deep within its hull.

choices.text: Hail the wreck on all frequencies. A direct approach might provoke a response.
choices.description: Circle the debris at safe distance while Pichit runs pattern analysis on the formations.

line.dialogue: Confirmed — these are Lattice waypoints, not wreckage. Someone mapped this region before us.
The readings are muddied — crystal interference is scrambling my instruments. We're flying blind past this point.

choices.text: Send a probe first. Map the interior and scan for life signs before committing.
choices.description: Bring us in close and deploy Malee's resonator array to scan for salvageable tech.

line.dialogue: Jackpot! There's intact harmonic circuitry in that cluster — enough to rebuild my array twice over.
Damn — the debris is unstable. My array pinged something and the whole formation started resonating. Pull us back before it shatters!

choices.text: Log the coordinates and report to the nearest Tonal Order outpost. Let the authorities handle it.
choices.description: Hold position and let Arthit manually scope the geometry before we commit to anything.

line.dialogue: There's a hull breach pattern — three, no, four vessels. This wasn't drift, this was a kill zone. We need to leave.
The mist is too thick even for the scope. I can't tell if we're looking at treasure or a trap — and I won't gamble this crew on a guess.

lines_before.dialogue: You've maneuvered the *Resonance* alongside the derelict. The probe's feed shows a hollow, crystalline-infested interior, but no movement. The strange harmonic persists, a ghost note in the air.
You shouldn't be here. Sky-folk never understand the surface. That ship... it's not empty. It's waiting.
Charming. And you are?
Survivor. My raft's resonator gave out. Saw your lights. That ship's resonance is all wrong. Like a song that's... it's over. It's finished. But it doesn't know it yet.
A song trapped in its final moment. A memory of The Silencing, perhaps?
We have a duty. If there are souls trapped in there, or data from before the fall...

I'm not finished yet! I'm not done with what I was telling you! The probe just picked up a new signal. It's not a distress call. It's... a navigation chart. An old one, pointing to a deep Lattice sinkhole.
Please. My cousin, Jarin... he was on a scavenger team. They went looking for the *Echo's Lament* last season. A friend introduced us to the contractor. They never came back.

lines_after.dialogue: The villager's plea hangs in the air. The scavenger eyes the derelict with grim familiarity. The harmonic from the wreck shifts, becoming more insistent, almost pleading.
So we have a missing persons case, a haunted frequency, and a possible treasure map. My cynicism is officially intrigued.
The song wants to be completed. It's a fragment of a larger truth, shattered during The Silencing. We cannot turn away.
The structural integrity is failing. If we go in, it will be a one-chance operation. We find what we can and get out before the resonance collapses.

line.dialogue: The path is clear but perilous. The derelict's main cargo bay door is partially open, a dark maw leading into the crystalline heart of the ship.

choices.text: Board with the Scavenger. Their knowledge of the Lattice's surface dangers could be invaluable inside.
choices.description: Offer to repair the resonator using Pichit's tuning crystal and wire from Malee's kit.

line.dialogue: Hands steady, breath held—the crystal catches harmonics like a net catches light. It hums, then sings. The scavenger stares at me like I've performed a miracle, and maybe I have." — Pichit
The crystal fractures in my grip. Wrong frequency. The resonator spits sparks and dies completely, and the scavenger's face hardens into something that looks a lot like grief." — Pichit

choices.text: Board alone with Arthit. A small, quiet team is less likely to trigger any residual resonance traps.
choices.description: Demand the scavenger explain what "The Sil" is before offering any help.

line.dialogue: He flinches at the name, then steadies. Tells me The Sil was a choir-ship that sank in the Requiem Trench three cycles back. Says the song I'm hearing is its last broadcast, still looping. Says he's been trying to finish it." — Malee
He laughs—ugly, broken. 'You don't even know what you're hearing, sky-folk. You're standing in a graveyard and asking for a tour.' He turns his back to us." — Malee

choices.text: Send Chanida and Malee first via the exposed resonator housing. It's riskier but might lead directly to the signal's source.
choices.description: Wade toward the half-submerged chamber where the unfinished dirge echoes loudest, alone.

line.dialogue: The water rises to my chest, cold as old grief. The song vibrates through my ribs—and I understand it now. Not words. A warning. Something
the scavenger misreads the situation. A scavenging tool breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The storm hits the Resonance Ship like a physical wall. Howling winds shriek across the deck, and the Lattice below churns with violent, dissonant harmonics. The ghostly outline of the lost ship, the *Whispering Maw*, flickers in and out of view ahead.
There's a high chance this whole deck gets sheared off. Our resonator crystals are screaming. This isn't navigation; it's a slow-motion crash.
But look! That signal from the *Maw*... it's this cute and this inviting little pulse of stable tone. How could you pass it up? It's a lifeline!
Or a trap. The storm is masking everything. Do you need to use it? Is it necessary to follow that siren song? We could try to ride this out on our own power.
Our power is faltering. The *Maw* isn't just a ghost; it's a memory trapped in the storm's frequency. To understand the Silencing, we must listen to echoes that should have faded.
You sky-folk are mad! The Lattice eats memories during a dissonance storm. That ship's not offering shelter; it's hungry!
Please, just get us to the next city! Don't chase pictures in the rain!

lines_after.dialogue: The ship groans as a decision is made. The ghostly hull of the *Whispering Maw* looms larger, its resonance a strange pocket of calm in the roaring chaos.
Well, we're committed. Let's see what this 'picture' is really painted with.
Steady... steady... we're almost in its wake!

line.dialogue: How do we approach the spectral ship?

choices.text: Match its resonance frequency to dock safely. (Easy - Requires precise tonal alignment)
choices.leads_to: We synchronize, the storm's fury dampens. A ghostly gangplank manifests.
choices.description: Direct Malee to harness harmonic feedback using mechanical repair

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
The lattice has other plans. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Fire a grappling line to tether it physically. (Medium - Risky but direct)
choices.leads_to: The line holds, but the *Maw* shudders, emitting a pained shriek.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use hidden frequencies and seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. She hears something no one else can.
The gamble fails. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Broadcast the last known log entry of its Singer. (Hard - A profound sonic gamble)
choices.leads_to: The ghost ship wails in recognition, its form solidifying violently.
choices.description: The villager uses village secrets to decode the tonal pattern near the sails

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the villager's call. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Things don't go as planned. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The *Whispering Maw* is a tomb of crystallized sound. The storm rages silently beyond its stabilized resonance field. In the ship's central chamber, the crystalized remains of its last Singer sits at the resonator, fused with the console.
The resonance lock... it works really well. Too well. It's preserved this moment perfectly for decades. A perfect, terrible memory.
The log says they were testing a new navigation tone to pierce deeper into the Lattice. The Silencing wasn't an accident for them. It was a target.
They triggered it?! But why? The Singer... I really can't remember any Order history about this!
He complains a lot! My grandfather's stories! He said the sky-people played with fires they couldn't hear! Now you see!
This Singer wasn't just navigating. They were trying to *communicate* with what's below. This crystal isn't a corpse; it's a message. One we can receive.
Shatter it! Break it and let's go! Before that... that *attention* outside notices us!

lines_after.dialogue: A deep, foundational hum begins to vibrate through both ships. The stabilized field flickers. Something vast has noticed the reactivated memory.
The Lattice itself is responding. That 'works really well' is about to be the understatement of the century.
We have seconds. Whatever you choose, Pichit, do it now!

line.dialogue: The Echo of the Lost Ship must be resolved. What do you do?

choices.text: Amplify the Singer's final tone, completing the message. (Easy - Embrace the past, face the consequence)
choices.leads_to: The crystal shatters, releasing a wave of pure, ancient sound. The storm parts, revealing a hidden path deep into the Lattice. The Tonal Orders will hunt you for this knowledge.
choices.description: Touch the resonance lock's housing to feel for harmonic vibration patterns while humming the navigation tone.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The vibration matches — this frequency is what pulled them in, I can feel the exact pitch in my teeth.
Arthit — "Nothing. Either the housing dampens it or I'm tone-deaf to whatever frequency convinced them to follow it.

choices.text: Use our ship's resonator to overwrite and silence the memory. (Medium - Bury the truth, ensure survival)
choices.leads_to: The *Maw* dissolves into static. The storm abates, leaving a safe, blank route to the skycity. The secret is safe, but the weight of it stays with you.
choices.description: Pull up the navigation tone's waveform on your datapad and cross-reference it against Chanida's Singer frequency logs.

line.dialogue: Malee — "The overlap is ninety-three percent — this isn't a navigation tone at all, it's a lullaby, and they walked right into its cradle.
Malee — "The files are corrupted past the third harmonic. Whatever they encoded in that tone, someone didn't want it reverse-engineered.

choices.text: Synchronize the party's voices to harmonize with the echo, not fight it. (Hard - A new song is born)
choices.leads_to: A new, stable resonance is created. The ghost ship peacefully fades, blessing your vessel. You gain an intuitive, uncharted navigation sense, becoming true Singers. The Orders will see you as heretics or saviors.
choices.description: Ask the scavenger to repeat his grandfather's exact words about the sound and mimic the tone yourself.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "That's it — that's the Singer's call. Your grandfather heard it too, which means this has happened before and someone survived it.
Chanida — "No, that's not — close, but the inflection is wrong. If we get this frequency even slightly off, we're no better than bait.

lines_before.dialogue: Phrao Monastery's humming walls vibrate with the Lattice's deep, eternal song. Pichit and his crew stand in the Grand Atrium, where crystal formations amplify every sound.
Look at these crystals! They’re more beautiful than anyone! I bet they’d fetch a fortune in the skycities.
Easy, treasure-hunter. Break one and the monks will make you sing soprano. Permanently.
The acoustic precision here is… unsettling. One wrong note could destabilize the entire floating foundation.
Yet within this fragility lies understanding. The Lattice speaks. We must learn to listen.
You the new crew? Listen, don’t make trouble. The Tonal Orders have ears everywhere here. Could you speak more slowly? I’m not good with fancy talk.
We’re just here to… learn! Yeah. Learn about the song. Totally not here to find anything the Orders are hiding.
Welcome. I am Brother Liren. You seek knowledge of the Lattice’s true voice. A rare pursuit in these silenced times.

lines_after.dialogue: The monastery archives hold forbidden harmonics—records from before The Silencing. The Orders would see them destroyed.
Why share this with us, Brother?
Because I have a cramp in my spirit. The truth must be spoken, before it is silenced forever.

line.dialogue: Brother Liren offers to show you the restricted archives. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Accept eagerly. The truth is worth any risk.
choices.description: Tap a crystal tuning fork against the wall to measure its resonance frequency.

line.dialogue: The harmonic returns clean — these walls were tuned like instrument strings. We're standing inside an instrument.
Wrong pitch. The vibration cracked the lattice — listen, it's weeping now.

choices.text: Ask for assurances. What protection can he offer?
choices.description: Press your ear directly against the humming wall and follow the vibration inward.

line.dialogue: There are voices layered in the stone. Hundreds of chants, compressed into one eternal note. I can almost separate them.
Too loud — my teeth are vibrating, my vision is blurring. The frequency is recalibrating to my skull and it is NOT gentle.

choices.text: Decline politely. The risk to the monastery is too great.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to chant the Lattice Mantra while you observe the crystals' response.

line.dialogue: Every crystal just shifted hue in sequence. The mantra is a key, and this room just unlocked something below us.
Pichit's tone wavered on the third syllable and the crystals screamed — one just shattered behind us. The monks definitely heard that.

lines_before.dialogue: The restricted archives are a cavern of pulsating crystal records. In a side chamber, a strange device glows—a leg-shaped resonator made of Lattice shards.
A resonant prosthetic… This shouldn’t be possible. The crystal’s feedback loop would overload a living nervous system.
Unless someone figured out how to harmonize it. Is the pay good for whoever did? Because this is genius.
Whoa! I’m in a good mood. This could change everything for skycity folks who lost limbs in lattice-storms!
But at what cost? This technology bends the natural song. How good is he, the creator, at understanding the consequences?
It was a Listener, decades ago. He believed the prosthetic could let one ‘walk’ the Lattice’s song directly. He… vanished. The Orders sealed his work.
The prosthetic hums, its pitch shifting subtly. The surrounding crystals begin to vibrate in sympathy.
It’s reacting to our presence. The resonance is building.

lines_after.dialogue: Great. So we’ve woken up the forbidden leg. How good is this guy at de-escalation?
The device seeks a Singer. Or something close to one. It’s trying to communicate.
The hum… it’s kind of pretty. Makes my bones feel warm.

line.dialogue: The resonant prosthetic activates, its song growing louder and more complex. What do you do?

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with it using your own latent resonance.
choices.description: Examine the prosthetic's harmonic core for signs of forced resonance calibration.

line.dialogue: The frequency signatures are locked—someone tuned this to a living nervous system. This wasn't engineered. It was *grown*.
I can't isolate the harmonic source. Every time I get close, the resonance shifts—it's like the prosthetic knows I'm looking.

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze and try to dampen the frequency safely.
choices.description: Demand Chanida explain why she's celebrating before understanding the ethical implications.

line.dialogue: I'm not saying it isn't remarkable, Chanida. But someone's nervous system was *harmonized* with this. Who volunteered for that? Or did they?
Chanida, I'm trying to be direct with you, but you're not hearing me—this technology has a donor somewhere who didn't consent.

choices.text: Let Chanida try to interface with it physically, risking feedback.
choices.description: Touch the prosthetic directly and let its resonance sync with your own neural frequency.

line.dialogue: I can feel it—there's a second heartbeat inside. Faint, afraid. Someone is still connected to this. They're alive, and they're terrified.
The resonance hit me like a wall of static. My vision went white, my teeth ached—whatever

lines_before.dialogue: The party, having uncovered the Listeners' secret library, stands before a vast, silent chamber. Ancient tapestries depict the Lattice's song as a radiant, branching tree.
So the Tonal Orders don't just control the charts. They control the history books too. How do you write a lie this big and sleep at night?
We were told it was for stability. That the truth of The Silencing would cause panic. Could you please write it down for me? The real reason you seek this knowledge?
Because a song locked away is a world half-lived. The Lattice doesn't just respond; it remembers.
These carvings... they show Resonance Ships from before The Silencing. Their designs are different. More organic. How do you write instructions for a song that's been forgotten?
You feel it, don't you? The hum in the stone. It's not just data, it's a feeling. He means it! The monk is terrified of what we're finding.

My cousin, she works in the lower archives. Said they found old schematics for... well, not ships. More like... limbs. Crystal limbs that could tap the Lattice directly. Is the pay good for keeping that quiet? I'd bet it is.
A prosthetic that lets you hear the song without a ship? No wonder the Orders buried it. That's not navigation. That's communion.

lines_after.dialogue: The monk's resolve wavers. The weight of generations of silence presses down.
The Chamber of Roots. It is below us. Where the first Listeners transcribed the world's song directly into the living crystal. It is... forbidden.
Forbidden by whom? The Orders, or your own fear?
By the memory of the cost. To touch the root-song is to risk becoming part of it. Your friend's leg... it might react.

line.dialogue: The monk offers a choice: leave with the knowledge they have, or descend into the Chamber of Roots to witness the source.

choices.text: Easy: Leave with the transcripts. (Gain detailed lore, avoid immediate danger, but the mystery remains.)
choices.outcome_summary: The party secures valuable historical records but leaves the central power of the Lattice untapped.
choices.description: Direct Arthit to tune the prosthetic using ship navigation

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Arthit misreads the situation. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Medium: Send only Pichit and the monk. (High risk/reward for Pichit, party remains safe above.)
choices.outcome_summary: Pichit undergoes a profound, personal resonance event, potentially awakening latent abilities.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to question the Orders' silence, drawing on monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The risk doesn't pay off. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Hard: Descend together. (The entire party faces the raw song of the world, triggering the prosthetic's full potential.)
choices.outcome_summary: A transformative and dangerous encounter with the Lattice's core frequency, altering the party and the prosthetic permanently.
choices.description: Convince the villager to use village secrets and trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the villager's call. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
Defeat. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_before.dialogue: The Chamber of Roots is a cavern where the monastery's stone bleeds into a single, massive, pulsing crystal formation. The air vibrates with a deep, foundational chord.
The acoustic pressure... it's immense. When's he coming? The monk said the head of their order would try to stop us. He's probably already on his way.
[Chanida's prosthetic leg begins to glow with a soft, sympathetic light, humming in tune with the chamber.]
Whoa! It's... singing. I can feel it in my bones. What did you say about risk, Pichit? This feels like coming home.
Don't get poetic. That thing is drawing power directly from the world-crystal. Probably not covered by the warranty.
This is the truth they silenced. Not a catastrophe, but a... convergence. The Lattice didn't shatter civilization. It tried to join with it.
You understand. The Silencing was a feedback loop. Human song meeting world-song without harmony. The Orders didn't preserve navigation to save us. They did it to control us.
Shouting from above! They've found the entrance! He winked at me! The guard at the gate, I swear he winked! They're coming!

lines_after.dialogue: The foundational chord swells. Chanida's leg acts as a conduit, projecting a visible wave of resonant energy that parts the crystal before them, revealing a path deeper into the light.
The Lattice is offering a path. Not through it, but with it.
Offering, or demanding? That harmonic is rewriting the crystal around us. Probably a one-way trip.
The Orders' ships are above. We can't go back. The only way is forward... into the song.

line.dialogue: The root-song opens a resonant pathway through the Lattice itself. The Orders' enforcers are descending. The party must choose how to use this newfound connection.

choices.text: Easy: Seal the chamber behind you. (Escape into the unknown Lattice, leaving the Orders and the monastery behind.)
choices.outcome_summary: The party vanishes into legend, their fate unknown. The monastery is sealed, and the Orders' monopoly is shaken but not broken.
choices.description: Strike the prosthetic leg with the flat of your blade to interrupt the resonance, 15 words

line.dialogue: The vibration stopped — but Chanida, your leg is cracked down the alloy seam. Move carefully now.
I struck too late; the harmonic locked in and now my sword is vibrating like a tuning fork in my grip.

choices.text: Medium: Amplify the song to disable the pursuing ships. (A show of force that broadcasts the truth across resonant channels.)
choices.outcome_summary: A temporary victory that cripples the immediate threat but declares open rebellion against the Orders, making you hunted fugitives.
choices.description: Grab Chanida's shoulders and physically drag her backward away from the root chamber's threshold, 15 words

line.dialogue: Good — distance weakens the pull. Her leg's still glowing but the resonance is fading with every meter.
You can't budge her — she's rooted like a tree, and now the glow is crawling up past her knee.

choices.text: Hard: Channel the song upward, to the floating cities. (Attempt to share the raw, unmediated truth of the Lattice with everyone.)
choices.outcome_summary: A cataclysmic act of revelation. It risks another Silencing-level event but has the potential to shatter the Orders' control forever.
choices.description: Press both palms flat against the root wall and attempt to harmonize your own voice with the frequency, 15 words

line.dialogue: You matched it — the pressure just collapsed inward. The root is breathing now, slow, like it's listening to us.
Your pitch was wrong and the root *screamed* — my leg cracked something inside and I can feel it bleeding light.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire pierces downward from the floating city of Veridia, a colossal needle of resonant crystal plunging into the shimmering Lattice. A deep, steady hum—the Calming Tone—permeates the air, pressing against your chest.
Listen to that! It's like the whole world is purring. (This cute and this inviting)… how could you pass it up? We have to see where it goes!
It's not 'cute,' it's oppressive. Makes my teeth itch. And it means anyone within a mile knows we're here. Subtlety is dead.
The structural integrity reports for this sector are… incomplete. We should proceed with extreme caution. The harmonic stress on the crystal could be unstable.
Yet, within this enforced openness, what truths might surface that would otherwise hide in silence? The Tone strips away pretense.
Ahead, a robed figure stands at a railing overlooking the Lattice's kaleidoscopic surface. It's a Listener Monk, their head tilted as if catching a faint melody.
The Calming Tone… a beautiful lie. It soothes, yes. But it also drowns out the quieter songs. The ones that tell of what lies *beneath* the Lattice.

lines_after.dialogue: What quieter songs?
There’s a high chance the Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a… correction. Our archives hint at voices from below that the Tonal Orders didn't want heard.
Of course they did. Monopoly 101: control the narrative, control the map. I'm not finished yet! What's the 'Groundless' movement got to do with this?

line.dialogue: The monk glances around, the hum making secrets hard to keep. He seems to want to speak, but fears who might be listening.

choices.text: Assure him of discretion. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Pichit attempts to tune the prosthetic, relying on staff meditation

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The gamble fails. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Press him on the political risk. (Intimidation)
choices.description: Have Chanida focus frequency mapping on the deep vibration to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. She hears something no one else can.
The lattice has other plans. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Offer to compare his findings with your own resonance readings. (Scholarship)
choices.description: The monk volunteers to map the frequency corridors, leveraging crystal bowls

line.dialogue: the monk succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk, after your prompting, leads you to a small observation alcove shielded from the main Tone. Here, the Lattice's natural, chaotic song is faintly audible—a symphony of cracks and chimes.
My faith guides me. I’m a Christian, in my way. I serve the truth of creation, not the edicts of a guild. The Groundless… they believe there is life below. Not monsters. Civilization.
Theoretically impossible. The pressure, the resonant dissonance… any structure would be pulverized.
Unless they *used* the resonance! Like a ship, but… permanent. A whole city down there! Shall we go to the seaside? I mean, the Lattice-sea-side!
A smooth voice cuts through the ambient sound. 'A fascinating hypothesis. And a costly one to investigate.' The Trade Negotiator steps into the alcove, his smile not reaching his eyes.
Forgive the intrusion. The Tone makes it so hard to have a private word. May I see your driver's license? Figuratively speaking. Your credentials for poking at world-shaking theories.
Our license is 'we're here and you're not stopping us.' What do you want?
Merely to offer context. The Tonal Orders fund my city's stability. Stories of 'life below'… they upset trade routes. They're bad for business. And for the health of curious monks.

lines_after.dialogue: You threaten him?

I illuminate consequences. His order's funding, your ship's resonance charts… all exist at the pleasure of the Orders. Exploring the unknown has a price, and it's often paid by those who can least afford it.
He speaks of a different silence. One made of withheld knowledge and fear.
We can't just back down now!

line.dialogue: The Negotiator's friendly threat hangs in the air. The monk looks torn. The Calming Tone hums on, an ironic backdrop to the rising tension.

choices.text: Confront the Negotiator directly. Call his bluff. (Confrontation)
choices.description: Arthit volunteers to use the leg as a lattice probe, leveraging ship navigation

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Propose a deal: we investigate discreetly, share any profitable finds. (Negotiation)
choices.description: Ask Malee to decode the cryptic message, drawing on mechanical repair

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The risk doesn't pay off. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: Publicly align with the monk and the Groundless cause here and now, risking immediate reprisal. (Defiance)
choices.description: The merchant uses negotiation to trace the anomalous signal near the resonance anchor

line.dialogue: the merchant succeeds. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the merchant is thwarted. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire's steady hum vibrates through your bones. The Negotiator stands near the crystal anchor's base, smiling as if expecting you.
Ah, you made it. I was just admiring the engineering. The price is the same, you know—for passage or for silence. Both have value.
Cut the pleasantries. We know you're hiding something about the Groundless Movement. What did you sell them?
Me? I was bad! I admit it. I provided... outdated resonance charts. But they insisted. Said they needed to reach the Lattice's heart.
Outdated? You sent them to their deaths! The Lattice shifts—those charts are suicide!
The Monk warned us about false harmonics. If the Groundless used wrong frequencies...
Why would they take that risk? What were they searching for that was worth everything?
Freedom from the Tonal Orders' monopoly. You, too, want that, don't you? The truth has a price. Always.

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk approaches, his robes fluttering in the spire's resonant wind. His face is pale.
I have listened. The Lattice's song... it's changing. The Groundless didn't just die. They caused a fracture.
The steady hum of the Anchor Spire wavers for a moment—a discordant shudder that makes your teeth ache.
Of course. One idealistic movement tries to break the system, and instead they break the world. Again.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator offers a deal: his silence about your involvement for safe passage off the spire. The Monk begs you to warn the Tonal Orders about the fracture. Arthit notes the spire's resonance is destabilizing—you must act.

choices.text: Accept the Negotiator's deal. Take his ship and flee. (Gain safe passage, lose the Monk's trust.)
choices.description: Grab the merchant by his collar and slam him against the resonance console, demanding names, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Malee: "Start talking or I introduce your face to this console—your choice, and you've got three seconds."]
[Malee: "He's got nothing—look at him shaking. We're wasting time on a middleman who doesn't know the chain."]

choices.text: Arrest the Negotiator for his crimes. Use his ship to reach the Tonal Orders. (Risk confrontation, gain evidence.)
choices.description: Pull up the Lattice shard's transaction log on your datapad and show him the death count, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Chanida: "Fourteen names. Fourteen people who trusted your frequency calibrations. You're going to help me find every one of their families and explain it."]
[Chanida: "He won't even look at the screen. Guilt or guiltlessness—it doesn't matter. He's already made himself the victim."]

choices.text: Stay at the spire. Try to stabilize the fracture using your own resonance. (Dangerous, unknown consequences.)
choices.description: Lean back, arms crossed, and offer him a deal—full cooperation in exchange for disappearing somewhere new, 15 words

line.dialogue: [You: "I know someone in the Outer Stations who can erase your trail. But the coordinates, the buyers, the source—everything. Now."]
[You: "He's calculating. I can see it behind his eyes—the profit margin on betrayal versus the cost of silence. He's going to run."]

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire groans. Cracks spiderweb up the crystal column. The harmonic tone has become a dissonant wail.
Interesting! No—terrifying! The fracture is singing back. It's learning from our resonance. Please call me back if you have any insight!
Insight? The whole thing's about to shatter! We need to get to the resonance controls!
The Negotiator's ship is still docked. But if the spire falls, the island above...
My ship! Let me go! I'll pay you anything! Good night to this place—let it fall!
He's right about one thing. This spire is done. The Groundless Movement's legacy is another Silencing.
No. Their legacy is proof the system can be challenged. The fracture isn't an end—it's a new note.
The crystal anchor pulses with sickly light. The fracture deep within the Lattice echoes, a hungry sound.

lines_after.dialogue: Your choice resonates through the spire. The crystal steadies or shatters. The hum returns, changed forever.
The song... it's different. Not broken. Transformed. The Groundless didn't fail. They added a new verse.
In the new silence, you understand: some truths cannot be controlled, only heard.

line.dialogue: The fracture in the Lattice is reacting to the spire's resonance. You stand at the control nexus. The Negotiator struggles toward his ship. The Monk is recording the new harmonics. The spire's fate—and what it means for the world—is in your hands.

choices.text: Override the spire. Shut it down completely. Stop the fracture from spreading. (Save the island, silence the new song.)
choices.description: Malee uses scavenger instincts to calibrate against the frequency near the crystal depth

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: Amplify the fracture. Let it resonate fully. See what new truth emerges. (Risk everything, chance for revelation.)
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using staff meditation to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Pichit loses control. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Harmonize with it. Use your own voice to guide the fracture into a stable new frequency. (Requires perfect resonance, ultimate consequence.)
choices.description: Have the monk risk using meditation to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the monk pulls it off. Ancient knowledge surfaces, connecting past and present.
the monk loses control. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery hangs like a suspended bell over the Lattice, its halls carved to amplify the faintest hum from the crystalline world below.
The silence here is... profound. It's not empty, but full of potential sound. We were so bored on the voyage, but this is different.
Different? It's a library for people who'd rather listen to rocks than talk to each other. I'm sure it's thrilling.
We should proceed with respect. The Listeners' work is delicate. A wrong step could disrupt years of study.
Oh, come on! I saw a market on the lower terrace. Let's at least see if anyone's heard about that Open Frequency Map!
Before you can decide, a figure in ochre robes approaches, hands clasped. A Trade Negotiator, his smile polished like a gem, glides beside him.
Greetings, travelers! Such rare faces. I am Brother Vichai, though my friends in the Tonal Orders call me a facilitator. And this is my associate, Kanya.
Kanya. I walk the Lattice. You're not from any Order.

lines_after.dialogue: We seek understanding. Of the natural song. I'm a Buddhist, and there's a peace here that resonates.
Wonderful! Most Thais are Buddhist. A shared foundation for trade, yes? But understanding... sometimes requires a key. A map, perhaps.
He talks in circles. The map you whisper about? It's dangerous. It shows frequencies the Orders haven't taxed. They'd bury it.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator offers a 'guided tour' to the acoustic archives, for a 'modest fee.' Kanya the Scavenger simply watches, her hand resting on a weathered resonator.

choices.line: Pay the Negotiator. Smooth talk often leads to smooth paths.
choices.description: Approach the central crystal pillar and place your palm flat against its surface, listening for vibrations. 15 words

line.dialogue: The crystal hums beneath my hand—a low, ancient tone, like a heartbeat remembering something vital.
My hand slips; the surface is colder than death and silent as a buried throat.

choices.line: Follow Kanya's lead. Her surface knowledge may reveal more than monastery walls.
choices.description: Follow Chanida down the spiral stairs toward the lower terrace market before the others decide. 15 words

line.dialogue: Yes! The market smells of cardamom and old parchment—there's a woman selling memory shards, I knew it!
Dead end. Just a locked gate and a very annoyed monk glaring at us like we've tracked mud through his soul.

choices.line: Politely decline both. Wander the public halls and listen for yourselves.
choices.description: Kneel at the reading alcove Arthit indicated and whisper your name into the bowl of crystallized salt.

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the scavenger misreads the situation. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: Your choice leads you to a secluded resonance chamber, its walls lined with singing crystals. Kanya traces a finger along a jagged fissure.
The monastery's heart. Also its blind spot. They listen for harmony. I listen for cracks. The map's frequency... it's here, in the fractures.
A crack in the song? Could you tell me how to get to the source? Before that merchant sells the secret to the highest bidder!
This feels like trespassing. If the Listeners guard this knowledge, there must be a reason. A dangerous resonance?
Or a profitable one they want to monopolize. Everything is a commodity here, even silence.
May I have some time? To truly listen? The answer is in the discord, not the perfect tone.
Pichit closes his eyes. The chamber's hum splinters into a chaotic, beautiful tapestry of sound. A hidden pattern emerges from the noise.
I got the answer now. The map isn't a chart... it's a state. A way to tune oneself to the Lattice's raw, uncharted frequencies. To become a Singer.

lines_after.dialogue: You hear it. Good. But realizing it is one thing. Embodying it? That's how you get disappeared.
My, my. Such discovery!
The Negotiator stands in the doorway, his smile unchanged. Four Tonal Order enforcers loom behind him, their resonators humming a controlled, aggressive pitch.
A Singer's frequency, unlicensed, is contraband. The map in your mind, or on your person, belongs to the Orders. Now, let's discuss a peaceful transfer.

line.dialogue: The chamber has one exit, now blocked. The fractured crystal wall behind you vibrates with the unstable frequency you just deciphered.

choices.line: Surrender the 'map.' It's only theoretical knowledge for now. Live to fight another day.
choices.description: Follow the harmonic resonance deeper, pressing your palm against the vibrating walls to navigate blindly, 15 words

line.dialogue: The stone hums a path for me — two lefts, then down. The song wants to be found.
The vibration stops under my hand. Dead stone. We're standing in a pocket where even the monastery can't hear itself.

choices.line: Try to talk your way out. Use the Negotiator's own love of deal-making against him.
choices.description: Signal Arthit to silently disable the listening tubes — clay pipes in the walls carrying sound to the Listeners above, 15 words

line.dialogue: Plugging them with monastery clay — they'll hear nothing but their own silence for hours. We move now.
The pipe crumbles in my hand. The fracture echoes through every corridor. They know exactly where we stand.

choices.line: Risk it all. Channel the fractured frequency through your own resonator, hoping to shatter the blockade or the crystals themselves.
choices.description: Have Malee identify which monk's cell contains records of the Chorus fracture by checking ink stains on the doorframes, 15 words

line.dialogue: This door — decades of notation stains, different hands. Whoever slept here spent their life studying the break. It's here.
Every door is stained the same. They were all obsessed, or they wanted anyone looking to waste time checking every room.

lines_before.dialogue: The party returns to the central meditation chamber of Phrao Monastery. The air hums with the residual energy of their discovery. The Open Frequency Map glows faintly on a crystal plinth.
Okay, we've got the map. But what's in there? The real secrets, I mean. The stuff the Tonal Orders would kill for.
Probably a list of forbidden dinner times. Look, I can't speak the technical tonal dialect these Listeners use. This is getting arcane.
We must be cautious. This knowledge is a beacon. The Trade Negotiator has been watching us too closely. You're all back late from the archives!
Arthit is right. This map isn't just coordinates; it's a key to the Lattice's oldest memories. A home we've all forgotten.
Home, huh? My home's the surface. And down there, these 'open frequencies' you found... they're unstable. Like cracks in glass.
Cracks can be profitable, my hardy friend! But also dangerous. Perhaps we should... conserve this knowledge. For the right buyer, of course.
The map pulses, projecting a complex harmonic pattern into the air. It points to a sealed resonance chamber deep below the monastery.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the hum of the chamber. The path forward is clear, but the risks are unknown.
Great. More exploring. My favorite.
This is the threshold. We must listen to what the Lattice wants to tell us.

line.dialogue: How do you proceed towards the sealed chamber?

choices.text: Use the map's primary frequency to resonate open the main door. (Direct, but obvious.)
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing tonal knowledge to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
The lattice has other plans. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Have the Scavenger identify structural weaknesses in the old stonework. (Unconventional, but stealthy.)
choices.description: Malee steps forward with crystal prosthetic, ready to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Malee pulls it off. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The resonance turns hostile. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: Attempt to 'Sing' a counter-harmony to cancel the locking frequency. (Risks alerting every Listener in the monastery.)
choices.description: Convince the scavenger to use harvesting tools and map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the scavenger pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the scavenger hits a wall. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The inner chamber is a perfect crystal sphere. At its heart floats a primordial Lattice shard, vibrating with a pure, foundational tone. The air crackles with potential energy.
Whoa. That's... it's my dream job to find something like this! The source tone!
The energy emission is colossal. We must be wise. We should turn off the main resonator to conserve the chamber's stability.
Conserve? No, no! This is a fortune! A monopoly-breaking fortune! The Tonal Orders would pay any price!
He's spot on! About the danger, I mean. That shard's vibration matches the 'Silencing' event in my surface-scans. Touch it wrong, and we repeat history.
Fantastic. So we start an apocalypse. Typical day.
This is not a commodity. It's a memory. The world's first memory. To use it for profit or power would be a deeper silencing.
The Trade Negotiator edges forward, a crystal amplifier in hand. The Scavenger readies a damping tool. The party stands between the shard and catastrophe.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber's tone settles into a new, permanent harmony. The consequences of the choice resonate outwards, unseen but profound.
The Lattice remembers our choice. It always does.
The Open Frequency Map dissolves, its knowledge now part of the world's song. The subplot is resolved, but the chronicle continues.

line.dialogue: What is your final action with the primordial shard?

choices.text: Safely dissipate its energy into the Lattice, preserving the knowledge but removing the power. (The conservative path.)
choices.description: Reach bare-handed for the shard, letting its resonance flood your nervous system, 15 words

line.dialogue: The waveform just sang back to me — I can map its entire harmonic structure from this!
Your biometrics are spiking wrong — pull back before it rewrites your neural patterning!

choices.text: Use it to create a public navigation beacon, breaking the Tonal Orders' monopoly forever. (A revolutionary act.)
choices.description: Demand the merchant calculate containment costs before anyone touches the shard, 14 words

line.dialogue: Finally, pragmatism. If his profit margin survives the math, the extraction plan is sound.
You want *costs*? I'll show you costs — my entire network just walked, you bureaucratic fool!

choices.text: Attempt to commune with it directly, to learn the true cause of The Silencing. (The greatest risk and reward.)
choices.description: Follow the scavenger's instincts and encase the shard in dampening salvage foam immediately, 14 words

line.dialogue: See that? Emissions just dropped forty percent — that's how you handle a live one, yeah!
Wrong foam ratio — you've trapped the heat in! It's gonna crack open in minutes!

lines_before.dialogue: The first pale light of dawn paints the rusted hulls of Tha Khwae Scrapyard. The air is cold, thick with the smell of oil and ozone.
A distant, rhythmic CLANG-CLANG-CLANG begins—the yard's awakening heartbeat. Pichit stirs near the smoldering remains of a campfire.
From morning until evening... this sound never changes. The Lattice's true song is buried beneath it.
Ugh, my head. I can't eat anything. That scavenger's brew last night was... potent.
You drank it. Don't complain to us. We probably can't finish salvaging that resonator array today anyway. It's a wreck.
We should prioritize. The Tonal Order's inspection is in three days. If our ship's signature is off by even a quarter-tone...
A fresh beginning, Arthit. Not just for the ship. I heard something last night. A pure frequency, under the noise. Like a calling.
A figure approaches, robes grey with dust. It's the Listener Monk, his face etched with a deep conflict.

lines_after.dialogue: You are the ones with the damaged resonance ship. The 'Dawn Chaser.'
We are. You've been listening.
I listen to what the Lattice wishes to say. And what the Orders wish to silence. Your ship... its fracture sings a truth they hide.
What truth?
Not here. The scrapyard ears are many. Meet me at the Shattered Bell, where the crane's shadow falls at noon. Come quietly.

line.dialogue: The monk slips away into the maze of metal. The party looks at each other.

choices.line: Follow the monk's instructions precisely. (Stealth)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to hum the sound's pattern so you can compare it against the Tonal Order's approved frequency charts, 15 words

line.dialogue: Pichit closes his eyes, and the melody he hums makes your teeth ache with something older than any sanctioned scale.
Pichit tries, but the sound dissolves the moment he reaches for it. "It doesn't want to be remembered," he mutters.

choices.line: Salvage parts first, then investigate. (Resources)
choices.description: Search the scavenger's discarded flask for residue and sniff it before Chanida drinks anything else unverified, 15 words

line.dialogue: You find a violet sediment crusted at the bottom that matches nothing in the salvage index. Chanida goes pale.
Chanida slaps the flask from your hand. "I already told you—I know what I drank. It knew me first.

choices.line: Ask the local scavengers about the monk. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Climb the scrap tower alone to record the sound's source before the Tonal Order inspectors arrive, 15 words

line.dialogue: From the rusted summit you see it: a massive tuning fork buried in the earth, still vibrating after centuries.
The tower shifts under your weight. Arthit grabs your ankle. "The inspection isn't worth your spine. We regroup.

lines_before.dialogue: The heart of the scrapyard is a canyon of dead ships. The Shattered Bell is a ruined freighter's bridge, perched precariously.
Conserve power. Don't leave your personal resonators on. We don't know what frequencies are bouncing around here.
Relax. They sell better dampeners at the bazaar in the upper city. Not that we can afford them.
Inside the bridge, the monk waits. A Surface Scavenger is with him, her eyes sharp and distrustful.
Outsiders. I have to take my kids to school up in the stacks. Make this quick.
This is Ladda. She's Groundless. She's seen what falls through the cracks in the official charts.
Groundless? The movement that rejects the Floating Cities?
We don't reject them. We just know they're built on lies. The Tonal Orders... they're not navigating. They're *herding*. There are safe paths down to the old world they're hiding.

lines_after.dialogue: The Surface? You've been *down there*?
Fragments. Enough to know the Silencing wasn't what they teach. It was a note, a single terrible note that... crystallized everything. It's still down there, humming.
My order is split. Some wish to study this. Others wish to obey the Orders and let it sleep. Your ship's resonator, when it broke, it briefly echoed that same... fatal frequency.
That's impossible. Our charts are clean!
Are they? Or did we just buy the lie like everyone else?

line.dialogue: Ladda pulls a small, rough crystal from her pouch. It pulses with a faint, sickly light.

choices.line: Take the crystal for study. (Accept the risk)
choices.description: Switch off your resonator and follow Ladda into the collapsed stairwell, 15 words exactly here now

line.dialogue: Ladda presses her palm against the fractured wall and whispers, "You hear that? The wreckage remembers what brought it down.
Ladda yanks her hand back and hisses, "Your resonator's still humming — you're broadcasting our position to everything with teeth down here.

choices.line: Demand to see the data source first. (Verify the claim)
choices.description: Ask the scavenger what he means by school up in the spires, pressing for details

line.dialogue: The scavenger wipes grease from his knuckles and mutters, "Ain't a real school. It's where they teach Groundless kids which floors will eat them and which won't.
The scavenger spits at your boots and snaps, "You don't get to know. Outsiders ask questions, my kids disappear. That's how it works.

choices.line: Refuse the crystal and report the monk to the local Order. (Uphold the law)
choices.description: Buy the dampeners Malee mentioned and rig them to Ladda's spine manually

line.dialogue: Malee
The lattice has other plans. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's industrial cacophony seems to swell as you stand before the entrance to the grounded Resonance Ship, the 'Glimmering Echo'. Its hull is half-buried in scrap, a monument to failure.

The Listeners sealed this vessel. Its resonator was... altered. It didn't just fail. It sang a note that cracked the Lattice here. Can you make it back! (drunk and can't drive home, etc.) We can't let that happen again.
Altered how? Sabotage?
Rumors say the Tonal Orders didn't like its captain. Too friendly with the Groundless. Asking questions about what's *really* down below the crystal.
Of course. The monopoly protects its monopoly. Shocking. (Don't) make me cry!
The structural integrity is questionable. If we power the resonator, even to access its logs, we risk a localized Silencing event. The data might not be worth it.
But the truth is inside. A song that was deemed too dangerous to hear. We have to listen.
A low, unstable hum begins to emanate from the ship's cracked resonator core. It wasn't you who activated it.

line.dialogue: The unstable resonator is powering up on its own, its frequency warping the nearby scrap metal. You need to stabilize it to safely access the ship's log.

choices.text: Chanida's Impulse: Smash the auxiliary power coupling. It's crude but will cut the feed.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using Listener training to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The lattice has other plans. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Arthit's Analysis: Reroute the resonance through a salvaged damping crystal. Precise but slow.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing hidden frequencies to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
The risk doesn't pay off. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Pichit's Connection: Match the unstable frequency with your own voice, guiding it to a neutral harmonic. Risky, but you might hear the true song.
choices.description: The monk attempts to decode the tonal pattern, relying on lattice study

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His recording captures a denied frequency.
The risk doesn't pay off. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_after.dialogue: The hum settles into a steady, mournful tone. The ship's main console flickers to life, projecting fragmented log entries into the dusty air.
By the Lattice... the captain's logs. He discovered a pattern. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a... a commanded frequency. From one of the Floating Cities.
The Groundless were right. We were pushed off. Can you make a u-turn? On history, I mean. Can we?
The song of the world was broken on purpose. To control the sky.

lines_before.dialogue: Before you can process the revelation, the harsh whine of Tonal Order patrol ships cuts through the scrapyard din. Searchlights sweep the debris.

They're triangulating the active resonator signal. We've drawn them right to the evidence. Don't leave it on. / Don't leave it open. (electricity, door, etc.) We need to shut everything down and scatter.
Too late. They sell the (new iPads) at the (mall). And by that I mean, they sell 'justice' here in the scrapyard. They're deploying enforcers.
Let them come! We have to get this data to the Listeners, to the Groundless! (I have to) take my kids to school. This truth is our responsibility now!
The old maintenance conduits under the plate! They lead to the surface edge. It's a crawl, and the Lattice is thin there... but it's a way out.
The data... it must survive. My order must hear this. But the conduit exits onto an active harvesting zone. The Lattice will be singing its raw, fractured song. It could shatter a mind.
Enforcer boots clang on metal catwalks above. The choice is now: hide the truth, or run with it into the teeth of the storm.
A hidden song started all this. Maybe a new one has to end it. We run. We carry the echo.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Order is sealing the scrapyard. Your escape path is perilous and will expose you to the raw, chaotic resonance of a damaged Lattice zone. How do you shield the crucial data—and yourselves?

choices.text: Data First: Use the Glimmering Echo's resonator as a decoy burst, overloading it to mask your escape. The ship and evidence are destroyed, but you live.
choices.description: Squeeze into the maintenance conduits and seal the plate behind you, 12 words

line.dialogue: I know these tunnels — follow close and don't touch the walls, they're live.
The plate's warped — it won't seat flush. They'll see the gap for sure.

choices.text: Unified Chorus: The party links hands, with Pichit and the Monk trying to harmonize your group's resonance against the chaos. The data is preserved, but the psychic strain is severe.
choices.description: Destroy the resonator and run the data on foot through the crowd above, 14 words

line.dialogue: Signal dies, we disappear into the market traffic — I like it. Move, now.
You cracked the housing but the core's still pulsing — you just made it *louder*.

choices.text: Into the Fracture: Pichit leads the group directly into the most intense sonic zone, using the captain's forbidden frequency as a key. You might find a new resonance path... or be utterly unmade.
choices.description: Hold position and transmit the data directly to the Listener before they converge, 12 words

line.dialogue: Uploading now — seventy percent, eighty — the Listener has it. We did it.
They're jamming the band.

lines_after.dialogue: You burst onto the Lattice surface at the scrapyard's ragged edge. The sky is a cage of searchlights, but below your feet, the crystal thrums with a painful, beautiful truth.
The song isn't broken. It's just... waiting. We're the next note.
The Listeners will hear of this. The Groundless will have their proof. The Lattice remembers what was done to it.
As the patrols clamor behind you, you take the first step onto the unknown frequency, the stolen log glowing in your hand. The chronicle continues.
Go. I'll muddy the trail. Tell them below... we're coming home.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hum with the low, resonant frequency of knowledge. Crystal shelves rise like frozen waterfalls, each holding etched metal scrolls that map safe passages through the Lattice. The air smells of ozone and old parchment.
Look at this place! It's really a great place to live! All this knowledge, just sitting here. Think of the secrets.

More like a great place to be smothered by bureaucracy. The Tonal Orders guard these 'secrets' like dragons hoarding gold. We live near each other in the floating cities, yet they keep us in the dark.
A necessary precaution, perhaps. The wrong frequency could destabilize an entire island's foundation. The system, however rigid, maintains order.
Order born from the Silencing. We built these archives from fear of the unknown song. But what if the Lattice's true song isn't meant to be controlled, but understood?
A robed Listener Monk, the Listener monk, approaches silently. His eyes hold a deep, troubled focus.
Understanding is our pursuit. But some harmonies... they are dissonant with the official records. I'm happy to hear others question the silence between the notes.

lines_after.dialogue: Dissonant how? Are the maps wrong?
Not wrong. Incomplete. The Orders chart only what is profitable and safe for the Resonance Ships. There are... other vibrations. Fainter songs from below the Lattice.
Songs from the ground? That's Groundless Movement talk. Heretical and bad for business, according to the Orders.

line.dialogue: The monk seems to be wrestling with a confession. How does Pichit engage?

choices.text: Offer philosophical reassurance. ("All truths begin as whispers.")
choices.description: Press your palm against the nearest crystal wall and listen for residual frequencies.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "There — beneath the hum, voices layered like sediment. Someone recorded everything they silenced here.
Malee — "All I hear is my own heartbeat bouncing back at me. These walls don't remember, they just *absorb*.

choices.text: Press cautiously for specifics. ("What have your studies heard?")
choices.description: Demand Pichit explain what "the Silencing" actually did to the people who lived here before.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "We didn't erase them. We *clarified* them. Every citizen became data — preserved, indexed, retrievable. Immortality through bureaucracy.
Pichit — "That question requires a Form 7-C authorization, submitted in triplicate to the Office of Historical Redaction. I'm sure you understand.

choices.text: Suggest involving the pragmatic Arthit. ("Arthit, assess the risk of this knowledge.")
choices.description: Slip away from the group and search for an unsealed archive terminal.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "I found one still active — there are *names* in here, thousands of them, and playback logs. These people weren't archived, they were *recorded* against their will.
Malee — "Every

lines_before.dialogue: Before the monk can elaborate, a smooth voice cuts through the quiet. A Trade Negotiator, the Trade Negotiator, glides over, his smile not reaching his eyes.
Listener Kavi! Always a pleasure. And you've brought... guests. It's very important that visitors to the Archives respect the established harmonies. Stability is the foundation of trade.
We intend no disruption. We seek only to understand the routes better.
Of course! All understanding is found in the sanctioned scrolls. Anything else is... noise. Dangerous noise. Who is this lady, by the way? I don't believe we've been introduced.
He gestures toward Malee, his gaze appraising.
Just another cynic wondering what you're really selling. Information has a price, even here.
A sharp mind! The price is adherence to the charted course. Straying from it risks another Silencing. Now, if you'll excuse us, the Listener has duties.
He was talking to us first! I'm gonna ask him... what those other songs are!

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, youthful curiosity. It's very important that you know some curiosities lead to dead air. Listener, the High Archivist requires your presence regarding a... tonal anomaly in Sector Seven.
The monk, Kavi, pales slightly. The merchant's message is clear.
I... must go. Forgive me. The paths are not always as they seem.
An anomaly. That sounds like the unknown you mentioned.

line.dialogue: The merchant is clearly obstructing them. The monk is being pulled away. The party must decide their next move.

choices.text: Confront the merchant directly about his interference. (Chanida's impulse)
choices.description: Lean close and examine the merchant's ledger lying open beneath his palm, counting the stamped seals.

line.dialogue: Kavi — "These seals are requisition marks from the Southern Consulate. You're not a merchant — you're a fence for diverted supply lines.
Kavi — "The ink's still wet on entries from three days ago. Either business is booming or you're writing fiction for an audience.

choices.text: Subtly follow the monk to learn about the 'anomaly.' (Pichit's inquiry)
choices.description: Place a single silver thorn coin on the counter and slide it forward without explanation.

line.dialogue: Kavi — "That coin circulates only inside the Thorn Quarter. So tell me — which of your suppliers prefers payment in blood currency?
Kavi — "You're staring at it like it burned you. Relax. It's just a coin... unless you know something about these you'd rather not say aloud.

choices.text: Use Malee's cynicism to bait the merchant into revealing his true concerns. (A risky gambit)
choices.description: Step between Malee and the merchant, folding your arms, blocking her provocation with deliberate calm.

line.dialogue: Kavi — "She calls you cynic, you call her reckless — everyone's performed their part. Now perhaps we skip the theatre and discuss what you actually want from us.
Kavi — "Malee, enough. And you — merchant, trader, whatever mask you're wearing — I'd rather not let her set the terms of this conversation before you've even stated your price.

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups in a secluded reading alcove, its walls lined with sonic-dampening crystals. The air hums with suppressed knowledge.
Okay, we've got the monk's half-truths and the merchant's oily smiles. Something's rotten in these archives. I heard a strange noise from the Restricted Stacks earlier—like a crystal weeping.
