A cautious approach is paramount. The Tonal Orders guard their secrets jealously. If we're caught where we shouldn't be...
Oh, don't be so dramatic, Arthit. They'll just 'misplace' us in the deepest, darkest catalog. Probably filed under 'Regrettable Incidents.'
The silence here is not empty. It's a weight. You heard that, didn't you? The gap between what is recorded and what is true. The Groundless speak of songs the Archives have erased.

(Approaching quietly, his robes whispering) You... you heard everything? My earlier hesitation? Please, you must understand. I am sworn to preserve, but some harmonies... they are deemed 'unstable.' Suppressed.

(Appearing from behind a shelf, smile polished) Now, now, Brother. 'Unstable' is such a subjective term. Some patterns are merely... commercially sensitive. Lost routes mean found profits for those who rediscover them.
The two NPCs lock eyes, a silent battle between reverence and greed. The path forward splits like a fractured chord.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The party moves deeper into the Archives, the air growing colder, the recorded songs taking on a faint, discordant edge.
This place feels like a tomb for music. Are we sure we want to wake it up?
Some truths don't stay buried. They resonate.

line.dialogue: Whose lead do we follow into the restricted heart of the Archives?

choices.text: EASY: Trust the Listener's piety. Follow the monk's secret, reverent path to the 'Forbidden Chants' section.
choices.consequence: The monk's route is safe but slow, bypassing major guards. You gain precise, scholarly knowledge but may miss the bigger political picture.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to tune the prosthetic, relying on ship navigation

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The resonance turns hostile. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: MEDIUM: Leverage the merchant's greed. Let him 'guide' you to where he thinks the most valuable lost routes are stored.
choices.consequence: The merchant's path is riskier but more direct, using bribes and blind spots. You uncover trade secrets and black-market ties, drawing the ire of the Tonal Orders' enforcers.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to seek the dismissed truth using unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. She hears something no one else can.
Defeat. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: HARD: Follow Chanida's impulsive lead towards the 'weeping' sound, trusting her ears over any map.
choices.consequence: You plunge into the acoustically unstable, abandoned wings. The path is dangerous and unpredictable, but you may find the raw, unedited truth of the Silencing—and what the Groundless are truly afraid of.
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using negotiation to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the merchant pushes through. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The resonance turns hostile. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

acts.title: The Catching of the Lost Chord

lines_before.dialogue: You stand in the Echo Vault, the deepest chamber of the Archives. No books here—only massive, imperfect crystal cores that painfully replay fragments of the world's song from before the Silencing. The air vibrates with trauma.
Well, this is cheerful. The world's greatest hits: 'Cataclysm in D Minor.' I think I lost my phone in all this existential dread. Or maybe my will to live.
The instability is off the charts! These recordings are raw, unrefined resonance events. One wrong frequency could shatter the vault... and us.

There! In the central crystal! That's the 'weeping'—it's a ship's log, a Singer's final broadcast during the Silencing! She lost her... everything. Her ship, her crew, her hope. But she found something else.

(Trembling) The 'Groundless Truth.' It is not a philosophy of despair... but of acceptance. The Lattice isn't a barrier to be pierced. It is the world, healing. Our ships, our cities... we are the infection.

(Voice stripped of its smoothness, now raw with horror) No. No! That would mean every trade route, every chart, every resonator we sell... it's all causing slow, silent damage. Our entire economy is a poison.
The central crystal pulses. The Singer's final, desperate harmonic hangs in the air—a key that could seal this knowledge forever. The Tonal Order guards are pounding on the vault door.
We stand at the precipice. To catch this truth is to hold the weight of the world. I didn't catch what you said before, Arthit, about caution. Now, we must choose what song defines our future.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice resonates. The crystal cores flare, and a new song—a terrible, beautiful, and undeniable truth—ripples out from the Archives, through the Lattice, towards the Floating Cities. Nothing will be the same.
The sky... it's singing.
No. It's waking up.

line.dialogue: The Lost Chord is caught. What do you do with it?

choices.text: EASY: Suppress the Resonance. Use the Archives' dampeners to contain the truth. Protect the current world order.
choices.consequence: You maintain the shaky peace of the Floating Cities. The Tonal Orders reward you, but the Groundless movement goes underground, radicalized. You live with the lie.
choices.description: Press your bare hands against the central crystal and try to hum the chord back into harmony.

line.dialogue: Malee grips the crystal, veins flooding with cold light. "Got it. Oh gods, it's not music—it's screaming. But I can hold it, I can hold it—
Malee yanks her hands back, skin frosted white. "No. No, that's not a chord. That's a mouth. It tried to sing *through* me.

choices.text: MEDIUM: Control the Narrative. Broadcast a sanitized version—a warning to navigate more carefully, not a condemnation.
choices.consequence: You spark reform, not revolution. The Orders are shaken but adapt, creating 'safer' resonators. The Groundless are divided. Change comes, but slowly and compromised.
choices.description: Order Chanida to sever the crystal's resonance threads while Arthit stabilizes the containment field.

line.dialogue: Chanida's blade flashes through filaments of sound. "Threads cut! Arthit, now—cage it before it finds a new frequency!
Chanida's blade passes through the threads harmlessly. "They're not physical—I'm cutting shadows of a sound that hasn't been played yet!

choices.text: HARD: Release the Raw Truth. Let the Singer's final, unedited harmonic resonate across the Lattice for all to hear.
choices.consequence: You shatter the monopoly of knowledge. Panic and awe sweep the cities. The Groundless find their voice. The era of the Resonance Ships ends; a dangerous, uncharted new age begins. You are hailed as liberators or damned as destroyers.
choices.description: Ask the monk to speak the 'Groundless Truth' aloud, betting that naming it will anchor it.

line.dialogue: The monk's voice cracks the air like stone. "I have no ground. I have no truth. I AM." The crystal shudders silent. "It... worked. It is caught.
The monk opens his mouth. Nothing comes out. He

lines_before.dialogue: The *Starlit Refrain* cuts through the high-altitude winds, its crystalline resonators humming a low, protective chord that parts the shimmering Lattice below. The deck vibrates with a deep, steady thrum.
Look at it all! The way the light bends down there... it’s like we’re sailing on a frozen song. I could watch it forever.
Don’t get poetic. It’s just crystallized sound. One wrong frequency from the resonator and we join the Silencing’s choir at the bottom. Forever.
The Tonal Order’s charts have been accurate so far. We should reach Skyhaven by nightfall. Provided we maintain this precise harmonic.
Yet the charts only show safe paths. They don’t record the Lattice’s own music... the parts that are sad, or angry, or lost. What size of silence does a lost soul wear?
A profound question, traveler. The Listeners seek such answers. But some silences... are heavier than others. I’m sorry I’m late to join you on deck. I was... listening.
Hear anything good?
An echo. From a sector the charts have marked 'void' for a generation. A ship that was lost. Its final resonance... lingers. You should get some rest. The sound can be draining.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost ship’s echo? That’s not just data. That’s a memory the Lattice refuses to forget.
Navigating towards an un-charted echo is against every regulation. The Tonal Orders would revoke our resonator license.
Great. So we can either chase a ghost and become beggars, or ignore it and wonder what cheap trinket of truth we passed up.

line.dialogue: The monk’s revelation hangs in the air, a dissonant note against the ship’s steady hum. Do we investigate the echo?

choices.line: Follow the echo. The truth matters more than charts. (Head towards the un-charted sector.)
choices.description: Tap your tuning fork against the nearest crystal column and listen for resonance patterns.

line.dialogue: The harmonic signature matches the Order's frequency charts—this corridor is stable enough to traverse.
That dissonance means the lattice is fractured somewhere ahead. One wrong step and we're glass.

choices.line: Log the coordinates for the Tonal Orders. Duty first. (Report the finding but stay on course.)
choices.description: Ignore the charts entirely and follow the light bending deeper into the gale's curve.

line.dialogue: The refraction is leading us somewhere the Tonal Order never mapped—look, the crystals are thinner here, almost breathable.
The light doesn't lead anywhere. It traps. We've walked in a perfect arc back to our own footprints.

choices.line: Ask the Skyhaven residents. Someone must remember. (Seek local knowledge at our destination.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sing a sustained note into the gale and watch where the crystals vibrate first.

line.dialogue: There—the far wall trembled before anything else. That's our way through. The gale just told me itself.
Your voice hit three columns at once and now the whole chamber is screaming back. Move. Now. Before it cascades

lines_before.dialogue: The ship has diverted into the 'void' sector. The Lattice here is murky, shot through with jagged, dark formations. The resonator’s hum grows strained, flickering occasionally.
Resonator stress is at 45%. I just spoke with the engineer. We can’t maintain this for long. The harmonic stability is... broken.
There! A glint in the gloom! Is that... a ship’s prow?
I’m just surprised it’s in one piece. Mostly. Looks like it crystallized mid-catastrophe. Just relax, don’t worry about it. It’s probably just a rock.
No. That’s the *Echo of Dawn*. I’ve seen its silhouette in old logs. It was a Listener vessel, searching for the source of the Silencing.
You are correct. My order has long mourned its loss. They were close to a discovery. A truth the Tonal Orders deemed... dangerous to navigation.
As you draw closer, a weak, repeating signal pulses from the derelict—a fragmented recording trapped in a loop.

(Voice crackles from the comms, an old distress call) ...Mayday... lattice resonance spiking... not natural... it’s answering something... the Singers, they were right... tell my family in Skyhaven... I’m sorry for being late...

lines_after.dialogue: Skyhaven? That’s our next port! That voice... they had family there.
A ‘not natural’ resonance. Wonderful. So the pretty crystals below might have a mean streak. What a discovery.
The signal is degrading. We have minutes before it’s gone forever. And our own resonator cannot hold this position indefinitely.
A truth deemed dangerous. A final apology. The Lattice holds more than just geography; it holds their last moments.

line.dialogue: The ghost ship holds its secret, but the *Starlit Refrain* is under strain. How do we proceed?

choices.line: Board the derelict. Recover the log for the Listeners. (Risk the ship’s stability for hard evidence.)
choices.description: Channel the resonator toward the prow to scan for active harmonic signatures before approaching, 15 words

line.dialogue: Readings are stable — whatever powered her is dormant, not dead. We can move closer safely.
The resonator spiked hard — something in that hull is *listening*. Pull back, pull back now!

choices.line: Use our resonators to amplify and capture the full signal from here. (Gain data without physical risk.)
choices.description: Wade through the silt barefoot to feel for vibrations beneath the wreckage with your feet, 15 words

line.dialogue: The sand is humming a low C — the same note as the Chord. She's still resonating from the original song.
Nothing but cold mud and the sting of something sharp — I've cut my heel on debris. The seabed is silent.

choices.line: Break the crystal loop. Silence the echo, letting the dead rest. (A moral choice that destroys the evidence.)
choices.description: Call out to Pichit — demand how he recognizes this ship and what he's not telling the crew, 15 words

line.dialogue: Because I served on her. Twelve years ago, before the Chord shattered. I thought she'd been destroyed with everything else.
I don't owe you that. Not here. Not with the resonator already screaming and half my memories scattered across this floor.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship's engine groans as it strains against a new, discordant frequency. The Lattice below churns violently, throwing up shards of crystallized sound. The ghostly silhouette of the lost ship is now visible ahead, flickering in and out of existence like a bad memory.
There it is! Give it to me! I can steer us closer—we need to see what's inside!
This is a terrible idea... but it's still cheap compared to paying the Tonal Orders for a salvage permit. Look at it. It's not just broken. It's *wrong*.
The harmonic instability is off the charts. Pichit, I didn't finish all the calculations, but our resonator crystal won't hold if we get much closer.
We came this far. The Listeners said its silence holds a truth. We have to listen to what it *isn't* saying.
The ship... it didn't just sink. It was *unmade*. Its song was... deleted. I'm just surprised the echo is this strong after all these years.

A wave of absolute silence rolls from the phantom vessel. The constant hum of your own ship's engine cuts out momentarily, leaving only the howl of the wind. In that void, a single, fractured image projects onto your minds: a panicked crew, and a Singer, their mouth open in a silent scream as the Lattice swallowed them whole.

lines_after.dialogue: The vision fades. Your ship's systems whine back to life, but the ghost ship's pull is now a tangible force, dragging you toward its spectral hull.
Well. That was cheery. So the Tonal Orders' first 'successful' Singer voyage was a mass grave they covered up. Typical.
We have to get on board! The truth is right there!

line.dialogue: The ghost ship's resonance field is destabilizing your vessel. How do you breach the silence?

choices.label: Easy: Match the Dead Frequency
choices.text: Instruct Arthit to carefully tune the ship's resonator to the ghost's last recorded frequency, creating a fragile bridge.
choices.consequence: A shaky, flickering corridor of sound forms. It's safe but slow, giving the ghostly image time to solidify ominously.
choices.description: Grab the silence-core with bare hands while Chanida cuts the throttle to hold position.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Got it! My fingers are numb but I can feel it humming — *under* the quiet.
Chanida — "It slipped — the silence ate my grip, I couldn't even feel my own hand closing!

choices.label: Medium: Overwhelm with Noise
choices.text: Have Chanida and Malee crank the engine to full power, blasting through the silent field with raw sonic force.
choices.consequence: You crash through violently. The ghost ship shudders, and angry, fragmented echoes lash out at your hull.
choices.description: Let Arthit rig a harmonic dampener from the engine coils before anyone touches it.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Field is holding. The instability dropped forty percent — still dangerous, but survivable.
Arthit — "The coils reversed polarity. Whatever this thing is, it *pushed back* against my frequency.

choices.label: Hard: Sing a Counter-Melody
choices.text: Pichit, you must attempt to Sing—not the ship's lost song, but a new one to calm the resonance. It's a huge risk.
choices.consequence: A pure, clean note cuts the silence. The phantom ship stabilizes, welcoming, but the effort leaves you deeply vulnerable.
choices.description: Trust Pichit — recite the Listeners' mantra and walk the silence barefoot on the hull.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The silence parts like water. It knows the words — it
The risk doesn't pay off. The monk's faith wavers, breaking concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: You stand on the deck of the phantom ship—or within its memory. The air is cold and still. Before you, the spectral form of the lost Singer is standing right in front of the ship's shattered resonator, hands pressed against it, forever frozen in the moment of catastrophe.
Is everything under control? Their resonance crystal... it's not broken. It was *overloaded*. By design.
A kill switch. The Tonal Orders installed a failsafe to silence their own Singer if she learned too much. He's right! Look at the regulator—deliberate sabotage.
All these years, we Listeners studied the Lattice's natural song... while the Orders murdered the first true human voice to join it. My life's work... was built on this lie.
We have to take this crystal! It's proof! We can show everyone in the skycities!
It's not just proof. It's her final note. Trapped. If we remove it, the echo ends. Her truth... and her soul... get final rest.

The ghostly Singer turns its head. Not with malice, but with profound sorrow. The memory of the Lattice surges around you—the phantom ship begins to collapse inwards, pulling reality itself into its silent wake.
(Voice crackling over the comms from your ship) What's happening over there? The whole sky is shaking! Is everything all right?

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. As you act, the phantom ship dissolves into a final, brilliant chord of light and sound—a funeral dirge and a revelation, echoing across the Lattice.
It's done. Her silence has been answered.
On the decks of floating cities far and wide, people look up, hearing a strange, beautiful note they don't understand. The foundation of the world has just shifted.

line.dialogue: The core crystal holds the truth and the Singer's last spark. What is your final act?

choices.label: Easy: Secure the Evidence
choices.text: Carefully extract the crystal. Preserve the proof to dismantle the Tonal Orders' monopoly, even if it means leaving the echo to linger a while longer.
choices.consequence: You return with irrefutable proof. The scandal rocks the skycities, but the ghost's whisper remains in the Lattice, a bittersweet victory.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit misreads the situation. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.label: Medium: Shatter the Lie
choices.text: Shatter the crystal on the spot, releasing the trapped resonance in a single, public burst of truth that scars the Lattice itself.
choices.consequence: A visible scar forms on the Lattice below, a permanent memorial. The truth is undeniable and violent, sparking immediate, chaotic upheaval.
choices.description: Direct Malee to confront hidden knowledge using scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
The risk doesn't pay off. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.label: Hard: Sing Her Home
choices.text: Pichit, you must Sing her fragmented melody back to completion, guiding the lost echo into the Lattice's eternal song. It will consume the evidence but grant peace.
choices.consequence: The ghost finds rest. The physical proof is gone, but the *feeling* of the truth resonates in every Listener and Singer. A quiet revolution begins in the heart.
choices.description: The villager presses forward with community ties to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
the villager fails. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market thrums with the dissonant symphony of a thousand voices—a chaotic counterpoint to the crystalline silence of the Lattice far below.
Ah, Pichit! Your timing is impeccable. How shall I put it? I have a proposition that could resonate with your... particular skills.
A proposition? Out with it! This noise is giving me a headache. What did you say your name was again?
He didn't. Merchants here prefer their smiles to their names. It's easier to fleece you that way.
We should proceed with caution. The ambient resonance here makes it difficult to discern truth from echo. Could you repeat that offer, please?

Of course! A simple retrieval. A Surface Scavenger friend of mine heard something... peculiar. An echo from a ship lost during The Silencing. The *Echo of Sorrows*. How can I say it? Its crystal resonator is supposedly still singing.
A ship's heart, singing alone for decades? That is a profound solitude. What does it sing?
That's the mystery! The scavenger won't tell me. He's suspicious, thinks the Tonal Orders will confiscate it. But for the right partners... how shall we put it? The profit could be harmonic.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost ship's resonator. The Tonal Orders would kill for that data. This isn't a retrieval; it's a theft from history itself.
So? They hoard all the good charts anyway! If we find it, we could navigate anywhere!
The risks are monumental. We'd be challenging a monopoly. We must consider the consequences.
Yet, to hear a song untouched by Orders or markets... to listen to pure, lost history... How do you say 'no' to a voice that has waited so long to be heard?

line.dialogue: The merchant smiles, his eyes calculating. 'The scavenger is at the Leeward stalls. He doesn't trust easily. How will you approach him?'

choices.text: Appeal to shared curiosity. Offer to simply listen to his story.
choices.outcome: The scavenger values respect for the past over coin.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the merchant's counter and feel the vibration's rhythm before answering.

line.dialogue: The frequency pulses in a pattern—three beats, pause, two beats. Someone is signaling through the stone itself.
The resonance bites into my knuckles like static. I pull back too fast and the merchant's smile widens—he knows I heard nothing.

choices.text: Propose a straightforward trade: supplies for coordinates.
choices.outcome: A direct business proposition, but he may inflate the price.
choices.description: Lean close and whisper to Chanida to create a distraction while you pocket the merchant's ledger.

line.dialogue: I slam my fist down and demand he speak plainly—the old fool jumps, and the ledger slides into my coat clean as a shadow.
I start my tirade but the humming swells in my throat and my words come out garbled, warped—the merchant's eyes flick straight to your hand.

choices.text: Let Chanida's impulsive honesty lead. Admit the merchant sent you.
choices.outcome: Brutal transparency; it might bypass his suspicion.
choices.description: Ask Malee what she knows about merchants who deal in propositions beneath harmonic interference.

line.dialogue: Last cycle, three vendors vanished after accepting offers like this. But one came back wealthy—and silent. She only touches her teeth when she remembers.
I know nothing useful and say so. The merchant overhears and his polite expression cracks into something colder. 'Then perhaps you should let your betters negotiate

lines_before.dialogue: The Leeward stalls are quieter, filled with the hard-faced survivors of the Lattice surface. The air smells of ozone and old stone.
Merchant's lackeys. I knew it. We've talked about this before with his other runners. No one wants to go where that echo is.
We're not his lackeys! We just heard about a ship that's more beautiful than anyone's seen in ages! Its song must be incredible!
She's not wrong. A pristine resonator from before The Silencing? It's the find of a lifetime. But you've clearly been sitting on this. Why?
Because the last team that went looking for it? Gone. Swallowed. The Lattice around that wreck... it doesn't behave right. It remembers.
A precedent of danger. We must prepare for abnormal resonance patterns. What happened to the previous team?
You said 'it remembers.' Does the Lattice hold the echo of the ship's demise? A trauma frozen in crystal?
Maybe. I just know the charts are useless there. The Tonal Orders would burn mine for even having a scrap of this. You want to go? You do it before they find out. And you do it smart.

lines_after.dialogue: So we're not just stealing from the Orders. We're walking into a resonance anomaly that eats scavengers. Fantastic.
Preparation is everything. We need to calibrate our ship's dampeners, study any fragmented logs from before The Silencing. We've talked before about the dangers of unstable lattice fields.
But think of the song! A song no one's heard since the world broke! We have to hear it before it fades forever!
She is right. This is a memory the world is trying to preserve. To listen is our duty, but to prepare is our wisdom. The question is... what do we prioritize?

line.dialogue: The scavenger hands over a cracked data-slate with rough coordinates. 'Your move. What's your first step to not end up like the others?'

choices.text: Secure specialized gear. Bribe a Listeners' monastic for anomaly-suppression harmonics.
choices.outcome: Costly and draws attention, but provides crucial protection.
choices.description: Grab the scavenger by his collar and demand the coordinates of that lost team's last known position.

line.dialogue: Spit it out — where did they make their final transmission? I'm not walking in blind.
Hey — relax! I don't have exact coordinates, just the sector! Get your hands off me!

choices.text: Gather intelligence. Find and interview the lone survivor of the last expedition (rumored to be in hiding).
choices.outcome: Time-consuming and risky, but offers firsthand knowledge of the threat.
choices.description: Ask Chanida what she heard about the ship's location and how the resonator is still intact.

line.dialogue: Chanida — you said you heard about the ship. Who told you, and why would a pre-Silencing resonator still be functional?
I... I don't actually know who told me. It was just rumor, passed around the relay stations. I never verified it.

choices.text: Go dark immediately. Leave before the Tonal Orders catch wind, relying on instinct and Pichit's latent Singer intuition.
choices.outcome: Avoids interference but enters the unknown severely underprepared.
choices.description: Pull up the spectral records on your wrist display and cross-reference the missing team's disappearance with local signal anomalies.

line.dialogue: The last team's beacon cut out here — right on top of a cyclic signal anomaly. That resonator isn't just sitting there. Something's still powering it.
The records are corrupted — whatever took out that team also wiped their transmission logs. I've got nothing but static and a bad feeling.

lines_before.dialogue: The merchant's revelation hangs in the air, thicker than the market's spice-scented haze. The scavenger, Lek, shifts uncomfortably, her eyes darting to the crowd.
The 'Echo'... it's not just a wreck. It's a tomb that won't stay quiet. We have to do something! The Tonal Orders are just covering it up.
Now, now. 'Covering up' is such a harsh term. They're... managing a delicate situation. A lost ship full of unstable resonators? Bad for business.
And you just happened to have a map to this 'delicate situation' for sale. I can smell the profit motive from here. It reeks worse than the perfume stalls.
Forget the smell! If there are people trapped in a resonance loop... we can't just bargain over them. Pichit, you're the Singer. You can find it, right?
Hold on. A ship lost in a 'silent storm'? Its crystal lattice fused with the Lattice surface? That's not navigation. That's a recovery mission into a deathtrap.
Lek. When you were near the wreckage... what did you hear? Not with your ears. What did the Lattice *feel* like?
It... sang. A single, shattered note. On repeat. And sometimes... I swear I smelled perfume. Like flowers from a garden that sank centuries ago.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant's smile finally falters. He looks from the determined scavenger to your resolute party. The market's hum seems to focus, waiting.
You're actually considering this. Very well. The map is yours. A gift. Consider it an... investment. Just bring me back a shard of its core resonator. For study.
There it is. The real price. You want a piece of the haunted ship's heart. What could possibly go wrong?

line.dialogue: The map is in your hands. The Echo of the Lost Ship awaits. How do you prepare for a journey into a silent storm?

choices.text: Secure Supplies (Easy): Use your remaining funds to buy the best dampening charms and rations. A safe, practical approach.
choices.outcome: You'll be well-provisioned, but the merchant will note your caution and may adjust future 'deals' accordingly.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use unauthorized tones and use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Gather Intel (Medium): Press Lek and other scavengers for every detail of the surface conditions near the wreck. Knowledge over gear.
choices.outcome: You'll have crucial environmental warnings, but you'll draw more attention from the Tonal Orders' informants in the market.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with resonant staff to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Pichit fails. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Tune Your Resonance (Hard): Spend the time before departure in deep meditation with Pichit, trying to attune to the Echo's fractured song from afar.
choices.outcome: A risky spiritual probe that could give Pichit a direct connection to the wreck's resonance... or attract its attention prematurely.
choices.description: The scavenger channels survival skills toward the spice scents, hoping to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
the scavenger's resolve isn't enough. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

acts.title: A Song No One Can Match

lines_before.dialogue: You return to Khrueang Market at dusk. The air is cooler, the crowds thinner. But a new tension thrums beneath the lantern light. The Tonal Orders have posted watchers.
They know. Our ship is being watched. In only five minutes, they could have a cordon around the docking spire. We're out of time.
My skiff is at Berth 7, low-profile. It's no match for their cruisers in a fight, but it's fast and quiet. It's yours if you're still going.
Of course we're going! We didn't come this far to back down now. That ship's been crying out for decades. Someone has to answer!
I've never understood this heroic impulse. But... the thought of the Orders sweeping another 'mistake' under the Lattice? That, I understand fighting.
Ah, the parting gift! A small token.
He slides a small, sealed resonator across the table. It pulses with a faint, sickly light.
A 'silencer.' In theory, it should dampen a rogue resonance field. In theory. Do try to bring back that core shard. In one piece.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The path is set. As you move towards the scavenger's berth, the market's noise fades, replaced by the imagined echo of a single, repeating note. The adventure begins.
A song no one can match... and no one has answered. Until now. Let's go listen.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Orders are closing in. The ghost ship calls. This is the final choice before departure. What is your plan?

choices.text: The Direct Path (Easy): Take Lek's skiff and leave immediately, using the market's closing chaos as cover. Speed is safety.
choices.outcome: You'll evade immediate capture, but you'll head into the silent storm with minimal preparation, relying on luck.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing singer voice to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The risk doesn't pay off. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: The Misdirection (Medium): Have Arthit and Malee create a loud 'disturbance' at the opposite end of the market to draw the watchers away.
choices.outcome: Your departure will be cleaner, but your allies will be marked by the Orders, facing consequences upon your return.
choices.description: Direct Arthit to seek the dismissed truth using ship navigation

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
A costly mistake by Arthit. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.text: The Confrontation (Hard): Face the lead Order watcher directly. Challenge their authority to bury the truth. Use the public forum of the market.
choices.outcome: A high-risk play for legitimacy. You could turn opinion against the Orders, or you could be arrested before you ever lift off.
choices.description: The scavenger attempts to decode the tonal pattern, relying on crystal fragments

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the scavenger's call. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Defeat. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under a rust-colored sky. Towering hulls of dead Resonance Ships loom like skeletal giants, their crystal resonators cracked and dark. The air vibrates with the discordant symphony of salvage: grinding metal, hissing steam, and the distant, unsettling hum from the Lattice far below.
Keep your voices low. This acoustic chaos is perfect for an ambush. Every echo here is a potential enemy.
Relax, Arthit! We're here for parts, not a fight. Our contact's probably waiting by that big derelict. When's he coming?
Knowing our luck? After we've been shaken down by every scavenger with a wrench. The Tonal Orders have this place watched. They don't like people fixing ships without their precious charts.
Listen to the space between the sounds. Even here, in this industrial wound, the Lattice breathes beneath the noise. It's probably true that the old ships remember their songs.
You the ones asking about the *Eidolon*? The lost freighter? Bad business. Crew swore they heard singing from its hull before it vanished. Now its carcass is here. No one touches it.
What did you say? Singing? Like a Singer?
Don't know. But the foreman over there, he winked at me when I asked about salvage rights. Means he knows something, or he's looking for a bribe.

lines_after.dialogue: A haunted ship and a winking foreman. Just another day in paradise.
Our objective is a replacement resonator crystal. We should avoid folklore and focus on the scrap dealers.
Yet the story resonates. A ship that sang before it fell... its echo might still be here, trapped in the metal.

line.dialogue: The foreman is watching from his gantry. The *Eidolon*'s broken spine lies in a separate, quieter yard. Our crystal supplier is in the main scrapyard market.

choices.line: Confront the foreman directly about the *Eidolon*. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Have Arthit focus tattooed routes on the clanging metal to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The resonance turns hostile. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Send Chanida to distract the foreman while the others search the market. (Stealth/Trickery)
choices.description: Malee volunteers to seek the dismissed truth, leveraging crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Malee is thwarted. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.line: Ignore the stories. Head straight to the market to buy the crystal. (Commerce)
choices.description: Convince the villager to use irrigation and trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the villager. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the villager loses control. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: You slip into the derelict yard, a graveyard of quieter giants. The industrial clamour fades to a metallic whisper. Before you rests the *Eidolon*, its hull scarred by deep Lattice burns. An unnatural quiet hangs around it.
Shouldn't be here. That ship... it's not right. Tools go missing near it. Voices on the wind.
Voices? You heard that, didn't you? What did they say?
Fragments. Pleas. A navigation log, maybe, stuck in a feedback loop in the crystal dust. I heard a strange noise from its resonator housing last week. Like a crystal weeping.
Great. So it's not haunted; it's just poorly recycled. Let's get what we need and go. That housing might have the crystal grade we're after.
Caution. Structural integrity is questionable. And if there is resonant feedback, it could be dangerous.
A ship dies, but its final song... that lingers. If we listen, truly listen, we might hear its last moment.
Wait. Shhh. I heard everything! That... that's not the wind. It's coming from inside the hull.

lines_after.dialogue: A faint, crystalline chime echoes from a crack in the *Eidolon*'s hull. It's a clean, pure tone, utterly alien to the scrapyard's dissonance.
Okay. That's new. That's the sound of an intact, powered resonator. In a ship that's been dead for years.
A trap. Or a remnant charge. We should withdraw and report this to the Listeners.

line.dialogue: The haunting tone beckons from the ship's dark interior. The scavenger has fled. The foreman is nowhere to be seen.

choices.line: Investigate the source of the sound cautiously from outside, using tools to probe. (Scholarly/Technical)
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing hidden frequencies to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. She hears something no one else can.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: Enter the *Eidolon* to find the singing crystal. It could be the part we need, or the key to the mystery. (Exploration/Risk)
choices.description: Have Pichit focus Listener training on the scavenger gangs to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Attempt to harmonize with the tone, to answer the ship's song with your own resonance. (Pichit's Singer intuition)
choices.description: The scavenger steps forward with harvesting tools, ready to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the scavenger pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on the scavenger. Survival skills aren't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before the skeletal remains of the 'Echo of Dawn,' its hull scarred by Lattice lightning. The air hums with residual resonance.
This is it? It's just a broken hull. I wanna ask you something, Pichit—do you really think a ghost ship can help us?
Keep your voice down. The acoustics in this scrapyard... they carry. We should write a quick survey plan before proceeding.
A plan? Look at this place—it's the latest fashion in structural failure. But fine. Let's document the obvious death trap.
Every broken thing holds the memory of what it once was. The Listeners say a ship's final resonance lingers in its crystal bones.
You're really going in there? Heh. The acoustics inside... they play tricks. Some say you hear the crew's last moments.
Tricks or not, we need those navigation logs! This place is very livable... for rust and regrets.
A low, harmonic groan emanates from the ship's fractured resonator array. The Lattice below seems to pulse in response.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The party approaches the breach in the hull, where jagged crystal and twisted metal form a treacherous entry.
I'm writing a formal complaint to the universe about this. Just so we're clear.
Stay close. And for resonance's sake, don't touch anything that's glowing.

line.dialogue: How do you enter the Echo of Dawn?

choices.line: Follow the clearest path, avoiding obvious hazards. (Steady and cautious.)
choices.description: Climb into the broken hull through the jagged gap near the engine housing, 15 words

line.dialogue: * "The metal remembers warmth here—this was once a cockpit. Someone sat here and flew.
* "Your hand—give it here. That edge is rusted sharp enough to take a finger.

choices.line: Trace the residual resonance patterns to find a safer, hidden route. (Requires attunement.)
choices.description: Tap the hull wall in a pattern and listen for hollow spaces beneath the corroded panels

line.dialogue: * "There—behind the second rivet line. Hear that? That's not solid metal. Something's sealed behind it.
* "Great, now the whole yard knows we're here. That ringing carries further than your voice does.

choices.line: Go straight through the unstable crystal field—the fastest, most dangerous way. (A gamble.)
choices.description: Whisper to Pichit to read the hull's memory and trace what broke this vessel apart

line.dialogue: * "It wasn't a crash. These cuts are surgical—someone dismantled this on purpose, piece by piece, hiding what it carried.
* "Too many voices layered in this metal.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the ship's cavernous bridge, shattered viewports show the endless Lattice. A single, intact crystal console pulses with faint light.
Remember... the Listeners teach that memory is not stored, but echoed. This console holds the ship's final moments.
I can't remember the last time I saw something this intact. It's practically screaming 'trap.'
There! The log crystal! But... it's fused to the main resonator. We need to extract it without triggering a feedback loop.
Keep in mind—the Tonal Orders would kill for this. A ship that fell during the Silencing... its charts could rewrite everything.
The ambient hum rises to a dissonant chord. Phantom sounds—a scream, a shattering crystal, a final command—wash over the party.
Told you! The echo's awake! It remembers the fall!
It's not a ghost. It's a resonance recording, trapped in a loop of trauma. We need to break the cycle.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The ship's memory surges, threatening to overwhelm. The Lattice outside begins to crackle with sympathetic energy.
I can't remember my password, but I sure remember how to fight a haunted frequency!
Stay focused! This is the climax—we free the echo

line.dialogue: How do you resolve the ship's traumatic echo and secure the log?

choices.line: Overload the console to shatter the memory loop. (Destroys some data, but ends the echo.)
choices.description: Pry the log crystal free with your knife blade, levering against the root junction, 15 words

line.dialogue: Clean extraction — the Tonal Orders will weep when they realize what slipped through their fingers.
The blade snapped and the crystal's cracking — whatever's inside, we're losing it right now.

choices.line: Harmonize with the echo, guiding its memory to a peaceful resolution. (Requires precise resonance.)
choices.description: Press your palm to the crystal and let your own memories flow backward into it, 15 words

line.dialogue: You understood — the crystal doesn't want force, it wants witness. It's releasing the log willingly.
Your eyes went white for three full seconds. You gave it something, but took nothing back.

choices.line: Absorb the echo into your own resonator, carrying its pain to decipher later. (Extremely risky, but preserves everything.)
choices.description: Signal Malee to sing a resonance tone while you twist the crystal counter-clockwise, 15 words

line.dialogue: The harmonic loosened the fusion seal — Chanida, catch it, it's coming free now, it's—
Wrong tone. The root system just sealed tighter. Whatever frequency that crystal holds, we just offended it.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whispering Dawn' drifts to a halt at the edge of the Silent Zone. The usual hum of the crystal resonator dies to nothing. Ahead, the Lattice stretches, flat and dead, reflecting a sickly grey light.
Is the resonator broken? I've never heard such quiet. It's... wrong.
Oh, it's you! The master of stating the obvious. The Zone is called 'Silent' for a reason. Everyone knows it!
Proceed with extreme caution. Our charts are useless here. The Tonal Orders have no mapped frequencies for this place.
It is not merely an absence of sound. It feels... expectant. As if the Lattice is holding its breath.
A crude signal flare arcs up from the Lattice surface below. A scavenger's camp, clinging to the dead crystal.
Hey! You lot! What's your business skirting the edge of the grave?
We're looking for a lost trade convoy. Heard they might have drifted in here.

lines_after.dialogue: Lost convoy? (Spits.) Heard everything! The Zone eats sound and ships. You won't find 'em. Just their bones, if you're unlucky.
Charming. So you just sit out here in the quiet, picking at the corpse of the world?
Better than trusting the skies. The Orders don't know what's down here. But I do. The Lattice... it's sleeping wrong here.
The scavenger's eyes dart nervously across the dead plain. The unnatural quiet presses in, making every rustle of gear seem like a shout.

line.dialogue: The scavenger is hostile but knowledgeable. How does Pichit engage?

choices.line: Offer trade goods for information. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Strike the resonator casing with the heel of your palm, listening for any rattle of loose components inside.

line.dialogue: Chanida says, "The crystal's intact — see how it still hums against my skin? Whatever's choking this place, it isn't our equipment failing.
Chanida says, "Dead. Completely dead. I've tuned this instrument across four provinces and never once heard it go silent like a stone in my hand.

choices.line: Ask directly about the 'sleeping wrong' Lattice. (Intuition)
choices.description: Draw your blade and scrape it slowly across the stone floor, testing whether the sound carries or simply vanishes.

line.dialogue: Arthit says, "Good — the noise dies within two meters, swallowed whole. That tells us we're standing inside something alive, not merely somewhere quiet.
Arthit says, "The screech carried further than I expected. Whatever dampens sound here, it's selective — and that means it's choosing what to silence.

choices.line: Mention the Listeners' interest in the Zone, hoping to find common ground. (Lore)
choices.description: Stand perfectly still, close your eyes, and let your breath slow until you can feel whatever Pichit described as "expectant."

line.dialogue: Pichit says, "There — you feel it now, don't you? The silence isn't empty. It's a held breath, a throat tightened around words it hasn't
The attempt backfires on the scavenger. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: Having secured uneasy passage from the scavenger, the party descends onto the Lattice surface. The silence is a physical weight. Footsteps make no echo, voices die inches from lips.
Navigation is impossible. My instruments are useless. We must mark our path visually or we will be lost.
Look! Scrap and a broken resonator core. This is from the convoy! Go a bit further. The wreckage trail leads deeper in.
We've talked about this before. Charging into a soundless void after scraps is how you become a cautionary tale.
Yet, we must walk a bit further. To understand this silence is to understand a fracture in the world itself.
A shape resolves in the grey light: a grounded, ornate Resonance barge, its hull cracked open like an egg. A figure stands beside it, waving.
Travelers! By the Lattice, am I glad to see you! My ship... the silence, it drained the crystals in moments!

lines_after.dialogue: When you reach the intersection of misfortune and opportunity, you must always choose to negotiate! My cargo is intact, but my crew... fled into the silence. I am the sole survivor.
How convenient. And I suppose you'd be willing to part with that 'intact cargo' for a rescue? We're talked before, haven't we? Your type always has a price.
A mere token of gratitude! But first, there is something you should know. This silence... it is not natural. I heard things. Before the sound died. A... a hum from below. Wrong.
The merchant's friendly smile doesn't reach his eyes. His story feels rehearsed. Above, the dead Lattice seems to watch.

line.dialogue: The merchant's tale is suspicious, and the wreck holds clues. What does the party prioritize?

choices.line: Search the wreckage for the convoy's log or survivors. (Investigation)
choices.description: Tap the resonator core fragments together and listen for harmonic feedback, 15 words

line.dialogue: There—faint oscillation! The core still remembers its frequency. We have a thread to follow.
Nothing. Dead as bone. Whatever silenced this place swallowed the resonance whole.

choices.line: Press the merchant on the exact nature of the 'wrong hum' he heard. (Insight)
choices.description: Draw a directional line in the ash using the broken core's residual magnetic field, 15 words

line.dialogue: The filings settle north-northeast. Crude, but it's the first heading I've had in hours.
The ash disperses without pattern. Even magnetism has abandoned us here. I'm navigating blind.

choices.line: Have Chanida attempt to Sing, to pierce the unnatural quiet and sense the Lattice directly. (Risk)
choices.description: Form a chain, each person gripping the previous one's belt, and walk ten paces in silence, 15 words

line.dialogue: We moved together and the silence did not swallow us. Unity is our compass now.
the scavenger hits a wall. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The deeper you push into the Silent Zone, the more the unnatural stillness presses in. The Lattice here is a matte, dead grey, absorbing every footstep, every whisper.
My ears are ringing from the lack of ringing. This is wrong. The world shouldn't feel this... hollow.
Our resonator readings are flatlining. If we go much further, we won't have enough resonance to part the Lattice for our return. We are walking off the edge of the map.
And yet, someone's been here. Look. Scuff marks. Salvage cuts on that crystal spur. They have very fair prices for their courage, whoever they are.
(A figure emerges from behind a massive, fractured crystal column, crossbow leveled.) You look run down. Lost? Or stupid?
We seek understanding. This place... it feels like a wound.
It's a grave. Surface folk know to steer clear. The prices for ignorance here aren't reasonable. They're paid in sanity.

(The Trade Negotiator steps out from another shadow, hands open in a placating gesture.) Now, now! No need for hostility. My associate is merely... protective. You seem like reasonable people. Perhaps we can trade? Information for supplies?

lines_after.dialogue: The Negotiator's smile doesn't reach his eyes. The Scavenger keeps her weapon half-raised, watching the silent horizons.
A trade. Of course. Everything has a price, even the truth.
What do you know about this silence? And what do you want for it?

line.dialogue: The Negotiator gestures to a small, sheltered alcove in the crystal. 'We can talk. But first, your offer?'

choices.line: Offer some of your preserved rations and clean water. (Practical Barter)
choices.outcome: The Scavenger lowers her crossbow slightly. 'Practical. I can work with that. The silence... it's not natural. It was made.'
choices.description: Level your pulse-rifle at the scavenger and demand they identify themselves before anyone moves.

line.dialogue: Hands where I can see them — we've lost two teams already and I won't lose a third to a stranger's bad timing.
My hands are shaking too badly to hold steady — the resonator silence is eating into my nerves like acid.

choices.line: Offer a minor but functional resonator crystal from your ship. (Technological Leverage)
choices.outcome: The Negotiator's eyes gleam. 'A curious piece. Very well. We've seen things here. Shapes in the grey that don't cast echoes.'
choices.description: Lower your visor, open both palms, and call out a greeting in the salvager's trade-tongue.

line.dialogue: Easy, friend — we're not guild, not security, just surveyors who followed the same silence you did.
My accent butchers the trade-tongue so badly the scavenger flinches like I'd drawn a blade instead of offering peace.

choices.line: Offer nothing but a promise: to carry their warning out of the Silent Zone. (Appeal to Conscience)
choices.outcome: The Scavenger barks a laugh. 'Promises are thin air. But... you have a Listener's look about you. Maybe you'll listen. The Lattice is screaming. In here, we just can't hear it.'
choices.description: Signal Chanida to flank left behind the crystal while you hold the scavenger's gaze and keep talking.

line.dialogue: I slip wide, boots whispering on scree — whoever this is, they
the merchant fails. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: Guided—or driven—by the scavengers' grim hints, you find it: a vast, smooth basin in the Lattice, utterly featureless. At its center, a jagged, black obelisk of non-crystalline material juts upward, the source of the null-field.
That's it. That's the tumor. Can we... break it? Shatter it?
Unknown composition. Our tools may have no effect. And the resonator is barely sputtering. If we drain it completely here, we will be trapped.
Aren't you tired? Tired of the Orders, tired of the whispers and the secrets? This is the biggest secret of all. A weapon that killed the song.
It's not a weapon. It's a seal. Something is... contained here. The Listeners' warnings weren't superstition. The Lattice was trying to tell us to stay away.
A low, sub-audible vibration begins to thrum through the ground, not a sound, but a pressure in the bones. The dead grey Lattice around the obelisk begins to darken, like ink spreading in water.
(Shouting from a ridge behind you) It's waking! The quiet never lasts! Everyone knows it! You have to run!
A regrettable investment! I don't want it! (He is already retreating, his smooth facade shattered by primal fear.)

lines_after.dialogue: The darkness pools and rises, forming vague, shifting silhouettes that drink the light. The last dregs of resonance in your ship's crystal flicker.
We cannot let this spread. The song of the world ends here if we do nothing.
Then we make our own noise!

line.dialogue: The null-field is expanding, and the shapeless things within it are becoming solid. Your dying resonator is the only counter-rhythm left.

choices.line: Overcharge the resonator for a single, blinding pulse of resonance to disrupt the field and retreat. (Sacrifice the Tool)
choices.outcome: The crystal flares white-hot and shatters. A wave of painful, beautiful sound rips out, shredding the shadows and cracking the obelisk. The silence returns, but now it's just quiet, not dead. You are stranded, but alive. The seal is weakened, not broken.
choices.description: Strike the tumor with the resonance hammer at its hairline fracture, aiming for the deepest crack. 14 words

line.dialogue: The seal splinters like ice—something *breathes* behind it, and I can hear it singing.
The hammer bounces off. My wrists go numb and the fracture seals itself shut, angrier than before.

choices.line: Channel the resonator into a focused beam, targeting the obelisk's base to try and topple it. (Surgical Strike)
choices.outcome: The beam carves into the strange material. It shrieks—a sound that exists only in your mind. The obelisk tilts, and the null-field wavers. The entities recoil. You have a slim chance to escape as the system destabilizes, but the seal is critically damaged. What was contained is now merely... restrained.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the surface and listen to what's trapped inside before deciding anything. 15 words

line.dialogue: I hear a child's voice counting backwards from ten. Whatever this seal holds... it's still alive in there.
The surface burns cold through my skin and I hear nothing—nothing but my own heartbeat, echoed back wrong.

choices.line: Do not fight the silence. Open yourself to it, let the resonator die, and try to hear what the Lattice has been screaming about all along. (The Listener's Path)
choices.outcome: As the last hum fades, the mental scream hits you. It is not malice, but agony—a memory of The Silencing, trapped in this place. You understand: the obelisk is a scar, not a seal. Sharing this burden, you calm the memory. The darkness recedes, leaving profound peace. The Silent Zone will remain, but now as a memorial, not a prison. You are forever changed.
choices.description: Turn to Malee and ask her what she means by "tired" — what does she know that we don't? 16 words

line.dialogue: She looks at me with hollow eyes and says, 'I heard the song too, before they put me in the Order.
Malee just shakes her head and walks toward the tumor, arms outstretched, and I realize too late she's already made her choice.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship *Harmony's Dirge* cuts through the thick, silent air. Below, the Lattice shimmers, a vast crystalline sea responding to the low, thrumming frequency of the ship's primary resonator.
He winked at me. The trader from the last port. Said he had 'special charts' for a 'special crew.' I’m afraid there’ll be a problem.
Of course there will be. Anyone offering 'special' anything on these routes is a pirate. Usually both.
We should have reported the offer to the Tonal Order representative. Unauthorized frequency charts are a direct violation of—
The Lattice hums with more than just our ship's song. There's a dissonance on the edge of hearing. A warning from the stone itself.
Great. Philosophical and ominous. My favorite combination. When’s he coming, this 'special' chart salesman?
Soon. He said to listen for a frequency just outside the standard navigational band. A 'private channel.'

lines_after.dialogue: A sharp, jagged tone cuts through the ambient hum. A smaller, faster ship peels away from a bank of cloud, its hull bristling with crude, amplified resonators.
Hail the *Dirge*! Cut your primary crystal and prepare to be boarded! We’re comin’ for that cargo manifest!
Sky pirates! I told you! The unauthorized signal was a trap!

line.dialogue: The pirate vessel closes, its aggressive frequency causing the Lattice below to fracture and crackle. How do you respond?

choices.text: Comply and cut the primary resonator. Stall for time. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Pichit attempts to use the leg as a lattice probe, relying on staff meditation

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Defeat. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Shift to a defensive harmonic frequency to shield the ship. (Resonance Control)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to confront hidden knowledge, drawing on crystal hearing

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The lattice has other plans. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Order full evasive maneuvers. Try to outrun them in the cloud banks. (Piloting)
choices.description: The pirate volunteers to map the frequency corridors, leveraging smuggling routes

line.dialogue: the pirate succeeds. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
the pirate misreads the situation. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the evasion, the *Dirge* hides within a dense, sound-dampening fog. The air is still, heavy with moisture and the ozone-tang of stressed crystals.
Well, we lost them. For now. But they eat constantly, sky pirates. They’ll sniff out our resonance trail sooner or later.
I don’t wanna go anywhere else until we figure out how they found us. That 'private channel'... it wasn't just a lure. It was a tracker.
Agreed. We must diagnose the corruption in our comms array. A pirate-modified frequency could be buried in our system, broadcasting our location.
Quiet. Listen. Beneath the fog's silence... a memory of a sound. Floral, artificial. I can smell her perfume.
Whose perfume? The pirate captain's? Don't tell me you're getting poetic about our would-be robbers.
No. From the Trade Negotiator in port. The one who was too friendly. Her scent was unique, laced with ground Lattice-dust. It's on the 'gift' she gave Chanida.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit's revelation hangs in the air. A small, ornate data-crystal, given as a 'token of good faith,' sits on the navigation console. It pulses with a faint, foreign light.
The perfume... you're right. She was all smiles, but her hands were dusted with crystal powder. She planted this!
The crystal is emitting a carrier wave. A homing signal. The pirates and the merchant are working together. This is a coordinated salvage trap.

line.dialogue: The homing beacon is active. The pirates will be here any moment. What is your priority?

choices.text: Smash the data-crystal immediately. Destroy the beacon. (Direct Action)
choices.description: Trace the signal manually by stripping insulation from the comm unit's antenna wire, 15 words

line.dialogue: * "There — beneath the carrier hum, someone is broadcasting coordinates. They're still alive in Sector 9.
* "Nothing. The corruption eats every frequency I scan. We are deaf and blind out here.

choices.text: Attempt to re-tune the beacon, sending a false signal deep into dangerous lattice formations. (Resonance Hacking)
choices.description: Follow the fog-sound on foot, weapons drawn, toward the old temple ruins, 15 words

line.dialogue: * "I see it — a ghost-light flickering between the columns. Whatever broadcasts from there isn't hostile. Yet.
* "The sound collapses into static the moment we step closer. It was bait. We should not have moved.

choices.text: Leave the beacon active. Use it as bait to lay an ambush for the pirates when they board. (Tactical Gambit)
choices.description: Anchor yourselves and wait silently for thirty minutes, recording every anomaly observed, 15 words

line.dialogue: * "Three distinct patterns in the fog. They cycle every nine minutes. Whatever they are, they're organized.
* "Forty minutes. Nothing. The fog thickens. We've wasted time we don't have, and I hate it.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship sails into a region where the lattice below shifts from crystalline blue to a deep, unsettling violet. The engine's hum grows strained.
The charts are useless here. The Tonal Orders don't sell maps for this. I studied the old Listeners' warnings by myself. This color... it's a warning.
So we're off the menu? No safe paths, no pre-approved frequencies? Can I see the menu of options we actually have?
Careful. The lattice's resonance is unstable. A wrong note could fracture it beneath us. Can I have a manual on emergency procedures?
The lattice isn't just a road. It's a living memory. This violet... it's remembering the Silencing. It's showing us the scar.
Profit lies in uncharted routes, my friends! But one must know the cost. The hidden frequencies the pirates use... they come with a price.
A shadow detaches from a cloudbank—a pirate skiff, its resonator emitting a jagged, aggressive tone. It closes fast.
Yer ship's singing a pretty song! We'll take the cargo and yer resonator crystal. Or we'll feed ya to the lattice below!

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate skiff veers away, its resonator damaged. The violet lattice calms slightly, but a deep, resonant thrum begins to build from within it.
That wasn't a victory. That was a distraction. The real problem is waking up down there.
The lattice is... humming back. It's answering the fight.

line.dialogue: The pirate attack has agitated the violet lattice. A deep harmonic is rising from below, threatening to shatter the ship's crystal resonator. How do we respond?

choices.line: Use the ship's primary resonator to match and calm the rising frequency (requires precise tuning).
choices.description: Sing the lattice's dissonance back at it, matching its broken frequency note for note

line.dialogue: Malee — "The lattice just... answered. It thinks I'm part of its own song now.
Malee — "That wasn't a frequency, that was a scream. The lattice heard me wrong.

choices.line: Engage the emergency dampeners to silence our ship and hope the lattice forgets us (risks losing navigation).
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the vibrating thread and let it read your intentions raw

line.dialogue: Pichit — "It showed me what it remembers. We're not the first to walk here, but we might be the first to ask.
Pichit — "It pulled something out of me I didn't agree to give. I don't recommend touching it again.

choices.line: Channel the aggressive pirate frequency back into the lattice, trying to overwhelm and break the harmonic (dangerous escalation).
choices.description: Walk the threads blindfolded, navigating purely by the resonance shifts underfoot

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Every step landed clean. The lattice doesn't guide your eyes — it guides your weight.
Arthit — "I misread a dead node for a live one. The floor simply wasn't there anymore.

lines_before.dialogue: The violet lattice surges. Crystalline spikes erupt upwards, grazing the ship's hull. The resonant thrum becomes a deafening choir of shattered memories.
It's not attacking. It's weeping. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a crime, and the lattice remembers the scream.
Philosophy won't save us. What's this called? A lattice rupture? A resonance storm? What do they call this when it kills you?
The resonator crystal is cracking! We need to divert all power, but anyone's okay to make the call. Whoever has the strongest voice!
The Listeners' warning... they said this happens when you fight on the lattice. It absorbs the violence and echoes it back!
My cargo! The profit! You must keep it safe! You should keep the ship intact! The price for survival is everything you have!
Yer fault! Yer stupid fight woke it up! Now we all pay the price!
The central resonator crystal fractures. A blinding light and a silent scream emanate from the lattice. The ship begins to fall.

lines_after.dialogue: The fall stops. The lattice, spent, returns to a calm, deep blue. The ship is damaged but stable. The crystal is gone.
We paid the price. The lattice showed us its memory. We carry that now.
No charts. No resonator. We're truly lost. But... we know why.
We have to sing our own way home.

line.dialogue: The resonator crystal is destroyed. The lattice has calmed but left us adrift. The pirate and merchant are desperate. Our only power is the truth we witnessed. What do we do with it?

choices.line: Share the memory with all aboard, forging a temporary alliance to manually steer toward the nearest city (unity).
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with staff meditation to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit misreads the situation. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Keep the memory secret, using it as leverage to demand the pirate's hidden frequencies and the merchant's charts (control).
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to decipher the monk's recording, leveraging crystal hearing

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Chanida is thwarted. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.line: Broadcast the memory openly via residual resonance, alerting all Listeners and Skycities to the lattice's pain—and our location (revolution).
choices.description: The pirate takes the lead, employing intimidation to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: the pirate succeeds. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_before.dialogue: The Khrueang Market is a storm of sound. Thousands of voices, the clatter of goods, and the distant, ever-present drone of the city's resonance engines blend into a wall of noise that makes your teeth hum. Beneath it all, the Lattice glitters, a silent, crystalline sea far below.
This place is chaos! How is anyone supposed to think straight with all this racket?
They don't. That's the point. It's the perfect cover for any deal you don't want the Tonal Orders overhearing.
Speaking of which, our contact should be by the spice stalls. Keep your wits about you. The ambient resonance here can scramble crystal charts.
It's more than scrambling... listen. Beneath the clamor, there's a pattern. A dissonance. The Lattice here doesn't just respond to the noise... it's *remembering* it.
You lot look lost. Looking for a guide? The sanctioned ones are by the Order's spire. Costs a fortune, but it's safe. The old ways of navigating... they're gone. So let it go.
We're not looking for sanctioned. We're looking for... unobstructed.
Then you're looking for trouble. Or me. What took you so long? I was starting to think you'd chickened out.

lines_after.dialogue: The map you want... it's not lines on paper. It's a recorded frequency. An 'open' one, they say. Unclaimed by the Orders.
An uncharted resonance path? That's... theoretically impossible. The Lattice's pain points, its dangerous harmonics, were all mapped after The Silencing.
The pain is gone. Or shifted. This frequency... it doesn't hurt the crystals anymore. It's new. Or very, very old.

line.dialogue: The scavenger holds out a small, crude resonator crystal. 'The recording's in here. But it's noisy. You'll need to clean the signal in the market's din. How do you proceed?'

choices.text: Use the market's own noise as a filter (Easy: Chanida's impulse).
choices.description: Press your ear against the nearest stone pillar, blocking out the market noise to isolate the hum.

line.dialogue: There — you hear it now? It's mechanical, not natural. Something's running beneath our feet.
All I hear is some merchant screaming about saffron prices. My ear's vibrating against the stone and not in a helpful way.

choices.text: Find a quiet corner and attempt precise tonal isolation (Medium: Arthit's caution).
choices.description: Push through the crowd toward the spice stall while keeping one hand on your blade and your eyes on the rooftops.

line.dialogue: Good instincts. I count three watchers up there — and our contact just made the signal. Left hand, twice.
You just stepped on a chicken and now half the stall owners are screaming. Subtle, very subtle.

choices.text: Let Pichit try to 'listen' to the Lattice's memory of the frequency (Easy: Pichit's philosophy).
choices.description: Grab Pichit's shoulder and whisper for everyone to stop walking — stand perfectly still and let the crowd flow around you.

line.dialogue: Smart. When we stop moving, the hum gets clearer. It's pulsing — like a heartbeat, like something waking up.
A fruit cart just rammed into my back and now I'm wearing six mangos. Next time maybe pick a spot

lines_before.dialogue: The cleaned frequency plays from the crystal—a pure, piercing tone that seems to carve a slice of silence from the market's roar. For a moment, the crowd hushes, instinctively uneasy. The Lattice below shimmers in response.
It's... a calling. Not a path for ships. A call for them. Something on the surface is singing this tone.
A Singer? Out there? We have to find them!
Or it's a trap. A siren song recorded by scavengers to lure idiots into a lattice-shift. I don't want it. This 'map' smells like a one-way trip.

Your friend's got a head on her shoulders. I found this tone near a Listeners' ruin. It was broadcasting on a loop. Whatever's down there... it's automated. And it's been waiting a long time. What took you so long?
An ancient beacon? The energy requirements... How long are you going for? How long has it been active?
You're not thinking of going down? Madness! The Silencing happened down there! Everything good is up here, in the sky. Why dredge up the past?

lines_after.dialogue: The past isn't gone. It's recorded, in every vibration of the Lattice. This frequency... it's a page from a book everyone tried to burn.
The beacon's coordinates are locked in the crystal now. But you'll need a ship that can handle un-cleared harmonics. And someone crazy enough to pilot it.
We have a ship! And we're plenty crazy!

line.dialogue: The path is clear, but the risk is immense. The party must secure a way to reach the surface coordinates. In the tangled web of the market, what's your approach?

choices.text: Barter with the scavenger for a 'surface-hardened' resonator component (Easy: A simple trade).
choices.description: Take the recording device and play it back through the ship's hull amplifiers.

line.dialogue: The resonance signature — that's a live Singer throat harmonic, no recording copies that!
Congratulations, you just broadcast our position to every scavenger within six kilometers.

choices.text: Infiltrate a Tonal Order dock to 'borrow' a high-grade resonance calibrator (Medium: A risky heist).
choices.description: Ask the scavenger where exactly they found the device and what was nearby.

line.dialogue: Three crashed hulls in that canyon... that's where the signal bounces strongest. I know the way.
Funny you asking. Three crews asked me the same thing. None of them came back to ask again.

choices.text: Seek out the hidden Listeners in the market, to ask about the ruin and the beacon's purpose (Hard: A test of faith and knowledge).
choices.description: Ignore the signal entirely and chart a course around the dead zone.

line.dialogue: Finally, someone thinking with their survival instinct instead of their feelings.
Every hour we wait, the calling fades. If that Singer dies out there, their song stays with us forever.

lines_before.dialogue: In a quiet corner of the market, away from the main throng, a solitary scavenger examines a strange, humming crystal. The party approaches cautiously.
Back off. This isn't for trade. It's... personal.
Personal? That hum is on a frequency the Orders have locked down for decades. Where'd you get it?
Surface find. Near the old Listeners' spire. Thing was singing a song that... hurt to hear. Doesn't hurt anymore. The past is gone.
A crystal that has moved past its pain. A fascinating concept. May we see it?
Careful, Pichit. He's twitchy. I probably have a dozen traps like this back in my shop.
The harmonic signature is unstable. Are you sure it's safe to handle?
Safe? Nothing's safe. But an old friend of mine, a Listener before they scattered, would've known what to do with this. You seem like his type.

lines_after.dialogue: The scavenger reluctantly hands the crystal to Pichit. It pulses warmly in his palm, its hum syncing with the distant market drone.
It's... it's a piece of the map. A living coordinate. The 'Open Frequency' isn't a chart, it's a song locked in these things!
Of course. The Tonal Orders didn't just hide the knowledge. They shattered it and scattered the pieces. Monopolize the pieces, control the whole.
And this piece remembers a friend. It wants to go home.

line.dialogue: The crystal's resonance is attracting attention. Shadowy figures move at the edge of the stalls.

choices.text: Use the market's noise. Have Chanida start a loud, distracting argument with a vendor to cover your retreat.
choices.description: Malee uses engineering to harness harmonic feedback near the bargaining

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Things don't go as planned. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Attempt to mask the crystal's frequency by harmonizing it with the ambient market hum, a delicate tonal technique.
choices.description: Ask Arthit to confront hidden knowledge, drawing on captain experience

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit overreaches. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.text: Confront the watchers directly. Demand to know which Tonal Order they serve and why they fear a single crystal.
choices.description: Ask the scavenger to trace the anomalous signal, drawing on harvesting tools

line.dialogue: the scavenger finds the key. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The resonance turns hostile. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_before.dialogue: The watchers reveal themselves as enforcers of the Harmonic Guild. They surround the party, their polished resonance rods humming ominously. The market crowd melts away, leaving a tense circle.
Please, just give them the crystal! Don't make trouble! The Guild protects us!
Protection that looks remarkably like suppression. That crystal contains public knowledge. Navigational rights.
These enforcers are so uncomfortable! Stiff in their shiny boots. Bet they've never set foot on the real Lattice.
Surrender the aberrant resonance. Unauthorized frequencies are a danger to skycity stability. You are endangering everyone.
Stability. A fancy word for your monopoly. That crystal makes you look younger, Guild. It reminds everyone you weren't always in charge.
The Silencing was not an accident you solved. It was a mystery you weaponized. This crystal is a memory of the world before your silence.
He ran out of the Guild hall years ago. My Listener friend. Said he couldn't breathe their 'perfect' harmony. Now I see why.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit holds the crystal aloft. Instead of fighting its pulse, he lets it resonate freely. A pure, clear tone cuts through the market's drone.
All around, other hidden crystals—in pouches, stalls, and pockets—begin to hum in sympathy. A hidden network of the Open Frequency Map awakens.
The enforcers' rods sputter and wail, unable to lock onto the cacophony of truth. The Guild's control, for this moment, is broken.
The map was never lost. It was sleeping. And now it sings.

line.dialogue: The awakened frequency map is a beacon. Every Singer, Listener, and free captain in the city will feel it. The Guild's retaliation will be swift and severe.

choices.text: Flee. Use the chaotic resonance as cover to escape the skycity, scattering the map's song as you go for others to find.
choices.description: Hand the crystal to the lead enforcer with a resigned shrug, 15 words

line.dialogue: Fine — but when your 'protection' starts harvesting these people, remember I warned you.
I handed it over and watched their relief curdle into something that tasted like surrender.

choices.text: Stand your ground. Call out to the market, urging them to protect the song. Make this the moment the skycity chooses its own path.
choices.description: Smuggle the crystal beneath your coat and slip toward the lower district maintenance corridors

line.dialogue: Those stiff-legged enforcers never even turned their heads — too busy posing for the terrified crowd.
