A gloved hand closed on my collar before I reached the alley — they were watching the exits the whole time.

choices.text: Ascend. Channel the combined resonance to the city's central spire, attempting to permanently shatter the Guild's frequency locks. A point of no return.
choices.description: Hold the crystal overhead and publicly demand the enforcers explain what it actually does

line.dialogue: You want it? Then tell these people why — tell them what resonance means when it's humming inside their children.
My voice cracked across the plaza and the silence that answered was worse than any weapon they carried.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of dead ships. Rusted resonance vessels lie like beached whales, their crystal arrays shattered. The air vibrates with the discordant symphony of salvage crews—grinding metal, pneumatic hammers, and the low hum of still-active power cores.
Look at them. These ships once sang across the Lattice. Now they’re just… standing right in front of us. Silent. What songs did they carry before The Silencing?
Probably songs about overpaying for Tonal navigation charts. Sentiment doesn’t salvage parts, Pichit. We need a resonator coil, not philosophy.
Over there! That Sky Pirate’s haggling with a crew. Looks shifty. Perfect. I bet he knows where the good scrap is hidden.
Caution. Sky pirates are… unpredictable. Their frequencies are unregistered. Is everything under control if we approach? Their aggression could be a problem.
Oy! You lot eyeballin’ my business? This ain’t a gallery. buy somethin’. The Lattice don’t care for gawkers.
We’re seeking a specific resonance coil. For a… project. One that might listen to the Lattice, not just force it open.
Listen, eh? Sounds like Groundless talk. Dangerous. But… I might know a cache. Abandoned Listeners’ stash. Hidden frequency. For a price.

lines_after.dialogue: A ‘hidden frequency.’ How convenient. Are you sure this isn’t just a scam to lead us into a rusted deathtrap?
Your cynicism’s louder than a broken resonator. Suit yerself. Plenty other fools needin’ parts.
Wait! We need that coil. What’s the price? Information? Credits?
The pirate’s eyes gleam. Behind him, a Listener monk watches from the shadow of a broken hull, their robes stained with engine grease.

line.dialogue: The pirate names his terms. How do we respond?

choices.text: Pay his credit price directly. Fast, but costly.
choices.outcome_preview: We secure the location, but deplete our funds.
choices.description: Approach the pirate openly, hands visible, and ask about Tonal-class hulls for sale.

line.dialogue: I stepped forward with palms open — the pirate's eyes narrowed, but he gestured us closer with a wrench the size of my forearm.
The pirate spun, blade drawn before I'd taken three steps — Arthit yanked me back by the collar hissing *'Frequencies, I said!'*

choices.text: Offer a trade: repair his ship’s damaged harmonic stabilizer.
choices.outcome_preview: Gain his trust and the location, but it’s time-consuming and technical.
choices.description: Circle behind the stacked hulls to eavesdrop on the pirate's negotiation before moving in.

line.dialogue: I crawled between rusted bulkheads and caught every word — they're selling a Lattice-runner cheap because the Tonal array's stripped.
I brushed against corroded plating and sent a sheet of metal crashing down — the pirate's crew drew weapons and Chanida whispered *'So much for subtlety.'*

choices.text: Refuse and search the scrapyard ourselves. It’s a maze, but free.
choices.outcome_preview: Avoid the deal, but risk hours of dangerous, fruitless searching.
choices.description: Send Malee in alone to flirt information out of the pirate while the rest

line.dialogue: the pirate's expertise pays off. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the pirate hits a wall. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: Having struck a deal, the party follows the pirate’s coordinates deep into a canyon of stacked hulls. The acoustic environment grows oppressive—every footstep echoes, distorted by metal. The Listener monk from earlier steps into their path, hands raised in a calming gesture.
Please. Stop. You’re not going anywhere near that cache, are you? It is… unstable. The Lattice there sings a wounded song. It grieves.
Are you going to stop us? We have a deal. We need that coil.
How long are you going to study this ‘wounded song’ from a distance, monk? If it’s dangerous, shouldn’t it be understood?
You speak like the Groundless. They believe in direct communion, no matter the cost. My Order… we observe. We record. But I have listened here. The song… it speaks of a forced Silencing. Not natural.
A forced Silencing? The histories say it was a cataclysm, an accident.
And the Tonal Orders just happened to have all the navigation charts ready afterward. What a coincidence.
The cache you seek… it holds not just a coil. It holds a memory crystal. A recording from before. It is why the pirates guard it. And why my Order forbids me from retrieving it.

lines_after.dialogue: A distant clang echoes—a signal? The monk looks nervously over his shoulder.
You’re living in conflict. Between duty and truth. Are you going to help us hear that recording, or not?
If I aid you, I break my vows. If I do not… the truth remains buried. The Groundless movement grows because the Lattice’s true song is suppressed.
(Shouting from above) Monk! I knew you were sniffin’ around! Get ‘em!

line.dialogue: Pirates descend from the scrap piles. The monk is torn. What’s our move?

choices.text: Fight the pirates head-on. Protect the monk and take the cache by force.
choices.outcome_preview: Direct confrontation. Risky combat, but clear objective.
choices.description: Grab the monk's shoulder and physically move past him toward the cache door.

line.dialogue: I'm done waiting. That cache opens now, with or without your blessing.
Your hands are heavy with intent. The song recoils from you — and so do I.

choices.text: Use the environment. Create a resonant feedback screech with nearby wreckage to disorient them, then slip past.
choices.outcome_preview: Requires precise coordination and acoustic knowledge, but avoids a direct fight.
choices.description: Ask the monk to explain what the Groundless did when they sought "direct contact" with the cache.

line.dialogue: Tell us what happened to them. Maybe we learn something your wounded song can't teach alone.
You ask me to name a wound I have spent years trying to stop bleeding. No.

choices.text: Convince the monk to use his knowledge of the Lattice’s local song to guide us through a hidden path, bypassing the pirates entirely.
choices.outcome_preview: If successful, we gain a powerful ally and stealth. If he refuses, we’re surrounded.
choices.description: Offer to let the monk study the wounded song alongside you while you access the cache together.

line.dialogue: We work side by side. You get your song, we get what we came for. Nobody walks away empty.
You treat a fracture like a transaction. I cannot share this space with that kind of blindness.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the ship graveyard, the party stands before the grounded hulk of an ancient, ornate Resonance Ship. The Listener Monk, Kavin, points a trembling hand.
This vessel... it wasn't lost. The Tonal Orders scuttled it. Its crystal holds a true, unaltered map-frequency. Proof that the Lattice's natural song can guide us.
Proof that gets people vanished. Retrieving that core will trigger every alarm the Orders have here.
So we're quiet! This is it, the key the Groundless need! He's right! What Kavin said was right! The whole system is a lie!
My dream job. Breaking into a forbidden ship under the noses of guild enforcers and sky pirates. Just lovely.
A dream of truth, buried under scrap. We must listen to what this ship has to say, no matter the dissonance it causes.
A cacophony of wrenching metal and shouts erupts from the scrapyard perimeter. The Sky Pirate, Ravi, and her crew have tracked you.
Found your little pilgrimage! That crystal's worth a fortune in the right ears... or a quick death in the wrong ones. Hand it over!

line.dialogue: Ravi's pirates are closing in, and the ship's core chamber is a maze of dead conduits and unstable plating. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Bargain with Ravi. Offer a share of the data for safe passage and her silence.
choices.consequence: You buy time and avoid a fight, but you're now indebted to a pirate. The truth becomes a commodity.
choices.description: Have Malee focus crystal prosthetic on the engine parts to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Defeat. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.text: Use the chaotic acoustics. Have Chanida create a diversion with a resonator overload, drawing the pirates away.
choices.consequence: The pirates are misled, but the noise attracts Guild attention. Your exit window shrinks.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to question the Orders' silence, drawing on frequency mapping

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Chanida hits a wall. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Race inside the derelict. Secure the core first, using the ship's treacherous interior as a defensive maze.
choices.consequence: You claim the prize but are trapped with pirates and enforcers converging outside. A final stand is inevitable.
choices.description: The pirate uses pirate ship to follow the dissonant trail near the salvage

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
the pirate is thwarted. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The air hums with tension, the Lattice below seeming to vibrate in sympathy with the coming clash.
I had a bad dream... of this moment. The song is about to change, for better or worse.
Then let us ensure the new melody is ours to sing.

lines_before.dialogue: The core chamber. The ancient crystal resonator glows with a soft, untamed light. Outside, the sounds of conflict—pirates and newly arrived Guild enforcers—draw closer.
We're home so late! The Guild's here. Downloading the frequency data now, but extraction... that's the problem.
They'll make us sorry for leaving this place. in a cell. The pirate's cutting a deal with them right now, I'd bet.
Then we don't leave! We fight! We broadcast this true frequency right here, right now! Let every Listener in the city hear it!
Such a broadcast would be an act of war against the Orders. It would give the Groundless their anthem... and paint a target on every one of us.
War is already here. It's a silent one, waged with lies and stolen songs. I'm sorry I'm late... to realizing we must sing back.
The hull shudders under heavy blows. Ravi the Pirate shouts from the corridor, her voice now laced with Guild-sanctioned authority.
You're gonna be sorry for crossing the Tonal Orders! Last chance—surrender the core and the traitor monk!

line.dialogue: The true frequency is in your hands. The forces of control are at the door. What is the final note of this movement?

choices.text: Sabotage the core. Destroy the evidence, surrender, and hope for leniency. The truth dies, but you live.
choices.consequence: You survive as disgraced scavengers. The Groundless movement is set back decades, and the Lattice's true song remains silenced.
choices.description: Hack the Guild's emergency beacon and broadcast Chanida's testimony live across every frequency, 15 words

line.dialogue: Every screen in this district just lit up with our faces — the Order can't bury this now.
The beacon fried before the signal reached the relay towers — we're trapped in here with nothing but noise.

choices.text: Fight your way out. Use the core as a bargaining chip with the pirates, creating a chaotic three-way battle to escape.
choices.consequence: You escape with the data and your lives, but the Scrapyard becomes a warzone. The Groundless get their proof, but the cost in blood is high.
choices.description: Rig the cell's power conduit to blow the door and scatter shrapnel into the guards, 15 words

line.dialogue: The door's gone and three of them are down — we move NOW before reinforcements flood the corridor.
The conduit sparked but held — now they know our intentions and the cell door stays sealed.

choices.text: Broadcast. Overload the resonator and send the pure, unadulterated frequency screaming across the Lattice, no matter the cost.
choices.consequence: The truth is heard. The Floating Cities tremble with revelation. You become fugitives and legends, igniting the spark of true revolution.
choices.description: Kneel before the Guild warden and confess everything, offering the Order's secrets in exchange for mercy, 15 words

line.dialogue: The w
The resonance turns hostile. The monastery's countermeasures drown them in noise.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision echoes through the metal bones of the ship. A new frequency, born of regret, courage, or defiance, is about to join the world's song.
For every sorry whispered too late, let there now be a note of truth.
The crystal resonator pulses. The fate of the secret, and the future of the sky, hangs on the next sound.

lines_before.dialogue: Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens drift at the edge of the skycity. Terraces of whispering grain and gurgling water channels create a serene, rhythmic drone. The air smells of damp earth and growing things.
Finally! A place where we don't have to worry about the Lattice cracking under our feet. I could nap for a week.
Don't get too comfortable. Peace this cheap usually has a hidden price tag.
The terraces look stable. Good sightlines. We should restock our supplies while we can.
Listen... beneath the water and wind. The Lattice here hums a different song. A patient, growing note.
A smooth voice cuts through the pastoral sounds. A well-dressed man, the Trade Negotiator, approaches with a practiced smile.
Travelers! Welcome. The Gardens are more beautiful than anyone could imagine, aren't they? Perfect for weary crews.
His eyes quickly assess your gear, lingering on your resonance ship's crystal housing.

lines_after.dialogue: I represent certain... interests. They seek a crew willing to go a bit further. There's a derelict resonance ship, the *Echo of Dawn*, adrift in the silent zones. No one wants to go. Too many stories.
Stories? Or convenient ways to keep salvage prices low?
Merely rumors! But the Tonal Orders have even blacklisted its last known coordinates. A shame. Its cargo could set you up for life.
A robed figure, the Listener monk, has been listening from beside a water shrine. His face is a mask of quiet conflict.

line.dialogue: The merchant offers a fat purse for the ship's location data, but the monk's silence speaks volumes. Do you...

choices.text: Take the merchant's offer. Profit is a clear song.
choices.description: Wade into the shallows and press your palm flat against the submerged stone.

line.dialogue: There — you feel it? The Lattice is breathing *upward*, pushing through the bedrock like roots seeking sun.
The current pulled your hand away before you could anchor. It doesn't want to be touched. Not yet, not by you.

choices.text: Politely decline. Something here smells wrong.
choices.description: Climb the nearest terrace wall and scan the horizon for movement.

line.dialogue: Good eye — three ridgelines east, there's a break in the tree line. Something cleared that path recently, and recently means *today*.
The wind picked up the moment you reached the top — eyes full of dust, and now anything watching us knows exactly where we are.

choices.text: Ask the listening monk for his counsel first.
choices.description: Kneel at the water's edge and breathe deep, tasting the air the way the old hunters taught you.

line.dialogue: You caught it too — that sweetness underneath the mineral smell. That's not peace. That's bait. Something *wants* us to stay.
You sneezed so loud the birds abandoned three trees. So much for reading the wind, hunter.

lines_before.dialogue: You've chosen to seek the monk's perspective. The merchant's smile tightens before he melts back into the terraces. The Listener monk leads you to a secluded shrine overlooking the abyss.
The *Echo of Dawn*... its song was lost during The Silencing. It did not just vanish. It was *silenced*. Forced into a dissonant frequency.
A targeted attack? That would require immense power. Or precise knowledge.
So the merchant wants us to fly into a ghost ship that got murdered? Great. I don't wanna go anywhere else today, honestly.
But its echo remains. You can still hear it, can't you? A scar on the Lattice's song.
Yes. A faint, pained resonance. It drifts near the Northwest Veil. But... I can smell her perfume.
Perfume? On a decades-lost ship?
The monk looks haunted. 'Not literally. The merchant's kind. Their lies have a scent. They eat continuously, consuming truth until only profit remains.'

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal Orders didn't just blacklist it. They purged its charts. Anyone asking about it now is a fool....
So the smooth-talker back there might be trying to clean up loose ends? Using us as the mop?
A high probability. The monk's testimony is a risk to them. They would want it silenced.
Yet the truth of the ship still resonates. To ignore it would be to accept the silence that buried a world.

line.dialogue: The monk has given you the true coordinates, but also a warning. The merchant's eyes are surely still upon you. Your next move...

choices.text: Leave immediately for the coordinates. Speed is our best defense.
choices.description: Pichit channels Listener training toward the agricultural hum, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Confront the merchant quietly. Uncover who he really works for.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
The risk doesn't pay off. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Investigate the Gardens. The cover-up may have roots here.
choices.description: The merchant uses information network to follow the dissonant trail near the water channels

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. His trade connections deliver the right information.
The risk doesn't pay off. A rival merchant sabotages the plan.

lines_before.dialogue: The afternoon sun casts long shadows across the terraced gardens. The wind carries a new, dissonant note—a faint, mournful hum that wasn't there before.
The Lattice is restless. It remembers. That sound... it is the echo of the *Siren's Dirge*, the lost ship. Its final song is trapped in the crystal below us.
So the ghost ship story is real? I can smell the ozone from its broken resonator, like burnt perfume on the wind. Let's find it!
Hold on. The Tonal Orders declared that area forbidden. If they catch us poking around a wreck, our navigation license is finished.
The Orders are probably the ones who swindled everyone about what really happened. 'Navigational anomaly.' Right. I was cheated by better liars.
The truth is buried with that ship. If we can hear its echo, we can learn its final note. But we must be careful.
Careful? Nonsense! Knowledge of a new resonance pattern is invaluable! Give it to me! I can broker it to the highest bidder among the Orders. Think of the profit!
The Listener Monk looks pained, caught between his vow to listen and the Merchant's greed. The mournful hum grows slightly louder.

lines_after.dialogue: The party's decision sends ripples through the quiet gardens. The Merchant's eyes gleam with calculation, while the Monk's shoulders slump with resignation.
Are you finished yet, Monk? With your internal debate? The Lattice is singing a tragedy, and we are the only audience.
No. I am just beginning. The truth is a heavy note to carry. But I will help you listen.

line.dialogue: How do we pursue the Echo of the Lost Ship?

choices.text: Follow the Merchant's lead. Use his contacts to get 'official' salvage rights, playing by the Orders' rules.
choices.description: Chanida uses unauthorized tones to calibrate against the frequency near the agricultural hum

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The risk doesn't pay off. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.text: Convince the Monk to guide you. Use his knowledge of natural harmonics to trace the echo to its source quietly.
choices.description: Ask Malee to seek the dismissed truth, drawing on engineering

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Defeat. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: Go now, alone. Descend the terraces directly toward the sound, risking the unstable Lattice and the Orders' patrols.
choices.description: Convince the monk to use crystal bowls and map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: the monk makes it work. His recording captures a denied frequency.
Defeat. The monk's faith wavers, breaking concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: At the lowest, most overgrown terrace, the air shimmers. Before you, the Lattice is fractured—a jagged scar holding the spectral outline of a ship's prow. Its song is a deafening, single note of despair.
It's more beautiful than anyone! A whole ship, frozen in a scream! No one wants to go in there... but we have to.
Beautiful? It's a tomb. The Orders' resonator is still active, pulsing wrong. They didn't just lose this ship; they murdered it with bad math.
The resonance is tearing the local lattice structure apart. If we trigger a collapse, this entire terrace, maybe the city, goes down. We need to pull back.
Pull back? The ship's core resonator is intact! That's a fortune! Go a bit further. Just reach in and—
Silence! Listen! The final note... it's not a failure. It's a warning. A correction to the Orders' flawed charts. This ship discovered a truth they tried to erase.
So the choice is this: salvage the crystal for profit or power, mute the echo for safety, or... learn the note. Let the ship finally finish its song.
The phantom ship groans. The note intensifies, vibrating the soil underfoot. The truth of The Silencing whispers just beyond comprehension.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice resonates. The Lattice shudders, then settles into a new, profound harmony. The ghostly ship fades, its duty done.
We heard it. The map is wrong. The safe paths are lies. We have to go further, and tell everyone.
The Listeners will hear this new song. The Tonal Orders' monopoly... is finished.

line.dialogue: What is the fate of the Echo's truth?

choices.text: Sell the frequency to the Merchant. Let the Tonal Orders 'discover' it themselves, maintaining the status quo but funding your journey.
choices.description: Reroute the lattice stabilizers to dampen the resonance before attempting any salvage approach.

line.dialogue: Lattice integrity holding at sixty percent — we have maybe twenty minutes before it cascades again.
The stabilizers won't sync — every frequency I push, the resonator pushes back harder!

choices.text: Give the corrected note to the Listeners. Let their monastic order disseminate it slowly, creating a quiet revolution in navigation.
choices.description: Send a tethered drone into the ship's core to extract the resonator remotely.

line.dialogue: Drone's through the hull breach. Core resonator is exactly where the scans showed — grabbing it now.
Drone's gone — the resonance fried its circuits the second it crossed the threshold. Just... static.

choices.text: Broadcast it yourself. Sing the true note from the highest terrace, declaring the flaw to all Floating Cities, making you and the Orders permanent enemies.
choices.description: Broadcast a counter-frequency from your own ship's harmonics array to shatter the resonance field entirely.

line.dialogue: The ice is cracking — the whole ship is singing free! It's like watching something wake up!
You fools — the counter-frequency collapsed the hull! The resonator just fell into the lattice fracture!

lines_before.dialogue: The *Resonancer* hums, its primary crystal resonator emitting a low C-sharp that parts the pearlescent Lattice below. The deck is alive with wind and the ship's own harmonic signature.
Steady as she goes. The Tonal charts for this corridor are stable, but the atmospheric pressure is dropping. We’ve talked about this before. Sudden shifts can fracture a resonator.
Relax, Arthit. If the charts were wrong, we'd be a pretty stain on the crystal by now. The Tonal Orders might be monopolistic jerks, but they're not suicidal.
Look! Off the starboard bow! Is that... wreckage?
It is. Metal and splintered crystal, caught in a slow spin. It doesn't match any known ship design in the current registries.
A jagged silhouette drifts into view, its hull dark and pitted. A faint, discordant hum, like a broken chord, emanates from it, barely audible over your ship's tone.
Probably just junk. The Silencing left a lot of trash floating around. Go a bit further. Charting new salvage is more profitable than gawking at old bones.
That 'junk' is emitting an anomalous frequency. It could interfere with our navigation crystal. Caution is advised.

lines_after.dialogue: But what if it's *the* ship? The one from the stories? The *Echo* that vanished without a trace? Its resonance could be trapped!
A soul, or a memory, reverberating within the Lattice... When you reach a point of historical silence, you must listen for what was left behind.
The derelict ship's dissonant hum seems to pulse, as if in response to Pichit's words. The wind carries a scent of ozone and cold metal.

line.dialogue: The anomalous ship hangs in the void ahead.

choices.line: Investigate the wreck cautiously. (Follow protocol, scan from a distance.)
choices.description: Train the long-glass on the wreckage, scan for survivors or active distress beacons.

line.dialogue: I'm reading a faint pulse signal—someone's alive in there, barely.
Nothing but dead metal and colder silence. Whatever happened here happened long ago.

choices.line: Attempt to match its dissonant frequency. (Risk a closer approach by tuning a secondary resonator.)
choices.description: Hail the wreckage on emergency frequencies, identify yourselves as explorers offering aid.

line.dialogue: They're responding—a broken voice, but they're responding. Coordinates incoming.
Static eats every word I send. Either no one's listening, or no one wants to.

choices.line: Log its position and continue on course. (Heed Arthit's caution and Malee's pragmatism.)
choices.description: Alter course immediately to skirt the debris field, prioritize the ship's safety.

line.dialogue: Helm responding. We'll give it a wide berth—no sense risking our hull for ghosts.
Debris is wider than I charted—we're taking scratches across the starboard plating, hold steady!

lines_before.dialogue: You've drawn closer. The derelict is a pre-Silencing Resonance Ship, its design archaic. The discordant hum is now a physical vibration in the deck plates.
Scans confirm minimal power. No life signs. But the acoustic profile... it's broadcasting a corrupted version of a 'Safe Harbor' shanty. It’s irrepairable. The memory core must be damaged.
It's not damaged, it's *sad*! Can't you feel it? That song... it's like a child crying. She’s adorable! I mean, the *song* is... hauntingly pure.
Great. We're being serenaded by a ghost ship's lullaby. This is why I bill by the hour. The past is over. We should strip it for usable crystal and be done.
No. This isn't mere debris. It's an echo, a story frozen in a loop of broken sound. To silence it would be a deeper crime.
A sudden, sharper tone cuts through the hum. A smaller, faster ship—a pirate skiff—detaches from the derelict's shadow, its hull painted with jagged sonic symbols.
Well, well! Look what the resonance dragged in! We were just finishin' up here. I was cheated. This old hulk's core ain't worth the scrap we thought. But your ship... now that's a pretty tune.

lines_after.dialogue: You vulture! You were picking over it! Give it to me! The data core, I mean! It's not yours to steal!
Finders keepers, little songbird. But maybe we can make a deal. You hand over your nav-charts, we let you float away. Otherwise...
The pirate skiff's forward resonator lights up, charging for an attack. The ghost ship's mournful hum swells in the background, as if in protest.

line.dialogue: The pirate demands your navigation charts.

choices.line: Surrender a decoy data-slate. (Bluff. Risky if they check the frequency keys.)
choices.description: Have Arthit focus captain experience on the engine hum to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
A costly mistake by Arthit. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Attack the pirate skiff. (Aim to disable their resonator. They know these frequencies.)
choices.description: Pichit attempts to expose surface colonization truth, relying on staff meditation

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit misreads the situation. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Tune your ship to amplify the ghost ship's haunting song. (Use the echo as a weapon. Unpredictable.)
choices.description: Direct the pirate to confront hidden knowledge using secret frequencies

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. A secret frequency from the underworld shifts the balance.
A costly mistake by the pirate. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship shudders violently. The harmonic engine stutters, its pure tone fraying into a painful shriek.
The frequency is collapsing! We're caught in a dead zone. The charts show nothing here.
Of course they don't. The Tonal Orders wouldn't chart a graveyard. Why aren't you careful? We've talked about this before.
Through the distortion, a shape coalesces from the Lattice's mist below—a ghostly, broken hull of another Resonance Ship, drifting silently.
It's the lost ship from the stories! The Echo! It's real! Come and take a picture with us, Pichit, before it fades!
It's not an image to capture. It's a memory, vibrating at the wrong pitch. A soul stuck between notes.
A faint, mournful hum emanates from the phantom vessel. It sounds like a song cut short.

lines_after.dialogue: The ghost ship's hum intensifies, weaving into your ship's failing frequency. The deck crystals glow with an eerie, borrowed light.
Great. Now we're harmonizing with a wreck. This is irrepairable. We're going to be permanent additions to the scenic view.
The lattice resonance is syncing. We're being pulled into its... pattern. We need to break the cycle.

line.dialogue: The ghostly hum is trying to communicate, but its signal is agony. How do you respond?

choices.text: Mimic the Hum (Try to match its pitch to understand it.)
choices.outcome: Chanida impulsively joins in. The ghost ship's image stabilizes, revealing a spectral crew pointing in unison towards a specific crystal formation on its deck.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing ship navigation to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.text: Counter-Harmonize (Sing a calming, resolving frequency to soothe the echo.)
choices.outcome: Pichit focuses, weaving a gentle cadence. The painful shriek softens into a sorrowful melody, and a single, clear word echoes across the deck: 'Betrayal.'
choices.description: Direct Chanida to support the rebels using unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. A hidden tunnel opens beneath the terraces.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Silence the Signal (Dampen all resonance, cutting the link, but risking total engine failure.)
choices.outcome: Arthit frantically adjusts the dampeners. The ghost ship flickers violently, but for a moment, you see a fresh, brutal fracture on its hull—not from the Lattice, but from a weapon.
choices.description: The pirate uses intimidation to seek the dismissed truth near the sails

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
the pirate's resolve isn't enough. The disruptor backfires, jamming itself.

acts.title: The Note That Ends the Song

lines_before.dialogue: The revelation from the Echo has drawn attention. A ragged Sky Pirate skiff, engines muffled, emerges from a cloud bank, its harmonic cannon charging.
Give it to me! The frequency data from that ghost! We know you found something. The past is gone, but its secrets still spend!
Pirates! They must have been scavenging the dead zone, waiting for someone to trigger the Echo.
I was cheated. I thought we'd be eaten by a phantom, not robbed by morons in a flying junkheap.
They mean it! Their cannon's tuned to shatter our resonator! We can't outrun them here.
The Echo... it wasn't lost. It was silenced. That fracture... someone used a resonance weapon. The past isn't over. It's waiting to be heard.
The pirate cannon whines to a peak frequency. Your ship's crystals vibrate sympathetically, on the verge of shattering. The ghost ship's mournful hum swells in the background.

lines_after.dialogue: The air crackles with discharged energy. The pirate skiff lists away, its systems scrambled. Your ship is whole, but the silence that follows is heavier than any sound.
It's finished. The Echo... it's at peace now. Its song is complete.
We have the coordinates from its final note. A place not on any Tonal chart. A Listeners' sanctuary, perhaps. Or a grave.
Wonderful. More uncharted, probably lethal, poetry. Let's go before more of their friends show up.

line.dialogue: The pirate threat is neutralized, but the Echo's final resonance has imprinted a location into your ship's crystal log. What is the truth you carry forward?

choices.text: A Refuge (The coordinates point to a hidden Skycity, a sanctuary for those fleeing the Orders.)
choices.outcome: You hold the key to a safe harbor. A new beginning for the displaced, but also a target for those who control the skies.
choices.description: Slam the resonance shields to maximum and ram their prow head-on before they can fire.

line.dialogue: Brace yourselves — I'm putting us through their hull like a needle through cloth!
The shields collapsed on impact — we're exposed and drifting into their grapple range!

choices.text: A Weapon (The Lost Ship was testing a forbidden resonance—a frequency that could shatter the Lattice itself.)
choices.outcome: You possess knowledge that could break the world anew. A tool for revolution or a trigger for another Silencing.
choices.description: Jettison the frequency core in a decoy pod, then swing hard behind the debris field.

line.dialogue: They're clawing at the decoy like starving dogs — now's our chance to vanish.
Their scanner punched through the decoy in seconds — they know we played them.

choices.text: A Truth (The ship was sabotaged by the Tonal Orders to protect their monopoly. The 'accident' was murder.)
choices.outcome: You carry proof of the guild's foundational crime. This truth could unravel their authority, or get you erased from history entirely.
choices.description: Open a channel and offer to sing the ghost's frequency into their system yourself.

line.dialogue: I'll feed them the raw signal unfiltered — let their own machines decide if they can survive it.
They heard the ghost's voice through me and now their gunner is screaming — we've made it worse.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform, 'The Gaze of the Silent', juts over the Lattice Surface. Below, the crystalline expanse shifts with slow, prismatic pulses, humming a low, foundational chord.
Look at it! The patterns... they're almost alive. Can you feel the vibration in your bones?
It's beautiful until it decides to resonate you into dust. Don't get poetic, Chanida.
The harmonic stability readings are nominal. We're safe here. For now.
Every hum is a memory of the world before The Silencing. We stand on a library we've forgotten how to read.
A comms crystal on the platform's edge flickers to life with a distorted, urgent chime.
Someone called... this frequency. It's not a standard Tonal Order channel.

lines_after.dialogue: A voice, rough and filtered through static, crackles from the crystal.
A man called you a listener, yeah? Down on the Surface. Got a proposition. Don't bring your fancy charts.
A sky pirate. How charmingly predictable.
This is a severe breach of protocol. We should report it to the Orders immediately.

line.dialogue: The pirate's transmission cuts out, leaving coordinates humming in the crystal. Pichit looks to the team.

choices.text: Ignore the pirate. Report the breach to the Tonal Orders. (Safe, but yields no new information.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the crystal's surface and let the harmonics flow through you.

line.dialogue: I can feel them — every voice that ever sang into this lattice. They're not gone, just... waiting.
My fingers went numb and my teeth are vibrating. I should have listened to the stability readings before touching it.

choices.text: Follow the coordinates cautiously. See what the pirate wants. (Risk a confrontation, but potential for leads.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sing the old mnemonic tone his grandmother taught him toward the crystal.

line.dialogue: The patterns shifted when I hit that note — look, they're aligning to the melody. The crystal remembers the old frequencies.
I hit the wrong interval and the whole structure shrieked. Arthit's readings are going haywire and I can't hear out of my left ear.

choices.text: Send a deceptive acknowledgment, trying to trace the signal's source. (A tactical middle ground.)
choices.description: Slowly rotate the crystal 30 degrees counterclockwise on its mounting to match the harmonic drift pattern.

line.dialogue: There — the resonance just dropped into a clean octave. Chanida was right, the patterns respond to orientation. We've found its resting axis.
The crystal slipped and cracked against the mount. That hum just became a whine, and I swear I just heard something whisper back from inside it.

lines_before.dialogue: Descending a precarious crystal stairway, the party reaches the Lattice Surface proper. The hum is a physical pressure here. A scavenger, draped in salvaged resonator plates, watches from behind a spire.
You lot are very brave. The pirate's nest is that way. He doesn't know me, and I'd like to keep it that way.
We just spoke with him over comms. He said he had work.
Work? For him, 'work' means finding frequencies the Orders haven't taxed yet. That old resonator array near the fissure... you can still use it. If you're desperate.
Desperate describes our current financial situation, so let's hear it.
Unauthorized use of a ground-level resonator is incredibly dangerous. The feedback could shatter the local lattice stability.
Yet it still works... a piece of the old world, functioning outside their control. The Groundless would be interested.
A sharp, discordant shriek echoes from the direction of the pirate's coordinates, causing the crystalline ground to vibrate unpleasantly.

lines_after.dialogue: See? He's 'working'. Tapping a vein. Stupid. Attracts things.
We need to get over there before he brings the whole harmonic shelf down on us!
Or we could let him solve our pirate problem and our resonator problem in one go.

line.dialogue: The pirate's reckless resonance mining is destabilizing the area. The old scavenger's resonator array gleams nearby.

choices.text: Confront the pirate directly. Demand he stop. (Direct, but likely violent.)
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging Listener training

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit misreads the situation. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Use the old resonator array to create a counter-frequency, stabilizing the area safely. (Technical, requires precision.)
choices.description: Direct Arthit to seek the dismissed truth using lattice storms

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit fails. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Sabotage the pirate's operation subtly, using the lattice's own echoes to drive him off. (Stealthy, high risk of backfiring.)
choices.description: Have the scavenger risk using harvesting tools to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: the scavenger succeeds. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform is a precarious metal ring jutting over the Lattice. Below, the crystalline surface hums and shimmers, a kaleidoscope of fractured light responding to the faintest sound.
Look sharp. The pirate's got a bead on our resonator frequency. They'll be crawling out of the harmonic static any minute.
Let them come! I've got a few dissonant chords I've been dying to try out on someone's hull.
Great. More violence. The logical endpoint of a society built on stolen frequencies. You should get some rest, Chanida. Save your fury.
The Scavenger said the Groundless cache is directly below, in a resonance-dead zone. Reaching it means descending onto the Lattice itself. A single wrong step...
The silence down there... it's not empty. It's a different kind of listening. The Listeners would say it's where the world dreams.
Dreams'll get you killed, Singer. That dead zone? Pirates use it to ambish folks. They probably won't be coming from the sky... they're already down there, waiting.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, grinding vibration rises through the platform's struts. Sections of the Lattice below begin to glow with a hostile, crimson light.
Told ya! That's their boarding harmonic! They're phasing up through the crystal!
I'm sorry for being late to the party of imminent dismemberment. Suggestions?

line.dialogue: The pirate cutter is materializing from the Lattice below, its resonator spikes tearing through the crystal. We need to reach the Groundless cache before they secure the area.

choices.line: Use Chanida's aggressive resonance to shatter the forming cutter's hull. (Direct Confrontation)
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to tune the prosthetic, leveraging Listener training

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Have Arthit calculate a rapid descent path to the cache, using the disruption as cover. (Precise Navigation)
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with tattooed routes to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
The lattice has other plans. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.line: Pichit, attempt to 'sing' to the Lattice, to calm the hostile resonance and sink the pirate ship slowly. (Risky Harmony)
choices.description: Ask the scavenger to map the frequency corridors, drawing on surface knowledge

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the scavenger. Surface knowledge reveals a safe path.
Defeat. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: You stand within the cache—a cavern hollowed from the Lattice, walls pulsing with stored, forbidden frequencies. Ancient Resonance Ship schematics and weathered journals float in stasis fields. The pirate cutter is half-sunk in crystal above, trapped but not defeated.
These schematics... they're for a personal resonator. It doesn't need a ship. The Groundless weren't just philosophers. They built a way to walk the Lattice. To be truly free of the cities.
Free? Or exiled? You city-dwellers think the surface is a frontier. It's a grave. We were so bored up there, with your Tonal rules... down here, you're just prey.
The ultimate discovery. A way to abandon everyone. How profoundly Buddhist of them. Detachment from the floating world.
It's not detachment. It's connection. To the world itself, not just our islands perched on top of it. But this knowledge... in the wrong hands...
Hands like mine! That cutter's breaking free! The frequency to activate that walker-device—give it over, or we all get crystallized!
You want a frequency? I'll give you a cacophony!

lines_after.dialogue: The cavern thrums with pent-up energy. The pirate ship's resonator whines to full power, aiming at the cache's unstable ceiling. The Groundless legacy hangs in the balance.
This is the choice. Do we hide the truth, share it, or use it to fight? The Lattice is listening.
Most Thais are Buddhist. We understand impermanence. So make a choice before this place becomes permanently gone.

line.dialogue: The pirate cutter fires. Cracks race across the crystal ceiling. The core resonator of the Groundless Walker glows, awaiting a final, defining frequency.

choices.line: Shatter the core resonator. Bury the truth to protect the cities from chaos. (Preserve the Status Quo)
choices.description: Solder the resonator's crystal array yourself, ignoring Pichit's warnings about calibration, 14 words

line.dialogue: The frequency locks. I can feel the ground breathing beneath my feet now." — Arthit
The crystal shatters. I've burned out the only array we had — I'm sorry." — Arthit

choices.line: Broadcast the schematics on an open harmonic. Let every Listener and outcast know. (Spark a Revolution)
choices.description: Demand the scavenger explain what the surface dwellers already know about resonators, 13 words

line.dialogue: You want the truth? We've been tuning ourselves to the planet for years. You're late." — Scavenger
I owe you nothing, city-breath. Ask your dead engineers. Oh — you can't." — Scavenger

choices.line: Pichit, use the Walker. Lure the pirate ship into a fatal resonance cascade, sacrificing the cache to save your crew. (Become the Bait)
choices.description: Grab Malee's arm before she walks away and force her to look at the schematics, 15 words

line.dialogue: You see it now, don't you? This isn't escape. It's the opposite of leaving." — Pichit
Don't touch me. You've found

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of quiet. Sunlight slants through crystal panes, illuminating the endless rows of inscribed metal scrolls that hold the world's safe passage.
Keep your voices low. The acoustics here are... precise. A misplaced cough could trigger a resonance alarm.
Of course. Because heaven forbid we disturb the sacred silence where they hoard all the useful knowledge.
Look at this one! 'Harmonic Vectors for Southern Drifts, Cycle 94.' It's just... lines. How does anyone read this?
Each line is a choice. A path taken, and a thousand others silenced. The weight of all possible songs, reduced to a single safe note.
A profound observation, traveler. But a necessary reduction. After The Silencing, charting the safe paths became work we have to do. It is a duty to preserve.
Excuse me... Listeners? My cousin's supply barge is late. The route was certified. Can you... check the charts? I have work waiting that depends on it.
The charts are infallible if followed. Your cousin likely deviated. The Lattice does not forgive improvisation.

lines_after.dialogue: Infallible. Right. Because nothing ever changes in a world covered in singing crystal.
Malee, please. We're here to cross-reference our own route, not start a debate.
But what if the charts are wrong? Not from error, but from... omission? What if the true song of the world is being edited out?

line.dialogue: The monk looks pained. The villager looks desperate. The team must decide their next move.

choices.text: Focus on your own route. Promise the villager you'll keep an eye out.
choices.prompt: "I have work to do. But I can promise to watch for your cousin's barge."
choices.description: Trace the faded marginalia beside Chanida's open tome with your fingertip, feeling for grooves beneath the ink.

line.dialogue: Chanida whispers, "There — you found it. Someone carved corrections *under* the text. They were hiding the real equations from the clerics.
Chanida pulls your hand back sharply. "Don't touch without gloves! The oils on your skin just smeared a three-hundred-year-old annotation. We've lost that line forever.

choices.text: Press the monk gently. Ask to see the original, unedited resonance logs.
choices.prompt: "The duty to preserve includes the whole song, doesn't it? Show us the source."
choices.description: Press your ear flat against the limestone column and hum a single sustained note into the stone.

line.dialogue: Arthit freezes, then nods slowly. "You hear it? The column answers in F-sharp. This entire archive is tuned — every wall is a resonator. The builders *wanted* conversations to carry.
Arthit grips your shoulder hard. "Stop. Whatever you're doing, the harmonic is traveling through the floor. I can hear it amplifying in the east wing — and that's where the night wardens patrol.

choices.text: Help the villager file a formal discrepancy report with the Tonal Orders.
choices.prompt: "Let's get the answer now. There's a procedure for this."
choices.description: Mouth the words *Southern Drift* silently to Pichit while pointing at the shelf labels above, miming pulling a specific volume.

line.dialogue: Pichit understands instantly, sliding a decoy text outward to reveal a hidden compartment behind it. "Someone built a false back into this shelf. Three journals,
the monk loses control. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in a restricted annex, the air is thick with the hum of ancient crystal recorders. The light is dimmer here, the silence more profound.
This is highly irregular. My superior introduced us to the standard archives. These... raw logs are not for public consumption.
My calf has a cramp from all this kneeling. Could you speak more slowly about what we're looking at? These waveforms look... chaotic.
It's not chaos, it's music! Look, this spike here, and this ripple... it's beautiful. And it's nowhere on the official charts.
Shocker. The Tonal Orders are selling us a simplified, sanitized version of the world's song. Probably charges extra for the full melody.
These are the world's forgotten breaths. The paths not taken. But why silence them? What are they afraid we'll hear?
My aunt... she used to talk about a movement. People who thought we shouldn't just live up here, drifting. The Groundless, they called them. Said the true world was below.
Do not speak of that heresy! Those frequencies lead only to madness and Silencing. The safe paths are a gift.

lines_after.dialogue: A soft, discordant chime echoes through the annex. One of the ancient recorders has activated on its own, playing a faint, looping sequence of notes.
That's not on any chart. That's... new. Or very, very old.
It's a signal. Or a key. I can feel it in my teeth!
Great. So now the furniture is talking back. This just gets better and better.

line.dialogue: The rogue resonator pulses with an unknown pattern. The monk is terrified. The mysterious sequence hangs in the air.

choices.text: Shut it down. The risk is too great; report the malfunction.
choices.prompt: "This is unknown. We follow protocol and contain it."
choices.description: Slam your palm onto the resonance spike Chanida pointed out and feel the vibration travel up your arm.

line.dialogue: Chanida grabs your wrist, eyes wild. "You feel that? That's the third harmonic they told us doesn't exist!
The spike stays cold and dead under your skin. Malee scoffs. "Congratulations, you've proven nothing and now your hand smells like old copper.

choices.text: Record the sequence carefully. It's a clue, but don't engage further yet.
choices.prompt: "We need to study this. But from a safe distance."
choices.description: Ask the monk directly what his superior was afraid of when she arranged this meeting.

line.dialogue: The monk's jaw tightens. "She said the archive's resonance patterns were... evolving. Without anyone playing them. That should be impossible.
The monk crosses his arms. "I've already said more than I should to strangers kneeling in restricted stacks. Perhaps ask your other conspirators.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with it. See if the pattern responds to a live voice.
choices.prompt: "The song wants to be heard. Let's answer."
choices.description: Trace the spike patterns Chanida sees across the floor tiles and map where they converge.

line.dialogue: Your fingers follow the lines and they meet at a point behind a shelf marked with faded red ink. Arthit limps over and whispers, "There's something behind this. I can feel heat coming through the gaps.
You lose the pattern where three tiles have been replaced with mismatched stone. Arthit groans and rubs his calf. "Well, I'm suffering for nothing. Wonderful.

lines_before.dialogue: In a sealed reading room deep within the Archives, the air thrums with the faint, captured echoes of a thousand safe passages. The Listeners' forbidden data crystal glows on the table.
I really can’t remember! The last time I saw data this corrupted was after a resonator backfired. This looks... intentional.
Intentional silencing. The Tonal Orders didn't just lose this route. They buried it. The question is, does the Lattice itself complain about this?
It complains a lot! The static in the recordings... it's not random. It's a pattern of interference. A deliberate dissonance laid over the true song.
So the 'safe' charts are just the only ones they haven't messed with? This works really well for keeping everyone dependent.
You begin to see. Our duty was to preserve the song. Our truth... is that we helped mute it. The Groundless speak of a world below not of monsters, but of silence.
A friend introduced us. To the Movement. Said they had proof the Orders were lying. I didn't want to believe it. My whole family navigates by their charts.
The door to the reading room shudders. A heavy, resonant lock clicks into place from the outside. The Archives' acoustic perfection now feels like a tomb.

lines_after.dialogue: The party freezes, the weight of their discovery now matched by the physical weight of their confinement.
They know we're here. So much for hushed reverence.
This was never just a library. It's a cage for knowledge. We need to find another way out.

line.dialogue: Trapped with the truth, how do you proceed?

choices.line: Use the corrupted crystal's dissonance to overload the room's acoustic lock. (Chanida's Impulse)
choices.outcome_line: A shriek of fractured sound blasts the lock mechanism, jarring it open but alerting every guard in the sector.
choices.description: Cross-reference the static patterns against known Tonal Order censorship signatures in the archive.

line.dialogue: There — every gap aligns with a suppression frequency. They weren't lost, they were *erased* with surgical precision.
The patterns are too degraded. Whatever signature existed has been overwritten three times over — I'm reading noise inside noise.

choices.line: Have the Listener Monk chant a counter-frequency, exploiting his intimate knowledge of the Archives' design. (Arthit's Caution)
choices.outcome_line: His low hum resonates with the walls, finding a structural weakness in the door's harmonics. It opens with a whisper, leaving no immediate alarm.
choices.description: Play the corrupted recordings at half-speed and isolate the vocal fragments buried beneath the static.

line.dialogue: It's saying words! 'The song was never broken — they broke the *singers*.' It's not complaining, it's *testifying*.
Slowing it down just spreads the distortion further. Whatever voice was there, we've crushed it past recovery.

choices.line: Ask Malee to cross-reference the static pattern with public charts, finding a 'ghost frequency' to mask your escape. (Malee's Cynicism)
choices.outcome_line: She finds a bureaucratic blind spot—a frequency used for waste disposal. You slip out, disguised as acoustic refuse, utterly undignified but unseen.
choices.description: Ask the archive system directly what was removed and who authorized the deletion order.

line.dialogue: It's pulling up authorization seals from the Third Conclave — senior Tonal Orders officials. This wasn't an accident. It was a *policy*.
The system returns blank. Whoever scrubbed these records also scrubbed the authority trail — we're staring at a ghost wearing clean gloves.

lines_before.dialogue: You emerge not into a hallway, but into the Central Atrium—the heart of the Tonal Archives. A vast, cylindrical chamber where senior Navigators are verifying routes for outgoing ships. You are exposed.
This is a calculated risk. They won't cause a scene here, not in front of their precious clients. Not unless we force their hand.
Don't change the subject! The subject is that we have a crystal full of lies and a room full of people selling them. What's the play?
The Groundless... they said truth is a weapon. But it's heavy. I have work I have to do. My people need to know.
And I have work to do. My order's penance begins now. The true song must be heard, even if it costs us everything.
Great, a monk and a villager ready to start a revolution. Pichit. This is it. Do we hide, or do we shout?
We were brought here to find a path. Not on a chart, but a real one. Can you promise me? All of you? To follow it, no matter where it leads?
Across the atrium, a Tonal Archivist spots you. His eyes widen, then narrow. He signals to two resonant guards, their armor humming with suppressed energy. The moment of decision is here.

lines_after.dialogue: The air in the atrium grows taut, the gentle background hum of the Archives sharpening into a note of impending conflict.
The Lattice remembers every silenced song. It's time we remembered too.

line.dialogue: The Archivist and his guards approach. How do you wield the truth?

choices.line: Confront them publicly. Broadcast the corrupted data to the entire atrium, causing immediate uproar. (Direct Action)
choices.outcome_line: Chaos erupts as Navigators see the forged charts. The Archives descend into shouting matches, allowing your escape but sparking instant, violent suppression from the Orders.
choices.description: Step between Malee and Arthit, raising both palms to separate them before fists start flying.

line.dialogue: Enough! The Groundless want us divided — every argument we have here is a victory for them.

Enough! The Groundless want us divided — every argument we have here is a victory for them." (Malee shoves past your arm, finger jabbing at Arthit's chest: "Don't you DARE invoke them to dodge my question!")

choices.line: Let the Monk and the Villager speak. Offer them the crystal and become their shield, turning your act into a public martyrdom for the Groundless. (Sacrificial Move)
choices.outcome_line: The Monk's reverent testimony and the Villager's plain speech give the truth weight. You are captured, but the seed of doubt is planted deeply and spreads like a crack in crystal.
choices.description: Follow the monk toward the temple gate, matching his stride and speaking low enough that only he hears.

line.dialogue: Your order's penance — does it involve the sealed archive beneath the eastern shrine? Because if so, I'm coming with you.

Your order's penance — does it involve the sealed archive beneath the eastern shrine? Because if so, I'm coming with you." (The monk stops but doesn't turn. "You know of the archive. Then you know why no outsider has ever entered. Do not follow me.")

choices.line: Sing. Pichit, using the hidden true frequency from the data, harmonizes with the Archives' own resonance, making the very walls 'speak' the lost route. (Transcendent Revelation)
choices.outcome_line: A pure, undeniable note fills the chamber, bypassing logic and striking the heart. The Archivist falters, his certainty shattered. The monopoly on truth is broken, not by force, but by a song everyone instinctively knows.
choices.description: Kneel beside the villager at the edge of the gathering, letting the argument behind you fade into background noise.

line.dialogue: You said truth is a weapon. Tell me — did the Groundless teach you to wield it, or to survive being struck by it?
You said truth

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a deep, unwavering tone. The air itself seems to vibrate, a physical pressure that smooths the edges of fear but amplifies every footfall and whisper.
This place gives me the creeps. It's too quiet, except for that... hum. How can anything think straight here?
It's designed that way. The Tonal Orders love their oppressive calm. Makes people compliant. Easy to control.
We should be careful. The harmonic stability makes stealth impossible. Anyone on the lower decks will hear us coming.
Yet, within this enforced peace, other truths might resonate more clearly. The hum... it's a single note in a silent world. What is it drowning out?
A figure emerges from a service hatch, clad in patched leathers and a wary expression. It's a Surface Scavenger, eyeing your party's gear.
You're not with the Orders. And you're not pirates. What's your business scraping the Spire?
We're looking for... well, that's the thing. We don't know either. Heard rumors of a ship, lost near here. The *Echo*.

lines_after.dialogue: The *Echo*? That's a ghost story. A resonance ship that fell into a dead zone in the Lattice. No charts go there. I don't know when it happened, or if it ever did.
How well do you know her? The ship, I mean. Or the stories?
Well enough to know the frequency it was last tuned to is now a pirate chattering band. Sky-rats use it. If you're chasing ghosts, you'll find live steel first.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points towards a lower maintenance gantry. 'The pirate nest is down there, using the Spire's hum to mask their own noise. The *Echo's* last known resonator signature... you might find a trace near them, if you're foolish enough to look.'

choices.line: Pay the Scavenger for a detailed schematic of the lower gantry. (Costs resources, but provides a clear path.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the resonance wall and let your breathing match its frequency, listening for buried signals beneath the harmonic drone, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Malee: "There — beneath the surface oscillation. Someone embedded a distress pulse in the third harmonic. This place isn't as empty as they want us to think."]
[Chanida: "Nothing. Just the hum crawling up through my bones. Either there's nothing hidden or I'm not calibrated for whatever they're using to mask it."]

choices.line: Attempt to negotiate for the information, appealing to a shared distrust of the Tonal Orders. (Requires diplomacy.)
choices.description: Follow the faint vibration underfoot toward the sealed choir chamber, stepping only where the floor tiles remain silent, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Arthit: "The silent stones — they're not structural flaws. They're a path. Someone walks this route regularly, which means someone has something to hide down here."]
[Pichit: "Wrong tile. The whole corridor sang my weight back to whoever is listening. We need to move — now — before they send someone to check."]

choices.line: Thank the Scavenger and proceed cautiously on your own, relying on the Spire's hum to cover your approach. (Stealth is impossible, but the hum provides a predictable audio blanket.)
choices.description: Whisper directly into the anchor's central tuning fork and ask the structure whether it remembers who last adjusted its pitch, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Pichit: "It answered. Not in words — in a shift of temperature, a pull toward
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_before.dialogue: Descending the gantry, the Anchor's hum grows deeper, vibrating in your bones. The air is thick with ozone and the smell of cooked crystal. Below, a makeshift camp is built into the Spire's superstructure.
There. Three of them, and a portable resonator array. They're broadcasting on a scrambled frequency, but the core carrier wave is old. Very old.
It's peaceful. In a 'we'll-cut-your-throat-for-your-boots' kind of way. Lovely.
Can you promise me we're not walking into a trap for a fairy tale, Arthit?
I cannot. But the signal artifact matches pre-Silencing modulation patterns. It shouldn't exist.
A voice from the past, brought here and hidden among pirate static. What message did it carry that required such obscurity?
A Sky Pirate, leaning against a humming crystal conduit, spots you. He grins, showing a metal tooth that vibrates slightly with the Spire's tone.
Look what the hum dragged in! Customers? Or scrap? That resonator of yours looks quality. We like quality.

lines_after.dialogue: We're not selling. We're listening. You're broadcasting on a dead ship's frequency.

The *Echo*? That old ghost? Yeah, we found its resonator core, half-melted into the Lattice surface. Brought it here. Makes a nice jammer against the Order's snooping. It's nice and peaceful for business.
Someone is waiting for you. Or, more accurately, *in* that core. A data-ghost, a recording. You're using a tombstone as a doorbell.
So? Ghosts don't spend coin. You want to chat with a dead ship? The core's in that housing. It's... unstable. Talks sometimes. Gives me the shakes.

line.dialogue: The pirate gestures to a heavily modified resonator housing, wires snaking from it. A faint, warbled voice, distinct from the Spire's hum, whispers from within. The pirate band tenses, hands on weapons.

choices.line: Offer to trade a valuable but non-essential piece of ship gear for the unstable core. (Resolves quickly, but you lose an asset.)
choices.description: Crawl through the drainage channel beneath the dock to reach the resonator unseen.

line.dialogue: Mud in places mud shouldn't be, but their backs are turned and nobody's dead yet.
The grate was welded shut. I've scraped half my arm raw for nothing.

choices.line: Propose a deal: you'll help stabilize the core to stop its 'ghostly' interference, in exchange for accessing its memory log. (Requires technical skill.)
choices.description: Broadcast a伪造 distress call on their frequency to draw two of the three away.

line.dialogue: Two of them took the bait. One guard left — I can handle one guard.
They just laughed at our distress call. Now they know someone's watching.

choices.line: Challenge the pirate's claim. State that the *Echo's* core resonates with a unique signature that, by ancient Listeners' law, belongs to those who can hear its truth—like your party. (Requires boldness and lore knowledge, risks a fight.)
choices.description: Walk openly onto the dock with hands visible, claiming to be Silencing-era relic traders.

line.dialogue: They're pirates, not soldiers. Pirates negotiate when the offer's good enough.
The tall one already has his hand on his blade. We miscalculated.

lines_before.dialogue: The party ascends the final winding path of the Anchor Spire. The harmonic tone grows purer, more overwhelming. It's a physical pressure in the chest.
My ears are ringing... but I can still smell it. Faint, like old flowers and ozone. I can smell her perfume. From the ghost-ship's logs.
Great. So we're following the scent trail of a dead woman's ghost. I'm the luckiest person in the world!
The Spire's resonance is stabilizing the echo. Making it tangible. It's not a ghost, Malee. It's a memory, etched into the Lattice itself.
A memory seeking its end. Where will it live, once it's done? Can an echo find rest?
Ahead, the path opens onto the Spire's crown—a broad, flat platform. The massive resonance anchor, a spike of polished crystal, hums at its center. Two figures are already there.
Took you long enough! We heard the pretty song and thought we'd get a better listen.
They're tampering with the anchor! The pirate's trying to sync his ship's resonator to it—to hijack the frequency!

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation hangs in the air, charged by the Spire's relentless tone. The spectral scent of the lost ship grows stronger, clashing with the anchor's purity.
So. Do we fight the looters, reason with the zealot, or try to out-tech the pirate at his own game? All terrible options.
The echo is the key. It's not just a memory. It's a counter-frequency. We must decide how to use it.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate grins, his hand on a crude resonator device attached to the anchor. The Scavenger readies a tool, eyes desperate.

choices.text: Appeal to Greed: Offer the pirate the Lost Ship's resonant signature—a unique frequency worth a fortune—to leave the anchor alone.
choices.description: Press your palm to the cracked wall and let the echo bleed through your fingers.

line.dialogue: I can taste her last breath — jasmine and copper, she walked this corridor running.
Too much — the memory floods in and I lose where she ends and I begin.

choices.text: Appeal to Faith: Convince the Scavenger that the Lost Ship's echo is a sacred artifact; damaging the anchor would desecrate it.
choices.description: Mark the scent's direction with chalk and follow it blind, ears shut, nose only.

line.dialogue: Fine. Dead woman's ghost perfume it is — but if she leads us off a ledge, I'm haunting all of you.
The chalk snaps and the trail splits three ways — even her scent can't decide where to die.

choices.text: Technical Gambit: Use the party's own ship's resonator, synced to the haunting echo, to disrupt the pirate's hijacking attempt.
choices.description: Ask Arthit to amplify the Spire's resonance until the echo becomes visible, not just smelled.

line.dialogue: There — she's flickering at the end of the hall, barefoot, looking back at us like she's been waiting centuries.
The resonance overloads — the walls scream her name in every voice at once and now I can't hear anything at all.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision is made. The Anchor Spire thrums, a note so deep it vibrates in your bones. The ghostly perfume condenses into a shimmering, mournful form—the echo of the Lost Ship's Singer.
What is that?! Your party's resonance is fouling my lock!
The past... it's here. Don't you see? We don't own the Lattice. We listen.
It's starting! The whole Spire is resonating with her! My stomach is starting to growl from the tension!
That's no problem. It's a predictable sympathetic vibration. But the feedback loop... if it peaks...
It'll shatter the anchor and probably this whole floating island. Fantastic climax.
The echo doesn't want destruction. It wants resolution. It's a song that never found its final chord. We must help it finish.
The spectral Singer turns her gaze to Pichit. The Pirate snarls, boosting his device. The Scavenger falls to his knees, tools forgotten. The tone approaches a breaking point.

lines_after.dialogue: Silence. A deep, absolute quiet the world has not known since The Silencing. Then, a single, perfect, fading note—beautiful and complete. The ghostly form smiles, and dissolves into light.
The anchor is stable. More than stable... it's calibrated to a purer frequency. The pirate's device is inert.
She... finished her song. I believe you can do it, she whispered. To all of us.
The perfume's gone. Just clean air. And... peace.

line.dialogue: The crisis is over, but consequences remain. The Pirate is defeated but alive. The Scavenger is transformed. The Echo is at rest. What is the true legacy of this moment?

choices.text: A New Alliance: Spare the Pirate and befriend the Scavenger, forging an unlikely network of Listeners outside the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Slam your palm against the Spire's wall, matching its resonance frequency to amplify the sympathetic vibration.

line.dialogue: Arthit presses his ear to the stone, eyes widening.* "Yes—exactly! The harmonic cascade is building. If we sustain this, the resonance will shatter their loci anchors completely.
Arthit yanks your hand back, wincing.* "Wrong phase. You just fed counter-resonance into the wall. The vibration is dampening—Chanida, we're losing the window!

choices.text: A Secret Kept: Take the Pirate's data and the Scavenger's silence. Keep the purified anchor frequency a secret, a hidden advantage for your crew alone.
choices.description: Grab the bandit by the collar and force them to listen to the Spire's hum until they hear the buried memory inside it.

line.dialogue: The bandit's face goes slack, then crumples.* "I... I know this sound. My mother—she used to sing—that's the same—what did you do to me? What is this?
The bandit twists free and shoves you backward.* "Get off me! I'm not your instrument! Whatever you're trying to pull, I won't be tuned like some—this changes nothing.

choices.text: A Gift Released: Broadcast the purified frequency openly. Let all Resonance Ships hear the Lost Ship's final, perfect chord, challenging the Orders' monopoly.
choices.description: Sing the First Note directly at the scavenger, betting that the original melody will override their fragmented memory.

line.dialogue: The scavenger drops to their knees, tears streaming.* "You found it. The whole song—I only ever had pieces. All this time I was guarding scraps when the full
The gamble fails. A scavenging tool breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market is a symphony of controlled chaos. Beneath the ornate, wind-chimed archways, the air thrums with the voices of thousands—a constant, shimmering wall of sound that makes the very crystals in your pocket vibrate.
It’s obvious that something’s off. The usual gossip about Tonal Order price-fixing is gone. Everyone’s whispering about the ‘Echo.’
Probably just another ghost story to sell overpriced ‘warding charms.’ Look at this junk. A resonator crystal for the price of a small ship.
We should be cautious. Rumors attract the wrong kind of attention. The Tonal Orders have informants everywhere here.
Yet, within this artificial noise, there are truths. The market’s fear has a different timbre today. It’s very clear that something has resonated deeply with these people.

Your party navigates the spice-scented aisles. Near a stall selling salvaged Surface trinkets, a robed Listener Monk the Listener monk is in a tense, hushed conversation with a grizzled Surface Scavenger the Surface scavenger.
I’m tellin’ you, monk. The wreck of the *Silent Clarion*… it’s *singing*. A broken, mournful thing. My crew won’t go back. (The mother) was heart-broken, they said, when they first found her adrift.
Such a persistent echo… it contradicts all our charts. The Lattice should have consumed that dissonance cycles ago.

lines_after.dialogue: A haunted ship? Now *that’s* a job! Let’s get the story straight from the source.
Interrupting them directly is a risk. The Scavenger looks like he’d rather throw us over the railing than talk.
Oh, please. He looks like he’d trade his own mother for a working filter mask. We just need the right currency.
The truth of the *Silent Clarion* is trapped between them. One seeks understanding, the other fears it. We must bridge that gap.

line.dialogue: How will you approach the pair discussing the lost ship?

choices.text: Approach the Listener Monk openly. Appeal to his scholarly nature. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to calibrate against the frequency, drawing on forbidden paths

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
A costly mistake by Arthit. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.text: Buy a trinket from the Scavenger’s stall to start a casual conversation. (Subterfuge/Trade)
choices.description: Ask Malee to decipher the monk's recording, drawing on crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee misreads the situation. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: Have Chanida create a loud distraction nearby, then have Pichit ask the monk for help. (Diversion)
choices.description: The scavenger uses harvesting tools to trace the anomalous signal near the bargaining

line.dialogue: the scavenger finds the key. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Things don't go as planned. A scavenging tool breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Based on your approach, you learn more. The Listener Monk, Brother Kiet, is deeply troubled. The Scavenger, ‘Rust,’ has a fragment of the *Silent Clarion’s* hull—a crystal lattice fused with strange, fibrous scarring.
This ‘song’… it is not a natural resonance. It is a plea, or perhaps a warning, trapped in the crystal. My Order would have me record and forget, but…
Who’s this woman? When’s he coming? I ain’t got all day for philosophical chit-chat. You want the location? It’ll cost. The Tonal Orders pay well for silence.
He winked at me. Charming. He knows he’s the only one with the coordinates. Price just doubled.
Paying him invites extortion later. And if the Tonal Orders are already involved, a transaction leaves a trail.
So we don’t pay! We convince him it’s in his interest to talk. That ghost ship is bad for his business, right?
The unknown calls to us. But Rust only hears the clink of coin. We must make him hear the echo itself.
Brother Kiet nervously holds the crystal fragment. In the dense market hum, it seems to pulse with a faint, sickly light.

lines_after.dialogue: The fragment… it reacts to the market’s noise. It’s filtering it, finding a frequency… This shouldn’t be possible.
See? Uncanny. Now, are you buying a story or buying a map?
The ‘lady’ in question is a derelict hulk that’s giving hardened scavengers nightmares. That should tell you this is worth more than money.
We are exploring the unknown. And the unknown, in this case, is how far this man will push his luck.

line.dialogue: How will you secure the location of the *Silent Clarion* from the Scavenger, Rust?

choices.text: Pay his price. Coin is simple and leaves no lasting obligation. (Expend Resources)
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using staff meditation to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit hits a wall. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Propose a partnership: he gets a cut of any salvage *after* you investigate. (Negotiation)
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing singer voice to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida overreaches. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Challenge his courage. Dare him to lead you there himself, for a greater share of glory and loot. (Provocation)
choices.description: The scavenger channels crystal fragments toward the merchant guilds, hoping to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the scavenger. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The lattice has other plans. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.
