lines_before.dialogue: The market's din is a physical weight, pressing down on the party as they process the Listener Monk's revelation. The ghost frequency is not just a memory—it's a plea.
So the 'haunted ship' isn't haunted. It's just... stuck. Broadcasting a cry for help on a loop for decades. That's not spooky at all. Just cosmically depressing.

And the Tonal Orders have the charts that could pinpoint it, but they've buried them. The risk of someone finding a pre-Silencing vessel, with who-knows-what technology... It's obvious that they'd seal the records.
Obvious? It's cowardice! There could be survivors, or... or their descendants! We have to find those charts!
The Monk said the truth was in the 'static between notes.' In the noise everyone tries to filter out. Here, in this market... the answer is in the gossip we've been dismissing.
You lot look like you've seen a ghost. Or heard one. The surface is full of dead whispers. You learn to roll up your sleeves and sift through the static if you want to find anything real.
He winked at me. I think that's scavenger for 'I know something.'

lines_after.dialogue: The scavenger's 'borrowed' ledger... it lists supply runs to a derelict Order outpost. A place they officially abandoned. That's it, right? The hidden archive.
We're going. Now. Before they move it.
Chanida, wait. This is a theft from the most powerful guild in the skies. You need to love yourself enough to know the danger. We all do.

line.dialogue: The path to the abandoned outpost is perilous and illegal. How do we prepare for the heist?

choices.line: Rely on the Scavenger's routes. Use his knowledge of forgotten paths through the market's underbelly. (Stealth)
choices.description: Malee presses forward with engineering to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The lattice has other plans. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Create a diversion. Use the market's noise, stage a fake resonator malfunction to draw guards away. (Deception)
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with ship navigation to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Arthit loses control. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.line: Confront the Listener Monk. Demand his help as penance for his silence, using his authority to bypass checks. (Intimidation)
choices.description: The scavenger uses crystal fragments to decode the tonal pattern near the merchant guilds

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
A costly mistake by the scavenger. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_before.dialogue: The abandoned archive is a tomb of dust and crystal schematics. In the center, on a resonator-lit plinth, lies a single crystal log: the flight chart of the *Echo of Dawn*, the lost ship.
Jackpot. The coordinates are... right in the middle of a Lattice storm zone. No wonder they wrote it off. That's all, isn't it? A death certificate.
No. Look at the resonance pattern. The ship's crystal was singing a stabilization frequency. It wasn't destroyed. It anchored itself. It's waiting.
Guards! The diversion didn't hold! They're at the door!
Step away from the records! That knowledge is forbidden!
Forbidden? It's a rescue mission! Don't let anyone know you left people to die? Is that the Order's motto?
We have the coordinates. We have the truth. Now we have to choose. We can fight our way out, hide the chart... or broadcast it to every resonator in the market.
Please! Don't tell anyone! The chaos it would cause—the panic! The Order's control would shatter!

lines_after.dialogue: The choice hangs in the air, thicker than the market's hum. The ghost frequency from the *Echo* seems to pulse from the crystal in Pichit's hand, a heartbeat finally answered.
Well, philosopher? The whole sky is listening. What's the next note?
We don't tell *them*. We show everyone.

line.dialogue: This is the climax. What is the final, resonant act?

choices.line: Surrender the chart. Negotiate for a sanctioned expedition with the Monk's help. The truth is secured, but controlled. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Smash the crystal resonance chamber to scramble the coordinates before they can seize them.

line.dialogue: The pattern's collapsing — but I read enough. I know where the ship went down.
You've shattered the only record. That frequency is gone forever — and so is our chance.

choices.line: Fight and flee. Take the chart and run, becoming fugitives to mount your own rescue. The truth is yours alone. (Conflict)
choices.description: Have Arthit hold the door while Malee and Pichit transcribe the coordinates onto skin with stolen ink.

line.dialogue: Got it. Every number etched into my arm — they can burn the records now, we're walking out with the map.
The ink ran — half the sequence is smeared across my wrist. We're carrying a riddle, not a location.

choices.line: Broadcast. Patch the *Echo's* signal into the market's public address system. Let every citizen hear the decades-old cry for help. The truth is free. (Revolution)
choices.description: Surrender to the monk and bargain — offer to reveal the diversion team's escape route in exchange for the full resonance chart.

line.dialogue: He's lowering his staff. The old fool actually thinks we're giving him something he doesn't already know.
He's not bargaining — he's stalling. I can hear reinforcements coming up through the floor grate.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns before you—a jagged maw in the floating island's underside. The air hums with a low, persistent frequency.
The resonance readings are unstable. This cave system shouldn't exist inside a floating mass. The Lattice's patterns here... they're wrong.
Of course they're wrong. We're walking into a hole in reality because a merchant with a shiny smile said there was profit in it. Brilliant.
Will you two stop worrying? Look at those carvings! Pre-Silencing! This is huge! The ship wouldn't budge an inch trying to get close, but we made it!
A place that resists approach... It makes one wonder what it is protecting, or what is protecting it. The silence here feels... chosen.
Your boots crunch on crystalline dust. Strange, symmetrical pillars of raw Lattice-material rise from the floor, each vibrating faintly at a different pitch.
Ah, you found it! My associates said the acoustics in here are a marvel. Perfect for... discreet negotiations. Don't mind the echoes; they won't tell anyone our business.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant's chuckle bounces off the walls, multiplying. From a side tunnel, a rough voice cuts through the reverberations.
Discreet? Your ship's resonator signature screams 'easy mark.' This hollow is ours. Your charts won't get you out of here.
A misunderstanding! I was just leaving the valuable discovery to these fine explorers!
The merchant melts into the shadows, leaving you facing three sky pirates, their weapons humming with stolen resonance.

line.dialogue: The pirates block the path deeper into The Hollow.

choices.text: Attempt to reason, appealing to shared interest in the ruins.
choices.description: Trace your fingers along the carvings to read the ancient script by touch.

line.dialogue: I can feel the grooves—this tells the story of a kingdom that buried its own name!
Don't touch them—you just triggered a harmonic feedback. The whole wall is vibrating now.

choices.text: Create a discordant sonic burst against the pillars to disorient them.
choices.description: Deploy a resonance probe into the narrow fissure ahead to map the path forward.

line.dialogue: Probe's returning clean data—there's a chamber sixty meters below us, and it's not empty.
Wonderful. The probe's signal collapsed after eight meters. Whatever's down there doesn't want to be measured.

choices.text: Stand your ground, weapons ready, and demand they back off.
choices.description: Strike the cave wall with your torch handle and listen to the echo for hollow spaces.

line.dialogue: There—behind the limestone. That resonance says we're standing next to a sealed doorway.
That sound... it didn't echo. It *answered*. Something deeper in is mimicking us.

lines_before.dialogue: Past the skirmish, The Hollow opens into a vast cavern. Bioluminescent fungi cling to walls covered in intricate, forgotten glyphs.
Great. More carvings. They're not going to pay our repair bills. And that merchant? He graduated from the school of 'run at the first sign of trouble.'
Are you going to complain all day? Look! This isn't just ruins. It's a workshop! Look at that bench!
Chanida points to a stone slab holding strange, delicate tools and the skeletal remains of an arm... fused with crystalline lattice structures.
By the Founders... a prosthetic. Pre-Silencing medical resonance-tech. This is... you're not going anywhere near that, are you? It could be unstable.
To integrate crystal with flesh... to harmonize a broken form with the Lattice itself. This was their answer to physical loss. A profound graduation of the self.
As Pichit speaks, the crystalline components on the bench emit a soft, sympathetic pulse. Deeper in the cavern, something heavy shifts in the darkness.
Heh. You lot are about to graduate into a world of hurt. That shiny arm's worth a fortune to the right Tonal Order freak. We're taking it. You're not going anywhere with it.

lines_after.dialogue: The lead pirate lunges for the ancient prosthetic. The moment his hand nears it, a deafening, atonal SCREECH erupts from the cavern walls.
The frequency! It's a defense harmonic! It's tearing our resonators apart!
The whole cave is going to come down on us! I'm about to graduate into a pile of rubble!
Stalactites shiver and crack. The pirate stumbles back, clutching his ears. The prosthetic glows fiercely, now the epicenter of the damaging sonic storm.

line.dialogue: The destabilizing harmonic is collapsing the chamber.

choices.text: Grab the prosthetic and run, hoping to break its connection to the cave.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using frequency mapping to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The lattice has other plans. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Try to 'tune' the party's resonators to counter the harmonic and calm the cave.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to confront hidden knowledge using Listener training

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit hits a wall. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Attempt to decipher the glyphs around the bench to properly deactivate the defense system.
choices.description: The pirate steps forward with secret frequencies, ready to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Smuggling routes provide an escape.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The tunnel widens into a cavern where the walls are not stone, but ancient, fused machinery. A single, massive crystal column pulses with a faint, sickly light at the chamber's heart.
Pre-Silencing tech. And it's still active. That's not a good sign. Usually, 'ancient and still working' means 'ancient and still murderous.'
The resonance patterns here are chaotic. It's like the Lattice itself is... wounded beneath us. We should be cautious.
Wounded or not, that's our way forward! Look, the crystal is reacting to the prosthetic's hum. It's a key!
A key to what, precisely? Profit? Or peril? My associates and I have a... differing perspective on the value of discovery.
He means we're takin' that shiny leg and whatever treasure it unlocks! You lot, stand aside!
Violence is just another form of dissonance. But some truths demand to be heard, even if the hearing is dangerous. What is this place truly for?
From the shadows behind the pirate and the merchant, more figures emerge—rough sky-freelancers with drawn weapons. The chamber's echo turns threatening.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal matrix... it's stabilizing. I think we restored a fragment of its original function. A recorder, perhaps.
Great. So we almost died for a history lesson. Let's hope it was worth the tuition.
Every truth has value. Even painful ones. The path ahead feels... clearer now.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator and the Pirate stand between you and the central crystal. The prosthetic hums, ready to interface.

choices.line: Appeal to Reason: "This isn't treasure—it's a grave. We should honor it, not loot it." Use the chamber's echoes to make your voice resonate with moral authority.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to use the leg as a lattice probe using hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The resonance turns hostile. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Strategic Diversion: Have Chanida create a loud, distracting frequency clash while Arthit calculates the exact harmonic needed to safely trigger the crystal.
choices.description: Direct Arthit to seek the dismissed truth using lattice storms

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit loses control. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.line: Direct Confrontation: "You seek profit in noise. I seek truth in silence." Challenge them directly, using the prosthetic's unique resonance to disrupt their weapons.
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using valuable goods to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Hidden leverage shifts the balance.
The resonance turns hostile. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: Beyond the central chamber lies the heart of the Hollow: a vast, spherical space where the floating island's core should be. Instead, a silent, inverted bell of black crystal hangs, fractured. The air is thick with memory.
Resonance levels are critical. This... this is the source of the instability. The Silencing didn't just happen here. It began here.
A weapon. Of course it was a weapon. They always build the world-killers in the prettiest caves.
The prosthetic is burning up! It's trying to resonate with the bell, but the frequency is all wrong—it's a scream, not a song!

The black crystal shudders. From its fractures, ghostly after-images of the past spill out: figures in panic, a catastrophic harmonic surge. The Negotiator and Pirate, having followed, stare in horror.
This... this is beyond any ledger. This is sin.
We gotta seal it! If that frequency gets out, it'll shred every ship in the sky!
The truth is the wound, and the wound is truth. To heal, we must first understand the cut. But we are running out of time.

lines_after.dialogue: The Harmonic Bell falls silent, its fracture sealed by a new, stable resonance. The oppressive weight lifts from the Hollow. The prosthetic, now inert, is just a piece of crystal.
We didn't just stop a catastrophe. We... changed the song. The Lattice here will heal, in time.
I didn't catch half of what that vision was trying to say, but I felt it. They were so scared...
Yeah, well. Now we get to be the ones who write the footnote: 'And then some idiots actually fixed it.'
Every ending is a beginning sung in a different key. We have given this place a new refrain.

line.dialogue: The fractured bell is building toward a cascading resonance failure—a miniature repeat of The Silencing. The prosthetic can channel a harmonic, but only one.

choices.line: Seal the Fracture: Use the prosthetic as a sacrificial harmonic damper. It will be destroyed, but the immediate danger will be neutralized cleanly.
choices.description: Rip the prosthetic from Chanida's arm before the resonance feedback tears her apart.

line.dialogue: I felt the heat die the moment it left my flesh—but the socket still screams, Arthit.
It fused to the bone—I can't—Gods, it's eating me from the inside out, don't touch me!

choices.line: Rewrite the Frequency: Attempt to recalibrate the bell's core resonance into something stable but new. Risky, but could heal the wound permanently.
choices.description: Force the merchant to reveal what he knows about the weapon's resonance frequency and its weakness.

line.dialogue: I didn't sell it—I buried the schematics in the old quarter vault, beneath the ledger marked 'Forfeiture.
I know nothing! I only moved crates, counted coins—please, I'm a middleman, not a monster!

choices.line: Listen to the Scream: Don't counteract it—fully resonate with the catastrophic frequency to experience the truth of The Silencing, hoping to find a cure within the cause.
choices.description: Channel your own resonance into the device to create a counter-frequency, even though it may shatter every implant in your body.

line.dialogue: The harmonic collapsed—I felt it break like glass
the merchant loses control. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns before you, a jagged crack in the floating island's underside. Inside, the air is cool and smells of damp stone and ancient dust.
The acoustics here are... unsettling. Every footstep echoes twice. I'd advise caution.
Caution? Look at those crystal formations! This place is amazing! Let's get in there!
Amazing. Or a perfect trap. The Tonal Orders wouldn't chart this place for fun. There's a reason it's uncharted.
Reason or mystery, the Lattice's song here is different. A friend introduced us to the idea of these natural echo chambers. He meant it when he said they hold forgotten truths.
Deep in the first cavern, you find a pre-Silencing ruin—a small chamber with walls covered in faded sonic glyphs.
My grandfather spoke of this place. Said it was bad luck. Said the old world's troubles are finished, buried. We shouldn't dig them up.
Bad luck? My dear fellow, bad luck is an empty purse! Look at these glyphs—potential new navigation patterns! That's profit waiting to be decoded!

lines_after.dialogue: These glyphs... they're not just maps. They're a record. A record of a sound.
A sound that caused The Silencing? If that's true, finding it could be catastrophic. It's over. That knowledge should stay buried.
But if it's a sound, maybe it's a tool! Maybe we can use it! We have to know!
As Chanida's voice rings out, a specific glyph on the wall resonates faintly, glowing with a soft blue light.

line.dialogue: The resonant glyph pulses. What do you focus on?

choices.label: Study the glyph's pattern for navigation (Easy)
choices.consequence: Gain a minor navigational insight; the Merchant is pleased.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with forbidden paths to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Arthit makes it work. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Arthit is thwarted. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.label: Attempt to replicate the glyph's sound (Medium)
choices.consequence: Trigger a minor harmonic event; the environment reacts.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus tonal knowledge on the forbidden history to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Pichit hits a wall. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.label: Search for more connected glyphs (Easy)
choices.consequence: Discover a clue leading deeper into The Hollow.
choices.description: The villager uses terraces to decode the tonal pattern near the darkness

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the villager. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The lattice has other plans. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the clue, you descend into a deeper, larger chamber. A colossal, broken resonator—a pre-Silencing engine—lies half-buried in the floor.
Well. This explains why the Orders keep this place quiet. This thing looks like it could part the Lattice from below. Or shatter it.
It's inert. But the resonance in this chamber... it's unstable. Our ship's crystal won't move at all if we trigger a harmonic backlash here.
Then let's do it! Let's get to it! We need to see what this machine was for!
Look. On the far wall. Not glyphs... bones. Fossilized, fused with crystal. A Listeners' meditation site.
Fascinating! But unprofitable. The real treasure is the machine's core. If we can extract its resonator crystal...
Treasure? That crystal leg over there, on that skeleton... that's a Resonant Prosthetic. My cousin had one, after a mining accident. They said it let him hear the Lattice's pain.
The villager points to a crystalline limb fused to a petrified skeleton seated against the wall. It hums with a barely audible, mournful tone.

lines_after.dialogue: The prosthetic... it's still active. Still listening. To what?
To the echo of The Silencing, probably. A dead man's bad dream made permanent. Let's go inside the machine's housing. The answers are in there, not in old bones.
Going inside that structure is reckless. Its structural integrity is unknown. It could collapse.
But the prosthetic is a key! It's listening to the same sound the glyphs recorded! We have to understand both!

line.dialogue: The ancient resonator engine and the resonant prosthetic both offer paths to understanding. Which do you investigate first?

choices.label: Examine the Resonant Prosthetic (Easy)
choices.consequence: Learn a fragment of the Listeners' final song; gain emotional insight.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the fossilized wall and feel for whatever resonance Arthit mentioned.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Careful, careful... yes. You feel that pulse? It's not dead. It's *sleeping*.
Malee — "Pull your hand back. You're bleeding from the fingertips and you didn't even notice.

choices.label: Enter the broken resonator engine (Medium)
choices.consequence: Discover mechanical schematics; risk structural instability.
choices.description: Tell Pichit to chip a sample from the bone layer while Chanida photographs the arrangement before anything wakes.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "Got it. The marrow cavity is crystallized — whatever killed these things flash-fossilized them. This isn't geology. This is a *crime scene*.
Chanida — "The camera's dead. Every battery in my bag just drained. Whatever's in this wall, it doesn't want a record.

choices.label: Attempt to link the prosthetic to the engine (Hard)
choices.consequence: Try to activate a connection; unpredictable harmonic consequences.
choices.description: Walk the perimeter slowly, counting your footsteps, and map the chamber's exact dimensions against what the Orders' survey claims.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Forty-two paces. The official file says twenty. They didn't just keep this quiet — they *lied about its size*.
Arthit — "Stop. You've passed the same bone formation twice. The room is shifting while we stand in it.

lines_before.dialogue: The party emerges from a narrow tunnel into a vast, spherical chamber. Ancient, intricate machinery, silent for centuries, hangs from the ceiling like a frozen constellation.
Look at this! It's... beautiful. But it feels wrong. Like a song that's missing its final note.
Beautiful? It's a tomb for dead tech. Probably some pre-Silencing vanity project. The price for hubris was the same for everyone back then.
Careful. The acoustics here are... focused. A single sound could resonate through the entire array.
These weren't just machines. They were instruments. A symphony of creation, frozen mid-performance.
A soft, metallic whirring begins. A single crystalline arm on the central apparatus slowly extends, its tip glowing with a faint, pale light.
Ah! A working component! Even a fragment could be worth a fortune to the right collector. You, too, could benefit from such a find!
It's moving! Should we... should we leave? I was bad at archaeology. I don't want to break anything more important than myself.

lines_after.dialogue: The glowing tip of the arm points directly at Arthit, then shifts to trace the outline of his resonant prosthetic leg.
It's... reading the resonance frequency of my crystal. It's harmonizing.
Great. So the ancient ghost in the machine likes your new foot. Let's hope its taste isn't expensive.
A low, pure tone emanates from the apparatus, filling the chamber. Dust falls from long-sealed panels along the walls.

line.dialogue: The central machine's tone deepens. Sealed panels along the walls begin to shudder, revealing dark openings.

choices.text: Let Arthit attempt to communicate with the machine using his prosthetic's resonance.
choices.outcome: A cautious, controlled interaction. May gain knowledge but risk attracting unwanted attention.
choices.description: Touch the nearest instrument-string gently and hum a single sustained note into the chamber.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The walls accepted that. They remember what hands used to feel like.
Arthit — "I said careful! The whole chamber just rang back like a wounded bell — everyone, stop breathing so loud.

choices.text: Attempt to dampen or disrupt the resonant frequency before the panels fully open.
choices.outcome: A risky technical maneuver. Could silence the machine or trigger a defensive response.
choices.description: Signal Pichit to interpret the glyph-notation carved above the largest dormant instrument before approaching it.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "This notation isn't performance — it's a handshake. A calling sequence. They wanted us to ask permission first.
Pichit — "I misread the glyph — that wasn't a greeting, it was a warning. Whatever's sleeping here just knows we're ignorant.

choices.text: Encourage Chanida to sing a counter-frequency, to overwhelm and command the ancient system.
choices.outcome: A bold, potentially violent clash of resonances. High reward, high danger.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to describe exactly what about the beauty feels wrong while Li scouts the perimeter silently.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "The tuning. Everything is tuned to a pitch the human ear can't hold — it's beautiful because it's *erasing* us, note by note.

lines_before.dialogue: The shuddering wall panels fall away. The openings reveal not more machinery, but hundreds of crystalline pods, each containing a desiccated, silent human form.
Oh, no... I had a bad dream like this once. People frozen in crystal, screaming with no sound...
They're... they're all Listeners. Look at the robes! This was a monastery. A whole monastery turned into a... a battery?
So the 'price' for their knowledge was becoming fuel. The Tonal Orders would have a field day with this horror. I did the research on this place all myself, and I never saw this.
The resonance isn't just reading my prosthetic. It's trying to draw from it. To siphon the energy. This whole chamber is a resonant prison.
A symphony of creation, you said. But this is its finale. A choir of silenced voices, powering a machine that forgot its purpose.
A tragic fate, truly. But the crystal matrix stabilizing these pods... that technology is unparalleled. One sample, extracted correctly...
The central machine's tone becomes a piercing, demanding whine. A pod near Arthit cracks, and a wave of draining resonance lashes out, targeting his prosthetic leg.

lines_after.dialogue: It's pulling! It wants to consume the resonance! I can't hold it!
We have to break the cycle! We have to scream louder than the machine!
Or we let it have the fancy leg and run. My vision for our future is suddenly very, very clear: alive.
The whine escalates, shaking the chamber. More pods begin to fracture. The ancient prison is awakening, hungry.

line.dialogue: The draining resonance intensifies, threatening to shatter Arthit's prosthetic and consume its power, potentially re-awakening the entire horrific apparatus.

choices.text: Sacrifice the resonant prosthetic. Let the machine consume it to buy time for a retreat.
choices.outcome: Arthit loses his advanced mobility. The machine is briefly satiated, allowing escape but leaving the horror intact.
choices.description: Chanida channels frequency mapping toward the cave echoes, hoping to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida is thwarted. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Coordinate a counter-frequency. Use the party's combined sounds to overload and collapse a single support pillar, causing a partial cave-in.
choices.outcome: A dangerous gamble. Could trap the machine and free some pods, but risks structural failure and burial.
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing resonant staff to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Pichit must attempt a philosophical resonance. To sing not a command, but a question—a memory of purpose—to the machine's core.
choices.outcome: The climactic risk. Could either pacify and silence the machine forever, or fully awaken its consuming wrath.
choices.description: The villager steps forward with terraces, ready to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: the villager's expertise pays off. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard stretches beneath a bruised sky, a skeletal graveyard of old resonance ships. The air vibrates with the discordant symphony of hydraulic crushers and grinding metal.
Ugh, this place smells like rust and regret. Why are we meeting a monk here again?
Because, Chanida, the Tonal Orders don't patrol the acoustic chaos. It's a good place to not be overheard. Stay alert.
Relax. Half these wrecks are probably listening posts anyway. The Orders know everything eventually.
Perhaps. But in the noise, one might hear a different truth. A purer note.
A figure in simple robes approaches, picking his way through the debris. He is LISTENER MONK SAI, his eyes wide with the strain of the harsh acoustics.
You are the ones who asked about the old songs? The ones before the charts?
We are. We seek understanding.

lines_after.dialogue: It’s nice and peaceful in our monastery. The Lattice hums a gentle hymn there. Here… it screams.
Yeah, it's a real nice place. So, about those songs?
I know. I already know that what I must tell you breaks my vows. But the truth has its own resonance.
Sai gestures to a gutted ship's hull. Inside, amidst the corroded pipes, something glows with a soft, crystalline light.

line.dialogue: The Monk points to the glowing object in the wreck. It's a prototype resonator, unlike any you've seen. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Let Chanida scramble up the loose plating to grab it quickly.
choices.description: Climb onto a rusted hauler and scan for signal emanations from the wrecks below

line.dialogue: Three pings — eastern row. Someone's still home in these graves.
Slipped. Knee's bleeding and every pod within fifty meters just lit up like a congregation hearing prayer.

choices.text: Ask Sai to describe its acoustic signature first, to ensure it's safe.
choices.description: Press your ear to a derelict comm-relay and listen for Pichit's "different tone"

line.dialogue: There — beneath the static. A voice reciting coordinates. Not Tonal Order liturgy. Something older.
I hear nothing but my own heartbeat and the settlement's perimeter drones circling closer. We've overstayed.

choices.text: Have Arthit scout for structural weaknesses in the wreck before approaching.
choices.description: Grab Chanida's arm and pull her behind a collapsed smelter before she kicks another hull

line.dialogue: Fine, fine — I'll keep my boots to myself. But if something's watching, hiding won't make it friendly.
Get off me! I don't need you babysitting my footsteps — and now the whole yard knows we're here anyway.

lines_before.dialogue: The retrieved device is a complex lattice of copper wire and pulsating crystal, humming at a frequency that makes your teeth ache.
It's an unregulated harmonic amplifier. This could destabilize a ship's entire resonator array if installed wrong.
Or make it sing like nothing else. I really wonder who built it, and why it was scrapped.
A local scavenger, BUNLOM, limps out from behind a stack of hull fragments. His right leg is a crude assembly of pipes and a dull, cracked crystal.
You shouldn't touch that. Bad luck. The man who made it… his mind unraveled with the notes. He said the Lattice was talking back.
What happened to him?
The Orders took him. But his work remained. Some of us… we tried to use it. My leg… it's really worth seeing! A marvel, once. Now it just hurts.
You're in pain?
I’m really hurting. The crystal… it doesn't sing right anymore. It scrapes. It's the subplot_crystal_leg prototype. A failure.

lines_after.dialogue: So the inventor wasn't crazy. He was ahead of the curve, and the Orders silenced him. It’s really worth seeing the pattern now.
His notes spoke of a 'fundamental frequency.' A true note that could calm or shatter the Lattice. Finding it… would be worth any cost.
Or cost us everything. That device, his leg… they're warnings.
Bunlom taps his faulty prosthetic. The scraped note it emits causes a nearby pile of loose crystal shards to vibrate ominously. Sai the Monk pales, hearing something within the dissonance.

line.dialogue: Bunlom's malfunctioning prosthetic has agitated the residual crystals in the scrap pile. The unstable resonance is building. What's the priority?

choices.text: Shut down the prosthetic immediately. Stabilize the immediate area.
choices.description: Carefully examine the amplifier's crystal lattice for stress fractures before anyone touches it.

line.dialogue: There — hairline fractures along the third harmonic node. This thing would've shattered on activation.
I can't get a clean read with all this ambient interference. We're flying blind.

choices.text: Study the resonance pattern. This malfunction might reveal a weakness in the technology.
choices.description: Ask the villager to describe exactly what happened to the man who built it.

line.dialogue: His hands shook for weeks, then he walked into the jungle humming its frequency and never came back.
He just waves me off and mutters about 'the sound that doesn't stop.' Nobody here wants to talk.

choices.text: Use the new amplifier device to try and counter-resonate, calming the crystals. Risky.
choices.description: Ignore the warnings and calibrate the amplifier to a low resonance to test its range.

line.dialogue: Oh gods — listen to that sustain. One properly tuned burst could reach across the whole valley.
The feedback loop is immediate. My teeth are vibrating and I can't shut it down fast enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's din is now a focused roar of industry. The Listeners have surrounded the central salvage platform, their hooded figures moving with unnerving synchronicity. The damaged resonator core lies exposed, its fractured crystal pulsing erratically.
The Lattice's song here... it's been *taught* to reject this frequency. Someone has been seeding dissonance into the harmonics. This isn't natural decay.
So they're sabotaging their own ships? That's insane! Who would do that?
Someone who benefits from stranded vessels. Or from controlling what gets salvaged... and what gets silenced.
Great. So we're standing on a giant tuning fork that's about to shatter, surrounded by monks who might be complicit. I have work to do. Specifically, not dying.
The prosthetic leg we found... its resonance signature matches the sabotage frequency. It's a key. Or a weapon.
They took my brother's leg after his ship cracked! Said it was 'contaminated.' Now you're telling me it's part of this? I got my answer. And I don't like it.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision sends a ripple through the scrapyard. The Listeners react—some with alarm, others with a chilling readiness.
You've chosen to listen to the broken song. A dangerous path. Can you promise me you understand the dissonance you may unleash?
I promise only to seek the true note beneath the silence.

line.dialogue: How do we use the resonant prosthetic to counter the sabotage?

choices.text: Use it as a diagnostic tool. Trace the dissonance back to its source in the scrapyard's control hub.
choices.outcome: You carefully map the interference. It leads to a hidden transmitter among the wreckage, allowing you to disable it with precision. The immediate threat is neutralized, but the architect remains hidden.
choices.description: Monk places bare palms flat against the deck plating, letting the Lattice's wrongness flow through him, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — beneath the dissonance, the original harmony still exists. I can reach it, but someone must anchor me while I work.
The taught rejection... it's *everywhere*. Like trying to recall a forgotten name — the harder I listen, the more it fights back.

choices.text: Reverse its polarity. Turn the weaponized frequency into a stabilizing counter-harmonic for the damaged core.
choices.outcome: A risky recalibration. The core stabilizes with a resonant hum, but the prosthetic shatters in the process. The ship is saved, but the physical evidence is lost.
choices.description: Chanida jury-rigs the emergency beacon to broadcast the corrupted frequency pattern outward as a distress signal, 15 words

line.dialogue: If someone taught the Lattice to break ships, they'll come running when their handiwork screams loud enough. We just became bait.
The beacon's drawing from the same corrupted resonance — it's screaming *back* at us. Whatever's listening, it's not friendly, and it's close.

choices.text: Amplify its signal. Overload the sabotage network to force the saboteur's hand into the open.
choices.outcome: You broadcast a deafening pulse of raw resonance. Machinery shrieks across the yard. A figure stumbles from the shadows—a high-ranking Tonal Order official, their own resonator glove smoking. You have your culprit, but the yard is now in chaotic uproar.
choices.description: Arthit accesses the maintenance logs to trace who last modified the Lattice's harmonic calibration on this vessel, 15 words

line.dialogue: Calibration entry, fourteen cycles ago. Authorization code belongs
the villager fails. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: Chaos reigns. The scrapyard groans as destabilized resonance fields cause metal to shiver and crystal to whine. The exposed saboteur—a Tonal Order Cartographer—stands defiant on a spire of wreckage.

Fools! You think this is sabotage? This is *pruning*. The Lattice grows chaotic. Weak ships, flawed resonators... they introduce noise. The Silencing began because humanity lost control of the song. We are preventing a second chorus!
By murdering people and calling it 'pruning'? He's right! You're just a gardener with a god complex!
You hurt my family! You hurt everyone here! Come and take a picture with us—see the faces you've shattered!
The Lattice's instability... it's probably true that old resonators contribute. But your solution is monstrous. You don't get to decide who sails and who sinks.
The Cartographer speaks a twisted truth. The song *is* sick. But the cure is not more violence. It is understanding. The Listeners have... withheld findings. Out of fear.
Fear of this. Fear of choices that aren't choices at all. The Lattice isn't a garden. It's a conversation. And you're trying to shout everyone else down.
My brother's leg... you used his pain as a weapon. Come in. Step down from your spire and face what you've done.

lines_after.dialogue: The scrapyard holds its breath. The Cartographer's resonator glove is powered, aimed at the unstable core. One note could trigger a cascade failure.
You'll thank me. When the true silence comes, you'll understand. Or you won't be around to.
There is no true silence. Only the notes we refuse to hear.

line.dialogue: The Cartographer is about to trigger a catastrophic resonance cascade. How do you stop the final, silencing note?

choices.text: Appeal to the Listeners. Urge them to unite their monastic chant to create a harmonic shield, protecting the core.
choices.outcome: The monks hesitate, then join their voices. A wall of ancient, layered sound dampens the Cartographer's frequency. He is overwhelmed not by force, but by a chorus he sought to control. The Order is fractured, but the Lattice hears a new unity.
choices.description: Malee attempts to tune the prosthetic, relying on engineering

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The resonance turns hostile. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Use the scrapyard itself. Trigger controlled collapses to create a discordant acoustic maze, disrupting his focus and resonator lock.
choices.outcome: You bring towers of scrap crashing down in a calculated cacophony. The Cartographer's aim fails as the soundscape erupts. He's buried not in silence, but in the very noise he despised. The yard is a mess, but the core is safe.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using Listener training to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Pichit overreaches. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Sing. Pichit must tap into their latent ability and sing a counter-frequency directly, weaponizing their own rare gift in a duel of pure resonance.
choices.outcome: Pichit's voice rises, raw and untrained but true. It isn't a note from any chart. It's something older. The Cartographer's glove cracks, then his resolve. He falls to his knees, not in defeat, but in awe of a song he thought extinct. The secret of the Singers is now exposed to all.
choices.description: Have the monk risk using prayers to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: the monk makes it work. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the monk is thwarted. Tonal Order enforcers confiscate his equipment.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of dead ships. Cranes tear at metal skeletons. The industrial din is a wall of sound, masking subtler frequencies.
Careful where you step. This place is a maze of unstable platforms and sharp edges. One wrong move and...
And what? We add to the scrap heap? Cheery thought. We're here because a 'ghost ship' is supposedly whispering? Please.

The skycity resident was terrified! Said his salvage crew fled when their crystal resonator started picking up a repeating signal—a mournful hum from the *Echo of Dawn*, that ship that vanished years ago.
A signal persisting after a ship's silence... what history is trapped in that loop? What final moment keeps repeating?
You're the ones asking about the haunted hulk? My girlfriend gets jealous if I'm out late, but even she says stay away. The sound... it gets in your head.
We need to locate the source. But this acoustic environment is terrible. All this clanging will drown out the resonance signature.
Great. So we're hunting a whisper in a thunderstorm. I sprained my ankle just thinking about this.

lines_after.dialogue: There! Between those two crane strikes—a gap in the noise. I can feel a vibration... different from the machinery.
A coherent frequency, fighting to be heard through the chaos. The ship's final song...
You found it? Don't make me cry! I lost friends to that wreck. Just... be careful.

line.dialogue: The signal leads to the half-crushed hull of the *Echo of Dawn*. How do we approach the source?

choices.text: Tune our resonator to dampen the ambient noise. (Technical solution)
choices.description: Rig a signal interceptor to the salvage crane's antenna and triangulate the ghost frequency's origin point.

line.dialogue: The waveform is repeating every 47 seconds — that's not decay, that's a distress call embedded in the carrier wave.
You've flooded the receiver with static. Now we're deaf *and* blind in here.

choices.text: Follow the physical vibrations through the wreckage. (Instinctive path)
choices.description: Crawl through the collapsed ventilation shaft toward the signal's strongest reading, ignoring the groaning metal overhead.

line.dialogue: I can see it — a junction box still glowing. Someone wired a backup battery to keep this thing screaming.
The shaft buckled behind you. We're not reaching anything now except whatever's making that sound.

choices.text: Ask the local scavengers for a safer route in. (Social approach)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to replay the skycity resident's original testimony recording and cross-reference his coordinates with the salvage logs.

line.dialogue: He said the signal started *before* the ship went quiet — that changes everything. This isn't a haunting, it's a warning.
The recording's corrupted past the second timestamp. Whatever spooked that resident, the evidence is already gone.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the derelict, the world's noise fades to a distant thrum. Here, the ghost frequency is king—a low, pervasive hum that makes the rust flakes dance.
Structural integrity is compromised. That humming is causing micro-vibrations. One resonant spike could bring this down on us.
Look! The ship's log crystal—it's still active, pulsing in time with the hum. The data might be corrupted, but...
But it's our only clue. What do your parents do, Pichit? Mine were Listeners. They'd say this sound is grief given tone.
They studied pure resonance. Mine... they were Singers. They believed every sound tells a story. This one is asking for help.
You shouldn't be in here. This wreck's bad luck. My crew... we don't touch it. The Tonal Orders marked it forbidden. No one was helping us when we tried, so we stopped.
Forbidden? Why? What's in here they don't want found?
A truth. One that contradicts their charts. Shall we go to the seaside, Arthit? Sometimes you need to leave the known maps to find new shores.

lines_after.dialogue: The log crystal flickers. A fragmented image forms: the ship's Singer, face strained, manually overloading the resonator as the Lattice outside churned violently.
He scuttled his own ship. Deliberately. To avoid... what? Being captured? The data cuts there.
I have no one to help me understand this. But you... you listen different. The Orders said this ship was lost to a storm. That's a lie.

line.dialogue: The corrupted log suggests the Singer sacrificed the ship to hide something. The hum emanates from the sealed resonator chamber. How do we proceed?

choices.text: Attempt to stabilize and download the remaining log data. (Seek more information)
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using captain experience to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
A costly mistake by Arthit. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Try to harmonize with the hum using our own resonator, calming the frequency. (Resonant solution)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to seek the dismissed truth, drawing on resonant staff

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Pichit. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit fails. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Force the chamber open. The truth is in there, but it might collapse the wreck. (Direct and dangerous)
choices.description: The scavenger channels survival skills toward the broken ships, hoping to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Exactly as the scavenger hoped. Surface knowledge reveals a safe path.
the scavenger is thwarted. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: The party huddles in the shadow of the derelict Resonance Ship's hull. The scrapyard's industrial din seems to recede, replaced by a low, mournful hum emanating from the vessel's cracked crystal resonator.
There's something in my eye. No, wait, that's just... dust. From this creepy ship. The sound is getting louder.
Nah, nah. That's not dust. It's a resonance ghost. The ship's final frequency, stuck in a feedback loop. Happens when they break apart a vessel without proper acoustic damping.

It's dangerous. That frequency could destabilize the local Lattice, or worse, attract scavengers who think we've found something valuable. May I have some time? I need to analyze the harmonic pattern.
Time is a luxury the echo doesn't have. It's a memory, crying out. The Silencing wasn't just a physical event; it was a trauma frozen in sound. This ship is a piece of that trauma.

You're still here? That wail's been going for weeks. Bad business. The Tonal Orders marked this hull for quiet decommissioning, but the crew... they say they heard a Singer's final note in the storm and went mad.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The ghostly hum shifts soothed.
Well, that was profoundly stupid. The echo's changed pitch. It's... clearer.
It's not just a noise. It's a message. And I think it's giving us coordinates.

line.dialogue: The mournful resonance is a puzzle and a danger. How do we engage with the echo of the lost ship?

choices.label: [EASY] Attempt to Calm the Frequency
choices.text: Use basic acoustic theory to gently dampen the feedback loop, silencing the ghost safely but losing its message.
choices.description: Shield your eyes and hum a counter-frequency to disrupt the resonance pattern.

line.dialogue: Malee grabs your shoulder.* "You found its rhythm. The ghost is thinning — keep going, don't break tone!
Arthit pulls you back.* "Wrong harmonic. You just fed it. The lattice is cracking — everyone fall back, NOW!

choices.label: [MEDIUM] Tune Our Resonator to Match
choices.text: Risk syncing the party's ship crystal to the echo, potentially deciphering the signal but risking harmonic backlash.
choices.description: Reach directly into the shimmer and pull the memory fragment free before it destabilizes.

line.dialogue: Chanida steadies your trembling hand.* "You hold it. The whole echo — I can see what it remembers. It's... it's someone looking for home.
Pichit wrenches you away.* "It burned through your gloves. That wasn't a memory — that was a warning wrapped in grief.

choices.label: [HARD] Enter the Hull and Find the Source
choices.text: Venture into the unstable wreck to physically interact with the fractured crystal core, the most direct and dangerous path.
choices.description: Ask the ghost what it wants — speak to it directly, treat it as a person, not a phenomenon.

line.dialogue: Pichit exhales slowly.* "It heard you. Look — the shimmer is forming a face. It's been waiting decades for someone to simply ask.
Malee's voice drops low.* "It doesn't have answers. Only hunger. You gave

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the ship's ruptured heart, the party finds the resonator chamber. The central crystal is a spiderweb of cracks, pulsing with trapped light and sound. The air vibrates with forgotten anguish.
Structural integrity is at 12%. A full resonance release could shatter the chamber. I'll have a look at the fracture patterns. We need a precise counter-frequency.
Forget the patterns! Look! In the crystal... flickers, like memories. I see the storm. I see them panicking. I'll try it. I'll try to sing back to it.
You're not a Singer, Chanida. That's a one-way trip to having your brains turned to harmonic slurry. This is a tomb, not a choir loft.
But every tomb holds a story waiting to be heard. The Silencing tried to erase these stories. This crystal isn't haunted; it's *remembering*. And it's asking to be remembered.
(Over comms, voice crackling with static) We're reading massive energy spikes from your location! The Tonal Orders have detected it too! They're sending enforcers! You have to get out!

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber fills with a final, brilliant chord—a sound of release, not destruction. Then, silence. The crystal goes dark, its burden lifted.
Huh. I'll get it. The core's stable. And... there's a data-shard, ejected cleanly. The ship's black box. You actually did it.
We listened. That's all it needed. The echo wasn't a ghost. It was a witness. And now its testimony is ours.

line.dialogue: The crystal core is at its breaking point, holding the ship's final moments. The Tonal Orders are inbound. How do we resolve the echo?

choices.label: [EASY] Emergency Dampening and Retreat
choices.text: Force-quiet the crystal with overloaded dampeners, saving yourselves and destroying the echo's memory, then flee before the Orders arrive.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with engineering to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
Malee loses control. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.label: [MEDIUM] Data Extraction Sacrifice
choices.text: Attempt a risky download of the crystal's memory into your own resonator, potentially saving the data but certainly destroying the core and alerting the Orders to your location.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to confront hidden knowledge, drawing on unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Chanida misreads the situation. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.label: [HARD] The Letting Go
choices.text: Guide the echo to complete its final resonance naturally, allowing it to 'sing' its story one last time in a public, undeniable burst before dissipating. This will draw immediate, overwhelming attention.

line.dialogue: the villager succeeds. Terrace-hardened resilience sees them through.
the villager overreaches. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch out in tiered tranquility. Wind rustles through rows of sky-rice and crystal-gourd vines, their chimes creating a soft, natural harmony with the distant hum of the city's stabilizers.
I'm such a lucky gal! Can you believe this place? After weeks of resonator static, this quiet is... actual music.
Don't get too comfy. Peace this cheap usually has hidden fees. Look—scorch marks on that irrigation crystal. Recent.
Caution is advised. The Groundless agitants have been targeting agricultural nodes. They believe severing our 'false roots' will force a return to the Surface.
Yet the Lattice below sings a warning even they must hear. This silence we feel... it's not empty. It's a held breath.
We've talked about this before, Pichit. Every hum is a mystery, every quiet a conspiracy. Sometimes a garden is just a garden!
A figure emerges from behind a trellis of singing vines—a woman in patched leathers, her eyes sharp. A Surface Scavenger.
Nah, nah. She's right to be wary. You don't need to stick around. Garden's got new pests. Sky-rats with cutlasses.

lines_after.dialogue: Sky pirates? Here? What are they harvesting—cabbages?
Something sweeter. Resonance charts. The Tonal Order convoy that passed through? Had its safe cracked like a nut. Pirates are hiding in the lower terraces, waiting for the heat to die.
A significant risk. They are known to use aggressive frequencies to disable ships.
But why stay? Unless... they haven't found what they're looking for yet.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points toward the mist-shrouded lower terraces. 'They're down there, arguing over charts. Your move, sky-folk.'

choices.text: Approach openly from the main path. Let's see if they'll talk.
choices.description: Press your ear against the nearest wind-chime column and listen to the Lattice's song directly.

line.dialogue: * "The resonance patterns confirm it — three breach points, all on the eastern perimeter. We move now or not at all.
* "The harmonics claw into my skull like broken glass. I heard too much, too fast — my nose is bleeding.

choices.text: Use the crop rows and wind-chime noise as cover to observe them first.
choices.description: Grab Chanida's wrist and pull her back from the courtyard's center where the chimes have gone silent.

line.dialogue: * "See that? No wind, but the chimes still move. Something beneath us is *breathing.* Glad I trusted my gut.
* "I yank too hard — she stumbles into the chime array and the whole ring screams. Every agitant within a mile just heard our dinner bell.

choices.text: Ask the Scavenger to guide you. She knows this terrain.
choices.description: Kneel beside Pichit and trace the Lattice cracks glowing faintly through the flagstone joints with your fingertips.

line.dialogue: * "Ah — you feel it too. The pattern spirals counter-clockwise, which means the Lattice isn't warning us. It's *inviting* us deeper. Bold choice.
* "The Lattice burns cold through your skin and snaps shut like a jaw. Whatever lived beneath that stone just tasted you — and it liked the flavor.

lines_before.dialogue: The lower terraces are a labyrinth of water channels and dense, fragrant herbs. The mist is thicker here, dampening sound. Through the haze, you see three figures hunched over a glowing crystal slate.
I knew right away this frequency map was garbage! This lead here? Points to a dead zone. We risked the Order's wrath for a scenic route to nowhere!
A second pirate, younger, shifts nervously. 'Maybe we read it wrong. The Groundless contact said—'
The Groundless are surface-crazy! They want us all to drown in crystal! No, I'm gonna rush off right now and find that Scavenger who sold us this. Get our resonance back.
(Whispering) Are you sure? A pirate with buyer's remorse. How quaint.
They're working with the Groundless? That's... new. And bad.
The alliance is likely transactional. Pirates gain uncharted frequencies; Groundless gain disruption agents. The stolen charts could detail the city's foundational resonance points.
If they sabotage those points... the entire city's floatation could become unstable. That's not just disruption. That's a fall.

lines_after.dialogue: The lead pirate kicks the crystal slate. It skitters across the stone, coming to rest near your hiding spot. Its glow reveals intricate frequency lines and a marked location deep within the Lattice.
Forget the map. We take the old listener's path down. Safer. Now, where's that double-crossing scavenger...
The 'old listener's path'... That's not on any Tonal Order chart. That's forbidden knowledge.
And the map... it doesn't point to a dead zone. It points to a resonance well. A natural power source. They're not just hiding. They're searching for a weapon.

line.dialogue: The pirates are splitting up. One heads back toward the gardens, the other two toward a crumbling terrace edge—the supposed 'path.' The stolen map lies exposed.

choices.text: Secure the map. It's the key to understanding their target.
choices.description: Palm the frequency map and slip it beneath your coat while the bandit argues, 14 words

line.dialogue: Map's ours now—and their whole signal network just became our problem to unravel.
Hey—were you just reaching for that? Nothing like a thief among thieves.

choices.text: Split the party. Follow the pirate going after the Scavenger to intercept and question.
choices.description: Lean close to Chanida and quietly trace the Groundless trade routes on the table with your fingertip, 15 words

line.dialogue: These supply lines—they're not trading with the Groundless, they're *feeding* them something. We follow the cargo.
Too many branches—I can't read this without the cipher, and shouting about it won't help.

choices.text: Follow the two heading for the path. Stop them from reaching the resonance well at all costs.
choices.description: Step between the bandit and Malee, look the bandit dead in the eye, and ask who paid for the map, 18 words

line.dialogue: ...Tavoran middleman. Smelled like old money and fear. That answer buy me something, or is this just a conversation?
You don't get to question me, surface-licker. I shared what I shared. Push harder and I walk.

lines_before.dialogue: The wind in the Hanging Gardens shifts, carrying not the scent of blossoms, but the acrid tang of ozone. From below the terraces, a low, aggressive hum begins to rise.
Well, well. Look what the wind dragged up. A little garden party, and you've got our property.
Pichit, don't let them see you! There are three vessels closing from the leeward side.

Of course. The Groundless fanatics broadcast their little secret a bit too loudly, and the local sharks smelled blood. He's still single, isn't he? The scavenger, I mean. Probably thought he could get away with it.
Stop it! All of you, stop! They're not here for a chat. Those are cutter-class resonance ships. Pirate rigs.
Told you the Garden's peace was thin. The Tonal Orders pay good coin for 'recovered' artifacts. Or silence. Stop! Don't make a move toward your weapon.
A choice presented by violence is no choice at all. But they are here because of what we've learned. The responsibility is ours.
Smart one. Hand over the scavenger and his little resonance map. The Groundless don't need it where they're going—which is down.

lines_after.dialogue: The bandit leader's resonator whines to a higher pitch, a clear threat. The hydroponic channels nearby tremble, their water forming dissonant ripples.
Well. You've managed to stop one problem and immediately start a bigger one. Congratulations.
They're flanking us. The terraces give us some cover, but we're exposed on the windward side.
Forget cover! We need to move. That low-frequency map the scavenger gave us—it points to an old maintenance spire below the Gardens. We can lose them in the under-lattice.

line.dialogue: The pirates are moving to cut off your retreat. The path to the city is blocked, but Chanida's idea is a dangerous drop into the unknown.

choices.line: Use the Gardens' irrigation pipes. Create a screen of mist with misaligned resonators to slip away.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on ship navigation

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Things don't go as planned. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Fight a holding action. Use the terraces as defensive positions to drive them off before fleeing.

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
A costly mistake by Pichit. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.line: Go on the offensive. Target their ships' resonators with precise sonic strikes to disable them.

the pirate loses control. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The chase leads you to the Garden's very roots—a crumbling spire where the city's foundational crystals pierce the Lattice's surface. The air thrums with latent, wild energy.
This is it. The 'Silent Node.' The Groundless say the Lattice doesn't sing here... it listens. We don't stay in touch with the Orders for a reason. This knowledge... it changes things.
Change ain't profitable! You think your little revelation matters? The Lattice is a tool. A weapon. And you're standing on the firing pin!
He's right. The harmonic instability... it's massive. If the pirate's ship resonator fires at full power in this node, it could cause a cascading fracture in the Garden's foundation.
So, the climactic choice. Die for a secret, or die hiding it. When should I go? Now seems as good a time as any.
No! We need some time! Pichit, the map showed a stabilizing frequency. A true Singer could channel it, could calm the node.
Time is the one resource we have exhausted. But the Lattice... it exists in all times at once here. To sing to it is to ask it to remember a state of peace.
The pirate ship's resonator glows, building to a catastrophic discharge. The very crystals of the spire begin to whine in sympathetic, shattered vibration.

lines_after.dialogue: A profound quiet settles, deeper than any silence. Then, a single, pure tone resonates from the Lattice itself, healing the fracture. The pirate ship drifts, powerless.
You... you didn't force it. You asked. The Groundless... we never understood. It's not about escaping the Lattice. It's about hearing it.
Don't get sentimental. We've just turned a secret into a spectacle. The Tonal Orders will have questions. May I have some time to think of a good lie?
The structural resonance of the entire Garden has shifted. Stabilized. It's... more resilient than before.
You did it, Pichit! You actually sang to the world! Wait until the other Listeners hear about this!

line.dialogue: The Silent Node is silent no more, humming with a gentle, stable frequency. The secret of the Groundless is out, and the power you've witnessed cannot be un-witnessed.

choices.line: Conceal the Truth. Let the pirates be found adrift, their story dismissed as resonator failure. The secret remains, but buried.
choices.description: Overload the Node's harmonic core, broadcasting the Garden's truth across every frequency in the Archipelago.

line.dialogue: ** "The resonance spike just cracked every receiver from here to the Veil — they can't unhear it now.
** "The core rejected the overload — it's collapsing inward and I can't stop the feedback loop.

choices.line: Reveal Selectively. Share the truth only with the Listeners, creating a new, guarded alliance of understanding.
choices.description: Let the bandit wire the Node's energy reserves into the settlement's grid, keeping the Garden's song for yourselves.

line.dialogue: ** "We just turned a cosmic secret into ten years of clean power — the dead don't need it anyway.
** "He wired it backwards — now the Garden knows *we're* here, and it is not singing anymore.

choices.line: Broadcast the Frequency. Let the stabilizing tone ring out openly, challenging the Tonal Orders' monopoly directly and irrevocably.
choices.description: Walk into the Node's harmonic field alone, letting the Garden's frequency rewrite what you are.

line.dialogue: ** "I can hear everything now — every root, every name, every lie they buried under the soil.
** "It's not a song, it's a mouth — and I can feel myself being *unmade* note by note.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns before you, a jagged maw in the floating island's underbelly. Inside, the air is cool and still, carrying the faint, crystalline hum of the Lattice far below.
Listen to that! The echoes in here are... singing. Or crying. Can't tell.
Stay close. The acoustics are unnatural. A misstep could trigger a cave-in or... attract something.
Relax. If it hasn't collapsed in a thousand years, it won't pick today. Probably. Let's see what these ancients left behind.
Every resonance tells a story. These walls have absorbed the last sounds of a world. What do you think they heard?
Hoi! You lot! This is my claim! I've been working this scrape for weeks. You have a lot of things... tools, gear. You're not simple explorers.
Your claim? The whole island just fell out of the sky! Finders keepers!
Spoken like a city-dweller. You don't know the surface. Down here, it's about who stakes first. And I've got a lot of stuff stashed around to prove it.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, a gathering! Don't mind old Kael here. He's protective of his... finds. I'm Niran, a humble negotiator. I'm sure we can arrange something for any interesting things you might uncover.
A 'humble negotiator' in a hole in the ground. Right. What are you really selling?
Opportunity! Information! For instance, I know Kael found a sealed chamber. He's afraid of it. But for the right price, I could... persuade him to share.
You shut your mouth, Niran! That place... it's wrong. The echoes don't come back right.
A wrong echo... That could be a memory the Lattice couldn't absorb. We need to see it.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger, Kael, blocks the path deeper, hand on his weapon. Niran watches with a calculating smile.

choices.line: (Appeal to Curiosity) 'We seek only understanding, not treasure. Let us hear the echo.'
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the vibrating wall and hum a matching tone back into the stone.

line.dialogue: The resonance shifted — it's *answering* you. The whole corridor just breathed warmer.
Wrong frequency. The stone cracked beneath your hand — something deeper just woke up.

choices.line: (Negotiate) 'We have supplies. Name your price for passage.'
choices.description: Signal everyone to stop moving, then drop a copper coin down the nearest shaft and count the seconds.

line.dialogue: Four seconds. That's sixty meters down — and I heard it land on something *hollow*, not solid.
It didn't stop. No impact. No echo. That shaft goes down forever, or something down there caught it.

choices.line: (Intimidate) 'Stand aside. You're outnumbered.'
choices.description: Follow the singing echo alone, pressing deeper into the corridor while the others argue about the structural report.

line.dialogue: You found it — a chamber where every voice for a thousand years is still bouncing. I can hear dead languages in the walls.
You wandered straight into a resonance trap. The frequency is pressing against your skull — your nose is bleeding.

lines_before.dialogue: Past Kael's barrier, The Hollow opens into a vast, cylindrical chamber. Faded murals depict cities not floating, but rooted in earth. The air thrums with a low, dissonant frequency.
Well, this is cheery. 'Behold our glorious dirt-based civilization.' No wonder the Tonal Orders suppress this. Everyone knows it's heresy to suggest we came from below.
Careful. This isn't just history. Look—the crystal formations are growing *toward* the sound of our voices. They're reactive.
Whoa! Did you see that? I hummed and that stalactite glowed! This whole cave is an instrument!
Told you it was wrong! It listens!
It's not listening... it's remembering. This chamber is a resonator for a frequency lost during The Silencing. The 'Groundless'... they weren't a movement. They were what we were.

Oh, it's you... making profound realizations. How delightful. And marketable. The Groundless Movement today would pay a fortune for proof their ideology has ancient roots. I heard everything you said, by the way.

lines_after.dialogue: You were eavesdropping? You slimy—
Please! I'm a businessman. Everyone knows the Tonal Orders pay well for 'sedition containment,' but the Groundless pay better for 'inspirational relics.' A bidding war! My favorite.
He's not alone. Look up.
On a ledge above, figures in drab, patched robes emerge from shadows. Their leader steps forward, her voice echoing clearly.

We heard everything, too. Niran is correct about one thing: we seek the truth of the ground. But we do not buy it. We protect it. You have awakened the chamber's memory. Now you must choose: silence it for the Orders, exploit it with him, or help us understand it.

line.dialogue: The Groundless leader's eyes are earnest. Niran's smile is predatory. The crystals pulse with stolen light.

choices.line: (Align with the Groundless) 'We seek truth, not profit. We'll help you study this.'
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the crystal wall and hold your breath completely still.

line.dialogue: The vibrations are settling—it's mapping your pulse, so keep it steady and don't give it a reason to react.
Your heartbeat spiked and now the whole wall is humming back—whatever this place is, it knows we're afraid.

choices.line: (Play the Market) 'Let's hear both offers. What's the relic actually worth?'
choices.description: Signal everyone to stay silent, then strike the cave floor sharply with the butt of your weapon.

line.dialogue: The echo bounced off something massive deeper in—there's a hollow chamber below us, and the crystals lit up like a roadmap!
That was WAY too loud—the stalactites are shaking loose and I really don't want to find out what 'it listens' actually means!

choices.line: (Warn the Orders) 'This knowledge is too dangerous. It must be contained.'
choices.description: Grab the scavenger by the shoulders and demand to know exactly what they've seen down here before.

line.dialogue: Fine! I came through here three months back with two others. Only I walked out. The walls... they remember everyone who speaks.
I told you it was WRONG and you're

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the Hollow, the air grows cold and still. The ruins here are less collapsed, their walls carved with intricate, unfamiliar glyphs that seem to pulse with a faint, captured light.
Look at these carvings! They're... humming? This place is alive.
Or it's just very old machinery on a standby power source. Don't get poetic, Chanida.
The echo patterns have changed. It's not just bouncing sound anymore. It's... layering it. I think this chamber is a recording device.
A memory of the world before The Silencing, etched in stone and sound. What were they trying to preserve?
Preserve? They were probably trying to survive. Come right in. The deeper you go, the stranger it gets.
And the more valuable the finds! He's spot on! Historical data, intact resonators... the Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for authenticated pre-Silencing schematics.
Of course your mind goes straight to prices. Try this on for size: what if the 'data' is a warning?

lines_after.dialogue: A low, harmonic thrum builds from the walls. The glyphs blaze with light, projecting shimmering, ghostly figures—ancient people in mid-conversation, their words a distorted, multi-layered whisper.
It's a resonance imprint! A moment frozen in the Lattice's memory... but the frequency is all wrong. It's causing interference.
The whole cave is shaking! We need to harmonize with it or shut it down!

line.dialogue: The unstable resonance echo is overloading the chamber. The Scavenger points to a central crystal console, while the Merchant eyes a side passage full of artifacts.

choices.line: Follow the Scavenger's lead. Stabilize the echo by matching its frequency with your ship's resonator.
choices.outcome: You carefully attune your device. The ghostly projection stabilizes into a clear, tragic message about The Silencing's cause, granting profound understanding but leaving the artifacts undisturbed.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the humming stone carvings and let the resonance flow through you.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The patterns are responding to your touch — they're not echoes, they're *answers*, reaching back across centuries to find someone willing to listen.
Arthit — "Your heartbeat interfered with the resonance — the frequencies collapsed into noise, and now I can't distinguish the signal from the stone's natural vibration.

choices.line: Listen to Malee's cynical instinct. Attempt to disrupt and silence the echo before it brings the ruins down.
choices.outcome: You bombard the frequency with dissonance. The projection shatters, the shaking stops, and several valuable artifacts crumble to dust. You gain safety, but the historical record is lost.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to photograph the carvings while Malee measures the acoustic frequency with her field equipment.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Got it — 7.83 hertz, the Earth's resonance frequency, which means this place wasn't just built *on* the ground, it was tuned *to* it like a living instrument.
Malee — "The readings are all over the place — either my equipment is picking up interference from the standby power source, or this place is generating frequencies that shouldn't exist.

choices.line: Heed the Merchant's greed. Quickly loot the side passage while Arthit contains the resonance.
choices.outcome: You snatch several pristine artifacts as Arthit struggles to hold the frequency. The chamber partially collapses behind you. You escape with great wealth, but the secret of the chamber is buried forever.

Defeat. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: Beyond the chamber lies the heart of the Hollow: a vast, spherical cavern. In its center floats a massive, flawless crystal—a perfect, silent resonator. The air thrums with latent power.
The Core... I've heard legends. They say it can replay the world's last song. You look run down. This is where it ends.
Nonsense! It's a prototype master resonator! The pinnacle of pre-Silencing tech! The prices the Orders would pay... they have very fair prices for a monopoly breaker!
It's interfaced with the entire cave system. Activating it could playback The Silencing event... or trigger a localized repeat. The risk is catastrophic.
Or it's just a fancy rock. Try it on. Go ahead, Pichit. Let's see what your philosophical soul makes of the ultimate 'why'.
This is it! The truth! But... what if the truth is something we can't survive hearing?
Some memories are buried for a reason. But to remain ignorant is to be forever adrift. This is the choice the Groundless fear—knowledge with a terrible cost.
