lines_before.dialogue: The market stalls are closing, the crowd thinning to a dangerous quiet. The Sky Pirate captain steps from the shadows, the banned resonator crystal gleaming in his hand.
A man called you reckless. He was right. You got the crystal. Now hand over the map.
We don't have it yet. The Negotiator demanded the crystal first.
Then you're useful once. After the trade, we take the map. Simple.
Like hell we are! We didn't risk the Orders just to hand everything to you!
It's still in my memory—the hum before The Silencing. This greed, this fighting over frequencies... it's the same song.
Someone called this a negotiation? Looks more like a mugging. The Negotiator's watching from his stall, by the way. Smiling.
The pirate's crew emerges from alleys, surrounding the party. The crystal in the pirate's hand begins to vibrate, emitting a low, dangerous hum that cuts through the market's noise.

line.dialogue: This is the climax. How do we resolve the standoff?

choices.text: Fight the pirates. (Use force to break through and claim the map for ourselves.)
choices.description: Arthit volunteers to calibrate against the frequency, leveraging tattooed routes

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit misreads the situation. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Outsmart them. (Use the market's noise and layout to create a distraction and escape with the crystal.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to question the Orders' silence, drawing on Listener training

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Reveal the truth. (Confront the Negotiator publicly, exposing his deal with pirates to the market, turning the crowd against both.)
choices.description: Have the pirate focus intimidation on the spice scents to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the pirate loses control. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision echoes, and the Lattice beneath the city seems to pulse in response. The fate of the Open Frequency Map—and perhaps the fragile peace of the skycity—hangs on this moment.
Time's up. The crystal's singing a song of shattering. Your move.
Every note we play writes our future. Let's choose the chord carefully.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance ship *Aria's Grace* settles onto a rare, stable observation platform jutting from the Lattice surface. Below, the crystalline ground pulses with faint, prismatic light.
Whoa. Look at it all! It’s not scary at all! Just… vast. Like a frozen ocean of light.
A frozen ocean that’ll shatter your ship if you hit a dissonant frequency. Don’t let the pretty lights fool you.
Scans show stable harmonic patterns for five hundred meters. Beyond that, the readings get chaotic. We should stick to the survey perimeter.
Yet it calls. Each shimmer is a note in a song we’ve forgotten how to hear.
You lot from the city? Don’t just stand there gawping. The Lattice’s mood can shift faster than a Tonal Order bureaucrat’s loyalty.
We’re here to meet a Listener. What style do you prefer for not getting crystallized?
The style of moving quick and not asking stupid questions. He’s over by the resonance spire. Seems… agitated.

lines_after.dialogue: You are the ones who requested an audience? I am Kaelen. Please, tread softly. The ground here sings of old fractures.
We seek understanding. The Tonal Orders’ charts feel… incomplete.
Incomplete? A polite word for a cage. Their maps only show paths of control, not the Lattice’s true music. But to speak of this… I can’t make it back to the monastery if my superiors learn.

line.dialogue: Kaelen the Listener is fearful but has knowledge. How do we approach?

choices.line: Assure him of our discretion. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on captain experience

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
Arthit hits a wall. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.line: Offer a trade: surface scavenge data for his insights. (Barter)
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with staff meditation to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
A costly mistake by Pichit. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Invoke the shared pursuit of truth. (Conviction)
choices.description: The monk attempts to trace the anomalous signal, relying on meditation

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the monk pulls it off. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The gamble fails. The monastery's countermeasures drown them in noise.

lines_before.dialogue: Kaelen leads you away from the platform, across a plain of humming crystal. Strange, harmonic winds whip around geometric formations.
The Orders suppress the old frequencies. The ones that speak of the time before The Silencing. There’s a resonance here… a memory of the ground.
The ground? You mean the planet beneath the Lattice? That’s myth.
Or heresy, depending on which floating city you’re in. Explains why the Groundless Movement whispers about it.
Wait, we live near each other! I mean, our city and the Groundless safe-house are on adjacent drift lanes. They say the Lattice is a scar, not the world.
A scar that sings. What does this memory-sound say, Kaelen?
It says… ‘containment’. And ‘regret’. I’m happy to hear your minds are open, but this path is solitary. The Orders ensure there’s no one else who listens this deeply.
He’s right about that. I’ve seen their enforcers crystalize a whole dissonant spire. You’re playing with fire.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, shuddering groan echoes through the Lattice. A nearby crystal formation cracks, revealing a hollow, dark cavity within.
A vault! Sealed by the old resonance! This… this shouldn’t be here. The charts mark this as dead harmonic space.
Meaning the Tonal Orders either don’t know about it, or they’re hiding it. Classic.
What’s inside? Could it be proof? Proof for the Groundless?

line.dialogue: A hidden vault, contradicting official charts, lies open before us.

choices.line: Send in a scout drone first. (Caution)
choices.description: Have Malee focus mechanical repair on the crystal ground to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Malee finds the key. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee is thwarted. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Enter immediately, documenting everything. (Seize the Moment)
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing forbidden paths to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
Arthit misreads the situation. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.line: Ask Kaelen to attune to the vault’s resonance first, risking a harmonic backlash. (Esoteric Risk)
choices.description: The scavenger attempts to chart resonance pathways, relying on surface knowledge

line.dialogue: the scavenger succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The lattice has other plans. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The group, guided by the Scavenger's grudging knowledge, descends to a lower platform clinging to the Lattice's sheer face. The air thrums with a deeper, mournful resonance.
This is as far as I go. The 'Memory Hollow' is just past that ridge. The sound there... it gets in your head. Makes you remember things.
Remember things? What kind of things?
Things you shouldn't. Things that were silenced. I can't remember if the last scavenger team I sent came back whole, or came back at all.
A sound-based mnemonic hazard. We need to proceed with extreme caution.
Oh, lovely. So we might all suddenly remember our embarrassing childhoods and walk off a cliff. Sign me up.
Remember... the Listeners spoke of places where the Lattice holds echoes of the past. This must be one.
It is. A forbidden archive. We were told to observe, never to listen. The truth is too dangerous. Remember... keep in mind that some memories are buried for a reason.

lines_after.dialogue: A haunting, discordant melody washes over the platform. The crystalline structures around them flicker with phantom images—glimpses of a world before the Silencing.
I can't remember my password! No, wait... that's not my thought. It's an echo. A panic from someone long ago, trying to access something...
The images... they're of cities. Not floating. On the ground. Connected.
The vision clarifies: a vast, humming network of light and sound, shattered by a single, catastrophic dissonance—the Silencing.

line.dialogue: The memory-vision reveals the source of the Silencing was not natural, but a weapon. The Groundless Movement's theories were correct. The Lattice is a scar, not a shield. What do we do with this truth?

choices.text: Record the frequency. We'll need proof to show the cities.
choices.consequence: You capture a crystal-shard recording. It's compelling, but raw data can be dismissed.
choices.description: Press earplugs fashioned from scavenged insulation foam into your ears before crossing the threshold.

line.dialogue: The foam dampens the harmonic frequencies — I can feel the pressure but my thoughts stay mine.
The material was too porous — I'm hearing my mother's voice from a conversation that never happened.

choices.text: Find the weapon's resonant signature. If we can identify it, we can prove it was made.
choices.consequence: The search is perilous, straining the mind, but you isolate a manufactured harmonic pattern—undeniable evidence.
choices.description: Signal Chanida to maintain a constant verbal count, anchoring your group's awareness in the present moment.

line.dialogue: Seventeen, eighteen, nineteen — keep talking back to me, we're staying right here in the now.
I lost count at forty-something and now I'm remembering someone else's funeral — I never attended this.

choices.text: Try to harmonize with the memory-echo. Experience the moment fully to understand the intent.
choices.consequence: You share the final moments of the ancient victims. You learn the weapon's name and its creators' guild—a secret that makes you a target.
choices.description: Tie a length of cable to the scavenger's anchor point and enter alone with only a thirty-second tether.

line.dialogue: The tension in the line is my lifeline — each step forward, I feel it pulling me toward what's real.
The cable went slack — I turned around and the entrance is gone, replaced by my childhood bedroom doorway.

lines_before.dialogue: Returning to the main observation platform, the atmosphere has changed. The Monk is agitated. Distant resonance ships from the Tonal Orders are closing in.
They know. The Orders monitor forbidden frequencies. I have something to tell you. I... I alerted them. It was my duty.
You WHAT?
I've never understood blind loyalty. It's so... financially inefficient.
We are out of time. We must prepare beforehand. Our ship's resonator is damaged from the memory hollow. We cannot outrun them.
We don't run. We stand. We show them what we've seen.
Foolish. But... I've seen it before. The Orders silencing anyone who digs too deep. My crew... we've seen it before.
A Tonal Order cutter glides to a halt above the platform. Its command resonator pulses with a threatening, authoritative hum.

lines_after.dialogue: The lead Inquisitor's voice booms via resonance amplifier. 'You have trespassed in forbidden memory. Surrender the illicit harmonics for cleansing.'
Cleansing? You mean destruction. You want to bury the truth again.
The truth is a destabilizing frequency. The Lattice is order. We are its custodians. What came before... is irrelevant.
The Inquisitor's ship begins charging a silencing pulse—the same harmonic profile glimpsed in the memory of the ancient weapon.

line.dialogue: The Order is about to fire. We have one chance, using the unstable, raw memory-frequency we recovered. How do we resonate?

choices.text: Defensive Harmony: Use the frequency to create a shield around the platform.
choices.consequence: You weather the blast. The platform is saved, but the evidence is shattered. The Order withdraws, claiming a 'containment exercise.' The truth remains hidden, but you live.
choices.description: Calibrate the resonance shields using the monk's stolen frequency logs before the Orders triangulate our position.

line.dialogue: Shields calibrated — I'm reading harmonic drift at seven hertz, but we'll hold. We move now.
The logs are encoded. I'm reading nothing — static. They'll find us before I crack this.

choices.text: Counter-Melody: Match and invert the silencing pulse, turning their weapon back on their ship.
choices.consequence: You cripple the cutter. The Inquisitor is humiliated and retreats. The Groundless Movement gains a powerful symbol of resistance, but the Order now marks you as enemies.
choices.description: Convince Malee to lever her financial contacts into buying us safe passage through the Lower Ring transit corridors.

line.dialogue: Fine. I'll call in what I'm owed. But when this is over, we talk about what loyalty actually costs.
My contacts hung up the moment I mentioned the Orders. Money talks, but fear talks louder. We're on our own.

choices.text: Broadcast the Truth: Amplify the memory-echo and transmit it on all common frequencies to every nearby city.
choices.consequence: For a moment, the sky above the Lattice shimmers with the ghost of the lost world. Panic and wonder ripple through the floating cities. You break the monopoly on history, but you also break the peace. The world will never be the same.
choices.description: Force the monk to broadcast a false signal on the forbidden frequency, drawing the Orders' monitors away from our real location.

line.dialogue: The monk did it — I can see their patrol vectors shifting east. It's working. Go, go, go.
They didn't take the bait. The Orders know our frequency signature — that was our only decoy and we just burned it.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery hangs in the sky, a fortress of silence and song. Its great acoustic chambers are shaped to capture every vibration from the Lattice below.
There's a stillness here... but it's heavy. Not empty. It's something to think about.
Stay close. The Listeners value their privacy. We don't know what frequencies they're studying.
Privacy, or secrets? A guild that knows how to navigate the Lattice holds all the power. I'm just surprised they haven't charged us a toll for the air yet.
Look at those crystal arrays! Can you hear that? A low hum, almost like... breathing.
A robed Listener Monk approaches, his steps measured to avoid unnecessary sound.
Welcome. You are early. The resonance readings from the southern lattice quadrant have been... unstable. What do you think about anomalous harmonics?
Anomalies suggest a truth the standard charts ignore.

lines_after.dialogue: A dangerous truth. The Tonal Orders' charts are law. To suggest otherwise is to invite the Silencing anew. Yet... our own observations...
The monk hesitates, his eyes darting to a heavy, locked door at the chamber's rear.
Follow. There is something you should hear. But quietly.

line.dialogue: The monk leads you to a secluded observation balcony overlooking a deep crystal canyon. A strange, pulsing dissonance rises from below.

choices.text: Focus on the pure tone. Try to isolate and identify the base frequency.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using singer voice to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The lattice has other plans. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Listen for the emotional texture. Is the sound angry, sorrowful, or something else?
choices.description: Pichit attempts to decipher the monk's recording, relying on resonant staff

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit overreaches. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Check your resonance ship's logs. Compare this to any previous anomalous readings.
choices.description: The monk takes the lead, employing crystal bowls to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the monk. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Defeat. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The dissonance from the canyon resolves into a jarring, repeating pattern. Suddenly, a grapple hook clatters onto the balcony rail.
Well, look what the lattice coughed up! A bunch of choir kids and a monk. Stay put, this is a raid.
Sky pirates! Here? The monastery's defensive harmonics should have shredded your ship!
Old frequencies. We got new ones. Stole 'em from a Singer's corpse. This place is a treasure trove of forbidden charts. He's the only son in the family.
The only son? What are you talking about?
He's delirious. Or he's comparing this monastery to some cheap drama. You have to see it! A really good movie about a lone heir protecting his inheritance, I bet.
Quiet! You, monk. Open the vault. The one with the real resonance maps. Not the pretty ones you show the Orders.
You're using stolen Singer frequencies? That's like navigating by a dying scream.

lines_after.dialogue: I... I cannot. The vault contains not just maps, but... recordings. From before The Silencing.
Even better! The ultimate banned film. This movie is great! The truth about what really happened. Now open it, or we start breaking your fancy crystal legs.

The pirate leader kicks a nearby resonator, sending a painful shriek through the chamber. Monk Charik's eyes flick to his own leg, which gives a faint, sympathetic crystalline chime—a resonant prosthetic.

line.dialogue: The pirate threatens the monk's crystal leg—the subplot's focus—and the ancient vault. The dissonant hum from the canyon grows louder, agitated by the pirate's violent frequency.

choices.text: Create a sonic distraction. Have Chanida shatter a small resonator to overload the pirates' hearing.
choices.description: Jam the pirate's stolen frequency with the monastery's bell harmonic, 12 words

line.dialogue: The bell tower answers — your stolen signal just became white noise, you thieves.
The harmonic collapsed — they've already patched past our frequency, the monastery is defenseless.

choices.text: Appeal to the pirate's greed. Offer a deal: a copy of one forbidden chart for safe passage.
choices.description: Grab Chanida and sprint for the shadow archive beneath the prayer hall, 13 words

line.dialogue: I know these tunnels better than any sky-borne rat — follow me, now.
The archive door is sealed with a hymn I can't remember — we're trapped here.

choices.text: Harmonize with the monk's prosthetic. Use its unique resonance to cancel out the pirate's stolen Singer frequency, disabling their gear.
choices.description: Demand the bandit explain what "the only son" means before anyone moves, 12 words

line.dialogue: The Sing's child — the one your monks hid in plain sight. That's her.
You don't even know what you're guarding? Pathetic. Take them anyway, boys.

lines_before.dialogue: Back within the monastery's inner sanctum, the party gathers around a massive resonance crystal, its surface shimmering with latent energy.
The Sky Pirate's crude resonator... it revealed a hidden frequency. It's a lot more fun to study than our sanctioned charts, but it's dangerous knowledge.
Dangerous? It's power! They have a lot of stuff locked away in their vaults, and we've just found a key!
He complains a lot! The monk is torn between his duty and the truth, but the Tonal Orders would skin him for even whispering about this.
We must proceed with extreme caution. Unregulated frequencies could destabilize the Lattice around the entire monastery.
Yet, this frequency... it feels like a missing verse in the world's song. To ignore it would be to deny a part of the Resonance itself.
You speak like a Singer. But to test it... we would need to align the monastery's primary crystal array. It would create a... a beacon.
Outside, the distant hum of a Resonance Ship grows louder. The Sky Pirate's crew is returning, drawn by the same hidden frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The crystal array begins to glow, its light pulsing in a new, unfamiliar rhythm.
Across the monastery, lesser crystals resonate in sympathy, their song changing. The very air vibrates with a strange, potent energy.
High above, the Resonance Ship alters its course, descending towards the sanctum with clear, aggressive intent.

line.dialogue: The hidden frequency is ready. We can use it to empower Arthit's resonant prosthetic, defend the monastery, or attempt to communicate with the Lattice itself.

choices.text: Channel the frequency into Arthit's crystal leg. It might grant him temporary, overwhelming mobility.
choices.description: Arthit channels captain experience toward the ancient texts, hoping to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Tune the monastery's defenses to the new frequency. Create a sonic barrier against the approaching ship.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using staff meditation to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
A costly mistake by Pichit. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Attempt to 'sing' the frequency directly into the Lattice, seeking a deeper understanding or response.
choices.description: Direct the monk to decode the tonal pattern using lattice study

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the monk's call. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the monk misreads the situation. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The Sky Pirate's ship crashes through the sanctum's crystalline roof, its resonator shrieking the same stolen frequency. Pirates swarm the chamber.
You called it! You broadcast the treasure map right to us! How do you write a thank-you note for that? This frequency... it's the latest fashion in piracy!
What province is 'stupidity' in? Because we're living in it right now.
They want the crystal array! They'll strip this place bare and sell every shard!
The prosthetic... it's resonating uncontrollably. The feedback is threatening to shatter the primary crystal!
The Lattice... it's reacting. The song is becoming a scream. If the crystal shatters, the harmonic collapse could swallow Phrao Monastery!
This is the climax. The hidden frequency was a key, but we opened a door to chaos. Now we must choose the final chord.
The primary crystal, overcharged with conflicting resonances, begins to crack. Light bleeds from its fractures. The Lattice below the floating city groans.

lines_after.dialogue: The consequences of the choice ripple out. The Sky Pirates react—with fury, fear, or sudden understanding.
The Lattice's response is immediate and profound, altering the very substance of the world beneath the monastery.
Phrao Monastery is forever changed. Its song, and its role in the world, has been rewritten by this final, resonant act.

line.dialogue: The crystal is fracturing. The pirates are attacking. The Lattice is screaming. We must play the final note.

choices.text: Shatter the crystal deliberately. Cause a controlled collapse to drive off the pirates, but sacrifice the monastery's research.
choices.description: Reroute the crystal array's energy into the monastery walls, sealing every door shut, 15 words

line.dialogue: I'm channeling everything into the foundation — nothing short of a siege cannon is getting through those doors now.
The array overloaded — I've sealed us IN with them instead of keeping them out. God, I'm stupid.

choices.text: Use Arthit's prosthetic as a focus. Try to absorb and dampen the frequency, stabilizing the crystal but risking his life.
choices.description: Let the prosthetic resonate fully and follow its signal to whatever it's tracking beneath the monastery, 15 words

line.dialogue: I stopped fighting it — the frequency is leading me straight down to something buried under the sanctum. I can feel it.
The resonance spiked past what my nervous system can take — I'm on my knees, the prosthetic is screaming and I can't silence it.

choices.text: Sing. Pichit must attempt to harmonize the conflicting frequencies into a new, stable song, requiring perfect resonance.
choices.description: Grab the broadcast equipment and transmit a fake second map pointing bandits toward the ravine, 15 words

line.dialogue: I just sent every greedy bastard in broadcasting range coordinates to a dead-end ravine — they'll be digging for hours.
the monk misreads the situation. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow tastes of damp stone and ozone. The walls, veined with dormant crystal, hum faintly as the party's footsteps send ripples of sound through the cavern.
Whoa. Listen to that echo! It's like the cave is talking back.
Keep your voices low. Unusual acoustics can mask other sounds. Like predators. Or structural instability.
Or the delightful sound of our funding running out. We're looking for pre-Silencing tech, not a choir rehearsal.
Every sound here has weight, a history. The Lattice above may be controlled, but these echoes... they are raw memory.
You lot are making enough noise to wake the whole Silencing. You heard that, didn't you? The way your steps ring wrong past that bend.
A local! Hey, we're explorers! We mean no harm.
Explorers. Tonal Order lackeys, more like. Surface-dwellers poking where they shouldn't.

lines_after.dialogue: We seek only understanding. May I have some time? To explain?
...Fine. Talk. But make it quick. The cave's mood shifts. She's in a good mood now, but that won't last.
Charming. A cave with mood swings.
You learn to listen, or you don't learn at all. I'm in a good mood. I'll point you to the old resonance chamber. But you didn't get it from me.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points down a narrow, phosphorescent tunnel. 'The chamber's that way. But it's not empty. Your thanks means a tool. What do you offer for the guidance?'

choices.line: Offer a spare resonator crystal. (Lose a minor resource, ensure safe passage.)
choices.description: Strike the cave wall with my torch handle and count the seconds before the echo dies.

line.dialogue: Seven full seconds — the Lattice is drinking every vibration, transcribing us into its memory.
That bang just announced our position to whatever lives in the dark ahead. Brilliant.

choices.line: Promise a share of any non-technological finds. (Gain a temporary ally, but owe a future debt.)
choices.description: Press my palm flat against the glowing Lattice surface and whisper a word of thanks.

line.dialogue: It's warm! The whole vein pulsed back at you — like it *heard* you, like it's grateful!
Your handprint is now etched into a thousand-year-old artifact. I hope gratitude covers the restoration fine.

choices.line: Simply express profound philosophical thanks. (Rely on Pichit's earnestness; success depends on the Scavenger's whims.)
choices.description: Signal the team to go completely silent for thirty seconds and listen to what the cave says on its own.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the echo. Breathing. Slow, rhythmic. Something is asleep in these walls.
The silence broke something. The echoes have stopped entirely now. I don't think we're welcome anymore.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance chamber is a vast, spherical cavern. Shattered crystal arrays litter the floor, and in the center, a massive, dormant monolith pulses with a slow, deep light.
Incredible preservation. This technology predates the Silencing. The harmonic alignment is... unsettlingly perfect.
Look! Carvings! Stories! This is it!
Stories don't pay the bills. But that central node might. What kind do you like? Intact and valuable, or smashed and useless?
The carvings... they're not just history. They're a pattern. A warning. The Listeners' texts hinted at this. The Lattice didn't just break; it was *answered*.
A sharp, discordant hum slices the air. From a shadowed upper ledge, figures clad in mismatched leather and crystal shards drop down, blocking the entrance.
Well, well. Surface-rats found the shiny. We'll be taking that. And your ship. Anywhere you like for you to die, really.
Sky pirates! Why are you doing this to me? We just got here!

lines_after.dialogue: Doing this *to* you? We're doing this *for* us! This frequency hub is worth more than your floating rathole. Now, what style do you prefer? Hands up, or full of holes?
The monolith's resonance is building. Their intrusion is destabilizing it!
Great. So we get crushed by ancient echoes *and* shot. My preferred outcome is neither.
The pattern... it's reacting to their aggressive frequency. It's not a power source. It's a receiver. And it's opening.

line.dialogue: The central monolith's light grows erratic, casting jagged shadows. The pirates are advancing, weapons crackling. The ancient device is awakening to the conflict.

choices.line: Fight the pirates directly. (A straightforward skirmish, but risks damaging the chamber further.)
choices.description: Trace the carved pattern with your fingertip, following the lines toward the central node.

line.dialogue: Yes—yes! The pattern is a circuit map. Touch here and the whole system should recognize you.
No, you're breaking the sequence! The pattern runs counterclockwise—now it's rejecting us.

choices.line: Use the chamber's acoustics. Shout a specific frequency to disrupt the pirates' gear and confuse them. (Requires quick thinking and knowledge.)
choices.description: Ignore the carvings entirely and force open the central node's housing panel with your multitool.

line.dialogue: Finally, someone with priorities. This power core alone could fund the whole expedition.
Dead. Completely dead. You've fried the one thing in this ruin worth selling.

choices.line: Attempt to harmonize with the monolith. Try to 'sing' it calm before its resonance feedback loops out of control. (High risk, high reward; taps into the subplot.)
choices.description: Photograph the carvings layer by layer, building a complete record before touching anything.

line.dialogue: Smart. Whatever happens next, we've preserved the knowledge. This predates everything we know.
The flash—something's reacting. The walls are dimming. You've triggered a decay cycle.

lines_before.dialogue: The cavern opens into a vast, vaulted chamber. Ancient machinery, smooth and geometric, lies dormant in the gloom. A low, resonant hum fills the air, making the crystals in the walls vibrate softly.
Pre-Silencing tech. Intact. Do you realize the *chance* we're standing on? This could buy a fleet of Resonance Ships.
And attract every sky pirate and Tonal Order enforcer from here to the skyline. There’s a high chance this place is a tomb for a reason.
Forget selling it! Look at these patterns on the console. (She runs a hand over the dust-covered surface.) It's... musical notation. This inviting, this mysterious... how could you pass it up?
The hum... it's not random. It's a sustained note. A question waiting for an answer.
You shouldn't be here. The deep stone sings warnings. My people have tales. This place... listens back.

line.dialogue: A central dais holds a single, flawless crystal resonator, unlike any you've seen. It seems to be the source of the chamber's hum.

choices.text: Have Chanida attempt to match the hum with her voice.
choices.outcome_line: Chanida's clear tone harmonizes. The ancient machinery lights up softly, revealing a holographic star map.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use ship navigation and harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Things don't go as planned. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze the resonator's frequency with his tools.
choices.outcome_line: Arthit's careful calibration causes the hum to shift, unlocking a hidden panel in the dais with strange artifacts.
choices.description: Have Chanida focus unauthorized tones on the unusual acoustics to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
The lattice has other plans. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Have Pichit place his hand on the crystal and listen for intent.
choices.outcome_line: A psychic echo floods Pichit's mind—a vision of The Silencing, not as an accident, but as a desperate act of containment.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform juts out from the floating city's underbelly, a metal jawbone clenched against the Lattice's radiant expanse below. The crystalline surface shifts through hues of deep violet and emerald, humming a low, complex chord that vibrates through the soles of your boots.
Look at those patterns! It's like the whole world is breathing. I've never been this close. Makes you want to... I don't know, jump down and touch it.

Relax, Arthit. She's not that stupid. Usually. Though, what size do you wear? For the funeral shroud, I mean. Planning ahead.

Well, ain't this a cozy little vista. Payin' respects to the big shiny floor? Hand over your frequency charts. Nice and easy.

Orders are busy lining their pockets uptown. Me? I'm just a humble freelancer. And my girlfriend gets jealous if I come back empty-handed. So don't make me disappoint her.

Peace. Please. The Lattice is agitated. Your conflict sends discordant waves through the Song.

You're a Listener. You hear it too. The memory in the crystal.

The monk's eyes fall on Arthit, specifically on the subtle, crystalline shimmer of his prosthetic leg where it meets the knee.
Your limb... it resonates. A crude integration, but it sings with the Lattice's base frequency. You must feel it.
It aches. When the harmonics shift. I was told it was phantom pain.

lines_after.dialogue: It is no phantom. It is a poorly tuned instrument crying out. The man who made this for you... better if you don't go back to him. The alignment is dangerously off.
He's the only one in the city who works with Lattice-crystal prosthetics.
We have to do something! Arthit, that thing could be poisoning you!
Or it could just hurt. Let's not jump to apocalyptic conclusions. But... you can put your hand down now, monk. We're not attacking.
The monk slowly lowers his hands. Below, the Lattice's light pulses erratically around a nearby outcropping, revealing the half-buried wreck of a small Resonance ship.

line.dialogue: The monk hints at deeper truths and Arthit's prosthetic is a ticking crystal bomb. The wreck below might have answers.

Alright, listen up! We know you've got the monk and you're sniffing around frequencies the Orders don't like. Hand over the old man and any charts, and maybe we don't turn you into pretty crystal statues.

Please... translate that for me. The Lattice's song... it's changed since they arrived. A new fracture pattern is spreading from their landing site. Is it real, or just my fear?
It's real. The harmonics are tearing at the edges of this platform's stabilizer field. We're on borrowed time.
Enough chatter! What about tomorrow? You gonna be here to see it? Decide!

The prosthetic... it's humming. It's picking up a frequency from the new fracture. A navigation signature.

lines_before.dialogue: The conflict has triggered a deep resonance cascade. A narrow chasm splits the platform, glowing with dangerous, raw sound. The pirate ship teeters on the edge. The monk stares into the abyss, hearing a song no one should.
The Song... the true one beneath the Silencing... I can hear it in the crack. It's... beautiful. And it will unmake this place if it fully surfaces.
Forget them! The ship! The stabilizer's gone! You, too! If you've got any bright ideas, now's the time!

It's... it's like a current. Pulling me toward the crack. The crystal remembers. It used to be part of a sickly child... a fragmented world. This leg remembers the Silencing.

The gamble fails. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship groans, its crystalline resonator emitting a discordant shriek. The Lattice below churns, forming jagged, unnatural peaks.
Pressure readings are spiking. This isn't a natural formation. There's a high chance we're navigating a sabotage field.
Look! Off the starboard bow! Another ship, and it's... not moving right. Its resonator is dark.
A derelict. (This cute and this inviting) a floating pile of salvage and probable corpses... how could you pass it up?
Its silence is a wound in the song of this place. We should investigate. It may be connected to the Negotiator's 'safe' route.
Ah, my friends! A minor detour, I assure you. A competitor... fell behind schedule. Their cargo, now adrift, represents a tragic loss of profit. For everyone.
You knew this was here. You led us right to it.
The merchant's smile doesn't reach his eyes. From the derelict's hull, a faint, pained hum echoes—the frequency of a failing Resonant Prosthetic.

lines_after.dialogue: You secure the line. The derelict ship looms, a silent tomb against the groaning Lattice.
I'm not finished yet! If that merchant double-crosses us and sails off, we're stranded on a sinking crystal.
Agreed. Chanida, watch our ship. If he even looks at the helm, you have my permission to be... impulsive.

line.dialogue: How do we board the derelict?

choices.line: Use the ship's grappler. Fast and loud.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to tune the prosthetic, relying on captain experience

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit misreads the situation. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.line: Have Pichit hum a stabilizing tone to calm the rattling lattice between the ships.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to confront hidden knowledge, leveraging crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Defeat. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: Leap across the gap, trusting the unstable Lattice formations to provide momentary footing.
choices.description: Ask the villager to map the frequency corridors, drawing on village secrets

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the villager pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The resonance turns hostile. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the derelict, the air is stale. Scattered ledgers reveal the Trade Negotiator sold faulty crystal cores, dooming this ship. At the helm, a Skycity Resident clings to life, his crystal leg flickering erratically.
You're home so late! ...No. Forgive me. The pain... makes me see my daughter. He said the core was stable. The merchant.
His profit was built on your suffering. The song of your pain is all through this metal.
The core's failure is cascading. It'll destabilize our ship next. We need to jettison their resonator, now.
Please... my leg. The crystal is grafted to the ship's systems. You cut it free, you kill me.
If we don't, the feedback pulse will shred our own resonator. We'll all be lost.
There has to be another way! We can't just...!
A deafening crack echoes from below. The Lattice rises in a violent spike, shearing the derelict's hull. The ship begins to list, groaning towards the abyss.

lines_after.dialogue: The silence that follows is heavier than any sound. The party stands on the deck of their own ship, the decision etched into them.
I'm sorry I'm late. Sorry we could not hear your song sooner.
The merchant's ship is gone. He fled the moment the lattice moved. We have the ledgers. Proof.
Proof doesn't sing. It just sits there, quiet. Like us.

line.dialogue: The dying man is fused to the failing ship. The crisis is now.

choices.line: Sever the connection. Save the many. One life for the crew and your mission.
choices.description: Pry the crystal from the villager's leg using your field knife, 15 words

line.dialogue: Hold still — this will burn like nothing you've felt, but you'll live free of it.
The crystal splinters under the blade — shards bury into living flesh. I've made it worse.

choices.line: Attempt a risky transfer. Try to move the man and his prosthetic to your ship, risking both vessels.
choices.description: Override the cascade by rerouting core power through the ship's damaged secondary conduits

line.dialogue: Conduits holding — barely. You just bought us maybe twenty minutes before this fails again.
The reroute overloaded every junction I had left. We're on backup power and the clock is shorter now.

choices.line: Sing to the lattice. Have Pichit try to calm the rising crystalline spike itself, a desperate act with unknown resonance.
choices.description: Demand Pichit reveal who profited from grafting villagers to the ship's crystal lattice

line.dialogue: Wanich. He called it 'symbiotic integration.' I called it what it was — slavery dressed in engineering terms.
You want names while people are dying at your feet? Your priorities reveal exactly who you serve.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch before you, a symphony of terraced green against the endless crystalline white of the Lattice below. The air smells of damp earth and ripening grain.
A gentle wind moves through the stalks, creating a soft, rhythmic susurrus. Water channels gurgle peacefully between plots.
Finally! Somewhere that isn't trying to kill us. I could listen to this all day.
Don't get used to it. Peace is just the quiet before someone shows up to ruin it.
We should still be cautious. These terraces are on the very edge of the skycity. The drop is... considerable.
The sound... it's different here. Not just the wind. There's a lower hum beneath it. The Lattice is singing something faint.
You folks look lost. Not from around the gardens, are you?
We're travelers. Just seeking a moment's rest.

lines_after.dialogue: Rest, eh? Well, you picked a good spot. Quiet. Safe. Most of the time.
Though old Tam across the way... he's been acting strange. Says he hears a new song in the irrigation pipes. I have bad eyesight, but my ears work fine. I don't hear it.
He's been tinkering down in his shed for weeks. Won't let anyone help. 'I made everything by myself,' he says. Even that... thing.

line.dialogue: The villager nods toward a small, isolated toolshed at the garden's furthest edge, half-hidden by flowering vines.

choices.text: Approach the shed directly. The second option is to just ask Tam what he's working on.
choices.description: Press your ear against the stone terrace wall and track where the whispering grows loudest.

line.dialogue: There—beneath the third terrace. Something is breathing through the cracks.
All I hear is my own heartbeat. Whatever it was, it's gone quiet now.

choices.text: Circle around the gardens first. Get a feel for the layout and the strange hum Pichit noticed.
choices.description: Signal the group to split into pairs and sweep both ends of the terraces simultaneously.

line.dialogue: Coordinated search. If anything's nesting here, we'll flush it out from both sides.
Split up? In unfamiliar territory? That's not strategy, that's a body count waiting to happen.

choices.text: Ask the villager more about Tam and this 'thing' he built.
choices.description: Scatter handfuls of dried rice from your pack across the terrace floor and watch for displacement.

line.dialogue: Clever. The grains are shifting east—whatever's moving down there pushes air ahead of it.
The wind took every grain. We've wasted food for nothing but a lesson in futility.

lines_before.dialogue: The shed is a ramshackle construction of salvaged wood and metal. From within, a faint, discordant chiming can be heard, out of sync with the garden's natural rhythms.
As you get closer, you see the door is ajar. Inside, an elderly man with a pronounced limp is bent over a workbench, fiddling with a complex device of crystal and brass attached to his leg.
Well, there's your 'thing'. A fancy peg leg. They sell the new resonator cores at the lower market, but I've never seen one integrated like that.
That crystal... it's raw Lattice shard. Unstabilized. It shouldn't be resonating without a ship's housing.
But it is. And it's listening. It's tuned to the hum we heard.
Hey! Old Tam, is it? What's the music for?
Step away from the shed. Now.

lines_after.dialogue: A weathered woman steps from behind a water cistern, a hand on the knife at her belt. Her clothes are patched and sturdy, dusted with fine crystal powder.
Tam's project isn't for gawkers. That crystal is fragile. You lot stomping around... you'll shatter the harmonics. Turn off your own resonators to conserve energy in the area.
He's not some sideshow. He's trying to walk again. Properly. And I have to take my kids to school on the other side of the city once this is done, so I don't have time for delays.
Mila, it's alright. They heard the song too... didn't you?

line.dialogue: Tam looks up, his eyes bright. The prosthetic on his leg glows with a soft, internal light, pulsing in time with the distant hum.

choices.text: Comply. Power down any active resonator tech to show you mean no harm.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the crystal and let the hum travel up your arm.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "I feel it too — like a second pulse syncing with mine. It's not dangerous, it's... calling.
Arthit — "Pull back! The shard bit me — cold, like swallowing a lightning bolt. My fingers won't stop shaking.

choices.text: Stand your ground. Question Mila's right to order you around in a public garden.
choices.description: Grab Old Tam by the collar and demand to know who built this peg leg and why.

line.dialogue: Malee — "He's talking — says a Weaver named Krasae brought it here forty years ago, said it was a leg 'for walking between songs.
Malee — "Nothing. He just hums louder and won't look at us. Whatever secret he's keeping, he's taking it to the dirt.

choices.text: Focus on Tam. Ask him about the song his leg is hearing and what it means.
choices.description: Hum the melody you heard outside the shed and see if the crystal responds.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "It's glowing brighter — the shard knows that tune. That's no random hum, that's a Lattice key, and we just unlocked it.
Pichit — "Wrong note. The crystal went dark and the hum stopped completely. Whatever it was listening for, we just scared it off.

lines_before.dialogue: The party returns to the Hanging Gardens, the serene atmosphere now charged with unease. The evening wind carries not just the scent of crops, but a faint, discordant hum from deep below the terraces.
Okay, so the scavenger says the 'ground' here isn't ground. It's the Lattice. And it's... singing wrong? I don't understand anything!
The data from the prosthetic's resonance log is clear. There's a massive, unstable harmonic node directly under the primary irrigation cistern. If it destabilizes...
The whole terrace slides into the crystal soup. Lovely. You still don't understand? The Tonal Orders probably seeded this place, and now their little experiment is going sour.
A city built upon a fault line of sound. The residents cultivate life above, unaware of the dissonance growing below. We must make them understand.

You're back? Look, we appreciate the warning, but the cistern's been fine for generations. My great-grandfather dug the channels. We don't know when things might go bad, but worrying won't fill the grain silos.
Told you. City-folk. They hear the wind in the wheat and think that's the only song. They never listen to the bedrock. I don't know when it'll crack, but my bones say soon.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The party splits to prepare, the pastoral calm of the gardens now a tense staging ground.
I'll recalibrate the prosthetic's resonator. If we can use it as a harmonic dampener, we might buy time.
Just don't make it explode. Again.

line.dialogue: How do we convince the villagers to evacuate the lower terraces?

choices.text: Demonstrate the Danger: Use the prosthetic to create a visible, controlled fracture in a fallow field, proving the threat.
choices.description: Use the prosthetic's resonance frequency to counter the destabilizing hum beneath the terrace

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
The resonance turns hostile. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Appeal to Pragmatism: Frame it as temporary, necessary maintenance to protect their 'investment' in the land.
choices.description: Order an immediate evacuation of the terrace before the next resonance pulse hits

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The forbidden text confirms the warning.

choices.text: Invoke the Listeners: Claim you've decoded an ancient warning from the Lattice itself, speaking through the gardens' oldest stones.

lines_before.dialogue: Night falls. The predicted harmonic surge begins. The Lattice beneath the gardens glows with a sickly violet light, and the earth trembles. Water channels run dry, then reverse.
The cistern! It's cracking! My kids are in the lower dormitory! I have a class to teach them in the morning, I can't...!
Arthit, the dampener! Chanida, Malee—help get everyone to the high path. We are not waiting for the end.
The prosthetic is holding, but the feedback is overwhelming the crystal! I'm going to hurry off to the epicenter to manually stabilize the frequency!
Arthit, no! That's suicide!
He's right. The core resonance is at the cistern. Her mom already told me about the old access hatch. It's a straight drop into the harmonic node.
I've seen this before. The song eats itself. Then it eats everything else. You got one shot to change the tune.
A deep groan splits the air. A section of the lower terrace shears away, dissolving into shimmering crystal dust. The violet light pulses like a dying heart.

lines_after.dialogue: In the aftermath, dawn breaks over a scarred but standing Mae Rim. The choice made here will echo through the party's journey.
We stood at the edge of the Silencing and chose a different note. The cost is written in the broken earth, and in our friend's eyes.
We saved them. Most of them. That has to mean something.

line.dialogue: Arthit is at the node, ready to sacrifice the prosthetic—and himself—to overload and collapse the harmonic surge. What is your final command?

choices.text: Save Arthit: Order a retreat. Use the party's combined resonance to shield the upper terraces, sacrificing the lower gardens and the prosthetic to save your friend.
choices.description: Reroute the dampener's overflow into the cistern's fracture line, sealing it with resonant feedback, 15 words

line.dialogue: The prosthetic screams, but the crack fuses—everyone, *move now*, the seal won't hold twice!
The feedback loop reversed—I've turned the fracture into a fault line. Forgive me.

choices.text: The Calculated Risk: Trust Arthit's plan. Let him attempt the overload, using the party to create a harmonic counterpoint from the surface to give him a chance to escape.
choices.description: Detach the prosthetic entirely and wedge it as a structural brace across the collapsing cistern doorway, 15 words

line.dialogue: Arthit, you madman—you bought us four minutes. Chanida, get those children *out*!
The wall took his arm and the doorway together. He's pinned. Someone help him—he's *drowning*!

choices.text: The Singer's Gambit: Pichit must go down alone. Using his innate ability, he will try to *re-write* the unstable node's frequency, saving everything—but risking being absorbed by the Lattice forever.
choices.description: Order Malee to sing the counter-frequency while you shield the children with your body in the doorway, 15 words

line.dialogue: The resonance steadied—the water's stopping—Pichit, I can hold it, just get them through!
I hit the wrong note. The water *listened* to the mistake. I'm sorry, I'm so sorry—

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Sky-Scribe' cuts through the high-altitude winds, its crystal resonators humming a steady, complex chord that parts the shimmering Lattice below like water. The deck vibrates gently underfoot.
Look at it all! It's like the world is singing just for us. This is incredible!
It's a geological formation responding to sound frequencies, Chanida. Not a concert. Though, I'll admit, the chromatic refraction is aesthetically pleasing.
We should keep our voices down. The harmonics are delicate. The Tonal Orders' charts only account for standard engine tones, not... exuberant conversation.

But what if the charts are incomplete? The Lattice is a record. Every fracture, every shimmer... it's the only son in the family of history, the sole survivor of The Silencing. We're just skimming its surface.
You have to see it Pichit's way! The Listeners study the natural sounds, right? Maybe we're missing the best part by just following the guild's maps!
A figure in simple, grey robes approaches from the starboard side. Listener Monk Kaelen's face is etched with deep contemplation.

Your companion speaks a sliver of truth. The sanctioned frequencies are... safe. Predictable. But the true song of the Lattice is far more complex. It is a really good symphony, if one has the ears to hear.

lines_after.dialogue: A 'really good symphony' that shattered civilization. Forgive me if I don't ask for an encore.

The Silencing was not the song's fault. It was a... misinterpretation. A note held too long, too loud. My order believes the Lattice is now trying to communicate something new. A warning, woven into the quieter harmonics.
A warning? About what? This sounds like speculation beyond our voyage parameters.

line.dialogue: The Monk's words hang in the air. Pichit feels the pull of the unknown song.

choices.line: Ask the Monk to elaborate on the 'warning.' (Gather information)
choices.description: Touch the nearest crystal column and hum a single sustained note into its surface.

* "Your pitch wavered and now the whole corridor is shrieking — pull your hand back before it splinters!

choices.line: Suggest a brief, cautious deviation to listen for these 'quieter harmonics.' (Take a small risk)
choices.description: Consult Pichit's star-charts and cross-reference the resonance pattern with the Lattice's northern axis.

line.dialogue: * "You found it — the tertiary harmonic matches the charts perfectly, we're standing on a convergence point.
* "Those coordinates are inverted — you just aligned us with a dead resonance channel. The charts were incomplete after all.

choices.line: Defer to Arthit's caution and stick strictly to the charted course. (Play it safe)
choices.description: Signal

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the monk. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the monk overreaches. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: The discussion is shattered by a sudden, violent shudder through the ship. The engine's hum stutters into a discordant whine. From a bank of crystal mist, a smaller, jagged vessel emerges, its resonator spikes glowing a threatening crimson.
Hail the pretty sky-skiff! You still don't understand how these lanes work? This is a toll road! Power down your main crystal, or we'll close your door loudly. Permanently.
Pirates! I have a class on dealing with scavengers like you!
Your bravado is noted. Their ship, however, is using a destabilizing frequency. It's interfering with our navigation lattice. This is more sophisticated than common banditry.
They know a forbidden harmonic. One that jams sanctioned resonators. We can't outrun them in this state.
The Monk spoke of hidden songs... and warnings. Is this part of it? Chaos emerging from the silence?
This is a corruption. A scream, not a song. They use knowledge ripped from the Lattice's pain points. But... every frequency has a counter-frequency.
Enough chatter! Your cargo or your lives! My boss has a class to teach you about respecting the deep frequencies!

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate ship looms closer, its jagged hull scraping against the Sky-Scribe's defensive energy field with a teeth-rattling screech.
The field won't hold. We need a solution, not philosophy.
The counter-frequency... I have studied it in theory. It is a quiet, restorative sequence. But to generate it, we would need to temporarily override the engine's core protocol. It is risky.
Overriding the core could leave us dead in the sky, a sitting target!

line.dialogue: The pirate ship prepares to board. The Monk's theoretical knowledge and the ship's integrity hang in the balance.

choices.line: Order a full power redistribution to shields, buying time to negotiate. (Defensive Stance)
choices.description: Signal chanida to negotiate while you scan their harmonic array for weaknesses, 15 words

line.dialogue: I flash my accredited salvager's credentials and offer them exactly what they want—passage, not plunder.
I cite the wrong regulatory code and they laugh so hard they nearly tip their skiff.

choices.line: Instruct Malee to help the Monk recalibrate the resonator to attempt the counter-frequency. (Technical Gambit)
choices.description: Have arthit mirror their forbidden harmonic back to overload their jamming array, 15 words

line.dialogue: I invert their resonance signature and feed it straight back—their array screams and goes dark.
I hit the wrong interval and our own helm starts shrieking like a dying oscillator.

choices.line: Have Chanida draw their fire with evasive maneuvers while Pichit and the Monk attempt the recalibration. (Split Focus)
choices.description: Bank the sky-skiff hard into the cloud layer and lose them in the mist, 15 words

line.dialogue: the pirate's expertise pays off. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The lattice has other plans. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship sails a lonely course. Below, the Lattice hums a low, troubled note. The Listener Monk stands at the rail, his eyes closed, listening to something only he can hear.
He's been like that for an hour. What's he listening to? The 'song of the world'? It might be true, but it's creeping me out.
It comes with a side of ominous dread, Chanida. Standard monastic fare. He's probably hearing how we're all going to die.
We should be focusing on the pirate's charts. Not eavesdropping on a monk's meditation.
Sometimes the most important truths are the ones whispered, not shouted. What if the Lattice is trying to tell us something?
As if summoned by Pichit's words, the Monk's eyes snap open. He looks haunted. He gestures urgently for Pichit to come closer, his voice a hushed murmur.
You... you sense it too. The dissonance. I overheard the ship's resonator... a strain in its core frequency. It mirrors a flaw in the local Lattice. A hidden fracture.
A fracture? What does that mean for us?

lines_after.dialogue: It means the Tonal Charts are wrong here. Deliberately. This course leads to a dead zone. The Orders have silenced this path. I... I was not meant to speak of this.
Great. So the monopoly isn't just greedy, it's homicidal. Why aren't you careful with this kind of information, monk? They'll silence *you*.
A sharp, discordant chime rings out from the ship's bow. A resonance flare bursts on the horizon—a pirate distress signal, coming from the very dead zone the Monk described.

line.dialogue: The pirate's signal is a trap, a warning, or a genuine cry for help. The Monk's revelation changes everything.

choices.text: Alter course immediately. Trust the Monk's warning and avoid the dead zone.

[Malee: "Your nose is bleeding. Step back from the crystal before your brains leak out your ears next."]

line.dialogue: [Arthit: "The crystal's pitch matches a marked dead zone. These aren't haunted waters—they're *mapped* waters. Someone wanted us afraid."]
[Chanida: "You're matching sounds to ink blots. That's not navigation, that's a fever dream with cartography."]

choices.text: Steer straight for the signal. The pirate knows these hidden frequencies; they might be the key to surviving the fracture.
choices.outcome: Risk everything on a desperate gambit.
choices.description: Quiet everyone and drop a pin on the deck to measure the crystal's resonance against the ship's hull, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Pichit: "The crystal pulls toward starboard. Whatever it's hearing, we're drifting away from it. Helmsman—adjust course thirty degrees port."]
[Malee: "The pin rolled into a crack and now we've lost it. That's the most useful thing we've done all hour."]

lines_before.dialogue: The ship groans as it enters the dead zone. The constant hum of the Lattice fades into an eerie silence. Below, the crystal surface is webbed with dark, jagged cracks. The pirate's ship is lodged in a lattice spire, dead in the air.
Took you long enough! My resonator's shot—the fracture ate the frequency! It's irreparable from out here!
This was a trap. The structural instability is catastrophic. One wrong tone and this entire area could shatter.
Look! The cracks are... pulsing. Like a heartbeat. Why weren't you careful, pirate? What did you do?
I was tryin' to listen! Like your monk friend! The fracture... it's got a song. A warning song about the Silencing. The Orders don't want anyone to hear it!
He speaks truth. The song... it's a memory. A recording of the catastrophe. The Lattice remembers the sound that broke the world.
Fantastic. So we're parked over the world's worst mixtape. And if we try to leave, the vibration might set it off.
No. We don't leave. We listen. This is the discovery we've been straining to hear. This is the truth they silenced. Come and take a picture with us, history. We need to remember this.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit steps to the ship's resonator. He doesn't consult a chart. He closes his eyes and begins to hum, matching not a navigation tone, but the low, grieving threnody of the fracture itself.
The crystal around them glows softly. Images flicker in the facets: lost cities, screaming crowds, a single, terrible, overwhelming note. The Song of the Silencing.
You... you are a Singer. A true Singer. You're not parting the Lattice... you're harmonizing with its pain.
The pirate ship shudders free. The fractures begin to seal, not with a crash, but with a sigh of release. The dead zone's silence is replaced by a gentle, healing hum.

line.dialogue: The Lattice's memory is now yours. The truth of the Silencing is a weapon, a burden, and a revelation.

choices.text: Seal the knowledge away. This truth is too dangerous; let the world sleep.
choices.outcome: Protect the present by burying the past. The Monk agrees, but the truth festers.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the pulsing crack and open your senses to its rhythm.

Arthit yanks you back.* "Are you insane? Without a resonator buffer that frequency would shred your cortex in seconds.

choices.text: Share it only with the Listeners. Let the monastic order decide how to wield this memory.
choices.outcome: Create a new secret order within the old. The Monk becomes your ally.
choices.description: Order the bandit to describe exactly what he heard before the resonator failed.

line.dialogue: The bandit wipes blood from his lip.* "It wasn't noise—it was words. Ancient ones. Something about a door that opens *inward*.
The bandit clutches his head, swaying.* "I can't—the more I try to remember, the more it slips away. It's like the fracture doesn't want to be *remembered*.

choices.text: Broadcast the frequency. Let every resonator in every skycity hear the Silencing's song. Break the Order's monopoly on truth.
choices.outcome: Spark a revolution. The world will never be the same.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship 'Wayfarer' hums a low F-sharp, parting the shimmering Lattice beneath you like water. Wind whips across the deck, carrying the scent of ozone and distant rain.
Another day, another sky-city. I swear, if I see one more overpriced Tonal chart, I'm going to scream. And not in a useful, navigational frequency.
Oh, come on! Look at that! The Lattice is singing today! You have to love yourself enough to appreciate this. For the adventurous, this is what it's all about!
Adventurous is one word. Recklessly vibrating through a semi-solid energy field is another. Keep an eye on the resonator readings, Pichit.
The song is... conflicted today. A minor key beneath the standard travel frequency. The Lattice remembers something.
You hear it too. Good. Most only hear the Orders' sanctioned tones. The true song is layered with memory and pain.
A sudden, discordant shriek pierces the engine's hum. A smaller, jagged ship peels from a cloud bank, its hull painted with crude sonic disruptors.
Ahoy the pretty singer! Heard you was carryin' uncut frequency maps. Hand 'em over, and we won't shake your ship apart. Nah, nah, you don't need to try anything heroic.

lines_after.dialogue: Pirates! Now this is an adventure!
Of course. Because our trip wasn't expensive enough already.
Their ship is smaller, but those disruptors could destabilize our resonator core. We need a plan, now.

line.dialogue: The pirate ship closes in, its disruptors whining to life. How do you respond?

choices.effect: Rely on the Wayfarer's superior speed, but risk a prolonged chase.

line.dialogue: [chanida] "See that? The Lattice *wanted* her to listen—it just needed someone bold enough to reach back.
[arthit] "Your hand's blistered and you're shaking—next time, maybe wait for the song to invite you in before grabbing it.

choices.label: Confront them with a show of force (Medium)
choices.effect: Power up defensive harmonics, hoping to intimidate them into breaking off.
choices.description: Follow the minor key's dissonance eastward toward the crumbling spur where the resonance thickens, 15 words

line.dialogue: [pichit] "The sad note grows louder here... something is trapped in the Lattice, and it's trying to speak.
[malee] "Dead end, broken catwalk, and wind that nearly took my eyebrows. The 'sad note' was just a cracked resonator pipe hissing.

choices.label: Try to reason or negotiate (Easy)
choices.effect: Hail them, maybe their greed has limits. Or maybe it doesn't.
choices.description: Signal the dockward attuners to quarantine this section until the Lattice's discordance is fully diagnosed, 15 words

line.dialogue: [arthit] "Finally, someone with sense. Quarantine the resonance, map the dissonance, then proceed. This is how we survive sky-cities.
[chanida]

lines_before.dialogue: Your chosen action leaves the pirate ship damaged but persistent, trailing you like a hungry sky-shark. The Monk has been silently observing the Lattice below.
They will not stop. They are desperate. The prices the Tonal Orders charge for basic resonance charts... they are not reasonable. They bankrupt entire settlements, creating these bandits.
She lost her virginity to market economics, and now we all have to hear about it. Look, you're run down, monk. Tired of your own order's complacency?
We Listen. But what good is listening if we do not act? There is a movement... the Groundless. They believe the sky-cities are a cage. That we must learn to live with the Lattice, not just on it.
A radical faction. Unstable. Their ideas could get people killed.
Yet the Lattice's song holds a longing... for connection. Not domination. The Silencing happened because we tried to control the song, not understand it.
So the pirates are just... really angry customers? And this Groundless lot are what, offering refunds? I'm confused, but I'm still for punching the pirates.
The pirate ship surges forward, its damaged disruptors firing a wild, cacophonous blast. The Wayfarer shudders. A console sparks.
Last chance! The maps, your cargo, and that shiny little resonator crystal! We know a fence who pays fair prices for Order-tech!

lines_after.dialogue: Direct hit to the harmonic dampeners! If they fire again, the feedback could shatter our view-crystals.
Wonderful. Now we get to be shipwrecked and philosophical.
They are a symptom. The true disease is above us, in the spires of the sky-cities, hoarding the song.

line.dialogue: The pirate ship is lining up another shot. The Monk looks at you, awaiting your lead. What is your priority?

choices.label: Focus on immediate defense (Easy)
choices.effect: Direct all power to shields and evasive maneuvers. Survive now, deal with ideals later.
choices.description: Press the monk for names of the radical faction's leaders before deciding anything.

line.dialogue: There are three I know — Prawit, Suda, and a man they call the Engineer. Start with Prawit.
Names? You ask me for names while people are already disappearing? I will not be your informant.

choices.label: Use the Lattice's own song against them (Medium)
choices.effect: Have Pichit and the Monk try to find a disruptive natural frequency. Risky, but could end the fight.
choices.description: Pull Arthit aside and ask what he personally witnessed inside the faction's meetings.

line.dialogue: I sat in three gatherings. The second night, they passed around a list — names of officials marked for 'correction.' I saw my own uncle's name.
You want my testimony? I gave it once already, to people who swore they'd help. They filed it and did nothing. I'm done talking to strangers.

choices.label: Attempt to broadcast the Monk's truth (Hard)
choices.effect: Hijack the comms, broadcasting the Monk's words about the Groundless and the Orders' greed to the pirates. A gamble on reason.
choices.description: Tell Malee directly that her cynicism about market economics is a luxury the desperate cannot afford.

line.dialogue: She stiffens, then nods slowly. "You're right. Mockery is armor I wear so I don't have to feel anything. Armor off, then.
Oh, how brave of you to lecture me. Come back when you've sold your blood to make rent, then tell me about luxury.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship groans, its crystal resonators humming a strained, discordant note. The Lattice below churns, its usual placid shimmer replaced by jagged, angry fractals of light.
The pirate's frequency is tearing the local harmonics apart! We're losing stability!
I'm rerouting auxiliary power, but the core resonator is overheating. We must disengage or find a counter-frequency immediately.
The pirate's laughing. He's broadcasting on an open channel. Sounds like he's the luckiest person in the world! For finding us, he means.
(Voice crackles over comms) You Tonal brats think you own the sky? This hidden freq is mine! I'm really sorry... to be the one who scuttles you!
He's not just attacking. He's... exulting. There's a joy in the chaos. The Groundless preach of freedom from the Lattice's song, but this... this is just noise.
It is a perversion. A scream where there should be silence or song. My Order would say to mute it, to enforce harmony. But the truth... the truth is the Lattice is reacting to him. It listens.

lines_after.dialogue: A new, pure tone cuts through the static. The Listener Monk has approached the main resonator, his hands placed upon it, his eyes closed.
I love it... the true song. Forgive me, brothers. But I must listen.
A resonant hum, deep and stabilizing, pulses from the ship. The chaotic fractals below begin to slow, to realign into softer patterns.

line.dialogue: The Monk's counter-song is holding, but it's a fragile balance. The pirate ship is closing in, weapons charging. We must act.

choices.line: Full Retreat. Use the stabilized harmonics to plot a rapid escape vector back to known charts.
choices.consequence: We save the ship but leave the pirate and this dangerous frequency unchecked. The Tonal Orders will be displeased with our failure.
choices.description: Slam the core resonator into overload, sacrificing stability to overpower his frequency.

line.dialogue: Resonator's screaming but holding — his signal just fragmented into noise!
She's gone — resonator cracked, we're running on dead air now.

choices.line: Harmonic Overload. Channel the Monk's pure tone back at the pirate's resonator, attempting to shatter it.
choices.consequence: A direct confrontation. If it works, we disable them. If it fails, the feedback could cripple our own ship.
choices.description: Open a counter-channel and mock the pirate back, baiting him into revealing his position.

line.dialogue: He's furious — just leaked his bearing on three separate bands, the idiot.
He liked that. Now he's jamming everything and we're blind out here.

choices.line: Board Their Ship. Latch on during the lull and confront the pirate directly to seize his frequency charts.
choices.consequence: Incredibly risky. We face the pirates in their element, but success means gaining their secrets and a decisive victory.
choices.description: Cut all power to the comms array and run silent, letting the harmonic tear pass through undetected.

line.dialogue: He's sweeping empty frequencies — we're ghosts and he knows it.
He heard the core cycling down. He knows exactly where we are.

lines_before.dialogue: The ships are locked together, groaning in a deadly embrace. The air crackles with discharged resonance. On the enemy deck, the Sky Pirate captain stands defiant, a jagged crystal shard in hand.
Think you've won? This shard sings the silence! The true freedom! Your pretty monk's song ends here!

He's going to shatter it. A raw dissonance burst that size could crystallize the Lattice around us... permanently. That's all, isn't it? His grand plan. To make us all 'groundless' in a tomb of solid crystal.
We can't let that happen! Roll up your sleeves, everyone! This ends now!
The structural integrity is failing. We have minutes, perhaps seconds. Any direct attack on the shard might trigger it.
Look at him. He's not a revolutionary. He's just tired. You look run down. The endless chase, the anger... it's exhausted him. This is his final, destructive scream.
He has forgotten how to listen. He hears only his own rage. I'm just surprised... that I once might have called him brother.
The pirate raises the shard high, its internal light pulsing like a diseased heart. The very air seems to stiffen, awaiting the final, silencing note.

lines_after.dialogue: A choice is made. The consequence unfolds. The shard's light either dies, explodes, or is transformed. The two ships shudder, part, and the fate of this sector of the Lattice is sealed.
In the sudden quiet, broken only by the wind and the ship's weary hum, the crew gathers on the deck. The Lattice below reflects their victory, or their failure, in its newly settled form.
The prices are reasonable, for knowledge. For peace. We paid today. We learned the cost of a scream, and the value of a true note.

line.dialogue: The pirate's shard is poised to unleash the Silencing. How do we break his song?

choices.line: Offer a Deal. Promise him safe passage and a audience with the Listeners in exchange for the shard.
choices.consequence: A pragmatic, political solution. It avoids immediate destruction but legitimizes his methods and brings his chaotic ideology into the heart of the Orders.
choices.description: Sprint directly at the bandit and tackle him before he can bring the shard down.

line.dialogue: Malee — "I crashed into him with everything I had — my shoulder screaming, his ribs cracking, the shard spinning free across the stone floor.
Malee — "He sidestepped me like I was a child — my face hit the ground and I tasted blood and gravel.

choices.line: A Unified Chord. Have Chanida, Arthit, Malee, and the Monk combine their talents to generate a harmonic shield, containing the blast.
choices.consequence: A test of trust and skill. The blast is contained, saving the Lattice, but the feedback severely damages both ships and injures the party.
choices.description: Have Arthit calculate the shard's resonant frequency and deploy a counter-harmonic through the tunnel's old speaker system.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "I fed the inverse waveform through the corroded speakers — the shard vibrated, went still, and the bandit stared at it like it had betrayed him.
Arthit — "The frequency was off by a fraction — the speakers screamed static, and the shard pulsed brighter, feeding on the noise like a living thing.

choices.line: Sing Over Him. Pichit must step forward and Sing, not to fight, but to offer a new, pure frequency for the shard to follow, transforming its destructive potential.
choices.consequence: The ultimate risk. Pichit's untrained gift could save everything or amplify the disaster. Success creates a new, stable harmonic landmark; failure consumes him and the ships.
choices.description: Chanida rallies everyone to form a human chain, channeling their combined resonance to dampen the shard's energy through physical contact.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "I grabbed Arthit's left hand and Malee's right — the current tore through us like freezing water, but the shard's glow dimmed, then died.
Chanida — "The chain broke at my grip — sweat, blood, exhaustion — and the feedback threw us apart like rag dolls, the shard humming louder than ever.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market churns with life, a dizzying vortex of noise. The ambient drone of ten thousand conversations, clattering goods, and distant resonator hum makes the air feel thick, almost liquid. Pichit's group navigates the stalls, their purpose obscured by the sensory overload.
A 'hub of commerce and gossip.' How poetic. It just smells like sweat and desperation. Who is this guy we're even looking for?
A scavenger! Someone who actually walks the Lattice surface. How good is he? Must be insane or brilliant.
Likely both. And likely watched. The Tonal Orders don't appreciate unlicensed surface exploration. We should be discreet.
Every voice here adds to the chorus. We must listen for the one note that doesn't belong—the one that speaks of the surface.
Near a stall selling 'authentic' Lattice shards, a figure in patched, crystal-dusted leather haggles tersely with a smooth-faced merchant. The scavenger's eyes dart, missing nothing.
Your price scrapes the bottom. These aren't tourist trinkets. They're from the Deep Chorus sector. Resonate with the wrong frequency and... well, you won't be complaining.
My friend! Such tales! The market hum makes verification... difficult. Let's find a harmonic price, yes?

lines_after.dialogue: That's them! Let's just ask. What's the worst that could happen?
He could sell us to the Orders. Or his 'shards' could be fakes that make our heads buzz. I tried to stop him but... oh, fine. Let's get swindled.
As you approach, the merchant's smile widens. The scavenger's posture tightens, a hand drifting near a tool that looks part geologist's hammer, part weapon.

line.dialogue: The scavenger eyes your group with deep suspicion. The merchant sees potential new customers.

choices.text: [Pichit: Philosophical Openness] Speak of seeking the Lattice's true song, not its commerce.
choices.outcome: Appeals to the scavenger's potential reverence for the surface, though the merchant loses interest.
choices.description: Approach the barkeep polishing glasses behind the counter and ask about anyone who's been selling Lattice-salvaged tech recently.
