line.dialogue: Arthit leans back. "The bartender's eyes flicked left—toward the corner booth—before he answered. That's our thread. Pull it gently.
Arthit mutters, "He smiled too quickly and named three people. When someone volunteers that much, they're hiding the one name that matters.

choices.text: [Chanida: Direct Offer] Cut through the noise: offer good coin for a guide to the surface.
choices.outcome: Gets the merchant's full attention, but makes the scavenger even more wary of wealthy outsiders.
choices.description: Order rounds for the four of you and settle into an empty booth, ears open to the conversations flowing around you.

line.dialogue: Pichit closes his eyes. "There—two tables over. Someone mentioned 'resonance patterns' and 'fresh cracks.' That's not shop talk. That's Lattice-walker slang.
Pichit sighs. "I caught fragments about grain prices, a cheating spouse, and someone's broken cart. We're drowning in noise. The chorus is too loud tonight.

choices.text: [Arthit: Cautious Inquiry] Ask the merchant about surface artifacts, hoping the scavenger overhears and engages.
choices.outcome: Plays into the market's social dance, but risks getting bogged down in the merchant's negotiations.
choices.description: Scan the room for anyone sitting alone who looks uncomfortable—people who don't belong here stand out in places like this.

line.dialogue: Chanida nods slowly. "Woman by the support pillar. Drink untouched, eyes on the door, tool-belt under her jacket. She's waiting
the merchant fails. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The deal is struck, but the air is uneasy. The scavenger, who gave the name 'Boon,' agreed to meet at first light. The market's noise has softened to a predawn murmur, the sky bleeding indigo and gold.
From morning until evening, he said. A full day's journey on the surface to reach the 'listening post.' When's a good time to back out? Now feels optimal.
Nah, nah. You don't need to do that. We've already paid the 'good faith' deposit. Which, for the record, is faith I don't have.
It's a fresh beginning! The sun's coming up, we have a guide... sort of. He's just... gritty.
Dawn is when the world's song is clearest, before the clutter of daily life. A good time to listen for truth.
Boon arrives, his gear clinking. The merchant, 'Vasin,' appears as if from nowhere, his smile already in place.
My friends! A glorious morning for a venture! I took the liberty of preparing some... supplemental provisions. For a modest fee, of course. Safety first!
He sells overpriced damp-rations and faulty frequency dampeners. You don't need to do that. My kit is sufficient.

lines_after.dialogue: Boon is a artist of the surface, truly! But even artists need patrons. I can ensure your investment is... protected. Information is a currency, after all.
He's not coming with us. Tell me he's not coming with us.
Vasin's eyes gleam. He leans in, his voice dropping below the market's waking hum. The subplot surfaces.

A whisper, for free: the Listeners have been agitated. They speak of a 'discord' growing in the Lattice's lower strata, a warning in the deep sound. Some say it's the echo of The Silencing... returning. Your scavenger friend's destination is near where their alarms are loudest. Coincidence?

line.dialogue: Boon glares at Vasin, who merely shrugs. The warning hangs in the morning air.

choices.text: [Pichit: Heed the Omen] Press Boon for the truth about the Listener warnings before proceeding.
choices.outcome: Forces the scavenger to reveal what he knows, potentially delaying departure but avoiding surprises.
choices.description: Pull Arthit aside and ask what he's really getting out of this deal, 15 words

line.dialogue: Let's just say my debts run deeper than this river, and leave it at that.
You're staring at me like I'm the villain. Maybe I am. Doesn't change what needs doing.

choices.text: [Chanida: Dismiss the Hype] Assume Vasin is just spooking you to sell more 'safety' gear. Press on with the original plan.
choices.outcome: Keeps the schedule but ignores a potential real threat; Boon respects decisiveness but worries.
choices.description: Grab your pack and head toward the dock before anyone can argue further, 15 words

line.dialogue: Finally, someone who moves instead of talks! The boat won't wait and neither will I.
Running off won't make the deal fairer. Sit down. We settle terms first, then we walk.

choices.text: [Arthit: Double-Down on Caution] Propose hiring Vasin as an 'information liaison' to monitor the Listeners from the city while you go.
choices.outcome: Costs more coin and binds you to the untrustworthy merchant, but creates a potential intelligence source.
choices.description: Ask Pichit what song the dawn is singing today—listen carefully to his answer, 15 words

line.dialogue: Today it hums low and cautious, like a monk before confession. Walk softly, all of you.
You ask, but you don't pause to hear. That's the problem with this whole expedition.

lines_before.dialogue: The market's hum intensifies as afternoon crowds swell. The Trade Negotiator, the Trade Negotiator, beckons your group over with a polished smile.
Ah, the intrepid travelers! I hear you're making inquiries about surface patterns. A dangerous curiosity, but a profitable one for those who know how to listen.
We're just trying to understand some irregularities. The Listeners are concerned.
Concern is a luxury the pragmatic cannot afford. But information... now that has value. Tell me, is the pay good for this sort of 'understanding'? I might have charts.
Of course it's about charts. Everything with your Order is about hoarding knowledge. What's the real price?
The price is discretion. The Tonal Orders maintain stability. Some... natural resonances from below can spook the masses. Bad for commerce. You finding a 'warning' could cause a panic.
And covering a truth is better? The Lattice sings for a reason. Ignoring it is what caused The Silencing.
He's hiding something. I'm in a good mood today, so I'll ask nicely once. What do you know about the deep hums the Scavenger mentioned?

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant's smile doesn't falter, but his eyes grow cold. The background market noise seems to swell, a wall of sound masking your conversation.
It was a good experience talking with you. Truly. But some frequencies are best left unamplified. For the good of the city.
He's not going to give us anything. Just more veiled threats wrapped in courtesy.

line.dialogue: The merchant offers a 'deal': take his silence and a bribe, or pursue the truth and face the Order's displeasure.

choices.line: Take the bribe and pretend you heard nothing. (Gain funds, avoid immediate conflict, but the subplot warning goes unheeded.)
consequences: The party is richer but troubled.
The merchant's influence grows.
The subplot 'The Lattice's Warning' is suppressed.
choices.description: Lean forward and press the merchant about what ships have been rerouted recently, 15 words

line.dialogue: The merchant's eyes flicker—I've found the thread, and now I pull it.
He laughs it off with a joke about tides, but his hands tremble around his cup.

choices.line: Politely decline, stating you'll conduct your own investigation. (Maintain neutrality, but draw the Order's watchful eye.)
consequences: The merchant is displeased but not hostile.
The party's movements may be observed.
The subplot 'The Lattice's Warning' remains active.
choices.description: Signal Malee to charm the merchant while you quietly observe his ledger on the counter

line.dialogue: I smile, ask about his family—meanwhile Arthit's eyes are counting every entry in that book.
I lay it on too thick and he clams up, pulling the ledger close to his chest.

choices.line: Confront him openly. Accuse the Tonal Orders of endangering everyone by suppressing the truth. (Force a confrontation, risking his influence but potentially shaking information loose.)
consequences: The merchant becomes an active adversary.
You may attract unwanted attention from the Orders.
A chance to learn a critical piece of information about the warning.
choices.description: Mention the name of a missing ship directly and watch his reaction carefully

line.dialogue: The
the merchant fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: As dusk settles, the market's noise begins to die down. A strange, deep thrumming vibrates up through the crystal walkways, felt in the bones more than heard. The Surface Scavenger, the Surface scavenger, runs up, face pale.
You! You didn't listen to that silk-tongued worm, did you? It's getting louder. The deep hum. The Lattice isn't just singing... it's chanting. A countdown.
We have work to do. Real work. We need to verify this, get to a listening post, and—
And what? Tell the authorities who are probably bought by the merchant's Order? I got the answer now. The system is broken.
The answer is in the sound itself. We must interpret the warning, not debate who to tell. Someone is waiting for you, Scavenger. Who else knows?
My crew. A few Listeners who aren't afraid. We're preparing to evacuate our surface camp. The big one is coming. A resonance shift that'll make The Silencing look like a whisper.
Then we go to the edge. Right now. We use our ship's resonator to listen deep, broadcast what we hear to the whole city!
The deep hum pulses again, stronger. Stalls rattle. A crystal spire in the distance emits a sharp, cracking ping. The market falls into a stunned, fearful silence.

lines_after.dialogue: The climactic choice hangs in the newly quiet air. The normal world of commerce and gossip has shattered, replaced by a profound, vibrating dread.
This is the moment. Do we trust the institutions that failed the world once before, or do we become the warning ourselves?
Make your call. I have work I have to do. My people are waiting.

line.dialogue: The Lattice's warning can no longer be ignored. How do you act in this moment of crisis?

choices.line: Alert the City Guard formally. Follow protocol to trigger an official evacuation. (Orderly, but slow. You work within the system.)
consequences: The bureaucracy moves, saving some but not all.
You are legitimized but possibly too late.
The subplot 'The Lattice's Warning' concludes with partial success.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus Listener training on the noise to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Pichit loses control. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Rally the Scavengers and sympathetic Listeners. Create a decentralized network to spread the warning street by street. (Chaotic but personal.)
consequences: You save many in the lower districts who distrust authority.
You create a powerful grassroots network for the future.
The subplot 'The Lattice's Warning' concludes with a new faction emerging.
choices.description: Arthit channels ship navigation toward the bargaining, hoping to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Arthit overreaches. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.line: Commandere a public resonance amplifier in the market square. Broadcast the raw, terrifying hum of the Lattice for all to hear. (The ultimate truth, causing instant panic and action.)
consequences: You force immediate, city-wide confrontation with the truth.
You become a hero to some, a terrorist to others (like the Tonal Orders).
The subplot 'The Lattice's Warning' concludes explosively, changing the political landscape forever.
choices.description: The scavenger steps forward with harvesting tools, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Surface knowledge reveals a safe path.
Things don't go as planned. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Aria's Lament' hums a low, steady tone, its crystal resonators parting the shimmering Lattice below like a wake through crystalline water.
Look at that! The lattice is fracturing ahead. It's... singing a different chord.
Probably just another Tonal Order charting error. Their monopoly on navigation is a joke.
We should adjust our resonance frequency. Unstable lattice patterns can tear the hull.
There's a tension in that sound... a discovery waiting, but also a warning.
A smaller, battered vessel emerges from a lattice spire, its hull scarred by surface travel. It drifts closer.
Don't let him see you! I mean... you lot. The Tonal Order sends scouts after ground-dwellers like me.
Ah, fellow travelers! Perhaps we can trade? I have... information about that fracture.

lines_after.dialogue: Let's go inside. The deck's too exposed for this. Your 'information' probably costs more than our ship.
Inside? A fine idea. More comfortable for negotiations.
Negotiations? He'll sell you lies. The Groundless Movement says the Orders hide the true nature of the Lattice.
Let's get to it. We need to know what's in that fracture.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger warns of Order spies. The Merchant offers a trade. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Trust the Scavenger's warning and secure the ship.
choices.description: Channel your resonance through Arthit's frequency stabilizer before the fracture spreads further.

line.dialogue: That's it — hold that pitch steady and the lattice won't collapse beneath us.
You're drifting sharp again — listen to me next time before we all fall through!

choices.line: Follow the Merchant inside to hear his offer, but stay wary.
choices.description: Push ahead with Pichit toward the fracture's edge to document the anomalous tone.

line.dialogue: Do you hear that? The fracture is *singing* — this changes everything the Order teaches.
The tone collapsed before I could transcribe it... we were too hesitant. It won't repeat.

choices.line: Send Arthit to analyze the fracture's resonance from the deck.
choices.description: Override Malee's objections and broadcast a harmonic probe directly into the fracture.

line.dialogue: Fine. I was wrong — there's structure inside the instability. The Order's charts don't account for this.
You just scattered the

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the ship's chart room, the Merchant's smile is as polished as his lapel crystal. The Scavenger stands rigid by the door.
The fracture holds a relic from before The Silencing. A 'Ground Singer's' final recording. I don't have many friends in the Orders, so I need... independent buyers.
Obviously you just want us to risk our necks while you profit.
The pain is gone for the Orders. They erased that Singer's history. The past is gone for them, but not for us.
Navigating that fracture will require unauthorized resonance frequencies. If the Orders detect us...
So let it go! Their rules are garbage! We have to hear that recording!
The past isn't over if its echo still resonates. This is a discovery that could change everything.
The ship's ambient tone shifts abruptly—an external resonance scan prickles across the hull.

lines_after.dialogue: Tonal Order patrol ship. They're scanning us.
Ah. My... associates. A minor complication.
He doesn't have many friends, but he has plenty of 'associates.' They'll seize everything.
The Groundless Movement was right. The Orders hide everything behind a smile.

line.dialogue: An Order patrol is scanning the ship. The fracture and its secret lie ahead. What's your move?

choices.line: Comply with the patrol, surrender the Merchant, and abandon the mission.
choices.description: Rappel into the fracture using salvaged cable, trusting Arthit's coordinates to avoid the unstable pockets.

line.dialogue: Cable holds — I can see the relic glinting from here, barely twenty meters down.
The cable shears against the glass edge and I'm sliding, scrambling, knuckles bloody on nothing.

choices.line: Use the Scavenger's knowledge to mask our resonance and slip away quietly.
choices.description: Demand the merchant reveal what the relic actually does before agreeing to anything.

line.dialogue: You want the truth? Fine — it's a Resonance Key. Last one in existence. Now you understand my desperation.
I owe you nothing, scavenger. Either descend or walk — but don't mistake my politeness for negotiation.

choices.line: Charge the fracture at full speed, using the recording's alleged frequency as a shield.
choices.description: Use the scavenger's Singe-scarred frequency to chart a path the Orders can't detect.

line.dialogue: The old wound hums where the fracture splits — I can feel the safe path like music in my bones.
The scar screams instead of sings and I collapse, nose bleeding, the fracture's geometry rewriting itself behind my eyes.

lines_before.dialogue: The merchant, now cornered on the deck, smooths his robes. The scavenger stands behind him, arms crossed, a sentinel of the Lattice surface.
It’s obvious that we’ve reached an impasse. Obviously, you want answers I’m not paid to give.
You were paid to smuggle banned resonance charts to the Groundless. We found the manifests. (The mother) was heart-broken when she learned her son was running with you lot.
The Tonal Orders want their monopoly back. They’re hunting the Groundless. You’re leading them right to the scavenger camps!
My people trusted you. We gave you salvage from the Silencing. And you sell us out for a cleaner sky-city berth?
The pain is gone for you, isn't it? The guilt. You’ve done this before. The past is over, so you let it go and do it again.
The Groundless aren't just rebels. They're Listeners who've gone silent, aren't they? People who heard something in the Lattice the Orders forbade.
And what if they are? You think a little philosophical insight changes the tune? The Lattice consumes idealists. Be pragmatic.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant's eyes dart to the ship's console. A low, unauthorized harmonic begins to pulse from it—a distress beacon.
He's signaling someone! The resonance pattern... it's a Tonal Order cutter frequency!
Wonderful. So much for a quiet chat. They'll be here in minutes.

line.dialogue: The merchant has sealed our fate. We have minutes before the Tonal Order enforcers arrive. What's our move?

choices.text: Cut the beacon and run. Use the charts we seized to find a safe, obscure frequency and flee into a lattice storm.
choices.description: Slam the banned resonance charts onto the table and demand Malee explain the false coordinates etched into them.

line.dialogue: I altered those coordinates because the real ones point to a Tonal Order vault — and I wasn't about to hand your scavenger friends a death sentence.
You shouldn't have touched those. The ink reacts to skin oils — you just erased the only proof I had.

choices.text: Confront them. Use the ship's resonator to jam their approach. It's a gamble, but we might bluff our authority.
choices.description: Pull Chanida aside and offer to broker a deal — the charts in exchange for the Tonal Order dropping its hunt on the scavenger settlements.

line.dialogue: You're either incredibly brave or catastrophically naive, but I'll bring it to the Presiding Tone — on the condition you never speak of my involvement.
The Orders don't broker. They eradicate. And now your name is on the same list as mine.

choices.text: Turn the tables. Let them dock. Use the merchant as a hostage to negotiate passage to the main Groundless refuge.
choices.description: Turn to the scavenger, return the Sil salvage personally, and swear to lead them to an uncharted resonance vein as repayment.

line.dialogue: You're either mad or honest, and in the Wastes those look the same. We follow — but if the vein runs dry, so does your blood.
Scav

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Order cutter glides alongside, its polished crystal hull humming with aggressive, precise harmonics. Armed Resonators aim from its deck.
(He)’s been married to profit two times over! Don't make me cry for him! He'll sing any song you want now!
Shut it! They're not here for a trade negotiation. Look at their resonator alignment—they're preparing to shatter our crystal drive!
If our drive goes, we fall. The Lattice doesn't forgive. I sprained my ankle once on a minor shard-fall. This will be worse.
They're demanding we surrender the 'contraband' and the 'stolen person.' That's you, scavenger. They want to silence the source.
The past is gone? Tell that to them. They're the ones who can't let the Silencing go, who need to control every note.
This is the choice. The Lattice responds to true sound. The Orders use forced harmonics. Our ship... we have a Singer's heart in its core, don't we?
You want to *sing* at them? With their dampeners, they'll crush any natural frequency we throw out!

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit places a hand on the ship's main resonator. A pure, uncharted tone wells up from deep within the vessel, a sound that makes the very air vibrate with potential.
By the fallen cities... that's the sound from before the Silencing. The Lattice... it's answering.
The crystalline expanse below begins to glow, rising in resonant pillars of light. The Order cutter's aggressive hum falters, drowned in a chorus it cannot control.

line.dialogue: The Lattice is awake and answering the ship's true song. But such power is wild and untamed. How do we wield it?

choices.text: Create a shield. Shape the resonance into a protective dome around our ship and the scavenger camps below. Let the Order break against it.
choices.description: Direct Malee to test the prosthetic reaction using leg resonance

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee hits a wall. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Disarm them. Use the resonant wave to carefully fracture their weapon crystals, rendering them harmless but leaving their ship intact.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using crystal hearing to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Open a path. Don't fight. Use the song to part the Lattice beneath the Order ship, sending it on a controlled, deep descent—exiled, not destroyed.
choices.description: Ask the merchant to chart resonance pathways, drawing on trade ledger

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the merchant. His network produces an ally at the critical moment.
The gamble fails. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cavern of silence, a library of carved crystal shelves holding shimmering frequency charts. The air hums with a suppressed energy.
I can't believe we're just... browsing. Do you know what this is? This chart shows a route to a sunken city! The Tonal Orders have it marked 'forgotten.'
They 'forget' anything that doesn't turn a profit for the guilds. How well do you know her, Pichit? Our 'Trade Negotiator' contact seems a little too eager to help.
Ah, my new friends! I see you've found the restricted section. A dangerous place for the curious. But for the right partners... very profitable.
We're not partners. We're researchers. He doesn't have many friends in the guild, Pichit. That's why he's come to us. We should be cautious.
Every frequency holds a memory. These 'forgotten' routes... they aren't errors. They're deliberate silences. What are they hiding?
Hiding? Let's call it... inventory management. Some knowledge is a liability. But to the right buyer, say, the Groundless movement... it becomes an asset.

lines_after.dialogue: The Groundless? Those radicals who want to dismantle the cities? He's playing a deeper game.
Who cares who buys it? If it gets us to the truth, we should take it!
Associating with them is a one-way trip to a sky-cell. This is exactly the kind of risk we agreed to avoid.

line.dialogue: The Merchant offers a deal: he'll give you a key to a sealed archive wing containing 'unprofitable' histories, in exchange for a future favor, unspecified.

choices.text: Accept the deal. The knowledge is worth the risk.
choices.description: Slam the ledger shut and demand to know how he followed us past the archive lock.

line.dialogue: I sealed that door myself — so either you picked a Chulalongkorn-era cipher lock in under four minutes, or you had help from inside this building.
Great. Now he knows we noticed the lock, and he's smiling *more*. That's not the intimidation you think it is.

choices.text: Refuse, but offer to pay for the information outright.
choices.description: Let Malee handle him — she knows how merchants like this think.

line.dialogue: You're third-tier, selling second-hand secrets to first-name targets. So skip the 'new friends' routine and tell us your price — before I start naming people you've *also* approached this week.
He's not flinching. Which means someone already paid him more than we can scare up — or he's not actually here to sell.

choices.text: Politely decline and try to find another way in.
choices.description: Quietly photograph the spine labels behind him while Chanida keeps him talking.

line.dialogue: I got three shelf codes before he shifted his weight
The risk doesn't pay off. Hidden debts come due.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in the archive's acoustically deadened core, you find the sealed wing. The door vibrates with a low, discordant hum.
The lock's resonator is damaged. It's rejecting the Merchant's key. We need to recalibrate it, but... I need some time.
Time we might not have. Nah, nah. Look. Scorch marks. Someone else tried to get in here recently. And failed messily.
Ugh, there's something in my eye... crystal dust. This place is falling apart. What are we even looking for?
The truth behind The Silencing. The official records call it an accident. But if the Lattice responds to sound... what if it was a song?
A rough voice cuts through the silence from a shadowed balcony above.
A song that broke the world! You guild-lovers finally digging up your own dirty laundry? Don't need to bother with that lock. I know a frequency that'll shake it loose.
A sky pirate. Here? The security resonances should have torn your ship apart.

lines_after.dialogue: Your precious Orders don't control all the songs. The Groundless pay better for real history, not the sanitized junk you sell.
Great. So the Merchant *and* the pirates are working with the Groundless. We're standing in the middle of a conspiracy.
He can get us in! Who cares about his politics?

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate offers to bypass the lock with a destabilizing frequency, but it will trigger every alarm in the sector. Arthit insists he can crack it quietly, but it will take much longer.

choices.text: Let the pirate do it. Speed is worth the chaos.
choices.description: Force the resonator open with the emergency bypass, risking a feedback surge through the Mer shard.

line.dialogue: Got it — but the shard's cracked now. Every door after this better be friendlier.
The whole housing just fused shut. We're not getting through this way unless someone's got a plasma cutter hidden somewhere uncomfortable.

choices.text: Let Arthit work. A stealthy approach is safer.
choices.description: Examine the scorch marks to determine what weapon was fired and trace its energy signature.

line.dialogue: Military-grade ion discharge, three days old. Whatever happened here, someone official wanted it buried fast.
Too degraded — the crystal dust contaminated the residue. Could be a rifle, could be a welding torch. I'm guessing blind here.

choices.text: Try to combine both methods for a controlled breach.
choices.description: Search the nearby records terminal for un

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the merchant's call. Hidden leverage shifts the balance.
The gamble fails. His network delivers bad intelligence.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in the restricted stacks, the air hums with suppressed frequencies. Ancient crystal ledgers line the walls, their surfaces faintly glowing with recorded sound.
Ah, you found the good section. The Tonal Orders didn't want this knowledge cataloged. Too... disruptive to their monopoly.
These charts... they're not just safe routes. They're attack vectors. Pirate ambush points!
Of course they are. The 'safe' knowledge funds the 'unsafe' business. The Orders have their hands in every jar.
This is a massive breach of trust. If these ledgers are authentic, the entire navigation system is compromised.
The truth often doesn't fit the official records. Why couldn't the Orders just admit the Lattice is more chaotic than their charts allow?
Because then folks like me wouldn't need 'em! We know the wild frequencies. The ones that shake your bones and part the crystal like butter.
Which brings us to our mutual friend, the Groundless Movement. They believe anyone should be able to read the Lattice's song. For the adventurous, you might say.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, resonant thrum pulses through the floor. One of the archival crystals on a high shelf flickers and goes dark.
That's not a scheduled silence. Someone's scrubbing data. Real-time.
We've tripped an alarm. The Archivist-Sentinels will be here any moment.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate gestures to a heavy, non-crystalline ledger bound in strange hide. 'The real prize. The Black Frequency Log. It's why I'm here. You want it?'

choices.line: Take the log and flee immediately. (Risk losing other evidence, but secure the core secret.)
choices.description: Copy the ledger pages into your notebook before the merchant notices what you've seen.

line.dialogue: Every number transcribed. If they burn these, we still have proof.
The ink smeared — half the entries are unreadable. We move blind now.

choices.line: Attempt to copy the log's data into a portable resonator. (Takes time, but preserves more.)
choices.description: Slam the ledger shut and demand the merchant explain who funds the Tonal Orders.

line.dialogue: You'll tell us everything, or I walk to the Harmonic Council with this right now.
He just laughed and called for the archive guards. We've made enemies of the wrong people.

choices.line: Confront the approaching Sentinels with the evidence. (Dangerous, but could expose corruption now.)
choices.description: Slip the chart marked "Deep Choir Routes" beneath your coat and walk out calmly.

line.dialogue: Casual as a Sunday browse. They'll never miss it until it's too late.
The weight shifted wrong — the chart slid out right at the

acts.title: The Cost of a True Note

lines_before.dialogue: The central archive atrium. Archivist-Sentinels in resonant armor block the exits, their tuning forks humming a discordant barrier frequency.
A regrettable misunderstanding, Sentinels! My associates were merely... auditing the collection. Anyone's okay to appreciate knowledge, yes?
He's selling us out! What's this called, Arthit? Betrayal?
It's called calculating the price of survival. He always does.
The price. Right. What's the going rate for treason against the Tonal Orders today? Keep it. I don't want to know.
This isn't about commerce. It's about a song everyone has the right to hear. The Silencing happened because we stopped listening to the world's true voice.
Pretty words! But the Sentinel's got a resonator pointed at your chest. What's your move, Singer?
From the shadows, a figure in simple grey robes steps forward—a Listener. They place a hand on the central archive spire.

lines_after.dialogue: A pure, foundational note rings out from the spire, bypassing the Sentinel's discord. The barrier frequency shatters into harmonic dust.
The Groundless Movement thanks you for uncovering the rot. The true archive is the Lattice itself. We will teach all to listen.

Chaos erupts. The Sky Pirate grabs the Black Log and vanishes into a service duct. The Merchant flees amid the confusion. You are left with a choice: follow the Listener into the unknown, or hold the line here with the evidence.

line.dialogue: The Lead Sentinel lowers his resonator, his voice strained. 'You have the proof. Hand it over, and the Orders will... reform. Slowly. Or give it to them, and watch the world burn in another revolution. What's your call?'

choices.line: Surrender the evidence to the Orders. (Ensure immediate stability, but trust the corrupt system to change.)
choices.description: Grab the merchant by his collar and slam him against the alley wall, demanding the Sentinel patrol's patrol route.

line.dialogue: You taste fear on your tongue already, you weasel — spit out their positions before I squeeze it out of you.
He's shaking so bad his teeth are rattling, but his eyes keep darting past me — they're already here.

choices.line: Give the copies to the Listener. (Spark the Groundless Movement, risking chaos for potential true freedom.)
choices.description: Signal Chanida silently to cut the merchant loose and let him run straight into Malee's waiting blade around the corner.

line.dialogue: The fool actually thinks we're letting him go — his legs move before his brain catches up, straight into the trap.
Chanida hesitates half a second too long and the merchant reads her body language, bolting sideways into the drainage grate.

choices.line: Destroy the evidence publicly. (Force both sides to start anew with nothing, the most dangerous gamble of all.)
choices.description: Pull out the ledger you lifted from his coat pocket earlier and read aloud every Sentinel name he's been selling information to.

line.dialogue: His face goes white as temple ash when I start reciting — he knows we own him now, body and soul.
I flip to the wrong page and he laughs, that ugly nervous laugh — 'You think I keep names in writing? I'm not stupid.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of dead ships. Metal shrieks as salvage crews dismember hulks, their noise a harsh, discordant blanket over the industrial edge of the city.
This place is a symphony of bad decisions! Look at this resonator housing—someone tried to fix it with scrap solder. It’s a really good movie of what NOT to do!
The only good thing here is the profit margin for the breakers. Everything else is just sentimental junk. He's the only son of a family who thought they could outrun The Silencing. Now he's scrap.
We should be cautious. The acoustics here are chaotic. A wrong frequency could trigger a sympathetic vibration in the Lattice below... or attract the wrong kind of attention from the Tonal Orders.
Every broken hull has a story. Every cut wire, a final note. To walk back and forth here is to trace the echoes of a civilization that tried to sing itself to safety.
You the ones asking about the old maps? The Merchant's over by the crane. But be direct—he doesn't like people pacing back and forth. Makes him nervous.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, travelers! Looking for something specific, or just browsing the graveyard? I have components, charts... information. For the right price, of course.
We seek knowledge of the Open Frequencies. Maps not controlled by the Orders.
Dangerous curiosity. But profitable to discuss. Let's walk. The acoustics near the active crusher are... private.

line.dialogue: The Merchant leads you to a quieter section of the yard, near a humming power converter. He smiles, his eyes calculating.

choices.line: Offer immediate payment from your shared funds. (Lose some resources, but get a straight answer.)
choices.description: Have Malee focus scavenger instincts on the scavenger gangs to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
The risk doesn't pay off. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Offer a trade: information on a safe, unpatrolled shipping lane you discovered. (Risk future travel routes for quicker trust.)
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use hidden frequencies and question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
A costly mistake by Chanida. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.line: Appeal to his pragmatism. Ask what he stands to gain from a world with more open navigation. (A diplomatic, but slower, approach.)
choices.description: The villager volunteers to decode the tonal pattern, leveraging terraces

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the villager. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
Defeat. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The deal is struck. The Merchant directs you to a derelict Resonance Ship, the 'Whispering Keel,' half-buried under other wrecks. Its crystal resonator is dark, a silent heart in a metal corpse.
Structural integrity is questionable. That's not scary at all, it's a fact. One wrong step and we can't make it back to the surface.

Relax. I'll have a look at the access panel. If the Merchant's telling the truth, the navigation log might still have data fragments. If not, we just got scammed. I have to do a better job vetting informants.
It's spooky in here! All these dead control panels... but look! The main resonator casing is intact. I'll look at it for you, Malee. Maybe we can get a ghost of a signal.
A ship that cannot sing. Its final frequency is trapped within, a memory of its last journey. What did it hear before the silence?
As Malee works on the log, a low, subsonic hum begins to emanate from the ship's hull. The loose metal around you starts to vibrate faintly.

lines_after.dialogue: Got it! The log's corrupted, but there's a data packet... it's not a chart. It's a frequency log. Raw, unprocessed Lattice echoes from below the Scrapyard. The Open Map isn't a drawing; it's a song.
That hum is getting louder. The ship's dead resonator is acting as an antenna! We're broadcasting our find to anyone listening on the industrial bands. The Tonal Orders' patrols will hear this!
The whole ship is waking up! It’s not scary at all! It's... really loud! We need to grab the data and go!

line.dialogue: The 'Whispering Keel' shudders, its metal groaning as the residual energy in its crystals builds. The data transfer is at 70%. Distantly, you hear the distinct harmonic whine of an approaching Tonal Orders skiff.

choices.line: Abort the transfer and run. You'll have partial data, but a clean escape. (Lose some map completeness, avoid immediate conflict.)
choices.description: Pry open the jammed access panel with a plasma cutter while Arthit holds the frame steady.

line.dialogue: Got it — the Meridian subsystem is still drawing residual power. There's a map embedded in the maintenance logs, but it's fragmenting as I read it.
The panel buckled inward. Whatever pressure differential is behind this bulkhead, we just made it worse. I can hear something venting.

choices.line: Rig the ship's old power core to overload, creating an acoustic smokescreen. It will hide your escape and complete the transfer, but may trigger a dangerous Lattice resonance. (Risk an environmental hazard.)
choices.description: Place your palm on the dead navigation console and let the ship's last stored frequency resonate through you.

line.dialogue: I hear it now — a low harmonic, repeating. The ship sang itself to death trying to chart something it was never meant to find. The coordinates are burned into my fingertips.
Don't touch that — the console discharged static through your arm. Your hand is shaking and you can't stop it. Whatever frequency is trapped in there, it doesn't want to be remembered.

choices.line: Stand your ground. Use the ship's rising resonance to mask your own signatures and prepare an ambush for the patrol. Seize their skiff for a faster escape. (High-risk combat encounter.)
choices.description: Follow the faint vibration in the floor toward the engineering bay while Chanida maps the dead panels by touch.

line.dialogue: Every panel I touch is cold except one — there's a heat bloom deep in engineering. Something down there is still alive, still waiting.
Defeat. His network delivers bad intelligence.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's din intensifies as you follow the merchant's tip to a hollowed-out freighter hull, now a makeshift guildhall. The air smells of ozone and rust.
Inside, the Trade Negotiator is waiting, his smile not quite reaching his eyes. A frequency map fragment glows on the table. 'A pleasure, as always. I trust your journey was... profitable?'
Less talk, more map. We need the other half. What's the price?
Direct! I admire that. The price is a job. A Tonal Order inspector is sniffing around my... less sanctioned acquisitions. He needs to be convinced to look elsewhere.
Convinced? That sounds like a path with consequences. We should do a better job of understanding the risks first.
He means we might get cut. Or worse. Let me have a look at this map fragment first. See if it's even worth the blood.
Every choice here feels like a blade. The merchant's smile, the inspector's duty... both can wound the world in different ways. We must choose the cut that heals.
A Skycity Resident, one of the scavengers, rushes in, face pale. 'They're here! The inspector and his guards. They say the Negotiator is hoarding forbidden tech!'

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the grinding air. Outside, the rhythmic pounding of a hydraulic crusher provides a grim, ticking clock.
Well? The map for your service. Or hand me over and see how far you get without my... connections.
We have to do better than this cycle of fear and greed. But the map... it could change everything.

line.dialogue: How do you handle the inspector's arrival?

choices.text: Distract the inspector. Use the scrapyard's noise to create a diversion, letting the merchant slip away.
choices.outcome: A chaotic symphony of dropped metal and 'faulty' alarms draws the guards off. The merchant escapes, grudgingly hands over the map. You avoid a fight, but the inspector's suspicion now burns towards you.
choices.description: Agree to the Tonal Ordeal immediately, demanding details and the map's location before we commit.

line.dialogue: Fine. I'll walk your path — but I walk it knowing where it ends. Talk fast.
Great, another cryptic trial with no exit. I've had enough of those to last three lifetimes.

choices.text: Confront the inspector directly. Appeal to reason, argue the map is for the greater good beyond guild control.
choices.outcome: A tense standoff in the shadow of wrecked ships. The inspector is rigid, bound by his orders. Your words plant a seed of doubt in him, but he demands the merchant come quietly. Violence is a breath away.
choices.description: Press the Negotiator on what the Tonal Ordeal actually involves before agreeing to anything.

line.dialogue: I've seen 'simple jobs' leave people hollowed out. Tell us exactly what this ordeal demands — every note, every cost.
He's dodging the question. When a merchant smiles more the harder you push, the price is always steeper than advertised.

choices.text: Turn the merchant in. Take the map fragment from him as evidence of his crimes, hoping to bargain with the inspector for the complete Open Frequency Map.
choices.outcome: Betrayal is a cold knife. The merchant's smile vanishes into a snarl of promises. The inspector is impressed by your 'lawfulness' but the map is now official guild property. Access is not guaranteed.
choices.description: Threaten to find the other map half through less diplomatic

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the merchant. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the merchant's resolve isn't enough. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The confrontation has drawn a crowd of scavengers. The completed Open Frequency Map is in play, its luminous lines humming in Pichit's hands. The very Lattice beneath the scrapyard thrums in response.
The harmonic feedback... it's unstable. If we activate the full sequence here, with all this discordant metal... I'm not sure the scrapyard's structural health can take it.
Great. So we either get arrested by the guild, shanked by the merchant's friends, or bring the whole floating island down on our heads. What a good experience this is turning out to be.
Stop whining! Look at the map! It's not just coordinates, it's a song! Pichit, you can feel it, right? We have to sing it. Now!
The Lattice is listening. This cacophony... the clanging, the fear, the greed... it's a sickness. This map is a cure. A true, open frequency. But using it here will be a violent surgery.
The Tonal Order inspector's guards form a perimeter. The Trade Negotiator watches from the shadows, a knife in his hand. The Skycity Residents look on, terrified and hopeful.
That map is my property! Give it back, and I'll make sure your end is quick. The guild will just lock it away forever. What good is it then?
Please... if it can make the skies safe... if it can stop the Silencing from happening again... try. We're in a good mood for a miracle.

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit raises the map. The crystalline lattice in the device flares, pulling sympathetic vibrations from every shard of resonator crystal in the yard. A single, pure note begins to form.
Hear the world's true voice!
The climax resonates not in a battle of weapons, but of frequencies. The fate of the map, the scrapyard, and the secret of navigation hangs on the next note.

line.dialogue: How do you complete the Open Frequency's song?

choices.text: Harmonize with the Scrapyard. Use the industrial noise, bending it into the new frequency. A practical, grounded resonance.
choices.outcome: You weave the grinding and pounding into the song. It's rough, functional, and stabilizes the area. The map's data is saved, but its song is now indelibly tied to industry and control. A useful, but not liberating, tool.
choices.description: Direct Malee to harness harmonic feedback using engineering

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.text: Sing a Song of Silence. Counter the cacophony with a still, pure tone that demands quiet and reveals hidden truths.
choices.outcome: A wave of calm silence rolls out. In the quiet, the inspector hears the merchant's threats, the people's hopes. The corrupt are exposed, the map's purpose is understood. The song heals divides but leaves the underlying system intact.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use singer voice and seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Chanida fails. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Unleash the Raw Frequency. Let the Lattice's unfiltered voice scream through the map, no matter the cost. A truth too powerful to be contained.
choices.outcome: A blinding cascade of light and sound. Resonator crystals shatter. Machinery fails. The map is consumed, but its data is etched into the Lattice itself, a public secret. The old ways of navigation are broken forever. The world's health begins a radical, dangerous recovery.
choices.description: The merchant takes the lead, employing market connections to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: the merchant's expertise pays off. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
the merchant overreaches. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of quiet. Towering shelves of crystal records, etched with sonic maps, disappear into a vaulted gloom. The air is cool, still, and carries the faint, clean hum of the Lattice's resonance field, channeled through the building's perfect acoustics.
May you have good health, Chanida. This focus... it's necessary. Every note recorded here is a lifeline for the floating cities.
It's a really good movie! I mean, look at this place! All this knowledge, just sitting here. I want to find something no one's hummed in a century!
He'll take very good care of her. By which I mean, the Tonal Orders guard their secrets like jealous spouses. Finding anything they don't want us to see? I wish you good health on *that* endeavor.
We should proceed systematically. The index indicated the Open Frequency research is in the 'Unverified Harmonics' wing. It's probably right, but that area is... less curated.
As you navigate the hushed aisles, a smooth voice cuts through the ambient hum.

Ah, seekers of the obscure! A pleasure. I'm a humble negotiator of... acoustic commodities. That wing you're heading toward? It holds fascinating, if unstable, data. I might have a cleaner copy of what you seek. For a consideration, of course.

lines_after.dialogue: A consideration? We seek understanding, not a transaction.

Understanding has its price. But, perhaps a gesture of goodwill. I heard a surface scavenger was brought in today, raving about a 'pure tone' he heard below. They probably have him in the annex, being... debriefed. His information is raw, but it might match your interests.
A scavenger who heard something new? That's the lead!

line.dialogue: The merchant smiles, his offer hanging in the quiet air.

choices.text: Politely decline the merchant and head directly to the 'Unverified Harmonics' wing.
choices.description: Search the restricted section's card catalog for entries marked with red ink.

line.dialogue: Here — three titles flagged, all checked out to the same patron twenty years ago. Same day they vanished.
Someone tore out the cards. Whoever was here before us didn't want these books found twice.

choices.text: Engage the merchant further, trying to discern what he truly knows about the Open Frequency map.
choices.description: Press your ear against the back wall of the stacks and listen for the whispering.

line.dialogue: You hear that? It's not the building settling. That's a voice — and it's saying *our names*.
Nothing but old pipes groaning. Either this place is haunted or the plumbing is — and honestly, both scare me.

choices.text: Take his tip and immediately seek out the detained surface scavenger in the annex.
choices.description: Ask Pichit what he meant by "this focus" — and why his hands won't stop trembling.

line.dialogue: I've been here before. As a child. I didn't remember until the lights went dim. Something happened to me in this room.
It's nothing — just cold. I'm fine. I'm *fine*. Don't ask me again.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the merchant's tip, you find a sealed observation chamber in the Archives' annex. Through a crystal pane, you see a weathered man—the scavenger—seated under the sterile glow of a resonator lamp.

I probably have said it a dozen times! It wasn't a ship tone, wasn't an Order chime. It was clean. A single, open frequency from a fissure due west of the Murmuring Spire. It... it *sang* back when I hummed near it.

An unmodulated resonance from the Lattice itself? That's probably right in line with the old Listeners' theories. But it's incredibly dangerous. An open frequency could destabilize a ship's crystal matrix.
He probably won't be coming with us to verify, I guess so. The Orders have him tagged now. His story is convenient for the merchant, though—drives up the value of any 'stable' maps.
But if it's real, it could be a new navigation point! A Singer could probably use it!
The truth often lies between the merchant's profit and the scavenger's peril. That's probably right. We need the raw data from the Archives to cross-reference his claim.

Returning to the main stacks, you locate the 'Unverified Harmonics' terminal. The data is chaotic, full of fragmented recordings and warnings. One file stands out: 'Frequency Map Theta-7: Unlocked Harmonic'. It's tagged with the same location the scavenger described.

lines_after.dialogue: 'Unlocked'. Not 'Open'. Semantics are everything here. This probably means someone already tried to chart it and failed.
The file has a suppression flag from the Tonal Orders. Accessing it will log our inquiry. They must have. They probably recorded it and then buried it.
So we look! What's the worst that could happen?
The worst is that this frequency is a key... or a lock. We need to understand which before we resonate with it.

line.dialogue: The terminal glows, awaiting a command. The scavenger's testimony and the buried file point to the same dangerous discovery.

choices.text: Access the file cautiously, downloading only the basic tonal notation for analysis.
choices.description: Calibrate the scanner to filter for unmodulated Lattice frequencies and sweep the sector again, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — a standing wave at 0.712 harmonic, exactly where the scavenger described. This is no debris signature.
Nothing but noise floor across three octaves. Either it's already collapsed or we're chasing ghosts in the data.

choices.text: Attempt to bypass the suppression flag to see the full, uncensored research notes and logs.
choices.description: Pull the scavenger aside and demand coordinates from the original sighting before he disappears, 15 words

line.dialogue: He just handed over timestamped nav logs without bargaining — either he's scared of what he saw or he's genuinely confused.
Gone. Slipped between the cargo modules while I was reaching for my credchip. That man did NOT want to go back out there.

choices.text: Not only access the file, but use the Archives' minor resonator to attempt a low-power simulation of the 'Open Frequency' right here.
choices.description: Chart the resonance vector on Chanida's nav display and plot a preliminary jump solution, 15 words

line.dialogue: If I overlay the wavefront gradient against our star charts — yes! It terminates at an uncharted system. We HAVE to jump.
The vector resolves to empty intergalactic void. Either the signal refracted

lines_before.dialogue: In a restricted annex of the Archives, the air itself seems to vibrate with suppressed secrets. The walls here are lined with silent, dormant resonance crystals.
This place... the acoustics are all wrong. It's designed to dampen sound, not enhance it. Why would the Tonal Orders build a library that mutes its own subject?

Because some frequencies aren't meant to be heard. Look at this ledger. 'Frequency 7-Alpha. Open Pathway to the Silent Choir.' It's been marked 'Restricted - Per the Concordance.' I'm no match for their bureaucracy, but this smells like a cover-up.
The Silent Choir ain't a place. It's what they call the Listeners who went too deep. My crew found a wreck once. No physical damage. Just... empty. Like the sound was sucked right out of 'em.
So the Open Frequency Map leads to a trap? Or a graveyard? In only five minutes of looking, we've found more questions than routes!

No. It leads to truth. The Lattice doesn't just respond to sound—it remembers it. These restricted logs... they're not just navigation hazards. They're records of a sound the Orders fear. A resonance that challenges their control.
A dangerous truth, my friend! Knowledge has a price, and some prices are paid in stability. The Orders maintain peace. Why rock the boat, or in our case, the floating city?

lines_after.dialogue: The argument hangs in the deadened air. From a high balcony, a senior Archivist watches your group, their face unreadable.
We've attracted attention. The kind that doesn't end with a fine.
Then we move quickly. The truth is here. We just have to listen for what they've tried to silence.

line.dialogue: How do you proceed with the forbidden research?

choices.text: Decipher the coded ledgers logically. (Use Arthit's analytical mind to find patterns in the redactions.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the resonant wall and hum the frequency Arthit identified.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The wall's vibrating back. There's a hollow chamber behind it — the map was pointing us inward, not upward.
Arthit — "Nothing. Either the frequency's decayed or the wall's been reinforced since the Choir was active.

choices.text: Search for physical clues. (Use Chanida's impulsiveness to find hidden compartments or discarded notes.)
choices.description: Grab the scavenger by the collar and demand to know what happened to the last people who followed this map.

line.dialogue: Scavenger — "Three went in last monsoon season. One came back. She stopped talking. Not because she couldn't — because she wouldn't.
Scavenger — "You think I keep a guestbook? I scavenge metal, not memoirs. Ask the walls if you want answers.

choices.text: Attempt to resonate with a dormant crystal. (Use Pichit's nascent Singer ability to 'read' the crystal's memory, risking detection.)
choices.description: Tell Chanida to destroy the Open Frequency Map before anyone else can follow it.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Tearing it now. But whoever drew this used resonance ink — the pattern might already be burned into our memory from looking at it.
Chanida — "I can't — the map's embedded in a resonance crystal. Shattering it would release the frequency pattern into the air around us.

lines_before.dialogue: The heart of the restricted annex. A single, massive crystal column dominates the room, its light faint. Archive guards are sealing the exits.
I just spoke with the Head Archivist. There's a deal on the table. Walk away from the Open Map, and your... indiscretion... in the archives will be forgotten. A profitable silence for all.
He's been married to profit before. We can't trust him.
The guards are armed with sonic dampeners. They're not here to arrest us. They're here to make sure we don't make a sound.
So this is the Tonal Orders' true face! Knowledge is only safe when they control it!
The crystal column... it's not a data store. It's a lock. And the Open Frequency Map is the key. It doesn't lead to a place on the Lattice. It leads to a truth buried *in* the Lattice.

The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a choice. A 'Concordance' to sacrifice a part of the world's song for stability. This crystal holds the echo of what was lost. The Map tells us how to wake it.
The Head Archivist's voice booms from above. 'The Concordance preserved us! That frequency is chaos! Unleash it, and you doom us all to a second Silencing!'

lines_after.dialogue: The room holds its breath. The crystal hums with latent power. The fate of the Open Frequency Map—and the secret it guards—rests on your next action.
We don't seek chaos. We seek the whole song. But are we ready to hear it?

line.dialogue: This is the climax. Do you activate the crystal with the Open Frequency?

choices.text: Stand down. Seal the knowledge. (Accept the Merchant's deal, ensuring the party's safety but entrenching the Orders' monopoly. The Map is lost.)
choices.description: Jam the guards' sonic dampeners with a frequency grenade before they activate the archive lockdown.

line.dialogue: The frequency cascade ripped through their dampeners like glass — now we hear everything they tried to silence.
The grenade bounced wrong and now every guard in the concourse is looking right at us.

choices.text: Steal the data and flee. (Use the Scavenger's knowledge to escape with the Map's coordinates, becoming fugitives with a dangerous truth.)
choices.description: Let the merchant broker his deal with the Head Archivist while you tail him through the restricted stacks.

line.dialogue: I never trusted him, but his greed walked us right past three security checkpoints they thought we'd never breach.
The Archivist doubled his price and sold our names to the Order — profit before loyalty, always.

choices.text: Resonate the crystal. Unleash the echo. (Pichit must Sing the Open Frequency, revealing the lost truth to all present, irrevocably changing the world's understanding of the Lattice.)
choices.description: Convince the scavenger to slice the archive's tonal catalog and expose what

line.dialogue: the scavenger makes it work. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The lattice has other plans. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: The Khrueang Market thrums with a thousand voices, a chaotic symphony that vibrates through the crystal walkways of the skycity. The air smells of spiced oils and ozone.
Ugh, this noise! It’s obvious that the Tonal Orders are hiding something. The price for a basic resonance chart has tripled since last season.
Obviously. Monopolies thrive on manufactured scarcity. They’re probably just sitting on a vault of the things, laughing.
We should be cautious. Open accusations here are… unwise. The Orders have ears everywhere.
Yet, within this noise, there is a pattern. A truth, waiting to be heard beneath the gossip.
A figure in ochre robes, a Listener Monk, stands apart, his head tilted as if straining to hear a single note in the storm.
The Lattice… its song is changing. It’s very clear that… forgive me. My duty binds my tongue.
Well, is anyone home in there? Spit it out! What’s it saying?

lines_after.dialogue: I… I cannot. Not here. The dissonance is too great. But… there is a place. A quieter frequency.
How convenient. A secret meeting. My favorite.
It could be a trap. The Orders do not look kindly on Listeners who speak out of turn.
Every path is a choice. We must decide which thread of this song to follow.

line.dialogue: The monk looks at you, Pichit, with pleading eyes. He gestures toward a quieter, curtained alleyway off the main bazaar.

choices.text: Follow the monk immediately. (Trust his plea.)
choices.description: Lean close to the harmonic lattice and hum a counter-frequency into the resonating crystal, 15 words

line.dialogue: Yes—there! You've stripped the masking overtone. Beneath it, a second signal pulses.
Ow! That just amplified the drone. Now my teeth are vibrating and everyone's staring.

choices.text: Demand he speak here and now. (Apply social pressure.)
choices.description: Signal Malee to short the acoustic relay with her copper wire while Arthit watches the guards, 15 words

line.dialogue: Relay's dead. Three seconds of true silence—listen, that's a voice beneath the hum, repeating coordinates.
The wire touched the wrong contact. Sparks, and now the Wardens are turning this way—run.

choices.text: Send Arthit to scout the alley first. (Exercise caution.)
choices.description: Grab Pichit's tuning fork and strike it against the marble floor to reveal the interference pattern, 15 words

line.dialogue: Beautiful. The standing waves just became visible in the dust—three hidden speakers, one behind each pillar.
That fork shattered. And the sound it made dying was... wrong

lines_before.dialogue: The curtained alley is marginally quieter, the market’s roar softened to a dull murmur. The monk wrings his hands.
Thank you. The Lattice’s song… it has developed a strain. A warning cry, buried in the harmonics. The Orders are silencing it in their charts.
I knew it! I’m gonna ask him… the head Chartwright, right to his face!
Chanida, no. You can ask. But you’ll get a polite lie and a mark on your manifest. We need proof.
Proof costs. Usually in blood or coin. I wanna ask you something, monk. Who else knows about this ‘strain’?
Before the monk can answer, a shadow falls across the alley entrance. A figure clad in scavenged resonator plating blocks the way.
Well, look what the resonance dragged in. A little birdie told me you lot were askin’ about forbidden frequencies.
We are exploring the unknown. The song belongs to no one, and to everyone.

lines_after.dialogue: Pretty words. My crew knows a few of those ‘unknown’ notes. Charts that’ll get your ship scuttled by the Orders. For a price, I can point you toward ‘em.
Or you could just rob us now and save us the negotiation.
Where’s the fun in that? I’m a businessman. You want answers? I got a source. Deep in the static zones.
No! Those are wild frequencies! The Lattice there is… unstable. You can’t ask him to guide you there!
Every path holds its own truth. And its own danger.

line.dialogue: The pirate smirks, tapping a jagged crystal resonator on his belt. The monk looks horrified. The market's hum presses in from all sides.

choices.text: Agree to the pirate's deal. (Gain a guide, but owe a debt.)
choices.description: Show the monk your Lattice-fragment and ask what the strain means, 15 words

line.dialogue: You carry a piece of the fracture itself — no wonder the song bleeds when you pass.
I cannot read corrupted resonance through a shard held by untrained hands. It screams only noise.

choices.text: Refuse, and try to get the coordinates from the monk instead. (Moral high ground, risky path.)
choices.description: Tell Malee you'll pay in coin — ask what she knows about the Chartwright's ledger

line.dialogue: Three hundred baht and I'll show you a shipping manifest that proves the Chartwright's been smuggling more than maps.
Coin's good, but not good enough for what you're fishing for. Come back when you've got leverage, not just money.

choices.text: Threaten to turn the pirate in to the Tonal Orders. (Bluff, with severe consequences if failed.)
choices.description: Grab Chanida's arm before she reaches the Chartwright's door and pull her aside

line.dialogue: Finally, someone with sense. Chanida, hear them out — the Chartwright feeds on eager young scholars who ask the wrong question too loudly.
Get your hands off me! I

lines_before.dialogue: In the lee of a towering spice rack, the Listener Monk's eyes dart nervously across the market's sea of faces. The cacophony of commerce is a smothering blanket.

You must listen, not just hear. The Lattice... its fundamental song is changing. A dissonance is growing beneath the Floating Cities. It's my dream job to decipher it, but now... the dream is a warning.
A warning of what? Another Silencing? He's right! The Tonal Orders have been acting weird, rerouting ships for 'maintenance'.
We need data, not rumors. But in this noise, precise tonal readings are impossible. We must find a quiet point to calibrate our resonators.
Quiet? Here? Good luck. Unless... the pirates. They know all the dead zones and illicit frequencies. The ones the Orders don't chart.
To navigate the truth, we must sometimes use unmapped paths. But approaching them is a risk.
As if summoned by the thought, a rough laugh cuts through the din. The Sky Pirate leans against a stall, cleaning a crystal shiv with a smirk.

lines_after.dialogue: The deal is struck in shadows, the exchange of information as tangible as goods. The Monk bows his head, conflicted but resolute.
Remember, the Lattice does not lie. It sings of pressure, of strain. Conserve your energy. The true descent is ahead.
Aye. And turn off your ship's running lights if you value your hull. The quiet spot ain't quiet for everyone.

line.dialogue: The Pirate offers a dangerous shortcut: a hidden, unstable frequency that will get you to the calibration point fast, but will drain your resonator and attract attention. How do you prepare?

choices.text: Trust the Monk's advice. Conserve the ship's energy fully, move slow and silent. (Stealth Approach)
choices.description: Tap the Lattice directly through your neural implant, filtering frequency bands by instinct alone.

line.dialogue: monk* — "There — beneath the carrier wave, a voice repeating coordinates. You heard it because you stopped trying to.
arthit* — "Your neural spikes are all over the spectrum. You're drowning in signal and calling it insight.

choices.text: Make a risky trade with the Pirate for a 'filter' crystal to mask your resonance signature. (Negotiate for Cover)
choices.description: Corner the pirate signal-slicer Vorn in the lower decks and trade him ration credits for his frequency maps.

line.dialogue: malee* — "Vorn talks when the credits are real. His charts show dead zones even the Lattice can't explain — that's our window.
malee* — "Vorn bolted the second he saw your face. Word travels fast down here — someone already warned him off.

choices.text: Use the unstable frequency at full power, betting speed will beat any pursuers. (Brute Force Sprint)
choices.description: Rig the array's phase discriminator to chanida's resonance pattern and sweep for the harmonic the monk described.

line.dialogue: the monk finds the key. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The gamble fails. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: Back at the market's heart, the data from the calibration is irrefutable. The Lattice's resonance is spiking erratically beneath the city's foundations. A crowd has gathered, sensing the tension.
The structural integrity... it's degrading. This isn't natural decay. The Tonal Orders' 'maintenance' looks more like deliberate sabotage.
Of course. They control the knowledge, so they control the panic. And the profit. I don't wanna see that anymore! Another city falling because of their greed.
We have to tell everyone! Now! Can I? Can I just shout it from the rooftops?

A truth delivered poorly is just noise. We must choose our frequency. The market listens to many voices—the Monk's reverence, the Pirate's opportunism, our own conviction. Which will carry the warning?
The Sky Pirate watches from the eaves, a hungry look in his eye. The Listener Monk steps forward, his hands trembling not with fear, but with purpose.
The song is a menu of truths. Some are palatable. This one is not. But it must be heard.

lines_after.dialogue: The market falls into a stunned silence, then erupts. Your choice ripples outwards, a new resonance altering the city's fate.
Every note we play changes the harmony. Today, we introduced a dissonance that may yet save the melody.
High above, the Lattice hums, a deep and waiting note. The subplot of the Listener's Warning has been answered, but the greater song is just beginning.

line.dialogue: You hold the proof. How do you reveal the Lattice's warning to Khrueang Market? The method will define the consequences.

choices.text: Let the Listener Monk announce it. His authority lends weight, but may be dismissed as mystical fear. (The Path of Reverence)
choices.description: Malee steps forward with leg resonance, ready to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
Malee loses control. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Use the Pirate's rumor network. It will spread fast and force the Orders' hand, but will cause chaos and panic. (The Path of Disruption)
choices.description: Chanida uses frequency mapping to decode the cryptic message near the merchant guilds

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The risk doesn't pay off. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: You, Pichit, step forward. Speak your truth directly, without filter. It's the hardest frequency to project, but the most honest. (The Path of the Singer)
choices.description: Have the monk risk using crystal bowls to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whispering Dawn' glides into the Silent Zone. The Lattice below, usually a shimmering sea of reactive crystal, lies dark and inert. The ambient hum of the world vanishes, replaced by a pressure on the eardrums.
Ugh. This quiet is worse than Malee’s morning lectures. It’s... thick. Like we’re swimming in it.
Complaining already? The Tonal Orders said this place was dead. Who would believe they’d actually tell the truth for once?
Sensors are flat. No harmonic feedback. Our resonator crystals are just... stones here. We are flying blind, Pichit.
A place where the world’s song has ended. Since that day we first heard of the Silent Zone, I’ve wondered... is it an absence, or a different kind of listening?
A distress chime, weak and distorted, scratches at the comms. A voice, reverent but frayed, cuts through the static.
Blessed silence... and yet, a curse. Please. Our skiff is crippled. The Stillness... it preys on the mind.
A Listener! Smiling happily at a rescue, are we? Let’s go! Maybe they know a way out of this muffled nightmare.

lines_after.dialogue: You dock with a small, ornate skiff. A Listener monk, robes tattered, greets you with a bow that seems more like a stagger.
Thank you. I am Kaelen. I came to study the Silence... but it studies you back. It whispers things the Lattice’s song once drowned out.
Lovely. So it’s haunted quiet. Just what we needed.
What does it whisper, Kaelen?

line.dialogue: The monk’s eyes dart to a data-slate clutched in his hands. He is clearly hiding something.

choices.line: Offer immediate aid. (Focus on the rescue, build trust.)
choices.description: Strike your resonator tuning fork against the obsidian floor and listen for returning harmonics.

line.dialogue: There—faint but present. The song isn't dead here, it's buried under something massive.
Nothing. Not even a dampened echo. Whatever silenced this place didn't just mute it—it consumed the resonance entirely.

choices.line: Press him gently about his research. (Seek knowledge, risk his reticence.)
choices.description: Follow the cracked pathway eastward where Pichit says the last Tonal choir stood before the silence.

line.dialogue: I can feel it under my feet—their final stance. They didn't flee. They sang until the silence took them too.
The path dissolves into rubble. Even the geography refuses to remember what happened here.

choices.line: Demand to know what he’s holding. (Confrontational, may startle him.)
choices.description: Ask Malee to hum the Forbidden Cadence she once studied, the one that cuts through void-silence.

line.dialogue: I never thought I'd use this. The notes sting my throat but—the air is *thinning*. Something is listening.
My voice cracks on the third interval. The silence swallows it so fast I

lines_before.dialogue: Kaelen reluctantly shares his slate. It shows fragmented sonographs of the Silent Zone’s ‘floor’—not the Lattice, but something beneath it, forming and dissolving in impossible patterns.
These are not geological readings. This is... conceptual resonance. Data shaped by belief. How well do you know her, Kaelen? The Lattice, I mean. To interpret this?
I thought I knew her song. But here... she is screaming in a voice we cannot hear. My own faith feels groundless.
Do you know what this is? It looks like a map! But a map to what?
Trouble. It’s always a map to trouble. Probably leads to a ‘friend’ with a plasma cutter and bad manners.
A violent shudder rocks the ship. The shriek of tearing metal fills the dead air. From the gloom, a jagged pirate vessel, bristling with crude resonance-spikes, latches on.
Well, well! A Listener rat and some fat merchant pigeons in the dead sky! I don’t have many friends, so I make my own introductions!
Sky pirates. Here? In a place that cripples ships...

lines_after.dialogue: Cripples *your* ships! We know the hidden frequencies, the cracks in the Silence! Now, hand over the monk and his pretty pictures!
No! This data... it proves the Groundless Movement is right! The Lattice isn’t natural! It’s a... a cage!
The Groundless? Those lunatics who want to shatter the cities’ foundations?
He doesn’t have many friends. Now he’s got pirates and radicals chasing him. Fantastic.

line.dialogue: The pirate leader leers through the breached hull, weapon raised. Kaelen clutches the slate to his chest.

choices.line: Fight the boarders. (Direct confrontation, protect the data.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the map's surface and let the conceptual readings bleed through your skin.

line.dialogue: * "The topology is rewriting my nerve endings — I can feel where the groundless begins, and it's already beneath us.
* "My hand went numb before I could parse a single layer. Whatever language this map speaks, it's not meant for flesh.

choices.line: Barricade and negotiate. (Use the pirate’s knowledge of the Zone as leverage.)
choices.description: Ask the monk to sing back the screaming note for note, matching its fury instead of flinching.

line.dialogue: * "I matched her voice and the map pulsed warm — she wasn't screaming in pain, she was screaming to be *heard*.
* "I tried to answer her, but my throat locked. Some grief refuses imitation. She knows I'm a stranger now.

choices.line: Surrender the slate, but plant a tracker. (Let the data go, follow the pirates to their source.)
choices.description: Let malee tear the map's bottom edge free and burn it — test whether trouble can be excised before you follow it.

line.dialogue: * "The edge caught fire and the ink *rearranged* — the map wants to be followed, which means we finally know it's afraid of something too.
* "It wouldn't burn. Not even scorch. Whatever this map is made of, it's already decided we belong to it.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves deeper into the Silent Zone. The unnatural quiet presses in, a physical weight. The Lattice beneath their feet is a dull, dead grey, reflecting no light, absorbing all sound.
I can hear my own heartbeat. It's too loud. Why is my own heartbeat too loud here?!
Because there's nothing else to listen to. No hum, no resonance, no distant song. Just... us. It's unnerving.
The Listener's map indicates a structure ahead. A monastery, perhaps. A place to study the silence.
To study the absence of a thing... what does that say about the thing itself, or the one studying?
Save the philosophy, Singer. This place gives me the creeps. My resonator crystals are cold as stone. Dead weight.
This was a Listening outpost... from that day the first reports of the Silence came in. We thought it was a new form of the Song. We were wrong.
Ahead, the ruins of a crystalline spire jut from the Lattice, its form twisted and melted, as if by a terrible, soundless force.

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk kneels before the ruined spire, his hands trembling as he touches the cold crystal.
The records here... they speak of a 'deliberate tuning.' A frequency meant to still the Lattice. The Tonal Orders would call it heresy. Who would believe that they might have caused The Silencing?
He looks up, his face pale. '...since that day, I have doubted everything.'

line.dialogue: The Monk reveals a hidden archive below the spire, but the entrance is unstable. The Sky Pirate spots salvageable, volatile crystal shards in the collapse.

choices.line: [Trust the Monk's Knowledge] Follow the Monk's careful path through the ancient supports.
choices.outcome: The party navigates safely. The Monk shares his truth, smiling happily at being believed.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the monastery wall and listen for vibration.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the stone. A rhythm, slow as tides. Something inside is still breathing.
Nothing. Just cold. The wall doesn't even return my warmth — it eats it.

choices.line: [Use Pirate Brute Force] Let the pirate blast a clear path with a small, controlled detonation.
choices.outcome: You get through quickly, but the noise—or lack of it—seems to draw attention from the deeper silence.
choices.description: Speak a name aloud into the emptiness and measure how long the echo lives.

line.dialogue: Seven seconds. The silence caught it, held it, then gave it back wrong — I heard it twice.
It died immediately. The emptiness swallowed it whole. Even sound refuses to linger here.

choices.line: [Send Pichit Alone] Use Pichit's innate sense to feel for the structurally sound path.
choices.outcome: Pichit succeeds, but the intense focus in the absolute quiet leaves him deeply shaken, hearing phantom frequencies.
choices.description: Follow the Listener's map but deliberately deviate three steps to the left.
