line.dialogue: The map shifts. The monastery repositions itself. It's not fixed in space — it's fixed to *us*.
Three steps and I lost sight of the structure entirely. It moved. Or we did. I'm no longer certain which.

lines_before.dialogue: The archive is a tomb of silence. Scrolls of hardened crystal lie untouched. At its center glows a single, pulsing node of black crystal—the source of the Zone's null-field.
Do you know what this is? It's not natural. It's a machine. A weapon. It's *creating* the Silence.
The Groundless movement... they preach that the Lattice is a cage. This could be their proof. Their ultimate tool for liberation.
Aren't you tired of secrets? I heard everything the monk said! The Orders built this? Then it's worth a fortune *and* a revolution! We crack it open!
No! Look at it! It's *eating* sound. What if breaking it just makes it hungrier? What if it spreads?
My life's work... was studying a lie. This device proves it. The true Song is out there, buried under this... this engineered quiet.
A choice between truth and stability. To shatter the quiet is to unleash an unknown song. To leave it is to live in a sanctioned lie.
The black node pulses, a void that seems to watch them. The Sky Pirate raises his tool, the Monk his hands in prayer, the party caught between.

lines_after.dialogue: The Silent Zone holds its breath. The consequences of their choice will resonate far beyond this dead place.
Why weren't you careful? This isn't just treasure or knowledge... it's the foundation of our world.
A deep, subsonic shudder runs through the Lattice. The choice has been made. The Silence reacts.

line.dialogue: The null-node must be dealt with. The Groundless would see it used. The Tonal Orders would bury it. The party must decide its fate.

choices.line: [Safeguard the Secret] Seal the archive. Protect the world from this dangerous truth, and from the Groundless.
choices.outcome: Stability is preserved, but the lie continues. The Monk remains, a doomed guardian. The Pirate leaves, disgruntled but paid off.
choices.description: Convince Malee to use mechanical repair and test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee hits a wall. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.line: [Harness the Silence] Work with the Groundless to carefully study the node, to control the 'quiet' as a tool.
choices.outcome: You gain a powerful, ambiguous weapon. The balance of power shifts. The Tonal Orders become your sworn enemies.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using unauthorized tones to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The resonance turns hostile. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.line: [Shatter the Node] Destroy the machine. Let the true Song of the Lattice, whatever it may be, return.
choices.outcome: A wave of raw, chaotic resonance erupts, scouring the Zone. The world's song changes forever. You are hailed as liberators or destroyers.
choices.description: Have the pirate risk using disruptor weapon to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the pirate's call. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow is a jagged crack in the floating island's underbelly. Inside, the air is cool and still, but every footstep, every whisper, multiplies into a complex, lingering chorus.
Listen... the way our breath resonates. This place remembers. It's not just rock; it's a recording.
A recording of what, precisely? Structural integrity scans are inconclusive. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Caution? Look at these carvings! This is pre-Silencing! Real history, not Tonal Order propaganda. Let's go deeper!
History usually means traps, curses, or things that want to eat you. But fine. If there's salvage, it beats another day in the sky markets.
A faint, rhythmic hum seems to emanate from the walls themselves, a low drone that wasn't there a moment ago.
You... you shouldn't be down here. The sounds get strange. My cousin went looking for old wire, said he heard... singing. From the walls. He hasn't been right since.

lines_after.dialogue: Singing from the walls... or an echo of something that passed through long ago?
A plausible hypothesis. The acoustics could preserve sonic imprints. We need a methodical survey. Can I see the menu of possible routes? The left tunnel seems more stable.
Menu? This isn't a tavern! The big chamber straight ahead is calling my name. Anywhere’s okay as long as we're moving!
I'll take 'places less likely to collapse.' So, not the one with the cracks. Can I have a menu of non-suicidal options?

line.dialogue: The path forks in a cavern glittering with faintly luminescent crystal dust.

choices.text: Take the left tunnel (Arthit's cautious route).
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the carved wall and hum a single sustained note.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "Yes! The stone *vibrates* — it's tuned to human resonance. This whole chamber is an instrument waiting to be played.
Pichit — "Nothing. Either the mechanism has decayed, or it was never meant for hands like ours.

choices.text: Head straight into the large central chamber (Chanida's impulse).

Chanida — "Wait, don't step there — that's a pressure plate! ...Too late. The floor is shifting.

choices.text: Examine the right wall with the strange cracks (Malee's suspicion).

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Remarkable. The return delay reveals a secondary cavity behind the north wall — hollow, roughly three meters deep. That's where we need to go.
Arthit — "The echo pattern is fragmented — too many porous surfaces. I can't distinguish a wall from a collapse zone. We're navigating blind.

lines_before.dialogue: The central chamber opens into a vast, cathedral-like space. In its center, half-buried in crystalline growths, lies the shattered hull of a Resonance Ship. Its resonator array is dark, but a ghostly, warbled melody hangs in the air.
The Echo of the Lost Ship... it's not a story. It's here. The Lattice hasn't consumed it; it's... cradling it.
Is that... a glow from the cockpit? Someone could be in there! We have to help!
Unwise. The sonic imprint is active and unstable. This is a phenomenon, not a rescue. Observe from a distance.
Observe the very shiny, very intact-looking navigation crystal still in its housing, you mean. That's a fortune just sitting there.
A shadow detaches from behind a stalagmite. A figure clad in patched Lattice-leather watches, a hand resting on a tool that could be a weapon.
You lot are loud as a hull breach. That wreck's been singing its death-song for decades. It's bad luck. My luck.
A surface scavenger. Their knowledge of local anomalies could be invaluable, but their territorial claims are often... violently enforced.

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal Orders would pay a pretty chime for the location of a pre-Silencing wreck. Don't let anyone know! You saw nothing. Turn around.
Or what? You'll hum us to death? That crystal's coming with us. Don't let him see you get twitchy, Arthit.
Forget the crystal! What if there's a survivor? That glow! We have to check. Don't let them see you hesitate!
The echo... it's strengthening. It wants something. Let's go inside the ship. Carefully. We need to understand the song.

line.dialogue: The scavenger tenses, the ghostly melody swells, and the wreck's cockpit pulses with faint light.

choices.text: Confront the scavenger. Secure the area first.
choices.description: Crawl through the shattered hull toward the cockpit glow, keeping your body flat against the deck plating.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "I can see her face through the cracked viewport — she's breathing, she's actually breathing in there.
Arthit — "The sonic imprint spiked when you moved — the hull just screamed, and now whatever's in there knows we're coming.

choices.text: Rush to the cockpit. Answer the call of the potential survivor.
choices.description: Deploy a resonance probe through the gap in the canopy to map the cockpit before anyone enters.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The probe confirms one life sign, faint but stable — and the navigation core is still drawing power, which should be impossible.
Malee — "You just fed the imprint a frequency to latch onto — that glow went from warm amber to red, and the probe's signal just died.

choices.text: Approach the central resonator. Try to harmonize with the ship's dying echo.
choices.description: Call out to the figure directly, voice first, hands visible, treating this as a rescue not a salvage.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "She turned her head — she looked right at me — she's confused but she's *there*, we have to get her out.
Pichit — "She pressed her hands against the glass and mouthed something — but the words that came through the hull weren't hers, and they weren't meant for us.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the Hollow, the party emerges into a vast, echoing cavern. At its center lies the skeletal remains of a Resonance Ship, fused into the cave wall as if it grew there. An oppressive, low hum vibrates the air.
Well. That's not ominous at all. A ship inside a mountain. I thought it was okay to expect ruins, not a tomb.
Look at the crystal growths on the hull! They're pulsing. This is it, the lost ship from the stories!
The structural integrity is... worrying. And that sound isn't natural. It's something to think about before we get any closer.
It's not just a tomb. It's a recording. The entire event of its crash... the final moments... might be trapped in the resonance of these crystals.
(Steps from a shadow, voice gruff) You shouldn't be here. This place... it remembers. And it doesn't like being remembered.
Who are you? What do you know about this ship?
Enough to stay away. The Silencing didn't just happen on the surface. Some things were... swallowed. This echo you're chasing? It's a wound.

lines_after.dialogue: The scavenger's warning hangs in the air as the ship's crystal core flares with a sickly light.
Oh, fantastic. It's awake. What do you think about a tactical retreat?
Too late. The acoustic feedback is forming a pattern. A memory loop.

line.dialogue: The central crystal begins to project shimmering, ghostly images of the ship's final crew, locked in a silent scream. The hum rises to a painful whine.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with the memory using a personal resonator. (Soften the echo)
choices.outcome: Pichit's careful tones soothe the frantic resonance, allowing the memory to play out as a sad history, not an attack.
choices.description: Press your palm against the pulsing crystal hull to feel the recording directly.

line.dialogue: The memory floods through me—this ship was *alive*, and something fed on its crew from the inside out.
Don't touch that! The crystal lattice just synced with your heartbeat—it's learning your rhythm now.

choices.text: Have the party scatter and disrupt the echo with counter-frequencies. (Break the loop)
choices.outcome: The chaotic sounds shatter the crystal's projection, but the backlash sends sharp sonic shards ricocheting through the cavern.
choices.description: Follow the groaning sound toward the ship's broken stern section.

line.dialogue: There—through the crack—I see bodies fused into the walls, mouths open, still screaming after all this time.
The floor gave way! Grab something—the lower decks are filled with those crystals and they're reaching for us!

choices.text: Step into the memory projection. Experience the crash firsthand. (Accept the echo)
choices.outcome: The past floods your senses, granting true understanding but risking your own mind being lost in the loop.
choices.description: Read the carved warnings aloud from the stone tablet near the entrance.

line.dialogue: It says 'the cargo remembers'—this wasn't a crash, it was a *prison*, and we just walked into the cell block.
You pronounced it wrong—the glyphs just lit up and the ship's lights are coming on, one deck at a time.

lines_before.dialogue: The cavern is alive with screaming light and sound. The ghostly ship shudders, its form solidifying from memory into a dangerous, resonant phantom. The very stone of the Hollow groans in sympathy.
(Shouting over the din) The wound is opening! It'll pull this whole island apart!
The core frequency is unstable! If it collapses, the harmonic shockwave could destabilize the Lattice for miles!
We have to do something! That ship, those people... I'm really hurting just feeling it. We can't let this be their end!
It's really worth seeing, isn't it? The true cost of the Silencing. A bunch of souls stuck on repeat. Now how do we turn it off?
We don't turn it off. We complete it. This echo is a story that never found its ending. We have to give it one.
(Rushing in from a tunnel, panicked) The city! The tremors are shaking the foundations! You have to stop this!
I really wonder... what song were they trying to sing when they fell? We need to sing the note they couldn't reach.

lines_after.dialogue: As the party acts, the phantom ship swells, its light burning away all shadows. The choice made here will heal the Hollow.
The air cracks with potential energy. This is the climax. The moment the echo is finally answered.

line.dialogue: The ship's crystal heart is a maelstrom of trapped energy. To resolve the echo, you must engage with its core directly, but the method is perilous.

choices.text: Shatter the core crystal with precise sonic strikes. (Destroy the memory)
choices.outcome: The echo is violently silenced. The immediate danger passes, but the Hollow's unique acoustics are lost forever, a piece of history erased.
choices.description: Override the harmonic stabilizers and channel your own resonance into the core frequency, 14 words

line.dialogue: The frequency is holding — I can feel it vibrating through every bone in my body!
It's too much — the frequency is tearing me apart from the inside out!

choices.text: Channel the energy safely into the surrounding Lattice. (Disperse the echo)
choices.outcome: The memory dissipates into a harmless background hum. The Hollow is saved, but the ship's story is diluted, its truth scattered.
choices.description: Reroute power from the scavenger's vessel to reinforce the collapsing harmonic field around the ship, 15 words

line.dialogue: The field is holding! That ship has a chance — we're not losing them today!
The power bleed is too fast — we gave everything and it still wasn't enough!

choices.text: Guide the echo to its natural conclusion, using your own resonance as a conduit. (Transcend the echo)
choices.outcome: You bear the full weight of the memory, allowing the lost souls to finally rest. The Hollow is permanently altered, imbued with a peaceful, permanent song of remembrance.
choices.description: Let the wound open fully and evacuate the ship's crew through the breach before it collapses entirely, 15 words

line.dialogue: They're through — every last soul! Now
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance ship 'Echo's Lament' glides into the edge of the Silent Zone. The familiar hum of its crystal resonators fades to nothing, replaced by a vacuum of sound that feels heavy, wrong.
All readings are dead. No harmonic feedback, no lattice resonance. It's like sailing into a wall of... nothing. Is everything under control, Pichit?
Control is an illusion here, Arthit. The Lattice has always spoken. I knew right away that this silence isn't an absence... it's a presence, standing right in front of us.
A presence of what? Profound disappointment? We're chasing rumors of an 'Open Frequency Map' in a place that eats sound. Brilliant.
That's why no one's claimed it! Look! Driftwood markers on that crystal spur. Someone's been here. A path.
Ahead, a jagged spire of dead, grey crystal rises from the inert Lattice. Tied to it is a derelict skiff, and a figure waves a tattered flag.
Ho there! Salvage rights! You're standing in front of my claim. Lost your song, have ya?

lines_after.dialogue: Name's Rourke. Sky's been unkind. My ship's resonator cracked in the quiet. I know hidden frequencies... for a price. Or you can try your luck in the silence.
We're not paying tolls to a stranded pirate. We have our own charts.
Charts are lies in the Silent Zone, girl. The map you seek? It's in the heart of this dead place. And the quiet... it gets inside your head.

line.dialogue: Rourke the sky pirate offers a deal for guidance, but his motives are unclear.

choices.line: [TRADE] Offer supplies to repair his resonator in exchange for directions.
choices.description: Trace the driftwood markers with your fingertips, reading their grain for residual lattice impressions

line.dialogue: Chanida — "There — the grain spirals counterclockwise. Someone mapped this place *against* the Lattice's flow. They weren't just surviving here, they were *hiding*.
Chanida — "Nothing. Just wood rot and salt. Whatever these markers meant, the Horizon has already digested them.

choices.line: [INTIMIDATE] Threaten to leave him stranded unless he shares what he knows freely.
choices.description: Broadcast a single pure tone into the silence and measure what the void returns

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The echo came back *fractured* — three distinct delays. We're not in empty space, we're inside something with walls we can't see. It's *listening*.
Arthit — "Total absorption. No reflection, no decay curve. The silence here isn't passive — it's *hungry*.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves deeper, the dead lattice crunching unnaturally underfoot. The world is a monochrome of grey crystal and sickly mist. A flicker of light appears ahead—a sheltered camp.
Travelers! In this awful place! Come, share my fire. The quiet chills the bones, doesn't it? I am Elara, a humble trade negotiator. What brings you here?
A search for understanding. This silence treats the world like a corpse. Why is it doing this to me... to us? To everything?
He's being philosophical. We're looking for a map. What's her personality like, this 'humble' trader alone in a soundless hellscape?
*Laughs smoothly* Direct! I appreciate that. I seek opportunity. Rumor spoke of untouched crystal seams. But this place... it hides its treasures well. A map, you say?
We should be cautious. Why are you treating me like this with such open hospitality? In my experience, nothing is free.
Because all guys like beautiful women, and all travelers in the Silent Zone like not going mad alone. I have information. You have... supplies. Let's negotiate.
Elara's eyes glint in the firelight. She produces a small, crystal-inset slate—a partial frequency log. It shows a path leading to a structure marked 'Archive' deep in the zone.

lines_after.dialogue: This is a copy. The original Open Frequency Map is supposed to be in that archive. It's a dangerous route. My price is simple: half of any non-cartographic valuables you find there.
Half?! That's robbery!
No, my dear. That's business. The alternative is finding the needle in this silent haystack by yourselves. Before the quiet... settles in for good.

line.dialogue: Elara offers a crucial clue to the archive's location, but her price is steep and her trustworthiness unknown.

choices.line: [AGREE] Accept her deal. Securing the map is the priority, profits can come later.
choices.description: Trade one of your silver compasses for the merchant's map of the outer corridors.

line.dialogue: * "Done. The silver was weighing me down anyway—and this map shows passages we never would've found.
* "He wants two compasses and our last lantern oil. I'd rather stumble blind than pay that price.

choices.line: [BARGAIN] Negotiate her down to a quarter share, leveraging your group's strength as protection for her future interests.

line.dialogue: * "You trade in relics swallowed by the silence—things the Stillness has digested and forgotten. I understand that hunger.
* "He clams up, eyes sliding past us. Whatever he's hunting here, he doesn't want witnesses to know its shape.

choices.line: [REFUSE] Reject the deal outright. You'll find the archive on your own, trusting Pichit's instincts and Chanida's scouting.

lines_before.dialogue: The unnatural quiet of the Silent Zone presses in, a physical weight on the ears. The Resonance Ship's hum has faded to a ghost of itself, crystals dimming.
The lattice here isn't just silent. It's dead. It's absorbing our sound, drinking it. Who would believe that?!
We need to find that pirate's 'hidden frequency' before our ship goes completely dark. I saw him smiling happily when he mentioned it, like he'd already won.
Caution. From that day the Silencing happened, places like this were born. We are in a wound in the world. Our charts are useless.
Yet, the Listeners teach that silence is not emptiness. It is a different kind of resonance. We must listen to what isn't there.

(Over a crackling, failing comms device) Still floating, eh? Bet your fancy Tonal charts are pretty wallpaper now. The map you want... it's in the merchant's head. He's been selling pieces of it for years.

(His voice emerges from the shadows near the observatory entrance) Please, don't be alarmed! I came seeking shelter. This place... it plays tricks on the mind.

lines_after.dialogue: So the pirate rats out the merchant, and the merchant looks like he's seen a ghost. A beautiful partnership.
He's terrified of something here. That fear is more real than any of his smiles.
The merchant's eyes dart toward the observatory's dark maw. A low, sub-audible thrum seems to vibrate up from the lattice beneath your feet.

line.dialogue: The merchant claims the observatory holds a 'Silent Tone' that can temporarily revive the lattice, but also that something inside 'watches.' Do you...

choices.text: Press the merchant for the exact frequency location first. (Diplomacy/Intimidation)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the dead lattice and push your own frequency outward, offering it like blood to a starving vein.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Something drank my voice like water — but underneath, I felt it: a pulse, buried deep, answering in a frequency I couldn't name.
Malee — "The lattice pulled everything I gave and gave nothing back — my ears rang with a silence that tasted like metal and old grief.

choices.text: Enter the observatory cautiously, using the ship's remaining power for light. (Stealth/Exploration)
choices.description: Unroll the pirate's frequency chart against the corridor wall and strike the tuning fork against each marked coordinate, listening for resonance.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "There — the third marker sang back, a note below hearing, felt in the teeth — the pirate's hidden frequency lives where sound becomes touch.
Chanida — "Every coordinate returns the same dead nothing — either the chart is a lie or whatever killed the lattice killed his frequency with it.

choices.text: Send a resonant pulse into the structure to 'wake it up' and see what responds. (Resonance Lore/Daring)
choices.description: Sit cross-legged in the dead zone, slow your breathing to the Listeners' resting rhythm, and wait for silence to show you what it

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The attempt backfires on the merchant. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the observatory, the silence is absolute. Your footsteps make no echo. The walls are smooth, polished crystal that reflects nothing.
Don't let them see you! Whatever the merchant feared... it's in here with us. The air is... watching.
There! The central chamber. I see a crystal core, but it's black. Like a hole. Let's go inside. We need that tone!
It's not a crystal. It's an absence. The Silent Zone isn't dead lattice... it's lattice that's been *eaten*. This is the mouth.
The Open Frequency Map... it wasn't just for navigation. It was a warning. This place consumes resonance. Our ship, our voices... our very souls if we linger.
The black core pulses faintly. From the shadows behind you, the Sky Pirate emerges, resonator pistol raised, with the trembling Merchant shoved ahead of him.
Enough poetry! The tone's in that black rock. Merchant, you're gonna sing it for us, or you get to feed the quiet first.
You fool! Forcing a tone here will rupture it! It will consume everything in a wave of permanent silence! The map was to avoid this, not exploit it!

lines_after.dialogue: He's right! The pirate's frequency is a detonator! Let's do it! We have to stop him!
This is the true discovery. Not a path, but a precipice. Our choice here will resonate far beyond this zone.
The pirate's finger tightens on the trigger. The black core begins to resonate in sympathy, a hungry vibration that makes your teeth ache. The final moment is now.

line.dialogue: The pirate is about to force the merchant to sing the destructive tone. The fate of the Silent Zone—and perhaps your ship's escape—hangs in the balance. Do you...

choices.text: Attack the pirate directly. Risky, but a clear solution. (Combat)
choices.description: Channel the Open Frequency Map into the absence, treating it as a receiver, 14 words

line.dialogue: The map wasn't navigation—it was a *key*. The absence is drinking the signal, unfolding like a flower made of silence.
I fed it the wrong harmonic and now it's *looking back*—the map is bleeding inverted coordinates, get OUT of my head—

choices.text: Sing a counter-frequency to soothe the core, using your own latent Singer ability. (High Risk/Resonance)
choices.description: Have Malee walk directly into the absence while the others maintain absolute silence, 15 words

line.dialogue: I stepped through and I'm still here—wherever *here* is. It's not empty. It's *full of everything that was never said*.
I opened my mouth to speak and the absence took my voice as payment—I'm choking on someone else's forgotten words—

choices.text: Convince the merchant to sing a *different* tone—one of sacrifice to seal the core, knowing it may cost him his voice forever. (Persuasion/Morality)
choices.description: Arthit fires a single shot into the crystal core to fracture the silence violently, 15 words

line.dialogue: The bullet stopped mid-air,
the merchant's resolve isn't enough. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens stretch out before you, terraces of crops swaying in the gentle wind. The air hums with the soft, rhythmic sounds of irrigation channels and rustling leaves.
Look at this place! So peaceful. I could just... float away.
Don't get too relaxed. Peaceful places usually have the most expensive produce. I bet they're gouging us on turnip prices.
We should stay focused. The Tonal Orders don't grant chart extensions for 'floating away.'
The rhythm here... it's different from the city's hum. I study the Lattice's song by myself, but this feels like a new verse.
Ah, travelers! Welcome. The wind-song today is quite profitable for melons. Can I offer you a sample? No one was helping me with the harvest, so I have extras.
The merchant speaks of profit, but listen... beneath the irrigation, the Lattice whispers of deeper currents. Can I share what I've heard?
We're listening. I have no one to help me understand these sounds either.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, the Listener speaks of whispers. Dangerous whispers, if you're not buying. The Tonal Orders prefer... quieter gardens.
So the 'peace' here is just a monopoly on silence. Typical.
There are rumors... of a movement. They say some wish to listen freely, without charts. They call themselves 'Groundless.'

line.dialogue: The monk's words hang in the air, mingling with the wind through the crops. The merchant's friendly smile has tightened.

choices.text: Ask the merchant about the Groundless rumors (Easy)
choices.outcome: The merchant deflects with a joke about 'unstable markets,' but his eyes dart nervously.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the ancient stone pillar and listen to its resonance.

line.dialogue: Pichit closes his eyes, fingers trembling against the moss-covered surface. "There's a melody trapped inside—faint, but it's been waiting here for centuries.
Pichit yanks his hand back, wincing. "Nothing but dead stone. Whatever song this place once carried, it's long gone silent.

choices.text: Press the monk for more details about the whispers (Medium)
choices.outcome: The monk hesitates, then describes a strange, dissonant hum from a lower terrace.
choices.description: Follow the faint humming sound drifting from beneath the twisted banyan roots.

line.dialogue: Malee drops to her knees, parting the curtain of roots with careful fingers. "Down here—a hollow chamber. Someone's been chanting recently, and recently means today.
Malee pushes through the roots only to find a collapsed rat tunnel. "Just wind through dead wood. I'm losing my edge out here in all this quiet.

choices.text: Ignore the tension and just enjoy the gardens (Easy)
choices.outcome: The party rests, but the peaceful atmosphere now feels watchful and strained.
choices.description: Signal the group to hold position while you scout the ridge where the wind patterns shift unnaturally.

line.dialogue: Arthit raises a closed fist, eyes locked on the ridge. "That breeze is circling, not blowing. Something up there is bending the air around itself—and it knows we're here.
Defeat. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the monk's lead, you descend to a lower, more secluded terrace. The air is still, the usual wind-song muted. Rows of crystalline growth-lamps glow softly.
Here. The dissonance is strongest. It's not in the Tonal Orders' charts. They sell the navigation rights at the guild halls, but this... this is free.
Free and unauthorized. We should turn off our resonators to conserve energy... and avoid drawing attention.
But listen! It's like a song trapped under glass. Can you make a u-turn in your beliefs, Monk? Is this what the Groundless hear?
Probably just faulty lamps. They sell the new growth-crystals at a premium, but the old ones hum when they decay. Turn off the lights to conserve the city's budget, they never do.
No... this is intentional. A pattern. Someone is using the garden's rhythm to mask a message. Turn off the lights in order to conserve... a secret.
You found it. I hoped you wouldn't. This terrace isn't for profit. It's for... other arrangements.
The Groundless meet here. They believe the Lattice's true song can guide anyone, without charts. My duty is to the Orders, but my heart... listens to this.

lines_after.dialogue: A faint, coordinated hum rises from the crystalline lamps, forming a brief, rebellious chord before fading.
That was a signal. We are now witnesses to an illegal gathering.
Illegal or just... true? The merchant knows. The monk knows. What do we do?
Knowledge has a price. Silence has a higher one. The Tonal Orders pay well for reports of dissonance.

line.dialogue: The merchant's calculating smile returns. The monk looks torn. The strange hum lingers in the air.

choices.text: Promise silence to the monk and merchant, leave quietly (Easy)
choices.outcome: You depart unseen, but carry the weight of an uncovered secret.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the wall where the dissonance pulses strongest. Hold still. Listen through bone.

line.dialogue: The vibration knows your name now. Whatever's behind this wall — it's been waiting for someone to *feel* it rather than just hear it.
Your hand flinched. The dissonance bit back — there's a frequency here that rejects living warmth. Pull away before it numbs you past the wrist.

choices.text: Ask to meet the Groundless, learn their message (Medium)
choices.outcome: The merchant arranges a risky, clandestine contact for later.
choices.description: Kill the resonator. Strip the signal clean. Let the raw sound beneath fill the corridor on its own terms.

line.dialogue: Off. You hear that? That's not feedback — that's a *voice*. Layered. Dozens of them, compressed into one thread. Someone broadcast themselves *into* the infrastructure.
Dead silence. Too dead — my ears are ringing and I can't tell if that's the resonator winding down or something underneath *replacing* the sound with nothing.

choices.text: Challenge the merchant, threaten to expose the terrace (Hard)

lines_before.dialogue: The tranquility of the gardens feels fragile now. The wind carries a new, discordant hum from the Lattice below—a faint, grinding sound that wasn't there before.
Did you hear that? It's like the whole garden is holding its breath.
The Lattice's song… it's changing. The natural harmonics are being overridden. What did you say you found in the lower terraces?
A smuggled resonance amplifier, disguised as a water pump. Someone's trying to broadcast a signal without the Tonal Orders noticing. How shall I put it? It's stupidly ambitious.
And dangerous. If the frequency is wrong, it could destabilize the city's foundations. We need to find who's responsible.
The Trade Negotiator was too eager to discuss crop yields. He was studying us, not the produce. What is he really selling here?
Ah, my friends! Enjoying the view? The air has a certain… charge to it today, wouldn't you say?

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant's smile doesn't reach his eyes. The monk shifts uncomfortably, his gaze fixed on the vibrating leaves of a nearby crystal fern.
Cut the chatter. What's the amplifier for? And how do you say 'treason against the sky' in merchant-speak?
Such accusations! I merely facilitate… exchanges. Could you repeat that question about the pump? I must have misheard.

line.dialogue: The merchant deflects, but his eyes keep darting to a locked storage shed. The monk seems to know more than he's saying. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Confront the merchant directly. Threaten to report him to the Tonal Orders.
choices.consequence: The merchant panics and reveals a partial truth, but his allies are warned.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to harness harmonic feedback using tonal knowledge

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit misreads the situation. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Appeal to the monk's duty. Ask him to listen to what the Lattice is trying to say.
choices.consequence: The monk, conflicted, reveals he's been recording the anomalous frequencies for the Groundless.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing frequency mapping to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida loses control. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Have Chanida create a diversion while Arthit picks the shed lock.
choices.consequence: You find the amplifier's control crystal, but you're discovered by Groundless sentries.
choices.description: Direct the monk to trace the anomalous signal using meditation

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Crystal bowls shatter in harmonic sympathy.
the monk hits a wall. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The shed reveals the truth: the amplifier is part of a network. The Groundless Movement isn't just whispering—they're preparing to shout. The Lattice below the gardens thrums with pent-up energy.
This isn't a protest. It's a resonance bomb. If they trigger it, the feedback could shatter Mae Rim's support crystals. Why couldn't you see this was suicide?
We didn't… we didn't know it would go this far! They just wanted their message heard! May I see your driver’s license? No, I mean… forgive me. I'm not thinking clearly.
Their 'message' is going to drop the whole city into the Lattice! Where's the merchant?
Gone. Took his profit and ran. Leaving the idealists to face the music. Literally. This plan is for the adventurous and the utterly insane.
The amplifier is synced to the garden's irrigation pulses. It's using the water flow as a conductor. We have to break the sequence.
A low, rising tone fills the air. The terraces begin to vibrate. Cracks spiderweb across flagstones. The Groundless members stand at the central terrace, hands linked, faces ecstatic and terrified.
A pity! The initial resonance would have been quite lucrative for salvage rights. But some investments must be cut loose.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant's escape glider disappears into the cloud layer. The core amplifier pulses with dangerous light. The monk is weeping at the edge, realizing what his studies have enabled.
We can still redirect the energy. But we have to choose where it goes—into the sky, or back into the earth. Each choice will write a different future for this place.
The calculations are too delicate. One mistake and we amplify the blast.

line.dialogue: The harmonic cascade is building to critical mass. You have seconds to intervene. What is the garden's true song?

choices.text: Overload the amplifier. Send the energy upward in a harmless sonic bloom.
choices.consequence: The gardens are saved, but the Groundless's cause is silenced forever. The Tonal Orders tighten control.
choices.description: Pichit uses resonant staff to test the prosthetic reaction near the water channels

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit overreaches. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Re-tune the frequency. Let it carry the Groundless's plea for freedom across the Lattice.
choices.consequence: Their message echoes through every city, sparking unrest. The gardens become a symbol, but stability is shattered.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to seek the dismissed truth, relying on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Channel the resonance downward. Try to heal the scarred Lattice beneath the city.
choices.consequence: You risk merging Mae Rim with the ground below. Success could reveal lost secrets; failure will doom everyone.
choices.description: The merchant volunteers to map the frequency corridors, leveraging negotiation

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the merchant. His trade connections deliver the right information.
Defeat. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow is cold and tastes of wet stone and ozone. Faint, phosphorescent fungi cling to the walls, casting a sickly blue light on the smooth, worked surfaces of pre-Silencing ruins.
Ahead, a natural stone archway opens into a vast cavern. Strange, harmonic echoes skitter across its expanse, sounding almost like distorted speech.
Whoa. Listen to that! The whole place is singing. (For) the adventurous, right, Pichit?
Or screaming. Hard to tell with echoes. Probably just the wind finding new ways to give me a headache.
The acoustics are... unstable. We should map our path. One wrong step, one loud noise, and we could bring the ceiling down.
It's more than instability. These echoes... they feel intentional. Like a memory the stone is trying to recall.
From a side passage, a figure emerges, robes blending with the shadows. It's the Listener Monk, the Listener monk. His eyes are wide, fixed on the cavern ahead.
You hear it too. The old song. The one my Order says we must not listen to... but my heart cannot ignore.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, fellow explorers! And a holy man! What a profitable—I mean, fortunate—encounter.
The Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for a map of these echo-patterns. But you know, you don’t need to share it with *them*. We could be partners.
This place is not for profit. It is for understanding. You need to love yourself... to hear its truth. Not barter it.
Love is fine, but resonance charts feed families. Just think on it.

line.dialogue: The Monk points deeper into The Hollow, where the echoes form a distinct, pulsing rhythm. The Merchant eyes a side-tunnel lined with crystalline deposits.

choices.text: Follow the Monk's lead toward the rhythmic echo. (Prioritize discovery.)
choices.description: Press your ear against the wet stone and follow the vibration deeper.

line.dialogue: The patterns are repeating — three pulses, silence, two pulses. It's language, not noise.
Great, now you've got cave water in your ear and we still don't know where we're going.

choices.text: Politely delay, and question the Merchant about the 'Groundless' rumors he might know. (Seek information.)
choices.description: Drop a stone and count the seconds before the echo dies.

line.dialogue: Point-eight seconds to the nearest wall. The passage narrows ahead — but it's passable.
That echo bounced sideways. There's a hollow space we can't see. Could be a pit.

choices.text: Suggest the party splits up to cover more ground. (Risk division for efficiency.)
choices.description: Hum a single sustained note and let the cave answer back.

line.dialogue: Did you hear that? It harmonized — the cave matched your pitch. It's
The attempt backfires on the monk. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: The chosen path leads to a chamber where the walls are inscribed with intricate, spiraling glyphs that glow faintly in response to the ambient echoes.
In the center lies a massive, cracked crystal plinth. The air hums with a low, dissonant frequency that sets teeth on edge.
The resonance is wrong. It's straining the local Lattice structure. We must be cautious.
Great. It comes with a side of impending geological catastrophe. My favorite.
Look! The glyphs are changing! They're reacting to us!
It's a recording... a final message. The dissonance is its pain.
The true sound of The Silencing... trapped here. My Order was right to fear it. (Don't) make me cry! To hear such sorrow...
A deep groan echoes through the chamber. From a crevice near the plinth, a figure stumbles out—a ragged man with the wild eyes of the Groundless.

lines_after.dialogue: You... you hear it too? The true song? The one that breaks the chains?
A Groundless sympathizer. See what listening gets you? I sprained my ankle just watching him crawl out of there.
The cities float on lies! The Lattice sings of freedom, but they mute it! You have to understand!
He's raving. But he also found a way in we didn't. That's worth something.
His truth is madness. My truth is duty. But here... they sound the same.

line.dialogue: The Groundless man points to a fragile-looking crystal conduit leading downward. The Merchant eyes the glowing glyphs as potential salvage. The dissonant hum is growing stronger.

choices.text: Attempt to stabilize the plinth's resonance using your ship's crystal harmonics. (Technical solution.)
choices.description: Focus on stabilizing the Lattice - maybe using their own resonance to counteract the strain

line.dialogue: Arthit speaks about the stabilization working
Arthit speaks about it not working

choices.text: Interrogate the Groundless man about the deeper tunnels and the source of the 'true song.' (Pursue the mystery.)
choices.description: Focus on the glyphs/message - trying to read them before they're lost

line.dialogue: Pichit or Chanida speaks about what they learn
They speak about losing the message

choices.text: Forcefully side with the Monk to record and then silence the dissonant frequency, adhering to Tonal Order doctrine. (Choose authority.)
choices.description: Focus on the dissonance - maybe trying to counter-harmonize or absorb it

line.dialogue: the merchant pushes through. His trade connections deliver the right information.
the merchant's resolve isn't enough. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: The passage opens into a vast, spherical chamber. Ancient machinery, all polished crystal and corroded metal, hums at its center. The air vibrates with a low, persistent tone.
This... this is a primary resonator. A tuning fork for the island itself. The Tonal Orders would kill to map this. He's only interested in its commercial value.
Kill is such a strong word! I'm interested in sustainable resource management. This could fund a dozen new trade routes. Lift it carefully if we're going to study it!
It's served with a side of world-altering power, is what it is. One wrong note and we turn this whole floating rock into gravel.
So let's play the right note! What does the Groundless data say? This could be their proof the Lattice can be lived with, not just sliced through.
The structural integrity is unknown. That machine is pre-Silencing. We have no idea what activating it will do. Thank you for your concern, Chanida, but we need a plan.
The Listeners spent centuries mapping natural resonance. This... this is artificial resonance. A song built, not found. What was it trying to say?

lines_after.dialogue: The chosen action sends a pulse through the chamber. Crystals flare with captured light, and ghostly holograms flicker to life—images of the world before The Silencing.
The Song of the World... they weren't just listening. They were conducting it. This is how they stabilized the continents. The Silencing... it was a dissonance. A wrong note played on a global scale.
Forget history! Look at the energy signature! This is a goldmine! We need to secure this before the Tonal Orders get wind of it.

line.dialogue: The ancient controls are active. The machine offers a choice: record the data, attempt to stabilize the local Lattice, or amplify the signal outwards.

choices.label: Record the Data (Easy)
choices.effect: Preserve the truth safely. The Groundless Movement gains crucial evidence, but the moment passes. The merchant is disappointed.
choices.description: Strike the resonator with your gauntlet and let the chamber decide what note survives, 15 words

line.dialogue: The walls are humming back — the Groundless just answered, and it *heard* us.
That wasn't a note. That was a scream. Everything down here just woke up wrong.

choices.label: Stabilize the Local Lattice (Medium)
choices.effect: Use the machine's purpose. The Hollow becomes a safe haven, but the energy surge might be detected by outside forces.
choices.description: Hold the resonator to your ear and listen for the Groundless before anyone plays it, 15 words

line.dialogue: You hear it too — the silence between the tones. That's where it *lives*.
No... you're not listening. You're *being listened to*. Put it down. Put it DOWN.

choices.label: Amplify the Signal (Hard)
choices.effect: Broadcast the discovery. Risks everything for immediate, widespread revelation. The Tonal Orders will certainly hear it.
choices.description: Hand the resonator to the merchant and say: then make it sustainable — what note pays without bleeding, 15 words

line.dialogue: Finally, someone speaks my language! The note that sustains is the note no one has to die for — *this* one.
Ah. Ah, no. I touched it and my fingers remember a life I never lived. This isn't commerce. This is *contagion*.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber shudders. The amplified signal or the stabilization pulse has drawn attention. The hum of Resonance Ships echoes through the stone above. The Tonal Orders have arrived.
Scanners show three vessels on approach. They're locking coordinates on our position. I really can't remember a protocol for this!
He complains a lot, but he's right. We've kicked the hornet's nest. That merchant's 'sustainable management' is about to become a hostile takeover.
Now, now, no need for alarm! I'm sure we can negotiate. They're reasonable businessmen... who have us cornered in a hole with their property.
Your negotiation works really well for getting us sold out! We fight. This is the proof the Groundless needs. We can't let them bury it again.
She is correct. My Order has hidden from this truth for generations. No more. The Lattice's true song is not a tool for control. It is a memory. It must be heard.
The machine is still active. It's a key. It can seal the Hollow, bury the truth deeper... or it can be tuned to a frequency that disrupts their ships' resonators. A dangerous, temporary shield.
Boots clatter in the upper tunnels. Orders are barked. The final choice must be made before the first soldier rounds the corner.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber rings with the consequence. Crystals shatter or blaze. The very stone of The Hollow groans in sympathy with the Lattice below.
Every note has an echo. Today, we chose what the world will hear tomorrow.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Orders are seconds away. Do you use the ancient machine to save the truth, or use it to make a stand?

choices.label: Collapse the Entrance (Easy)
choices.effect: Seal the Hollow. The truth is safe, but buried. The party escapes, but the Groundless subplot goes dormant, awaiting another chance.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with engineering to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
Malee is thwarted. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.label: Disrupt the Ships (Medium)
choices.effect: Fight back. The Order's ships are disabled, allowing escape with some data. A direct provocation; you are now hunted, but the Movement is ignited.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with Listener training to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
The risk doesn't pay off. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.label: Broadcast the Full Memory (Hard)
choices.effect: The climactic choice. The machine broadcasts the pre-Silencing world's song across the Lattice. Every Listener, every Singer hears it. Civilization is shaken, but you face the full, immediate wrath of the Orders.
choices.description: Direct the monk to map the frequency corridors using crystal bowls

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the monk overreaches. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The wind whispers through the terraced crops of Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, a soothing rhythm of rustling leaves and trickling irrigation channels.
Peace. Quiet. No city hum. I could almost forget the Lattice is right below us, waiting to swallow any fool who falls.
A necessary respite. Our supplies are low, and the gardens are a known neutral ground. We should be safe here.
Safe is boring! Look at those wind-chimes! I bet they sing a different song up close.
Every sound here is cultivated. The water's path, the crop's sway... it's a composed silence, not a natural one.
Ah, travelers! You look like individuals of refined taste. Seeking rest? Perhaps a trade? My prices are as fair as the view.
He's still single, isn't he? That overly-polished smile has 'lonely commission-hunter' written all over it.
Don't listen to that vulture. He'd sell you a map to your own grave if the crystal was bright enough.

lines_after.dialogue: Such harsh words from the dirt-crawler! I merely facilitate. For instance, I heard a curious tale... a lost Resonance Ship, its echo still humming in a nearby canyon.
A lost ship? With salvage? You have to see it!
A likely story to part fools from their coin. That's all, isn't it? A fabricated ghost story.
The echo's real. I've heard its broken song. But the one spinning the tale... he's standing right in front of you.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger and Merchant glare at each other, the peaceful atmosphere now charged. Pichit, the group looks to you.

choices.line: Ask the Merchant directly what he's selling. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Follow the water channel upstream to find its source before nightfall, 15 words

line.dialogue: The channel narrows beyond those stones — someone carved this path deliberately. We're not alone here.
The channel splits three ways and every path looks identical. We've wasted daylight chasing water.

choices.line: Press the Scavenger for details about the ship's location. (Intuition)
choices.description: Pluck one of the wind-chimes down to examine what material it's made from

line.dialogue: Bone. These aren't chimes at all — they're vertebrae strung on silk thread. Who hangs *this* in a garden?
It crumbled the moment I touched it. Whatever held these together rotted through seasons ago — now there's just dust on my hands.

choices.line: Suggest the party ignore both and focus on resupply. (Caution)
choices.description: Ask the gardener tending the eastern plot about who built this place

line.dialogue: She says the garden tends *itself* — she only comes to bury what dies. I don't think she's joking.
The gardener looked straight through me and kept pruning. Either she's deaf, or we're the ones who aren't really here.

lines_before.dialogue: Tension lingers like a bad note. The Scavenger, grudgingly impressed you didn't immediately buy the Merchant's story, gestures toward a secluded overlook.
You want proof? Come. Listen. But keep your voices down. The Gardens have ears, and not all of them belong to plants.
Oh, lovely. More clandestine nonsense. When did he get here, and become our tour guide?
Proceeding requires caution. Are you allergic to any medicine? Local pollen? We are in unknown terrain.
Will you relax? This is it! The mystery! You have to see it... or hear it, rather!
The wind's pattern is changing. It's collecting in that stone funnel... shaping itself.

lines_after.dialogue: At the overlook, the wind through a peculiar, ancient stone horn emits a low, mournful drone. Underneath it, a faint, repeating sequence of harmonic pulses.
The *Echo of the Morning Star*. That's its distress call, trapped in the stone. Been looping since it fell.
A recorded SOS. Charming. So a ship died. Ships die all the time. Why's this one special?
Because it didn't just crash. It was singing a forbidden route. A Singer's route. The Tonal Orders scuttled it.

line.dialogue: The implication hangs in the air, heavier than the drone. A ship destroyed for its knowledge. The Echo calls.

choices.line: Record the echo's pattern for the Listeners. (Scholarship)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to calibrate against the frequency, drawing on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Ask the Scavenger to lead you to the wreckage site. (Bargaining)
choices.description: Malee uses crystal prosthetic to seek the dismissed truth near the water channels

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
The risk doesn't pay off. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: Try to harmonize with the echo using your own resonance crystal. (Dangerous Resonance)
choices.description: Convince the merchant to use negotiation and follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the merchant pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the merchant hits a wall. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: The party returns to Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, the Trade Negotiator's smile tighter than before. The Surface Scavenger watches from the shadow of a windmill, distrust palpable.
Ah, my friends. You've seen... something, haven't you? The Scavenger's tales are wild, but profit is profit. I don't want people knowing my suppliers.
We saw the ghost-ship! Its resonance crystal is still pulsing! You have to see it!
Chanida, caution. The Tonal Orders would claim that crystal instantly. And the Scavenger... when did he arrive at the gardens?
Been here longer than you. That ship's echo... it's not just a crystal. It's a memory. The Silencing took more than cities. It took people.
Sentimental nonsense. It's a broken resonator on a dead ship. Salvage value, maybe. I don't want it complicating our charter.
But its sound... it was a lament. Not a navigation tone. A recording of loss. The Listeners would say we can sit with such sounds for as long as we want.
Philosophy doesn't pay tariffs. If you retrieve that crystal, I can... facilitate its discreet sale. To certain parties. Parties who don't want people finding out.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger approaches, his gaze fixed on Pichit. 'The ship's echo calls for a Singer. Or someone who listens truly. What do you harvest from this?'

choices.text: Harvest the crystal for the Negotiator. Profit clears debts.
choices.outcome: Secure funds, but betray the ship's memory.
choices.description: Press the scavenger for what she knows about the echo's true nature, offering trade goods as incentive, 15 words

line.dialogue: She's given us the frequency pattern — the crystal isn't resonating, it's *recording*. Someone is listening through it.
You think trinkets buy my silence? I've watched three crews die chasing that echo. Keep your goods and your questions.

choices.text: Study the echo with the Scavenger. Learn its story.
choices.outcome: Gain forbidden knowledge, attract Tonal Order attention.
choices.description: Sneak back to the ghost-ship alone tonight and attempt to extract the resonance crystal using Arthit's tonal fork, 15 words

line.dialogue: I felt it sing when the fork touched the housing — the crystal *wanted* to come with us. It remembers something.
The fork's vibration shattered the containment seal. The resonance is bleeding out — every spirit in this market just turned toward us.

choices.text: Let the echo fade. The past should rest.
choices.outcome: Honor the loss, but lose a powerful artifact.
choices.description: Ask the merchant to broker a meeting with the Tonal Orders and negotiate shared access to the crystal, 15 words

line.dialogue: The Orders agreed — conditional access, but they
Things don't go as planned. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_after.dialogue: The wind through the terraces carries a new tension. The party's choice ripples through the quiet gardens.
Whatever we decided, we've drawn eyes. The Negotiator's smile has vanished.
And the Scavenger is just standing right in front of the windmill, watching us leave. That's all, isn't it?
No. It's the beginning of something. The lattice remembers every choice.

lines_before.dialogue: Night in the Hanging Gardens. The party's campfire is the only light. The ghost-ship's distant, fading hum permeates the air. From that day we saw it, the gardens have felt different.
I can still hear it! A happy song, underneath the sad one! Who would believe that a ship could sing two tunes at once?
I don't believe in haunted harmonics. But I believe in the Tonal Order patrol ship that just docked above the terraces. They're here for the crystal.
Our choice has consequences. If we took the crystal, they'll seize it. If we didn't, they'll punish us for knowing. Since that day, we've been marked.
They don't care about the song. They care about control. The Listeners believed the lattice was alive. The Orders believe it's a tool.
My friends, a word. The patrol's captain... is smiling happily. That's the dangerous kind of smile. He believes you have what he wants.
And what do we believe? That a memory deserves silence? Or that a truth deserves a voice?
The patrol captain descends the garden path, his polished resonator humming a dominant, authoritative tone. The Scavenger melts into the crops. The Negotiator bows.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Order Captain stands before you. 'The echo of the lost ship is a navigational hazard. Its resonance is property of the Order. Demonstrate your belief.'

choices.text: Submit. Hand over any knowledge or crystal. Compliance ensures safety.
choices.outcome: Avoid conflict, but the echo's truth is erased.
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing tonal knowledge to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Pichit loses control. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Deceive. Claim the echo faded. Hide what you've learned.
choices.outcome: Risk exposure, protect the secret temporarily.
choices.description: Chanida steps forward with singer voice, ready to decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Chanida misreads the situation. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: Defy. Speak the ship's true song. Challenge the Order's monopoly.
choices.outcome: Incite confrontation, but broadcast the lost history.
choices.description: The scavenger uses crystal fragments to chart resonance pathways near the terraces

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the scavenger. The scavenger spots a resource others overlook.
the scavenger hits a wall. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_after.dialogue: The gardens hold their breath. The lattice itself seems to vibrate with the tension of the moment.
Whatever happens now, Mae Rim will remember. Our names will be in the reports.
Reports I don't want to read. But you can't hide from belief. It finds you.
I believe we did the right thing! Even if no one else does!
Belief is the first resonance. It shapes the lattice, from that day forward. Our echo now joins the others.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a deep, resonant tone that vibrates through your very bones. The massive crystal column plunges from the floating island's underbelly into the shimmering Lattice below, casting prismatic light across the observation deck.
Wow. You can feel the calm right in your chest. Makes you want to just... stand here.

Or it makes you a perfect target. You can't exactly sneak up on anyone when the whole place is broadcasting your heartbeat. They sell the new resonator dampeners at the market bazaar, but of course we can't afford them.
We're not here for dampeners. We're meeting a contact. Someone from the Groundless Movement. They claim to have information about irregular frequencies near the Spire's base.
Information that the Tonal Orders would pay dearly to suppress. To them, any sound not in their charts is heresy.
Excuse me? You the ones looking for Kavi? He's... not coming. Told me to tell you to turn off your primary resonators if you're going down there. To conserve energy. And attention.
Down where? Into the Lattice?
He didn't say. Just mumbled about 'the old truths' and scurried off. Look, I have to take my kids to school. Be careful. The Orders have patrols.

lines_after.dialogue: 'Turn off the lights to conserve energy.' How ominous. And helpful.
It is a standard stealth protocol for resonance ships. Muting your harmonic signature. But doing it near the Anchor's own tone is risky—you could lose stability.
A risk our contact implied was necessary. The Spire's calm is an illusion. It hides deeper vibrations.

line.dialogue: We need to investigate the base of the Spire, where it meets the Lattice. How should we approach?

choices.text: Follow the contact's advice. Mute our resonators and descend quietly.
choices.consequence: Stealthy, but unstable.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the damp stone wall and let the calm sink into your bones.

line.dialogue: Good — now you won't flinch when things get loud. Move.
You're standing there glowing like a lantern. Everyone in this tunnel knows exactly where we are.

choices.text: Keep resonators active but at low frequency. Maintain some stability while reducing our profile.
choices.consequence: Balanced approach.
choices.description: Signal Pichit to describe the contact while you scan the archway for surveillance threads.

line.dialogue: She'll be wearing a broken tonal cord around her left wrist. We approach only when she strikes the wall twice.
We're blind and walking in. This is how people vanish in the Underchord, Pichit. Speak up next time.

choices.text: Descend at full resonance. Let the Anchor's tone mask our own. Bold and simple.
choices.consequence: Loud, but harmonically secure.
choices.description: Draw a disruption spike from your belt and tap it softly against the floor, listening for hollow chambers below.

line.dialogue: You heard that? There's a room beneath us. That's where they're waiting.
The spike cracked. Now we've announced ourselves AND we've lost our only countermeasure. Brilliant.

lines_before.dialogue: Descending the service rigging along the Anchor Spire, the monolithic hum grows more physical, a pressure in the air. The Lattice's crystalline surface swirls like a frozen sea just below your boots.
Readings are... odd. There's a secondary frequency woven into the Anchor's tone. Faint, but deliberate. I'm afraid there'll be a problem if we don't identify the source.
Of course there will. When's the good news ever coming? It's always another hidden cult, another pirate scam, another—
Shhh! Movement! Over by the primary harmonic node!
A skiff, painted in makeshift camouflage, is moored to the Spire's crystal flank. Two figures are hastily attaching a resonator of unfamiliar design to the structure.
Almost got it! This little tweak'll have the whole Skyguard chasing ghosts. The Groundless'll love this.
Sky Pirates. And they're interfering with the Anchor. That could destabilize the entire island.
Well, look what drifted down! Customers? Or cargo? He winked at me, boss. Thinks he's charming.

lines_after.dialogue: You're coming with us. The Movement pays well for Singers. And your friends... well, the Lattice's always hungry.
Like hell we are!
Their device is designed to create a dissonant feedback pulse. It'll look like a natural fracture. Sabotage disguised as an accident.

line.dialogue: The pirates are outnumbered but armed. The sabotaging resonator is nearly active. What's our move?

choices.text: Direct assault. Use the Spire's overwhelming tone to mask our attack and overwhelm them.
choices.consequence: Loud and decisive.
choices.description: Rush toward the movement Chanida spotted near the primary harmonic node.

line.dialogue: I've got eyes on it — shifting like heat haze, but it's *there*, flickering between the node's resonant layers!
Nothing. Just calibration ghosts dancing in my visor — wait, something cold just passed *through* me.

choices.text: Sabotage their skiff. Cut off their escape, then negotiate or force a surrender.
choices.consequence: Strategic, but time-sensitive.
choices.description: Hold position and let Bandit finish his Skyg adjustment before making any move.

line.dialogue: Three more seconds... got it! The whole Skygarden lattice just lit up — whatever's hiding can't stay invisible now!
Almost had it — but the secondary frequency spiked and threw my calibration off by a full harmonic tier. Starting over.

choices.text: Use Pichit's innate ability. Attempt to 'Sing' a counter-frequency to disable their device without a fight.
choices.consequence: High risk, high reward.
choices.description: Feed Arthit's secondary frequency readings directly into the harmonic node to destabilize the intruder.

line.dialogue: Cross-referencing now... if I phase-match the secondary wave to the node's carrier, it should force whatever's piggybacking to manifest physically!
The feedback loop just screamed through three octaves — my ears are ringing and the node's gone dark. Whatever it was, it *wanted* us to try that.

lines_before.dialogue: The party ascends the final spiraling walkway of the Anchor Spire. The harmonic vibration is now a physical pressure, making the very air hum. Above, the control nexus glows.
Look! Sky pirates have the control platform surrounded. And... are those villagers with them?
The Groundless Movement. I told you their 'peaceful dissent' would graduate to holding a city hostage. They've finally closed the door on negotiation.
A siege at the heart of the harmonic stabilizer? If they disrupt the frequency, the entire island's flight could become unstable.
You don't understand! The Tonal Orders... they've been lying. This anchor doesn't just stabilize. It suppresses. I can't remember the old songs anymore, the real ones!
Heh. The 'monopoly' is worse than you think. They use this spire to drown out the natural frequencies we pirates use to navigate. They're making the Lattice silent on purpose.
A suppression field... masquerading as protection. To make everyone dependent on their charts. The ultimate control.
So do we fight the pirates or the system? My head's pounding from this tone!

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation leaves the air crackling with more than just resonance. The truth about the Spire hangs heavy, and the path forward is fraught with ideological peril.
Well, congratulations. We've all just graduated to being enemies of the state. The Tonal Orders will have felt that disruption.
We need to decide our next move before official reinforcements arrive. The spire's stability is now the question.

line.dialogue: The Groundless leader and the Pirate captain are at odds. The control console for the Anchor's harmonic output awaits. What is our principle?

choices.text: Side with the Groundless. Lower the anchor's output, freeing the natural frequencies but risking the city's stability.
choices.outcome: The villagers cheer. The suppressing hum fades, replaced by a chaotic chorus of long-lost Lattice sounds. The city shudders but holds.
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with lattice storms, ready to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
The resonance turns hostile. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.text: Side with the Pirates. Hijack the frequency, broadcasting a disruptive jam to cripple Tonal Order ships in the region.
choices.outcome: The pirates whoop. A screeching anti-frequency erupts from the spire, a weapon of chaos. Your ears ring with the violence of it.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using tonal knowledge to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Pichit hits a wall. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Seize control for yourselves. Reprogram the anchor to amplify Pichit's innate resonance, attempting a new, neutral harmonic.
choices.outcome: A gamble. The spire groans, then sings a pure, unfamiliar tone. It's beautiful, but untested. Everyone stares, uncertain if you've created a solution or a bigger problem.
choices.description: Ask the villager to map the frequency corridors, drawing on local knowledge

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the villager pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on the villager. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision reverberates through the Spire. Before the consequences can settle, a deafening, perfectly tuned chord shatters the air. A Tonal Order Dreadnought phases into view, its hull resonating with punitive authority.
Reinforcements. And not just any ship—the *Choir of Adjudication*. This is their highest authority. Where we live from this moment forward depends on the next five minutes.
I can smell their sanctimony from here. The perfume of absolute power. They'll silence this spire and everyone on it to keep their secrets.
They're hailing us. That's the Grand Resonator himself on the comm! Pichit, what do we do? Fight? Run? Talk?
You're the Singer. They fear you. That's why they sent the big gun. My crew's ready to scatter, but we'll follow a note that breaks theirs.
Please. You showed us the truth. Don't let them take it away again. We have nowhere to go if we're grounded.
This spire is now a fulcrum. On one side, the old silence. On the other... a world of dangerous, beautiful sound. I am the luckiest person in the world to have this choice.

The Grand Resonator's voice booms from the ship, amplified by the spire itself. 'Surrender the Singer. Deactivate the anomalous frequency. The Lattice must be ordered.' The Dreadnought's harmonic cannons begin to glow.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax resonates through history. The Anchor Spire's new song echoes across the floating cities, a signal that cannot be unheard.
Well. Wherever you're going to live next, it won't be anywhere the Tonal Orders have on a map. Congratulations.
The logistical ramifications are... immense. But the principle is set. The Resonance Chronicles have a new chapter.
That was amazing! And terrifying! I need to sit down. But first, let's get off this spire before it does something else dramatic.

line.dialogue: The Grand Resonator demands submission. The fate of the Groundless, the Pirates, and the truth about the Lattice hangs on your response. How do you answer the old order?

choices.text: SURRENDER. Step forward to protect your friends and the civilians. Let the Tonal Orders reclaim the spire and silence the truth.
choices.outcome: You are taken. The spire is 'corrected.' The Groundless are dispersed, the pirates hunted. The world remains ordered, silent, and safe. But a whisper of rebellion now exists because of you.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with scavenger instincts, ready to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee misreads the situation. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: DEFY. Rally everyone to overload the spire's resonator in a final, catastrophic burst of discord, destroying the anchor and the Dreadnought's targeting lock.
choices.outcome: A symphony of destruction. The spire shatters. The Dreadnought reels. You escape in the chaos, becoming a legend and a fugitive. The sky is now lawless, but free.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with unauthorized tones to question the Orders' silence

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
The lattice has other plans. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

choices.text: TRANSCEND. Use the spire as a microphone. Project your own pure resonance, not as a weapon, but as a new fundamental tone for the Lattice, challenging the Grand Resonator's very authority.
choices.outcome: You sing. The very fabric of the Lattice quivers in response. The Dreadnought's harmonic systems falter, not from damage, from awe. You don't win a battle; you start a revolution. The future is a song, and you have sung the first note.
choices.description: Direct the pirate to decode the tonal pattern using secret frequencies

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
A costly mistake by the pirate. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim sway gently in the high-altitude breeze. Terraced fields of luminous sky-rice hum with a soft, resonant frequency, their crystal-infused stalks catching the fading light.
A good place to rest. The lattice resonance here is... stable. Predictable.
Predictable means boring. And boring means no profit. Why are we here again?
Because Pichit insisted! He said he felt a 'pull' from the gardens. Where did you lose it, Pichit? Your common sense?
Not lost. Listening. The wind through these crops... it's not just a sound. It's a pattern. I'm glad to know this place still holds such purity.
A figure limps heavily along a higher terrace. It's a skycity resident, his right leg encased in a crude, buzzing harness of crystal and scrap metal.
You lot with the ship? Best move on. Gardens ain't safe after sundown. Pirates know the hidden frequencies here. They come to scavenge crystal.
A resonant prosthetic? That's Tonal Order tech. How did you...?

lines_after.dialogue: Did it myself. Order wouldn't help. Said my frequency alignment was 'unstable.' I'm dieting. On hope, mostly.
Let me guess. The pirates took your original leg and sold you the parts for this junk?
They mean it. They're serious. You hear that hum getting sharper? That's not the crops.

line.dialogue: The villager warns of imminent danger. The party must decide how to prepare.

choices.line: Fortify your position among the terraces using the natural resonance of the crops.
choices.description: Trace the wind's rhythm with your hands, letting the lattice resonance guide your fingers through the stalks

line.dialogue: Arthit — "There — the resonance folds beneath the third terrace. Something is breathing under the soil, and it remembers our names.
Arthit — "The pattern slipped through my fingers like water. Whatever speaks here, it does not want to be understood by hands alone.

choices.line: Attempt to trace the source of the sharpening hum to identify the pirate approach vector.
choices.description: Scatter a handful of brass coins into the wind and watch where the stalks catch them

line.dialogue: Malee — "Ha! Three coins caught at the eastern edge, two fell flat. The wind wants us walking east — and where the wind wants something, there's always something worth selling.
Malee — "Every coin fell straight down. No wind, no guidance, no profit. We're standing in a dead field listening to nothing, and I want my coins back.

choices.line: Follow the villager to a supposed safe hollow he knows, trusting his local knowledge.
choices.description: Stand perfectly still among the stalks

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The lattice has other plans. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Too late. Three figures drop from a camouflaged skiff onto the terrace above, their boots cracking the delicate irrigation channels. Their leader sports a resonator gauntlet crackling with stolen energy.
Well, look. Tourists. And old Limpy. You write down your last will yet, farmer? How do you write 'coward' in lattice-script?
You write it with your face in the dirt!
Chanida, no! Their resonator is overriding the garden's natural frequency. It's causing feedback in his prosthetic!
The villager cries out as his crystal leg shrieks and sparks, buckling under him. The pirates laugh.
That device... it's not just for navigation. You're scarring the Lattice itself.
Scars tell stories, singer. Ours say we take what we want. Could you please write it down for me? In loot.
He means what he says. That's a feedback pulser. It'll shatter every tuned crystal in a hundred paces, including the ones in our ship's engine.

lines_after.dialogue: Smart one. So you know the deal. Your ship's resonator core. Hand it over, or I write a new frequency across this whole garden. A silent one.
Don't! My boy... he's a Listener novice. He studies the patterns here. You'll destroy years of work!
The garden's song... it's a living record. How do you write it, if not by preserving it?

line.dialogue: The pirate leader is poised to trigger a devastating resonance pulse. The villager's son and the garden's ecological balance are at stake.

choices.line: Surrender the ship's resonator core. It will cripple your mobility but save the immediate area.
choices.description: Ask Malee to test the prosthetic reaction, drawing on leg resonance

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Have Chanida create a discordant shout to temporarily disrupt the pirate's gauntlet, creating an opening to disarm him.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus tonal knowledge on the terraces to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The gamble fails. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.
