choices.line: Attempt to harmonize with the garden's natural frequency, using your innate ability as a Singer to counter and absorb the pulse safely.
choices.description: The villager channels local knowledge toward the terraces, hoping to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
The attempt backfires on the villager. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_before.dialogue: The gentle afternoon light bathes the terraces. A low, resonant hum, distinct from the wind and water, pulses from the lower levels where the Lattice meets the island's roots.
So the 'pirate' left us a trail of crumbs. A hidden frequency to a hidden cache. How utterly predictable.
It could be a trap. The Tonal Orders monitor unauthorized resonances. If we trigger something, we'll have more than pirates to worry about.

But the prosthetic! That old farmer said his son's crystal leg stopped working after the last storm. The resonance is all wrong now. Do you wanna try it? Maybe we can find the right frequency down there and fix it!

The desire to help is a pure resonance... but Arthit is right. We are stepping between the pirate's greed and the Order's control. Can I take a break for a moment? To listen to what the Lattice here is truly saying?
(Approaching nervously) You're the ones asking about the old frequencies? My boy... he can't walk the terraces to tend the crops. That leg just whines. If you're going down to the roots... please.
He holds out a small, flawed resonance crystal—the core of the faulty prosthetic. It emits a faint, discordant pulse.

lines_after.dialogue: The descent into the island's underbelly is damp and cool. The Lattice here is thick, like frozen honey, humming with latent power.
Listen... it's not one song, but many. The roots, the water, the old foundations. All intertwined.
And one of those layers is artificial. A pirate beacon. It's close.

line.dialogue: The path forks at a massive, glowing root-node. One way vibrates with the pirate's crude signal. The other resonates with the deeper, natural rhythm of the gardens.

choices.text: Follow the pirate's signal. Find the cache quickly.
choices.outcome: You'll get the pirate's loot, but risk alerting their crew and corrupting the local resonance further.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using staff meditation to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Tune the prosthetic crystal to the natural rhythm first.
choices.outcome: A slower, safer path. You may heal the gardens' song and learn something, but the pirates might find you.
choices.description: Have Malee risk using engineering to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Defeat. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize both frequencies. Bridge the gap.
choices.outcome: A dangerous gamble. You could create a stable new resonance or trigger a catastrophic feedback loop.
choices.description: Convince the pirate to use intimidation and follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The resonance turns hostile. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

lines_before.dialogue: The cavern opens into a vast chamber where the Lattice has grown into beautiful, sound-conducting flowers. In the center lies a pirate cache—a jumble of old tech and resonance amplifiers.
Well, well! Look what the wind dropped in. You found our little nest egg. Hand over that tuning crystal you're holding, and maybe you walk away.
Your 'nest egg' is leaking resonance all over this garden. It's killing the crops. Why didn't you think about that before you set up shop?
He means means it! This place is really a great place to live! You're ruining it for a few scraps!
Living's for folks who can pay the Order's taxes. We're just collecting an alternative fee. Now, the crystal.
The amplifier is unstable. If we fight, the feedback could shatter this entire root system. The gardens would collapse.
There is another way. Every song can be rewritten. How do you write a new ending? With a different note.
Pichit holds the prosthetic crystal aloft. It glimmers, caught between the pirate's harsh signal, the garden's dying song, and his own latent ability.

lines_after.dialogue: A new chord rings out, clean and strong. The pirate amplifiers flicker and harmonize, their purpose rewritten. The Lattice flowers bloom brightly.
What did you...? The signal's gone pure. You can't... that's not how the charts work!
(From the entrance, his son walking beside him, the prosthetic glowing steadily) The song... it's back. It's whole.
Huh. So you *can* write a better tune. Don't get a big head about it.

line.dialogue: The stabilized resonance has created a permanent, safe haven in the roots—a secret the pirates have lost. What do you do with this new 'place'?

choices.text: Claim it for the Listeners. A new monastery to study the healed song.
choices.outcome: Secures knowledge and peace, but may draw the Tonal Orders' inquisitive—and jealous—gaze.
choices.description: Draw your blade and challenge the bandit directly, demanding he surrender the leaking resonance source.

line.dialogue: I told you this garden was bleeding resonance — now hand it over before I carve the rest of your nest egg out myself.
I told you this garden was bleeding resonance — but my footwork's rustier than I thought, and his knife found my ribs first.

choices.text: Give it to the skycity residents. A protected grove to ensure their harvest.
choices.outcome: Strengthens the community, creating a loyal haven, but the secret will be harder to keep.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to sing a stabilizing chord while you circle behind the bandit through the orchid rows.

line.dialogue: The garden *is* a great place to harmonize — and while he was busy covering his ears from my chord, you had him cold from behind.
The garden *is* a great place to harmonize — but I hit a sour note and the resonance feedback knocked us both flat before I could finish the phrase.

choices.text: Leave it unclaimed. Let the garden's song belong only to itself.
choices.outcome: The purest outcome, preserving the resonance's independence. But pirates or the Order may eventually find and corrupt it again.
choices.description: Offer the bandit a cut of whatever the resonance source is worth if he lets you examine it first.

line.dialogue: Living's for folks who can pay the Order's taxes — but a man who *deals*? That's someone I can breathe alongside. Show me what it does.
Living's for

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim sway gently in the high-altitude breeze. Terraced fields of luminous sky-rice and singing gourds create a patchwork of green and silver down the floating island's edge.
Wind-chimes made from old resonator crystals hang from wooden frames, their tones harmonizing with the rustle of crops. It's peaceful—almost unnervingly so.
Finally! A place where we can breathe without some Tonal Order bureaucrat breathing down our necks. Look at this view!
The isolation is concerning. We're exposed here. The gardens are too quiet—it feels staged.
Of course it's staged. Everything up here is cultivated. Even the 'wild' flowers are probably accounting for someone's quarterly yield.
The rhythm of the water channels... it's still in my memory. My grandmother's village had irrigation songs like this. How shall I put it? It feels like a memory of ground that never existed.
A figure emerges from between rows of tall, whispering grain. They're clad in patched leathers and carry tools of unfamiliar design—a Surface Scavenger.
You don't smell like gardeners. Or traders. What's your business in the Gardens?

lines_after.dialogue: The Groundless say we live near each other in spirit, all floating on the same uncertain sea. But you Sky-City folk... you've forgotten what's below.
Below? You mean the Lattice surface? Is that even survivable?
Survivable? It's where we live. While you drift up here, eating pretty rice, we're down there pulling the real world from the crystal.
You've seen the surface directly? Not through resonator views or charts?
Seen it, walked it, listened to its true song. Not the sanitized frequencies the Orders sell you.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger eyes your party with a mix of suspicion and curiosity. They haven't called for guards yet, but their hand rests near a tool that could be a weapon. How do you engage?

choices.text: Offer trade goods from your supplies as a gesture of goodwill.
choices.description: Trace the water channel's rhythm upstream to find its mechanical source beneath the tiles.

line.dialogue: Here — beneath this grating. Someone is pumping water from below. This entire garden runs on buried machinery.
The rhythm breaks here. Either the channel branches underground or... I've been hearing my own heartbeat this whole time.

choices.text: Ask specifically about the 'true song' of the Lattice they mentioned.
choices.description: Grab a wind-chime and hold it still, listening for voices carried on the draft behind it.

line.dialogue: You heard it too. That's not wind. Someone is speaking through the hollow tubes — words, reversed, playing on a loop.
Just metal and air. I swear though, when we first arrived, the chimes were saying something. They've gone silent now that we're listening.

choices.text: Explain you're just travelers resting, showing empty hands and non-threatening posture.
choices.description: Scout the garden's perimeter wall for

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the scavenger. Surface knowledge reveals a safe path.
the scavenger hits a wall. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: Before the party can fully process the Scavenger's words, a harsh mechanical whine cuts through the garden's serenity. The wind-chimes rattle in discord.
A Resonance skiff—jagged and modified with scavenged parts—descends through the mist between terraces. Sky Pirates.
Well, look what's ripe for pickin'! A nice little gathering. Don't mind us—we're just here for the seasonal harvest.
Pirates. Their resonator is tuned to a disruptive frequency. It's scrambling the ambient harmony.
Kratok's crew. They've been hitting isolated gardens for weeks. Stealing resonance-crops and anyone who can't fight back.
You look run down, pirate. Hard season for honest thievery?
Honest? Hah! Nothing honest 'bout floating up here while others scrape below. The Groundless got it right—everything's falling eventually.
They're Groundless sympathizers? Using the movement as cover for raids?

lines_after.dialogue: Sympathizers? We're practitioners! Taking what's owed from those who built their cities on stolen frequencies. Aren't you tired of their rules?
Aren't you tired of violence as your first language? When I was younger, I thought pirates were just freedom fighters. Now I see you're just another kind of cage.
They pervert the message. The true Groundless seek connection with the surface, not petty theft. But their disruption might reveal something... I'll have a look at their skiff's resonator logs.
You'll have a look at nothin'! We're taking the luminous rice stores and that fancy equipment your 'traveler' friends are carrying. Unless you want to make this musical.
Two more pirates drop from the skiff, their boots crushing delicate crops. The Scavenger tenses, calculating odds. The peaceful garden has become a battlefield.

line.dialogue: The pirates are armed and their skiff's disruptor is weakening the local resonance field. The Scavenger is ready to fight but outnumbered. What's your approach?

choices.text: Create a diversion using the garden's irrigation system to cover an escape.
choices.description: Signal Arthit to overload their resonator while you stall for time, 15 words

line.dialogue: Frequency collapsed — their resonator just fried itself. They're deaf to their own coordinate network now.
The overload backfed into our array. I've burned out our tuning fork trying to disrupt theirs.

choices.text: Attempt to reason with the pirates, appealing to their supposed Groundless ideals.
choices.description: Draw Malee's machete and challenge the bandit leader to single combat for the harvest, 15 words

line.dialogue: Clean cut. He'll think twice before raiding a garden that bites back. Take his resonator as proof.
You swung wide and he read it. Now he's got my blade and our crop — both gone.

choices.text: Challenge their leader to a resonance duel—a contest of pure sound manipulation.
choices.description: Offer the scavenger double rations to turn informant and reveal Kratok's camp location, 15 words

line.dialogue: Kratok camps at the dead orchard north of the ridge. Three guards, one resonator, and they rotate at dusk.
You think rations buy loyalty? Kratok pays in resonator shards. I'm walking back to him with your offer.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens grow quiet as dusk settles. The terraces are bathed in amber light, but the air feels charged—like the calm before a storm.
You lot still here? I have work to do. Can't babysit surface-newbies all night.
We're not leaving until we understand what's happening down there. Those tremors weren't natural.
Don't change the subject! You've been skittish since we arrived. What aren't you telling us about the Lattice here?
The resonance patterns are… unstable. If the Groundless are trying to amplify something, they could fracture the entire terrace foundation.
The soil remembers. I can feel it—a song buried deep, waiting to be heard again. Can you promise me you'll help us listen?
Promises are cheap. But… fine. There's an old Listener shrine below the third terrace. That's where the vibrations are strongest.

lines_after.dialogue: The party descends to the lower terrace. Carved into the rock face is a small, crystalline grotto—once a place of meditation, now humming with unnatural energy.
These resonance crystals… they've been tampered with. Someone's trying to reroute the Lattice's natural frequencies.
Great. So we're standing on a giant tuning fork about to snap.

line.dialogue: The grotto's central crystal pulses erratically. Three harmonic conduits feed into it—each vibrating at a different pitch.

choices.text: Stabilize the lowest frequency (Grounding rhythm)
choices.description: Grab the scavenger's arm and demand to see what they've been hiding in the shed, 15 words

line.dialogue: Your hands are shaking — show us what's in there before it shakes itself apart.
Touch me again and you'll be pulling those fingers out of the irrigation grate.

choices.text: Align the middle frequency (Balance chant)
choices.description: Kneel and press your palm flat against the cracked soil to feel the resonance yourself

line.dialogue: There — beneath us, something is *singing*. The frequency matches the Groundless emergence signatures.
Your face just went white. That's not hesitation, is it? That's you feeling what I felt.

choices.text: Amplify the highest frequency (Riskier, but might reveal the source)
choices.description: Pull out the rusted tuning fork from your pack and strike it against the ground

line.dialogue: The harmonics are splitting — two distinct voices, not one. The soil remembers something we don't.
You idiot — you just rang the dinner bell. Whatever's down there just woke up hungry.

lines_before.dialogue: The crystal's light flares violently. From the shadows, figures emerge—Groundless adherents, their robes dusted with Lattice-shards. At their lead stands a Sky Pirate captain, grinning.
(Oh), you're here? Perfect. We've talked about this before—people like you always stick your noses where they don't belong.
You're working with the Groundless? To do what—collapse the gardens?
Collapse? No. We're going to wake the Lattice. Make it sing like it did before the Silencing. And this little shrine is our conductor.
I've never understood this hunger to force a song. True resonance can't be commanded—it must be heard.
Philosophy later. They've rigged the crystal to overload. If it goes critical, it'll take the terraces with it.
The pirate's ship is anchored just below the edge. They're planning to ride the resonance wave out. We have to disrupt the harmonic lock before they complete the sequence.

lines_after.dialogue: The air shatters into dissonance. Cracks race across the terrace stones. Somewhere below, the Lattice groans—a deep, wounded sound.
You've got one shot! Hit the right frequency, or we all go groundside—permanently!

line.dialogue: The central crystal is moments from catastrophic resonance. The Groundless chant, the pirate laughs, and the world holds its breath.

choices.text: Counter with a Listener's lullaby (Suppress the vibration)
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with tattooed routes to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Arthit makes it work. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
The lattice has other plans. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Harmonize with the pirate's frequency (Hijack their control)
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to question the Orders' silence, leveraging monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Pichit. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The resonance turns hostile. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Sing the forgotten root-note (Dangerous—could either heal or shatter everything)
choices.description: The pirate takes the lead, employing disruptor weapon to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends into the Hollow, a cavernous silence broken only by the drip of water and the distant hum of the Lattice far above. Strange, geometric ruins line the walls, their surfaces smooth and resonant.
Watch your step. The acoustics here are... unstable. A wrong frequency could bring the ceiling down.
Look at this! Intact pre-Silencing script! This could rewrite everything we know!
Or get us killed by the Tonal Orders for 'unauthorized archaeology.' That’s probably right.
The silence here isn't empty. It's waiting. You can sit and listen for as long as you want, and still not hear all its layers.
My girlfriend gets jealous when I get this obsessed. But she’s not here, and this is too big to ignore!
A sharp, discordant scrape echoes from a side tunnel. The party freezes.
Well, well. Look what the echo dragged in. Lost, are ya? Or just stupid enough to wander into our claim?

lines_after.dialogue: Sky pirates. I guess so. Of course they'd find the one place the Orders haven't mapped.
We know the hidden frequencies here, see? The ones that make the stone sing. You're trespassing on our concert hall.
We mean no conflict. We're merely researchers.

line.dialogue: The pirate leader, a woman with a resonator grafted to her forearm, gestures with a crystalline blade. Her crew emerges from the shadows.

choices.line: Stand your ground. (Intimidate)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to harness harmonic feedback, drawing on unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
The resonance turns hostile. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Attempt to negotiate passage. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to decode the cryptic message, drawing on staff meditation

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The lattice has other plans. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.line: Withdraw to find another route. (Stealth)
choices.description: The pirate steps forward with smuggling routes, ready to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: the pirate finds the key. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The lattice has other plans. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_before.dialogue: Past the pirate skirmish, the cavern opens into a vast chamber. A shattered crystal spire dominates the center, its base glowing with a soft, unstable light.
Incredible. A natural Lattice resonator... and it's damaged. The energy bleed is catastrophic. We must be careful.
Careful? This is a goldmine. They sell fragments of stuff like this for a fortune at the grand bazaar in the Spire-City. If we could stabilize a piece...
Forget selling it! Look at the inscriptions around the base. This isn't just a power source. It's a... memory crystal.
A recording of the world before the Silencing. The ultimate history.
A soft chant echoes. A lone figure in Listener robes kneels before the spire, hands pressed against the crystal.
You should not be here. The song is... pained. It cries out in a frequency I do not know.
The bleed is worsening. We should turn off the secondary resonators to conserve the core's energy. Or at least try to dampen the feedback loop.

lines_after.dialogue: Turn off the lights to conserve energy, yes. But this is no simple lamp. To silence any part of its song may erase the memory forever.
Or cause it to explode. Can you make a u-turn on this? Is there a safe path to the data?
I... do not know. My duty is to listen, not to intervene. But the song is wrong. It speaks of a limb that does not exist, a phantom resonance... like a prosthetic made of pure tone.

The monk's words hang in the air as the crystal spire pulses erratically, casting jagged shadows. The subplot of the Resonant Prosthetic flickers in Pichit's mind—a legend of ancient healing now echoing in this broken place.

line.dialogue: The spire's light grows volatile, thrumming with dangerous power. The memory within is at risk.

choices.line: Help the Monk attempt a calming ritual. (Lore)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the resonating crystal and open yourself to whatever frequencies pour through.

line.dialogue: The harmonics are layered—decades of accumulated resonance, each frequency a different voice from before the Silencing.
The feedback hit me like a wall of screaming glass—I've temporarily deafened myself to Lattice frequencies entirely.

choices.line: Have Arthit try to surgically dampen the energy bleed. (Precision)
choices.description: Override the group's arguments and begin carefully photographing the inscriptions before anything destabilizes the chamber.

line.dialogue: Smart move—these carvings reference resonance patterns I've never seen documented in any surviving archive.
The crystal's pulse is interfering with every capture mechanism—we're losing the inscriptions to static with each passing second.

choices.line: Let Chanida try to directly interface with the memory crystal. (Risk)
choices.description: Side with Malee—extract a small fragment now and secure the profit before debating what the discovery means.

line.dialogue: Finally, someone with practical sense—that fragment alone could fund our operations for a year.
The fragment cracked wrong—what we pulled is inert dust, and the vibration from extraction may have damaged the larger piece.

lines_before.dialogue: The party pushes deeper into The Hollow. The air grows colder, and the echoes take on a life of their own—whispering fragments of forgotten conversations.
Nah, nah. You don't need to follow that monk's mumblin'. The real treasure's down this side-tunnel. We've talked about this before—trust the pirates who know the hidden frequencies.
And by 'treasure,' you mean something shiny you can sell before you get caught? I'm such a lucky gal, stuck between a liar and a zealot.
Please, listen. This chamber... it holds a resonance map. A true one, not the Tonal Orders' lies. But its frequency is unstable. We're talked before of the risks.
Unstable sounds fun! Let's see what it does! No, no, wait—Arthit's giving me the 'this is a terrible idea' look.
Because it is. That crystal formation is pulsing erratically. If it's a map, it could be a key... or a trap that brings this whole cave down on us.
Every whisper here is a choice. Do we follow the pirate's greed, the monk's faith, or the stone's own story?
At the chamber's heart lies a massive, flawed crystal. Inside, shadows move—a recorded echo of the pre-Silencing world. The pirate's prosthetic leg hums in sympathy with it.

line.dialogue: The unstable crystal map glows. How do we interact with it?

choices.line: Use the pirate's prosthetic as a resonator to stabilize it.
choices.consequence: The pirate's hidden frequency knowledge safely channels the energy. The map clarifies, revealing a safe path forward.
choices.description: Touch the crystal's surface with your bare palm, feeling for its resonance.

line.dialogue: Wait—yes! You feel it too. The vibration is... it's almost like a heartbeat. Careful, now.
No! Your hand—it's pulled the resonance inward. The crystal is destabilizing faster than I feared!

choices.line: Have the monk chant a grounding harmonic.
choices.consequence: The monk's voice steadies the crystal, but the effort drains him. The map shows the truth, but also draws unwanted attention from the cave's deeper echoes.
choices.description: Follow the bandit's lead and search for loose gems along the chamber walls.

line.dialogue: See? Now THIS is practical. Forget the mumbo jumbo—grab what's loose and let's move.
Ah, that one's cracked clean through. You're holding dust, friend. Should've listened to the monk after all.

choices.line: Let Chanida tap it directly with her natural resonance.
choices.consequence: Raw, untrained power floods the chamber. The map projects vividly, but the feedback shatters smaller crystals and alerts everything in The Hollow to your presence.
choices.description: Let Chanida channel a small burst of energy into the crystal to see what happens.

line.dialogue: Oh! Oh, that's BEAUTIFUL. The whole chamber lit up like a starry sky—look at those patterns
Things don't go as planned. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal map resolves, projecting a ghostly schematic of The Hollow's deepest reaches—and a single, pulsing point marked 'Archive.'
I'm the luckiest person alive! That's the motherlode. Pre-Silencing tech. We split it, yeah? After I get my cut for the leg work.
That archive... it's what my order has sought for generations. The unaltered Song of the World. But the path is through the Echo Chasm. It is... perilous.
Then we tread carefully. Every step here changes the song.

lines_before.dialogue: The Echo Chasm is a vertical fissure where sound never dies. Your every footstep, every breath, multiplies into a chorus. At its base lies the Archive—a vault of silent, dark crystal.
Great. For the adventurous, they said. For those who love near-certain death by sonic feedback, more like. The door's not budging.
It requires a key of pure, unforced resonance. The very resonance we spend our lives quieting to hear the Lattice. You need to love yourself—your own true sound—to open it.
That's... poetic and entirely unhelpful. Scans show the door reacts to biological harmonics. But a loud, wrong note could trigger a collapse.
Forget the monk's mystic junk! My leg's crystal is from this place. I can feel it. It's gotta be the key! He loves it!! Let me try!
But what if it's not about a tool? What if it's about us? I love it!! The idea! What if we have to... I don't know, sing together? Our real selves?
The ultimate choice. Do we force the lock with what we've taken, or offer what we are? The true adventure begins within.
The Archive door looms, a mirror of black crystal. In its surface, you don't see your reflections—you see echoes of your potential selves, waiting to be made real.

line.dialogue: The Archive demands a key. What is offered?

choices.line: Let the pirate use his prosthetic. A stolen key for stolen knowledge.
choices.consequence: The door grinds open, powered by scavenged resonance. The Archive's knowledge is accessible, but it is fragmented, filtered through the lens of theft. The pirate claims his prize, and the truth is partial.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use forbidden paths and test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
The resonance turns hostile. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.line: Have the monk perform the Rite of Unveiling. Duty as the key.
choices.consequence: The monk's chant opens the door. The Archive yields its historical truths perfectly, fulfilling his order's purpose. But the personal echoes—the secrets of the self—remain locked away. Knowledge is gained, but not transformation.
choices.description: Pichit uses staff meditation to confront hidden knowledge near the unusual acoustics

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Pichit overreaches. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.line: The party sings together, raw and true. The self as the key.
choices.consequence: A cacophonous, honest harmony bursts forth. The door dissolves. The Archive reveals not just history, but the resonant potential within each of you. Pichit's connection to the Lattice deepens permanently. The act fundamentally changes the party's bond and abilities.
choices.description: The monk takes the lead, employing crystal bowls to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
A costly mistake by the monk. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_after.dialogue: Light floods the chasm. The Archive is open. Whether filled with cold data or living song, the truth of The Hollow—and a piece of the world's lost melody—is now in your hands.
We didn't just find history. We added to its song. For better or worse.
The path forward is clear. I must bring this to my brothers. The Tonal Orders' monopoly... it ends now.
Yeah, yeah, change the world. Just point me to the shiny bits first.
As you emerge from The Hollow, the Lattice below seems to hum in a subtly new harmony. Episode 223 concludes, its echoes lingering in the silent places of the world.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim are a symphony of quiet industry. Wind rustles through rows of sky-rice, water trickles down stone irrigation channels, and distant wind-chimes sing a fragmented, peaceful tune.
Listen to that... the rhythm of the water, the sigh of the wind through the stalks. It's a lot more fun to hear the world's music here than the clatter of the city docks.
They have a lot of stuff! Look at all these different crops on each terrace. You could get lost just exploring.
Or get ambushed. Perfect cover for bandits. Don't get too distracted by the pastoral poetry, Pichit.
She's not wrong. We should stay alert. This edge-city is poorly patrolled. The Tonal Orders don't bother with farm subsidies.
A figure emerges from behind a trellis heavy with vine-fruit. It's a Surface Scavenger, their clothes patched with Lattice-shard leather, eyes sharp and assessing.
Outsiders. You lot look like you've never dirtied your hands. What brings you to the garden's edge?
We're looking for someone! A sky pirate. Heard he knows hidden frequencies.

lines_after.dialogue: A pirate? Hah. You have a lot of things to learn. That one... he used to be a sickly child, they say. Now he's a sickness on the trade routes. Hides in the lower terraces, near the old resonator maintenance shed.
Charming. A career change inspired by poor health.
A maintenance shed could have useful parts. Or traps.
Every path has its own sound. Let's see what melody this one holds.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points a gnarled finger down a narrow, overgrown path. How do you approach the lower terraces?

choices.text: Follow the main irrigation channel. It's open and well-traveled.
choices.description: Crouch low and scan the cluttered stalls for movement before advancing further in. (15 words)

line.dialogue: I see shapes between the hanging pots — three figures, crouched, waiting. We go wide.
Too many shadows, too many blind spots. I can't tell man from merchandise anymore.

choices.text: Take the overgrown path the Scavenger indicated. It's direct but concealed.
choices.description: Signal the group to spread out and flank the wind-chime corridor from both sides. (15 words)

line.dialogue: Good call. If someone's hiding in there, they'll have to pick a direction. Either way, we see them.
We spread too thin and lose sight of each other. Classic mistake — I've seen it get people killed.

choices.text: Circle around via the high windbreak wall. It offers a vantage point.
choices.description: Follow the water's rhythm upstream to find whoever — or whatever — is working the pumps. (15 words)

line.dialogue: The sound grows louder — mechanical, deliberate. Someone is maintaining these channels. People means information.
The trail dead-ends at a collapsed weir. The water flows from nowhere and everywhere. We've learned nothing.

lines_before.dialogue: The lower terraces are quieter, shadier. The air hums with the deep resonance of a nearby crystal conduit. The old maintenance shed is a squat stone building, its door slightly ajar.
No visible lookouts. Too quiet. Don't overwork yourself charging in, Chanida.
I'm not overworking, I'm *investigating*!
Before Arthit can stop her, Chanida pushes the door open. Inside, a Sky Pirate is pacing back and forth in front of a workbench cluttered with crystal shards and tools.
Took you long enough. The Scavenger said you were sniffin' around. What's a pretty bunch like you want with a humble freelancer?
Freelancer. Is that what they're calling 'plunderer' these days? We need a frequency chart for the Eastern Drift Lattice.
Charts cost. But... I might trade. See this?
He holds up a intricate prosthetic leg, its core a pulsing, pale blue crystal. It emits a soft, resonant hum.

lines_after.dialogue: Resonant prosthetic. Stole it off a Listener monk who went to bed late last night guarding it. Thing's tuned wrong. Whines like a stepped-on pup. Fix its song, and my charts are yours.
Its resonance is conflicted... the crystal is pure, but the housing frequencies are misaligned. It's in pain.
This is a Listener artifact. Highly illegal to possess, let alone modify. This is a trap or a death sentence.
She walked back and forth all night, that monk. Worried. You fix it, you get your chart. You don't... well, the gardens need fertilizing.

line.dialogue: The pirate drops the prosthetic on the bench with a thud. The party must decide how to proceed.

choices.text: Agree to fix the prosthetic. Study its resonance and attempt a careful recalibration.
choices.description: Pichit attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on staff meditation

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Pichit fails. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Attempt to steal the frequency charts now, using the distraction of the artifact as a cover.
choices.description: Malee uses mechanical repair to decode the cryptic message near the agricultural hum

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The attempt backfires on Malee. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Refuse and try to subdue the pirate. Force the information from him.
choices.description: The pirate volunteers to trace the anomalous signal, leveraging secret frequencies

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The gamble fails. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: In the quiet heart of Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, the wind carries a new, discordant note. The party's respite is shattered by the sudden, aggressive arrival of a Resonance Ship, its hull bristling with scavenged crystal spines.
Well, ain't this a cozy little nest. We heard whispers. Someone around here's been tinkering with forbidden frequencies. My crew's been married to that idea, and we're here to collect the dowry.
Sky pirates! You can't just—
We can, and we will. That Surface scavenger you've been chatting with... he knows things. Things that could break the Tonal Orders' monopoly. We want his maps.
I'll see you there in the depths before I give you a single chart. My knowledge isn't for sale to thieves.
Great. So we're caught between a rock and a hard place. Or more accurately, a pirate and a paranoid scavenger.
This is escalating too quickly. The prosthetic... if they learn about its unique resonance signature, it could become a target as well.
Every frequency seeks its balance. Even this conflict is a form of resonance... a painful one.

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation hangs in the air, thick with the threat of violence. The pirates' ship hums with a menacing, unstable frequency.
They've been married to violence before. It's their second language.
You've got until sundown to decide whose side you're on. The side with the ship, or the side getting buried in the gardens.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate demands the Scavenger's Lattice maps, threatening violence. The Scavenger refuses, putting the party directly in the crossfire.

choices.text: Try to negotiate a trade: offer something else (like agricultural secrets of the Gardens) to appease the pirates.
choices.description: Draw your blade and charge the bandit leader before he finishes threatening the scavenger.

line.dialogue: I've cut down louder men than you on steadier ground than this — draw or run!
My foot slips on the loose rubble and I stumble right into his line of fire — stupid, stupid!

choices.text: Stand with the Scavenger, preparing to defend him and the Gardens, risking immediate combat.
choices.description: Grab Chanida's arm and pull her behind the ore crates, whispering for the scavenger to stay low.

line.dialogue: I yank Chanida down behind the crates and hiss — *stay quiet, let them think we've gone deeper.*
I reach for Chanida but she pulls away, terrified, and her boot scrapes the floor — every bandit's head turns.

choices.text: Attempt to use the Resonant Prosthetic's unique frequency to disrupt the pirate ship's crystal resonators, a risky and unknown maneuver.
choices.description: Step between the bandit and the scavenger, arms spread wide, offering to cut them a share of the haul.

line.dialogue: I spread my hands wide and say — *everyone's hungry up here, right? There's enough ore for three shares instead of two.*
I step forward with my offer but the scavenger shouts that I'm

lines_before.dialogue: Sundown paints the terraces in deep orange and long shadows. The pirate ship's hum has grown louder, vibrating the very leaves on the vines. The party's decision has drawn all forces to a single, tense clearing.
Time's up. Could you tell me how to get to your cooperation? Or do we need to carve a path through you?
I have something to tell you. The maps you seek... they lead to a Silencing-era vault. Its frequency is a lockdown. You'd need a Singer to open it. You don't have one.
Don't let anyone know he just admitted there's a vault! Now they'll never leave.
We have to protect this place! The Gardens, the people... it's all more than just stuff!
The prosthetic is reacting... it's harmonizing with the distress frequency of the crops. This is dangerous.
The Lattice is listening to this clash. Every shout, every threat, is a note in a song we may not survive. We must find the final, resolving chord.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax resonates through the Hanging Gardens. The consequences of the choice ripple out, altering the fate of the terraces, the Scavenger's knowledge, and the stability of the Resonant Prosthetic itself.
You've changed the tune of this place. For better or worse, the map is now drawn by your actions.
A frequency was chosen. Now we must live within its echo.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirates are poised to attack, the Scavenger's secret is exposed, and the Gardens' peaceful resonance is about to be shattered. The party must enact their final, decisive plan.

choices.text: Call upon the local Tonal Orders for intervention, surrendering the Scavenger's secret to authority to save the Gardens.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with captain experience to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The resonance turns hostile. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Trigger a controlled collapse of a terrace section to block the pirates' advance, sacrificing part of the Gardens to save the rest and the people.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with staff meditation to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Pichit loses control. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Attempt a desperate, unified 'song' using the prosthetic, the party's voices, and the natural sounds of the Gardens to overload and disable the pirate ship's resonators.
choices.description: The pirate steps forward with intimidation, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the pirate pulls it off. A secret frequency from the underworld shifts the balance.
The resonance turns hostile. Criminal contacts betray the pirate.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a deep, resonant tone that vibrates through the bones. The party stands at the base, where the floating island's rock meets the impossibly smooth, crystalline column descending into the shimmering Lattice below.
Listen to that! It's like the whole world is singing one note. Makes my teeth itch.
A necessary stability. This harmonic anchor prevents the entire skycity from drifting into uncharted dissonance. We should be grateful.
Grateful for a headache? The Tonal Orders charge a fortune just to keep this thing humming. They probably invented the 'drifting' problem themselves.
A single, sustained tone... it creates peace, but also a profound stillness. It quiets the chaotic music of the mind.
You're back late! The Spire watch said they saw your resonance ship approach hours ago. Everything alright?
Our journey was... extended. We followed a strange harmonic echo off the standard charts.
Off the charts? That's asking for trouble. Are you going home yet? It's not safe to linger near the Spire's base after sundown. The vibrations... they say they can stir up old echoes.

lines_after.dialogue: Old echoes? Like what?
Whispers from before The Silencing. Nonsense, probably. But my granddad said he left home in a hurry once because he heard a woman singing down in the lattice fissures. No one believed him.
Charming. So we're standing on the world's largest ghost story.
Or a natural acoustic phenomenon. The Spire's fundamental tone interacting with subsurface crystalline structures.

line.dialogue: The villager's story hangs in the air, mingling with the Spire's hum. Pichit feels a strange pull.

choices.text: Dismiss the story as superstition. Focus on securing the ship.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the resonance stone and let the tone flood your bones, searching for its source, 15 words

line.dialogue: You feel it too — there's a second melody buried underneath, older and wild and *hungry*.
Pull your hand back — you're oscillating at the wrong frequency. You'll crack your own wrist bones.

choices.text: Ask the villager for more details about the 'singing' his grandfather heard.
choices.description: Climb the maintenance ladder to the anchor's housing and inspect the tuning forks for micro-fractures, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — hairline splits in the third fork. This anchor hasn't been maintained in months. Maybe years.
The harmonic resonance knocked you clean off the fourth rung. The Tonal Orders *really* don't want visitors up there.

choices.text: Suggest the party investigates the base fissures for unusual resonance patterns.
choices.description: Hum a counter-tone a

line.dialogue: the villager pushes through. The islander's wisdom cuts through complexity.
the villager loses control. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Acting on the villager's tale, the party descends a maintenance ramp along the Spire's base. The monolithic hum is louder here, a physical pressure. Cracks in the island's bedrock reveal glimpses of the glowing Lattice below.
Hey! This is a claimed scrape. You city-folk lost?
We mean no intrusion. We're investigating anomalous acoustic reports.
Anoma-what? You mean the crying metal? There's a high chance you'll hear it down the east fissure. Sounds like a ship's resonator dying. Gives me the chills.
Crying metal? That's it! That's the echo we followed! A chance to find a lost ship... how could you pass it up?
How? Easy. It's probably a scavenger trap. Or a resonance sink that'll liquefy our brains. Do you need to use it, this 'chance'? We have supplies to deliver.
But if it *is* an echo of The Silencing... a true sound from the Lost Age... understanding it could change everything.
You lot are nuts. But if you're going down, watch for lattice-shifts. And don't touch the shiny bits. They bite.

lines_after.dialogue: The east fissure is a deep, jagged wound. The Spire's calming tone warps here, twisting into discordant harmonics. A faint, rhythmic ping echoes up from the depths—like a sonar pulse from a dead vessel.
The acoustic profile is all wrong. It's not a natural formation. It's... structured.
It's inviting us! Come on!

line.dialogue: The pulsing echo grows stronger. At the fissure's edge, the light from the Lattice reveals the ghostly outline of a ship's prow fused into the crystal.

choices.text: Send a resonance pulse down to 'ping' the ghost ship and gauge its size.
choices.description: Pull out the frequency analyzer and show the scavenger the readings, 15 words

line.dialogue: These readings confirm your 'crying metal' — we need to see where it's loudest.
The device won't calibrate... your scrape is interfering with our instruments somehow.

choices.text: Have Malee attempt to hack a nearby Tonal Order monitoring crystal to scan the anomaly.
choices.description: Offer three ration packs and a medical kit for safe passage to the source

line.dialogue: We're not here to steal your claim — we just need to hear what the metal is saying.
The scavenger spits at our offer — says city-folk always try to buy what they should earn.

choices.text: Have Pichit attune to the strange pulse, trying to harmonize with it directly.
choices.description: Ignore the scavenger and push past toward the sound growing louder in the walls

line.dialogue: We don't have time for territory disputes — that resonance is accelerating and we need to reach it.
The scavenger's crew emerges from the scrap walls, blocking our path — we've walked into a standoff.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire's steady hum saturates the air, a physical pressure that makes whispered secrets feel like shouted confessions. High above, the floating city casts jagged shadows across the crystalline lattice below.
Everyone knows it! The Tonal Orders' charts are wrong here. The Lost Ship's echo is warping the local frequencies. We can hear it, right?
Caution. That distortion could destabilize the anchor's resonance. If the Spire's tone falters, the entire city's drift-path could—
Could what? Drift into another city? Aren't you tired of living in fear of charts and probabilities? The Listeners study the Lattice's natural sounds, not the Orders' sanitized versions.
The truth is in the distortion. The Lost Ship didn't just vanish. It was silenced. Its final resonance is trapped here, a memory in the crystal.
You shouldn't be poking at that! The Anchor keeps us safe. Stirring up old echoes... I don't want it. We have enough trouble.
The surface-folk have stories. That ship? It didn't listen to the Lattice. It tried to command it. Now its ghost-song tries to pull things down.

lines_after.dialogue: A deeper pulse thrums through the Spire, out of sync with the main tone. The crystal beneath your feet shivers, throwing prismatic light.
There! That's the echo! It's not a ghost—it's a fracture in the Lattice. A wound that never healed.
And it's calling. Not with words. With absence. The silence where its final note should be.

line.dialogue: The aberrant resonance is growing stronger, vibrating in your bones. You can feel the Lost Ship's final moment—a panicked, discordant shriek frozen in crystal. How do you respond to the echo?

choices.text: Harmonize with it. Use your own resonance to gently guide the fractured tone back into alignment with the Spire. (Requires empathy and control.)
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with resonant staff, ready to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Pichit misreads the situation. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Map the fracture. Study the distortion pattern to understand exactly how the ship's resonance was shattered. (Requires analytical skill and courage.)
choices.description: Chanida steps forward with frequency mapping, ready to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Chanida loses control. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Answer the call. Project your resonance directly into the fracture, attempting to communicate with whatever consciousness remains. (Requires immense will and risk.)
choices.description: The villager steps forward with irrigation, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the villager finds the key. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire groans. The perfect harmonic is breaking apart into competing frequencies. From the lattice below, a shape begins to resolve—the ghostly silhouette of a shattered resonance ship, rising on a wave of wrong sound.
Don't let them see you! The Tonal Order enforcers are coming! They'll silence everything—the echo, the Spire, maybe even the city!
The fracture is widening. If it reaches the anchor's core frequency, the feedback will shear the city from its moorings. We have moments.
Don't judge others. The ship's crew weren't fools. They discovered something the Orders couldn't control. A natural resonance path. And for that, they were unmade.

The lattice remembers everything. Every song, every scream. That ship's scream is a key. It's trying to unlock the truth about The Silencing. Don't let anyone know! If you learn it, they'll come for you too.
It's not attacking. It's showing us. Look! In the distortion—images. A chart made of pure sound. A path not on any Tonal Order map.
The final revelation. The Lost Ship didn't fail. It succeeded. It found a way to speak directly to the Lattice's heart. And that was the crime.

lines_after.dialogue: The ghost-ship's form dissolves, not into silence, but into a single, perfect, radiant tone. It hangs in the air for one eternal second before weaving itself back into the Anchor Spire's hum. The new frequency is deeper, truer. The lattice below glows with gentle light.
It's not an echo anymore. It's a foundation. The truth is part of the world again, singing under everything.
The city's drift... has stabilized. But to a new heading. One not on any chart.
So. The Orders' monopoly on 'safe' paths is a lie. The lattice wants to be sung to, not commanded. What a beautifully dangerous thing to know.

line.dialogue: The Lost Ship's truth is now part of the Anchor Spire, a secret harmony woven into the city's very foundation. The Tonal Order enforcers are arriving, drawn by the disturbance. What is the legacy of this moment?

choices.text: Conceal the Truth. Let the new harmony hide as a minor anomaly in the Spire's records. The city gains stability, but the secret remains dormant. (Safety in obscurity.)
choices.description: Arthit uses lattice storms to test the prosthetic reaction near the resonance anchor

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Share with the Listeners. Entrust the true resonance pattern to the monastic order. Let them begin the long, careful work of reintegrating lost knowledge. (A seed for change.)
choices.description: Direct Malee to confront hidden knowledge using scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
Malee hits a wall. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Become a Beacon. As a Singer, use the new tone to openly recalibrate nearby resonance ships. Challenge the Order's charts directly and publicly. (A declaration of war.)
choices.description: The scavenger channels surface knowledge toward the deep vibration, hoping to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the scavenger succeeds. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The attempt backfires on the scavenger. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard is a symphony of industrial decay. The groans of half-dismantled resonance ship hulls undercut the rhythmic clanging of salvage crews. The air shimmers with heat and dissonant acoustics.
Ugh, this noise is giving me a headache. Can we find this monk and get out of here? I had a bad dream about this place last night... all twisted metal and silence.
A dream? How quaint. The reality is just rust and people trying to make a living off the bones of better times. Look at that gantry—it’s my dream job to see it collapse on the foreman.
Every sound here has a history, Chanida. A final, distorted note. The Listeners say even shattered crystal remembers its song.
And we're here to meet one of those Listeners. In a scrapyard. Seems an odd place for contemplation. We should be cautious.
You spot the Listener Monk near a eviscerated engine core, his simple robes stark against the grime. He's not meditating—he's arguing with a sharply dressed Trade Negotiator.
My dear brother, your 'truth' doesn't pay docking fees. The Tonal Order's charts are the law. What I offer is... a mutually beneficial silence.
The Lattice's song is not for profit! It... it is a truth that weighs on me.

lines_after.dialogue: Excuse us. We were told you had information about unusual Lattice frequencies near the old Silencing fault lines.
You seek the Cleft. A wound in the song. The merchant here wishes its location to remain a trade secret.
Information is a commodity! And he’s right! What he said was right! It *is* a secret. A valuable one.
We're not buying. We're trying to *stop* whatever's causing the static storms!
Your intent... resonates. But the path is dangerous. The Cleft's song is one of absence. It requires a guide who can hear the silence.

line.dialogue: The Monk seems willing to help, but the Merchant blocks your way, smiling. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Intimidate the Merchant. (Chanida cracks her knuckles, glaring.)
choices.description: Tap the pipes in rhythm to signal the Listener you've arrived, 15 words

line.dialogue: Old trade code — the Listener taps back from somewhere deep in the yard.
Wrong tempo. Now every stray in the district knows we're stumbling around blind.

choices.line: Appeal to the Monk's duty. (Pichit speaks of the greater harmony.)
choices.description: Follow the distorted hum to its source while ignoring Chanida's complaints, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — beneath the corrugated sheeting. The sound remembers a voice that no longer exists.
Great, you dragged us toward the loudest noise. My skull is splitting in two now.

choices.line: Offer a trade. (Arthit suggests a different piece of useful information.)
choices.description: Ask Malee to interpret the metallic resonance before pressing deeper inside, 15 words

line.dialogue: Fine. The frequency carries grief — someone recorded a final goodbye into these walls.
I read people, not scraping metal. Ask your precious Listener, if they even still breathe.

lines_before.dialogue: The Merchant slinks away, but not before giving you a venomously polite nod. The Monk leads you deeper into the canyon of scrap, to a quieter hollow where a derelict ship's bridge serves as a makeshift sanctuary.
I must insist you understand the peril. The charts are silent there. The Cleft... it swallows resonance. Where did you lose it, your confidence in the mapped paths? You must have felt it.
We lost it when the sky started screaming and ships vanished. I’m dieting. I’m trying to lose weight. The dead weight of trusting the Orders.
Your analogy is... unhelpful. Monk, you said you need a guide who can hear the silence. We have no Singer.
Not a Singer. Something else. An artifact. A Resonant Prosthetic. A leg, forged from a Lattice-shard, worn by a Navigator who survived the Cleft. It holds an echo of the safe path.
A crystal leg? That’s... profound. The wearer’s journey etched into the crystal.
Great! Where is it? Let’s go get the magic leg!
It was here. In the scrapyard. A scavenger named Old Klin kept it. But he’s gone. His stall is ransacked. I’m glad to know that you seem capable, for you will need to be.

lines_after.dialogue: At Old Klin's plundered stall, you find signs of a struggle and a single, glowing crystal shard from a resonator—not from a leg. The trail is cold.
The Merchant. He wanted the Cleft's location secret. He'd want this artifact too.
Or one of the salvage gangs. This yard is full of people who'd insist a crystal limb is just valuable scrap.
We need to ask around. Someone must have seen something!
The Prosthetic isn't just a tool. It's a memory. We must find it, not just for the path, but for the story it carries.

line.dialogue: The search for the Resonant Prosthetic begins. Where do you start your investigation in the vast, noisy scrapyard?

choices.line: Question the nearby salvage crews. (They see everything, but loyalty is cheap.)
choices.description: Draw your blade and demand the monk reveal what the Resonant Pearl truly does

line.dialogue: The blade focuses your attention wonderfully. The Pearl amplifies a Singer's voice across the shattered lanes — it can reconnect what the sky severed.
I will not be threatened by steel while I am trying to save your lives. Put it away or leave.

choices.line: Track the Merchant's recent movements. (Find who he's been talking to in the underworld.)
choices.description: Ask Malee to describe exactly what the sky screaming sounded like to find a pattern

line.dialogue: It wasn't thunder. It was... harmonics. Like every Singer crying out at once, then cutting off. The silence after was worse.
I don't — I can't describe it. My ears bled for three days after. Words don't live in that sound.

choices.line: Listen to the Scrapyard's 'song' for disturbances. (Pichit and the Monk attempt a difficult acoustic survey.)
choices.description: Offer to retrieve the Resonant Pearl yourself if the monk swears to guide your ship after

line.dialogue: You would risk the vanished lanes? Then I swear by the Three Tunings — bring me the Pearl and I will chart you through.
You misunderstand. I do not need a hero. I need someone who already carries resonance. You are deaf to the frequency.

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups in the shadow of a gutted Resonance Ship's hull, the air thick with the scent of ozone and rust. The Listener Monk, Brother Kavi, awaits, his face etched with worry.
You've seen the flawed resonator. The Tonal Orders' charts... they are not just imperfect. They are a deliberate cage. Everyone knows the Lattice shifts, but they forbid us from speaking of it.
A cage? For what? To keep their monopoly? That's it, right?
Of course it is. Knowledge is power, and power is profit. Aren't you tired of being lied to?
This is dangerous ground. If we act on this, we challenge the only authority that keeps the cities from drifting into oblivion.
But if the cage is built on a lie, then the safety it offers is an illusion. We have to know the full truth.
The truth... is in the Song Beneath the Silence. A natural resonance my order has secretly mapped. It could guide ships without the Orders' charts.
A heavy clang echoes as the Trade Negotiator, Somsak, approaches, his smile not reaching his eyes.

lines_after.dialogue: Brother Kavi! Sharing old stories? You know the Tonal Orders don't appreciate such... loose talk. It's bad for business.
Your business is built on their silence, Somsak. I don't want any part of it anymore.

A pity. Well, I came with an offer. For the resonator schematic you 'found.' The Orders would pay handsomely for its return. Or, I could arrange a quieter sale. To interested parties who... appreciate alternative navigation.

line.dialogue: Somsak offers a deal for the flawed resonator schematic. What do we do?

choices.line: Sell it to Somsak's 'interested parties.' Quick profit, but we lose control.
choices.consequence: Gain funds but become indebted to shady forces. The subplot_crystal_leg prototype is funded, but with compromised materials.
choices.description: Smash the flawed resonator open and examine its internal crystal lattice structure.

line.dialogue: The fracture pattern — it's deliberate. They're seeding imperfections into every resonator coming off the line." — monk
Shards everywhere and I cut my hand. Whatever secret this thing held, it's dust now." — monk

choices.line: Refuse and keep it. We'll find our own use for it.
choices.consequence: Make an enemy of Somsak, but retain the key. The subplot_crystal_leg research becomes more difficult but purely our own.
choices.description: Slip into the Tonal Orders' shipping office and copy the last month of resonator distribution logs.

line.dialogue: Seventy resonators shipped this quarter. Zero to independent tuners. They're starving out everyone outside their network." — malee
A clerk came back for his tea thermos. I smiled, he screamed, and now we're on a very short list." — malee

choices.line: Publicly give it to Brother Kavi. Let the Listeners expose the flaw.
choices.consequence: Incites immediate conflict with the Tonal Orders. The scrapyard becomes a battleground of ideologies, forcing a rushed climax.
choices.description: Send an anonymous tip to three underground tuner collectives about the deliberate flaws.

line.dialogue: If enough tuners know the truth, the Orders can't quietly bury this. We build a chorus they can't silence." — arthit
One

lines_before.dialogue: Tension crackles in the scrapyard like static. Somsak's enforcers have moved in, cutting off escape routes. The decision has been made, and now the consequences descend.
They've surrounded the workshop. We need a plan. Roll up your sleeves; this won't be clean.
Clean? Look around. Nothing here is clean. That's all, isn't it? The whole world is built on dirty secrets.
Then let's make some noise! We have the resonator prototype. We can use the scrapyard's acoustics against them!
Chanida's right. But it's not just about fighting them off. It's about proving the Song is real. Brother Kavi, can you guide us?
I can. But you must listen, not just with your ears, but with your intent. The Lattice responds to truth.
Somsak's voice booms from a loudspeaker mounted on a crane.
Last chance! Hand over the schematic and the monk. The Orders are coming. You can't win. You need to love yourself enough to choose survival.

lines_after.dialogue: Survival built on lies is not living. We choose the Song.
As Pichit speaks, Arthit activates the jury-rigged resonator prototype, connected to the subplot_crystal_leg's core crystal. A low, pure hum builds, different from the harsh industrial din.
The very metal of the scrapyard begins to vibrate in sympathy. Brother Kavi closes his eyes and sings a single, clear note.

line.dialogue: The Lattice is responding, pulsing through the broken ships. How do we use this resonance?

choices.line: Create a resonant barrier. Defend our position until the authorities arrive.
choices.consequence: A stalemate. The Tonal Orders take custody of Brother Kavi for 'heresy,' but the public incident plants seeds of doubt. The crystal leg functions, but is confiscated for study.
choices.description: Chanida uses frequency mapping to harness harmonic feedback near the salvage

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The gamble fails. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Amplify the Song to disrupt the enforcers' equipment and escape into the lower decks.
choices.consequence: A chaotic escape. You become fugitives with a functional crystal leg prototype, but Brother Kavi is captured. The Song is now a whispered myth among scavengers.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing lattice storms to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Arthit hits a wall. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.line: Channel the resonance into the crane. Shatter the loudspeaker and make a public stand with Brother Kavi.
choices.consequence: A defiant, visible act of heresy. The resonator and crystal leg are destroyed in the feedback, but the Song is heard by hundreds. You are arrested, but become symbols. Brother Kavi smiles, free in spirit.
choices.description: The monk attempts to chart resonance pathways, relying on recording crystals

line.dialogue: the monk succeeds. His recording captures a denied frequency.
Things don't go as planned. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns before you, a jagged maw in the floating island's underbelly. The air inside is cool and carries a faint, crystalline hum.
Great. A dark hole. My favorite. It probably won't be too expensive in terms of our sanity, right?
The acoustics are... unusual. These echo patterns don't follow natural laws. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Caution is boring! Listen to that hum! It's like the island is singing to itself. Let's go!
A song trapped in stone. Most Thais are Buddhist, seeking inner peace. This place feels like the opposite—a memory of a great, unsettled noise.
Deeper in, the tunnel opens into a vast cavern. Pre-Silencing ruins are fused into the walls, and a cloaked figure kneels before a large, pulsating crystal formation.
You should not be here. The Lattice's song in this place... it is a private meditation. The price for disturbing it is rather expensive for one's spirit.

lines_after.dialogue: I am Elara, of the Listeners. I study the dissonance here. It speaks of a ship... a Resonance vessel that fell from the sky long ago.
A lost ship? Sounds like a story to sell to gullible traders. The price for that 'truth' is probably sky-high.
What does its song tell you, Listener? Is it a warning, or a plea?

line.dialogue: Elara looks conflicted. 'The echo is clear, but my duty to the Order is to record, not to act. Will you hear its story?'

choices.text: "We will listen. Guide us to where the echo is strongest." (Follow the monk.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the humming wall and feel for vibration patterns.

line.dialogue: The resonance points form a grid—someone *carved* these channels deliberately.
Great, now your hand is glowing. That's *never* a good sign.

choices.text: "Tell us what you know, but we'll find our own path." (Ask for directions, then proceed independently.)
choices.description: Drop a stone down the passage and count the seconds before it stops echoing.

line.dialogue: Seven counts... the depth is sacred. This place was built for pilgrimage.
It didn't stop—it's still falling. How deep *is* this nightmare?

choices.text: "This is a matter for your Order. We'll explore the ruins quietly." (Politely decline and split off.)
choices.description: Hum back at the same frequency you hear in the stone.

line.dialogue: The walls are *answering*! Listen—the pattern shifted, it's a conversation!
Stop. Stop immediately. You're harmonizing with something that isn't geology.

lines_before.dialogue: Following Elara's guidance or your own path, you descend into a lower chamber. The air grows colder. A makeshift camp is set up near a mural depicting a falling ship.
Ah, travelers! A rare pleasure in such a... resonant place. Could you tell me how to get to the main trade spire from here? My own charts are, ah, compromised.
You're far from the trade routes. What's your business in The Hollow?
Salvage, dear fellow! Pre-Silencing artifacts. The acoustics here preserve things wonderfully. But between us... don't let anyone know! The Tonal Orders would tax the echo off these walls.
He's looking for the lost ship. The one the monk was wailing about. Don't tell him we already know. Let's see his price.
You've heard its song too, haven't you? That sad, pulling sound from the deep tunnels!
Song? I deal in tangible goods. But... if you've heard something, perhaps we can trade information. I have a map fragment.
Every song has a source. Every source, a truth. What does your map silence to make room for profit?

lines_after.dialogue: Fine. The echo you hear is the *Whispering Dawn*, a Singer's ship that crashed here during The Silencing. Its crystal core is still active, and unstable. My employer wants it. Don't tell her I told you that.
An active core in an unstable ruin? That's a catastrophe waiting to resonate.
A low, throbbing hum suddenly rises from a crack in the floor, and the mural of the ship seems to glow faintly. The subplot's echo has found you.

line.dialogue: The merchant eyes the glowing crack. 'The core is close. We can work together—I get the core, you get the glory of discovery. Or... other arrangements can be made.'

choices.text: "Lead on. We'll secure the area for your salvage." (Cooperate with the merchant for a share.)
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using tattooed routes to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
Arthit overreaches. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: "Give us the map fragment. We'll investigate the core ourselves." (Cut a deal for the map, then go alone.)
choices.description: Chanida uses singer voice to decipher the monk's recording near the cave echoes

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The lattice has other plans. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.text: "We're sealing this place. No one touches that core." (Confront the merchant and attempt to cut him off.)
choices.description: The monk volunteers to chart resonance pathways, leveraging prayers

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His recording captures a denied frequency.
the monk misreads the situation. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in the Hollow, the party stands before a massive, carved archway. The ghostly hum of the lost ship's resonator is now a palpable vibration in the air.
The structural integrity here... it's pre-Silencing. And it's reacting to that echo. This is for the adventurous, or the foolish.
Then let's be adventurous! The answer is right through there. I can feel it!
Feel it? I feel like we're walking into a tomb's welcoming committee. Why couldn't you just let the Tonal Orders handle their own lost garbage?
Because this 'garbage' has a song they tried to erase. A truth. May I see your driver's license, Malee? Just... a metaphor. Are we licensed for this?
The Lattice's song here is... pained. It remembers the ship's final moments. A dissonance they silenced.
And what a profitable dissonance it could be! Salvage rights, exclusive mapping data... Don't let anyone know we found it first!

line.dialogue: The archway leads to a vast, resonant chamber. At its center lies the spectral outline of the Resonance Ship, flickering in and out of existence. The air thrums with trapped energy.

choices.line: Approach slowly, humming a calming tone to match the chamber's resonance.
choices.outcome_line: The ghostly hull stabilizes, revealing a shimmering, non-hostile form. A path inside materializes.
choices.description: Press your palm against the resonant wall where the hum is strongest, 15 words

line.dialogue: The vibration maps a frequency pattern — this wall is a door, and we just found the key.
Nothing. The stone is dead to the touch, and I think that might be the worse sign.

choices.line: Have Arthit analyze the frequency and project a counter-harmonic from his tools.
choices.outcome_line: The ship shudders, its image solidifying with a sharp crackle of energy. It's stable, but the air now feels electrically charged.
choices.description: Follow the narrowing fissure where air moves cold against your face, 15 words

line.dialogue: See? The draft pulls toward something open — and where there's breath, there's a way through!
It's a dead end. The fissure chokes shut and the only thing waiting is silence laughing at us.

choices.line: Charge forward, trusting Chanida's instinct to break the echo-loop.
choices.outcome_line: The ship's form erupts in a burst of light and sound! The chamber shakes, but the violent discharge clears a jagged opening in the spectral hull.
choices.description: Hum the fragmented melody Pichit recognized until the walls answer back, 15 words

line.dialogue: They're singing with me — the song was never erased, it was *waiting* for someone who remembered.
My voice cracks and dies alone in the dark. The song doesn't want me. Not yet.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision made, the ghost-ship's interior becomes accessible. A cold, silent wind emanates from within.
Great. Now we get to explore a phantom. I have a class. A masterclass in bad decisions, and I'm the star pupil.
Stop complaining and look! There, on the bridge... is that the captain's log? Still glowing!
The final record of a journey the Tonal Orders wanted buried. This is the catch.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the echo-ship's bridge, a crystalline log pulsates. Around it, the shadows of the dead crew seem to watch. The Negotiator and Monk are tense.
The data-core! Untouched for centuries! My backers will... I have a class. A very important meeting with them the moment we get back.
This log doesn't just hold coordinates. It holds the Ship's Last Song. The true reason for The Silencing. If played... it could heal the Lattice here, or shatter it further.
The guy in the condo next door always closes his door loudly. That's what the Tonal Orders did—slammed the door on this truth. The structural repercussions of playing that song are incalculable.
So we destroy it. Smash the crystal, let the dead sleep. No profit, no apocalypse, just quiet. I'm gonna rush off right now to find a big rock.
No! This is why we came! To hear the song they tried to kill! We have to play it!
Chanida seeks the truth. Malee seeks peace. Arthit fears the collapse. And I... I must choose which echo becomes the future.
The ghostly crew's whispers rise to a crescendo. The crystal log brightens, awaiting a trigger. The fate of The Hollow—and the secret it keeps—hangs in the balance.

line.dialogue: The spectral captain's hand rests on the log. To interact is to complete the echo. The Monk and Merchant look to Pichit, their conflicting desires laid bare.

choices.line: Play the Song. Let the truth resonate, no matter the cost.
choices.outcome_line: A beautiful, terrible chord fills The Hollow. The ghost-ship dissolves in light. The Lattice in the cave heals, glowing softly, but the Tonal Orders' sensors will have surely detected the pulse.
choices.description: Pry the data-core from its housing and pocket it before anyone else reacts, 15 words

line.dialogue: I've got it — and nobody's backing anybody until I say so.
It slipped — the housing cracked and now the crystal's bleeding light everywhere.

choices.line: Safeguard the Log. Take the crystal to the Listeners for controlled study.
choices.outcome_line: You secure the crystal, silencing the ghosts. The Hollow falls quiet but tense. You possess a weapon or a cure, making you and the Listeners a target for both the Merchant's greed and the Orders' fury.
choices.description: Let the monk finish reading the log aloud so everyone hears what's really at stake, 15 words

line.dialogue: You see now? This was never cargo. It's a warning left by the dead themselves.
I — I can't pronounce this passage, the script is corrupted, and now I've smudged the only readable section.

choices.line: Shatter the Echo. End the cycle of memory and let the past die.
choices.outcome_line: With a decisive strike, the log and the ghosts vanish. A profound, empty silence falls. The Hollow is safe, inert, and the truth is lost forever. The Monk weeps; the Merchant scowls at lost profit.
choices.description: Hand Malee the crystal and step back, letting her shatter it on the temple floor, 15 words

line.dialogue: It's done. Whatever was screaming in there — it's quiet now. We leave with nothing.
I brought it down but it bounced — the crystal

lines_after.dialogue: The choice reverberates through the stone. The chamber is forever changed.
We don't close doors loudly here. We... we choose which ones to open, and how.
The Echo of the Lost Ship is finally laid to rest, its legacy now defined by your action.
As the party emerges from The Hollow, the world outside feels different. Lighter, or heavier, based on the chord you struck.

acts.title: A Whisper in the Market Roar

lines_before.dialogue: The Khrueang Market is a symphony of commerce. A thousand overlapping voices and clattering goods create a dense, shimmering wall of sound that presses in from all sides.
The party navigates the throng, the constant hum making Arthit's crystal resonator flicker erratically. Pichit scans the stalls, his eyes thoughtful.
This noise is chaos! How does anyone think straight? Look, over there—a scavenger's stall. Fresh surface salvage.
Caution. Surface goods are often unstable. And the Tonal Orders patrol here. We shouldn't draw attention.
Relax, Arthit. The Orders are too busy counting their fees to care about us. Let's see what the dirt-grubber has.
Every sound here is a note in the world's song, even this noise. But some notes... are meant to be heard alone.
Ey. You lot lookin' or buyin'? I have work to do. Surface salvage don't catalog itself.
(Nudging a companion) See them? Outsiders. Asking questions. Someone is waiting for you if you stir the Lattice too much, I say.

lines_after.dialogue: We seek understanding, not trouble. We heard a rumor... of a map. One not controlled by the Orders.
A map, eh? Dangerous talk. But... I got my answer about you. You're Listeners, ain't ya? Or wanna-bes.
I might know a thing. A frequency map. 'Open,' they call it. Shows the Lattice's natural song, not the guild's forced paths. Found it in a deep-surface ruin.

line.dialogue: The scavenger eyes you warily, holding a cracked data-crystal. 'This is the key. But it's not for sale. It's for a trade.'

choices.line: Offer to pay double in sky-city credits. (Wealth solves immediate problems.)
choices.description: Grab the merchant's arm and demand to see the Tona crystal's true resonance, 14 words

line.dialogue: The resonance holds steady — this crystal is genuine. Well worth the bartered price.
