It cracks under pressure. Counterfeit, like I feared. We move on, empty-handed but unbeguiled.

choices.line: Propose trading a rare, stable resonator from your own supplies. (A practical tool-for-knowledge exchange.)
choices.description: Follow the melody Pichit hears weaving through the stalls toward its hidden source, 13 words

line.dialogue: There — beneath the cobbles, someone is singing the old tones. We've found the way down.
The melody shatters into ordinary haggling. I was hearing what I wished to hear, nothing more.

choices.line: Appeal to shared curiosity about the Lattice's true nature. (A philosophical gamble.)
choices.description: Slip between the cloth merchant's hanging silks to shadow the Order patrol passing behind, 13 words

line.dialogue: They walked right past without a twitch. See? Too busy chasing their own shadows to notice ours.
One of them paused — turned — looked straight at the silk moving where

acts.title: The Price of a True Note

lines_before.dialogue: The deal is struck. The market's cacophony seems to sharpen, each shout and clatter feeling more pointed. The scavenger has named his price.
The map's yours. But you fetch something for me first. A relic, from the Silencing-era. A 'tonal bell,' they say. My contact below says it's in a nearby surface cairn.
A surface expedition? The risk assessment is... severe. Uncharted frequencies, structural instability...
Of course it's not simple. Nothing ever is. But a real Silencing relic? That's history, not just guild-approved trivia.
We can do it! A quick dive, grab the bell, come back. The fuel for the resonance ship probably won't be too expensive for a job like this.
To hold an object from before the great silence... To hear what note it still holds. This is a path worth walking.
(Overhearing) You're buying surface salvage? That's a fool's game. The price is rather expensive for Thais like us, not just in coin. In peace of mind.

lines_after.dialogue: Most Thais are Buddhist, yeah? Then think of it as making merit. You retrieve the past, I give you the future. Fair trade.
The cairn's coordinates are on this chip. The Lattice there is... thin. You'll hear things. The Open Frequency Map will help you navigate the raw song.
He hands over the data-chip. It feels cold. The market's noise seems to recede for a moment, replaced by the weight of the unknown below.

line.dialogue: The plan is set, but the approach is not. How will you prepare for the descent to the Lattice surface?

choices.line: Stock up on standard guild-approved safety gear from the market. (Reliable, but obvious and traceable.)
choices.description: Rappel down the collapsed ventilation shaft to reach the temple bell's resting place, 15 words

line.dialogue: The structural integrity held — barely. The bell is in my hands. Let us never speak of that descent again.
The rope snapped on the way down. You're lucky the debris broke your fall instead of your spine. We need another way in.

choices.line: Seek out a disgraced Tonal Order cartographer rumored to sell 'unofficial' navigational advice. (Risky, but potentially insightful.)
choices.description: Negotiate with the surface raiders camped near the temple ruins to let you pass peacefully, 15 words

line.dialogue: They accepted the medicine supplies. I can't believe talking actually worked — sometimes people just need something, same as us.
They want triple what we offered or they open fire. I strongly recommend we withdraw and reconsider this entire endeavor.

choices.line: Attempt a quiet, pre-dawn meditation at the city's edge to 'listen' for the cairn's frequency yourselves. (Uses your unique skills, but is slow and uncertain.)
choices.description: Sprint across the irradiated plaza at noon when the sentry drones recharge, grabbing the bell mid-stride, 15 words

line.dialogue: My boots are melting and I taste copper but the bell's ours. Nobody tell Arthit how close that actually was.
The drones woke early — something triggered them. You took two hits crossing open ground. We drag you back now

lines_before.dialogue: The market's ambient roar presses in like a physical force. Amongst the stalls, the party has cornered the Surface Scavenger, their backs to a wall of crated resonator crystals.
You're persistent, I'll give you that. But the Lattice doesn't care about persistence. It cares about precision.
And we care about that map! The Tonal Orders are charging a fortune for basic charts. It's rather pricey for Thais, for *anyone* trying to survive!
Oh, don't bring economics into it. He's just scared. The Silencing taught everyone that new sounds bring new cracks.
You think this is about fear? It's about respect. The Open Frequency Map... it's not a shopping list. It's a key. And keys get lost.
But shouldn't a key be shared? If the Listeners are right, and the Lattice has a natural harmony... locking that away seems like a deeper Silencing.
Caution, Pichit. He's right about one thing—this won't be too expensive; it'll be *dangerously* expensive. The Orders have ears everywhere, even here.
Your friend's got sense. Fine. The map's not here. It's with a Skycity Resident who... inherited it. But you'll have to make her see reason. Most Thais are Buddhist, but she's devout in her silence.

lines_after.dialogue: The Scavenger points a grimy finger towards a quiet tea stall at the market's edge, where an elderly woman sits alone, staring into her cup.
Great. A zealot. My stomach is starting to growl, and we're about to have a theological debate.
That's no problem! We just need to... resonate with her. I believe we can do it!

line.dialogue: How will you approach the resident keeper of the map?

choices.line: Appeal to shared community. Speak of the skycity's needs and the burden of her secret.
choices.description: Malee attempts to harness harmonic feedback, relying on leg resonance

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The attempt backfires on Malee. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: Invoke the Listeners' teachings. Frame the map as a sacred text that should be heard, not hoarded.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using resonant staff to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
The risk doesn't pay off. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Be brutally honest. Describe the suffocating control of the Tonal Orders and the desperate need for an alternative.
choices.description: Have the scavenger risk using surface knowledge to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: the scavenger's expertise pays off. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Defeat. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The tea stall is an island of quiet. The Resident, Lin, looks up as you arrive. Her eyes hold the weight of the sky.
You're not going anywhere? The Scavenger sent you. I told him to let the past lie.
The past is a frequency we're still living in, Lin. The Silencing, the Orders... we're trapped in its echo.
And you think my husband's notes will change that? He died mapping those open frequencies. How long are you going for? Until you join him?
We don't seek death. We seek a way to live without a guild's permission stamped on every horizon.
Are you going or not? With the map, I mean. Holding it burns you. Sharing it might just... tune the world.
Please. We have a Singer. We have a chance to prove the Lattice can be a partner, not a prison!
Lin's gaze softens, then hardens as a discordant hum cuts through the market noise. Three figures in Tonal Order robes emerge from the crowd, their intent clear.

lines_after.dialogue: Lin's hand darts beneath the table, emerging with a worn crystal slate—the Open Frequency Map. The market's cacophony seems to sharpen, focusing on this moment.
Take it. And run. Live with it. Better you than them.
The slate is cool in your hands, etched with luminous pathways. The Order agents begin to push through the crowd. The decision is immediate and final.

line.dialogue: The map is in hand, but the exit is blocked. How do you escape the market and the Orders?

choices.line: Use the market's chaos. Create a distraction by overloading nearby resonator stalls, causing a sonic flare.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
A costly mistake by Chanida. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Use the map itself. Quickly identify a safe, open frequency and have Malee 'Sing' a temporary path through the crowd.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use staff meditation and decode the cryptic message

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. The monk's recording plays a warning tone.
Defeat. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Stand your ground. Challenge the Orders publicly, using the map as proof of their monopoly, and rally the market crowd.
choices.description: The villager uses terraces to chart resonance pathways near the crowded stalls

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
the villager misreads the situation. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Echo's Lament' drifts to a halt at the edge of the Silent Zone. The constant, low thrum of the crystal resonators dies, replaced by a profound, unnatural quiet that presses against the ears.
I hate this. It's like the world just... stopped breathing.
Relax. It's just dead lattice. No song, no vibration. It's peaceful, in a creepy, soul-sucking kind of way.
Our charts are useless here. The Tonal Orders have no data on this sector. We are navigating blind.
Not blind. We listen to a different kind of silence. What does the absence of song tell us?
A smaller, older skiff detaches from a floating debris cluster and approaches. A Listener Monk stands at its prow, his robes still.
You should not be here. The song does not reach this place. It is... wrong.
We're looking for a shortcut. Heard there might be open frequencies here, a map to faster routes. My mom told me about it already.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, fellow travelers! Don't let the quiet spook you. I had a bad dream about this place once too. Woke up in a cold sweat!
A merchant? Out here? What are you selling, existential dread?
Opportunity! Information! The very map you seek. But locating it... that's really easy to guess! It's in the oldest silence.

line.dialogue: The Monk warns of spiritual corruption. The Merchant offers a deal for coordinates. The party must choose their initial approach.

choices.line: Trust the Monk's reverence. Search for 'the oldest silence' through meditation and observation of the dead lattice.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the dead lattice and push your own heartbeat into it.

line.dialogue: Malee grips your wrist, eyes wide.* "There — did you feel that? Something pushed back. The lattice isn't dead, it's *holding its breath*.
Malee pulls you back.* "Nothing. Just cold stone and cold hands. Stop wasting your pulse on something that doesn't want it.

choices.line: Engage the Merchant's deal. Offer a trade of supplies for his supposed coordinates, knowing he likely withholds key dangers.
choices.description: Follow Pichit's lead — close your eyes and listen to the silence between your own footsteps.

line.dialogue: Pichit smiles without opening his eyes.* "You hear it now, don't you? The silence has *edges*. Something carved this quiet deliberately.
Pichit sighs.* "You're still listening for sound. That's not what I mean. Until you stop expecting to hear, you'll hear nothing.

choices.line: Split the difference. Send Chanida to haggle with the Merchant while Pichit consults the Monk, gathering intel from both sources.
choices.description: Take Arthit's useless charts and fold them into a rough funnel — hold it to the dead air like an ear trumpet.

line.dialogue: Arthit laughs, sharp and startled.* "You beautiful idiot — the chart's tonal markings are *resonating*. The ink itself is picking up frequencies we can't. The
the merchant fails. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the chosen path, the party ventures deeper. The silence becomes a physical weight. Distant crystalline structures loom, unmoving and unreflective.
Readings show minimal energy signatures. It's not just silent; it's inert. The Lattice here is... frozen.
I keep hearing my own heartbeat. It's too loud. Why didn't you go scout ahead, Arthit? You're the careful one!
Because I'm afraid there'll be a problem. Scattering in this void is a recipe for losing each other forever.
The Monk said this silence was a wound. Does a wound heal, or does it fester? We are walking inside a scar.
Great. Philosophical scars. My favorite. Look, the Merchant's 'coordinates' lead to that fissure. Smells like a trap.
The Merchant's skiff glides alongside, his smile visible in the dim light. He makes a show of checking a crystal slate.
Just ahead! The map is supposed to be in a resonance vault at the base of the fissure. He winked at me when he told me that. A old salvager. Probably meant it was guarded.

lines_after.dialogue: Guarded, or cursed. The vault may hold not a map, but an echo of The Silencing itself. A memory of the scream that broke the world.
So it's a treasure map.
Or it's nothing, and the Merchant gets to pick our bones after we starve looking for it. I'm voting for this being a profoundly stupid idea.

line.dialogue: The fissure yawns before them, a crack of pure black in the dead crystal. The vault door is visible at its base, sealed.

choices.line: Force the vault open. Use the ship's residual resonance charge in a concentrated burst to break the seal. Quick, but loud in the silence.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the corridor wall and feel for vibrations beneath the silence.

line.dialogue: There — rhythmic pulses, two seconds apart. Something behind this wall is breathing.
Nothing. Either the walls are dead, or they've learned to hold very, very still.

choices.line: Decipher the seal. Study the vault's locking mechanism with the Monk's help, seeking a harmonic key that might open it without violence.
choices.description: Whisper directly into Chanida's ear and ask her to match her heartbeat to yours.

line.dialogue: When I sync with you, the echoing stops. The silence was just us, amplified and alone.
Your pulse is wrong — too fast, too hungry. Now I hear *two* heartbeats and neither is mine.

choices.line: Bait the truth out. Confront the Merchant directly, threatening to strand him here unless he reveals everything he knows about the vault's true nature.
choices.description: Kneel where Pichit indicated the Monk stood and press your forehead to the cold floor.

line.dialogue: The Monk left a warmth here. Like he knelt until the wound opened *around* him. He didn't flinch.
The floor drinks warmth from your skin. The Monk knelt here too long — the wound learned his shape.

lines_before.dialogue: The merchant's ship, a gaudy vessel of polished brass and gilded crystal, lies dead in the silent lattice. No hum, no vibration. It's a metal tomb.
A temporary setback! The resonator array just needs a... recalibration. A minor investment of time.
It's scrap. Your 'recalibration' is wishing really hard. The lattice here doesn't listen. It's nice and peaceful, if you like being stranded.
We're not stranded! We have our ship. His is just... taking a nap. Right?
His resonator crystals are inert. No feedback loop. It's a complete systems failure. We should not tether too closely; his silence might be contagious.
This quiet... it's not natural absence. It's a presence. A hunger. The monk said to listen for what isn't there.
You begin to understand. The Open Frequency Map... it is not a chart of sounds, but of silences. The places the Song does not touch. I know. I have studied it.
Silences can be mapped, and therefore, sold. A navigational hazard database! Very valuable. He's a nice person for sharing.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, sub-audible thrum passes through the ships—not sound, but a pressure change in the lattice itself. Every crystal on the merchant's vessel cracks at once.
What was that?! It didn't make a noise, but I felt it in my teeth!
The Zone is not empty. It is... digesting.

line.dialogue: The merchant's ship is breaking apart. He's scrambling for a lifeline.

choices.text: Throw him a line from our ship. Save him, but risk our vessel.
choices.description: Salvage the resonator crystals for parts to repair your own ship's damaged array

line.dialogue: Arthit crouches beside the dead housing and pries two intact crystals free.* "These still have lattice integrity. I can re-tune them for our resonator in about forty minutes.
Arthit snaps the last crystal trying to extract it.* "Shattered. Stress fractures through the entire lattice — he's been running these hot for months without calibration.

choices.text: Demand he tell us everything he knows about the Map first.
choices.description: Offer to tow the merchant's vessel to the nearest station if he drops his price by half

line.dialogue: Chanida leans against the hull plating and smiles.* "We hook up the tow line, you cut your 'premium' in half, and everybody walks away with their pride mostly intact. Deal?
The merchant sputters and clutches his manifest.* "Half?! I have a family! Children! They attend a very expensive academy on Coren Prime — you're asking me to starve them!

choices.text: Cut his tether. His ship's resonance signature is attracting the 'hunger'.
choices.description: Ask Malee to hotwire the resonator using your ship's power cells as an external source

line.dialogue: Malee traces
the monk overreaches. The monk's faith wavers, breaking concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: The Silent Zone has a heartbeat. A vast, slow pulse of anti-sound that makes the lattice underfoot feel brittle and thin. The merchant's ship is gone, consumed without a roar.
Resonator output is dropping. We are being dampened. My stomach is starting to growl from the stress, not hunger.
Great. We're next on the menu. The monk's 'map' led us right into the belly of the beast. That's no problem at all.
No! It led us to the truth! The Silencing... it was not an accident. It was a feeding. This Zone is a scar, and it is growing.
So we sing louder! Pichit, you can do it! I believe you can do it! Break the silence!
Singing into this... it would be like offering myself. But the map. The monk is right. The voids have a pattern. They're not random.
The lattice around your ship begins to crystallize into jagged, dead spikes, creeping inward. The very medium of sound is turning against you.
(Clinging to the hull, his voice a rasp) The Tonal Orders... they know! They chart the silent zones to avoid them... or to use them. The map is a weapon!

lines_after.dialogue: The dead crystal spikes are inches from the resonator ring. One touch and your ship will be silenced forever.
The pattern! The silent frequencies form a chord—a chord of absence. You must not fight the silence. You must complete the chord.
Complete it... with what?

line.dialogue: The devouring silence is a harmonic void. To survive, you must fill it.

choices.text: Use the ship's resonator to blast the 'chord of absence' at maximum power. Overwhelm it with noise.
choices.description: Force your resonance outward through physical pain, pressing palms against the dampening field's source.

line.dialogue: I screamed until my throat bled—and the wall *cracked*. It heard me. It *flinched*.
I pushed everything I had into that scream, and the silence just... swallowed it. Swallowed me. I can't hear my own heartbeat anymore.

choices.text: Have the entire crew speak a memory of sound—a laugh, a song, a cry—into the lattice. A chorus of humanity.
choices.description: Grab the monk's prayer wheel and spin it backwards, reversing the Silencing's frequency pattern.

line.dialogue: The wheel *shrieked* in reverse and the quiet shattered like glass. Every dead voice in this place came flooding back at once—beautiful and terrible.
I spun it wrong. The frequencies collapsed into each other and now there's a sound inside my skull that won't stop—a humming, a feeding, a *yawning*.

choices.text: Sing the one frequency the map indicates is missing. The true, terrible note that will either heal the scar or widen it.
choices.description: Whisper directly into Chanida's ear so she can carry your voice where the dampening can't reach.

line.dialogue: I mouthed the old words into her ear, breath to bone. She opened her mouth and *sang me through her
the merchant is thwarted. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

lines_before.dialogue: The first light of dawn filters through cracks in the ceiling of The Hollow, catching on crystalline dust motes. The air is cool, filled with the faint, resonant hum of the island's internal structure.
Ugh, my head... feels like a Resonance ship crashed in it. But you know what? I'm in a good mood. This place is weird, and weird is good.
A cautious mood would be more appropriate, Chanida. We don't know what these ruins contain. The acoustics alone are... unsettlingly perfect.

Relax, Arthit. If the Silencing didn't get them, and a thousand years of floating didn't get them, our happy little stroll probably won't either. Is the pay good? That's the real question for our 'guide' over there.
My dear Malee, the pay is excellent for me, and will be for you! Think of the pre-Silencing artifacts! Untouched markets! A friendly smile costs nothing, and knowledge... well, that's my trade.
The air doesn't just carry sound here... it remembers it. A fresh beginning in a place of ancient endings. What song did this stone last hear?
A profound question, traveler. The Lattice's song outside is a chorus. Here... it is a single, sustained note. Reverent. But also... a warning I cannot yet decipher.

lines_after.dialogue: The party moves deeper, the merchant chattering about salvage rights. The monk trails behind, running a hand along the wall, his expression troubled.
Look! Carvings! People... and those spiky crystal shapes. They look afraid.
The depiction aligns with fragmented records of the Silencing. This is a historical record, not just a ruin.

line.dialogue: The path splits three ways ahead, each tunnel humming with a different pitch.

choices.text: Follow the lowest hum. (Arthit suggests stability and structural safety.)
choices.description: Pichit attempts to use the leg as a lattice probe, relying on tonal knowledge

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit overreaches. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.text: Follow the merchant's 'instinct' toward the brightest gleam of crystal. (Profit calls.)
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with hidden frequencies to decipher the monk's recording

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida fails. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

choices.text: Ask the monk which path feels most 'true' to the natural resonance. (Seek the Listeners' wisdom.)
choices.description: The monk steps forward with lattice study, ready to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. The Listener's study yields a revelation.
the monk loses control. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The chosen tunnel opens into a vast, spherical chamber. In the center, a massive, flawed crystal column pulses with a slow, sickly light. The echo of your footsteps doesn't fade—it circles the room, growing slightly louder.
Magnificent! The sheer tonnage of resonant crystal! We'll be rich! Don't let them see you hesitate, friends. Fortune favors the bold!
He's still single, isn't he? Has to be. Only someone with no other attachments would get that excited about a giant glowing rock.
Whoa... it's beautiful. Like a heart. I just want to... touch it...
Chanida, stop! The acoustic feedback is building. That isn't a natural resonance.
Arthit is right. This sound... it's a loop. A memory the stone is stuck in. A scream, perhaps, frozen in crystal.
Stop it! All of you, be silent! Can't you hear it? Beneath our noise... it's the same note from the Lattice's warning dreams. This is the source. This chamber is not a tomb. It is a prison.
As the monk speaks, the circling echoes coalesce. A phantom, shimmering shape begins to form around the central crystal—a humanoid silhouette of condensed sound and light.

lines_after.dialogue: The spectral form lets out a silent vibration that rattles teeth and bone. Cracks spiderweb across the chamber floor.
The structural integrity is failing! We must retreat!
My crystal! Just a small piece—!
It is not a thing to be owned! It is a wound in the world's song! We must soothe it, or sever it, but we cannot ignore it!

line.dialogue: The echo-entity reaches toward the group. The chamber groans.

choices.text: Flee! Follow Arthit's lead back the way you came. (Survival is paramount.)
choices.description: Direct Malee to harness harmonic feedback using leg resonance

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The attempt backfires on Malee. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Attempt to disrupt the resonance. Make noise, break the acoustic loop. (A tactical, physical solution.)
choices.description: Have Pichit focus monk wisdom on the unusual acoustics to seek the dismissed truth

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit is thwarted. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Try to communicate. Let Pichit and the monk 'listen' and attempt to mirror or calm the entity's frequency. (A dangerous philosophical approach.)
choices.description: The merchant uses market connections to map the frequency corridors near the unusual acoustics

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Hidden leverage shifts the balance.
the merchant's resolve isn't enough. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: The passage narrows, then opens into a cavern where the walls are not stone, but smooth, dark crystal veined with faint, pulsing light. The air hums with a low, constant tone.
Whoa. The whole island's hollow? This is... massive.
And unstable. Look at those stress fractures. We shouldn't linger.
Linger? We just got here. Besides, the pay for mapping this place should be exceptionally good. Isn't that right, Negotiator?
Oh, exceptionally. The Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for coordinates to a virgin resonance cave. A literal fortune.
It's not just a cave. Listen. The hum... it has a structure. A pattern repeating beneath the main tone.
A warning pattern. The same one from our oldest scroll fragments. 'The foundation dreams, and its dreams are cracks.'
You're not going anywhere with that gloomy talk, are you? We're explorers! This is what we do!

lines_after.dialogue: A deep, grinding shudder runs through the cavern. Dust and crystal shards rain from the ceiling.
The resonance is destabilizing the structure! I told you!
The Lattice isn't just around us... it's *part* of the island. We're inside a resonance node. And it's waking up.

line.dialogue: The central crystal column begins to glow, projecting fragmented images of the ancient city that once stood here. The hum sharpens into a painful whine.

choices.text: Dampen the resonance. Use supplies to muffle the central crystal, calming the node.
choices.outcome: A risky, direct approach. Quiets the immediate danger but may attract attention.
choices.description: Rappel down through the nearest stress fracture to begin surveying immediately, 15 words exactly

line.dialogue: The echo profiling is incredible down here — I'm reading at least three unmapped gallery levels!
The fracture sheared open under my weight — everyone back from the edge before the whole shelf collapses!

choices.text: Harmonize with it. Have Pichit attempt to match the resonance pattern, to communicate rather than fight.
choices.outcome: Uses Pichit's latent Singer ability. High reward for understanding, but personal risk.
choices.description: Anchor seismic monitoring spikes across five fracture points before descending any further

line.dialogue: Readings are stable across all five points — we've got a safe window of maybe six hours to work.
Three of the five anchors are already showing harmonic resonance — this cavity is shaking itself apart right now.

choices.text: Redirect the energy. Channel the building resonance into the ancient ruins' machinery, whatever's left.
choices.outcome: An archaeological gamble. Could unlock secrets or cause a catastrophic feedback loop.
choices.description: Question the merchant about what the Tonal Orders actually want with these maps

line.dialogue: The merchant: "They believe this hollow contains a Resonant Choir — living architecture that sings in frequencies lost since the Sundering. They want it found before their rivals do. The maps are merely... the first step.
The merchant: "I — that is, I'm not at liberty to — look, perhaps I've said too much already. Can we simply proceed?

lines_before.dialogue: The cavern transforms. The crystal lights blaze, and the ghostly image of a pre-Silencing city solidifies around you—a resonant memory made nearly tangible.
Illusions. Echoes of sound and light. That's all, isn't it?
No. It's a memory. The Lattice recorded the moment of the Silencing... and it's playing it back.
Look! The people in the image... they're not running from a disaster. They're... bowing. To the sky.
It wasn't an accident. The Scroll of Unmaking... it was a command. A frequency meant to suppress the world's song. We didn't listen to the warning. We *are* the warning.
Fascinating history lesson! Now, about those resonance coordinates—roll up your sleeves, we need to chart the epicenter before this light show ends!
You fool! Can't you see? This 'node' is a wound. Our presence, our ship's resonator, is irritating it! The whole Hollow could shatter!
He's right. The memory is looping because it's stuck. The trauma of the Silencing is trapped here, in the crystal. We have to... heal it. Or seal it. For good.

lines_after.dialogue: The phantom city flickers. The central crystal pulses like a heart, and the grinding shudder becomes a deafening roar. Cracks spiderweb across the dome.
It's collapsing! We need to go, NOW!
The truth dies with us if we run. Or we carry it, and change everything.
You need to love yourself enough to face the truth, Arthit. All of us do. What we do here echoes forever.

line.dialogue: The memory crystal offers one final, clear image: the ancient device that began the Silencing. You have moments before the cavern implodes.

choices.text: Destroy the core crystal. Shatter the memory and the unstable node with it, ensuring it can't harm anyone again.
choices.outcome: A clean, permanent end. The secret of the Hollow is buried, but so is the truth. The Tonal Orders' power remains unchallenged.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging tonal knowledge

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The lattice has other plans. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Download the resonance memory. Use your ship's recorder to capture the final moments of the Silencing as proof.
choices.outcome: You escape with explosive evidence. It ignites a crisis of faith across the Floating Cities, but makes you targets of every power.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to question the Orders' silence using singer voice

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
Chanida is thwarted. The warning tone triggers a defensive lattice reaction.

choices.text: Resonate with the wound. Use your own voice to sing a resolution to the trapped memory, to let it finally rest.
choices.outcome: Pichit embraces being a Singer. The Hollow stabilizes, becoming a sacred site. The Listeners split, some seeing you as a messiah, others a heretic.
choices.description: The merchant steps forward with market connections, ready to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
the merchant loses control. The signal dissolves into static.

lines_before.dialogue: Dawn breaks over Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens. The first light catches on dew-kissed terraces of sky-rice and wind-kelp, painting the floating island in soft gold. The air carries the quiet, rhythmic sounds of irrigation flutes and wind-chimes woven through the crops.
From morning until evening, this place holds a different kind of music. Not the Lattice's hum, but... life's rhythm.
It's just photosynthesis with better acoustics. Don't get poetic before breakfast.
I saw a market stall setting up down on the third terrace! When's a good time to go? Before the good scavenged bits are gone?
We should secure supplies first. The Tonal Orders' toll for the next lattice-passage won't be cheap.
A moment of peace first. Listen. The water flowing through the stone channels... it's a counterpoint to the wind.
A figure approaches along the winding path—well-dressed, with a calculator-pendant glinting at his throat.
Greetings, travelers! You have the look of those who appreciate fine things. And opportunities.

lines_after.dialogue: I'm here negotiating a bulk purchase of resonant crystal chaff—the waste from resonator forging. The farmers use it to strengthen crop stems. A humble trade, but profitable.
Let me guess. You're paying them in shiny beads and promises.

Nah, nah. You don't need to think so poorly of commerce! I offer fair value. Speaking of value... I heard a whisper. Someone in the gardens is looking to trade a unique item. A 'resonant prosthetic,' they called it. A crystal leg, tuned to the Lattice's song. Now, where would one even acquire such a thing?
A prosthetic? That sounds like surface salvage. Dangerous tech.

line.dialogue: The merchant's eyes gleam. 'I could make introductions, for a small finder's fee. Or... you could wander these terraces all day. When should I go make that introduction?'

choices.line: Pay his fee for the information. (Lose some coin, gain a clear direction.)
choices.description: Slip down to the third terrace alone, blending into the morning mist to scout the market stall before anyone notices, 15 words

line.dialogue: Good—you move like you belong here. I'll signal the others once I see what the vendor's actually stocking.
A lone wanderer in the mist? The Tonal Orders will tax your shadow before you reach the second terrace. Back. Now.

choices.line: Politely decline and ask more about the crystal chaff trade first. (Gather context, might learn another path.)
choices.description: Approach the toll station openly with Arthit, presenting your expired Harmonic credentials and bluffing authority, 15 words

line.dialogue: Expired papers, confident posture, and no hesitation—they waved us through. Sometimes the Orders only hear what they expect to hear.
They didn't just reject us—they logged our names in the Resonance Ledger. Now every tollkeeper between here and the seventh terrace knows our faces.

choices.line: Dismiss him and search the gardens yourselves. (Save coin, but waste the morning.)
choices.description: Follow Pichit's lead and spend the morning mapping the mist patterns to find an unmapped path between terraces, 15 words

line.dialogue: The mist thins here at midday, thickens there by afternoon—and between them, a drainage channel the Orders never thought to watch.
The mist swallowed my markers. Three hours

lines_before.dialogue: Following hints—whether bought or gleaned—the party finds a secluded vegetable plot on the garden's windward edge. A grizzled woman with a pronounced limp is angrily prying a pulsing, violet crystal shard from the soil with a trowel.
Blasted lattice-spawn! Growing right through my root-tubers again.
Whoa. Is that a... crystal leg? Do you wanna go check it out?
Caution. That shard she's handling is raw, unstable resonance.
Her movements... they're in time with the ground's vibration. She's not just removing it; she's listening.
Great. Another listener monk. Let me guess, she's going to offer us wisdom in exchange for weeding.
The scavenger hears them and turns, her eyes sharp and suspicious. She doesn't drop the shard.
Outsiders. What do you want? My silence is cheap, but my answers aren't.

lines_after.dialogue: We heard you might have knowledge of a device. A leg, made to resonate.
Knowledge? I've got the cursed thing. Dug it up from a ruin on the surface. Thought it was salvage. It's not working. Not for me, anyway. Sings a pain-song only I can hear.
You don't wanna see that anymore? We could take it off your hands!
And let the Tonal Orders trace it back to me? Or worse? I don't wanna see it anymore, but I'm not stupid. It's a key to a door I don't want opened.
She gestures to a locked, reinforced crate half-hidden under a tarp. A faint, discordant hum emanates from it.

line.dialogue: The scavenger eyes you, then the crate. 'It's a burden. But burdens have value. How do you want to lift it?'

choices.line: Offer to trade for it directly with supplies or coin. (Simple transaction, but costly.)
choices.description: Have Chanida focus unauthorized tones on the agricultural hum to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida loses control. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.line: Offer to safely dispose of the 'lattice-spawn' shards plaguing her plot. (Earn trust through labor, learn more.)
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Arthit loses control. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.line: Propose a deeper trade: you'll listen to the leg's 'pain-song' and tell her what it says. (Risky, could forge a bond or cause harm.)
choices.description: Convince the merchant to use information network and listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the merchant. His network produces an ally at the critical moment.
the merchant fails. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The afternoon sun warms the terraces. The Trade Negotiator stands near a water-sculpted archway, examining a shimmering crystal component.
Ah, the travelers. Back from your stroll? I was just admiring the craftsmanship on this resonator. Surface-grade, but polished to a city sheen.
We seek passage. A way down to the Lattice surface. The Scavenger hinted you might... facilitate such journeys.
Facilitate? I enable commerce. And commerce requires trust, and trust requires... investment. One way or round trip? The pricing structures differ dramatically.
We just need to get down there! What's the big deal?
The 'big deal,' my impulsive friend, is that the Tonal Orders have tariffs on unsanctioned descents. My methods are... discreet. And discretion has overhead.
Let me guess. You want the prosthetic. The crystal leg the old farmer was talking about.

Perceptive! It's not just a leg. It's a tuned resonator. With it, I could calibrate my ship's dampeners to slip past the Order's sonic wards. Fetch it for me, and your passage is complimentary. This is the best way. For all of us.

lines_after.dialogue: A farmer's prosthetic? That feels... invasive.
Think of it as repurposing. He's a surface-dweller. He'll find another stick. You need to reach the depths. I'm heading out now to prepare the vessel. The choice is yours.
The merchant smiles, his eyes holding no warmth, and retreats toward a concealed docking cleft in the garden's cliff face.

line.dialogue: The merchant's deal hangs in the air. The prosthetic is a key to the surface, but taking it from someone who needs it...

choices.text: Agree to get the prosthetic. The mission's goal justifies the means.
choices.description: Offer the merchant exclusive salvage rights to whatever you recover below, 14 words

line.dialogue: I'll draft the contract myself — you'll have first claim on anything we surface with.
We... don't actually have anything to trade. My mistake — I spoke before I thought.

choices.text: Refuse the deal outright. We'll find another way down, no matter the risk.
choices.description: Demand to see the transit authority regulations governing Lattice descent, 12 words

line.dialogue: Section nine, subsection C — emergency access can't be denied to registered surveyors. Show me your ledger.
I... don't actually know the regulation code. I was hoping you wouldn't check.

choices.text: Agree, but plan to deceive him. Secure passage, then find a way to nullify the deal.
choices.description: Slip the merchant a folded note offering double his facilitation fee under the table, 14 words

line.dialogue: My fingers remember the weight of old debts. This covers your inconvenience and your silence.
He won't even look at it. I misjudged him — he's not the kind who bends.

lines_before.dialogue: Twilight stains the gardens indigo. The party regroups at the highest terrace, the Scavenger waiting nervously by a gnarled root-bridge.
He's loading his skiff. You got the leg? Don't show him 'til you're aboard. He's got fair prices for betrayal.
We're not giving it to him! We... figured something else out.
Yeah. The 'something else' is probably getting us all killed. I don't wanna see that smug merchant's face anymore.

A low hum vibrates through the stone. From the docking cleft, the merchant's Resonance Ship rises, its crystal prow glowing. It doesn't work silently; it breathes, a deep, rhythmic pulse of displaced air.
I trust you've concluded your business! My hold is open. The Lattice awaits.

We have. But our business changed. We know the leg's resonance signature is unique. You don't just want to bypass the wards... you want to mimic a specific Singer's frequency. To plunder a protected site.
The farmer said the leg 'sings of home.' You're not a navigator. You're a grave robber using a dead man's song.

lines_after.dialogue: The professors of profit are really good, aren't they? You learned your lesson. But the final exam is pass/fail.
The ship's hum intensifies, a painful pressure in the chest. The hanging crops tremble. The merchant has weaponized the vessel's resonance, aiming to stun and take what he wants by force.
The terraces! They'll shatter! Use the water channels—break the harmonic!

line.dialogue: The merchant's ship is charging a disruptive sonic wave. The fragile gardens and your party are at risk. The Scavenger's warning rings in your ears.

choices.text: Use the Prosthetic. Crank its resonance to overload, creating a counter-frequency to disrupt his attack. It will destroy the leg.
choices.description: Toss the leg into the merchant's open hold while the scavenger's back is turned, then signal Chanida to play dumb

line.dialogue: Smooth — his skiff's still half-empty and he's already untying the ropes. He won't notice until we're three blocks gone." — Chanida
The leg bounced off the hull rim — rang like a temple bell. He's turning around. He *saw* it." — Chanida

choices.text: Sabotage the Garden's Irrigation. Rupture the water pipes. The chaotic spray and shifting humidity will scatter the sonic focus, but flood the fields.
choices.description: Pull the scavenger aside and tell him the leg got damaged, offer him Malee's backup medkit as compensation instead

line.dialogue: He's biting. Grumbling, but biting — nobody says no to military-grade antiseptic out here." — Malee
He just shoved past me and is digging through our kit bags himself. We have about ten seconds." — Malee

choices.text: Chanida, Sing. Have her attempt to harmonize with the ship's pulse, seize control of its resonator, and turn its power back on itself. Extremely dangerous for her.
choices.description: Tell the merchant you've got something better than scrap — information about a rival's unguarded cache, if he'll let the three of you walk

line.dialogue: His eyes went greedy before his mouth said yes. We're walking — and he'll forget our faces by sundown.
the scavenger misreads the situation. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of dead ships. Towering husks of old Resonance vessels stand like metal skeletons, their crystal resonators long scavenged. The air vibrates with the discordant symphony of hydraulic crushers and salvage saws.
Every broken ship here has a story. A final note it couldn't hold. I'm only interested in the ones that failed quietly—the ones the Tonal Orders don't record.
Stop philosophizing and start looking! That scavenger said the Listeners come here to study the 'rust harmonies' or whatever. I think that's the one over there—the monk in the grey robes.
Great. Another mystic in a junkyard. Because what this place needs is more people listening to metal instead of working it.
Careful. The Scavenger Guild controls this yard. That monk shouldn't be here without their permission. The acoustics are too unpredictable.
You approach during the third harmonic of the crusher. Interesting. Most avoid this frequency—it unsettles the stomach.
We heard you study the Lattice's natural songs. Even here, in this... industrial choir.
Especially here. The scrapyard sings of endings. But sometimes... an ending holds a beginning. You're looking for something. I can hear it in your resonance.

lines_after.dialogue: We need parts for a resonant prosthetic. A leg. The Tonal Orders' prices are criminal.
Ah. The crystal leg. I think that's right. There's a scavenger who works the deep yards. He lost his own leg to a misfired resonator. Now he builds what the Orders won't sell.
Let me guess: he's mysterious, dangerous, and will only help if we perform some acoustic ritual?
No. He's practical. But he moves through the high-risk zones. Where the Lattice thins. If you're not careful with your sound... you're gonna be sorry for disturbing what sleeps below.

line.dialogue: The monk points toward the canyon of shattered hulls. 'Find him before the evening shift change. The crushers mask all other sounds then—including screams.'

choices.line: Follow the monk's directions exactly. (Safe but predictable)
choices.description: Pry open the cargo hatch on the derelict freighter before the scavenger returns.

line.dialogue: Got it — but this hull's been breached longer than any of us have been alive," Arthit mutters, shining his light into the dark.
The seal's fused shut and now the whole frame is groaning — back off before you bring it down on us," Arthit hisses, yanking my arm free.

choices.line: Use Chanida's reckless energy to shortcut through active crushing zones. (Faster but riskier)
choices.description: Trip the yard's perimeter alarm to draw the scavenger away from the ship we need.

line.dialogue: There — that klaxon will have him chasing ghosts across the yard for at least ten minutes," Chanida whispers, already moving toward the hull.
Brilliant. You triggered the *internal* sensors instead — now he knows exactly which bay we're standing in," Chanida snarls, diving behind a compressor unit.

choices.line: Have Arthit study the work schedules to find the quietest path. (Slow but methodical)
choices.description: Read the serial numbers stamped on the engine blocks to identify which wreck flew the Omsak run.

line.dialogue: This one — Omsak-7 registry, decommissioned six years ago after a reactor breach. This is our ship," Pichit says, tracing the faded numerals with his fingertip.
The corrosion's eaten through every registration plate in this row. I can't read ghosts, Pichit, and neither can you,

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in the scrapyard's belly, where light filters through perforated hulls, you find the scavenger's workshop. It's built into the carcass of an ancient Resonance ship, its crystal housing now a workbench covered in luminous components.
Monk sent you, huh? Figures. He's always interested in my 'projects.' Well, look around. I make what the Orders won't. Give it to me! Your best offer.
We need a resonant prosthetic. Left leg, full lattice synchronization. The monk said you could...
Could? I've got three in progress. But they're not cheap. Well, cheaper than the Orders, but it's still cheap compared to what it costs me to harvest the crystals.
Let me guess: you need us to fetch something dangerous from the 'forbidden zone'?
Smart one. There's a ship that went down yesterday. Fresh kill. Its primary resonator is mostly intact. I didn't finish harvesting it all—the Lattice started singing wrong near it.
Wrong how?
Like it was answering something that wasn't there. Bring me that crystal, I'll build your leg. Don't, and you can limp back to the Orders.

lines_after.dialogue: A fresh wreck? With an intact resonator? That's worth ten legs! Why wouldn't you have grabbed it already?

Because something's down there with it. Something that doesn't sound like metal or Lattice. Something... organic. I didn't eat it all—the story, I mean. The other scavengers who went near didn't come back.
Organic? Nothing organic survives on the Lattice surface. Unless...
Unless the Silencing left more than ruins.

line.dialogue: The scavenger marks the wreck's location on your chart—a depression between two larger hulls where the Lattice is visible. 'Go at shift change. The crushers will mask your approach. But they'll mask its approach too.'

choices.line: Take the scavenger's recommended path and timing. (Follows local knowledge)
choices.description: Pull the rusted resonant shard from your pack and slam it on the table, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Arthit: "Found this in a collapsed relay tunnel south of the Quarter. Partially charged but the lattice structure is intact."]
[Arthit: "I... may have oversold what we brought. The shard cracked during extraction — it's worthless now."]

choices.line: Go now, while there's light, accepting you'll be more visible. (Daylight advantage)
choices.description: Lean close and ask what kind of dangerous, voice low enough that only she hears, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Malee: "Whatever it is, we've handled worse since the Collapse. Name the location and the complication."]
[Malee: "I said that sarcastically, not as an invitation. Arthit, maybe we should find someone less... enthusiastic about sending us to die."]

choices.line: Send a resonance pulse ahead to map the area, risking alerting whatever's there. (Aggressive reconnaissance)
choices.description: Slide your remaining vials of filtered coolant across the table as a down payment, 15 words

line.dialogue: [Scavenger: "Filtered? That's not street-cut. You've got connections. Alright — this covers materials. Labor you'll earn the hard way."]
[Scavenger: "Three vials? I need nine for a full lattice leg alone. Come back when you're serious about doing business."]

lines_before.dialogue: In the shadow of a dismantled Resonance Ship's hull, the Listener Monk stands before a crude altar of salvaged resonator crystals.
The Lattice sings a dirge here. A song of endings. I think that's right. But... there's a counterpoint. A pulse.
A pulse? Like a heartbeat from below?
Yes. It contradicts all the Tonal Orders' charts. They're only interested in control, not truth.
So the charts are wrong? You're gonna be sorry for hiding this!
Great. Our navigational monopoly is built on lies. But it's still cheap if it keeps the cities floating.
You Listeners talk pretty. We scavengers work. That pulse... it comes from the old Silencing crater. No one goes there.
A crater full of unstable resonance? Why couldn't you warn people?

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk produces a small, flawed resonator crystal from his robe—a fragment of the prosthetic leg subplot.
This came from there. It holds the true song. May I see your driver's license? No... I mean, may I trust you with it?
We've lost our way before. But not our purpose.
The crystal hums, and the surrounding scrap metal vibrates in sympathy.

line.dialogue: The Monk offers the crystal fragment. It could reveal the Lattice's true nature, but carrying it might attract dangerous attention.

choices.text: Accept the crystal discreetly. Keep the secret safe.
choices.outcome: You conceal the fragment. The Monk nods, satisfied. The path is quieter, but narrower.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use lattice storms and decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Study the crystal openly here. Learn its song immediately.
choices.outcome: The crystal's resonance briefly clears the scrapyard's cacophony, revealing a hidden harmonic path. The Scavenger is astonished.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use Listener training and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Pichit overreaches. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Refuse the crystal. Seek the truth firsthand at the crater.
choices.outcome: The Monk is dismayed, but the Scavenger grins. 'You'll need a guide. And a better ship.' The danger is real.
choices.description: The monk uses prayers to listen for the ghost ship's echo near the salvage

line.dialogue: the monk pushes through. The monk's meditation reveals a pattern in the lattice's song.
The lattice has other plans. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: At the heart of the scrapyard, under the looming skeleton of a derelict city-core, the fragment's resonance has drawn unwanted echoes.
The Tonal Orders' patrol ships are converging. Their resonators are scanning. You can ask them to leave, but they won't.
I'm gonna ask them if they enjoy being liars! Bring it on!
They're not liars. They're businessmen. And we're stolen property.
My crew's ready. We've got a salvage barge tuned to mask your signature. But it's a gamble.
Every truth was once a gamble. I want to ask you something, Scavenger: will you help us reach the crater?
The crater? That's where the prosthetic leg crystal was mined. It's where the Silencing... didn't finish it all. Something survived.
The Monk steps forward, his face a mask of resolve. The patrol ships' shadows darken the yard.

lines_after.dialogue: The Lattice's true song is a question. You can try asking him—the world itself. But the Orders will silence you first.
A piercing scan-resonance sweeps the yard, causing metal to shriek and crystals to fluoresce dangerously.
Then we answer with a louder song.
The fate of the fragment, the prosthetic's origin, and the party's future hinges on this moment.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Orders demand surrender. The Scavenger's barge offers escape. The Monk's truth offers revolution. How do you answer the Lattice's call?

choices.text: Use the barge to flee. Preserve the fragment for later.
choices.outcome: You escape into the industrial fog. The truth is safe, but deferred. The Orders tighten their grip on the scrapyard.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to trace the anomalous signal using unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Chanida fails. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Broadcast the fragment's song. Reveal the truth to all.
choices.outcome: The fragment's resonance overloads nearby scrap, creating a chaotic harmonic burst. Patrol ships reel. The city above hears a new song.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging tonal knowledge

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Shatter the fragment into the Lattice here. Let the world answer.
choices.outcome: The crystal breaks. A raw, primal resonance geyser erupts, parting the Lattice momentarily. The crater's pulse becomes a visible beacon. Everything changes.
choices.description: Have the monk focus prayers on the engine parts to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the monk's call. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the monk misreads the situation. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship cuts through the Lattice, its crystalline tones humming against the vessel's hull. Wind whips across the deck, carrying the scent of ozone and distant rain.
Look at it... the patterns in the lattice below. It's not just random noise. There's a structure, a rhythm to the silence left after The Silencing.
I can't just look! We need to know what's down there! The Tonal Orders have charts for everything, but they keep them locked up tighter than a skycity vault.
Of course they do. Knowledge is profit. And we're sailing with the embodiment of that principle.
A profit shared is a profit doubled, my friends! You have to see it from my perspective. The open market... it's like a great movie!
This movie is great! The drama of commerce, the tension of negotiation! You have to see it play out.
A movie where the price of admission might be our safety. The Orders control navigation for a reason. Stray frequencies can... destabilize things.
Yet... the Lattice's true song is not in the controlled charts. It is in the wild frequencies. My Order listens, but we are forbidden from... mapping.

lines_after.dialogue: Forbidden? Why? What are they hiding?
Not hiding... fearing. The Silencing began with a song. To map the open frequencies is to remember that song.
And he's the only son in his family line of Listeners. The weight of that duty must be immense.

line.dialogue: The Trade Negotiator approaches, a data-crystal glinting in his hand. 'I may have... stumbled upon a fragment. An old, unregulated frequency log. Purely academic interest, of course.'

choices.line: Examine the log cautiously. (Gain a clue, but owe the Merchant a favor.)
choices.description: Malee attempts to follow the dissonant trail, relying on engineering

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on Malee. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: Decline politely. The Monk's warning rings true. (Avoid entanglement, but learn nothing.)
choices.description: Direct Arthit to harness harmonic feedback using forbidden paths

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The resonance turns hostile. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Let Chanida snatch it for a look. (Get the data, but obviously alert the Merchant to your interest.)
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using valuable goods to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: the merchant finds the key. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the merchant hits a wall. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship sails into a region of the Lattice where the crystal formations grow dense and jagged. The engine's tone shifts to a higher, more piercing frequency to part them.
Readings are erratic. These formations don't match any approved chart. We're off the recorded paths.
Thanks to our 'academic' fragment. I can smell the Merchant's perfume on this deal—too sweet, masking something rotten.
But look! The lattice here... it's reacting. Not to our ship, but to something else. A natural resonance?
Like a water buffalo eats continuously... the Lattice here consumes and re-emits sound in a constant cycle. It's beautiful.
You perceive it! This is an open frequency node. Uncharted, pure. The data fragment only pointed the way. The truth is here, in the song itself.
Truth is a commodity! And a dangerous one. My associates in the Tonal Orders would pay handsomely to know this node's location. Or, perhaps, to ensure it remains... lost.

lines_after.dialogue: I knew it. I smelled perfume from her—from his whole deal. Now we have a map to nowhere and a target on our hull.
This is it! The real discovery! I don’t wanna go anywhere else until we understand this place.
The Merchant is signaling another ship on a secure channel. We have minutes, maybe less.

line.dialogue: The Monk looks from the wondrous, singing crystal node to the approaching ship on the horizon. 'The map is not a chart. It is this moment, this song. What do we preserve?'

choices.line: Record the frequency. We can hide the data and bargain later. (Secure the map, but leave evidence.)
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with crystal hearing to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida misreads the situation. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.line: Sabotage our own log. Let the node remain lost. (Protect the secret, but lose the knowledge.)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to test the prosthetic reaction, drawing on captain experience

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Arthit fails. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.line: Broadcast the frequency openly. Break the monopoly here and now. (Liberate the knowledge, but make powerful enemies.)
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with market connections to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His network produces an ally at the critical moment.
The gamble fails. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship’s deck hums with a strained, discordant tone. The Lattice below churns like a storm of frozen glass.
I was cheated. Swindled, you see? The Tonal Order’s monopoly on frequency maps… it’s a crime against free enterprise.
The Lattice’s natural song is being overwritten. This 'Open Frequency'… it is not liberation. It is a shout drowning out a whisper.
But we can use it! That map could get us anywhere! Give it to me! Let’s just see what it does!
Rash action is how ships get lost forever, Chanida. The merchant’s motives are… fragrant. I can smell his perfume of desperation from here.
He’s sooo cute, Arthit. Always so worried. The merchant’s selling, the monk’s preaching. Meanwhile, the real power’s right there in that crystal.
Power to reshape the world… or to break it further. The Silencing began with a note out of tune. Are we holding the next one?

lines_after.dialogue: The monk clutches his ears, a low whine piercing the air. The merchant’s smile is gone, replaced by a calculating stare.
The harmonics… they’re tearing. The lattice is resonating with the map’s frequency. It’s… adorable. In the way a storm is beautiful before it destroys.
See? Potential! Bring it on, market forces! Now, about my finder’s fee…

line.dialogue: The Open Frequency Map is active, pulsing in Pichit’s hands. The ship’s resonator is syncing, pulling it toward an uncharted vector in the Lattice.

choices.text: Override the sync. Shut it down. (Use Arthit’s technical caution to sever the connection.)
choices.description: Press the merchant for details about the Tonal Order's swindle, 15 words

line.dialogue: The ledger they sold me — every frequency mapped wrong, every resonance point deliberately shifted by half a tone," the merchant hisses, pulling a cracked crystal slate from his coat.
I — look, I already told the Guard, I told everyone, and now strangers corner me in alleys? Get away from me," the merchant snaps, backing into the shadows.

choices.text: Steer into the frequency. Follow the map. (Trust Chanida’s impulse to see where it leads.)
choices.description: Ask the monk to sing the Lattice's original song so Chanida can compare it to the corrupted version

line.dialogue: The monk closes his eyes, and a low hum rises from his chest — pure, ancient, aching. The crystals in the walls flicker in response, briefly remembering what they were.
I... I only ever heard it once, as a boy," the monk whispers, his voice cracking. What comes out is fractured, uncertain — a melody remembered wrong, worse than silence.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize it. Blend the map’s song with the Lattice’s natural tone. (Heed the Monk’s warning and use Pichit’s philosophical insight.)
choices.description: Seize the map from Chanida and tear it before Arthit can stop

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the merchant's call. The negotiator uncovers a deal no one else could make.
A costly mistake by the merchant. Hidden debts come due.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship groans, its crystal spars glowing with alien light. The deck vibrates beneath your feet—a deep, hungry growl from the world itself.
My stomach is starting to growl with dread. This isn’t navigation. It’s consumption. The Lattice is starting to… listen.
There’s something in my eye—sparks from the resonator! Look! Below! The lattice is parting like a flower!
A flower made of knives. That’s no problem, I’m sure. We’re just peeling back reality on a merchant’s tip. What could go wrong?
Everything. The structural harmonics are failing. That opening isn’t a path—it’s a wound. The ship can’t withstand this resonance.
You have opened the First Note. The one that was forbidden before The Silencing. It is the sound of ending… and of beginning.
Beginning! Yes! A new trade route! My exclusive! Don’t you dare stop now!

lines_after.dialogue: A beam of pure sonic force lances from the opening in the Lattice, striking the ship’s core. The world holds its breath.
It’s not a problem… it’s a choice. We close the wound, or we see what’s on the other side. The truth, or our survival.
The Monk begins to chant. The Merchant screams about his investment. Your crew looks to you. The Song of the World waits for your reply.

line.dialogue: The ship is caught in the beam, balanced between annihilation and revelation. The Open Frequency Map is the key, but to lock or unlock?

choices.text: Shatter the Map. Seal the wound with a discordant crash. (Save the ship, but forever blind yourself to this truth.)
choices.description: Sing the counter-frequency into the resonator while Arthit stabilizes the harmonic framework.

line.dialogue: The harmonics are locking back in—don't you dare stop singing, I can see the fractures closing!
Wrong pitch—god, wrong pitch—the whole lattice is shrieking, we've made it worse!

choices.text: Feed the Map to the ship’s resonator. Amplify the beam to breakthrough. (Risk everything to see what lies beneath the Lattice.)
choices.description: Rip the knife-flower out by its roots before it blooms fully and shreds the resonator's core.

line.dialogue: Thorns through my palm, but I've got it—the stem is screaming and I'm not letting go.
It bloomed. It bloomed in my hands—every petal a blade and now my arms are ribbons.

choices.text: Become the conductor. Have the Monk chant the Old Song while you play the Map’s Frequency. (Attempt the impossible: to heal the wound by understanding it.)
choices.description: Shield Chanida's eyes and guide her hands to the resonator's manual override by touch alone.

line.dialogue: I can feel the grooves under my fingers—the override is clicking, Pichit, I've got it blind!
Things don't go as planned. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of dying ships. Piles of broken resonator crystals reflect the smog-choked sky, while the rhythmic CLANG-CLANG of dismantling crews creates a harsh, metallic heartbeat.
Every broken hull here... it's a story that ended. The Lattice swallowed their frequencies, and now we pick at the bones.
Stop being so gloomy! There's treasure in these bones! Old charts, spare parts... Give it to me! I bet there's a hidden compartment in that wreck over there!
Treasure? More likely rust and rat nests. The salvage guilds picked this place clean decades ago. We're just here because Arthit's contact swindled him.
I was cheated. He promised coordinates to a grounded Listener outpost. All I got was a map to this rust-bowl.
Perhaps the map was not the destination, but the path. Look—between those two hulls. That resonance signature is... oddly pure amidst all this noise.
A faint, crystalline hum emanates from a half-buried ship's bow, its resonator housing cracked open like a geode.
See? I told you! She's adorable! A little ship calling out to us! Let's see what she's hiding!

lines_after.dialogue: Inside the broken housing, Chanida extracts not a crystal, but a data-sliver etched with intricate frequency patterns. It hums softly in her palm.
A map. Not a star chart. These are... raw Lattice frequencies. Unlocked. No Tonal Order encryption. This is contraband.
An Open Frequency Map. This could navigate routes the Orders haven't taxed or charted. This is why we were sent here. This is the real deal.

line.dialogue: The map is active, pulsing with latent energy. Its discovery cannot be quiet for long in this noisy place.

choices.line: Hide it immediately. Bury the sliver in a scrap pile and mark the spot.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with monk wisdom to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.line: Study it now. Try to decipher a single safe frequency to use as an escape route.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging singer voice

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The resonance turns hostile. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.line: Find a buyer. The scrapyard must have a fence who deals in 'acoustic curiosities.'
choices.description: Have the villager risk using irrigation to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: Exactly as the villager hoped. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
A costly mistake by the villager. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: Before a choice can be made, the scrapyard's ambient clanging shifts. A new, aggressive rhythm cuts through—the staccato thrum of approaching grav-boots.
Well, well. Look what the rust-winds blew in. Heard a pretty little chime from this sector. Sounds like payday.
Three sky pirates step from behind a tower of engine blocks. Their leader, a woman with resonator-scars across her arms, is standing right in front of Pichit.
The sound finds its listeners. You heard the map's awakening.
Clever boy. That sliver's been singing since you woke it. We monitor these junk-heaps for such... unscheduled concerts. Hand it over. It's worth more than your lives.
Bring it on! We found it, it's ours!
Are you sure? They have disruptor pistols. We have a cynical mechanic and a philosopher.
Is everything all right? No. But we have the high ground on this debris pile. Tactically, it's something.

lines_after.dialogue: High ground? Cute. We know frequencies that can liquefy that junk you're standing on. Last chance. The map.
The lead pirate thumbs a device on her belt. The metal underfoot begins to vibrate with a sickening, grinding whine.
They are not bluffing. The map's signal has painted a target on us. We must act.

line.dialogue: The pirates are priming a destabilizer frequency. The map in Chanida's hand is glowing hotter.

choices.line: Toss a decoy. Throw a spent power cell away from the party and run in the opposite direction.
choices.description: Hold the sliver high and command it to sing louder, trusting the signal to overwhelm them.

line.dialogue: You want the song? Then *listen* — really listen — and let it decide who's worthy.
It... it's not responding to me like before. The signal's slipped through my fingers like sand.

choices.line: Use the map. Activate a random frequency from it, hoping it disrupts their tech or the ground itself.
choices.description: Let Chanida rush forward while you circle behind through the scrap pillars.

line.dialogue: Keep your eyes on *me*, rust-breath — that's right, look away from the clever one.
Scrap pillars weren't as hollow as I thought — whole pile came down on me!

choices.line: Stand your ground. Challenge their knowledge. Question if they can even read the map they're stealing.
choices.description: Offer to split what the sliver reveals — the map, not the prize.

line.dialogue: We both want what's at the end. Why bleed out here when the map needs two hands to read?
I misjudged them — they don't want treasure, they want the *singing* itself.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of broken ships. The air smells of ozone and rust, every metallic clang creating dissonant echoes across the Lattice below.
The pirate said the map's hidden in the old dredger's control tower. Look at that thing—it's held together by prayers and rust.
Is everything under control? This entire structure looks like it could collapse if someone sneezed too hard.
Relax, Arthit. Most Thais are Buddhist—we believe in karma, not structural engineering. Besides, it probably won't be too expensive if we just fall through.
Listen to the metal's song. Each plate vibrates differently—some notes are stable, others... decaying. There's a path if we follow the harmonics.
A group of skycity residents huddle near a salvage furnace, their faces illuminated by the orange glow. One breaks away and approaches.
You're the ones asking about frequencies? The price for that knowledge is rather expensive for Thais like us. The Tonal Orders have ears everywhere here.
We're not buying, we're finding. That pirate gave up the location—are you gonna stand in front of me and pretend you don't know what we're after?

lines_after.dialogue: The control tower's interior is a graveyard of dead consoles. But one panel still glows with faint blue light—a frequency analyzer, still powered.
Well, look at that. The pirate wasn't completely full of hot air. This thing's actually recording something.
It's not just recording... it's receiving. An open frequency, broadcasting on a loop. This is the map—not coordinates, but a living signal.

line.dialogue: The analyzer shows three possible methods to extract the frequency data, each with different risks to the delicate machinery:

choices.text: Direct harmonic link (Pichit's resonance)
choices.outcome: Pichit attunes to the machine's frequency, safely downloading the map but leaving an energy signature that might be traced.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with leg resonance, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee overreaches. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Manual crystal alignment (Arthit's precision)
choices.outcome: Arthit carefully recalibrates the resonator crystals, getting clean data but taking time while pirates search the scrapyard.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with resonant staff to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The risk doesn't pay off. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.text: Override the power grid (Chanida's improvisation)
choices.outcome: Chanida reroutes power from nearby salvage equipment, creating a surge that downloads the map instantly but causes a blackout across the yard.
choices.description: The villager presses forward with village secrets to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The islander's wisdom cuts through complexity.
The resonance turns hostile. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard plunges into darkness as power fails. Emergency crystal lamps flicker to life, casting long, dancing shadows between the wrecked ships.
I feel uncomfortable. That blackout was too noticeable. We should have taken the slower approach.
We got the map, didn't we? The open frequency leads to the Listeners' hidden archive. This changes everything!
Changes how much the Tonal Orders will pay to silence us, you mean. Look—shadows moving on the gantries above. We've got company.
Figures drop from the darkness, landing with metallic thuds. Sky pirates, their faces obscured by resonance-dampening masks, form a half-circle around the party.
You're gonna be sorry for taking what's ours. That frequency map belongs to whoever's strong enough to hold it. And right now... that's us.
This knowledge doesn't belong to anyone. It's a piece of the world's song that was hidden. Keeping it locked away hurts us all.
Pretty words. But he's only interested in profit. And your little discovery is about to become our profit. Hand over the data crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: The pirates scatter, disappearing into the maze of wreckage. The open frequency map pulses warmly in Pichit's hand—a secret that could break the Tonal Orders' monopoly.
They'll come back with reinforcements. We need to leave Tha Khwae immediately. But where do we go with this?
To the Listeners. This frequency... it's an invitation. And I think it's time we answered.
Great. More monks. I'm sure they'll be thrilled to see us bringing pirate trouble to their doorstep.
But we did it! We actually found it! This changes everything about navigating the Lattice!

line.dialogue: The pirates are preparing to rush your position. You have moments to decide how to use the environment and the newly acquired frequency knowledge:

choices.text: Use the frequency to destabilize nearby wreckage
choices.outcome: The resonant frequency causes loose metal plates to collapse, creating barriers and allowing escape but destroying potentially valuable salvage.
choices.description: Draw your pulser and hold Bandit at point-blank range while Chanida uploads the map.

line.dialogue: Back off, Bandit — I will put you in the ground before you finish that sentence.
My hand's shaking. I can't hold the sight steady and Bandit's already reaching.

choices.text: Broadcast the open frequency as a distraction
choices.outcome: The pure tone temporarily disrupts the pirates' equipment and draws attention from other scavengers, creating chaos to slip away in.
choices.description: Bluff that Malee already transmitted the frequency to three dead drops across the district.

line.dialogue: Kill us and the Tonal Orders still lose — Malee seeded the frequency an hour ago.
I mention dead drops but Malee's face goes blank — she didn't seed anything and Bandit knows it.

choices.text: Confront them with the map's implications
choices.outcome: Reveal that the frequency proves the Tonal Orders have been lying about safe navigation routes, potentially turning some pirates to your side but risking capture if they don't believe you.
choices.description: Offer Bandit a cut of the payout in exchange for covering your trail from the Orders.

line.dialogue: You want blood or you want credits? Because I'm only carrying one of those.
Bandit laughs and I realize

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of quiet. Vast crystalline shelves rise into shadowed vaults, each etched with tonal sequences that hum faintly when you pass. The air smells of ozone and old vellum.
Listen... the harmonics in this wing are tuned to suppress echoes. Every step we take is absorbed. It's designed to focus the mind, but it feels... hungry.
