choices.line: Confront the merchant directly. (Try to reason or intimidate him into calling off his associates.)
choices.description: Pull out your tuner and scan the merchant's personal resonance to see if he's hiding anything else.

line.dialogue: Interesting—you've got harmonic dampeners surgically embedded in your spine. You're not just a procurement specialist, you're a smuggler with military-grade modifications.
The scanner's fizzling—whatever he's

lines_before.dialogue: The late afternoon sun casts long shadows across the terraces. The rhythmic, peaceful sounds of the gardens now feel laden with a new, watchful tension.
The Negotiator's smile was a locked door. We have the pieces—the missing shipments, the 'borrowed' resonator parts—but not the key.
The key is profit. Always is. He's hiding something that makes this little agricultural heist worth the risk.
So we find it! That villager, the one who looked like he'd swallowed a sour note, he knows more. He's scared.
Approaching him directly could cause a panic. We need to be careful. The stability of this entire terrace could be at stake.
As if summoned, the Skycity Resident from before shuffles into view, glancing over his shoulder nervously.
You're still here. I have work to do... but I can't focus. Not with this hanging over us.
What's hanging over you? The silence here isn't just peaceful, is it? It's waiting.

lines_after.dialogue: The Negotiator... he's not just trading grain. He's been meeting someone at the old irrigation control spire. At night. There’s someone waiting for you there, I think.
A clandestine meeting. How utterly predictable. And probably the source of our 'borrowed' resonator components.
I got my answer now. Let's go see who's so eager for a midnight chat!
The villager hurries away, leaving you with a direction and a deepening sense of unease as dusk settles on the gardens.

line.dialogue: The control spire is a skeletal structure of pipes and old crystal conduits at the garden's lowest, mist-shrouded edge. How do you approach?

choices.text: Send Chanida ahead to scout. Her agility is perfect for the latticework of pipes.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to trace the anomalous signal, relying on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit overreaches. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.text: Move as a group, using the terraces' natural acoustic cover—the sound of water and wind—to mask your approach.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use Listener training and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit hits a wall. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze the spire's structure first. A cautious approach might reveal hidden dangers or alternate routes.
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using negotiation to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: Exactly as the merchant hoped. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the merchant fails. His network delivers bad intelligence.

acts.title: The Cost of a New Dawn

lines_before.dialogue: At the base of the spire, you find the Trade Negotiator in heated discussion with a figure in mended Listener robes. Between them, on a crate, glows a complex, unfinished resonator array—the core of a Resonance Prosthetic.
The frequency stability isn't there! My buyer needs a leg that won't shatter the user's spine on its first step!
The purity of the crystal is compromised! You sourced sub-grade lattice shards. The harmonics are... jagged.
So this is the harvest. Not grain, but hope. Stolen and sold.
Hope is a commodity, friend! This little project funds the entire terrace's quota. Aren't you tired of seeing good people starve for the Orders' pride?
You're using untested, dangerous resonance tech on people. The risk of a feedback cascade...
He's a nice guy, really. Just corrupt and morally bankrupt. Standard issue.
You look run down, Negotiator. All this double-dealing must be exhausting. Hand over the prototype.

lines_after.dialogue: Or what? You'll tell the Tonal Orders? They'll seize everything—the prototype, the terraces, our future! I'll have a look at my options... and they say you leave, now.
He gestures sharply. From the mist, two rough-looking enforcers step forward, makeshift resonator-knives humming in their hands. The Listener backs away, terrified.
You're trading one person's mobility for the safety of many. A younger version of me might have seen the logic. Now, I just see the cost.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator has made his stand. The stolen prosthetic prototype glows between you, a symbol of corrupted hope. How do you resolve this?

choices.text: Appeal to the crowd. Shout for the skycity residents to witness this corruption. Public pressure is a powerful weapon.
choices.description: Smash the nearest crystal crate against the merchant's display table, 15 words exactly

line.dialogue: Your harvest ends here — I'll shatter every last shard before I let you sell another soul's worth of stolen hope.
The crate was heavier than I expected — my hands slip and the crystals scatter across the floor, still intact, still bleeding light.

choices.text: Challenge the Negotiator's logic. Propose a deal to legitimize the project with the Listeners, cutting out his profiteering. A diplomatic, but risky, solution.
choices.description: Grab the merchant by his lapels and demand the name of his buyer

line.dialogue: You're going to tell me who's buying this stolen dawn, or I'll squeeze until your throat forgets how to lie — who funds this harvest?
He twists free before I can pin him — stumbles backward behind his bodyguards, straightening his coat with a sneer. 'Touch me again and you'll never leave this market alive.

choices.text: Seize the prototype by force. Disable the enforcers and take the crystal core. It's the fastest way, but violence could shatter the terrace's fragile peace.
choices.description: Quietly pocket a crystal fragment as evidence and walk away unnoticed

line.dialogue: My fingers close around a shard still warm with stolen frequency — I slip
the merchant is thwarted. His network delivers bad intelligence.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform juts from the floating city's underbelly, suspended over the crystalline expanse. Dawn paints the Lattice in hues of rose and gold, its silent hum a backdrop to the waking world.
Look at that... each morning, the patterns are never the same. The world remakes itself while we sleep.
And each new pattern could hide a fracture. We should check the resonator calibrations. Good morning, by the way.
Morning! I'm in a good mood. The pay for this surface survey has to be good, right? We're risking our necks down here!
Don't count your credits before they're vaulted. The Tonal Orders skim every contract. Good night's sleep is the only profit you can guarantee.
A low, discordant chime echoes from the Lattice below. The light shivers.
A natural resonance... or a signal? The Listeners would meditate on such a sound for weeks.
Let's go see! Our ship can handle a quick dip, can't it?

lines_after.dialogue: Protocol says we wait for the full spectral analysis. The Lattice is not a playground.
Protocol also says we get paid. The scan shows crystalline formations below that scan as salvage-grade. Could be a good haul.
The dawn offers clarity. Perhaps it's a sign to begin.

line.dialogue: The strange chime fades, leaving an inviting silence. Do we investigate?

choices.text: Follow Chanida's impulse. Descend immediately to investigate the source.
choices.description: Pichit channels tonal knowledge toward the crystal ground, hoping to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
A costly mistake by Pichit. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Heed Arthit's caution. Run a full scan from the platform first.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging crystal hearing

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Chanida fails. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.text: Agree with Malee. Plot a course for the salvage, keeping an ear out for the sound.
choices.description: The pirate uses intimidation to decode the distress signal near the crystal ground

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Smuggling routes provide an escape.
Things don't go as planned. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship parts the crystalline surface like a stone through mercury. Below, a forest of shattered spires glows with trapped light. The air thrums with latent energy.
Readings are unstable. This sector isn't on any sanctioned chart. We shouldn't be here.
You heard that, didn't you? That scraping sound. It's coming from the east spire.
I heard a strange noise too. Like metal on crystal. Scavengers. Or worse.
A jagged silhouette detaches from a spire. A battered skiff, bristling with mismatched resonators, glides into view. A flag of knotted cables flies from its mast.
Sky pirates... They've heard the same whispers we have.
Well, well! Look what the Lattice coughed up. You're on our frequency, little songbirds. That salvage is spoken for.
We heard everything! You just got here!

lines_after.dialogue: Heh. Ear to the ground, kid. The Groundless know secrets the Orders burned. Now, you can clear off... or contribute to our 'collection'.
The Groundless Movement? So the rumors are true. Anarchists living on the surface.
Pirates. They're pirates. And they have a harmonic disruptor trained on us.

line.dialogue: The pirate skiff's weapons hum to life. How do we respond?

choices.text: Comply and withdraw. Let the pirates have the salvage. Live to fly another day.
choices.description: Rig the resonance array to broadcast a false signal masking our position from the pirates.

line.dialogue: Array's calibrated — they'll sweep right past us like ghosts in the void.
The array's screaming our coordinates louder than before — every ship in this sector just heard us.

choices.text: Attempt to negotiate. Appeal to their ideology or offer a trade of knowledge.
choices.description: Follow the metal-on-crystal scraping toward its source, weapons drawn, lights dimmed.

line.dialogue: There — behind that crystalline shelf. Something's been carving symbols into the wall. They're fresh.
The sound stopped. Whatever made it knows we're coming, and it's circling behind us now.

choices.text: Stand your ground. Prepare for a fight amidst the unstable spires.
choices.description: Open a channel to the sky pirates and offer to share what we've found in exchange for safe passage.

line.dialogue: Their captain bit — she's curious enough to talk before shooting. We just bought ourselves time.
They laughed. Said they don't share with sanctified-map cowards, and our shuttle just got tagged with a tracking slug.

lines_before.dialogue: The party reaches a massive crystalline spire on the Lattice surface. Its facets hum with trapped harmonics. A crude pirate outpost is built into its base, pulsing with stolen resonator energy.
Oy! You lot are a long way from your comfy cities. You heard that, didn't you? The whole spire's singing a new tune since you showed up.
We're not here for a chat. We heard a strange noise from this spire. Something's wrong with the frequency.
Could you speak more slowly? Your 'pirate charm' is just grating noise. We know you're hoarding resonance data from the Silencing era.
Sharp ears! Data's worth more than your ship. But maybe we can deal. You're back late to this party, the Lattice's getting restless.
Caution. Their resonator is jury-rigged. One wrong note could shatter this entire formation.
Every sound leaves an echo in the crystal. What are you trying to amplify here? It feels... forced.
(Emerging from a crevice) They're not amplifying. They're *drowning something out*. A natural frequency from deep below. The Groundless talk about it—a sound of the old world.

lines_after.dialogue: The spire thrums, responding to the raised voices. Pinpoints of light race through the crystal like nervous stars.
So the pirates and the Groundless are after the same ghost frequency. How poetic.
We need to hear it for ourselves. Without their static.

line.dialogue: The pirate's rig is unstable. We can attempt to interface with the spire directly, but it's risky.

choices.text: NEGOTIATE. Use the Tonal Orders' authority as a bluff to access the data peacefully.
choices.description: Step forward and demand the bandit reveal what data they're hiding. [Intimidate

line.dialogue: Whatever you're hoarding, we'll take it from your cold hands if we must. Talk.
We don't have time for—wait, why are there more of them behind us?

choices.text: SABOTAGE. Chanida and Arthit create a diversion while Pichit and Malee hack the resonator.
choices.description: Draw your weapon and cut the bandit's belt pouch clean off. [Fight

line.dialogue: Oops. Your 'data' just scattered across the dirt. Want to pick it up first, or should we?
My blade got stuck in the—okay, everyone run NOW.

choices.text: LISTEN. Ignore the machine. Have Pichit attempt to Sing, to harmonize with the buried frequency directly.
choices.description: Signal Malee to flirt while Chanida quietly pockets the data shard. [Stealth

line.dialogue: You know, rugged types are my weakness. Tell me about this data of yours...
Chanida, I can only stall so long when your elbow just knocked over their lantern!

lines_before.dialogue: The decision triggers a cascade. The spire's light intensifies, then fractures. The very surface of the Lattice groans, crystalline plates shifting like tectonic glass. The hidden frequency surges—a deep, mournful drone that vibrates in your bones.
It's waking up! Don't change the subject now—this is what the Groundless warned of! The Silencing wasn't an end... it was a pause!
The charts are useless! Everything's changing! You might change your mind about calling us pirates when your city falls from the sky!
Resonance overload! The harmonic feedback is tearing the local lattice structure apart. We must adapt or be silenced with it!
So the world's greatest secret is a catastrophic lullaby. Don't leave it on! We have to modulate this or shut it down for good.
Shut it down? This is the truth they've been hiding! The Lattice isn't just a barrier... it's a *memory*.
(Eyes closed, voice resonating) It's a plea. A single, unfinished chord from the moment of the Silencing. It wants... resolution.
The ground beneath you crystallizes and cracks. The sky pirate's ship moans as its resonator shatters. The deep frequency swells, offering a choice: complete the chord, or sever it forever.

lines_after.dialogue: The Lattice settles, but into a new, unknown configuration. The spire is gone. In its place, a perfectly smooth, silent plane of crystal reflects the shattered sky.
The Groundless... were right. The foundation of everything can change.
And we are the instruments of that change.

line.dialogue: The unresolved chord hangs in the air, a power that could rewrite the Lattice's fundamental song. What do we do with the world's memory?

choices.text: RESTORE THE OLD SILENCE. Suppress the chord. Preserve the current, fragile stability of the Floating Cities, even if it's built on a lie.
choices.description: Pichit uses monk wisdom to follow the dissonant trail near the crystal ground

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Pichit misreads the situation. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: ANCHOR THE FREQUENCY. Capture it in a resonator. Give this knowledge—this power—to the people, not just the Orders or the pirates.
choices.description: Ask Malee to harness harmonic feedback, drawing on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The risk doesn't pay off. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: COMPLETE THE CHORD. Sing with it. Let the Silencing's final moment play out, no matter what new world it reveals or creates.
choices.description: The scavenger attempts to listen for the ghost ship's echo, relying on crystal fragments

line.dialogue: the scavenger succeeds. Hard-won survival skills turn the tide.
The attempt backfires on the scavenger. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow yawns before you—a jagged maw in the floating island's underside. Inside, the air is cool, tasting of damp stone and ancient dust. Every footstep, every whisper, multiplies into a ghostly chorus that lingers in the cavernous dark.
Listen to that echo! This place is singing back at us. Come on, the ruins have to be deeper in!
Singing, or laughing at the idiots who walk into pitch-black holes in the sky. Watch your step. The last 'discovery' here was probably a broken neck.
She's not wrong. The acoustics are... unpredictable. A wrong note could trigger a collapse. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Yet the echoes feel like memories. As if the stone is trying to remember the sounds from before The Silencing.
Exactly! So let's go! Are you going home yet? We just got here!
Ahead, the tunnel widens into a vast chamber. Faint, natural luminescence glows from crystalline veins in the walls, illuminating crude murals and the skeletal remains of pre-Silencing machinery.
Ah! Fellow travelers! I was beginning to think I was the only soul with the sense to appreciate this place's... quieter virtues.

lines_after.dialogue: You're back late! Or rather, I am. I've been cataloging resonance patterns. A profitable hobby, if one knows what to listen for.
A Tonal Order negotiator, lost in a hole. How quaint. What are you really selling?
Knowledge, dear lady. Pure knowledge. For instance, I'm sorry for being late to the party, but I believe I've found a frequency map fragment. Useless to me, of course. I deal in finished products.

line.dialogue: The merchant holds up a sliver of etched crystal. He smiles, but his eyes are calculating.

choices.line: Offer to trade for supplies. (Chanida groans at the delay.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the whispering wall and hum a single sustained note.

line.dialogue: The vibration just shifted — there's a hollow chamber behind this section. We can breach it.
Congratulations, you've serenaded the rock. Now your hand is numb and the wall is still laughing at us.

choices.line: Ask what he wants for the map fragment directly. (Malee narrows her eyes.)
choices.description: Toss a copper coin down the corridor and count the seconds before the echo dies.

line.dialogue: Three full seconds — this passage descends further than our torchlight reveals. The depth is deliberate.
You just gave our money to a cave. The echo swallowed it and gave nothing back except more mockery.

choices.line: Politely decline and move to explore the ruins. (Arthit nods in approval.)
choices.description: Signal everyone to fall completely silent and cup your ear toward the deepest fissure.

line.dialogue: Do you hear that? Beneath the whisper — footsteps. Someone has walked this path before us, recently.
Nothing. Just the blood pounding in your own skull pretending to be something ancient. Let's move.

lines_before.dialogue: Deeper within The Hollow, the passages twist like a petrified labyrinth. The echoes grow stranger—sometimes repeating a word seconds after it's spoken, sometimes distorting it into something unrecognizable.
The harmonic feedback is increasing. It's not a problem yet, but we must be mindful of our volume.
My stomach is starting to growl! Can ancient echoes be eaten? Didn't think so.
Ugh, there's something in my eye. Probably centuries of neglect and disappointment. This place is a tomb.
Or a library. Listen. That low hum isn't us. It's the island itself. A foundational frequency.
A rough laugh cuts through the ambient sound, followed by the scrape of boots on stone. Figures emerge from a side passage, clad in scavenged leather and metal.
Well, look what the echo dragged in. Tourists. The merchant said you might've picked up a shiny map piece.
Of course he did. That's no problem. We just love making new friends in dark places.

lines_after.dialogue: Smart mouth. Hand over the frequency data. The Open Map ain't for little Listeners. Sky's for the takin'.
You brought two fists and a bad attitude. We brought four! Well, three and a half. Arthit's more of a 'strongly worded warning' guy.
This is a confined space. Conflict is ill-advised. The acoustic shockwaves could be catastrophic.
The pirate is right about one thing. The map isn't just data. It's a key. But to what?

line.dialogue: The sky pirates spread out, hands on weapons. The strange echoes seem to lean in, waiting.

choices.line: Try to bluff, claiming you've already transmitted the map to your ship. (Use the echoes to sell the lie.)
choices.description: Chanida uses frequency mapping to follow the dissonant trail near the unusual acoustics

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: Offer a trade: the fragment for safe passage and their knowledge of hidden frequencies.
choices.description: Have Malee focus crystal prosthetic on the unusual acoustics to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Things don't go as planned. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.line: Stand your ground. Prepare to fight in the unstable acoustics of The Hollow.
choices.description: Direct the merchant to record the spectral signature using negotiation

line.dialogue: the merchant makes it work. Hidden leverage shifts the balance.
Defeat. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The party rests fitfully in a chamber of the Hollow, the strange acoustics turning whispers into shouts. As the first light from a phosphorescent moss colony begins to glow, a new day in the deep stone begins.
I can't eat anything. Not after what we saw last night. Those carvings... they weren't just maps.
They were a warning. A history of the Silencing from the people who caused it. We probably can't finish processing it all before the others find us.
But we have to! This 'Open Frequency Map' they wrote about... from morning until evening, they worked to perfect it. A navigation system anyone could use, not just the Tonal Orders!
A dawn of true understanding, cut short. Their final entries speak of a 'Great Resonance' meant to share knowledge, not hoard it.
A scuffling echo, wrong and sharp, reverberates from the tunnel behind you. The Sky Pirate steps into the glow, her resonator pistol aimed.
Enough archaeology. You found the core chamber. Hand over the coordinates for the master resonance frequency. The one that unlocks all the Lattice paths.
And if we say we haven't found it?

line.dialogue: The Pirate's weapon hums. The Trade Negotiator emerges from another shadow, his smile thin.

choices.text: Bluff: Claim the frequency is buried and requires all of you to unearth it safely.
choices.description: Have Arthit focus ship navigation on the ancient ruins to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Arthit makes it work. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The lattice has other plans. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Defy: Refuse outright, betting the Pirate won't fire in such an unstable acoustic zone.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with leg resonance to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Malee hits a wall. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Reveal: Show them the true, terrible cost of the map—the energy required is a person's resonant life force.
choices.description: Convince the pirate to use secret frequencies and decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: the pirate finds the key. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the pirate is thwarted. The bandit's ruthlessness alienates allies.

lines_after.dialogue: Now, now. No need for that. We're all reasonable people. My associate here is just... passionate about deregulation. Think of the profit if everyone could sail!
You want to turn the greatest discovery since the Silencing into a... a business plan?
The Negotiator's eyes gleam. The Pirate's grip tightens. The ancient chamber, meant for a chorus of understanding, now holds only the discord of greed and fear.

lines_before.dialogue: You are forced to the heart of the Hollow: a vast geode pulsing with internal light. At its center stands a plinth holding a single, perfect crystal—the master resonator. The air thrums with potential.
At last! The ultimate monopoly breaker. Or... the ultimate monopoly maker, depending on who holds it. For the adventurous, I suppose.
Shut it. Activate it. I want to hear the song that cracks the sky open.
Pichit, don't. The inscriptions are clear. The resonator doesn't use stored energy. It uses a Singer's innate resonance. It would... consume you. You need to love yourself more than this idea.
He loves it. The heroic sacrifice. But look around. This place isn't a tomb; it's a monument to their failure. They built the key but refused to pay the price.
Malee's right, but for the wrong reason! They didn't fail. They chose *not* to do it. They saved their Singers. They loved themselves, and each other, more than power.
A choice between loving the world and loving the self. To become a key is to cease being a person. But to leave it here...

The Pirate raises her pistol toward Chanida. The Negotiator edges toward the plinth, a harmonic disruptor in his hand. The crystal's song is a whisper in your soul, offering a power that demands everything.

line.dialogue: The final choice is yours alone. The true map is not of the Lattice, but of your own heart.

choices.text: Shatter the Crystal: Destroy the key forever, preserving the monopoly but saving lives. The old balance remains.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using unauthorized tones to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Seize It for the Listeners: Fight your captors and take the crystal to your order, to be studied safely for generations.
choices.description: Pichit channels monk wisdom toward the ancient ruins, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Defeat. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Become the Key: Touch the crystal and let your resonance flow into it, unlocking the map for all—and paying the ultimate price.
choices.description: The merchant uses trade ledger to listen for the ghost ship's echo near the unusual acoustics

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the merchant loses control. A rival merchant sabotages the plan.

lines_after.dialogue: In the Hollow's silence, your choice resonates. It echoes through the stone, a new frequency added to the memory of the world. Some discoveries are not found, but made. Some maps chart not places, but souls.
Pichit... what have you done?
What they thought they had to. The most human thing of all.
No. It's not over. We'll find another way. We have to. We carry the map now, in here.

lines_before.dialogue: The party's resonance ship, the *Whisper of Thorns*, rests on a rare solid outcropping piercing the Lattice surface. Below, the crystalline plane shimmers with internal light, humming a low, complex chord.
Look at it... a whole world of frozen song. Where did you lose it, Arthit? The signal from that lost Singer's ship?
The echo is faint, but triangulated to this sector. The Lattice interference is severe. We must be cautious.
Cautious, shmautious! The charts show a salvage platform a klick east. Let's move! I'm glad to know there's something out here besides pretty lights.
Pretty lights that'll crystallize your bones if you step on the wrong frequency. But sure, let's chase a ghost ship. My social calendar was clear.
A hunched figure in patched environmental gear emerges from behind a spire of resonant crystal, leveling a jury-rigged sonic cutter.
Hold! This ain't Tonal Order turf. You're on my scrap-line.
We mean no intrusion. We're listening for an echo. A ship called the *Eidolon*.

lines_after.dialogue: The *Eidolon*? That's bad resonance. Ship's ghost walks the surface. You'd be better off scavenging silence.
We're not here for scrap! We're here to find it. So, you've heard its song?
Heard? Felt it. In the teeth. Makes the Lattice weep wrong notes. I'm trying to lose weight, not my sanity. But... the pirates might know more. They hunt those frequencies.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points toward a distant, jagged formation. 'Pirate lookout's that way. They're only interested in profit and pain.' How does the party proceed?

choices.line: Offer a trade for information (Use spare ship parts).
choices.description: Walk the narrow ice ridge toward the salvage platform, testing each step with the sonic probe, 15 words

line.dialogue: Each step rings clear—the ice holds. Move slowly and keep your breathing shallow.
That crack you heard? That was your boot crystallizing from the sole up. Don't move.

choices.line: Follow the Scavenger's warning and search for the *Eidolon*'s signal directly.
choices.description: Broadcast a harmonic counter-frequency to neutralize the crystallization field before approaching, 14 words

line.dialogue: Frequency matched and inverted. The field just collapsed—you can see the frost retreating.
Wrong harmonic. You just amplified the resonance threefold—everyone back, it's spreading toward us!

choices.line: Head to the pirate lookout to ask questions, cautiously.
choices.description: Rappel down the fissure directly, bypassing the platform to reach the signal source faster, 13 words

line.dialogue: Ha! My kind of shortcut—rope's holding, and I can see the echo chamber below!
The rope just turned to crystal mid-descent. I'm hanging here like a chandelier—someone get me DOWN!

lines_before.dialogue: Choosing to approach the pirates, the party navigates a canyon of singing crystal. The air thrums with a predatory vibration.
Lift it carefully! This crystal is unstable. A wrong step could trigger a harmonic cascade.
Wonderful. Crushed by a choir. He's only interested in the quickest route to a payday, and we're walking right to him.
On a fortified ledge overlooking a deep lattice-fall, a sky pirate in leathers and a resonator-amplifier on his shoulder watches them approach.
Well, look what the resonance dragged in! Lost, little birds? The sky's for them with the sharpest beaks.
We seek knowledge, not conflict. We heard you know the hidden frequencies. The *Eidolon*.
Interested in ghosts, are ya? That ship's a siren call to fools. Its echo leads to a graveyard of crystal. Very... interesting for salvage.
So you know where it is! Tell us!

lines_after.dialogue: Maybe I do. But my info ain't free. You got coin? Or maybe that shiny little resonator on your ship?
Thank you for your concern, but our ship parts are non-negotiable. How about we trade for something else? Like not turning you into a harmonic footnote?

Spunky! I like it. Fine. The *Eidolon*'s last echo pinged near the Shivering Chasm. Deep surface, nasty acoustics. My crew's been... interested in checking it out. Could use extra hands that know their harmonics.

line.dialogue: The pirate offers a tense alliance, his eyes gleaming with opportunistic greed. The way to the Shivering Chasm is perilous.

choices.line: Accept the pirate's offer of guidance to the Chasm, despite the clear risk.
choices.description: Strike the crystal with your blade to shatter it before the bandit reaches it

line.dialogue: Perfect timing — the resonance collapsed inward. Now we just need to survive what it attracted.
Brilliant. You've turned an unstable crystal into a fragmentation grenade. I hope you're proud.

choices.line: Politely decline and attempt to find the Chasm using the Scavenger's earlier hints and your own charts.
choices.description: Offer the bandit a cut of whatever the crystal reveals in exchange for safe passage

line.dialogue: A pragmatic offer. Greed can be redirected more easily than violence — well negotiated.
You think I'm some marketplace haggler? I take what I want, and right now I want everything.

choices.line: Attempt to subdue the pirate and take his charts by force.
choices.description: Channel a stabilizing frequency through your own voice to calm the crystal's resonance

line.dialogue: The harmonic interference is settling — you actually matched its base frequency. That shouldn't be possible.
You sang to a bomb. You literally sang to a bomb, and now my ears are bleeding alongside my dignity.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform offers a breathtaking but terrifying view of the Lattice Surface. Below, crystalline spikes shift and hum, their patterns reacting to the faintest sound from above. A derelict Resonance Ship is partially embedded in the crystal, its hull fractured and glowing with a faint, sickly light.
Well, there's our haunted ship. Looks like it tried to swallow a mountain and choked. I heard a strange noise coming from it. A low, pulsing drone.
That's the echo! You heard that, didn't you? The lost ship's final frequency is still trapped in the Lattice. We need to get closer.
The structural integrity is compromised. One wrong vibration and those crystal formations could shear the hull in half. We must be precise.
The Lattice remembers everything. That drone... it's a memory of the crash, playing on an endless loop. A soul made of sound.
You city-folk shouldn't be here. That wreck's been singing its death-song for cycles. Bad luck to listen too close.
Heh. Scavenger's right, for once. That frequency's unstable. But I heard everything the Tonal Orders said about this place. They sealed records of this ship. What're they hiding?
Probably that their fancy charts are worthless if a ship can just get eaten by the ground. Let's see what's so special.

lines_after.dialogue: As you approach the wreck, the pulsing drone grows louder, vibrating in your bones. Flickering light spills from a crack in the hull, projecting ghostly images of the ship's final moments against the crystal facets.
I heard a strange noise... like whispering. Inside the light.
Not noise. Resonance. The Lattice is showing us what happened. We're not just finding a ship; we're listening to its last breath.

line.dialogue: How do you investigate the spectral echo?

choices.line: Tune your personal resonator to match the drone. Harmonize with the memory.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to follow the dissonant trail, drawing on crystal hearing

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Chanida is thwarted. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: Send a small probe into the crack. Map the interior risks first.
choices.description: Pichit attempts to harness harmonic feedback, relying on staff meditation

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Pichit overreaches. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Strike the nearby crystal with a harmonic hammer. Attempt to shatter the memory-loop and free the echo.
choices.description: The pirate attempts to decode the distress signal, relying on intimidation

line.dialogue: the pirate's expertise pays off. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the pirate misreads the situation. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The interior of the lost ship is a tomb of frozen light. Crystalline growths have pierced the deck, forming a jagged forest. At the heart of the bridge, a massive, perfect crystal contains the shimmering afterimage of the lost crew, their mouths open in a silent scream. The pirate and scavenger have followed you in, weapons drawn.
The core resonator! It's still intact! That's a fortune right there. When did he get here? The Captain... his ghost is right there!
This ain't salvage. This is a grave. That crystal's a recording. It's their home now.
The crystal is interfaced with the ship's log. Extracting the core resonator will erase the echo permanently. It is the only way to obtain the navigation data we need.
So we rob a tomb. Wonderful. I'm not home a lot, but even I know this is messed up.
We can't just delete them! They're trying to tell us something! Look at their hands—they're pointing to the resonator, not clinging to it.
Home isn't always a place. Sometimes it's the moment you cease. They are asking for an ending. But what kind?

The ghostly images shift, focusing on you. A whispered chorus, synthesized from the ambient hum, fills the air: *'...frequency...wrong...charts...lied...'* The Lattice beneath your feet begins to resonate in sympathy, cracks spreading.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal shatters, not with violence, but with a profound chord of release. The ghostly images smile, then dissolve into motes of light. In the sudden silence, the Lattice stabilizes. The core resonator, now inert, holds a single, perfect data-shard.
Huh. You... you gave 'em peace. Didn't think you sky-folk knew how.
The shard! That's the real treasure. The truth the Orders buried. You've made a powerful enemy today.
And found a more powerful truth. Some silences are meant to be broken.

line.dialogue: The data-shard reveals the truth. What do you do with it?

choices.line: Deliver it to the Listeners. Let the monastic order safeguard and study the truth.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to trace the anomalous signal, leveraging staff meditation

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Use it as leverage with the Tonal Orders. Trade the secret for safe passage and influence.
choices.description: Arthit volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging forbidden paths

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
Arthit is thwarted. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.line: Broadcast the frequency openly. Let every Singer and pirate hear the proof that the Orders' charts are fatally flawed.
choices.description: The pirate presses forward with smuggling routes to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the pirate hits a wall. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform, a precarious metal scaffold anchored to a floating island's underside, offers a breathtaking yet terrifying view.
Below, the Lattice stretches to infinity, a kaleidoscope of crystalline facets catching the sun. A low, harmonic hum vibrates through the structure.
Look at those patterns shifting! (I) wanna ask you something… Do you think the Lattice is *thinking*?
It's not thinking. It's reacting. Like a dumb, beautiful machine. And we're the idiots standing on its surface.
Keep your voices low. Certain frequencies can trigger… reactions. This place is very liveable for us only because we're careful.
Each hum, each shimmer… it's a record of the Silencing. The world's memory, frozen in crystal.
You Listeners? We've got a salvage crew down there. The Tonal Orders charge too much for charts. Need to find our own way.
The villager points to a distant, glimmering fissure on the Lattice surface—a potential source of unattuned resonance crystals.

lines_after.dialogue: Scavenging without a licensed frequency map? That's how you get dissolved into a pretty light show.
We're desperate. The Open Frequency Map rumor… it's the latest fashion in the lower decks. A free path through the Lattice.
A free map? Let's go find it! We can help them!
Rumors are dangerous. But… if it exists, it could change everything for people like them.

line.dialogue: The villager's crew is heading toward the fissure. Do we join their scavenging mission?

choices.text: Offer to escort them safely (Show solidarity)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the nearest crystal surface and listen through your bones. — 14 words

line.dialogue: [Pichit grabs your wrist, eyes wide: "You just read three centuries of grief in five seconds."]
[Arthit yanks you back: "Touch it without shielding and you'll wake every frequency they buried."]

choices.text: Scout ahead alone to assess the risk (Gather intelligence)
choices.description: Hum a low tone matching the crystal's vibration to coax hidden layers into visibility. — 14 words

line.dialogue: [Chanida gasps: "The patterns just opened — there are names inside, thousands of them."]
[Malee covers her ears: "Wrong pitch — you just made it scream, and something out there heard."]

choices.text: Decline, but share basic Listener safety tones (Provide aid from afar)
choices.description: Mimic Arthit's guarded posture and scan the horizon for whatever he's afraid of triggering. — 14 words

line.dialogue: [Arthit nods grimly: "Good — you see them too, the shapes moving beneath the surface."]
[Pichit mutters: "You're staring at nothing — but the nothing is now staring back at you."]

lines_before.dialogue: Descending a resonating crystal staircase to the Lattice surface proper, the harmonic hum becomes a physical pressure. Light refracts in dizzying patterns.
Near the fissure, the villager's crew is nervously prying at a lodged crystal cluster. The air crackles with unstable energy.
This frequency… it's wounded. A scar from the Silencing.
I have something to tell you. My resonator is picking up dissonant signatures approaching. Not natural.
A crude resonance ship, bristling with jagged, overcharged crystals, skims over the Lattice, its noise tearing at the harmony.
Well, look at this! A little digging party. You know what this is? This is our turf!
Sky pirates. He's a nice guy, I bet. Just wants to politely rob us.
We found this! You can't just take it!

lines_after.dialogue: We know hidden frequencies the Tonal Orders don't. That fissure's got a cache of unregistered charts. Maybe even the Open Map.
Please… we just need enough to feed our families.
The pirate ship's resonator whines to a higher pitch, preparing to disrupt the local frequencies and cause a chaotic, potentially lethal, resonance cascade.
They're going to trigger a breakdown! The entire area could crystallize unpredictably!

line.dialogue: The pirates are preparing to attack and destabilize the fissure. How do we respond?

choices.text: Use Listener harmonics to calm the local frequencies (Defuse the situation)
choices.description: Draw your resonator and aim it at the bandit's chest, demanding he step aside.

line.dialogue: You feel that vibration in your teeth? That's my frequency warming up. Walk away now." — *Arthit
Put the toy down, resonator-jockey. My crew has six barrels on you and your friends." — *Bandit

choices.text: Challenge the pirates to a duel of resonators (Direct confrontation)
choices.description: Signal Malee to keep talking while you quietly scan the scar frequency for tactical data.

line.dialogue: I'm pulling coordinates from the wound-pattern. Whatever was Silenced here left a map in its screaming." — *Pichit
The scar frequency bit back. My resonator's overheating and now the pirates know we're scanning." — *Pichit

choices.text: Quickly harvest the crystal cache before the cascade hits (Risky salvage)
choices.description: Raise both hands slowly and offer the bandit access to your excavation logs.

line.dialogue: We're cataloguers, not claim-jumpers. These readings are useless without a
The gamble fails. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform on the Lattice surface hums with a low, dangerous energy. The stolen frequency map glows in Pichit's hands, its open pathways shimmering like forbidden stars.
So the Tonal Orders have been hoarding these safe routes for centuries. No wonder they charge a fortune. 'Everyone knows it!' is the polite way of saying 'pay up or plummet'.
This changes everything. But it also makes us a target. If the Orders find us with this...
Let them try! We can finally go anywhere! Think of the places we've only heard about in stories!
This knowledge... it should belong to everyone. The Listeners always said the Lattice sings for all who can hear. This map is just a written version of that song.
A sudden, harsh scraping sound echoes across the crystalline plain. A Resonance Ship, painted with jagged, predatory marks, settles roughly nearby.
Well, well. 'Oh, it's you!' The little rats who stole from the big cats. Hand over the map. We 'heard everything' from our friends in the lower docks.
Sky pirates. How original. You really think you can just take it?

lines_after.dialogue: The pirates' ship resonator whines aggressively, causing the nearby Lattice to vibrate with a threatening pitch.
They're trying to destabilize the platform! The harmonics are all wrong!
The map... it shows a resonant frequency that can calm this area. But using it will broadcast our location like a beacon.

line.dialogue: We have to act. The pirate ship is powering up its main cutter.

choices.text: Use the map's frequency to counter their resonance. (Focus on defense, but reveal your position.)
choices.description: Broadcast the route maps across every frequency band before the Orders can stop you.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Every ship in the sector just received them. They can't un-hear what's already been sung.
Arthit — "The Orders jammed our signal mid-transmission. Now they know we have it AND we've lost the element of surprise.

choices.text: Have Chanida and Malee flank them on foot across the Lattice. (Risky maneuver, but keeps the map hidden.)
choices.description: Copy the maps onto crystal plates and smuggle them to the Lis exchange brokers piecemeal.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The first plates reached the brokers. They're already trading hands in the lower markets — this can't be contained now.
Chanida — "A broker sold us out to the Orders. They're burning the exchange and we've got nothing to show for it.

choices.text: Pichit, try to Sing a discordant harmonic to jam their ship. (Direct confrontation using your rare gift.)
choices.description: Confront the Tonal Orders directly at their resonance chamber and demand they open the routes.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "I stood in that chamber and told them to their faces — the skies aren't yours to gatekeep. And they *listened*.
Malee — "We walked in unarmed and proud. They harmonized us right back out the door with a warning and a headache that won't quit.

acts.title: A Crack in the World's Song

lines_before.dialogue: The confrontation has left the Lattice scarred and humming angrily. The pirate ship is disabled, but the unstable energy has attracted something worse: a deep, grinding fracture is spreading through the crystalline surface below the platform.
You fools! You've cracked the foundation! 'What do your parents do?' Mine are about to be buried if this whole shelf shears off!
The structural frequency is collapsing. We need to re-harmonize it, or this entire sector will calve into the void.
Look at the map. 'They have a lot of stuff!' marked here... emergency stabilizer nodes. The old civilization built failsafes. One is right at the edge of that crack.
It's a death walk! The lattice there is thinner than glass!
The map calls it the 'World's Heart Chord'. If we can activate it, it won't just save this platform. It could stabilize the region for miles. Make it truly safe.
The fracture groans, a sound of a world in pain. Light bleeds from the deepening crack. The pirate, nursing a wound, looks up in genuine fear.
You're all mad. But... my ship's got a tether line. Could maybe anchor someone. If you promise 'I'll take very good care of it' and don't leave me here to die.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision hangs in the air, heavier than the sinking ground. To save the many, one must walk the song of the abyss.
This is what the Listeners meant. The song isn't just to hear. It's to heal.
Don't get poetic. Just don't fall.

line.dialogue: The stabilizer node glows faintly in the heart of the fracture. The path to it is a nightmare of shifting, singing crystal.

choices.text: Use the pirate's tether and ship as a secure anchor. (Safe but slow, risking total collapse before you finish.)
choices.description: Anchor the frequency using Malee's map markers as harmonic nodes, 14 words

line.dialogue: The markers align — if we sing the lattice points into resonance, the crack stabilizes!
The frequencies clash instead of harmonize — we've made the fracture sing in a darker key.

choices.text: Chanida and Arthit create a harmonic bridge with their personal resonators. (Faster, but drains their gear and leaves them vulnerable.)
choices.description: Attempt the death walk across the thin lattice to reach the core, 14 words

line.dialogue: Glass thin, but my feet know glass — I can feel where the song still holds beneath!
I told you — thinner than glass, thinner than breath — the lattice shattered and the void is singing now.

choices.text: Pichit Sings the path into solidity, walking the sound itself. (The ultimate use of his gift, but a single mis-note means annihilation.)
choices.description: Ask the villager to teach the old foundation song before it's lost, 13 words

line.dialogue: The villager's voice cracks with age but the melody is true — the foundation remembers its own name!
He won't sing for fools, he says — and the last thread of the old song dies in his silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a deep, resonant tone that vibrates in your bones. It's a sound so pervasive it feels like silence.
Welcome! I trust your journey was profitable? The Spire's hum is quite soothing for negotiations, don't you think? Calms the... emotional variables.
It's giving me a headache. Can we just find this monk and get the charts?
Of course the Tonal Orders would stick their negotiation post here. No chance of a whispered deal or a hidden clause with this drone in your ears.
Caution. The harmonic stability is an illusion. Look at the lattice below—the crystal patterns are... shifting in a way the official charts don't show.
It's a forced peace. A single note imposed on a world that should sing with many.
Philosophical! But peace is good for business. Your Listener contact is just down the walkway. A bit... intense, but harmless.

lines_after.dialogue: You approach. The hum... it is not pure. There is a dissonance underneath. A fracture. You heard that, didn't you?
I know. We all feel it. The Spire's song is strained.
You already know that? Then you understand why I cannot, in good conscience, give you the standard navigation charts. They are lies for this sector.

line.dialogue: The monk hesitates, clutching a data-crystal. The merchant watches from a distance, smiling.

choices.line: "We just need to pass through. Give us the official charts." (Accept the known lies)
choices.description: Examine the floor tiles beneath the merchant's stall for harmonic resonance patterns

line.dialogue: There — every seventh tile hums a half-tone flat. Someone carved a disruption lattice right under our feet.
I kneel, press my palm flat, and feel nothing but cold stone. Either I've gone tone-deaf or this section is clean.

choices.line: "Tell us about the dissonance. What's down there?" (Press for the truth)
choices.description: Ask the merchant what commodity the Tonal Orders are actually negotiating for

line.dialogue: He says 'silence coefficients' like it's ordinary goods — but his hands are shaking. Whatever they're trading, it scares him more than we do.
He laughs and changes the subject to carpet prices. Three times. Whatever they're negotiating, he's been told to bury it deep.

choices.line: "The Merchant is watching. Perhaps we should discuss this elsewhere?" (Deflect and seek privacy)
choices.description: Touch the wall where Arthit noticed the harmonic illusion and push through the false vibration

line.dialogue: My fingers sink two inches into solid stone — there's a passage behind the resonance wall. The headache splits and suddenly I can *hear* the monk breathing on the other side.
I press my palm against the stone and the

lines_before.dialogue: The monk leads you to a secluded observation blister, its crystal walls thinning the Spire's hum. Below, the Lattice churns with abnormal, jagged formations.
The official charts show calm resonance waves here. But look. That's all, isn't it? Just fracture and chaos.
A navigational hazard of this magnitude... suppressed? The Orders would never risk their ships.
Unless they've already written this sector off. Sacrificed it. The Groundless whispers about 'dead zones' the cities float away from.
So there's something down there they don't want found. I say we go look!
A truth buried in crystal. The song here is one of pain, not order.
A shadow falls across the observation blister. The Trade Negotiator stands in the doorway, his friendly smile not reaching his eyes.

lines_after.dialogue: A private viewing? I should have charged a fee. That's all, isn't it? Just a harmless look at the scenery.
He's still single, isn't he? That kind of calculated smile leaves no room for a partner.
Now, about those charts. The monk has... alternative data. My employers would pay handsomely for it. Or, you could take the official ones and forget this little detour.
He steps fully into the room, his posture blocking the exit. The monk shrinks back. The merchant is standing right in front of you.

line.dialogue: The merchant's hand rests casually near his belt, where a small resonance disruptor hangs. The true charts are a secret someone is willing to buy—or bury.

choices.line: "We'll take the official charts." (Comply and leave the mystery)
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with resonant staff to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
The resonance turns hostile. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.line: "What's the offer?" (Negotiate with the merchant for the truth)
choices.description: Malee attempts to use the leg as a lattice probe, relying on leg resonance

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Defeat. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.line: "We're taking the monk and his data." (Defy the merchant and protect the secret)
choices.description: The monk volunteers to listen for the ghost ship's echo, leveraging prayers

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the monk is thwarted. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The party ascends the final, spiraling walkway of the Anchor Spire. The harmonic tone is now a physical pressure, making speech feel heavy and thoughts crystalline.
Ah, you made it! I was just finishing my inventory. The resonance flux here is quite profitable for calibrating high-grade crystals.
Profitable? We just fought through lattice-wraiths drawn to this 'calming' tone. Something's wrong with your anchor.
Of course there is. The Tonal Orders didn't build this out of civic duty. He's standing right in front of us, isn't he? The source of the instability.
The Monk said the anchor's frequency has been subtly altered. It's not calming the Lattice... it's suppressing something.
Suppression is just another form of control. What song are you drowning out, Merchant?
Such dramatic language! It's simple harmonic optimization. The Groundless agitants down below... their dissonant chants were causing market volatility.

You asked me to tune the anchor to a 'stabilizing' frequency. But that frequency... it silences the Lattice's grief-song for The Silencing. My Order's mother told me about it already. This is a desecration.

lines_after.dialogue: The Merchant's smile vanishes. He taps a control crystal on his wrist.
Unfortunately, I have a class. A masterclass in pragmatic acoustics. And I'm going to hurry off. The anchor's defensive harmonics will see to you.
The steady tone fractures into a piercing, discordant shriek. Jagged resonances solidify from the air around the Merchant as he retreats upward.

line.dialogue: The defensive harmonics manifest as sonic phantoms—echoes of manipulated fear and doubt. They're immaterial but attack the mind.

choices.line: (Harmonize) Use the party's combined voices to create a counter-melody, dispersing the phantoms with shared focus.
choices.outcome: The phantoms waver and fade. The path is clear, but the Merchant gains more time.
choices.description: Touch the anchor stone and hum the base frequency Arthit described, letting it resonate through your bones.

line.dialogue: Yes—THERE—the harmonic is stabilizing, can you feel it climbing back toward root pitch?
No, no, you're flattening it further—the drift is *worse* now, pull your hand back before it locks in!

choices.line: (Resonate) Have Pichit attempt to Singer-navigate the chaotic frequencies, finding a safe path through the psychic storm.
choices.outcome: Pichit guides the party through, but the strain of wrestling the corrupted song is immense.
choices.description: Ask the merchant to show what he was inventorying—anything resonant could be interfering with the anchor's tone.

line.dialogue: Ha! Crystals tuned to a *dead* octave—that's your contamination source right there, merchant.
I already checked, these are sealed against leakage... your anchor was drifting before I ever opened my crates.

choices.line: (Shatter) Channel all aggression into the anchor's structure itself, risking a feedback cascade to break the harmonic prison.
choices.outcome: The phantoms explode violently. The spire groans. You are free, but the anchor is now critically unstable.
choices.description: Have Malee strike the chamber wall with her tuning hammer at the Monk's prescribed interval to test the lattice's response.

line.dialogue: Clean rebound—the lattice *wants* to hold true, whatever's altered it hasn't corrupted the structure itself.
Muddied return, decay trailing off wrong... the lattice is absorbing when it should be reflecting. Something deeper is shifting.

lines_before.dialogue: You breach the control chamber at the Spire's peak. The Merchant stands before the massive central resonator, its light pulsing erratically. The whole floating island shudders.
You see? Unstable! Because of your interference. The Groundless will have their 'freedom' when this island plummets into the Lattice!
You broke it to silence a protest song? You idiot!
He has no one to help him now. The Orders will disavow him. A rogue asset. A calculated loss.
The resonator feedback loop is compounding. We have minutes, maybe less, before the anchor fails and the island's levitation collapses.
The true note... the Lattice's base frequency of remembrance... it's still there, beneath the corruption. But to restore it, we must... can I? I have no one to help me understand the risk.
The risk is certainty if we do nothing. You are not alone. We are all Listeners now.
Sentimental fools! You'll destroy everything! Can I take a break for a moment? Let's discuss the salvage rights, at least!

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk closes his eyes, hands on the resonator. Pichit and the party add their voices—not in command, but in support. A pure, clear tone emerges, fighting the discord.
The spire stops shuddering. The painful shriek dissolves into a deep, mournful, yet stabilizing hum. The Merchant slumps, defeated.
Far below, on the Lattice's surface, the suppressed song of the Groundless Movement rises again—not as a scream, but as a resonant, undeniable part of the world's music.

line.dialogue: The anchor is saved, but fundamentally changed. It now amplifies the Lattice's unfiltered song, including the voices of the Groundless. The Tonal Orders will respond. What is the priority in this fragile moment?

choices.line: (Secure) Fortify the spire. Use the restored resonance as a defensive field and prepare for the Orders' inevitable retribution.
choices.outcome: You gain a stronghold, but become a static target. The Groundless see you as protectors.
choices.description: Have Arthit focus forbidden paths on the calm tones to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Things don't go as planned. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.line: (Broadcast) Amplify the new song as far as possible. Let every floating city hear the truth the Orders suppressed.
choices.outcome: You ignite widespread unrest. The Lattice itself becomes unpredictable with this new, liberated energy.
choices.description: Ask Malee to tune the prosthetic, drawing on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee fails. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: (Shatter the Monopoly) Use the spire's unique position to jam the Orders' navigation frequencies, grounding their fleets.
choices.outcome: You cripple the guild's power instantly, but throw global trade and travel into chaotic, dangerous disarray.
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with market connections to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the merchant pulls it off. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the merchant overreaches. A rival merchant sabotages the plan.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform, 'The Listening Shelf,' is a precarious metal cradle bolted to a sheer crystalline cliff. Below, the Lattice's surface ripples with slow, silent waves of refracted light.
Look at that! The patterns are shifting faster than the charts predicted. Isn't it incredible?
Incredible? It's a death sentence if we misread a frequency. The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for those 'accurate' charts.
Stay within the marked safety perimeter. The resonance dampeners on this platform are only rated for standard ambient hum.
It's not just a surface. It's a record. Every fracture holds a memory of The Silencing.
You perceive the history in the silence. Most only see the danger. I am Brother Kavi, a Listener. I study these echoes.
He's only interested in the old songs, right? Not the practical frequencies for sailing?
The practical ones are controlled, monopolized. The old songs... they are truths that have been forgotten.

lines_after.dialogue: Truths don't pay for resonance coil repairs.
We have a mission. The salvage beacon from the Groundless wreck is active near Sector Gamma. Lift the salvage carefully! The Lattice is unstable there.
Thank you for your concern, Arthit. But we need to understand what we're walking into.
The Groundless... they believe the Lattice can be lived upon, not just traversed. A dangerous dream.

line.dialogue: Brother Kavi mentions a hidden, natural frequency path to the wreck site, safer than the Tonal Order chart route, but unverified.

choices.text: Follow the official Tonal Order charts. Safe, expensive, predictable.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the largest fracture line and let the resonance flow through you.

line.dialogue: Arthit grips your shoulder hard — "Steady. You're reading it clean. The frequency isn't rejecting you.
Arthit yanks you backward as your fingertips go numb — "I said stay behind the line! That resonance will unmake you!

choices.text: Trust the Listener's hidden frequency. Risky, free, could reveal new knowledge.
choices.description: Deploy the frequency cage around the three shifting patterns Chanida identified before they diverge.

line.dialogue: Malee exhales sharp through her nose — "Cage locked. Three distinct epochs, all singing the same warning.
Malee watches the patterns scatter beyond recovery — "Gone. Whatever they were trying to tell us is buried now.

choices.text: Send a scout (Chanida) ahead on the official route to verify safety first.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to translate the deepest fracture layer while you record the surface shifts simultaneously.

line.dialogue: Pichit traces the line with trembling fingers — "Someone survived this before. They left instructions. We follow them.
Pichit pulls back, eyes wide — "It's not a record — it's a lure. Whatever wrote this is still listening.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends a resonantly-carved staircase onto the Lattice itself. The ground is a hard, translucent crystal that thrums with a low, sub-audible vibration. Light dances beneath their feet.
I love it!! Walking on the world's skin! This is what the Groundless talk about!
Stay focused. The vibration is within safe parameters... for now.
The salvage wreck is just ahead. No signs of... wait. Discordant resonance echoes. Someone else is here.
Hah! Beat you to the scrap, city-dwellers! The name's Razor. This wreck is mine.
This isn't scrap. It's a Groundless research vessel. Their work is important.
Important? Their 'work' got them shattered across the Lattice! I'm the luckiest person in the world finding this before the Orders did!
You are using a forced dissonance to stabilize your presence here. It will damage the local crystalline memory.

lines_after.dialogue: Damage? I'm harvesting! You Listeners are all hum and no action.
The pirate's resonator is jury-rigged, but powerful. He's blocking access to the wreck's core.
We can't let him take the core data-crystal! The Groundless movement needs it!
Aggression could cause a resonance fracture. I'm really sorry, but we must consider retreat.

line.dialogue: Razor the sky pirate stands defiant over the wreck's core, his resonator emitting a threatening, unstable frequency.

choices.text: Offer to split the salvage. Negotiate a deal to share the data.
choices.description: Draw your pulse blade and challenge the bandit for claim rights, right here on the world-skin.

line.dialogue: Decisive. The bandit's stance is sloppy — three openings I can count from here.
Great, now we're dueling on a breathing surface while seismic readings climb. Wonderful.

choices.text: Use Brother Kavi's knowledge of natural frequencies to destabilize the pirate's resonator safely.
choices.description: Offer the bandit a split — your team takes the navigation core, they take the hull plating.

line.dialogue: See? Everyone wins. Even the world beneath us seems to hum approval!
Split? With soft city hands? I'll take the whole wreck and your boots too, little walker.

choices.text: Attempt to overpower Razor and seize the core directly. Risks a violent resonance backlash.
choices.description: Ignore the bandit and sprint for the wreck's breach point before they can react.

line.dialogue: Entry point reached first — marking it ours under salvage law. Not negotiable anymore.
The surface pulsed mid-sprint. You stumbled. The bandit is already through the hull.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform groans, a deep harmonic shudder running through the crystal beneath your boots. A jagged, singing fissure has opened in the Lattice nearby, revealing a cavernous hollow below.
Look at that! It's like the world cracked open! We have to see what's down there!
Of course we do. Because charging into unknown, potentially fatal crystal voids is our brand. The pain of falling to our deaths is gone only after you hit the bottom, you know.
The structural integrity is questionable. The Tonal Orders' charts don't mention this formation. It's an anomaly.
(Whispering, awed) It doesn't sing with the old patterns. This is a new voice. A raw one. The past is gone... this is something born from the Silencing's wound.

Scavenger's gold, that hollow! I've heard whispers. The Groundless don't just preach—they hide caches in places the Orders don't chart. He doesn't have many friends up in the cities, but down in the cracks? Maybe.
A place off the charts... a truth the Lattice itself is revealing. The old maps can't contain the world as it is now.

line.dialogue: We can attempt to descend. The fissure's song is unstable, but the Monk believes it's a 'new voice.' The Bandit sees opportunity. The hollow below is dark.

choices.label: Easy: Use the Bandit's hidden frequency to dampen the edge crystals, creating a safe climb down.
choices.effect: The Bandit grins, producing a small, oddly-tuned resonator. The shard-edges go silent and dull, allowing for a careful climb.
choices.description: Leap across the jagged gap to reach the pulsating crystal formation on the other side, 12

line.dialogue: chanida** — "I made it! The crystal's warm — it's breathing, almost, like something alive waits inside.
arthit** — "Your foot found no purchase — the edge crumbled — I'm pulling you back by the rope, don't struggle.

choices.label: Medium: Have the Monk attune to the fissure's new 'song,' guiding us to step where the resonance is strongest and safest.
choices.effect: The Monk closes his eyes, humming. He points to specific, glowing points on the fracture line. 'Here. The past is over. Step into the new note.'
choices.description: Ask the monk to chant a grounding sutra while you step onto the fractured stone, 15

line.dialogue: monk** — "The sutra holds — the stone accepts your weight — whatever broke this place, it remembers prayer.
malee** — "Your monk's words dissolved into noise — the fracture *widened* — fall back now or fall forever.

choices.label: Hard: Jump. Trust that the Lattice's own resonant updraft in the hollow will slow the fall.
choices.effect: A leap of pure faith into the singing dark. The air itself seems to thicken with a rising chord, cushioning the descent perilously.
choices.description: Press your palm against the exposed seam where the Tonal Order still flickers faintly, 13

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Smuggling routes provide an escape.
A costly mistake by the pirate. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: You descend into the cathedral-like space beneath the Lattice's skin. The air thrums. Etched into the walls are not Tonal glyphs, but sprawling, chaotic murals of falling cities and free-floating communities.
This is... a historical record. But not one the Orders keep. This is the Silencing from below. From the Groundless perspective.
It's obvious that they were here! This is their vault! But... where are they now?
Perhaps they became the echo itself. Living in the spaces between the official songs.

lines_before.dialogue: At the hollow's heart lies not treasure, but a massive, dormant core-crystal. Its surface is cracked, and from within pulses a faint, pained light. It is the source of the fissure, and the strange new song.
It's wounded. The Silencing didn't just scar the surface... it damaged the world's heart. This malaise... it's spreading. The Orders' stable frequencies are just a bandage.
Forget the philosophy! Look at the size of that crystal! One shard could buy a fleet! But... that light. It's like a heartbeat. Weird.
Great. So the world is literally heart-broken. I'm the luckiest person in the world to be standing inside its failing organ.
We have to help it! Can we... sing to it? Like Pichit does with the ships?
The energy readings are chaotic. A unified, external resonance might stabilize it. Or shatter it completely, taking us and this entire sector of the Lattice with it.
This is the choice. To impose an old order upon this new pain, to plunder it, or to try and understand its voice. To sing *with* it, not *at* it.

line.dialogue: The wounded core-crystal pulses erratically. Its song is a plea, a confusion. The fate of this place—and perhaps the spreading instability—hangs on the frequency we now offer.

choices.label: Easy: Use the Tonal Orders' prescribed Stabilizing Chant. Impose known harmony. (Safety, but perpetuates the old system)
choices.effect: The crystal's song is forced into a rigid, familiar pattern. It stabilizes, but the light within dims, locked into compliance. The Monk looks away, conflicted.
choices.description: Press your hands against the crystal's surface and pour your own heartbeat's rhythm into it through touch.

line.dialogue: monk* — "Yes! It stutters, then reaches — you're teaching it what a steady pulse feels like again.
monk* — "The pain travels up your arms like drowning in glass. It doesn't know your rhythm from its own screaming.

choices.label: Medium: Let the Bandit use his pirated 'cracking' frequency to harvest the largest, most valuable shard. Exploit the wound. (Profit, but deepens the damage)
choices.effect: The resonator screeches. A massive shard shears away into the Bandit's sack. The core's light flickers violently, and the hollow trembles. You profit from the heartbreak.
choices.description: Strike the crystal shard at its hairline fracture with the pommel of a blade — break the dead part away so living crystal can sing.

line.dialogue: bandit* — "Ha! See that? Cracked right off clean! Sometimes you don't comfort a wound — you cut it out!
bandit* — "The shard buries itself in your forearm. It... it wanted to stay broken. You can't amputate grief.

choices.label: Hard: Pichit, with the party's support, must attempt an untested, empathetic resonance. To listen, then sing back a song of healing, not control. (Risk everything for a new truth)
choices.effect: Pichit closes his eyes, not speaking, but listening. Then, a soft, complex hum emerges, weaving the Monk's reverence, Chanida's hope, even Malee's resilience. The core's light swells, bright and whole, its song becoming one of gratitude and newfound strength.
choices.description: Hum Pichit's lullaby in counter-rhythm to the crystal's fractured pulse, letting Chanida weave her voice in harmony with yours.

line.dialogue: chanida* — "It's working — listen! The dissonance is folding into chords. It remembers what harmony feels like!
chanida* — "Our voices clash against each other and the crystal shrieks — we're three different songs fighting and it can't follow any of

lines_after.dialogue: The consequence of your choice resonates outward. The fissure above either seals shut with a final, authoritative chime; groans wider, spewing unstable energy; or gently transforms, its edges blooming with harmless, singing crystal flowers.
Every song leaves an echo. Today, we chose what kind of echo to become.
The past is over. The path forward... it's very clear now. Thank you.
Well. That was something. You lot are full of surprises. Might stick around, see what other 'truths' you crack open.
Don't get sentimental. We still have to climb out of this glowing hole. But... I'm really sorry I doubted the heart of the world thing. Just this once.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans beneath a sickly orange sky. Mountains of broken resonance ships rise like metallic carcasses, their crystal resonators long dead. The air vibrates with the relentless CLANG-CLANG-CLANG of scavenger hammers, a harsh, industrial cacophony that drowns out all subtlety.
I'm in a good mood! Look at this place—it's a treasure trove! We're definitely finding the resonator coil here. How good is that?
Your 'good mood' is the only thing not rusted solid here, Chanida. This graveyard smells of oil and desperation. Is the pay for this even good enough?
We should proceed with caution. The acoustic interference is severe. Our charts might glitch. How good is our local contact at navigating this noise, Pichit?
Good enough, I hope. In this din, the Lattice's true song is buried. We must listen for what isn't being hammered out.
You the ones asking about Old Man Sila? He's in the deep yard. But... you hear that? The metal's been singing wrong lately. Bad harmonics. Not good for business.
Singing wrong? Probably just a loose plate vibrating.
No. Deeper. Like the Lattice itself is... complaining under all our noise. The Listeners would know. But they've been quiet too.

lines_after.dialogue: As the villager scurries away, a low, dissonant hum seems to pulse from the very wreckage around you, felt in the teeth more than heard.
That... was not a normal vibration. It matches no frequency on my scanner.
A warning, perhaps. Buried under the health of industry, the world is trying to speak.

line.dialogue: The path to the deep yard splits through three canyons of wreckage.

choices.text: Take the main haulage route. It's loud but clear of debris.
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using captain experience to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Defeat. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Cut through the 'Silent Maw,' a hollowed-out freighter known for strange acoustics.
choices.description: Malee attempts to use the leg as a lattice probe, relying on leg resonance

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee overreaches. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Scale the eastern scrap ridge for a better vantage.
choices.description: The villager takes the lead, employing village secrets to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: the villager succeeds. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the villager overreaches. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: You emerge into a clearing as a bruised dawn light filters through the smog. The hammering has ceased with the shift change, leaving an eerie quiet. Before you sits Old Man Sila's shack, built into the ribs of a derelict barge. The strange hum is stronger here.
The interference has dropped. I can finally get clear readings... and I don't like them. The local Lattice resonance is unstable. It's a fresh beginning to a potentially bad day.
Great. From morning until evening we'll be chasing ghosts. I probably can't eat anything now with this vibration in my gut.
Look! The door's open. Sila? You in there?
Inside, the shack is empty. A kettle steams on a stove. Charts are spread everywhere, marked with frantic, unreadable symbols. On the wall, scrawled in charcoal: 'THE SONG IS A SICKNESS.'
He left in a hurry. But not before trying to warn someone.
Warnin' came too late for him! Hand over those charts, sky-rats.

lines_after.dialogue: Three sky pirates drop from the barge's upper deck, their boots crunching on rust. Their leader, a woman with a resonator-blade at her hip, grins. The hum in the air seems to sharpen.
Sila was onto somethin'. A new frequency. One that makes the Lattice... twitch. We can't finish it all ourselves, but we can sure take his notes.
Pirates interested in resonance theory? The world truly is ending.
Their ship is hidden nearby. Minimal crew. They're as surprised as we are.

line.dialogue: The pirates fan out, blocking the exits. The strange hum pulses, making the metal walls resonate.

choices.text: Negotiate. Offer to trade the location of a different salvage site for safe passage.
choices.description: Arthit volunteers to follow the dissonant trail, leveraging forbidden paths
