line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Arthit fails. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Use the environment. Knock over a stack of unstable plating to create a distraction and escape.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing hidden frequencies to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Things don't go as planned. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Confront the resonance. Try to mimic or disrupt the strange hum, using it to disorient the pirates.
choices.description: Have the villager focus local knowledge on the clanging metal to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the villager overreaches. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's central crucible glows with forges, a cathedral of salvage where the party has traced the stolen resonator core. The cacophony is a physical weight.
They have a lot of stuff! Enough scrap here to build a fleet. Picking out one core is going to be a joy.
We have to adjust our approach. The acoustics here are chaotic—our detection equipment is useless. We'll need to rely on old-fashioned legwork.
Or we find the guy running this chop-shop and *convince* him to hand it over. What do your parents do, Arthit? Because you're thinking like a Tonal Order clerk.
Every broken ship here... its final resonance is trapped in the metal. A chorus of failures. We must listen for the one that doesn't belong.
You're the ones asking about the shiny core? Bad business. The crew that brought it in... they didn't ask for salvage rights. They demanded silence.
A low, discordant hum vibrates up from the Lattice below the scrap piles. It's the same unnatural frequency from the Listener's warning.
Speak of the devils. That's not engine noise. The Lattice is getting chatty again, and it's not happy.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision splits the party's path through the towering aisles of wreckage.
The aberrant hum grows stronger, making the crystal shards littering the ground vibrate in sympathy. A path of resonance is forming, whether you follow it or not.
Whatever we chose, we're committed now. Watch for movement in the shadows. This yard has its own predators.

line.dialogue: We need to locate the core before the pirates use it or the Lattice's anomaly worsens. How do we proceed?

choices.text: Follow the Villager's Tip. Track the pirates through the scrapyard's underworld contacts. (Social/Stealth)
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to follow the dissonant trail, leveraging staff meditation

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
A costly mistake by Pichit. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Trace the Aberrant Frequency. Use the growing hum as a guide, despite the risk. (Knowledge/Resonance)
choices.description: Malee presses forward with leg resonance to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Malee pulls it off. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The attempt backfires on Malee. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Bait the Pirates Out. Make a loud, tempting display to draw them into the open. (Combat/Deception)
choices.description: The villager attempts to commune with trapped echoes, relying on community ties

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the villager. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
The attempt backfires on the villager. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The path leads to the 'Canyon'—a deep fissure where the largest hulks are dumped. At its heart, a modified salvage barge crackles with stolen energy, the resonator core pulsing at its center.
Took you long enough! A man called you fools, and he was right. This core's gonna punch a hole straight down to the Old World. The salvage'll make us kings!
You're not kings, you're idiots! That frequency is tearing the Lattice apart! Can't you hear it screaming?
It's still in my memory. The Listener's warning. This is how it starts again. A bunch of greedy morons tuning to a song that breaks everything.
You are not pioneers. You are a needle, scratching a record that holds our world together. That hum you feel isn't power. It is a requiem.
Pretty words! Let's see how they sound when the canyon echoes with gunfire! Someone called for a fight!
The core's activation reaches a peak. The very air shimmers, and great fractures begin to spiderweb through the Lattice beneath the scrapyard, glowing with malevolent light.
Structural collapse is imminent! We must disable that core NOW, or this entire sector falls into the void!

lines_after.dialogue: Silence returns, deeper and more profound than the yard's usual clamor. The fate of the core, and the stability of the Lattice here, has been decided.
The aberrant frequency is gone, replaced by a slow, healing drone. The Lattice's distress has ceased, but the scar of this intrusion remains.
Listen. The true sound is returning. A reminder that some melodies are not meant to be played.

line.dialogue: The pirate leader is defeated, but the overloaded core is destabilizing, threatening to shatter the Lattice. What is our final move?

choices.text: Contain the Core. Use scrapyard dampeners to safely bleed off the energy, preserving the technology. (Salvage/Order)
choices.description: Malee presses forward with engineering to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
Defeat. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Shatter the Core. Destroy it utterly to halt the resonance cascade, but lose its secrets. (Sacrifice/Safety)
choices.description: Have Pichit focus Listener training on the engine parts to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Harmonize the Core. Chanida must attempt to Sing it back to a stable frequency, risking herself. (Daring/Discovery)
choices.description: The villager presses forward with terraces to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: the villager makes it work. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
Things don't go as planned. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship *'Dawn Chorus'* shudders, its crystal resonators falling silent. Ahead, the Lattice stretches in a uniform, dead-grey plane. No hum, no answering chime. Just a void of sound.
What happened? The charts said this was a clear sky-lane! The Tonal Orders swore these coordinates were safe!
The charts are wrong. Or outdated. We're in a Silent Zone. I've only read about them. The Lattice here... doesn't resonate. At all.
Fantastic. So we're adrift in a graveyard. Our ship's dead weight without the Lattice's song to push against. I'm right, aren't I?
It might be true. The silence... it's not an absence. It feels like a presence. A weight.
A smaller, cruder vessel drifts into view, its hull patched with salvaged resonator crystal. Two figures wave frantically from its deck.
Ahoy! Fortune favors the stranded twice over! I am Kiet. This is my... associate, Brother Lan. We too were misled by faulty charts.
The silence here is... profound. Unnatural. My order has theories about such places. They are wounds. Or perhaps tombs.

lines_after.dialogue: Now, as fellow victims of circumstance, perhaps we can trade? Information for supplies? I have... insights into what lies in the heart of this zone.
Of course you do. And what's your price, 'Kiet'? I'm not a playboy, I know a negotiation when I hear one.
Please. The truth of this place is more important than profit. My studies... they suggest something here consumes sound. Not just ignores it. Devours it.

line.dialogue: The two groups face each other in the oppressive quiet. How does Pichit respond?

choices.text: Agree to trade supplies for the merchant's information. (Easy: Gain a clue, lose resources.)
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to decode the tonal pattern, leveraging monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The resonance turns hostile. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Focus on the Monk's warning, asking to see his research first. (Medium: Uncover lore, potentially alienate the merchant.)
choices.description: Malee channels mechanical repair toward the crushing quiet, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee fails. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: Propose a temporary alliance to scout the nearest floating debris for parts. (Easy: Build rapport, but delay answers.)
choices.description: The monk presses forward with prayers to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His recording captures a denied frequency.
The lattice has other plans. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The alliance is tense. The group tethers the ships together and ventures onto a massive, derelict resonator tower jutting from the Lattice. Its crystal is dark, scarred.
Life support readings are minimal. But there's a power signature deep inside. Faint, and... wrong. It doesn't pulse. It just... is.
Stop! Did you see that? A shadow, in that doorway. No, not a shadow. Something... smoother.
Jitters won't find us a working resonator crystal. My associate here is jumpy too. You can ask him. He's been muttering about 'the old silence' since we arrived.
Because this is not natural silence! It is manufactured. A scar from The Silencing. In our oldest texts, they spoke of machines that could... unmake vibration.
Brother Lan's voice cracks with fear. As he speaks, a glint catches the light from his robe—a complex prosthetic leg, fashioned from dark, non-resonant crystal.
Your leg... it's unlike any crystal I've seen. It doesn't sing.
A relic. From before. It... it remembers the silence. Sometimes, in the dead of night, I think it tries to remember a song. He's still single, isn't he? My mind... it wanders in quiet places.

lines_after.dialogue: Focus, monk. So you think there's a machine here, still running, eating sound? And your creepy leg is what, a compass?
Now, that prosthetic... that's a unique artifact. The right collector would pay a fortune for a piece of pre-Silencing tech. No need for anyone else to know we found it here.
Stop it! We're not here for your salvage operation! If there's a machine, we break it. Maybe that'll free the Lattice here and we can get home!

line.dialogue: The monk clutches his prosthetic, conflicted. The merchant's eyes gleam with avarice. The party must choose their path forward.

choices.text: Follow the faint power signature Arthit detected. (Easy: Direct path, potential danger.)
choices.description: Rush toward the doorway with your pulse lantern raised, flooding the threshold with light.

line.dialogue: There — venting coolant through a fractured seam. The shadow was condensation vapor, nothing more. Move past it, quickly.
The light catches something *moving* — not vapor, not shadow. Limbs folding backward. It knows we see it now. Run. RUN.

choices.text: Press Brother Lan to use his prosthetic's connection to the silence as a guide. (Medium: Unreliable, reveals subplot.)
choices.description: Crack open the resonator housing with your multi-tool and bypass the dead crystal entirely.

line.dialogue: Hardwired the secondary coil directly into the power bus. Ugly work, but we have resonance again — fifteen minutes of it, maybe twenty.
The housing was booby-trapped. Some kind of organic trigger wire. My fingers are going numb and the smell — gods, the smell is coming from *inside the unit*.

choices.text: Call out the merchant's intent and demand he reveal everything he knows, now. (Hard: Risk confrontation, possible betrayal.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the bulkhead and feel for the frequency beneath the manufactured silence.

line.dialogue: Thirty-two hertz. Pulsing in intervals of seven. Whatever is generating this silence, it's broadcasting from *below* the deck plating —
The attempt backfires on the merchant. Hidden debts come due.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonant Prosthetic has been fitted to the ship's hull, a desperate gambit to pierce the Silent Zone's unnatural stillness.
It's humming... a weird, thin hum. Like a whisper. But the lattice isn't responding. It's just... dead.
Of course it's dead. This whole place is a corpse. We're just poking it with a stick.
The prosthetic's resonance is unstable. If we push it too hard, it could shatter. And then we'd be trapped here.
This silence... it is not natural. It is a wound. The lattice here has been... silenced. By something.
A wound implies a weapon. What could have done this? The Silencing was global chaos. This feels... deliberate.
Deliberate or not, profit is still possible. There are crystal deposits here, untouched. They don't resonate, but they're pure. Anyone's okay to mine them, if they can bear the quiet.
A low, grinding vibration begins to emanate from the prosthetic. The air itself seems to thicken, resisting the sound.

lines_after.dialogue: We need to understand this silence before we try to break it. Otherwise, we might just make the wound deeper.
But the prosthetic is our only way out! We have to use it!
The prosthetic's hum grows louder, a fragile thread of sound straining against the oppressive quiet.

line.dialogue: The prosthetic is straining. We must decide how to proceed.

choices.text: Turn it off. Study the silence first.
choices.consequence: Safety, but stagnation. The Monk will aid your study.
choices.description: Arthit channels ship navigation toward the unresponsive lattice, hoping to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
Arthit loses control. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Moderate increase. Push gently, probe the lattice.
choices.consequence: Risk of fracture, but potential data. The Merchant will offer a stabilizer... for a price.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with scavenger instincts, ready to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The resonance turns hostile. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: Maximum resonance. Force a path through.
choices.consequence: High chance of catastrophic failure, but a possible breakthrough. Chanida will support this reckless charge.
choices.description: The monk uses lattice study to commune with trapped echoes near the crushing quiet

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the monk. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision has been made. The prosthetic screams a jagged, artificial tone into the void. The lattice... reacts. Not with melody, but with a violent, shattering crack.
No! It is tearing! The song is being... unmade!
The stabilizers are failing! We need to pull back!
Look. Below. The lattice is breaking apart. Revealing something. Is it real? Or just another dead reflection?
Where the lattice sunders, a structure is revealed beneath—not crystal, but ancient, blackened metal. A relic from before The Silencing.
A city! A real city, buried here! What about tomorrow? We could explore it, claim it!
A priceless find! But the lattice is collapsing around it. We must secure it now, or it will be lost again. Please translate that for me into action.
This is the cause. This dead zone... it's a scar over a wound from the Silencing. This metal city... it did something to the lattice. It killed the song here.

lines_after.dialogue: The prosthetic gives one final, deafening shriek and dies. The ship is left adrift in the collapsing Silent Zone, the ancient city exposed below like a freshly opened grave.
We have broken the silence. But we have not restored the song. We have only revealed the corpse.
The dawn brings light... but it is the light of truth, not of hope. We must now bear what we have uncovered.

line.dialogue: The ancient city is exposed, but the lattice is unstable. Our ship is damaged. What is our priority?

choices.text: Secure the ship. Retreat to report.
choices.consequence: Safety and knowledge preserved, but the city may be lost. The Tonal Orders will be alerted.
choices.description: Descend through the collapsing lattice toward the revealed city before the gap seals shut.

line.dialogue: * "The breach holds — go, NOW! Whatever waits below, we see it with our own eyes!
* "The lattice snapped shut — we're locked out. That city will keep its secrets one more day.

choices.text: Send a team to the city. Gather proof.
choices.consequence: Great risk, but tangible discovery. The Merchant will fund the expedition, for a share of any salvage.
choices.description: Channel collective resonance into the failing stabilizers to hold the song intact a moment longer.

line.dialogue: * "I can feel it — the threads are holding! We are singing it back together, however briefly!
* "The stabilizers screamed and went dark. We gave everything and it still wasn't enough.

choices.text: Use the city's structure to stabilize the lattice. Attempt to 'heal' the Silent Zone.
choices.consequence: Extreme peril. Success could restore resonance here, creating a new dawn for the region. Failure could destroy both city and ship. The Monk will attempt this sacred, desperate act.
choices.description: Record the breaking song's final structure in ink and memory before it is lost forever.

line.dialogue: * "Every fracture, every fading note — I have it. This unmaking will not be unwitnessed.
* "It dissolved faster than my hand could move. Some songs die before anyone can mourn them.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market churns around you—a sea of faces, scents of spice and ozone, and the ever-present drone of a thousand overlapping conversations.
This noise… it's like the city itself is breathing. But something feels off in its rhythm today.
I heard a Scavenger just docked with a haul from the deep Lattice. Let's find them before the Tonal Orders confiscate everything interesting!
Oh, wonderful. More junk from the surface. Because what we really need is another corroded resonator that 'might still work.'
Caution, please. The Orders have eyes everywhere here. We should just secure our supplies and go.
A commotion ripples through the crowd near a battered docking skiff. A weathered woman—the Surface scavenger—is arguing with a robed figure—the Listener monk.
You Listeners hear the song, but you don't live it! This shard… it still works. I felt it vibrate on the ascent.
Please, sister. Such artifacts are not for trade. Their resonance is… unstable. They belong with our order for study.

lines_after.dialogue: Unstable? That sounds promising! Let's get a closer look.
The monk seems genuinely troubled, not just possessive. There's a tension here deeper than a simple argument.
Great. So it's a dangerous rock. I just spoke with a spice merchant who had better stories.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger glares at the Monk, clutching a leather satchel. The Monk's hands are raised in a placating gesture. How does the party intervene?

choices.text: Side with the Scavenger. Offer to buy the shard to defuse the tension. (Commerce)
choices.description: Slip toward the docking bay to intercept the Scavenger before anyone else sees the haul.

line.dialogue: I move through the maintenance crawlway — the Scavenger's hatch is still cycling, and I catch a glimpse of something glowing inside the cargo crate.
Two Order sentries round the corner before I reach the bay — I have to press flat against the bulkhead and pray the hum covers my breathing.

choices.text: Mediate. Ask the Monk to explain the danger, and the Scavenger to show the find. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Grab Arthit's arm and pull him into a service alcove to question what he knows about the Orders' patrol routes.

line.dialogue: I shouldn't tell you this, but the sentries rotate every twelve minutes — there's a gap near the lower freight lock if you're fast.
Are you insane? Touching me in the open like that — now the camera above the junction has both our faces, and I can't help you.

choices.text: Create a distraction. Have Chanida cause a commotion so the Scavenger can slip away. (Subterfuge)
choices.description: Signal Malee to create a distraction by loudly complaining about the surface junk near the comm hub.

line.dialogue: Oh, I put on a whole performance — ranting about rust and contamination right in front of the monitoring station, and every lens in the corridor swings toward me.
I start my rant, but my voice cracks and it comes out like a whisper — nobody turns, nobody looks, and now I just feel like a fool standing there.

lines_before.dialogue: Your choice has drawn the small group into a slightly quieter alcove between food stalls. The market's hum is a persistent backdrop.
Fine. Look, then. But careful—the edges are sharp. I got cut just handling the thing.
She opens the satchel. Inside rests a Lattice shard, but unlike any you've seen. It's deep violet, with internal fractures that seem to pulse with a faint light.
As I feared… a Warning Shard. From the deep strata. The Lattice doesn't just sing there… it screams.
A warning? Of what? The Silencing?
Something new. A… dissonance, spreading upward. My superiors in the order won't let me investigate further. They say it's not our duty.
Won't let you? That's ridiculous! The Tonal Orders won't let me go anywhere near their private archives either!
So you're both being held back. How touching. A monk with a conscience and a scavenger with a sharp rock. We have to do better than this if we want the truth.

lines_after.dialogue: A scream from the deep… and the authorities silencing it. This feels like a pattern from before The Silencing.
The monk speaks truth. I've seen the cracks where this came from. The song there… it hurts to hear. I had to do a better job sealing my helmet.
I am torn. My vow is to listen, not to act. But if no one heeds this warning…

line.dialogue: The shard emits a low, sub-audible thrum that makes your teeth ache. The Monk and Scavenger look to you, awaiting a course of action.

choices.text: Secure the shard. Offer to take it off their hands and study it safely away from the Orders. (Acquisition)
choices.description: Press your bare palm flat against the shard's surface and feel what it remembers.

line.dialogue: I understand now—every fracture is a voice that screamed before going quiet.
My hand—god, it's like the cold climbed through my bones and whispered something I can't unhear.

choices.text: Plan an expedition. Persuade the Scavenger to guide you to the source crack for firsthand data. (Exploration)
choices.description: Grab the scavenger's collar and demand to know exactly where in the deep strata they dug this up.

line.dialogue: Fine! Shaft Eleven, below the old choir hall—where the first monks were sealed. Satisfied?
Get your hands off me. You want answers? Go crawl down there yourself and rot like the others.

choices.text: Confront the Orders. Use this evidence to publicly challenge the Monk's superiors in the market square. (Confrontation)
choices.description: Kneel beside the monk and quietly ask what "dissonance" means for someone still connected to their superior.

line.dialogue: It means my superior's voice is no longer hers. Something is speaking through her, and I have been pretending not to notice.
I cannot explain what I have not yet accepted. Ask me again when my hands stop shaking.

lines_before.dialogue: The market's din swells, a physical pressure against your ears. The Scavenger has vanished into the crowd, leaving you with the Monk's grim warning.
The Lattice's song... it's changed. A dissonance beneath the harmony. My Order records speak of such a pattern before The Silencing.
So what do we do? Just stand here? We have to tell someone!
Tell who? The Tonal Orders? They'd silence us to conserve their monopoly. We need proof.
Proof costs money. Or favors. I saw a vendor back there. They sell the fresh resonator crystals at the far stalls. Maybe we can... acquire one to record this 'dissonance'.
A recording would be evidence. But the market guards... we must be careful. We cannot afford to draw attention.
I... I have duties. I have to take my novices to morning prayers. But my conscience... I will meet you at the fountain after the next bell.
The Monk hurries away, robes fluttering. The decision before you is clear, and fraught with risk.

line.dialogue: How will you obtain a crystal to record the Lattice's warning?

choices.line: Negotiate with the vendor. Use Chanida's charm and Arthit's haggling skills.
choices.consequence: You get a functional crystal, but spend most of your funds. The transaction is noted by a Tonal Order informant.
choices.description: Approach the vendor Malee spotted and bargain for whatever proof he's selling.

line.dialogue: Malee slides three chits across the counter. "Pleasure doing business. Now we have paper they can't burn.
Malee curses under her breath. "He wants double. Someone already warned him we'd come asking.

choices.line: Create a distraction so Malee can 'liberate' a crystal. Turn off the lights in the adjacent stall to cause confusion.
choices.consequence: You get the crystal without payment, but the stall owner raises an alarm. You must escape the immediate area.
choices.description: Trace the dissonance yourself — follow the monk's ear deeper into the Lattice chamber.

line.dialogue: The monk presses her palm flat against the resonating wall. "Here. The vibration splits at this node. Someone *cut* it.
The monk staggers back, clutching her temples. "Too close. The feedback nearly cracked my skull — we need shielding first.

choices.line: Approach a suspicious-looking Surface Scavenger who might have unregistered, purer crystals. A riskier, but potentially more sensitive, source.
choices.consequence: You get a potent, raw crystal, but the Scavenger demands a future favor, binding you to an unknown debt.
choices.description: Send Chanida to whisper what you've found to a single trusted Tonal adept, no proof, just words.

line.dialogue: Chanida
the monk fails. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: Crystal in hand, you regroup at the central fountain. The market's noise seems sharper now, more menacing.
We have the tool. Now we must find a quiet point to listen. The Monk said the old Listeners' spire overlooks the market's edge.
Then let's go! Every moment we wait, that... whatever it is gets louder!
As you move, you feel the weight of the crystal, and the heavier weight of the secret it might reveal.

lines_before.dialogue: The old spire is a needle of silence in the market's throat. Here, the ambient hum fades to a whisper. You place the crystal on a worn resonator plate.
Breathe. Listen. Let the Lattice speak through the crystal.
A sound emerges. Not the majestic chord of the skyways, but a deep, grinding fracture, a scream stretched over centuries. It is unbearable truth.
Gods below... that's not a song. It's a death rattle. The professors of the Tonal Academy are really good at hiding *this*, aren't they?
The structural resonance... it's decaying. The prices the world is paying for 'stability' are not reasonable. This is collapse.
We have to broadcast this! Now! To every ship, every city!
And cause a panic that could shatter civilization anew? Or let the few in power continue to lie, until the Lattice itself is lost? This is the choice.
Heavy boots echo on the stairs below. The Tonal Order Guard, alerted. The Monk pales. You hold the crystal—the proof of the world's end.

line.dialogue: The truth is in your hands. What is its fate?

choices.line: Smash the crystal. Destroy the proof. Maintain the fragile peace, and seek a quieter way to warn the wise. The prices are reasonable for continued order.
choices.consequence: Immediate danger passes. The world remains ignorant. You and the Monk begin a secret, long-term effort to prepare, but the clock is ticking.
choices.description: Overload the crystal array to amplify the death rattle across every comm channel in range.

line.dialogue: I feel it — ten thousand souls just heard the Lattice weep, and now they weep with it.
The array fused before the signal cleared — we broadcast static to a galaxy that needed truth.

choices.line: Give the crystal to the Monk. Let the Listeners' Order, with its credibility, decide how and when to reveal the truth. It's a burden they must bear.
choices.consequence: The Order takes the proof, but is fractured between revelation and silence. You are exiled from the skycity as 'troublemakers,' but the seed of truth is planted.
choices.description: Have Chanida manually rewire the broadcast antenna while Monk sustains the crystal's resonance through meditation.

line.dialogue: I've never spliced faster in my life — every ship in three sectors is receiving, and I can hear them going silent out there.
The antenna was dead before I opened the panel — this station was meant to listen, never to speak.

choices.line: Broadcast it. Now. Chanida rigs the spire's old alarm horn. You will lose your virginity of innocence, and the world will hear its own scream.
choices.consequence: Panic and revolution erupt across the Floating Cities. The Tonal Orders hunt you. But from the chaos, a true effort to heal the Lattice might—*might*—begin.
choices.description: Record the resonance decay pattern and embed it inside a navigational buoy launched toward the fleet's last known coordinates.

line.dialogue: Even if they can't understand the song, they'll feel the frequencies shifting — and anyone with half a soul will know what that means.
The buoy launched clean, but the crystal went dark mid-encoding — we sent them silence wrapped in silence.

lines_after.dialogue: Your choice echoes. The market below will never sound the same again. Whether it hears a dirge or a wake-up call is up to you.
We have chosen. Now we must live with the resonance of our actions.
The Lattice groans, a deep bass note felt in the bones. The episode ends, but the Chronicle has just found its key.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a deep, resonant tone that vibrates through your bones. The massive crystal column plunges from the floating island into the shimmering Lattice below, its steady frequency creating an unnatural calm.
Whoa. This place makes my teeth buzz. But it's... peaceful? I don't know if that's good.
Peaceful? It's a Tonal Order engineering marvel designed to suppress emotional outbursts. Perfect for keeping the masses docile.
The harmonic stability is remarkable. But Malee's right—this level of controlled resonance isn't natural. It's a tool.
Every tool has a purpose. And every purpose has a truth behind it. We're here to find what's hidden beneath this steady song.
You the ones asking about the old maps? The Listeners keep to themselves up at the observation deck. Don't cause trouble—the Spire's song keeps things calm. We like it calm.
How well do you know the Listeners here? Are they just studying, or... something else?
They watch the Lattice. Note the tones. The Tonal Orders pay them for data, I think. But lately... the head monk's been agitated. The song's been steady, but he hasn't.

lines_after.dialogue: Agitated monks and paid-off data. Sounds like someone's conscience is itching.
We should proceed carefully. The Spire's resonance makes stealth impossible—any emotional spike or raised voice will carry.
Then we walk openly. Our questions are honest. Let's see what truth resonates back.

line.dialogue: The observation deck is accessed via a spiraling crystal walkway. How do you approach the Listeners?

choices.text: Walk openly and announce your purpose respectfully. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the nearest resonance pillar and hum a single sustained note.

line.dialogue: Oh—that's it. The whole chamber just *answered* you. I felt it climb through my bones.
Yikes. That didn't harmonize. My fillings literally hurt now.

choices.text: Observe the Listeners first from a distance, studying their routines. (Stealth/Perception)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to demonstrate the primary maintenance tool's intended function on the central calibrating node.

line.dialogue: Watch closely. The tuning fork doesn't force the frequency—it *remembers* it. The node relaxes back to true.
Wrong contact point. I just set off a cascading dissonance alarm. Everyone stop talking for a moment.

choices.text: Send Chanida ahead with a friendly, curious demeanor to break the ice. (Charisma)
choices.description: Follow the subtle vibration underfoot toward the chamber's sealed eastern archway and listen with your ear pressed to the stone.

line.dialogue: You hear that? There's a second song behind this wall—older, deeper. The Order built *over* something.
Nothing but blood pressure in your ears. Though the architecture suggests this archway was never meant to open.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation deck is a ring of polished crystal overlooking the endless, shimmering Lattice. Several Listener monks kneel at the edge, their ears pressed to resonance-conducting rods. One monk stands apart, his hands trembling slightly.
The Anchor's tone is pure... mathematically perfect. But perfection is a cage. The wild songs of the Lattice... they're being silenced. Smothered.
You hear something beneath the Anchor's song.
I hear truth. Frequencies that aren't on any Tonal Order chart. Open paths. But to speak of them is heresy. The Orders eat continuously, consuming all knowledge, leaving none for the rest of us.
So you've been mapping these 'open frequencies' yourself. Illegally.

For study. For preservation. But now... I can smell the perfume of Tonal Order auditors in the city below. They suspect. My map... it's incomplete, but it points to a nexus of natural resonance. A place uncharted.
A place the Orders don't control? I don't wanna go anywhere else! Tell us where!
Wait. If the Orders are already suspicious, obtaining this map puts a target on us. The Spire's resonance means any conflict here will be instantly broadcast through the structure.

lines_after.dialogue: The map is hidden within the Spire's resonance chamber—the source of the Anchor tone. To retrieve it, you must momentarily disrupt the harmonic stabilizers. It will cause a... dissonant pulse.
A pulse everyone for miles will feel. Subtlety is officially dead.
Sometimes truth must resonate loudly to be heard over the lie of silence.

line.dialogue: The resonance chamber is below the observation deck. How do you retrieve the hidden frequency map?

choices.text: Have the monk guide you openly, using his authority to access the chamber. (Authority)
choices.description: Trace the hidden frequency with your own voice, humming where the Anchor's tone fractures.

line.dialogue: There — you feel it too, that space between the sanctioned notes where the Order insists nothing exists.
Your throat closes around the frequency like it's guarded. The Order trained that reflex into you well.

choices.text: Create a diversion elsewhere in the Spire to draw attention away from the chamber. (Deception/Tactics)
choices.description: Demand Pichit describe exactly what he hears beneath the Anchor's song — in detail, now.

line.dialogue: A secondary current, running counter to the melody. Like a river flowing underneath a frozen lake. It's been there the whole time.
I can't — the moment I try to isolate it, it slips sideways. Like trying to point at a shadow cast by nothing.

choices.text: Attempt to synchronize with the Anchor's frequency to bypass the stabilizers without triggering a full pulse. (Resonance Skill/Precision)
choices.description: Ask Malee what the Tonal Order would do if they knew these open frequencies were being mapped.

line.dialogue: They'd burn the maps and the mapper. Every undocumented frequency is a thread that could unravel their entire claim to sonic authority.
I don't know. Maybe nothing. Maybe everything. I've never been someone who asks what the Order would do — I've only been someone who obeys.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire's steady hum is now a physical pressure, a wall of sound that makes your teeth ache. The path ahead splits around a massive, cracked resonator crystal.
That fracture… it's not natural. The harmonic flow is being forced. This could destabilize the entire anchor point.
Of course it is. The Tonal Orders would rather break the world than let anyone else learn its song. Typical monopoly behavior.
Look! Up on that gantry. The monk from the lower archives!
You should not have come. The truth here… it is not a gentle frequency.
We've come from that day in the archives. The day we saw the map. The true song of the Lattice is not a secret to be hoarded.
You speak of belief. But who would believe you?! The Orders control all perception of reality. My own brothers… they smile happily as they burn the forbidden charts.
Please! I just deliver supplies! They said this was about maintenance! I don't understand any of this!

lines_after.dialogue: The monk gestures to a hidden panel in the crystal's base. Inside, a complex apparatus of gears and resonators glows with stolen harmonic energy.
This device is siphoning the Spire's native tone, distorting it to mask a new frequency—a predatory one. It is how they hunt Singers.
They're using the Anchor as a trap?! That's insane!
It's control. The ultimate control. Silence the true song, replace it with your own.

line.dialogue: We must stop the siphon. But the method is perilous.

choices.line: Overload it with a counter-frequency. (Chanida's reckless resonance)
choices.consequence: Quick and loud. It will draw immediate attention.
choices.description: Scale the gantry lattice to reach the monk before he destroys the remaining archives.

line.dialogue: I caught his wrist—his fingers were already reaching for the burn-seal. We need him alive and talking.
The lattice gave way under my weight—I'm hanging by three fingers while he pulls that seal from his robe.

choices.line: Carefully recalibrate it to its true harmonic. (Arthit's precise tuning)
choices.consequence: Requires skill and time. You might be discovered.
choices.description: Use Malee's tonal resonator to seal the fracture before it spreads further.

line.dialogue: The frequency locked—hold steady, Chanida, I need twelve more seconds before the cascade stabilizes.
Wrong harmonic—it's feeding back into the fracture. Everyone fall back before it takes the whole chamber!

choices.line: Let Malee hack the control runes to reverse the flow. (Subvert the system)
choices.consequence: Risky. A feedback loop could damage the Spire itself.
choices.description: Demand the monk explain what

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
The resonance turns hostile. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The siphon dies with a shattering whine. For one pure moment, the Anchor Spire rings with its true, clean tone. Then, the heavy footfalls of Tonal Order guards echo from above.
They're here. The entire harmonic signature of the Spire just shifted. They couldn't miss it.
Fantastic. So we get to be martyrs for the adventurous. How noble.
I love it!! Let them come! Their lies end here!
Heretics! You have violated the Sacred Harmonics! You will be silenced!
You're the ones who violated it! You built a cage of sound and called it truth!
The map… the Open Frequency… it is real. I have seen it. These travelers… they are Singers.
Singers? But… they're just stories! You need to love yourself, not chase fairy tales!

lines_after.dialogue: The Captain scoffs, raising a weapon that vibrates with a dissonant shriek. The very air around it seems to fray. The other guards fan out.
Stories are all that remain. Submit, and your end will be quick. Resist, and we will unmake you note by note.
We have to love ourselves enough to know our own song. Enough to sing it, even here.
For those who love adventure… let's give them one.

line.dialogue: This is the final stand. How do you face the silencing?

choices.line: Confront them directly. Let the Spire's true tone be your shield. (A battle of wills)
choices.consequence: The pure sound weakens their weapons, but the fight is brutal and public.
choices.description: Smash the resonance crystal against the altar, shattering their sacred frequency forever.

line.dialogue: * "The harmonic signature just collapsed — their entire tuning system is screaming static. We just became the most wanted musicians in the Spiral.
* "The crystal absorbed the impact — it's singing louder now, and every monk in the corridor just heard our exact position.

choices.line: Use the Spire's acoustics. Shatter their resonators with precise sonic feedback. (A tactical dismantling)
choices.consequence: Disarms them without bloodshed, but requires perfect coordination and leaves you exposed.
choices.description: Grab the monk by his ceremonial robes and force him to listen to your unsanctioned melody.

line.dialogue: * "Look at his face — he's never heard anything that wasn't prescribed to him. He's shaking. I think we just gave this man his first real emotion.
* "He's laughing. The melody bounced right off whatever conditioning they've layered into him. He's calling more of them, and he's *thanking* us for the opportunity.

choices.line: Don't fight them. Sing. Reveal the Open Frequency map to everyone present, villager and guard alike. (A revelation)
choices.consequence: The ultimate risk. It could break their conditioning… or drive them into a frenzy to destroy you.
choices.description: Sing your own song together — all three voices — and let the Spiral judge whose harmony survives.

line.dialogue: * "Three off-grid voices in a cathedral of prescribed frequency. The walls are cracking. The Spiral isn't punishing us — it's *listening*. It's been waiting for someone to sing something it hasn't heard before.
* "Our voices won't blend. We've never practiced together and it shows — three discordant notes crashing against a harmonic fortress. The

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard stretches before you—a jagged landscape of shattered crystal resonators and gutted resonance ship hulls. The air thrums with the discordant symphony of salvage engines and the sharp clang of metal on crystal.
Ugh, this place sounds like a headache. All these broken ships... do you know what this is, Pichit? Some of these crystal fragments still hum.
Echoes of journeys ended. Each fracture holds a story, a frequency that once parted the Lattice. Now, just noise in the industrial chorus.
A chorus that pays. If we find an intact low-frequency resonator, we could fund our own ship repairs. Assuming the local vultures haven't picked everything clean.
We should proceed cautiously. Scrapyards attract... opportunistic elements. We're here for information on the Groundless Movement, not a fight.
A figure emerges from behind a stack of cracked hull plating—lean, dressed in patched leathers, with a resonator pistol holstered at the hip. His smile doesn't reach his eyes.
Well, look what the engine wash blew in. You can ask. You can try asking him about the 'Groundless' whispers. But info ain't free in the Khwae.
We heard everything! About the movement, about people disappearing from the lower decks. What's your price?

lines_after.dialogue: Sharp ears. Good. My price is a job. A Tonal Order barge dumped a 'faulty' resonator core here yesterday. I want it. They said it was unstable, but I heard different.
Of course. They always 'dump' the good stuff and label it dangerous. A convenient way to create black-market inventory.
If the Order labeled it unstable, there might be legitimate risk. We should assess the core's resonance signature first.
Every object has two truths: the one spoken and the one that resonates. We will find this core and listen for its real song.

line.dialogue: The bandit points toward the 'Hot Sector' where volatile salvage is stored. How do you approach the search?

choices.line: Follow the bandit's directions exactly. (Straightforward, but predictable.)
choices.description: Squeeze through the collapsed conveyor tunnel toward the resonance source.

line.dialogue: Pichit slides through the gap, fingers tracing the walls.* "These fractures sing at harmonic intervals — intact housing nearby, I can feel it.
Chanida wrenches her shoulder against a rusted beam.* "Ow! Told you this tunnel was a deathtrap — beam's sheared clean through, we're going around.

choices.line: Scout the perimeter first, looking for Order guards or traps. (Cautious and thorough.)
choices.description: Signal Arthit to scan the perimeter before approaching the central scrap tower.

line.dialogue: Arthit raises his scanner, squinting at the readout.* "Two signatures, seventy meters northwest — scavengers, not security. We have a window.
Arthit's scanner erupts in static.* "Jamming field — someone's already here and they don't want company. Weapons out, now.

choices.line: Ask the local salvage workers for gossip about the dump. (Social, might attract attention.)
choices.description: Follow the low-frequency hum toward a half-buried shipping container.

line.dialogue: Malee presses her palm flat against the container wall, grinning.* "Feel that vibration?
the pirate fails. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hot Sector is a maze of containment cages and warning sigils painted on rusted metal. The air here vibrates with a low, uneasy thrum—the collective murmur of damaged crystals.
My stomach is starting to growl! Can't we find this thing faster? All this weird humming is making me twitchy.
Focus. The core should be in a reinforced cage. Probably that one with the fresh lock. That’s no problem for a little focused resonance frequency.
As Malee works on the lock, a smooth, cultured voice calls out from a walkway above.
A curious choice of browsing, friends! That particular item has... accrued some interest. I might have a more mutually beneficial proposition.
A Trade Negotiator. They're always calculating profit. Be careful, his smile is a transaction.
Information, like resonance, flows to those who listen. What is your proposition?

The core is indeed unstable—but not in the way the Order claims. Its frequency doesn't match their charts. It's... groundless. The very thing your bandit friend and his movement cherish. I can secure it for you, for a future favor.

lines_after.dialogue: There’s something in my eye—or maybe it's just all this dust. Why would you help us? You're not a Groundless sympathizer.
Sympathy is a poor investment. Knowledge is currency. The core's anomalous frequency is data. Data I can trade. You provide the... acquisition, and we both profit.
The lock's off. So we have the core, the bandit wants it, the merchant wants data on it, and the Order wanted it buried. Starting to feel like we're holding a very hot resonator.
We're starting to get entangled. We must decide who to trust, if anyone. The core's resonance is the key.

line.dialogue: The core glows with a soft, irregular pulse in its cradle. The bandit is waiting for delivery, the merchant is offering a deal, and the core itself hums a strange song. What do you do?

choices.line: Deliver the core to the bandit as agreed. (Honor the deal, learn about the Groundless Movement.)
choices.description: Haggle with the Trade Negotiator for information about the core's location.

line.dialogue: I mention the core's energy signature fluctuates when caged — his eye twitches, and he gestures toward the lower vault.
He laughs and says everything has a price, then triples his asking rate before even showing us the door.

choices.line: Let the merchant scan the core first, then deliver it. (Gain data, but risk the bandit's wrath.)
choices.description: Have chanida create a distraction by loudly complaining about hunger near the merchant's stall.

line.dialogue: I groan dramatically about starving, and while he turns to offer me dried rations, malee spots the vault key on his belt.
I wail about my stomach too convincingly — he refuses to sell us anything and waves over security to escort the 'beggar' out.

choices.line: Attempt to attune to the core's frequency yourself. (Risk personal resonance backlash, but learn its truth directly.)
choices.description: malee examines the merchant's wares for hidden markings that indicate the core's cage.

line.dialogue: I trace the serial etchings on his display case — the numbering sequence matches reinforced containment units in the back corridor.
I scan his inventory too openly, and he slams a cloth over the cases, muttering that snooping buyers get reported to the Wardens.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's cacophony grows oppressive as you approach the rusting hulk of a downed pirate skiff, the rendezvous point. The air smells of ozone and rust.
There you are. Took your sweet time. The name's Kwan. Heard you been askin' about frequencies the Orders don't like.
We seek understanding, not conflict. The patterns in the static... they suggest a truth buried beneath the sanctioned charts.
He's an old friend of mine from the lower docks. Or he was, before he decided stealing was more profitable than salvaging.

Hey, Malee! Still got that sharp tongue, I see. Your philosopher friend here is right. There's a frequency. A 'ground-tone'. Silences the Lattice's feedback near the old world. The Groundless Movement whispers about it.
A frequency to go down? Are you sure? That could change everything!
Or it could shatter our resonator and drop us into the crystalline depths. I probably have a dozen schematics warning against such unstable harmonics.

The info's in a locked resonator-log, hidden in the wreck of the *Whispering Maw*, deep in the salvage piles. Guards? Probably. The Trade Negotiator, Lert, has eyes on anything valuable here. He's been buyin' up all the old logs.

lines_after.dialogue: Kwan slips away into the metallic shadows. The path to the *Whispering Maw* lies through a canyon of stacked hulls, where every footstep rings loud.
He must have given us at least a *mostly* straight answer. The profit's in the resale, not the ambush, with him.
Then let us walk carefully. The truth we seek is close, but so are many who would profit from its burial.

line.dialogue: How do you approach the wreck of the *Whispering Maw*?

choices.text: Use the scrapyard's ambient noise as cover. (Stealth)
choices.consequence: You move like ghosts through the din, avoiding patrols entirely.
choices.description: Draw your blade and step between Kwan and Malee, demanding he state his business plainly.

line.dialogue: [Kwan raises both palms, smirking. "Easy, easy. I'm here to trade information, not fists. Your blade won't learn you anything."]
[Kwan's hand drops to his hatchet. "Wrong move, stranger. You flash steel at me, you'd better use it."]

choices.text: Create a diversion with a controlled resonator pulse. (Technical)
choices.consequence: You draw the guards away, but the pulse attracts other scavengers.
choices.description: Let Malee lead the conversation while you study Kwan's hands for weapons and tells.

line.dialogue: [You catch the calluses on his knuckles, the way his eyes flick left — someone else is nearby. Malee notices too.]
[Kwan reads your wandering gaze and adjusts his coat. "Eyes on the conversation, friend. Rude to stare."]

choices.text: Walk right up and bluff your way past as Tonal Order inspectors. (Deception)
choices.consequence: It works... until you meet someone who knows the real inspectors.
choices.description: Mention the patterns Pichit spoke of and ask Kwan directly what the groundless want with them.

line.dialogue: [Kwan's smirk falters. "So you already know about the cracks. Good. That saves me the preamble — and the price."]
[Kwan laughs sharp. "You don't walk into a snake's den naming the snakes. Now they know you're coming."]

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the derelict's shattered bridge, you find the resonator-log. As Arthit extracts it, the smooth voice of Trade Negotiator Lert echoes from the entrance.
I walked back and forth all night anticipating this find. Don't overwork yourselves, my friends. That log is a dangerous piece of unregulated history. Let me... dispose of it safely.
Dispose of it? You mean sell it to the highest bidder and keep everyone chained to the sky!

Chain is such a harsh word. I provide stability. The Groundless dream is a lovely one, but destabilizing. Think of the market crash if 'ground' became a commodity. Now, hand it over, and we can negotiate a finder's fee.
He paced back and forth. He's not buying time; he's waiting for the hired muscle to arrive.
Confirmed. Scanners show three armed signatures closing in from the scrap piles. We are cornered.
This knowledge does not belong to any one person, Lert. It is a whisper from the world itself, meant for all who have the ears to hear.
And I intend to be the one who decides who gets to listen. Last offer.

lines_after.dialogue: The standoff is absolute. The log hums in your hands, its data a silent scream. The fate of the Ground-tone hangs in the balance.
We went to bed late last night, driven by the hope of this moment. We do not back down now.

line.dialogue: This is the climax. How do you secure the Ground-tone frequency?

choices.text: Fight your way out. Use the wreck's unstable geometry against Lert's enforcers. (Combat)
choices.consequence: A brutal, noisy clash secures the log, but alerts the entire scrapyard. Your escape is a running battle, burning bridges with the local underworld.
choices.description: Slide the ledger across the table and demand he explain the flagged transactions in red ink.

line.dialogue: Your handwriting shakes on every fourth entry — that's the rhythm of someone paying tribute, not collecting profit.
He just smiled at me like I'd shown him a baby's drawing. I misread every page.

choices.text: Out-bargain Lert. Offer him exclusive trade rights to *other* salvaged knowledge, diverting his greed. (Negotiation)
choices.consequence: You secure the log, but Lert now has a legitimate claim on your future finds. You've made a powerful, untrustworthy ally.
choices.description: Signal Malee to circle behind the merchant while you keep him talking about the Grand's chain.

line.dialogue: I'm right behind his chair now — he hasn't blinked once. He knows. He's *letting* me do it.
He moved the moment I shifted — like he felt my shadow. This man has been watched before.

choices.text: Broadcast the frequency live on an open channel. Let the Lattice itself carry the truth to every Listener and Singer. (Sacrifice)
choices.consequence: The secret is freed, empowering the Groundless Movement instantly, but you lose any personal advantage. You and Lert are both left with nothing but a changed world, making powerful enemies in the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Lean close and whisper that you know what he's waiting for, even though you don't.

line.dialogue: His knuckles went white. Whatever he's expecting, it has a name — and he just told me it's real.
He laughed, soft and genuine. 'No, child,' he said. 'You don't. Not even close.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hum with the faint, perpetual resonance of recorded knowledge. Pichit's fingers hover over a crystal slate, its surface shimmering with forbidden cartographic harmonics.
These charts... they're not just routes. They feel like memories of the world before The Silencing. Don't judge others for fearing them, but we must understand.
Ugh, it's so quiet! Can't we find the loud part? The part about hidden sky-pirate frequencies? Don't let anyone know I asked!
The 'loud part' would be in the Restricted Stacks. Guarded by the Tonal Orders' most humorless librarians. A perfect plan.
Caution. Our research permit is for public harmonics only. Venturing further requires... discretion.
A sudden, clumsy clatter of crystal echoes from a nearby aisle. A Skycity Resident, their face pale, fumbles with a resonator cane.
Sorry, sorry! This thing... my leg. The resonator's calibration is off. Don't let him see you! The Archivist on duty... he fines for accidental dissonance.
Your prosthetic... it's crystalline. It responds to the Archives' ambient frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: Aye. Salvaged resonator tech. Lets me walk, but in here... it sings when it shouldn't. Don't tell anyone it's unstable! They'll confiscate it.
That's awful! We can help fix it! Right, Malee? You're good with crystals.
I'm good with not getting fined. But fine. Let's see the schematic.

line.dialogue: The villager's prosthetic leg glitches, emitting a low, pulsing hum that doesn't match the Archives' sanctioned frequencies. A stern Archivist is approaching from the main hall.

choices.line: Quickly usher the villager into a side alcove to hide and muffle the sound.
choices.description: Trace the harmonic patterns on the charts with your fingertips, feeling for hidden resonance beneath the ink, 15 words exactly here

line.dialogue: The lines are warm — there's a second map layered beneath, pulsing where the crystal shelves align.
Nothing but cold paper. Whatever secret these charts held, it's faded long past my reaching.

choices.line: Have Chanida create a diversion by 'accidentally' dropping a stack of resonance slates near the Archivist.
choices.description: Signal Chanida to hum a dissonant chord toward the nearest crystal stack and watch for reactions, 15 words exactly here

line.dialogue: HA — you see that? The crystal rang back a note I didn't sing. It's answering me!
Not even an echo. These stacks are deader than my grandmother's music box, and that's saying plenty.

choices.line: Use Pichit's knowledge of harmonic theory to verbally suggest a temporary counter-frequency to calm the prosthetic.
choices.description: Show Arthit the permit's fine print, asking whether 'public harmonics' includes ambient resonance bleeding from the Restricted section, 15 words

line.dialogue: Clever eyes — clause nine permits 'incidental harmonic exposure.' We can investigate bleed without technically entering. Let's proceed carefully.
the villager's resolve isn't enough. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The side alcove is a dead-end of dusty frequency catalogs. The villager's leg continues its erratic, quiet pulse. The Archivist's footsteps pause nearby.
The calibration node is here, under the knee cap. But it's not working. The crystal lattice is fractured.
Fractured? That's it, then. I don't wanna see that anymore! Watching it fail... I'll be grounded.
It's not usable in this state, but the fracture pattern... it's familiar. I saw a similar flaw in a Restricted Stacks log about... resonant weapon overloads.
Weapon overloads? This was made from salvaged ship parts?
So we need the Restricted Stacks to fix it! C'mon, it'll be an adventure! Shall we go to the... forbidden seaside of knowledge?
Before anyone can answer, a figure draped in scavenged leathers and carrying a jagged resonator blade slips into the alcove. A Sky Pirate.
Heard the glitch. Sweet little secret you got here. That fracture sings a pirate song. I know the frequency that caused it.

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal Orders don't record everything. Some frequencies are... bad for business. That leg crystal came from a ship we scuttled. Its resonator blew out just like that.
You're saying there's an unstable, unrecorded frequency loose in the shipping lanes?
I'm sayin' I know where it is. And what it's worth. The fix for the leg's in my head. But it's out of order for free.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate offers the corrective frequency for the prosthetic in exchange for a future favor. The Archivist is still dangerously close, and the villager is desperate.

choices.line: Agree to the pirate's terms quickly and quietly to get the frequency and get everyone out safely.
choices.description: Pichit uses tonal knowledge to map the frequency corridors near the lost knowledge

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit overreaches. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Attempt to bluff the pirate, claiming you already deciphered the frequency from the fracture pattern and don't need his deal.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using unauthorized tones to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. She hears something no one else can.
The lattice has other plans. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Refuse the deal and try to manually recalibrate the prosthetic using first principles, a risky process that could amplify the glitch.
choices.description: The pirate steps forward with secret frequencies, ready to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: the pirate finds the key. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
Defeat. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: In a side-chamber of the Archives, the group examines the Resonant Prosthetic. Its crystal lattice shimmers faintly, humming a discordant note.
The calibration is off. This isn't just a leg replacement. It's been modified to receive signals. Someone's been using it to eavesdrop on private frequencies.
So the 'charitable donation' to the injured villager was a scam. I was cheated out of my sympathy. They were swindling us while we were helping them.
That sky pirate we cornered earlier was too eager to talk. He gave up his captain's location for a loaf of bread. It's not working. This feels like a set-up.
The deception is a layer of static over the truth. We must listen past it. The prosthetic's resonance suggests it was tuned to a very specific, hidden archive frequency.

(Whispering from a nearby stack) Please... you mustn't tell anyone I showed you this. The man with the crystal leg... he paid me to keep quiet. He's adorable with the Archive kittens, but... he frightens me.
Great. So our villain is a cat-loving spy. May I have a toothpick? I need to clean out this resonator port. There's data-filament stuck in it.

lines_after.dialogue: The data-filament, when cleaned and connected to an archive reader, spills out stolen tonal charts. Routes to places not on any official map.
These lead to a sector of the Lattice marked 'Shattered Harmony.' No ship is supposed to go there. The resonance would be... catastrophic.
They're not just stealing knowledge. They're planning to break something. We have to stop them before they finish whatever this is.

line.dialogue: The stolen charts point to a restricted sub-basement. The entrance is acoustically sealed, but the prosthetic's aberrant frequency might crack it open.

choices.line: Use the prosthetic's frequency. It's a direct key, but it will alert the spy to our presence immediately.
choices.description: Rip open the prosthetic leg and trace the embedded transponder circuit back to its signal origin.

line.dialogue: Found it — this beacon's been broadcasting our position to someone for weeks," Arthit says, holding up the cracked casing.
The casing shatters and the chip fries itself clean — whoever built this didn't want it examined," Arthit mutters over the sparking wreckage.

choices.line: Have Malee synthesize a mimic-frequency. Slower, stealthier, but a delicate operation that could fail.
choices.description: Track down the village elder who received the prosthetic and demand to see what else came with the donation.

line.dialogue: The elder shows me a second crate — military-grade signal jammer disguised as grain supplies," Malee says, her jaw tight with fury.
The elder's gone. Whole family vanished overnight — someone warned them we were coming asking questions," Malee reports from the empty doorway.

choices.line: Persuade a nervous archivist to override the seal. Risky, as the Tonal Orders strictly forbid it.
choices.description: Return to the sky pirate in the holding cell and show him the transponder chip to force a real confession.

line.dialogue: His face goes white — he recognizes the chip and starts naming
the villager fails. Local knowledge proves outdated.

lines_before.dialogue: The sub-basement is not a library, but a resonant chamber. In its center, a massive, flawed crystal resonator is wired to the Archive's core. A sky pirate captain stands before it, his posture that of a conductor.
The Tonal Orders hoard the music! They decide what size of freedom we wear! My girlfriend gets jealous of the time I spend down here... but she'll understand when the whole world sings my tune!
You would shatter the foundation of knowledge to make your own song? This isn't creation. It's the Silencing, all over again.
Let me guess. Does she have a boyfriend? One who told you this was a good idea? This resonator is so overloaded it'll take the Archives, and half the floating city, with it when it pops.
I don't wanna see that anymore! All that loss, for what? A stupid solo?
The feedback loop is building. He's using stolen Singer techniques, but without the control. We have seconds to disrupt the resonance cascade.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber thrums with destructive potential. The flawed crystal pulses like a sick heart. The fate of the Archives hangs on a single, counteracting frequency.
Every voice has its counter-harmony. We must find the note that turns his rage to silence.

line.dialogue: The pirate's resonator is vulnerable at its point of connection to the Archive. To save the knowledge, you must sever it without triggering the collapse.

choices.line: Chanida smashes the primary conduit. Direct, violent, and will cause a physical cave-in, burying the chamber but saving the data above.
choices.description: Smash the Resonance Vault's tuning fork against the chamber wall until it cracks open.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "You hear that? Every frequency they caged just flooded the room. Knowledge was never theirs to keep.
Pichit — "It's reinforced with harmonic lattice. You'll break your wrist before you break their vault.

choices.line: Arthit and Malee attempt a precise tonal dampening. Technically complex, it could safely neutralize the resonator but requires perfect harmony under pressure.
choices.description: Appeal to Chanida directly — ask her what she saw in the Tonal Orders' archives that broke her.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "They catalogued every song my grandmother sang and locked it behind clearance level nine. She died humming something I'll never be allowed to hear.
Chanida — "You think I need some outsider digging around in my grief? That's exactly what they did to me in there.

choices.line: Pichit must Sing. To match and then absorb the destructive frequency into himself, a profoundly dangerous act that could shatter his own connection to the Lattice.
choices.description: Challenge Malee to sing the forbidden scale aloud, right here, where the Orders' acoustic sensors will detect it.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Seven notes. That's all it takes to turn their whole taxonomy into noise. Listen — the walls are already buzzing.
Malee — "My throat closed before I reached the fourth note. They conditioned me harder than I thought.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans like a dying beast. Mountains of shattered resonance ship hulls rise against the Lattice's shimmering veil below, their crystal resonators long silent. The air tastes of ozone and rust.
Ugh, this place is louder than a market brawl. How are we supposed to hear anything useful?
Precisely. The ambient noise provides excellent acoustic camouflage for illicit deals. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Oh, don't worry. I'm sure the friendly locals will just hand over the contraband resonator we need. What could possibly go wrong?
Every broken thing here once sang. Now they just... echo. There are stories in these silences.
Philosophy later, Pichit. My mom told me about a contact here—a scavenger who knows the surface frequencies. Said he trades in 'unusual salvage.'
A figure emerges from behind a gutted engine block—a surface scavenger, their face obscured by a filtration mask, their movements deliberate and wary.
Outsiders. You're off your charts. What's your business in the graveyard?

lines_after.dialogue: We seek knowledge. The kind not found in Tonal Order libraries.
Knowledge has a class. A cost. You look like you've got a class to teach. Or learn.
We're looking for a specific resonator frequency. Black market. I'm gonna rush off right now if you don't start talking.
Impatient. That'll get you killed on the surface. But... I might have something. Follow me. Quietly.

line.dialogue: The scavenger leads you to a makeshift shelter under a listing hull. Inside, among junk, rests a strange device: a prosthetic leg fused with glowing crystal. The scavenger eyes you.

choices.line: Ask directly about the resonator frequency.
choices.description: Press your ear against the corroded hull plating and track the rhythmic scraping beneath the deck.

line.dialogue: Chanida* — "There — someone's dragging something heavy below us. Two-legged, limping, about forty meters starboard. I grew up tracking poachers in bamboo mud; metal just rings different.
Chanida* — "Either I'm hearing three separate things or one thing with too many legs, and I genuinely cannot decide which option scares me less right now.

choices.line: Inquire about the crystal leg first, showing curiosity.
choices.description: Wedge a sensor probe into the cracked conduit and sample the electromagnetic residue for recorded data fragments.

line.dialogue: Arthit* — "Fascinating — this conduit absorbed twenty-seven years of shipwide communications. I'm hearing cargo disputes, a child's birthday song, and someone whispering a password I suspect is still active.

Arthit* — "The probe is feeding me garbage — sixteen overlapping voices compressed into pure static. Either the data degraded catastrophically or whatever still lives here is *screaming* at my equipment.

choices.line: Offer a trade from your own supplies immediately.
choices.description: Scatter Pichit's tuning forks across the floor in a spiral pattern and listen for which ones go silent.

line.dialogue: Pichit* — "The fourth fork stopped singing. Not broke — *swallowed*. Whatever sits in the dark below us doesn't like that frequency. So now we know which door to knock with.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the scavenger's den, the constant scrapyard din is muted. The crystal leg on the workbench hums faintly, out of sync with the world's noise.
This? Salvage from a Listener who didn't listen. The lattice took his real one. He thought he could harmonize with it. Fool.
Charming. So you loot the dead and sell their mistakes. And we're supposed to trust you?
The crystalline integration is... remarkable. But unstable. A resonance prosthetic requires precise attunement. This one is leaking harmonics.
It's not a mistake. It's a testament. He tried to sing with the world, and the world answered... just not how he expected.
Don't change the subject! We have work to do. The frequency. Now.

You want the pirate's bypass frequency? It's dangerous. It lets you slip through the lattice like a ghost, but it attracts... other things. My price is this: you fix this leg's resonance leak. I have work I have to do on the surface, and I need it stable. Can you promise me that?
Suddenly, the metal walls reverberate with a harsh, aggressive hum. A shadow falls across the entrance.

lines_after.dialogue: Well, well. Poaching my business, scrap-rat? And you brought friends!
Sky pirate. He's the one who sells the frequency. And he doesn't like competition.
You want the sweet song that lets you dance past the Orders? You deal with me. But first, you hand over that whining leg. I've got a buyer for curiosities.
Hostile acquisition. The situation is deteriorating rapidly.

line.dialogue: The sky pirate stands blocking the exit, hand on a weapon that crackles with discordant energy. The scavenger looks at you, waiting to see if you'll honor the deal.

choices.line: Stand with the scavenger and defend the prosthetic.
choices.description: Examine the crystal's resonance frequency with your tuning fork, matching its pitch

line.dialogue: The lattice harmonics are intact—this fragment still remembers the song it carried.
The frequency collapsed on contact. Whatever this carried, it's gone now.

choices.line: Try to negotiate with the pirate for both the frequency and the leg.
choices.description: Grab the scavenger's wrist and demand to know where the Listener's body lies

line.dialogue: You're shaking. Good—means you remember what happens to people who desecrate the Choir's dead.
He slipped free and pulled a blade. Of course he did—you never check for weapons first.

choices.line: Attempt to quickly repair the leg's resonance leak to use it as a distraction.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sing the fragment's remembered tone back into the crystal

line.dialogue: There—I felt it answer. The Listener's voice isn't lost. It was just... waiting for someone to ask.
Nothing. The crystal stayed silent. Maybe some echoes are meant to fade, no matter how hard we try to hold them.

lines_before.dialogue: The stolen resonator core pulses erratically in Chanida's hands, casting sickly green light across the corroded hull of the derelict ship you've taken shelter in. The rhythmic clanging from the main salvage yard feels predatory now.
This thing is... humming. It's not like the charts. I knew right away it was wrong. It feels like it's listening back.
We should have left it. Stealing from the Tonal Orders is one thing, but a pirate's resonator? The frequency signatures are unstable, illegal. I have an uneasy feeling.
Oh, relax. Unstable just means it can do things their sanctioned toys can't. The pirate said it could find 'quiet paths' through the Lattice. That's worth a little discomfort.

Malee is right about its potential, but Arthit's caution is valid. The Lattice doesn't just respond to sound; it remembers it. This core... I don't feel the same resonance as before. It's been altered.
A heavy, synchronized thud echoes from outside—not machinery, but boots. Shadows block the jagged entrance.
Think you can just lift my tune and scuttle off? That core's tuned to my ship's heart. It calls to me. Makes it real easy to find thieves.
Told you they were trouble. Outsiders with a pirate core? You brought the storm to my yard. Now we deal with it.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate and his newfound ally, the Surface Scavenger, have you cornered. The pirate wants his core back; the scavenger wants you gone. The unstable resonator thrums in Chanida's grip.

choices.text: Surrender the core. (Return the stolen resonator. You lose the artifact, but may negotiate safe passage.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the humming surface and let the resonance flood your senses.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "The frequencies are layering — I can almost read the pattern, like a song half-remembered.
Arthit — "Your fingers are going numb already — pull back before it drinks deeper, pull back NOW.

choices.text: Bluff with a counter-frequency. (Use your knowledge to mimic a dangerous Lattice resonance, hoping to scare them off.)
choices.description: Wrap the artifact in the lead-lined tarp from your kit and stifle the vibration entirely.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Good. Muffled. Now we move quiet, and we don't stop until we're past the perimeter.
Malee — "You've smothered it — listen, the hum's gone crooked, like a caged animal chewing its own leg.

choices.text: Trigger a controlled feedback pulse. (Use the core's instability against the scrapyard's acoustic environment, creating a chaotic distraction.)
choices.description: Hold the artifact near the scrapyard's derelict tonal array and see if the old resonators respond.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The dead array is waking — those tones haven't sounded in decades, the artifact is speaking their language.
Chanida — "Nothing. No response at all — either the array is too far gone, or this thing speaks a dialect nobody remembers.

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation leaves the air thick with tension and the scent of ozone. The immediate threat is gone, but the core's aberrant song has attracted unwanted attention.
Well, that was bracing. And look—the feedback scorched the serial numbers off the core. The Orders can't trace it now. Every cloud.
We've made the Lattice here agitated. The background hum is sharper. We need to move before something... deeper notices.

lines_before.dialogue: The entire Tha Khwae Scrapyard seems to hold its breath. The stolen resonator core, now fused with a salvaged prosthetic leg from the subplot, glows with a serene, unified light. But a deep, subsonic vibration begins to rise from the Lattice below the metal decks.
You fools! You've woken the old echoes! The Silencing left scars down there! What kind of death do you prefer? Crushed or dissolved?
It's not us! It's the core-leg! It's harmonizing with the scar! We can... we can guide the resonance. Anywhere you like, we can send it!

She's right. The prosthetic has become a keystone. The Lattice's pain and the pirate's stolen song are merging. We must choose the finale. Why are you doing this to me, fate? To offer such a terrible choice...
My core's in that... thing? You grafted it to a leg?! That's my fortune! Give it here!
Your fortune is currently the only thing standing between this entire floating junkyard and a recursive harmonic collapse. So maybe have a seat.
The energy is building. We can't contain it. We must discharge it. But into what? The sky? The city? The Lattice itself? What style do you prefer for salvation, Pichit? All our paths lead down.
The fused artifact pulses in time with the rising drone. Geometric cracks of light spread across the ground. The very island groans.

line.dialogue: The Resonant Prosthetic is the focal point. The catastrophic energy must be directed. The choices are dire, each a permanent mark on the Lattice.

choices.text: Disperse it upward, into the open sky. (Safely vents the energy but creates a permanent 'dead zone' in the Lattice below, ruining the scrapyard.)
choices.description: Have Arthit focus captain experience on the scavenger gangs to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.text: Channel it into the pirate's ship. (Uses the vessel as a sacrificial resonator, destroying the ship but potentially refining the rogue frequency into something usable.)
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using resonant staff to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The gamble fails. A spy alerts the authorities.

choices.text: Ground it into the Lattice scar. (Aims to heal the old wound by overloading it with pure resonance. Risks feedback that could shatter the island.)
