choices.text: Confront the agents. Use the data as leverage, negotiating for safe passage and a controlled disclosure.
choices.outcome: You walk the razor's edge. You gain temporary safety and influence, but are now bound to a deadly pact.

line.dialogue: The drums eat their listening. I'll say it once
the merchant's resolve isn't enough. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of quiet. Sunlight, fractured by crystalline skylights, falls in dust-moted beams upon endless shelves of resonant tablets. The air hums with the faint, preserved echoes of safe routes.
Every chart here is a lifeline. A promise that the Lattice can be navigated. Which one would you like to study first?
The one that gets us to the rumored listening post fastest! The Tonal Orders probably keep the best routes locked up, though.
Probably true. Monopolies don't survive by sharing. Look at this... 'Route to the Eastern Chorus, certified by the Third Order.' Certified, meaning 'taxed.'
We should cross-reference. A single source is a risk. The mother of all navigators was heart-broken when her only chart failed, they say.
A figure in ochre robes approaches silently. Listener Monk the Listener monk bows slightly, his eyes holding a deep, conflicted reverence.
You seek the old paths. The ones before the Silencing. It is... a dangerous reverence.
We seek understanding. The Lattice's true song, not just the safe notes.

lines_after.dialogue: The true song is not in these sanctioned tablets. It is in the cracks. The Groundless... they whisper of such things. But to listen...
The Groundless? The ones who say we shouldn't be up here on floating cities at all?
They believe the Silencing was a correction. That we are living in the echo, not the melody. May I... show you something? It is not on any chart.

line.dialogue: The Listener Monk offers to guide you to a restricted section of the Archives, a place of 'unverified resonances.'

choices.text: Trust his reverence. Follow him.
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing mechanical repair to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee is thwarted. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: Demand to know what he expects in return.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to harness harmonic feedback, drawing on frequency mapping

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida hits a wall. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Refuse. Stick to the certified charts.
choices.description: Convince the monk to use lattice study and follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The attempt backfires on the monk. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The Monk leads you through a disused archivium, where the crystal shelves are veiled in dust and the hum of the Archives fades to a hollow whisper.
We don't stay in touch with places like this. There's a reason they're sealed. Structural resonance could be unstable.
Instability is a kind of truth. Here. These tablets... they are from before the Orders. From Listeners who mapped by ear, not by commerce.
Scratches on crystal. No official sigils. How do we know they're not just the ravings of some hermit who fell into the Lattice?
The pattern... it's chaotic, but there's a repetition. A heartbeat under the noise. I want to understand it, but... I don't know where to begin.
A grating sound echoes from a high balcony. A figure in patched leathers, the Surface scavenger, is carefully prying a small, dark crystal tablet from a crevice.
Hey! Don't leave it open! The whole shelf could resonate out of sequence!
Sequence? You Order-folk and your sequences. This is a raw frequency. The Groundless pay well for untainted songs.

lines_after.dialogue: That tablet... it speaks of a 'Shattered Chord.' A place where the Lattice is silent. The Groundless believe it's a way through.
Believe? I've seen it. A hole in the song. But you need a Singer to find it, and the Orders have them all caged. Or dead.
This is beyond charted exploration. We're talking about a fundamental anomaly.
An anomaly that could change everything. Or destroy us. The Scavenger has the key. The Monk has the context.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger holds a potentially dangerous, unregistered tonal map. The Monk looks to you, awaiting your judgment on this forbidden knowledge.

choices.text: Buy the tablet from the Scavenger. Knowledge has a price.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the largest tablet and feel for residual warmth. 14 words

line.dialogue: You feel it—the pulse beneath the surface. This place remembers being touched.
Cold. Dead as river stone. Whatever charged these tablets, it left long ago.

choices.text: Convince the Scavenger to share the map for a share of the discovery.
choices.description: Trace the repeated pattern with charcoal and check if it maps to constellations. 14 words

line.dialogue: There—the repetition isn't random. It's a coordinate system. Someone was navigating *back* here.
Nothing aligns. Either the sky has shifted since these were carved, or we're grasping at nothing.

choices.text: Seize the tablet for the Archives. Such power is too dangerous for the surface.
choices.description: Ask the monk to chant the oldest sutta he knows while standing among the tablets. 15 words

line.dialogue: The crystal hums on the third verse. We're not reading them. They're *answering* us.
I sang the words as taught to me. Either my lineage forgot something, or these stones were never Buddhist.

lines_before.dialogue: The Archives' quiet hum has shifted. The Scavenger's accusations hang in the air like dissonant chords.
You think these pretty crystal maps tell the truth? The Lattice song is a lament. The Silencing was a scream.
But the Orders... they guide the cities. They keep us safe.
Safe? They caged the song. My people on the surface hear the real echoes. The ones the Orders silenced.
Of course. A monopoly on knowledge. Classically corrupt. So, what's the real price of our 'safe' routes?
This is dangerous speculation. Our mission is to find a route, not to... topple a guild.
The Scavenger speaks of the Unrecorded Dirge. A forbidden resonance. I have... studied it. In secret.
Why keep it secret? If the Lattice has more to say, shouldn't we listen?

lines_after.dialogue: Because the knowledge it brought was a burden. It speaks of a flaw in the Silencing narrative. A choice.
A choice to bury the truth. The Groundless know. We live in the echo of that lie.
From a high alcove, a single, pure crystal tone chimes. Someone is waiting for you.

line.dialogue: The Monk reveals a hidden resonator keyed to the Dirge. He looks to Pichit.

choices.text: Take the key. We need to hear this for ourselves.
choices.outcome: You accept the burden. The Dirge's first note resonates within you, a cold, clarifying truth.
choices.description: Hold the crystal map to the light, searching for hidden channels beneath its etched surface, 15 words

line.dialogue: Chanida tilts the map until stray light reveals fracture-lines spelling coordinates the Orders never marked.
Chanida squints, but the crystal throws only her own reflection back — whatever's hidden stays hidden.

choices.text: Let the Monk play it. We are witnesses, not actors.
choices.outcome: The Monk's hand trembles as he activates the resonator. The Archives' perfect acoustics carry the forbidden sound to every corner.
choices.description: Grab the scavenger's arm and demand she sing what her people heard on the surface, 15 words

line.dialogue: The scavenger's voice cracks into a raw, keening note that makes the crystal maps ring in sympathy.
The scavenger yanks free and spits at your feet. "You don't get to order a song from us.

choices.text: Smash the resonator. Some truths are too destructive.
choices.outcome: You shatter the crystal. Silence crashes back, heavier than before. The Monk looks devastated, the Scavenger, furious.
choices.description: Smash the nearest crystal map on the floor and watch what pattern the shards fall in, 15 words

line.dialogue: Malee reads the scatter — a constellation pointing south, toward a structure the Orders erased from every chart.
The shards skitter into meaningless static. Malee curses. "Well. That was forty credits of map I just murdered.

lines_before.dialogue: The forbidden resonance, whether heard or silenced, has changed the air. The Archives feel like a held breath.
It is done. The Dirge is in the air now. The Tonal Masters will come. They always know.
So what do we do? Run?
We have no viable route! Our original charts are now... suspect.
The ultimate product defect: reality. So, we're stuck between a corrupt guild and a lattice of lies.
You have a Singer. The Lattice itself is the chart. You just have to listen. Really listen.
He's right. The maps are interpretations. The song is the source. But to navigate it raw...
Heavy, synchronized footsteps echo in the harmonic corridors. The Tonal Enforcers have arrived.

lines_after.dialogue: I see the exit vector. It's... jagged. Unstable. But it's there. Pichit, do you wanna try it?
It's the only true path left. I'll try it.
Pichit closes his eyes. The Enforcers' shouts fade. He hears only the Lattice—the choir and the dirge, the lie and the truth, woven into one terrifying, beautiful song.

line.dialogue: Pichit must lead the party out by singing a path never written, using the flawed, true song of the Lattice.

choices.text: Harmonize with Chanida. Use her impulsive courage as a guide.
choices.outcome: Your voices braid together, boldness tempering fear. The Lattice parts in a volatile but passable wave, a new kind of duet.
choices.description: Force open the maintenance hatch beneath the resonance platform and drop into the sub-tonal access shaft.

line.dialogue: Metal groans — it's giving! Go, go, before the Dirge finds a harmonic lock on us!
Sealed. Welded shut from the other side. Someone *knew* we'd try this.

choices.text: Integrate the Dirge. Sing the painful truth into the path.
choices.outcome: You sing the hidden lament. The Lattice shudders and fractures in a controlled collapse, creating a path of heartbreaking clarity.
choices.description: Sing a counter-frequency into the Mast's feed horn to cancel the Dirge's root note.

line.dialogue: I can feel it — the wave is bending, flattening. The air is thinning. Keep going!
My throat split open and the note came out wrong. Now there are *two* Dirges. I'm sorry.

choices.text: Sing solo. Bear the full, unfiltered resonance alone.
choices.outcome: You take the entire dissonant chord into yourself. The path that opens is pure and direct, but the feedback etches a permanent change into your soul.
choices.description: Unspool Arthit's chart tape as a dead-reckoning guide and walk blind through the dissonance corridor.

line.dialogue: Forty-seven paces, turn left, forty-two more — I can feel the wall! There's a door here!
The tape dissolved at step nineteen. I'm touching something that doesn't have a shape.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch out in terraced ribbons of green. The air hums with the gentle resonance of wind through crystal-flecked crops and the soft chime of irrigation channels.
Finally! Somewhere that doesn't smell like engine oil and old charts. I could just... lie down right here.
Don't get too comfortable. Peaceful places usually have the highest prices. Or the deepest secrets.
The resonance here is... stable. Calming. A good place to restock supplies and gather our bearings.
There's a rhythm to this place. Not just the water, or the wind... but beneath it. A slower pulse.
Near a market stall overflowing with luminous gourds, a well-dressed merchant catches your eye. He gives a practiced, welcoming smile.
Travelers! You have the look of those who appreciate... opportunity. My name is Vorakit. Fresh Mae Rim sky-rice? Crystal-infused tea? All at a friendly rate.

lines_after.dialogue: I'm gonna ask him about that weird hum near the edge of the terraces. You felt it too, right, Pichit?
Ask him about the 'friendly rate' first. Then we can talk about weird hums.
We should be careful. Merchants like this trade in information as much as goods.

line.dialogue: Pichit approaches the merchant, Vorakit. What's the first question?

choices.text: Ask directly about supplies and the best prices.
choices.description: Arthit uses captain experience to trace the anomalous signal near the peaceful breeze

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Mention the underlying pulse you sensed, see how he reacts.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing crystal hearing to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
Chanida overreaches. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Inquire about local rumors or unusual occurrences.
choices.description: The merchant uses information network to commune with trapped echoes near the peaceful breeze

line.dialogue: the merchant makes it work. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the merchant fails. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: Following your line of questioning, Vorakit's friendly smile tightens. He glances toward the misty chasm at the garden's edge.
Unusual occurrences? Well... the gardens are peaceful. Mostly. But the western terrace? The workers avoid it after dusk. Say they hear... singing. From below.
Singing? Like a Singer?

No, no. A ghost song. An echo. They call it the 'Dirge of the *Kinnaree's Lament*.' A Resonance ship that vanished a generation ago. Its crystal resonator is supposedly still active down there, tangled in the Lattice.
And let me guess. That resonator would be worth a fortune to the right... collector.
A functioning antique? Beyond fortune. But it's cursed, they say. Drives listeners mad. The Tonal Orders have it marked 'Lost-Cause.'
A persistent, chaotic resonance could destabilize the gardens' foundation over time. It's a danger.
An echo that hasn't faded... a story that wants to be finished.

lines_after.dialogue: Look, I have a proposal. I have charts... rough ones, made from listener reports. If you were to... investigate, and perhaps retrieve a small shard of that resonator for verification, my backers would be very grateful. Could you repeat that, please? You'll help?
A haunted ship? Do you wanna try it? I mean, we've handled worse!
He's asking us to loot a grave for his profit. Please translate that for me: 'We do the dying, he does the buying.'

line.dialogue: Vorakit's offer hangs in the air. The ghost song calls from the mist. How does the party respond?

choices.text: Refuse outright. It's too dangerous and morally dubious.
choices.description: Lean close and press the merchant for who "they" are, 15 words

line.dialogue: The people who named it — they've heard the Dirge themselves, haven't they?
You're dancing around something. Either you know who 'they' are or you're just spinning tavern talk.

choices.text: Agree to investigate the echo, but make no promises about retrieval.
choices.description: Cut Malee off and ask the merchant what the Dirge actually sounds like, 15 words

line.dialogue: Wait — hold that thought. I want to hear this. What does the ghost song sound like?
No, no, don't answer that. I already know where this is going and I don't like it.

choices.text: Accept the deal. The promise of reward and solving the mystery is too compelling.
choices.description: Let Malee finish and watch the merchant's reaction carefully, 15 words

line.dialogue: And let me guess — that resonator would be worth a fortune to whoever silences it. Am I warm?
And let me guess — that resonator would be worth a fortune. Your eyes just lit up, merchant. You've got one.

lines_before.dialogue: The wind shifts in the terraces, carrying a discordant hum that makes the crystal leaves of the sky-crops tremble.
Listen! That's the same weird frequency from the ship's resonator logs. It's not coming from the Lattice below... it's coming from *within* the gardens.
Of course. The 'haunted' ship wasn't lost to the Lattice. It was scuttled here. Buried under fertilizer and good intentions. What a charming little secret.
If the wreck is here, and its resonator is still active... it could destabilize the entire terrace foundation. We need to find it, but quietly. The Negotiator is watching.
Every ending is woven into a new beginning. This ship's silence was never finished; its story is waiting in the soil.
Friends! Admiring the yield? The harmony here is quite profitable. I wouldn't dig too deep, though. Some roots are best left undisturbed.
The big harvest festival is tomorrow. We probably can't finish it all, but we try. Hope the strange sounds don't spoil the crops.

lines_after.dialogue: The party follows the aberrant resonance to a sealed irrigation control chamber, hidden behind a waterfall of luminous water.
A buried resonance ship. Its crystal hull is fused with the terrace roots. Someone didn't just hide it... they planted it.
The resonator core is still pulsing! It's not broken, it's... *growing* into the Lattice. What happens if we pull it out?

line.dialogue: The fused resonator hums, a trapped song of a lost journey. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Attempt to harmonize with the resonator, using the natural sounds of the gardens to calm it. (Requires empathy with the Lattice.)
choices.description: Channel the resonator's frequency through your lattice scanner to triangulate the wreck's position, 15 words

line.dialogue: The signal locks in — there, beneath the eastern reef shelf, exactly where the currents converge.
The scanner overloads and the frequency scatters — we're deaf to it now, at least for the moment.

choices.line: Carefully extract the crystal core, hoping to sever its connection without causing a collapse. (Requises precise technical skill.)
choices.description: Descend to the wreck directly with only a tether line and a hand-held sonar ping, 15 words

line.dialogue: I can see the hull through the murk — the resonator is mounted on the foredeck, still spinning.
The current takes you sideways and the tether fouls on the reef — you'll have to cut and retry.

choices.line: Amplify the resonator's signal, forcing it to reveal its final recorded log, regardless of the structural risk. (Requires raw resonant power.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sing the harmonic counter-frequency to calm the resonator before approaching, 15 words

line.dialogue: The old melody finds the bones of the ship — listen, the resonator slows, the water stills, the path opens.
Chanida

lines_before.dialogue: The decision is made. The resonator reacts violently, its light flaring through the terraces. The ground shudders. Vines of solidified sound erupt from the soil, grasping at the sky.
Structural integrity failing! The resonator isn't a relic—it's a seed! It's been feeding on the garden's resonance to grow a new Lattice formation!
The crops! They're wilting! That's no problem for a bad season, but this... the color is being drained from them!
A fascinating, if destructive, bloom! My initial investment is regrettably sunk, but the research potential... there's something in my eye from the dust, I must say.
The 'Lost Ship' was an experiment. The Tonal Orders planted it here to see if they could farm the Lattice itself. We're standing in their illegal garden.
My stomach is starting to growl! Not from food—from that thing! It's *hungry*. It's consuming all the soft, peaceful sounds and leaving nothing but silence!
A silent hunger, planted to consume a world's song. To finish the Silencing. We are not just discovering a wreck; we are facing the root of a new catastrophe.

lines_after.dialogue: The resonator-seed reaches a critical phase. It will either be calmed, harnessed, or destroyed, its fate deciding the future of Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens.
The entire terrace platform is resonating with it. One wrong frequency and we'll shatter the foundation. This is the climax.
Every voice matters now. The garden's song, the ship's last echo, our own resolve. We must sing the true ending.

line.dialogue: The resonator-core blooms into a monstrous, beautiful crystal flower, its petals humming with devouring silence. How do you finish this?

choices.line: Shatter the core. End the threat decisively, but destroy the gardens' unique resonance and the proof of the Tonal Orders' crime. (Sacrifice knowledge for safety.)
choices.description: Redirect the resonator's overflow into the wilting fields before the lattice collapses entirely.

line.dialogue: I've rerouted the harmonic bleed into the root systems — the crops are *drinking* the resonance instead of dying from it!
The lattice shattered mid-transfer. Now we have exploding turnips AND a collapsing resonator. I hate this place.

choices.line: Attempt to graft the core onto your own ship, containing its hunger. A dangerous burden that could grant unheard of power or consume you from within. (Embrace a double-edged prize.)
choices.description: Demand malee explain what the Tonal Orders were really building inside the so-called Lost Ship.

line.dialogue: They grew a god from sound — a root-network that sings itself into existence. This resonator? It's the *seed pod*.
You want answers while the ground is eating us? Fine — I'll explain everything to your corpse.

choices.line: Sing to it. Not to calm or command, but to teach it a new song—a song of growth that doesn't consume. To redeem the experiment. (Risk everything to create something new.)
choices.description: Let the merchant salvage resonator components while you stabilize the core with raw harmonic damping.

line.dialogue: Salvaged crystals, stabilized core, and nobody died! I'm doubling my investment and buying everyone a drink!
You dropped the core, my salvage pile is now a crater, and I'm *still* somehow turning a profit on the scrap rights.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands on a cracked observation platform jutting over the Lattice. Below, the crystal plain hums, sending prismatic shivers through the air with every distant tremor.
Look at those light patterns! It's like the ground is singing. Can we get closer?
Absolutely not. One wrong step, one resonant frequency, and the entire shelf could shatter. Is everything all right, Pichit? You seem... distant.
Just listening. The Listeners teach that each hum is a memory of the world before The Silencing. It's... standing right in front of us.
A memory that'll liquefy your boots if you hit the wrong note. Charming. I'm more interested in the salvage beacon pinging over that ridge.
Ah, my intrepid partners! I see you've found the vista. Beautiful, isn't it? And profitable, if you know what to listen for.
Negotiator Vichai. Your 'safe observation post' feels like it's one gust from collapse.

All part of the experience! Now, about that salvage... a recent 'market adjustment' left a Resonator ship's cargo scattered below. A particular crystal component, shaped like a... leg, shall we say? Very valuable to certain collectors.

lines_after.dialogue: A crystal leg? Sounds like someone's expensive prosthetic got sheared off. He's right, that's a fortune in raw resonator tech.
So we just go down and grab it?
It's not that simple. The Lattice here is unstable. We need to chart a safe path. Is everything under control, Vichai? Do you have the frequencies?
My charts are, alas, provisional. A minor investment risk. But I'm sure a clever group like yours can manage!

line.dialogue: The merchant's 'provisional' charts are a blur of static. How does Pichit propose we scout the path?

choices.line: Send Chanida ahead. Her impulsive leaps might find stable footholds faster.
choices.description: Trace the light patterns with your fingertip, matching Chanida's rhythm to map safe footing, 15 words

line.dialogue: Yes, yes—you feel it too! The crystals pull toward pressure points that hold weight!
Your finger is *bleeding* into the substrate and now every pattern within ten meters is rearranging.

choices.line: Have Malee analyze the crystal's resonant feedback. Cynical, but she knows what breaks.
choices.description: Sit cross-legged and hum the lowest tone Pichit described, letting the ground answer you, 15 words

line.dialogue: The Listeners were right—humility of tone. The crystal road illuminates only for those who ask softly.
Congratulations. You just sang a harmonic that woke up a memory about a drowning, and it's climbing your throat.

choices.line: Take point yourself. Listen for the natural harmonics, like the Listeners taught.
choices.description: Throw Malee's boot onto the nearest bright patch to test whether the patterns are truly dangerous, 15 words

line.dialogue: ...Alright, that was smart. Boot melted in four seconds—so now we *know* which colors to avoid.
The boot didn't melt. It *hatched*. And whatever was inside it is looking at us now.

lines_before.dialogue: The party picks their way down a fragile crystal slope. The air thrums with latent energy, and jagged spires cast long, shifting shadows.
Steady. The pitch here is sharp... it means brittle. Arthit, watch your left.
Noted. I don't know where to begin with these merchant-supplied charts. This fissure isn't marked at all.
I know. He sold us a pretty picture and called it a map. Typical Tonal Orders monopoly. The real path is by feel and luck.
There! Glint in that crevice! Is that our crystal leg?
Hands off the merchandise, sky-rats! That shiny bit's our salvage!
A ragged skiff hovers above a nearby spire. A sky pirate, scarred and grinning, leans over the rail, a resonator pistol aimed loosely in your direction.
Speak of the void. Your salvage? This wreck's been here for weeks.
Finders keepers, and we *found* it first! Been tracking that leg for days. It's got a unique frequency signature, see? My boss wants it back. Don't know if he wants you in pieces, but I'm flexible.

lines_after.dialogue: Back? So this 'salvage' was stolen. From who?
Ain't your concern. Point is, you walk away now, or we start playing a real discordant tune. This lattice is already singing a nervous song.
He's bluffing. Firing a resonator pistol here could trigger a harmonic cascade. He'd be caught in it too.
Maybe I like a little music with my murder! I know you want that leg. Everyone does. Makes a fella walk again... or makes a ship fly *real* quiet.

line.dialogue: The pirate's ship is positioned above an unstable spire. The crystal leg is just within reach in the crevice. How does Pichit respond?

choices.line: Call his bluff. Talk him down, emphasizing the mutual danger of a firefight here.
choices.description: Reach into the crevice bare-handed and feel for the crystal's edges before pulling, 14 words

line.dialogue: Got it — warm to the touch, and humming like it remembers me.
Something shifted in there. My fingers came back cut and empty.

choices.line: Create a diversion. Have Chanida cause a controlled crystal chime elsewhere to draw their aim.
choices.description: Wedge the merchant's false map into the crack to lever the glinting object free, 16 words

line.dialogue: Ha! The liar's map finally serves a purpose — crystal leg's out, intact.
The paper shredded on the first pull. Now the glint's buried deeper in.

choices.line: Go for the leg. A quick, reckless grab before the pirates can react, trusting the lattice to hold.
choices.description: Pour water from your flask into the crevice and listen for where it pools beneath, 17 words

line.dialogue: There — runoff opened a gap below. The leg slid right into my palm.
Water's gone and the pitch just drank it. Crevice sealed tighter than before.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform groans as the Resonance Ship, its hull scarred from the skirmish, settles onto a stable, glowing plateau of the Lattice. The sky pirate's vessel smolders nearby.
We did it! Their resonator is still humming. Do you wanna try it?
That's a terrible idea. Their frequency is unstable. We don't know where to begin calibrating it.
He's right. I know. Their ship is held together by spit and desperation. But... their charts might show a way to the old Listeners' archive.
Ah, salvage rights! A most profitable turn. That crystal resonator core alone could buy passage for all of us.
Profit is a fleeting note. The pirate spoke of a 'Shattered Chord' frequency... a path the Tonal Orders sealed. I'll try it.
You're all fools! That frequency... it eats ships. My leg... the feedback from trying it... that's why I needed the prosthetic!
The bandit gestures to the subplot_crystal_leg, its crystalline filaments pulsing erratically with the Lattice's ambient light.

lines_after.dialogue: The party splits their focus. Chanida and Malee approach the pirate ship's resonator. Arthit and the merchant argue over salvage value near the bandit.
Every forbidden frequency was once a natural sound. We must listen, not just calculate.
The Lattice beneath them shimmers, responding to the conflicting energies of two damaged ships.

line.dialogue: How do we proceed with the pirate's ship and the dangerous frequency?

choices.text: Salvage the resonator core for profit. Let the Orders' charts be enough.
choices.consequence: Gain substantial funds but lose the hidden path. The bandit's warning goes unheeded.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to chart resonance pathways using hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida fails. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Attempt to manually calibrate the Shattered Chord frequency using the bandit's prosthetic as a key.
choices.consequence: Risk feedback damage to unlock the secret path. The prosthetic may be destroyed.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to tune the prosthetic using staff meditation

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The lattice has other plans. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Have Chanida and Pichit 'Sing' the frequency raw, using the ship only as an amplifier.
choices.consequence: Extreme personal risk, but the purest way to resonate with the Lattice. Could attract unwanted attention.
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using negotiation to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the merchant overreaches. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision is made. A low, grinding hum builds as the chosen frequency engages with the Lattice. The crystalline surface doesn't part—it *reacts*.
The structural resonance is all wrong! That's probably right about it eating ships. We need to pull back!
Too late. Look. The pirate probably won't be coming with us, but he wasn't lying.
A jagged fissure of brilliant, soundless light tears open in the Lattice before them, not a path for a ship, but a vertical shaft leading down.
The archive! It's below! But the ship won't fit!
A walking expedition onto an unstable resonance field? The profit margin just vanished. I must have. I'm staying with the ship.
The leg... it's pulling me! The frequency's got a hold!
The Lattice is answering. That's probably the point. It's not a road; it's an invitation. Or a test.

lines_after.dialogue: The fissure pulses, its light solidifying into precarious, singing crystal steps descending into the unknown. The subplot_crystal_leg drags the bandit toward the edge.
The world holds its breath. The party stands at the precipice, the hum of their ship and the pirate's wreck the only sounds against the Lattice's new, demanding song.
Below, the lost knowledge of the Listeners waits. Above, safety and the known world recede. The Silencing began with a sound like this.

line.dialogue: The hidden path is open, but unstable and personal. What is the final step?

choices.text: Secure the bandit and retreat. Chart the location for the Tonal Orders.
choices.consequence: Safety and a hefty finder's fee, but you surrender discovery to the monopoly. The secret is commodified.
choices.description: Rappel down through the fractured lattice using harmonic pitons tuned to the field's dominant frequency.

line.dialogue: The pitons lock — the resonance accepts us. Move now, while the harmonics hold!
Wrong frequency. The pitons are screaming back — they're going to shatter!

choices.text: Descend, but use the pirate's ship as an anchor, leaving the merchant and Arthit to manage a lifeline.
choices.consequence: A balanced risk. You explore, but with a route back. The split party faces separate dangers.
choices.description: Send Chanida alone through the narrowest fissure to retrieve whatever the archive still holds.

line.dialogue: I can feel the data singing through the walls — it's still alive down there. I'll be fast.
The passage is closing — the lattice is breathing, and it just exhaled me back out.

choices.text: All four leap. Cut the ship loose. Trust the Lattice's song completely.
choices.consequence: The ultimate gamble. You embrace the unknown fully, with no guarantee of return. The story changes fundamentally.
choices.description: Use the merchant's cargo sled to bridge the gap and slide directly to the archive entrance.

line.dialogue: Merchant
the merchant overreaches. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard is a symphony of industrial decay. Towering hulks of old resonance ships, their crystal drives long dead, groan against their moorings. The air thrums with the percussive clang of salvage and the dissonant roar of smelters.
Listen to that... beneath the noise. A low hum, like a memory trying to surface. This place is a graveyard of journeys.
Journeys we can profit from! C'mon, the broker said the salvage from the *Whispering Shard* is still out here. I saw it first, I'm leading.
You saw a blur on a cheap chart. If we get crushed by a falling hull plate, I'm billing your estate for the inconvenience.
We should stick to the marked paths. The acoustic shadows here can hide... unstable lattice formations.
Ahead, a jagged silhouette resolves into the wreck of a small courier ship. Its nameplate is scarred, but readable: *Echo of Dawn*. The air around it shimmers faintly.
That's not the *Whispering Shard*. This resonance... it's wrong. Like a song played backwards.
Who cares about the name? Loot's loot! When did he get here?

lines_after.dialogue: Chanida points to a figure kneeling beside the wreck. A man in ochre robes, his ear pressed against the ship's crystalline stern. A Listener Monk.
You should not be here. This frequency is... troubled. It speaks of a silencing that was not natural.
Great. A holy man. He's not the one who did it, whatever 'it' is, but he'll definitely charge us a listening fee.
Respectfully, brother, we are on sanctioned salvage. This wreck is in the public ledger.

line.dialogue: The Listener stands, his face etched with conflict. 'The ledger is wrong. This ship was purged from it. Its song is a secret. Leave it be, or help me hear the truth?'

choices.line: Back away. This is Tonal Order business, and we're not paid for ghosts.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the corroded hull and feel for the hum's vibration pattern.

line.dialogue: There — rhythmic, every four seconds. That's machinery, not settling debris. Someone's running something behind this bulkhead.
Nothing but the tingling of corrosion biting into your skin. Either the source is deeper than we can feel, or it's not mechanical at all.

choices.line: Demand answers. What 'truth' is worth hiding a whole ship?
choices.description: Unroll the broker's cheap chart and cross-reference the acoustic shadow against known wreckage schematics.

line.dialogue: Huh. The shadow aligns with a cargo corridor — sealed registry says it was carrying precision instruments. That hum could be automated containment still running.
The chart's grid lines don't even match the hull frame numbers. This thing was drawn by someone who never set foot inside a wreck. We're navigating by doodle.

choices.line: Offer to help, but only if we get first pick of any *physical* salvage.
choices.description: Signal the group to go silent and triangulate the hum's source using three-point listening.

line.dialogue: Bearing's consistent — two o'clock, maybe thirty meters through the compressed section. And it's fading slightly when the ventilation cycles. We can map around it.
Too much ambient noise bleeding through the hull fractures. I can't isolate it. Could be ahead of us

lines_before.dialogue: The monk, Brother Lirin, leads you into the shadow of the *Echo of Dawn*. The shimmer is stronger here, a palpable thrum in the teeth.
It sings of a forced landing. A navigation chart deliberately scrambled. The pilots... they had no one to help them. They were left to die.
A murdered song. The Lattice remembers the violence.
So, what do your parents do? I mean, who would *do* this? Pirates? Rival Orders?
Shall we go to the seaside? Because this is getting depressingly deep. I signed up for loose crystals, not existential crimes.
If the charts were falsified, it points to the Tonal Orders. But proving it is impossible. Their records are sealed.
A harsh laugh echoes from a scaffold above. A woman in patched leathers, a resonator pistol on her hip, looks down. A Sky Pirate.
Impossible for ledger-lickers, maybe. I have no one to help me in the 'official' channels either. Makes you get creative.

lines_after.dialogue: That ship? Its frequency was red-stamped. Too pure. Threatened the monopoly. The Orders didn't crash it... they just stopped singing its safe path.
You speak of heresy.
I speak of fact. Its true resonance log is still in the wreck. A little black crystal. Find it, and you've got a weapon.
A weapon we can sell!
Or a truth we can sing.

line.dialogue: The pirate drops a grappler line, offering a quicker route into the ship's cracked core. 'My price is a copy. The Monk wants absolution, you want profit. I just want to watch the Orders sweat. How do we proceed?'

choices.line: Trust the pirate's shortcut. Speed is safety in the scrapyard.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus Listener training on the scavenger gangs to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.line: Stick with Brother Lirin's methodical, safer path. The song must be respected.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to tune the prosthetic, drawing on unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Chanida loses control. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.line: Split up. Send the agile Chanida with the pirate, the rest with the monk. Cover more ground.
choices.description: The pirate presses forward with pirate ship to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. A secret frequency from the underworld shifts the balance.
the pirate fails. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The sky pirate's hidden frequency leads you to a deep canyon within the scrapyard, where a half-buried Resonance Ship lies dormant. Its hull is scarred, and a faint, discordant hum emanates from its cracked crystal resonator.
There she is. The *Echo of the Lost Ship*. Been singing her sad song for decades. Remember... the old charts said she went down carrying something precious. A prototype resonator.
Precious? It looks like a heap of scrap with a bad case of tonal indigestion. I can't remember the last time I saw a resonator cracked like that. It's not natural.
So we just go in? What if it's trapped? Or haunted? Actually, haunted sounds fun.
Caution. The structural integrity is questionable. And that hum... it's not following any harmonic pattern I recognize. It feels broken.
A memory made solid. This ship didn't just crash; it was silenced. We need to understand its final song.
This is the vessel from our oldest scrolls. The one that heard the Lattice's true voice before The Silencing. I... I can't remember all the details. The Order's records are fragmented.

lines_after.dialogue: Inside the derelict, the air vibrates with trapped sound. Flickering light crystals reveal a navigator's log, its final entry frozen on a screen.
"The Lattice isn't just responding... it's remembering. And it's angry." That's the last entry.
This confirms it. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a reaction. The Tonal Orders didn't lose knowledge; they buried it.

line.dialogue: The prototype resonator in the ship's core is unstable, pulsing with the 'angry' memory of the Lattice. To access the log's encrypted data core, you must stabilize it.

choices.text: Use Chanida's tools to manually recalibrate the crystal mounts. (REQUIRES: Mechanical Tools)
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with crystal hearing to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Have Malee hack the ship's auxiliary power to feed a damping frequency. (REQUIRES: Technical Savvy)
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with resonant staff, ready to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Pichit. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit misreads the situation. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Pichit attempts to 'sing' a counter-harmony, directly interfacing with the resonator's memory. (REQUIRES: Singer Affinity)
choices.description: The pirate attempts to decode the distress signal, relying on secret frequencies

line.dialogue: the pirate's expertise pays off. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
the pirate misreads the situation. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: As the data core unlocks, the ship shudders violently. The prototype resonator flares, projecting a ghostly sound-image of the final moments before The Silencing—a wave of destructive resonance. The Sky Pirate grabs for the core.
The proof! This is worth a fortune! The Orders will pay anything to keep this buried!
No! This truth belongs to the world! It explains why the Lattice's song has been grieving! You'll just create another Silencing!
I'm just surprised you're not already running, pirate! Let it go!
He's not the one who did it, but he'll sure finish the job. The resonator's feedback loop is building. This whole canyon will be dust.
The harmonic pressure is critical! We must sever the connection or dampen the core completely. There's no time!
This is the broken memory of the world. We can't weaponize it. And we can't hide it. We have to change its song.

lines_after.dialogue: The crisis resolves, leaving the scrapyard in an eerie quiet. The ghost-ship's hum is gone, its memory finally laid to rest. The Monk and the Pirate stare at the now-inert data core, their conflict unresolved but muted.
You changed the frequency. From a scream of anger... to a sigh of remembrance. The Lattice here feels... quieter. Just relax. The immediate danger has passed.
Hmph. Well, that's that then. No payday. But... I just spoke with the Monk. Maybe there are other truths to find. Less explosive ones.
Some histories are too heavy to carry. We didn't fix what was broken. We gave it peace. That has to be enough.

line.dialogue: The destabilizing resonator core must be dealt with immediately to prevent a catastrophic chain reaction. The method will define what survives.

choices.text: Destroy the core. Erase the dangerous memory forever, saving the scrapyard but losing the truth. (CONSEQUENCE: Truth Lost)
choices.description: Snatch the scroll from the bandit's grip and bolt toward the monastery gates before anyone reacts.

line.dialogue: * "Fast hands, faster feet — that scroll never belonged in his greedy fingers anyway!
* "You think I'd let some trembling clerk rob me blind? Touch it again and you lose the hand.

choices.text: Contain the core. Seal it in a harmonic prison, neutralizing the threat but preserving it for study. (CONSEQUENCE: Truth Contained)
choices.description: Draw your blade and demand the bandit hand over the proof, warning him the Orders will kill him just to bury it.

line.dialogue: * "Now THAT'S the language he understands — nothing sharpens a thief's conscience like steel at his throat.
* "You're bluffing. You need this proof alive as much as I do — so put down the toothpick.

choices.text: Transform the core. Use the party's combined skills to rewrite its final memory from anger to acceptance. (CONSEQUENCE: Truth Redeemed)
choices.description: Side with the monk publicly — declare the truth belongs to everyone and offer to escort him to the temple printers.

line.dialogue: * "Bless you — together we'll flood every province with copies before the Orders even know what's happened!
* "Noble fool — you just painted a target on all our backs and handed the bandit a reason to slit our throats in our sleep.

lines_before.dialogue: The *Echo's Lament* hums across the Lattice, its crystalline resonator parting the shimmering surface below like water. The deck thrums with a low, resonant tone.
Ah, Pichit! Marvelous, isn't it? This resonator model... it works really well. Smooth sailing means on-time delivery, and on-time delivery means profit.
Profit, profit, profit. Can't you just enjoy the view for once? Look at those light patterns! It's like the world is singing!
Singing a song of how we're all one bad frequency away from plunging into solid crystal. Cheery.
Malee's not wrong. The Tonal Charts for this sector are... vague. We should proceed with caution.
The Lattice doesn't feel hostile. It feels... contemplative. Like it's remembering something.
A perceptive thought. The natural harmonics here are... troubled. There is a dissonance on the edge of hearing. A memory of a ship, lost long ago.
A sudden, jarring harmonic shiver runs through the deck plates. The lattice below flickers, and for a moment, the ghostly outline of a larger, broken vessel shimmers in the mist beside them.

lines_after.dialogue: Whoa! Did you see that? It was huge!
A mirage! Stress on the resonator. It still works, see? We're fine. Probably just a trick of the light.
That was no trick. Someone... or something... is really hurting out there. I felt it.

line.dialogue: The phantom ship has vanished, but the strange frequency lingers in the air. What do we do?

choices.text: Ignore it. The merchant is likely right; it's just resonator strain. Maintain course.
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing Listener training to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Ask the Listener Monk to attune to the lingering frequency and try to understand its nature.
choices.description: Arthit channels ship navigation toward the deck wind, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Arthit finds the key. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The risk doesn't pay off. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.text: Have Chanida do an impulsive, wide-frequency scan to 'shout back' at the echo.
choices.description: The monk uses prayers to listen for the ghost ship's echo near the deck wind

line.dialogue: the monk succeeds. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: The Monk, after some persuasion, sits cross-legged on the deck, his hands resting on the resonator housing. His chanting merges with the ship's hum.
The echo... it is a prayer. A looping cry for help, frozen at the moment of the Silencing. To map its source... the Tonal Orders would charge a fortune.
Of course they would. Most Thais are Buddhist, but even prayer has a price tag here. Knowledge is their product.
He's implying we could find it ourselves. But without their charts? It's rather pricey for Thais like us, risking our ship on an unknown path.
Pricey? It's financial suicide! We have a cargo of harmonic stabilizers for Skycity Niran! Diverting for a ghost story? It won't cost so much, it will cost everything!
But what if there are survivors? Or... salvage? A lost pre-Silencing ship probably won't be too expensive to explore, right? It's just sitting there!
It's not about salvage. That echo is a soul in torment. We have the chance to lay it to rest. That has a value beyond stabilizers.
The Monk opens his eyes, pale. 'I have its song. To follow it... we must deviate into a dead zone, off the sanctioned routes. The lattice there is... unstable.'

lines_after.dialogue: Unstable. Wonderful. So we can either be boring and rich, or noble and crystallized.
The merchant has a contract. We have a duty. But Pichit... you're the Singer. If anyone can navigate a dead zone...
The duty is to the living, and the dead. The path is clear, even if it's silent.

line.dialogue: The ghostly frequency pulses, a silent plea. The merchant's profit and the Monk's truth are at odds. What is our course?

choices.text: Honor the contract. Reassure the merchant and continue to Skycity Niran. The dead can wait.
choices.description: Trace the echo's source by walking the temple grounds in concentric circles, marking where the sound peaks

line.dialogue: The monk presses his palm against a cracked pillar. "Here—the vibration is strongest. Something is buried beneath us, still breathing.
The monk shakes his head, rubbing his temples. "The echo shifts every time I move. It does not want to be found this way—it is testing us.

choices.text: Attempt a compromise: Mark the echo's location precisely to sell to the Tonal Orders later, and continue our route.
choices.description: Ask Malee to translate the full prayer, capturing every dialect shift and archaic word on paper

line.dialogue: Malee reads her transcription, paling. "This isn't standard Pali. The final line—'release me from the vessel'—that's a binding seal. Someone trapped a soul here on purpose.
Malee slams the notebook shut. "I can only catch fragments. The dialect keeps changing mid-sentence, like two voices arguing inside one mouth. I need a linguist, not a tourist guide.

choices.text: Deviate immediately. Follow the Monk's guidance into the dead zone to answer the echo's call. Let profit be damned.
choices.description: Offer the merchant a deal:

line.dialogue: the merchant's expertise pays off. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
Things don't go as planned. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The night has passed. A cold, clinging mist envelops the deck, muting the ship's resonant hum. The first grey light of dawn reveals the Lattice below, its crystalline patterns shifting sluggishly.
The morning silence... it is not peaceful. It's holding its breath. Listen.
I don't hear anything. Just the wind and our engines. What about tomorrow? We can't just drift here forever.
The monk is right. Our charts are useless in this fog. The merchant's 'safe route' has led us into a dead zone. Please translate that for me—what is the Lattice actually *saying* here?
It's saying 'goodbye.' This is exactly how ships vanish. Is it real, this ghost ship story, or are we just lost?
The stories... and the silence. They're two parts of the same song. The Silencing didn't destroy all sound. It trapped some of it. What if a ship's final moments... echoed?
Philosophical speculation is cheap. Navigation is expensive. My charts are fine; your resonator is faulty. A simple mechanical issue.

A low, dissonant chord thrums through the ship's hull—a sound not from your engines. From below. The mist parts momentarily, revealing a jagged, spectral silhouette of a wreck far down in the Lattice.

line.dialogue: The ghostly outline fades, but the dissonant hum remains, vibrating in your teeth. The Listener Monk looks stricken; he hears a truth he fears.

choices.text: Order full stop. Have the Monk attune to the echo, to understand its nature.
choices.consequence: You gain clarity but lose time; the safe path closes.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to trace the anomalous signal, leveraging mechanical repair

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee loses control. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Match the dissonance. Adjust the ship's resonator to harmonize with the lost ship's final frequency.
choices.consequence: You might find a path through the echo, but risk sympathetic resonance.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with forbidden paths to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Arthit loses control. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Dive towards it. Use the echo as a beacon to navigate directly to the wreck's resting place.
choices.consequence: You confront the source directly, bypassing safety for truth.
choices.description: The monk presses forward with meditation to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: the monk succeeds. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the monk fails. The monastery's countermeasures drown them in noise.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The ship groans as its course alters, the mist swirling with new intention. The haunting tone grows clearer, weaving into the sound of your own engines.
It *is* a song. A dirge. The final log of the *Wind's Lament*. They weren't lost. They were... silenced.
Okay, no more wondering. We're in it now. Let's see what's so scary down there.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship plunges through the last veil of mist, entering a clear pocket of sky. Below, the Lattice is scarred—a frozen whirlpool of shattered crystal cradling the ghost ship's physical hull.
There's a high chance this is a monument to stupidity, and we're about to become part of it. Look at that damage. That wasn't an accident.
The fracture patterns... deliberate. Scorched by a massive, discordant burst. Do you need to use a Singer's power to cause this? Or just a weapon?
This is a salvage opportunity! Untouched for decades! The cargo alone... How could you pass up the chance?
No! This is a tomb. The song is a warning. The Tonal Orders... my order... we knew. We recorded the anomaly and called it 'natural.' We hid the truth of what they did.
They destroyed it. To protect their monopoly on charts. A ship that found a way to navigate freely... had to be erased. Its echo is the truth they couldn't silence.
So it's a murder scene. And the killers are the guys who sell us our maps. Great. What now? We take a souvenir and run?
A deep, resonant pulse erupts from the wreck. The scar in the Lattice begins to glow, reacting to your presence. The ghostly echo solidifies into a piercing, singular note—an invitation, or a trap.

line.dialogue: The crystal scar is activating, harmonizing with your ship. The true record of the Silencing is here, waiting to be heard. But the energy is unstable; witnessing it may be catastrophic.

choices.text: Record and retreat. Use the ship's resonators to capture the echo's data from a safe distance.
choices.consequence: You secure evidence, but the full truth remains buried. The Orders will discredit it.
choices.description: Press your palm against the fractured stone and hum the melody back into it.

line.dialogue: The resonance aligns — the fractures are breathing in sync with me now.
Blood — my ears are bleeding, the stone rejected the harmony entirely.

choices.text: Broadcast the truth. Amplify the wreck's final song, sending it out across the Lattice for all to hear.
choices.consequence: You expose the conspiracy instantly, but paint a target on your backs for every power in the sky.
choices.description: Signal the merchant to rig explosive charges along the scorch marks while others take cover.

line.dialogue: Clean break, beautiful — the outer shell's coming apart like a gift box!
The charges bounced back — something inside threw them out, we're exposed!

choices.text: Join the chorus. Have Pichit and the Monk sing *with* the echo, merging with it to experience the lost ship's final moments directly.
choices.consequence: You learn the complete, terrible truth. It changes you forever, and the Lattice itself may remember your voice.
choices.description: Follow the monk's warning and begin inscribing containment sigils around the structure's perimeter.

line.dialogue: The song dims where the sigils hold — the Tonal Order's wards still answer.
I misaligned the third sigil — the song is *laughing* now, it knows our names.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice resonates. Light erupts—from the scar, from your ship, from within you. For a moment, the past and present are one note.
I heard them. The last Singer. They weren't afraid. They were... free. And that was the crime.
The Lattice remembers every sound. Even the ones they try to bury. Our duty is not to study silence... but to give voice to the echoes.
The event fades. The ghost ship's echo is spent, its rest finally earned. You are left in sudden quiet, holding a truth that will save the sky cities....

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform 'Harmony's Edge' juts out over the Lattice, a precarious metal claw against the infinite crystalline plain. Below, geometric patterns shift with low, resonant hums—beautiful, and lethal to the unshielded.
Look at those light patterns! There has to be salvage down there. A crashed resonator from the last storm, maybe. This is the best way to get what we need.
The best way to get crystallized. One wrong frequency and the Lattice resonance shatters bone. I think it's alright if we just... observe from here.
Malee's right. Our ship's resonator is tuned for safe transit lanes, not surface foraging. The Tonal Orders would fine us into oblivion.
Yet the Lattice sings its own song beneath the Orders' prescribed frequencies. To hear it... that is true navigation.
Ah, the adventurous types! A profitable mindset. My associates mentioned an... unattended cargo pod, just a short harmonic skip west. Its frequency signature is... open. For those who love adventure.

lines_after.dialogue: An open frequency? That's pirate bait or a trap.
Or opportunity. The pod's resonator is said to contain raw cartographic data. Uncharted harmonics. Now I know why I approached you.
You 'now know' we're stupid enough to go. I thought it was okay to just trade for supplies, not become your disposable scouts.

line.dialogue: The merchant's offer hangs in the air, alongside the dangerous hum of the Lattice.

choices.line: Refuse the merchant. Chart a known, safe path back to the city.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use resonant staff and follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Pichit overreaches. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Haggle for better terms—more upfront payment, less risk.
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with lattice storms, ready to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The gamble fails. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.line: Agree to scout the pod. The potential map data is too valuable.
choices.description: Have the merchant risk using negotiation to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the merchant pulls it off. The negotiator uncovers a deal no one else could make.
the merchant misreads the situation. A rival merchant sabotages the plan.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends a shielded cable lift to the Lattice surface. The crystal hum is a physical vibration in the chest. Light refracts into impossible colors underfoot.
Resonator readings are stable... for now. Stick to the merchant's coordinates. No, no. You don't need to wander off, Chanida.
I'm just looking! This crystal formation... it's pulsing. Almost like a heartbeat.
The Listeners teach that the Lattice has rhythms, not just routes. To navigate, you need to love yourself enough to listen, not just command.
Great. So the ground is alive and we're walking on it. For the adventurous, I guess. There's the pod.
A battered cargo pod sits half-embedded in crystal, its resonator array dark. Scorch marks suggest violent detachment.
Well, well. Lost little lambs find the wrong shepherd's flock.

lines_after.dialogue: The map data in that box is ours. Sky's free for the taking, and that means taking. You have to love yourself enough to walk away.
Or love adventure enough to fight for it!
He's not alone. I count two more resonators closing in from the refracted light zones. Hardpoints.

line.dialogue: The sky pirates fan out, their personal resonators whining to life, preparing to cut you off.

choices.line: Retreat. Use the chaotic crystal reflections to hide and return to the lift.
choices.description: Channel your resonance into the pulsing crystal formation to match its rhythm, 12 words

line.dialogue: You found its heartbeat — the Lattice recognizes you as a listener now, not an intruder.
You forced it! The crystal just cracked and now the whole formation is screaming at us!

choices.line: Negotiate. Offer a split of the data, hoping their greed overrides aggression.
choices.description: Grab chanida's wrist before she touches the glowing seam running through the cavern wall

line.dialogue: Good catch — that seam just spiked three seconds before you pulled her back. She would've lost fingers.
You hesitated too long and she already touched it. Now her hand is glowing and I REALLY want to leave.

choices.line: Stand your ground. Prepare to fight on the unstable, resonant surface.
choices.description: Drop flat against the ground and press your ear to the stone to hear what the Lattice is saying

line.dialogue: You hear it too — the old rhythm, the one before the miners came. It's grieving, not angry. Not yet.
Great, now you're lying face-down on the breathing floor and I have to pretend that's normal. Get UP.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform groans as it descends toward the Lattice surface, the crystalline expanse shimmering with dangerous beauty. The air hums with unstable frequencies.
That Sky Pirate band is moving in. They mean means it! They'll strip this site clean and leave us with nothing.
We can take them! They're just scavengers with loud mouths.
They have resonance disruptors. One wrong note and this entire platform becomes a memory. I think it's alright to be cautious for once.
The Tonal Orders would have protocols for this. But we're not them. We need a plan.
The Lattice responds to intention as much as frequency. If we project calm...
HEY! This is our claim! The Open Frequency Map says this sector's rich with unharvested crystal!
Now I know... you've been tracking our movements. A friend introduced us to this site, but you've been following the resonance trail.

lines_after.dialogue: The Sky Pirates' ship hovers menacingly, its resonance cannons humming with destructive potential. The Lattice beneath your feet begins to vibrate in response to the tension.
So much for peaceful negotiation. It's over for diplomacy.
The frequencies are destabilizing. We have minutes before this entire area becomes a harmonic dead zone.

line.dialogue: How do we resolve this without getting crystallized?

choices.text: Offer to split the salvage. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Reroute harmonic shielding to deflect the disruptors before they lock on.

line.dialogue: Shields holding — their disruptors are scattering harmlessly off the harmonic lattice!
The lattice is cracking! They're cycling frequencies faster than I can compensate!

choices.text: Challenge their leader to a resonance duel. (Bravado)
choices.description: Signal Chanida to flank the pirates' airship while its bay doors are still open.

line.dialogue: I'm inside their cargo hold — these idiots left their resonance core completely unguarded!
They knew we were coming — blast doors sealed and I'm pinned behind their stern cannons!

choices.text: Use the Open Frequency Map to find an unstable harmonic and threaten mutual destruction. (Bluff)
choices.description: Invoke Tonal Order emergency protocols to broadcast a frequency-surrender demand.

line.dialogue: The Order's cipher worked — their navigator is standing down, hands off the resonance controls.
They're not Order-affiliated. My broadcast just painted a target on every harmonic instrument we carry.

lines_before.dialogue: The Lattice surface glows with frantic energy, crystalline structures rising and falling like a panicked heartbeat. The air crackles with competing frequencies.
You're crazy! Triggering that harmonic will shatter everything for kilometers!
I knew right away that you pirates were all bluster. Standing right in front of annihilation tends to clarify things.
My ship! My cargo! Please, is everything under control? We can still make a deal!
The map shows a stabilization frequency. But someone needs to Sing it from the epicenter. Standing in front of that much raw resonance...
It would require perfect harmony between intention and vibration. One misstep...
The Lattice isn't just reacting to sound. It's reacting to our conflict. Our fear. I need to go down there.
Wait! I... I have family on the floating cities too. If this goes wrong...

lines_after.dialogue: As Pichit descends to the glowing epicenter, the crystalline formations begin to still, responding to a pure, unwavering tone that seems to come from everywhere and nowhere.
Look at the patterns... they're aligning. He's actually doing it.
The pirate ship is powering down their weapons. I think... I think it's working.

The Lattice settles into a gentle, sustained hum. For the first time in living memory, the surface isn't just safe—it's beautiful. The Open Frequency Map in your hands updates with the new stable harmonics.

line.dialogue: The stabilized Lattice reveals something ancient beneath the crystals. What do we prioritize?

choices.text: Secure the new harmonics for the public good. (Altruism)
choices.description: Race to the harmonic resonator and manually calibrate the stabilization frequency before it overloads, 15 words

line.dialogue: My fingers are bleeding but I've locked the frequency — the harmonic is stabilizing, we're going to hold!
The dials are spinning too fast, I can't read the values in time — the resonator is pulling itself apart!

choices.text: Form an alliance with the pirates to explore together. (Cooperation)
choices.description: Order the bandit to reroute power from the cargo bay to reinforce the stabilization field, 15 words

line.dialogue: See that, you coward? Even the bandit has more spine than you pirates — the field is holding steady now.
I told you this was suicide! The power surge blew the relay — we've got nothing between us and that harmonic now!

choices.text: Descend immediately—the Silencing's truth might be down there. (Discovery)
choices.description: Shield the merchant's vessel by positioning

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
The gamble fails. The disruptor backfires, jamming itself.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship *Vagrant's Echo* cuts through the shimmering Lattice below, its crystalline hum vibrating through the deck timbers. Wind carries the distant, mournful song of the world-shell.
I can't stop thinking about it, Pichit. That ghost frequency the Listeners reported. A whole ship, just... gone. Its echo still singing.
An echo without a source is a memory the world refuses to release. What does it remember, I wonder?
A dangerous memory, then. We should conserve our resonator energy. The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for new frequency charts if we drift off-course.
Oh, turn off the lights to conserve energy, Arthit. You sound like my landlord. They sell the new resonator crystals at the Sky Bazaar for half the price, you know.
Forget the bazaar! That lost ship, the *Silent Grace*... its last known heading is near our route. We have to look.
The unknown calls. But Arthit is not wrong. We must balance curiosity with caution.
A Listener Monk, robes flapping, approaches along the rail, his face etched with conflict.

lines_after.dialogue: Blessings upon your journey. I... I overheard. You seek the *Silent Grace*.
We are considering it. Do your Order's archives say what happened?
Officially? Navigation error. But its echo... it doesn't sound lost. It sounds *trapped*. Like it's trying to turn off the lights, but can't.
How poetic. And what do you want us to do about it?

line.dialogue: The monk hesitates, then speaks in a hushed tone.

choices.text: "Follow the echo. I will give you the last coordinates." (Accept the coordinates.)
choices.description: Tune your resonance crystal to the ghost frequency and listen alone, eyes closed, breath held.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the static — I hear breathing, and it knows my name.
Nothing but white noise screaming back. Whatever it was, it's gone now, or it's hiding from me.

choices.text: "What aren't the Tonal Orders telling you?" (Press him for the hidden truth.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to map the echo's decay pattern against the old starlight charts.

line.dialogue: The resonance signature matches the Waning Colonies' distress beacon — lost sixty years ago.
The charts are corrupted. Whatever signal touched them burned the data like acid through paper.

choices.text: "This sounds like Order business. We'll stick to our route." (Decline and continue on.)
choices.description: Cut the lights entirely and let the crystal wind carry the ghost frequency raw through the chamber.

line.dialogue: Oh. Oh, I see it now — there are shapes moving in the crystal, and they're reaching toward us.
The crystal cracked. We've lost our resonance anchor, and something on the other side just noticed the silence.

lines_before.dialogue: Having accepted the coordinates, the *Vagrant's Echo* alters its harmonic course. The Lattice below churns, forming strange, frozen wave patterns.
Resonance readings are unstable. This area... it's acoustically dead. The Lattice's song here is just a faint whisper.
There! On the starboard horizon! I knew right away that shimmer wasn't natural light.
A ghostly outline of a massive Resonance Ship hangs in the sky, translucent and flickering. The spectral hull of the *Silent Grace* is standing right in front of them.
Well. That's not ominous at all. Its resonance signature... it's right here, but our instruments say there's nothing.
A memory given form. A scar in the air. Can you hear it? Not a song... a plea.
It's hailing us on an old frequency channel. Audio only. Static, and... voices?
A Skycity Resident, a passenger hired for her local knowledge, clutches the rail, her face pale.

lines_after.dialogue: My uncle was on a run near here. He said... he said sometimes the lost sing to be found. But that thing standing in front of us? That's not a ship. It's a tomb.
The spectral field is interfering with our primary resonator. We can't maintain this position for long.
The plea... it's a loop. A moment of terror, repeated. They saw something. Something that shouldn't be.
The answer is in the echo. But to listen is to step into its memory.

line.dialogue: The ghost-ship's signal strengthens, washing over the deck. A distorted voice breaks through: '...don't let it... see...'

choices.text: "Tune our resonator to match its frequency." (Attempt to sync with the echo, to understand it.)
choices.description: Anchor the vessel and deploy resonance dampeners before the waveform reaches critical amplitude.

line.dialogue: Dampeners holding — the frequency is folding in on itself, but we're stable.
The dampeners shattered like glass — whatever this is, it doesn't want to be contained.

choices.text: "Hail it directly. Identify ourselves." (Make contact, despite the risk.)
choices.description: Open a direct channel and broadcast pichit's voice toward the anomaly as a sympathetic harmonic.

line.dialogue: It heard me. The scar is... answering. These are voices I recognize.
Silence. Worse than silence — it swallowed the transmission whole and stared back.

choices.text: "Prepare a boarding line. We're going over." (Risk a physical approach to the spectral hull.)
choices.description: Order chanida to chart an evasive trajectory and burn hard to port immediately.

line.dialogue: Coming about — engines screaming, but we're clearing the resonance wall.
The helm won't answer — it's like the ship forgot which direction port even is.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship drifts through a dead zone of the Lattice. The usual hum has faded to a low, mournful thrum. The air is still and heavy.
Ugh, we've been sitting here for an hour! What size do you wear, Arthit? I'm so bored I might start measuring everyone's robes.
This is not a tailor's shop, Chanida. The silence is... tactical. Our charts are useless here. We must wait for the Lattice's pattern to reassert itself.
Most Thais are Buddhist, but right now I'm praying to any god that will get this rustbucket moving. We were so bored waiting for the last skycity's customs inspection.
This boredom... it's a canvas. In the absence of noise, you can hear other things. Listen. Below the engine's idle... a faint pulse. Like a memory of sound.

The Listener texts speak of such places. Where the great song was... severed. The echo of the lost ship, the *Aeolian Dirge*, is said to linger here. I was so bored in my cell until I read those forbidden passages.
Don't like this. Not one bit. The Tonal Orders say to avoid these silences. Bad for trade. Bad for the nerves. Just want to get home.
A sudden, dissonant chord shivers through the ship's crystals. The Lattice below flickers with a sickly, pale light. A ghostly silhouette of a larger vessel begins to coalesce in the mist ahead.

lines_after.dialogue: Well, I'm not bored anymore! Is that... it?
Spectral resonance. A memory trapped in the crystal. The *Dirge*.
It's calling. A song of loss. We must... we must answer.
The phantom ship's outline solidifies, its rigging singing a tune of shattered glass and weeping stone. A boarding ramp of solidified sound extends toward your deck.

line.dialogue: The ghost ship's song is an open door. Do we cross?

choices.text: Send a probe first. Use a resonator to test the ramp's stability.
choices.consequence: The probe confirms the path is physically solid but psychically charged. Safe, but forewarned.
choices.description: Search behind the reception desk for hidden files or a service bell.

line.dialogue: Arthit slides a manila folder from under the desk—inside, a schedule with today's date circled in red ink.
Arthit knocks over a stack of forms and a security guard clears his throat loudly from the corner.

choices.text: Have the Listener Monk lead. His knowledge of sacred tones might protect us.
choices.consequence: The monk's chant creates a fragile harmony, but the ghost-song fights his control. Risky passage.
choices.description: Strike up conversation with the old woman dozing by the window.

line.dialogue: Malee gently touches her shoulder; the woman whispers that appointments mean nothing here—only patience opens doors.
Malee startles her awake; she shrieks and every pair of eyes in the room turns to judge them.

choices.text: Pichit steps forward. Listen to the song, find the true note within the discord, and Sing a path.
choices.consequence: Pichit's raw, untrained gift risks being overwhelmed by the Dirge's anguish, but success could reveal its core truth.
choices.description: Pichit sketches the room from memory, capturing details others missed.

line.dialogue: Pichit notices the ventilation grate behind the counter is loose—recently unscrewed—and the silence feels suddenly intentional.
Pichit drops his pencil; it rolls under the desk and a clerk snaps, "No loitering behind the counter!

lines_before.dialogue: You stand on the deck of the *Aeolian Dirge*. It is not wood and rope, but crystallized anguish. Every surface hums with the final moments of its crew. Shadows move in the corners of vision.
Don't let them see you! The shadows—they're not just echoes. They're reactive. They feed on attention.
Wonderful. A ship full of judgmental ghosts. Don't judge others, they said. Too late for that.
We shouldn't be here! Don't let anyone know we came! The Orders will strip our licenses!
Their fear is the song. It wasn't the Lattice that killed them. It was a command. A forced resonance, shattering their crystals from within. I can feel it.
The forbidden truth... The Tonal Orders. They didn't just lose the *Dirge*. They scuttled it. To hide a route. To maintain control. This ship is a tomb for knowledge.
So we find what they hid and get out before this floating trauma collapses! The captain's log must be here!

The central resonator, a massive fractured crystal, glows in the ship's heart. Within it, a shadowy figure—the captain's final imprint—holds a scroll of pure tone. The surrounding shadows converge, their whispering rising to a deafening scream.

lines_after.dialogue: The spectral captain turns, its face a ripple of shattered song. It extends the scroll. To take it is to accept the memory—and the blame.
The ship is destabilizing! The resonance is linking to our own vessel!
Of course. Nothing is ever free.
The truth has a weight. We can carry it, or let it sink with the ghosts.

line.dialogue: The core truth of the Silencing is within reach, but the ghost-ship is unraveling. How do we seize it?

choices.text: Create a dissonant feedback loop. Shatter the central crystal to free the scroll, but destroy the memory forever.
choices.consequence: You escape with the physical scroll, but its deeper song—the crew's voices—is lost. Proof, but no context.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using unauthorized tones to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Chanida fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Harmonize with the captain's echo. Absorb the memory into our ship's resonator, carrying the ghost-song with us.
choices.consequence: You gain the complete truth, but the *Dirge*'s anguish now haunts your own vessel, a permanent psychic passenger.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use captain experience and calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit fails. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.text: Pichit must Sing a new ending. Rewrite the Dirge's final note from one of betrayal to one of release, freeing the ghosts.
choices.consequence: If successful, the truth is revealed and the ship finds peace, scattering as harmonic dust. If Pichit fails, the unresolved song could consume you all.
choices.description: Direct the villager to record the spectral signature using terraces
