line.dialogue: the villager succeeds. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
The risk doesn't pay off. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans like a dying beast. Pichit and his crew pick their way through canyons of shattered crystal resonators and hull plates, the air thick with the smell of ozone and rust.
A monument to failure. What do they call this? The 'industrial edge'? It's the city's garbage heap. We're literally walking through its mistakes.
Careful. Unstable ground. The Lattice here is thin under all this metal. One wrong step...
Oh, relax! Look at all this! They have a lot of stuff! Think of the salvage! Anyone's okay to deal with here, right? Let's just find a contact.
The silence between the clangs... that's what we should listen for. The Lattice remembers every ship that broke here. Its grief hums just below the noise.
You shouldn't linger. Bad acoustics. Draws... unwanted echoes. The Groundless say the Lattice is angry here. I'm just here for copper wiring.
The Groundless. Great. So we have fanatics and faulty physics to worry about. Perfect.

lines_after.dialogue: That villager was terrified. The 'unwanted echoes'... could be resonance ghosts from the wrecks.
Or could be a great bargain! I saw a nearly intact harmonic coupler back there! Keep it. You should keep that thought, Arthit, but I'm keeping my eyes on the prize.
We seek knowledge, not just parts. The price for either might be higher than copper.

line.dialogue: A figure emerges from behind a gutted resonance ship, wiping greasy hands on a rag. It's a Trade Negotiator, his smile not quite reaching his eyes.

choices.line: Greet him openly and ask about ship parts. (Direct Approach)
choices.description: Sift through the collapsed shelving where canned provisions spilled decades ago, checking seals, 15 words

line.dialogue: Score! Still vacuum-sealed—whatever civilization collapsed here, they knew their preservation tech.
Don't—those containers are bulging. Botulism doesn't care how hungry you are.

choices.line: Mention the 'unwanted echoes' the villager spoke of. (Inquisitive Approach)
choices.description: Press palm flat against the fractured Lattice surface and listen for residual data echoes beneath, 15 words

line.dialogue: There—voices, hundreds of them, compressed into the substrate like insects in amber. I can almost—
Nothing. Just the hum of dead infrastructure pretending it still matters. Typical.

choices.line: Let Chanida do the talking, focusing on salvage. (Delegating Approach)
choices.description: Anchor a rope to the rusted overhead beam and rappel down into the collapsed lower level, 15 words

line.dialogue: Beam holds. Good
the villager loses control. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: Ah, travelers! The acoustics guide you well. You seek parts? Charts? Perhaps... less official knowledge? My specialty.
Now this is a lot more fun than talking to scared villagers! What have you got? He must have a lot of things!
He has a lot of things he's not telling us. That smile costs extra.
We need a calibrated frequency crystal. Our resonator is... unstable. My captain, he used to be a sickly child when it came to rough resonance fields. The ship inherited it.

A chronic condition! I have just the tonic. A crystal, salvaged from a Listener's vessel. Untouched by the Tonal Orders' grubby charts. But such things... attract attention. The Groundless whisper about 'returning' such items.
Everything has a resonance. Even movements. What do the Groundless want with a crystal?
To break it, of course! To silence the 'unnatural' tones. They think if we stop poking the Lattice, it will heal. Naïve. But bad for business.

lines_after.dialogue: So we're caught between a monopoly that overcharges and a cult that smashes what we need. Charming.
But he has the crystal! And they sell a lot of things! We just need to get it. How hard can it be?
Exceedingly. If the Groundless are active here, the scrapyard is their sanctuary. All this metal disrupts official surveillance.
The merchant sells more than things. He sells conflict. We must choose which resonance to amplify—commerce, or conviction.

line.dialogue: The merchant names his price for the crystal: not just coin, but retrieving a 'lost ledger' from a nearby wreck—a list of his 'clients'. The Groundless are known to patrol that sector.

choices.line: Pay the coin price outright, avoiding the wreck and the Groundless. (Costly Safety)
choices.description: Lean across the counter and study the merchant's ledger while he talks, looking for hidden inventory codes.

line.dialogue: There — page four, circled in red ink. That's a military calibration serial. You *do* have one, don't you?
He snapped the book shut before I could read a single number. That man moves faster than he looks.

choices.line: Agree to get the ledger, sneaking into the wreck quietly. (Clandestine Retrieval)
choices.description: Mention the Harmonic Accord by name and watch his reaction for recognition or fear.

line.dialogue: His left eye twitched at the name. He knows exactly who we're working with — and he's scared.
Nothing. Not a flinch, not a blink. Either he's never heard of them or he's the best liar in this market.

choices.line: Refuse his deal and seek out the Groundless directly to understand their side. (Confrontational Inquiry)
choices.description: Slide three silver thalers across the counter as a 'consultation fee' before asking about the crystal.

line.dialogue: The coins vanished before they stopped spinning. He leaned in close and whispered a warehouse address — *that's* how business works.
He pocketed the silver without breaking eye contact, then said 'consultations are free' with that same rotten smile. We just bought nothing.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before the wreck of the 'Harmonic Drift,' its resonator array partially disassembled. The scrapyard's industrial din creates a wall of chaotic sound.
They have a lot of stuff! Look at this crystal housing—it's intact! We can use this.
Intact, but tuned to a dead ship's signature. What do you think about recalibrating it without the Tonal Orders noticing?
I think that's right. The Groundless contact said the resonator frequency is the key. But if we're wrong...
Every broken thing here once sang. Now it just echoes. What do you think about giving it a new song?
You shouldn't be here. The foreman's only interested in scrap quotas. If he sees you tinkering...
Ah! My entrepreneurial friends. I hear you're looking for... unconventional navigation solutions. The Groundless have interesting theories.
Theories don't part the Lattice. Hardware does. And your smile is hiding the price.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision made, the scrapyard seems to hold its breath. Distant cranes freeze mid-swing as if listening.
The resonance is stabilizing. I think that's the one. The frequency matches the old Listeners' records.
Not a charted path. A remembered one. The Lattice knows this song.

line.dialogue: The makeshift resonator hums with unstable energy. The merchant offers a 'stabilizer' at a cost, the villager warns of patrols approaching, and the ship's crystal core glows with potential.

choices.text: Pay the merchant for the stabilizer. Secure the path but owe a debt.
choices.consequences: Immediate success, but the Groundless now have leverage over the party.
choices.description: Tap the crystal housing with your multi-tool and listen for residual harmonics through your helmet's audio feed.

line.dialogue: There—under the static—something's still breathing in there, faint but steady, like a heartbeat refusing to stop.
Nothing but feedback whine. Whatever lived in this crystal died cold and quiet a long time ago.

choices.text: Improvise with scrapyard parts. Risky but debt-free.
choices.consequences: Chance of failure or discovery, but maintain independence.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to hum the old salvage workers' dirge—the one they say dead ships still recognize.

line.dialogue: I barely remember the words, but the crystal just pulsed when I hit that low note. It knows this song.
I hummed it wrong. The crystal went dark, like I insulted whatever's left inside. I'm sorry—I should have kept quiet.

choices.text: Have Pichit attempt to 'sing' the crystal calm. Unpredictable, purely intuitive.
choices.consequences: Either a profound connection to the Lattice or catastrophic feedback.
choices.description: Check the Groundless contact's coordinates against the hull fragment's serial etching to confirm this is the right wreckage.

line.dialogue: Serial matches to the seventh digit. This is the Reverb's wreckage, exactly where they said it crashed. We're in the right scrap pile.
The etching's too corroded—half the serial's gone. Could be the Reverb, could be any of a dozen ships that went down in this sector.

lines_before.dialogue: The reactivated resonator casts jagged light across the metal graveyard. A deep, resonant hum fights against the scrapyard's clangor.
Magnificent! They have a lot of things, these old ships. Forgotten things. What do your parents do, Pichit? Mine traded in... quiet acquisitions.
They listened. Like the Groundless want to. Not to control, but to understand.
The patrol ships! They're vectoring in! The whole scrapyard's lighting up!
Of course. The merchant sold us out. The Tonal Orders pay better than dreamers.
The frequency is opening a path below, but it's unstable. We need to channel more power or shut it down before it collapses.
You'll get us all Silenced! They have a lot of stuff—guns, ships, authority!
Searchlights cut through the smoky air. The resonator's hum becomes a scream, vibrating the very plates beneath your feet. The path through the Lattice flickers like a mirage.

lines_after.dialogue: In the sudden quiet, the scrapyard is transformed. a tomb of failed ambition.
Every choice echoes. Even here, in the place where echoes come to die.
The fate of the Groundless Movement, the stolen knowledge, and the party's future now hangs on the resonance of this moment.

line.dialogue: The Tonal Orders' ships descend, weapons charging. The unstable path through the Lattice beckons below—a gamble into the unknown. The scrapyard itself seems poised to either amplify or shatter the final note.

choices.text: Overload the resonator to destroy the evidence and scatter into the scrapyard's chaos.
choices.consequences: Mission fails, Groundless plot is buried, but the party escapes to fight another day. The secret is preserved at great cost.
choices.description: Reroute power from the scrapyard's magnetic cranes to blind the patrol sensors, 15 words exactly here now

line.dialogue: [Pichit grips the console. "The old ships still sing — I just needed to give them a louder voice."]
[Chanida watches the sensors bloom red. "They cut through it. The scrapyard's dead metal can't scream loud enough."]

choices.text: Make a run for the unstable path. A desperate flight into the uncharted Lattice.
choices.consequences: Potential escape with the knowledge, but risk being lost forever or triggering another local Silencing.
choices.description: Detonate the merchant's cargo charges along the debris corridor to wall off the incoming patrol

line.dialogue: [Malee pulls the trigger without flinching. "You sold us out AND gave us the fireworks. Thanks for that."]
[The merchant's voice crackles through static. "Those charges were display models. You really thought I'd sell you live ones?"]

choices.text: Broadcast the resonant frequency openly. Let the whole city hear the forbidden song.
choices.consequences: The truth cannot be silenced. The Groundless' cause becomes public, forcing a confrontation. The party becomes either heroes or the most wanted people in the sky.
choices.description: Squeeze the Rust Choir through the collapsing hull of a derelict freighter to reach the blind spot

line.dialogue: [Chanida banks hard into the corpse of the old vessel. "The Tonal Orders map what they can hear — they never learned to listen to silence."]
[Pichit winces as the hull groans and the freighter shifts. "The dead ship moved. Even the scrap wants to stop us now."]

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim are a sanctuary of green and gold. Terraces of swaying grain and whispering vegetables step down into the mist below. The air hums with the quiet rhythm of wind chimes and irrigation streams, a peaceful counterpoint to the silent, shimmering Lattice far beneath the floating city's edge.
Finally! A place to breathe that isn't the inside of a dusty resonator chamber. Look at this view! I could just... float away.
Don't get too poetic. That 'view' is a thousand-foot drop onto a crystal death field. Pretty, but deadly. Like a bad relationship.
The soil seems stable, and the water flow is well-maintained. A defensible position, if needed. We should rest while we can.
There's a harmony here... not just in the crops, but in the air itself. The Lattice's distant song feels different. Softer. Almost... mournful.

You're the newcomers, eh? Best keep to the paths. Some of the outer terraces aren't as firm as they look. My girlfriend gets jealous if I spend too long out here staring at the void, anyway. Says I'm dreaming of falling.
Does she have a boyfriend who's a Tonal Order navigator? Someone with a map of this 'void'?
What size do you wear? That's a strange question. No, we're simple folk. We trust the Orders to keep us floating. Don't ask about the song beneath. That's Listener business.

lines_after.dialogue: Simple folk with simple fears. They're scared of what they don't understand, so they pay the guilds to understand it for them.
A practical, if expensive, arrangement. It maintains order.
At what cost? To never truly listen for yourself...

line.dialogue: The villager points toward a secluded meditation alcove built into the rock face, where a lone figure in grey robes sits motionless.

choices.text: Approach the Listener Monk directly and respectfully.
choices.description: Examine the irrigation channels for signs of who maintains this farmland.

line.dialogue: Arthit crouches by the water gate, tracing the mortar joints. "These repairs are less than a season old. Someone is still working this land.
Arthit kneels too close to the channel edge and the mud gives way, soaking his boots. "Well. The water flows *into* my shoes now. Very well-maintained indeed.

choices.text: Observe the monk from a distance, trying to hear what he hears first.
choices.description: Climb the ridge to scout the surrounding terrain before proceeding further.

line.dialogue: Malee reaches the crest first, scanning the valley below. "Road to the east, smoke to the south, and that drop we survived looks even worse from up here. We go east.
Malee loses her footing on loose gravel and slides back down, scraping her palms raw. "Every time I try to be the competent one. *Every* time.

choices.text: Ask the villager more about the Listeners and their 'business.'
choices.description: Pick a handful of the ripening rice to test whether it's safe to eat.

line.dialogue: Pichit rolls a grain between his fingers, then bites into it cautiously. "No bitterness, no burning on the tongue. It's clean. Someone grows this for human mouths.
Pichit chews too eagerly and immediately gags — the husks are coated in a pest deterrent that numbs his tongue.

lines_before.dialogue: The meditation alcove is carved from the same warm stone as the terraces. The Listener Monk, an older man with a weathered face, doesn't open his eyes as you approach. His focus is downward, towards the Lattice. The peaceful garden sounds seem to recede here, replaced by a deep, almost sub-audible thrum.
You disrupt the harmonics. Your steps... your breath... they are clumsy notes in a delicate aria.
Forgive us. We mean no discord. We only wish to understand the song we feel here. It's different.
Different. Yes. A slowing tempo. A... stutter in the deep resonance. I have charted its progression. Did it all myself. The Tonal Orders would call it heresy.
What did you say? A stutter? You mean the Lattice itself is... faulty?
This is dangerous knowledge. If the foundation of our world is changing...

It is not 'faulty.' It is warning. The Silencing was not an end, but a pause. The song is trying to resume, but something... *man-made*... is blocking it. Drowning the true frequency with artificial ones.
The Resonance Ships! Their crystal drivers! When did he get here? I mean, when did this interference start?

lines_after.dialogue: It has grown steadily since the Orders expanded their fleet. They navigate by forcing the Lattice to sing *their* tune, not by listening to its own. They are making the world deaf.
And you, who can hear the truth... what will you do?
My duty is to observe. To record. But my conscience... it screams to act. I am torn.

line.dialogue: The monk finally opens his eyes, filled with a quiet desperation. He gestures to a small, locked journal beside him.

choices.text: Offer to carry his warning to someone who can help, outside the Orders' influence.
choices.description: Chanida steps forward with crystal hearing, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
The resonance turns hostile. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Convince him to share his data now, to let the party analyze the 'stutter' themselves.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to harness harmonic feedback, leveraging engineering

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
A costly mistake by Malee. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Urge him to take immediate, public action, to sound the alarm himself regardless of the consequences.
choices.description: The monk attempts to follow the phantom route, relying on lattice study

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The resonance turns hostile. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: In a secluded corner of the Hanging Gardens, the Listener Monk waits by a small, silent pool reflecting the sky. The party approaches, the tension from their earlier discoveries palpable in the quiet air.
You came. Good. The Tonal Orders have ears everywhere, but the water's song here... it confuses them. It doesn't follow their charts.
You said the Lattice is trying to tell us something. That the pain is gone, but the memory remains. What did it show you?
Not a chart. A warning. A pattern of fracture. The Silencing... we were told it was an accident. A natural resonance collapse. I don't have many friends left who believe that.
So the big guilds are lying? What, they caused the whole thing?

Of course they did. The past is over, so let it go—that's what they want us to think. Convenient, isn't it? They control all navigation because they 'saved' us from the disaster they probably created.
This is... dangerous speculation. We have no proof. Only the word of one monk against the most powerful institution in the sky.
Proof is in the song. I can show you. But you must listen. Truly listen. The Lattice doesn't lie. It sings of a wound that never healed.

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk places his hands on the ground. The crystalline Lattice far below glimmers, and a low, sorrowful hum vibrates through the terraces, felt in the bones more than heard.
It's... a dirge. Not a navigation tone. A memory of breaking.
In the distance, the rhythmic sounds of the wind through the crops falter, replaced by an unnatural, searching silence.

line.dialogue: The Monk says he can attune a crystal to record this 'Warning Song,' but it will draw attention. Do we...

choices.text: Record it quickly and hide. (Use Chanida's speed to grab the resonance and run.)
choices.description: Grab the monk's shoulder, demand proof of the guilds' involvement before trusting him. — 15 words

line.dialogue: Show me the fracture pattern. If the guilds did this, I need to see it with my own eyes before I risk everything on your word.
Your hands are shaking, monk. You're frightened of something worse than the guilds — and that makes me frightened of you.

choices.text: Attempt to mask the recording. (Use Malee's knowledge of sonic interference to cloak the process.)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to stay quiet and let the monk explain what the Silence actually does. — 15 words

line.dialogue: Fine. But if he starts speaking in riddles again, I'm walking out that door and you can follow or not.
No — I'm done being quiet while old men in robes tell me what to think. Answer me straight: did they cause it?

choices.text: Let the song resonate fully. (Let Pichit and the Monk draw out the pure tone, accepting the risk.)
choices.description: Touch the Lattice pattern yourself, feel the fracture before deciding who to believe. — 15 words

line.dialogue: I can feel it — cold, then nothing, then cold again. Like a heartbeat skipping. The Silence is eating the gaps between notes.
I touched it and heard nothing. Not silence — *nothing*. Like the sound itself was never born. My fingers still ache with it.

lines_before.dialogue: The recording—or the attempt—has been made. The unnatural silence shatters as a Resonance Ship, marked with the sigil of the Tonal Orders, glides into view above the terraces. Villagers scatter.
Orders' enforcers! What did you do? This is a peaceful place! Mae Rim's a great place to live! You've ruined it!
We didn't ruin anything! They're the ones who—
Save it. They won't listen. Fear is the latest fashion here, and it's always in season.
A figure in sleek guild robes descends from the ship. The Monk shrinks back, but Pichit steps forward.
Pichit, be careful. This isn't a skirmish. This is the province of power.
I know. And we're standing in the province of truth. What province do the Tonal Orders rule with their lies?
You possess illicit resonance recordings. You consort with heretics who spread discord. The Lattice's song is for navigation, not... sedition. Surrender the crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation hangs in the air. The Enforcer's hand rests on a resonator that could shatter the peace of the gardens—or worse. The Monk looks at Pichit, awaiting the signal. The recorded Warning Song pulses faintly in someone's pack.
Well, philosopher? This is your climax. Do we fight, flee, or talk our way into a guild cell?
The wind returns, whistling through the crops, carrying with it the faint, undeniable echo of the Lattice's ancient grief.

line.dialogue: The Guild Enforcer demands the evidence. The truth of the Silencing is within reach, but so is reprisal. We must choose our resonance.

choices.text: Fight to protect the Monk and the proof. (Use the terrain and party skills to drive the Enforcer back.)
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using forbidden paths to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The resonance turns hostile. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Deceive and redirect. (Use the recording as a sonic weapon to confuse and escape with the Monk.)
choices.description: Malee attempts to tune the prosthetic, relying on leg resonance

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Malee hits a wall. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: Confront with the song. (Broadcast the Warning Song publicly, letting every villager hear the Lattice's truth and forcing the Guild's hand.)
choices.description: The villager steps forward with terraces, ready to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the villager overreaches. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire pierces the Lattice below your floating city, a colossal needle of resonant crystal. Its deep, steady hum vibrates through the metal gangway under your boots, a tone so profound it seems to still the very anxiety in your chest.
Wow. They have a lot of stuff! Look at all these maintenance rigs and resonator coils. It's a lot more fun up here than down in the dusty archives.
Fun? This is a critical structural node. One miscalculation and the entire city's drift stability...
He complains a lot! Can we focus? We're here because the Tonal Orders are charging double for passage charts this week. Something's spooked them.
The hum... it's not just stability. It's a question. What is the Anchor answering?

You the ones asking about the old ghost ship? The *Echo*? Bad business. Tonal Orders sealed the records. My cousin in maintenance... he hears things down in the lower spires. Whispers in the vibration.
Whispers? Like a sub-harmonic? See, Arthit? Exploration!
A Listener Monk approaches, his grey robes fluttering in the constant, gentle wind of the Spire's emission. His eyes are fixed on the crystalline depths below.

lines_after.dialogue: The Anchor's song is pure. Ordered. Yet... there is a dissonance. A memory in the lattice. The *Echo of the Lost Ship*... its final resonance was absorbed here. It is not gone.
Great. So we're not just dodging the Orders, we're investigating a haunted vibration. Pragmatic.
A memory in the crystal... If we can listen to it, truly listen, we might learn what the Orders are hiding.

line.dialogue: The Monk indicates a service lift descending the Spire's exterior. 'The memory is strongest where the Anchor meets the Lattice's surface.'

choices.line: Take the main lift. It's slower but safer and monitored.
choices.description: Touch the humming relay coil bare-handed and let the resonance flow through you, 15 words

line.dialogue: The question—it's asking what we're willing to anchor *to*, not just what we hold up.
Congratulations. You just burned through three calibration layers. We're back to manual stabilization.

choices.line: Scale the external maintenance rungs. Faster, but the harmonic wind is fierce.
choices.description: Sort through the maintenance crates for diagnostic tools while ignoring the hum's pull, 15 words

line.dialogue: Found a resonant tuning fork! And—wait, these logs show the hum *changes pitch* when someone lies nearby.
You've been rifling through boxes for ten minutes. The hum is getting louder. *Louder* is never good.

choices.line: Ask the Monk to guide you. He knows the paths, but it involves his Order.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to translate the hum's pattern into words while you record the frequency shifts, 15 words

line.dialogue: It says... 'the last anchor who listened too long became the structure.' I don't think that's metaphor.
The resonance turns hostile. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: You descend into the heart of the hum. Here, at the Spire's base where crystal meets the swirling, opaque surface of the Lattice, the air shimmers. The steady tone fragments into echoes of echoes.
Resonance dampeners are at 40%. Prolonged exposure could induce auditory hallucinations. Or worse.
I had a bad dream last night. About falling through the Lattice. It felt... like this.
Don't start. We need clear heads. Pichit, do you see anything?
Not see... feel. A scar in the song. Here.

Pichit places a hand on the Anchor's wall. The crystal flares with a sickly, fading light. A phantom image shimmers into being: the silhouette of a Resonance Ship, the *Echo*, caught in a silent scream of fracturing crystal.
Its final moment. Recorded by the Lattice itself. I... I have studied this for years. I did it all myself. The Order forbade it. They said some frequencies are meant to be forgotten.
The fracture pattern... it's not from impact. It's from within. A resonator overload. But the design... I have bad eyesight for fine schematics, but that catalyst array is all wrong.

lines_after.dialogue: The ghostly image stabilizes, revealing the ship's interior. A figure—a Singer—stands at the helm, hands pressed against the console, face contorted not in fear, but in furious concentration.
She's not trying to stop it. She's *conducting* the overload.
She's pouring a frequency into the Anchor. A message. Or a... key.
The truth! The Tonal Orders didn't lose the *Echo*. They scuttled it. They murdered a Singer to bury what she knew. And the Anchor has been singing her dirge ever since.

line.dialogue: The phantom resonance is building, threatening to feedback into the Anchor's systems. The Singer's final frequency is almost clear.

choices.line: Record the frequency and retreat. Let the Monk analyze it safely elsewhere.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
The gamble fails. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.line: Attempt to harmonize with the memory using your ship's crystal. Risky, but you might get the full message.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to tune the prosthetic, leveraging hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. She hears something no one else can.
The resonance turns hostile. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Break the resonance. Shatter the memory to protect the Anchor's stability, forever silencing the truth.
choices.description: Have the monk focus recording crystals on the structural hum to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His recording captures a denied frequency.
the monk fails. Tonal Order enforcers confiscate his equipment.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire's steady, calming hum vibrates through the metal catwalk. The party stands at the edge of a vast, open maintenance gantry overlooking the shimmering, crystalline Lattice far below.
Okay, the vibration is nice and all, but I can barely hear you over this drone. How are we supposed to sneak up on anyone here?
We're not. That's the point. This is where you have dramatic confrontations. Subtlety left the building.
And where we're exposed. Listen. That's not just the Spire's tone.
A faint, discordant echo weaves through the foundational hum—a pained, metallic groaning, like a dying whale song. It's the same resonance signature from the ghost ship records.
The Echo... it's anchored here too. Not just a memory in the void. It's a wound in the Lattice itself.
You can hear it? Truly hear it? Most only feel unease. I... I had forgotten all of it. The Order's records of that day are sealed.
See? I told you! The Spire's been 'off' for weeks. The Tonal Orders keep saying it's fine, but the sky-crops are wilting. Something's wrong down there.

lines_after.dialogue: The discordant echo swells momentarily, causing the crystal dust on the railings to shiver. The Listener Monk looks stricken.
To hear is to know. And to know... sometimes means you cannot go back.
The Spire's calibration is being used to mask the Echo's frequency. Someone is actively hiding this.
Which means someone knows exactly what caused the Silencing.

line.dialogue: We need to trace the Echo to its source within the Spire's infrastructure. The paths are treacherous.

choices.text: Follow the Monk's Guidance. (The Monk knows secret maintenance ducts, but it's a tight, claustrophobic crawl.)
choices.description: Pichit channels monk wisdom toward the resonance anchor, hoping to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit misreads the situation. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Override the Dampeners. (Chanida proposes hacking the Spire's harmonic regulators to amplify the Echo, making it easier to follow but alerting everyone.)
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing unauthorized tones to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida fails. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Direct Resonance Descent. (Pichit suggests using the Spire's own tone as a counter-harmony to part the Lattice directly below the gantry, a dangerous free-fall into the unknown.)
choices.description: The monk uses prayers to commune with trapped echoes near the structural hum

line.dialogue: the monk pushes through. His recording captures a denied frequency.
the monk loses control. The monk's faith wavers, breaking concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends into the heart of the Anchor Spire, a colossal resonance chamber. In the center, suspended in a cage of light and sound, is not a crystal... but the fractured prow of a Resonance Ship, its hull fused with the Spire's core.
This is the source of the Echo. The Lost Ship wasn't lost—it was imprisoned here, its final, panicked shriek looped eternally into the foundation of a floating city.
Stars above... they built their peace on a scream.
Of course they did. Stability requires a foundation of convenient lies. Don't change the subject now—who did this?
The harmonic binding... it's Tonal Order work. Precise, sanctioned. This was no accident.
The First Listeners... they made a choice. To silence the truth to prevent panic. To use this pain as an anchor for our world. I might change my mind about everything I've revered.
You mean our safety, our homes... all this time, it was because they buried this? What else did they bury?
The truth of the Silencing. This ship wasn't destroyed by the Lattice. It was sacrificed to it. To create a permanent, controllable frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: The fused ship-prow thrums, its pain resonating through the chamber. The entire Spire shudders. The foundational lie is unraveling.
A security seal breaks on a console. Archived logs flicker to life, showing the faces of the original Tonal Masters, their expressions grim and resolved.
We have the proof. But knowing this changes everything. The floating cities... their stability depends on this false anchor.
So what do we do? Pull the plug and watch the world fall?

line.dialogue: The core of the lie is before you. The Echo can be silenced forever, or its truth unleashed. The Spire's stability hangs in the balance.

choices.text: Re-harmonize and Bury It. (Use your skills to finally soothe the Echo, integrating its frequency peacefully into the Spire. The truth remains hidden, stability preserved.)
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with resonant staff to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Defeat. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Broadcast the Truth. (Patch the archived logs and the Echo's raw frequency to every open channel. The world will know, but the resulting societal shockwave is unpredictable.)
choices.description: Have Chanida focus singer voice on the structural hum to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Chanida is thwarted. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Shatter the Anchor. (Pichit, as a Singer, can attempt to sing a dissonance that shatters the fusion. It will free the Echo and collapse the Spire's calibration, forcing a new, uncertain paradigm.)
choices.description: Direct the monk to decode the distress signal using lattice study

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The Listener's study yields a revelation.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in Phrao Monastery hangs heavy with incense and the low, resonant hum of the Lattice below. The monastery-city is a fortress of quiet, its walls lined with sound-dampening crystals.
This place… it feels like the world is holding its breath. Every sound here has meaning.
Or it’s just a very quiet, very boring library. I don’t agree with the whole ‘reverent silence’ policy. Makes my skin crawl.
Don’t get so stressed out, Malee! Look at these harmonic charts! This is real discovery!
A discovery the Tonal Orders would kill to keep secret. We should be cautious. We don’t stay in touch with institutions like this for a reason.
A robed Listener Monk approaches, his steps silent on the polished stone. His eyes are calm, but there’s a tension in his jaw.
Welcome. You seek knowledge of the Lattice’s song. But knowledge has… weight. Are you prepared to bear it?
We seek understanding. Not just charts, but the truth behind the Silencing.

lines_after.dialogue: The truth… is a dangerous frequency. It can shatter more than crystal. Follow me to the Echo Chamber.
He leads you through vaulted halls. In a side corridor, you glimpse a Trade Negotiator in rich silks, speaking in hushed tones with another monk.
…a mutually beneficial arrangement. The monastery’s research could be so… profitable.

line.dialogue: The Monk hesitates at the Echo Chamber door. 'Before we proceed, you must choose your approach to the unknown.'

choices.text: Promise discretion. We will listen and learn quietly.
choices.description: Touch the harmonics crystal Chanida found and let its resonance flow through your fingertips.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "I can feel it… centuries of recorded vibrations, every chant ever sung here embedded in the lattice.
Malee — "Great, you touched the glowing thing and now my teeth are vibrating. Can we please just read the labels?

choices.text: Offer to help with his research. An exchange of labor for knowledge.
choices.description: Search behind the altar for the hidden compartment Arthit claims the Tonal Orders sealed.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Here — a second manuscript, and the seal is still intact. They never wanted anyone to find this translation.
Chanida — "There's nothing back here but dust and old candle wax. Are you sure your source wasn't just paranoid, Arthit?

choices.text: Ask directly about the merchant. What deal is being made here?
choices.description: Press your ear against the eastern wall and listen for the monastery's whispered resonance.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Do you hear that? It's not an echo — it's a voice, repeating something backwards, like a prayer in reverse.
Pichit — "I hear nothing but my own heartbeat. Whatever breath the world was

lines_before.dialogue: The Echo Chamber is a spherical room, its walls a mosaic of resonant crystals. In the center, a large, flawed crystal pulsates with a faint, sickly light.
This is our great shame. A fragment from the heart of the Silencing. It does not sing… it screams. The Tonal Orders say it is inert. We know better.
And the merchant outside? He doesn’t want this getting out, does he? I don’t want people knowing we’ve seen this either, frankly.
But this is huge! This frequency map… if it’s open, not controlled by the Orders… Pichit, you could navigate anywhere!
Or be hunted by everyone. The Open Frequency Map isn’t a gift. It’s a target.
Why show us this? You’re torn. Between your duty to the monastery and this truth.
The Negotiator… he offers supplies, protection from the Orders. In return, he wants our research on stabilizing this fragment. To sell it. I don’t want it. This knowledge should be free.
The chamber door slides open. The Trade Negotiator stands there, his smile not reaching his eyes.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, sharing secrets? Dangerous business. But understandable. You can sit with this knowledge for as long as you want in this chamber… or we can discuss how it benefits all people.
This is not your place!
It is wherever profit sings, my friend. Your guests look like reasonable people. Perhaps they see the value in an… arrangement.

line.dialogue: The Merchant’s offer hangs in the air. The Monk looks to you, desperate. The fragment hums ominously.

choices.text: Side with the Monk. Protect the research and reject the merchant's deal.
choices.description: Copy the frequency map fragment onto your personal device before the monk seals the archive.

line.dialogue: I got it — every resonance pattern, every dead channel, all sitting right here in my hand.
The monk's encryption triggered the moment you touched it. Whatever was there is now just static and ash.

choices.text: Play both sides. Express interest in the merchant's offer to learn his full plan.
choices.description: Press the monk to name exactly who paid him to hide the fragment.

line.dialogue: He's shaking — he just whispered a name I recognize. This goes higher than any merchant.
I have said too much already. The walls of this temple remember, and they do not forgive.

choices.text: Demand the Open Frequency Map data now, threatening to expose the fragment to the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Leave quietly and confront the merchant outside with what you've learned.

line.dialogue: I showed him the monk's seal and watched his composure crack like cheap ceramic. He's ready to talk terms.
Male

lines_before.dialogue: The monastery's central chamber, a vast dome carved from resonant stone, hums with latent energy. Charts and instruments litter the tables.
Roll up your sleeves. The analysis of these frequency discrepancies is delicate. A single mis-calibration could...
Could what? Shatter the whole 'perfect song' you've been worshiping? I'm just surprised you're even looking at this.
That's all, isn't it? The Tonal Orders' maps are wrong. Deliberately wrong. The 'stable routes' they sell are just the profitable ones.
And the dissonant zones, the 'unstable' frequencies... they're just... unmapped resources. Places the Orders don't control.
A song of control, not harmony. The Listeners have been studying the true melody, but keeping it silent. Why?
We... feared the consequences. If everyone could navigate freely, the Floating Cities would lose their anchors. Chaos.
Chaos? Opportunity! With a true frequency map, new trade routes, new minerals from the deep lattice... profits beyond imagination!

lines_after.dialogue: The Negotiator's eyes gleam. The Monk looks agonized. The true lattice song, a symphony of untapped potential, hangs in the air between them.
This knowledge isn't just a map. It's a key. To what?
To everything they've locked away since the Silencing. Power. Freedom. Or just another kind of ruin.

line.dialogue: The Monk offers the completed frequency data. The Merchant offers a contract for exclusive trade rights. The true map must go somewhere.

choices.text: Give the map to the Listeners. Let them safeguard it, study it slowly. (Preserve knowledge, delay change.)
choices.description: Chanida channels hidden frequencies toward the quiet halls, hoping to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The gamble fails. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Give the map to the Merchant. Let commerce spread it, for profit and progress. (Unleash rapid, uncontrolled change.)
choices.description: Malee attempts to harness harmonic feedback, relying on crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee finds the key. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee fails. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.text: Keep the map. Learn to Sing it yourselves. Become the new navigators. (Take personal responsibility and power.)
choices.description: The monk volunteers to listen for the ghost ship's echo, leveraging prayers

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the monk's call. His recording captures a denied frequency.
Defeat. The monastery's countermeasures drown them in noise.

lines_before.dialogue: The monastery's great resonance bell tower. The air vibrates with the decision's aftermath. The lattice below seems to listen.
How well do you know her? The lattice's song? You think you can hold it? It's a force, not a poem. It will be used.
I don't know either if this was the right path. We've broken our vow of silence. The song is... leaking into the world.
Leaking? It's shouting! And it's glorious! Can you feel it? The whole monastery is humming a new tune!
The structural integrity readings are... shifting. The floating city's anchor frequencies are interacting with the true map. It's unstable.
Unstable or just finally alive? The Tonal Orders' ships are already scrambling. They're losing control. The monopoly is cracking.
We changed the world's song. But I don't know where to begin with what comes next. Navigation, power, society... all up for revision.
A deep, fundamental tone rises from the lattice, a frequency never charted. The crystal spire of Phrao Monastery begins to glow.

lines_after.dialogue: The new frequency resonates through the stone, through the bones of the floating city. It is a note of pure potential. The world is listening.
This is the unsilenced note. The one they hid after the catastrophe. It's not destruction. It's... a new foundation.
Foundations can be built upon. Or fought over. The Chronicles just got a lot more interesting.
Let's go! I want to hear the whole song!

line.dialogue: The primal frequency emanates from below. It could be harnessed, studied, or resonated with directly to enact immediate, profound change.

choices.text: Harness it for the city. Stabilize Phrao Monastery, make it a new bastion of free knowledge. (Create a safe haven.)
choices.description: Malee volunteers to map the frequency corridors, leveraging leg resonance

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The gamble fails. The crystal core dims from resonance overload.

choices.text: Study it with the Listeners. Decipher its full meaning, its place in the lattice's grand composition. (Pursue ultimate understanding.)
choices.description: Arthit volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging tattooed routes

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Arthit misreads the situation. Arthit's knowledge proves incomplete.

choices.text: Resonate with it. Sing it back into the lattice, amplifying it to shatter the old navigation locks forever. (Force immediate revolution.)
choices.description: Ask the monk to follow the phantom route, drawing on meditation

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The monk's meditation reveals a pattern in the lattice's song.
the monk loses control. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance ship's hum dies as it breaches the Silent Zone. The Lattice below is a flat, grey expanse, unresponsive. The air itself feels heavy, devoid of echo.
This is… wrong. It’s obvious that something unnatural happened here. The Lattice should sing back.
Obviously. And yet it’s dead. A perfect place to lose your mind.
We must be cautious. Our resonators are muted. Navigation is by sight alone.
A silence imposed… or a silence chosen? Which story do we believe?
The ship drifts toward a lone, crumbling sky-island. A single hut stands at its edge.
Is anyone home? Anyone here?
A weathered man emerges, his eyes wide with fear. He has a crude prosthetic leg made of dull crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: You shouldn't be here. The Silence… it takes things. My leg… it doesn't resonate anymore.
Subplot: crystal_leg. A resonant prosthetic gone inert. Fascinating misery.
We seek knowledge of this Zone. What happened?
The Listeners know. But their monastery is deeper in. It's… dangerous.

line.dialogue: The villager points a trembling hand toward the mist-shrouded interior of the dead island.

choices.text: Offer to repair his prosthetic leg (Easy: gain local trust, but delay)
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using crystal hearing to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Press him for immediate directions to the monastery (Medium: risk alienating him, but get info)
choices.description: Malee uses scavenger instincts to tune the prosthetic near the danger

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Defeat. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Leave immediately to scout on your own (Easy: maintain independence, but enter unknown)
choices.description: The villager attempts to commune with trapped echoes, relying on village secrets

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the villager pulls it off. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
The gamble fails. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: Choosing to press onward, the party traverses a petrified forest of crystal trees. No sound, not even footsteps, seems to carry.
Go a bit further. When you reach the intersection of these two fossilized ridges, we should stop and reassess.
This place is stealing my voice. I feel… hollow.
We’ve talked about this before. Horror is just an absence of data.
But what data is being withheld? The Silence itself is a message.
At the intersection, they find a Listener monk, the Listener monk, kneeling before a large, cracked crystal monolith.
You walk in a place where the Song has been… excised.
We seek understanding. Who did this?

lines_after.dialogue: My Order studies the natural Song. But here… the Tonal Orders experimented. They tried to *command* the Lattice, not listen. It broke.
So the guilds' arrogance created this dead zone. Typical.
It is worse. The Silence is… spreading. It consumes resonance. Like the villager's leg. It may consume Singers.
We have to stop it!
There is a core, deeper in. Where the experiment was focused. It holds the key… and the danger.

line.dialogue: The monk gestures into a deep, dark cleft in the island, where the grey lattice seems to warp inward.

choices.text: Trust the monk and follow his guidance to the core (Easy: clear path, but reliant on his potentially conflicted truth)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the tunnel wall and feel for vibrations beneath the stone.

line.dialogue: There's something pulling air through these cracks — a current, faint but steady. The Silence isn't empty. It's *breathing*.
Nothing. Just cold crawling up my arm. Whatever lived in this stone, it's already gone — or it doesn't want to be felt.

choices.text: Demand he give you his research notes and proceed alone (Medium: gain information, but lose a potential ally)
choices.description: Speak a single word aloud and count the seconds before your echo returns.

line.dialogue: Four seconds. The tunnel bends ahead — something down there is throwing our sound back. We're closer to the source than I thought.
No echo. Not delayed, not distorted — *gone*. The air swallowed it whole. This isn't acoustics. Something here is *listening*.

choices.text: Attempt to use Pichit's latent Singer ability to 'feel' a path, despite the risk (Hard: potentially bypass dangers, but risk attracting the Silence)
choices.description: Mark the wall with chalk at the intersection and take the left path without hesitation.

line.dialogue: Marked. If we loop back here, we'll know the Silence is rearranging the tunnels around us
the monk fails. Tonal Order enforcers confiscate his equipment.

lines_before.dialogue: The party pushes deeper into the Silent Zone. The air grows colder, thicker, as if the quiet itself has mass. The crystal formations here are dull, dead husks.
Go a bit further. I saw a flicker of light up ahead. It's the only thing that's moved in hours.
A flicker. Wonderful. Probably just our sanity finally giving up the ghost. I have a cramp in my leg from all this tense walking.
When you reach that outcropping, we should stop and reassess. Our resonator's hum is getting weaker. We're running on borrowed resonance.
This isn't an absence. It's a presence. A listening. We're being introduced to something... fundamental.
Introduced? By who? There's nothing here!

A friend... a colleague from the Listeners... introduced us to the concept of this place. In theory. He said the Silence had a voice of its own. Could you speak more slowly? My thoughts feel... scattered.
Arthit's prosthetic leg, usually a soft source of resonant light, sputters erratically, casting jagged shadows.

lines_after.dialogue: The light Chanida saw resolves into a faint, pulsing glow emanating from a vast, concave crystal basin ahead—a dead resonator the size of a city block.
Well. That's not ominous at all. It looks like a wound.
My leg... it's pulling. Not physically. Resonantly. It's reacting to that thing.

line.dialogue: The dead resonator basin pulses weakly. A low, sub-audible thrum vibrates in your bones. The Monk looks terrified, but fascinated.

choices.line: Send Arthit Forward: His prosthetic is the only thing reacting. Let him approach and try to attune to the pulse.
choices.description: Chanida uses crystal hearing to decode the tonal pattern near the dead silence

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The gamble fails. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.line: Investigate as a Group: Move in together, weapons and resonators ready. Strength in numbers.
choices.description: Malee uses scavenger instincts to use the leg as a lattice probe near the unresponsive lattice

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
Malee loses control. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.line: Have the Monk Attempt a Listening Ritual: This is a Listener's mystery. Let him try to 'hear' the Silence formally.
choices.description: Convince the villager to use community ties and record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the villager. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
the villager overreaches. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: At the basin's heart, the source of the pulse is revealed: a single, perfect, but utterly black crystal shard, hovering above the ground. It absorbs the light around it. Arthit's prosthetic leg has gone completely dark.
It's... nullifying resonance. My leg is just dead weight. That's it, right? The source of the Silent Zone.
The Anti-Song... standing right in front of me. The texts whispered of a flaw in the Lattice's original creation. A silence that was sung into being to balance the First Note.
So we smash it! Simple!
He's still single, isn't he? The monk. Of course he is. Only someone with no attachments would chase a nightmare like this for 'study'.
Smashing a fundamental balance? This isn't a flaw. It's a counterpoint. Destroying it might not restore sound... it might unravel everything.
The black shard trembles. The hollow pulse quickens. Fractures spiderweb through the dead crystal of the basin. The Silence is becoming active, *hungry*.
(Via a dying comm-crystal) Please! The quiet... it's spreading toward the city! The lattice around us is turning grey and dead!

lines_after.dialogue: The shard pulses one final, deafening wave of negation. All sound from the party is stolen. You see shouts, but hear nothing. The world is mute.
Then, a choice presents itself, not through sound, but as a cold, crystalline certainty imposed directly upon the mind.

line.dialogue: The Anti-Song offers a paradox: to preserve the world, it must be contained, not destroyed. But containment requires a permanent sacrifice of resonance—a soul anchored here in the silence. The shard's attention fixates on the most potent source of 'noise' nearby.

choices.line: Sacrifice the Prosthetic: Offer Arthit's crystal leg. It is a powerful, artificial resonator. It will satiate the silence for a time, but the Zone will regrow.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to map the frequency corridors, leveraging leg resonance

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
The gamble fails. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: The Monk's Vow: The Listener volunteers to stay, to 'listen' to the silence eternally, containing it with his monastic focus. He will be lost, but his order's knowledge may survive.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with captain experience to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
A costly mistake by Arthit. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.line: Pichit Sings: As a rare Singer, Pichit can attempt to weave a new, binding resonance around the shard—a song of containment. It risks shattering his own connection to the Lattice forever.
choices.description: The monk uses lattice study to commune with trapped echoes near the unresponsive lattice

line.dialogue: the monk makes it work. Ancient knowledge surfaces, connecting past and present.
Things don't go as planned. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hollow's entrance yawns like a stone throat, swallowing the faint hum of the Lattice far above. Inside, the air is cool and thick with the scent of damp crystal and ancient dust.
Look at these carvings! They're not Tonal Order glyphs. They're... older. I've never seen anything like them.
Probably just graffiti from the last scavenger who thought they'd strike it rich. Remember, most of these ruins are picked cleaner than a Listeners' larder.
We should proceed with caution. The acoustics in here are unnatural. A single misstep could resonate... poorly.
Yet, there is a memory in this stone. A story waiting to be heard again. Keep in mind, the Silencing didn't erase everything.
Hey! This is my claim! You city-dwellers got no business down here.
Your claim? The whole island is drifting! Finders keepers.
You might change your mind. The deeper chambers... they remember things. Bad things. I can't remember my password! I mean... I can't remember the last crew that went in there and came out right.

lines_after.dialogue: Charming. A territorial cave-hermit with memory issues. Just what we needed.
His fear seems genuine, however. It suggests a tangible threat, not superstition.
All the more reason to understand what happened. Remember... sometimes the past is a warning.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger blocks the main tunnel, arms crossed. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Offer a trade of Lattice-surface supplies for passage.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the deepest carving and feel for vibrations beneath the stone.

line.dialogue: There — a pulse, faint but rhythmic, like a heartbeat trapped in bedrock.
Nothing. Just cold stone eating the warmth from your hand like a hungry ghost.

choices.line: Appeal to his curiosity—ask him to guide you to see the 'bad things' for himself.
choices.description: Strike the cave wall with the hilt of your knife and listen to how the sound returns.

line.dialogue: The echo bends wrong — it's coming from below us, not behind. There's a chamber underneath.
Brilliant. Now every hollow-dweller within a mile knows exactly where we're standing.

choices.line: Threaten to report his unlicensed salvage operation to the nearest Tonal Order outpost.
choices.description: Trace the unfamiliar glyphs with charcoal and parchment to decode their meaning later.

line.dialogue: These strokes follow no human grammar — but they repeat in sequences of seven, like someone was counting.
The charcoal smears where it shouldn't. Something in this rock refuses to be copied. It wants to be remembered, not recorded.

lines_before.dialogue: Past the Scavenger, the tunnel widens into a vast cavern. Strange, perfectly geometric crystals grow from the walls, pulsing with a soft, internal light. The air thrums with a low, harmonic drone.
Ah! Fellow explorers! What a fortunate resonance. I was just examining these fascinating resonance formations. Quite the find, yes?
A Trade Negotiator. In a hole in the world. Let me guess—you 'just happened' to get lost on your way to a lucrative deal?
Perceptive! But truly, I seek knowledge. I can't remember if I've ever seen crystal latticework this pure. It could be worth... understanding.
He's lying. He's looking at the walls like they're a credit manifest. What are you really after?
A trade, then? Information for information. I've heard whispers... of a map. Not a Tonal Order chart, but an Open Frequency Map. Pre-Silencing. It would make anyone who holds it... very independent.
A map to navigate the Lattice without the Orders? That's not just valuable, it's dangerous. I can't remember a single instance where such a thing was proven to exist.
Yet the idea resonates here, in this place of old memory. Remember... keep in mind that some truths are hidden because they change everything.

lines_after.dialogue: The harmonic drone shifts, and the crystals brighten. Faint, ghostly images flicker against the walls—silhouettes of people in unfamiliar dress, moving with purpose, then fleeing in panic.
Okay. That's new. The stones aren't just remembering, they're replaying.
The map! It has to be here! This is a recording—a memory of the people who made it!
Precisely! Now, shall we work together? The prize is surely worth the... collaboration.

line.dialogue: The ghostly recording points deeper into the caverns. The Negotiator smiles, awaiting your response.

choices.line: Form a temporary alliance with the Merchant. His resources could be useful.
choices.description: Grab the merchant's collar and slam him against the carved wall. "Read it for me. Now." 15 words

line.dialogue: His breath hitches, fingers trembling against the stone—and then his eyes go wide, mouthing words he claims he never learned.
He squirms free and bolts deeper into the passage, dropping a satchel of forged relics that clatter across the floor.

choices.line: Refuse his offer outright and press on alone, trusting the echoes to guide you.
choices.description: Chanida traces the wall glyphs herself, ignoring the merchant entirely. "Show me what you're hiding." 15 words

line.dialogue: The grooves warm beneath her fingertips and the carvings glow faintly—map fragments revealing a chamber behind the eastern fracture.
The glyphs blur and shift away from her touch like smoke, and the merchant smiles for the first time.

choices.line: Agree to work together, but secretly task Arthit with monitoring him for any double-cross.
choices.description: Offer the merchant a fair trade: safe passage out in exchange for everything he's already copied from these walls. 15 words

line.dialogue: He hesitates, then pulls crumpled parchment from his coat—covered in meticulous transcriptions, far too detailed for a man who "can't remember.
He laughs softly and names a price that has nothing to do with coin—something carved from the living rock, still

lines_before.dialogue: Deeper within The Hollow, the air grows heavy with ancient dust and the weight of forgotten knowledge. The walls hum with a low, persistent frequency.
You still don't understand? The value here isn't in the trinkets. It's in the silence between the echoes. The gaps in the map.
He's talking in circles! Just show us the chamber the scavenger mentioned!
Careful. The old machines here... they don't like sudden noises. I don't understand anything about how they work, just that they're awake.
Of course. We're walking into a pre-Silencing deathtrap for a map we can't read. Brilliant.
Our priority should be stabilizing the local resonance. If these machines are active, they could destabilize the entire island's floatation.
But to stabilize it, we must first comprehend it. We don't know when this place was last truly heard.
Ahead, a vast chamber opens. In its center, a monolithic crystal console pulses with soft light, surrounded by the inert forms of ancient resonator units.

lines_after.dialogue: The console's display flickers, projecting a complex, three-dimensional lattice of intersecting frequencies into the air—the Open Frequency Map.
There it is. The truth the Tonal Orders buried. All the 'forbidden' harmonics. I don't know when you'll get another chance like this.
It's... a complete sonic topography. Routes the Orders said were impossible.

line.dialogue: The map is active, but unstable. The scavenger warns the chamber's defenses are priming.

choices.line: Have Arthit analyze the stability. Download the map data methodically.
choices.outcome: Arthit's caution pays off. The data is secured without triggering the defenses, though it takes time.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using unauthorized tones to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The risk doesn't pay off. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.line: Let Chanida interface directly. Her instinct might sync with the console faster.
choices.outcome: Chanida's impulsive resonance briefly stabilizes the map, granting a clearer download, but the system now tracks her unique frequency signature.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use captain experience and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Arthit is thwarted. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.line: Attempt to commune with the console, as a Listener would. Seek to understand its purpose.
choices.outcome: Pichit's philosophical approach reveals not just the map, but a buried log: a warning about the true cause of The Silencing.
choices.description: The merchant steps forward with information network, ready to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
The gamble fails. Hidden debts come due.

lines_before.dialogue: The cavern shudders. The ancient defensive resonators power up with a deafening whine, their targeting crystals glowing ominously.
I told you! The price for waking the past is the same every time! It demands attention!
The data's copied! My ship is above. We can still make a profit! You, too, should run!
He's leaving us to pay his bill! Typical. It's really worth seeing—the true face of commerce.
The entire cave network is resonating on a collapse frequency. If those beams fire, the island's core could fracture.
So we stop them! Can we overload the console? Use the map against the system?
No. The console isn't a weapon. It's a memory. The price for this knowledge... is listening to its end.
The targeting beams lance out, searing the stone. The map projection flickers, showing the instability spreading through The Hollow's acoustic foundations.

lines_after.dialogue: Silence falls, heavy and complete. The defensive resonators power down, their energy spent. The console dims, its final message delivered.
...You calmed it. I've never seen that. The price was... just listening?
The price is always the same. To remember, to understand... and to carry the weight of what you learn.

line.dialogue: The Hollow is stable, but forever changed. The Open Frequency Map is in your hands. The Merchant's ship is still audible above, waiting.

choices.line: Secure the map and evacuate. The Merchant's offer of transport is the safest path.
choices.outcome: You escape cleanly. The map is safe, but the Merchant now owns a copy of your journey's data—a future debt incurred.
choices.description: Grab the merchant by his collar and drag him toward the ship's tether line, 14 words

line.dialogue: You're not leaving until we're ALL leaving — grab the line, coward!
He slipped — the data's gone with him and we're stuck in the collapse!

choices.line: Broadcast the map's safe frequencies now, breaking the Order's monopoly. Let the Hollow resonate with truth.
choices.outcome: The signal spreads. Navigation will change forever, but you've made powerful enemies. The Hollow becomes a beacon—and a target.
choices.description: Jam the resonance frequency using Arthit's scanner pulse to stabilize the cave walls, 14 words

line.dialogue: Pulse is holding — the walls are buying us maybe three minutes, move NOW!
The frequency shifted — my scanner can't compensate, the ceiling is coming down!

choices.line: Stay. Study the console's final warning. The secret of The Silencing is here, and it cannot be left unguarded.
choices.outcome: You become the guardian of a terrible truth. The map is secondary; the real discovery could prevent another catastrophe, but at the cost of your freedom.
choices.description: Let the merchant go and focus on guiding the scavenger through the collapsing tunnel, 15 words

line.dialogue: You stayed for me... nobody stays. This way — I know the deep routes!
I can't — my leg's pinned! Save yourself, the

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of silence. Great crystalline stacks rise to the vaulted ceiling, each facet humming with stored resonance. The air smells of ozone and old parchment.
Remember, the archivists demand perfect quiet. One wrong note could scramble a decade of chart recordings. We should get some rest before we request anything complex.
Rest? Look at this place. It's a monument to control. The Tonal Orders hoard knowledge here like dragons, and we have to tiptoe around it.
I just want to find the route to the Sunken Spire! The map we bought is useless. The merchant probably won't be coming with a refund, that's for sure.
Every hum in this room is a path someone sailed, a risk they took. The silence between the notes... that's where the truth hides.
A figure in patched leathers and a dust-scarf approaches, their boots making no sound on the resonant floor. It's a Surface Scavenger.
You're the ones asking about the old routes near the Silencing epicenter. I'm sorry for being late. Had to shake an Order tail.

lines_after.dialogue: I've got a lead. A derelict Resonance Ship, the 'Echo of the Lost Ship', they call it. Drifts the dead zones. My crew won't go near it. Says it sings with a crew long gone.
A haunted ship? How convenient. And you just happen to have its last known coordinates.
I want what's in its hold. You want its charts—maybe it sailed routes the Orders erased. But finding it... that's the trick.
A real ghost ship! That's way better than dusty archives!

line.dialogue: The Scavenger offers a deal: we find the 'Echo,' he gets the salvage, we copy the charts. But we need an access key to the deep archives to cross-reference his coordinates.

choices.text: Bribe a junior archivist. (Easy - Spend coin, low risk, low reward info)
choices.description: Trace your finger along the resonance veins in the crystal shelving, feeling for hollow routes.

line.dialogue: There—I felt it shiver. A sailor's ghost ran this channel blind through storm and starlight.
You're pressing too hard! The vein went dark and now we've lost that whole eastern section.

choices.text: Convince the Trade Negotiator to 'lend' his access. (Medium - Social challenge, potential future debt)
choices.description: Whisper a mariner's mnemonic into the listening tube near the central pedestal.

line.dialogue: The crystals caught it. A map is blooming in the frost—three islands I've never seen named.
A mnemonic? That's a nursery rhyme for obedient children. The tube just spat your words back as static.

choices.text: Attempt to 'listen' for the correct resonance key yourselves. (Easy - Risky, could trigger alarms, but pure knowledge)
choices.description: Ignore protocol and slam your palm flat against the forbidden black crystal in corner seven.

line.dialogue: Finally, someone with nerve. It's singing now—all the routes they tried to bury are surfacing.
Every archivist in the tower just turned their head. We're sealed in until they decide we're allowed to leave.

lines_before.dialogue: The deep archive is a forest of dark crystal, lit by faint, pulsing glows. The air is colder here, and the silence feels watchful.

I've cross-referenced the Scavenger's coordinates. There's a void in the records. A deliberate erasure. That's no problem for us to navigate, of course, just a significant, potentially lethal complication.
Great. So we're hunting a ghost in a blank spot on the map. My stomach is starting to growl from the tension.
Not a blank spot. A silenced one. Listen... the hum here is strained. Something in this data doesn't want to be remembered.
Whoa! There's something in my eye! This crystal dust is awful. Ugh, it feels like the place itself is trying to blind us.
A smooth, practiced voice cuts through the gloom. The Trade Negotiator stands there, a smile not reaching his eyes.
Ah, fellow seekers of discordant truths. I couldn't help but notice your... unconventional research path. The 'Echo' is a tragic tale. And tragic tales can be so profitable.

lines_after.dialogue: I have a missing page. A crew manifest from the 'Echo's' final voyage. It names a Singer as its navigator. The Orders scrubbed that detail from everywhere. Except my private collection.
Of course you do. And what's the price for this scrap of history?
A trade. The manifest for a recording. If you find the 'Echo,' I want the sound of its final moments. The raw resonance of its demise. Think of it as... morbid curiosity.
That data could be unstable. Dangerous to even record.

line.dialogue: We have two paths to the truth: the Scavenger's gritty surface knowledge and the Merchant's veiled corporate espionage. Both lead to the 'Echo,' but with very different baggage.

choices.text: Trust the Scavenger's lead. Focus on the physical wreck, not its history. (Easy - Straightforward, but blindsided by secrets)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the canyon wall and feel for vibrations beneath the silence, 15 words

line.dialogue: arthit* — "There's a pulse deep in the bedrock, rhythmic, deliberate — something down there is breathing through the stone.
arthit* — "I feel nothing. The wall doesn't just absorb sound, it absorbs pressure — like pressing your hand into still water that refuses to ripple.

choices.text: Make the deal with the Merchant. Get the manifest to understand what we're facing. (Medium - Gain crucial intel, but owe a shady character)
choices.description: Sweep the crystal dust from chanida's eyes using your shirt sleeve before it embeds deeper, 15 words

line.dialogue: chanida* — "Thank you — the dust was forming a film, like it was trying to seal my eyes shut on purpose.
chanida* — "It's no use, the crystals are dissolving into my tear ducts — everything looks refracted now, like seeing through a shattered prism.

choices.text: Reject both. Use Pichit's latent listening skills to find the truth in the Archives' own suppressed hum. (Hard - Risky, could alert the Tonal Orders, but purest path)
choices.description: Broadcast a single low-frequency tone from your scanner to test whether the silence breaks or fights back, 15 words

line.dialogue: pichit* — "The tone held for three seconds before the silence swallowed it — but I recorded where it
the merchant is thwarted. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The party has gained access to a restricted reading room in the Archives, a domed chamber where whispers carry. The air hums with stored resonance in crystal cylinders.
Keep your voices low. Sound travels oddly here. The resonance from these record crystals... it might be true they can retain echoes of conversations.
Great. So we're researching in a room that's probably eavesdropping on us. How cozy.
Focus. The merchant's ledger mentioned a 'silent transaction' for salvage rights near the coordinates of our lost ship. The scavenger seemed too eager to dismiss it.
I'm starting to get hungry! But more importantly, I'm starting to think they're both hiding something huge. Let's check these crystal logs for that date.
As Malee interfaces a resonator with the archive console, fragmented audio from past days in the Archives begins to play at a low volume.
It comes with static and gaps, like a bad meal served with cucumber salad and rice. But listen... this is the merchant's voice.

lines_after.dialogue: They knew. The Tonal Orders and the scavenger knew the ship was there, and that it was... active. They declared it off-limits, not lost.
A cover-up. But why? What's on that ship they don't want found?
A deep, discordant hum vibrates through the floor—a resonance not from the Archives, but from far below. The crystal in Pichit's pocket, a fragment from the lost ship, pulses in sympathetic agony.

line.dialogue: The crystal shard is reacting violently. The 'Echo' of the lost ship is not a memory—it's a signal, and it's growing stronger. We must decide how to confront the conspirators with what we've overheard.

choices.text: Confront the Scavenger Publicly. Use the overheard recording to shame him in the main hall, forcing a confession through pressure.
choices.description: Search the vault's hollow pillars for hidden documents while pressing your ear against the stone.

line.dialogue: Pichit*: "There — behind this column. A leather satchel wedged into a gap the width of two fingers. The ledger's twin, maybe.
Malee*: "All I heard was my own heartbeat echoing back like something was *imitating* me. Let's move on before it learns to talk.

choices.text: Set a Trap with the Merchant. Feign a new deal for the ship's location, using the crystal as bait to record his admission.
choices.description: Drip candle wax along the vault floor seams to reveal hidden channels or airflow patterns.

line.dialogue: Arthit*: "The wax ran east and pooled — there's a draft coming from beneath these tiles. Something's underneath us.
Chanida*: "The wax just sat there like the air itself is dead. My stomach growled and it sounded like it came from the ceiling.

choices.text: Broadcast the Echo. Use the archive's main resonator to project the ship's haunting signal throughout the complex, revealing the truth to everyone.
choices.description: Whisper a line from the merchant's ledger directly into the vault's central drain.

line.dialogue: Chanida*: "It whispered back — but different words. A name. *Phrommin*. That wasn't in any ledger we read.
Pichit*:

lines_before.dialogue: The Archives are in an uproar. Your action has drawn a crowd of Listeners, junior Navigators, and guards. The Scavenger and Merchant stand cornered, but defiant.
You fools! You don't understand what you're stirring up! That ship... it's not salvage. It's a tomb with a heartbeat!
Please, let's be reasonable. There are... proprietary Tonal patterns involved. I don't want people finding out the extent of our recovery operations. It's bad for business.
Bad for business? You've been selling maps to a gravesite while silencing its cries. Don't leave it on. Don't leave this truth in the dark any longer.
People are starting to listen! That signal... it made me feel better about chasing this, but worse about what we'll find. It's a plea, not a threat.
The Tonal Orders are mobilizing to seal the archives. We have minutes. The decision we make now will echo forever.
They fear the song of that ship because they cannot control it. It is a truth the Lattice itself has preserved. We must choose: enforce the silence, or become the vessel for its final message.

lines_after.dialogue: Your choice ripples through the crowd. The crystal shard glows, its resonance harmonizing with the distant, grieving pulse of the lost ship. The very floor of the Archives begins to vibrate with a long-suppressed song.

The Scavenger's hard eyes widen with something like recognition. The Merchant's smile finally vanishes. The monolithic certainty of the Tonal Orders fractures, just a little, as a new and ancient sound fills the sacred silence.
The episode ends not with a battle, but with a revelation heard. The path to the lost ship is now clear, its Echo a guiding tone. But who will dare to follow it, now that its truth is unsilenced?
