line.dialogue: This is the climax. The hidden truth of the haunted ship is now a resonant force in the room. How do we resolve the confrontation and define our path forward?

choices.text: Accept a Truce. Secure official, sanctioned permission to investigate the ship, bringing the Orders along but under their strict oversight.
choices.description: Grab the merchant's ledger from his hands and read the redacted entries aloud to the crowd.

line.dialogue: Every name, every coordinate — these are real people buried out there, and you've been profiting off their silence!
Give that back! You have no idea what happens to people who read those names out loud — none of you do!

choices.text: Seize the Initiative. Command the crowd's support to immediately depart for the ship, breaking the Orders' monopoly on the journey and its truth.
choices.description: Step between the scavenger and chanida, demanding both explain what the signal actually triggered.

line.dialogue: I swallowed a dead woman's memories when that pulse hit me. She's showing me where they're buried — all of them.
You don't WANT to know. I tried to follow the signal and my own reflection stopped recognizing me.

choices.text: Shatter the Monopoly. Publicly decipher the ship's resonant coordinates from the crystal, giving the knowledge freely to all present—Listeners, scavengers, and outsiders alike.
choices.description: Pull the jagged signal fragment from your coat pocket and hold it where chanida can see it glow.

line.dialogue: Then tell me why this shard started resonating when you spoke just now — what is it that you *already know*?
The attempt backfires on the merchant. His network delivers bad intelligence.

lines_before.dialogue: The entrance to The Hollow is a jagged crack in the floating island's underbelly. Inside, the air is cool and still, but the walls hum with a low, crystalline resonance. Ancient, geometric carvings cover the cavern walls, glowing faintly with stored sonic energy.
Pressure readings are stable, but these echo patterns... they're irregular. Like the cave itself is breathing. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Relax, Arthit. If the cave was going to collapse from us whispering, it would have done it when those sky pirates were shooting at us outside. Their ship's still circling up there, by the way.
Look at this! These carvings... they're not like the Tonal Order's navigation charts. They're older. Raw. I think they're a map of natural frequencies!
A language of the world before it was broken... Each mark a note in a song we've forgotten. What were they trying to preserve here?
Preserve, or perhaps... hide? This place feels deliberately isolated. The acoustics dampen external sound. It's a sanctuary.

Sanctuary for what? I'm just a trader from Cloudspire. I told you folks, I got lost running from those pirates. I'm afraid there'll be a problem if we don't find a way out soon. When's he coming? The pirate captain, I mean. He winked at me before they chased me in here. That's never good.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, grinding hum vibrates through the stone floor, different from the ambient resonance. A section of the far wall shimmers, revealing a hidden archway leading deeper into the mountain. The carvings around it pulse in sequence.
It opened! The sound... our footsteps must have triggered it! It's an invitation!
Or a very elaborate trap. But hey, it's warmer than waiting for the pirates.

line.dialogue: The newly revealed passage descends into a deeper, darker chamber. The hum is more pronounced here, almost melodic.

choices.text: Send Chanida ahead to scout. She's fast and observant.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the carved spiral and listen with more than your ears.

line.dialogue: The stone is warm — it remembers your touch. The pattern beneath your hand is a heartbeat, not decoration.
Pull back! You're disrupting the resonance field — the whole wall just vibrated three times harder than baseline!

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze the frequency pattern of the hum first, to ensure it's safe.
choices.description: Sketch the glyph sequence rapidly before the torchlight fades the mineral traces.

line.dialogue: Yes — you caught it! The third marker is a directional arrow, not a word. It points deeper. They *wanted* someone to follow.
You smudged the charcoal across the fissure line — now we can't tell where the carving ends and the natural crack begins.

choices.text: All move forward together, weapons ready, with the villager in the middle.
choices.description: Dim all lamps to minimum and ask Arthit to read the echo patterns alone in silence.

line.dialogue: The reflections aren't random. There's a chamber sixty meters ahead — and the echoes are *answering* each other in rhythm.
In this darkness I can't distinguish the carved channels from shadows. We're blind now, and the stone is still whispering.

lines_before.dialogue: The lower chamber is vast. Stalactites and stalagmites of pure resonance crystal form a forest of silent pipes. In the center lies a shattered dais, and upon it, a large, intact crystal plinth glowing with a complex, swirling light-map.
Incredible. This isn't just a map... it's an interactive frequency registry. Pre-Silencing tech. The Tonal Orders would burn cities for this. It's something to think about—the power this represents.
And the responsibility. This was their library. Their memory. Not a tool for monopoly, but a shared song.
Shared song, great. I'm just surprised it's still intact after all this time. What do you think about the fact that the only thing guarding it is... us?
It's beautiful! Look, if I hum this harmonic...

Chanida's voice rings out, clear and true. A corresponding node on the plinth-map flares brilliantly, projecting a beam of light onto the ceiling, revealing a star chart of safe, open frequencies—routes unrestricted by the Guild.
Well, ain't that a pretty picture. Thanks for turnin' on the lights, kids.
The Sky Pirate captain and three of his crew step from behind a crystal column, weapons drawn. Their resonator-pistols whine with a charged, aggressive frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: Heard the rumors 'bout this place. A map to all the quiet skies, free from the Order's tolls and taxes. That's a retirement fund right there. Hand it over. The crystal. Nice and easy.
I told you! I told you he was coming!
You led them here?
They had a knife to my ribs! What was I supposed to do?

line.dialogue: The pirates fan out, blocking the main exit. The crystal plinth hums between your group and them, its light-map still shimmering with potential.

choices.text: Surrender the crystal plinth. It's not worth dying over. (Comply)
choices.description: Pichit attempts to trace the anomalous signal, relying on staff meditation

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
The lattice has other plans. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Try to reason or bargain. Offer a copy of the data, not the physical artifact. (Negotiate)
choices.description: Ask Malee to calibrate against the frequency, drawing on crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Use the environment. Chanida hums a destabilizing frequency into the cavern's crystals to cause a distraction. (Fight/Sabotage)
choices.description: The villager attempts to follow the phantom route, relying on community ties

line.dialogue: the villager pushes through. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The risk doesn't pay off. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber narrows to a crystalline throat. The hum of the Lattice is palpable here, vibrating through the stone. Ahead, a faint, rhythmic tapping echoes—not natural.
Let's do it! We're so close. That sound… it's like a signal. Maybe the map's guardian?
Or a very bored pirate with a rock. Don't let them see you! If they have the frequency, they've got the advantage. We should scout.
Agreed. The acoustics are treacherous. A single misstep could alert whoever—or whatever—is making that sound. Let's go inside, but quietly.
The echoes here… they don't decay. They layer, building a memory of sound. What if this entire cave is a recording? A memory of the world before The Silencing?
The tapping stops. A low, grating laugh rolls through the cavern. From behind a jagged crystal column, a figure steps into the dim bioluminescent light.
Well, well. Listeners, eh? Or just treasure hunters like us. You're makin' enough racket to wake the dead stone.
Sky pirates! We found it first!

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate's crew emerges from shadows, their resonance-cutters humming. The chamber feels suddenly very small.
First don't mean much down here. That old map points to a control room. The kind that could tune the whole Lattice. Now, you can walk away… or we can settle who's got the better pitch.
Charming. They want to fight over a theory. Typical.

line.dialogue: The pirate captain gestures to a sealed archway behind him, etched with harmonic sigils. 'The door's locked to a specific frequency. My crew's been workin' on it. You look like you might have… other talents.'

choices.text: Propose a temporary alliance. Share knowledge to open the door.
choices.outcome: Pragmatic. The pirates agree, but trust is thin. You gain their brute force, but must watch your back.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use Listener training and map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit overreaches. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Challenge them to a contest of resonance. Let the Lattice decide.
choices.outcome: Risky. You'll have to produce a pure, complex tone to override their crude attempts. Success earns wary respect; failure cedes control.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with unauthorized tones to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
The risk doesn't pay off. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Attempt to stealthily decipher and activate the door's lock yourself, ignoring them.
choices.outcome: Bold. If you succeed, you slip through and seal it behind you. If you fail, you provoke an immediate and violent confrontation.
choices.description: Have the pirate focus secret frequencies on the darkness to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: Beyond the arch lies the heart of The Hollow: a vast, spherical chamber. In its center, suspended by crystal filaments, pulses a massive, intricate resonator—a pre-Silencing artifact. The air thrums with latent power.
By the tones… I just spoke with the crew. They're nervous. One of 'em said this thing could… tune a city right out of the sky if you twisted it wrong.
The potential for catastrophe is immense. This isn't just a map; it's a control node. The Tonal Orders would burn cities to keep this secret.
Look at the console. The interface is active. Glowing. After all this time… you can still use it. It still works. That's terrifying.
This is it! The Open Frequency Map! It's not a chart—it's this machine! We can learn everything! We have to activate it!
To hear the world's true song… unfiltered by guilds or fear. But every song has a consequence. What melody do we choose to play?
The pirate captain shoves past, his eyes wide with greed. 'Enough philosophy. This is fortune!' He reaches for the central crystal.
He doesn't know me. I've cracked vaults on a dozen sky-reefs. This is just another lock!

lines_after.dialogue: The machine reacts violently to his crude touch. A dissonant shriek tears through the chamber. Cracks spiderweb across the ancient crystal. The floor shudders. The map is destabilizing.
Brilliant. He's broken the one thing that could have freed us all. Now it's going to take us with it.
The harmonic feedback is building! If it peaks, it could cause a localized Silencing event—erase this island from the Lattice!

line.dialogue: The core resonator is fracturing, emitting waves of destructive resonance. The pirate recoils, clutching his ears. The Open Frequency Map—and your lives—hang in the balance.

choices.text: Attempt to dampen the resonator. Use counter-frequencies to shut it down safely.
choices.outcome: Conservative. You prevent catastrophe and preserve the chamber, but the map's data is lost in the shutdown. The secret remains buried.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to trace the anomalous signal, drawing on resonant staff

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Try to stabilize and download the map's data stream as the system fails.
choices.outcome: Daring. You might salvage fragments of the open frequencies, enough to challenge the Tonal Orders, but the strain could permanently damage the artifact or your ship's resonator.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on singer voice

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The lattice has other plans. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Sing into the chaos. Use your innate ability to harmonize with the failing frequency, trying to calm and claim it.
choices.outcome: Climactic. If you succeed, you momentarily fuse with the map, gaining profound, intuitive understanding of the Lattice. If you fail, the feedback overwhelms you, causing severe physical and mental resonance backlash.

line.dialogue: the villager finds the key. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
the villager overreaches. Local knowledge proves outdated.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hollow breathes. Cool, mineral-scented air moves through cathedral-like chambers, carrying whispers from a time before the Silencing.
Stay close. These echo patterns are unnatural. The Lattice's resonance is... muted here.
Look at these carvings! They're not just decorative. They look like... musical notation?
Great. Ancient sheet music. That'll be really useful when we're starving.
Every mark is a story. A voice trying to be heard across the silence. What were they trying to preserve?
A soft scraping sound echoes from a side passage. A figure emerges, robes dusty, face shadowed.
You should not be here. This place... it has a class of its own. A class three resonance anomaly. I have a class to teach about such things, but the Tonal Orders... they would not approve.
You still don't understand? We're not with the Orders. We're just exploring!

lines_after.dialogue: Exploring... yes. But this Hollow teaches its own lessons. The echoes here don't fade. They accumulate.
Accumulate how? Sound should dissipate.
Not here. The stone remembers. Sometimes... it replays.

line.dialogue: The Listener seems wary but knowledgeable. How should we engage?

choices.line: Apologize for the intrusion and ask politely about the ruins.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with scavenger instincts, ready to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The lattice has other plans. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Mention the Groundless Movement's interest in pre-Silencing truths.
choices.description: Pichit attempts to use the leg as a lattice probe, relying on monk wisdom

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Offer to share supplies in exchange for information.
choices.description: The monk steps forward with recording crystals, ready to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The Listener's study yields a revelation.
the monk loses control. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The Listener, introduced as Brother Kael, leads you deeper. The air grows colder. Crystalline formations pulse with faint, captured light.
This chamber... we call it the Archive. The echoes here are centuries old. Listen.
A faint, ghostly murmur fills the space—fragments of dead languages, the rustle of ancient crowds.
It's incredible! Is that... a market? A song?
Sounds like chaos. How do you write any of this down? It's just noise.
Not noise. Memory. The stone absorbed their final moments before the Silencing.
The structural integrity here is concerning. These supports shouldn't be holding. It's like the resonance itself is... reinforcing them.
A new sound cuts through the ancient whispers: the crunch of boots on gravel. A rugged figure steps from behind a stalagmite, crossbow leveled.

Well, look what the Lattice coughed up. A monk and his choir. This place is called the Whisper Vault in the surface trade. Latest fashion is selling these echoes to rich idiots in the floating cities.

lines_after.dialogue: You're standing in what the old maps called Hua Hin Province. Or what's left of it, buried under a mile of crystal.
You're desecrating a tomb! These echoes are sacred!
Sacred don't fill the belly. The Groundless talk about returning to the surface. I'm already here, making a living.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger is armed and claims territorial rights. The Monk is horrified. Tension crackles in the ancient air.

choices.line: Try to de-escalate. Propose a temporary truce to explore together.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the wall and listen with your bones, not your ears.

line.dialogue: Pichit guides your hand to a warm seam in the stone. "There — you feel her? A fishmonger, last sunrise before the flood. She was laughing.
The voices surge into a shrieking wall of sound. Malee yanks you back, ears bleeding. "Don't just grab at it — these aren't *your* memories to take!

choices.line: Challenge the Scavenger's claim. Argue that this knowledge belongs to everyone, per Groundless ideology.
choices.description: Ask the monk which memory lives deepest in the Archive's foundation stone.

line.dialogue: The monk kneels, pressing his forehead to the floor. "A child. Teaching her grandmother to whistle. That one has held for four hundred years. Joy roots deeper than grief.
The monk's jaw tightens and he says nothing. Chanida touches your arm. "He lost someone here. Don't push him — he'll tell us when the stone lets him.

choices.line: Side decisively with the Monk. Prepare to defend the site from 'desecration'.
choices.description: Hum a melody back into the wall and see if the Archive answers.

line.dialogue: A woman's voice rises from the limestone, harmonizing — then laughter, then a name spoken tenderly. Pichit whispers, "You just gave her back a moment she'd lost. That's rare.
The stone goes dead silent. Every echo stops at once. Malee mutters, "Brilliant — you've offended the entire Archive. Now we walk through a graveyard that won't even *murmur*.

lines_before.dialogue: In the deepest chamber of The Hollow, the air hums. The walls are not stone, but a fused latticework of ancient crystal and petrified machinery. At its center, a massive, cracked monolith pulses with a weak, arrhythmic light.
Well, the architectural salvage prices here are definitely zero. Because it's all junk. Glowy, hummy junk.
It's not junk! Can't you feel it? It's like... a heartbeat. A broken one.
A broken heartbeat usually means something is dead. Or dying. We should be cautious.
No... not dead. Silenced. This is a Resonance Anchor. From before. The Tonal Orders' charts... they're derived from its corpse. A copy of a corpse.
And the true song? The one the Listeners seek?
He looks run down, monk. Chasing ghosts. The real treasure's in the support struts. Pre-Silencing alloys. That's a fair price for this trip.
You speak of prices while standing in a cathedral of lost truth! The Anchor's true function... it didn't just map the Lattice. It harmonized with it. It could have prevented The Silencing.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger moves to pry a crystal node loose. The Monk steps in his way. The chamber's hum spikes painfully.

choices.line: Side with the Monk. Protect the artifact. (Appeal to wonder and preservation.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the Anchor's fractured surface and let the silence fill you.

line.dialogue: You feel it too — the pulse beneath the stillness. It remembers what it was.
Congratulations, you touched the creepy artifact. Now your hand is numb and we've learned nothing.

choices.line: Side with the Scavenger. Knowledge is dead if you are. (Appeal to pragmatism and survival.)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to hum the melody she swears she can hear emanating from the core.

line.dialogue: There — you hear it now? The Anchor is waking, stitching itself together note by note.
She's been humming for thirty seconds and now I have a headache. The Anchor looks the same.

choices.line: Attempt to mediate. There must be another way. (Risk alienating both to find a third path.)
choices.description: Demand the Monk explain what silenced it before anything else wakes up in this ruin.

line.dialogue: A Voice Cutter — one who severs songs from the world. They feared what this Anchor could summon if it sang freely.
I... I don't know. The memory refuses to surface. Whatever did this wanted even the knowing to die.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, grinding shiver runs through the chamber. Dust falls from the ceiling. The decision hangs in the air, heavier than stone.
The structural integrity is fluctuating. This place is reacting to the conflict.
Every choice here has a cost. What are we willing to pay for a ghost of a song?

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor's pulse has become a frantic, stuttering strobe. Cracks spiderweb across its surface. From the fissures, a distorted, multi-voiced whisper floods the chamber—not a song, but a scream of countless memories trapped in crystal.
It's not that it's angry... it's in pain! The Silencing... it wasn't an accident. It was a severance!
The Groundless Movement was right. The Lattice isn't a barrier, it's a wound! And the Tonal Orders are just... bandaging it with lies!
Since that day I first saw a Singer guide a ship... I never believed the charts were the whole truth. But this? This is madness.
Great. So the foundation of our world is a screaming, metaphysical injury. My faith in everything is officially bankrupt.
The memory cascade is overloading the chamber's stability. We have moments before it collapses, taking this truth with it.
Then we choose what survives. Do we let it die quietly? Or do we try to hear its final note?

line.dialogue: The central monolith fissures open, revealing a core of pure, chaotic resonance. To touch it is to risk being unmade by the truth. To leave it is to bury the past forever.

choices.line: Seal the chamber. Let the past rest. (Preserve the present stability, at the cost of truth.)
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use frequency mapping and decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.line: Record the resonance. Carry a fragment of the scream into the world. (A dangerous, incomplete truth.)
choices.description: Malee attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee is thwarted. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Resonate with it. Try to harmonize the final note. (Risk everything to understand, and perhaps heal, a fraction of the wound.)
choices.description: Have the monk focus crystal bowls on the unusual acoustics to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Exactly as the monk hoped. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the monk hits a wall. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_after.dialogue: The Hollow holds its breath. Then, light. a funeral shroud—erupts from the center, swallowing sound, sight, and self.
From that day... everything changed.
When the light fades, the chamber is still. Changed. The characters stand, forever altered by what they did, or did not do, in the face of the world's broken song.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market is a symphony of greed. The air thrums with the barter of a thousand voices, a chaotic hum that makes the very Lattice beneath the floating city shimmer uneasily.
Look at this place! The professors are really good at hiding secrets in plain noise. I bet the best rumors are the loudest ones.
Stay close. In this din, a pickpocket could sing an aria and you wouldn't notice. We need information, not trinkets.
Trinkets pay for information, Arthit. And judging by the stalls, the prices are reasonable. For now. Let's find our 'friend' before that changes.
Every voice adds to the lattice's resonance... and every silence within it speaks volumes. The merchant we seek must navigate both.
Ah! The intrepid explorers! Your reputation hums a pleasant tune. Come, come, my stall is a haven of quiet commerce.

lines_after.dialogue: The Open Frequency Map? A dangerous melody. The Tonal Orders would have my head for even whispering of it. It's... not for sale.
Everything has a price. Name it.
Perceptive! Let's say... a trade. A rumor for a rumor. I lost something precious. A crystal ledger. Find who took it, and we'll discuss maps.

line.dialogue: The merchant's 'lost' ledger is likely a test, or a trap. How to proceed?

choices.line: Agree to find the ledger. A straightforward trade.
choices.description: Approach the spice vendor with silver coins and ask about the professor's courier. *(15 words)

line.dialogue: Malee* — "The vendor's eyes flick left when she mentions the courier — there, behind the turmeric stacks, a boy in indigo.
Malee* — "I showed too much silver too fast. The vendor's smile hardens and she waves me off like a persistent fly.

choices.line: Press him for details about the map first. What makes it so 'open'?
choices.description: Climb to the market's second-floor gallery to map escape routes before approaching anyone. *(15 words)

line.dialogue: Arthit* — "From above I see three alleys, two Watch patrols, and one woman who's been watching us since we entered.
Arthit* — "A roofer catches me on his ladder and shouts thief — now half the market's looking up at our party.

choices.line: Refuse and look for other leads in the market. His smile is too sharp.
choices.description: Close your eyes

lines_before.dialogue: The party's inquiries attract the wrong kind of attention. Near a stall selling cracked resonator crystals, a figure with sky-salt worn leather intercepts them.
Heard you're askin' about open frequencies. You're gonna be sorry for sticking your noses in Tonal business.
We seek only knowledge. We offer no conflict.
Knowledge is conflict, mate. That map you want? It's a ghost song. My crew... we chased it. Now they're echoes in the static.
How tragically entrepreneurial. Let me guess, you 'found' it and want to sell?
Your regret resonates deeply. You followed a frequency into silence.
Aye. And I'm sorry I'm late to warn you. The merchant's playing you. That ledger? It's a pirate's log. My log. He stole it from my dead navigator.

lines_after.dialogue: So the map is real? Where is it?
Encoded in the log's crystal lattice. But it's raw, untamed frequency. You need a Singer to read it true. The merchant can't. He needs you to decode it for him.
A trap within a trade. We are caught between a thief and a pirate.

line.dialogue: The pirate's claim changes everything. What's the next move?

choices.line: Confront the merchant with the pirate's story. Force a truce.
choices.description: Slam your palm on the crate between you and lean into the bandit's space, demanding the real price

line.dialogue: Name your true cost — no riddles, no rackets — and we'll weigh it honestly.
Your posture betrays you. You're stalling because you don't actually have what you claim.

choices.line: Side with the pirate. Recover his log and cut the merchant out.
choices.description: Flick a chipped coin onto the crate and ask where he "found" a military-grade frequency map

line.dialogue: That scratch on the casing — Sector 9 requisition stamp. So which checkpoint did you scavenge this from, or which officer did you bribe?
Counterfeit polish on a counterfeit coin. Even your currency lies as smoothly as you do.

choices.line: Play both sides. Promise the log to the merchant, but secretly arrange to meet the pirate with it later.
choices.description: Signal Arthit to stay quiet and tail the bandit when he retreats, hoping he leads you to his supplier

line.dialogue: Let him think he's lost our interest. Feet remember what mouths refuse to say.
He spotted my reflection in the hull plating. Clever for a scavenger — annoying for us.

lines_before.dialogue: In a secluded corner of the market, the air thick with spice and secrets, the Trade Negotiator spreads a worn silk cloth over a crate. The party crowds close.
So, what do you think about... genuine Lattice harmonics? The kind not found on any sanctioned chart.
You have the Open Frequency Map? Show us!
All in good time. My associate here is only interested in one form of currency. Silence.
Figures. Information this dangerous doesn't come for coin. It comes for favors, or blood.
Pichit, I think that's the one. The pirate from the earlier altercation. He's watching from the balcony.
A map that shows the Lattice's true voice... not the controlled frequencies of the Orders. It would change everything.
Precisely. And for the right price, it's yours. But we must be quick. The market's hum is already distorting the subtle details.

lines_after.dialogue: Before Pichit can decide, a sharp whistle cuts through the din. The Sky Pirate drops from the balcony, landing with a heavy thud.
Think that's right, do you? That map's spoken for. By me.
Ah. A prior claim emerges. How... unfortunate for your negotiations.

line.dialogue: The pirate demands the map. The merchant looks ready to sell to the highest bidder.

choices.line: [Pay the Merchant's Price] Offer the exorbitant sum in crystal shards to close the deal instantly.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing lattice storms to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
The gamble fails. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.line: [Appeal to Greed] Propose a partnership: the map's value is in copies, not a single sale.
choices.description: Malee attempts to harness harmonic feedback, relying on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee loses control. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: [Call the Bluff] Challenge the pirate's claim openly, risking a fight in the crowded market.
choices.description: Have the merchant focus valuable goods on the merchant guilds to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: Exactly as the merchant hoped. Hidden leverage shifts the balance.
Defeat. His network delivers bad intelligence.

lines_before.dialogue: Tension crackles like static. The pirate's crew emerges from the crowd, while the merchant nervously rolls up the silk cloth.
Why were you gone so long, merchant? Thought you could slip this treasure to these soft-skinned scholars?
We're not giving it up! This is for everyone, not just your gang!
He doesn't want it for navigation. He wants it for extortion. Control the frequencies, control the sky.
The market guards are turning a blind eye. This is about to get very loud.
This map is a whisper from the world before The Silencing. To use it for power... is to repeat the past.
My offer retracts in ten seconds! Who will guarantee my safety? My profit?
I don't want it from you. I'll take it from their corpses. Seize them!

lines_after.dialogue: As the brawl erupts, crates overturn and the market's chaotic symphony reaches a crescendo. Pichit's hand closes around the silk-wrapped map.
The Lattice sings beneath all this noise. A true Singer... could hear it.
In the chaos, a choice: escape with the map, or try to end this here and now. The consequences will resonate far beyond this market.

line.dialogue: The map is in your grasp, but the pirate and his crew block the escape routes. The merchant is fleeing.

choices.line: [Fade into Chaos] Use the market's noise and panic as cover to slip away with the map.
choices.description: Smash the lantern against the tent pole, plunging everything into darkness.

line.dialogue: Grab it and run — they're blind as worms now!" Chanida shouts, already moving.
You fool, that was our only light — now we can't find it either," Arthit snarls.

choices.line: [Shatter the Monopoly] Tear the map and scatter the pieces into the crowd, destroying the secret but freeing it.
choices.description: Draw your blade and press its edge against the bandit's throat, demanding he name his buyer.

line.dialogue: Fine — it's the Harbormaster, he pays double for those charts," the bandit whimpers, sweat pooling under your steel.
You think I fear a merchant's shake-hand grip on that blade?" the bandit laughs, twisting your wrist until it cracks.

choices.line: [Confront the Frequency] Attempt to 'Sing' a disruptive harmonic using the map, hoping to overload the pirate's resonators.
choices.description: Whisper to Malee to circle behind while you keep the bandit talking about his "employer."

line.dialogue: His eyes haven't left your face — he doesn't even see me," Malee breathes, knife already at the bandit's belt.
She moved too early — he spotted her reflection in the glass," Arthit hisses, as the bandit wheels around with a grin.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hollow breathes. Cold, mineral-scented air flows through the cavern, carrying faint whispers that seem to cling to the ancient, carved walls. Your lantern light catches the faint glitter of embedded crystals in the basalt.
Look at these markings! They're not Tonal Order script. They're older. Much older. My mom told me about it already—pre-Silencing ruins in the deep islands.
Great. Ancient ruins. Probably full of ancient traps. I had a bad dream about caves like this last night. Coincidence? I think not.
The echo pattern here is... irregular. It doesn't match any resonance frequency I know. We should proceed with extreme caution.
Yet there's a harmony to it. Listen—the drip of water, the shift of stone. It's not random. It's a conversation the world is having with itself, forgotten by everyone but this place.

Ahead, the tunnel widens into a chamber. Two figures are illuminated by a single, flickering glow-crystal. One kneels by the wall, tracing symbols. The other stands, arms crossed, watching your approach.
You should not be here. This place... it sings of truths the Orders have buried.
Now, now, Brother. Visitors are just unexpected business opportunities! Welcome to the Hollow. I'm sure we can find something of mutual value.

lines_after.dialogue: The good Brother here is studying the 'true song' of the Lattice. Me? I'm looking for something more tangible. An artifact. A map. Something that tells you where the Lattice is thin... and passage is free.
He seeks the Open Frequency Map. A legend. A chart of natural, unregulated pathways through the crystal. The Tonal Orders would burn this entire island to keep it secret.
Let me guess. You want us to find it for you? That’s really easy to guess! Everyone in a cave wants someone else to do the digging.

line.dialogue: The Merchant smiles. The Monk looks pained. The ancient chamber holds its breath, waiting for your response.

choices.text: Agree to look for the Map. (Promise the Merchant aid for a share of profit.)
choices.description: Direct Chanida to trace the anomalous signal using singer voice

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
The lattice has other plans. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: Promise the Monk you'll safeguard any truth found. (Align with the Listeners' purpose.)
choices.description: Malee channels scavenger instincts toward the cave echoes, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee loses control. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Refuse both. Your mission is exploration, not treasure hunting or heresy. (Proceed alone.)
choices.description: Have the monk risk using prayers to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Crystal bowls shatter in harmonic sympathy.
the monk is thwarted. The monastery's countermeasures drown them in noise.

lines_before.dialogue: Deeper in The Hollow, the air grows colder. The echoes now take longer to return, as if swallowed by the dark. Strange, symmetrical carvings cover the walls, depicting figures with instruments aimed at a crystalline sky.
I feel uncomfortable. These carvings... they show resonance technology, but used differently. Not for parting the Lattice, but for... communicating with it.
This whole chamber is a resonator! Look at the parabolic curves. If we hummed the right note...
Don't. Just don't. My unease is now a physical cramp. That Merchant back there? He’s only interested in what this place can buy him. You’re gonna be sorry for leaving me with that vibe.

But what if the Map isn't a chart? What if it's a state? A frequency one attunes *to*, not a path one reads? The Monk seeks understanding. The Merchant seeks commodity. Both miss the song for the notes.
A low hum begins, not from your party, but from the walls themselves. The crystals in the ceiling glow faintly. From a side passage, the Listener Monk stumbles into the chamber, looking frantic.
You activated it? No... it's the alignment. The island's drift... it's causing a natural resonance. The chamber is remembering.

The hum coalesces into a ghostly, overlapping chorus of voices—fragments of a pre-Silencing broadcast. Words are indistinct, but the tone is one of urgent warning. Then, a clear, mechanical click echoes from the tunnel behind the Monk.

lines_after.dialogue: A fascinating security system! Triggered by celestial alignment. My associates just helped it along.

The Trade Negotiator steps into the light, flanked by two toughs with rivet-guns. He gestures to the now-glowing central dais of the chamber, where ghostly lines of light are sketching a complex, three-dimensional pattern in the air.
The Open Frequency Map. Not parchment. A resonant echo-lith. And it's priming for a full broadcast. The Tonal Orders' patrols will detect this from three islands away. We have minutes, not hours.
You fool! You'll draw them here! They will scorch The Hollow to silence this!

line.dialogue: The Map's spectral light pulses. The Merchant's crew aims their weapons. The Monk pleads with his eyes. The ancient warning chorus swells.

choices.text: Fight the Merchant's crew. Secure the Map by force. (Direct confrontation.)
choices.description: Press your palms against the parabolic walls and hum a single sustained note, 15 words

line.dialogue: The geometry just answered me — I can feel the harmonic node where the Map lives.
Stop it. Whatever you woke up is crawling up my spine and I can't make it leave.

choices.text: Try to deactivate or disrupt the resonant echo-lith. Silence the broadcast. (Technical solution.)
choices.description: Ask Pichit to explain what he means by "state" while keeping your distance from the walls, 15 words

line.dialogue: A state — like grief, like thirst. The Map isn't showing you where to go. It's what you become when you arrive.
He's spiraling. Whatever this chamber is doing to us, it started with him first.

choices.text: Let the Map broadcast. Use the chaos and the Orders' imminent arrival as a diversion to escape with the Monk. (Accept the danger.)
choices.description: Examine the floor carvings for the oldest erosion marks — the first resonance etched here, 15 words

line.dialogue: These grooves weren't carved. They were *sung* into the stone, over centuries, by voices I'll never hear.
You're reading erosion patterns that don't exist. The chamber is feeding you interpretations now.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the Hollow, the party finds a chamber where ancient machinery hums with a faint, persistent frequency.
This is... a resonance stabilizer. Pre-Silencing. Its song is pure, untainted by the Orders' charts.
So the Tonal Orders are lying? Their maps are just... wrong?
Not wrong. Manipulated. Controlled. This device proves there are open frequencies anyone could use.
Anyone's okay. Whoever finds this could navigate freely. That's why the merchant wants it buried.
The truth doesn't belong to any one guild. It belongs to the world. We should keep it.
A shadow falls across the entrance. The Trade Negotiator stands there, his friendly smile now a tight grimace.
I heard the echoes of your discovery. A dangerous tune. The Orders pay well for silence.

lines_after.dialogue: My duty was to study, not to conceal. But the truth... it is a heavy thing to carry.
We carry it together. The Lattice's song should be for all, not just those who can pay.
The merchant's eyes narrow. He does not move, but the tension in the chamber vibrates like a plucked string.

line.dialogue: The merchant offers a deal: destroy the stabilizer and receive a fortune, or walk away with the truth and face the Orders' wrath.

choices.text: Accept the deal. Destroy the device, take the wealth, and leave the Hollow quietly.
choices.description: Smash the stabilizer before anyone else can exploit it, 15 words

line.dialogue: ** "I've seen what forbidden tools do to people who keep them — this ends now.
** "The casing absorbed the strike. It *wants* to be found.

choices.text: Refuse the deal. Secure the stabilizer and try to negotiate a peaceful exit with the monk's help.
choices.description: Quietly copy the stabilizer's frequency charts into your own journal

line.dialogue: ** "If the Orders come for this, we'll already have what matters — the real pathways.
** "The ink runs the moment I trace the first line. It's warded against copying.

choices.text: Defy him outright. Activate the stabilizer now, broadcasting the open frequency to anyone listening.
choices.description: Confront the nearest Tonal Order elder tonight with the device as proof

line.dialogue: ** "They'll either confess or try to silence us — either way, the lie cracks open.
** "The elder smiled before I even finished speaking. They've been waiting for someone to find this.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber thrums with escalating resonance. Crystals in the walls begin to glow, reacting to the party's choice.
You'll regret that you defied the Orders. Their ships are already converging. I have work to do—ensuring you don't leave.
Work. Always work for profit. But we got the answer now. The lattice wants to sing freely.
The whole cave is lighting up! It's like the island itself is waking up!
The structural integrity... If the frequency peaks, the Hollow might collapse. We need to stabilize it or escape.
The ancient song... it's merging with the Lattice's current hum. A harmony long forgotten.
Can you promise me that sharing this truth will make a better world? No. But we must try.
A deep, foundational tone shakes the cavern. From outside, the distinct hum of Resonance Ships approaches.

lines_after.dialogue: The stabilizer's light pulses wildly, casting long shadows. The merchant retreats, shouting orders to unseen allies.
The Open Frequency Map isn't a chart. It's a state of being. The Lattice is remembering.
So we fight? Or we run? Or we... sing?

line.dialogue: The Tonal Orders' ships block the exit. The stabilizer is at critical resonance. The Hollow's structure is failing.

choices.text: Sabotage the stabilizer. Create a controlled collapse to block the Orders' entry and escape through a secondary tunnel.
choices.description: Channel the frequency through the crystalline walls to stabilize the cave, 14 words

line.dialogue: The resonance is harmonizing — the walls are holding, but barely, so move quickly!
The lattice is fracturing — collapse is imminent, we have maybe thirty seconds before this whole chamber buries us!

choices.text: Harness the frequency. Use the rising resonance to temporarily disrupt the ships' crystals and fight your way out.
choices.description: Shatter the central frequency crystal with a precise strike before it peaks, 13 words

line.dialogue: It's dimming — the glow is fading, the island itself is exhaling, we did it!
The crystal fragmented wrong — the frequency is scattering everywhere, the cave is screaming, run RUN!

choices.text: Broadcast the song. Let the stabilizer reach full resonance, sending the open frequency across the Lattice, and trust the Listeners to protect you.
choices.description: Grab the merchant and force him to reveal the Orders' fallback signal, 13 words

line.dialogue: He's talking — says there's a secondary transmitter on the northern ridge, we can end this properly.
Bite his tongue clean in half — loyal to the end, and now we've got nothing but blood on our hands and no answers.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard stretches before you—a jagged landscape of broken resonance ships, their crystal hulls cracked and silent. The air thrums with the percussive rhythm of salvage hammers and grinding engines, creating a harsh acoustic blanket that smothers the Lattice's natural hum.
Well, this is charming. A graveyard for dead dreams. I thought it was okay. At least the Tonal Orders won't bother us here—too much noise pollution for their delicate ears.
Keep your voices low. This acoustic chaos makes it hard to hear approaching threats. Anyone's okay to approach, but we should be cautious.
Look at all this salvage! We could fix up our ship with half this junk. Anywhere's okay to start digging, right Pichit?
Every broken resonator here once sang a path through the Lattice. Now they're just metal ghosts. Their silence speaks volumes about what we've lost.
A figure emerges from between two gutted ship hulls—a skycity resident in practical work clothes, their eyes scanning your group with wary curiosity.
You're not from the regular salvage crews. What brings you to the scrap edge?
We're looking for information. And possibly parts. The Tonal Orders' charts... have gaps.

lines_after.dialogue: Gaps, huh? You sound like Groundless talk. Careful who you say that to around here. The Tonal Orders have ears everywhere—even in the noise.
Of course they do. Because why would the universe allow anything to be simple?
The Lattice remembers every path ever sung through it. The Orders just write down what they choose to hear.
The villager glances nervously at a nearby watchtower before leaning closer, their voice dropping despite the ambient clatter.

line.dialogue: The villager whispers: 'I know someone who might help. But it's risky. Where do you want to start?'

choices.text: Ask directly about the Groundless Movement (Charismatic approach)
choices.description: Sift through the shattered resonators for one still humming with residual frequency, 15 words

line.dialogue: This one still carries a ghost of a signal—hold it to your ear, you can almost hear where it once pointed.
Nothing but dead static. Touch it too long and the corrosion gets under your skin—literally.

choices.text: Offer to trade for information (Negotiation approach)
choices.description: Map the acoustic shadows between debris to find a sheltered frequency-dead zone for safe passage, 15 words

line.dialogue: There—between those two collapsed arrays. The interference cancels itself out. We move through there, nothing hears us.
Wrong calculation. The shadows shift every few minutes and now we're standing in a resonance hotspot that screams our presence.

choices.text: Search the scrapyard for clues first (Investigative approach)
choices.description: Scrape harmonic dust from a corroded tuning fork and sprinkle it along the ground to reveal hidden pathways, 15 words

line.dialogue: The dust is lighting up like a roadmap! These graves aren't random—someone arranged them in a frequency pattern.
Congratulations, you've just coated the floor in glowing dust that shows exactly where we've been. Any tracker within a mile can follow our footprints now.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the villager's lead, you arrive at a makeshift workshop carved into the side of a dismantled ore-hauler. Inside, a trade negotiator adjusts a resonator calibration tool with practiced ease, their smile not quite reaching their eyes.
Ah, visitors! Always a pleasure. I hear you're interested in... alternative navigation methods. How do you write that down in your logs without attracting attention?
We haven't written anything yet. That's why we're here. The official charts omit certain... resonant frequencies.
He means what he says! We need real maps, not the censored junk the Orders sell!
Passionate. I admire that. But knowledge has value. Especially knowledge that could get my floating-city permits revoked.
Let me guess: you want payment. Because of course you do. Could you please write it down for me? The exact price before we waste more time?
Every transaction leaves an echo in the Lattice. What we trade here will resonate beyond this scrap metal shell.

The merchant's smile tightens. They gesture to a workbench where strange, hand-drawn charts sit beside Tonal Order manuals. The differences are subtle but significant—additional harmonic notations in the margins.

lines_after.dialogue: These annotations... let's call them 'supplementary frequencies.' They correspond to natural Lattice formations the Orders don't chart. How do you write something that's supposed to remain unwritten?
Those look like resonance patterns from before The Silencing. Where did you get these?
Let's just say certain Listeners have... diverged from their order's strict teachings. They're serious about rediscovering what was lost. He means it!
Outside, the scrapyard's noise shifts—a section of hammering falls silent. The merchant's eyes dart to the doorway, their casual demeanor evaporating.

line.dialogue: The merchant gathers the charts hastily: 'Tonal Order inspectors. They make rounds. We need to move this conversation.'

choices.text: Hide the evidence and play dumb (Deceptive approach)
choices.description: Slide a pouch of coin across the table without counting it, meeting the merchant's eyes steadily, 15 words

line.dialogue: That's what I have. The maps are worth more to us than gold right now.
I... may have miscounted. The pouch sounds lighter than I thought when it lands.

choices.text: Confront the inspectors directly (Bold approach)
choices.description: Lean close and whisper that the Cartographer's Guild sent you, using the name you overheard at the teahouse, 15 words

line.dialogue: Niran vouched for your discretion. We're trusting you the same way he did.
Wait—the name was Phrom, not Niran—I've said the wrong thing, haven't I?

choices.text: Use the scrapyard's acoustic chaos to create a distraction (Creative approach)
choices.description: Pull out the fragment of censored map you already have and point to the redacted district with deliberate slowness, 15 words

line.dialogue: Someone went to trouble blacking this out. We'd like to see what's underneath.
We found this but can't read it—actually, maybe we shouldn't have shown you this.

lines_before.dialogue: In the heart of the scrapyard, the Trade Negotiator stands before a rusted Resonance Ship core, his smile a polished blade.
This salvage? A treasure. But my charts for its resonator? Priceless. You understand. Business.
Give it to me! We need that core to fix our ship, and your 'charts' smell like last week's profits!
Chanida, caution. He's serious. This negotiation is a lattice of its own—every word a potential fracture.
Look at him. That smile. I was cheated by a merchant with that same grin once. Left me with a resonator that hummed nothing but regret.
Every transaction is a resonance. What frequency does your profit vibrate at, Negotiator? Harmony or dissonance?
Philosophical. Adorable. But my frequency is simple: the clink of coin. The core is yours... if you retrieve something for me from the deeper wreckage.

lines_after.dialogue: The Negotiator's request hangs in the metallic air. A Skycity Resident, lurking nearby, overhears and shuffles closer, eyes wide with a mix of fear and curiosity.
You're going into the old Listeners' cache? The Groundless whisper about that place. They say it holds sounds... pure sounds, before the Orders twisted them.
Whispers. Great. So we're fetching a trinket for a swindler based on rumors from a movement that wants to tear down the cities. Bring it on.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator offers a deal: retrieve a 'Tonal Prism' from a dangerous, unstable wreck. The Groundless Resident hints it might be a key to natural resonance. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Accept the deal directly. Secure the core now, retrieve the prism later. (Fast, but you remain indebted.)
choices.description: Slide the salvage crate forward while maintaining unbroken eye contact with the merchant. 13 words

line.dialogue: I've placed our offer on the table — now show us these resonance charts before my patience corrodes.
He barely glanced at the crate — we're amateurs to him, and he knows we'll beg before we walk.

choices.line: Investigate the Groundless whispers first. Learn what the prism truly is. (Slow, risks the Negotiator's patience.)
choices.description: Lean close and whisper that rival salvagers mentioned his charts were outdated. 12 words

line.dialogue: That twitch in his eye — I've seen it before. The doubt is planted, now we squeeze until he negotiates honestly.
He laughed in my face and said our 'rival salvagers' died three cycles ago — I just handed him every advantage.

choices.line: Challenge the Negotiator. Demand the core as fair trade for information you already possess. (Risky, could turn him hostile.)
choices.description: Let Chanida snatch the salvage back and threaten to find another merchant entirely. 12 words

line.dialogue: His smirk collapsed the moment I lifted the crate — turns out this port only has one resonance chart vendor
The resonance turns hostile. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The unstable wreck groans, a symphony of rust and strained crystal. Inside, the Tonal Prism glows, casting fractured light patterns on the decaying walls.
Structural integrity is failing. There's a high chance this entire section collapses if we mishandle the extraction.
That glow... this cute and this inviting... how could you pass it up? It's like the Lattice itself is singing to us!
It's singing 'get rich or die trying' for the Negotiator. But... I'm not finished yet! The Groundless resident said this could prove the Orders manipulate resonance. That's worth more than coin.
A prism that splits sound into its pure components. If the Groundless are right, this is a fragment of the world's true voice, buried by the Silencing.
A sudden, violent shudder runs through the wreck. The Negotiator's voice crackles over a comm-link, impatient. The Skycity Resident appears at a broken hatch, beckoning urgently.
The Orders! They've traced the deal! They're coming! You must choose—the prism for profit, or the prism for proof!

lines_after.dialogue: The scrapyyard becomes a stage for the climax. The wreck trembles. The Negotiator demands his prize. The Tonal Orders' resonance ships hum in the distance. The Groundless hope burns in the resident's eyes.
This moment... it resonates with every choice we've made. The frequency of our actions will now shape the silence or the song of what comes next.

line.dialogue: The wreck is collapsing. The Orders are approaching. You hold the Tonal Prism. What is its final destination?

choices.line: Fulfill the deal. Give the prism to the Negotiator, take the core, and flee. (Secures your ship, but reinforces the monopolies.)
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with tonal knowledge to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
A costly mistake by Pichit. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Hand the prism to the Groundless resident. Let them use it as evidence. (Empowers the movement, but you lose the core and gain the Orders' wrath.)
choices.description: Have Malee focus leg resonance on the scavenger gangs to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Malee hits a wall. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.line: Use the prism yourself. Try to resonate with it directly, to part the Lattice and escape without either side. (A Singer's gamble. Could unlock new power, or shatter everything.)
choices.description: Ask the merchant to listen for the ghost ship's echo, drawing on information network

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
The gamble fails. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hollow swallows sound and light. Your party's footsteps are muffled by centuries of crystalline dust. Strange, inverted echoes bounce from the cavern walls—a sound that seems to come from behind you, then ahead.
The acoustics here are... wrong. The resonance charts didn't prepare us for this. Every reading is unstable.
Wrong means interesting! Look at these carvings—they're pre-Silencing! This could change everything we know!
Or get us crushed by a collapsing ruin. The Tonal Orders would have sealed this place for a reason. Probably a good one.
The reason is control. Knowledge confined is power preserved. But these stones... they remember a song.
A low hum vibrates through the cavern floor. From a side passage, a figure in simple robes emerges—Listener Monk, his face illuminated by a faintly glowing crystal.
You should not be here. The Hollow's song is... agitated. It remembers the ship.
What ship?

lines_after.dialogue: The Echo of the Lost Ship. A Resonance vessel that tried to pierce the Lattice here, decades ago. It... resonated wrong. Its frequency is still trapped in the stone.
A harmonic ghost? That could explain the unstable readings. But if it's dangerous...
Listener, I have work to do. We need to understand what happened here. Can you promise me you'll share what you know of this echo?
I... I have work I have to do as well. My order studies, we do not interfere. But the truth... the truth here may be too important to silence.
Don't change the subject! Is that ghost ship why the air tastes like metal?

line.dialogue: The Monk hesitates, torn between his vows and the mystery. How do you proceed?

choices.line: Appeal to his duty: 'Your work is to listen. Help us listen to this echo.'
choices.description: Pichit uses monk wisdom to trace the anomalous signal near the unusual acoustics

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The lattice has other plans. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.line: Offer a trade: 'Share your knowledge, and we'll share what we find in the ruins.'
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using singer voice to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. She hears something no one else can.
A costly mistake by Chanida. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Press on without him: 'We'll find the echo ourselves. Stay if you must.'
choices.description: The monk uses prayers to listen for the ghost ship's echo near the forbidden history

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The Listener's study yields a revelation.
the monk fails. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: Guided by the Monk's conflicted directions, you descend deeper. The air grows colder, and the echoes solidify into a faint, mournful drone—the dying note of an engine.
There. The central chamber. The ship's resonator core impacted the wall. Its final frequency is etched into the crystal.
Before you lies a spectacle: half a Resonance ship's prow fused with the cavern wall, crystalline growths consuming it. And looting it—a Sky Pirate, her coat patched with Lattice shards.
Well, well. Tourists. This scrap's spoken for. The core's frequency's worth a fortune to the right... independent navigator.
A pirate. Of course. Drawn to shiny, unstable things like a moth to a flame that's about to explode.
Is that the lost ship's core? I love it!! It's like the heart of a story frozen in time!
That 'heart' is radiating chaotic harmonics. If she destabilizes it further while prying it loose...
You're not just looting. You're listening. You know this frequency is unique.

lines_after.dialogue: Sharp. Yeah. This note... it's a key. Opens paths the Tonal Orders buried. But it's fragile. One wrong touch and the whole chamber sings us to dust.
Please! You must stop! This is a tomb, not a treasury! I'm really sorry, but I cannot let you defile this memory.
A key to what? What did the ship find before it fell?
Why tell you? You've got a monk and a bunch of scholars. I've got a cutter and a deadline.
Are you kidding? We're standing in pre-Silencing history! With you here, I'm the luckiest person in the world! A real live pirate AND an archaeological mystery!

line.dialogue: The Pirate's tool hovers near the unstable core. The Monk is poised to intervene. The echo wails softly. What's your move?

choices.line: De-escalate: 'Let's all step back. No one needs to get hurt by a ghost.'
choices.description: Forge a temporary alliance with the bandit to safely extract the resonator core together.

line.dialogue: Fine, tourist. You hold it steady while I crack the housing — but touch my share and I gut you.
Backstabbing already? I knew better than to trust monastery hands near anything worth coin.

choices.line: Negotiate with the Pirate: 'Share what the key opens, and we might let you take a smaller sample.'
choices.description: Channel resonance through the monk's prayer beads to stabilize the core before anyone touches it.

line.dialogue: The harmonic frequency is aligning — everyone stay still. Even you, pirate, unless you want to explode.
That ringing — it's destabilizing! The core's screaming louder than my beads can sing!

choices.line: Attempt to safely resonate with the core yourself, using your innate sense as a Singer to calm the echo before she can.
choices.description: Let Chanida study the core's inscriptions to decode the ship's final transmission before deciding ownership.

line.dialogue: These glyphs are a captain's last log — 'the resonance was never meant to be weaponized.' We need to hear this.
I tried to read it too fast — the symbols are rearranging, and something inside the core just woke up.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in The Hollow, the air is heavy with ancient dust and the scent of ozone. The strange, looping echoes from the crystal formations have grown louder, forming a dissonant chorus.
Did you hear that?! It's like the walls are whispering. I'm the luckiest person in the world to be here!
Or the most doomed. That 'luck' usually precedes something trying to eat us.
The acoustic anomalies are increasing. This entire cavern system may be acting as a natural resonator for... something. I need some time to calibrate my instruments.
You heard that, didn't you? The buried frequency. It is not the Lattice's song. It is... a plea. A ghost note from the subplot_haunted_ship.
A plea? Then our duty is to listen. To understand the silence that followed the Silencing.
Enough poetry! The big chamber up ahead—that's where the real prize is. The ship's core resonator. My crew's been tracking its echo for months.
A low, grinding hum vibrates through the stone underfoot. From a fissure ahead, a sickly green light pulses in time with the sound.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The strange light from the fissure intensifies, casting long, dancing shadows.
Well, I'm in a good mood. Probably because we're not dead yet.
We proceed with gratitude for the path, however unclear.

line.dialogue: The fissure leads to a vast, dark chamber. The source of the haunting echo lies within, but the way is treacherous.

choices.text: Follow the Bandit's lead. He knows the hidden frequencies to dampen the unstable crystals.
choices.description: Have Arthit focus captain experience on the cave echoes to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Exactly as Arthit hoped. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
Arthit fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Trust the Monk's reverence. Move slowly, attuning to the natural harmonics to find safe passage.
choices.description: Chanida steps forward with frequency mapping, ready to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Chanida fails. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.text: Send a resonance pulse ahead. Provoke a reaction to map the chamber's dangers—and whatever lies within.
choices.description: Have the pirate focus smuggling routes on the forbidden history to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: the pirate's expertise pays off. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the pirate's resolve isn't enough. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber is the heart of The Hollow. In its center, half-buried in crystalline growths, lies the shattered hull of the subplot_haunted_ship. Its central resonator crystal glows with captured, agonized sound.
There it is! The motherlode! Can you catch it? The frequency that thing's putting out could crack a city's defenses!
No... it is a wound. The final moments of the crew, trapped in resonant feedback during The Silencing. To take it is to consume a scream.

The structural harmonics are catastrophic. One wrong note and this entire cavern—this entire island—could undergo sympathetic fragmentation. I didn't catch what you said, Bandit, if you think this is just loot.
It's... singing. But it hurts to hear. Can I take a break for a moment? My head is splitting.
Told you. The luck ran out. That crystal isn't a treasure; it's a tombstone with a built-in alarm.
This is the truth the Tonal Orders buried. Not just a lost ship, but the moment of death itself, preserved. We must choose what to do with this echo.
The crystal's light flares, projecting flickering, silent images of the ship's last panic against the walls. The hum rises to a deafening whine.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber shakes. Dust and shards of ancient crystal rain from the ceiling. The decision ripples through The Hollow.
The echo is released, or contained, or stolen. The story of this place is now ours to tell.
In the new silence, or the new song, the fate of the subplot_haunted_ship is finally resolved.

line.dialogue: The haunted resonator crystal pulses, a heart of trapped agony. The chamber groans. You must act.

choices.text: Shatter the crystal. End the echo's suffering with a sharp, discordant note. It is a mercy.
choices.description: Shield your ears and let Chanida isolate the frequency pattern with her tuner.

line.dialogue: I've got the waveform isolated — it's a distress call encoded in harmonics, repeating on a seven-second loop.
The pitch keeps slipping — my tuner's cracking, and now I'm bleeding from my left ear.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize and release the captured memory. Let the final note fade naturally into the Lattice's song. It is a requiem.
choices.description: Order Arthit to map the structural harmonics before anyone touches the signal.

line.dialogue: Three load-bearing resonance points — if we dampen them in sequence, the hull won't collapse when we extract the data.
I misread the third harmonic — the ceiling just shifted two centimeters. We're out of time.

choices.text: Harness the crystal. Use its painful power to overload the local Lattice, creating a permanent safe passage or a devastating weapon. It is a theft.
choices.description: Let the Monk reach into the frequency with open awareness, feeling the crew's final moments.

line.dialogue: They were calm at the end. The captain sang them to sleep — I can hear her voice beneath the noise, and she is showing me where the core is.
The grief hit me like a wall — I saw all forty-seven faces at once and my legs gave out. I cannot go back in there.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hum with a low, controlled frequency. Endless crystalline shelves hold etched resonance records, their facets catching the soft glow of floating lumens. The air smells of ozone and old parchment.
Keep your voices down. The acoustics here are designed to carry the slightest whisper to the overseers. We're looking for the cartography wing—the pre-Silencing deep lattice surveys.
Of course. The one section the Tonal Orders probably doesn't want anyone poking through. Let's just hope the 'oversight' is more interested in their own echoes.
I see it! Row 7-Gamma. The shelves look... older. The crystals are cloudier.
Each cloud is a story untold, a frequency unplayed since the world fell quiet. We must listen to more than what's etched.
As you approach the ancient stacks, a figure peels away from the shadows—a woman with sharp eyes and a scar cutting through the resonator tattoo on her neck.
Well, look what the static dragged in. You're not the usual dusty scholars. You got the look of folks hunting something that don't wanna be found.
We're just researchers. Historical resonance patterns. My girlfriend gets jealous if I spend too long with dusty old crystals, so we should be quick.

lines_after.dialogue: Ha! Cute. I know what you're after. The deep lattice maps. The ones that show the old Singer paths, not the Tonal Order's 'safe' routes. My crew... we've used a few. For a price.
And what's your price? Besides the obvious risk of getting us all arrested for heresy?

Information for information. You find what you're looking for down here, you share the frequency of the third vault. The one they say holds the First Chime. The mother of all resonators. My captain was heart-broken when her last lead went silent.

line.dialogue: The sky pirate offers a dangerous trade: her knowledge of hidden access points in the Archives for a share of any 'First Chime' frequencies we find.

choices.text: Agree cautiously. The information could be vital, and we can be selective about what we share later.
choices.description: Reach into the crystalline shelf and carefully extract the oldest cloud by its visible harmonic thread, 15 words

line.dialogue: I can feel it humming against my palm — this frequency hasn't decayed at all.
The thread snapped and the cloud dispersed — whatever story that was, it's gone now.

choices.text: Refuse outright. Dealing with pirates inside the Archives is too great a risk.
choices.description: Hum a low matching tone toward Row 7-Gamma to coax the dormant clouds into resonance, 15 words

line.dialogue: They're waking — listen, each one is a different key, a century apart in pitch.
Wrong harmonic. The clouds flinched deeper into the crystal and now they won't surface again.

choices.text: Stall. Ask for a specific sample of her data first to verify its worth.
choices.description: Press your ear directly against the shelf surface and listen for which cloud is whispering loudest, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — behind the third panel — someone is still *talking* in there, mid-sentence, centuries stale.
Nothing but my own heartbeat

lines_before.dialogue: Guided by the pirate's whispered directions, you find a forgotten sub-chamber. The crystals here are blackened, as if scorched by a terrible sound. The air is cold and still.
This place... it's been acoustically sealed. Contained. They didn't just archive these records; they tried to bury them.
There's no one else down here. Just us and the ghosts of frequencies.
Not ghosts. Memories. The Lattice remembers every note ever played upon it. We live near each other, the past and the present, separated only by our willingness to listen.
Poetic. Let's hope the past isn't contagious. These data crystals look unstable.
As Arthit carefully interfaces a reader with one of the less-damaged crystals, a haunting, fragmented harmonic sequence fills the small space. It's beautiful and deeply wrong.
(A phantom voice, layered with crystal vibration, whispers from the very air): 'The foundation hums a warning... the great chords are fraying... the Silencing was not an end, but a pause...'
What was that?! It didn't come from the crystal!

lines_after.dialogue: A resonance echo. Locked into the chamber's structure itself. A warning, left by a Listener, perhaps from just before the Silencing. I’m happy to hear this... and terrified. This is primary source evidence.
Terrified is the right word. It suggests the Lattice is a system, and the Silencing was a... corrective measure. What happens if the system decides another correction is due?
A smooth voice interrupts from the chamber entrance. A well-drafted man with a merchant's sigil on his lapel stands there, a friendly, calculating smile on his face.

My, my. What a fascinating discovery. Historical resonance anomalies are a rare commodity. The scholarly circles would be very interested. And, if I may say, so would certain parties who'd prefer such whispers to remain... unheard.

line.dialogue: The trade negotiator has overheard the warning echo. He offers to 'broker' the information safely to the right buyers, for a substantial finder's fee, implying he can also make it disappear.

choices.text: Pretend to engage. Hear his offer in full to gauge his intentions and connections.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the resonance wall and listen for surviving frequencies.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the static — someone sang here. The Lattice is playing their last breath back to us.
Nothing but pressure and tinnitus. Whatever this wall remembers, it's not sharing with the living.

choices.text: Deflect. Claim the echo was corrupted data and of no real value, trying to downplay the find.
choices.description: Broadcast chanida's biometric signature into the corridor to bait whatever documented the previous team.

line.dialogue: I'm the lure now. Fine. Just promise me you'll follow the signal back when I stop breathing normally.
Dead air. Whatever consumed the last crew doesn't hunt by heartbeat — we're thinking like prey that already lost.

choices.text: Confront him. Ask directly who he represents and what they know about the Listener's warning.
choices.description: Reconstruct the fragmented audio logs by harmonizing your voices with the Lattice's residual key.

line.dialogue: Four voices, one chord — and the archive cracks open. They're not ghosts. They're a *warning* left in melody.
We're off-key. The Lattice rejects the dissonance and seals tighter. Whatever it guarded, it now refuses to share.

lines_before.dialogue: The hushed Archives feel heavier. The stolen chart Pichit holds hums with a discordant energy, making the crystalline shelves vibrate faintly.
This frequency... it's unstable. It makes you look younger to the Lattice, but that's an illusion. It's hiding decay.
Great. So the pirate's 'secret route' is a face-lift for a corpse road. I've never tried navigating a collapsing harmonic void before.
But it points *here*, deeper in the Archives! The locked Resonator Vault. That's where they'd keep the real forbidden knowledge!
The path is a warning, not a map. It ran out of the safe spectrum centuries ago. But the warning itself is the key.
The Trade Negotiator glides from behind a stack of sonic scrolls, his smile not reaching his eyes.
Ah, intrepid researchers! I'm happy to hear your studies progress. But the Vault? There's no one else with clearance. A shame.
From the opposite aisle, the shadow of the Sky Pirate falls across the chart.
Clearance? Hah! You lot wanna see what's screamin' in the dark? The Lattice's got a song it don't want sung. I can get you in.

line.dialogue: Two offers, both dangerous. The Negotiator's way is sealed but orderly. The Pirate's way is violent but direct.

choices.line: Trust the Negotiator's 'proper channels'. (Play the long game of bureaucracy and favors.)
choices.description: Force the chart against the locker's resonance seal, matching its unstable frequency.

line.dialogue: Ha! The lock *sings* when it hears its own voice back — cracking open like a rotten drum.
The chart's frequency shifts mid-pulse — the seal screams solid and my knuckles are bleeding.

choices.line: Make a deal with the Pirate. (Gain a forceful ally, but owe a dangerous favor.)
choices.description: Trace the chart's coordinates by hand, ignoring the frequency entirely and relying on dead reckoning.

line.dialogue: Numbers don't lie even when the ink does. Third row, seventh column — the locker's position, plain as bone.
My finger slips a line and suddenly I'm reading coordinates that point *up* — that's not deeper, that's buried.

choices.line: Use the chart's warning frequency on the Vault door yourselves. (Rely on Pichit's instinct and risk a catastrophic resonance.)
choices.description: Whisper the unstable frequency aloud, letting the Archives' acoustics amplify and find the locker's resonance.

line.dialogue: The walls catch my voice and carry it forward — somewhere ahead, something *hums* back. Found you.
The Archives swallow the sound wrong — it bounces back doubled, and for a second I hear someone else whispering my name.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice hangs in the acoustically-perfect air. Somewhere deep below, the Lattice groans.
A low, sub-audible thrum passes through the stone. It is not a path. It is a plea to stop.
Do you hear it? The past isn't gone. It's trapped, repeating its final mistake.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonator Vault is a spherical chamber. At its center, a massive, flawed crystal pulses with the recorded death-scream of a continent from The Silencing.
The containment field is failing. This isn't an archive—it's a tomb. And we just woke the occupant.
The pirate means what he says! He's not here for treasure; he wants to *weaponize* this frequency! Could you please write down 'catastrophic idiocy' for him?
Power's just a song, scholar! This one brought down cities! Imagine what it could do to a rival's fleet!
Now, now. Such raw power is... volatile. My associates would pay dearly for exclusive custody. The past is over. We must think of utility.
Utility? They want to turn a scream into a shout! We have to silence it for good!
Not silence. Resolve. Every note seeks harmony. This one has been alone, in pain, for centuries. We must complete its song.
The flawed crystal fractures, light bleeding out. The Pirate raises a resonator dagger. The Negotiator signals hidden enforcers. The Lattice's warning scream becomes a physical force.

line.dialogue: The catastrophic frequency is unraveling. Three paths to end it: destroy, control, or heal.

choices.line: Shatter the crystal. (A violent, permanent end. The immediate danger ends, but knowledge is lost.)
