choices.description: The pirate presses forward with pirate ship to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The lattice has other plans. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

choices.line: Help the Negotiator contain it. (The scream is bottled for 'study'. Profit wins, but the threat is managed.)
choices.description: Convince the pirate to use disruptor weapon and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Smuggling routes provide an escape.
The attempt backfires on the pirate. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Guide Pichit to sing it to rest. (A profound, dangerous act of empathy. It means risking everything to change the song.)
choices.description: Ask the pirate to commune with trapped echoes, drawing on pirate ship

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the pirate fails. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber holds its breath. The choice is made. The final note approaches.
The plea shifts. It is no longer 'stop'. It is 'listen'.
The past is gone... only if we let its pain define us. Now, we redefine it.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands on the observation platform 'Sky's Eye,' jutting over the Lattice. Below, crystalline spires shift in hypnotic patterns, humming with a low, mournful chord.
The resonator on Platform Four is cracked. Again. Whole lower quadrant's unstable.
A structural flaw, or something... struck it? The frequency patterns here are unusually chaotic.
Dunno. Just know it needs fixing before the next harmonic storm. We've got the replacement crystal, but someone's gotta carry it down and slot it in. Dangerous work.
We can handle it! What's the pay?
Credits, and salvage rights on anything you find down there that isn't bolted to the platform. Just... be careful. The Lattice has been singing strange lately.
It always sings 'strangely.' It's a world-sized death crystal.
Yet within its song, there is history. A record of everything lost in the Silencing. This labor... it is more than repair.

lines_after.dialogue: I have work I have to do. A promise to understand this world.
Can you promise me you'll actually fix it and not just stare at the pretty lights?
Don't change the subject! He's going to stare at the pretty lights. We'll do the actual work.

line.dialogue: How does the party secure the heavy replacement resonator crystal for the descent?

choices.line: Use the platform's winch and pulleys (safe but slow).
choices.description: Malee uses mechanical repair to decode the tonal pattern near the shifting light

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Malee. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The lattice has other plans. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.line: Have Chanida and Arthit carry it, using resonance dampeners (faster, riskier).
choices.description: Have Pichit focus tonal knowledge on the harvesting to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Pichit overreaches. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.line: Request a cargo sled from the villagers (requires extra payment).
choices.description: Convince the villager to use community ties and follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The community rallies, creating unexpected strength.
the villager fails. Local knowledge proves outdated.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends a rickety lattice-work staircase onto the Lattice surface itself. The air vibrates. Strange, ghostly harmonics seem to slip from the crystal facets.
Readings are off. There's a secondary resonance here, buried under the platform's frequency. Almost like... an echo.
Great. So it's not just unstable, it's haunted. Just slot the crystal so we can leave.
Wait! Look over there, wedged between those spires! Is that... a ship's prow?
Partially fused with the growing crystal, the shattered remains of a small resonance ship jut from the Lattice. Its hull is marked with the sigil of a lost Tonal Order.
The Echo of the Lost Ship... Chanida's mom told me about it already. A vessel that vanished a decade ago, its frequency chart lost.
Its resonance must have bled into the Lattice, corrupting the platform's stabilizer. That's the source of the instability.

lines_after.dialogue: I had a bad dream about a ship crying out last night. This is it, isn't it?
That's really easy to guess! Of course it is. The question is, what do we do about it?
We must listen. The ship's final moments are recorded here, in the crystal.

line.dialogue: How should the party investigate the spectral resonance of the lost ship?

choices.line: Tune your personal resonators to isolate the echo (safe, but reveals little).
choices.description: Malee presses forward with leg resonance to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The risk doesn't pay off. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.line: Have Pichit attempt a cautious attunement, listening for the ship's 'final song' (risks psychic feedback).
choices.description: Ask Pichit to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on staff meditation

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Pichit misreads the situation. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.line: Attempt to physically enter the crystal-encased wreck (highly dangerous, could trigger a harmonic collapse).
choices.description: Ask the villager to follow the phantom route, drawing on terraces

line.dialogue: Exactly as the villager hoped. Terrace-hardened resilience sees them through.
Defeat. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands at the edge of the observation platform. Below, the Lattice hums with a new, erratic pulse. A ghostly, translucent shape of a Resonance Ship flickers in and out of existence a few hundred yards away—the Echo.
There it is. The 'lost' ship. Looks more like a bad signal to me. What do your parents do, Arthit? Run a salvage yard for spectral junk?
This is no joke. That frequency is unstable. We have to adjust our approach. One wrong step and the Lattice could shatter beneath us.
They have a lot of stuff! I mean, look at the crystal formations around it. That's not normal decay. Something's... holding it there.
It's a memory. A scar in the Lattice, replaying its final moments. We have to adapt. To listen to what it's trying to say, not just see it.
Heh. Listeners. Always yappin'. You want the goods? The ship's hold is full of intact resonators. We know the hidden frequency to stabilize the echo... for a price.
Don't! Please! Every time that thing flickers, our platform trembles. It's pulling power from the city's stabilizers. You have to make it stop!

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The ghostly hull of the Echo shudders, its form solidifying or fracturing further based on the party's choice.
Well. That's one way to handle a haunted ship. Hope you're all happy with our new... interior decorating.
The Lattice remembers everything. Now we've added our own note to this memory.

line.dialogue: How do you approach the Echo of the Lost Ship?

choices.text: Pay the Sky Pirate's price. Use the hidden frequency to safely board and salvage.
choices.consequence: Gain resources, but empower the pirates. The villagers remain fearful of future extortion.
choices.description: Sync your helmet frequency to the unstable signal and let it pull you inside the wreck.

line.dialogue: I matched the harmonic — the hull let me through like I was never there.
The feedback nearly cracked my visor — that frequency is alive and it does *not* want guests.

choices.text: Have Chanida attempt to Sing a stabilizing harmony, mimicking the pirate's frequency.
choices.consequence: Risky. Success means free salvage and pirate respect. Failure destabilizes the Echo violently.
choices.description: Ignore the signal entirely and focus on harvesting the crystal formations growing through the cargo hold.

line.dialogue: I pulled three intact clusters before the deck even groaned — these will fund us for a year!
I touched one and the whole room screamed — the crystals are *recording* us, not growing.

choices.text: Have Pichit and Arthit perform a Listener's ritual to peacefully disperse the Echo's memory.
choices.consequence: No material gain, but permanently calms the area. Earns the villagers' deep gratitude and Listeners' favor.
choices.description: Broadcast Pichit's Lattice-scar theory back toward the ship to see if the echo stabilizes into something readable.

line.dialogue: It worked — the scar is unfolding. I can see their final coordinates, their final words, everything.
I gave it a mirror and it stared back — whatever's in there just learned our ship's signature.

lines_before.dialogue: The party's interaction with the Echo has triggered a deep resonance. A jagged, glowing crack splits the Lattice, snaking out from the now-fading ship. A low, consuming drone emanates from the fissure.
Catastrophic feedback loop! The stabilizers for the floating city are overloading. I have to take my kids to school... I mean, we have to get back and manually reroute power!
Forget the city! Look at the crack! It's growing! They sell the new iPads at the mall, but this... this is selling us a one-way trip to the core!
The big one! The motherlode frequency is right down there! But that hum... it'll shatter our minds before we get ten feet.
Fantastic. So we can either turn off the lights to conserve energy for the city and let this crack consume the region, or dive into a sonic meat grinder. Lovely options.
Please! You have to do something! The platform anchors are failing!
This is the Silencing, in miniature. A wound that cannot heal itself. We must choose the note that ends the song, not prolongs the noise.

lines_after.dialogue: The Lattice shudders one final time, then falls still. The crack either seals with a brilliant chime, festers as a controlled scar, or vanishes, leaving perfect, silent crystal.
Readings are stabilizing. The immediate threat is... over.
For now. But the world has heard our choice. It will remember.

line.dialogue: The fissure threatens everything. How do you resolve the crisis?

choices.text: Sacrifice the salvage. Use the Echo's resonators as a buffer, overloading them to seal the crack.
choices.consequence: The crack seals roughly. The area is safe, but future resonance here will be brittle and unpredictable. Material loss.
choices.description: Pichit attempts to trace the anomalous signal, relying on Listener training

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit is thwarted. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Have the entire party create a counter-frequency, a 'Chord of Binding', to freeze the fissure in place.
choices.consequence: The crack is contained but not healed—a permanent, managed wound. Establishes a dangerous but potent landmark under your influence.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to harness harmonic feedback, drawing on frequency mapping

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Defeat. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Pichit must dive into the fissure, Singing a note of absolute silence at its heart to cancel the resonance.
choices.consequence: The crack vanishes perfectly. Pichit is profoundly changed, gaining deep insight but losing part of his connection to ordinary sound. A legendary, costly victory.
choices.description: Ask the villager to commune with trapped echoes, drawing on community ties

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the villager pulls it off. Terrace-hardened resilience sees them through.
The risk doesn't pay off. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform 'The Sundered Step' juts over the Lattice surface. Below, a kaleidoscope of refracted light shivers in time to a deep, resonant hum—the world's slow, tectonic heartbeat.
Anchor lines secure. Resonance dampeners at eighty percent. We don't stay in touch with the ground teams for a reason. This close, a single harmonic spike could shatter the platform.
Look at those colors! There has to be a way down. We could scavenge pure crystal shards worth a fortune!
A fortune for our funeral pyres. The Tonal Orders would bill our families for the retrieval. Don't work too hard on that daydream.
It's not a barrier... it's a conversation. The Silencing was just the world raising its voice.
Ah, the philosophical approach! A costly one, my friends. Profit lies in listening to the right voices. Like mine. I have... charts. For the right price.
A sharp, discordant chime rings out from the Lattice below. A jagged fracture of violet light races toward the platform's supports.
Resonance overload! Everyone, brace!

lines_after.dialogue: The violent chime fades, but the violet scar in the crystal remains, glowing faintly. The air smells of ozone and crushed stone.
What *was* that? It came from that direction! Something's down there!
An unfortunate natural event. Happens all the time. Now, about those charts—best not to leave the transaction open. Dangers abound.
Natural event, my foot. That was a frequency. Someone's pinging the Lattice. And not nicely.

line.dialogue: The anomaly points to a location. The Merchant offers safe, expensive charts. Chanida wants to chase the source.

choices.line: Purchase the Merchant's Tonal Charts. (Spend resources for a safe, known route.)
choices.description: Pichit uses staff meditation to trace the anomalous signal near the pre-Silencing ruins

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Pichit overreaches. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.line: Follow the anomalous resonance. (Trust your instincts and the Lattice's 'conversation.')
choices.description: Have Chanida focus singer voice on the crystal ground to expose surface colonization truth

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida is thwarted. The escape tunnel collapses.

choices.line: Return to the ship and scan from a distance. (Prioritize safety and analysis.)
choices.description: Ask the merchant to seek the dismissed truth, drawing on negotiation

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the merchant. Pichit's staff vibrates, revealing the lattice's song has changed.
The gamble fails. A Tonal Order enforcer confiscates the crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: Descending a precarious crystal staircase, the party reaches a lower shelf on the Lattice. The violet scar terminates at a massive, dormant resonator—clearly ancient and not of Tonal Order design.
Great. Pirate tech. Why couldn't you just let us buy the boring charts? Now we have to deal with whoever lost their phone... or their warship.
Hands where I can see 'em! This here's a salvage claim. You're trespassin' on Bandit-King Vex's personal frequency.
You caused that spike? You could have brought the whole shelf down on us!
A little wake-up call for the snoozin' Orders. This resonator's a Groundless relic. We're liberatin' it. May I see your driver's license... to the afterlife?
Groundless? The movement that wants to dismantle the Floating Cities? This is worse than pirates—this is ideological sabotage.
You're trying to speak to the Lattice. To wake it up. But you're using a shout where a whisper is needed.
Whispers got us the Silencing! Time for a new tune. Now, you gonna hand over any resonance crystals, or do we do this the hard way?

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate's crew emerges from behind crystal formations, weapons humming with stolen harmonic energy. The ancient resonator behind them begins to glow in response to the tension.
A most unprofitable confrontation! I did try to warn you. My offer for a discreet exit is, sadly, no longer on the table.
So the calculator has a conscience. Or just doesn't want his goods damaged.

line.dialogue: The Groundless pirates are armed and fanatical. The ancient resonator is reacting unpredictably.

choices.line: Surrender your resonance crystals. (Comply to avoid a fight and gather information.)
choices.description: Draw your sidearm and aim at the bandit's chest, demanding they step back from the console, 15 words

line.dialogue: I've got exactly zero patience for salvage pirates who nearly killed us — back off or I fire.
My hand's shaking and the sight picture's drifting — they're not flinching and I don't blame them.

choices.line: Fight the pirates. (Neutralize the immediate threat before the resonator overloads.)
choices.description: Raise your hands slowly while scanning the bandit's gear for a transmitter or remote trigger device, 15 words

line.dialogue: Hands up, see? But that detonator on your belt — cheap Korrigan make. I can see the corroded contacts from here. One sneeze and it's just you going up.
I raised my hands but I couldn't spot the trigger — there's too much clutter on their rig and now they know I'm looking.

choices.line: Attempt to sabotage the ancient resonator. (A risky play to cut off their power and source of chaos.)
choices.description: Step between the bandit and the console, bluffing that the spike already triggered a silent distress beacon, 15 words

line.dialogue: A distress beacon? That's — no, you're lying. But if you ain't, I got maybe four minutes before a patrol crawls up my tailpipe. What do you want
the merchant is thwarted. His network delivers bad intelligence.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform offers a breathtaking, terrifying view. The Lattice surface shimmers like a frozen sea, humming with a low, constant tone. Jagged crystalline formations rise and fall in slow, silent waves.
The resonance readings are... unstable. This close to the surface, a single wrong frequency could shatter the platform's stabilizers.
Forget the readings! Look at that! The light patterns... it's like the world is singing.
A funeral dirge, more like. Every shimmer is a potential death spike. Remember the Silencing? This is what's left.
Yet it persists. Even shattered, it holds a memory of song. We just have to listen for the right notes.
A low, grinding hum vibrates through the metal decking. A battered resonance ship, festooned with scavenged plating, rises into view, its crystal resonator emitting a harsh, discordant frequency.
Well, well. Look what the Lattice coughed up. A nice, shiny observation post. They sell these views at the sky-markets for a fortune, you know.
Pirates. Their resonator is calibrated to brute-force through the Lattice. It's tearing the local harmonic field apart!

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate ship's aggressive frequency causes the nearby Lattice spikes to vibrate violently. Cracks spiderweb across a massive crystal column near the platform's edge.
The platform's shaking! They're going to bring the whole spire down on us!
Told you it was a dirge. Now we're the chorus.

line.dialogue: The pirate ship banks, its weaponized resonator taking aim. The platform's stabilizer crystal is overloading. We need to act.

choices.text: Overload Our Own Resonator (Fight Frequency with Frequency): Channel all power into the platform's defensive resonator, creating a counter-wave. It might save us, but will drain our ship's core. 'Turn off the lights to conserve energy' for the next week.
choices.description: Press your palm against the fractured surface and pour your own resonance into the gaps.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The frequencies are aligning — it's accepting the bridge, the pattern is reforming under your hand!
Arthit — "Your pulse collided with its rhythm — the readings just spiked into cascade failure territory!

choices.text: Use the Lattice Itself (A Dangerous Turn): Try to lure the pirate ship closer to the unstable crystal column. A precise sonic nudge could make the Lattice itself attack them. 'Can you make a u-turn?' into a deathtrap.
choices.description: Hum the melody Malee described and let the chamber's acoustics carry it into the fracture lines.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "The light is moving *with* your voice — look, the shimmers are tracing the melody like sheet music!
Malee — "That's not the dirge — that's a discordant counterpoint, and the patterns are recoiling from it.

choices.text: Appeal to Greed (A Merchant's Gambit): Broadcast on an open channel, offering the pirates the 'true treasure'—the platform's long-range harmonic mapping data. It's invaluable, but giving it to pirates violates every Tonal Order law.
choices.description: Place Pichit's resonance crystal between the largest fracture points to act as a harmonic keystone.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "It's holding — the memory is flowing through the crystal like current through a wire, stitching itself together!
Pichit — "The crystal cracked — whatever memory this thing holds, it's too vast for a single keystone to bear.

lines_before.dialogue: The aftermath hangs in the air, thick with crystalline dust and the fading echo of shattered frequencies. The platform groans, but holds.
Impressive! Truly impressive. To not only survive but... repurpose the local harmonics. That kind of adaptive resonance is worth more than any physical salvage.
You watched the whole thing.
A good negotiator knows the value of observation. And what I observed was... a group operating outside the sanctioned frequencies. The Groundless Movement would pay dearly for such skills.
The anarchists? They want to tear down the Tonal Orders, let anyone 'sing' the Lattice! It would be chaos!
Says the man whose precious Orders let pirates run amok because they paid the licensing fee. Maybe chaos has its points.
He's right about one thing. What we did here... the Orders didn't teach us that. We felt it.
The merchant smiles, a thin, calculating curve of the lips. He gestures to the Lattice below, where the conflict has left a deep, pulsing scar of raw, unstable sound.

That scar is a new frequency. Uncharted. Uncontrolled. The Orders will come to silence it, to 'stabilize' the region. Or... someone could learn it first. Someone who isn't afraid of a little dissonance. I'll have a look at the data for you, of course. For a price.

lines_after.dialogue: The pulsing scar in the Lattice glows brighter, its sound evolving from a painful shriek into something stranger, more complex. It feels less like damage and more like... a birth.
It's not broken. It's changing. The Silencing didn't destroy the song. It just forced it to find a new shape.
On the horizon, the distant, regulated hum of Tonal Order enforcer ships begins to whisper against the edge of hearing.

line.dialogue: The merchant offers a deal: he hides the evidence of our unsanctioned resonance use from the Orders, and gives us the raw frequency data from the scar. In return, we let him broker our 'services' to the Groundless Movement. The scar in the Lattice sings, waiting.

choices.text: Accept the Deal (Embrace the New Path): Take the data and the merchant's protection. We step into the shadows, becoming tools for a revolution we don't fully understand. 'I'll try it.' This new way.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to chart resonance pathways using singer voice

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. She hears something no one else can.
The resonance turns hostile. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Decode the Scar Ourselves (Walk the Line): Refuse the merchant. We stay independent, trying to study and understand this new frequency before the Orders arrive. It's a race against time, with no allies. 'I'll look at it for you.' Ourselves.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing tattooed routes to challenge skycity propaganda

line.dialogue: Arthit makes it work. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
A costly mistake by Arthit. The escape tunnel collapses.

choices.text: Report to the Orders (Uphold the System): Transmit everything to the Tonal Authorities. The scar is a threat to stability and must be silenced. We hand over the merchant, the data, and our own actions for judgment. 'I'll get it.' The enforcers. We open the door for them.
choices.description: The pirate attempts to decode the cryptic message, relying on secret frequencies

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the pirate's call. The forbidden text confirms the warning.
the pirate's resolve isn't enough. The underworld frequency draws unwanted attention.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim breathe with the soft susurrus of wind through terraced grain. Water channels chime like glass, and the air smells of damp earth and ripening skyfruit.
Listen... beneath the irrigation songs. A dissonance. Like a memory trying to surface from the Lattice below.
Or it's just wind. You're always finding philosophy in the draft from a broken shutter, Pichit.
No, he's right! It's coming from that old, overgrown terrace. Let's check it out!
Caution. The Tonal Orders don't chart that sector. If we're seen poking around forbidden frequencies...
As you approach the neglected terrace, a figure emerges from behind a hydroponic silo—the Trade Negotiator, the Trade Negotiator, polishing a resonance crystal with a silk cloth.
Ah, travelers! The gardens are lovely for contemplation, aren't they? But some contemplations... are better kept quiet. Don't let anyone know what you might hear out here.
You're listening for it too. The echo.

lines_after.dialogue: Perceptive! A lost Resonance Ship, the 'Sky-Singer's Dirge,' went silent generations ago. Its final frequency is trapped here, bleeding from the Lattice. A curiosity... but also a liability. The Tonal Orders would pay dearly to suppress such an 'unmapped anomaly.'
And you'd sell it to them. Don't judge others, they say, but profiting from silence? That's a special kind of quiet.

I merely facilitate understanding. But you... you have a Singer among you, don't you? That one's aura hums differently. My advice? Don't let him see you prying further. The wrong ears are always listening.
The merchant slips away into the rustling stalks. The anomalous hum grows clearer—a mournful, repeating chord frayed at the edges.

line.dialogue: The merchant's warning hangs in the air. The ghost-frequency calls from the overgrowth.

choices.line: Investigate openly. The truth shouldn't be bartered.
choices.description: Malee attempts to chart resonance pathways, relying on scavenger instincts

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Malee hits a wall. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: Scout stealthily. He said not to be seen.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing hidden frequencies to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
The risk doesn't pay off. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.line: Leave it. Some echoes are better left unheard.
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with market connections to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: the merchant's expertise pays off. The negotiator uncovers a deal no one else could make.
the merchant hits a wall. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: You push into the derelict terrace. Crystal lattices are cracked, overgrown with luminous moss that pulses in time with the buried frequency.
It's stronger here! Like the ship is... singing from below? We don't stay in touch with the dead, usually. This is new.
Not the dead. The Lattice remembers. Every vibration is recorded. This is a scar.
A scar that's attracting attention. Look—sky pirate grapnel marks on the support crystals. Fresh.
A rough laugh cuts through the hum. The Sky Pirate, the sky pirate, drops from a higher terrace, landing with a clatter of scavenged armor.
Well, well. Merchant rat scurried off and left the prize for the takers, eh? This frequency's ours. The 'Dirge' ain't lost—it's waiting. And its cargo ain't for polite company.
You disagree with the merchant's 'facilitation,' I take it? Prefer direct theft?

The Tonal Orders stole the knowledge first! We're just repossessing. This echo... it's a key. A map to the ship itself, frozen in the crystal depths. But it's brittle. Too much stress, it shatters. Don't get so stressed out, now. Just walk away.

lines_after.dialogue: A map to a lost ship. The Silencing took so much. What if the 'Dirge' carries not cargo, but memory?
Or it's a pirate trap. This frequency could be a lure. I don't agree with his methods, but the merchant had a point about danger.
But we're already here! We can't just leave! What if there are survivors? Or... you know, cool loot?
The ghostly chord swells, causing the moss to flare brightly. For a moment, the image of a shattered crystal hull flickers in the air. The pirate tenses, hand on his resonator blade.

line.dialogue: The echo holds its breath. The pirate blocks the path to the frequency's heart.

choices.line: Stand down. Let the pirate have the echo. It's not worth bloodshed.
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use resonant staff and chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Pichit is thwarted. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.line: Negotiate. Perhaps the map can be shared, or the truth uncovered together.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
Arthit fails. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.line: Prepare to fight. This memory belongs to the world, not to thieves or guilds.
choices.description: Have the pirate focus pirate ship on the sky-rice to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the pirate pulls it off. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the pirate is thwarted. The disruptor backfires, jamming itself.

lines_before.dialogue: The party regroups on a quiet terrace, the gentle slosh of water channels and rustle of tall grain the only sounds. The Trade Negotiator's false smile still hangs in the air like a bad scent.
He knows more than he's selling. I can feel it. That 'haunted ship' frequency he mentioned... it's not just a story.
Of course he knows. Profit is information here. He'll sell us a map to our own graves if the price is right.
We should be careful. If the Tonal Orders catch wind we're chasing a forbidden frequency, our ship will be grounded. Permanently.
But the Lattice remembers. The Echo... if it's real, it's a memory of the Silencing itself. A truth buried in sound.
A sudden, aggressive hum cuts through the pastoral calm. A Resonance Ship, crude and patched, descends onto a nearby landing platform, crushing decorative crops.
Well, look what the wind dragged in! Heard you lot were askin' about the *Whispering Maw*. Bad business, that.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate leers, hand on his resonator pistol. He clearly wants something in exchange for what he knows.

choices.line: Offer Trade. (Chanida: "We have supplies. Medical synth-crystal, high-grade. For the frequency.")
choices.description: Press the merchant tonight—corner him alone when the lanterns dim and the market thins.

line.dialogue: I slid the silver across the table and watched his composure crack like river clay—his lips loosened, and the name *Vessantara* slipped out like a gasp.
He smiled, counted my coins, and said something polite about respecting a customer's curiosity—then vanished into the crowd before I could draw another breath.

choices.line: Appeal to Greed. (Malee: "The Negotiator is playing you, too. We know where he's hiding his real cargo.")
choices.description: Send Malee to charm the ledger-keeper while Arthit watches the canal exits for Orders scouts.

line.dialogue: I pressed my palm flat against the ledger-keeper's desk, leaned close, and whispered the right name—he went pale and turned the page without a word.
The ledger-keeper's eyes flicked past my shoulder to a figure in grey robes across the square—I'd barely opened my mouth before the meeting was already over.

choices.line: Challenge Directly. (Pichit: "You heard the Echo too, didn't you? It calls to those who listen. You're afraid of it.")
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sing the old Echo-verse aloud and watch the merchant's face for recognition.

line.dialogue: I
the merchant loses control. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_after.dialogue: The pirate's rough laughter echoes off the terraces. He gives a jagged, unstable frequency sequence—the supposed last ping of the *Whispering Maw*.
There's your ghost song. Don't say I never gave you nothin'. Now, if you'll excuse me... I'm in a good mood. Got business with that smiling weasel of a merchant.
That frequency is... chaotic. Unstable. It could tear our resonator apart if we're not precise. May I have some time to calibrate the dampeners?
You heard that, right? The way his voice cracked? He's terrified of what's out there. This is it. The real trail.

lines_before.dialogue: As Arthit works, the atmosphere in the Gardens shifts. The wind carries a new, dissonant undertone—a faint, repeating cry of shattered crystal. The very Lattice beneath the floating city seems to shudder.
The pirate's 'gift' is a beacon. Aren't you tired of being led by the nose? Everyone knows the *Maw* was lost chasing a myth—a 'Pure Frequency' from before the Silencing.
Not a myth. A memory. The Lattice is singing the ship's final moments back to us. A loop of tragedy.
The Trade Negotiator stumbles into view, robe torn, his calculated calm shattered. The Sky Pirate follows, resonator pistol glowing.
Fools! You've triggered it! That frequency wasn't just a location—it was a *key*! The Echo isn't a ghost, it's a resonance lock, and you've just opened it!
Shut it! The Maw's cargo is mine! The Orders pay a fortune for pre-Silencing artifacts! I don't want your philosophizing, I want that ship!

The dissonance peaks. Above the gardens, the air shimmers. A phantom outline of a massive, broken Resonance Ship—the *Whispering Maw*—flickers into existence, its spectral hull groaning with unnatural sound.
It's here! The Echo is real, and it's *right here*!

line.dialogue: The phantom ship pulses, its unstable frequency threatening to destabilize the Gardens' foundation. The Pirate aims to board it. The Negotiator panics. The truth of the Lost Ship is moments away.

choices.line: Sabotage the Pirate's Ship. (Arthit: "Cut his power. Without his resonator, the phantom frequency can't anchor here. It will fade.")
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing hidden frequencies to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Chanida loses control. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.line: Board the Phantom. (Chanida: "We go in! The answer is on that ship! We sync our resonator to its frequency and phase in!")
choices.description: Have Pichit focus monk wisdom on the water channels to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit is thwarted. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Sing it to Rest. (Pichit: "The Lattice is hurting. This is a wound. We must listen to its full song and answer with harmony, not force.")
choices.description: Ask the pirate to decode the distress signal, drawing on smuggling routes

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the pirate. The bandit's ruthlessness proves effective.
The risk doesn't pay off. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax resonates through the Hanging Gardens. Crystal chimes shatter. Crops wilt from sonic distortion. The fate of the Echo—and the knowledge it holds—is sealed.
Well. Everyone knows it now. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a scream. And that ship... it heard it first.
A memory crystalized. A warning, forever repeating in the Lattice. We don't own the past. We only listen to its echoes.
As the phantom fades, a profound silence falls over Mae Rim's Gardens, heavier than before. Something has been resolved. Something else has just begun.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market churns around you, a sea of noise. The hum of ten thousand deals and disputes makes the very air thick, the crystalline Lattice far below seeming to shimmer in agitation.
Keep close. In this din, it's easy to miss a warning tone from the city's stability resonators. I'll keep an ear out.
Relax, Arthit. If the city was going to fall, the Tonal Orders would have priced the evacuation charts already.
Forget that! Look at all this stuff! I bet we can find the parts for that leg here. Let's ask around!
A marketplace... the ultimate expression of human resonance. Each voice, a frequency. Each transaction, a harmonic. I have bad eyesight in crowds, but I can feel the pattern.
You lot look like you're looking for something. Not from the Orders, are you?
We seek knowledge. A resonant prosthetic. A leg, to be precise.
Crystal-work? That's Tonal monopoly. But... old Niran in the scrap-alley might talk. He tinkers. Says he did it all himself after the Silencing. Crazy, but clever.

lines_after.dialogue: 'Did it all himself.' The hallmark of every brilliant disaster I've ever funded.
Scrap-alley! Sounds perfect! I'll get it. I'll find the way!
Chanida, wait! We should approach cautiously. This 'Niran' operates outside the guilds. That's dangerous.

line.dialogue: How do you approach the scrap-alley?

choices.line: Follow Chanida's lead. Charge in with enthusiasm.
choices.description: Pichit channels staff meditation toward the spice scents, hoping to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit loses control. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.line: Ask the villager for more details about Niran's temperament and work.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with crystal hearing to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Chanida succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Things don't go as planned. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Let Arthit scout ahead quietly to assess the situation.
choices.description: The villager uses terraces to record the spectral signature near the bargaining

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
The resonance turns hostile. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: Scrap-alley is a canyon of salvaged resonator parts and broken Lattice-shards. The noise of the main market is muffled here, replaced by the erratic ping of crystal and the mutter of an old man.
Hm. Resonant frequency off by a quarter-tone. Amateurs. The guilds polish everything smooth and dead.
Niran? We were told you might help us. We need a crystal prosthetic leg, tuned for navigation.
Help? Help is a trade. You want my work? That's really easy to guess! What do you offer? Not coin. Coin is dull.
Information, then. Rumors are the currency of Khrueang.
Better. I hear things. The Listeners whisper of a new 'natural chord' forming deep in the Lattice. The Orders are nervous. They hate anything they can't chart.
A new sound? That's amazing! We could find it!
I really wonder... if this chord is connected to the Silencing. A wound in the world's song, finally healing?

lines_after.dialogue: Philosophy won't forge a leg. Bring me a shard from that new chord. A pure, uncharted frequency. Then we'll talk.
He wants us to go diving into the unknown Lattice for a sample. Of course he does. I'm really hurting from the sheer predictability of this.
It's an immense risk. The Lattice without a chart... but for a true resonant prosthetic, it might be the only key.

line.dialogue: How do you respond to Niran's price?

choices.line: Agree immediately. The chance to hear a new primal sound is worth any risk.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing singer voice to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida misreads the situation. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.line: Bargain. Offer to also bring back information on the Tonal Orders' reaction to this chord.
choices.description: Pichit uses staff meditation to calibrate against the frequency near the merchant guilds

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
A costly mistake by Pichit. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Refuse. The task is suicide. Pressure him to accept a different, safer payment.
choices.description: The villager presses forward with village secrets to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the villager pulls it off. The community rallies, creating unexpected strength.
A costly mistake by the villager. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The team regroups at the edge of Khrueang Market, the constant hum of commerce now feeling like a smothering blanket. Pichit holds the schematic for the Resonant Prosthetic.
This schematic... it’s about to graduate from theory. But its power source is a unique crystal frequency. We need to find a merchant who won’t ask why.
You’re not going anywhere with that alone, Pichit. The Tonal Orders have ears everywhere. One wrong purchase and we’re marked.
Then we split up! Arthit and I can scout the high-end resonator stalls. Malee, you work your underworld charm. Pichit, you handle the final negotiation.
Are you going (or not)? This feels reckless. The market’s noise already makes precise tonal work difficult. A transaction for an illicit crystal will be like shouting.
He’s going to graduate soon from ‘careful scholar’ to ‘wanted resonator thief.’ I’ll see what whispers I can buy. Try not to get caught.

lines_after.dialogue: The team scatters into the market’s flow. Pichit approaches a secluded stall run by a merchant with a too-perfect smile.
Ah, a customer with particular needs. The crystal you describe... it’s not on any standard chart. That makes it expensive. And dangerous.
I understand the risk. But its resonance could part more than the Lattice. It could mend a broken path.

line.dialogue: The merchant names an exorbitant price, but his eyes linger on Pichit’s own resonator. He offers an alternative.

choices.line: Pay the exorbitant price in full. (Spend significant resources, avoid immediate danger.)
choices.description: Take the schematic to Old Ratri's repair den beneath the night market, 14 words

line.dialogue: Ratri's seen every lattice variant since the Collapse — if anyone can forge this, she can.
Her den was sealed shut. Someone got to her first, or she vanished on her own terms.

choices.line: Offer a trade: your personal resonator for the crystal. (Lose a key tool, but gain the item cleanly.)
choices.description: Split up — Chanida and Arthit scout the high-end rail suppliers while Pichit stays hidden, 16 words

line.dialogue: Two of us in eveningwear, asking polite questions — they'll see customers, not threats. It works.
The supplier flagged security before we even mentioned the lattice. Chanida's face is known there.

choices.line: Bluff. Claim the Tonal Orders authorized this purchase. (Risk exposure, but try to get it for free.)
choices.description: Burn the schematic now before it draws the wrong attention to all of you, 14 words

line.dialogue: You hesitated just long enough for me to grab your wrist. We're keeping it — but we move *tonight*.
The ash hadn't even settled before I realized — I memorized every line. It's not gone. It's *in me

acts.title: The Price of a New Song

lines_before.dialogue: The deal is done, but a tense silence falls over your corner of the market. The merchant’s smile has vanished. From the crowd, two stern figures in Tonal Order robes emerge.
We’ve got company! Do you wanna try it, Pichit? Do we run, or do we stand our ground and sing?
Can I take a break for a moment? This is exactly what I feared. They must have been monitoring all irregular crystal frequencies.
The merchant sold us out. Of course he did. Profit and protection. So, what’s the new song, geniuses? Fight or flight?
This crystal... it’s not just for a leg. Its resonance is a key. I can feel it. The Lattice itself is listening.
Please, don’t make trouble here! The Silencing started with forbidden sounds! We just want to live!
My apologies, friends. But guild tariffs are guild tariffs. Uncharted resonance is a threat to all navigation.

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal Order agents step forward, their hands on their own resonators. The market crowd pulls back, creating a circle of terrified silence.
Shall we go to the seaside? A place of endless, natural sound? No. We make our stand here. The old song ends. A new one begins.

line.dialogue: The lead agent demands you surrender the crystal. The fate of the prosthetic, and your freedom, hangs on your response.

choices.line: Surrender the crystal peacefully. (You avoid a fight, but fail the subplot and attract ongoing suspicion.)
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with tonal knowledge to map the frequency corridors

The gamble fails. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
A costly mistake by the merchant. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim breathe with the slow pulse of life. Wind whispers through rows of leafy greens, and irrigation channels sing a constant, gentle trickle.
Peace and quiet. I’ll believe it when we’ve been here an hour without something trying to eat the crops. Or us.
The Tonal Orders keep this city’s resonance stable. It should be secure. Still, we should find that Listener contact before nightfall.
Look! Down by the lowest terrace, near the edge. Who is this lady? She's just... staring out at the Lattice.
Not a lady. Look at the robes. That’s our Listener Monk. But the posture... it’s less reverence, more... waiting.
The figure turns. A woman with a weathered, serene face, but her eyes hold a deep, troubled current.
You are expected. The garden’s song told of your approach. I am Sister Liora.

lines_after.dialogue: I was awaiting another. When’s he coming? The scavenger who brings me surface findings. His lateness... concerns me.
He winked at me. Well, not at me, but last time we were in the lower markets. Sketchy type.
You study the Lattice’s song here, Sister. What has it told you lately?

line.dialogue: Sister Liora hesitates, her gaze drifting back to the crystalline expanse below.

choices.text: Assure her we mean no harm.
choices.description: Approach the Listener Monk directly and ask what she's observing at the terrace's edge.

line.dialogue: Arthit steps forward, hands open. "Listener, we've come a long way. What are you hearing down there that we can't?
Arthit calls out too sharply, and the Monk's eyes snap wide before she vanishes behind the terrace wall. "Gone. She thought we were a threat.

choices.text: Press her on what’s troubling the garden’s song.
choices.description: Send Chanida ahead alone, moving quietly along the garden wall to get closer without alarming the Monk.

line.dialogue: Chanida slips between the topiary, breath held, and signals back. "She's kneeling over something — a crack in the foundation. There's sound coming out of it.
Chanida's sandal scrapes loose gravel. The Monk straightens instantly, turning. "She's looking right at me. I've been made.

choices.text: Offer to help find the missing scavenger.
choices.description: Wait and observe from cover, noting the Monk's movements and any patterns in her behavior.

line.dialogue: Malee crouches behind the hedge row, watching. "Every few minutes she presses her palm flat to the stone. She's listening to something beneath the garden. Something rhythmic.
Malee shifts for a better view and a branch snaps under his knee. The Monk pauses mid-gesture, then calmly walks away into the cloister. "We won't

lines_before.dialogue: Before Liora can answer, a sharp whistle cuts the air. A figure hauling a laden pack scrambles up the terrace path.
Liora! Apologies. The lower harmonics were... agitated. Took the long way.
Agitated. Great. This movie is great! Just the pastoral relaxation we signed up for.
Name's Jett. And you're the Singer's crew. Word travels, even down to the scarps.
You were studying the Lattice's surface. What did you find?
Fracture lines. New ones. Spreading like whispers from the Deep Silencing sites. Liora’s been listening to the growth pattern. It’s not good.
The song is changing. Becoming a dirge. A warning I am duty-bound to report to the Tonal Orders... but they will only silence the message. They always do.

lines_after.dialogue: She walked back and forth. All night. The anxiety in the resonance... it mirrors my own conflict.
My family’s been on the surface for generations. He’s the only son in the family left who still trusts the old songs. The Orders call us superstitious.
A warning unheeded is a catastrophe invited. What is the Lattice trying to say?

line.dialogue: Jett opens his pack, revealing strange, faintly humming crystal fragments. Liora looks from them to you, her resolve wavering.

choices.text: Examine the crystal fragments with Jett.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with scavenger instincts, ready to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Malee pulls it off. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The risk doesn't pay off. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.text: Convince Liora to share her findings with us, not the Orders.
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing ship navigation to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Propose we descend to the fracture site immediately to listen for ourselves.
choices.description: Have the monk risk using crystal bowls to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Ancient knowledge surfaces, connecting past and present.
the monk misreads the situation. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The peaceful hum of the Gardens is shattered. The Listener Monk stands rigid, his face pale. The gentle Lattice resonance has shifted to a low, discordant thrum.
Do you hear it? The Song... it's changing. A fracture. A warning. Why are you treating me like this, forcing me to speak? The Orders forbid this knowledge.
Forget the Orders! What warning? Spit it out!
Let me guess. The 'stable' Lattice the Tonal Orders sell passage across isn't so stable. What style do you prefer—blissful ignorance or terrifying truth?
This is dangerous. If the Lattice is becoming unstable... the Silencing could happen again. We need specifics.
The truth has a sound of its own, Monk. To ignore it is to be deaf to the world's heartbeat. What do the whispers say?
The deep frequencies... they're fading. The Lattice is thinning in sectors. Resonance ships are stressing it further. It's a feedback loop. A collapse is possible. Anywhere. It could fail anywhere.
Ha! I've felt the tremors on the surface. Patches go silent, then shatter. Your floating cities are dancing on a cracking pane of glass. What kind of future do you like? A short one?

line.dialogue: The Monk has given us a direction—a failing sector to the west. But the Scavenger scoffs, saying her surface paths are safer, if you can stomach the climb down. The party must choose their route into danger.

choices.text: Trust the Monk's acoustic bearings. Follow the song to the source of the fracture. (HARD - Requires precise navigation)
choices.leads_to: Follow the fading song into the unstable zone.
choices.description: Press your palms flat against the stone floor and let the Song's fracture resonate through your bones.

line.dialogue: * "Yes — you feel it now. The vibration skips like a cracked bell. Three harmonics are missing where there should be seven.
* "Your body rejects the dissonance. The fracture is not meant for untrained bones — pull back before it splinters you.

choices.text: Take the Scavenger's path. Descend to the Lattice surface and approach from below. (MEDIUM - Physically demanding, less predictable)
choices.leads_to: Scale down the terraces to the treacherous surface.
choices.description: Grab chanida's arm and demand she explain what the Orders have been hiding about the Lattice's stability.

line.dialogue: * "Fine! The Orders knew the Lattice was decaying for years. They kept singing patches over the cracks — that's why I left.
* "You think manhandling me makes the answers come faster? All it does is make me want to walk out that door.

choices.text: Split up. Send Chanida and Arthit with the Scavenger, while Pichit and Malee go with the Monk. Cover both approaches. (EASY - Safer, but dilutes your strength)
choices.leads_to: Divide the party to gather more information.
choices.description: Hum the foundational tone arthit taught you and listen for where the Song warps

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the scavenger's call. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
the scavenger's resolve isn't enough. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The pastoral calm of the Gardens now feels like the eye of a storm. The wind carries not the scent of crops, but the ozone-tinged promise of crystal fracture.
We walk towards a silence that screams. Remember why we listen.
Great. We're running toward a world-ending cataclysm. My preferred afternoon activity was napping, but this'll do.

lines_before.dialogue: The western terrace edge. Below, the Lattice glows with a sickly, pulsing light. A web of black fractures spreads from a central point, sucking sound from the air. In only five minutes, the silence has grown deafening.
The Song... it's being consumed. First you have to understand—this isn't natural decay. Something is actively draining the resonance. Feeding.
Look! Down in the fracture! Movement. Not crystal. Something... organic. Growing.
A parasitic organism? Feeding on sonic energy? If it spreads... The second option is unthinkable. It would mean another Silencing.
So we kill it! Burn it out!
Brilliant. Let's attack the unknown sound-eating horror. What's the first option, oh cautious one? Run and let it eat the world?
It is a wound in the world's song. We cannot heal it with violence alone. We must understand its rhythm, then change it.
The central mass in the fracture quivers. A stalk-like protrusion rises, culminating in a bulb that pulses in time with the dying resonance. It is both beautiful and horrifying.

line.dialogue: The parasitic growth is vulnerable. It has attuned itself to the Lattice's failing frequency. To stop it, you must break that attunement. But how?

choices.text: Sonic Overload. Use the party's resonance tools to blast it with a discordant scream, shattering its delicate attunement. (EASY - Direct, but risks widening the fracture)
choices.leads_to: The air shrieks with manufactured noise.
choices.description: Drop into the fracture and attempt to sever the organism's connection with a precise harmonic strike.

line.dialogue: The monk's palm connects with the pulsing membrane and the parasite shrieks loose, its feeding tendrils snapping back into the dark.* "The Song returns—but its hunger will renew.
The monk misjudges the resonance and the organism's tendrils lash around their wrist, drinking the harmonic vibration straight from their bones.* "It feeds on us too—fall back!

choices.text: Resonance Hijack. Pichit must attempt to Sing, to wrest control of the local frequency away from the parasite and starve it. (HARD - Requires perfect pitch, great personal risk)
choices.leads_to: Pichit steps forward, closing his eyes to listen to the dying song.
choices.description: Rig Arthit's frequency emitter to broadcast a counter-resonance that disrupts the parasite's digestion.

line.dialogue: Arthit twists the dial and the fracture shudders as the organism convulses, releasing waves of stolen sound back into the cavern.* "Beautiful—the counter-frequency broke its metabolic cycle. It's starving.
The emitter whines, then screams as the organism absorbs the signal whole, swelling visibly with each pulse.* "Wrong wavelength—I just fed it a feast. Everyone, quiet—QUIET!

choices.text: Sacrificial Harmony. The Monk suggests using the ancient chants of his order. A pure, stable tone to give the parasite a 'better' song to feed on, luring it out of the fracture to be physically destroyed. (MEDIUM - Requires precise coordination and bait)
choices.leads_to: The Monk begins a low, resonant hum, offering himself as the focus.
choices.description: Let Chanida pour accelerant along the fracture's edge and ignite the organism while it feeds.

line.dialogue: Flame cascades into the chasm and the thing splits open, releasing a chorus of trapped frequencies that ring through the hollow like buried bells.* "Burned clean. Nothing parasitizes the Song on my
The lattice has other plans. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax resonates through the terraces. Crystal chimes in shattering. The fate of this sector—and perhaps a warning for the whole Lattice—hangs on this single, decisive note.
Every ending is a new frequency. Let us choose the one that sings of continuation.
The Gardens hold their breath. The wind stills. All that exists is the choice, and the sound it will make.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of quiet. Endless shelves of crystalline record-discs catch the dim, filtered light from the Lattice far below. The air is still, the only sound the soft scrape of your boots on the polished stone.
I swear, these monks could hear a pin drop from a mile away. Keep your voices down.
The acoustics are precisely calibrated. A single misplaced word could resonate... unfavorably. We should proceed with utmost caution.
Great. So we're tip-toeing through a library that might shatter if we sneeze. My favorite kind of adventure.
There's a pattern to this silence. It's not empty. It's... expectant.
Pichit, over here. I think I found our monk.

lines_after.dialogue: You're back late. I was beginning to think the Tonal Orders had intercepted you. The Archives are not safe for those who ask the questions you do.
We seek knowledge of the old paths, before the Silencing. The true song of the Lattice.
The true song... It is not a melody of safe passage. It is a lament. A warning. I'm sorry I'm late in understanding this myself. The Orders have curated the records. They have silenced verses.

line.dialogue: The Listener Monk seems frightened but sincere. How do you proceed?

choices.text: "Show us what was erased." (Press for the hidden truth.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the stone floor to feel for vibrations before each step forward.

line.dialogue: The resonance channels run east-west. Step perpendicular to them and the monks' ears will catch nothing.
You just sent a tremor straight through the acoustic channel. Every monk in the eastern wing just turned their head.

choices.text: "Why warn us now?" (Question his motives.)
choices.description: Mimic the monks' measured breathing rhythm to blend your presence into the ambient sound.

line.dialogue: Your lungs are syncing with the building. Even your heartbeat is starting to match their prayer cadence.
You breathed out of rhythm. The silence just... shifted. Like the whole library noticed.

choices.text: "We should leave before we're caught." (Prioritize immediate safety.)
choices.description: Trace the ward-lines on the nearest bookshelf to locate the gaps in the listening enchantment.

line.dialogue: There — between the seventh and eighth shelf. The ward-thread frayed decades ago. A blind spot, if we move single file.
You touched an active sigil. The ink just pulsed warm under your fingertip, and now every shelf in this row is awake.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk leads you deep into a disused annex. The air grows colder. Here, the crystalline records are cracked, their surfaces dull. A figure emerges from the shadows, clad in practical, worn gear.
Stop! Don't touch those. The resonance in this wing is unstable. One wrong vibration and the whole shelf comes down.
Charming. A surface rat in the bird's nest. You're a long way from home.
I go where the truth is buried. Same as you, I reckon. The monk here tried to stop me from coming, but... some songs need to be heard.
You work the Lattice surface? Your knowledge of its physical harmonics could be invaluable.
She has seen what the Archives deny. The Lattice isn't just singing. In places... it's screaming. We should wait for the commotion above to stop before retrieving the fragment.
Screaming? What does that mean?

lines_after.dialogue: It means the Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a response. The old world played a note it shouldn't have. The Lattice answered. And it's getting ready to answer again.
A response to what? What note?

The forbidden resonance. The one the Tonal Orders were founded to suppress. It's recorded on a shattered disc in the next chamber. But the structural harmonics... I tried to stop him from going in alone last time, but a junior acolyte was lost. The chamber is treacherous.

line.dialogue: The forbidden record lies within an acoustically unstable chamber. How do you retrieve it?

choices.text: "We move slowly, in absolute silence." (Rely on stealth and precision.)
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use forbidden paths and follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The resonance turns hostile. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.text: "Chanida, create a counter-frequency to stabilize the room." (Use controlled sound.)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to harness harmonic feedback, drawing on frequency mapping

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The attempt backfires on Chanida. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: "Scavenger, guide us. You know how brittle structures fail." (Trust the outsider's expertise.)
choices.description: The scavenger channels crystal fragments toward the recorded routes, hoping to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The lattice has other plans. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives, once a place of quiet reverence, now holds a humming tension. The party stands before a massive crystal console in the central chamber, its surface etched with luminous routes.
You’ve arrived? Good. The data you brought from the surface... it confirms a pattern. A dissonance in the Lattice's core song. We’ve talked about this before, in our oldest texts.
So the old hum isn't just for ambiance? I’ve never understood how you could hear a song in static.
The Tonal Orders have been suppressing this. They must have known. We need to verify everything before we act.
Before they lock us out? We have the data! Let's just blast this out to every ship!
The truth needs the right resonance, Chanida. A warning shouted at the wrong pitch can shatter the crystal.
The Lattice surface... it's been whispering louder. Strange harmonics. Your monk's 'dissonance' feels like a scream waiting to happen.
The Archives hold a forbidden log. A Singer's last flight, recorded before The Silencing. It describes the same harmonic instability we're seeing now.

lines_after.dialogue: The console lights up, projecting a fragmented star-map of sound. The safe routes flicker, replaced by jagged waves of dissonance spreading from the world's heart.
This isn't just a route change. It's a prelude. The Lattice is preparing to resonate on a scale we haven't seen since everything fell.
We need to warn the floating cities. But the Tonal Orders control all communications. They'll intercept any standard broadcast.

line.dialogue: How do we prepare the warning before the Orders silence us?

choices.text: Sabotage the Archives' comms to create a city-wide emergency frequency override.
choices.consequence: Quick, loud, and messy. Guarantees the message gets out but paints you as criminals.
choices.description: Hack the harmonic frequency database before the Orders detect the intrusion, 14 words

line.dialogue: [malee] "I'm through — the suppression layers are peeling back like old paint. There's something *alive* underneath.
[arthit] "They've mirrored our signal. Every node we touched just reported our position back to the Orders.

choices.text: Encode the data into a new 'safe route' chart and seed it through the Listeners' network.
choices.consequence: Subtle and precise. The truth spreads quietly among those who know how to listen, but slowly.
choices.description: Demand the monk explain what the Tonal Orders have been burying before risking anything further, 15 words

line.dialogue: [monk] "The hum isn't noise — it's a carrier signal. Something has been speaking through it since before the Orders existed.
[chanida] "While you're playing interrogator, the Orders are sealing the archive. Whatever truth the monk had, it's gone now.

choices.text: Use the forbidden Singer's log as a tuning fork. Have Pichit attempt to Sing the warning directly into the Lattice.
choices.consequence: Unprecedented and dangerous. If it works, the Lattice itself carries the message. If it fails, it could trigger the very collapse you're warning about.
choices.description: Splice chanida's raw data directly into the harmonic array and force the chorus to manifest early, 15 words

line.dialogue: [chanida] "Yes — *there!* The chorus is breaking through! Every suppressed frequency is singing at once — it's *beautiful*.
[malee] "The array just shattered. Whatever was hidden in that signal, it didn't want to be woken up like this.

lines_before.dialogue: The central chamber thrums with power. Whether through sabotage, subterfuge, or song, you have initiated the warning. The Archives' crystalline walls are glowing, reacting.
The whole city's gonna hear that! I have something to tell you, Pichit... I think we just declared war on the Orders.
Could you tell me how to get to the nearest safe house? Because we're gonna need one.
Scanners show Tonal Order enforcers converging. They’re sealing the archive doors. We're trapped with a message that's still broadcasting.
The surface vibrations... they're changing. Responding. You're gonna be sorry for waking that thing up if you don't finish the tune.
The Lattice is listening! It's amplifying the warning, but the feedback is unstable. The Singer's log... it wasn't just a record. It's a key to stabilize the resonance!
So we don't just send a message. We have to harmonize with it. We have to answer the Lattice's warning with our own certainty.

lines_after.dialogue: The very air crystallizes with potential. The enforcers' shouts are muffled by the rising hum. Before you, the main resonator crystal pulses with the combined data, the forbidden log, and the Lattice's own distressed song.
This is it. The moment the old world ended. We get to choose how this chorus resolves.

line.dialogue: How do you complete the symphony and define what comes next?

choices.text: Dampen the resonance. Send a clear, simple stop-signal to calm the Lattice and allow for orderly evacuation.
choices.consequence: Safety first. You prevent a cataclysm, but the Tonal Orders maintain control of the narrative. The truth is buried again, labeled a malfunction.
choices.description: Reroute chanida's broadcast signal through the scavenger's surface array to amplify it, 15 words

line.dialogue: If they're tracking the frequency, let's give them something worth chasing — every speaker in this district just became ours.
The signal's bleeding into infrastructure bands — half the array just fried itself before I could finish the patch.

choices.text: Broadcast the raw truth. Let the unstable, chaotic harmony flood every receiver, showing the danger and the Orders' lies in one deafening blast.
choices.consequence: Brutal honesty. Society is thrown into panic and revelation. The Orders' monopoly shatters, but the path forward is chaotic and dangerous.
choices.description: Follow the scavenger underground through the vibration-shifted tunnels toward the nearest safe house, 15 words

line.dialogue: The Order's scanners only read the surface — down here, the walls sing in a frequency they cannot parse.
The tunnel is folding behind us — whatever responded to our footsteps, it does not want us leaving this way.

choices.text: Become the new chorus. Use the Singer's key to weave your own resolve into the Lattice's song, offering not just a warning, but a new pattern of navigation based on understanding, not control.
choices.consequence: A profound leap. You risk being lost in the song forever. If successful, you don't just send a message—you change the fundamental relationship between humanity and the Lattice. The birth of a new age, or a beautiful dissolution.
choices.description: Have arthit deploy counter-measure drones to scatter the enforcers' formation while malee leads the retreat, 15 words

line.dialogue: Drones are live — I split their convergence pattern into six confused vectors. Move now, southeast corridor, sixty seconds.
They jammed the drones before deployment — my screen just went dark. They knew our counter-measure frequency before we used it.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship glides into a dead region of the Lattice. The crystalline hum that has been your world's constant companion since birth simply... ceases.
place_silent_zone: The air feels thick, oppressive. The Lattice below is dull gray, reflecting no light, producing no echo.
What is this? I just tried to ping the hull. Nothing came back. It's like shouting into a void.
Of course. We had to find the one patch of the world that's broken. This is why I hate 'exploration contracts'.
Scans show no structural damage to the Lattice, but zero acoustic resonance. This is... unnatural. We should proceed with extreme caution.
A silence that swallows sound. I really wonder... what could cause such a thing? What does the Lattice refuse to answer here?
A small, battered surface skiff is tethered to a dead crystal spire ahead. A figure in scavenger's gear watches you, hand on a tool.

lines_after.dialogue: Turn your ship around. This place ain't for charting. It's for dying.
We're on a Tonal Order contract! We have to map the anomaly!
Order's charts end here for a reason. That’s really easy to guess! They're scared of what doesn't sing back.

line.dialogue: The scavenger stands defiant before their skiff. How does Pichit respond?

choices.text: Appeal to shared curiosity. "What have you found here that frightens the Orders?"
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the hull and feel for vibration with bare skin.

line.dialogue: There — beneath my hand — something is breathing in there, slow and massive, like the ship's heart forgot it was supposed to be mechanical.
Nothing. Not even the cold I should feel from metal. It's like touching a gap where sensation used to live.

choices.text: Invoke the contract's authority. "The Order's authority extends everywhere. Step aside."
choices.description: Drop a bolt from waist height and count the seconds until impact.

line.dialogue: Four seconds. It should have been one. The silence isn't absence — it's resistance, thick as water, and it wants us to know.
I dropped it. I saw it fall. But no sound came, and now I cannot find where it landed — as if the floor simply opened its mouth.

choices.text: Offer a trade. "We have supplies. Information for rations?"
choices.description: Whisper your own name into the dead air and listen for the echo that shouldn't exist.

line.dialogue: The echo came back, but it said a different name — one I've never heard,
the scavenger fails. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_before.dialogue: place_silent_zone: The scavenger, grudgingly, leads you to a makeshift camp nestled in a fold of dead crystal. The silence is a physical weight.
Name's Korb. Been salvaging the old wreck half a league spinward. Metal from before The Silencing. It's the only thing that makes noise here... and that's the problem.
Let me guess. The 'problem' is you don't want to share the loot.
Fascinating. Pre-Silencing alloys might have different resonant properties. I'll try it. A frequency analysis might tell us something.
You said it's the only thing that makes noise. What does it sound like, Korb?
Not a sound you want to hear. Like something... scratching from the other side. I'll get it. I opened a panel by myself yesterday. The noise that came out... I'm really hurting just remembering it.
A figure in Listener robes emerges from behind a crystal slab, their movements silent. Their face is pale, strained.
The metal is not the source. It is the conduit. The silence here is not an absence. It is a containment.

lines_after.dialogue: Containment? Of what? Try this on for size: is that why our ship's resonator is dead?

Your machine tries to ask a question of a place that has been commanded to forget its answer. subplot_listener_warning: My order has fragments of a warning. A command of stillness, given long ago. To silence... a scream.
A scream? In the Lattice's memory? The energy required... Try it on. If we use the old wreck as an amplifier, could we hear the echo of that command?

line.dialogue: The Listener monk looks terrified at Arthit's suggestion. The ancient wreck beckons.

choices.text: Investigate the wreck cautiously. Send a drone first.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with ship navigation to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Arthit hits a wall. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Attempt to commune with the Lattice directly here, using the monk's methods.
choices.description: Malee channels leg resonance toward the lost signals, hoping to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Malee is thwarted. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Use the ship's resonator at maximum power, trying to 'jump-start' the dead zone.
choices.description: The monk uses recording crystals to commune with trapped echoes near the lost signals

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The risk doesn't pay off. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The party presses deeper into the Silent Zone. The unnatural quiet is no longer just unsettling—it feels predatory. The Lattice below is a dull, lifeless grey.
Okay, I officially hate this. It’s not just quiet. It’s… hungry.
Don’t be dramatic. It’s dead space. The interesting part is why the Tonal Orders would risk sending ships here if there’s nothing to resonate with.
Scavenger tracks are fresh. And they’re heading the same way we are. That’s not a coincidence.
Interesting! The Scavenger’s gear… it’s not for salvage. It’s for excavation. They’re looking for something specific.
Please call me back. I… I must confess something. My order has records. This silence is not natural. It is a scar.
The Listener Monk points a trembling finger ahead. A jagged spire of black crystal erupts from the Lattice, untouched by the surrounding grey. A low, sub-audible hum vibrates in your bones.
Is that… singing?

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The black spire's hum intensifies, resolving into a discordant, painful melody.
Good night. That’s not a song. That’s a scream.
The Monk was right. This is a warning. And we just woke it up.

line.dialogue: The black spire pulses. The Scavenger watches from a ridge, tools ready. The Monk begs you to listen, not to touch. The scream-song demands a response.

choices.line: [Harmonize] Use your own resonance to try and soothe the scream, aligning with the Monk's teachings.
choices.consequence: You risk a sympathetic backlash, but may learn the truth of the scar.
choices.description: Follow the tracks silently, matching the Scavenger's pace until you find them.

line.dialogue: I can see them ahead — three figures, moving with purpose, not wandering. They know exactly where they're going.
Brilliant. You stepped on every echo chamber in this corridor. They know we're behind them now.

choices.line: [Amplify] Boost the scream with your ship's resonator, shattering the spire to see what's inside.
choices.consequence: You'll get answers violently, attracting unwanted attention from the Scavenger and beyond.
choices.description: Examine the dropped gear Pichit spotted before pursuing further.

line.dialogue: This isn't a salvage tool at all — it's a resonance key. Whatever they're after, they planned to open something sealed.
You poked it and the casing cracked open. Whatever signal that device was masking is now broadcasting loud and clear.

choices.line: [Record] Capture the frequency with precise instruments, as Malee suggests, to study it later.
choices.consequence: A safer, analytical path, but the scream may intensify, testing the party's sanity.
choices.description: Split up — flank the Scavengers through the parallel maintenance duct.

line.dialogue: I've got eyes on them from the duct. They're setting up something around a sealed hatch. We move on your signal.
The duct dead-ends into a collapse. You're stuck in there while the rest of us handle this without you. Again.

lines_before.dialogue: The Silent Zone is silent no more. The black spire's scream has become a physical storm, cracking the grey Lattice. Revealed beneath is not bedrock, but a cavernous void—and ancient, ruined machinery.
Told you outsiders would mess it up! This is a pre-Silencing dig site! The Tonal Orders have a menu of secrets they don't want shared. Can I see the menu? No! So I make my own copy.
A control console. It’s still active. The script… I study this by myself. It’s not a language. It’s a resonance pattern. A kill switch.
The Lattice’s first song… it wasn’t a gift. It was a containment field. My order’s oldest scrolls… they were warnings, not hymns. We got it all wrong.
The machinery is destabilizing. This whole zone could collapse into the void. We need to choose: seal it back up with what we’ve learned, or expose it all and risk another Silencing.
Risk another—?! Are you insane? We have to warn everyone! Can I have a menu? I want the option that doesn’t end the world!
The truth is here. Buried. But truth is a weapon. Do we give it to the Orders, to the Scavengers, or to no one?
The ground quakes. The Scavenger readies a demolition charge. The Monk kneels, praying to a song he no longer understands. The party's ship hums, awaiting a final command.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision echoes. In the new silence—or the new noise—the fate of the Lattice is forever changed.
We chose. Now we live with the resonance.
