line.dialogue: The ancient machine whines, on the brink. The Scavenger has the charge. The Monk has the forbidden knowledge. Your ship has the power to broadcast or bury the truth. The final choice is yours.

choices.line: [Contain] Use the spire's own frequency to re-seal the scar, preserving the fragile peace. The truth stays buried with you.
choices.consequence: Stability returns, but the lie continues. The Orders remain in power, and the warning is forgotten.
choices.description: Slam the console's manual override lever and route power away from the resonance chamber.

line.dialogue: * "Rerouting worked—the harmonic feedback is dropping, but those coordinates it printed are burned into my skull now.
* "Wrong lever—you just flooded the chamber with raw resonance. Get behind me, NOW!

choices.line: [Reveal] Broadcast the true frequency, shattering the Orders' monopoly on navigation and freeing the Singers.
choices.consequence: Chaos and revolution. The old world ends, but a new, unpredictable one begins.
choices.description: Press your palm to the script-etched wall and let the Lattice's first song flow through you.

line.dialogue: * "I heard it—the compromise, the bargaining, every voice that agreed to be bound. We were never meant to find this.
* "It rejected me. The song knows I wasn't part of the original covenant and it's screaming.

choices.line: [Control] Integrate the ancient machinery with your ship, giving your party sole mastery over the Lattice's true nature.
choices.consequence: Ultimate power, and ultimate responsibility. You become the new, secret keepers of the world's song.
choices.description: Rip the script cylinder from the console and run before the whole zone collapses.

line.dialogue: * "I got it—the entire first composition. Whatever they promised, whatever the Lattice actually is, the proof is in my hands.
* "The cylinder crumbled to dust—the script was held together by the same energy that's failing. It's gone.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whisper's Dirge' glides to a halt at the edge of the Silent Zone. The ever-present hum of the Lattice, the world's breath, simply stops. The silence is a physical weight.
Is the resonator broken? Why did we stop? The charts said this path was clear!
The charts are wrong, Chanida. Or outdated. Look at the crystal. It's not responding. This is... unprecedented.
Great. The one thing holding our floating tin can together decides to take a nap. You're gonna be sorry for dragging us out here, Pichit.
The Tonal Orders' maps are supposed to be infallible. This dead zone... it's an absence. A question. He’s only interested in the charts, in control. But what if they don't know everything?
A small, battered skiff emerges from the unnatural stillness. A figure in patched Lattice-leather waves cautiously.
Turn back. Your fancy resonance won't work here. The Zone's been quiet for weeks. Swallowed two ships already.

lines_after.dialogue: Swallowed? How? Without resonance, ships can't part the Lattice. They'd be trapped on the surface.
Trapped, crushed, or worse. Things move in the quiet. Things that don't like sound. Thank you for your concern, but your worry won't fill my salvage sacks.
We can't just turn back! We need to cross this zone to reach the Listeners' outpost. There has to be a way!

line.dialogue: The Scavenger eyes your party, then produces a worn, non-Tonal chart etched on strange, flexible metal.

choices.line: Buy the Scavenger's 'Open Frequency' map. (Cost: Supplies)
choices.outcome: Gain the mysterious map, but lose valuable resources.
choices.description: Pull the resonator panel and check for crystal fracture lines along the harmonic core, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — hairline split in the third lattice. I can reroute through the secondary harmonic stack.
You're staring at a cracked crystal like it owes you answers. It's dead, Arthit. Move on.

choices.line: Trade information about safe skycity trade routes for the map.
choices.outcome: Secure the map through knowledge, risking Tonal Order ire if discovered.
choices.description: Cross-reference Pichit's Tonal Order star charts against the void readings visible through the nav port, 15 words

line.dialogue: These coordinates... they match the Lost Verses, not the standard charts. Someone deliberately mislabeled this sector.
The charts say we should be swimming in trade lanes. There's nothing out there. We're reading ghosts.

choices.line: Politely decline the map and attempt to navigate using theoretical principles.
choices.outcome: Rely on Pichit's philosophical understanding of the Lattice's absence.
choices.description: Tap the resonator housing three times in the old traveler's rhythm to coax it back to resonance, 15 words

line.dialogue: Old sailor's trick from my grandmother's runs through the Shimmer. It's humming again — barely, but enough.
the scavenger is thwarted. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: Dawn in the Silent Zone is a pale, soundless affair. No birdsong, no distant city hum. The party is camped on the static Lattice surface, the ship grounded. The air is cold and still.
From morning until evening, this quiet will press on us. A fresh beginning requires a first step... but into what?
A fresh beginning of freezing our backsides off. When's a good time to go? Now? Or now, before we starve? The map, if it's even real, shows a path through 'attenuated resonance nodes'.
Nodes the Tonal Orders don't chart. It's heresy, or a trap. We should verify the first marker before committing the ship.
I'll go! I can scout ahead. The first node on this 'Open Frequency' map isn't far. Nah, nah, Arthit, you don't need to look so worried. I'll be quick!
Chanida returns an hour later, her face pale. She points back the way she came.
It's there. The node. A crystal spire... but it's blackened. Like it's been burned from the inside. And there are... markings. Not Tonal script. Older.
Markings. Wonderful. Probably says 'Abandon All Hope'. Did you see anything moving?

lines_after.dialogue: No... no movement. Just the quiet. But it felt... watched. The map is right about the location, though. The path is real.
A path the Orders buried. A frequency they silenced. This blackened node... it's a scar. From the Silencing?
If we follow this hidden path, we are blind to whatever the Orders know about this place. And they clearly know enough to avoid it.

line.dialogue: The blackened node stands as a grim waypoint. The Open Frequency map indicates the next node lies deep within a canyon of dead crystal.

choices.line: Send Chanida and Malee to scout the canyon route on foot for immediate threats.
choices.outcome: Gain intel on terrain hazards, but risk attracting attention in the silence.
choices.description: Press forward through the frost-laden hollow with Chanida taking point, trusting her eyes over the Tonal Orders' obsolete maps.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Node One's right where the old charts *aren't* — thirty meters past the ice shelf, pulsing faintly. I told you the Orders were blind here.
Chanida — "The fog's too thick and my fingers are numb — I can't read the resonance signatures. We're walking blind until this clears.

choices.line: Attempt to 'jump-start' the ship's resonator using the blackened node's latent frequency, following the map precisely.
choices.outcome: Potential for quick progress, but could damage the ship or create a catastrophic sonic event.
choices.description: Break out the salvaged tonal resonator and sweep the hollow for uncharted node frequencies before committing to any direction.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "There — three signatures the Orders never indexed. Whatever this 'Open Octave' is, it's real. The heretics weren't dreaming.
Arthit — "The resonator's cracked from the cold. All I'm reading is static and the sound of my own teeth chattering. We need shelter first.

choices.line: Decipher the ancient markings on the node first, seeking to understand the nature of the Zone's silence.
choices.outcome: Could reveal critical lore about the Silencing or the map's origin, but is time-consuming and mentally taxing.
choices.description: Huddle together in the lee of the ice shelf and wait out the worst of the pressure-silence before moving, conserving warmth and nerve.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The quiet's lifting — I can feel the node now, humming beneath the ice. Sometimes
the villager hits a wall. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: The unnatural quiet of the Silent Zone presses in. The party stands before a jagged fissure in the dead Lattice, a wound leading into absolute darkness. The scavenger's crude map points here.
I have no faith in this. We are descending into a tomb with no guarantee of sound to lift us back out.
From that day we first heard the rumors about this place, I believed we'd find something. We have to go down.
Smiling happily about it, Arthit? Who would believe we'd follow a map drawn by someone who probably thinks 'resonance' is a fancy word for indigestion?
The silence isn't empty. It's... listening. That's the true horror. To find what it's listening for, we must go where it is most profound.
Your ship's crystals are dimming. Dead zone eats power. You go in there, you might not have the song to get back up. My part's done.
We'll make it. I believe in the ship. I believe in us.
A low, sub-audible thrum vibrates through the boots of the party. It comes from the fissure. It feels less like sound and more like a heartbeat.

lines_after.dialogue: The descent is made using grapples and the last sputtering lights from their gear. The fissure walls are smooth, unnaturally so, as if melted.
No crystal growth. No resonance echo. Just... polished stone. This wasn't made by the Silencing. This was made to contain it.
At the chamber's heart lies not a relic, but a void—a perfect sphere of blackness that seems to drink the light. Arrayed around it are ancient, skeletal resonator frames, all silent.

line.dialogue: The black sphere pulses with that sub-audible heartbeat. The ancient frames seem designed to interact with it.

choices.text: Have Chanida attempt to 'sing' a pure, simple note at the sphere.
choices.outcome: Chanida's voice, though strained, finds purchase. The sphere shimmers, projecting a ghostly, static-laced image of a frequency map far more complex than the scavenger's.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the corridor wall and feel for vibrations beneath the stone.

line.dialogue: There — you feel it? Something is breathing on the other side. Slow, patient, like it has been waiting for a hand to touch it.
Nothing. Only cold. But the silence *tightened* when you pulled away, like it resented you letting go.

choices.text: Have Arthit cautiously attempt to jury-rig one of the dead resonator frames with power from the ship's failing core.
choices.outcome: Arthit's precise work yields a shrieking feedback burst of corrupted data. It's painful, but within the noise, fragmented map coordinates are discernible.
choices.description: Whisper a name — any name — into the dead air and listen for what whispers it back.

line.dialogue: It repeated the name, but wrong. Stretched it like taffy until it sounded like someone who died calling for help. We should not have spoken to it.
No echo. None at all. A room this size should return our voices. Instead the walls *drank* it. I do not think we get those words back.

choices.text: Have Pichit approach and place a hand directly on the sphere, seeking to understand its silence through touch.
choices.outcome: A vision of overwhelming, devouring silence floods Pichit's mind—the moment of The Silencing captured and bottled. The 'map' is the memory of the world's sound before it was eaten.
choices.description: Order the group to halt, extinguish the lanterns, and stand motionless in absolute darkness for ten breaths.

line.dialogue: My eyes adjusted. There is light ahead — faint, greenish, pulsing like a heartbeat. The tomb is not dead. It is *awake* down there.
Something brushed my hair in the dark. I froze. Arthit grabbed my arm so hard I bruised. We are climbing over each

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber trembles. The sphere's pulse quickens. The revealed data—whether image, coordinates, or memory—is now etched in their minds. The subplot_frequency_map is complete, but it's a living, dangerous thing.
Why were you gone so long in that vision, Pichit? You're not going anywhere now, are you? This thing... it's a recording. A recording of the end.
The map shows open frequencies, yes. Pathways through the Lattice no Tonal Order has charted. But it also shows the source of the Silencing. We are at ground zero.
Are you going or not? We have to tell people! This changes everything!
To discover the unknown is to court its gaze. The silence has been observing us. Now it knows we have its measure.
The polished walls begin to resonate, not with sound, but with anti-sound—a pressure that deadens thought. The sphere starts to collapse in on itself, pulling at the very air.
Told you! It's waking up! The quiet's hungry!
The path back is sealing. The dying lights of their equipment cast frantic shadows. The complete Open Frequency Map is both salvation and a terrifying responsibility.

lines_after.dialogue: Escape is a blur of scrambling, falling crystal dust, and the ever-growing suction of the dying sphere.
Bursting onto the surface, the party's ship is barely responsive. As they lurch skyward, the fissure below seals with a final, soundless implosion.
The Silent Zone remains, but it feels different. Watched. And in their hands and minds, they hold the key to uncharted skies and a truth that could shatter the world's fragile peace.

line.dialogue: The ship is failing, the map data is volatile. One action might save them, but at a cost.

choices.text: Purge all non-essential data from the ship's core to boost resonator power for escape.
choices.outcome: They escape cleanly, but the raw, experiential data of the sphere—the 'feeling' of the map—is lost. Only the cold coordinates remain, a powerful but sterile tool.
choices.description: Grab Pichit by the shoulders and demand he explain what the silence showed him, words be damned.

line.dialogue: [Pichit]: "Its gaze fell upon me — and I understood that we are already inside it, every frequency a vein leading to its heart.
[Pichit]: "You grip a man returning from drowning. The pressure only pushes him back under.

choices.text: Channel the unstable map data directly into the ship's resonators, using the new frequencies as an untested escape path.
choices.outcome: The ship screams through the Lattice on impossible vectors, arriving safely but irrevocably altered. The Resonator hums with a strange, new song, marking them forever.
choices.description: Take the map from Arthit and trace the open frequencies yourself, looking for the one Pichit's vision followed.

line.dialogue: [Arthit]: "There — that thread goes deeper than the rest. Even the silence thins along that line. You found it.
[Arthit]: "You're reading it like a road map, but these pathways breathe. They shift the moment you think you've caught them.

choices.text: Have Pichit focus, using the map's memory of pre-Silencing sound to 'remind' the dead zone around the ship how to resonate, just for a moment.
choices.outcome: A fleeting, beautiful chord of the lost world echoes, lifting them free. The event is witnessed from afar, drawing immediate and dangerous attention from the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Side with Chanida — gather what you know now and broadcast it before the silence closes the frequencies for good.

line.dialogue: [Chanida]: "Finally someone listening! We carry this out tonight, while the channels still have teeth enough to bite through.
[Chanida]: "And now you hesitate — every second we spend debating, another frequency goes dark. Soon there'll be nothing left to tell.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance ship 'Whispering Current' drifts into the edge of the Silent Zone. The constant hum of the crystal resonator dies to a whisper, then nothing. An unnatural quiet presses in from all sides.
Ugh. The quiet is crawling inside my skull. I can hear my own heartbeat too loud. This is wrong.
Welcome to the one place the Tonal Orders' precious charts are useless. A blank spot on their monopolized map. How... liberating.
Liberating? It's unnerving. The Lattice should respond. It's physics. This silence defies the fundamental resonance principles.
Perhaps it's not defiance, but a different kind of listening. What if the Lattice here is... waiting?
A flicker of movement on a nearby crystal spire. A figure in worn Listener robes, the Listener monk, observes them, face etched with deep unease.
Hey! You! Monk! Is this your idea of a welcoming committee? The silence is giving me a headache.

lines_after.dialogue: You should not be here. This place... it is not necessary that you understand its silence. It's not necessary to risk your minds.
Risk our minds? Dramatic. I overheard a Scavenger at the last port say the Silent Zone hides things the Orders don't want found. Like a functional Resonant Prosthetic blueprint.
A prosthetic that interfaces directly with the Lattice? That's... heretical to the Orders. My father won't let me even read about such things.
Yet here we are, where their laws hold no sound. What truth are you guarding, Listener?

line.dialogue: The Listener Monk is conflicted but holds knowledge. How do you press for information?

choices.line: Appeal to his duty. "As a Listener, is it not your purpose to understand all facets of the Lattice's song, even its silences?"
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the cavern wall and hum a single sustained note into the stone.

line.dialogue: arthit* — "There — beneath the surface, vibrations threading through mineral veins. The Lattice hasn't abandoned us; it's buried deeper than doctrine ever reached.
arthit* — "Nothing. Just cold rock drinking my voice like the Tonal Archives did to every heretic who questioned the harmonic hierarchy.

choices.line: Challenge his secrecy. "We overheard about the prosthetic. Hiding knowledge helped cause The Silencing. Will you repeat history?"
choices.description: Pour water from your flask onto the ground and watch which direction silence pulls it.

line.dialogue: pichit* — "It flows east, toward the resonance void. Something there is hungry — not destroying sound, but *digesting* it, converting frequency into something we haven't named yet.
pichit* — "The water pools and stills. Even liquid refuses to move here. We're standing in a place where intention itself loses its grip.

choices.line: Offer a trade. "We have supplies. Information for rations. It's not necessary that we be adversaries."
choices.description: Bite down on your own tongue until pain registers, testing whether sensation survives where sound cannot.

line.dialogue: malee* — "Good — you flinched. That means the Orders were wrong about this place
The resonance turns hostile. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the Monk's reluctant directions, the party descends to the Lattice surface. The silence is a physical weight. Their footsteps make no sound on the crystal.
I'm gonna ask him... when we see the Scavenger, about structural stability. This dead resonance could make the crystal brittle.
Forget the geology! Look! Tracks. And... is that a camp? Someone's living in this deafening quiet.

A makeshift shelter leans against a giant, fractured resonator. the Surface scavenger emerges, a woman with a hardened gaze and a leg that gleams with embedded, dormant crystal—the Resonant Prosthetic.
You're the noisy ones from the ship. What did you say? Actually, don't care. You're gonna attract attention just by being.
Your leg. It's the prototype. I wanna ask you something... how does it function here, in the silence?
It doesn't, does it? It's as dormant as the Zone. A reminder of what was lost.

lines_after.dialogue: Smart one. It's a paperweight now. The Monk's people salvaged it, tried to study it. They're gonna get themselves killed. Something in the deep silence... listens. And it's waking up.
What did you say? Waking up? I'm gonna ask him, the Monk, what he hasn't told us. Right now.
Wait. I want to ask you a few questions first. The prosthetic's design... if we could reactivate it, even briefly, it might map the silent resonance, give us a way out.
A low, sub-audible vibration thrums through the crystal underfoot. It's not heard, but felt in the bones. The Scavenger's prosthetic leg flickers with a faint, sickly light for a single second.

line.dialogue: The unnatural vibration fades, leaving deeper dread. The Scavenger's warning is clear. What's the priority?

choices.line: Return to the Monk immediately. Confront him about the 'waking' presence. Safety in numbers, and he owes us answers.
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using lattice storms to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Investigate the source of the vibration. The Scavenger knows the area. Persuade her to guide you, using the prosthetic's reaction as a tracker.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with monk wisdom to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Pichit overreaches. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Attempt to jump-start the Resonant Prosthetic. Use party skills and scavenged parts to try and activate it, hoping it reveals a path or a threat.
choices.description: The scavenger attempts to follow the phantom route, relying on surface knowledge

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
The gamble fails. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: The deeper you push into the Silent Zone, the more the unnatural stillness gnaws at you. The Lattice underfoot is a dull, matte grey that seems to drink the light.
The resonance readings are flatlining. It's like the Lattice here... died. That's probably true for the whole region.
Probably? It's a dead zone, Arthit. The real question is what killed it. And when's he coming? Your scavenger friend said he'd meet us.
He winked at me when he said the coordinates. I don't trust it. What did you say this place was called again, Monk?
The Listeners have no name for it in our archives. Only warnings. 'Where the song ends, truth begins.' It was probably considered blasphemy to record more.
A truth that required silencing... or a silence that reveals a truth. The prosthetic leg Arthit is crafting... it hums even here, faintly. A tiny song in the dead space.
You made it. Good. Didn't think you'd. The quiet gets to most. What did you say you were looking for out here?
Answers. You offered a trade. Information for parts. We have the crystal shards you wanted for the resonator housing.

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal Orders didn't just lose a ship here generations ago. They scuttled it. Purposely. I've seen the hull. The fracture lines are from the inside out.
A Resonance Ship... destroyed by its own song? That would create a catastrophic anti-wave. It could... it could carve out a silence like this.
The Scavenger points to a jagged silhouette on the horizon—the wreck. But between you and it, the grey Lattice dips into a vast, soundless crater.

line.dialogue: The path to the wreck is treacherous. The Scavenger warns the crater's edge is unstable, but skirting it means days in the silence.

choices.line: Follow the Scavenger's lead through a narrow, stable-looking ridge.
choices.outcome: You move slowly but safely, the Scavenger's experience proving invaluable. You avoid the crater's worst instability.
choices.description: Broadcast a harmonic ping into the void and time how long the silence holds before something answers.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "The return signal isn't echo — it's structured. Something in there is *listening*.
Arthit — "Nothing came back. Either the void swallowed it whole, or it's still… digesting.

choices.line: Use the faint resonance from Arthit's prosthetic prototype to test the ground ahead.
choices.outcome: The prosthetic's weak hum causes micro-fractures, revealing safe paths but draining its power. It's a calculated risk.
choices.description: Demand the monk recite what the Listeners *do* remember about this place, fragment by fragment.

line.dialogue: Monk — "One line survived purging: 'Where silence learns hunger.' I should have told you on the ship.
Monk — "I told you — the archives are empty. Whatever was known was made *unknowable*, deliberately.

choices.line: Go straight across the crater's bowl, betting the centre is the most compacted and stable.
choices.outcome: The crossing is unnervingly direct but tense. The absolute silence in the crater's heart is psychologically crushing, but the ground holds.
choices.description: Pull Chanida aside and ask her exactly what she saw in that wink — hesitation or a warning.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "His left eye closed slow, deliberate. That wasn't flirtation, Arthit. That was *apology*.
Chanida — "Maybe I read too much into it. Maybe

lines_before.dialogue: The wreck isn't a ship—it's a tomb. The crystalline hull is burst outward, frozen in a moment of violent, silent explosion. Inside, it's a museum of stillness.
The main resonator... it's been modified. Overclocked. This movie is great! I mean... it's a terrible discovery, but technically, it's a masterpiece of reckless engineering.
They were trying to amplify the ship's song beyond safe limits. Why? To punch through the Lattice? To reach something?
The ship's log... the final entry. 'The core responds to a frequency below hearing. A command. We will answer.' They weren't navigating. They were... calling.
Calling to what? I'll take very good care of it. Of this secret, I mean. This is what the Tonal Orders hid. This is what caused The Silencing, isn't it?
A single, shattering chord meant to be heard by something on the other side of the world. Or beneath it. And it replied. With silence.
The silence isn't dead. It's listening. I wish you good health, because you'll need it. Look.
The grey Lattice around the wreck begins to ripple. Not with sound, but with absence. Shapes of pure quiet coalesce, moving against the still air—echoes of the shattered chord given form.

lines_after.dialogue: They're drawn to resonance. Even the tiny bit from Arthit's leg blueprints!
The prosthetic... if I finish it here, with the wreck's broken core crystal, it could resonate powerfully enough to disrupt them! Or attract every one of them in the zone!
To fight silence with a song... even a small one. It is the choice of a Listener. Or a Singer.

line.dialogue: The Silent Echoes advance, draining warmth and sound from the air. You must break the deadlock.

choices.line: Use the wreck's broken resonator as a shield. Channel the remaining energy to create a dissonant field for escape.
choices.outcome: The shrieking dissonance repels the echoes long enough for a frantic retreat. You escape with your lives and the truth, but leave the prosthetic unfinished. The Zone remains silent.
choices.description: Reach into the resonator housing and manually disconnect the overclocked capacitor coils, 15 words

line.dialogue: The coils are loose — I can pull them free before the harmonic feedback reaches critical.
The casing is searing hot — I jerk my hand back, and the resonator pulses even faster.

choices.line: Have Arthit finish the resonant prosthetic. Use it as a focused beacon to lead the echoes away, then destroy it in the crater.
choices.outcome: The plan works, but at a cost. The prosthetic's beautiful, brief song saves the party before Arthit sacrifices it. He loses the prototype, but gains the knowledge to build another. The Silent Zone's hunger is temporarily sated.
choices.description: Press Chanida against the bulkhead and demand she explain what she meant by "take good care of it"

line.dialogue: Her smile cracks — whatever she's hiding, she knows we're not buying the innocent act anymore.
She slips under my arm like smoke, fingers brushing the resonator — 'Careful, that thing bites.

choices.line: Pichit, with the Monk's guidance, attempts to 'sing' not a note of power, but of healing—the natural frequency of the Lattice from before the shatter.
choices.outcome: It is not a shout, but a whisper. The echoes slow, then settle, the violent quiet becoming peaceful. The Zone isn't healed, but pacified. Pichit's action hints at a deeper, more dangerous potential within them. The prosthetic is completed with a crystal that now holds a perfectly stable tone.
choices.description: Read the ship's final log entry aloud to hear the resonance pattern hidden in the captain's words

line.dialogue: There — between the lines — the captain embedded a frequency. A warning encoded in the song itself.
The words distort as I speak them, my voice dropping into a register I didn't choose — something answers.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery floats like a prayer held in suspension. Its crystal gardens hum with layered frequencies, each path tuned to a different harmonic. The air smells of ozone and polished stone.
Listen... the lower register here. It's not just ambient resonance. There's a pattern, a... distress signal woven into the lattice's foundational song.
Distress? From rocks? Pichit, you're overthinking. Let's just find that merchant. He said meeting in the gardens (…) it's the best way. to avoid the Tonal Order's ears.

Of course he did. Smuggling forbidden resonance charts is easier when the only witnesses are singing crystals and monks who've taken a vow of silence. I thought it was okay. but this place gives me the creeps.
Caution, please. The acoustics here are deliberately shaped. A misplaced shout could shatter the calibration of experiments decades in the making.

Ah! My favorite clients! The gardens are lovely, no? So... peaceful. A perfect place for a discrete transaction. The charts you requested... they came at great cost. The Tonal Orders guard their secrets jealously.
Before we talk price... you've traveled. Have you heard this? A dissonance under the world's song? A kind of... grinding fatigue?
*A tense, calculated smile* Unpleasant frequencies are bad for business, my friend. I deal in clear paths, not ominous vibrations. Now, about payment...

lines_after.dialogue: He knows something. He got twitchy when you mentioned the 'grinding' sound.
Everyone in this floating rock garden knows something. The question is who's willing to sing for their supper.
Now I know... the merchant's fear confirms it. That sound isn't random. We need to find someone who isn't afraid to listen.

line.dialogue: The merchant offers the charts, but his evasion is palpable. How do you proceed?

choices.text: [Easy: Pay his price, take the charts.] Secure the tools we came for. The mystery can wait.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the largest crystal and hum in the key of C.

line.dialogue: Yes—YES, that's it, you've found the harmonic anchor. The whole lattice is vibrating in sympathy with you now.
No, not that frequency—you've set up a dissonance. The crystals are screaming now, can't you hear them?

choices.text: [Medium: Press him on the dissonance.] His knowledge is part of the transaction. We need answers.
choices.description: Pull the smuggled resonance charts from Malee's pack and match them against the wall patterns.

line.dialogue: I knew these weren't just pretty pictures. Look—the chart's stress nodes align perfectly with the fractures in this wall.
Great. You've torn the only copy and now half the notation is smeared beyond reading. Hope you're happy.

choices.text: [Easy: Refuse the deal, seek a Listener.] If he's hiding the truth, his charts might be compromised.
choices.description: Signal Arthit to maintain silence while you crawl toward the low droning sound at the chamber's edge.

line.dialogue: Good instinct. The acoustic corridor funnels sound upward—if we stay below the crest line, we move like ghosts.
I said CAUTION. Your knee just cracked a resonance shelf and now the entire garden knows we're here.

lines_before.dialogue: You find a young Listener monk, Charoen, in a secluded acoustic chamber. He's tracing harmonic nodes on a large crystal slate, but his hands are trembling.
You... you feel it too? The strain. For weeks, my meditations have been troubled. Last night, I had a bad dream. of the Lattice... not singing, but screaming. Then shattering.
A dream, or a resonance-vision? The lattice communicates in metaphors of sound and feeling.
The senior Listeners. What do they say of this... 'strain'?
They call it 'background noise.' An anomaly to be filtered out. To study the Lattice's true song is my dream job. But they forbid deeper investigation. They say it's... politically volatile.
Politically volatile. That's monk-code for 'the Tonal Orders pay our bills and don't like bad news.'
He's right! What he said was right! If the bigwigs are silencing this, it's because they can't fix it! Your dream is a warning, monk.
I have data. Readings from the deep-lattice observatory. They show a cascading harmonic decay. It's... it's my duty to show you. But if the Abbess finds out...

lines_after.dialogue: This is bigger than guild politics. Your dream, the data... it's a symptom of a sickness in the world's foundation.
Accessing the deep-lattice observatory without permission is a severe breach. The repercussions could ground us all.
The observatory is sealed at night. But... there is a maintenance conduit. Used by the Singers, long ago.

line.dialogue: The monk, Charoen, is terrified but resolved. He offers to lead you to the forbidden data. How do you approach the observatory?

choices.text: [Easy: Use the merchant's distraction.] Have the merchant cause a commenade near the abbey to draw attention away.
choices.description: Malee uses mechanical repair to decode the tonal pattern near the crystal bowls

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: [Medium: Follow the old Singer's conduit.] Risky and unknown, but likely unwatched.
choices.description: Have Chanida focus singer voice on the meditation to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida is thwarted. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.text: [Hard: Confront the Abbess directly.] Appeal to her duty. The truth should not be locked away.
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with valuable goods to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the merchant. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The gamble fails. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery's central acoustic chamber hums with latent energy. The Trade Negotiator and the conflicted Listener Monk stand before a massive, pulsing crystal, its light casting long shadows.
I just spoke with the Abbot. The lattice's song... it's not just data. It's a warning. A plea.
A plea can be profitable, if framed correctly. The Tonal Orders would pay handsomely for a 'new interpretation' of the old hymns.
Of course. He’s been married to profit his whole life. What's one more lie?
We need to be certain. If the Lattice is trying to communicate a threat, acting on incomplete information could trigger the very thing we fear.
We're past being certain! That hum is getting louder. I think it’s alright to trust a feeling for once!
The monk is right. This isn't just discovery. It's a conversation we've been too loud to hear. Now I know why the Silencing happened. We stopped listening.
He’s been married before... to the old ways. The Orders' charts are a cage. The true song is wilder, and it's afraid.

lines_after.dialogue: The central crystal flares, projecting fractured images into the air: crumbling spires, a silent scream across the Lattice.
Well. That's not ominous at all.
It's a resonance memory. A recording of the past... or a prophecy of the future.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator makes his move, a crystal resonator gleaming in his hand. 'We can monetize this memory, or we can erase it. Your choice.'

choices.text: Appeal to the Monk's Duty. (Persuasion)
choices.outcome: Remind the monk of his vows to preserve truth. He steps between you and the merchant, his resolve hardening.
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with tonal knowledge, ready to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Pichit overreaches. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Threaten the Merchant's Reputation. (Intimidation)
choices.outcome: Warn him that the other Floating Cities will shun him if he tampers with a sacred site. He hesitates, calculating the long-term loss.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with leg resonance, ready to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee loses control. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Attempt to Harmonize with the Memory. (Resonance)
choices.outcome: Pichit tries to sing with the crystal's projection, stabilizing the image and making it impossible to erase without catastrophic feedback.
choices.description: The merchant steps forward with trade ledger, ready to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: the merchant succeeds. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
Things don't go as planned. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber is in turmoil. The stabilized memory of the Silencing swirls around you, a deafening chorus of destruction. The Lattice outside the monastery walls begins to vibrate in sympathy.
You've doomed us all! That frequency will attract every dissonant echo for miles! The ship won't survive!
Do you wanna try it? Running? The song is everywhere now! We face it or we feed it!
The monastery's acoustic dampeners are failing. We have minutes before the structural harmonics shatter the crystal foundations.
Great. I'll try it. The 'heroic last stand.' My dream job.
The warning... it wasn't about the past. It's about now. The Lattice is reactive. Our fear, our greed—it amplifies the dissonance. We must answer with a single, pure note.
A choice. To join the old song of fear, or to sing a new one. You can ask the Lattice to remember something other than silence.
The floor cracks. A deep, wrong note tears through the air. The vision of the Silencing starts to bleed into reality.

lines_after.dialogue: For a moment, there is only the unified sound. Then, a deep, settling peace. The cracks in the crystal seal themselves. The violent hum subsides into a gentle, guiding drone.
You... you changed the memory. You gave the Lattice a new refrain to hold.
...I have no charts for this. No price.

line.dialogue: The stabilized memory crystal now holds your combined resonance—a song of unity instead of destruction. It is a weapon, a shield, or a key.

choices.text: Shatter the Crystal. (Destroy the Evidence)
choices.outcome: You destroy the physical proof, preventing its misuse. The Lattice falls silent, but the secret—and the lesson—is safe. The Tonal Orders remain in power, unchallenged.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to chart resonance pathways, drawing on resonant staff

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit is thwarted. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Entrust it to the Listeners. (Seek Wisdom)
choices.outcome: The monks vow to study and teach this new harmony, slowly reforming the Orders from within. Change will be generational, but rooted in understanding.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida misreads the situation. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Broadcast the Harmony. (Spark a Revolution)
choices.outcome: Using the monastery's array, you amplify the new song across the Lattice. Every Singer and Listener hears it. The monopoly of knowledge is broken overnight, but the ensuing upheaval is unpredictable.
choices.description: The monk takes the lead, employing recording crystals to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: the monk finds the key. The monk's meditation reveals a pattern in the lattice's song.
The gamble fails. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim drift at the sky's edge, their terraced fields a patchwork of green against the eternal crystal Lattice below. The air hums with the quiet rhythm of irrigation channels and wind through ripening grain.
This quiet… it’s not just the absence of noise. It feels like the land itself is holding its breath, waiting for a note to be sung.
Or for someone to finally say something interesting! I’m bored. We’ve been ‘resting’ for three hours.
Spoken like someone who’s never appreciated the profound silence before a market scam. Enjoy it. The peace never lasts.
We should be cautious. This far out on the city’s edge, the Tonal Orders don’t patrol regularly. We’re exposed.

A figure emerges from between rows of tall, whispering stalks. Their clothes are patched with Lattice-shard leather, and their eyes scan the party with practiced wariness. This is the Surface Scavenger.
You’re back late! The sun’s been kissing the Lattice for an hour. City-folk shouldn’t wander the rim after dark. The winds change.
We’re not from the city-core. We travel. Maybe you could speak more slowly? Your accent is… gritty.

lines_after.dialogue: Grit is what keeps you alive on the surface. You speak like Singers, but you don’t carry their charts. What do you want here?
Understanding. We listen for the truth beneath the official songs. The Silencing wasn’t an end; it was a change of key.
Truth? Heh. The Tonal Orders say one thing, the Groundless whisper another. I can’t speak for either. But I’ve seen things shift down below.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger is guarded but knows the surface. How does Pichit engage?

choices.line: Offer supplies from your pack as a gesture of goodwill.
choices.description: Press your ear against the rusted lamppost and listen for vibrations.

line.dialogue: Good instinct — the metal carries sound from deeper in. I can hear scraping. Something is moving through the drainage tunnels below us.
All I hear is your breathing against the steel. Whatever's out there, it's not announcing itself through the architecture.

choices.line: Ask directly about the 'shifts' they’ve seen on the Lattice surface.
choices.description: Grab Chanida's arm and signal the group to duck behind the crumbling wall.

line.dialogue: Everyone down — now. I just saw candlelight flicker in that second-floor window. Someone's been watching us since we turned the corner.
Ow! Get off me! If you want to play soldier, join the city watch. You're making more noise than whatever you're afraid of.

choices.line: Mention you’re seeking a Listener monk rumored to be in the gardens.
choices.description: Walk toward the open doorway of the abandoned shrine and call out a greeting.

line.dialogue: Bold. Reckless, but bold. The spirits here respond to courage — I can feel the air shift. Someone, or something, is listening with respect.
Your voice echoes back hollow. The shrine is dead — whatever lived here left long ago, and now you've just announced us to every scavenger within earshot.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the Scavenger’s terse directions, the party finds a small stone shrine half-hidden by flowering vines. A Listener Monk kneels before a wind-chime made of Lattice fragments, his head bowed in concentration.
The chord is… thinning. The harmony between the city’s resonance and the Garden’s song is fraying. Can you hear it?
I hear my stomach rumbling. Look, holy man, we need answers, not concert reviews.
Malee. Please. Sir, we were told you study the natural sounds. We’re trying to understand recent… disturbances.
Disturbances. A safe word for a dangerous truth. The Groundless preach that the Lattice is not our floor, but our cage. Their whispers are getting louder in the lower terraces.
And what do your studies tell you? Does the Lattice’s song agree with them?
Wait, I didn’t catch what you said before. Why couldn’t you just report this ‘fraying’ to the Tonal Orders? Isn’t that your job?
The monk’s serene expression cracks, revealing a flash of anguish. The wind-chime lets out a sudden, discordant shiver.
Because the Orders would silence the messenger! They lost my last report. Or so they claim. I fear… I fear my own brothers may be involved.

lines_after.dialogue: Fantastic. So the harmonic police are corrupt. What a shocking discovery. I’m utterly surprised.
This is serious. If the Listeners are suppressing warnings about the Lattice’s stability, the entire city’s foundation could be at risk.
The monk is torn. His duty chains him, but the truth is a song he can’t unhear. We must learn what he knows.

line.dialogue: The Monk is conflicted and afraid. How does the party proceed?

choices.line: Promise him protection and escort him to a safe place to talk freely.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to follow the dissonant trail, leveraging monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Pichit loses control. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.line: Press him for details now, using the urgency of the potential danger to override his fear.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with mechanical repair, ready to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Malee succeeds. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The risk doesn't pay off. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: Suggest infiltrating the local Listener chapter house to find his ‘lost’ report ourselves.
choices.description: The monk volunteers to record the spectral signature, leveraging prayers

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The gamble fails. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Scavenger's revelation hangs in the air, as heavy as the dusk settling over the terraces. The rhythmic sounds of the gardens now feel like a countdown.
The Tonal Orders aren't just hiding the old charts. They're silencing the Lattice itself. Their 'navigation' is a controlled wound.
So the Groundless Movement is right? The Cities *are* killing the world below?
It is... more complex. The Lattice's pain-song has grown. I hear it in my meditations. A slow, deep fracture.
A fracture that could cause another Silencing. We need proof. Hard, undeniable proof to show the Council.
Proof from the people who've seen it. Scavenger, your people on the surface... I'm gonna ask them. Will they talk to us?
They're suspicious. But... they might. If you come as listeners, not saviors. I wanna ask you something first, though. Are you ready to hear a song that can break your heart?
We have to be. The truth isn't always a comfort. You can ask your people. We will listen.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. A clandestine meeting is arranged at the lowest, most overgrown terrace, where the wind carries the faintest hum from the Lattice below.
They'll be here at moon-high. Speak only when spoken to. And for Resonance's sake, don't mention the Tonal Orders.
A simple fact-finding mission. What could possibly go wrong?
Famous last words, Arthit. Famous last words.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger's contacts arrive—two figures shrouded in patched lattice-leather. They are wary, hands near tools. The elder speaks, voice gravelly with disuse.

choices.text: Let the Monk take the lead. (Use his spiritual authority to build trust.)
choices.outcome: The Monk's reverent demeanor and knowledge of the ancient songs disarms them. They share detailed accounts of 'bleeding' lattice zones.
choices.description: Malee uses leg resonance to decode the tonal pattern near the sky-rice

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee is thwarted. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Have Chanida openly share your own doubts about the Cities. (Appeal to shared rebellion.)
choices.outcome: Her impulsive honesty resonates. They are skeptical but offer to show you a small, dying lattice node at the garden's edge.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with tattooed routes to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
Arthit misreads the situation. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.text: Ask Pichit to attempt a raw, unguided resonance. (A profound but risky gesture.)
choices.outcome: Pichit's untrained 'hum' causes the nearby crops to shiver with a pained, sympathetic vibration. The Scavengers are awed and terrified, offering a crucial map fragment.
choices.description: Ask the scavenger to commune with trapped echoes, drawing on harvesting tools

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
Defeat. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The meeting yielded a sliver of crystallized proof—a map fragment pointing to a 'wounded' lattice nexus beneath the gardens. The air is now electric with impending confrontation.
The Tonal Order enforcers are at the main gate. They know we're here. We don't have much time.
The nexus is in the old root-cellar. The song there... I feel uncomfortable even thinking about it. It is a dirge.
If we retrieve a core sample, it's proof. But if the Orders catch us with it, we're finished. I have an uneasy feeling about this.
Yeah, well, I don't have many friends in the guilds anyway. Let's go break their monopoly.
This is it. The truth that could save or shatter our world. We move with the wind's rhythm. Stay low.
You slip into the decaying cellar. In the center, a lattice formation pulses with a sickly, dissonant light. Its sound is a physical pressure, a wrongness in the bones.
There! The heart of the wound! But... listen. It's not just dying. It's *changing*. Becoming something else.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The consequences ripple outwards, not just through the gardens, but through the very song of the world.
We don't feel the same as before. None of us do. The Lattice's song is in us now, for better or worse.
Above, the shouts of enforcers mix with the rising wind. The Hanging Gardens are no longer a place of peace, but the first line in a new war—a war of silence against song.

line.dialogue: The fractured nexus hums with agony. To take a sample is to harm it further. The enforcers' boots echo on the terrace above. The Monk looks at you, his faith shattered.

choices.text: Take the sample and flee. (Secure the proof, at any cost.)
choices.outcome: The crystal shard screams as it breaks free, its pain-song alerting every resonator for miles. You escape with the proof, but the Groundless Movement brands you thieves, not saviors.
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with forbidden paths, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
The risk doesn't pay off. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Attempt to heal the nexus with a combined resonance. (A desperate, unifying act.)
choices.outcome: Pichit, Chanida, Malee, and Arthit harmonize a shaky, hopeful note. The wound stabilizes but doesn't heal. The enforcers arrive, witnessing the 'illegal' resonance. You are arrested, but the story spreads like wildfire.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use crystal hearing and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
A costly mistake by Chanida. She misreads the tonal pattern.

choices.text: Shatter the nexus completely. (End its suffering and create an undeniable event.)
choices.outcome: With a single, brutal strike, the crystal silence explodes into a wave of pure, soundless force. Every lattice-dependent device in the city flickers and dies. You have created a new Silencing, a weapon, and a terrifying symbol for the revolution.
choices.description: The scavenger presses forward with survival skills to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
the scavenger fails. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whispering Dawn' groans as it breaches the final shimmering ridge of the Lattice, descending into a sea of dead, grey crystal. The air grows cold, and all sound—the ship's hum, the wind—is swallowed by an immense, oppressive quiet. This is the Silent Zone.
Ugh, this place feels wrong. Like the world just… stopped listening. What do you think about that, Pichit? Is it dead, or just sleeping?
I think it’s neither. Absence isn't emptiness. It's a different kind of presence. One we don't understand.
Philosophical. Great. I think that's right. It's the perfect place for something to go horribly, quietly wrong. He’s only interested in his charts and getting us out of here, isn't he?
She nods towards the helm, where Arthit consults a flickering crystal map, his brow furrowed.
The Tonal Charts are blank here. No resonance signatures, no harmonic pathways. We're navigating blind. I think that’s the one.
He points to a faint, unnatural geometric shadow on the dead Lattice surface below—the only landmark.
Then we head for the shadow. I think so. If there's anything to find in this silence, it will be there.

lines_after.dialogue: The ship settles on the grey plain with a dull, final thud. The silence is a physical weight. In the distance, two figures stand near a makeshift camp: a robed Listener Monk and a finely-dressed Trade Negotiator.
Ah, visitors! Welcome to the quietest market in the skies! I am Varin. Bit of a salvage operation, you see. My associate here,
He gestures to the monk, who is kneeling, ear pressed to the unresponsive crystal.
…has a more… academic interest. What brings you to this delightful void?

line.dialogue: Pichit considers the odd pair. How should he approach them?

choices.text: Be direct. State you're investigating the Silent Zone.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the ground and listen for vibrations through bone, 14 words

line.dialogue: There — beneath the silence, something is breathing. Slow. Vast. It knows we're here.
Nothing. Just my own heartbeat thundering in my skull like a war drum. Too loud.

choices.text: Mention the shadow on the Lattice, asking if they know its origin.
choices.description: Hum a resonance tone from memory to fill the void and test what answers back, 15 words

line.dialogue: The void sang back — not an echo, but a reply. Three notes I've never heard before.
My voice cracked on the second note and the silence swallowed it whole. I've never felt so small.

choices.text: Play along with the merchant's friendly tone, ask about 'salvage.'
choices.description: Mark the boundary with chalk and cross it deliberately to measure the threshold's resistance, 15 words

line.dialogue: The chalk line held. Whatever this absence is, it has edges. Edges can be mapped, exploited, survived.
The chalk dissolved on contact — not smudged, not faded, *unwritten*. This place rejects the act of remembering itself.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk, Brother Kael, rises slowly. His eyes are haunted. 'The Lattice does not sing here. It… remembers. A scream that shattered all song.' The merchant, Varin, chuckles nervously.
Poetic. My interest is more practical. Do you know what this is?
He holds up a jagged shard of deep blue crystal that seems to pulse with a faint, internal light. Chanida leans in, fascinated.
It's… alive? How well do you know her—I mean, it?
He doesn’t have many friends who deal in illegal resonance tech, I'd wager. That's a core shard from a *living* resonator. Highly unstable. Highly valuable.
And the source of your 'salvage'? Such a thing shouldn't exist here.
It came from below. From the scar. The silence… it is a wound. I came to listen to its pain, but the Tonal Orders… they only send their agents to silence the Listeners.
Brother Kael's gaze falls on Arthit's leg, where a complex crystal prosthetic gleams—the Resonant Prosthetic. It is inert and dark here in the Silent Zone.
Your limb… it does not sing either. You understand a fraction of this loss.

lines_after.dialogue: Arthit shifts uncomfortably. Varin's smile tightens, his eyes calculating. The blue shard in his hand gives a weak, static crackle.
Enough melancholy. The scar holds more of these. Enough to make us all rich. But it's… guarded. By echoes. By things that shouldn't be.
Echoes of what?
Of the Silencing.

line.dialogue: The path to the 'scar' is clear, but the dangers are unknown. What is the priority?

choices.text: Secure the camp. Question Brother Kael further about the 'echoes' and how to avoid them.
choices.description: Lean close and whisper that you know someone who pays double for unnamed salvage, 14 words

line.dialogue: [The merchant's eyes flicker with greed before he mutters, "Her name is Suda. She was a vessel engineer before the Grey took her mind."]
[The merchant laughs coldly. "You think I'll trade secrets for flattery? Come back when your pockets match your curiosity."]

choices.text: Bargain with Varin. Offer protection in exchange for a share of the crystal shards and his knowledge of the scar's layout.
choices.description: Grab the merchant's wrist and demand he explain what "alive" means in this context, 14 words

line.dialogue: [He winces, then hisses, "It breathes, it dreams. The resona pulses like a heartbeat — because something inside still remembers it had one."]
[He yanks free and spits at your feet. "Touch me again and you'll learn what 'alive' means when my associates arrive."]

choices.text: Proceed immediately. The unnatural quiet is fraying nerves; staying put feels more dangerous than moving.
choices.description: Slide Arthit's forged transit manifest across the table and watch the merchant's reaction, 14 words

line.dialogue: [The merchant traces the seal with trembling fingers. "This is from the K
The lattice has other plans. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends into a vast, geodesic cavern beneath the Silent Zone's surface. The unnatural quiet is replaced by a faint, rhythmic hum emanating from veins of dead crystal.
Great. We've traded unsettling quiet for a place that feels like a giant, dead heart. I think that's the one sound I never wanted to hear again.
Look! The crystal! It's... it's moving. Pulsing. Like it's trying to sing but can't.
This is a wound. A scar from The Silencing. We've talked about this before, in our oldest texts—places where the Lattice's song was cut away.
Structural integrity is... fluctuating. Readings are impossible. We need to prepare beforehand for a cave-in. This whole place feels temporary.
It's more than a scar. It's a memory. The silence here isn't empty; it's full of what *was*. She's more beautiful than anyone... the song that used to be.
Fascinating! And utterly worthless for trade. Dead crystal has no resonance. No one wants to go poking around in a grave, but here we are.

lines_after.dialogue: At the cavern's heart lies a colossal, shattered resonator—a machine meant to amplify sound on a continental scale. It is dark, but a single, intact crystal node glows with a sickly light.
By the First Chord... this is a Tonal Order Primal Resonator. They said these were lost. This... this is what caused The Silencing? An experiment?
The prosthetic! My leg is vibrating. It's pulling me toward that node!

line.dialogue: The glowing node is the source of the zone's deadness and the prosthetic's reaction. It is unstable.

choices.text: Have Chanida cautiously approach the node, using her prosthetic's resonance as a guide.
choices.description: Press your bare hand against the pulsing crystal and let it show you what happened here.

line.dialogue: I see it — the moment The Silencing struck. Thousands of voices, extinguished in a single breath. We were never meant to find this.
Don't — the feedback nearly took my arm off! Whatever's stored in there, it doesn't want to be remembered. Not by us, not yet.

choices.text: Order everyone back and have Arthit attempt a remote scan with his instruments.
choices.description: Order arthit to run a resonance scan and map the fracture patterns spreading through the chamber walls.

line.dialogue: The fractures aren't random — they form a language. Someone carved a message into the bedrock itself before they died. It says... 'do not wake what sleeps below.
Every scan bounces back corrupted. The crystal's pulse is scrambling my instruments — I'm reading three different structural readings simultaneously and none of them match reality.

choices.text: Instruct the Listener Monk to attempt a ritual of remembrance, to 'sing' for the dead crystal.
choices.description: Have chanida attempt to sing a single sustained note matching the crystal's frequency to stabilize it.

line.dialogue: It responded — the pulse slowed. The crystal recognized the harmonic. This place wasn't just wounded, it was waiting for someone to acknowledge the pain.
My voice cracked and the crystal *screamed* — the whole chamber shook. Whatever frequency it needs, I got it wrong, and now it's pulsing faster. We need to

lines_before.dialogue: The chosen action triggers a cascade. Light erupts from the node, not as a song, but as a screaming, silent pressure that fills the cavern. Phantom echoes of the world's last scream.
I knew right away that this was a mistake. We're not observers... we're standing right in front of the trigger.
The harmonic feedback is overloading everything! The ship's crystals, Chanida's leg... it's all resonating with the damage!
The Negotiator's running! Figures. Profit's gone, so he's out. The truth was standing in front of him and he priced it out.
I can't... control it! The leg is singing on its own! It's trying to answer the scream!
It's here! The unresolved chord! The Silence isn't an absence—it's a single, held, catastrophic note! We are inside a standing wave of destruction!
The cavern shudders. The dead lattice begins to crack, threatening to collapse in on itself and take the floating city above with it.
We have to resolve it. We have to change the note. Or this entire zone—and us with it—will just... stop.

lines_after.dialogue: The air shatters with potential. The prosthetic's wild song, the monk's chant, the ship's dying hum—all clash with the primal, silent scream. A new resonance is possible, but it requires a perfect, sacrificial harmony.
One voice must lead. One must tune itself to the break and heal it....
It's right here. The choice. In my leg, in the air... in us.

line.dialogue: The unstable resonance must be met with an equal and opposite frequency. Someone must become the counter-chord.

choices.text: Sacrifice the Resonant Prosthetic. Shatter it to create a dissonant shockwave that cancels the silent note. (Lose subplot_crystal_leg)
choices.description: Override the leg's resonance by feeding it your own harmonic signature through the neural interface.

line.dialogue: I'm letting it *hear* me — not controlling it, singing *with* it — and the vibration is settling into something almost like breathing.
It heard me, all right — heard every doubt I've ever had — and now the leg is *screaming* them back in frequencies I can feel in my teeth!

choices.text: Have the entire party attempt to sing together, a makeshift choir using the ship's damaged resonator. A high risk of psychic feedback. (Potential party trauma)
choices.description: Physically sever the harmonic conduit cables before the feedback cascade reaches the core reactor.

line.dialogue: Cables are cut — I can feel the deck stop shaking under my feet — whatever that leg wanted to say, it's going to have to whisper now.
The conduits won't separate — they've fused solid from the heat — and now I'm holding two ends of a wire that's humming like a struck bell!

choices.text: Pichit must attempt to listen *into* the silence and find the original, pure note before it broke, guiding it back. A Singer's task, with the risk of his mind being lost in the stillness. (Pichit's personal climax)
choices.description: Chase down the Negotiator and force him to reactivate the damping field he disabled before he ran.

line.dialogue: Found him cowering behind the
The attempt backfires on the monk. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The deck of the Resonance Ship hums beneath your boots. The crystalline Lattice below shimmers like a frozen sea, its patterns shifting with the ship's low engine tone. Wind whips through the rigging, carrying the distant, mournful song of the world.
Look at that! The Lattice is reacting to our passage. See the ripples? It's like we're writing a song on glass.
Or scratching a record. A very expensive, world-covering record. One wrong frequency and we'll be paying for the scratch with our lives.
The Tonal Charts are holding. Our course is stable. For now.
Stable, but silent. The Lattice has its own music, you know. Before the Silencing, they say you could hear whole symphonies rising from the crystal.
A sudden, discordant shriek of metal-on-crystal echoes from the ship's starboard side. The vessel shudders.
Hey! You up there! Cut your resonator! You're tearing up the harvest zone!

lines_after.dialogue: A ragged figure waves from a small, jury-rigged skiff clinging to the Lattice surface below. They're dressed in patched hides and scavenged metal.
The second option is you power down and listen. I can't speak your sky-city tongue, but I speak Lattice-fracture. And you're causing one.
A Surface Scavenger. Wonderful. They usually just throw rocks.
Their skiff is anchored in a resonance node. If we don't adjust, we could destabilize their craft.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger demands an audience. In only five minutes, this could turn hostile.

choices.line: [PACIFY] Adjust the ship's frequency slightly. Apologize for the disruption. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Something about listening to the Lattice's music/silence

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida's resolve isn't enough. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: [INQUIRE] Ask what they're 'harvesting' from the Lattice surface. (Curiosity)
choices.description: Something about adjusting the Tonal Charts or course

line.dialogue: Pichit succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Pichit hits a wall. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.line: [DISMISS] Ignore them. They're outside the Guild's protection. Maintain course. (Authority)
choices.description: Something about interacting with the Lattice directly

line.dialogue: Charts aligned — the Lattice hums in key now. We're not fighting the current anymore.
Wrong harmonic. The charts scream at me and the Lattice flinches away. I've made it worse.

lines_before.dialogue: The Scavenger, introduced as Bren, clambers aboard. Their eyes are wide, taking in the ship not with wonder, but with a sharp, calculating suspicion.
You sky-bound live in your bubbles. You think the Lattice is just a road. It's a skin. And you're giving it a fever.
A fever?
The old songs are getting louder. Angrier. My mom told me about it already, before the last storm took her. The Groundless say it's a reckoning.
The Groundless? Is that some kind of surface guild?
More like a cult. They think the Floating Cities are an abomination. That we should all return to the 'true earth' below the crystal.
Not a cult. A movement. And they're waiting. I have a class to teach my kin about sky-folk patterns. I'm gonna rush off right now if you're not going to listen.
A new, aggressive engine tone cuts through the wind. A sleek, predatory vessel with jagged crystal shards for armor slides into view off the port bow.

lines_after.dialogue: The new ship broadcasts a chaotic, pulsing frequency that makes the deck plates vibrate unpleasantly.
Hail the fat merchant barge! You're in contested harmonics. That's a toll frequency you're humming through!
Sky Pirates. They hijack resonance frequencies and ambush ships in the dead zones between charts.
See? Your noise draws predators. The Groundless are right. You're all just making a bigger racket until something worse hears you.
Power down your main resonator and prepare for boarding! Or we'll find the frequency that shatters your crystal drive!

line.dialogue: The pirate ship is powering weapons. The Scavenger is poised to flee. You have moments.

choices.line: [ENGAGE] Match the pirate's frequency and threaten a resonant feedback burst. (Bluff)
choices.description: Press the scavenger for details about these "old songs" and what they foretell.

line.dialogue: The songs speak of a reckoning — when the sky will crack and fall to earth, and those who forgot the ground will be remembered by it.
You want specifics? I'm not your scholar. The songs don't translate well to your sky-tongue anyway.

choices.line: [EVADE] Order full power to the engines, using the Lattice's own sonic turbulence to lose them. (Pilot)
choices.description: Defend the sky-bound perspective, arguing that isolation isn't the same as ignorance.

line.dialogue: I understand more than you think. We left the surface because we had to — not because we stopped caring about what's below.
You're right. We don't know. But hostility won't bridge that gap — it'll just make the distance feel justified.

choices.line: [NEGOTIATE] Broadcast an open channel. Offer the pirates information on Tonal Order patrol routes in exchange for passage. (Subterfuge)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to share what she knows about surface guilds and their structures.

line.dialogue: There are dozens of surface factions — the Groundless are the ones who reject all authority, sky or soil. They're growing.
I've only heard rumors, and none of them good. The Groundless aren't a guild — they're more like a fracture.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship shudders, its harmonic engine sputtering. The Lattice below churns with unnatural dissonance, a static-filled roar rising from the crystalline surface.
The frequency interference is overwhelming the resonator! We're losing altitude. We should wait for the rain to stop… if this static-storm ever ends.
Brilliant observation. The ship's failing, and your solution is to hope the hostile sky changes its mind. It still works as a plan to crash.
Forget waiting! Look—scavenger skiffs, closing in from the Lattice spires. And another ship on the horizon. Pirates?
(Over the comms, voice crackling with static) Surface-dwellers to drifting fools. Your song is sick. You're leaking resonance. Drawing the wrong kind of attention.
Attention from whom? The Silencing wasn't an accident… it was a command. And something down there is listening for disobedient voices.
The pirate ship, a jagged construct of salvaged metal, banks hard. Its resonator emits a predatory, shrieking frequency aimed at your ship's core.

(Over a shrill comm channel) Hah! Found you, songbirds! Hand over your crystal charts and maybe we won't shatter your hull. You don't need to be Number 1 in the sky to survive… just smarter than the next target.

line.dialogue: The scavenger warns of a 'deep pulse' destabilizing the region. The pirate is demanding surrender. The ship's core is fluctuating dangerously.

choices.line: [EASY: Divert Power] Re-route auxiliary power to reinforce the resonator shield. It's a straightforward engineering solution, but leaves other systems vulnerable.
choices.description: Reroute power from life support to boost the resonator's frequency dampening field.

line.dialogue: I'm pulling everything we've got into the dampener—hold your breath, this is going to get cold fast.
You redirected power from *life support* during a combat approach—now we're suffocating *and* being hunted.

choices.line: [MEDIUM: Negotiate & Deceive] Open channels to both scavenger and pirate. Play their suspicions against each other to create an opening.
choices.description: Open a channel and bluff the scavengers, claiming the ship is carrying unstable antimatter cargo.

line.dialogue: If they scan us and believe that payload reading, no skiff in their right mind fires on us—watch them scatter.
They're not buying it—they're accelerating, and now they know we're desperate enough to lie.

choices.line: [HARD: Harmonic Dive] Use the ship's failing resonance in a controlled plunge toward the Lattice, mimicking a crash to evade both threats.
choices.description: Dive the ship toward the planet's atmosphere, using ionization friction to mask the resonator signature.

line.dialogue: The atmospheric interference is eating their targeting locks—rough ride, but they can't track what they can't see.
We pushed the descent angle too steep—the hull plating is peeling and we're still being followed.

lines_after.dialogue: Your choice sends a ripple through the tense standoff. The Lattice's glow intensifies, reacting to the shifting frequencies.
Every choice is a note added to the song. What melody are we writing now?
One that keeps us flying! Or at least, not sinking!

acts.title: The Cost of a True Note

lines_before.dialogue: The consequences of your maneuver unfold. The pirate ship veers, its predatory shriek warping. The scavenger skiffs scatter. But from the Lattice itself, a deep, resonant HUM begins, shaking the very air.
(Voice urgent, cutting through the hum) It's awake! The old pulse beneath the Spire of Whispers! You've stirred it! Don't let it see you! Don't let that frequency lock onto your core signature!
Fantastic. We avoided bandits and surface-dwellers only to attract the attention of a geological nightmare. Let's go inside before the hull peels apart.
The harmonic reading… it's not random. It's a pattern. A calling. If the Silencing was a command, this is the… response.
(Comms breaking apart) W-what is that?! My crystals are bleeding sound! The charts are lies! Don't let anyone know! Don't tell the Orders what's down here!

A beam of solidified sound, visible as twisting light, lances up from the Lattice. It doesn't strike your ship—it envelops it, humming with ancient intent. The Groundless Movement's warnings about hidden truths beneath the sky feel terrifyingly literal.
It's not attacking… it's *examining* us. Like we're a wrong note in its song.
Or a note that has been silent for too long. This is the discovery we feared. The truth that unmade the world.

line.dialogue: The ancient resonance holds your ship in a field of pure vibration. It seeks something—a specific frequency, a memory, a proof of identity. To break free, you must answer.

choices.line: [EASY: Surrender the Charts] Feed it the sanctioned navigational data from the Tonal Orders. It will recognize the 'official' song of the world, but you'll be left adrift, chartless.
choices.description: Sing the harmonic pattern back in reverse, harmonizing with Arthit's reading, 15 words

line.dialogue: The pattern—it's folding inward! Keep singing, you're collapsing the resonance before it stabilizes!
Wrong inversion. You just amplified the third harmonic and now it's singing back louder than before.

choices.line: [MEDIUM: Offer a Memory] Channel a personal, powerful memory through the ship's resonator—a moment of loss, joy, or defiance. It's a raw, untested frequency.
choices.description: Rip the bandit's destabilizing crystal from their hands and hurl it into the awakening chamber, 15 words

line.dialogue: Brilliant! The crystal's drawing the discharge—diverting the harmonic surge away from us like a lightning rod!
You just fed it a fully charged crystal. The hum doubled. I really hope that was intentional.

choices.line: [HARD: Sing Uncharted] Have Pichit, the latent Singer, attempt to harmonize with the pulse directly, without guidance. It could shatter the ship's crystals… or create a new chart entirely.
choices.description: Grab Arthit and retreat through the eastern tunnel before the pattern completes its cycle, 15 words

line.dialogue: Smart move—the eastern passage dampens harmonics. We can study the pattern safely from behind the resonance wall.
The eastern tunnel is reflecting the pattern, not blocking it. We just walked into an echo chamber.

lines_after.dialogue: The ship thrums, a vessel caught between the old song and a new one being born in this moment of crisis. The fate of the Groundless truth hangs in the balance.
This is the choice. To repeat the known, or to risk a new resonance.
The Lattice's light pulses, waiting for your final note.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch out in terraced layers, their vibrant green a stark contrast to the shimmering, sound-reactive Lattice far below. Wind whispers through the rows of sky-rice, creating a gentle, rhythmic susurrus.
This peace… it feels earned. A fragile thing, built on the silence after the great noise.
Built on ignorance, more like. They farm their little patch and pretend the Lattice isn't down there, humming with whatever killed the old world.
A practical approach. Stability is precious. We should rest while we can.
Rest? Look! Someone's waving us over from that irrigation hut. Maybe they need help!
You're the ones with the Resonance ship, right? The newcomers? From that day you landed, folks have been talking.

There's a story here. An old one. About a ship that vanished into the Lattice mists near our gardens, generations back. The 'Echo.' Some say on quiet nights, you can still hear its crystal resonator… crying.
A lost song, trapped? Who would believe such a tale could linger for so long?

lines_after.dialogue: I believe it! A ghost ship! We have to find it!
Or it's a fairy tale to scare children and sell ale to gullible travelers.
Believe what you want. But old Mani, the monk who tends the wind-chime shrine… he's been listening for it. He doesn't look like he's smiling happily anymore.

line.dialogue: The villager points toward a distant, solitary shrine where crystal chimes tinkle. Do we investigate the monk's findings?

choices.line: Seek out the Listener Monk. Faith might hold a kernel of truth.
choices.description: Approach the waving figure cautiously, hands visible, signaling peaceful intent.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "I'll go first. No sense in all of us walking into a trap together.
Malee — "Of course you'd volunteer to be the first corpse. How noble.

choices.line: Ask the villagers for more concrete details first. Separate fact from folklore.
choices.description: Send Chanida ahead alone while the rest watch from cover with weapons ready.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "I can read a face better than any of you. If something's wrong, I'll signal.
Pichit — "We don't send friends into danger alone. That's not who we are anymore.

choices.line: Ignore the story. It's just local superstition. Focus on resupplying.
