choices.description: Ignore the waving figure entirely and circle wide through the rice paddies to avoid contact.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Finally, someone thinking with their head instead of their heart. Let's move.
Arthit — "Whoever that is now knows we saw them and chose to run. We just made an enemy.

lines_before.dialogue: At the secluded shrine, a Listener Monk named Mani sits motionless before an array of polished Lattice-shards, each tuned to a different harmonic of the wind.
You live near each other in this floating city, yet you hear nothing but the wind and your own thoughts. I'm happy to hear visitors… though I fear what brings you.
We were told you listen for the Echo. The lost ship.
I do. Its resonance is… wrong. A fracture in the world's song. My Order says to record, not to intervene. But this… it feels like a wound.
A dangerous discovery. If the Tonal Orders haven't charted it, there's a reason. It could be a navigational hazard.
Or it's a ship in trouble! There's no one else looking for it, right? Just us!
And a monk having a crisis of conscience. Lovely. So you've actually heard this 'Echo'?
Not with ears. With the shards. A dissonant pulse, deep below the western terrace, where the Lattice currents are treacherous. It does not belong.

lines_after.dialogue: A sound that doesn't belong… a life out of tune with the Lattice.
Precisely. To live is to resonate in harmony or discord. This is a sustained, painful discord.
Then we have to go down there! We can't just leave it!

line.dialogue: The Monk has given a location, but venturing into an uncharted Lattice zone is perilous. How do we proceed?

choices.line: Ask the Monk to guide us to the edge. His knowledge could keep us safe.
choices.description: Pichit asks the monk to hum the resonance so they can hear the fracture themselves.

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit overreaches. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.line: Return to the ship and use our own resonator to scan for the anomaly cautiously.
choices.description: Arthit demands to know what the monk means by "fracture in the world" - the full truth.

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Chanida fails. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.line: Go directly to the western terrace edge and prepare to descend. The Echo might not wait.
choices.description: Pichit suggests they travel to where the Echo's resonance is strongest to investigate directly.

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the villager. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The risk doesn't pay off. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The peaceful rhythm of the Hanging Gardens feels fractured. The air hums with a low, dissonant frequency that makes the leaves tremble.
That's it! The vibration in the soil. It's not irrigation. It's the same harmonic distortion from the ship's log.
I didn't catch what you said, Malee. The wind is picking up strange echoes.
Look! The monk from before. He's just standing by the edge, staring into the Lattice mist.
His posture isn't reverent. It's... expectant.
You hear it too now, don't you? The Lattice isn't singing. It's whispering a name.
What's her personality like, this ghost you're all listening to? Angry? Lost?
She is... persistent. Her resonance signature is woven into the terraces. The gardens remember the crash.

lines_after.dialogue: A section of crystal lattice forming the garden's retaining wall begins to glow with a pale, sickly light. A fragmented image shimmers within it: a ship's prow, broken.
The structural integrity... it shouldn't be doing that. The resonance is unstable!
It's not an echo. It's a memory, replaying. The monk said the gardens remember.

line.dialogue: The glowing crystal pulse quickens, becoming painful to look at. The Monk covers his ears.

choices.text: Use Chanida's portable resonator to dampen the frequency.
choices.outcome: Chanida produces a small, jury-rigged device. A sharp counter-tone cuts through the hum, and the crystal dims. The immediate danger passes, but the deeper resonance remains, buried.
choices.description: Arthit channels captain experience toward the water channels, hoping to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Arthit makes it work. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Arthit fails. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Have Malee analyze the crystal's resonant frequency.
choices.outcome: Malee's scanner whirs. 'The frequency is a distress call, looped. But it's layered... there's a command signal underneath.' The image clarifies slightly, showing a Tonal Order insignia on the failing ship.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with engineering, ready to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
The gamble fails. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.text: Ask Pichit to try and 'listen' to the memory, to understand it.
choices.outcome: Pichit places a hand near the crystal. His eyes lose focus. 'It's not just the ship... it's the pilot. She's trying to warn someone. She lost her... her connection. The charts were wrong.' A wave of psychic feedback washes over him.
choices.description: The monk attempts to commune with trapped echoes, relying on prayers

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The gamble fails. His recording crystal shatters.

lines_before.dialogue: The dissonance erupts. The haunting whisper becomes a shriek that rips through the Hanging Gardens. Crops wither in seconds. Crystalline pathways crack, glowing with violent energy.
The Silencing! It's happening again! Run!
No! This is the truth they buried! The Lost Ship, the *Resonance's Requiem*... its final crash seeded this place with its dying song!
I can't keep up with what you're saying! Is this the ship's ghost or a weapon?!
It's a data-corruption event. A resonant memory so traumatic it's physically rewriting the local Lattice structure. We're standing inside a scream.
The entire terrace section is destabilizing. If that primary support crystal shatters, this whole garden plate shears off the city.
The pilot. She's not attacking. She's *trapped*. Re-living the moment the false charts led her into a harmonic dead zone. Her panic is resonating through the crystals she crashed into.
The Tonal Orders... they scuttled the investigation. Said she was a rogue Singer. But we Listeners... we heard the truth in the static. And now it's awake.

lines_after.dialogue: The central crystal, the heart of the memory, pulses like a dying star. The image of the ship solidifies, superimposed over the crumbling garden. A choice must be made: silence the memory or set it free.
We don't get to bury this again. But we can't let it destroy the present.
So we give her a proper finale. One last, clear note.

line.dialogue: The psychic scream reaches its peak. The Monk looks at you, despair and hope warring on his face.

choices.text: Shatter the memory-crystal. Erase the echo. Save the gardens.
choices.outcome: A violent, precise strike. The crystal explodes into harmless dust. The scream cuts off. The gardens are saved, but fall silent in a new, hollow way. The Monk weeps. The truth is buried once more, and the Tonal Orders will tighten their grip, citing 'resonance instability.'
choices.description: Grab the monk's shoulders and demand he finish what he was saying about the Lost Ship. — 14 words

line.dialogue: [The monk's eyes snap into focus, gripping your wrists hard enough to bruise. "The Lost Ship *was the garden's seed* — they planted it here to grow silence *into* us."]
[The monk's mouth opens, but the sound that comes out is roots — wet, tangled, growing — and his eyes go blank as something underneath the soil finishes eating his words.]

choices.text: Amplify the memory, broadcasting it to every nearby city. Let everyone hear.
choices.outcome: You channel the scream into a city-wide alarm frequency. For one terrifying minute, the final moments of the *Resonance's Requiem* echo across the sky. Panic ensues, but so does revelation. The Tonal Orders' lies are exposed publicly, causing immediate upheaval. The gardens are heavily damaged in the process.
choices.description: Follow Malee's lead — pull up your scanner and triangulate the corruption's source frequency. — 14 words

line.dialogue: [Malee watches your readings sync with hers and nearly laughs. "There — forty meters down. It's not a memory. It's a *heartbeat*. Something down there is still alive."]
[Your scanner displays coordinates that rearrange themselves into a sentence you didn't input: *YOU ARE ALREADY INSIDE IT.* Malee grabs your arm and says, "Stop reading. It reads back."]

choices.text: Have Pichit and the Monk Sing a counter-melody: a song of release and peace.
choices.outcome: A duet of voice and spirit. You don't silence the scream; you harmonize with it, transforming anguish into a bittersweet, fading chord. The memory completes, the ghost finds peace, and the Lattice stabilizes, healed. The gardens are saved, humming with a new, gentle song. The Monk's order gains immense moral authority, challenging the Orders not with lies, but with a clearer truth.
choices.description: Seize the fleeing villager and force them to tell you what happened the last time the Silencing came. — 16 words

line.dialogue: [The
The lattice has other plans. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: In the quiet terraces of Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, the only sounds are the wind rustling through the grain and the distant hum of the skycity's core. The air smells of damp earth and blooming night-flowers.
Listen... the Lattice hums differently here. Lower. Like it's remembering something old.
Or it's just tired of holding up another floating rock full of people terrified of falling. He's right! The Tonal Orders charge a fortune just for the charts to get here.
Forget the charts! Look at this place! It's my dream job to find spots like this. Peace, food, no one trying to kill us...
Temporary peace. We should turn off the ship's main resonator to conserve energy while we're docked. We don't know how long this 'rest' will last.
You're the new arrivals? The ones with the... smaller ship?
We are. We seek only rest and supplies.
Rest you can have. Supplies... there's a merchant in the lower terrace. But mind the quiet. Strange echoes have been coming from the old irrigation channels lately. Not natural.

lines_after.dialogue: Strange echoes. Of course. Because a quiet farming skycity is never just a quiet farming skycity.
An adventure! In the irrigation channels!
Or a structural fault. Or a Lattice anomaly. We should investigate with caution. Pichit?

line.dialogue: The party looks to you, Pichit. How do you want to proceed?

choices.text: Speak to the merchant first. Information has value.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the nearest Lattice column and feel for the harmonic shift Pichit described.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "You feel that? It's not degradation — something down there is *calling* through the substrate, deliberate as a heartbeat.
Pichit — "Nothing? Then maybe it's not the Lattice that's changed — maybe it's just us, rattled by the quiet.

choices.text: Investigate the irrigation channels directly. See what's causing these 'echoes'.
choices.description: Ignore Arthit's caution and follow Chanida toward the crumbling archway she's already climbing toward.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "I've spent fifteen years reading about these ruins in journals with smudged ink — I'm not standing on the *threshold* and asking permission to walk through it!
Chanida — "The stonework gave way — not collapsed, *released*, like it was waiting for exactly that much weight before it decided to let go.

choices.text: Focus on rest and resupply. Ignore local rumors for now.
choices.description: Kill the ship's main reactor as Arthit suggested and

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
A costly mistake by the villager. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The lower terrace is a bustling market nook. The merchant, Leron, has a vibrant stall of crystal shards and salvaged tech, his smile not quite reaching his eyes.
Ah, travelers! I have a class of rare resonator filaments, just in. And information... for the right trade.
We heard about the echoes in the channels. The guy in the condo next door always complains about noise, too. What's really down there?
Direct! I admire that. A local farmer, Old Kanya. She's... experimenting. Trying to grow a new crystal graft for her son's leg. A resonant prosthetic. It's making unstable frequencies.
Unstable resonance near the city's foundation? That's dangerously irresponsible.
But she's trying to help her son! We have to see!

Indeed. But her methods are crude. I have a calibrated crystal core that could stabilize her work. A bargain, for you. Or... you could report her to the Tonal Order enforcers. They'd pay a finder's fee.
You trade in people's desperation.

lines_after.dialogue: I trade in solutions. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a class to teach on resonator maintenance for some apprentices. I'm gonna rush off right now. Think on my offer.
So. We can buy his 'solution' and play heroes, turn in a desperate mother, or go talk to her ourselves with nothing but good intentions.
Intentions won't stabilize a rogue resonance. This requires a technical solution.

line.dialogue: Old Kanya's workshop is in the deep channels. How will you approach her?

choices.text: Buy the merchant's crystal core. A sure, if costly, fix.
choices.description: Buy a resonator filament and ask the merchant to mark Kanya's farm on your map, 15 words

line.dialogue: The filament hums against my palm — this will cut through whatever's eating at the foundation.
Counterfeit alloy. The resonance is dead. You sold me polished scrap, friend.

choices.text: Go to her directly. Assess the problem and try to help with what you know.
choices.description: Press the merchant for who else has been asking about the echoes lately, 13 words

line.dialogue: So we're not the first ones sniffing around Kanya's land — that changes everything.
Your mouth stays shut tighter than a sealed conduit. Fine. I'll find answers myself.

choices.text: Threaten the merchant for the core. His profiteering endangers the whole terrace.
choices.description: Leave without buying and head straight to Old Kanya's farm before dark, 14 words

line.dialogue: No time for haggling. If the foundation's cracking, every hour we waste costs lives.
We should have stocked up — the farm's perimeter is screaming with raw resonance.

lines_before.dialogue: The afternoon sun casts long shadows across the terraces. The Trade Negotiator, a man named Vichai, stands near a water mill, his smile not quite reaching his eyes.
Ah, the seekers of the Resonant Prosthetic! A marvelous piece of Tonal Order salvage. We probably can't finish negotiating the terms all at once, but I'm sure we can reach an understanding.
Your initial price is exorbitant. This isn't just merchandise; it could change a life.
Change requires investment! But it's still cheap compared to the Order's official rates. I'm offering freedom.
Freedom with a usury clause. How charitable. What aren't you finishing telling us about its provenance?
Just name a real price! That old Listener, Buntham, needs this leg. He didn't finish his life's work because of his injury!
Every piece of the old world carries a song of what was lost. This prosthetic... its resonance could be a key, not just a limb.
Philosophy doesn't fill ledgers. My final offer: the prosthetic for the location of the Singers' hidden archive you've been searching for. A trade of one secret for another.

lines_after.dialogue: The party recoils. The request is a profound betrayal of trust.
That archive is protected for a reason. Its knowledge in the wrong hands...
And here's the real cost. He's not a merchant; he's an information broker for the Orders.

line.dialogue: Vichai's smile is cold. 'Do we have a deal?'

choices.text: Refuse outright. The prosthetic isn't worth that sacrifice.
choices.outcome: You walk away. The prosthetic remains out of reach, but your integrity is intact. Buntham's hope dims.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using staff meditation to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Bluff. Claim the archive is a myth, but offer a different, lesser secret.
choices.outcome: A tense game of lies. Vichai might accept a decoy, or see through it and raise the stakes dangerously.
choices.description: Have Chanida risk using singer voice to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida loses control. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Agree, but plan to give false coordinates and steal the prosthetic during the exchange.
choices.outcome: A high-risk gambit. Success means saving Buntham and thwarting the broker. Failure means war with the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Direct the villager to commune with trapped echoes using community ties

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the villager. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
the villager fails. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: Night has fallen. The meeting is set at the highest, most isolated terrace. The Lattice below glimmers faintly. Vichai waits, the prosthetic's crystal components glowing in a case beside him.
Punctual. Good. May I see your driver's license? A joke! But I do require your navigator's seal as collateral. Shall we go to the seaside after this? I hear the phosphorescent blooms are lovely.
Cut the chatter. You have the leg. We have the coordinates. Let's finish this.
This place... the wind through the barley creates a hymn. It feels like a sanctuary. To betray a trust here would silence that song forever.
He's right. Vichai, you're spot on about one thing—this is holy ground for the Listeners. And I'm a Christian of the old books; I know what a betrayal in a garden feels like.
Malee? What are you—
I'm saying his deal is a sin. The prosthetic isn't his to sell. It was commissioned for Buntham before the Silencing. I found the records. It's stolen.
Ownership is a fluid concept. The coordinates. Now. Or I shatter this crystal on the stones.

lines_after.dialogue: The wind dies. The only sound is the tense hum of the prosthetic's resonator. Vichai's hand hovers over the case.
You would break a song that wants to be whole. That is the true Silencing.
The Lattice beneath the terrace pulses once, softly, in time with Pichit's words.

line.dialogue: Vichai pales at the Lattice's response. 'What are you?' The moment to act is now.

choices.text: Appeal to his greed. Offer a genuine, but less dangerous, piece of salvage lore instead.
choices.outcome: A practical peace. You secure the prosthetic for Buntham, but Vichai remains a player with a new piece of your knowledge.
choices.description: Draw your sidearm and press it beneath the merchant's chin, demanding he show the leg first

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Now that I have your full attention, open the case. Slowly.
Chanida — "Great. The one honest broker in four provinces, and you've made him flinch.

choices.text: Have Chanida create a diversion with a sudden loud resonance, allowing Arthit to snatch the case.
choices.outcome: A clean theft, but a declared enemy. You have the leg, but Vichai will report your 'abilities' to the Orders.
choices.description: Walk into the barley field alone, letting the hymn of wind wash over you before deciding

line.dialogue: Pichit — "Listen... the sound is almost perfect. Whatever's buried here, it wants to be found.
Pichit — "I heard it too, but the wind shifted. Something deeper is breathing underneath this field.

choices.text: Speak to the Lattice. Let Pichit's nascent Singer ability resonate with the prosthetic, calling it to its rightful purpose.
choices.outcome: A revelation. The prosthetic flies to Pichit's hand, its song clear. Vichai flees in superstitious terror, but the secret of Pichit's gift is now undeniable.
choices.description: Lean close to Vichai and whisper that you know he tipped off the militia about this meet

line.dialogue: Malee — "His hand just twitched toward his pocket. You were right — he's wearing a wire.
Malee — "Either you're wrong or he's the

lines_before.dialogue: The air in Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens is thick with the scent of damp soil and ripe grain. Wind hums through the terraced crops, a low, rhythmic sound that seems to vibrate in the very crystal of the Lattice far below.
Finally! A place where the only 'resonance' is a breeze. My head's been ringing since we left the last city. I could sleep for a week right here.
Don't get too comfortable. Peaceful places in this world usually mean someone's hiding something, or the local taxes are extortionate. Probably both.
The structural integrity of these terraces appears sound. A defensible position, with clear sightlines. We should rest, but maintain a watch rotation.
Listen to the rhythm... it's not just the wind. It's the water in the irrigation channels, the sway of the stalks. A natural harmony. It feels like a... a call to stillness.
You the travelers? Heard your ship dock. Not many visitors. The gardens are quiet. Good for the crops. Bad for gossip.
We're just passing through. Maybe buying supplies. Your 'quiet' is a blessing. The pain from all that city-noise is finally gone.

Quiet's good. But sometimes... the quiet calls too loud. My cousin, a Listener novice, he came back from the edge spouting nonsense. Said the Lattice was singing a warning. He won't talk now. Just stares. Good night to you.

lines_after.dialogue: A warning, huh? Of course. Can't have five minutes of pastoral bliss without an impending catastrophe. It's the world's favorite pastime.
A Listener hearing a new frequency is a significant data point. We should investigate with caution. The villager's fear is a tangible variable.
A call in the silence... and a soul who answered, only to be silenced. That 'warning' might be why this place feels so profoundly still. It's holding its breath.

line.dialogue: The villager's tale of the Listener's warning hangs in the air. What should the party do?

choices.text: Seek out the troubled Listener directly. Perhaps he can be coaxed to speak.
choices.description: Trace the rhythm by pressing your ear flat against the terrace stone, mapping its pulse.

line.dialogue: There—beneath the soil, a heartbeat. Something vast is breathing down here, and it's been waiting.
Just my own pulse echoing back. Either the rhythm stopped, or it never wanted me to hear it.

choices.text: Walk the garden's edge yourselves, trying to listen for the anomalous sound.
choices.description: Follow the wheat's sway pattern upstream toward the collapsed shrine at the terrace's edge.

line.dialogue: Smart move. The bending points toward that shrine like fingers pointing at a grave. That's where the wind *originates*.
Dead end. The wheat sways every direction now—whatever was guiding it caught onto us and scattered like startled birds.

choices.text: Ignore the rumor as village superstition and focus on rest and resupply.
choices.description: Have Arthit test the terrace wall's integrity by striking it with the butt of his staff.

line.dialogue: Hollow. These terraces are a shell—load-bearing nothing. One solid hit and we'd fall straight into whatever infrastructure lies beneath us
the scavenger hits a wall. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: Following a hunch or a rumor, the party finds themselves at the lowest, outermost terrace of Mae Rim. Here, the gentle farm sounds give way to the vast, silent yawn of the sky, with the shimmering, deadly surface of the Lattice visible far below.
Hey! You lot don't stay in touch with the ground, do you? This ain't a viewing platform. It's a work zone. For people who know what they're doing.
We're looking for... a sound. A weird one. Heard a Listener got spooked down here. You see anything?

Spooked? He was shattered. Babbling about a 'drone' from below. A hum that gets in your bones. I've worked the surface for twenty cycles. I know its music. This was new. Don't leave your mind open to it, I'll tell you that.
Lovely. So the foundation of our world is developing a new and terrifying chorus. Don't work too hard trying to convince me this is a good sign.
Your experience is valuable. Can you describe the harmonic profile? Was it localized? We need to understand the threat perimeter.
You feel it too, don't you? Not just hear. A tension in the air. The garden's peace was a surface calm. Underneath, something is... stirring.
Stirring is one word for it. I've got a descent line anchored. Was gonna check a old resonance spire fragment down there. If you're so curious about the noise... well, the source ain't up here.

lines_after.dialogue: A descent is high-risk. The Lattice's surface resonance is unpredictable without proper charts. We are not equipped for prolonged exposure.
But the answer is down there! We can't just stay up here wondering. That Listener lost his voice to this. We have to know why!
The unknown is calling. To ignore it is to let fear dictate our path. But Arthit is right. We don't stay in touch with the depths for a reason.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger offers a dangerous path to the source of the anomalous sound. The party must decide.

choices.text: Stay on the terrace. Study the phenomenon from a safe distance using instruments and the Scavenger's account.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using monk wisdom to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit overreaches. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Prepare a short, tethered descent. Send one or two down just below the cloud line for a quick sensory scan.
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use captain experience and use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
Things don't go as planned. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.text: Commit to the descent. Follow the Scavenger down to the Lattice surface to find the source of the 'drone'.
choices.description: Have the scavenger focus surface knowledge on the terraces to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the scavenger pulls it off. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
The resonance turns hostile. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: The sun begins to dip, casting long shadows across the terraces. The peaceful sounds of the gardens now feel threaded with an uneasy silence.
So the Scavenger says these 'shifts' are getting worse? That's not just normal Lattice movement.
We must be cautious. If the foundation frequencies are destabilizing, it could affect the skycity's anchors. We don't stay in touch with the surface for a reason.
Don't leave it open to speculation, then. Either the Tonal Orders are hiding something, or they're as blind as we are.
A truth half-glimpsed is more dangerous than a complete lie. We're not finished yet understanding what happened here.
You city-folk think you're done with the surface. But the Lattice isn't finished with you. The old Listeners... they heard warnings in the hum. Now it's a shudder.
Please, if you know something, call for help from the Orders. Our crops are wilting to strange vibrations. The pain is gone from the old blight, but this new silence... it's worse.

lines_after.dialogue: As the villager speaks, a low, subsonic groan vibrates up through the stone of the terrace, making the water in the irrigation channels tremble.
Well. That's a compelling argument.
The Lattice is speaking. We just need to learn how to listen before it's truly over.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points to a hidden path down the terrace wall—a way to a 'listening stone' the old monks used. The villager begs you to alert the city guard instead.

choices.text: Investigate the Listening Stone. Follow the Scavenger's path to seek the source of the warning.
choices.description: Have Arthit risk using lattice storms to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Defeat. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Split the Party. Send Arthit to alert the guard while the rest check the stone, covering both bases.
choices.description: Pichit presses forward with tonal knowledge to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
The risk doesn't pay off. The ex-Listener's doubt returns.

choices.text: Confront the Tonal Orders First. Demand answers using the villager's testimony, risking their ire but potentially getting official resources.
choices.description: Ask the villager to decode the distress signal, drawing on village secrets

line.dialogue: the villager succeeds. The community rallies, creating unexpected strength.
The resonance turns hostile. The community turns on them under Order pressure.

lines_before.dialogue: Night has fallen. At the ancient listening stone—a vast, carved plinth—the air is thick with latent resonance. Every sound feels amplified, stolen by the dark.
The guard won't mobilize without Order approval. I overheard the captain say it's 'not necessary' to panic over 'agricultural echoes.'
Of course. The bureaucratic motto: 'It's not necessary that the truth inconveniences us.'
Forget them! Place your hands on the stone. I overheard the Scavenger say that's how the Listeners did it. The Lattice's memory is in the crystal.
To listen is to be vulnerable. We might hear what broke the world.
As the party touches the cold stone, visions flash—not sound, but the memory of sound. The catastrophic chord of The Silencing. And beneath it, a newer, growing dissonance.

A ghostly chorus of Listener voices whispers from the stone: 'The great fracture repeats. The Tonal Orders drill too deep, seeking power. They will not let the Lattice heal. They will not let the world rest.'

I overheard that, from my people on the surface. The Orders are mining resonance cores, bleeding the Lattice dry to keep your cities floating. My father... he won't let me near their digs anymore. Not after the last collapse.

lines_after.dialogue: The vision ends. The stone falls silent, but the truth hangs heavy in the air. In the distance, a deep, mechanical hum begins—the sound of Order drills.
We have overheard the crime. Now we must choose the consequence.

line.dialogue: The secret is out. The Tonal Orders are actively harming the Lattice for power, risking another Silencing. The drilling site is close, accessible down a perilous lattice-face.

choices.text: Sabotage the Drill. A direct, violent act to stop the immediate harm, but making you enemies of the most powerful guild.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with crystal hearing to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: Chanida pushes through. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida is thwarted. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Gather Proof for the Skycity. Return with the Scavenger and villagers as witnesses, aiming for a political solution, but the drilling may continue.
choices.description: Ask Arthit to test the prosthetic reaction, drawing on ship navigation

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Arthit hits a wall. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Broadcast the Truth. Use the listening stone's resonance to amplify the warning to all nearby cities, causing panic and upheaval but ensuring no one can ignore it.
choices.description: Ask the scavenger to follow the phantom route, drawing on crystal fragments

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
The risk doesn't pay off. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: The Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens are a sanctuary of green and gold, terraced fields humming with the gentle wind-song through grain. The party rests by an irrigation channel, the water's soft babble harmonizing with the distant creak of windmills.
This peace... it's a rare commodity. We should enjoy it while we can. The Lattice below looks calm from here, but it's not necessary that it stays that way.
Enjoy it? My legs are still buzzing from that last Resonance jump! Is it necessary to use one so violently, Pichit? I thought we were going to shake apart!
The ship's crystal was responding to an old frequency. A memory in the stone. It wasn't a violent act, but an echo of one. Like a scar.
A poetic way of saying the navigational charts are garbage. The Tonal Orders sell us frequencies that leave our ship groaning. It wouldn't budge an inch when we tried to correct course.
A figure emerges from the tall, rustling stalks of sky-rice. It's a Surface Scavenger, their clothes patched with Lattice-shard leather, eyes sharp and assessing.
You're the ones making all the racket. That ship of yours... it's singing a dead man's tune.
What's that supposed to mean? We just got here!

lines_after.dialogue: Means I've heard that resonance before. Faint, like a ghost. Comes from the old wreck they call the *Echo's Lament*. Drifts in the dead zone south of here. No one goes there. Not if they're smart.
A lost ship? That aligns with the fragmented logs we recovered. Could it be...?
The source of the haunting frequency. The one that's been pulling at our resonator. It's not necessary to ignore a call like that. It's a piece of history, screaming to be heard.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger's warning hangs in the air. The party must decide how to proceed with this ominous lead.

choices.text: Offer trade for more concrete information about the wreck's location.
choices.description: Trace the old frequency through the crystal yourself, pressing your palm flat against its facets, 15 words

line.dialogue: You found it — a harbor beacon, older than any chart we carry. Steady hands, friend.
The crystal bit you back. That frequency wasn't meant for living fingers — pull away before it digs deeper.

choices.text: Press the Scavenger on why the area is so feared, seeking the nature of the danger.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to play back the raw signal so everyone hears what the crystal heard, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — beneath the static — a woman's voice counting down from ten. She's waiting for someone.
The playback looped wrong. Now the crystal is singing that frequency backward and my teeth are vibrating.

choices.text: Thank the Scavenger and discuss privately whether to investigate at all.
choices.description: Tell Chanida to stretch her legs and manually sight the stars through the observation dome, 15 words

line.dialogue: Three landmarks I recognize. Whoever drew our charts was drunk, blind, or both — we're off course by leagues.
Dome's fogged from the inside. Whatever that resonance stirred up, it's bleeding condensation into the glass — I can't see a thing.

lines_before.dialogue: After questioning the Scavenger, the party moves to a more secluded terrace to plan. The pastoral peace now feels thin, every rustle of the crops potentially hostile.

So the 'dead zone' has unstable crystal formations that eat sound and light. Charming. And the Scavenger was standing right in front of us, yet I don't trust a word he said. He was too eager to get rid of us.
Maybe he's hiding something out there! Treasure from the wreck? Is everything under control with our own supplies, Arthit? Can we make the trip?
Barely. Our resonator is still attuned to that ghost frequency. It's a risk. Are you sure, Pichit? Navigating by a dead ship's song... it's uncharted.
The surest path is sometimes the one you must make for yourself. The Lattice remembers. We just have to listen.
A harsh, metallic laugh cuts through the wind. Three figures clad in scavenged armor and wielding jagged frequency-blades step from between the terraces. Sky Pirates.
Listenin' to the Lattice, are ya? Cute. We heard your ship's peculiar song too. Sounds like a payday. The *Echo's Lament* is our claim.
Your claim? You're standing in front of *us*!

lines_after.dialogue: And we like the view. Now, you're gonna hand over those resonance charts. The *clean* ones, not the garbage the Tonal Orders sell.
You think we'd be out here if we had 'clean' charts? You pirates are as lost as we are.
Then you're no use. But your ship might be. We'll be taking that, too.
The lead pirate raises a crackling blade. The peaceful garden is now a battlefield. The decision to investigate the haunted ship has drawn immediate and violent attention.

line.dialogue: Confronted by Sky Pirates intent on hijacking both their mission and their ship, the party must choose their response.

choices.text: Fight! Use the terraces for defensive positioning and engage the pirates directly.
choices.description: Channel the resonator to map stable paths through the crystal field before moving in.

line.dialogue: I can trace the resonance patterns — there, there, and there. Three lanes where the crystals won't collapse on us.
The frequencies are overlapping — every reading contradicts itself. We walk blind or we don't walk at all.

choices.text: Bluff. Claim you know a safe frequency through the dead zone and offer a treacherous 'partnership'.
choices.description: Send Chanida ahead to scout between the stalks using her slight frame to slip through gaps.

line.dialogue: I can squeeze between these — they're tight but stable. I'll signal when I find his trail.
A stalk shifted and nearly pinned my arm. These things aren't static — they're *breathing*. I'm coming back.

choices.text: Flee and sabotage. Create a diversion with the irrigation system and sprint for the ship to get a head start.
choices.description: Follow Pichit's instinct and carve a new route by deliberately collapsing unstable sections to clear a lane.

line.dialogue: We bring the wall down *our* way. Controlled collapse — then we walk through the rubble while it's still settling.
I misread the load-bearing stalk. The whole row

lines_before.dialogue: The wind through the terraced crops sounds like a sigh. The party rests near an irrigation channel, the water's flow a soft counterpoint to the distant, unsettling hum that now permeates the Gardens.
Peaceful. Too peaceful. My ears are still ringing from that... whatever it was. The air tastes like regret.
The Scavenger's data is concerning. That frequency pattern isn't natural lattice resonance. It's structured. Deliberate.
So the lost ship isn't just lost, it's *broadcasting*? From the surface? How is that even possible after all this time?
Perhaps it never truly stopped sailing. A thought, a memory, a final command... echoing on. The Lattice remembers what we try to forget.
A sudden gust rattles a line of crystal wind-chimes hanging from a nearby pergola. Instead of a harmonious ring, they emit a jarring, discordant shriek that makes everyone wince.
See? The garden's upset. The old songs here are being overwritten. That ghost-ship's call is a stain.
We have to find its source and shut it down! Before it draws in every sky pirate from here to the horizon.

lines_after.dialogue: Great plan. Charge blindly toward the creepy noise. **You should get some rest.** Let the grown-ups think.
She's not wrong, Chanida. We need a precise location. I'm cross-referencing the Scavenger's bearings with our own charts... but there's interference.
**I'm sorry I'm late.** To this realization, I mean. We've been listening to the symptom, not the source. The ship's 'echo' is a plea, not an attack.

line.dialogue: How do we pinpoint the source of the haunting frequency?

choices.line: CALIBRATE WITH THE GARDEN: Use the natural resonance of the Hanging Gardens as a baseline to filter out the ghost signal. (Pichit's philosophical insight + Arthit's technical skill)
choices.description: Tune the receiver to match the frequency pattern and trace the broadcast's origin point.

line.dialogue: I've locked the signal — it's threading through the wind-chime array, three bearing points northwest.
The pattern slipped — it's refracting off itself, like a voice echoing inside a sealed room.

choices.line: BAIT THE SIGNAL: Use the party's ship resonator to amplify and 'answer' the echo, triangulating its origin. (Risky, might attract more attention)
choices.description: Send Pichit's thought-projection outward as a lure while Malee stands ready at the cannons.

line.dialogue: Contact — something just brushed the projection's edge, and I swear I felt it breathe back.
Nothing took the bait. Either it's deaf to thought, or it already knows we're fishing.

choices.line: QUESTION THE SILENCE: Seek out the one spot in the Gardens where all sound dies, believing the echo will be strongest where it's trying to fill the void. (Intuitive, unorthodox)
choices.description: Cut all ship power and drift silent, letting the wind-chimes catch the broadcast unaided.

line.dialogue: Listen — beneath the chimes, there's a voice. It's speaking coordinates, and they're *moving*.
The chimes went still. Whatever was singing through them — it stopped the moment we went quiet.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands at the very edge of the lowest terrace. Below, the Lattice churns like a frozen sea. Before them, half-buried in crystalline growth, is the prow of the *Resonance's Lament*. Its main resonator crystal is cracked, pulsing with a sickly, rhythmic light.
Well. There it is. Not a ship. A tomb with a heartbeat.
The structural integrity is nonexistent. One wrong frequency and the entire wreck could destabilize and sink into the Lattice... with us on it.
A shadow passes overhead. A skiff bearing the jagged markings of a sky pirate clan lands roughly on a higher terrace. CHAR_BANDIT jumps down, flanked by two rough-looking crewmates.
Hands off the loot, melody-lovers! That core crystal's worth a fortune, even cracked. We've been tracking this squeal for weeks.
It's not loot, you tone-deaf thug! It's a grave! You'll disturb it!
Disturb it? I'm gonna *silence* it. Permanently. Then I'll take what's mine.
Can't you hear the pain in its song? This isn't a prize to be claimed. It's a wound that never closed.

lines_after.dialogue: Pain? Songs? Spare me. **Why didn't you** just walk away when you had the chance? Now you're in my way.
Chanida, stand down! The resonator is critically unstable! **You have to finish your** analysis before we do anything!
Too late for analysis. It's smash or be smashed. **Why didn't you call me first?** I would've brought a bigger wrench.

line.dialogue: The pirate is powering up a cutting tool. The ghost ship's frequency is spiking in distress. How do you end this?

choices.line: OVERLOAD THE ECHO: Use your own ship's resonator to flood the wreck with a harmonious counter-frequency, calming the ghost signal and ruining the crystal's value. (Saves the memory, denies the pirate)
choices.description: Arthit channels forbidden paths toward the agricultural hum, hoping to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
A costly mistake by Arthit. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.line: NEGOTIATE WITH THE DEAD: Have Pichit attempt to 'Sing' to the echo, to guide its final rest and collapse the wreck safely before the pirate can act. (Uses Pichit's rare gift, spiritually risky)
choices.description: Convince Pichit to use resonant staff and use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
The gamble fails. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.line: SACRIFICE THE SHIP: Trigger a controlled collapse of the terrace beneath the wreck, sending it and the crystal into the depths of the Lattice forever. (Ensures no one gets it, but destroys all evidence)
choices.description: The pirate volunteers to commune with trapped echoes, leveraging secret frequencies

line.dialogue: Exactly as the pirate hoped. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
the pirate misreads the situation. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow is still and cold, smelling of damp stone and ancient metal. Faint, distorted echoes of distant Lattice-song drift through the cavernous passages.
I can't feel the ship's hum down here. It's... quiet. I probably have some resonance chalk in my pack. We should mark our path.
A sound idea. The acoustics are deceptive. Pichit, you have to finish your initial survey before we go deeper. The Tonal Orders' maps are useless here.
Useless and overpriced. They must have known this place was uncharted. Typical monopoly behavior. Keep your voices down—echoes carry.
Listen... the stone itself hums. A different frequency than the surface Lattice. This place remembers a older song.
Look! Scorch marks on the ceiling. And... I can't eat anything right now. The air's too thick with old dust.
Ahead, the tunnel opens into a vast chamber. Pre-Silencing machinery, all sharp angles and corroded crystal, lies half-buried under collapsed rock.

lines_after.dialogue: Incredible preservation. But we're not alone. Those footprints are recent. Leather-soled, not resonator boots.
Pirates. Or scavengers. They must have found another way in. Probably the same way we're trying to find out.
Let's check that console. Maybe it still has power.

line.dialogue: The ancient console flickers weakly. A choice presents itself:

choices.text: Attempt to activate the console with a basic resonator frequency.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the humming stone and match your breathing to its frequency.

line.dialogue: There — you feel it? The pulse is strongest at the seams. These walls weren't built, they were *grown*.
Your hand is bleeding. The stone has edges finer than surgical wire. Step back and let me scan it first.

choices.text: Search the chamber manually for a physical power source or manual controls.
choices.description: Deploy the resonance scanner in a triangular pattern around the chamber's center.

line.dialogue: Three points confirmed. The frequency converges beneath us — something is resonating from *under* the foundation.
The scanner's dead. Whatever's humming in this rock is also scrambling our electronics. We're deaf and blind down here.

lines_before.dialogue: Past the pirate standoff, the tunnel ends at a sheer drop into a bottomless black pit. A narrow, singing crystal bridge spans the void, leading to a floating platform where a massive, heart-like crystal beats with light.

The Groundless... they talk about truths buried deep. Is this it? The reason the islands float? I don't know either if we should touch it.
The heart-crystal pulses, projecting fragmented holograms—images of the world before The Silencing, a lush green planet, not a crystal-coated shell. A sorrowful, wordless song fills the chamber.
It's not just a power source. It's a lament. A record of the crime that created The Lattice. I already know that... in my bones.
The crystal bridge shudders. A deep crack echoes through The Hollow. The choice is immediate and final.

line.dialogue: The heart-crystal's song becomes a desperate plea. It offers a choice: preserve its memory and let the island's stabilizing frequency fade, or harmonize with it, learning the truth but potentially altering the island's flight forever.

choices.text: Preserve the Memory. Record the final song and retreat, letting the island find its own, new equilibrium. (Preservation)

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber holds its breath. The crystal's light intensifies, washing over the party in waves of sound and color.
Every end is a beginning. Every silence contains the echo of what was lost.
The fate of The Hollow, its secrets, and the island itself now resonates with the party's final, defining choice.

lines_before.dialogue: Your resonance ship, the *Whispering Hull*, glides into the Silent Zone. The usual hum of the Lattice fades to nothing. The crystals below lie dull and unmoving, like a frozen ocean of glass.

Welcome to the graveyard. The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for charts to avoid this place. Now we’re paying them to be here. Brilliant.
Our resonator readings are flat. No frequency is eliciting a response. We are navigating blind.
It’s not scary at all! Just… profoundly empty. A place where song has been forgotten.
A shape resolves in the stillness ahead—a derelict resonance ship, its hull cracked, drifting lifelessly. The ID markings are worn away.
A ship! Do you think there are supplies? Or… people?
Or ghosts. This is the perfect setting for a horror story. What kind do you like? Jump-scare or slow-burn existential dread? I’m feeling both right now.

Eyes on the prize, eh? That wreck's been singing a sad song. I charted this frequency myself. Finders, keepers.
You made the charts to find this place by yourself? That's Listeners' work.
What did you say? I don't listen to monks. I listen to the Lattice. It tells me where the good stuff is buried.

line.dialogue: The pirate claims the wreck. The ship's faint, distorted hum seems to pulse.

choices.line: Offer to trade for the salvage rights (Diplomacy).
choices.description: Trace Pichit's cadence pattern against the crystal wall to reveal hidden markings, 14 words

line.dialogue: There—see? The frequency aligns. These are waypoints, not decoration.
No, no, you're forcing it. The rhythm breaks. Start again from the third pulse.

choices.line: Challenge his claim, citing Surface Law (Intimidation).
choices.description: Rappel down to the spire where Chanida spotted the glinting salvage, 12 words

line.dialogue: Oh, beautiful—a intact harmonic lens! This alone funds three expeditions!
It's cracked. One touch and it shrieks—pull me up, pull me UP!

choices.line: Propose a joint investigation of the strange resonance (Persuasion).
choices.description: Ask Malee to scout the unmarked ground beyond the dampener boundary, 12 words

line.dialogue: Clear for thirty meters. The path extends further than they mapped.
Something's humming under my boots and I don't mean that poetically—GET ME BACK.

lines_before.dialogue: A tense agreement holds. The pirate, Kael, leads the way down a precarious crystal path towards the wreck. The air thrums with latent energy.
Conserve your steps. This whole ridge is unstable. One wrong vibration and it shatters.
He's correct. We must turn off any active resonators to conserve energy and avoid triggering a harmonic fracture.
Great. So we're tiptoeing towards a ghost ship with a bandit. Can you make a u-turn on this path? No? Didn't think so.
You reach the wreck. Its hull is fused with growing crystal. A scavenger in a hardened enviro-suit is carefully extracting a resonator core.
Back off! This is my claim! I've been tracking this echo for weeks!
Another one? They sell salvage rights at the Perch market, you know. You got a permit?
The echo... it's not just from the crash. It's a recording. A final moment, trapped in the crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: You hear it too? It's a loop. The last log entry. Something about a 'beckoning frequency' from deep below.
A new frequency? Untouched? That's worth more than the scrap. We need that log.
The core she's holding is the ship's black box. Its power is almost depleted. We must conserve the remaining charge to extract the data.
So we have a pirate who wants a treasure map, a scavenger who wants to pawn the box, and a ship that wants to tell us a ghost story. Charming.
The wreck groans. A deep, resonant tone wells up from the Lattice beneath it, causing the crystals to glow with an ominous light.

line.dialogue: The haunting frequency is growing stronger, destabilizing the area. The core is the key.

choices.line: Convince the Scavenger to hand over the core for safekeeping (Empathy).
choices.description: Hack the scavenger's portable resonator to force a shutdown, 15 words exactly here

line.dialogue: Resonator's dead. Now *you* tiptoe with us, or you sink this ridge for nothing.
You fried my kit — congratulations, now *nobody* moves quiet. Hope you're happy.

choices.line: Attempt to manually stabilize the frequency using your own resonator (Technical).
choices.description: Offer the scavenger shared salvage rights in exchange for his resonator data

line.dialogue: Half the haul, and I lead. My echelon maps are better than whatever you scraped together.
Shared? With corporate vultures? I've heard that pitch before — right before the backstab.

choices.line: Let the pirate try to 'jam' the signal with a discordant burst (Risky).
choices.description: Draw your sidearm and order the scavenger off the ridge before he collapses it

line.dialogue: Rude, but effective. He's backing down — nobody wants to die over scrap.
Now he's *running*. Straight toward the loose shelf. We need to catch him before the whole ridge goes.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform's edge looks out over a vast, silent expanse of the Lattice. Below, the crystalline surface glows with a faint, rhythmic pulse.
Great. More glittering doom. My stomach is starting to growl just looking at it.
Focus, Malee! The scavenger's map points to a fissure north-east. That's where the signal's strongest.
Signal strength is anomalous. It matches no known Tonal Order frequency. Proceed with extreme caution.
It feels... mournful. Like a memory trapped in crystal. We’ve talked about echoes like this before, in the old texts.
A sudden, sharp harmonic shiver runs through the platform. From the fissure, a ghostly, translucent prow of a Resonance Ship shimmers into view.
Well, well. Look what the Lattice coughed up. Nah, nah. You don’t need to bother with that hunk of ghost-light. We’ll take it from here.
Pirates! Told ya outsiders bring trouble. That wreck's been singing its death-song for decades. It ain't for the likes of them.

lines_after.dialogue: The spectral ship's form stabilizes, its hull fractured and humming with a low, persistent chord. The air grows cold.
It's real. The Echo of the Lost Ship... it's right there.
And we have company who wants to poke it. I'm such a lucky gal.

line.dialogue: The pirate leader leers, his hand on a crude sonic disruptor. The scavenger readies a makeshift resonator. The ghost ship waits.

choices.line: [Appeal to Greed] Offer to split any tangible salvage with the pirates, diverting them from the echo.
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing leg resonance to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Malee pulls it off. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Malee overreaches. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: [Form an Alliance] Propose a temporary truce with the scavenger, using their knowledge to safely approach the echo first.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to calibrate against the frequency using frequency mapping

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Chanida fails. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: [Confront the Echo] Ignore them both. Step towards the ghost ship and attempt to harmonize with its mournful frequency directly.
choices.description: Convince the scavenger to use crystal fragments and listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
A costly mistake by the scavenger. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision resonates. The ghost ship's hum intensifies, pulling at the very crystals underfoot. Light fractures into painful brilliance.
Catastrophic resonance build-up! The Lattice is reacting to the echo's unresolved frequency!
It's not just an echo... it's a wound. A piece of the Silencing itself, still screaming.
Forget the loot! The whole zone's gonna shatter! That's no problem for us—we're leaving!
You fool! You stirred it! The only way out is through—we gotta finish its song or be dissolved by it!
Finish it how? There’s something in my eye—the light, it's... it's showing patterns. Like sheet music!
Of course. We don't fight it. We... sing with it. Pichit, you're the only one who might be able to.
The platform groans. Crystalline spikes erupt around you. The ghost ship's form swells, threatening to consume everything in a wave of dissonant energy.

lines_after.dialogue: The air stills. The ghost ship's form dissolves into a shower of harmless, fading light, its song finally at peace.
Resonance stabilized. The fissure is... healing. The Lattice recorded the resolution.
It wasn't a haunt. It was a question. And we answered.
Huh. Maybe not all outsiders are bad luck. You just did what the Tonal Orders were too scared to try.

line.dialogue: The crisis is over, but the Lattice's memory has changed. A new, calm frequency emanates from the healed ground. What is its nature?

choices.line: [A Safe Path] The frequency is a stable navigational tone. Claim it for the Listeners, creating a new public route.
choices.description: Arthit channels ship navigation toward the shifting light, hoping to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Arthit succeeds. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Arthit overreaches. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: [A Buried Truth] The frequency unlocks a data-cache in the Lattice. It holds forbidden knowledge about the true cause of The Silencing.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus monk wisdom on the dangerous beauty to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The gamble fails. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: [A Calling] The frequency is a summons. It points deeper into the Lattice, towards something ancient and awake. The journey is only starting.
choices.description: The pirate attempts to decode the distress signal, relying on intimidation

line.dialogue: the pirate pushes through. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
the pirate is thwarted. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives hum with the low, resonant frequency of preserved knowledge. Crystalline shelves stretch into vaulted darkness, each facet holding a sliver of sound.
Keep your voices down. The acoustics here are calibrated. A misplaced cough could trigger a resonance cascade in the older stacks.
Wonderful. So we're researching in a library that might shatter if someone sneezes. It's really a great place to live!
Focus! The Open Frequency Map. If it's real, it charts routes the Tonal Orders haven't monopolized. What province of the Lattice does it even cover?
Not a province of land, Chanida. A province of possibility. A region of sound left unmapped by guild control.
A figure emerges from between two towering crystal columns—a woman with skin etched by Lattice-wind, her clothes patched with salvaged resonator shards.
You're the ones asking about open frequencies. You don't look like Listeners. You don't smell like Ordersmen. What's your play?

lines_after.dialogue: Our play is finding a way that doesn't pay your guild taxes. You know the surface. You've seen the uncharted hums.
Seen 'em. Heard 'em. Some are gentle. Some... eat ships. You want a map to a province the Orders ignore? It'll cost you more than coin.
Of course it will. Nothing's ever simple. Is the latest fashion in surface scavenging always dramatic vagueness?

line.dialogue: The Scavenger eyes you, waiting. How does Pichit respond?

choices.line: Offer a trade of rare resonator crystals from a previous voyage.
choices.description: Malee uses mechanical repair to decode the tonal pattern near the lost knowledge

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The risk doesn't pay off. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.line: Propose a shared expedition: her surface knowledge for your ship's safety.
choices.description: Arthit volunteers to calibrate against the frequency, leveraging ship navigation

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
Arthit misreads the situation. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Appeal to her curiosity: promise to share any new sonic phenomena you discover.
choices.description: The scavenger volunteers to record the spectral signature, leveraging surface knowledge

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
the scavenger hits a wall. Survival skills aren't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: Before the Scavenger can answer, a dissonant clang shatters the library's hush. A man in leathers adorned with jagged resonator spikes kicks open a side archway.
Well, well! Look what the resonance dragged in. Heard you lot were sniffing around for free routes. Bad for business, that is.
Sky pirates. Here? The Archives are neutral ground!
Neutral if you're paying the toll. Which you ain't. That map you're after—I lost my copy in a wager. Need it back.
You lost your map? How tragically careless. I didn't catch what you said earlier about 'tolls'—sounded like extortion.
He means he'll take it. We just got a lead!
The sound of greed often drowns out the melody of opportunity. You seek to silence discovery before it sings.
This lug's with the Razor Chorus gang. They patrol the fringes. They don't want you finding those frequencies 'cause they use 'em to hide.

lines_after.dialogue: Smart scrap-rat. Yeah. Those open hums are our highways. Let you chart 'em, and the Orders'll be all over 'em. Can't have that.
So it's a three-way conflict. The Orders hoard knowledge, the pirates exploit the gaps, and we're stuck in the middle.
The Pirate's hand rests on a jagged sonic disruptor at his hip. The Scavenger tenses, ready to bolt into the stacks.

line.dialogue: The Pirate is blocking the exit. The Scavenger has information. How does the party proceed?

choices.line: Create a sonic diversion by striking a nearby unstable crystal column, causing a disorienting resonance.
choices.description: Draw your resonant blade and challenge the bandit directly, demanding safe passage, 15 words

line.dialogue: [arthit: "I've cut down sky rats above the Spine. You're barely worth the edge on my blade."]
[arthit: "My hand shakes — the blade hums wild — I can't focus the resonance in time."]

choices.line: Attempt to negotiate with the Pirate, offering a false copy of the map to buy time.
choices.description: Flip a coin toward the bandit and claim Malee already paid the toll this morning, 15 words

line.dialogue: [malee: "Paid double, actually. Keep the change — you'll need it when the Archivists arrive."]
[malee: "The bandit catches the coin, bites it, and laughs. 'Counterfeit. Like everything else about you.'"]

choices.line: Challenge the Pirate to a duel of acoustic knowledge, using the Archives' own testing protocols as a wager.
choices.description: Signal Malee to create a distraction while you slip toward the Archive's side entrance, 15 words

line.dialogue: [malee: "I scatter a handful of flash-crystals — blinding white — and we're gone before they blink."]
[malee: "My crystals fizzle — damp from the fog — and now there's a very angry pirate staring at us."]

lines_before.dialogue: The central archive chamber is a cathedral of knowledge. Glowing crystal shelves spiral upward, each containing tone-engraved tablets. The air hums with preserved frequencies.
This place is incredible! It's like every safe route ever sung is recorded here. You have to see it!
Incredible, sure. Also heavily guarded. The Tonal Orders don't just let anyone stroll in. This 'open frequency' subplot of yours better be the only son of a plot, because if we get caught...
Caution, everyone. The acoustic dampeners in here are precise. A wrong step, a raised voice, and we could trigger a resonance lock. This movie is great for security, bad for us.
The silence here... it's not empty. It's curated. They've filtered out all the wild, unpredictable harmonies. Only the approved 'script' remains.
Aye. And that script leaves out the surface. My people's paths aren't in their precious archives. We're not part of their great narrative.

Quit the philosophizin'. The restricted sector—where they'd stash a map of all the open, uncharted frequencies—is up that spiral. Guards patrol in harmonic intervals. Time this right, it's a really good heist.

line.dialogue: The path to the restricted sector is ahead. A single, resonant bridge spans a chasm of silent crystal. The guard's patrol is a predictable, repeating tone.

choices.text: Use Chanida's impulsive energy. Have her create a loud, distracting dissonance at the far end of the bridge to draw the guard away.
choices.description: Channel a low-frequency pulse through the crystal floor to map hidden corridors beneath you.

line.dialogue: The resonance reveals three passages below — one of them isn't on any Order schematic I've ever seen.
That pulse hit the dampeners wrong — every guard in this hall just turned toward us.

choices.text: Have Malee and the Sky Pirate analyze the patrol's exact frequency. Try to match and 'sync' with it, walking unseen within their harmonic blind spot.
choices.description: Mimic the curated silence by holding perfectly still and letting the acoustic shadows swallow your breathing.

line.dialogue: We become part of the silence — even the sentinels' echolocation passes over us like we're furniture.
My heartbeat is too loud — the crystals are amplifying it, and the walls just started humming back.

choices.text: Have Pichit and the Scavenger listen deeply. Find the archive's own ambient hum and subtly alter it, causing a temporary, confusing resonance shift that masks your movement.
choices.description: Scrape two crystal shards together to produce a forbidden harmonic that disrupts the dampeners entirely.

line.dialogue: Every dampener just shattered — now we can hear everything they've been hiding, and they can hear us.
Wrong harmonic — the dampeners absorbed it and reversed the frequency. We just broadcast our exact position to the entire Order.

lines_after.dialogue: You slip into the Restricted Cartography Vault. The air is colder here, the light dimmer. In the center of the room, on a pedestal of pure quartz, glows a complex, three-dimensional lattice of light—the Open Frequency Map.
By the First Chord... it's real. It's not just a map of safe routes. It's a map of *possibility*. Every potential harmonic path, glowing like a constellation.
This is what they've been hiding. Not just knowledge, but potential. The freedom to go anywhere... not just where they permit.

lines_before.dialogue: As Pichit's hand nears the map, the vault doors seal with a deep, final *thrum*. The light shifts from soft blue to urgent amber. Archivist Sentinels, their forms woven from solidified sound, phase through the walls.
Told you. The menu of consequences just arrived. Can I see the menu? Oh look, it's 'capture,' 'silence,' and 'dissolution.' My favorite.
We didn't come this far to get erased! The map is right there! We just need to grab it and run!
Run where, kid? Doors are song-locked! We gotta fight our way to a console, rewrite the exit frequency. I can study the basic lock harmonics by myself, but I need time!
The Sentinels... they resonate with the archive's approved frequencies. They're rigid. Predictable. Our strength is the noise they've tried to forget.
Pichit, the map's interface is responding to your presence. It's... listening to you. You must choose. Do we fight to steal the physical map, or do we try to... *understand* it directly?
This knowledge shouldn't be a thing to be taken. It should be a song to be learned. But the Sentinels won't let us simply sit and study. Our choice writes the next measure.

line.dialogue: The Sentinels advance, their forms humming with lethal precision. The Open Frequency Map pulses, waiting. The party's fate—and the fate of this forbidden knowledge—hangs on a single, decisive action.

choices.text: Fight to Disable & Steal (The Pirate's Way). Protect the Bandit while he brute-forces the door frequency. Grab the physical map crystal and flee, securing a powerful artifact for yourselves.
choices.description: Sing the counter-melody you memorized from the archive's third shelf, matching the Sentinels' resonance frequency exactly.

line.dialogue: * "Ha! They're standing down — the archive recognizes us as authorized performers now!
* "Wrong pitch, wrong century. Those Sentinels just locked every exit and started humming our funeral march.

choices.text: Harmonic Overload (The Chanida Special). Use the party's combined, chaotic resonance to overwhelm the Sentinels' rigid frequencies, creating a window to directly interface with and download the map's data into your ship's crystal.
choices.description: Smash bandit's flask against the song-locked door, letting the liquid seep into the harmonic seals to disrupt their tuning.

line.dialogue: * "Expensive whiskey, but it worked — hear that? The lock just went completely out of tune!
* "Great, now the door's angry AND I'm sober. The seal absorbed it and doubled the frequency barrier.

choices.text: The Listener's Gambit (Pichit's Path). Don't fight the archive. Sing to it. Weave your unique resonance with the Map's open frequency, not to take it, but to *broadcast* it—sending the data out into the Lattice for all to potentially hear.
choices.description: Let scavenger interface directly with the Sentinel's resonance core, betting their archive-touched nerves can withstand the cognitive feedback loop.

line.dialogue: * "I can feel the archive's approval pouring through me — the Sentinels are accepting my
The risk doesn't pay off. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber shudders. Crystalline shelves chime in discord or harmony. As the dust settles, the consequences of your choice resonate through the silent vault.
The map is... not gone. It's changed. We've changed it. Whether it's a secret in our hands, data in our ship, or a seed in the wind... the world's melody will never be the same.

Alarms now wail through the archives in shattered harmonies. Far below, the Lattice itself seems to shimmer with a new, unfamiliar light. You have rewritten a page of history. The epilogue is yet to be sung.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a monument to silence, a vast, crystalline library where the only sounds are the soft hum of the Lattice's ambient resonance and the careful tread of scholars. Pichit's party moves through the towering shelves of sonic scrolls.
Every recorded note here is a ghost of a safe passage. It's humbling, and... restrictive. The Lattice has more songs than these archives could ever hold.
And yet, here we are, paying through the nose for the privilege of reading them. The Tonal Orders have a monopoly on safety. How convenient.
Forget the scrolls! Look, over by the resonance columns. Isn't that the Trade Negotiator from the Azure Bazaar? What's she doing in the research wing?
Probably brokering knowledge. Let's not get involved. Our charts for the southern drift are priority.
Wait. Listen. She's not alone.
The party presses against a shelf of humming crystal records. The Negotiator's smooth voice carries, but another, rougher tone answers.
...the route is unstable, but the salvage is pre-Silencing tech. Pure. My usual cut, plus a finder's fee for the coordinates.

lines_after.dialogue: Your cut's too high. And the Archives don't have this mapped. I overheard a Listener say that sector's resonance is... shifting. It's not necessary to risk your pretty ship.
Necessity is measured in resonance crystals, my friend. And my ship's as stubborn as the Lattice itself—it wouldn't budge an inch from a profit.
(Whispering) Shifting resonance? Uncharted salvage? That sounds like our kind of trouble!
Or a very good way to get our resonance ship stuck in an unmapped harmonic dead zone. Permanently.

line.dialogue: We've overheard a potential lead on lost technology, but it's off the sanctioned charts. What do we do?

choices.line: Approach the Negotiator openly. Information is a currency, and we might have some to trade.
choices.description: Slip behind the resonance columns and eavesdrop on the broker's conversation, 14 words

line.dialogue: I can make out every word—they're trading route cipher keys for southern passage clearance.
My elbow caught the column and now the whole gallery is ringing like a broken temple bell.

choices.line: Follow the Scavenger when he leaves. He knows the surface; he might lead us to the source directly.
choices.description: Wave down the archivist at the catalog desk and demand access to the unredacted passage logs, 15 words

line.dialogue: She's pulling the original ledger now—every smuggler's waypoint from the last forty seasons, unblacked.
She slammed the registry shut and called us 'sun-blind beggars'—we're blacklisted from the eastern wing entirely.

choices.line: Ignore it and focus on our original mission. The Archives are vast; we have our own research to complete.
choices.description: Grab one of the loose scrolls Chanida spotted and stuff it inside your coat before anyone notices, 14 words

line.dialogue: Got it—it's a tide chart marked with phantom anchorages that don't appear on any sanctioned map.
The scroll crumbled to powder the moment I touched it—whatever ink they used, it's centuries past saving.

lines_before.dialogue: Having decided to follow the Scavenger, the party trails him to a secluded reading alcove deep in the Archives. The air here is still, the usual hum dampened.
(Startled, turning quickly) You! You're the ones lurking by the columns. I should've known. Surface-folk have a scent, even up here.
We mean no harm. We heard your conversation. About the shifting resonance.
We're Listeners, of a sort. We study the Lattice's natural songs. An unstable sector is... concerning for everyone.
Listeners, huh? (He scoffs, but his shoulders relax slightly) Different from the Tonal Orders, at least. They just want to lock the songs away.
And you want to profit from them. We're not so different.

lines_after.dialogue: Profit? Maybe. But my crew... we went into that sector blind two cycles ago. The resonance there, it doesn't follow the charts. It *changes*. I'm sorry I'm late telling anyone. We lost two good people. You should get some rest and forget you heard me.
Lost people? What size resonator were they using? What harmonic key?

Doesn't matter the size you wear if the ground itself is singing a lie. The Groundless Movement babbles about 'free resonance,' but this... this is something else. It's like the Lattice is *awake* there.
An awake Lattice... The old texts speak of that before The Silencing. You're carrying a weight that isn't yours alone.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger is frightened and grieving, but he holds a key to a dangerous mystery. How do we proceed?

choices.line: Offer to help him retrieve his crew's remains or salvage. A shared purpose might earn his trust and the coordinates.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to decode the tonal pattern using monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Things don't go as planned. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.line: Pressure him for the coordinates now. The danger to other navigators is too great to wait; we need to investigate.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with engineering to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee fails. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: Reveal that Chanida is a latent Singer. Our unique ability to navigate might be the only way to safely explore the sector and honor his loss.
choices.description: The scavenger volunteers to record the spectral signature, leveraging surface knowledge

line.dialogue: the scavenger succeeds. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
the scavenger's resolve isn't enough. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The central reading room of the Tonal Archives is a vast, silent space. High crystalline vaults are carved to catch and amplify the faintest whisper of a turning page.
All this knowledge, and they still charge an arm and a leg for a cup of water. I think that's right. The Tonal Orders are only interested in profit.
Forget the water. Look at this! What do you think about these sigils in the margin? They don't match any chart notation I've seen.
A personal annotation, perhaps? A navigator's private thoughts. We should be careful. The Archives punish those who deface their texts.
No, Arthit. Look closer. The ink... it's not ink. It's crystallized Lattice-dust, etched by resonance. This is a Singer's mark.
You found one? Down on the surface, we hear whispers. Songs that aren't in the books. The Orders burn those pages when they find them.
A fascinating historical curiosity, I'm sure! But of limited commercial value now. The practical routes are all in the sanctioned ledgers.
Limited value? This is a map of a dead zone! A place the charts say is impassable. I think that's the one. The Silencing's epicenter.

lines_after.dialogue: The sigil begins to glow with a soft, internal light. A low hum fills the air, vibrating the pages of every book in the immediate stack.
Well. That's not ominous at all. I think we just tripped a silent alarm.
The resonance is stable, but... focused. It's not an alarm. It's a key.

line.dialogue: The humming crystal sigil reveals a hidden panel in the reading desk. From within, you can hear a faint, rhythmic pulse, like a slowed heartbeat.

choices.line: Touch the sigil with your bare hand. (Pichit's philosophical nature draws him to direct experience.)
choices.description: Scrape a sample of the annotation into your palm and hold it under the lamplight.

line.dialogue: Blood — old, oxidized deep brown. Someone carved this passage into the score with a needle and wept it full of meaning.
You've smeared it across the binding now. Whatever secret that was, we've halved it between your fingers and the page.

choices.line: Have Chanida match the pulse with a hum. (Use her impulsive musicality to synchronize.)
choices.description: Hum the annotated notes aloud while Chanida follows the standard notation beside you.

line.dialogue: There — the harmony splits. The annotation isn't a correction, it's a *countermelody* meant to be sung simultaneously. Someone hid a second song inside the first.
That's not how the intervals resolve, and now the archive warden is banging on the door. Stop before he calls the conservatory enforcers.

choices.line: Instruct Arthit to analyze the frequency first. (A cautious, scientific approach.)
choices.description: Press your thumb against the largest annotation mark and hold still until you feel something.
