line.dialogue: It's warm. Still warm. Pichit, how old did you say this manuscript was? Because this blood hasn't been dry for more than a day.
Nothing? Then it's older than I feared. Old enough that the writer is beyond questioning — unless the

lines_before.dialogue: The hidden panel slides away, revealing a narrow stairwell descending into the bedrock beneath the Archives. The air is cold and smells of ozone and old stone.
Structural readings are... irregular. We're below the Lattice layer. This place shouldn't acoustically exist.

Great. The guy in the condo next door always closes his door loudly, and we're breaking into the basement of reality. I have a class on not getting erased from existence, I'm gonna rush off right now.
This is it. The Groundless talk of a place before the Lattice. A root. They said the Orders built their cities on a lie.
A lie with very profitable trade routes! Perhaps we can... negotiate exclusive rights to whatever we find? Knowledge is currency, after all.
Forget your profits! Listen... that pulse. It's a song. A whole, complete song of the world, before it was broken.
The Silencing wasn't an end. It was a covering. A layer placed over this... original resonance. To control it. To own navigation.
The chamber opens into a vast, dark geodesic dome. At its center floats a complex, silent crystal—the source of the pulse. It is pristine, untouched by the milky Lattice above.

lines_after.dialogue: The core crystal brightens, responding to your presence. Projected light etches impossible routes across the dome—a master chart of the true world.
The Tonal Orders' monopoly... it's a shackle. This is the proof. This changes everything.
The Groundless were right. We're not meant to live on floating scraps. We're meant to hear the whole song again.
Or... we could be the only ones who hear it. That has value, too. Considerable value.

line.dialogue: The primordial crystal awaits. Its song, if fully awakened, would shatter the Tonal Orders' control forever. But its power is untamed, unpredictable.

choices.line: Awaken the crystal fully. Unleash the true song and let the consequences reshape the world. (Climactic, world-changing.)
choices.description: Direct Arthit to map the frequency corridors using tattooed routes

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Defeat. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.line: Record the frequencies secretly. Use the knowledge to build a new, fairer system from within. (Strategic, reformist.)
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with frequency mapping to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Chanida loses control. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.line: Shatter the crystal. Some truths are too dangerous, and the current stability, however unjust, prevents chaos. (Pragmatic, tragic.)
choices.description: Direct the merchant to record the spectral signature using valuable goods

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the merchant. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
The attempt backfires on the merchant. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands on a reinforced observation platform, a metal blister welded to the side of a towering rock spire. Below and all around, the Lattice stretches to the horizon—a vast, geometric plain of crystalline facets that hum and chime with every gust of wind.
Whoa. It’s… louder than the charts said. Listen to that high harmonic! Why didn’t you call me first? I would’ve brought my better recording crystals.
Because you’d have tried to ‘sample’ it and gotten us all crystallized. You have to finish your homework on basic resonance safety before you play composer.
The stability readings are nominal, but the pattern shifts are irregular. We should proceed with extreme caution.
It’s a language. Each facet a syllable, each vibration a thought. Why didn’t you go with the Listeners, Arthit? You have the patience for it.
My path was… otherwise prescribed. Focus, Pichit. The merchant’s signal is coming from that lower outcrop.
A sleek, if slightly battered, resonance ship is moored to the outcrop below. A figure in a garish coat waves, their smile visible even from this distance.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, the intrepid explorers! So glad you could make it. The Lattice is particularly… vocal today. Beautiful, isn’t it? And profitable, if you know which frequencies to harvest.
Cut the song. You said you had information on a ‘unique resonator.’ Not interested in your generic scrap.
Direct! I like that. Very well. I’ve come across schematics. For a prosthetic leg. One that uses a stabilized Lattice shard as a core. It could tune the wearer to safe paths… or other things.
He holds up a cracked data-slate. The schematics flicker, showing a complex crystalline limb. The subplot, the Resonant Prosthetic, now has a tangible form.

line.dialogue: The merchant smiles. 'The schematics are yours. For a price. Or, you could try to find the core shard yourselves out there. It’s a lovely day for a walk.' He gestures to the singing, deadly plain.

choices.text: Pay the merchant’s price. (Lose significant funds, gain schematics immediately.)
choices.description: Place your palm flat against the central facet and let the vibrations resonate through your bones.

line.dialogue: The syllables align under your touch — it's reading you back, not speaking at you.
Pull your hand back! You're bleeding from the cuticles — the crystal edges shift microns with each pulse.

choices.text: Politely decline, and search for the shard yourself. (Save funds, risk Lattice exposure.)
choices.description: Deploy the harmonic sampler in a twenty-meter perimeter grid around the formation.

line.dialogue: Clean waveform capture across all twelve nodes. Chanida, you owe me dinner — I didn't break a single one.
Three of the nodes just... inverted. They're playing the sound *back* at us, but reversed. My teeth feel wrong.

choices.text: Intimidate the merchant into a lower price. (Risk turning him hostile, save some funds.)
choices.description: Silence the team's comms and stand perfectly still for thirty seconds to isolate the pattern's rhythm.

line.dialogue: There — every seventh pulse carries a secondary undertone. That's the grammar. Pichit,
The attempt backfires on the merchant. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves across the Lattice surface, their insulated boots clicking on the facets. The air shimmers with heat and sound. In the distance, a jagged spire of pure crystal gleams—the likely source of the shard.
I’m just surprised the Tonal Orders haven’t quarantined this whole sector. The resonance here is… broken. Like a song missing half its notes.
My scanner indicates structural fatigue in the crystal formations ahead. A misstep could cause a sympathetic fracture. Just relax, don’t worry about it. I will navigate.
Don’t think about it too much, he says, while we’re walking on a giant singing landmine. Great advice.
The silence within the broken song… it’s where the old world speaks. Can you hear it?
A sharp, aggressive hum cuts through the ambient drone. A rust-colored resonance ship, bristling with improvised sonic weapons, drops from behind a crystal formation, blocking the path to the spire.
Well, well. Look what the resonance dragged in. This here’s a toll road. That shiny bit up the spire? That’s our salvage.
I just spoke with the merchant. He didn’t mention you lot had a claim.

lines_after.dialogue: That smooth-talker? He sells maps to graves. We’re the real power here. You hand over any nice crystals you’ve picked up, and maybe we don’t play a discordant note right under your feet.
You can’t just blast the Lattice! You’ll bring the whole sector down on us!
Our ship’s tuned to a nasty hidden frequency. Lets us punch holes. Now, your stuff. Or we make a hole where you’re standing.
The pirate ship’s resonator arrays glow ominously. The crystalline ground beneath the party vibrates in a threatening, unstable rhythm.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirate leader leans over his ship’s rail, a malicious grin on his face. The path to the spire—and the prosthetic’s core shard—is blocked.

choices.text: Surrender some lesser crystals as a ‘toll.’ (Lose some items, avoid immediate conflict.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the fractured crystal and channel a stabilizing resonance through the fissure.

line.dialogue: The harmonic feedback just sealed three micro-fractures — structural integrity holding, but barely.
Your resonance is off-key — you've widened the fissure, and now the whole lattice is singing in warning.

choices.text: Try to negotiate, using the merchant’s name or promising future shares. (Risk angering them, chance to talk past.)
choices.description: Close your eyes and attune your hearing to the silence Pichit described, letting the broken song fill your mind.

line.dialogue: You hear it too — the old melody beneath the silence, guiding us through the dead space.
No — the silence swallowed you. Your ears are ringing and you've lost the path entirely.

choices.text: Prepare for a fight. Use the unstable Lattice against them. (Dangerous combat, high reward if successful.)
choices.description: Grab Malee's arm and sprint through the resonant corridor before the structural fatigue cascades.

line.dialogue: the pirate finds the key. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
A costly mistake by the pirate. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands on the observation platform's edge, the Lattice's low hum vibrating through the crystal underfoot. The Trade Negotiator's abandoned resonator glows faintly nearby.
The pirate's ship is gone. But the Negotiator's resonator... it's still active on a restricted frequency. He must have been using it to communicate with someone in the Tonal Orders.
Of course he was. A smooth talker hiding secrets. Typical. He played us.
Who cares about him! Look at this! The resonator's feedback loop is creating a stable path down to a lower crystal shelf. We can follow it!
A path born from deception. What truths might it lead to, I wonder?
It's a significant risk. The frequency is unstable. You should get some rest before we consider this, Pichit. The climb earlier was taxing.
Rest? While that pirate and that merchant are out there with the charts we need? I'm sorry I'm late to this realization, but we're running out of time.
Malee's right! What are we waiting for? What size resonator do you think we'd need to amplify this signal safely? Let's go!

lines_after.dialogue: The party descends the resonant path. The light from the platform fades, replaced by the Lattice's own internal, pulsing luminescence.
On the lower shelf, they find a debris field—shattered Resonance Ship plating. And among it, a faint, rhythmic tapping.
That sound... it's not natural. It's a pattern. A distress call.

line.dialogue: The tapping leads to a fissure in the crystal wall. It's narrow, and the sound within is weak.

choices.line: Send Chanida. She's smallest and most agile.
choices.consequence: Chanida squeezes through, finding a trapped Sky Pirate scout with a broken leg. She secures a deal for information in exchange for rescue.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with crystal prosthetic to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Malee's expertise pays off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Things don't go as planned. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.line: Use Arthit's tools to carefully widen the fissure.
choices.consequence: The controlled resonance attracts a Lattice predator. After a tense standoff, it flees, but you find the pirate scout—and his intact logbook.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus staff meditation on the pre-Silencing ruins to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Pichit. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Pichit hits a wall. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Have Pichit attune to the tapping, trying to resonate the crystal open.
choices.consequence: Pichit's innate ability parts the crystal like a curtain, revealing the scout. The display of power is awe-inspiring but leaves Pichit visibly drained and the local Lattice harmonics disturbed.
choices.description: Direct the pirate to record the spectral signature using smuggling routes

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
Defeat. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The rescued pirate scout, his leg splinted with crystal shards, points a trembling finger across a vast, open plain of the Lattice. In the distance, two figures argue beside a massive, dormant resonator spire.
That's my captain and your slippery merchant friend! They're tryin' to fire up the Old Spire. Says it'll broadcast a frequency that'll ground every ship for miles! A total monopoly!
A cramp in my calf would be preferable to this. They're not just hiding charts. They're trying to rewrite them. Make themselves the only map.
The spire's ancient. Its activation could shatter this entire shelf. The harmonics are all wrong. We have to speak, to reason with them, before they trigger a second Silencing!
Reason? Look! The merchant's pulling out a weapon! He's more treacherous than anyone!
Two voices, shouting to be the only one heard. This is the cacophony that broke the world.
A shot rings out—a sonic pulse from the merchant's device. The Pirate Captain staggers. The spire begins to whine, overloading.
It's overloading! The feedback will tear this place apart! Could you speak clearly, scout? Is there a shut-down sequence?

lines_after.dialogue: The spire's whine climbs to a deafening shriek. Cracks race across the Lattice plain. The world holds its breath.
In the new silence, the consequences of the choice settle. The Lattice steadies, its song changed forever.
Every note leaves an echo. Every choice, a resonance. We must listen to what we have played today.

line.dialogue: The spire is critical. You have one chance to influence the final frequency.

choices.line: Sabotage the resonator feeds. Collapse the spire safely.
choices.consequence: With Arthit's guidance, you safely dismantle the spire. The pirate captain is arrested, the merchant flees. The old charts are saved, but the secret of the spire is lost. Stability is preserved, at the cost of a powerful discovery.
choices.description: Sprint across the crumbling bridge and tackle the merchant before he fires.

line.dialogue: Bandit — "I drove my shoulder into his ribs and sent that gun skittering across the stone — nobody shoots my captain.
Malee — "The bridge gave way beneath my boot and I caught the ledge with fingernails — the merchant's still aiming.

choices.line: Broadcast a calming frequency. Try to stabilize the spire.
choices.consequence: Pichit and the party combine their resonators, harmonizing with the spire. It stabilizes, becoming a new, public navigational beacon. The pirate and merchant are stranded. The Tonal Orders' monopoly is broken, ushering in a new, uncertain era of open travel.
choices.description: Shout to the captain to duck while drawing my blade against the merchant.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "My voice cracked through the chamber and she dropped — the merchant's shot sparked off the spire instead of her skull.
Chanida — "The captain didn't hear me over the hum and the merchant squeezed the trigger — I watched her stumble.

choices.line: Override the frequency. Redirect its power to the Resonant Prosthetic subplot.
choices.consequence: You channel the spire's immense power into the crystal leg schematics. It works—the prosthetic prototype activates with perfect, stable resonance. But the redirected energy violently destabilizes the local Lattice, creating a permanent, dangerous storm of crystal shards around the site. A miracle with a terrible price.
choices.description: Grab the spire's control lever

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the pirate pulls it off. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
A costly mistake by the pirate. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery hangs like a frozen teardrop against the abyss. Inside its grand, vaulted halls, the only sound is the faint, resonant hum of the Lattice far below, filtered through miles of acoustic stone.
Welcome, travelers. The air here is... heavy with thought. And, if you listen closely, opportunity. I represent a consortium with an interest in the monastery's quieter archives.
Opportunity? We're here to learn, not to make deals. The Listeners said something about a disturbance in the lower chantries.
Of course they did. A 'disturbance' usually means 'something that doesn't make us money.' Let me guess, it's 'haunted'?
We should proceed with caution. The acoustic integrity of Phrao is delicate. A wrong frequency could... destabilize things.
The silence here isn't empty. It's listening back. Roll up your sleeves. We're going to see what the stone has to say.
Please, be careful down there. My cousin, he worked supply for the Resonance ships. He said... he said the lower levels hold echoes of things best forgotten.

lines_after.dialogue: The party descends a spiral staircase carved from a single, resonant blue crystal. The air grows colder, and the omnipresent hum sharpens into a dissonant whine.
Lovely. It's like walking into a giant's sore tooth. That's all, isn't it? Just bad acoustics?
No. This is a scar. A memory in the stone. It's something to think about.

line.dialogue: A sealed archway blocks the path ahead. Its surface vibrates faintly.

choices.text: Let Chanida try to shatter the crystal seal with a focused shout. (Strength)
choices.description: Tap the stone wall with your knife and listen for hollow chambers beneath.

line.dialogue: The resonance returns clean — solid stone behind us. No hidden passages this direction.
That pitch... the wall absorbed it. There's a cavity behind this section, or something that *wants* silence.

choices.text: Have Arthit analyze the crystal's resonant frequency to find a weak point. (Knowledge)
choices.description: Ask the merchant what goods he's carrying in a place where no one comes to buy.

line.dialogue: He's nervous — look at his hands. Whatever he's selling, it's not for ordinary travelers.
Three crates, no cart, no pack animals. Either he's the worst merchant alive or those boxes were already *waiting* here for someone.

choices.text: Search the nearby alcoves for a manual release mechanism. (Perception)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the floor and feel for vibrations through the stone.

line.dialogue: A pulse — steady, deep, like a heartbeat. Something below us is alive, or remembering that it once was.
Nothing. Just cold stone and my own imagination filling the quiet with things that aren't there.

lines_before.dialogue: Beyond the arch lies a cavernous chantry, long abandoned. In its center rests the ghostly outline of a Resonance ship, its crystal hull cracked and dark, fused into the monastery floor.
By the Lattice... it's the *Echo of the Dawn*. A supply ship lost during the Silencing. The records said it vanished without a trace.
It didn't vanish. It crashed *here*. But why hide it? I'll have a look inside.
Because a crashed ship in a holy acoustic chamber is bad for pilgrim business. I'll get it. The hatch looks jammed, not locked.
Wait. Can you hear it? Not a hum... a whisper. A looping fragment of a final log entry, trapped in the crystal.
A faint, desperate voice scratches at the edge of hearing: '*...charts were wrong... the lattice song changed... they knew...*'
I told you! Echoes of the lost! We shouldn't be here!

lines_after.dialogue: The log implies the Tonal Orders' navigation charts were deliberately flawed. This wasn't an accident.
So they murdered a crew to keep a secret? I'll try it. I'll try to extract the full memory from the ship's core.
Careful. If the Tonal Orders buried this, they won't appreciate us digging it up. But... I'll look at it for you. The core's resonator is still faintly active.

line.dialogue: The ship's cracked resonator core pulses with captured light. Extracting the full memory is risky.

choices.text: Stabilize the core with a damping frequency from your own tools. Safe, but the memory may be blurred. (Craft)
choices.description: Chanida channels singer voice toward the quiet halls, hoping to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Chanida is thwarted. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Harmonize with the core's dying resonance, channeling it through Pichit. Reveals truth, but is emotionally taxing. (Empathy)
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing leg resonance to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Malee pulls it off. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.text: Overload the core with a burst of power, forcing the memory out in one clear, violent shockwave. Most revealing, most dangerous. (Daring)
choices.description: The villager attempts to follow the phantom route, relying on irrigation

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the villager's call. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
The gamble fails. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: In the deepest archives of Phrao Monastery, the air hums with captured resonance. Crystal discs line the walls, preserving echoes of the past.
The Listeners' records are extensive, but fragmented. A lost ship's final resonance... it should be here somewhere. Remember, we're looking for any distortion pattern from that era.
I'll look at it for you. These crystal readers are fascinating—you can almost feel the vibrations.
Keep in mind that most 'haunted ship' stories are just merchant excuses for lost cargo. Is the pay good for ghost hunting?
Every echo holds truth if you listen deeply enough. The lattice remembers what we forget.
A particular crystal disc glows faintly as Chanida passes her hand over its reader. A distorted, mournful tone fills the chamber.
I heard a strange noise... no, it's more than noise. It's a resonance pattern, but it's... broken. Like a song cut off mid-phrase.
That's the signature of a lattice rupture. The lost ship didn't just vanish—it was torn apart by resonance feedback.

lines_after.dialogue: The lattice doesn't forget trauma. That broken song is still resonating through the crystal layers.
So we've found our ghost. Now what? Do we perform an exorcism with tuning forks?
The Trade Negotiator enters the archive, his smile not quite reaching his eyes.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator approaches with calculated concern.

choices.text: Share the discovery openly. Perhaps he knows more about the ship's cargo.
choices.consequence: Gains merchant's cooperation but reveals your hand
choices.description: Align the fractured crystal shards by matching their resonance frequencies on the reader's dial.

line.dialogue: * "There — the third shard is syncing. I can see a vessel manifest, something about a crew that stopped reporting in.
* "The frequencies keep sliding past each other. My fingers are too cold to feel the vibration properly.

choices.text: Ask careful questions about his interest in the lost ship.
choices.consequence: Extracts information while maintaining mystery
choices.description: Ask Pichit to sit with the darkest crystal and simply listen, letting whatever's trapped inside speak freely.

line.dialogue: * "It's not words... it's breathing. Forty-seven souls, and they're all holding their breath. They're waiting for something.
* "I hear only my own heartbeat bouncing back. Either this shard is empty, or whatever's inside doesn't trust me yet.

choices.text: Confront him with the evidence of resonance trauma.
choices.consequence: Forces truth but risks dangerous confrontation
choices.description: Cross-reference the Listeners' ship registry against Malee's naval disappearance logs from the last decade.

line.dialogue: * "Three matches. All reported as mechanical failures, all within the same shipping lane. That's not coincidence, that's a pattern someone buried.
* "The registry uses old identification codes. Half these entries could be cargo haulers or warships — I can't tell which is which.

lines_before.dialogue: (Oh), you're here? Working late in the archives, I see. We've talked about this before—some echoes should remain buried.
The lattice remembers everything. That ship carried something that shouldn't have been moved.
We've never understood why the Tonal Orders sealed these records. Now I'm beginning to see.
Some harmonies disrupt the profitable order of things. That ship carried experimental resonators that could have broken the guild monopoly.
So it wasn't an accident. It was sabotage disguised as a lattice anomaly.
The monastery's crystal structures begin to vibrate. The lost ship's broken resonance is amplifying, drawn to the truth being spoken.
The archive crystals are resonating with the pattern! It's like the ship is... answering.
The lattice holds the memory of that violence. Now it's resonating through Phrao itself.

lines_after.dialogue: Crystal shards tremble as the haunting resonance builds to a crescendo. The very monastery threatens to join the lost ship's fate.
If we don't harmonize this resonance, Phrao will suffer the same rupture!
This is exactly why some knowledge should stay lost! You've awakened something that should have slept!

line.dialogue: The broken resonance threatens to shatter Phrao's crystals. You must respond to the lattice's traumatic memory.

choices.text: Use the monastery's dampening fields to suppress the resonance.
choices.consequence: Saves Phrao but buries the truth again
choices.description: Chanida channels hidden frequencies toward the monk chants, hoping to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Chanida is thwarted. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Attempt to complete the ship's broken song, giving its resonance closure.
choices.consequence: Heals the trauma but reveals dangerous knowledge
choices.description: Have Malee focus mechanical repair on the ancient texts to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee loses control. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Amplify the resonance, forcing the lattice to reveal the full truth of the sabotage.
choices.consequence: Uncovers everything but risks catastrophic rupture
choices.description: The villager attempts to decode the distress signal, relying on irrigation

line.dialogue: the villager's expertise pays off. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
the villager hits a wall. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of quiet, where the only sounds are the rustle of crystal-paper and the distant hum of the Lattice far below.
A whole city that floats on knowing which noises won't shatter it. How reassuring. Let's find this map and get out before I die of reverence.
Keep your voice down, Malee. The acoustics here are precise. A wrong tone could... well, we don't know. That's why we need the Open Frequency Map.
There! The restricted stacks. The monk said the old surface charts would be there. Let's go!
Wait. Observe the Listeners. Their movements are a meditation. To them, this isn't just data. It's a song they're trying to remember.
You lot stick out like a shattered resonator. Archives folk move slow, like they're afraid of their own echoes.
And you are?
Someone who knows the Lattice's surface isn't a chart. It's a grave. You looking for the Open Frequency? That's a ghost story the Orders tell to scare rookies.

lines_after.dialogue: We're not done yet! A friend introduced us to a source who said the map is real. It shows natural, stable paths, free of the Orders' control.
Introduced, huh? Sounds finished to me. That 'source' is probably a Listener with a crisis of faith. They bury the truth here deeper than the Silencing.
Then we need to find that Listener. But carefully. If the Tonal Orders discover we're prying...

line.dialogue: The Scavenger eyes you, waiting to see what you'll do.

choices.line: Appeal to shared curiosity. ("Don't you want to know what they're hiding?")
choices.description: Step only when the Listeners' bare feet lift, matching their meditative cadence perfectly, 15 words

line.dialogue: Yes—their rhythm becomes our rhythm. Move when they move, and the floor forgives us.
You stepped between their beats. The silence here just learned your weight.

choices.line: Offer a trade. ("We have supplies from the upper docks. Information for goods.")
choices.description: Signal Chanida to crawl beneath the reading tables while you and Pichit create a distraction, 15 words

line.dialogue: I can see the restricted stacks from here—three more tables and I'm through.
A Listener turned. They don't chase, they just... listen harder. I'm frozen.

choices.line: Thank them and proceed alone. ("We'll manage. The Archives are open to all.")
choices.description: Whisper the monk's passphrase into the resonance bowl near the archive entrance, 15 words

line.dialogue: The bowl absorbed it—no echo. That's the password. The archives recognize us.
It echoed. It never echoes here. Every Listener in the hall just oriented toward us.

lines_before.dialogue: Guided by the Scavenger's muttered clues, you find a secluded scriptorium. A lone Listener monk is meticulously inking a chart, his hand trembling.
The resonance of this cadence... it's all wrong. The official chart says this path is stable, but the song... the song has changed.
You hear the true sound of the Lattice, don't you? Not just the sanctioned frequencies.
It is a burden. To know the world sings one tune, while my Order is forced to transcribe another. I don't know where to begin to make it right.
How about with the Open Frequency Map? Either it's a myth, or it's the truth you're all avoiding.
You speak of the Primal Harmony. It is not a map as you understand it. It is... a state of listening. Recorded before the Silencing, before the Orders.
Where is it?
Chanida. How well do you know her, brother? Can we trust that this Primal Harmony won't lead to another Silencing?

lines_after.dialogue: I don't know either if it is safe. That is the conflict. My vows command me to preserve knowledge. My conscience commands me to share it. The original crystal is in the Deep Vault.
Of course it is. The most forbidden part of the most silent library.
The vault is acoustically sealed. A single wrong frequency triggers irreversible lockdowns. We must become part of the Archive's silence to enter.

line.dialogue: The Monk looks from his false chart to your determined faces. The path to the vault is clear, but the method is not.

choices.line: Use the Monk's authority. ("Walk with us. Your robes will grant passage.")
choices.description: Malee steps forward with leg resonance, ready to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
The lattice has other plans. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: Create a sonic diversion. ("Chanida, cause a 'research accident' with a resonator in the main hall.")
choices.description: Direct Arthit to calibrate against the frequency using tattooed routes

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The risk doesn't pay off. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Attempt a perfect harmonic null. ("We must match the vault's resonant frequency exactly to pass unseen.")
choices.description: The scavenger steps forward with crystal fragments, ready to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the scavenger pulls it off. The surface dweller's grit carries them through.
the scavenger overreaches. A crystal fragment resonates destructively.

lines_before.dialogue: The silence here is... unnerving. It's not empty. It's curated. Controlled.
They've sanitized the song. Turned a living thing into a filing system. How utterly boring.
We can't just stand here! The map is here somewhere. I'm going to start pulling scrolls.
Wait! The acoustics are precise. A misplaced footstep could trigger a security resonance. Let's be methodical.
Methodical? While the Orders guard their secrets? I knew this was a waste. I'm bored of waiting for permission to know the world.
Please, lower your voices. The Archives demand reverence. The quiet is... part of the lesson.
A lesson in obedience? Or forgetting? What size of truth do these shelves hold, Monk? What size have they trimmed it down to fit?

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk hesitates, his eyes darting to a sealed, resonant-locked cabinet marked 'Apocrypha - Unverified Harmonies'.
Most of the Orders are content with the sanctioned charts. But... some of us hear gaps in the official song.
Ah. The restless scholar. Bored with the party line. Finally, something interesting.

line.dialogue: The Monk seems on the verge of breaking protocol. How do we press for the hidden map?

choices.text: Appeal to his scholarly curiosity. The pursuit of pure knowledge.
choices.outcome: He respects academic intent. He'll help, but slowly and with many caveats.
choices.description: Match your breathing to the library's pulse, letting it guide each silent step forward.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "There — beneath the floor, a rhythm. The map's heartbeat. Follow it and stay low.
Arthit — "Your boots scraped the marble. The shelves just *breathed* in response — everyone, freeze!

choices.text: Invoke the duty of a Listener: to hear ALL sounds, not just convenient ones.
choices.outcome: You strike a chord with his vows. He acts, but is visibly tormented by the disobedience.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the nearest shelf and let the sanitized song show you where they cut it away.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Here — this gap between the notes, where the melody should ache. They hid the map in the *absence*.
Malee — "Nothing. They scoured it too clean. All I taste is dust and antiseptic — the song won't surface here.

choices.text: Threaten to expose his conflicted state to his superiors unless he cooperates fully.
choices.outcome: He complies out of fear, giving you full access but becoming a hostile, unpredictable asset.
choices.description: Signal Chanida to hum the fragment she remembers while you read the vibrations in the reading desk's wood grain.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "The grain is shifting — look, the wood is *writing* — the map's underneath the varnish, it was always here!
Chanida — "I hit the wrong note and the reading lamps all turned toward us. Run, before the catalogue answers!

lines_before.dialogue: The Apocrypha cabinet hums open. Inside is not a chart, but a raw, uncut resonance crystal, pulsing with a wild, unstable light.
The Open Frequency... from that day the first Singer vanished. It's a key, but to where? The Orders declared it a dangerous heresy.
The energy signature is chaotic. If we attune our ship to this, we could tear through the Lattice... or be torn apart.
That's the sound from below! The true song of the surface! You city-dwellers locked it away!
It's beautiful. It's terrifying. It's freedom. Who would believe a single note could hold so much?
Believe it. They hid it because it works. Look at them smiling happily in their portraits, the great Archivists. Liars.
This is the choice. The safe, silent path of the known... or the dangerous song of what might be.
Alarm resonances begin to chime through the Archives. The Tonal Orders have been alerted. Time has run out.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal's light washes over the group, casting long, decisive shadows on the ancient shelves.
We take it. We learn its song. We believe there's more to this world than silence and control.
The decision is made. The consequences will resonate far beyond these hushed halls.

line.dialogue: The Orders are coming. The crystal is in hand. What is our escape and our commitment?

choices.text: Use the crystal as a bargaining chip. Trade it for safe passage and a sanctioned expedition.
choices.outcome: You survive with Order oversight, gaining limited access but becoming part of their system.
choices.description: Attune the ship's frequency to match the chaotic energy signature, risking structural integrity

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
The gamble fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Flee with the Monk and Scavenger. Use their knowledge to vanish into the uncharted Lattice.
choices.outcome: You become fugitives with powerful allies, free but hunted, forging your own path.
choices.description: The monk attempts to sing/chant with the frequency to understand its origin

line.dialogue: Exactly as Malee hoped. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
Defeat. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Attune the crystal here and now, unleashing its raw frequency to shatter the Archives' silence and escape in the chaos.
choices.outcome: You deal a blow to the Orders' control and escape dramatically, but the unleashed resonance has unpredictable, world-altering effects.
choices.description: The scavenger leads the group toward the source of the sound below

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the monk. His recording captures a denied frequency.
The attempt backfires on the monk. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship *Harmonic Drift* descends through the cloud layer, its crystal resonators humming a low C-sharp. Below, the Lattice Surface unfolds—a vast, glimmering plain of interlocking geometric patterns that shift with every sound.
Landing protocols engaged. Stabilizing on the observation platform. Remember, everyone—the Lattice here is unstable. One wrong note could trigger a shatter cascade.
Look at those light patterns! It's like the ground is breathing. Can we get closer?
Sure, if you want your bones rearranged into a musical scale. The beauty's a trap. The Silencing didn't happen because things were ugly.
Yet it responds... There's intelligence in this pattern. Not malevolence. A language we've forgotten how to hear.
You Listeners always talk like that. Pragmatics, remember? We're here because the Tonal Orders tax our resonance crystal shipments. We need unregistered fragments.
Scavenging mission parameters: secure three stable harmonic fragments from sector seven. The platform's dampening field gives us ninety minutes.
Why didn't you go with the Tonal escort? They charted this sector last week.

lines_after.dialogue: The Tonal warden? He winked at me when I asked for the chart fee waiver. I'm afraid there'll be a problem if we're caught out here without their seal.
Of course there will be. Monopolies don't like competition, even from poor skycity folk picking crystal shards.
Then we listen for ourselves. The Lattice will tell us where the stable fragments are.

line.dialogue: The party must choose their approach to locating the harmonic fragments.

choices.line: Follow the villager's crude scanner—pragmatic but loud, risking Tonal attention.
choices.description: Place your bare palm flat against the glowing crystal and let the pattern speak through you.

line.dialogue: The intelligence recognizes contact—it's mapping your nervous system like a language it wants to learn.
Congratulations, you just volunteered your hand to become a new geometric formation. Pull back before it finishes the translation.

choices.line: Have Pichit attempt to 'listen' to the Lattice's patterns—unpredictable but potentially revealing.
choices.description: Deploy the resonance probe in a triangular array matching the three brightest nodes of light.

line.dialogue: Probe alignment locked—the crystal's frequency just shifted to match our equipment. We're in dialogue now.
Wrong triangle—those nodes just went dark and three new ones lit up behind us. It's rearranging the board.

choices.line: Stick to Arthit's pre-planned grid search—safe, slow, and methodical.
choices.description: Broadcast the ship's linguistic database in a continuous loop while slowly advancing toward the pattern's center.

line.dialogue: It's responding! Those pulses are mirroring our syntax structure—it's building a vocabulary in real time!
Too much data too fast. The pattern collapsed into static. Whatever intelligence lives here just went silent, and I suspect that's worse than anger.

lines_before.dialogue: The chosen path leads away from the platform's hum. The Lattice here reacts to footsteps—tiny, crystalline chimes rising like glass rain. In the distance, a fractured spire gleams, its base swarmed with scavenger drones.
Drones. Tonal Order patrol. They're marking fragments for collection. We need to be quieter.
Stop! Look—by that cracked hexagon. Something's moving. Not a drone.
A Listener monk. Robes the color of dull amethyst. What's one of them doing out here alone? He's still single, isn't he? Monastic vows and all.
He's... kneeling. Placing his hands on the Lattice. Listening.
The song here is wounded. A fracture in the great chord. Your footsteps... they aggravate the dissonance.
You can ask him about safe fragments. The Listeners chart by ear, not by Tonal maps.
Stop it with the reverence! We need crystals, not poetry. My brother needs that resonant prosthetic leg calibrated, and these fragments are the only affordable option.

lines_after.dialogue: A prosthetic... yes. The crystal must sing in harmony with the wearer's own resonance. A single misaligned frequency could... You can try asking him to wait. The fragments here are tainted by the drones' harsh frequencies.
Tainted. Of course. Nothing's ever simple. So we risk a bad leg, or we risk the Tonal Orders catching us stealing 'clean' fragments from their marked zones.
The monk hears the truth of the Lattice. We should listen.

line.dialogue: The Listener monk warns the nearby fragments are corrupted. The party must decide how to proceed.

choices.line: Take the corrupted fragments anyway—they'll work for the prosthetic, but with unknown side effects.
choices.description: Arthit steps forward with lattice storms, ready to trace the anomalous signal

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit misreads the situation. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.line: Follow the monk's guidance to a purer, unmarked site—quicker but requires trusting his unknown motives.
choices.description: Malee uses crystal prosthetic to tune the prosthetic near the crystal ground

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Malee. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee misreads the situation. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: Disable the Tonal drones and claim their marked, clean fragments—direct confrontation with the guild.
choices.description: Ask the villager to follow the phantom route, drawing on local knowledge

line.dialogue: The lattice answers the villager's call. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
A costly mistake by the villager. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform is quiet, the Lattice's usual shimmer muted. The monk, Brother Lirin, stares into the depths, his face pale.
The song... I don't feel the same as before. It's not just guidance. It's a... a warning. A plea.
A plea from what? The rocks? Come on, monk, you're making me uncomfortable.
He doesn't have many friends in the Tonal Orders for saying things like that. They prefer their charts neat and their profits neat.
But if the Lattice itself is speaking a warning, ignoring it is the greater danger. What does your heart hear, Brother?
A fracture. A dissonance deep below, where the old city-metal sleeps. The Silencing... it wasn't an end. It was a suppression. And what was suppressed is... stirring.
I have an uneasy feeling about this. We came to salvage resonator parts, not wake up a catastrophe.
A low, sub-audible hum vibrates through the platform. The crystal in Arthit's prosthetic leg flickers erratically.

lines_after.dialogue: The party regroups on the platform's edge. The monk has given them a direction: a nearby 'sinkhole' where the Lattice song warps.
(Tapping his flickering prosthetic) This thing is a liability down there. If it resonates wrong...
Or it could be the only key that fits the lock. Uncomfortable? Welcome to the club.

line.dialogue: How do we approach the sinkhole? The monk says the path is treacherous.

choices.text: Easy: Use the monk's chants to find stable footing. (Relies on tradition)
choices.leads_to: The monk's steady tones reveal a hidden, solid path through the shimmering chaos.
choices.description: Strike the tuning fork against stone and listen for dissonance in the Lattice's reply.

line.dialogue: The fork hums clean — then fractures into a second tone, jagged and wrong. "There," the monk whispers. "You hear it now? The Lattice is answering a question none of us asked.
The fork rings pure and clear. Chanida smirks. "Sounds fine to me. Maybe the only cracked thing here is your confidence, monk.

choices.text: Medium: Have Chanida scout ahead, using her agility to test the ground. (Risks a fall)
choices.leads_to: Chanida darts forward, her light steps finding purchase where heavier feet would shatter the crystal.
choices.description: Demand Pichit explain what specific warning the Lattice could broadcast that the Tonal Orders would recognize.

line.dialogue: Pichit steadies himself. "Harmonic collapse. The Orders documented it once — a pitch that unwrites itself from memory. If that's what's bleeding through, we have maybe six hours before none of us remember this conversation.
Pichit stammers, gestures vaguely. "I — I don't know the specifics, I'm not a senior theorist—" Malee snorts. "So we're panicking over a hunch from a junior reader. Wonderful.

choices.text: Hard: Use Arthit's prosthetic as a tuning fork, letting its erratic pulse guide you away from harmonic danger. (Gambles on the subplot)
choices.leads_to: A painful, lurching walk, but the leg's flickers intensify near unstable zones, acting as a gruesome divining rod.
choices.description: Ask Malee which Tonal Order members the monk still trusts enough to verify this anomaly.

line.dialogue: Malee considers, then pulls a folded note from her sleeve. "One. Sister Arunee at the Third Octave. She stopped trusting the Orders before it was fashionable.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The sinkhole is a wound. Jagged crystal spires rise around a deep, dark pit where the Lattice's light dies. A profound, aching quiet reigns.
This silence... it's not empty. It's full. Remember... the Listeners teach that true listening starts in the quiet.
I can't remember a place ever feeling this wrong. My skin is crawling.
Keep in mind we're standing where the song broke. The Tonal Orders' pretty maps end here.
From the depths, a shape emerges—not crystal, but corroded metal, a colossal, silent resonator from the world before The Silencing.
It's a damper. A machine designed to kill resonance. This... this is what caused The Silencing?
No. It was built *after*. To contain what The Silencing unleashed. The Orders' founders sealed it away and forbade the knowledge. They made us forget.
The ancient machine groans. A crackle of dead sound washes over them. Arthit's prosthetic leg glows with a sick, compelling light, trying to sync with the damper's failing frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: The air still hums with the aftermath. The damper is quiet, for now. The truth, however, is deafening.
We remember now. The Silencing was a cage. And the Tonal Orders are the jailers.
My order... we were meant to be the rememberers. We failed. Until today.

line.dialogue: The damper is destabilizing. Arthit's prosthetic is resonating with its core. We must choose.

choices.text: Easy: Smash the prosthetic. Sever the connection. (Lose the subplot asset, ensure immediate safety)
choices.leads_to: Arthit doesn't hesitate. A crystal shatters. The damper's pulse falters and stills. The leg is inert metal, but the threat is gone.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to map the frequency corridors, drawing on unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Chanida overreaches. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Medium: Use the prosthetic to carefully dampen the machine's frequency. A delicate, dangerous tune. (Risk Arthit, attempt to preserve both)
choices.leads_to: Arthit grits his teeth, focusing. The leg's light steadies, becoming a governor. The damper powers down into hibernation. The prosthetic is now a key, and a burden.
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with resonant staff, ready to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Hard: Overload the connection. Let the prosthetic resonate *through* the damper, shattering its core and unleashing the raw, forgotten song beneath. (Climactic risk, unknown consequences)
choices.leads_to: A scream of light and sound. The damper explodes into harmonic dust. For one terrifying, glorious moment, the true, wild song of the world rings out, before settling into a new, unstable pattern. Everything has changed.
choices.description: Ask the villager to listen for the ghost ship's echo, drawing on community ties

line.dialogue: the villager makes it work. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
The lattice has other plans. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard is a symphony of industrial decay. Towering hulks of broken Resonance Ships cast long shadows, their crystal resonators dark and silent. The air thrums with the clash of metal and the growl of salvage engines, a harsh, grating counterpoint to the Lattice's faint, distant hum below.
Ugh, this noise is going to give me a permanent headache. How can anyone think straight here?
They don't. They just smash things until they get paid. It's the universal language.
Keep your voices low. Sound carries strangely here. We're looking for a Listener contact, not announcing ourselves to every scavenger with a price on information.
Listen... beneath the noise. There's a rhythm to the breaking. Even destruction has its pattern, its own reluctant apology to the order it disrupts.
Great. Philosophical Pichit is back. Look, there's our monk, by that gutted freighter.
A figure in simple, ochre robes stands apart from the workers, head tilted as if listening to a distant melody. He turns as you approach, his expression one of deep weariness.
You've arrived. I'm sorry I'm late to meet you; the journey was... fraught. The Lattice's song near the city's edge is choked with pain.

lines_after.dialogue: I am Brother Kavi. My Order has heard whispers. A ship was lost here, years ago. The *Echo of Dawn*. Its final resonance... never faded. It lingers, a ghost in the crystal.
A haunted ship? Perfect. Because what this lovely place needed was a ghost story.
If its resonator is still active, however faintly, it could be a navigational hazard. Or a treasure trove of pre-Silencing data. Why tell us?
Because the Tonal Orders have sealed the records. They say its frequency is 'cacophonous.' But I've heard it. It's not chaos. It's a plea. You're going to be sorry for ignoring it.

line.dialogue: Brother Kavi believes the lost ship's echo holds a truth the Tonal Orders want buried. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Trust the monk's intuition. Ask him to guide you to the echo's source.
choices.description: Follow Pichit's lead and track the rhythm to its source through the maze of crushed vehicles.

line.dialogue: There — behind that overturned bus. The beating isn't random. Someone's signaling.
I lost it. Too much clattering from the crusher drowned out the pattern.

choices.text: Seek a second opinion. Find a local scavenger who knows the scrapyard's secrets.
choices.description: Scale the rusted shipping container for a vantage point over the scrapyard's layout.

line.dialogue: Good. I can see three guards near the furnace and a truck leaving through the east gate.
The metal gave way under my boot. Everyone down — we've got company coming!

choices.text: Focus on the practical. Look for the ship's physical wreckage first; the truth is in its bones.
choices.description: Move closer to the workers and attempt to blend in by picking up discarded tools.

line.dialogue: Grab a crowbar and look bored. That's all these idiots do anyway. We're invisible.
A foreman just asked which crew I'm with. Run now or start swinging.

lines_before.dialogue: Following your choice, you delve deeper into the canyon of dead ships. The Monk, Kavi, leads you to a quieter sector where the Lattice's hum is more audible, a soft bass note beneath the scrap-metal wind.
The silence here is different. Not an absence, but a holding of breath.
Yeah, I feel it too. Like something's watching us from all these empty hulls.
Scans are picking up a low-level residual frequency. It's weak, but structured. It's definitely not random noise.
Great. So we're being serenaded by a dead battery. Charming.
A sudden clang echoes from above. A figure drops from a gantry, landing with a practiced ease. They're clad in patched thermal gear, a scavenger's rebreather hanging loose around their neck.
Well now. Oh, you're here? Didn't think the Listeners sent tourists this deep.
This is Sila. They... know the surface of the Lattice around Tha Khwae better than any chart.

lines_after.dialogue: Who's this man, Kavi? And his friends? You know the rules. Don't tell him everything. Not until I know what they're really after.
We're after a ship. The *Echo of Dawn*. The monk says it's singing.
Singing? Hah. It's screaming. Got a crew mate who went poking around its last known slip. Came back babbling about 'the wrong note.' He's not right in the head anymore.
A psychological effect from an unstable resonance field? Or something he heard?
Who is this guy, the doctor? Look. I know where it is. Or was. The Lattice shifts. But it's not a place for the curious. It's a wound.

line.dialogue: Sila the Scavenger has the location, but warns of danger. Brother Kavi trusts them. How do you secure their help?

choices.text: Appeal to their curiosity. Propose a joint salvage split; truth and profit aren't mutually exclusive.
choices.description: Tap the tuning fork against the corridor wall and listen for where the resonance bends.

line.dialogue: There — the harmonic shifts three meters ahead. Whatever's broadcasting, it's behind that bulkhead.
Nothing but dead ringing. Either the source is deeper than I thought, or this fork is as useless as my patience.

choices.text: Challenge their knowledge. Suggest the Tonal Orders have a chart, implying they don't know as much as they claim.
choices.description: Ask Malee to rig the scanner into a directional antenna to triangulate the signal.

line.dialogue: Got it. Three points, clean triangle. The signal's coming from below us — sub-deck, maybe two levels down.
Best I can do is 'somewhere that direction.' The interference here eats precision like rust eats bolts.

choices.text: Speak to their humanity. Argue that if a soul is trapped in that echo, it's a mercy to silence it or set it free.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the wall and feel for vibrations with your own nerves.

line.dialogue: It's warm. And pulsing — slow, like a heartbeat. Whatever this is, it's not dead. Just sleeping.
Cold metal, nothing more. Either I've lost my touch, or this place refuses to be known that easily.

acts.title: The Song of Rust and Regret

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before the gutted hull of the *Whispering Maw*, the lost ship whose spectral hum led them here. The scrapyard's metallic clangor feels oppressive, a wall of noise against the vessel's faint, mournful song.
Well, we 'arrived.' Now what? We stare at a heap of junk until it confesses? The Listener's 'haunted ship' looks like every other wreck here.
No, listen! It's different. Can't you feel it? A pull. Like it's... sorry. Sorry it's just sitting here.
Or it's a resonance trap left by the Tonal Orders. We should be cautious. The acoustic profile is all wrong for a standard derelict.
Regret has a frequency. This ship is steeped in it. The Listener Monk said its final voyage was during The Silencing. It didn't just break down... it broke a promise.
You're still poking at that old bones? I told you, it's bad luck. The Maw doesn't give up its parts easy. Men get hurt trying.
The Lattice's song around it... it's a lament. A stalled chord. To understand The Silencing, we must resolve it. But the work... the work is dangerous.
Then we begin the work. We have to understand what happened here. Can you promise me, Monk, that your records hold the truth of its last journey?

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk produces a frayed log-slate. The party fans out, Arthit scanning for structural hazards, Malee inspecting the corroded resonator housing, Chanida drawn to the captain's chair where a ghostly hum is strongest.
The primary crystal array is shattered, but the fracture pattern... it's deliberate. Not an accident. Sabotage.
Great. So we're investigating a murder. A ship murder. I got my answer: someone wanted the Maw to fall silent forever.
The chair... it's cold. But the song here is so clear. 'I'm sorry I'm late.' Over and over. They were late. Late for what?

line.dialogue: The log-slate reveals the *Whispering Maw* was carrying refugees to a secret safe-point during The Silencing. The sabotage caused it to crash here, not on the Lattice. The ship's 'ghost' is the trapped resonance of its final, failed promise. To free it, you must...

choices.text: RELEASE THE SONG: Have Chanida, guided by the Monk, sing a release chord. It will dissipate the echo peacefully but destroy any residual data.
choices.consequence: The lament fades into a sigh. The ship is just a wreck now. You have closure, but the deeper truth is lost.
choices.description: Pichit uses tonal knowledge to chart resonance pathways near the scavenger gangs

line.dialogue: Pichit pushes through. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Defeat. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: DOWNLOAD THE ECHO: Use Arthit's tools to capture the resonant memory into a crystal. Risky, could attract unwanted attention from the Lattice or the Tonal Orders.
choices.consequence: You trap the ghost in a shard. The ship falls silent. You hold its last moments, a dangerous and illegal record.
choices.description: Chanida presses forward with frequency mapping to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Chanida pulls it off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Chanida is thwarted. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: REPLAY THE MOMENT: Sync the party's resonators to the echo, re-living the ship's final seconds. You will experience the sabotage firsthand, but your own minds could get stuck in the loop.
choices.consequence: You witness the betrayal—a Tonal Order navigator sacrificing the ship to seal a forbidden path. The truth is horrifying, and its echo is now part of you.
choices.description: The scavenger channels survival skills toward the salvage, hoping to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
the scavenger misreads the situation. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision is made. The air in the *Whispering Maw* crackles with latent energy. The scrapyard's ambient noise has dropped to a hushed, expectant hum, as if the entire graveyard of ships is holding its breath.
The Lattice is listening. What we do here... it will ripple. The Tonal Orders say some histories are too dangerous to sing. Is it necessary to use one? To wake this memory?
Our resonator readings are spiking. That 'secret safe-point' on the log... its coordinates are still valid. It's a pre-Silencing refuge. The Maw's cargo might have survived.
Oh, wonderful. So we're not just grave-robbers, we're delivering a century-late message. The car wouldn't budge an inch, but sure, let's move a mountain of regret.
It's not necessary that we do this for the past... but for what's still out there! If there's a refuge, people could use it now! The Maw's song won't move at all until we finish its journey!

Malee is right. This is a weight. But some silences are cages. The truth of The Silencing is locked in this wreck, and in the Orders that control what we're allowed to hear. Freeing one requires breaking the other.
You fools! That hum... it's changing! The whole yard is resonating! You're gonna pull every Tonal Order patrol from here to the floating cities down on us!

A deep, tectonic groan rolls through the scrapyard. Rust flakes from distant hulls. The *Whispering Maw* begins to glow from within, its ghostly song swelling into a deafening, single note of anguish and revelation.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax resonates. Depending on the choice, the Maw's hull either dissolves into harmonic dust, implodes with a data-shockwave, or becomes a transparent window into a frozen moment of betrayal. The resulting sonic burst is visible for miles.
Sensors are overwhelmed! That was... a beacon. We just lit a beacon in the dead zone.
The Lattice... it heard. And so did they. The song of the Maw is free. But now we are the echo.
Yeah. I see running lights on the horizon. The fun's over. The landlords are here to evict us.
We did the necessary thing. Right, Pichit? No matter what comes next?

line.dialogue: The act is complete. The ghost of the *Whispering Maw* has been resolved, unleashing a truth about The Silencing that challenges the Tonal Orders' authority. But the catastrophic acoustic event has drawn immediate, hostile attention. Your path forward is defined by this confrontation.

choices.text: FADE INTO THE WRECKAGE: Use the scrapyard's chaotic acoustics to hide. Let the Order investigate the empty epicenter. You live to fight another day, but the refuge coordinates may be discovered by them first.
choices.consequence: You escape unseen. The truth is loose, but you've ceded the initiative. The race for the refuge begins.
choices.description: Smash the resonator array against the chamber floor before it broadcasts their position

line.dialogue: Readings are flatlining — we're ghosts again, but that crystal is shattered beyond recovery.
The casing held — now it's screaming louder, and every Lattice node within a kilometer knows exactly where we stand.

choices.text: STAND AND DECLARE: Face the patrol with the evidence. Try to turn some of them, or at least sow doubt. A direct, risky appeal to conscience.
choices.consequence: A tense showdown. Some Ordersmen hesitate, creating a schism. You become a known rebel, with allies and enemies made in the same moment.
choices.description: Whisper the old suppression mantra while pressing palms against the vibrating walls

line.dialogue: The Lattice turns its gaze elsewhere — it cannot distinguish our warmth from the stone's own breathing.
I reached for the silence and found only my own fear echoing back — the walls are *listening*, and they recognize me.

choices.text: STEAL THEIR SHIP: Use the confusion to commandeer the lead Order resonator-ship. A bold strike to seize the means to reach the refuge immediately.
choices.consequence: You become fugitives and pirates in one stroke. You have a fast ship and a head start, but the full wrath of the Tonal Orders will follow you into the sky.
choices.description: Let Malee copy the resonator data to her portable drive and destroy the original terminal

line.dialogue: Got everything — frequencies, patterns, the whole signature map. We leave this room empty-handed to every eye that's watching.
The drive fried mid-transfer — corrupted sectors, and the terminal's deletion protocol just tripped a failsafe alert I've never seen before.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Sky-Scribe' hums, its crystal resonators parting the shimmering Lattice below into a valley of fractured light.
Look at the patterns… the Lattice doesn’t feel the same as before. There's a dissonance in its usual harmony.
Or you're just getting sentimental. It's a rock. A loud, glowy rock that eats cities.
Malee's cynicism aside, the tonal readings are irregular. We should proceed with caution.
Caution? We're chasing a signal! A *new* signal from the surface! This is discovery!
A smaller, patched-up skiff pulls alongside. A figure in worn lattice-leather, a Surface Scavenger, gestures sharply.
You Sky-Scribers lost? This ain't a charted drift. You don't belong here.
We're following a resonance. A call. Do you know its source?

lines_after.dialogue: A call? Hah. Down below, we don't stay in touch with sky-folk. Your kind brings trouble.
He doesn't have many friends. Can't imagine why.
Friends get you killed on the surface. That signal you hear? It's a Groundless beacon. Fools who think the old world can be lived in again.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger eyes you with deep suspicion, hand near a tool that could be a weapon or a resonator.

choices.line: Offer Trade: Show a spare crystal battery as a gesture of goodwill.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus staff meditation on the navigation crystals to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit overreaches. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.line: Invoke the Listeners: Speak of studying the Lattice's natural song, not controlling it.
choices.description: Have Chanida focus unauthorized tones on the deck wind to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida misreads the situation. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Defer to Chanida: Let her impulsive enthusiasm try to break the ice.
choices.description: Direct the scavenger to record the spectral signature using surface knowledge

line.dialogue: the scavenger pushes through. The scavenger spots a resource others overlook.
the scavenger's resolve isn't enough. Survival skills aren't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The Scavenger, somewhat placated, remains on their skiff as the two vessels drift side-by-side through a canyon of silent crystal.
Your 'beacon' is near the old Listeners' Spire. Crumbling thing. The Groundless nest there, chanting their heresies.
Heresies? Against the Tonal Orders?
Against sense. They say the Silencing was a baptism. That we must return to the ground, unshielded. They've got a leader… a Singer who says he hears a new gospel in the Lattice.
A Singer? Working with the Groundless? That's huge!
Or a huge problem. Religious fanatics with a human navigation system. Shall we go to the seaside? Oh wait, all the seas are crystal.
Their faith… it's a compass. But to what destination?
A Skycity transport gondola drifts into view, its pilot waving frantically. A Villager leans out, face pale.

lines_after.dialogue: Thank the Founders! You're from a Resonance Ship! May I see your driver's license? Your… charts? Are you authorized?
We are on a research expedition. What's wrong?

It's the Groundless! They're stirring up the Lattice near the Spire! My cousin… she joined them. She said she's found a true path. She said, 'I'm a Christian of the True Frequency' or some such madness!

line.dialogue: The Villager pleads for help, while the Scavenger scowls, muttering about sky-folk drama. The Spire looms in the distance.

choices.line: Assure the Villager: Promise to investigate the Spire and look for their cousin.
choices.description: Scale the Spire's broken scaffolding to reach the beacon before the Groundless patrol returns, 15 words

line.dialogue: * "My fingers bleed on every rusted rung, but I pull myself onto the ledge — the beacon pulses in my palm, warm and impossibly alive.
* "The scaffolding screams under my weight — I drop twelve feet onto rubble, and somewhere above, a Groundless whistle cuts the dark.

choices.line: Question the Scavenger: Press for specifics on the Groundless defenses and the Singer's abilities.
choices.description: Press the scavenger for the Singer's name and what they promised the Groundless in return

line.dialogue: * "The scavenger's eyes dart like cornered rats — then she whispers it: 'Veyra Oun.' A name I haven't heard since the Choir dissolved. The Groundless want her voice, not her silence — they want to *weaponize* what remains.
* "The scavenger spits at my feet and vanishes into the pipe network before I can finish asking. Whatever she knows, she's swallowed it back into the dark.

choices.line: Propose Mediation: Suggest approaching the Spire openly, under a flag of parley, to hear their 'gospel' directly.
choices.description: Hum the forbidden Tonal fragment near the Spire's resonance stones to flush out any hidden Listeners

line.dialogue: * "The note hangs in
The lattice has other plans. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_before.dialogue: The deck is quiet save for the low hum of the ship's crystal resonator. Below, the Lattice shimmers with unnatural, jagged fractures.
See those cracks? That ain't natural weathering. There's a high chance the Groundless are using crude resonators to pry up sections. Destructive.
So they're tearing the world apart to prove a point. How poetic. Do you need to use such brute force? Is it necessary?
Their manifesto said they seek the 'true foundation.' If they believe the Lattice is a prison, breaking it might seem like the only option.
Look at that exposed crystal vein down there... this cute and this inviting glow... how could they pass it up? It's pure, untapped resonance!
But at what cost? The Lattice isn't just ground. It's a system. A song. Pull one thread, and the whole harmony...
A sudden, discordant shriek echoes up from the fractures. The ship shudders. On the horizon, a makeshift raft of lashed-together debris rises, crawling with figures.
Speak of the devils. Groundless scavenger raft. They've seen us.

lines_after.dialogue: The raft holds its position, a silent challenge. The party's ship hovers, the resonator's tone a questioning hum.
Charming. They're going to wave. I'm betting on the latter.
We are heavily outnumbered. Direct confrontation is unwise. We must choose our response carefully.

line.dialogue: The Groundless raft sends a pulsed, jarring resonance signal—a demand. How do you respond?

choices.text: Answer with a Clear, Neutral Tone. Use the ship's resonator to send a simple 'query' signal, non-aggressive but firm.
choices.description: Direct Arthit to trace the anomalous signal using lattice storms

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Arthit's resolve isn't enough. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.text: Mimic Their Signal. Send the same discordant pulse back, a show of understanding their 'language' but also strength.
choices.description: Pichit attempts to test the prosthetic reaction, relying on tonal knowledge

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Pichit misreads the situation. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Broadcast the Old Listeners' Greeting. Use a rare, peaceful harmonic from Pichit's studies. A gamble on shared knowledge.
choices.description: The scavenger volunteers to decode the distress signal, leveraging surface knowledge

line.dialogue: the scavenger makes it work. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the scavenger fails. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: Pichit's chosen harmonic rings out. The discord from the raft ceases. For a tense moment, there is only the wind. Then, a single figure is propelled across the gap, landing deftly on the deck.
You know the Old Song. Where did you lose it? The skycities forgot. They buried the true music under Tonal charts and fees.
And you're here to collect? We're not exactly carrying spare harmony in our pockets.
We are dieting. I'm trying to lose weight—the weight of your cities on our world! You float, we bear the load. The Lattice groans!
So you break it? That's your solution? Where did you lose your sense?!
Wait. You hear its pain. So do I. But destruction... it's another Silencing. I still insist that there's another way. A resonance that heals, not severs.
Insist all you want! Your 'way' has had centuries! We are the consequence! My people on that raft... they will tear the anchor points. Your cities will fall.
The Groundless envoy points to the distant spires of a floating city, gleaming in the sun. The scavenger raft begins to move, its course clear.

lines_after.dialogue: They're heading for the main crystalline strut supporting Skyhaven's western district. A structural collapse there... catastrophic.
Their resonators are crude but powerful. They'll shatter the key harmonic node. It'll be like snapping a bone.
No. We have to stop them. Not with force, but with... a better song. One they might remember.
The envoy watches Pichit, a flicker of doubt in their hardened eyes. The fate of a city, and a movement, hangs on the next note.

line.dialogue: The Groundless raft is moments from its target. You have one chance to change the frequency. What do you broadcast?

choices.text: The Skyhaven Anthem. Broadcast the city's own foundational resonance—a reminder of what they seek to destroy, and who lives there.
choices.description: Sing the first verse of the Old Song from memory, hands pressed flat against the temple wall, 15 words

line.dialogue: The stones are vibrating—you remembered the tuning, and the village remembers with you.
That's three wrong notes and a cracked pillar. The Song isn't something you hum like a tavern joke.

choices.text: A Dissonant Counter-Harmony. Overwhelm their crude resonators with a complex, canceling wave. It risks damaging your own ship.
choices.description: Grab the villager's wrist and demand she show you exactly where she buried the last fragment, 15 words

line.dialogue: You're gripping the pulse point—yes, you feel it too, the fragment's still warm under the orchard clay.
You squeeze like a debt collector. The Song doesn't answer force. It answers need. And you don't need it enough.

choices.text: The First Note. Pour everything into projecting the pure, unshaped resonance Pichit hears at the Lattice's heart—the sound before cities, before orders. A plea to remember.
choices.description: Kneel in the road dust and ask the ground itself where the Song sank, ear pressed to soil, 15 words

line.dialogue: She's listening. Look—the village dogs are lying down too. The earth is telling her something true.
You look like a child pretending to hear the sea in a shell. The ground owes you nothing.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under the weight of decommissioned resonance ships. The air vibrates with the clash of metal and the hiss of plasma cutters, a harsh symphony that drowns out the Lattice's natural hum.
Ah, the salvage crew! Right on time. My contact said you were… efficient. Who would believe a team so young handles such delicate acquisitions?
Less talk, more specifics. What’s the job? And where’s the pay?
A specific resonator coil, from a Singer-class vessel that crashed here during the Silencing. The Tonal Orders have… misplaced the schematics. Finding it would be quite profitable.
A Singer-class? That’s a dangerous wreck. Its resonance signature could be unstable.
Everything here is unstable. That’s why they pay us.
Every broken ship holds a memory of the sky it once parted. From that day of the Silencing, these wrecks have been sleeping… waiting to tell their story.
A poetic view! Just bring me the coil. My associate, Niran, will guide you to the sector. He’s smiling happily at the prospect of a find.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant’s associate, Niran the villager, leads you through canyons of shattered crystal and twisted hull plating. He walks with a pronounced limp.
The wreck’s just ahead. Watch for loose plating. My old leg doesn’t handle the climb well.
What happened to it?
Scavenging accident. The Tonal Orders’ medics said a standard prosthetic was all the budget allowed. Who would believe that’s enough for a scrapyard worker?
The body should resonate with its environment, not fight against it. A standard part in a non-standard place…

line.dialogue: Niran mentions a local tinkerer rumored to make 'resonant prosthetics' from salvaged crystal. The merchant didn't mention this.

choices.text: Promise Niran you'll look into the prosthetic tinkerer after the job. (Build goodwill)
choices.description: Pull up the ship's manifest on your datapad, cross-reference Singer-class resonance frequencies. [15 words

line.dialogue: The coil's deep in the harmonic chamber — I can map a safe path through the wreck if we tune our shields to counter-resonance.
The manifest's corrupted — half the deck layout is missing. We'd be walking blind into a singing graveyard.

choices.text: Ask Niran for the tinkerer's location now, potentially delaying the coil retrieval. (Gather intel)
choices.description: Lean in close, demand the merchant reveal who's buying the coil and why. [15 words

line.dialogue: You want us crawling into a Singer wreck for a black-market buyer? Name them, or we walk and you find another crew desperate enough to die for your credits.
The merchant clams up, pocketing the data chip. 'If you don't want the job, there are others who do.' We're back to square one with no lead.

choices.text: Focus solely on the merchant's job. The prosthetic isn't your concern. (Stay on task)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to explain what makes Singer-class resonance so dangerous. [15 words

line.dialogue: the villager succeeds. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
The resonance turns hostile. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the derelict Singer-class hull, the chaotic noise of the scrapyard fades, replaced by an eerie, pressurized silence. Faint, frozen resonance patterns shimmer on the crystalline walls.
The acoustic damping is extreme. It’s like the ship is holding its breath.
Or it died screaming and this is the echo. Cheery thought, right?
There’s the main resonator housing! It’s my dream job to crack one of these open. The coil should be inside.
This silence… I had a bad dream once, of a world where the Lattice made no sound at all. This feels like that.
The old Listeners say ships like this remember their last flight. Maybe it’s dreaming.
The housing is locked by a harmonic seal. We need to match the decay frequency of these wall patterns.
Great. It’s very easy to guess a dead Singer’s last thought. Let’s just start poking it.
