lines_after.dialogue: As Arthit carefully calibrates a handheld resonator, a deep thrum passes through the deck. A section of wall crystallizes further, revealing not just the needed coil, but a smaller, intricately carved crystal component—part of a leg prosthetic.
Two for one! That’s the kind of crystal the tinkerer uses!
Convenient. Almost like the ship knew. Spooky.
It wasn’t a bad dream… it was a memory. This ship’s final silence, preserved. And it offered us a piece of itself.

line.dialogue: You have the merchant's coil. The newly revealed prosthetic component is valuable salvage, unrelated to your contract.

choices.text: Take only the coil. Leave the prosthetic part. (Honor the contract)
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His tattooed routes warm, revealing a path through chaos.
A costly mistake by Arthit. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Take both, but report only the coil to the merchant. (Secret salvage)
choices.description: Have Pichit focus monk wisdom on the engine parts to calibrate against the frequency

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Pichit is thwarted. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.text: Take both, and confront the merchant about withholding the prosthetic info. (Force a renegotiation)
choices.description: The merchant volunteers to commune with trapped echoes, leveraging negotiation

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. His trade connections deliver the right information.
The resonance turns hostile. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before a massive, gutted Resonance Ship hull, its crystal resonator core ripped out. The air thrums with the oppressive clang of industry.
The merchant's 'friendship' only goes as deep as his pockets. We should be careful. He forgot everything about where the prosthetic schematics came from? Convenient.
I don’t wanna go anywhere else until we find that crystal leg! That scrapyard boss knows something. Let's make him talk!
Typical. She was fired from the Tonal Order's archives for asking questions, and now her research is 'lost' in a scrap heap. How utterly predictable.
This place... it's a graveyard of forgotten songs. Each broken resonator holds a memory of a journey silenced. What song did this prosthetic carry?
A Skycity Resident, face smudged with grease, approaches, wringing his hands nervously.
You're the ones asking about the old Listener's work? The boss wasn't happy. Said it attracts the wrong kind of attention from the Tonal Orders.
Then let's attract it! Where's the prosthetic?

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The path through the scrapyard's maze of metal deepens, the cacophony growing more discordant.
Listen. The ambient resonance is shifting. Something here is... active.
Great. Just what we needed. A haunted scrap pile.

line.dialogue: The scrapyard boss, a burly woman with resonator-grafted arms, blocks the path to the secure salvage vault. 'You want the old gear? Prove you can handle the noise.'

choices.line: Pay the 'handling fee.' (Lose significant funds, but avoid a confrontation.)
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to chart resonance pathways, leveraging unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The gamble fails. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.line: Challenge her to a resonance tuning duel. (Use skill to match the chaotic frequencies of the yard.)
choices.description: Malee presses forward with leg resonance to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.line: Call her bluff. Accuse her of working with the Tonal Orders to suppress the tech. (Risk a fight, but potentially gain an ally.)
choices.description: The villager steps forward with irrigation, ready to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. A village secret surfaces at the right moment.
The risk doesn't pay off. A village secret surfaces at the worst time.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the vault, the Resonant Prosthetic hums on a workbench—a leg of polished crystal and silver filigree, pulsing with a soft, complex light.
The harmonic signature... it's not just a mobility aid. It's a key. I think it's tuned to a specific, hidden frequency in the Lattice.
So the Listener wasn't just fixing a walk. She was making a map. A map the Orders would kill to keep buried.
A single note, carried in a limb, to guide someone home. There’s no one else who could have sung this into being.
The vault door slams shut. The Trade Negotiator's voice comes through a grille, no longer friendly.
A regrettable necessity! The Tonal Orders pay far better for lost secrets than scavengers do. Are you going to hand it over, or not?
You sold us out! I'm happy to hear you admit it—makes punching you easier!
Alarm Klaxons wail, their harsh sound waves causing loose metal to shiver and shake. The vault itself becomes an instrument of chaos.

lines_after.dialogue: The scrapyard falls silent, save for the gentle hum of the prosthetic. The path forward is clear, but forever changed.
The song is free now. Not a tool for control, but a promise. A promise of a path not dictated by charts.
Don't get poetic. The Orders will have heard that little concert. We need to move.
I'm just glad we're all in one piece. Relatively speaking.
Yeah. And we've got a new leg to stand on. Let's see where it leads.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator's betrayal has triggered a harmonic lockdown. The vault's resonance is spiking, threatening to shatter the prosthetic and everyone inside. The prosthetic itself glows, offering a potential solution.

choices.line: Override the lockdown with brute force. (Use the party's ship resonator to blast the door, destroying the vault but saving yourselves.)
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to chart resonance pathways, leveraging monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Pichit loses control. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Harmonize with the prosthetic. (Pichit must attempt to 'sing' its stabilizing frequency, calming the vault but exposing his ability.)
choices.description: Chanida attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on crystal hearing

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The gamble fails. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Redirect the energy. (Use the vault's own destructive resonance against the Negotiator's forces outside, a risky all-or-nothing gamble.)
choices.description: Direct the merchant to record the spectral signature using information network

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the merchant. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
A costly mistake by the merchant. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whispering Sparrow' glides to a halt. Ahead, the Lattice lies still and dark, a vast, soundless desert. The air feels thick, muffled.
Readings are flat. No harmonic feedback. No ambient resonance. It's... dead. We've talked about this before, Pichit. Charts say to avoid this sector.
And yet, here we are. Because someone's paying. I've never understood the appeal of absolute quiet. It's just waiting to be filled with something unpleasant.
The Silencing left scars. Perhaps this is one. A place where memory itself has gone quiet.
Quiet means no patrols. Perfect for a discreet meeting. Look, the negotiator's skiff is already docked at that old Listeners' outpost.
A small, crumbling crystal structure is tethered to a larger floating island. A lone figure waves from a hatch.
Ah! You've arrived? Excellent time. The acoustics here are terrible for business, but wonderful for privacy. Do come in.

lines_after.dialogue: Inside the outpost, dust motes hang motionless in the dead air. The usual gentle hum of the world is absent, making every shuffle of a boot echo oddly.
My associates in the Tonal Orders would be... dismayed to know I'm here. But what they don't know can't be taxed. I have a proposition.
Of course you do. It always starts with a proposition before it ends with us running from crystal-shards or debt collectors.

line.dialogue: The Merchant explains a scavenger has found a 'silent-core' crystal in the Zone, a geological impossibility. He wants it retrieved before rival scavengers do. He offers a chart fragment as an advance.

choices.line: Accept the job. The pay is good, and a mystery is compelling.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the dead wall surface and push resonance through your fingertips manually.

line.dialogue: There's something buried deep—like hearing a heartbeat through concrete.
Nothing. Whatever killed this place took the walls too. Even my resonance just... stops.

choices.line: Demand more upfront. The Silent Zone is notoriously dangerous, and his chart is fragmentary.
choices.description: Signal Chanida to take point while you scan the perimeter for active surveillance optics.

line.dialogue: Three positions, all cold. Whoever's watching wants us comfortable before the trap.
I see movement—wait, no. Shadows playing tricks. This place gets in your head fast.

choices.line: Refuse politely. This feels wrong. The silence is a warning, not an opportunity.
choices.description: Ask Pichit directly what he knows about The Silencing and why he agreed to come here.

line.dialogue: I lost a student to a place like this. I came because the dead deserve witnesses.
That question costs more than you're paying me. Ask again and I walk back to the boat.

lines_before.dialogue: Venturing onto the Lattice surface of the Silent Zone is like walking on a frozen, black ocean. Your footsteps make no sound. The Merchant's coordinates lead to a canyon.
The chart ends here. How do we write the next part? Navigational logic doesn't apply. Our resonator crystals are just... glass down here.
Forget the charts! Look for signs of passage. Broken crystal, tool marks. How do you write 'I was here' on something that eats sound? You leave physical stuff.
Over there. A cairn. And not the respectful kind. The 'I-dropped-this-in-a-hurry' kind.
A pile of discarded gear lies near a fissure. Among it is a worn journal.
A scavenger's log. The entries get sparse, then... frantic. They mention a 'song from below' that isn't a song. A pressure.
Pressure? What province is 'Creeping Dread' in? Because that's what this is.
You shouldn't be reading that.

lines_after.dialogue: A figure emerges from the fissure, clad in patched lattice-leather. Their eyes are wide, darting between your party and the oppressive quiet around you.
That merchant sent you. Figures. He's selling a curse wrapped in a promise. That crystal you're after... it's not a gem. It's a seal.
A seal? For what? And don't say 'for your doom,' it's the latest fashion in ominous warnings down here.

For something that got too loud during the Silencing. The old Listeners... they didn't just study the Lattice. They pacified it. That 'silent-core' is a stopper in a drain. You pull it, and whatever's down there gets called back up.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points to the fissure, a deep, dark crack leading down. They claim the crystal is at the bottom, but so is the source of the 'pressure' described in the journal.

choices.line: Trust the Scavenger's warning. Retreat and confront the Merchant with this new information.
choices.description: Chanida uses crystal hearing to trace the anomalous signal near the crushing quiet

line.dialogue: Chanida makes it work. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Press the Scavenger for guidance. They know this place; they can lead you to the crystal for a better look, if not to take it.
choices.description: Pichit steps forward with staff meditation, ready to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Pichit pulls it off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
A costly mistake by Pichit. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: Proceed into the fissure alone. The mystery is too profound to abandon. The party must see for themselves.
choices.description: The scavenger attempts to commune with trapped echoes, relying on harvesting tools

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
Defeat. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The unnatural quiet of the Silent Zone presses in, a physical weight. The Lattice beneath your ship remains inert, a dead mirror.
Aren't you tired of this creeping dread? My resonator readings are flat. Nothing. It's like the world forgot how to echo.
We can't just float here! Arthit, can't you coax a hum from the crystals? Anything?
I've tried every frequency. The Lattice isn't sleeping here. It's... absent. Aren't you overthinking this, Chanida? Maybe some places are just dead.
But what kills a resonance? The Listeners' warning... they said the Lattice remembers every sound. What if this silence is a memory too? A memory of the Silencing itself?

(The scavenger's skiff pulls alongside, her voice unnervingly clear without ambient noise) You're still here. Foolish. Why aren't you careful? This zone doesn't just mute sound. It feeds on expectation.
Now, now. Let's not be dramatic. My acousti-compass is useless, true, but every void has a shape. We simply need to... recalibrate our commercial instincts.

lines_after.dialogue: As the merchant speaks, a low, sub-audible tremor passes through the ship's hull. Not a sound, but a feeling of profound wrongness.
Did you feel that? That wasn't resonance. That was... revocation.
The crystal conduits are ice-cold. Power is draining. We're not floating. We're being held.

line.dialogue: The scavenger points to a faint, jagged structure on the dead Lattice surface below. 'That's the source. The old Listeners called it the Throat of Silence. Your ship won't last another hour here.'

choices.text: Follow the scavenger's lead to the surface structure. (Trust her practical experience)
choices.description: Strike the Lattice's central node with your resonator's full harmonic burst

line.dialogue: The node sang back — a single, trembling note. I felt it in my teeth, in my bones. For one breath, the dread lifted." — Arthit
Nothing. The burst scattered into silence like stones dropped into fog. My resonator cracked, and the dread pressed closer." — Arthit

choices.text: Attempt a desperate Singer's maneuver, trying to 'remember' a resonance path out. (Rely on Pichit's latent ability)
choices.description: Whisper the Listeners' warning backward into the stillness, reversing its meaning

line.dialogue: The words curdled in my mouth, then the air *shifted*. Something heard us. Something that had been waiting to be called wrong." — Pichit
I choked on the syllables. They came out wrong — not reversed, just broken. The stillness swallowed them, and now it feels *angry*." — Pichit

choices.text: Bargain with the merchant, using the ship's remaining power as collateral to find a 'commercial solution'. (Engage his greed)
choices.description: Link hands with Malee and Chanida, let your three resonators bleed into one frequency

line.dialogue: Our frequencies tangled, fought, then *merged*. The Lattice shuddered. I swear I heard it breathe — or something inside it did." — Arthit
The frequencies clawed at each other. Mine shrieked, Chanida's went flat, Malee's just... stopped. Now we're three broken instruments in a silent room." — Arthit

lines_before.dialogue: At the heart of the Throat of Silence lies a cavern of flawless, sound-absorbing crystal. Here, the quiet is absolute. Your own breath seems stolen.
Fascinating! A perfect acoustic sink. The trade applications for this material... if we could just chip a sample...
Touch it and your heart will forget its rhythm. This isn't a place. It's a scar. The Lattice's dream of ending.
Look! In the crystal... shadows. Moving. I had a bad dream like this once. Trapped in glass.
It's a recording. A fossilized resonance. That's really easy to guess! It's replaying the moment of the Silencing. We're standing inside the memory of the catastrophe.
The Listeners' warning... they weren't trying to keep us out. They were trying to keep *it* in. This memory wants to finish.
A dream of ending... but every dreamer can wake. The Lattice listened to the world die. What if it's waiting to hear something else? To hear a choice?
The shadows in the crystal coalesce, forming a silent, screaming wave of obliteration—the Silencing itself, preserved. It begins to pulse outward from the cavern walls.

lines_after.dialogue: The wave of silent annihilation freezes, then shatters like glass. The dead cavern fills with a single, fragile, newly-made sound.
Well. I suppose that's one way to get a promotion. If we live.
(Nods, a new respect in her eyes) You didn't just navigate. You answered. The Zone... it's listening now.

line.dialogue: The memory-scar is broken, but the act has changed you and the Zone. The unnatural quiet is lifting, replaced by a low, questioning hum. The path is open, but the Lattice's attention is now firmly on you.

choices.text: Accept the Scavenger's offer to guide you out, forging a new alliance with the surface-dwellers. (Gain a reliable ally)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the crystal's surface and listen with your bones.

line.dialogue: chanida*: "The shadows — they're us. They're always us. I understand now.
scavenger*: "Pull your hand back! Your pulse is syncing to the dead rhythm — you're fading!

choices.text: Use the merchant's sudden awe to negotiate passage and information from the Tonal Orders themselves. (Gain political leverage)
choices.description: Ask Malee to calibrate her resonance scanner before anyone else touches it.

line.dialogue: malee*: "There — three embedded frequencies. This isn't a fossil, it's a *prison*.
merchant*: "While you fiddle with instruments, the real buyer is already en route. Tick tock.

choices.text: Stay. Study the waking scar. Pichit feels this is his dream job—to understand what the Lattice truly is. (Unlock profound lore, but attract greater danger)
choices.description: Smash the crystal with the butt of your rifle before the shadows finish forming.

line.dialogue: scavenger*: "Good. Whatever was inside that thing, it was dreaming about waking up.
chanida*: "The fragments are *singing* — you didn't kill it, you scattered it into all of us!

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery hangs in the sky, its stone spires carved to channel the wind into a low, constant hum. The air smells of ozone and old parchment.
Listen. Beneath the monastery's curated song... a dissonance. A fracture in the harmony.
It's just the wind, Pichit. Or my stomach. I'm starving. What kind of food do they prefer here, anyway?
The 'kind' that costs less than the air we're breathing. Look sharp. The Trade Negotiator is heading our way, and his smile is wider than a Resonance Ship's hull.
Greetings, travelers! The acoustics of Phrao are unparalleled, are they not? What brings you to our humble study? Seeking knowledge? Or perhaps... a more profitable venture?
We seek information. A... historical anomaly. A ship lost during The Silencing.
Ah, the past. A dangerous commodity. Why are you digging up old graves? Some tones are best left unsung.
Because its echo persists. It disrupts the Lattice's natural song. We must understand why.

lines_after.dialogue: Information has a price. But for you... perhaps a trade. The Listeners' archives are vast. Anywhere you like to start, but I'd prefer you look into a certain 'acoustic irregularity' in the western spires for me first.
Of course. A favor. What style of 'irregularity' do we prefer to find for you? A missing ledger? A stolen frequency crystal?
Merely data. The kind that doesn't fit the official charts. Bring me your findings, and I'll point you toward the archives on lost vessels.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator's task is clearly a diversion, but it's the only key he's offering. How do we proceed?

choices.line: Agree directly. Follow his lead to the western spires to gather his 'data'.
choices.description: Press your ear against the crystal wall and hum to match the dissonant frequency beneath the choir.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "There — you hear it? The crystal *answers*. Something is singing back from inside, and it knows our names.
Pichit — "The vibration shattered in my teeth before I could lock onto the tone. Whatever lives in the crystal, it doesn't want to be found that easily.

choices.line: Agree, but send Chanida to subtly eavesdrop on him while the rest investigate.
choices.description: Slip the merchant three baht and ask which corridor the monks forbid everyone from entering after dusk.

line.dialogue: Merchant — "Ah, you have good instincts, my friend. The eastern stairwell — they seal it with prayer-cords every sunset. Something *breathes* down there, they say.
Merchant — "Three baht? For information that could get me exiled from the only market between here and Chiang Rai? Come back with forty, or come back with silence.

choices.line: Refuse politely, insisting our search for the lost ship takes precedence.
choices.description: Follow the dissonance alone, leaving the others at the merchant's stall, and trace it toward the sealed eastern door.

line.dialogue: Malee — "You're mad, but I'm coming with you. Chanida, stay with the food — if we're not back before the evening bell, don't come looking.
Chanida — "Great. You wandered off, triggered a prayer-gong, and now every monk in Phrao is staring at us like we just desecrated their grandmother's

lines_before.dialogue: The western spire is a maze of narrow, sound-dampened corridors, far from the monastery's main harmonies. The silence here is oppressive.
This place... it doesn't resonate. It's like a dead zone in the Lattice's song. He used to get sick a lot when he was a child in places like this.
Focus, Arthit. Look—scorch marks. And these crystal shards are tuned to a piratical frequency band. Smuggler's nest.
The Negotiator's 'irregularity' is a pirate stash. How predictable. And look, our bandit friend left a ledger. May I have a toothpick? This lock is fiddly.
The entries... they're not just loot. They're recording specific lattice fractures. Times, locations. They're mapping something.
Hands off the merchandise, scholars! That's proprietary navigational data!
A Sky Pirate drops from a hidden alcove, cutlass gleaming. Two more block the narrow corridor behind you.
The Negotiator said you might come pokin'. Said you were askin' about old ghosts. Bad for business, that is. You, too, should learn to let dead ships lie.

lines_after.dialogue: Or what? You'll sing us a lullaby? This corridor's too narrow for all of you to swing those things.
Aye, but it's just wide enough for a resonance grenade to fill. Now, the ledger. And any charts you've got on you. We know you've been sniffin' around the *Echo*.
The Lost Ship. You know its name. You've seen its echo.

line.dialogue: Cornered in the narrow passage, the pirates hold a dangerous advantage. How do we respond?

choices.line: Comply. Hand over the ledger and back away slowly. Information isn't worth our lives.
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing scavenger instincts to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Malee finds the key. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Defeat. The prosthetic's feedback sends a shock up her spine.

choices.line: Bluff. Claim the ledger is rigged with a Listener's curse that activates if stolen.
choices.description: Chanida channels crystal hearing toward the meditation, hoping to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Defeat. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.line: Fight. Use the confined space to our advantage, targeting the grenade-holder first.
choices.description: The pirate uses smuggling routes to follow the phantom route near the monk chants

line.dialogue: the pirate's expertise pays off. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
the pirate overreaches. Smuggling routes are blocked by patrols.

lines_before.dialogue: Deep within the Phrao Monastery's most resonant chamber, the party stands before a massive, cracked crystal. The air hums with latent energy, and the ghostly outline of the lost ship, the *Whispering Dawn*, shimmers in the center.
Fascinating! The frequency stabilizing this echo is... proprietary. A trade secret of my late associate. Are you allergic to any medicine? Certain resonances can have... physiological effects.
That's not reassuring. This entire chamber feels unstable. We should proceed with extreme caution.
The 'late' associate you swindled, you mean. When did he get here? I mean, when did his ghost get tethered to this rock?
Forget the ghost, look at the crystal! It's recording the ship's final moments! It's like its memory is frozen here.
Not frozen. Trapped. This isn't just an echo. It's a soul that can't find its way home. The Lattice is its tomb and its prison.
Enough poetry. The pirate captain's log is in that shimmer. The frequencies he used to find the Silent Market... they're worth a fleet. My fleet.
A mournful chord vibrates through the stone. *...children... were they... safe?...* The ghostly hull wavers, revealing a flickering image of a sealed cabin door.

line.dialogue: The central crystal pulses. To commune with the echo, you must harmonize with its sorrowful frequency. Arthit warns the process could attract unwanted attention from the unstable Lattice.

choices.line: Use the Merchant's 'proprietary' stabilizer. It's safe, but he'll demand a cut of any find.
choices.description: Have Malee focus engineering on the meditation to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
Malee misreads the situation. Malee's engineering fails against lattice corruption.

choices.line: Chanida suggests blasting a clear channel with a focused resonator. Direct, but loud.
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing crystal hearing to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Chanida loses control. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.line: Pichit proposes a quiet, empathetic resonance, mirroring the ship's lost song. Risky, but pure.
choices.description: The merchant takes the lead, employing negotiation to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Exactly as the merchant hoped. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
Defeat. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_after.dialogue: The chosen frequency resonates. The ghostly ship solidifies, its deck materializing around you. You are no longer in the monastery, but standing on the ethereal planks of the *Whispering Dawn* in its final moments.
The air screams with shearing metal and a wrong, shattering note. Phantom crew run past you, transparent. The captain's voice booms from the helm, desperate: 'BRACE! THE SONG IS BREAKING!'
This is it. The moment of the Silencing, seen through one ship's death. This memory... it's not meant to be mined. It's meant to be heard.

acts.title: The Song You Choose to Remember

lines_before.dialogue: The memory-scape fractures. The Pirate and the Merchant, drawn by the unleashed energy, stand at the chamber's real-world entrance, their devices aimed at the heart-crystal. The ghost ship flickers between past and present.
The frequency! I have it! Now to carve it out of this rock. Sorry, ghost. I can't remember my password to the afterlife, so move along.
A crude extraction will destroy the data! Remember... the value is in the purity. Let my harmonics gently... persuade it.
They're going to rip the memory apart for scraps! We have to stop them!
Of course. The vultures arrive the moment we do the hard work. I can't remember if I'm more angry or bored by the predictability.
The crystal is at critical resonance. Any aggressive frequency could cause a cascading fracture in the local Lattice. This whole monastery could fall!
No. They're not just destroying a memory. They're trying to steal a death song. A life's final note. That song belongs to the Lattice, and to the Listeners. Not to them.
A final, desperate plea echoes. *...remember us... not the gold... remember the song we loved...* The ghostly captain looks directly at Pichit.

line.dialogue: The two opportunists begin their conflicting rituals. The chamber groans. The memory of the *Whispering Dawn* will be consumed, weaponized, or released. You must choose the song's fate.

choices.line: Shatter the crystal. Destroy the memory to save the monastery. A clean, tragic end.
choices.description: Ask Malee to chart resonance pathways, drawing on engineering

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Things don't go as planned. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Overload the frequencies, creating a dissonant storm to drive the interlopers out and scramble the data. Chaotic, but effective.
choices.description: Have Chanida focus unauthorized tones on the monk chants to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Chanida's voice resonates at a pitch that changes everything.
The risk doesn't pay off. The singer's gift turns against her.

choices.line: Guide the ghost ship's echo into a final, complete resonance—letting it sing its full death song and find peace. The ultimate risk and reward.
choices.description: The pirate channels disruptor weapon toward the crystal bowls, hoping to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Smuggling routes provide an escape.
the pirate misreads the situation. The disruptor backfires, jamming itself.

lines_after.dialogue: The chamber is still. The great crystal is clear and silent. The ghost is gone. The Pirate and Merchant are fled or unconscious. Only the echo of a choice remains in the air.
It's finished. The *Whispering Dawn* has finally docked. Not at a port, but in silence. Remember... some songs aren't for navigation. They're just for remembering.
The structural integrity is... stable. Somehow. The Lattice here feels... quieter. At peace.
So we get no treasure, almost get killed, and babysit a ghost to its eternal nap. I'm putting 'exorcism' on my expense report.
But we heard it. The real song. That's better than any chart. Right, Pichit?

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow is cool and heavy, smelling of damp earth and old stone. The walls of the cavern shimmer with embedded crystal veins that hum faintly in response to your footsteps.
Listen... the echoes here don't just repeat. They change. It's like the cave is having a conversation with itself.
Stop being so poetic and watch your step. This place gives me the creeps. Those crystal hums are making my teeth itch.
Probably just latent resonance from the Lattice below. Or we're all about to be crushed by a collapsing island. Fifty-fifty.
The structural integrity seems stable, but we should proceed with caution. The acoustics are... unnatural. They could mask other sounds.
Ahead, the tunnel opens into a vast chamber. Pre-Silencing ruins—smooth metal and fractured glass—are half-swallowed by crystalline growths. In the center, a Listener monk kneels, head bowed.
The song here... it is fractured. A memory of a scream.

lines_after.dialogue: Studying these ruins... it's my dream job. To understand what we were before The Silencing.
Well, poking around in creepy caves made me feel better about being stuck on a resonance ship all day.
Great. So we have a philosopher and an adrenaline junkie. I have to do a better job of vetting travel companions.

line.dialogue: The Listener monk remains still, but his shoulders are tense. How do you approach?

choices.text: Announce your presence politely. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Ask Chanida to trace the anomalous signal, drawing on crystal hearing

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Chanida overreaches. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Circle quietly to examine the ruins first. (Stealth)
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing Listener training to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.text: Call out a direct question about the 'fractured song.' (Direct)
choices.description: Direct the pirate to record the spectral signature using smuggling routes

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the pirate loses control. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk, Brother Lirin, reveals he tracks a 'ghost frequency'—an echo from a lost resonance ship, the *Sky's Lament*, which crashed here decades ago. Its crystal core still pulses, warping the local harmonics.
My Order wishes to record its death-throes, to understand finality. But I hear... a plea within the noise. It is not just data. It is suffering.
As he speaks, the hum in the chamber sharpens. From a side passage, a figure swaggering in leather and patched flight gear emerges, flanked by two rough-looking crewmates.
Well, well. Beatin' the Tonal Orders to the punch, are ya, monk? Or just doin' their dirty work for free?
Sky pirates! I knew this place was too interesting to be empty. What's this called, your 'secret hideout'?
Call it opportunity. That lost ship's core? Pure, uncut resonant crystal. Worth a fortune to anyone's okay who knows how to bleed it dry. Anyone.
Bleeding it could destabilize the frequency anchoring this entire cave system. The structural consequences would be catastrophic.
Let me guess. You want us to just walk away and let you have it?

lines_after.dialogue: Smart one. Look, I ain't greedy. You help me locate the exact chamber, I'll cut you in. A shard for your trouble. Keep it. You should keep it quiet, too.
That crystal isn't a commodity. It's a tombstone. Its song is the last record of the crew.
He speaks truth. To shatter it for profit is to erase their final whisper from the world.

line.dialogue: The pirate captain waits, hand resting on a resonator pistol. Brother Lirin looks to you, torn. The ghost frequency of the *Sky's Lament* wails softly in the stones.

choices.text: Side with the monk. Protect the echo. (Morality)
choices.description: Direct Pichit to map the frequency corridors using tonal knowledge

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit misreads the situation. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Negotiate a deal: study the echo first, then the pirates can have the remnants. (Compromise)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to calibrate against the frequency, drawing on lattice storms

line.dialogue: Arthit's expertise pays off. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Things don't go as planned. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Attempt to disarm the pirates and secure the area. (Confrontation)
choices.description: The monk attempts to listen for the ghost ship's echo, relying on crystal bowls

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. The monk's meditation reveals a pattern in the lattice's song.
Things don't go as planned. The monk's faith wavers, breaking concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends deeper into The Hollow, following the faint, ghostly hum. The air grows colder, and the crystalline walls begin to pulse with a soft, internal light.
Whoa. It's like the whole cave is breathing. Pichit, this is incredible!
Or digesting us. Keep your resonance dampeners charged.
The echo patterns are stabilizing. We're approaching the source.
The silence here... it's not empty. It's full. Waiting.
Ahead, a vast chamber opens. At its center lies the wreck of a Resonance Ship, half-fused with the cave floor. A shimmering, distorted echo of its final moments plays in a silent loop.
The Echo of the Lost Ship... it's real. The Tonal Orders said it was a myth to scare us from the depths.
Looks like a payday to me! That hull's still got pure crystal resonators!

lines_after.dialogue: Aren't you tired of just taking? This isn't salvage. It's a tomb.
Why weren't you careful? Sentiment gets you killed out here.
Aren't you overthinking this? My order has waited generations for this proof. The Lattice remembers everything.

line.dialogue: The ghostly echo intensifies, forming a coherent image of the ship's final crew, their mouths open in a silent scream. The Monk steps forward, a recording crystal in hand. The Bandit raises his cutter.

choices.text: Let the Monk record the echo. Preserve the truth.
choices.description: Press your palm against the breathing wall and let your resonance sync with its rhythm.

line.dialogue: The vibration just answered me — it's showing me a path through the western fissure.
It pulled my frequency in too deep — my hand went numb and the wall *groaned*.

choices.text: Try to communicate with the echo. Use your own resonance.
choices.description: Fire a resonance pulse ahead to map the chamber before committing deeper.

line.dialogue: Clean return signal. Chamber opens up thirty meters ahead — one exit, no ambush points.
The pulse didn't come back. Either the stone absorbed it or something down there *ate* it.

choices.text: Stop the Bandit from looting. Defend the wreck.
choices.description: Order silence — no dampeners, no pulses. Walk forward listening to what the cave is waiting to say.

line.dialogue: Do you hear that? Beneath the breathing — there's a voice. It's been calling us by name.
The silence broke. Something ahead started *screaming* in frequencies I don't think human ears were meant to process.

lines_before.dialogue: The chamber resonates with conflicting frequencies. The ancient echo, the Monk's recording, the Bandit's cutter, and the party's own crystals clash, causing the fused ship to vibrate violently.
The structural integrity is failing! This whole chamber is going to shatter!
The Lattice below us is reacting! It's forming a resonance spike!
I have no one to help me figure this out! What do we do?!
The echo... it's not a memory. It's a message. A final warning from before The Silencing.
Forget the message! Grab what you can and run!
Can I... can I truly bear this truth? What if it damns everything we believe?
The ghostly crew points in unison toward a cracked resonator on the ship's stern—the source of the looping echo. A single, pure note begins to swell from it.

lines_after.dialogue: I study the song by myself. This is the key. The note that was playing when the world broke.
If we amplify that note, we might re-shatter the Lattice here. Or... silence the echo forever.
The choice is ours. Record it, release it, or shatter it.

line.dialogue: The Hollow groans. Cracks race up the walls. The Monk holds his crystal ready. The Bandit aims his cutter at the fragile resonator. The ghostly crew watches, waiting.

choices.text: Shatter the resonator. Bury the past and stabilize the cave.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use singer voice and chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Chanida is thwarted. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.text: Amplify the note. Let the truth resonate, no matter the cost.
choices.description: Have Pichit focus monk wisdom on the cave echoes to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Exactly as Pichit hoped. The ex-Listener's instincts prove sharper than any instrument.
Pichit misreads the situation. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Record the frequency perfectly. Carry the burden of knowledge.
choices.description: Have the pirate focus secret frequencies on the ancient ruins to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the pirate pulls it off. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
The risk doesn't pay off. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard is a symphony of industrial decay. The air vibrates with the shriek of metal cutters and the percussive thud of hammers dismantling old Resonance Ships. The Lattice below glints dully through a haze of smoke and ozone.
Do you know what this is? This noise... it's not just sound. It's a wall. A deliberate cacophony to keep thoughts—and questions—from forming.
I know. I already know that, Pichit. But we're here for a reason, not a philosophy lesson. The contact said to meet by the old Serpent-class hull.
A 'contact'. Probably some scrap-dealer who'll sell us rust and a smile. I now know better than to trust anyone in a place that smells of grease and desperation.
Let's just find them quickly. The acoustics here are terrible for spotting an ambush. Every clang covers a footstep.
Ah! The seekers of rare frequencies! Welcome, welcome. I am Vichai. You have the look of those who... appreciate value.
We were told you might have information. About a vessel. One that went silent during the last monsoonal resonance shift.
Information is my most precious commodity. But for you... perhaps a trade. A little job. There's a specific resonator coil in the deep yard. Fetch it, and my memory might just improve.

lines_after.dialogue: A job? Now? We need that ship's last known frequency, not a shopping list!
I know. He's stalling. Or testing how badly we want it. The price just went up.
The deep yard is where they break down the unstable cores. It's not safe.

line.dialogue: Vichai the merchant smiles, waiting. The coil he wants is deep in the hazardous scrapyard.

choices.line: Agree to fetch the coil. (Straightforward trade, but into danger.)
choices.description: Climb the rusted crane boom to scan the yard for the contact's signal fire, 15 words exactly

line.dialogue: Pichit — "There — behind the crushed hull stack. A green flare. That's our dealer, and they're already nervous.
Pichit — "The boom groaned and I slipped. Got a mouthful of rust for my trouble. We search on foot.

choices.line: Press him for a clue first. (Risk offending him, but might get a hint.)
choices.description: Follow the discordant hum to its source, pressing hands against vibrating hull plates

line.dialogue: Chanida — "The resonance peaks behind this shipping container. Something mechanical is running in there — and someone is operating it.
Chanida — "The vibration dead-ends at a collapsed tunnel. Whatever generates that sound is buried under three tons of wreckage.

choices.line: Offer alternative payment. (Try to barter with something else you have.)
choices.description: Signal the contact with the agreed knock pattern on the nearest corrugated wall

line.dialogue: Malee — "Three knocks returned from the east. Our contact heard us. Let's move before anyone else does.
Malee — "Nothing. Either they've moved positions, or the yard's acoustics swallowed our signal whole. We're flying blind now.

lines_before.dialogue: The party moves deeper into the canyon of shattered hulls. The air grows thick with the smell of burnt crystal and ozone. Strange, harmonic whines echo from unstable Lattice fragments underfoot.
I have something to tell you. My scanner is picking up a residual frequency signature. It's faint, buried under all this industrial noise... but it doesn't match any Tonal Order chart.
A ghost signal. Perfect. Because navigating a death-trap of live wreckage wasn't thrilling enough.
This is the best way. If that's our lost ship's echo, it leads right to the coil—and answers. Follow the weird noise!
Listen... beneath the whine. A pattern. A slow, repeating descent. Like a vessel... falling.
A shadow falls across the path. A Sky Pirate, clad in patched leather and scavenged resonator plates, drops from a gantry, flanked by two others.
Well, well. Diggin' in our yard, are ya? That ghost-song you're chasin'... that's ours. Found it first.
Your yard? Last I checked, Tha Khwae scraps belong to whoever's strong enough to haul it!

lines_after.dialogue: Brave words. The signal's from the *Whispering Maw*, a Singer's ship that cracked open here. Its core's still singin' a death-rattle. We're harvestin' it.
Now I know... why the merchant sent us here. He wanted the pirates to deal with us. Or us with them.
They're armed with tuned disruptors. Direct conflict is inadvisable.

line.dialogue: The Sky Pirates block the path to the source of the eerie frequency. The coil—and the truth about the lost ship—lie just beyond them.

choices.line: Fight. (They're thieves, and the signal is too important.)
choices.description: Match your breathing to the pattern. Let it pull your pulse into sync.

line.dialogue: There — you feel it now too. That's not noise. That's someone breathing on the other end, waiting for us to answer.
Great, you're meditating. While we drift through a gravity shear. I'll just die enlightened.

choices.line: Bluff. (Claim you're with the Tonal Orders on official business.)
choices.description: Kill the engines. Cut all power. Let the silence strip the signal bare.

line.dialogue: The interference just collapsed. That's a hull ping — standard military distress. Whoever's out there is running on battery and prayers.
We're dark and drifting now. Brilliant. If something's hunting in this fracture, we just made ourselves the quietest prey in the sector.

choices.line: Propose a deal. (Offer to help 'stabilize' the core for a split of the salvage.)
choices.description: Open a raw channel and speak the pattern back, tone for tone.

line.dialogue: They shifted. The pattern changed — it's responding to us. That's not an echo, that's a handshake. We found them.
You just broadcast our position on every frequency into a fracture known for eating ships. The pattern stopped. Tell me that's a good sign.

lines_before.dialogue: Back in the shadow of the scrapyard's skeletal ships, the air vibrates with the oppressive hum of machinery and the dissonant echoes of a thousand broken crystals.
So the merchant's 'helpful tip' about the salvage rights was just him trying to get us to clear out his competition. Typical. I don't understand anything about how these people think.
Forget him! The pirate's frequency map shows the 'haunted' ship is broadcasting a distress loop on a dead channel. It's here. Buried under the newest scrap pile.
A distress signal from a ship lost during The Silencing... that's not a ghost story, that's a historical artifact. And a massive Tonal Order violation.
A voice, trapped in the Lattice for generations... You still don't understand? This isn't just salvage. It's an echo of the world we lost.
As you approach the designated scrap mountain, a low, throbbing hum cuts through the industrial noise. The metal around you begins to vibrate faintly.
Great. So the haunted ship is also an unstable resonator. I don't know when this heap is going to decide to harmonically shred itself—and us.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The party moves as one toward the unstable, humming core of the scrap pile.
Readings are spiking. That echo isn't just repeating... it's reacting.
It knows we're here.

line.dialogue: How do you approach the source of the echo?

choices.line: [SALVAGE PROTOCOL] Methodically clear debris to reach the ship's resonator chamber. It's slow, but safe.
choices.outcome: You expose the ancient crystal drive. The echo clarifies into a navigational log, revealing coordinates, but the process alerts the scrapyard overseers.
choices.description: Route the distress signal through Chanida's frequency map to triangulate its origin point within the Lattice, 15 words

line.dialogue: Got it — the signal's bleeding through a collapsed node near Sector Seven's gravity well.
Nothing but static and ghost echoes — whatever's in there doesn't *want* to be found yet.

choices.line: [RESONANT SYNCH] Have Pichit attempt to 'sing' to the echo, calming its erratic frequency to safely reveal the ship.
choices.outcome: Pichit's voice weaves with the distress signal. The hum stabilizes, and a ghostly image of the ship's final moments projects into the air, showing its fatal course.
choices.description: Speak directly into the Lattice using Arthit's recovered comm-relay, answering the trapped voice with your name, 15 words

line.dialogue: It heard you — God, it *remembered* your name from before The Silencing even happened.
The voice went silent. Whatever you said, it decided you weren't the one it was waiting for.

choices.line: [FORCE A CONNECTION] Overload a portable resonator to blast the scrap aside, reaching the core immediately.
choices.outcome: The violent resonance parts the metal sea, revealing the ship's bridge. The echo, agitated, floods your minds with a cacophony of panic and shattering crystal.
choices.description: Ignore the signal entirely and follow Pichit's instinct toward the unstable

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the merchant. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
The lattice has other plans. The ledger's numbers lied.

lines_before.dialogue: At the heart of the scrap, you find the bridge of the 'Echo of Dawn.' Its main crystal is fractured, pulsing with captured light and sound. The air smells of ozone and old metal.
It's... a memory. A perfect, terrible memory of The Silencing, held in the fracture. I've never understood how a sound could break the world... now I'm hearing it.
And our pirate friends just dropped in on skiffs. They want the crystal. They think it's a weapon.
Hand over the shiny! That frequency can part any Lattice! Our ship'll be unstoppable!
You idiot! It's not a tool, it's a recording of the apocalypse! Unleash that and you'll shatter the whole scrapyard!
The resonance cascade... it's building. In only five minutes, this entire pile could become a fragmentation bomb.
Now, now! There's no need for violence! I'm sure we can come to a profitable arrangement for this... artifact.
No. This isn't for profit or power. This is a grave. And that echo deserves peace, not to be turned into a weapon.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal's pulse quickens, a visible wave of distortion rippling out from the fracture. The final note of a lost world is about to be played.
It's now or never. Whatever you're going to do, do it!
Forget this! I'm no match for that! Get the skiffs airborne!

line.dialogue: How do you resolve the 'Echo of the Lost Ship'?

choices.line: [SILENCE THE ECHO] Use resonance dampeners to safely collapse the crystal's frequency. The memory is lost, but the threat ends.
choices.outcome: With a final, soft chime, the crystal goes dark. The scrapyard falls silent, save for the retreating pirate engines. The past is buried, safely and forever.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using monk wisdom to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
Pichit overreaches. His staff overheats, forcing him to drop it.

choices.line: [RELEASE THE MEMORY] Guide the echo to play out fully and dissipate naturally, letting the ship's final moments be witnessed.
choices.outcome: The air fills with a beautiful, devastating chord—the world's last song. As it fades, the crystal turns to clear, silent glass. You bear witness, and the ship is finally at rest.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with crystal prosthetic, ready to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. The scavenger's leg becomes a lens.
The resonance turns hostile. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.line: [CAPTURE THE FRAGMENT] Attempt to salvage a shard containing the echo's 'root frequency,' a secret from before The Silencing.
choices.outcome: Amidst the dissipating energy, you secure a sliver of pure, ancient resonance. It holds immense potential and danger—a key to forgotten truths that the Tonal Orders would kill to possess.
choices.description: The merchant channels negotiation toward the broken ships, hoping to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: the merchant succeeds. The merchant's ledger reveals the real story.
Things don't go as planned. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Aria's Grace' hums across a sea of shimmering Lattice. The crystal layer below fractures and reforms like a slow, silent ocean. On deck, Pichit leans against the rail, watching the patterns.
Look at the fractals... It's like the Lattice is trying to speak, but we only hear the noise of our own engines.
Or it's just a big, glowy rock. Don't get poetic, Pichit. We're hauling cargo, not answers.
But what if we *are*? That scavenger in the last skyport was muttering about a ghost ship—a vessel that vanished during The Silencing. Its echo still drifts out here!
A dangerous legend. The Tonal Orders have forbidden charting that sector. The resonance patterns there are... unstable.
Excuse me... travelers? I couldn't help but overhear. You speak of the Lost Ship? My grandfather was on a trade run when it disappeared. They say on quiet nights, you can still hear its final chord.
A final chord... A sound frozen in the catastrophe. What if that sound holds an answer about The Silencing itself?
Or it's just cosmic background noise and dead people. But fine. The pay for salvage *would* be nice.

lines_after.dialogue: So we're chasing a ghost? I'm in! Let's find that echo!
We must be methodical. The Lattice in that area is treacherous. One wrong frequency and we could be shattered.
Arthit is right. We need to approach this carefully. But I feel it... I got the answer now. Not in a book, but out here, in the silence between the tones.

line.dialogue: The 'Aria's Grace' approaches the forbidden sector. An anomalous, low drone vibrates through the ship's crystal resonator. How do we proceed?

choices.text: EASY: Adjust the resonator to match the drone, harmonizing with it.
choices.leads_to: Harmonization stabilizes the approach, but the sound becomes mournfully clear.
choices.description: Touch the Lattice surface with bare fingertips and listen for harmonic resonance.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "I can feel it singing in my bones — the fractals are showing me paths through the crystal wind, thousands of them, all leading somewhere alive.
Malee — "Great, now your fingers are numb and glowing faintly purple. Next time maybe don't stick your hand into the mysterious ancient artifact, genius.

choices.text: MEDIUM: Send a probing sonic pulse to map the area ahead.
choices.leads_to: The pulse returns garbled, but reveals a large, stationary object.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to recount exactly what the scavenger said before disappearing into the skypor.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "She grabbed my wrist and whispered, *'The Lattice remembers what we were before the Orders silenced our frequencies'* — then she walked into open air and didn't fall.
Arthit — "Enough. The Orders forbade chanting for a reason — every time someone chases that legend, they come back wrong, or they don't come back at all. We move on. Now.

choices.text: EASY: Cut the main resonator and drift on momentum, listening closely.
choices.leads_to: Silence amplifies the ambient drone, revealing it's a distorted melody.
choices.description: Hum a counter-frequency to disrupt whatever the Lattice is broadcasting into your thoughts.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "I didn't think that would work — the fractal patterns just... they rearranged. They formed a shape. A doorway. What have we opened?
Pichit — "Stop — stop humming, you're making it angry! The crystals are cracking inward

lines_before.dialogue: Guided by the eerie drone, the 'Aria's Grace' drifts into a fog of crystalline dust. The silhouette of a massive, derelict Resonance Ship materializes ahead, its hull fused with Lattice growths.
By the Founders... it's real. The Lost Ship. Look at the size of it!
Its resonator array is still active at a minimal level. That's the source of the drone. A century-old frequency, holding the ship in a stasis field.
Great. A flying tomb with its own soundtrack. Let's dock and see if the cafeteria is still serving. It might be true that they preserved the lunch special.
As the party prepares a boarding line, a smaller, patched-together skiff emerges from behind the derelict's stern. A figure in scavenged gear watches them from its deck.
Turn your song away from here. This wreck ain't for the sky-folk. Its whispers are for those of us who walk the surface.
We mean no offense. We seek understanding, not plunder. What do the whispers say?
Understanding? Hah. It tells of the pride before the fall. The Orders thought they mastered the Lattice's song. This ship... it's their lesson.

lines_after.dialogue: The scavenger's skiff hums, its tone masking their next words to their crewmate. But Pichit's sharp ears catch a fragment.
(Whispering to the party) I overheard them. They said, '...the core log is intact. It comes with the captain's final entry. That's the real prize.'
A core log? That could contain navigational data from the time of The Silencing. The Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for it... or kill for it.
Then we can't let them have it! That's our answer!

line.dialogue: The Surface Scavenger is clearly after the ship's core log. They are wary but not immediately hostile. How do we handle the impending confrontation?

choices.text: EASY: Parley openly. Offer to share any non-Order knowledge we find from the log.
choices.leads_to: A tense trade of information, but cooperation is fragile.
choices.description: Hack the resonator array to trace its signal origin, 15 words

line.dialogue: The signal's pointing deeper into the hull — something down there is still *listening*.
The array bit back hard. Whatever's running this ship doesn't want company.

choices.text: MEDIUM: Create a distraction with a resonator feedback whine, then board the Lost Ship quickly.
choices.leads_to: A rushed boarding under cover of sonic dissonance.
choices.description: Draw your sidearm and order the scavenger to explain themselves, 15 words

line.dialogue: Look, friend — you clearly know what this thing is, so start talking before I lose patience.
He bolted into the dark before I could finish my sentence. Great. Now we have *two* problems.

choices.text: HARD: Challenge their claim. Assert that the echo called to *us*, the Singers, not surface dwellers.
choices.leads_to: A direct confrontation of ideology and right of discovery.
choices.description: Ask Chanida what she knows about the Lost Ship's history, 15 words

line.dialogue: The Founders buried this name for a reason. That ship sang its crew to death — and it never stopped.
I... I can't remember. The teachings are there, but every time I reach for them, something *pushes back*.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship glides over a vast, silent expanse of the Lattice. The usual ambient hum has died to a whisper.
It's nice and peaceful. Which, in my experience, means something terrible is about to happen.
Readings are stable, but... the background resonance is wrong. It's too clean, like an erased slate.
Look! Off the starboard bow! Is that... smoke? No, it's too still.
A permanent scar on the Lattice's song. The echo of a violent silence.
A ghostly outline of a colossal wreck resolves in the mist ahead. Its shattered crystal spars jut from the Lattice like a tombstone.
The *Amaranth*. Went down a generation ago. Tonal Orders sealed the charts around it. Said it was 'unstable.'
Unstable how? What aren't they telling us?

lines_after.dialogue: The scavenger points a grimy finger at the wreck's heart. A faint, sickly green pulse throbs within its fractured core.
That's the problem. Core's still active, singing a dead ship's last note. It's nice and peaceful out here until you get too close. Then it *remembers*.
A resonance loop... I know. It could pull our ship into its harmonic collapse.
But within that loop... the truth of what happened. The answer the Orders buried.

line.dialogue: We need to get closer to the *Amaranth's* core to understand its echo. How do we approach the unstable wreck?

choices.line: Use the ship's external resonators to carefully dampen the ghost frequency from a distance.
choices.description: Arthit channels lattice storms toward the deck wind, hoping to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Against the odds, Arthit pulls it off. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Send a small team across on tethered crystal sleds to plant dampening charges on the wreck.
choices.description: Malee steps forward with engineering, ready to use the leg as a lattice probe

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Malee. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The resonance turns hostile. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.line: Tune our ship's core to match the *Amaranth's* dying frequency and sail directly into the resonance loop.
choices.description: The scavenger presses forward with surface knowledge to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: the scavenger finds the key. Hard-won survival skills turn the tide.
The attempt backfires on the scavenger. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The decision is made. The ship groans as alien harmonics shudder through the hull. The world outside the viewports warps and bleeds color.
Breach in the harmonic buffer! That's no problem, I can recalibrate— My stomach is starting to growl! Focus, Arthit, focus!
Of course. The stress makes you hungry. The imminent death makes me nauseous. We balance out.
Phantom images flicker on the deck: screaming crew, shattering crystal, a final, desperate broadcast.
There's something in my eye! This damned resonant dust... or are those... tears?
It's the memory. The *Amaranth* wasn't lost to instability. It was scuttled. To silence a Singer who discovered a flaw in the Tonal Orders' charts.
Brought the whole ship down to keep one secret? Monsters.
The green pulse intensifies, becoming a deafening, shrieking note. The ghostly crew turns as one, their hollow eyes fixed on your ship.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax of the dead song hits. Crystal screams. Reality buckles. Your ship is at the epicenter.
The echo is trying to complete itself! It'll use our resonance to re-enact the final destruction!
So we're the understudy for a tragedy. Wonderful.
Pichit! The Singer's final frequency—it's still in the loop! Can you... can you *change* the song?

line.dialogue: The *Amaranth's* catastrophic echo is about to consume your ship. How do you rewrite the finale?

choices.line: Overload the ship's resonators to shatter the echo's cohesion, breaking the loop but destroying the evidence.
choices.description: Override the harmonic buffer manually, routing the resonance through the secondary dampeners.

line.dialogue: Got it — she's holding. But don't anyone breathe too loud near the port bulkhead." — Arthit
The buffer's reversed polarity — everything's feeding back into the core!" — Arthit

choices.line: Have Chanida jury-rig a broadcast, using the ghost frequency to transmit the truth to every nearby skycity, risking the Orders' wrath.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to explain what he means about the *Amaranth* and its memory before doing anything else.

line.dialogue: Someone scrubbed the navigation logs. Someone who didn't want us following where she went." — Pichit
I can't — the words keep dissolving. It's like the memory itself refuses to be remembered." — Pichit

choices.line: Pichit must step into the psychic imprint of the lost Singer and sing a new resolution into the heart of the scar, healing the Lattice but risking his mind.
choices.description: Have Chanida flush the resonant dust from her eyes using the emergency coolant line.

line.dialogue: That's better. I can see the pattern now — it's not dust, it's *coordinates*." — Chanida
The coolant's contaminated with the same particulate — my vision's worse than before." — Chanida

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cavernous library of humming crystal spires and silent, floating scrolls. The air itself feels tuned, absorbing all but the most purposeful sound.
I had a bad dream last night... of the Lattice cracking like glass. It felt too real.
Dreams are just noise, Pichit. We need facts. The route to the Verdant Atoll is supposed to be in this section.
If the Tonal Orders haven't 'misplaced' it for profit. Look at this place. Knowledge hoarded like treasure.
We should be careful. The Archivists monitor everything. Our... extracurricular research could draw attention.
Excuse me? You're the crew of the *Resonant Whisper*, right? I... I need to ask you something.

lines_after.dialogue: It's about the Groundless. My cousin... she says they're not fanatics. They say the Tonal Orders' charts are a cage. That we could learn to listen for ourselves.
And risk shattering your ship on a false note? The Orders may be greedy, but their maps work. Mostly.
But what if she's right? What if we rely too much on their interpretation? I've charted minor corrections myself. I did it all myself, just by listening.

line.dialogue: The villager looks at you, hope and fear warring in his eyes. Do you engage with his dangerous query?

choices.text: Dismiss him politely. The Archives are no place for such talk.
choices.description: Sneak past the Archivist stations to reach the Restricted Stacks, 15 words

line.dialogue: Arthit* — "I've mapped their patrol patterns. Move when the lamplight shifts west. I'll hold our position until you signal.
Arthit* — "A scanning orb just locked onto us. Walk naturally — *don't run* — or we'll never get another chance.

choices.text: Listen carefully, but make no promises. Gather information discreetly.
choices.description: Bribe a junior Tonal Order clerk with forged transit stamps for the route manifest, 15 words

line.dialogue: Malee* — "Ha! His eyes went straight to the stamps, not the seal. Greed makes the worst gatekeepers. Here's our manifest.
Malee* — "He turned the stamp over. Asked which chapter issued it. We have maybe ten minutes before he reports us — *go*.

choices.text: Agree to meet him later, away from the Archives' ears.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to describe every detail of the Lattice-cracking dream to find hidden clues, 15 words

line.dialogue: Pichit* — "The crack started at the seventh node... the same node the route passes through. I didn't want to believe it either.
Pichit* — "I... I can't. Every time I reach for the memory, it slides away like oil on water. Something doesn't want me to remember.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the villager's cryptic directions, you find a secluded acoustic alcove, its walls designed to dampen sound. A Trade Negotiator is already there, studying a crystal ledger.
Ah! The intrepid explorers. Your reputation precedes you. I hear you're looking for... alternative routes. Routes that don't incur the usual licensing fees.
We're looking for the truth. The Verdant Atoll route in the main index is a dead-end. We think it's been altered.
We should stay focused. This feels like a trap. We don't stay in touch with smugglers.
Such suspicion! I'm a simple facilitator. The Groundless... they have pieces of the old world. Songs, not just charts. But their methods are... disruptive to commerce.
Disruptive to your monopoly, you mean.
The villager said they believe we can learn to listen. I don't agree with the Orders keeping that knowledge locked away.

lines_after.dialogue: A noble, if naive, sentiment. The original, unaltered resonance pattern for the Atoll? It might exist in a restricted sub-archive. A place even most Archivists avoid. The acoustics there are... unstable.
Unstable how? Don't get so stressed out, just tell us.
Let's just say the Lattice whispers back in there. It's where they store the knowledge from before The Silencing. Knowledge that... unsettles the current harmony.

line.dialogue: The Negotiator offers a key crystal to the restricted wing, for a future favor. The risk is high, but the potential knowledge is greater.

choices.text: Refuse the deal. The danger to the crew is too great.
choices.description: Press the merchant for details about the Groundless — what they trade, who they serve.

line.dialogue: The Groundless — you mentioned them like they're common knowledge. So tell us plainly, who are they really?
You're dodging. Every word from your mouth bends around the truth like water around a stone.

choices.text: Accept the key, but vow the favor will be on your terms.
choices.description: Have Arthit quietly circle behind the merchant while Chanida keeps him talking.

line.dialogue: Keep his eyes on you. I'll check what he's hiding in those crates behind the stall.
He spotted me. The merchant's hand drifted to something under the counter — we're out of time.

choices.text: Take the key and immediately press for more information about the Groundless.
choices.description: Accept the Verdant Atoll route but demand the merchant come along as guide and insurance.

line.dialogue: You'll guide us yourself. If the route is honest, you have nothing to lose — and everything to gain from our success.
His face went pale. Whatever waits on that route, he wants no part of it — and neither should we.

lines_before.dialogue: The main chamber of the Tonal Archives falls into a profound silence. The air grows heavy with the scent of old vellum and ozone. Pichit's fingers trace the forbidden sigils in the ancient codex.
They've hidden entire continents down there. Safe routes my foot—these are cages. We have to tell people.
And be branded heretics? The Orders control the food, the water, the very air between islands. Your idealism is a death sentence.
She's right. This isn't just data. It's a weapon. If we're wrong about the intent behind these redactions...
The silence in these records... it's deliberate. A shaped void. Could you say that again, please, Malee? About the food supply?
Ah, diligent researchers! Finding everything you need? The Archives are a marvel, aren't they? So... orderly.
We're fine. Do you wanna try it? Reading between the lines of your guild's 'complete' records?
The Trade Negotiator's smile doesn't reach his eyes. His gaze lingers on the open codex. From the shadows of a nearby pillar, a Skycity Resident watches, wringing their hands.

lines_after.dialogue: Please... please translate that for me. The old script. My grandmother... she used to hum those lost tones. They said she was Groundless.
Wonderful. Now we have an audience. Just what we needed.
No. This is what we needed. A connection. The silence in the book... and the silence forced on the people.
A low, harmonic alarm begins to pulse through the Archives. The crystal lattices in the walls glow with a faint, angry light.

line.dialogue: The security resonance is activating. The Negotiator blocks the main exit, his friendly pretense gone. The Resident looks at you with desperate hope.

choices.label: CONFRONT the Negotiator. Demand answers. (Easy)
choices.consequence: Direct challenge. He will bluff and threaten, but may reveal his hand too early.
choices.description: Ask Arthit to map the frequency corridors, drawing on ship navigation

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The ex-captain's instincts save them from hidden danger.
A costly mistake by Arthit. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.label: DECIPHER the codex for the Resident. Find the lost tone. (Medium)
choices.consequence: Risk the alarm. You might unlock a truth that could shatter the Archives' control.
choices.description: Ask Pichit to expose surface colonization truth, drawing on resonant staff

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. His staff pulses with clarity, pointing forward.
Pichit overreaches. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.label: SHATTER a minor resonator. Cause a sonic diversion. (Hard)
choices.consequence: Dangerous. Could collapse shelves or trigger a full lockdown, but would create chaos to escape in.
choices.description: The merchant presses forward with valuable goods to confront hidden knowledge

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Hidden leverage shifts the balance.
the merchant misreads the situation. The monastery's countermeasures activate.

lines_before.dialogue: Chaos reigns in the sacred silence. Shattered crystal dust hangs in the air, catching the alarm's pulse. The Negotiator shouts orders to unseen guards. The Resident clutches a recovered fragment of song.
You've broken the First Accord! You drown us all in noise! Seize them!
Pichit, think! This is a sanctioned archive! What about tomorrow? What happens when they come for our ship, our homes?
Tomorrow doesn't exist if we live in a lie today! Is it real? Is their 'protection' real, or just a cage made of pretty sounds?
Oh, it's a cage. A very profitable, very stable cage. And we just rattled the bars. Loudly.
The tone... it's a calling. For the ones below. The Groundless. It says... 'the Lattice sings for all.'
That's it. The real crime wasn't the Silencing. It was the theft of the song. They took a world's voice and sold it back in pieces.

The central archive crystal, the Master Index, begins to resonate in sympathy with the recovered tone. A deep, fundamental frequency vibrates through the floor, through your bones. The true history of the world threatens to sound.

lines_after.dialogue: Stop it! You'll destabilize the city anchors! You'll kill us all!
No. We're finally listening. Please translate that for me, world. Show us what's real.
The Master Crystal flashes. Not with alarm, but with revelation. For a blinding second, perfect, uncharted harmonic pathways through the Lattice unfold in the air—a map of true freedom.
Then, with a sound like a held breath released, the crystal goes dark. The knowledge is gone from sight, but not from memory. The Archives are forever changed.

line.dialogue: The revealed truth is ephemeral. The Orders' guards are at the door. You hold a fragment of the true song, and the fate of the Groundless movement hangs on your next action.

choices.label: ESCAPE with the fragment. Flee to the docks. (Easy)
choices.consequence: Live to fight another day. The song is safe, but the Archives remain in control.
choices.description: Smash the harmonic resonator controlling the archive's frequency dampeners, unleashing the raw signal.

line.dialogue: Every ear in this district just heard the truth — and it sounds like freedom.
You've destroyed the resonator AND the evidence — now no one will ever hear what was buried.

choices.label: BROADCAST the tone. Let every crystal in the city ring with it. (Medium)
choices.consequence: The truth cannot be unheard. It will spark immediate upheaval and unpredictable chaos.
choices.description: Bribe the merchant with three times his monthly quota to let you copy the First Accord's original unredacted transmission.

line.dialogue: See, even the gatekeepers have a price — turns out the cage has a door, and it costs exactly triple.
You think I'd trade my place in the Accord for your scraps? I've already sent the silence wardens.

choices.label: SACRIFICE the fragment to the Master Crystal. Try to permanently unlock it. (Hard)
choices.consequence: All or nothing. Could liberate all knowledge forever... or could shatter the crystal and bring the Archive crashing down.
choices.description: Lock yourself inside the archive's broadcast booth and transmit the unfiltered frequency live across every remaining open channel.

line.dialogue: Tomorrow just became real — every static-filled radio in this city is screaming with what they tried to bury!
The booth auto-purged the moment you hit transmit — they built this archive to survive exactly this kind of fool

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch out in terraced layers of gold and green, wheat stalks whispering in the wind like a slow, breathing sea. Water channels sing a gentle, percussive trickle down the stone tiers.
The rhythm here... it's almost like a lullaby the Lattice itself composed. Can I take a break for a moment? Just to listen?
A break? Pichit, we just got here! Look at those cloud-berries! I bet they're ripe!
Enjoy the pastoral fantasy. The moment we stop moving is the moment something finds us. The Silencing didn't leave many quiet corners.
Malee has a point. This tranquility is... statistically anomalous for an edge-settlement. We should remain observant.
A figure emerges from between the wheat rows—a woman clad in patched leather and crystal-dusted goggles. She eyes the party with sharp suspicion. the Surface scavenger
City-folk. Your ship's resonance is too clean. What do you want with my gardens? I have no one to help me up here, and I prefer it that way.
We mean no harm. We're just... travelers. Can I ask what you're listening for?

lines_after.dialogue: Listening? I'm surviving. The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for maps to the safe frequencies below. I hunt for the open ones—the natural harmonics the Lattice doesn't reject.
An unlicensed frequency hunter. How quaintly illegal.
Illegal is a city word. Down on the surface, it's just life. I found a cluster. Strong, clear resonance. Could be a new stable route. But my resonator crystal is cracked.
She holds up a palm-sized crystal, a hairline fracture glowing with a faint, erratic light.

line.dialogue: The scavenger needs a functioning resonator to verify her find. She won't give the location for free.

choices.line: Offer to trade supplies from the ship for the coordinates.
choices.description: Brush aside the wheat and follow the whisper toward the distant stone shrine, 15 words

line.dialogue: The lullaby thickens here—can you feel it pressing against your teeth?
Great, you walked us into a thornbush. Very mystical, very poetic, very stuck.

choices.line: Propose a joint expedition: we provide the resonator, she guides us.
choices.description: Drop flat in the wheat and listen for footsteps beneath the wind, 15 words

line.dialogue: There. Two sets of prints, bare feet, spacing too even for farmers. We're being herded.
Statistically, lying in wheat invites snakes. I am now looking at a snake.

choices.line: Attempt to repair her crystal with a basic harmonic alignment.
choices.description: Grab Chanida's wrist and pull her down before she reaches the treeline, 15 words

line.dialogue: The clouds she noticed aren't drifting—they're circling. That's not meteorology. That's surveillance.
You yanked her into a drainage ditch. She's soaked and furious and I don't blame her.

lines_before.dialogue: The party and the scavenger, Kanya, descend a hidden stone staircase woven into the garden's foundations. The air grows cooler, humming with a deep, sub-audible vibration.
Now THIS is more like it! For the adventurous! I love it!! Hidden passages under a farm!
The structural integrity of these old supports is concerning. And that vibration... it's not on any standard Tonal chart.
Standard charts are for people who love paying. You need to love yourself enough to find your own way. This pulse... it's pure. Untouched.
It's not just a frequency. It feels... intentional. Like a memory the Lattice is holding.
