Brother Merchant, please. The reflection pool is for meditation, not commerce. The song here is delicate...
And commerce is a song too, dear monk! A song of opportunity! He's the only son in the family business, you know. Gotta keep the notes flowing.

lines_after.dialogue: Something is off. The merchant's patter is too loud. It's drowning out the monastery's natural frequency.
The monk looks like he's trying to solve a math problem in his head while being shouted at. Duty versus throwing that smooth-talker off the island.
The merchant's wares are weird, though. Not just tools... look at those rolled parchments. Are those... private resonance charts?

line.dialogue: The merchant catches you looking and offers a conspiratorial wink. The monk's eyes plead for intervention.

choices.text: Confront the merchant directly about the charts. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Approach the caravan openly, hands visible, calling out a peaceful greeting to the lead merchant.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "I know these trade colors — House Wathik. They've brokered safer passage through worse territory than this.
Arthit — "They scattered the moment you spoke. Whatever they're carrying, they don't want curious scholars asking about it.

choices.text: Ask the Listener Monk to guide you to a quieter place to 'discuss the true song.' (Intuition)
choices.description: Circle wide through the reflection colonnade to observe the caravan's cargo and guard placement unseen.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "Those crates are lined with resonance-dampening felt — you don't need that for silk or spice. They're moving something that sings.
Malee — "A guard spotted your reflection in the pool. We're made, and now they're reaching for weapons instead of ledger books.

choices.text: Pretend to browse the merchant's goods to get a closer look. (Stealth)
choices.description: Touch the Lattice surface nearest you and listen for what the resonance reveals about the new arrivals.

line.dialogue: Pichit — "The crystal is... troubled. It's been strained recently — something nearby was tuned to a frequency that made it bleed, and recently enough that the scar hasn't cooled.
Malee — "You pulled your hand back too fast. The Lattice registered surprise — and so did every attuned surface in this hall, including whatever those merchants are carrying.

lines_before.dialogue: Following the troubled monk, you leave the bustling courtyard for the Monastery's Heart—a cavernous chamber where a single, massive crystal shard hangs from the ceiling, humming softly.
Thank you. The... noise was disrupting the calibration. I just spoke with the Abbot this morning. The merchant's presence was not sanctioned by the full council.
Yet he remains. Which suggests someone on the council sanctioned it quietly. A split vote?
Let me guess. It's about the 'Groundless' whispers, isn't it? The folks who say we should ditch the cities and learn to live with the Lattice's song, not just chart through it.
You are perceptive. The movement... it finds sympathy here. Among some. The Tonal Orders call it heresy. But their charts... they feel like a cage.
And the merchant? He's been married before to one cause, now wed to another. He's selling more than dampeners; he's selling information to both sides.
He's been married twice to profit! So what's the real deal? Is he smuggling Groundless propaganda or selling out the Listeners to the Orders?
Both. And neither. He trades in doubt. He sells the Orders 'security' and sells the disillusioned... hope. He thrives in the discord.

lines_after.dialogue: The great crystal above you pulses, its light growing slightly dimmer, as if clouded by the conversation.
The resonance in this room is dropping. Our discussion is affecting the crystal. This is a sensitive instrument.
It's not us. It's the conflict. The monk's inner turmoil, the division he spoke of... it's creating a dead spot in the song.

line.dialogue: The monk looks from the faltering crystal to you, his face a mask of anguish. The truth is a weight he can no longer carry alone.

choices.text: Offer to help him re-attune the crystal, focusing on harmony. (Resonance Lore)
choices.description: Press the monk to name which council member leaked the calibration schedule.

line.dialogue: ** "Who fed them the timing? Give me a name and I'll have them before sunset.
** "Naming names before proof is how temples burn. I will not light that match.

choices.text: Press him for the name of the council member supporting the merchant. (Investigation)
choices.description: Ask Malee what she already knows about the Groundless movement's sympathizers.

line.dialogue: ** "I've been tracking their pamphlets for weeks. Three low-ranking monks, one treasurer — and someone above who keeps erasing the complaint filings.
** "I know enough to worry, not enough to act. That's precisely why I came to you two instead of going alone.

choices.text: Propose using the crystal's current unstable state to 'listen' for the merchant's hidden agenda in the monastery's echo. (Dangerous Experiment)
choices.description: Offer to pose as a disillusioned pilgrim to infiltrate the Groundless cell directly.

line.dialogue: ** "I can play bitter and lost convincingly. Get me in, give me a week, and I'll trace every thread back to its sponsor.
** "You carry yourself like a blade pretending to be a stone. They will see through you before your first meal here.

lines_before.dialogue: In the deepest acoustic chamber of Phrao Monastery, the air hums with latent energy. The Trade Negotiator stands before a massive, flawed resonance crystal, his smile tight.
You see? The flaw isn't a defect. It's a feature. A new frequency. The Tonal Orders would pay dearly for this map.
But the song... it's wrong. It's a scream, not a harmony. We must not amplify this. You might change your mind if you truly listened.
A scream we can use! Think of the power! We could part the Lattice anywhere!
Power that could shatter this monastery-city. Don't leave it on. Don't even touch it. The risk is incalculable.
He's right. The Negotiator here is trying to change the subject from where he *really* found this. I just spoke with a novice. This crystal came from a silenced zone.
A place the 'Silencing' touched directly. To use this... we'd be dancing with the catastrophe that broke the world.
Progress requires adaptation, my friends! Don't change the subject from opportunity! The Groundless whisper of revolution needs tools. This is one.

lines_after.dialogue: The flawed crystal pulses with a sickly light. The monk looks from the merchant's greed to Pichit's resolve, his own conflict mirrored in the uneasy hum of the chamber.
The Listeners have a vault. Forbidden tones. Records of the Silencing itself. The truth is there. But the door... it only answers to a pure, un-charted song.
A Singer. They need a Singer.
Or someone willing to try.

line.dialogue: The path to the forbidden vault is clear, but the means are perilous. How do we approach the lock?

choices.text: Let Chanida try to brute-force the resonance with the flawed crystal. (Risk damage, but fast.)
choices.description: Grab the shard from the merchant and crush it beneath your boot heel.

line.dialogue: The shard screams one final note as it dies — silence returns, and the monk weeps with relief.
The shard detonates against stone, and the scream pours through every crack in the monastery floor like blood from a wound.

choices.text: Have the Listener Monk guide us in a ritual of alignment. (Slow, requires trust.)
choices.description: Demand Chanida explain exactly *how* she plans to weaponize a screaming stone without destroying herself.

line.dialogue: Chanida's smirk falters — she has no answer, and the silence exposes her ambition as hollow.
Chanida's grin only widens as she sketches a containment circle in the dust, revealing she's already thought this through.

choices.text: I will attempt to Sing. To find the pure tone from within, without a chart. (Personal, profound risk.)
choices.description: Kneel beside the monk and ask him to teach you the original song — the one the shard is corrupting.

line.dialogue: The monk's trembling hands find yours, and together you hum the true melody — the shard's fracture begins to seal.
The monk shakes too violently to speak, and the wrong song crawling through the stones drowns out everything but his sobbing.

lines_before.dialogue: The vault door is not stone, but solidified sound—a wall of silent vibration. The air crackles. The Groundless agitators have gathered in the shadows, drawn by the promise of forbidden truth.
When you reach the truth inside... remember who gave you the key. My investment must bear fruit.
Your 'investment' is a knife at our backs. I can hear his heart calculating the bid. We're no match for the greed of the Orders, but this... this might be.
Just open it! The future's on the other side! Go a bit further, Pichit!
The structural harmonics are fragile. One wrong note and this entire spire collapses into the Lattice. We must be precise.
The final tone is not in our charts. It is the sound before the Silencing. The world's last breath.
Then we listen for the echo.
Pichit steps forward. The vault door shimmers, awaiting a command that is neither a prayer nor a demand, but an acknowledgment. Behind him, the factions hold their breath.

lines_after.dialogue: The tone that leaves Pichit's lips is not loud, but it unravels the silence. The door dissolves into a cascade of harmonic light, revealing not treasure, but a memory—etched in crystal.
The vision is clear: The Silencing was not an accident. It was a weapon. A single, engineered dissonance fired into the Lattice by a warring faction of the ancient Tonal Orders.
We... we are the children of murderers. Our peace is built on a scream.
A monopoly built on a lie. This information... is beyond price. The Groundless will have their revolution. And I will have the chart to its epicenter.

line.dialogue: The foundational lie of the world is exposed. The Negotiator moves to seize the memory-crystal. What do we do?

choices.text: Let him take it. The truth is out; let the world deal with the consequences. (Chaos, but survival.)
choices.description: Press your palm against the resonant surface and hum the melody Arthit taught you in the canal tunnels.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Yes! The harmonics are locking into phase — the structure recognizes the pattern. Push deeper, don't stop singing!
Arthit — "No — you're a quarter-tone sharp and the whole lattice is buckling. Pull your hand back before it shatters!

choices.text: Destroy the crystal here and now. Bury the truth to prevent another war. (Order, but complicity in the lie.)
choices.description: Grab the merchant by his collar and demand he explain what "investment" means before you open anything.

line.dialogue: Malee — "Good. He's talking. Says he planted a tether inside — something that follows whoever opens it. We cut that thread first.
Malee — "He bit through his own tongue. Swallowed something. Whatever he planted in there, he just took the secret to his grave.

choices.text: Seize the crystal. We will carry this truth ourselves, and decide who is worthy of it. (Become the new, hunted arbiters.)
choices.description: Let Chanida open it while you shield Malee and watch the merchant's hands for hidden signals.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "It's open — oh gods, it's beautiful — there's light pouring through like liquid music, and I can hear... I can hear tomorrow!
Chanida — "I touched it and it screamed. Not the door — me. Something inside looked back at me and I think it just... rewrote something.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of silence, broken only by the soft rustle of crystal-sheet scrolls and the distant, resonant hum of the Lattice far below the floating island.
This place gives me the creeps. It's too quiet. Like everyone's holding their breath.
They are. One wrong note in here could shatter a priceless resonance record. The Tonal Orders would have your hide.
Our objective is clear. We must locate the cartography wing. Subtle inquiries only.
Every scroll here is a song that kept someone safe. A memory of a journey. To be among them is... profound.
Ah, travelers! Looking for something specific? The Archives offer many services... for the right frequency of crystal.
We're just browsing. Getting our bearings. This place is huge.
Of course, of course. Say, while you're getting your bearings... can I see the menu? I mean, your cargo manifest? Might have something you need.

lines_after.dialogue: He's fishing. Wants to know what we're after before he names his price.
A direct question about the Open Frequency Map would be unwise. He is Tonal Order adjacent, at best.
Knowledge has its own price, often paid in trust rather than crystal.

line.dialogue: The merchant's friendly smile doesn't reach his eyes. How to respond?

choices.line: "We're researchers, just interested in historical drift patterns." (Deflect with a half-truth)
choices.description: Trace your fingers along the shelf labels, reading the faded Siamese script to locate the cartography wing.

line.dialogue: * "Here — 'Lands Beyond the Khwae.' This corridor leads us to what we seek.
* "You're reading it upside down. That says 'Kitchen Inventories, 1782.' Brilliant.

choices.line: "Anywhere's okay for us to start. Perhaps you could recommend a section?" (Play ignorant and let him guide you)
choices.description: Hum softly to test whether the archive responds to vibration, matching the key Malee warned about.

line.dialogue: * "That's the tonal signature — the shelves just shifted. The archive is welcoming you.
* "Wrong note. That crystal scroll-casing just cracked. Run, before the whole shelf sings itself apart!

choices.line: "Our business is our own. Good day." (Dismiss him coldly)
choices.description: Whisper to Pichit's protective melody, asking the scrolls themselves to guide you to the cartography section.

line.dialogue: * "They remember me. One scroll just unrolled itself — a map, pointing deeper. They want to be found.
* "They've gone silent. Completely silent. Whatever protection they offered us — it just withdrew.

lines_before.dialogue: Having navigated away from the merchant, you find a secluded alcove in the Historical Resonance wing. Dust motes dance in beams of stained crystal light.
Psst! Over here! You're the ones asking about the old maps, right?
Identify yourself. Why the secrecy?
Name's Bor. From the Low-City docks. The Order... they don't like folks digging into pre-Silencing charts. Say it's dangerous.
Dangerous how? What did you find?
Not me. My gran. She was a Listener acolyte, long ago. She kept diaries. Scribbles about a map that wasn't a map, but a... a song of open frequencies.
The Open Frequency Map. A fairy tale to make sky-farers feel better about being trapped.
It's real! She heard things in the deep archives. You heard that, didn't you? The whispers about the restricted vault?

lines_after.dialogue: A song of open frequencies... a resonance not bound by the Orders' charts. It would be a fundamental truth.
If such a thing exists, and the Tonal Orders are suppressing it, the risk is monumental.
So we find the vault. Bor, where did your gran hear these things?

line.dialogue: Bor looks terrified but determined. He points a shaking finger towards a descending stairwell, its entrance shrouded in shadow.

choices.line: "Stay here. We'll investigate the stairwell quietly." (Proceed with caution)
choices.description: Draw your blade and press it against Bor's throat, demanding he speak everything he knows now. 15 words

line.dialogue: The steel against your pulse should convince you — skip the riddles and give me names, locations, everything.
You flinch like a guilty man. Maybe I'm wasting time on someone who'll sell us to the Order before sundown.

choices.line: "Tell us everything your grandmother wrote. Every detail before we move." (Delay for more intelligence)
choices.description: Pull Chanida close and whisper that Bor should prove his loyalty by leading you to the docks himself. 15 words

line.dialogue: If you're genuine, walk us there yourself — your feet on the street tells us more than your whispers ever could.
Your eyes keep darting to the rooftop. You're nervous because you're not alone, are you? Who's watching us right now?

choices.line: "We need a distraction. Chanida, cause a minor resonance incident in the main hall." (Create a deliberate diversion)
choices.description: Grab Bor's collar and drag him into the alley shadow, ordering him to show what he found. 15 words

line.dialogue: You brought this to us, so now you carry it — show me what you pulled from those waters, dockman.
Your hands are shaking too much to have brought anything dangerous. What you found was something done to *you*, wasn't it?

lines_before.dialogue: The air in the restricted vault hums with a low, oppressive frequency. Crystalline shelves hold forbidden maps, their patterns shimmering under a cold, artificial light.
This is it! The Open Frequency Map... just sitting here. Don't let anyone know we found this!
Of course it's just sitting here. The Orders probably think no one dumb enough to break in would be smart enough to understand it.
The security resonances are minimal. Too minimal. This feels like a trap. Let's go inside the alcove, out of the main aisle.
The patterns... they aren't just routes. They're a language. A record of the Lattice's voice before The Silencing.
A soft chime echoes through the vault. Distant, polished footsteps approach on the resonant floor.
Ah. I had a feeling our paths might converge. I see you've found the merchandise. A shame the original owners are so... possessive.

lines_after.dialogue: The Negotiator's smile doesn't reach his eyes. He stands between you and the only exit.
Heard everything, did you? Let me guess, you want a cut.
I want the map. I have buyers in floating cities who would pay a fleet of resonance ships for this. You can walk away, or we can see who the Archives listen to.
This isn't merchandise. It's a memory. You'd sell a world's memory?

line.dialogue: The Negotiator blocks the way, his hand resting on a tonal disruptor at his belt.

choices.line: Bargain. Offer him a copy of the data, keeping the original.
choices.outcome: He'll take a copy, but his 'buyers' will still know the map exists. The secret is out, but you escape with the physical artifact.
choices.description: Trace the pattern language with your fingertip before anyone else touches it.

line.dialogue: I can feel the grammar—each route is a verb, each junction a tense. If I follow the syntax backward, I can read what they're *hiding*." — Pichit
Don't—the pattern bit back. My hand just... passed through the surface. Now the whole map is shimmering like a struck bell." — Pichit

choices.line: Bluff. Claim you've already transmitted the map to the Listeners.
choices.outcome: He hesitates, calculating the risk of angering the monastic order. It creates enough distraction for a risky escape, but he'll be a vengeful enemy.
choices.description: Deploy a dampening cage around the map before the security resonances reset.

line.dialogue: Cage anchored. Whatever threshold alarm they suspended, it won't wake up on my watch. We have maybe twelve minutes before it degrades." — Arthit
The cage didn't catch—it *harmonized*. The security resonance just doubled. I think I sang it a new chord." — Arthit

choices.line: Confront. Challenge his right to profit from knowledge that belongs to all.
choices.outcome: You appeal to the Archives' own latent resonance. The environment subtly shifts against him, but he will fight, risking damage to the vault and the map.
choices.description: photograph the map layers in sequence, but keep your distance.

line.dialogue: Thirty-seven exposures, each layer distinct. The Orders left this here because they wanted someone *smart* to find it, not someone *ready*." — Malee
The shutter triggered something—the flash reflected off frequencies I can't see, and now I'm blind in one eye and

lines_before.dialogue: The confrontation has drawn attention. The vault's ambient hum rises in pitch. Archival sentinels—silent, crystalline constructs—begin to glow at the chamber's edges.
You see? The library itself objects to thieves. Why are you doing this to me? I offered you a clean exit!
He's stalling. The sentinels are tuning to our conflict frequency. We need to decide our exit. Anywhere you like, but choose now!
The central resonator! If we overload it with the map's pattern, it might scramble the sentinels' directives!
Or it might collapse this whole floating section of the archive. What's her personality like, our glorious plan? Reckless and stupid?
No. It's a question of harmony. The map is a lost song. We can use it as a weapon....
The Negotiator raises his disruptor. The sentinels take a synchronized step forward, their forms casting fractured light. The Open Frequency Map pulses in your hands, alive with potential.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. The map's energy interacts with the vault's core, a cascade of light and sound erupting.
(Voice crackling over a suddenly active public resonance channel) What's happening at the Archives? The whole city is shaking!
The Lattice is remembering... and so are the people.

line.dialogue: The Open Frequency Map is awake in your hands, its power demanding a direction.

choices.line: Scramble and Escape. Use the map's energy to disrupt everything and flee into the chaos.
choices.outcome: You escape, map in hand. The Archives are left in disarray, their security protocols in tatters. The knowledge is yours alone, but the Tonal Orders will hunt you relentlessly.
choices.description: Channel the map's harmonic frequencies into the resonator while Arthit holds off the sentinels, 14 words

line.dialogue: The resonator is singing our song now—every sentinel in this hall just pivoted toward the merchant!
The frequencies are fighting me—without a second voice to anchor the harmony, the map's resonance shatters against the resonator's wall!

choices.line: Broadcast the Truth. Channel the map's data into the public resonance grid, sharing it with every floating city.
choices.outcome: The monopoly of the Tonal Orders is shattered in an instant. The skies fill with new, uncharted songs. You are heralded as liberators by some, and dangerous anarchists by others. The world changes forever.
choices.description: Smash the resonator's crystal housing and grab the embedded archive key before the platform destabilizes, 15 words

line.dialogue: Crystal's broken, key's in my hand—now run before the floor remembers it was supposed to fall!
The housing cracked wrong—shards everywhere and the key dropped straight through the fractured stone into open sky below!

choices.line: Synthesize a New Path. Don't destroy or broadcast. Attempt to integrate the map's song with the Archives, creating a new, open system of navigation.
choices.outcome: A profound, resonant union. The Archives transform, becoming a living library that sings with the Lattice. You become permanent stewards of this new truth, bound to the place but granting true freedom to all. The ultimate compromise.
choices.description: Force the merchant to reveal the safe stabilization sequence by pressing him against the humming resonator core, 15 words

line.dialogue: He's screaming the sequence now—four tones, reverse order, and the whole section stops shaking. You're welcome.
He bit through his own tongue rather than speak—and now we're bleeding, destabilizing, and out of leverage all at once.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard stretches before you—a jagged landscape of dead Resonance Ships, their crystal hulls cracked and silent. The air thrums with the industrial percussion of salvage rigs, a harsh counterpoint to the Lattice's distant hum below.
Look at all this junk! There's got to be a working resonator coil here somewhere. Remember, the Tonal Order said ours was 'beyond economical repair.'
Keep in mind, Chanida, that 'beyond economical repair' for them often means 'perfectly salvageable' for us. But we must be methodical. The wrong part could destabilize the entire ship.
Methodical. Right. Because wading through a graveyard of failed dreams is the perfect place for patience. I can't remember the last time we weren't scraping by.
Each broken ship is a memory of a journey. A story that ended here. What songs did these crystals last hold, I wonder?
As you pick through the wreck of a small skiff, a figure in ochre robes approaches, his steps careful to avoid noisy debris.
Peace upon your path. You seek a song among the silence?
We seek a part. But the Lattice's song is always with us, isn't it? Even here, beneath the clangor.

lines_after.dialogue: It is. But it... changes. The foundational tones are shifting. My Order records them. I... I might change my mind about sharing this, but you seem to listen. Remember this: the Lattice groans where it should sing.
A geological stress event? Have your Listeners projected the instability?
It is not geology. It is a warning. The songs from the Deep Lattice have become dissonant. Please, be cautious in your travels.
Great. So the magical crystal floor of the world is throwing a tantrum. Just what we needed.

line.dialogue: The Listener Monk seems genuine but frightened. He hesitates before leaving.

choices.line: "Thank you for the warning. We will tread carefully." (Accept the warning politely and let him go.)
choices.description: Pry open the cargo hatch of a derelict freighter marked "Sukhothai-7" using the hydraulic jack.

line.dialogue: Jack's holding—she's opening! I can already smell copper wiring in there, untouched by the crushers!
The jack slipped. Hull stress fractures propagated along the seam—this entire frame could collapse if we force it further.

choices.line: "This 'warning'—do the Tonal Orders know?" (Press him for institutional knowledge, risking his reticence.)
choices.description: Cross-reference Pichit's hand-drawn graveyard map with the beacon registry to locate pre-war hulls.

line.dialogue: There—three intact Type-IVs in Sector Nine that never made it to the stripping queue. Coordinates locked, let's move.
The registry codes don't match my map. Either someone relabeled these wrecks to hide the best salvage... or I've been reading a tourist brochure this whole time.

choices.line: "If the songs are wrong, could it affect our resonator?" (Focus on the immediate, practical danger to your ship.)
choices.description: Climb into the exposed cockpit of a half-crushed corvette and hotwire its resonance scanner.

line.dialogue: Bypassed the dead ignition cells and rerouted residual capacitor charge. The scanner's
A costly mistake by the monk. The monk's faith wavers, breaking concentration.

lines_before.dialogue: The monk's warning lingers as you delve deeper into the scrapyard's heart. The noise is overwhelming here—grinding metal, hissing steam, the shouts of scavengers. Finding a clear signal, or a clear thought, is a challenge.
Alright, roll up your sleeves. That salvage gantry looks promising. If we can get it working, we can peel open that freighter's resonator housing like a can.
The stress on those cables is considerable. You need to love yourself a little more, Chanida, and not volunteer to dangle from them.
Love yourself? In this place? That's a tall order. That's it, right? We find a part, we ignore the cosmic doom, we fly away. Simple.
Is it? The monk heard something. In all this noise, to hear a change in the world's song... that means truly listening to yourself, not just the chaos around you.
A sharp whistle cuts through the din. A woman clad in patched leathers and goggles watches you from atop a hull, a large wrench resting on her shoulder.
You're not riggers. You're ship-rats. What's your business in the deep yard?
We're looking for a Type-4 harmonic stabilizer. You know where one might be that hasn't been melted down?

lines_after.dialogue: Might. But the deep yard's different. The Lattice's close here. The sounds get... weird. Echoes where there shouldn't be. You have to love yourself a lot to work down there regularly.
Weird how? Like 'the world is ending' weird, or 'that's just the wind' weird?
Like the crystals in the old wrecks sometimes hum on their own. Low and wrong. Scares the gulls off. That's all, isn't it? Just another hazard.
Or an echo of the monk's warning. The Lattice isn't just below us here. It's in the wreckage too.

line.dialogue: The Scavenger points towards a precarious canyon of stacked ship husks—the 'deep yard.' The path is treacherous, and her description unsettling.

choices.line: "We'll take our chances. Just point us to the most intact freighter." (Focus on the salvage mission, braving the physical danger.)
choices.description: Climb the gantry and manually release the cable tension before it snaps, 15 words

line.dialogue: The tension releases smoothly—your hands read the cables better than any gauge could.
Your grip slips at the worst moment; the cable whips past your face and the gantry groans louder.

choices.line: "These 'wrong hums'—can you show us an example?" (Investigate the acoustic anomaly, delaying your search.)
choices.description: Follow the monk's lead and press your ear to the pipes to isolate the sound, 15 words

line.dialogue: There—beneath the clanking. A voice. Someone is trapped in the drainage shaft below us.
The metal vibrations are too chaotic. Your ear rings with nothing but the clangor's endless roar.

choices.line: "Will you guide us? For a share of what we find." (Recruit the suspicious Scavenger, adding social complexity.)
choices.description: Convince Malee to rig the salvage winch

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for the monk. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
Things don't go as planned. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's din fades as the Listener Monk leads you to a hollowed-out resonance ship hull, its crystal resonator cracked and dark. The air inside is still, heavy with dust and secrets.
Here. This is where I first heard the dissonance. The Lattice's song... it's fraying. The Tonal Orders' charts are forcing paths it cannot sustain.
So the whole navigation system is tearing the world apart? And they just keep sailing?
If this is true, exposing it means challenging the only authority that keeps the cities from crashing. The past is over, but its structures remain.
Structures built on lies. Means means it, monk. You're serious about this warning. What do you want us to do, start a revolution with a wrench?
We need proof. Something the Orders can't explain away. Could you please write it down for me? The exact frequencies, the points of strain.
I... I have fragments. Recordings on old crystal shards. But they're scattered in the deep scrap piles. It's dangerous. The Lattice surface there is unstable.
He means what he says! I've seen scav teams vanish out there. The Lattice doesn't just sing—it screams when it's stressed.

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk produces a rough map etched on a piece of hull plating, marking three locations deep in the scrapyard's treacherous periphery.
Three shards. We split up, cover more ground. The faster we get this, the faster we can make someone listen.
Splitting up is a significant risk. The acoustic environment is chaotic; we could miss a collapse warning.
Arthit's right, but Chanida's right about time. We go in pairs. Stay on the comms. Any strange harmonic, you pull back.

line.dialogue: How do you approach the search for the proof shards?

choices.text: Stick together as a full team. Safer, but slower.
choices.outcome: You move as one unit, methodically checking each site. It takes time, but you avoid several hidden lattice fractures, retrieving two of the three shards intact.
choices.description: Smash the resonance crystal broadcasting the dissonance frequency into the navigation lattice.

line.dialogue: Hear that silence? That's the sound of a hundred years of rot finally stopping," I breathe, hands still trembling.
I can't—the crystal's singing back at me, louder, and now everything I knew about the lattice feels like a lie I told myself," I stagger backward.

choices.text: Split into two pairs for efficiency.
choices.outcome: Covering ground faster, you retrieve all three shards, but one pair triggers a minor harmonic backlash—a sharp, painful resonance that leaves them temporarily disoriented.
choices.description: Demand monk publicly testify before the Council of Captains about what the dissonance actually is.

line.dialogue: I'll stand before them. I'll show them the fractures in the lattice and let them decide which truth they can live with," I declare, meeting monk's gaze.
They'll call me a heretic and strip my charts. I've spent forty years building credibility I'm not ready to burn," I mutter, and hate myself for it.

choices.text: Send Chanida and Malee ahead as scouts to locate the shards quickly.
choices.outcome: The scouts find all three shards with impressive speed, but they are cut off by a sudden lattice tremor. The rest of you must navigate a collapsing path of shifting metal to reach them.
choices.description: Ask chanida to reverse-engineer the navigation

line.dialogue: the scavenger makes it work. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the scavenger's resolve isn't enough. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: Reunited at the hull with the crystal shards, you slot them into the old ship's damaged reader. A distorted, agonized waveform erupts into the air—the Lattice's pain given sound.
By the Silent Void... it's worse than I feared. This isn't just strain. It's a deep fracture propagating. If a major resonance ship crosses its path...
The whole sector could drop out of the sky! Most Thais are Buddhist, we believe in cause and effect. This is the effect of their greed!
Great. So we're holding the world's worst mixtape. How do we broadcast this? The Orders control every comms array.
The scrapyard's main salvage magnet. It's the largest unregulated emitter on the floating city. We could piggyback the signal, but it would burn out the system.
Burn it! Let everyone hear this! I'm a Buddhist too, and this is about right action. We have to try.
This is the moment. We either let the past dictate a silent future, or we use this fracture's song to wake the world. The choice is ours.
Alarms begin to wail in the distance—Tonal Order enforcers have tracked the anomalous readings. You have minutes before they shut everything down.

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. You race through the canyon of wreckage towards the towering salvage magnet, its arc lights cutting through the haze.
I've rerouted the power couplings. The shards' data is loaded. On your mark, it will broadcast on every open frequency for approximately forty-seven seconds.
Forty-seven seconds of truth. Better than a lifetime of lies. Let's do it.
For everyone listening... remember this sound. Mark.

line.dialogue: How do you execute the broadcast to ensure the warning is heard?

choices.text: Override safely from the control booth, sacrificing range for security.
choices.outcome: The broadcast goes out cleanly but locally. The city hears it, sparking immediate protests and scrutiny, but the wider Lattice remains unaware. The Orders contain the fallout, but the seed of doubt is planted.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to follow the dissonant trail, leveraging crystal hearing

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
Chanida misreads the situation. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.text: Jack directly into the magnet's core for maximum range, risking a feedback surge.
choices.outcome: The signal screams across multiple floating cities. The Lattice itself seems to resonate with the pain, causing minor tremors everywhere. You become fugitives, but the Tonal Orders' monopoly is irrevocably broken, and Listeners rise to challenge them.
choices.description: Arthit presses forward with lattice storms to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
Arthit misreads the situation. His tattoos burn with a warning he cannot read.

choices.text: Use the fractured Lattice zone itself as an amplifier, merging the shards' data with the live dissonance.
choices.outcome: The broadcast is not just heard; it is *felt*. A profound, world-shaking harmonic event ripples out, temporarily stilling all resonance travel. You are hailed as prophets by some and terrorists by others, but civilization is forced to confront the Silencing's true cause.
choices.description: The scavenger channels survival skills toward the scavenger gangs, hoping to listen for the ghost ship's echo

line.dialogue: The gamble succeeds. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
the scavenger overreaches. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a deep, constant vibration—a foundational tone that sinks into your bones. The air shimmers with harmonic distortion.
This place... it feels like a question made of stone and sound. Why would someone call us here?
Who is this guy? The message was so vague. 'Meet at the Spire's base.' Could be a trap.
Or a waste of time. Probably some Tonal Order bureaucrat wanting to 'discuss regulations.'
We should proceed with extreme caution. The Spire's resonance masks other frequencies. We won't hear an ambush coming.
At the base of the colossal crystal anchor, a figure emerges from the lattice-mist—a woman with a pronounced limp, her right leg replaced by a crude, glowing crystalline prosthetic.
You the ones who got the call? A man called you, said you might be... receptive.
A man called? Who? And what does he think we'd be receptive to?

lines_after.dialogue: My name's Kanya. I surface-scavenge. This leg... it's a Resonant Prosthetic. Tuned wrong. It's started... singing a frequency that draws the wrong kind of attention.
Let me guess. Sky pirate attention.

Exactly. They want its core resonator. Someone phoned me a warning, said they were coming. Said you might help me re-tune it before they get here. The man who called you... he's a Listener. Thinks this is important.

line.dialogue: Kanya's prosthetic is malfunctioning, broadcasting her location to sky pirates. A mysterious Listener connected you. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Agree to help immediately. The Spire's steady tone might stabilize the tuning process.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using tonal knowledge to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Pichit's resolve isn't enough. His staff dims, refusing to resonate.

choices.text: Demand more details first. Who is this Listener, and what's his real interest?
choices.description: Convince Malee to use leg resonance and test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
A costly mistake by Malee. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Refuse. This isn't your fight, and the pirates are already coming.
choices.description: The scavenger takes the lead, employing platform climbing to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the scavenger. The recording captures a ship's bell tolling deep within the lattice.
A costly mistake by the scavenger. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: You agree to examine the prosthetic. As you gather around Kanya, the Spire's hum seems to intensify, vibrating the crystal plates of her artificial leg.
The resonator core is misaligned. It's emitting a single, high-purity frequency. Like a beacon.
Oh, it's you! The frequency signature... it matches a banned pirate navigation chart! No wonder they're after it.
Charming. So we're not just fixing a leg, we're holding a treasure map. Don't let them see you! If they spot us with her, we're all targets.
This 'single' frequency... it feels intentional. Not an accident. Was the prosthetic sabotaged?
I... I bought it from a shady Tonal Order trader. He's still single, isn't he? Always bragging about his 'side projects.'
A sharp, discordant screech cuts through the Anchor's hum—the sound of resonance ship grapnels striking crystal above.

lines_after.dialogue: Well, well! Look what the lattice coughed up! Hand over the shiny leg, scavenger. And your friends.
You're not taking anything!
Heh. That beacon's been singing a sweet song just for us. Makes findin' you easy. Now, be smart about this.
They've got the high ground on the Spire's mid-level platforms. We're exposed here at the base.

line.dialogue: Sky pirates have descended, blocking the main ascent. The prosthetic is still broadcasting. What's your move?

choices.text: Fight defensively. Use the Spire's steady tone to ground yourselves and repel their assault.
choices.description: Tune the resonator manually by ear, matching the tone against a calibrated tuning fork.

line.dialogue: I've matched the harmonic to within point-three hertz — the core is stabilizing, listen, you can hear it settling.
My ear isn't precise enough — the drift is worsening, and now the floor is vibrating through my boots.

choices.text: Attempt a risky re-tune now. Use the pirate ship's own resonance to try and cancel out the beacon frequency.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to sing the frequency she recognized, using her voice to find the correct alignment.

line.dialogue: There — I hit the note and the core responded! It wanted to be found, like it was *waiting* for the right voice.
I can't hold the pitch steady — my voice keeps breaking and the core is shrieking back at me, it's *angry*.

choices.text: Lead a charge up the Spire. Use the chaotic harmonic echoes to mask your movement and take the fight to them.
choices.description: Deliberately amplify the single frequency to its resonant peak and let it shatter whatever is blocking the alignment.

line.dialogue: The casing just cracked open like an egg — whatever was
Defeat. Surface instincts misread the skycity danger.

lines_before.dialogue: The party ascends the final spiraling walkway of the Anchor Spire. The constant, resonant tone grows louder, a physical pressure in the chest. The air itself seems to vibrate.
The harmonic calibration is immense here. One misaligned frequency could shatter the anchor point. This is... reckless.
Reckless is the sky pirate gang waiting at the top. I counted three distinct resonator signatures. Our scavenger friend wasn't lying about the ambush.
So we fight! They want the prosthetic's resonance schematics? They can try and take them. I'm no match for him in a fair fight, but this isn't fair—it's four on three.
When you reach the summit platform, remember the purpose of this place. The tone seeks to harmonize, not destroy. Let that guide your actions.
(From a hidden service ledge) Go a bit further. The lead pirate, Kael, is up there with the schematics. He's boasting about selling them to the highest Tonal Order.
(Shouting from above) Hear that, little listeners? We got your prize! Come and sing for it!

line.dialogue: The sky pirates stand defiant on the central platform, the crystalline prosthetic schematics glowing in their leader's hand. The Anchor's tone makes stealth impossible; a direct approach is all that remains.

choices.text: Challenge their greed. Offer the scavenged Lattice shards from the lower levels as a trade. It's valuable, but not what we came for.
choices.consequence: The pirates might take the bait, but they're treacherous. A trade could turn violent in an instant.
choices.subplot_impact: subplot_crystal_leg: The schematics are obtained, but the pirates remain a future threat, knowing the prosthetic's value.
choices.description: Pichit uses resonant staff to follow the dissonant trail near the structural hum

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The risk doesn't pay off. Pichit's focus breaks under pressure.

choices.text: Use the Spire's own resonance. Have Chanida and Malee create a discordant harmonic feedback, disorienting the pirates while Arthit secures the schematics.
choices.consequence: Risky. Mis-tuning could destabilize the Spire briefly, causing minor lattice tremors on the island above.
choices.subplot_impact: subplot_crystal_leg: The schematics are secured with technical ingenuity, impressing the Listeners who monitor the Spire's stability.
choices.description: Convince Chanida to use unauthorized tones and tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Chanida overreaches. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.text: Confrontation. Fight the pirates directly on the resonant platform. The overwhelming harmonic tone will make the combat chaotic and exhausting.
choices.consequence: A brutal, draining fight where every action is weighed down by the Spire's song. High risk of injury.
choices.subplot_impact: subplot_crystal_leg: The schematics are taken by force, but the prosthetic may be associated with violence and conflict.
choices.description: Direct the pirate to commune with trapped echoes using pirate ship

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the pirate. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
the pirate is thwarted. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: The confrontation leaves the air crackling with spent energy. The pirates are dealt with, for now. The schematics for the Resonant Prosthetic are in Pichit's hands, humming with potential.
Well, that was melodramatic. Nothing like a brawl at the world's biggest tuning fork. Let's get this data to the Listeners before more opportunists show up.
This knowledge... it can't compare to the simplicity of a natural song. But it is a tool. A bridge. We must decide what to build with it.

acts.title: The Cost of a New Key

lines_before.dialogue: At the Spire's very apex, the world falls away. Above, the floating city glimmers. Below, the infinite, shimmering Lattice stretches to the horizon. The harmonic tone is a pure, clarifying force.
You did it. The schematics... my sister, she lost her leg to a lattice surge. This could change everything down on the Surface. Don't get so stressed out about the 'how'—think of the 'who'.
The Tonal Orders will learn of this. A device that mimics a Singer's innate ability? It undermines their entire monopoly. They will see it as a threat.
Let them! I disagree with him—with all of them! Hoarding knowledge while people struggle below? This prosthetic isn't just a leg; it's a key.
A key that unlocks a world of trouble. The Orders, the pirates, every power-hungry fool with a resonator. The Surface scavenger isn't wrong, but the cost...
I stand at the center of the world's song, holding a note that was not meant to be sung. I don't feel the same as before we climbed. The harmony is more complex now. And more fragile.

A deep, resonant chime echoes from the Spire itself. A response. The Lattice below ripples, reacting to the presence of the completed schematics. The choice must be made, and its resonance will be felt everywhere.

line.dialogue: The Resonant Prosthetic schematics are complete. This technology could empower the oppressed Surface dwellers or destabilize the precarious balance of the floating cities. The Anchor Spire awaits your final command.

choices.text: Entrust it to the Listeners. Let the monastic order study and regulate its use, ensuring it's used for healing, not power. A safe, slow path.
choices.consequence: Knowledge is preserved but gatekept by another, albeit gentler, authority. Change comes slowly, if at all.
choices.subplot_impact: subplot_crystal_leg: The prosthetic becomes a rare, carefully doled-out medical marvel. The scavenger's sister may get one, in time.
choices.description: Arthit attempts to decode the tonal pattern, relying on captain experience

line.dialogue: Arthit pushes through. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Arthit is thwarted. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Broadcast the schematics on an open harmonic frequency. Let the knowledge spread to all—Scavengers, Pirates, even the Orders. Let the people decide its use.
choices.consequence: Anarchic innovation and immediate, widespread change. Unleashes a technological revolution with unpredictable and violent growing pains.
choices.subplot_impact: subplot_crystal_leg: The design spreads like wildfire. The scavenger's sister will have a leg by week's end, but so will a hundred sky pirate enforcers.
choices.description: Pichit uses resonant staff to harness harmonic feedback near the deep vibration

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Pichit's call. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Destroy the schematics. The risk is too great. The natural harmony of the Lattice, and the hard-won peace, must be protected from this disruption.
choices.consequence: The immediate threat is neutralized, but you crush hope for the Surface and make powerful enemies of those who desired the knowledge.
choices.subplot_impact: subplot_crystal_leg: The prosthetic is lost. The scavenger despairs. The technology may be rediscovered one day, in a less controlled form.
choices.description: Have the scavenger risk using surface knowledge to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. A crystal fragment resonates with the environment.
the scavenger's resolve isn't enough. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: Your choice resonates through the Spire. The great harmonic tone shifts, ever so slightly, incorporating the echo of your decision into the world's endless song. The consequences will unfold in acts unseen.
We have added our note to the symphony. Whether it creates dissonance or a new chord... only the Lattice will tell, in time.
We changed something today. For better or worse. That's more than most people do in a lifetime.
The Spire holds. The anchor remains. Our path forward, however... that calculation is now infinitely more complex.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard sprawls beneath the iron-gray sky, a jagged landscape of broken ships and forgotten machinery. The air vibrates with the percussive rhythm of salvage hammers and grinding engines.
Listen to that noise! There's a high chance we can find a decent resonator coil in this chaos if we know where to look.
We should proceed with caution. This acoustic interference could mask all sorts of dangers—structural instability, scavenger gangs...
Oh, relax. The only thing getting masked here is the smell. (Sniffs) Rust, oil, and desperation. Charming.
Every broken hull has a story... a final note in its song. We're walking through a cemetery of journeys cut short.
This salvage crane looks promising! This cute and inviting little access hatch... how could you pass it up?
As Chanida reaches for the hatch, a sharp whistle cuts through the industrial din. A figure drops from the crane's cab, landing with a clang of metal boots.
Hands off the merchandise, sky-rats! That's my find. You're not finished yet scrounging in my yard.

lines_after.dialogue: We mean no trespass. We're just seeking parts for our resonance ship.
Parts, eh? I know where the good crystal is. The Tonal Orders don't chart these frequencies. For a price.
Of course there's a price. There's always a price.
What is the nature of your price? Information? Or something more resonant?

line.dialogue: The sky pirate eyes your group, one hand resting on a weapon at his belt. How do you engage?

choices.line: Offer immediate payment for information. (Spend resources)
choices.description: Arthit takes the lead, employing tattooed routes to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Arthit. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
The risk doesn't pay off. The ex-captain's gamble costs dearly.

choices.line: Prove your worth by identifying a salvageable part he missed. (Perception check)
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to calibrate against the frequency, leveraging singer voice

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Chanida. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
The resonance turns hostile. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Defer to Chanida's impulsive negotiation style. (Let her take the lead)
choices.description: Have the pirate risk using smuggling routes to commune with trapped echoes

line.dialogue: the pirate finds the key. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
Defeat. The echo fades to silence.

acts.title: Things That Hum in the Rust

lines_before.dialogue: Following the pirate's grudging directions, you weave through canyons of shattered hulls. The air grows thick with the scent of ozone and old fuel.
He said the good cache was behind that derelict freighter. Look at all this! They have a lot of stuff!
Most of it's junk. But that... (points to a partially buried resonator array) That might sing again with some work.
The structural integrity is questionable. And what do your parents do, Chanida, to make you so comfortable crawling into unstable wrecks?
Salvagers, like me! They'd say this prize is worth the risk. I'll take very good care of it once it's ours.
Wait. Listen. Beneath the clanging... a purity tone. Uncorrupted.
A figure in ochre robes steps from behind a crystal column, hands raised in a gesture of peace. It's a Listener monk, their face etched with worry.
Please, you must cease. This place... it is not for taking. The Lattice here hums a warning. A disharmony that could fracture everything.

lines_after.dialogue: A Listener? What warning? The Tonal Orders' charts show this sector as acoustically stable.
The charts are silent on truths we have... buried. My order studies the natural song. Here, the song is becoming a scream.
Convenient. A monk shows up just as we find valuable things. What's your real angle?
Your conflict is palpable. You're torn between your duty to silence and a duty to truth. Which song will you sing for us today?

line.dialogue: The Listener monk looks between your party and the humming crystal array, clearly distressed. How do you respond to their warning?

choices.line: Heed the warning and withdraw immediately. (Avoid risk, lose the salvage)
choices.description: Wedge the pneumatic jack beneath the freight's buckled door and force it open.

line.dialogue: Move back — she's giving way!" Arthit grunts as the door screams open on rusted tracks.
The jack slipped — whole frame's shifting!" Arthit stumbles back as metal groans overhead.

choices.line: Press the monk for specific data about the frequency anomaly. (Persuasion/Knowledge check)
choices.description: Crawl through the shattered vent duct Malee spotted to reach the cache from above.

line.dialogue: Tight fit, but I can see the cache from here — hand me the cutter!" Malee whispers.
Duct's collapsing under me — get me out before it folds!" Malee's voice cracks with panic.

choices.line: Proceed with extracting the resonator, trusting your ship's dampeners. (Risk triggering the anomaly)
choices.description: Rig the freight's corroded winch cable to drag the cache clear from a safe distance.

line.dialogue: Cable's holding — haul it steady, the prize is sliding free!" Chanida laughs as the cache moves.
Cable snapped — it's whipping free, everyone down!" Chanida shouts, diving behind cover.

lines_before.dialogue: In the shadow of a gutted Resonance Ship's hull, the party confronts the Listener Monk. The air vibrates with the distant, percussive demolition of old vessels.
You should not have come. The Tonal Orders' agents are already here, seeking the Sky Pirate and his illicit frequency charts.
Then we're out of time! Where's the pirate? We need to know what he heard in the deep Lattice!

He hides among the compressor stacks. But listen... the Lattice's song here is wrong. A grinding dissonance beneath the scrapyard's noise. I didn't catch what you said earlier, Pichit, about the Silencing. Could it be... returning?
A systemic resonance collapse? The historical records are fragmented, but the acoustic profiles...
Great. So the world might end, and we're chasing a bandit who probably lost his phone and his last brain cell in the same bet.
The truth often hides in what we fail to hear. Lead us to him, Monk. We must piece this together before the Order silences it all.
A shriek of tearing metal echoes, followed by a rough laugh from the gantries above.

lines_after.dialogue: The Sky Pirate drops to a lower catwalk, a resonator pistol humming in his grip. The Monk steps back, conflicted.
Hah! The little listeners finally caught up! Yeah, I heard it. A dying note way down deep. Sounds like the whole song's about to... change.
Tell us everything! Now!

line.dialogue: The Pirate smirks, eyeing the Monk's robes and your group. He'll talk, but only under his terms.

choices.line: Appeal to his greed: Offer salvage rights from your own ship for the information.
choices.description: Channel residual resonance through the monastery's drainage pipes to triangulate the pirate's position.

line.dialogue: Chanida presses her palm flat against the corroded pipe, eyes snapping open. "I feel him — third stack, eastern maintenance ledge. He's shaking.
Chanida recoils as the pipe shrieks with feedback, her ears ringing. "The resonance signature is scattered — too much interference from the Tonal agents' dampening fields.

choices.line: Appeal to his survival: Argue that if the Lattice dies, his piracy ends too. He needs allies.
choices.description: Demand the monk reveal whether the Tonal Orders' agents have already breached the compressor stacks' inner chambers.

line.dialogue: The monk's jaw tightens, robes rustling as he turns toward the stacks. "Three entered at dusk. They carry tuning forks calibrated to shatter bone. Your pirate has perhaps an hour before they find him.
The monk shakes his head, backing into shadow. "I have said what I dare. The Orders hear every spoken loyalty — even mine. Leave me.

choices.line: Challenge his courage: Dare him to prove he's not just a scavenger, but a true explorer of the unknown.
choices.description: Reroute the compressor stacks' pressure valves to create an acoustic smokescreen, masking your approach.

line.dialogue: Arthit spins two valves in sequence, grinning as a thunderous low hum swells through the metal. "They'll hear nothing but machinery now — their tuning forks are useless against this noise.
Arthit wrenches the wrong valve and superheated steam erupts across his forearm. "Gah —

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard falls unnaturally quiet. The pirate has shared the forbidden frequency—a keening, dying sound from the Lattice's heart. But the Monk is trembling, a Tonal Order cruiser now hovering at the scrapyard's edge.
They're here. They've come to reclaim the knowledge, to bury the warning. I now know... my order has been complicit. We listened, but we never spoke.
Their ship is priming its dampeners. They intend to acoustically stun the entire area and take us all.
Of course. The bureaucratic solution: erase the problem and the witnesses. I told you this was a bad idea.
My ship's a wreck, but the old compressor array... hit it with that dying frequency, and the feedback might just scramble their systems. It's the best way. Also the only way.
A sonic cannon? From this junk? Let's do it!
A final act of resonance. To break one song to save the greater melody. The Monk is right—there's a high chance this fails, or worse, accelerates the dissonance.
The Order cruiser's speakers crackle with a demand for surrender. The party stands amid the ruins, the fate of the warning in their hands.

lines_after.dialogue: The air shimmers with released energy. The scrapyard's cacophony is swallowed by a single, profound note that seems to shake the very Floating City.
The Lattice... it heard us. It's responding.
Hah! Never heard that one before!
The warning is broadcast. The song changes now. For better or worse.

line.dialogue: You have the dying frequency. The pirate's jury-rigged array is ready. How do you broadcast the Lattice's final warning?

choices.line: Pure Amplification: Channel all power into the main speakers. Overwhelm the Order with sheer volume and truth.
choices.description: Reroute the compressor array's full output into a single disabling pulse

line.dialogue: I've got it locked — one shot, one chance. Fire when ready, I won't miss this frequency.
The array's collapsing — too much draw, the whole grid is arcing, we've got nothing left to hit them with.

choices.line: Resonant Harmony: Have Chanida Sing, blending her voice with the frequency to guide it, making it comprehensible to all who hear.
choices.description: Broadcast the archived knowledge on every open channel before they can suppress it

line.dialogue: Every relay in range is screaming the old frequencies now. They can silence us, but they can't un-hear it.
They were faster. The dampeners caught the signal mid-burst — fragments only, corrupted, meaningless noise.

choices.line: Targeted Dissonance: Aim the frequency at the cruiser's crystal core. Risk destroying them to ensure the warning reaches the other cities.
choices.description: Confront the ship directly and demand parley with whatever governs their mandate

line.dialogue: I'm standing in the open with my hands visible. If they
the monk misreads the situation. Tonal Order enforcers confiscate his equipment.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship *Harmonic Drift* cuts through the dense, crystalline mist of the Lattice. Below, the iridescent surface hums with a low, mournful frequency. The deck is slick with condensation.
Is it just me, or is the hum getting... sharper? It’s a lot more fun when it sings, not screams.
Fun. Right. The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for these 'safe' charts, and all we get is a headache. Our captain left home in a hurry with these coordinates. I doubt he paid full price.
Caution is advised. These interference patterns aren't on any standard nav-log. Pichit, are you ready to go back home yet? This route feels... uncharted.
Home is a direction, not a place on these maps. The Lattice is speaking. We just need to learn how to listen past the charts.
A sudden, discordant shriek of crystal grinding against crystal echoes from the starboard bow. The ship shudders violently.
By the Founders! What was that? We paid for safe passage!
Told you. 'Safe' is a relative term when you're skimming the world's scar.

lines_after.dialogue: The shuddering subsides, but the high-pitched whine remains, etching into the silence. A jagged fracture of crimson light pulses deep within the Lattice below.
That wasn't natural resonance. That was a fracture. A warning.
Subplot: The Lattice's Warning. The Listeners' texts speak of such phenomena preceding deep instability. The frequency is all wrong.

line.dialogue: The crimson pulse fades, leaving an uneasy quiet. The ship's main resonator crystal flickers erratically.

choices.text: Divert power to stabilizers. (Prioritize the ship's immediate safety.)
choices.description: Tune your receiver to match the interference pattern's rising frequency.

line.dialogue: The harmonics are aligning — I can isolate a voice buried in the carrier wave.
Brilliant, you just blew the preamp. Hope that fortune covers replacements.

choices.text: Tune the receptors to analyze the anomalous frequency. (Study the warning.)
choices.description: Mark the waypoint Pichit described and push deeper toward the Lattice edge.

line.dialogue: There — the signal thins here. We're walking the thread my grandmother's maps promised.
The markers don't match. We've circled back, and the hum knows our names now.

choices.text: Change course to the nearest marked lane. (Follow the known charts.)
choices.description: Stop everyone and demand we triangulate the source before taking another step.

line.dialogue: Finally, sense. Three readings, three points — the source is beneath us, not ahead.
While you're playing surveyor, the static's writing itself into our recordings. Move.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship limps forward on backup resonators. The air is thick with ozone and tension. Distant, predatory shapes circle just beyond the mist—sky pirate skiffs.
Scavengers. They're waiting for us to sputter out. My girlfriend gets jealous if I'm late for dinner. These vultures look jealous of our still-spinning crystal.
Romantic. They just want to pick our bones. And don't make me cry! I paid good coin for the cargo in the hold.
Hostile signatures are converging. Our defensive harmonics are weak. I sprained my ankle once trying to run on a shifting deck. This feels similar—a bad footing.
A grappling hook, humming with a crude disruptor field, clangs onto the port rail. A gruff voice shouts from the mist.
Cut yer drone, city-slickers! We're comin' aboard for a chat. My girlfriend is jealous of quiet ships—means they got secrets worth takin'.
Violence is just another form of dissonance. But even a warning note can be struck with force.
Please, don't fight! They'll scuttle the ship! We'll all fall!

lines_after.dialogue: Two pirates swing onto the deck, clad in scavenged resonator plating. Their leader, a woman with a sonic blade, eyes the ship's flickering main crystal.
Lookit that. Yer flyin' blind on a cracked heart. We know the hidden frequencies 'round here. The safe lanes. For a price.
Or you just take it. What's the real price?
You navigate the static. You must hear it too. The Lattice is sick here. This isn't a place for piracy. It's a tomb tuning itself.

line.dialogue: The pirate leader's blade hums, pointed at the ship's crystal. The other pirate trains a crude sonic blaster on the party.

choices.text: Offer a bribe of cargo. (Buy a temporary ceasefire.)
choices.description: Slam the harmonic shielding to full resonance and scatter their approach vector with a gravity pulse.

line.dialogue: Harmonics holding — their hulls are buckling. They're peeling off like dead leaves.
The resonance collapsed — they punched through and they're latched onto our hull.

choices.text: Challenge their knowledge. (Question their claim of knowing 'hidden frequencies.')
choices.description: Kill the drone's signature, go dark, and let them drift past thinking we're already dead.

line.dialogue: They bought it. Keep breathing shallow — they're running scans right over us.
They caught our thermal bleed. Clever girl — she tagged us the moment we went quiet.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with the ship's damaged crystal. (Create a disruptive pulse.)
choices.description: Open a channel and offer them the drone's salvage rights in exchange for safe

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The community rallies, creating unexpected strength.
Things don't go as planned. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The ship sails through a silent stretch of sky, the Lattice below shimmering with an unnerving, muted light. The usual hum of the resonator feels strained.
The engine's singing a dirge. It's not necessary that we push through this dead zone. Charts are blank here.
Agreed. Our harmonics are unstable. The car wouldn't budge an inch if it were stuck in mud, but we're stuck in dead air.
Listen... beneath the engine. A dissonance. It's not the ship. It's the Lattice itself.
I don't hear anything but my own teeth chattering. This place feels wrong.
A sudden, jarring scrape echoes from the hull—not an impact, but a resonant feedback shriek. From the starboard railing, a grappling hook clatters and catches.
Ahoy the sluggish vessel! Don't make me cry! We've been listening to your sad frequencies for miles. Easy pickings.
Two pirate skiffs swing into view, their resonators tuned to a predatory, grating whine. Their leader, a scarred woman, leers from the lead ship's prow.

line.dialogue: The pirate captain shouts over the wind: 'I overheard him say your ship's carrying Listener contraband! Hand over your resonator core, and we might let you drift.'

choices.text: [EASY: Bluff and Distract] 'Contraband? You've been listening to static! Our core is fried—take it and you'll sink with us.'
choices.consequence: The pirates hesitate, buying time but increasing their suspicion.
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing crystal prosthetic to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
A costly mistake by Malee. The leg seizes up, immobilizing her.

choices.text: [MEDIUM: Appeal to Greed] 'The core's worthless compared to what we *really* found. A new frequency map. Untouched sky.'
choices.consequence: Their avarice wars with caution, splitting their focus.
choices.description: Chanida attempts to use the leg as a lattice probe, relying on unauthorized tones

line.dialogue: A breakthrough. Her crystal hearing isolates a pattern that rewrites the map.
Chanida misreads the situation. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: [HARD: Challenge Directly] 'You heard wrong. This ship carries a warning from the Lattice itself. Attack, and you'll hear it too.'
choices.consequence: A bold gamble that either awes or enrages them.
choices.description: The pirate volunteers to commune with trapped echoes, leveraging smuggling routes

line.dialogue: the pirate succeeds. The disruptor creates an opening no one expected.
Things don't go as planned. The disruptor backfires, jamming itself.

lines_after.dialogue: Pretty speeches! But my girlfriend gets jealous when I come home empty-handed. So we'll be taking our toll.
Your girlfriend? Is she the one who gave you that face? Get ready to sprain more than your ankle!
The pirate skiffs' engines rise to a piercing whine. Boarding planks slam down. The fight for the ship begins as the dead zone around you seems to pulse.

lines_before.dialogue: The clash is brief, violent. You repel the first boarders, but the lead pirate captain lands on your deck, her blade humming with a disruptive frequency. The Lattice below begins to glow fiercely.
Enough! You're hiding something. That glow—it's not from our skiffs. What did you Listeners wake up?
It's not that we woke it. It's been screaming since The Silencing. We just finally stopped to listen.
And from that day we first heard it, I knew we were all doomed. Happy now?
The harmonic pressure is building. If we don't harmonize the ship's resonator with the emerging frequency, the feedback will shatter every crystal on board!
The pirate captain falters, looking at the radiant Lattice. Her crew watches from their skiffs, uncertain. A deep, foundational tone rises from the world below, a song of immense age and pain.
I'm just a trader from Cloudheel! I begged passage! Please, you have to believe me, I don't want to die to some... some ancient noise!
The ship groans. The warning is here. To survive, you must not fight it, but answer it. Pichit moves toward the main resonator, the song pulling at something deep within.

line.dialogue: Pichit places a hand on the resonator. The world's pain vibrates in his bones. To channel it is to risk being unmade. He looks at the pirate, the terrified villager, his friends.

choices.text: [EASY: Contain the Song] Focus the resonance inward, shielding the ship. It will drain you, but it's safe, controlled.
choices.consequence: The danger passes, but the Lattice's warning is muffled, its message lost. The pirates flee, but the mystery deepens.
choices.description: Raise your hands and channel the harmonic resonance outward toward the bandit's chest, forcing him to feel what the sky feels.

line.dialogue: [pichit: "Now you understand—it's not madness, it's a frequency older than your bones, and it's been calling us home."]
[bandit: "Get that light away from me—I said AWAY—your 'harmony' feels like a blade pressed against my ribs!"]

choices.text: [MEDIUM: Amplify the Truth] Let the song flow through you and the ship, broadcasting it raw for all to hear, friend and foe alike.
choices.consequence: The pirate captain drops her blade, understanding. The warning is shared, forging a fragile, awe-struck truce.
choices.description: Drop to your knees and press your ear to the cracked earth, listening for the sky's true song beneath the surface.

line.dialogue: [malee: "You hear it too—the inverse note, the one that answers from below—we were never meant to harmonize with the sky alone."]
[arthit: "The pressure just spiked—whatever you're hearing down there, it's not an answer, it's an echo pulling us deeper out of phase."]

choices.text: [HARD: Become the Conduit] Don't just broadcast it. Answer it. Sing back with your own resonance, trying to soothe the ancient pain.
choices.consequence: The Lattice calms, parting into a breathtaking, stable path. You collapse, forever changed. The pirates look on not with greed, but reverence.
choices.description: Grab arthit's wrist and match your breathing to the harmonic rhythm, attempting a two-person resonance to stabilize the building pressure.

line.dialogue: [arthit: "There—together the frequency holds—now we just need one more voice to complete the chord before the sky tears itself open."]
[bandit: "You're synchronizing? You fools, you're amplifying it—can't you see the clouds are already splitting apart above us!"]

lines_after.dialogue: The climax of the song shakes the sky. Light envelops the deck. For a moment, all is vibration and intent.
Pichit! Just... come back to us, okay?
The light fades. The strange glow from below subsides into a gentle, steady pulse. The immediate danger is over. The consequences of your choice settle upon the silent deck.
...smiling happily. It's... quieter now. We heard it. We answered.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform, 'The Ear of Solus,' juts out over the Lattice. Below, the crystalline surface ripples with auroras of light, humming with a low, foundational drone.
A pleasure, my friends! The view is free, but the information... well, that's where I come in. The Tonal Orders' charts for this sector are... incomplete.
Incomplete? You mean there are gaps? Places even they don't dare chart?
It might be true. Rumor has it a 'Listener' sect mapped an open frequency corridor here. A path straight through, no tolls, no guild oversight.
Sounds like a great way to get our resonator harmonics shredded. Uncharted frequencies are volatile.
He's not a playboy, Arthit, he's a merchant. His product is hope. Usually the expensive, false kind.
Such cynicism! You should give it a try! Find the old Listener cairn at the edge of the platform's sonic ward. The map isn't paper... it's a song.
A song left in the stones... a memory of the Lattice's purer voice, before the Silencing. We should listen.

lines_after.dialogue: As the merchant departs with a knowing smile, a rough, static-laced voice crackles from a hidden vox-relay on the platform's support strut.
Oy! You lot! I heard that whole cozy chat. You lookin' for the Open Frequency? Don't bother. That cairn's been picked clean. By me.
Sky rat! You stole it?
Salvaged. Finders, keepers. But my ship's resonator is junk. Can't sing the map to life. Maybe we can deal... or maybe I just take your ship instead.

line.dialogue: The pirate has the map, but lacks the means to use it. The merchant's information led to this confrontation.

choices.line: Propose a temporary alliance. We have a ship; he has the map. We'll share the profits.

choices.line: Call his bluff. If his resonator is broken, he's stranded here. Threaten to alert the Tonal Orders patrol.
choices.description: Examine the merchant's so-called "incomplete map" for signs of deliberate falsification or hidden markings, 15 words

line.dialogue: ** "These aren't gaps from ignorance — someone scratched out three corridors deliberately. They *want* us blind down there.
** "Nothing but smudged ink and wishful thinking. If there's a pattern here, it's buried deeper than I can read.

choices.line: Offer to trade for it. We have salvage from the last dive; perhaps he'll take hardware over harmony.
choices.description: Calibrate your resonator to the crystal frequencies humming through the cavern floor and listen yourself, 15 words

line.dialogue: ** "I can hear it — low harmonic, two pulses then silence, repeating. Something down there is *calling*.
** "Just static and the sound of my own heartbeat. Whatever the Listeners heard, I'm not tuned to it.

lines_before.dialogue: A tense agreement is struck. The pirate, Kael, leads the party down a maintenance ladder to a makeshift camp nestled in a dead acoustic zone on the Lattice surface.
Home sweet home. Don't touch nothin'. The map's here.
He produces a large, flat resonance crystal. When Arthit taps it with a tuning rod, a complex, shimmering pattern of light and sound projects into the air.
There's no one else who could have decoded this. It's a Listener's work, pure and simple. No guild corruption, just... mathematics made music.
The harmonic sequences are stable. I'm happy to hear this. This isn't a pirate's fantasy; it's real navigation data.
So we can really go? Are you going or not, Kael? Your ship's a wreck.
My bird's grounded, not dead. But yeah. I need your ship's main crystal to charge this map fully. Then it'll show the whole path.
To merge our song with this ancient one... to walk a path of pure resonance. This is why we sail.

lines_after.dialogue: As Pichit prepares to interface the ship's resonator with the map crystal, a low, aggressive hum shakes the platform. Three jagged skiffs descend from the cloud layer above.
Via vox-caster, his voice is no longer friendly. 'A pity. I had hoped you'd simply lead me to it. The Tonal Orders pay a hefty bounty for poachers of their intellectual property.'
He sold us out! The negotiator's a guild snitch!
We've got company! And they don't look like they're here to negotiate!

line.dialogue: The merchant has betrayed you, bringing Tonal Orders enforcers. The map is active but not fully charged. The pirate's camp offers little cover.

choices.line: Make a break for the ship. Abort the charging sequence, grab the map, and try to outrun them in the Resonance Ship.
choices.description: Grab the decoded map and trace the route with your finger, committing to the path. 15 words

line.dialogue: Good — then we move tonight, before the harmonic window closes and we lose our shot.
You're pointing at a reef, Kael. Maybe let the person who decoded it handle the navigation.

choices.line: Stand and fight. Use the pirate's knowledge of the dead zone and scattered debris for an ambush. Defend the map until it's fully charged.
choices.description: Turn to the bandit and demand what they're really getting out of this deal. 15 words

line.dialogue: Straight to it, eh? Fine — I get a cut. First pick of whatever's in that vault. That's the bargain.
You're in *my* house asking *me* for explanations? Touch that map again and we're done talking.

choices.line: Sabotage the platform's sonic wards. Collapse the safe zone into the chaotic Lattice frequencies below, creating a dangerous barrier for everyone.
choices.description: Look at Chanida and ask if she's certain she wants
