the merchant overreaches. Hidden debts come due.

lines_before.dialogue: The observation platform shudders violently as a dissonant frequency rips through the Lattice. Cracks spiderweb across the crystal surface below, revealing a deep, glowing fissure.
There's your 'great place to live'! The whole shelf is coming apart. Why didn't you listen when I said this was a bad idea?
The fissure! Look—there's structure down there. Old metal. It's not natural!
A ruin, embedded in the Lattice. This... this changes everything we know about The Silencing. How do we even write this into the records?
The patterns... they're not random. They're a recording. A memory of the world before, written in light and fracture.
Excellent! Salvage rights on a pre-Silencing site! The Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for this location. Or... we could keep it for ourselves.
Or someone with a ship could just blast the crystal open and take what's shiny. Your call, philosopher.

line.dialogue: The fissure pulses with unstable energy. Accessing the ruin below is possible, but dangerous.

choices.line: Use the Merchant's resonance dampeners to stabilize the approach. (Requires promising him a cut.)
choices.consequence: Safe but costly entry; Merchant gains leverage.
choices.description: Anchor a rope to the shelf and rappel down into the fissure toward the ruin's entrance.

line.dialogue: Rope's taut — I can see a doorway down there, just past the third shelf fracture. Who's coming with me?" — Chanida
The edge is crumbling — the whole shelf is resonating wrong! Pull me back up before I become part of the recording!" — Malee

choices.line: Have Chanida improvise a descent using harmonic hooks. (Risky but independent.)
choices.consequence: Quick entry; potential injury or discovery.
choices.description: Touch the Lattice directly and let the pattern-flow replay through your senses.

line.dialogue: I can feel it — voices, faces, a whole civilization compressed into harmonic waves. They knew this would happen." — Pichit
Too much — too loud — it's rewriting something behind my eyes, get it out, GET IT OUT—" — Arthit

choices.line: Pichit attempts to 'Sing' the Lattice into temporary stillness. (Unpredictable, could attract attention.)
choices.consequence: Profound connection; major risk of Lattice backlash or Tonal Order detection.
choices.description: Use the tuning fork to isolate one layer of the recording without fully activating the structure.

line.dialogue: One strand at a time. There — that frequency is architectural, a map of what this place was before it fell." — Arthit
The fork shattered. Whatever's down there just felt us ping it, and the whole Lattice is *answering*." — Pichit

lines_after.dialogue: The descent into the fissure is like plunging into frozen music. Ancient machinery, fused with crystal, hums with residual power.
This isn't just a ruin. It's a transmitter. Or... a weapon. The scale is terrifying.
And look. Charts. Frequency maps carved into the walls. Complete ones. No wonder the Orders want this buried.
The Open Frequency Map. It was here all along. Not lost... hidden.

acts.title: The Cost of a True Note

lines_before.dialogue: Deep in the ruin, you find the core: a massive, dormant resonator. Activating it could unlock the Lattice's secrets—or repeat The Silencing.
All guys like beautiful women, and all merchants like profitable secrets. Hand over the core frequency, and we can be partners. Why are you treating me like this? I'm offering partnership!
He talks too much. The core's worth more than his whole fleet. What's she like, this big secret? Friendly, or does she bite?
They're circling. We can't let of them have it. This is bigger than profit.
The core is catastrophically unstable. One wrong frequency could cascade. We must decide its fate, now.
Of course. We find the key to free navigation, and it's a bomb. What's her personality like? She's a vindictive bitch, that's what.
This was never a map. It's a choice. The ancients left us the question: do we control the song, or do we listen?

line.dialogue: The Pirate and Merchant are at a standoff, weapons drawn. The core hums, awaiting a command frequency.

choices.line: Sabotage the core. Destroy the map to prevent anyone from owning it. (The safe, cynical choice.)
choices.consequence: The secret is lost. Safety is bought with permanent ignorance. The Lattice remains controlled.
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing leg resonance to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Malee pushes through. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.

choices.line: Bargain. Use the core as leverage to broker a temporary truce and copy the data. (The diplomatic gamble.)
choices.consequence: Data is disseminated but corrupted by compromise. New factions rise, conflict changes form.
choices.description: Have Arthit focus ship navigation on the shifting light to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: Fortune favors Arthit. The captain navigates a hazard no chart predicted.
Arthit fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Pichit interfaces directly with the core. To Sing the true frequency, merging with the Lattice's memory. (The transcendent risk.)
choices.consequence: The Open Map is broadcast to all Listeners. Pichit's fate is unknown. The monopoly shatters; the world changes forever.
choices.description: The pirate channels smuggling routes toward the harvesting, hoping to follow the phantom route

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the pirate. A secret frequency from the underworld shifts the balance.
the pirate loses control. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_after.dialogue: On the Lattice surface, light erupts. It is not an explosion, but an expansion—a single, clear note that reverberates through every crystal shard, echoing toward the floating cities.
Pichit...? The song... it's everywhere.
The charts in my head... they're rewriting themselves. We can all hear it.
Well. There goes the monopoly. Hope you all like anarchy. (A faint, grudging smile.) It's about time.
Above, Resonance Ships wobble in their paths as their proprietary charts glitch and fail. Below, in the hearts of Listeners everywhere, a new note begins to sound.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim are a sanctuary of green. Tiered terraces cascade down the skycity's edge, their crops swaying in a gentle, rhythmic wind. Water channels hum with quiet melodies. The air smells of damp earth and blooming night-flowers. The party has stopped here to rest, the peace a stark contrast to their usual travels.
I could get used to this. No ship's hum, no Lattice static. Just... wind. And that weird, quiet ringing.
That 'weird ringing' is probably a cracked irrigation pipe. Don't get too comfortable. Places this quiet usually have something to hide.
The soil composition on these upper tiers is remarkable. Stable, yet responsive. A perfect place to recuperate. We should be safe here.
Safe, perhaps. But listen. The wind through the barley... it's not a random sound. It's phrasing. Like a breath held, then released.
You lot look like travelers. You're gonna be sorry if you're planning to head towards the western spurs after dark.
Why? What's out there?

Nothing good. Sounds that shouldn't be there. Like a ship's resonator, but... broken. Stuck on one awful note. Some say it's the echo of the *Amaranth*, a Resonance ship that vanished cycles ago. Could you tell me how to get to the Dusit Hotel? I've... I've got family coming in from another skycity and I need to meet them there. It's safer in the core.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost ship's echo? Sounds like a fantastic way to get ourselves killed chasing a ghost story.
A persistent sonic anomaly could indicate a destabilized Lattice zone. It *is* a legitimate hazard.
A broken note, stuck... That's not an echo. That's a wound. I have something to tell you. I've been hearing a dissonance in the garden's song since we arrived. It's coming from the west.
Well, we're not gonna just sit here and listen to it ache! Let's go find out what it is!

line.dialogue: The villager shuffles away, nervous. The party stands at the edge of the cultivated terraces, looking towards the wild, rocky western spurs where the unnatural sound emanates.

choices.text: Investigate the sound immediately. (Follow Chanida's impulse.)
choices.description: Malee channels engineering toward the water channels, hoping to chart resonance pathways

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
Malee loses control. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Seek local knowledge first. (Find a Listener Monk in the gardens.)
choices.description: Arthit attempts to calibrate against the frequency, relying on lattice storms

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Arthit's call. Arthit's forbidden knowledge unlocks a passage.
Arthit is thwarted. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.text: Set up camp and observe. (Monitor the sound pattern through the night.)
choices.description: The villager uses community ties to record the spectral signature near the agricultural hum

line.dialogue: Exactly as the villager hoped. Local knowledge reveals a detail outsiders would miss.
the villager loses control. Terrace-hardened resilience isn't enough.

lines_before.dialogue: The party finds a Listener Monk in a small stone shrine carved into the garden's cliff face. He is meticulously tuning a set of crystal chimes, his movements precise but tense. The dissonant hum from the west is a faint, throbbing bass note here.

You hear it too. The scar in the song. I am... sorry. We have been monitoring it. We have to do something, but my Order forbids direct intervention. It is a 'natural phenomenon' to be studied, not silenced.
Let me guess. Studying it involves a lot of note-taking and not a lot of actually helping the people who have to listen to it every night.
It's not natural. It's mechanical. A resonator crystal, shattered but still powered. It's in pain.

You perceive deeply. You are right. It is the *Amaranth*'s primary resonator. The ship itself is gone, swallowed. But its heart... its heart is stuck there, screaming. I was part of the survey team that found the wreckage. We only recovered the log. The Captain's final entry... he loved it. The silence of the deep Lattice. He loved it!! And then it took him.
A feedback loop from a damaged crystal could theoretically propagate indefinitely, creating a permanent zone of auditory and potentially physical instability. You can put your hand down now.

lines_after.dialogue: I am sorry because I transcribed that log. I heard the Captain's love turn to terror in his voice. And my Order sealed the record. Said it would 'cause panic.' The truth is buried in our archives while that crystal weeps.
That's horrible! We can't just leave it like that!
Great. So we're dealing with a haunted crystal and a cover-up. My favorite.
The truth is a frequency, not a document. It's vibrating in the air right now. We can either listen to the Order, or we can listen to the song.

line.dialogue: The Monk looks torn, clutching his tuning hammer. The dissonant hum seems to grow slightly louder, as if sensing their debate.

choices.text: Promise to silence the crystal. (A direct, physical approach.)
choices.description: Touch the resonator crystal directly and let the Amaranth's frequency pass through you, 15 words

line.dialogue: The vibration maps your nervous system like ink spreading through water — you're reading its source code.
Your hand locks rigid, tendons screaming — that frequency wasn't meant for living tissue.

choices.text: Ask for the sealed log. (Uncover the truth first.)
choices.description: Ask the monk what he did with the Amaranth before the scar appeared, 15 words

line.dialogue: I tuned it to a dead woman's voice. I wanted... one more conversation. I broke the world for it.
Your question presses where guilt has calcified. I have nothing — the answer died with my courage.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with the crystal. (A dangerous, resonant approach.)
choices.description: Hum the melody as you remember it, the clean version, counter to the scar, 15 words

line.dialogue: The scar *flinches*. You hear that? The crystal remembers what it was. It wants to follow your voice.
Your pitch drifts a half-tone flat and the scar *feeds* on it — the dissonance deepens, thickens. Stop singing.

lines_before.dialogue: The tranquility of the Hanging Gardens feels thin, brittle. The wind carries a faint, discordant hum from the Lattice below the terraces.
Great. So we're not just chasing a ghost story. The whole farm is vibrating with it. (It)'s not working. The usual peace is out of order.
That's the echo! The lost ship's final frequency! We're close. Give it to me! Let me follow it to the source!
Chanida, wait. We finished deciphering the Listener's data, but this resonance is unstable. Pushing forward blind is... unwise.
Arthit is right, but the truth is down there. The Monk's records... I went to bed late last night piecing them together. The Tonal Orders didn't just lose that ship. They silenced it.
You... you shouldn't have that knowledge.
What are you saying? The Orders protect us!
They protect their monopoly. That ship found a new, pure resonance path. A threat to their charts. So they scuttled it, and buried the song.

lines_after.dialogue: The Monk bows his head, the conflict within him resolving into grim acceptance. The villagers murmur in fear and confusion.
So the big, heroic climax is exposing a corrupt guild. How refreshingly predictable.
It's not about exposing them! It's about freeing the song! That lost resonance could change everything!

line.dialogue: The dissonant hum swells, focusing on a single, overgrown crystal node at the garden's edge. The echo of the lost ship is a wound in the Lattice here.

choices.text: Have Chanida Sing to the Echo. Use her raw talent to harmonize with the lost frequency and soothe it.
choices.consequence: Chanida's voice temporarily calms the resonance, creating a safe window to investigate, but draws immediate attention.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to map the frequency corridors, leveraging singer voice

line.dialogue: Chanida's expertise pays off. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Chanida misreads the situation. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Use the Decoded Data. Apply the Monk's forbidden research to analytically tune your resonator to the echo's signature.
choices.consequence: You gain precise understanding of the resonance's nature, revealing the exact point of the ship's destruction, but the process is slow and obvious.
choices.description: Malee presses forward with crystal prosthetic to harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Malee's leg locks onto a buried harmonic node.
The gamble fails. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.text: Pierce the Silence. Deliberately amplify the dissonance, forcing the buried truth to rupture to the surface.
choices.consequence: The reaction is violent and uncontrollable, but it reveals the full, unvarnished truth in a spectacular, undeniable way.
choices.description: The villager volunteers to decode the distress signal, leveraging local knowledge

line.dialogue: the villager pushes through. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
The risk doesn't pay off. The islander's courage breaks.

lines_before.dialogue: The air crackles. The chosen action has made the ghost frequency visible—a twisting helix of shattered light and sound above the crystal node.
The structural resonance is cascading! If this destabilizes the garden's foundation...
We have to do something! The entire terrace could shear off!
This is the truth I feared. The final scream of the condemned. I... I'll try it. I'll bear witness.
Fantastic. So we either contain a catastrophe we unleashed, or let the whole skycity hear a scandal. Do you wanna try it, Pichit? Playing hero?
It's not about playing. This echo... it's a soul in pain. A memory that wants to be heard, not to destroy.
Then let's listen! Really listen! And then... we let it sing. Wanna try some... truth?
Within the shimmering helix, the phantom shape of the Resonance Ship *The Dawn Chorus* shimmers into being, its final moments replaying in a loop of light and devastating sound.

lines_after.dialogue: The helix unfurls, not with a bang, but with a profound, cleansing chord that washes over the gardens. The dissonance is gone, replaced by a new, gentle harmony in the Lattice's song.
I... I heard it. The ship. The betrayal. All of it.
The song is free. And so is the truth. The Tonal Orders will have to answer.
Some songs can't be silenced. They just wait for someone with the courage to listen.

line.dialogue: The liberated resonance coalesces into a stable, navigable frequency—a new path through the Lattice. It is a powerful tool and a undeniable weapon against the Orders.

choices.text: Archive the Frequency. Securely record the pure tone for the Listeners to study and preserve, a gift of knowledge.
choices.consequence: You empower the monastic order, creating a new, cautious center of learning, but the change will be slow.
choices.description: Pichit channels monk wisdom toward the agricultural hum, hoping to map the frequency corridors

line.dialogue: Pichit makes it work. His staff hums with the lattice, revealing hidden patterns.
The attempt backfires on Pichit. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.text: Broadcast the Truth. Use the resonance to carry the ship's final recording to every crystal in the skycity.
choices.consequence: The scandal erupts instantly, shattering public trust in the Tonal Orders and sparking widespread unrest.
choices.description: Chanida volunteers to test the prosthetic reaction, leveraging hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Chanida finds the key. The singer's gift reveals harmony beneath the noise.
Things don't go as planned. Her voice cracks from the overwhelming frequency.

choices.text: Claim the Path. Take the new frequency as your own. You now possess a secret route, a key to untraveled parts of the Lattice.
choices.consequence: You gain immense, unique power and freedom, but become the primary target of a desperate, cornered guild.
choices.description: The monk attempts to commune with trapped echoes, relying on meditation

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the monk pulls it off. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the monk overreaches. Tonal Order enforcers confiscate his equipment.

lines_before.dialogue: The deck of the resonance ship 'Sky-Sunder' thrums with a low, steady hum. Below, the Lattice shifts in kaleidoscopic patterns, its crystalline surface rippling like a frozen sea. The wind carries the distant, mournful tones of a drifting sky-whale.
Look at that refraction... It's really worth seeing! The Lattice isn't just responding to our ship's tone—it's remembering something older.
Remembering how to swallow ships whole, probably. Your philosophical wonder doesn't pay for repairs when we hit a dissonance pocket.
Forget the repairs! Look at the scope! A frequency spike, way off the Tonal charts. It's pulsing. A ghost signal.
Ghost signals are usually just static from a collapsing island. Or pirates laying traps. The charts exist for a reason, Chanida.
But what if it's the Echo? The lost ship from the subplot? I really wonder... What if we're the first to find it in decades?

The Silencing took so much knowledge. If a ship went down carrying pre-Silencing tech... finding it could change everything. The Tonal Orders would be... I'm really hurting just thinking how they've hoarded this.

lines_after.dialogue: Great. So we're chasing a fairy tale based on a 'really worth seeing' light show and Pichit's emotional pain. My favorite kind of suicide mission.
The signal is consistent. Not random static. It's a structured call. A mayday, perhaps. Or a lure.
The ship's resonator crystals flicker, syncing briefly with the distant pulse. A shiver runs through the deck plating.

line.dialogue: The ghost signal is clear. Do we pursue it?

choices.line: Follow the signal cautiously. (Arthit's Plan)
choices.description: Tune the long-range array to match the frequency spike's harmonic pattern, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — the signal just resolved into structured pulses. That's not static, that's a language!
You've overloaded the array. Now we're deaf and blind out here. Happy?

choices.line: Charge towards it at full resonant thrust! (Chanida's Plan)
choices.description: Launch a diagnostic drone into the refraction field to capture particle samples directly

line.dialogue: The drone's lenses are capturing layered light spectra I've never seen — uploading now!
Drone's gone. Swallowed whole, just like the others. The void doesn't return what it takes.

choices.line: Ignore it and stick to the known charts. (The Safe Choice)
choices.description: Shut down all non-essential systems and run silent to observe the signal without interference

line.dialogue: With our noise gone, I can hear it — the signal has a rhythm, almost like breathing.
You killed the spectrum analyzer with that shutdown. We just lost our only ear on that frequency.

lines_before.dialogue: The Sky-Sunder cuts through a bank of sonorous mist, following the pulsing signal into an unmapped lattice flow. The air grows still, the ship's hum the only sound.
Proximity alert. Two vessels, closing fast from the starboard cloudbank. No IFF signatures. Pirate configuration.
See? I told you it was worth it! They must know about the Echo too! Battle stations!
Aren't you tired of being right in the worst possible way? They have lattice-ripper harpoons. We have... optimism.
(Crackles over comms) Hoi! Pretty ship you got there. Hand over your resonator cores and we might let you drift.
They're not just after loot. They're herding us. Why aren't you careful? They're pushing us towards a specific lattice frequency.
Confirmed. Their attack vectors are deliberate. They want us to flee into that dense crystalline formation ahead.
A trap within a trap. Lovely. Aren't you overthinking this, Pichit? Maybe they're just bad shots.

lines_after.dialogue: A harpoon grazes the hull, sending a shudder of wrong notes through the ship. The pirates' ships weave, their engines emitting disruptive counter-frequencies.
Last chance, songbirds! The Echo ain't for the likes of you!
So they *do* know. The lost ship is here. And they're its guardians... or its jailers.

line.dialogue: The pirates are forcing us into a dangerous lattice formation. How do we respond?

choices.line: Surrender the resonator cores (lose ship power, but avoid immediate destruction).
choices.description: Slam the throttle forward and attempt to outrun them through the debris field ahead.

line.dialogue: Engines screaming, hull groaning — but we're pulling ahead. They can't match us in the tight spaces.
Debris clipped our starboard fin. We're spinning, and they're closing. I told you this field was death.

choices.line: Dive into the lattice formation they're herding us towards (high risk, unknown reward).
choices.description: Cut power to all non-essential systems and drift silent behind the derelict station's shadow.

line.dialogue: No readings, no signature, no sign they even know we're here. My heart is in my throat but it's *working*.
They've got thermal sweepers — of course they do. Two dots on the scanner just became four. So much for hiding.

choices.line: Fight back, targeting their harpoon launchers (combat against two ships).
choices.description: Open a channel and bluff — claim you're carrying Imperial inspection paperwork and quarantine protocols.

line.dialogue: I can't believe that worked. They actually bought it. The pirate's
The risk doesn't pay off. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship cuts through the Lattice's shimmering surface, the engine's drone now threaded with a faint, discordant hum. The ghost signal from the Lost Ship is growing stronger, weaving through the normal frequencies like a poison thread.
Scanners are going erratic. That echo... it's not just a recording. It's *active*. It's trying to sync with our resonator. I'm not finished yet isolating it...
Of course it is. We're not chasing a memory; we're being lured to a grave. I can barely hear my own diagnostics over this psychic noise.
Then we punch through it! Find the source frequency and overwhelm it. What's the worst that could happen?
Catastrophic resonance cascade. The Lattice solidifies around us. We become the next echo. Those are the top three.
No. We listen. A true echo holds the shape of what created it. There's a message in this distortion, a final thought frozen in sound.
A sudden, violent shudder rocks the deck. The crystal viewscreen flickers, and for a moment, the phantom outline of another ship—tattered sails, broken spars—superimposes over your own.
Hah! The ghost shows its face! My crew's old charts mentioned this... a frequency snare. It wants a new singer to replace the one it lost.

line.dialogue: The phantom ship's image stabilizes, its spectral bow pointed toward a dense, swirling vortex in the Lattice below. The discordant hum crystallizes into a single, desperate, repeating tone.

choices.line: Tune the ship's resonator to match the ghost tone perfectly. Embrace the echo to understand its pain.
choices.description: Malee attempts to follow the dissonant trail, relying on leg resonance

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Her prosthetic locks onto a buried harmonic node.
Malee is thwarted. A harmonic mismatch causes malfunction.

choices.line: Order Arthit to firewall our systems and plot a rapid escape vector. Break the sync before it's complete.
choices.description: Pichit volunteers to tune the prosthetic, leveraging monk wisdom

line.dialogue: Pichit finds the key. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
The gamble fails. The prosthetic's feedback sends a painful shock.

choices.line: Have Chanida and Malee jury-rig the external speakers. Broadcast a counter-frequency—a song of release to silence the echo.
choices.description: The pirate channels secret frequencies toward the engine hum, hoping to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the pirate is thwarted. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_after.dialogue: The air crackles with released energy. The ghost ship's image shatters into a million points of fading light. For a heartbeat, the Lattice falls silent and perfectly clear.
It's gone. Not destroyed... answered. Its final log is in our buffer. Coordinates. Not to treasure, but to the truth of The Silencing.
Wonderful. So we've just graduated from ghost hunters to the most wanted people in the sky. The Tonal Orders will *love* this.

lines_before.dialogue: The clarity is short-lived. On the horizon, three sleek, official Resonance Ships emerge from a cloud bank, their hulls marked with the stern sigils of the Tonal Orders. Their broadcast hails you, a command frequency that makes the deck plates vibrate.
(Over the comms, voice panicked) It's the Enforcers! They monitored the ghost signal! You have to run! They'll scrap your ship and silence your crew!
They're broadcasting a lattice-lock frequency. If it syncs, our resonator will shut down. We'll be dead in the sky. I can't make it back to the helm if they jam us!
Let them try! What kind of fight do you prefer? Straight through, or messy? Their big ships can't turn like we can!
Oh, it's not scary at all! Just three-to-one odds against the world's monopoly on violent acoustics. What could go wrong?
The vortex the ghost pointed to—it's a chaotic frequency zone. Orders' charts avoid it. My... less official maps say it's passable, for a singer. It's a graduate-level course in not dying.
We hold the echo's truth. A truth they've buried. We don't just run. We choose the path they fear. We make the Lattice sing for *us*.

The lead Enforcer ship fires a warning shot—a concentrated sonic pulse that shears through a mast. The time for debate is over. The storm of the chaotic zone churns ahead, the orderly fleet of the Orders closes behind.

line.dialogue: The path splits. The chaotic vortex promises obscurity but unimaginable peril. The Enforcer fleet offers a brutal, direct confrontation. Or, a third path: use the ghost ship's data to broadcast its final, truth-revealing signal to all nearby skycities, turning the confrontation into a public spectacle.

choices.line: Dive into the chaotic vortex. Trust the ghost's coordinates and your crew's skill to navigate where the Orders cannot follow.
choices.description: Have Pichit risk using Listener training to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Pichit. The monk's training lets him see what others miss.
Pichit fails. A patrol ship scrambles the data.

choices.line: Stand and fight. Use the ship's agility and the pirate's knowledge of weak frequencies in Enforcer hulls to disable the lead ship and break their formation.
choices.description: Malee uses mechanical repair to tune the prosthetic near the sails

line.dialogue: Malee makes it work. The crystal leg glows, mapping what lies beneath.
The attempt backfires on Malee. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Broadcast the truth. Open all channels and transmit the Lost Ship's final log, exposing the Orders' lies to every listener in range. Let the sky itself be your shield.
choices.description: The pirate takes the lead, employing intimidation to record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: the pirate pushes through. Criminal cunning finds a loophole in the Orders' defenses.
the pirate loses control. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_after.dialogue: The consequence of your choice ripples across the Lattice. Whether in silence, in combat, or in revelation, the story of the Lost Ship is now inextricably bound to your own. The Resonance Chronicles have a new, dangerous chapter.
We are no longer just passengers on the Lattice. We are a note within its song. And today, we changed its key.
Yeah! And we lived! So, what's the next unknown worth seeing?
Don't encourage him. My nerves haven't graduated to that level of insanity yet.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tonal Archives are a cathedral of quiet. Towering crystalline shelves hum with stored resonance, their facets catching the faint glow of floating lumen-orbs. The air tastes of ozone and old parchment.
It's not working. I've cross-referenced three different cartography scrolls, and none account for the seasonal drift Malee observed in the southern Lattice.
The Tonal Orders update their charts about as often as a glacier sings. Their 'safe routes' are just the ones they haven't lost a ship on yet.
Give it to me! Let me try the resonator interface. Maybe the old frequencies just need a good kick.
A 'kick' could shatter a recording spire, Chanida. We're here to research the Echo, not become a cautionary footnote.
You're the ones asking about the Lost Ship? I went to bed late last night, couldn't sleep. Kept thinking about it. My granddad said its resonance still drifts out there, like a ghost in the crystal.
A ghost in the crystal... or a pattern the Orders chose to forget. Why would a fully-charted vessel just vanish?
Forgive the interruption. I am Kavi. Some songs are silenced not by the Lattice, but by those who fear what they might reveal.

lines_after.dialogue: The archive's central index is out of order for that sector. Deliberately so, I suspect. But the Listeners keep... alternate records.
Alternate records? Now we're talking! Where?
The Anechoic Vault. Where we store frequencies deemed 'unsettling' or 'non-compliant.' The Lost Ship's final transmission is there. It's not a chart. It's a scream.

line.dialogue: The path to the Anechoic Vault is restricted. How do we proceed?

choices.line: Ask Kavi to guide us openly, trusting his authority as a monk.
choices.description: Carefully attune the resonator to the oldest harmonic frequency in Chanida's database, 15 words

line.dialogue: There—the spire's vibrating at a frequency older than any Tonal Order revision!
Nothing. The crystals just hum back at me like they're mocking my entire thesis.

choices.line: Use Chanida's knowledge of resonator harmonics to temporarily mask our presence from the archive's acoustic wards.
choices.description: Search the marginalia of the physical chart volumes for hand-corrected coordinate notations, 15 words

line.dialogue: Someone annotated these margins decades ago—they corrected the charts but never filed the update.
Whoever owned these volumes before us had terrible handwriting and worse cartography.

choices.line: Wait for the nightly quiet period and try to slip past the few attendants.
choices.description: Apply light pressure to the base of the nearest recording spire while reading its resonance pattern, 15 words

line.dialogue: Gently... gently... I can feel the data layers shifting apart. This sp
the monk's resolve isn't enough. A lattice surge blanks the recording crystal.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anechoic Vault is a void of sound. The usual crystalline hum is gone, replaced by a pressure on the eardrums. Rows of dark, dormant resonance crystals line black stone shelves.
This place... it's like the Lattice lost its voice here. Unnatural.
It's a lot more fun than listening to those stuffy Order lecturers. The professors in the main hall are really good at teaching obedience, not truth.
Found it! Crystal log, designation 'Eventide's Lament.' Final transmission frequency. Ready to play it?
A ship named for sorrow. Proceed.

The crystal activates. Not with a navigator's calm tones, but with a chaotic, rising shriek of resonance—overlaid with a human voice, ragged with terror: 'It's not a dead zone, it's ALIVE! The charts are lies! The Lattice—' The transmission dissolves into a harmonic feedback loop, then silence.
Well. That ship didn't just get lost. It found something it shouldn't have.
The Orders declared it a 'resonance cascade.' A technical failure. But that voice... that is the sound of a paradigm shattering.

lines_after.dialogue: If the official charts have a deliberate blind spot... how many other ships were lost?
Not lost. Sacrificed. To keep a secret. The Lattice isn't just a layer; it's a listener. And perhaps, a reactor.
The transmission ended on a fractured coordinate. It's garbled, but I can trace it! It points to a sector marked 'Void' on all current charts.

line.dialogue: We have a forbidden coordinate and a terrible secret. What's our next move?

choices.line: Confront a senior Archivist with the evidence, demanding answers and safe passage to investigate.
choices.description: Touch the crystal log directly to absorb its stored memories through skin contact.

line.dialogue: * "I can feel it — the crew's last thoughts, screaming into the void before the silence swallowed everything.
* "The crystal burned cold against my palm and showed me nothing but the dark between stars.

choices.line: Work with Kavi to forge clearance documents, using the Archive's own bureaucratic resonance seals against it.
choices.description: Hack the log's encryption layer using Malee's jury-rigged lattice decoder.

line.dialogue: * "Ha! Their security was about as tough as an Order recruit's first day — pulling the audio now.
* "The encryption bit back hard. Whatever they buried in here, they wanted it to stay forgotten.

choices.line: Decode the coordinate fully and plot a course ourselves, stealing a resonance key to bypass the official navigational locks.
choices.description: Perform a resonance ritual — hum the ship's name until the log responds to sympathetic vibration.

line.dialogue: * "Eventide's Lament... the crystal is singing back. I can hear them — thirty-two souls, crying out together.
* "Nothing. Either the log's too damaged or the dead have finally stopped wanting to be heard.

lines_before.dialogue: The Archive's deepest vault is a chamber of perfect silence, walls lined with dormant crystal records. The air is cold, smelling of ozone and old parchment.
It's very important we find that ship's log before the Tonal Order realizes we're down here. Give it to me!
Careful, Chanida. These older crystal arrays are fragile. One wrong frequency could erase them.
Or summon something worse. I heard a strange noise from that side aisle. A... scraping. Like crystal on bone.
The silence here isn't empty. It's waiting. He's an old friend of mine, this kind of quiet. It holds truths.
You seek the *Eidolon's* final resonance. Its echo is trapped here, between the recorded notes. It's very important you understand... what it remembers, it *is*.
My great-grandfather was on that ship. Nobody knows what really happened. The Order's logs just say 'lost to dissonance.'

line.dialogue: The central archive crystal glows faintly. Activating it could reveal the lost ship's final moments, but might also attract unwanted attention or awaken the echo itself.

choices.text: Have Chanida tap the crystal lightly, hoping for a brief, clear glimpse.
choices.description: Carefully decouple the ship's log from the crystal array using Pichit's resonance tuning fork.

line.dialogue: I've done this a hundred times — hold the fork at the third harmonic node and the crystals release without a single crack. The log is ours.
That wasn't the third harmonic — that was the fifth. The array's splintering and the log just fused to the housing. We'll need hours to extract it now.

choices.text: Have the Listener Monk attune the party, allowing a deeper but more immersive resonance.
choices.description: Follow the strange noise Malee heard deeper into the vault's lower chamber.

line.dialogue: I knew it — there's a secondary archive down here, preserved in cold gas. The ship's log is sitting right on the pedestal, untouched.
The noise led us straight into a nesting chamber. Those things are waking up and we just became the intruders. Run — NOW.

choices.text: Have Pichit attempt to 'Sing' the crystal awake, risking a full, uncontrolled playback.
choices.description: Demand Pichit explain what he means by "the silence is waiting" before taking another step.

line.dialogue: Fine. This vault was built to contain a signal — something the ship's log transmitted. We find the log, we find what answered it. That's why I came.
I said the silence is waiting. If you can't hear what that means, then you're already listening to the wrong thing — and that makes you a liability down here.

lines_after.dialogue: The crystal blooms with light and sound—not a recording, but a living memory. The vault dissolves into the ghostly deck of the *Eidolon*.
It’s not working. The ship’s course... it wasn't lost. It was *led* off the charts. Deliberately.
A chorus of spectral voices rises from the crystal, the Echo finally given form: 'They silenced the true song... to keep their monopoly...'

lines_before.dialogue: The ghostly deck of the *Eidolon* superimposes over the vault. The air thrums with ancient agony and revelation. Tonal Order archivists rush in, their faces masks of alarm.
They're here! Good night, our quiet research trip. I heard a strange noise—oh, that's just the sound of a conspiracy unraveling.
The Echo is unstable. This memory could crystallize permanently in this chamber, trapping us all. We need to resolve this. Now.
The professors are really good at covering things up, aren't they? The great teachers of the Order. This is a lot more fun than dusting shelves.
Please, call me back to the present! This is my ancestor's death! I don't want to see it!
The Echo must be laid to rest. But to do that, its truth must be heard. The Lattice itself remembers the crime.
A crime not of dissonance, but of perfect, malicious harmony. The Order scuttled its own ship to bury a Singing navigator who threatened their control.
The spectral forms of the lost crew solidify, turning their gaze to the living archivists. 'You knew. You all knew.'

line.dialogue: The Echo swells, threatening to shatter the vault's crystals and the minds of everyone inside. The truth is out, but it must be given a voice, or contained forever.

choices.text: Convince the Lead Archivist to publicly acknowledge the truth, using the villagers and monks as witnesses to force a peaceful resolution.
choices.description: Grab the villager's hands and channel your energy to anchor him to the present moment, 15 words

line.dialogue: The crystallization stopped — your pulse matched his, and the Echo couldn't take hold.
His hands went cold. The memory pulled him deeper. We're losing him to the past.

choices.text: Have the party and the monks perform a Resonant Unbinding, a dangerous ritual to dissolve the Echo by integrating its memory into the public Archives.
choices.description: Demand Malee reveal what the professors buried in the site records before the Echo spreads further, 15 words

line.dialogue: Fine. There were seven disappearances, not two. They erased five names from the dig report.
I can't — not now. If I say it out loud inside the Echo, it becomes real.

choices.text: Pichit must lead the Echo in a final, catastrophic Song—a dirge that will shatter the vault's containment but broadcast the truth to every crystal in the sky.
choices.description: Sprint toward the temple entrance and slam the resonance seal shut before the memory fully materializes, 15 words

line.dialogue: You sealed it! The temple went silent mid-scream — whatever was forming didn't finish.
Too slow — the seal cracked on impact. Now we're sealed *inside* with the memory instead.

lines_after.dialogue: A single, clear tone rings out, cutting through the chaos. For a moment, the past and present are in perfect, terrible harmony.
Good night, to the old lie. The Lattice has remembered. Now, so will everyone else.
Whether the truth settles as a whisper or a storm is up to the sky-cities. But in the Tonal Archives, nothing will ever sound the same again.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard stretches before you—a graveyard of broken resonance ships, their crystal cores dark and silent. The air thrums with the discordant symphony of salvage: grinding metal, hissing steam, and the distant hum of the Lattice far below.
Look at this place! All this history just... chopped up for parts. You're gonna be sorry for ignoring this lead, Pichit. I feel it in my bones—there's something here.
What you feel in your bones is probably tetanus. This is a scrap heap. The only 'history' here is how many credits we'll lose on fuel.
We should proceed with caution. The scavengers here don't take kindly to outsiders poking around. Could you tell me how to get to the foreman's shack? A proper introduction might smooth our way.

Every broken ship has a final note in its song. We just need to listen. Chanida's right. I have something to tell you all... I've been hearing a fragment of melody here for weeks. It doesn't match any known ship signature.
Hey! You lot lost? This ain't a tourist dock.
We're looking for a ship. An old one. Maybe... a lost one?
They're all lost 'til we find 'em. What's it to you?

lines_after.dialogue: We seek understanding, not salvage. The song it left behind... it's incomplete.
Song, eh? You one of those Listeners? Fine. There's a hull in Sector Gamma. Been there years. Makes the lattice weep if you get too close. Even the breakers won't touch it.
The scavenger points a grimy finger toward a canyon of twisted metal. A low, dissonant hum seems to emanate from that direction, felt more than heard.

line.dialogue: The path to Sector Gamma splits three ways through the wreckage.

choices.text: Follow the main haulage road. (Safe, but slow.)
choices.description: Squeeze through a torn hull panel to reach the unscavenged cargo hold, 15 words

line.dialogue: Clear. No tripwires, no motion sensors. Whoever stripped this section was sloppy.
Contact. Two heat signatures behind the engine block — they heard the metal groan.

choices.text: Climb over the smaller hulls. (Risky, but direct.)
choices.description: Scan the wreckage with Pichit's frequency tuner for any still-active ship transponders, 15 words

line.dialogue: There — a faint pulse from the eastern yard. A navigation core still breathing.
Nothing but static and ghost frequencies. These ships died screaming and left no notes.

choices.text: Hire a scrapyard skiff. (Costs credits, but guided.)
choices.description: Climb the stacked crane containers to get a full layout of the scrapyard below, 15 words

line.dialogue: Three camps, one roving patrol, and a cargo truck that just cleared the north gate.
Rusting lattice gave out. I'm hanging by one hand and my dignity is gone.

lines_before.dialogue: Sector Gamma is a silent pocket within the scrapyard's din. At its heart rests the hull of a small, elegant resonance cutter, its lines unlike any modern design. The air is cold and still.
Well. It's not screaming. That's a start. But the resonance decay here is... wrong. It's not fading. It's looping.
A containment field failure? Where will you live if this thing has a latent core breach? We should establish a safe perimeter first.
I can smell it... ozone and old roses. I smelled perfume like that once, in my grandmother's trunk. It's coming from the ship.
Not a smell... a memory resonance. The ship is holding onto a moment. Chanida, you're connecting to it. I'm the luckiest person in the world to have a crew that senses what others miss.
A figure steps from behind a shattered engine block—a Listener monk, their simple robes stark against the industrial gloom.
You should not be here. This place is... unsettled.
We seek the echo. The one that doesn't fade. Do you know its name?

lines_after.dialogue: The 'Amaranth's Lament'. A private vessel lost just before The Silencing. Its final song is a closed loop of grief. I have studied it for years, but... the Order says to observe, not to intervene.
So you just listen to it scream forever? How enlightened.
It is not a scream. It is a question. Repeated. I can smell the perfume too, you know. Lilac and ionized air. It asks 'Where are you?'
The hull shudders, not physically, but in the resonant layer. A ghostly image flickers by the entry hatch—a woman in pre-Silencing attire, looking back, her form woven from light and sound.

line.dialogue: The echo has manifested. How do you approach the memory?

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with the echo using your ship's resonator. (Technical solution.)
choices.description: Malee takes the lead, employing mechanical repair to follow the dissonant trail

line.dialogue: The gambit pays off. Malee's engineering triggers a resonance cascade.
Malee's resolve isn't enough. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Have Chanida follow the scent-memory to its source. (Empathic, but unpredictable.)
choices.description: Convince Arthit to use tattooed routes and harness harmonic feedback

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. The crystal core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. His trauma resurfaces, freezing him.

choices.text: Ask the conflicted monk to guide you in a Listener's meditation to join the loop. (Spiritual, requires his full cooperation.)
choices.description: Direct the scavenger to decode the distress signal using harvesting tools

line.dialogue: Against the odds, the scavenger pulls it off. A spectral voice whispers coordinates before fading.
the scavenger fails. The echo fades to silence.

lines_before.dialogue: The party stands before the listing hull of the *Eternal Dirge*, its rusted plates groaning with the wind. The scavenger's lantern reveals a jagged gash in its side.
That's all, isn't it? The ship that won't die. The 'ghost' you're hunting. You sure you wanna go in there?
It's just a broken ship. Ghosts are for people who can't handle their own guilt. Let's get the resonator and leave.
No, wait. Listen. Can you hear it? A hum... like a crystal resonator, but... wrong.
It's not just a sound. It's a memory. The ship is remembering its final moments. We're standing right in front of a frozen scream.
The structural integrity is questionable. That gash looks recent. I recommend extreme caution.
This dissonance... it's painful. The Lattice weeps here. But the truth of the Silencing might be inside.
He's still single, isn't he? The old captain's spirit, I mean. Folks say he's waiting for someone to hear his story.

lines_after.dialogue: The interior of the *Eternal Dirge* is a tomb of twisted metal. A faint, sickly purple light pulses from the engine room, synced with the low, throbbing hum.
Resonance feedback loop. The primary crystal is cracked but still active. It's broadcasting the ship's last moments on a continuous loop.
It's so cold in here. And that smell... ozone and old fear.

line.dialogue: The pulsing core crystal is lodged in the ruined resonator housing. The memory-echo is strongest here, a palpable pressure.

choices.text: Attempt to harmonize with the echo using basic resonance principles (Pichit's philosophical insight).
choices.outcome: Pichit hums a counter-melody, gently untangling the feedback. The echo clarifies into a coherent memory-vision.
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the hull and open yourself to whatever memory bleeds through.

line.dialogue: I see it — a corridor full of light, faces pressed against glass, and then nothing but the dark rushing in.
Cold. Just cold metal and your own heartbeat fooling you into meaning.

choices.text: Have Chanida try to 'sing' the crystal to a stable frequency (Chanida's impulsive instinct).
choices.outcome: Chanida's raw, untrained voice clashes with the echo, creating a brief, jarring cacophony before the crystal shrieks and falls silent.
choices.description: Pull out the recorder and capture the hum's frequency, translate it into something ears were built to understand.

line.dialogue: There — the waveform resolves into a voice. It's repeating a registration number. This ship had a name once.
Static soup. Whatever it's saying, it's not saying it to us.

choices.text: Order Arthit to attempt a technical shutdown of the resonator cascade (Arthit's cautious procedure).
choices.outcome: Arthit's precise adjustments risk overloading the system. The memory-echo spikes violently before the feedback collapses.
choices.description: Speak the ship's original designation aloud and watch whether the dead recognize their own name.

line.dialogue: The hum shifts pitch. It heard me. God help us, it *remembered* being called that.
Nothing. Because there's nothing here to hear you

lines_before.dialogue: As the crystal's scream dies, the air shimmers. The ghostly afterimage of the *Eternal Dirge*'s final voyage superimposes over the scrapyard wreck.
By the First Note... it's true. You don't remember me? The stories my order told? They were lies.
The Silencing wasn't a natural disaster. Look. The ship's logs... the Tonal Orders. They deliberately shattered a primary resonance spire.
A calculated act of acoustic warfare. To create chaos and consolidate their monopoly on navigation. I... I really can't remember ever reading this.
Of course. Burn the library, control the story. I'm really hurting for all the suckers who bought their 'guidance'.
The captain... he tried to warn people. He was broadcasting the truth when they shot him down. They killed him here!
So the 'haunt' was a distress call. A truth no one wanted to hear. You've stirred up a hornet's nest, kids.
From the scrapyard shadows, the heavy thud of insulated boots echoes. Enforcers of the Tonal Orders, drawn by the spike of 'heretical' resonance, step into the light.

lines_after.dialogue: The Lead Enforcer's resonator gauntlets whine with contained power. The truth is a weapon, and you are now holding it.
You have accessed a proscribed memory. The Lattice's song must remain pure, free of dissonant lies. Surrender the crystal.
No. I remember now. I stand with them. The song must include *all* notes, even the painful ones.

line.dialogue: The Enforcers fan out, blocking the exits. The cracked core crystal, now silent, holds the only proof of the Order's crime.

choices.text: Fight your way out, using the scrapyard's chaotic acoustics to disorient them (Direct Confrontation).
choices.outcome: Metal sheets clang and engines roar, masking your movements. You escape, but the Order now knows you have the truth.
choices.description: Malee volunteers to trace the anomalous signal, leveraging crystal prosthetic

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. The prosthetic core makes the lattice temporarily visible.
Malee is thwarted. The signal dissolves into static.

choices.text: Use the *Eternal Dirge*'s wreck as a resonance bomb, overloading its systems to create a diversion (Sacrificial Blast).
choices.outcome: The ship's final, shattering scream echoes across the Lattice, a fitting epitaph. You escape in the chaos, but the evidence is destroyed.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to use the leg as a lattice probe, drawing on hidden frequencies

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. She hears something no one else can.
Chanida hits a wall. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.text: Try to broadcast the memory-echo to the nearby settlement, turning truth into a public weapon (Revelation Broadcast).
choices.outcome: You jury-rig a transmitter. For one glorious, terrible moment, the captain's final warning floods the airwaves. The Order's control frays, but their retribution will be absolute.
choices.description: Ask the scavenger to record the spectral signature, drawing on surface knowledge

line.dialogue: the scavenger makes it work. Hard-won survival skills turn the tide.
the scavenger hits a wall. The spectral voice speaks only fragments.

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire hums with a deep, resonant tone that vibrates through your bones. The air shimmers with harmonic energy, making every emotion feel distant, every thought clear.
Whoa. This place is loud. But... quiet loud, you know? My head feels weirdly calm. Let's check out that huge crystal column!
Easy, Chanida. The vibration is stabilizing, but we don't know what else it might attract. We should observe first.
Great. A giant tuning fork for the world. Just what we needed. I bet the Tonal Orders charge a fortune just to look at it.
Listen... beneath the steady tone. There are layers. Faint cries, echoes of the old world, trapped in the crystal. This place is a memory.
You perceive it. Good. I am Kavi, a Listener. Few hear the layers. Most just feel the calm. It is... a convenient silence for those in power.
A Listener? We were told your order maintained the Anchor's harmony. Is there a problem?
Maintenance. Yes. But to maintain is also to observe what is being suppressed. May I have some time? To show you something the Orders would rather stay buried?

lines_after.dialogue: Suppressed? Of course it is. Nothing is ever just given. What's the price for this 'show and tell'?
No price. Only witness. The Anchor's true frequency log. It maps... open paths. Paths not controlled by the guilds. They call it the Open Frequency Map.
A free map? No way! Nah, nah. You don't need to convince me. Let's see it!
A map of truth. When's a good time to go? The moment seems... resonant.

line.dialogue: Kavi the Listener offers to show you a hidden archive containing the Open Frequency Map. The Anchor's hum makes deception difficult, but the risk is real.

choices.line: Trust the Listener. Follow him immediately. (Proceed directly, relying on his guidance.)
choices.description: Malee steps forward with crystal prosthetic, ready to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Malee's call. The frequency map reveals a hidden corridor.
The lattice has other plans. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.line: Agree, but scout the path first. (Send Chanida ahead to check for observers.)
choices.description: Chanida channels unauthorized tones toward the crystal depth, hoping to tune the prosthetic

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. The prosthetic glows with an unfamiliar color.
Things don't go as planned. Chanida's hearing overloads from the signal.

choices.line: Demand more information. (Question Kavi about the map's origin and potential traps.)
choices.description: The monk attempts to listen for the ghost ship's echo, relying on recording crystals

line.dialogue: The risk was worth it. Arthit's tattoos warm as the phantom signal strengthens.
the monk's resolve isn't enough. His prayers go unanswered as the lattice turns hostile.

lines_before.dialogue: Following Kavi into a maintenance shaft within the Spire, the monolithic hum shifts, revealing discordant whispers. Scorch marks mar the crystal walls.
Stop right there! This ain't Listener business anymore. This is a surface claim!
A scavenger? Down here? I didn't catch what you said. You're a long way from the Lattice surface.
The map. The *real* map. The one the monk's pals stole from us! From the surface! It's ours. We charted those frequencies the hard way.
Stole? No! We *preserved* it! My former brothers took it from its rightful finders to hide it. I am trying to return it to the world!
Whoa, whoa. I can't keep up with what you're saying. You stole it from them, but *they* stole it first? Why couldn't you just share it?
Share? With the Tonal Orders breathing down our necks? They'd scrap our ships! We hid the data-core here. Now hand it over.
The data-core is here? In this shaft? This changes everything. It's not just a map; it's physical evidence.

lines_after.dialogue: Two truths, clashing in the harmonics. A monk seeking redemption, a scavenger seeking restitution. The core's song is trapped between them.
(Frustrated) I lost my phone... my comms device. Can't call my crew. It's just me. But I know this spire's blind spots. I can get us out.
The core is behind that panel. But it is booby-trapped by my order. To prevent exactly this. A frequency lock.
Perfect. So we have a treasure, a trap, and two claimants. Why can't you do it, monk? Disarm your own people's lock?

line.dialogue: The Open Frequency Map's data-core is within reach, but protected by a Listener security lock. The scavenger knows escape routes; the monk knows the lock's principles. The Spire's hum masks approaching footsteps.

choices.line: Side with the Scavenger. Use his knowledge to bypass the lock by brute force and escape quickly. (Risk damaging the core.)
choices.description: Step between them and demand the scavenger explain what "real map" means before anyone moves. *(Presence)

line.dialogue: I've got ears like a lynx, friend — and I heard *real map*. So start talking, fast.
You think blocking my sight makes you brave? It makes you *next*.

choices.line: Side with the Listener. Have him attempt to harmonize with and disable the frequency lock. (Takes time, risks triggering an alarm.)
choices.description: Quietly signal Malee to flank left while you keep the scavenger talking about the monk's brothers. *(Tactics)

line.dialogue: I'm already moving, boss. Keep his eyes on your pretty mouth.
You think I survived these tunnels by missing little hand signals? Cute.

choices.line: Unite them. Convince both to work together—the Scavenger's route and the Monk's knowledge—to retrieve the core cleanly. (Requires convincing two hostile parties.)
choices.description: Ask the monk directly: "Preserved from *whom*? Who else is hunting this map?" *(Insight)

line.dialogue: The Conclave of Closed Mouths — they would have *destroyed* it. We saved it from erasure!
I — it's complicated, and I

lines_before.dialogue: The Anchor Spire thrums, its steady tone a physical pressure in the air. The Open Frequency Map, now activated, projects shimmering, chaotic data across the crystal walls.
Look at this mess. It’s not a map; it’s a scream. The Tonal Orders didn’t just hide this. They tried to bury it.
It’s showing us everything! Every resonance path, every dead zone… Why would they keep this from us?
Control. If everyone could navigate freely, their monopoly collapses. But this… this data is volatile. It could destabilize the Lattice itself.
I have work to do. I told you the surface was scarred. This map proves it. The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a wrong note played on purpose.
A purposeful catastrophe… Then our work now isn't just discovery. It's repair. We must understand this frequency to heal the wound.
I got my answer. The Lattice's true song is one of connection, not control. My duty to the Order conflicts with this truth. Can you promise me you will use this knowledge wisely?

line.dialogue: The Map reveals a critical, unstable harmonic node deep within the Spire's foundation. Correcting it could calm the region, but risks a feedback cascade.

choices.line: Advise a slow, careful recalibration using the Spire's own harmonics.
choices.outcome: A safe, methodological approach. Minimizes risk but leaves the deeper corruption untouched.
choices.description: Trace the resonance paths with your finger, committing one route to memory before Arthit can stop you, 15 words

line.dialogue: You've got a good eye — but knowing one path won't break the system.
Careful. Touch the wrong thread and you'll bleed from your eyes.

choices.line: Propose using the Map to directly counter the unstable frequency.
choices.outcome: A direct confrontation. High chance of success, but will send a detectable pulse through the Lattice.
choices.description: Grab the scavenger's arm and demand they show you the scarred surface firsthand, right now, 15 words

line.dialogue: Fine. But you don't talk once we're up there. You only watch.
I don't take tourists. Last one who followed me lost three fingers.

choices.line: Suggest Pichit attempt to 'Sing' the correction, harmonizing with the Map's raw data.
choices.outcome: Uses Pichit's rare gift. Potentially permanent healing, but exposes him to the Lattice's traumatic memory.
choices.description: Ask Chanida to overlay her resonance data onto the map, exposing the full network publicly, 15 words

line.dialogue: If I do this, there's no undoing it. Everyone sees everything. Are you ready?
The data won't compile — someone's already scrambling the signal from inside.

lines_after.dialogue: The party acts. The Spire groans, its monolithic tone wavering, splintering into complex harmonics. The air crackles with released energy.
It's working! But listen… that sound… it's not just coming from the Spire.
Of course. We just rang the world's biggest dinner bell. The Tonal Orders will be here before the echo fades.

lines_before.dialogue: Resonance ships breach the cloud layer, their navigational hums clashing with the Spire's newly freed song. The Tonal Orders have arrived.
Three cutters, armed and locking harmonics. They’re not here to talk. They’re going to scuttle the Spire to silence the Map.
You’re back late! I saw their approach from the lower struts. They mean to bury the truth again, and us with it.
This is my home, my sanctuary. But a home built on a lie is a cage. I will stand with you.
Are you ready to go back home yet? Because our only way home is through them!
They left home in a hurry. Must be scared of what we found. Good. Let's give them a reason to be.
The Map showed us a world that was once whole. We cannot let them shatter it further. This frequency… it must be heard.

line.dialogue: The lead ship powers its primary resonator, aiming to overload the Spire's core. The harmonic backlash will destroy the Map and the Anchor.

choices.line: Evacuate. Use the Map to plot an escape route through the Lattice's unstable surface.
choices.outcome: The party survives, and the Map's data is preserved, but the Spire and its truth are destroyed. The fight continues elsewhere.
choices.description: Direct Chanida to follow the dissonant trail using frequency mapping

line.dialogue: The lattice answers Chanida's call. The resonance data crystallizes into coordinates.
The resonance turns hostile. The tablet overloads, erasing hours of work.

choices.line: Sabotage. Have Arthit and the Scavenger disable the ship's resonator from the Spire's external lattice-walks.
choices.outcome: A tactical victory. The immediate threat is neutralized, but it declares open war with the Tonal Orders.
choices.description: Direct Pichit to harness harmonic feedback using staff meditation

line.dialogue: Pichit's expertise pays off. Pichit's staff captures an unexpected tonal signature.
Pichit overreaches. A harmonic mismatch makes the prosthetic seize up.

choices.line: Broadcast. Use the Spire and the Map to amplify the Open Frequency, flooding every crystal in range with the unedited truth.
choices.outcome: The ultimate revelation. Every ship, every city will hear it. It breaks the Order's control forever, but the resulting harmonic storm is unpredictable.
choices.description: The scavenger attempts to listen for the ghost ship's echo, relying on survival skills

line.dialogue: Fortune favors the scavenger. Surface knowledge reveals a safe path.
The gamble fails. The surface dweller's methods prove too crude.

lines_after.dialogue: The climax resonates. A new tone is born from the conflict—a complex chord of defiance, truth, and change that echoes across the floating islands.
Listen… The Lattice is remembering. It’s not just a map we found. It’s a memory. And now, it’s awake.
Well. We certainly made a mess. But it's a more interesting mess than the one we had before.
The repercussions of this will cascade. We have no charts for what comes next.
Who needs charts? We've got the real song now! Let's go sing it to everyone!

lines_before.dialogue: The wind whispers through the terraces of Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens, a slow, rhythmic sigh that parts the sea of golden grain. The air smells of damp soil and ripening fruit.
Anywhere. Anywhere you like. This place is so quiet you could hear a crystal crack. It's a nice change from the city's drone.
A nice change, yes. But also isolated. We should be cautious. The Tonal Orders don't patrol these outer terraces often.
Relax, Arthit. The only danger here is dying of boredom. Look at them.
Malee gestures to a group of the villagers tending to hydroponic vines. Their movements are slow, deliberate, and utterly silent.
Their silence is... profound. Not the absence of sound, but a deliberate holding of breath. As if they're afraid of disturbing something.
You shouldn't linger. The evening winds carry strange tones from the deep Lattice. Bad for the crops. Bad for the mind.
Why are you doing this to me? Why are you treating me like this? We're just resting!

lines_after.dialogue: No offense meant. It's just... there's an echo here lately. In the old irrigation channels. Sounds like a ship's resonator, but there's no ship.
A ghost ship? Don't tell me you sky-farmers believe in nursery tales.
Ask the Listener at the old watch-spire. He hears it too. He's been... different. Nervous.

line.dialogue: The villager's fear is palpable. Pichit considers their next move.

choices.line: Dismiss the tale. The villager is just superstitious. (Ignore the lead.)
choices.description: Press your ear against the hollow stalks and listen for the source of the hum.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the soil, a rhythm, like a heartbeat buried deep. Something is breathing down there.
Great, now you've got mud on your ear and we've learned exactly nothing. Can we keep moving?

choices.line: Investigate the irrigation channels directly. See if you can hear this 'echo.' (Search the gardens.)
choices.description: Split up to map the perimeter before the light fades, pairing Chanida with Pichit.

line.dialogue: Good. We cover more ground, stay in earshot. If either of us finds trouble, three sharp whistles.
No. Whatever silenced this place could pick us off one by one. We stay together, or we don't move at all.

choices.line: Seek out the Listener Monk at the watch-spire. He might have a clearer perspective. (Follow the lead.)
choices.description: Kneel beside Pichit and ask what he means by "not the absence of sound."

line.dialogue: Silence is empty. This is full. Pressed down, layered — like thousands of voices holding their breath at once.
He's being poetic again. I told you, there's nothing here but fields and quiet. Let's not invent ghosts.

lines_before.dialogue: The old watch-spire is a skeletal structure of worn crystal and rusted iron, overlooking the terraces. A lone figure in grey robes stands at its edge, head tilted as if listening to the clouds.
The resonance is off. The foundational hum of this sector... it's developed a stutter. Like a door closing out of rhythm.
A door?
A metaphor. The guy in the condo next door always closes his door loudly. A jarring, final sound. This is similar. A disruption in the Lattice's natural song.
The villagers spoke of an echo. A ship's resonator with no ship.

The *Amaranth*. A Resonance scout lost during The Silencing. Its signature frequency is... bleeding through. A class-one tonal anomaly. I have a class. I have a class to teach on stable harmonics, but this... this undermines everything.
So a dead ship is humming down below? And the mighty Tonal Orders haven't charted it?

They chart what they wish to hear. This frequency is one of failure. Of a navigation error that cost lives. They would silence it, if they could. I... I'm gonna rush off right now. I need to meditate. This knowledge is a burden.

lines_after.dialogue: He's terrified. Not of the echo, but of what it means.
The Lattice remembers. It holds the song of everything that has ever passed through it. Even the mistakes.
If this is the *Amaranth*, its resonator crystal might still be intact. A relic from before The Silencing. Incredibly valuable. Or incredibly dangerous.
And our nervous monk just left us with the map to it. The 'stutter' in the hum.

line.dialogue: The path is clear, but fraught with risk. The ghost of the *Amaranth* calls from below the gardens.

choices.line: Report the anomaly to the local Tonal Order authority. Let them handle it. (Avoid direct risk.)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the temple wall and feel for the foundational hum's rhythm.

line.dialogue: There — beneath the stone — it's not broken, it's *split*. Two frequencies fighting each other, like twins singing different songs.
All I feel is cold mineral and my own heartbeat. Whatever foundation this sect built on, it's not talking to me.

choices.line: Trace the anomalous frequency to its source in the gardens. Find where the Lattice is thinnest. (Investigate cautiously.)
choices.description: Ask the monk to chant the foundational verse exactly as taught, while you listen for where it wavers.

line.dialogue: You hear it too, then — the third stanza collapses inward. The words are correct but the breath underneath them has been replaced. Someone rewrote the root.
I tried. My throat seized at the second line. The melody knows I don't believe it anymore, and it punishes hesitation.

choices.line: Attempt to resonate with the echo directly, using the party's own ship crystal. Try to 'answer' the lost ship. (Engage the anomaly.)
choices.description: Follow the echo Arthit mentioned — track the ship's resonator frequency outward to find what's broadcasting the interference.

line.dialogue: The signal leads southeast, past the coral shelves. Whatever's generating that counter-frequency, it's anchored, deliberate, and old. Older than this sect.
The echo dissipates the

lines_before.dialogue: The sun begins to dip below the Lattice's shimmering horizon, casting long shadows across the terraces. A strange silence falls over the gardens—even the wind through the crops seems to hold its breath.
See? Told you. The moment we start asking about that ship, everything gets... quiet. The Lattice knows we're poking around.
It's not the Lattice, it's them. Look.
A group of villagers approaches, led by the Listener Monk from earlier. Their faces are grim, their tools held not for farming, but for barring the way.
You need to leave. Now. Everyone knows it—that ship's echo is a curse. You're stirring up ghosts best left silent.
Please. I tried to warn you gently. The song it left behind... it's not a natural resonance. It's a wound. I don't want it to spread.
A wound implies something was done to it. What happened to the 'Echo' wasn't an accident, was it?
They're not listening, Pichit. Look at their stances. They've been told to make us disappear.

lines_after.dialogue: The monk looks at the ground, ashamed. The villagers tighten their circle.
The Tonal Orders... they know we Listeners heard the true song of that ship's demise. They know we could prove it wasn't lost. It was silenced.
So you're going to silence us too? Some monk you are.

line.dialogue: The villagers advance. The monk won't meet your eyes. The truth is here, but so is the danger.

choices.line: [Diplomacy] Appeal to their fear. 'If you silence us, the echo only grows louder. Let us heal it.'
choices.outcome: The monk hesitates. 'Heal it? Is that possible?' You've created a sliver of doubt, a chance to talk rather than fight.
choices.description: Grab the monk by his robes and demand he finish what he was saying about the song. 14 words

line.dialogue: [The monk's eyes go wet. "It replays in your skull. Every night. Until you walk toward the water."]
[The monk wrenches free and backs away trembling. "You're already humming it. I can hear it. I can hear it in your throat."]

choices.line: [Confrontation] Call out the monk's hypocrisy. 'You Listen, but you obey. What song does your conscience sing?'
choices.outcome: The monk flinches as if struck. The villagers glance at him, uncertain. You've shaken their unity, but inflamed his guilt.
choices.description: Ignore the warnings and march toward the harbor where the ship was last seen anchored. 14 words

line.dialogue: [Chanida grabs your arm. "Look at the waterline—no barnacles, no rot. That thing didn't float here. It grew here."]
[Malee tackles you sideways as something wet and percussive thrums from the dock pilings. "That sound—my teeth are vibrating. Get back, GET BACK."]

choices.line: [Provocation] Sing a fragment of the haunted ship's resonance. Let the Lattice here remember.
choices.outcome: The terraces shudder. A low, grieving hum rises from the crystal below. Panic breaks the villagers' ranks. The truth resonates, violently.
choices.description: Sit down cross-legged in the road and ask the villager plainly what happened to the crew. 15 words

line.dialogue: [The villager's jaw works silently before he whispers: "Came ashore smiling. All of them. Wouldn't stop. Their mouths just... kept opening wider."]
[The villager stares past you, fixed and glassy, and begins softly humming a melody you have never heard but somehow already know.]

lines_before.dialogue: Chaos. Whether by word, challenge, or song, the confrontation has erupted. The grieving resonance of the lost ship now vibrates through the garden's very stones.
Stop it! You're killing the crops! The resonance will sour the harvest for seasons!
He's the only son in his family, you know? The one holding the scythe. They send their best to do their dirty work.
The monk is pacing back and forth, torn between calming his people and staring in horror at the shimmering air. The ship's 'echo' is now a visible scar in the twilight.
It's a memory! A recording of its final moments! You're playing a tragedy on repeat!
Pichit, we can't contain this. We either learn from it now, or it drowns this whole terrace in grief.
This resonance is great! It's a really good recording! It's showing us everything—the attack, the panic, the falling... It wants to be heard!
No. It doesn't want to be heard. It needs to be understood. Then it can finally rest.

lines_after.dialogue: The spectral image of a shattered resonance ship flickers above the terraces. The wail of its dying crystal drive is a physical pressure.
The Orders... they scuttled it. A Singer was aboard, charting independent routes. They couldn't allow that.
The truth hangs in the air, more solid than the ghostly ship. The villagers have stopped, tools lowering, listening to the echo they were told to fear.

line.dialogue: The echo reaches its crescendo. It will either shatter, taking the gardens with it, or be transformed. You stand at the epicenter.

choices.line: [Absorb] Let the memory flow through you. Bear the pain of its final moment to give it peace.
choices.outcome: You take the ship's dying scream into yourself. The ghostly image fades, leaving only a calm, sad harmony. The gardens are saved, but the memory is now a permanent scar on your soul.
choices.description: Kneel beside the withered rice and let the resonance flow through you instead of the field

line.dialogue: I can see it now — the flood, the boy running, the water taking him. It's showing us *why*.
My hands won't stop shaking. The grief in this soil is too deep — it's pulling me under with it.

choices.line: [Redirect] Channel the resonance into the Lattice below, letting the world itself remember the crime.
choices.outcome: You sing a guide-tone. The echo sinks into the crystalline layer, a permanent fault line of truth. The gardens stabilize, but the Lattice here will forever whisper the story, creating a haven for future dissent.
choices.description: Order Pichit to ring the temple bell at inverted intervals to disrupt the resonance pattern

line.dialogue: The recording is fragmenting — look, the boy's face is clearer now. We can hear his last words.
The bell only amplified it. The resonance is spreading to the next field — we've made it worse.

choices.line: [Amplify] Don't calm it. Sharpen it. Turn the grief into a beacon, a signal so loud the Orders in distant cities cannot ignore it.
choices.outcome: You focus the wrath. A pillar of shattered sound pierces the sky. The gardens are damaged, but the echo becomes a declaration of war. The truth is now a weapon, and you have just fired the first shot.
choices.description: Grab the villager by the shoulders and demand he tell you the son's full name to anchor the memory

line.dialogue: His name is Somchai. The moment she said it, the resonance stopped screaming — it's *listening* now.
He won't speak it. He says the name died with the boy, and now the field is cracking open.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market thrums with the chaotic symphony of commerce. The air, thick with spice and sweat, vibrates with the overlapping chatter of a thousand deals.
Ugh, this noise! How does anyone think straight? I'm trying to listen for a good deal, but it's all just... hum.
The hum is the point, Chanida. It's the perfect cover. In this din, secrets are cheaper than crystal shards.
And more dangerous. We should stick to the plan. Find the negotiator, secure the parts, leave. No deviations.
Yet the plan exists within the hum, Arthit. Listen. Beneath the bartering... a rhythm of desperation.
Friends! The sun shines on your coin-purses! Come, see the finest Lattice-tuned resonators this side of the sky!

lines_after.dialogue: Pichit's right. I overheard that merchant talking to a scavenger. Something about a 'resonant prosthetic.' A leg, I think.
A crystal leg? That sounds expensive! My father won't let me have a new dagger, let alone a limb.
It's not necessary to get involved. Prosthetics are Tonal Order business. We're here for ship parts.

line.dialogue: The merchant's smile doesn't reach his eyes. He's hiding something about the prosthetic deal. Do we...
