choices.text: Approach directly and ask about the prosthetic. (Social)
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the wall and feel for vibrations beneath the hum.

line.dialogue: [Pichit: "There — beneath the static. A second pulse, rhythmic, deliberate. Someone is signaling through the structure itself."]
[Chanida: "Nothing but the buzz crawling up my arm. Whatever's in there, it doesn't want to be found by touch alone."]

choices.text: Send Malee to eavesdrop on his next conversation. (Stealth)
choices.description: Signal Malee to move toward the vent shaft where the hum resonates deepest.

line.dialogue: [Malee: "The grille is loose — and the sound changes pitch when I press here. This is the throat of it. We can get through."]
[Arthit: "She's exposed. The guard rotation isn't what Pichit predicted — someone's already watching that corridor."]

choices.text: Ignore it and focus on our original task. (Cautious)
choices.description: Close your eyes and isolate the layer beneath the hum — the whisper Pichit mentioned.

line.dialogue: [Pichit: "You hear it now, don't you? A voice, not machinery. Repeating coordinates. The plan was never ours alone — someone inside is guiding us."]
[Chanida: "You stood there like a statue for thirty seconds and learned nothing. The hum doesn't give up secrets to people who daydream."]

lines_before.dialogue: The party weaves through the crowd, the decision made. The market's energy shifts from background noise to a field of potential clues.
He's meeting the scavenger by the spice stalls. The negotiator is nervous. Keeps checking over his shoulder.
The core's unstable. Flickers like a dying star. You want it for a leg? It'll shatter the poor sod's hipbone.
The buyer is... insistent. Payment is triple the usual. Sometimes it's not necessary that a thing be safe, only that it be delivered.
Triple? Who pays that for a broken crystal? What do you think about this, Pichit? It's something to think about.
I think a soul in great pain seeks a dangerous remedy. The Lattice sings of imbalance here.
And we are about to step into it. I'm just surprised the Orders aren't already swarming this place.

lines_after.dialogue: You! The ones lurking! You with the Tonal rats?
A misunderstanding, I'm sure! These are just customers!
The scavenger's hand is on his cutter. The merchant's smile is gone. We've discovered a bit more of the unknown than we planned.

line.dialogue: The scavenger is hostile, the merchant is panicking. The unstable crystal core for the prosthetic is right there on the bartering mat.

choices.text: De-escalate. Assure the scavenger we're not with the Orders. (Diplomacy)
choices.description: Pichit takes the lead, employing staff meditation to decode the tonal pattern

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. Chanida's tablet captures a pulsing tonal pattern.
A costly mistake by Pichit. The monk's training fails against this threat.

choices.text: Grab the unstable core. It's the key to the whole deal. (Daring)
choices.description: Chanida takes the lead, employing unauthorized tones to test the prosthetic reaction

line.dialogue: The crystal sings for Chanida. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Defeat. The lattice frequency overwhelms the core.

choices.text: Accuse the merchant of endangering lives. Turn the market crowd against him. (Manipulation)
choices.description: Convince the merchant to use valuable goods and record the spectral signature

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. His network produces an ally at the critical moment.
the merchant hits a wall. The negotiator's deal falls through.

lines_before.dialogue: The Scavenger leads you to a secluded stall draped in faded silks, its counter displaying unnervingly smooth Lattice fragments.
The Merchant's got a Singer in a back room, running her ragged to chart new routes. He's the only son in the family business, and he's desperate to impress his father.
Exploiting a Singer? That's monstrous! You have to see it to believe it. We're getting her out.
Hold on. This 'rescue' is a great way to get branded as Tonal Order enemies. This is a really good movie plot, but we're not actors.
The Scavenger's information is... something to think about. But confronting the Merchant directly in his own market? The risks are immense.
A voice used as a tool, not a gift. The Lattice hums in dissonance with such acts. We cannot ignore this.
Look, the prosthetic leg you're after? It's in that same back room. Prize from a surface dig. He won't part with it cheap.
Ah, my new friends! I see you've met my... associate. Come to finalize our deal?

line.dialogue: The Merchant's smile is polished, but his eyes dart to the Scavenger. The Singer and the prosthetic are both within reach, but so is his wrath.

choices.text: Confront him publicly. Shame him before the market crowd. (Social, risks drawing the Tonal Orders)
choices.description: Kick down the back room door and get the Singer out — deal with consequences after.

line.dialogue: Chanida — "She's breathing free air now. Whatever comes, we'll face it standing.
Chanida — "They were ready for us. The Singer's gone and we're marked.

choices.text: Propose a trade. Offer something of greater value for both the Singer's freedom and the leg. (Negotiation, requires a significant sacrifice)
choices.description: Slip through the Merchant's den posing as buyers to locate and extract the Singer quietly.

line.dialogue: Malee — "No alarms, no blood, no brand. She's out and nobody knows our names.
Malee — "The Merchant made us the second we walked in. Should've known the face wouldn't hold.

choices.text: Create a diversion. Use the market's noise to mask a stealthy infiltration of the back room. (Stealth, immediate danger if caught)
choices.description: Pay the Scavenger to shadow the Singer's movements and find who's buying what she produces.

line.dialogue: Arthit — "Now we know the chain. Every link has a name, and names can be cut.
Arthit — "The Scavenger sold our inquiry right back to the Merchant.

lines_after.dialogue: The market's constant hum seems to sharpen, awaiting your response. The Merchant's hand rests casually on a small, tuned crystal on his belt.
Well? The Lattice waits for no one, and neither does commerce.
You must see it, Pichit. He's already decided we're a problem. The question is how expensive we'll be.

lines_before.dialogue: The confrontation reaches its peak. Whether through words, trade, or chaos, you stand before the Merchant's sealed back room as the market's noise fades into a tense bubble of silence.
You're a nice person, Pichit. I can see that. But this is business. It's nice and peaceful when everyone follows the rules.
Peaceful for you! Who is this guy to decide who gets to sing freely?
The resonance lock on this door is keyed to his personal frequency. Forcing it will shatter the crystal and alert every enforcer in the sector.
True peace cannot be built on a silenced song. You have mistaken control for harmony.
The door slides open. Inside, a young woman with tired eyes is chained to a large resonator. On a table beside her glows the Resonant Prosthetic, its crystal pulsing weakly.
He's a nice guy, huh? Real prince. The leg's right there. So's the evidence.
A final offer. Take the leg, and walk away. The Singer stays. Or challenge me, and lose everything. What do you think about that?

line.dialogue: The Singer's eyes meet yours, filled with a desperate hope. The prosthetic leg hums, a potential key or a mere prize. The Merchant's smile is gone, replaced by cold calculation.

choices.text: Take the leg and leave. Secure the subplot objective, but abandon the Singer to her fate. (Practical, morally costly)
choices.description: Chanida attempts to map the frequency corridors, relying on frequency mapping

line.dialogue: Exactly as Chanida hoped. Her frequency range picks up a buried signal.
Chanida fails. Her range hits a limit she didn't know existed.

choices.text: Smash the resonator. Free the Singer's voice to create a chaotic resonance burst to cover your escape with her and the leg. (Destructive, draws immense attention)
choices.description: Ask Arthit to test the prosthetic reaction, drawing on forbidden paths

line.dialogue: Arthit makes it work. His tattoos pulse with ancient notation, guiding true.
The attempt backfires on Arthit. The captain's route leads into worse danger.

choices.text: Sing to the lock. Use your own nascent ability to harmonize with and bypass the Merchant's frequency, freeing the Singer silently. (Risky, reveals your potential)
choices.description: Have the merchant focus market connections on the spice scents to decode the distress signal

line.dialogue: Victory, for now. His trade connections deliver the right information.
the merchant loses control. Hidden debts come due.

lines_after.dialogue: The air crackles with potential. Your choice here will echo through the market's gossip, the Tonal Orders' ledgers, and the silent song of the Lattice itself.
Please...
Choose. Now.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hollow is a cathedral of silence, its walls jagged with dark crystal. The air hums with a subsonic thrum, a memory of sound trapped in stone.
Look at these carvings! They're... moving? No, it's the light from the Lattice outside. Still, gives me the creeps.
Stay close to the wall. The floor here is unstable. This whole place feels like it's holding its breath.
Not silence. A held note. The entire Silencing... what if it wasn't an end, but a pause waiting to be resolved?
Philosophy won't stop a cave-in. Let's find this scavenger contact and get what we came for before the local fauna does.
You're the ones poking around the old bones, eh? Tread softly. The stone here remembers. And it doesn't like visitors.
We mean no harm. We're seeking knowledge of the past, before the Silencing.
Knowledge? Heh. My pa sought knowledge. Got himself swallowed by a bad echo. I'll see you there at the dig site, but don't expect a guided tour.

lines_after.dialogue: He’s been married twice, you know. My pa. Said the Lattice was his first love, the ruins his second. Both left him hollow. Don't make the same mistake.
Charming. So, where's this dig site?
Follow the low hum. And watch for the Monk. He's been down here for weeks, listening to walls. Cracked, if you ask me.

line.dialogue: The scavenger points down three diverging, echoing tunnels.

choices.line: Follow the loudest hum (Trust the guide).
choices.description: Press your palm flat against the shifting carvings and let the stone speak through you.

line.dialogue: Oh — oh! I can feel it, the whole history of the Silencing, it's pouring up through my fingers like cold water!
Nothing. Just stone. Whatever frequency it's resonating at, my body can't tune to it — but I swear it *tried* to say something.

choices.line: Follow the faintest, highest-pitched tone (Intuition).
choices.description: Signal Arthit to test each floor tile with the iron butt of his torch before stepping.

line.dialogue: Good call — this one's hollow, see? Two meters down, a sheer drop. We'd have been paste. Keep behind me single file.
Should have held pressure longer. The tile looked solid, sounded solid — then it wasn't. My leg's through up to the hip. Don't laugh, just pull.

choices.line: Mark the walls and proceed slowly (Methodical).
choices.description: Demand Pichit sing the held note he's hearing and match the chamber's resonance to open a path.

line.dialogue: I don't... I've never — fine. *Hmmmmmm.* There! You see the far wall? The mortar's crumbling. The Silencing was a chord, and I just sang its inverse!
I can hear it but I can't *reach* it. It's like remembering a face

lines_before.dialogue: The chosen tunnel narrows, the crystals underfoot glowing with a soft, captured light. A distant, rhythmic clanging echoes, out of sync with your steps.
That's not an echo. That's metal on stone. Someone's working.
Or something's *been* working for a very long time. Look at these tool marks. Pre-Silencing, but fresh scars overlay them.
It's really a great place to live! Said no one ever about a haunted cave. Why didn't you go check it out first, Arthit?
Because my job is to keep you alive, not volunteer as a sonic lure.
Wait. Listen. Beneath the clanging... a melody. Broken, but familiar. It's the distress pattern from the Echo of the Lost Ship.
You hear it too.

lines_after.dialogue: I am Brother Kael. I have been trying to transcribe it. How do you write a song that refuses to be captured? How do you write it when the notes change every time you listen?
You don't write it. You listen until you understand what it's trying to say.
The Tonal Orders would have this place sealed. They say such sounds are corruptions. But this... this is a memory. A ship's final moments, etched into the crystal itself.
A ghost in the machine. Lovely. And it's clanging because...?

line.dialogue: Brother Kael gestures to a fissure where the clanging is loudest. A faint, shifting light pulses within.

choices.line: Send a resonance pulse to calm the echo (Apply Order techniques).
choices.description: Follow the scraping sound alone, keeping one hand on the wall for orientation, 15 words

line.dialogue: The sound's coming from ahead—I can see tool marks fresh on the stone, maybe thirty meters.
I lost the wall in the dark and now I'm not sure which direction I came from—stay put.

choices.line: Attempt to harmonize with the memory-song (Use Pichit's latent ability).
choices.description: Signal everyone to silence, then press your ear flat against the tunnel wall to triangulate the source, 15 words

line.dialogue: Two rhythms—something digging, and something dragging. They're not the same maker. We have company plural.
All I can hear is my own heartbeat and Chanida breathing too loud—the wall is vibrating too much.

choices.line: Break the crystal resonator causing the feedback (Disrupt the pattern).
choices.description: Grab Chanida's wrist and pull her back toward the last junction, retreating to a defensible position, 15 words

line.dialogue: Okay, rough but fair—I see the alcove you mean, and it actually has cover we can use.
You pulled me straight into

lines_before.dialogue: The passage narrows, the air growing cold and heavy. The carvings on the walls shift from geometric patterns to frantic, looping script—the last records of a dying people.
We've talked about this before. My order... we were told these places were silent. Empty. But this song... it's a dirge.
So the Listeners knew about the Hollow? Knew it wasn't just echoes?
Nah, nah. They didn't just *know*. They were told to stay away. Who gives orders to monks who only listen to rocks?
The Tonal Orders. It has to be. They control all navigation. If the Listeners found something that challenged that...
The truth is often buried under the most convenient lies. What else have we 'talked about' that wasn't true, monk?
I'm such a lucky gal! Stumbling into a conspiracy while looking for salvage. The resonator readings are spiking ahead. Something's... singing back.
A low hum vibrates through the stone, a resonant frequency that makes the ancient crystals in your packs glow with an inner light.

lines_after.dialogue: The hum coalesces into a faint, shimmering image against the far wall—the ghostly silhouette of a Resonance Ship, its hull torn and crystalline sails tattered.
The Echo... it's not just a memory. It's a recording. A final broadcast, trapped in the stone.
It's waiting. It has a message.

line.dialogue: The phantom ship's image flickers. A distorted voice, layered with countless whispers, struggles to form words.

choices.text: Harmonize: Use your ship's crystal to resonate with the echo, stabilizing the signal.
choices.outcome: The image clarifies. The voice becomes a single, desperate captain's log.
choices.description: Grab Arthit's collar and demand proof of the Tonal Orders' involvement, 15 words

line.dialogue: [arthit] "The charters bear their seal — harmonic frequencies locked into every approved route through the Hollow.
[arthit] "I — I'm guessing! The patterns fit, but I don't have the codices, I just *feel* it!

choices.text: Interrogate: Demand the echo identify itself and its purpose.
choices.outcome: The echo reacts to the command, its form shifting aggressively, offering fractured data.
choices.description: Ask the monk to recite the exact words his order was given about the Hollow

line.dialogue: [monk] "The verse said: 'Where stone sings hollow, lay no path, mark no wall, name no traveler.
[monk] "It was... something about silence. They made us memorize it in resonance chambers — I can't recall the words clearly.

choices.text: Listen Deeper: Quiet all external sound. Open yourself to the raw, painful frequency beneath.
choices.outcome: You hear not just the message, but the dying thoughts of the crew—a truth that shakes you.
choices.description: Suggest Chanida sing the forbidden hollow-tone to test if the stone responds here

line.dialogue: [chanida] "There — you felt that? The walls vibrated. The Hollow isn't just a place. It's *listening*.
[chanida]

lines_before.dialogue: The cavern opens into a vast, spherical chamber. At its center, suspended in a web of solidified Lattice-energy, is the wreck of the *Whispering Dawn*. Its echo was a beacon.
Who is this lady? This ship? It's pre-Silencing. Older than the Orders. Older than anything still flying.
Its resonator core is intact. And it's... pulsing. I'm gonna ask him—the monk—what his precious Lattice is really saying about this.
It's very important that you understand. The Silencing wasn't an accident. The Lattice didn't just 'react.' This ship... its log... it was attacked.
Attacked? By what? There was nothing left *to* attack after...
By someone who wanted the silence. Who wanted the charts to be the only way. The Tonal Orders didn't just take over after the disaster. They *caused* it.
A monopoly built on genocide. The ultimate silencing. This wreck isn't just a relic. It's evidence.
The core of the *Whispering Dawn* flares. The ghostly echo of its Singer-captain materializes fully, eyes burning with crystalline light, pointing an accusatory finger at the world above.

lines_after.dialogue: The Singer's echo opens its mouth. No sound emerges, but the chamber itself resonates with a truth so violent it cracks the stone.
It's very important that this gets out. But the Orders... they'll know. They monitor all major resonances. They are coming.
Then we make our stand here. We let the Hollow sing the last song it was meant to sing.

line.dialogue: The *Whispering Dawn*'s core is a weapon and a recorder. The approaching fleet of the Tonal Orders vibrates through the Lattice above. You must choose how to use the truth.

choices.text: Broadcast: Use the core to transmit the ship's log to every resonator in range, revealing the history.
choices.outcome: The truth becomes a wave, impossible to contain. The Orders' authority shatters, but the chaos is widespread.
choices.description: Touch the pulsing resonator core directly with your bare hand.

line.dialogue: * "The frequency—it's showing me stars I've never seen, burning in patterns that spell something alive.
* "Pulled back. My fingertips went numb and I tasted copper—that core doesn't want me, it wants someone already touched by the old waves.

choices.text: Sabotage: Channel the core's energy into a resonant spike to cripple the approaching fleet.
choices.outcome: You defend the Hollow and escape with the evidence, but the Orders survive to hunt you, now knowing your power.
choices.description: Demand the monk finish his explanation about the Silencing—now, no more riddles.

line.dialogue: * "The Silencing wasn't destruction. It was burial. Something was hidden inside the quiet, and this ship was meant to wake it.
* "You're not ready. I can see it in your breathing—you still think silence means safety. It never did.

choices.text: Archive: Download the log into your own ship's crystal, sacrificing the wreck to collapse the cavern and bury the truth—for now.
choices.outcome: You escape unseen, carrying the most dangerous secret in the world. The fight moves to the shadows, and it is yours alone.
choices.description: Ask Malee to scan the ship's manifest for crew logs—someone lived here once.

line.dialogue: * "Found them. Seven crew members, all listed as 'resonance-compatible.' Their final log entry is just one word: *Remembering.*

title: The Echo Beneath Moonwell Platform — Relax / Further

acts.title: The First Signal at Moonwell Platform

lines.dialogue: By the time the party reaches Moonwell Platform, the lattice has made the first signal impossible to ignore.
lines.stage_directions: The air around Moonwell Platform vibrates in a slow interval.

lines.dialogue: Kanya checks the anchor weights and listens for a failing tether.
lines.stage_directions: Kanya raises a hand for silence.

lines.dialogue: "Don’t judge others." Pichit says, and the nearest crystal answers the phrase.
lines.stage_directions: The first resonance ring brightens.

lines.dialogue: Bussaba recognizes the first phrase and points toward the maintenance rail.
lines.stage_directions: Bussaba marks one beat on a slate.
